cdmtools: an r package for cognitive diagnosis modeling cdmtools：认知诊断建模的r包 the cdmtools package contributes to the existing landscape of statistical software for cognitive diagnosis modeling (cdm) by providing functions that support both applied research and simulation studies within this framework. its main functionalities include (a) the estimation of recently proposed models for small-scale assessments (gnpc, r-dina) and alternative response formats (fc-g-dina), (b) the evaluation of test internal structure through dimensionality assessment and empirical q-matrix validation, (c) the assessment of model identifiability, and (d) auxiliary analyses such as reliability estimation and person-fit assessment. overall, the cdmtools package provides several useful tools for cdm analyses and can be easily integrated with other well-established packages in the field. applied psychological measurement

an individualised approach to autism and criminal intent purpose this paper aims to examine how autism spectrum disorder (asd) is treated in forensic evaluations of criminal intent and proposes an individualised, functional standard for weighing asd-related evidence. design/methodology/approach the paper synthesises recent empirical literature on asd and social cognition, emotional regulation, adaptive functioning, suggestibility and threat perception and examines virginia’s evidentiary statute on asd and specific intent as an illustration of an individualised functional legal framework. findings diagnosis alone provides insufficient information about criminal intent. autism-related differences in social cognition, emotional regulation and adaptive functioning are heterogeneous and only loosely tied to diagnostic status, so forensic relevance depends on documented, individualised impairment rather than the presence of an asd diagnosis. originality/value the paper integrates findings on theory of mind and criminal-intent recognition and on adaptive functioning in forensic asd samples, with virginia’s statutory framework to propose an individualised functional approach evaluators can apply directly to casework. advances in autism

prevalence of depression and dementia among institutionalized elderly in kenya: nairobi county objective the purpose of this investigation was to determine the prevalence of and the link between depression and dementia, and other risk factors among institutionalized elderly in kenya. methods this research utilized a cross-sectional design. the sample of 194 was selected through simple random sampling. this study used 6-item cognitive impairment test (6-cit), geriatric depression scale (gds) and the cornell scale for depression in dementia (csdd) to measure the point prevalence of depression and dementia, and a socio-demographic questionnaire to explore the other objectives. results 11% and 37% screened positive for depression and dementia respectively. identified risk factors for institutionalization were: being single, having an impairment, chronic illness, poor self-rated health, being dependent for basic daily functioning and having little social support. this study observed a positive relationship between depression and dementia ( r = .253, df = 186, p < .001). there was a statistically significant relationships between having supportive family and dementia ( r = -.181, n = 191, p = .012); and being dependent for basic daily functioning to both depression ( r = .191, n = 191, p = .008) and dementia ( r = .221, n = 191, p = .002). conclusion institutionalized elderly had a higher prevalence for depression and dementia. being married and having higher levels of education were noted to be important protective factors against dementia. overall study findings indicate that older adult’s mental health may be associated with multiple levels of factors including stressors and resources concurrently, which makes it imperative to further examine these relationships methodically. europes journal of psychology

exploring social identity as a mediator of the relationship between personality and wellbeing using latent profile analysis objective the well-established link between personality and wellbeing has been rarely explored using a social identity approach. this is despite social support typically mediating the association between personality and wellbeing, and the foundational importance of social identity to the provision and receipt of social support. methods this study employed a cross-sectional online survey research design with 308 adult participants (mean age = 25.31 ± 9.69, 82.4% female, 87.7% white). latent profile analysis was performed based on participants’ interpersonal sensitivity, dispositional optimism, type d personality and big-5 personality scores. data were analysed using a combination of manova, anova and mediation analysis to explore between-profile differences in wellbeing and social identity, and the mediating role of social identity within these associations. results latent profile analysis identified four personality profiles that differed in wellbeing and social identification. mediation analyses indicated a partial, modest indirect association for social identification linking profile membership and wellbeing when contrasting profiles characterised by higher versus lower optimism, emotional stability, and extraversion. conclusions these exploratory findings support social identification as a theoretically relevant pathway linking personality profile typology and wellbeing. future research could examine whether interventions designed to strengthen social identification can be adapted to reflect differences in personality profiles. europes journal of psychology

acceptance counts: a social psychological perspective on young men’s responses to baldness objectives male pattern balding is a common and benign process. however, some men report intense distress because of it. consistent with transactional coping theory and the idea of coping norms, this distress may not necessarily arise from baldness itself but rather from social judgments of men’s responses to baldness. across four studies (total n = 686 young adults aged 18 to 35 years; 61% women), the present research investigated which ways of responding to baldness were perceived as appropriate (studies 1a and 1b) and to what extent appropriate responses to baldness affected social attractiveness judgments (studies 2a and 2b). methods and results studies 1a and 1b revealed that participants mostly recommended a hypothetical male friend to accept his baldness or to pursue medical services (e.g., using pharmaceuticals), with the latter recommendation still relatively frequently given even when participants knew about the benign character of baldness. recommendations for cosmetic services (e.g., using special shampoos) and compensation (e.g., gaining muscle) were less frequently made, and avoidance (e.g., of mirrors) was never recommended. assessing impression formation, participants of studies 2a and 2b rated balding men who accepted their baldness as most, and avoidant men as least, socially attractive. compensating men and men pursuing medical or cosmetic services were ranked as moderately socially attractive. participant gender was controlled for in all analyses. conclusions collectively, these results suggest acceptance of baldness is judged most appropriate and makes the most favorable social impression, offering an important counter to commercialized baldness treatment. europes journal of psychology

cross-cultural validation of the aaq-ii in five countries: a sem and psychometric network analysis approaches background experiential avoidance (ea) describes the tendency to evade negative internal experiences (e.g., distressing thoughts, emotions). ea is implicated across mental health conditions, positioning it as a central target for interventions like acceptance and commitment therapy (act). the acceptance and action questionnaire-ii (aaq-ii) is widely employed to measure ea; however, its cross-cultural reliability and factorial stability have not been comprehensively validated across diverse contexts. aim this study aimed to assess the cross-cultural validity and psychometric stability of the aaq-ii across five countries (peru, mexico, usa, belgium, and hungary) using structural equation modeling (sem) and network analysis. method a sample of 3,719 adults, primarily female (63.65%), was collected from five countries. data analysis included sem to evaluate factorial structure and network analysis to examine item interrelationships, assessing expected influence (ei) as a centrality measure. multiverse analysis using 5,000 bootstrap samples further evaluated network stability across samples. results sem confirmed a unidimensional aaq-ii structure across all regions, indicating consistent factorial validity. network analysis identified "painful memories" (aaq4) and "painful experiences" (aaq1) as central nodes across cultures, with regional variations in item relationships reflecting unique sociocultural influences. for instance, individualistic societies (e.g., usa) emphasized ea linked to achievement and competitive concerns, while collectivist countries (e.g., peru, mexico) associated ea with familial and social obligations. multiverse analysis revealed stable ea constructs across samples. discussion results validate the cross-cultural applicability of the aaq-ii, with findings underscoring cultural impacts on ea manifestations. network analysis provided nuanced insights into item interactions, showing that cultural factors, such as individualism, historical trauma, and social norms, shape ea expression differently across regions. this supports the use of culturally informed approaches in ea interventions. conclusion the aaq-ii exhibits reliable cross-cultural validity, affirming its utility for assessing ea across diverse settings. these findings enhance the application of the tool in psychological therapies worldwide, suggesting that culturally tailored ea interventions may benefit from considering specific sociocultural factors influencing ea processes. future research should investigate additional variables that may affect ea in different cultural contexts. europes journal of psychology

statistical tests should inform behaviour in theory and practice objectives statistical hypothesis testing cannot establish a hypothesis as certainly—or even approximately—true, but it is valuable in guiding behaviour as if it were true. to make decisions in theory and practice, statistical testing in psychology should weigh the type i (α) and type ii (β) error probabilities according to their respective costs . methods we outline costs and how to approach the α-β balance for six common decision-making questions: (1) should a hypothesis be considered tentatively accepted? (2) should a model or theory cover a newly proposed effect? (3) should a new hypothesis be proposed? (4) should a new intervention be introduced? (5) are the psychometric properties of an instrument sufficient to use it? (6) are the assumptions of a statistical method met so that it may be used? we give a worked example with real cost figures for question (4). results we argue that parsimony—prioritizing low α over low β—often serves as a useful default stance in questions (1) to (5). this resembles the general preference for focusing on fewer, larger and more robust effects to allocate resources efficiently and to make scientific communication more reliable. conclusions the parsimony default invites transparent counterarguments to override it, justifying a preference for small β. examples include adding promising intervention components with little risk of adverse effects to well-established interventions. as with (6), statistical tests can sometimes introduce unnecessary errors when a sound decision can be made on substantive grounds alone, for example when setting up a model to test a given hypothesis. europes journal of psychology

adaptation of brief resilient coping scale (brcs) to brazilian portuguese this study aimed to adapt and validate the brief resilient coping scale (brcs) for a sample of brazilian adults. the adaptation process included translation and expert analysis using the three-stage delphi technique. a total of 698 brazilian adults, with a mean age of 48.4 years ( sd = 15.3), of whom 79% were women, completed the brcs. to examine construct validity, confirmatory factor analyses and correlation analyses with indicators of depression, anxiety, and stress were conducted. the one-dimensional theoretical model demonstrated good fit (cfi = .998, tli = .994, rmsea = .058 [.017, .107], srmr = .023), albeit not perfect, χ 2 (2) = 7.177, p = .028. the factor loadings were all above .30, varying from .62 to .82. the correlations between brcs and the dass-8 subscales were significant with p < .001 and r = -.31 for the correlation with depression, -.28 for anxiety and -.26 for stress. in comparison to previous studies of validity evidence of brcs, our results presented the best values indicating suitability for brazilian context. for that, we consider the brcs to be a valid and reliable instrument for assessing resilient coping in the brazilian population. europes journal of psychology

the indirect effects of social anxiety and social support on alcohol use among uk university students: the role of negative reinforcement background socially anxious students may be vulnerable to risky alcohol use, whereas perceived social support may be protective; however, the mechanisms through which social anxiety heightens risk and perceived social support reduces risk remain unclear. this study examined how social anxiety and perceived social support influence risky alcohol use through negative-reinforcement pathways of coping and conformity drinking motives. method a convenience sample of undergraduate students from a large university in the united kingdom ( n = 152; 74% female) completed an online self-report survey assessing perceived social support (mspss), social anxiety (sias), drinking motives (dmq-r), and past-year alcohol use (audit-c score). using a cross-sectional observational design, structural equation modelling was conducted to test direct and indirect associations among study variables. results social anxiety significantly predicted coping (β = .260, p = .001) and conformity (β = .222, p = .006) motives. past-year alcohol use was predicted by coping motives (β = .429, p < .001), but not by conformity motives. an indirect effect of social anxiety on alcohol use via coping motives was identified (β = .113, p = .005). perceived social support was associated with lower coping motives (β = –.172, p = .038), but not with conformity motives. a protective indirect effect of perceived social support on alcohol use via lowered endorsement of coping motives was also observed (β = –.074, p = .037). conclusion the findings suggest that social anxiety may increase risky alcohol use through coping motives, whereas perceived social support may protect against risky alcohol use by reducing coping-motivated drinking, thereby partially counteracting this risk pathway. europes journal of psychology

exploring empathy in individuals with brain injury: psychometric validation of the perth empathy scale. 探索脑损伤个体的共情：珀斯共情量表的心理测量学验证 empathy alterations are common after acquired brain injury (abi), with adverse effects on interpersonal relationships and social reintegration. however, the assessment of empathy remains relatively neglected in clinical settings, since no empathy measures have yet been validated for use in brain-injured populations. as such, this study aimed to psychometrically assess the recently developed perth empathy scale (pes) in an international sample of adults with abi ( = 341) and a community sample ( = 647). confirmatory factor analyses indicated a theoretically coherent three-factor structure for the pes, comprised of a general cognitive empathy factor and valence-specific affective empathy factors. measurement invariance was established between abi and community samples, and results showed good to excellent reliability, concurrent, convergent and discriminant validity. these results help to illuminate the multidimensional nature of the empathy construct in adults with abi, and suggest that the pes is a robust measure of empathy in this population. assessment

event-related potentials to alcohol images predict real-world collegiate binge drinking: a pilot study of “lab-to-life” associations using wearable alcohol biosensors abstract introduction: event-related potentials (erps) are described as neural markers of risk for hazardous drinking, but few studies have related “lab to life” by linking erps to temporally-sensitive measures of real-world drinking. we predicted that erps reflecting alcohol cue-reactivity (acr) and inhibitory control (aic) would correlate with real-world transdermal alcohol concentrations (tacs) measured via alcohol biosensor. methods: college binge drinkers (n = 27; mage = 21.2; 67% female) completed a two-condition alcohol go/no-go task, then wore a scramx biosensor for 12 days. partial correlations examined the relationships between drinking (retrospective self-reports, ecological momentary assessments, and tacs) and erps to alcohol images, controlling for control images. erps to alcohol go trials indexed acr. erps to alcohol no-go trials reflected aic. results: shorter n2 latencies to alcohol go, reflecting higher acr, were associated with faster tac rise rate, signaling faster alcohol absorption and intoxication. larger, more prolonged n2s to alcohol no-go, reflecting lower aic, were associated with greater average tac, peak tac, and area under the tac curve, indicating a greater alcohol consumption volume. p3s were larger and more prolonged to nogo versus go; no other relationships were significant. conclusion: this is the first study to include wearable alcohol biosensors in an erp-related, lab-to-life design. findings substantiate associations between erps and real-world drinking. while enhanced acr may spark a drinking episode, impaired aic may allow it to escalate into a binge. objective, temporally-sensitive tacs may provide targets for ecological momentary interventions to disrupt the speed of intoxication and the magnitude of drinking episodes. neuropsychobiology

anatolution, an online platform for consensus morphology abstract introduction: reliable cell annotations are essential for supervised image analysis, yet producing the annotations required for quantitative cellular morphometry is laborious, and results can vary with both tissue preparation and expert interpretation of ambiguous morphology. nissl staining has long underpinned comparative neuroanatomy, generating extensive and taxonomically diverse records of cellular organization across the nervous system. we developed anatolution to make this resource more amenable to standardized quantitative analysis by integrating independent annotations alongside explicit measures of rater agreement for quality control under computer vision bookkeeping. method: anatolution is an open-source web platform for annotating single images or 3d volumes (https://anatolution.herokuapp.com/public-tool/). multiple raters independently outline cellular structures using a shared set of labels or conventions, and the platform enables consensus analysis alongside conventional image segmentation. result: we evaluated 603,297 annotations produced by 48 raters across 1,024 image tiles and tested a subset of 68 fully annotated tiles against unsupervised segmentation. boundary overlap in cell drawings, scored from 0 (“no overlap”) to 1 (“identical”), rose from 0.30 for 1 rater to 0.79 with 7 users, and in a subset of 68 annotated tiles, 88% contained unsupervised segmentation results. conclusion: agreement between groups of raters increased as raters were added to an optimum of ∼7 users, and within a subset of images nearly 9 in 10 annotations were spatially anchored to unsupervised methods. anatolution supports the production of consensus labels whose stability can be quantified and improved by adding independent raters, providing structured reference data for training and evaluating cell segmentation models for quantitative histology. brain behavior and evolution

co-evaluation of co-production in mind and brain research: a dialogical approach. co-production is increasingly used in mental and neurological health research, but less is known about how co-production itself can be co-evaluated. we conducted a study that aimed to systematically co-evaluate a 9-month project that co-produced strategic priorities and internal research-funding procedures for a new mind and brain research centre. the co-evaluation used a mixed-method design, including qualitative, quantitative, dialogical and post-implementation approaches, informed by an adapted rq + 4 co-pro framework. the project involved 14 adult contributors who were also participants in the co-evaluation, including seven community partners alongside academic, clinical and research staff. contributors across these roles also brought lived or living experience of mental-health difficulties, neurodivergence and marginalisation. reflexive thematic analysis examined contributors' written reflections; perceived power was measured midway through the project and again at completion; findings were returned to the team for dialogical co-interpretation; and funding-panel members later reflected on implementation of the co-produced procedures. thematic analysis generated six themes concerning time and resources, roles and identities, leadership and power, communication, institutional barriers and emotional labour and gains. mean sense of power scores increased from 5.34 to 5.61 (p = .023). dialogical reflection revealed both convergent and differing interpretations of shared experiences. our central learning was that equitable co-production requires time to build trust, enough structure for collective work to progress without closing down shared influence and institutional systems able to support participation. by retaining rather than resolving different viewpoints, we show how systematic, dialogical co-evaluation can turn contrasting experiences into practical learning for future co-production. journal of neuropsychology

artificial observers and real individual differences: a roadmap for a computational psychometrics of vision computational models of vision, deep neural networks most prominently, are evaluated against the average observer: average performance, average neural response, and average representational geometry. this discards one of the richest constraints on theory: stable individual differences. fitting the average is necessary but not sufficient. i argue that future models should be judged not only by their fit to mean human performance but also by whether populations of artificial observers reproduce the covariance structure and latent factors found across human observers. two mature but disconnected literatures motivate this. decades of factor-analytic psychophysics and electrophysiology show that interindividual variation is signal, not noise: the pattern of correlations among observers reveals the number and tuning of underlying mechanisms, and fractionates vision into many narrow factors rather than one general ability. meanwhile, neural networks differing only in random initialization develop measurably different internal representations, so any single trained network is one sample from a distribution of possible observers. joining these yields a computational psychometrics of vision : construct a designed population of artificial observers (varying in architecture, initialization, training diet, and front-end sampling), submit them to the same latent-variable analyses used on humans, and test whether the recovered factor structure matches. recent work showing that seed-varied networks align with specific individuals is an existence proof. this article generalizes it into a framework, a staged roadmap, and a benchmark, together with the safeguards that keep such a benchmark from becoming an optimization target, for testing hypotheses about human visual variation with artificial observer populations. i-perception

language usage modulates the neural mechanisms of selective attention in bilinguals abstract the use of multiple languages modulates the neural mechanisms of selective attention, but it is unclear whether these adaptations require continuous engagement and active second language usage. here we examined whether language usage shapes selective attention in bilingualism, and what neural processes this might engage. 48 highly proficient english-french bilinguals listened to naturalistic speech streams in their first or second language, paired with either linguistic or non-linguistic interference. participants were matched on their l2 proficiency, but were either active, moderate, or inactive users of their second language. the results revealed usage-related modulation of oscillatory activity in the alpha band, with increased power in active and moderate users and decreased alpha power in inactive bilinguals, and behavioural comprehension accuracy mirroring this pattern of results. in contrast, there was no robust association between usage and perceptual tracking of speech, as captured by mtrf decoding of speech envelopes across frequency bands. taken together, our findings suggest l2 usage may be modulating the neural mechanisms of auditory selective attention in bilinguals primarily through the top-down attentional allocation, without substantially altering the neural tracking of speech itself. neurobiology of language

electromagnetic field theories of conscious experience: a conceptual review and reappraisal 意识体验的电磁场理论：概念回顾与重新评价 abstract this paper reviews and contrasts electromagnetic field (emf) theories of consciousness with traditional neural and functionalist accounts of phenomenal space and its contents. conscious experience is unified yet differentiated, intentional, reportable, and capable of influencing behaviour. these properties, available only from a first-person perspective, must correspond to distinct states or processes in an underlying physical substrate. conventional neural and functionalist theories explain conscious experience through local causal interactions among discrete units and symbolic processing. however, patterns of computation and causal organization exist only from an external observer’s perspective and therefore do not themselves explain subjective experience. in contrast, the brain’s endogenous emf, which integrates information spatially, provides a plausible substrate for phenomenal unity. evidence linking emf dynamics to conscious states and contents is abundant, particularly from eeg studies showing reliable correlations despite attenuation of extracranial fields. emf dynamics may also provide a more stable representation of short-term memory than variable neural firing patterns. evidence for ephaptic coupling further demonstrates that emfs influence neural activity, potentially contributing to rapid large-scale neural coordination and fluctuations in firing thresholds. experimental perturbation of endogenous emfs can alter conscious experience and modulate oscillations involved in memory consolidation. emfs can perform field computation through superposition, and a gradual evolutionary origin follows from the adaptive advantages of ephaptic coupling in simpler nervous systems. it is hypothesized that low-frequency oscillations provide the basis of phenomenal space, whereas localized high-frequency oscillations support experiential differentiation. intentionality is explained by locating the conscious emf between sensory input and motor output processes. eeg研究显示电磁场动态与意识状态和内容存在可靠相关，尽管颅外场被衰减。 作者提出电磁场动态可能比变化的神经放电模式更稳定地表征短期记忆。 ephaptic coupling证据表明电磁场影响神经活动，可能促进快速大规模神经协调与放电阈值波动。 对内源电磁场的实验性扰动可改变意识体验，并调节与记忆巩固相关的振荡。 作者假设低频振荡构成现象空间的基础，局部高频振荡支持体验分化。 neuroscience of consciousness

the eco-consumer’s paradox: an unusually eco-friendly item can make high-impact sequences appear worse 生态消费者的悖论：一件异常环保的物品会让高影响序列显得更差 abstract the environmental impact of everyday behaviors accumulates across time. how are individual behaviors integrated when people judge their combined environmental-friendliness? in three pre-registered experiments, we found that participants perceive a sequence as more environmentally friendly when an environmentally friendly item is added, but only if the sequence has a moderate-average environmental impact (d > 1). if the sequence has a high-average environmental impact (and is sufficiently long), the unusually eco-friendly item instead leads to a downshift in perceived environmental-friendliness of the whole sequence ( d > 0.45)—a contrast effect. the results are consistent with an account in which evaluations of individual items are made retrospectively, in relation to a mental representation of the sequence as a whole. within this account, an unusually environmentally friendly item may produce a contrast effect when it is perceived as distinct from the other items in the sequence, shifting the overall evaluation in the opposite direction. 在中等平均环境影响的序列中加入环保物品会提高整体环境友好性评价，效应量 d 大于 1。 在高平均环境影响且序列足够长时，加入异常环保物品反而使整体环境友好性评价下降，呈对比效应，效应量 d 大于 0.45。 结果与一种解释一致：个体项目评价是回溯性做出的，并参照序列整体的心理表征；当异常环保物品被视为与其他项目不同时，可能产生对比效应。 cognitive research-principles and implications

how do students bloom? re-considering maslow’s hierarchy of needs in educational settings 学生如何绽放？重新审视教育情境中的马斯洛需求层次理论 abstract the educational maxim “children must maslow before they bloom” has become a widely accepted folk pedagogy for understanding student motivation and learning. drawing on abraham maslow's hierarchy of needs and benjamin bloom's taxonomy of educational objectives, the phrase is commonly used to justify the assumption that students must satisfy basic needs before meaningful intellectual engagement can occur. we argue that this interpretation represents a particular reading of maslow rather than a complete account of his theory. examining educational textbooks, teacher preparation materials, and professional discourse, we show how hierarchical distinctions between “higher” and “lower” needs are frequently translated into assumptions about readiness, capacity, and academic potential. we further suggest that these interpretations are reinforced by broader hierarchical and individualistic assumptions embedded within the conceptual vocabulary available to maslow. drawing on indigenous perspectives, the medicine wheel, and relational developmental systems metatheory, we propose a non-hierarchical, relational framework that preserves maslow’s humanistic aspirations while offering a more equitable understanding of motivation, learning, and human flourishing. 作者指出“儿童必须先马斯洛再布鲁姆”这一说法已成为广泛接受的民间教育学，被用来为基本需求先于智力投入的假设辩护。 作者认为教育材料常把“高/低”需求的层级区分转译为关于准备度、能力与学业潜力的假设。 作者提出这些解读被马斯洛可用概念词汇中更广泛的层级化与个体主义预设所强化。 作者提出一种非层级、关系性的框架，以保留马斯洛的人本主义目标并给出更公平的动机、学习与人类繁荣理解。 human development

gender differences in pre-service physical education teachers’ visual behaviour: an eye-tracking study (1) background: teachers’ visual attention is central to professional vision, yet whether teacher gender influences gaze allocation in physical education remains unclear. this study examined gender-related differences in visual attentional deployment when teachers observed students’ motor competence, behavioural engagement, off-task behaviour, and gender. (2) methods: sixty pre-service physical education teachers observed video-recorded tasks from a class while wearing tobii pro glasses 3. fixation metrics were quantified across predefined areas of interest and compared between teacher genders. (3) results: female and male teachers showed comparable total and mean fixation durations. however, the former produced significantly more fixations during the closed task towards on-task students and with higher motor competence. female teachers also showed higher fixation frequency regardless of whether off-task behaviour was successfully identified, and made more fixations towards both female and male students during this task. these differences were not consistently observed during the open task. (4) conclusions: teacher gender differed primarily with fixation frequency rather than fixation duration, and this effect was context-dependent. additionally, greater visual sampling did not necessarily correspond to more accurate behavioural noticing. mobile eye-tracking can reveal gender-related and task-sensitive differences in teachers’ visual behaviour, with potential applications in physical education teacher education and professional development. journal of eye movement research

longitudinal associations among family function, psychological resilience, and frailty progression in older gastric cancer survivors: a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model abstract objectives older gastric cancer survivors after radical gastrectomy are vulnerable to frailty progression. family function may influence frailty by enhancing individual psychological resilience. however, few studies have examined these longitudinal associations. we aimed to evaluate the longitudinal associations among family function, psychological resilience, and frailty. methods a total of 412 older gastric cancer survivors who underwent radical gastrectomy were enrolled and assessed at hospital discharge, and again at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. family function was assessed using the family adaptability and cohesion evaluation scale ii, psychological resilience with the connor–davidson resilience scale, and frailty using the tilburg frailty indicator. the random intercept cross‐lagged panel model was used to assess within‐ and between‐person longitudinal associations. mediation effect analysis was conducted at the within‐person level. results family cohesion was indirectly associated with lower subsequent frailty through higher psychological resilience. the estimated indirect effects from t1 to t3 and from t2 to t4 were −.025 ( p = .012) and −.032 ( p = .004), respectively. while family adaptability was associated with psychological resilience at the between‐person level ( b = .707, p = .006), and psychological resilience was negatively associated with frailty ( b = −2.458, p = .003), the direct association between family adaptability and frailty was not significant ( b = −.097, p = .069). conclusion greater family cohesion was associated with lower subsequent frailty, with psychological resilience representing a potential pathway. these findings highlight the potential of resilience‐focused approaches to enhance the benefits of family support in addressing frailty. british journal of health psychology

italian version of the green work climate scale: validation and within-organization differences in an agrifood company abstract: this study validated the italian version of the green work climate (gwc) scale, which assesses employees’ perceptions of their organization’s and coworkers’ commitment to environmental sustainability, and examined whether these perceptions differ across organizational contexts. data were collected from 323 employees working at three sites of an italian agrifood company. confirmatory factor analysis supported the original two-factor structure and provided evidence of satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. green work climate perceptions differed across organizational contexts, with office employees reporting higher levels than production workers and significant differences emerging across company sites. these findings support the italian version of the gwc scale as a reliable tool for assessing sustainability climate and identifying contextual differences within organizations. journal of personnel psychology

nice words, or true words as well? the interaction effect between upward ingratiation and speak-up behavior abstract: employees frequently rely on influence tactics to shape how others evaluate and respond to them. although prior research has largely examined influence tactics in isolation, little is known about how different tactics operate together to shape workplace relationships and outcomes. drawing on the warmth–competence framework, we examine the interplay between two commonly used upward influence tactics – ingratiation and speak-up behavior. using a round-robin, two-wave, multisource survey of employees, leaders, and coworkers across 119 teams in a large metro operating company in china, we tested our hypotheses using multilevel modeling and monte carlo simulations. we propose that ingratiation signals warmth, whereas speak-up provides complementary competence and authenticity cues. consistent with our theorizing, speak-up strengthened the positive relationships of ingratiation with leader trust and coworker respect. furthermore, the indirect effects of ingratiation on leader-rated promotability through leader trust and on help received from coworkers through coworker respect were stronger at higher levels of speak-up behavior. together, our findings show how distinct influence tactics provide complementary social information that shapes interpersonal evaluations and workplace outcomes. journal of personnel psychology

integrating leader humility and integrity: pathways to enhanced employee pride and helping behavior abstract: drawing on social exchange theory, this study examines how and when leader humility promotes employee helping behavior. specifically, we propose that employee pride mediates this relationship and that leader integrity strengthens the positive effect of leader humility. to test our model, we conducted two studies. study 1 employed a scenario-based experiment with 212 participants, revealing that the positive effect of leader humility on employee pride was stronger when leader integrity was high. study 2 used a multisource, multiwave survey of 192 employees and their supervisors and replicated these findings. furthermore, employee pride was positively related to helping behavior, and leader integrity strengthened the indirect effect of leader humility on helping behavior through employee pride. theoretical and practical implications are discussed. journal of personnel psychology

a scoping review of adherence for caregiver-implemented intervention regimens for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities interventions for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities often require long-term caregiver adherence. a scoping review method was used to search for peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2024. studies were screened for inclusion based on if they measured caregiver adherence to an intervention for a child diagnosed with an intellectual or developmental disability. the search yielded 125 articles. of these, 26 articles met the inclusion criteria and were reviewed. articles were more likely to include female caregivers of younger children. most articles used quantitative correlational methodology. the most common adherence measurement tool was surveys. most articles reported caregiver adherence levels; however, there was substantial variation in how adherence was reported across articles. several variables related to the caregiver, child, caregiver training, and intervention were reported to influence adherence. future researchers should directly evaluate the effects of reported variables on caregiver adherence and evaluate how modifying potential barriers impacts adherence. behavior modification

why do histories of environmental change become anthropocentric memories? remembering french nuclear tests in the pacific to foster greater pro-environmentalism, recent work in collective memory studies extends frames of remembering to nonhuman losses and suffering – yet dominant memory cultures remain stubbornly anthropocentric. this article explains persisting anthropocentrism by focusing on the narrative architecture of collective memory. based on structuralist narratology, it argues that anthropocentrism is embedded in master narratives that organise the past around human protagonists and identity-affirming plots. the argument is developed through a case study of how french nuclear testing in the pacific is remembered in new zealand. although the tests caused profound environmental harm, analysis of a variety of memory texts from film, advertising and museums shows that this history is repeatedly narrated through an anthropocentric underdog plot centred on new zealand’s self-image of ‘a small nation punching above its weight’. the article concludes that making space for ecocentric remembering requires confronting the master narratives through which social groups make the historical past meaningful. memory studies

uneven resilience: memorializing mass death in the el paso–juárez borderlands this article investigates how two mass-fatality events in the el paso–ciudad juárez borderlands—a 2019 mass shooting and a 2023 fire in a detention center—produced profoundly different memorial ecologies, and what these divergences reveal about the politics of resilience in a binational community. in el paso, the idiom “el paso strong” channeled collective grief into sanctioned, commodified practices and durable forms of public memorialization. in juárez, the deaths of migrants in state custody generated fragile, actively suppressed memorials, reflecting their exclusion from recognized modes of public mourning. drawing on material culture studies, i treat these memorials as infrastructures whose forms, circulation, and durability reveal who is permitted access to public grief and who must mourn under conditions of precarity. i argue that these divergent memorial ecologies show how resilience in the borderlands is produced through bordering practices that distribute grievability unevenly across racialized and spatial categories. memory studies

the missing five minutes: practitioner lessons from building code calm as postcrisis recovery infrastructure high-intensity organizations often manage the beginning of a crisis more deliberately than its aftermath. drawing on my experience developing code calm, a brief postevent practice for acute-care teams, this practitioner's corner reflects on recovery as an organizational design problem rather than an individual wellness task. code calm creates a voluntary five-to-seven-minute transition after difficult events through acknowledgment, grounding, somatic awareness, resourcing, and structured re-entry. the practice evolved through a pragmatic action-learning cycle of noticing, trying, reflecting, and redesigning. this process highlighted four design principles: protect the pause, preserve voluntariness, separate restoration from evaluation, and pair microrestoration with structural accountability. i conceptualize code calm as a microboundary practice: a protected interval between high-intensity action and routine re-entry. its value lies not in promising rapid stress reduction, but in changing what organizations recognize as legitimate work and creating conditions in which recovery, sensemaking, and system learning can become possible after difficult work. journal of applied behavioral science

your wellness program remains underutilized … now what? many organizations offer wellness programs; yet they are unfortunately underutilized by employees. for that reason, we address concerns around how to get employees to participate, and more importantly, how to get employees to sustain behavioral health changes. specifically, we offer theoretically guided recommendations for implementing wellness program best practices. we make the case and provide examples to demonstrate that programs which fulfill psychological needs will benefit from greater participation and more sustained behavioral health changes. we also note that as an external motivator, financial incentives may encourage participation but likely do not facilitate sustained behavioral health changes. again, a need-supportive wellness program is necessary. we hope practitioners find our illustrative examples useful as they think about their own wellness program design. journal of applied behavioral science
nonverbal reasoning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: associations with gross motor function, mri, and eeg findings child neuropsychology

effectiveness of a combined paced-breathing and mobile app–based mindfulness intervention for chronic migraine: a randomized controlled trial background: mindfulness has been proposed as a non-pharmacological strategy for chronic migraine management. objective: this study evaluated the effectiveness of a combined paced-breathing and mobile app–based mindfulness intervention in adults with chronic migraine. methods: a randomized controlled trial was conducted in adults with chronic migraine. forty participants were randomized, and 38 were included in the final analyses. the intervention group was assigned to a 12-week combined intervention consisting of paced breathing followed by a mobile app–based mindfulness intervention delivered through the petit bambou® app; the control group remained on a waitlist and continued usual care. the primary outcome was migraine days per month. secondary outcomes included migraine episode pain intensity and duration, headache-related quality of life (headache impact test-6), anxiety sensitivity (anxiety sensitivity index-3), kinesiophobia (tampa scale for kinesiophobia-11), and sleep quality (athens insomnia scale). between-group differences at post-intervention were evaluated using analysis of covariance, adjusting each outcome for its corresponding baseline value. results: no statistically significant baseline-adjusted between-group differences were observed for migraine frequency or for any secondary outcome. for the primary outcome, the adjusted mean difference between the control and intervention groups was −3.07 migraine days per month (95% ci, −8.00 to 1.86; f(1, 35) = 1.599; p = 0.214; ηp2 = 0.044). effect sizes were small for all outcomes. conclusion: a 12-week combined paced-breathing and mobile app–based mindfulness intervention was not superior to waitlist usual care for reducing migraine frequency or improving the evaluated clinical and psychological outcomes. these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small sample size, the marked baseline imbalance in migraine frequency, the use of a waitlist control group, and the absence of objective adherence monitoring. future trials should include larger samples, active control conditions, objective measures of engagement, and longer follow-up periods. (australian new zealand clinical trials registry, actrn12624000611527 [prospectively registered on may 10, 2024]). health psychology research
on the representative state of peer review in behavior analysis perspectives on behavior science
an embedded design mixed-methods study of patterns in online discourse about school violence in thailand child & youth care forum
the role of embodiment in art therapy: an arts-based and phenomenological research art therapy

preliminary evidence of the effect of (anti)feminist discourse on attitudes towards feminism and the attribution of (im)morality to feminists / evidencia preliminar sobre el efecto del discurso (anti)feminista en la actitud hacia el feminismo y la atribución de (in)moralidad a las feministas within the framework of persuasion literature, this study empirically explores how (anti)feminist discourses influence recipients’ attitudes towards feminism, their attribution of morality and immorality to feminists and their perception of discrimination against men. furthermore, it evaluates whether the gender of the source and/or the recipient interacts with the type of discourse, considering ambivalent sexism as a covariate. a total of 306 individuals participated. the results indicate that antifeminist discourse generated a less favourable attitude towards feminism, as well as more attributions of immorality and fewer attributions of morality to feminists. no effects were found for the gender of the source or the recipient, nor were there any interaction effects. the findings underscore the importance of discourse in shaping attitudes towards feminism, with important implications for the promotion of gender equality and the containment of antifeminist rhetoric in society. international journal of social psychology

psychological factors and indirect associations between depression and suicide risk in university healthcare students abstract background suicide risk is a major public health concern among university healthcare students. although depression, hopelessness, experiential avoidance, and psychological well-being have each been associated with suicidal behavior, their simultaneous contribution to suicide risk and the indirect statistical associations among these variables remain insufficiently understood. methods a total of 319 university healthcare students completed the plutchik suicide risk scale, the acceptance and action questionnaire-ii, the beck hopelessness scale, the depression subscale of the depression anxiety stress scale-21 (dass-21) and the psychological well-being scale for adults. sequential logistic regression models were used to examine factors associated with suicide risk, and a parallel multiple mediation analysis was performed to assess the indirect statistical associations between depression and suicide risk through hopelessness, experiential avoidance, and psychological well-being. results depression [or = 1.117 (ci 95%: 1.050–1.190)], and hopelessness [or = 1.395 (ci 95%: 1.209–1.624)] were significantly associated with suicide risk ( p < 0.001). no other variable was significantly associated with suicide risk ( p > 0.05). in the parallel multiple mediation analysis, a significant direct statistical association between depression and suicide risk was observed [b = 0.0955 (95% ci: 0.0365–0.1545), p < 0.01]. among the indirect associations, only the statistical pathway through hopelessness was significant [b = 0.0673 (95% ci: 0.0385–0.1046)]. conclusions in university healthcare students, depression and hopelessness are significantly associated with suicide risk. discover psychology

the core-well model of primary school teachers’ occupational well-being as a multidimensional, relational, and process-oriented construct abstract background occupational well-being (owb) is central to teachers’ professional functioning​ and relates to teacher retention, instructional quality, and student outcomes. although teacher well-being research increasingly includes positive, engagement-related, and resource-oriented perspectives, many studies rely on predefined constructs, such as job satisfaction, stress, burnout, or emotion regulation. less is known about how primary school teachers connect these dimensions in everyday professional practice. aim this study examined how primary school teachers conceptualise owb, which conditions they perceive as shaping it, and how they relate professional efficacy, recovery, and boundary-setting to their well-being. method a theory-based qualitative exploratory study was embedded in an ongoing cross-sectional mixed-methods survey. the present paper draws on a defined data cut of n = 120 participants working in german primary school contexts; the qualitative model-building analysis ​included​ n = 51 cases and continue​ed until code saturation was reached. open-ended responses were analysed using structured qualitative content analysis, combining deductive category development informed by ​job demands-resources theoryand research on teacher well-being​ and resilience with inductive refinement. results teachers conceptualised owb as multidimensional, comprising affective experiences, cognitive evaluations, and perceived meaning. they described owb as shaped by job demands, contextual and relational resources, professional agency, and recovery-oriented regulation. relational experiences with children, perceived pedagogical impact, and boundary management were particularly salient. conclusion primary school teachers’ owb is best understood as dynamic, relational, and process-oriented. the findings specify how relational experiences, pedagogical responsibility, perceived impact on children’s learning and development, and boundary management are connected in primary school teachers’ owb. discover psychology

does the construct of valence really need fixing? an introduction to the special issue and a reconsideration of the intractable problems of valence affective science

clinician recommendations for behavioral interventions in adhd: a call to action for applied behavior analysis abstract attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adhd) is characterized by persistent pattens of inattention and/or hyperactivity‐impulsivity that interfere with functioning or development. pediatric guidelines call for the combination of behavioral intervention and stimulant medication to treat adhd. we conducted a survey among caregivers of children with adhd to identify interventions recommended to treat adhd by their diagnostic clinician. seventy percent of caregivers reported that medication was recommended. most caregivers reported that some form of behavioral intervention was recommended, but only 14% reported they received a recommendation for applied behavior analysis, specifically. in addition, the number of caregivers reporting a clinician recommendation for applied behavior analysis decreased as children aged. we discuss the potential of applied behavior analysis with this population and suggest some things that behavior analysts can do to increase their work with individuals with adhd. behavioral interventions

imperfect symmetry: a humanistic-relational model of negotiated power and dignity in psychotherapy some humanistic, relational, and collaborative traditions describe psychotherapy through ideals of equality, collaboration, and mutual recognition, although therapeutic relationships remain structurally asymmetrical: one person seeks help while the other holds professional authority, interpretive influence, and responsibility for the frame. this conceptual article proposes imperfect symmetry as a humanistic-relational model for distinguishing oppressive or humiliating asymmetries from those that can become clinically useful, dignity-preserving, and repairable. the model asks when asymmetries become sufficiently just, explicit, and negotiable to support growth. drawing on attachment, humanistic-existential, systemic, cognitive, recognition-theoretical, common-factors, critical, and multicultural traditions, the article defines dignity as equal moral worth and relational authorship under unequal conditions. it articulates three levels of asymmetry—intrapsychic, interpersonal, and institutional—and a six-step clinical cycle: detect, locate, name, test, negotiate, and repair. the article also addresses the naturalization of power—the treatment of historically and culturally produced hierarchies as if they were natural or inevitable and outlines implications for alliance, consent, rupture–repair, supervision, and human science research. journal of humanistic psychology

displacing hegemonic psychology through dissidence: dialogues between cultural psychology, decolonial epistemologies, and the go-along method this article offers a theoretical and methodological contribution to psychology through an articulation between the cultural psychology of semiotic dynamics and decolonial epistemologies. we interrogate hegemonic configurations and their complicity with modern-colonial logics, the universalization of us-eurocentric models of subjectivity, and the marginalization of relational, sociocultural, and historically situated dimensions of human psychological processes. drawing on the concepts of fractured locus (maría lugones) and nepantla (gloria anzaldúa), we approach dissidence as a site of rupture and traversal within dominant regimes of intelligibility, where insurgent modes of meaning-making emerge from lives positioned at the borders of normative orders. dissident life trajectories operate as epistemic forces that can strain established frameworks of recognition and open possibilities for alternative ways of inquiring, knowing, and relating across lived territories. the article articulates the go-along method through ignacio martín-baró’s notion of contact, conceptualizing it as an ethically implicated practice of inquiry grounded in embodied co-presence, relational accountability, and movement across memory-laden territories. selected episodes from three non-binary developmental trajectories illustrate the methodological possibilities and ethical tensions of this approach. by foregrounding dissident phenomena as generating epistemic displacements, the article contributes to the ongoing reinvention of psychology as a situated, relational, and ethically implicated practice. journal of humanistic psychology

intergenerational associations in intergroup contact and the moderating role of self‐expansion motivation among ethnic minority adolescents in china objectives intergroup contact is widely recognized as an important means of reducing bias and promoting positive intergroup relations among children and adolescents. however, less is known about whether and how parents′ intergroup experiences are reflected in their children′s own intergroup contact, particularly in non‐western settings. this study examined intergenerational associations in intergroup contact among tibetan adolescents in china and further tested whether self‐expansion motivation moderated these associations. method adolescents reported perceived parental contact quality, their own contact intention, contact quantity, contact quality, and self‐expansion motivation. latent profile analysis was used to identify self‐expansion motivation profiles. separate regression models were estimated for each profile, and regression coefficients for perceived parental contact quality were compared across profiles using coefficient‐difference z tests. results three self‐expansion motivation profiles were identified: low (21.1%), medium (41.9%), and high (37.0%). higher perceived parental contact quality was associated with stronger contact intention, greater contact quantity, and better contact quality among adolescents. self‐expansion motivation moderated the associations of perceived parental contact quality with contact intention and contact quality: these associations were significant in the medium and high‐motivation profiles, but not in the low‐motivation profile. in contrast, self‐expansion motivation did not moderate the association between perceived parental contact quality and contact quantity. conclusions the findings suggest that adolescents′ perceptions of parental intergroup contact are associated with their own intergroup contact in a non‐western ethnic minority context. they also indicate that adolescents′ self‐expansion motivation may help explain when perceived parental contact quality is more strongly associated with adolescents′ own intergroup contact. new directions for child and adolescent development
better memory for discourse in an auditory modality for heritage-speaking bilinguals: a language-dependent modality effect discourse processes

a deep time perspective on a rare anatomical variant: torus mandibularis presence in australopithecus africanus from sterkfontein, south africa abstract mandibular tori are benign bony exostoses located on the lingual aspect of the mandibular corpus that are common in modern human populations but rarely reported in the hominin fossil record. their aetiology remains unclear, with both genetic and environmental factors proposed, including masticatory stress and parafunctional activity. here we describe a pronounced bilateral mandibular torus in sts 52b, a subadult australopith specimen from member 4 deposits at sterkfontein, south africa (ca. 2.8–2.1 ma). the torus forms a large lingual projection extending from the canine-premolar region posteriorly along the mandibular corpus and is most consistent with a grade 4 expression. morphologically, it is stemless, monocystic, and composed primarily of compact cortical bone, closely resembling common clinical presentations in modern humans. its occurrence in a subadult is notable, as toral development is frequently attributed to cumulative masticatory loading and is typically reported in adults. moreover, the rarity of mandibular tori among fossil hominins with robust masticatory adaptations suggests that elevated occlusal forces alone are insufficient to explain their development. sts 52b represents one of the earliest and most pronounced examples of mandibular torus expression in the hominin fossil record, extending the known antiquity of this trait to beyond 2 million years. evolutionary human sciences

settling to reproduce: metabolic, immune, and reproductive trajectories after immigration in female bonobos abstract dispersal and social integration shape opportunities for cooperation and have played a central role in human evolution. yet, immigration and settlement often entail costs for dispersers, including elevated risks of injury, mortality, or reproductive suppression. in primates, female immigrants commonly face aggression and social instability during settlement. bonobos (pan paniscus) differ in that affiliative integration may mitigate these challenges, but the physiological and reproductive consequences of immigration remain poorly understood. we investigated post-immigration physiological and reproductive trajectories in wild female bonobos using longitudinal measurements of urinary cortisol, triiodothyronine (t3), neopterin, and a progesterone metabolite (pdg) over up to eight years post-immigration. t3 and neopterin levels showed no systematic change with time since immigration. cortisol levels increased gradually with time, a pattern consistent with developmental maturation. a post-immigration pdg elevation was detected in 13 of 17 females, with 12 detections occurring within two years after immigration. nine females gave birth at a median of 3.8 years post-immigration. we found no evidence of the predicted pattern of early physiological disturbance followed by recovery. these trajectories suggest an absence of prolonged settlement-related metabolic or immunological disruption and are consistent with the hypothesis that species-typical social tolerance and affiliation may buffer settlement-related challenges. evolutionary human sciences

an exploration of the roles of cognitive reactivity and ego depletion in the relationship between entrapment and suicidal ideation abstract objectives entrapment is theorized as a key driver of suicidal ideation, yet the cognitive processes leading to entrapment, particularly the activating role of negative affect, and those through which entrapment translates into suicidal ideation are not well understood. grounded in the integrated motivational‐volitional model, this study used mediation analyses to examine cognitive reactivity in relation to suicidal ideation via entrapment, and ego depletion as a mediator of the entrapment–suicidal ideation link. design a cross‐sectional online survey was used to collect self‐report data from participants recruited through opportunity sampling. methods the sample consisted of 312 adults living in the united kingdom. data analyses were conducted on a subsample of participants who reported a lifetime history of suicidal ideation and/or suicide attempts ( n = 269; m age = 28.50, sd = 10.06; 82.9% white; 66.5% female). results the relationship between cognitive reactivity and suicidal ideation was accounted for by entrapment; this indirect association was not moderated by trait mindfulness. additionally, the entrapment–suicidal ideation relationship was partially accounted for by self‐regulatory fatigue, but not by depletion sensitivity; this indirect effect remained significant after controlling for depression, but not anxiety diagnosis. conclusions the findings highlight cognitive reactivity as a cognitive vulnerability to suicidal ideation and underscore the value of understanding suicide risk through the lens of self‐regulation. the cross‐sectional design limits causal inference, and the observed associations should be interpreted as correlational in nature. british journal of clinical psychology
virtual rivals, real emotions: female jealousy in response to (un)attractive digital agents evolutionary psychological science

leader-member exchange quality (lmx), telework-life conflict, and professional isolation: a gender moderated mediation model the present study aims to analyze the mediating role of telework-life conflict in the relationship between lmx and professional isolation in telework and the moderating role of gender in conflict-isolation relationships. a sample of 524 teleworkers (261 women and 263 men) aged 18-67 years (m = 40.54, sd = 9.6) participated in the study. participants completed a survey assessing lmx, telework-life conflict, and professional isolation. lmx was negatively relatedto telework-life conflict and professional isolation. in addition, the results were consistent with a negative indirect effect of lmx on professional isolation through telework-life conflict (partial mediation). this indirect effect was conditional on gender, such that the positive relationshipbetween conflict and professional isolation was stronger for men than for women. our findings suggest that high-quality leader-member exchange (lmx) relationships characterized by support, trust, and autonomy are associated with lower feelings of professional isolation.given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted causally. the findings suggest three key practical implications: developing managerial training programs focused on the work-family dynamics of teleworkers; establishing informal communicationspaces that facilitate the negotiation of idiosyncratic deals (i-deals); and implementing hr information systems with a gender perspective that support inclusive organizational policies and reduce gender stereotypes. international journal of psychological research

jerarquías de legitimación del sufrimiento social: reconocimiento, responsabilidad estatal y reparación en el estallido social chileno the 2019 chilean social uprising produced heterogeneous forms of victimization that were not equally recognized. this study examines how recognition of victim status, attribution of responsibility for reparation, reparation preferences and perceived lasting effects of violence vary across victimization cases, and whether ideological positioning moderates the first of these judgments. an online survey of adult residents of the santiago metropolitan region (n = 5 000) randomly assigned each participant to one of five vignettes differing in type of harm, identity of the affected party and agent producing the harm. data were analyzed with contingency tables, cramér's v, mcnemar tests and a likelihood-ratio test for the case × ideology interaction. recognition varies across cases (40.2 % – 59.0 %; v = 0.093) and is lowest for diffuse emotional harm. reparation preferences align with the type of harm (v = 0.199 and 0.232). ideology moderates recognition (χ²(12) = 135.85, p < 0.001), with differences of up to 54.1 percentage points that reverse direction depending on the identity of the affected party. perceived lasting effects of violence are high and do not vary across cases (v = 0.024). recognition of suffering operates as a situated moral judgment. universitas psychologica

a measurement invariance study of the sexual cognitions checklist across sexual orientation and gender identity. the sexual cognitions checklist (scc) provides a unique framework for assessing both positive (psc) and negative sexual cognitions (nsc). few studies have examined sexual fantasies and cognitions in sexual orientation and gender diversity (sogd) populations. this study tested the measurement invariance, reliability, and validity of the spanish scc scores across sexual orientation and gender identity groups. using a nationwide strategy, a sample of 2,000 adults was recruited: 443 bisexual, 693 gay, and 829 heterosexual individuals; by gender, there were 963 cisgender men, 856 cisgender women, and 181 transgender and gender-diverse (tgd) individuals. results supported strict or partial strict invariance for both positive and negative subscales (scc-psc and scc-nsc), supporting meaningful cross-group comparisons. significant differences emerged across sexual orientation and gender identity in psc and nsc dimensions. psc showed the most consistent associations, in a positive direction, with self-reported sexual functioning (i.e., desire, arousal, and penile erection/vaginal lubrication), whereas nsc showed fewer, negative associations. these findings address a critical gap by including underrepresented populations and extending the evidence base beyond cisgender heterosexual samples. to our knowledge, the scc is currently the only instrument in the spanish context with psychometric evidence supporting its use across sogd groups, making it a potentially valuable tool for inclusive research and clinical practice in sexual health. journal of sex research

ecologically derived suicidal ideation in adolescents: proximal associations with self-referential thoughts. objective: suicide is the second leading cause of death among 10-14 and 25-34-year-olds in the u.s. suicidal ideation (si) is one of the strongest predictors of death by suicide in children and adolescents. there is a critical need for identifying time-variant short-term risk factors for suicidal ideation. although trait self-criticism (i.e. thinking focused on negative self-evaluation) and self-reassurance (i.e. providing self-compassion) are known vulnerabilities for si, their short-term, real-time association with si remains remarkably understudied. to address this critical gap, we examined how self-critical and self-reassuring responses may affect in-the-moment and subsequent si in a youth's environment.
method: levels of self-criticism, self-reassurance, and si were assessed 3 times per day over 2 weeks using ecological momentary assessment (ema) technology in 114 12- to 15-year-old youth recruited primarily from child psychiatric hospital programs in the northeast of the u.s. participants were asked to rate how self-critical and self-reassuring they had been since the last prompt.
results: a series of zero-inflated negative binomial mixed models showed that greater levels of self-criticism compared to one's own average levels beyond the overall sample's average were linked to higher si in both the current and the next assessment window. lower between but not within-person self-reassurance was linked to higher si.
conclusions: the findings highlight the need for further research on the clinical relevance of assessing and targeting self-criticism and enhancing self-reassurance in the day-to-day lives of youth to reduce si. journal of clinical child and adolescent psychology

psychometric assessment of the basic empathy scale (bes-20) in ecuadorian adolescents: a bifactor modeling approach and measurement invariance across sex. the present study examined the psychometric properties, structural validity, wording-related method effects, and sex measurement invariance of the basic empathy scale (bes-20) among ecuadorian adolescents, addressing the need for culturally adapted measures of empathy in latin american contexts. using a quantitative, cross-sectional, and instrumental design, valid data were collected from 635 adolescents (m= 15.05, sd = 2.32). for multi-group measurement invariance analyses across self-reported sex, a balanced subsample of 626 participants (313 male and 313 female participants) was analyzed after excluding nine participants who identified outside the two binary categories. to account for the ordinal nature of the five-point likert response scale, analyses were conducted using diagonally weighted least squares (dwls/wlsmv) estimation on polychoric correlation matrices. confirmatory factor analyses indicated that preliminary solutions grouping reverse-worded items into a third factor (often labeled "emotional insensitivity") were consistent with a wording-related method artifact rather than a substantive psychological dimension. incorporating an orthogonal method factor for the seven reverse-worded items within a bifactor-type confirmatory model recovered the original two-factor structure (cognitive and affective empathy) with good model fit (cfi = 0.963, tli = 0.957, srmr = 0.060, rmsea = 0.068, 90% ci [0.062, 0.073]), outperforming the correlated two-factor (cfi = 0.721) and unconstrained three-factor (cfi = 0.885) models. direct substantive items exhibited statistically significant factor loadings (λ = 0.451-0.795), and subscale reliability estimated via mcdonald's omega (ω) was adequate for direct indicators of cognitive empathy (k = 6, ω = 0.775) and affective empathy (k = 7, ω = 0.799). furthermore, sequential multi-group cfa supported full scalar measurement invariance across self-reported sex (∣δcfi∣ ≤ 0.007 < 0.010; ∣δrmsea∣ ≤ 0.005 < 0.015), indicating that latent empathy scores are comparable across male and female adolescents in this sample. overall, findings suggest that negatively phrased items introduce systematic method variance in adolescent self-reports. practically, the adapted bes-20 provides a structurally sound tool for educational and prevention research in ecuador, with potential applicability in clinical settings pending validation with clinical samples. acta psychologica

the role of u.s.-based professional societies in advancing and creating space for global psychological science. with growing recognition that psychological science has primarily focused on white euro-american samples, constructs, theories, and methods, there is an urgent need to broaden the scope and inclusiveness of the discipline. although journals, funding agencies, and individual scientists each play important roles in advancing this shift, u.s.-based professional societies are particularly well positioned to promote globally engaged psychological science. recognizing this potential, the u.s. national committee for psychological science, with assistance from the federation of associations in behavioral and brain sciences, undertook an effort to gather and compile information about what u.s.-based professional societies are doing to enhance global engagement. representatives of 24 professional societies across clinical, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology; statistics; behavioral medicine; neuroscience; and general psychology completed an online survey. our analysis indicated that international focus was very important or important to more than 70% of the society representatives surveyed, and various activities to promote global engagement were described, although membership of majority world scientists remained low, with limited integration of these scientists in leadership structures. on the basis of these findings and prior scholarship, we outline key approaches for inclusive, strategic, and scaffolded efforts to promote global psychological science. perspectives on psychological science

in defense of loneliness: the adaptive functions of a misunderstood state. loneliness is often portrayed as a public-health threat, yet this framing obscures important distinctions and empirical evidence that have been provided by different psychological frameworks. although chronic loneliness-especially when paired with social isolation-is linked to impaired social functioning and psychiatric risk, acute loneliness may serve an adaptive role. evidence suggests that acute loneliness can, in fact, enhance social attention, affiliative motivation, and readiness for interpersonal synchrony and may foster introspection and social cognition. loneliness, therefore, is not inherently pathological, and differentiating acute from chronic loneliness appears essential for clinical practice and public discourse. in this article, i challenge the deficit-based framing of loneliness by providing a brief synthesis of some of the relevant psychological, relational, and clinical frameworks. perspectives on psychological science

internationalization at home and global competence among chinese university students: the mediating role of intercultural self-efficacy. internationalization at home (iah) offers opportunities for intercultural learning without student mobility. drawing on social cognitive theory and intergroup contact theory, this study examined indirect associations between perceived iah and global competence through intercultural self-efficacy, alongside generalized self-efficacy. a two-wave survey of 435 chinese university students measured iah at t1 and both efficacy variables and competence at t2, approximately 4-6 weeks later. self-developed measures were assessed using nonoverlapping development and confirmation subsamples. the primary item-level latent model treated knowledge, academic competence, international attitude, and values recognition as separate outcomes. iah was positively associated with intercultural self-efficacy (β = 0.532). its indirect associations through intercultural efficacy were positive for all four outcomes in the primary bootstrap analysis, whereas generalized-efficacy indirect associations were significant for three outcomes, excluding values recognition. contrasts favored intercultural efficacy for knowledge and international attitude, but not conclusively for the other two outcomes. explained variance ranged from 0.27 to 0.35. inverse-probability weighting retained the knowledge, academic, and attitude indirect associations, while the values interval included zero. including communication as a fifth latent outcome retained the four-outcome path pattern. method-factor adjustment attenuated the iah-efficacy associations. the findings support examining efficacy specificity and competence facets separately, with the values-recognition association requiring greater caution. because efficacy and competence were measured concurrently, the indirect associations do not establish causal mediation. acta psychologica
