development of the sexual experiences survey-victimization-short forms (ses-v-sf) and a psychometric evaluation of ses-v standard and short forms. the sexual experiences survey-victimization (ses-v) was substantially revised in 2024 to broaden the range of sexual exploitation victimization assessed. although the revised ses-v offers important advantages, its length may limit its usefulness in some research and applied contexts. the purpose of this study was to develop a short form of the ses-v and to evaluate the psychometric performance of both the short-form and the standard-form ses-v. using a predefined process, we selected two to four items from each ses-v module. these items captured 89% to 96% of the victimization reported within each module in a national dataset. we then recruited 1,103 adults through cloudresearch, oversampling groups previously underrepresented in ses-v research. participants were randomized to complete the standard-form ses-v or one of two short-form versions along with measures to assess convergent validity. a subsample of participants ( = 640) completed the same ses-v form again two weeks later to assess test-retest reliability. the short forms performed well and were comparable to the standard form in convergent validity and test-retest reliability. endorsement rates on the short forms were similar to the standard form across three of four modules, and the short forms required less than half the administration time (i.e. a median of under five minutes). findings were generally consistent across demographic subgroups. this study provides psychometric support for the short forms and additional psychometric evidence for the standard form. future research should further examine whether the short forms capture the full range of victimization across diverse populations. journal of sex research

addenbrooke's cognitive examination-iii (ace-iii): preliminary psychometric properties, normative data, and normative thresholds for functionally independent french older adults. the addenbrooke's cognitive examination-iii (ace-iii) has demonstrated good psychometric properties across different languages and populations. however, psychometric evidence and normative data for the french version remain limited. therefore, this study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the ace-iii in functionally independent french older adults and to establish normative data. a total of 103 community-dwelling, functionally independent older adults living in france completed a semistructured interview, the ace-iii, fried frailty phenotype, geriatric depression scale, and university of california los angeles loneliness scale. internal consistency, construct validity, and concurrent criterion validity were examined. regression-based normative equations, normative trajectories, and individualized normative thresholds were developed using age and education. the ace-iii demonstrated good internal consistency (cronbach's α = .81) and satisfactory construct and concurrent criterion validity evidenced by strong correlations between the global score and subdomains (r = .67 to .92). age significantly predicted ace-iii performance. education was retained in the normative models following a theory-driven approach. regression-based normative equations, normative trajectories, and individualized normative thresholds were established for the total score and each neurocognitive domain. these findings support the use of ace-iii for neurocognitive screening in french older adults. longitudinal and process-based studies are warranted to further establish its clinical utility. applied neuropsychology-adult

tired of thinking? think again! an experience-sampling study of bidirectional dynamics between rumination and mental fatigue in athletes. recovery days are intended to support psychological and physical recovery, yet repetitive sport-related thinking may interfere with this process. this four-week experience-sampling study examined the dynamic interplay between rumination and mental fatigue during rest days in competitive athletes, as well as the moderating roles of perfectionistic concerns and perfectionistic strivings. a total of 134 athletes completed repeated rest-day assessments of rumination and mental fatigue, with perfectionism measured at baseline using a sport-adapted version of the fmps-brief. continuous-time structural equation modelling revealed significant bidirectional coupling between rumination and mental fatigue, supporting a self-reinforcing dynamic in which rumination fuels fatigue, and accumulated fatigue heightens the likelihood of further rumination, creating a 'vicious cycle'. the rumination → mental fatigue pathway was stronger than the reverse, underscoring the critical importance of mental rest and psychological recovery in sport. perfectionistic concerns significantly moderated this association, suggesting that athletes high in evaluative self-criticism may be more vulnerable to the rumination-fatigue cycle, whereas perfectionistic strivings did not exert a moderating effect. these findings advance a process-oriented understanding of psychological recovery in athletes and may inform future research on how short-term rumination-fatigue dynamics contribute to longer-term maladaptive recovery patterns, including burnout risk. interventions targeting repetitive negative thinking, such as mindfulness-, cognitive-behavioral-, or acceptance-based approaches, may help athletes preserve psychological recovery under performance demands. psychology of sport and exercise

bidirectional short-term associations between incidental affect and physical activity: heterogeneous effects beyond individual-specific diurnal patterns. physical activity and affective experiences play a relevant role in physical health and mental well-being and fluctuate substantially within individuals across the day. although intensive longitudinal studies increasingly examine bidirectional within-person associations between affect and physical activity in daily life, methodological approaches for analyzing these dynamics remain underdeveloped. further, it remains unclear to what extent short-term affect-activity associations exist beyond stable individual-specific diurnal patterns. two intensive longitudinal datasets were analyzed (n = 68 students; n =127 general population). momentary affective states (energetic arousal, calmness, valence) were assessed using ecological momentary assessment alongside continuously recorded step counts. physical activity was aggregated across moving time windows ranging from 15 to 120 minutes before and after each affect assessment. individual-specific diurnal trajectories of affect and activity were modeled using polynomial and fourier regressions. within-person associations were estimated before and after removing diurnal components. across both datasets, affect-activity associations were generally small and heterogeneous across individuals. energetic arousal showed the most consistent positive within-person associations with physical activity. calmness exhibited weak negative associations and valence showed little systematic coupling with activity. no specific time-lag window consistently produced stronger effects. associations between energetic arousal and physical activity persisted after adjustment for diurnal rhythms. affect-activity relations are weak on average across individuals, yet highly person-specific with large differences in the size and direction of associations and embedded within stable daily rhythms. future research should place greater emphasis on individualized modeling approaches that explicitly account for temporal structure and interindividual heterogeneity in within-person processes. psychology of sport and exercise

prospective dynamics of bullying perpetration and bullying victimization in adolescents: a two-wave cross-lagged network analysis. introduction: bullying perpetration and victimization frequently co-occur in adolescence, yet research relying on aggregate measures provides limited insight into how specific behaviors and experiences are prospectively connected. this study uses a network perspective to examine the transitivity, persistency, and centrality underlying the longitudinal overlap between bullying perpetration and victimization.
methods: data were collected from a public high school in china using a two-wave design in 2023. the final sample included 438 adolescents (mean age = 16.53 years; 39.3% girls). bullying perpetration (nine items) and victimization (four items) were measured using the illinois bullying and victimization scales. a lasso-regularized ordinal cross-lagged panel network was estimated to examine prospective item-level associations while controlling for age and sex.
results: persistency varied across specific perpetration behaviors, whereas all four victimization experiences showed positive autoregressive associations. cross-lagged associations were observed within and between perpetration and victimization, indicating behavior-specific patterns of transitivity. being called names showed the highest out-strength, whereas contributing to harassment, being hit and pushed, and teasing peers showed relatively high in-strength.
conclusions: bullying dynamics are behavior-specific. the prospective connections among specific perpetration behaviors and victimization experiences highlight potential points of attention for bullying prevention and intervention. network-based approaches provide refined insights into the victim-offender overlap and may inform more focused school-based prevention efforts. journal of adolescence

incidental social category information influences scene evaluation and memory across cultures. visual cognition in naturalistic settings is inherently social, yet much of what is known about social categorisation derives from tasks in which group membership is made explicitly relevant. the present study examined whether social category information influences visual evaluation and memory when it is incidental to the task and embedded within visual scenes, and whether these effects differ across cultures. two hundred and thirty-one participants from east asian (china), south asian (india) and european (united kingdom and poland) cultural groups evaluated images depicting either ingroup or outgroup individuals, followed by an unexpected memory test. racial attitudes and the quality and quantity of intergroup contact were also measured. images depicting ingroup members were evaluated more positively and remembered more accurately than those depicting outgroup individuals. memory for images containing outgroup (but not ingroup) individuals was selectively associated with perceived interest. negative racial attitudes predicted less favourable evaluation of outgroup images, but only among participants reporting lower intergroup contact. there was no evidence that these effects were moderated by participant nationality. together, these findings suggest that social category information can influence evaluation and memory even when it is task irrelevant, with effects shaped by racial attitudes and intergroup contact. british journal of psychology

personality traits shape emotion regulation strategies in children with developmental language disorder. children with developmental language disorder (dld) often face socio-emotional challenges beyond language needs, yet the role of personality traits in shaping their emotion regulation (er) remains underexplored. this study compared er strategies between children with dld and typically developing (td) peers, examined personality predictors of er and explored the associations between these er strategies and psychosocial adjustment. sixty-eight children (dld = 27; td = 41), aged 8-12 years, completed self-report measures of personality, er strategies, including cognitive reappraisal (cr) and expressive suppression (es), and psychosocial adjustment. children with dld reported higher es use, whereas no group differences emerged for cr. in the dld group, higher extraversion predicted greater use of both cr and es, neuroticism predicted lower cr and agreeableness predicted lower es. regarding adjustment, higher es predicted poorer psychosocial adjustment across both groups. findings highlight personality influences on er in children with dld, with implications for socio-emotional assessment. british journal of developmental psychology

cognitive impairments in a mouse model for huntington's disease correlate with presymptomatic locomotion and the number of cag repeats. huntington's disease (hd) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded cag repeat in the huntingtin (htt) gene. the disease is characterized by movement disorders, and it also presents with personality changes, including apathy and aggression, along with cognitive decline. while most animal models for hd have been validated for motor deficits, less is known about alterations in other behavioral functions. here, we performed a longitudinal study to analyze the behavior of a knock-in mouse model of hd with a chimeric mouse/human exon 1 containing 140 cag repeats inserted into the murine huntingtin gene. we specifically inquired about the onset of cognitive impairments in knock-in mice and whether changes in various behavioral functions, such as locomotion, anxiety, and cognition, correlate at the individual level. our data indicate that female and male knock-in mice exhibit reductions in body weight, locomotion, and long-term spatial memory retrieval, before to the onset of overt motor coordination deficits. however, social behavior, working, and short-term memory remain unaffected. within knock-in mice, lower open-field activity correlated with poorer remote memory performance. importantly, cag repeat length negatively correlated with locomotor activity and spatial memory, indicating that greater repeat expansion predicts more severe behavioral impairment. these findings identify early affective changes, followed by selective long-term memory and locomotor deficits, in knock-in mice, supporting this model as a useful platform for studying prodromal hd and repeat-length-dependent disease variability. behavioural brain research

psychometric properties of the pid-5-bf in young colombian population: factor structure, reliability, and invariance by sex the aim of this study was to analyze the psychometric properties of the personality inventory for dsm-5 brief form (pid-5-bf; 25 items) in a non-clinical young colombianpopulation. the sample consisted of 1,294 participants aged between 14 and 24 years (m = 18.6, sd = 2.8), of whom 43.1% were men and 56.9% were women. an observational,analytical, and cross-sectional design of an instrumental-psychometric nature was used. initially, an exploratory factor analysis was performed, showing adequate feasibilityof the matrix (kmo = .904; bartlett’s test, p < .001) and a five-factor structure that explained 49.6% of the total variance. subsequently, using confirmatory factor analysiswith wlsmv estimation, the theoretical model of five correlated domains was tested.the fit indices indicated an adequate fit of the model (cfi = .960, tli = .954, rmsea = .052, 90% ci [.048, .055], srmr = .057). internal consistency was acceptable for the fivedomains (ω = .698–.753; α = .696–.754), with high total reliability (ω = .898; α = .887). multigroup invariance analysis by sex confirmed configural, metric, scalar, and strictinvariance (cfi ≤ .01), supporting measurement equivalence between men and women.overall, the results provide evidence of structural validity, internal consistency, and measurement invariance of the pid-5-bf in non-clinical colombian youth, supporting itsuse in research and comparative studies in this population. international journal of psychological research

father involvement bei ambulanten psychotherapien von kindern und jugendlichen zusammenfassung: theoretischer hintergrund: in den letzten jahrzehnten verbringen väter mehr zeit mit ihren kindern und übernehmen mehr verantwortung in betreuung und erziehung. dennoch zeigen internationale daten, dass väter in den psychotherapien ihrer kinder unterrepräsentiert sind, obwohl ihre beteiligung den therapieerfolg deutlich erhöhen kann. fragestellung: ziel der studie war es, die teilnahmehäufigkeit von vätern an psychotherapien ihrer kinder zu untersuchen und mögliche einflussfaktoren zu identifizieren. methode: es wurde eine retrospektive analyse aller verfügbaren akten eines verhaltenstherapeutischen kinder- und jugendlichen-psychotherapieinstituts für den zeitraum 2010 – 2020 durchgeführt. ausschlusskriterien waren therapieabbrüche, fehlende dokumentation oder nicht verfügbare eltern. erfasst wurden alter, geschlecht und diagnose des kindes, zusammenleben und sozioökonomischer status (ses) der eltern, entfernung zum therapieort, therapeut_innengeschlecht, jahr des therapiebeginns sowie teilnahme an bezugspersonensitzungen. analysen erfolgten deskriptiv sowie mit t–tests, korrelationen, anovas und linearen regressionsanalysen. ergebnisse: väter nahmen im durchschnitt an 7,6 % der sitzungen teil und waren in 25 % der fälle nie anwesend, während mütter an 16,4 % teilnahmen und in 1,5 % nie erschienen. die väterliche teilnahme korrelierte positiv mit zusammenleben mit der kindesmutter ( r = 0,21, p < 0,01) und höherem ses ( r = 0,16, p = 0,012). in den regressionsanalysen erwiesen sich das zusammenleben der eltern ( b = 3,00, p < 0,01) und die anzahl der bezugspersonensitzungen ( b = 1.19, p < .001) als positive prädiktoren. signifikante mittelwertunterschiede zeigten sich zwischen vätern, die mit der kindesmutter zusammenlebten und getrenntlebenden vätern ( md = 3,14 prozentpunkte, p < 0,001) sowie zwischen vätern von söhnen vs. von töchtern ( md = 1,81 prozentpunkte, p = 0,033). diskussion und schlussfolgerung: väter nahmen etwa halb so häufig wie mütter an psychotherapiesitzungen ihrer kinder teil. um die teilnahmehäufigkeit von vätern zu steigern, sollten therapien väterfreundlich gestaltet sein, insbesondere im hinblick auf getrenntlebende väter, väter mit niedrigerem ses und väter von töchtern. zukünftige qualitative studien sollten faktoren identifizieren, die die teilnahme von vätern erleichtern. kindheit und entwicklung

unveiling the foveal rod scotoma through flicker under low-light conditions, vision relies on rod receptors only. the foveal region in the center of the visual field, however, is devoid of rods. nevertheless, humans usually do not perceive any gap in their center of vision at night, because the missing information is filled-in from the surround. in the present study, we show that the rod scotoma can be rendered perceivable with a continuous flicker. the flicker interferes with the filling-in process, leaving a grayish spot at the rod scotoma's location in the subsequent phase. the spot appears blurry, phantom-like, and circular. after we had determined suitable frequencies for each participant, they reproduced the spot sizes with peripherally viewed disks. participants more often reported seeing the spot when the flicker frequency was similar to their preferred frequency. neither the levels of dark adaptation, as tested with rod stimuli in a mesopic condition, nor the macular pigmentation accumulating in the fovea influenced the reported spot sizes. on average, the spots were 2.5 dva in diameter. this is substantially larger than the average anatomical scotoma of 1.25 dva, likely reflecting the rod-sparse regions around the fovea. we demonstrate that flicker is sufficient to make the rod scotoma visible, similar to the s-cone scotoma. the findings emphasize that percepts in central rod vision may not represent veridical information across areas larger than the anatomical rod-free region. i-perception

on the critical contributions of end‐of‐sequence switching to our understanding of sequence variation abstract there remains disagreement regarding whether variability is an operant response dimension. a critical issue related to this disagreement is the extent to which the variation observed under a variability‐reinforcement contingency is directly reinforced versus induced through other factors. the goal of the present research was to improve our understanding of behavioral variability by clarifying the effects of a significant source of between‐sequence variation—namely, end‐of‐sequence switching. pigeons emitted four‐peck sequences across left and right keys in two experiments. in experiment 1, sequence variation was significantly greater under a lag 2 contingency that encouraged switching at the end of sequences relative to contingencies that did not. experiment 2 extended these findings to an environment that did not require sequence variation. one group earned food only following a sequence with a changeover at its start, and another group only received food following a sequence with a changeover at its end. only the latter contingency engendered sequence variation. both experiments confirm that contingencies that promote end‐of‐sequence switching are a critical source of between‐sequence variation. the implications of these findings for the discussion about whether variability is an operant response dimension are presented. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

trauma education and training in us graduate counseling and health service psychology programs: a 26‐year scoping review abstract this prisma scoping review systematically mapped 42 peer‐reviewed articles on trauma education and training within us graduate counseling and health service psychology programs over a 26‐year period (1999–2024). we descriptively summarized publication characteristics and mapped findings concerning trauma education content and delivery, educator preparation and support, and programmatic structures and systemic initiatives. most articles were published since 2019 and were conceptual rather than empirical. coverage across the research questions was uneven. the literature focused primarily on trauma content, status of trauma education, and andragogy‐related content. educator preparation and support received comparatively less attention, whereas programmatic structures and systemic initiatives were addressed in nearly half of the articles. overall, the literature offered more guidance on what trauma education should include and how it might be organized than empirical evidence on its implementation, evaluation, and sustainment. further research should evaluate these educational approaches and the support needed to implement them. counselor education and supervision

mental health among children and youngsters in kosovo background: child and adolescent mental health remains under-researched and insufficiently addressed in many developing countries, including kosovo, highlighting the need to consider the influence of social and cultural dynamics. objective: the current study investigated the mental health of children and adolescents, taking into account the social and cultural factors that may influence their well-being. methods: a mixed-methods design, equally weighted, was employed. the quantitative study included 318 participants. data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the strengths and difficulties questionnaire. the qualitative study included 36 participants, who were interviewed using semi-structured interviews. results: the findings showed that 38.7% of participants scored emotional problems above the normal range. in the same range, but with different % is also conduct problems 84.6%, hyperactivity 73.6% and peer problems 93.2%. qualitative findings highlighted difficulties in identifying the early signs of psychological problems and emphasized the important role of families, teachers, and peers in helping children and adolescents cope with psychological difficulties. conclusion: the findings indicate a clear need to increase public awareness of psychological problems, as well as to strengthen professional mental health services. furthermore, there is a need to create supportive environments within families and schools that encourage open discussion of psychosocial difficulties and promote early identification and intervention. health psychology research

differential longitudinal patterns of change following a socioemotional intervention targeting empathic concern and perspective taking in adolescents with varying baseline skills: a single-arm pre–post–follow-up evaluation abstract background empathic concern and perspective taking (ecpt) are relevant to adolescent peer relationships, social motivation, and loneliness. longitudinal change may differ according to initial ecpt skill level. objective to examine preliminary longitudinal change following exposure to flip the focus , a school-based socioemotional program designed to support ecpt and explore change in social achievement goals and loneliness. methods year 9 students from four australian independent schools were assessed at baseline, 2–3 weeks post-program, and 16 weeks post-program. linear mixed-effects models included 176 students ( m age = 14.19 years, sd = 0.37; 52.8% female), classified from baseline ecpt z scores as low ( n = 33), average ( n = 117), or high ( n = 26). models examined time, baseline ecpt group, and time × group effects. no contemporaneous untreated comparison was retained. results ecpt showed a significant time × group interaction, ηp² = 0.132: ecpt increased in the low group, remained stable in the average group, and declined in the high group before stabilising. social development goals also showed an interaction, ηp² = 0.045, with declines by follow-up in the average and high groups. social demonstration-avoid goals showed a smaller interaction, ηp² = 0.032, reflecting a temporary increase in the low group. loneliness increased modestly across time without group-specific change. conclusions findings provide preliminary evidence of differing longitudinal ecpt trajectories following program exposure. however, baseline-defined ecpt groups are susceptible to regression to the mean, and without a contemporaneous untreated comparison, causal attribution and differential intervention benefit cannot be established. further controlled evaluation is warranted. child & youth care forum

companion animals as relational resources: pet attachment, pet comfort, and human relationship quality among university student pet owners abstract background: companion animals can provide attachment, comfort, and social support, but these pet-related experiences may not correspond uniformly with the quality of different human relationships. this study examined whether pet attachment and comfort from companion animals were associated with friendship and family relationship quality among university student pet owners, while also considering broader indicators of social connection and sample-level pet characteristics. methods: cross-sectional survey analyses included 425 university students who personally owned at least one pet. pet attachment was assessed with the lexington attachment to pets scale and pet comfort was assessed with the comfort from companion animals scale. friendship and family relationship quality were examined as separate outcomes. pearson correlations and multiple linear regressions were estimated, with self-esteem and social desirability included as controls. results: pet attachment and pet comfort were positively associated with friendship quality and remained significant after adjustment for self-esteem and social desirability (pet attachment: β = 0.19, p < 0.001; pet comfort: β = 0.18, p < 0.001). neither pet attachment nor pet comfort was significantly associated with family relationship quality in the full owner sample. greater attachment and comfort were also associated with higher perceived social support and lower loneliness. conclusions: human-animal bonds may function as relational resources in relationship-specific rather than uniformly positive ways. among these university student pet owners, pet attachment and comfort were consistently associated with friendship quality but not with family relationship quality overall. future research should clarify mechanisms linking human-animal bonds to distinct human relationship domains and consistently identify a focal companion animal. human-animal interactions

animal-assisted human services (aahs) competencies, credentials, and training: a powerful trio abstract canada presently lacks comprehensive data on skills, credentials, and training requirements within its animal-assisted human services (aahs) sector. consequently, this commentary emphasizes how this intricate and fragmented field could be recognized and exemplary industry sector grounded in transparency, accountability, and professionalism. aahs encompasses assistance/service animals, animal-assisted activities (aaa), animal-assisted learning (aal), and animal-assisted therapy (aat). despite its rapid growth and nationwide presence, the sector remains largely unregulated, difficult to navigate, and research. without a unified national framework and the infrastructure needed to support and guide practices and encourage innovation, the aahs sector remains compromised. nevertheless, persistent demand and need for aahs accentuate the significance of developing a coordinated strategy that safeguards the well-being of consumers and end users, the welfare of human services assistance animals (hsaas), and augments public confidence. ongoing engagement with consumers, end users, service providers, and other stakeholders is vital to preventing exploitation and ensuring services are ethical and evidence-based. the industry’s voluntary national standard of canada (nsc) was co-established in good faith to uphold the credibility of the aahs sector and to support animal-assisted human services providers (aahsp) and animal-assisted services professionals (aasp), enabling them to focus on the needs and well-being of consumers, end-users, and the welfare of human services assistance animals (hsaa) while preserving the credibility of both the service providers and the industry. moreover, this commentary features the numerous benefits of acknowledging and investing in canada’s aahs labour market, including promising careers, recognition through existing and evolving channels, and the creation of new employment opportunities that align with diverse educational and professional aspirations nationwide. human-animal interactions

sex differences among university students with autism spectrum disorder in japan: the past diagnosis influences subsequent suicidal behavior and career outcomes background previous studies suggest that asd diagnosis may be delayed among female university students with relatively high iq because of camouflaging behaviors. however, evidence from japan remains limited. therefore, this exploratory study examined sex differences in clinical characteristics and outcomes. aims the study is aimed at (1) comparing comorbidities, interpersonal problems, school absences, suicidal behaviors, and postgraduation outcomes between male and female university students; and (2) examining sex differences according to the presence or absence of a prior asd diagnosis. methods this study was designed as an exploratory retrospective observational study. this study analyzed clinical records of 93 university students with asd (49 males, 44 females) who attended a mental health clinic between 2013 and 2018. comorbidities, school absences, interpersonal problems, suicidal behaviors, previous asd diagnosis, and postgraduate career status (e.g., full‐time employment, part‐time employment, or unemployment) were compared using chi‐square tests. results male students had a higher rate of prior diagnosis. depressive disorders were the most common comorbidity in both sexes. among female students, suicidal behaviors were significantly associated with school absence. in terms of career outcomes, female students were less likely to obtain regular employment. conclusion female students with asd had lower rates of prior asd diagnosis and higher rates of multiple self‐harm behaviors than male students. camouflaging, although not directly assessed in this study, may be one possible explanation for the lower rate of prior asd diagnosis among female students. these findings highlight the importance of recognizing less apparent autistic characteristics and associated mental health difficulties in female university students. new directions for child and adolescent development

the stanford multifaceted dissociation questionnaire: a 9-item measure of trait and state dissociation. dissociation is a common and increasingly studied phenomenon with substantial relevance for mental health. to date, researchers have often relied upon broad conceptualizations and retrospective measures, making it difficult to identify a consistent subset of experiences for dissociation, explore their links to related phenomena, and differentiate habitual from momentary dissociation. to address these issues, we introduce the stanford multifaceted dissociation questionnaire (smdq), a 9-item measure that assesses three facets of dissociation and can be employed to assess either trait or state dissociation. in study 1, we evaluated the content validity of the initial smdq item pool using feedback from individuals with lived experience of dissociation (n = 73) and content experts (n = 14), detailing our focus on detachment-type experiences that may help the dissociation construct to be more cleanly distinguished from other clinical phenomena. in study 2 (n = 400), we described the item selection process and examined the factor structure, internal consistency, and convergent/discriminant validity of both the trait and state versions of the smdq. in study 3 (n = 500), we further investigated the psychometric properties of both versions, including their factor structure, measurement invariance, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and convergent/discriminant validity. across the studies, scores on the trait and state versions of the smdq showed strong content validity and a theoretically congruent factor structure, comprised of alteration in the perception of one's mind, body, and world (suggesting a tripartite model of dissociation). this structure was largely invariant across demographic groups and time. we also demonstrate good convergent and discriminant validity, internal consistency (ω > 0.80), and temporal stability over 1 week (r > 0.70 for the trait version). overall, we conclude that the trait and state versions of the smdq are promising measurement tools that can enhance our understanding of dissociation's structure, antecedents, and consequences. journal of clinical psychology

cultural and multicultural topics in neuropsychology journal titles from 2021-2024: a follow-up study to data from 2010-2020. cultural influences on brain function were recognized by early leaders in the field of neuropsychology. in articles from 13 neuropsychology journals published from 2010-2020, cultural or multicultural content was reflected in 6.2% of the titles (ready et al., 2025). to update these data, the current study determined the cultural or multicultural content in titles from the same journals published in 2021-2024.titles from articles published in 13 neuropsychology journals from 2021-2024 were collected and coded for cultural and multicultural content. the study aimed to (1) determine if cultural or multicultural content increased from 2010-2020 to 2021-2024 and (2) explore topics that were most and least likely to appear in publications pertaining to cultural or multicultural issues.cultural or multicultural neuropsychology content was coded in 14.8% of all titles in neuropsychology journals from 2021-2024 (range 2.7% to 21.3%), which is an increase from 6.2% in 2010-2020 (range 1.1% to 13.4%). normative data and psychometric topics were addressed significantly (< .05) more often in cultural/multicultural titles versus non-cultural/multicultural titles, whereas psychiatric, medical, and neurologic issues were addressed significantly less often. there were no significant correlations between year of publication and cultural/multicultural titles ( = -0.09) or between impact factor and cultural/multicultural titles ( = -0.24).the field of clinical neuropsychology is publishing more scholarship about cultural and multicultural topics in 2021-2024 than in 2010-2020. more research on how cultural issues interface with psychiatric, medical, and neurologic issues in a neuropsychological context are fruitful avenues for future research. clinical neuropsychologist

targeting and tracking personality functioning in psychotherapy: a clinical case using the diagnostic interview for personality pathology based on icd-11 (dipp-11). aspects of personality functioning are central to the world health organization's icd-11 dimensional classification of personality disorder and are operationalized in the diagnostic interview for personality pathology based on icd-11 (dipp-11). the present case report illustrates how the dipp-11 framework may be used to conceptualize, guide, and track psychotherapy with a young man, "alex," whose stylistic trait presentation was characterized primarily by negative affectivity and detachment in terms of anxiousness, shame, social withdrawal, and emotional inhibition. the report follows alex before, during, and after a course of eclectic outpatient psychotherapy in a public mental health setting and demonstrates how the 16 dipp-11 aspects of personality functioning can serve both as treatment targets and as indicators of therapeutic change. the case particularly shows how impairments in self-esteem regulation, self-direction, perspective-taking, emotional regulation, decision-making, and situational-interpersonal appraisal may gradually improve through a combination of supportive psychotherapy, corrective emotional experiences, and the mobilization of fundamental trust. treatment progress is illustrated through repeated dipp-11 ratings, showing change as movement from higher to lower dysfunction scores. the case is discussed as an example of how a focus on personality functioning may offer a more dimensional, individualized, recovery-oriented and less stigmatizing approach to psychotherapy with people presenting with personality problems. clinical implications are considered for treatment planning, outcome monitoring, and service implementation across who member states. journal of clinical psychology

agency, ai , and acting for a purpose of the agent's own a feature of the kind of agency that evolved in animals is that their capacity for goal‐directed behaviour is exercised in the service of persistence and reproduction. these are the purposes (in a specific sense) for which behaviour has been produced. further, there is feedback between having these purposes and goal‐directed behaviour becoming increasingly sophisticated. artificial intelligence (ai) systems are unlikely ever to have biological purposes. however, the same kind of feedback process could arise in ai systems if they acquire the right kind of organisation, and it promotes their individual persistence. that possibility is a significant new ai safety consideration. mind & language

the dark side of the fan: predicting different types of fandom elitism through fanship and dark traits using median regression and decision tree modelling abstract fandoms, or fanbases, are communities of people connected by a shared interest. although previous studies have addressed the positive aspects of belonging to a community, this study explores the dark side of fandom engagement. this study ( n = 511) aims to examine how gender, machiavellianism, sadism and types of narcissism (grandiose, hypersensitive and collective) predict two dimensions of fandom elitism: self‐inflation and other‐derogation. therefore, this study addresses the knowledge gap regarding predictors of fandom elitism in niche fandoms, as previous research has predominantly focused on sports fandoms. correlation analysis and median regression were used to establish correlates and predictors of self‐inflation and other‐derogation related to fandom elitism. a chi‐square automatic interaction detection (chaid) decision tree model (dtm) was used to find the most influential predictors of fandom elitism. the results contribute to a better understanding of the personality profile characteristic of members of diverse polish fandoms. journal of community & applied social psychology

a motivational analysis of perceived legitimacy of mafias the present research aimed to investigate a motivational antecedent of people’s perceived legitimacy of mafias and attitudinal tolerance toward mafia-related collusion. based on the quest for significance theory, we hypothesized that the need to matter, to count, and to “be someone” predicts perceived legitimacy of mafias, understood as an internalized attitudinal and value-based orientation toward mafia authority, through two parallel mediating mechanisms: (a) a stronger endorsement of self-enhancement values (i.e., influence, wealth, authority, power), and (b) a stronger endorsement of a masculine honor ideology. study 1 assessed attitudinal tolerance toward mafia-related collusion as an indirect indicator of legitimacy, whereas study 2 employed a more direct measure of perceived mafia legitimacy. results of two cross-sectional surveys (total n = 983) supported the hypothesis. overall, this research suggests a motivational dynamic underlying people’s perceived legitimacy of and attitudinal tolerance toward mafias as a potential route to achieve personal significance. journal of social and political psychology

is any body there? breakdown in recovery from traumatic dissociation 1 abstract the paper considers a countertransference of invisibility as pointing towards dissociative disturbance following interpersonal developmental trauma. alongside development in many areas, the ongoing dissociative state may attract a persistent threat of breakdown accompanied by loneliness, stress and anxiety without hope of containment in the safety of another’s understanding and concern. this is understood as the loss of a ‘vertical axis’ of psychic integration with body and emotional experience, from which the ‘horizontal axis’ of capacity to feel empathically related with any body, may also collapse. for the patient to work analytically involves reconnecting to states that were dissociated during early development – an encounter with extreme pain and intolerable emotions that must be borne within the body for healing and integration to occur. the paper presents a case in which a repeating cycle of breakdowns and partial recoveries was worked through, allowing the sense of an embodied analyst—some body who had been there all along—to emerge. three features of the analytic process are discussed: the threat of breakdown symbolised as a whirlpool circling around a deep hole; invisibility and isolation of the child’s experience as a factor in trauma; and, the internalized dark voices of critical self‐attack. journal of analytical psychology

do election outcomes matter for life satisfaction? abstract: prior research suggests declines in life satisfaction among supporters of losing parties, but evidence largely stems from two-party systems. drawing on goal-regulation and social-identity perspectives, we examined election-related changes in global and domain-specific life satisfaction in a multiparty system across the east german state elections 2024 ( n = 1,211) and the federal election in germany 2025 ( n = 301), considering objective and subjective indicators of electoral success and vote choice. across studies, these indicators were largely unrelated to changes in life satisfaction, with only isolated effects among afd and bsw voters. overall, even amid substantial political change, collective political outcomes had limited consequences for life satisfaction up to three months later, highlighting the limits of simple winner–loser accounts in multiparty contexts. social psychology

(backwards) into the future: nostalgic and anticipated deprivation as predictors of populist voting in a two-wave election study abstract: while populist voting is often explained by perceiving one’s group as unfairly worse off than others ( collective relative deprivation), the group’s past and future may provide further politically consequential benchmarks for deprivation. using two-wave panel data from the east german state election study 2024, we find that nostalgic and anticipated deprivation are strongly correlated and independently predict far-right populist voting beyond collective relative deprivation. in contrast, left-wing populist voting was negatively predicted by nostalgic deprivation, positively by collective relative deprivation, and unrelated to anticipated deprivation. following the election, anticipated deprivation decreased among far-right voters, while changes varied with perceived electoral success. these findings broaden the temporal lens on relative deprivation, highlighting how perceived status trajectories relate to present-day populist support. social psychology

rising support for political violence is associated with perceived political discrimination abstract: election periods can heighten political conflict and support for political violence. using two-wave panel data from the east german state elections study 2024 (egses24) in saxony, thuringia, and brandenburg ( n = 1,053), we examined how support for political violence changed from before to after the elections and whether this change was linked to perceived electoral loss and perceived political discrimination. support for political violence increased slightly after the elections. this increase was associated with increases in perceived political discrimination, particularly among individuals high in social dominance orientation. perceived electoral success did not explain the increase in political violence endorsement. these findings suggest that experiences of political discrimination, rather than electoral defeat as such, may help explain rising support for political violence during election periods. social psychology

do far-right populists (really) seem more authentic? abstract: this study examines the perceived authenticity of german politicians during the 2024 state elections in brandenburg, saxony, and thuringia using data from a two-wave survey panel. the results show that afd politicians were not perceived as more authentic than incumbents, challenging the notion of a general authenticity advantage for far-right populists. however, afd candidates enjoyed a relative authenticity advantage among their own supporters: afd voters perceived their party’s candidates as more authentic than voters of other parties perceived their candidates. perceived authenticity was positively associated with candidates’ voting propensity, highlighting its relevance for electoral preferences. finally, authenticity ratings increased significantly for four of six candidates during the campaign, suggesting that perceptions of political authenticity can change over time. social psychology

transtheoretisches lernen im psychotherapiestudium zusammenfassung: theoretischer hintergrund: die berufsqualifizierende tätigkeit iii (bqt iii) im masterstudiengang psychotherapie ermöglicht studierenden, reale therapiesitzungen zu begleiten und eigenständig therapeutische aufgaben zu übernehmen. fragestellung: untersucht wurden veränderungen der selbsteinschätzung therapeutischer kompetenzen im verlauf der bqt iii sowie die wirksamkeit der dort durchgeführten patientenbehandlungen. methode: an der studie nahmen 49 studierende teil, die vor und nach dem seminar fragebögen zur kompetenzeinschätzung bearbeiteten. patient_innen berichteten im behandlungsverlauf ihre psychische belastung. veränderungen wurden mit t-tests für verbundene stichproben analysiert. ergebnisse: nach dem seminar berichteten studierende mehr sicherheit in der behandlung ( t‍(8) = 5.47, p < .001, d = 0.85) sowie größere zuversicht in der anwendung therapeutischer fertigkeiten und im umgang mit herausforderungen ( t‍(8) = 6.46, p < .001, d = 0.82). patient_innen zeigten eine signifikante reduktion der psychischen belastung (hscl-11: t‍(26) = 2.68, p = .012, d = 0.38; phq-9: t‍(7) = 4.46, p = .003, d = 0.26; emi-10: t‍(7) = 3.79, p = .006, d = 0.56). schlussfolgerungen: die bqt iii geht mit gesteigertem kompetenzselbstvertrauen der studierenden und reduzierter psychischer belastung der patient_innen einher und unterstreicht das potenzial praxisorientierter ausbildungsformate. zeitschrift fur klinische psychologie und psychotherapie

experiences and acceptability of group‐based, remotely delivered functional imagery training intervention for weight loss: a qualitative study abstract objectives many weight management interventions prioritize education and behavioural prescription over the motivational processes that sustain change. functional imagery training (fit), a motivational intervention that uses multisensory imagery, has supported weight loss when delivered individually. this study explored participants' views of fit and the acceptability of delivering it remotely to small groups. design qualitative interview study embedded in a single‐arm feasibility study and the intervention arm of a pilot randomized controlled trial of remotely delivered fit for adults with a body mass index (bmi) over 35 kg/m 2 . methods participants attended four fit sessions delivered by video conference in small groups over 6 weeks. thirty‐two participants (28 female; aged 25–71 years) completed one‐to‐one semi‐structured interviews approximately 6 weeks post‐intervention. data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. results of five themes, three addressed participants' views of fit: fit as a practical bridge between knowing and doing; imagery as a tool for regulating emotional eating; and fit as a non‐judgemental alternative to healthcare encounters experienced as stigmatizing. two addressed the acceptability of delivery: remote delivery as accessible and psychologically safe; and peer support as normalizing and motivating. some participants wanted longer or more frequent sessions. conclusions among participants who engaged, group‐based, remotely delivered fit was described as acceptable and personally meaningful. interviewees lost more weight than the wider sample, and almost half of those randomized to fit in the pilot trial did not attend a session, so these views may not reflect those of non‐attenders. psychologically stigma‐sensitive and flexible delivery, group‐based, remotely delivered fit was experienced as acceptable and psychologically meaningful. the findings highlight the importance of psychologically informed, stigma‐sensitive and flexible delivery; warrants further evaluation models in supporting engagement with weight management interventions. british journal of health psychology

associations between long-term high-altitude exposure and cognitive function: a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on event-related potentials although long-term high-altitude (ha) exposure is associated with cognitive alterations, evidence regarding the corresponding event-related potential (erp) components is inconsistent, and a systematic synthesis across processing stages is lacking. this meta-analysis synthesized available erp evidence to examine neurophysiological alterations associated with cognitive processing following long-term ha exposure. the most consistent finding was a reduction in p300 amplitude among the ha groups (g = −0.476). reduced p100 amplitude was also observed (g = −0.325), although this finding was less robust, with a possible small-study-effect signal. rotation-related negativity amplitude was more negative in ha groups (g = −0.748), but this estimate was based on only four independent studies. no reliable between-group differences were observed for other evaluated erp outcomes. moderator analyses provided limited evidence of systematic moderation and are constrained by low statistical power. overall, the available evidence is heterogeneous and primarily based on cross-sectional comparisons. these findings suggest possible stage-dependent associations between long-term ha exposure and erp alterations, although rigorous longitudinal studies using standardized erp protocols are needed to substantiate these associations. journal of intelligence

within‐person relations between mobile phone addiction and mental well‐being among college students: the moderating role of negative self‐schema abstract mobile phone addiction has been linked to poorer mental well‐being, yet the direction of this relationship at the within‐person level remains unclear. a three‐wave longitudinal study followed 1462 college students (m age = 18.60, sd age = 0.83). mobile phone addiction, negative self‐schema, and mental well‐being were assessed at each wave, and a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (ri‐clpm) was used to separate within‐person dynamics from between‐person differences. negative self‐schema was assessed at each wave, and its between‐person component was used as the moderator. at the within‐person level, we found that higher‐than‐usual mobile phone addiction was associated with subsequent decreases in mental well‐being ( β t1→t2 = −0.09, p < 0.01; β t2→t3 = −0.09, p < 0.05), whereas the reverse path was not significant. in addition, negative self‐schema moderated this association. specifically, among individuals with higher levels of negative self‐schema, greater mobile phone addiction was associated with lower subsequent mental well‐being ( β = −0.134, p < 0.01), whereas this effect was not significant among individuals with lower levels of negative self‐schema ( β = 0.003, p > 0.05). these findings highlight negative self‐schema as an important vulnerability factor linking mobile phone addiction to poorer mental well‐being and may inform intervention efforts. applied psychology-health and well being

assessing measurement invariance with bifactor irt models 用双因子irt模型评估测量不变性 evaluating measurement invariance is essential for ensuring score comparability across individuals and groups. while unidimensional item response theory (irt) models are commonly used, their assumption of local independence is often violated. bifactor models provide an alternative by incorporating both a general factor and specific factors, making them suitable for assessments with locally dependent item clusters, such as reading comprehension tests based on shared text passages. this study examines measurement invariance in bifactor irt models using marginal maximum likelihood (mml) estimation and likelihood ratio testing, with simulations motivated by the norwegian national reading test (2022–2023). we first investigate the implications of using a misspecified unidimensional model to evaluate differential item functioning when data follow a bifactor structure. we then evaluate how alternative item parameter constraints in multiple-group bifactor models, constraining general slopes alone versus both general and specific slopes, impact invariance assessment. we further compare mml estimators for likelihood ratio testing, including adaptive gauss–hermite quadrature, laplace approximation, and the expectation-maximization algorithm with dimension reduction. the results show that all methods yield accurate size when specific-factor slopes are the same across groups. however, when these slopes differ across groups, models that fail to account for such differences can produce inflated size. educational and psychological measurement

the effect of bst via telehealth on caregiver implementation of incidental teaching the increasing prevalence of autism spectrum disorder has increased the need for accessible and scalable behavioral health services. incidental teaching is an effective naturalistic intervention for increasing communication skills in children with autism, and behavior skills training is an effective method for teaching caregivers to implement evidence-based practices. although telehealth has emerged as a viable modality for caregiver training, additional replications are needed. this study replicated and extended prior research by evaluating bst delivered via telehealth to train caregivers to implement incidental teaching. nine caregiver child dyads and three trainers participated. trainers used synchronous videoconferencing, and researchers evaluated outcomes using three multiple baseline single case designs. following training, all caregivers improved procedural fidelity and reached 100% accuracy across two consecutive sessions. caregivers also increased communication opportunities, resulting in increased child mands above baseline levels. findings support telehealth delivered bst as an effective model for caregiver training. behavior modification

dimension‐specific attentional sensitivity in fears of compassion: a dot‐probe investigation of three dimensions abstract the three dimensions of fears of compassion (foc)—fear of being compassionate to oneself (foc self ), of receiving compassion from others (fos from ), and of expressing compassion to others (foc others )—have been linked to a range of psychopathological outcomes, yet little is known about whether these fears are reflected in early attentional processing of socio‐emotional cues. using a dot‐probe paradigm with positive and negative emotional faces, the present study examined dimension‐specific attentional patterns in chinese university students. adopting the evolutionary‐motivational framework of compassion, and following recommendations to analyze the three fear of conpassion scale subscales separately rather than as a composite, participants were classified into high and low groups separately on each subscale, and three parallel linear mixed models were fitted with gender as a covariate. across all three models, high‐foc participants responded approximately 50–65 ms more slowly than low‐foc participants, with the largest group difference observed for foc from . significant group × congruence interactions emerged for the two interpersonal dimensions (foc from and foc others ) and a marginal interaction for foc self , with a consistent descriptive pattern across dimensions: high‐foc groups displayed a vigilance‐like congruence effect on negative‐face trials whereas low‐foc groups showed a negligible effect. the three‐way group × emotion × congruence interaction was not significant in any model, and the present design was not powered to detect such higher‐order effects. findings are therefore interpreted as preliminary evidence that fear of compassion—particularly from others—is associated with a subtle attentional sensitivity to the location of negative facial cues, consistent with attachment‐based accounts of foc. adequately powered confirmatory replication is required. psych journal

exploring dimensionality of the workers’ interest scale in engineering with latiné engineers this study investigated the dimensionality of the workers’ interest scale in engineering (wise) using data from 523 latiné engineers. exploratory graph analysis (ega) was conducted to identify the underlying structure of the wise, followed by bootstrap analysis to test item and dimension stability. we examined the conceptual alignment and statistical model fit of the dimensions. group differences across gender and engineering disciplines were also assessed. findings indicate that the final 39-item wise captures five distinct dimensions of engineering interests: technology and engineering innovation, teamwork and leadership, research and experimentation, business development, and project management. the final wise items demonstrated high item stability, meaningful conceptual alignment, and good model fit. moreover, group comparisons revealed variations in interests across gender groups (cohen’s d ranged between .53 and .86) and engineering disciplines ( η 2 ranged between .01 and .16). implications, limitations, and directions for future research are discussed. counseling psychologist

environmental factors and career adaptability: effects of school connectedness and economic constraints abstract this study examined the interactive effects of economic resources and school connectedness on career adaptability, grounded in career construction theory and supplemented by conceptualizations from social cognitive career theory and the psychology of working theory. participants were 3981 senior high school students from 91 high schools in hong kong. a latent moderated structural equation model was used to test the proposed framework. findings revealed that school connectedness can compensate for the negative effects of resource limitations on career adaptability; however, its positive effects plateaued among participants with ample economic means. furthermore, adaptability resources mediated the indirect, moderated effects of school connectedness on adapting responses. these results underscored the vital role that positive, relational school environments play in fostering career adaptability, particularly for students facing substantial economic constraints. theoretical, practice, and research implications are discussed. career development quarterly

associations between empathy dimensions, love language expression, and relationship satisfaction among university students in northern cyprus. objective: the study aimed to explore relationships among aspects of empathy, love language expression, and relationship satisfaction among university students. we also examined attachment styles as a theoretical framework; however, severe measurement limitations prevented valid inferences about attachment patterns.
method: we used a cross-sectional study of 513 students in northern cyprus (m = 20.99 years; 56.3% female) using the relationship scales questionnaire (rsq), five love languages scale (flls), basic empathy scale (bes), and relationship assessment scale (ras). we used snowball sampling with power analysis showing adequate power to detect medium effects. however, we found important limitations in the measurement: the rsq showed unacceptably low reliability (α = 0.27 to 0.61), and attachment measures are therefore uninterpretable.
results: after revising initial errors in scoring, we found that expression of love language frequency was positively correlated with relationship satisfaction (r = .45), with quality time (r = .48) and gift-giving (r = .45) being the strongest associations. cognitive empathy (r = .39) was significantly more highly related to satisfaction than affective empathy (r = .15). due to the extremely low reliability of the rsq (0.27-0.61; α), we cannot make any inferences regarding attachment patterns. gender differences had a small to medium effect, with females displaying greater empathy and increased use of some love languages.
conclusion: the expression of love language and cognitive empathy are positively related to relationship satisfaction in this sample of university students. however, severe measurement restrictions using the attachment scale preclude any conclusions about attachment patterns. upcoming research should use psychometrically sound measures, such as the experiences in close relationships-revised (ecr-r) scale. bmc psychology

social network transitions among middle-aged australians: relationship with health-related quality of life, loneliness, and social isolation. this study aims to identify transitions in social network characteristics over time and whether such transitions predict subsequent health-related quality of life, loneliness, and social isolation. we included nationally representative panel data of 3192 australians aged 45 to 64. latent transition analysis examined eight social network indicators assessed at 2010 and 2018 to reveal the corresponding transitions between social network profiles. multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the relationship between transition profiles with outcomes of interest measured in 2018. we found minimal transitions during the study period: most participants sustained their interactions (either diverse or relatively restricted), while about 3% of participants expanded and 8% constricted their network. compared to individuals with sustained restricted profiles across time, those who constricted their networks were more likely to be isolated (odd ratio 1.68, 95% confidence interval 1.09-3.18), and those who transitioned toward more expansive networks were less likely to be isolated (0.24, 0.03-0.95). participants who expanded their social interactions were more likely to report good mental health status compared to participants who maintained restricted social interactions (2.66, 1.16-6.12). healthy ageing policies should consider supporting diverse community participation and engagement, and quality relationships. applied psychology-health and well being

personality was robust to the transition to remote work under the covid-19 pandemic. objective: the current study examines whether the transition between work contexts (in-person work to remote work) during the covid-19 pandemic influenced an individual's personality in a sample of 1475 working adults. previous work on personality change during the covid-19 pandemic suggests that people experienced a significant change in personality.
method: drawing from the personality dynamics literature and frame-of-reference effects, we extend this work by conducting irt-based invariance analyses and by fitting linear mixed-effects models on longitudinal, archival data.
results: results indicate that transitioning to remote work did not affect either interpretations of personality items nor mean-level personality trait scores during the covid-19 pandemic.
conclusions: findings from the current study suggest that while many aspects of work and non-work life changed in 2020 and 2021, we did not find evidence that the pandemic and the sudden shift to remote work influenced personality assessment. findings also provide support for the established theory that personality is robust to situational changes, highlighting the robustness of personality to predict future behaviors and attitudes regardless of changing work contexts. journal of personality

partial visions of utilitarianism: a critical examination of the oxford utilitarianism scale and cni frameworks. this study aimed to clarify the psychological structure of utilitarian moral judgment by examining how individual differences in, and an experimental manipulation of, utilitarian thinking relates to scores on the oxford utilitarianism scale (ous) and the cni model. study 1 (n = 312) examined the associations between personality variables and scores from the ous and cni models using correlational analyses. the results revealed that the impartial beneficence dimension of ous was positively related with light triad traits, prosocial behavior, religiosity, and negatively related with machiavellianism. the n parameter of the cni was found to be positively associated with kantianism, religiosity, action-oriented prosociality, and negatively associated with the dark triad traits, instrumental harm and relativism, while the c parameter was only related to the i parameter. additionally, instrumental harm showed positive associations with dark triad traits. in study 2, participants in the experimental group (n = 80) read a text promoting utilitarianism, while those in the control condition (n = 86) read a neutral text. subsequent changes in participants' ous and cni scores were examined. the findings indicated a significant increase in impartial beneficence scores, a significant decrease in c scores, and a significant decrease in n scores in the experimental group. overall, the findings suggest that the cni and ous parameters capture different aspects of utilitarianism while also highlighting the potential for both approaches to be further developed to offer a more comprehensive understanding of utilitarian moral judgment. acta psychologica

exploring cognitive and emotional predictors of adaptive information search. adaptive information search often requires balancing competing cognitive goals. in selecting an information search strategy, individuals may face a trade-off between the speed and efficiency of information acquisition. evidence suggests that individual differences explain variability in how people trade-off deliberation time and accuracy when making decisions. however, less is known about how individuals might differ in how they balance search speed and efficiency in information-rich environments that require sequential information sampling and flexible goal coordination. in our exploratory study, n = 127 participants played a novel variant of the code-breaking game mastermind in three conditions: in the speed condition, participants were incentivized for rapid game completion; in the efficiency condition for using few queries; and in the mixed condition for both. we assessed individual differences in numeracy, working memory, state and trait emotion, personality and thinking styles in a pretest. our results suggest that both numeracy and working memory predict information search behaviour across these conditions. higher numeracy and working memory scores were associated with improved performance and more effective information search strategies across conditions, particularly under time pressure. emotional predictors showed smaller and condition-dependent effects. state emotional dominance was negatively associated with performance in the mixed condition, suggesting a modulating role of emotional dominance in the coordination of competing demands. state emotional valence was negatively associated with performance under the speed incentive, potentially reflecting a relationship between emotional valence and time-sensitive goal-directed behaviour. our exploratory findings stress the relevance of considering individual differences in research on adaptive information search. cognition

merkmale von patient:innen mit digitalen gesundheitsanwendungen für psychische erkrankungen – ergebnisse einer analyse von versicherten in rheinland-pfalz/saarland zusammenfassung versicherte, die eine digitale gesundheitsanwendung für psychische erkrankungen (psydiga) verordnet bekommen, erhalten von ihrer krankenkasse daraufhin einen freischaltcode. wir untersuchten merkmale von versicherten, die einen freischaltcode erhalten bzw. diesen einlösen. es wurden abrechnungsdaten von erwachsenen versicherten mit einer psychischen erkrankung der aok rheinland-pfalz/saarland der jahre 2020–2022 mithilfe von logistischen regressionsmodellen untersucht. die analysestichprobe umfasste 280 706 versicherte: 280 103 versicherte ohne und 603 versicherten mit freischaltcode (davon 457 eingelöst). versicherte weiblichen geschlechts, unter 35 jahren sowie mit depressiven störungen, angst- oder schlafstörungen erhielten eher einen freischaltcode (z. b. odds ratio (or) weiblich vs. männlich 1,32, 95% konfidenzintervall (ki) 1,12–1,57; depressive vs. andere störung adjustiertes or 2,36 (95% ki 1,94–2,89)). versicherte zwischen 35–44 jahren lösten einen freischaltcode seltener ein als 25-34-jährige (or 0,46, 95%-ki 0,27-0,78). der bereits von anderen krankenkassen berichtete fokus der verschreibung von diga an frauen und jüngere personen bestätigt sich auch in unserer auswertung von aok-daten hinsichtlich psydiga. besonders bei patient:innen zwischen 35–44 jahren sollten behandler:innen bei entsprechendem vorliegen einer indikation vor einer möglichen verordnung die integrierbarkeit von psydiga in den alltag besprechen. psychotherapie psychosomatik medizinische psychologie

20 jahre deutsche gesellschaft für essstörungen: entwicklung, aktivitäten und perspektiven einer interdisziplinären fachgesellschaft zusammenfassung zum 20-jährigen bestehen wird die entwicklung der deutschen gesellschaft für essstörungen (dgess) bilanziert. grundlage sind gründungsmitteilung, dokumentierte aktivitäten, tätigkeitsberichte, digitale kommunikation und publikationen geförderter arbeitsgruppen. die dgess hat strukturen für forschung-praxis-transfer, leitlinienarbeit, forschungs- und nachwuchsförderung sowie wissenschaftskommunikation entwickelt. künftige schwerpunkte sind die stärkere verbindung von forschung und versorgung, nachwuchsförderung und partizipation. die dgess verbindet wissenschaft, klinische praxis und öffentlichkeit und unterstützt den wechselseitigen wissenstransfer. psychotherapie psychosomatik medizinische psychologie

when i see you smile: links among experienced affect, expressed emotional components, and target readability in a supportive interaction abstract navigating supportive interactions is an important task of friendship that involves exchanging affective information. however, experienced affect is not always readable, and emotional expressions are not all equally helpful in conveying experienced affect. we examined associations between target readability (i.e., emotional expressive accuracy, or the degree to which individuals accurately communicate their experienced affect to others), and experienced and expressed emotional components (i.e., facial expressions and affect words), when seeking support from a friend. participants ( n = 137 dyads, m age = 19.61 years, sd age = 1.34 years) took turns discussing problems they were having. to measure experienced affect, participants reported their positive and negative affect during the interaction. expressed emotional components were participants' facial movements (i.e., eyebrow movements and smiles) and use of positive and negative affect words. to measure readability, observers continuously rated participants' affect during the interaction; their ratings were correlated with similar self‐ratings made by participants, and those correlations were averaged. participants were more readable when they reported experiencing greater negative affect. in terms of expressed emotional components, participants were more readable when they had more eyebrow raises, and fewer eyebrow furrows and smiles. results elucidate factors that contribute to effective communication of experienced affect when seeking support from friends. personal relationships

a systematic review of the existing parent‐led interventions to promote the psychosocial development of neurodivergent children abstract background this systematic review takes a transdiagnostic approach to understanding the active components commonly used across evidence‐based interventions, to inform the development of a novel psychosocial intervention for children with developmental language disorder (dld). methods searches were conducted in december 2020, august 2022 and july 2026 of 11 databases, including: psycinfo, psycextra, embase, pubmed, cochrane central and medline. inclusion criteria was: trials must have compared interventions to a control group, or have an 8‐week follow‐up, include parent‐led components and measures of child psychosocial outcomes, must be published in english after 2000, with participants aged 2–13 years old, who met diagnostic criteria for seven categories of neurodivergence (that share psychosocial difficulties to children with dld). synthesis was conducted by coding intervention content using a taxonomy and calculating effect sizes using baseline and follow‐up data on psychosocial outcomes. quality appraisal was assessed using the national institute of health's quality assessment measures. results a total of 11,583 studies were selected for abstract screening; 52 studies met the pre‐specified inclusion criteria after full‐text screening. all interventions analysed were designed for autistic children ( n = 26) and/or attention deficit hyperactive disorder (adhd; n = 23). across studies, 870 children with adhd and 832 autistic children received interventions; 730 children with adhd and 701 autistic children received a control. four intervention components were most used across effective interventions: parent‐child interaction training, parenting behaviours, and emotion management for both parent and child. an association between parent wellbeing and improved child psychosocial outcomes is suggested, however limited by the lack of data. therapeutic and researcher contact appears to impact intervention engagement. accessibility is discussed. conclusion evidence‐based psychosocial interventions are required for neurodivergent children other than children with autism and adhd. psychosocial interventions for children with dld should consider addressing parent‐child communication, wellbeing of both parent and child, and involve therapeutic support. jcpp advances
