navigating divorce and partner bereavement: personality and trajectories of change in life satisfaction and mental health. dissolutions of romantic relationships can elicit diverse reactions across various aspects of well-being, but they also offer an opportunity to examine which factors promote resilience and identify individuals at risk. in this preregistered multisample longitudinal study, we examined the heterogeneity in life satisfaction and mental health changes around and during divorce or partner bereavement and whether personality (i.e., traits and resilient vs. nonresilient personality profiles) may explain individual differences in change trajectories. data from 1,306 divorcees and 1,150 bereaved partners were drawn from nationally representative panel studies in the netherlands (= 12,551), germany (= 10,830), and china (= 28,628) and analyzed using growth mixture modeling. four life satisfaction trajectories and three mental health trajectories were identified for each event. recovery and resilience emerged as the most common trajectories across events, outcomes, and samples. among personality factors, neuroticism was the most consistent predictor of a lower likelihood of belonging to a resilience trajectory. this study advanced the generalizability of findings across diverse loss-based events, populations, and aspects of well-being. the findings further underscore the influence of neuroticism in shaping, and potentially complicating, psychological adjustment surrounding divorce and partner bereavement. a practical guide to self-organising maps in psychological research. 心理研究中自组织映射的实用指南 identifying shared and distinct profiles, whether of symptoms, personality traits, or cognitive abilities, is essential for understanding psychological phenomena, yet doing so requires navigating interrelated theoretical, conceptual, and technical complexities. first, most psychological phenomena typically exist along continuous spectra rather than discrete categories, complicating the characterisation of inherently heterogeneous constructs. second, studying individual differences requires balancing population-level generalisation with person-level interpretability, which is critical for applied science and clinical practice. third, psychological data often contain missing values, non-linear relationships, and high-dimensional patterns that violate standard statistical assumptions. commonly used approaches for profile detection often fall short of these demands, producing oversimplified or difficult-to-interpret results that are hard to map back to the individual. in contrast, self-organising maps (soms) offer a powerful, visual, and intuitive solution that addresses these challenges. despite growing interest, soms remain underutilised in psychology, likely due to a lack of accessible tutorials and clear guidelines tailored to the field. this tutorial introduces soms to psychologists without technical backgrounds, emphasising practical implementation. we provide evidence-based recommendations for key methodological decisions, accompanied by annotated r code. using a dataset of depressive symptoms as an illustrative case, we present a complete workflow covering data preprocessing, map initialisation, parameter optimisation, and interpretation. we further discuss advanced som extensions relevant to psychological research and highlight key limitations of the method. by making soms accessible, this tutorial supports nuanced, person-centred analyses that preserve the complexity of psychological phenomena. behavior research methods

a signal detection theory approach to quantify contextual effects on perceived signal the perceived value of a sensory stimulus is influenced by its surround. a classic visual example of such contextual effect is simultaneous brightness contrast, where the perceived brightness of a target patch is altered by the luminance of its background. here, we propose a signal detection theory (sdt) based approach to quantify how context parameters bias perception. we develop an extension of sdt in which we formalize contextual effects as either additive or multiplicative gains on the internal representation of a stimulus within a two-alternative forced-choice discrimination task. the model generates clear, testable predictions: additive gains shift the point of subjective equality without altering the slope of the psychometric function, while multiplicative gains affect both its shift and slope. we use this framework to characterize contextual effects in a brightness discrimination experiment where observers compare the brightness of two achromatic patches on different achromatic backgrounds. within the range of luminance conditions tested, the background produced an approximately constant shift of the point of subjective equality, which within our model corresponds to an additive rather than a multiplicative gain. this sdt-based paradigm provides a powerful and generalizable method for quantifying contextual effects in perception. i-perception

effects of concurrent task difficulty and physical effort on memory and perceptual performance and pupil response in younger adults abstract in daily life, cognitively demanding tasks are often performed while simultaneously exerting physical effort, yet the few studies that have examined their combined impact on performance have been limited to the working memory domain. this study systematically examined effects of concurrent task difficulty (easy vs. hard stimulus similarity) and physical effort (low vs. high handgrip) on both behavioral performance and task-evoked pupil response in three cognitive tasks (visual working memory, auditory perception, visual perception) in healthy younger adults. results revealed main effects of task difficulty on performance in all tasks, with participants being less accurate and slower in the hard vs. easy condition, and a main effect of physical effort on performance in the visual perception task, with participants being slower under high relative to low effort. however, there were no interactions between task difficulty and physical effort for any task or performance metric. the pupil response showed only significant main effects of physical effort for all tasks, with larger pupil response during high vs. low effort conditions. individual-level analyses also revealed no significant correlations between these behavioral and pupillary responses. overall, our findings do not support the notion that task difficulty and physical effort draw on common limited-capacity resources or that they similarly impact pupillary arousal, at least for the levels used here in healthy young adults. cognitive research-principles and implications

viewpoint dependence in scene recognition: testing the spatial limits of the reaction time-based concealed information test abstract background the reaction time-based concealed information test (rt-cit) is a highly effective memory detection paradigm that relies on the congruency between a suspect’s internal memory and external test stimuli. while previous research indicates the rt-cit is remarkably resilient to angular deviations when testing isolated objects, its efficacy and boundary conditions for complex, three-dimensional spatial scenes remain unexplored. objective the present study investigated whether the robustness of the rt-cit extends to spatial environments by testing how angular shifts between encoded and tested viewpoints impact memory detection. method participants encoded 10 unique interior scenes (5 targets and 5 probes) from a single viewpoint. during the rt-cit phase, participants were tested on these scenes rendered at five specific angular deviations: 10°, 45°, 90°, 135°, and 170°. results the rt-cit effect (the probe-irrelevant rt difference) remained robust across moderate viewpoint shifts, maintaining significance up to a 125° deviation. the rt-cit effect at the 160° deviation did not reach statistical significance. however, we still observed a small-to-moderate effect size ( d = 0.371), possibly suggesting an attenuated rather than absent effect. furthermore, unlike previous findings with isolated objects, spatial scenes exhibited an immunity to absolute presentation angle effects. the rt-cit effect also maintained high temporal stability across all test epochs. conclusion these findings establish the boundary conditions of the rt-cit: while global layout features provide robust memory anchoring against moderate rotations, extreme perspective inversions possibly attenuate cit efficacy. cognitive research-principles and implications

mixed-neurotype interactions in educational settings and autistic students’ mental health: a systematic review of qualitative findings abstract qualitative studies on social interactions between autistic and non-autistic students (mixed-neurotype interactions) provide rich insights but have limited generalizability. the objective of this review was to review and synthesize qualitative findings on mixed-neurotype interactions and autistic students’ mental health from students’ and teachers’ viewpoints. one hundred and eighteen papers were reviewed, and their findings were thematically analyzed. themes identified: main features (bullying, friendship, loneliness); identity (camouflaging/disclosing autism); support (teachers’ scaffolding, peer interventions); key environments (physical education classes, online interactions, unstructured settings). the most prevalent sub-theme was loneliness. a twofold camouflaging pattern was identified: concealing autism and associated mental health outcomes. support was described to decrease over time. findings flag support reduction, loneliness, and camouflaging as harming autistic students’ mental health. review journal of autism and developmental disorders

using caregiver-implemented structured work system to promote daily living skills for adolescents or young adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities daily living skills (dls) are essential for independence among individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (i/dd), yet many adolescents and young adults have difficulties acquiring such skills. structured work systems (sws), a visual support strategy grounded in behavior analytic principles, have demonstrated effectiveness in promoting independence but are rarely studied when implemented by caregivers. this study evaluated caregiver training to develop and implement a modified sws, focusing exclusively on the modified written work system (i.e., written instructions paired with pictures for complex steps). after the sws development training, caregivers improved their ability to design individualized sws. in experiment 1, a multiple-baseline design showed that caregiver training and on-going coaching increased treatment fidelity, with gains generalizing to the home environment. in experiment 2, individuals with i/dd demonstrated improved independent performance of dls following caregiver implementation of sws, and the improvements were maintained during follow-up probes. social validity ratings indicated high acceptability from both caregivers and individuals with i/dd. findings highlight the modified written sws as a flexible, feasible behavioral intervention that caregivers can use to promote independence in dls within natural settings. behavior modification

religion, memory and the making of resilience: post-secular insights from central and southeast europe this article examines how religious mnemonic repertoires shape divergent forms of collective resilience in contemporary crises. it conceptualizes religion as a reconfigurable mnemonic infrastructure linking past, present and future through narratives, symbols and ritual forms. by introducing a distinction between reproductive and transformative resilience, it explains how memory mobilization can either sustain existing normative and institutional orders, or enable their reinterpretation and reconstitution. drawing on case studies from serbia and poland, it shows how these dynamics are enacted by institutional and vernacular actors across different socio-political settings. at the same time, the analysis highlights overlapping configurations of mnemonic agency, resilience beneficiaries and outcomes, including competing trajectories and interpretative grey zones. memory studies

remembering property dispossession: family resilience after the holocaust in slovakia this study examines how family resilience is negotiated in the context of the dispossession of jewish property in slovakia during and after the holocaust. it asks what creates or disrupts an intergenerational sense of resilience in the family when legal, material, and moral injustices remain unresolved across generations. we do not understand resilience as a completed recovery from trauma, but as an ongoing intergenerational process through which families negotiate the enduring effects of adversity through memory transmission and moral positioning. based on long-term oral history, ethnographic, archival, and autoethnographic research, the article analyses two family cases set against the layered history of jewish property dispossession: from aryanization through postwar restitution and socialist nationalisation to restitution after 1989. the first case follows the descendants of a jewish family whose former property, a manor house, was confiscated, later destroyed by the construction of a reservoir, and reconstructed in an open-air museum. for the family members, the building became a mnemonic anchor for loss, trauma, and interrupted belonging. long-term ethnographic research into family memory and anthropological filmmaking reopened intergenerational communication and enabled symbolic redress, even though legal and material restitution remained impossible. this strengthened family members’ sense of resilience by supporting a narrative of family endurance despite continuing loss and trauma. the second case examines the memory of a non-jewish family whose morally coherent family narrative was disrupted by the discovery that a great-grandfather in the family had aryanised a jewish business. in their intergenerational communication, silence helped to preserve a family identity based on decency, self-making, and continuity. its disruption generated moral uncertainty and revealed the fragility of a sense of family resilience sustained through selective remembering. the article argues that a family’s sense of resilience is reshaped through processes of remembrance, silencing, acknowledgement, and moral positioning. it may be sustained or reconstructed when the past becomes narratable, symbolically acknowledged, and integrated into intergenerational communication and self-understanding. it may be constrained when institutional outcomes deny harm or legitimise contested legacies, or when selective family narratives prevent engagement with troubling knowledge. memory studies

transitional justice and memory agents: confronting the soviet past in kazakhstan in non-democratic settings, ruling leaders often seek to manage historical narratives, while establishing rehabilitation commissions to signal responsiveness to public sentiment. drawing on previously unused archival sources and 27 interviews, this article examines how diverse memory agents, including survivors, descendants of victims of soviet repression, officials, historians, lawyers, and opposition figures, engaged with two such commissions in kazakhstan, active from 1993 to 2006 and from 2020 to 2024. it argues that these commissions function as negotiated arenas in which ruling presidents pursue legitimacy-building, while incorporating memory actors whose bounded participation generates limited but consequential contestation. some actors, whose interests diverge from those of the government, use these processes to insert alternative perspectives into the public record, albeit in marginal ways. the article demonstrates that even in non-democratic contexts, such commissions can produce limited yet meaningful outcomes, creating openings for memory agents to shape official narratives and challenge dominant historical interpretations. memory studies

the emergence of redemptive storytelling during adolescence abstract adolescence is an important time for organizing a complex, relatively stable, and well‐integrated story of one's life. to accomplish this work, adolescents maintain autobiographical narratives. one strategy that adolescents can use in presenting autobiographical narratives involves redemption—approaches for recognizing and confronting past harm and ultimately progressing toward positive resolution in one's life. redemptive storytelling is positively related to well‐being. further, the capacities for redemptive storytelling fully emerge by adolescence. however, there remains less research addressing redemptive storytelling among adolescents. we review the concept of redemption in autobiographical storytelling, argue for the ways redemption should be relevant to the development of adolescents, and provide a call to action for more research in developmental and narrative sciences to consider redemptive storytelling among adolescent populations. social development

smartphone‐based nature noticing intervention for cultivating social connectedness and prosocial behaviour in female adolescents: a mixed methods study abstract a growing body of research indicates that exposure to nature has significant benefits for the health and well‐being of adolescents. however, few studies have assessed the benefits of simple and regular nature‐based activities for adolescents’ social connectedness and prosocial behaviour. this study assessed whether a 10‐week nature‐noticing intervention using a smartphone could improve adolescents’ connection to nature, empathy, social connectedness and prosocial behaviour. the paper utilises a sequential explanatory mixed‐methods design. a total of 127 female students (mean age 15.97; range 15–16 years) were recruited from a hong kong secondary school to participate in this quasi‐experimental study. half of the students ( n = 63) were asked to take pictures of nearby nature and share their thoughts on the group chat twice a week for 10 weeks. the other half of the students ( n = 64), who were not assigned any tasks, served as the control group. all participants were asked to complete a questionnaire containing six validated scales on nature connection, empathy and social well‐being before and after the intervention period. participants who actively shared photos of nearby nature were invited to participate in focus group discussions about their experiences with the nature‐noticing intervention. the 10‐week nature‐noticing intervention had a positive impact on female adolescents’ social connectedness, prosocial behaviour, and empathy. however, there were no significant improvements in self‐esteem. analysing pathways linking nature connectedness to social well‐being, we found that social connectedness and prosocial behaviour are significantly predicted by nature connectedness. regularly sharing nature‐noticing experiences with peers fostered a sense of identity, shared experience, and mutual support. this study provides evidence that a nature‐noticing intervention via photo‐taking and sharing improves students' social connectedness and prosocial behaviour. such integrated engagement with nature may thus serve as a promising pathway for promoting social well‐being in adolescents. social development

behavior and social issues across four decades: citation patterns and interdisciplinary exchange abstract behavior-analytic journals have historically exhibited high levels of self-citation and relatively limited exchange with other scientific disciplines. although bibliometric studies have examined citation patterns in journals such as the journal of applied behavior analysis and the journal of the experimental analysis of behavior , no large-scale investigation has analyzed the references cited in behavior and social issues ( bsi ). this study addresses this gap through a bibliometric analysis of all references cited in bsi between 1978 and 2022. a total of 562 publications and 14,765 references were classified according to research type, disciplinary alignment, authorship, and publication outlet. the results revealed the predominance of theoretical and interpretative publications throughout the journal’s history, as well as strong concentration around a relatively small group of behavior-analytic authors and journals, particularly b. f. skinner and s. s. glenn. at the same time, bsi consistently incorporated references from disciplines such as anthropology, economics, evolutionary biology, political theory, and environmental science. direct journal self-citation represented 7.91% of all references cited in bsi , substantially lower than rates previously reported for several other behavior-analytic journals. taken together, the findings suggest that bsi developed through the combination of a stable behavior-analytic intellectual core and broad interdisciplinary engagement with socially relevant problems, functioning as a comparatively permeable and interdisciplinary outlet within behavior analysis. behavior and social issues

to develop without becoming an individual an approach to the appeal of “collective personal development kits” from erich neumann contemporary individuals increasingly experience generalized disorientation, loss of meaning, and psychological distress—phenomena that empirical research has linked to alienation and meaninglessness. in response, a wide range of cultural, political, spiritual, and pop-psychological proposals have emerged that promise authenticity and development. this article problematizes a paradox at the heart of such proposals: although they claim to foster development, they often culminate in new forms of undifferentiation. the central hypothesis advanced is that these proposals—here termed collective development kits—can be read as deriving their appeal from a uroboric-incestuous dynamic, as conceptualized by erich neumann. drawing on neumann’s account of primordial unity, development, and the symbol of the uroboros, the article argues that these kits simultaneously activate two constitutive yet opposed human inclinations: the drive toward personal development and the temptation to regress into undifferentiated unity. rather than fostering human flourishing and development, they short-circuit its demands and dissolve singularity into pseudo-collective unities. the article proceeds by (i) reconstructing neumann’s theory of primordial unity and symbolic mediation, (ii) analyzing the regressive logic of uroboric incest, and (iii) applying this framework to explain the contemporary appeal and psychological risks of collective development kits. culture & psychology

ideologia mutata: turning points and affective mechanisms of ideological change in migrant intercultural experience drawing on life-story interviews collected in two waves, this study examines how forced migrants in italy narrate ideological change through emotionally significant encounters that alter judgments about dignity, belonging, and freedom. narrative analysis distinguishes corrective, disillusioning, and liberating turning points, tracing how shame and disgust, anger and indignation, and pride, gratitude, and relief become relevant to the reconsideration of ideological commitments. across the illustrative cases, experiences of exclusion, recognition, and care acquire biographical significance as narrators interpret their changing circumstances through shared expectations about moral worth, fairness, and acceptable ways of living. the typology clarifies how these interpretations sustain familiar frameworks, weaken confidence in their promises, or make alternative commitments desirable, situating ideological change within the cultural meanings and relationships through which personal experience is understood. turning points thus provide an analytical lens for examining how emotional experience enters the narrative explanation and justification of continuity and change in belief. culture & psychology

examining the expression and associations of positive and negative urgency across the spectrum of gambling severity abstract despite the well-established relationship between positive and negative urgency and gambling, the research examining how these impulsivity facets are expressed across the full spectrum of this behaviour is currently underdeveloped. as such, the current study sought to investigate the expression of positive and negative urgency across four established levels of gambling severity: non-problem, low-risk, moderately at-risk, and problem gamblers. a total of ( n = 630) gamblers aged between 18 and 73 ( m age = 38.56, sd age = 11.52; 12.6% non-problem gamblers; 29.0% low-risk gamblers; 20.0% moderate-risk problem gamblers and 38.4% problem gamblers) completed an online survey consisting of the short upps-p impulsive behavioural scale (s-upps-p), problem gambling severity index (pgsi) and short-marlowe-crowne social desirability scale (s-mcsds). one-way anova results showed that problem gamblers scored significantly higher on positive and negative urgency than the remaining three gambling groups. while controlling for age and social desirability, multinomial logistic regression revealed that elevated positive and negative urgency were associated with higher odds of membership in moderate-risk and problem gambling groups relative to non-problem gamblers, while only positive urgency was associated with low-risk group membership. findings support existing literature by highlighting the important role of both urgency facets across different levels of gambling severity, with positive urgency appearing to be particularly salient in low-risk gamblers. clinicians may use findings to gain a more precise understanding of the emotional correlates linked to an individual’s gambling, potentially informing future research on emotion-focused mechanisms in gambling interventions. discover psychology

the transpersonal worldview of fr. jaime c. bulatao (1922–2015): contributions to transpersonal psychology from the philippine experience jaime c. bulatao was a filipino jesuit priest who founded the psychology department of the ateneo de manila university and cofounded the psychological association of the philippines. he was known for his approach to clinical psychology that involved treating folk ailments using traditional healing techniques. despite his behaviorist training, bulatao prioritized the deeply personal and highly transpersonal aspects of human well-being. this paper explores bulatao’s transpersonal worldview, and what this may contribute to the flourishing of transpersonal psychology as a whole. in particular, it looks at his theory of transpersonal personhood, as well as his unique yet pragmatic approach to dealing with spiritual emergencies. journal of humanistic psychology

perfectionism predicting career adaptability: strengths use and deficit correction as behavioral mediators career adaptability is becoming more important for university students navigating increasingly uncertain career environments. drawing on career construction theory (cct), this study examined how perfectionistic strivings (standards) and perfectionistic concerns (discrepancy), as indicators of trait-like adaptivity, relate to career adaptability among 407 undergraduates in south korea. the study further investigated strengths use and deficit correction as proactive behaviors mediating these relationships. structural equation modeling revealed that standards positively predicted career adaptability, whereas discrepancy negatively predicted career adaptability. strengths use and deficit correction mediated these paths, with the indirect effect of discrepancy via deficit correction significant only among female students. by identifying behavioral mediators, this study contributes to understanding how indicators of adaptivity are translated into career adaptability within the cct framework. journal of career development

explaining the decline of impal marriage among the karo: an epidemiological approach abstract the karo people of north sumatra, indonesia, have long expressed a preference for matrilateral cross-cousin ( impal ) marriage, yet the practice has declined sharply over the past century. to identify the demographic and socio-cultural factors underlying this change, we applied an epidemiological approach to cultural evolution, using a case–control design coupled with structural equation modelling. ethnographic data from 176 married individuals across 62 villages were analysed to assess the effects of demographic, alliance, religious, cosocialisation, and modernisation variables on the likelihood of impal marriage. the model fit was strong (comparative fit index = 0.96, root mean square error of approximation = 0.04), revealing significant direct and indirect effects. marrying an impal was positively associated with the number of marriageable impal and with arranged or strategically motivated unions, but negatively associated with reported religious conflict between spouses. indicators of modernisation such as schooling and infrastructure were non-significant. these results indicate that the decline of impal marriage likely reflects demographic contraction and the weakening of alliance-based strategies rather than a rejection of the cultural norm itself. framed within an epidemiological approach to cultural evolution, the findings illustrate how ecological and demographic change may contribute to the decline of culturally-prescribed social practices, even where aspects of the underlying cultural ideal persist. evolutionary human sciences

a decision-making framework for neuromodulation modalities in psychiatric disorders nature mental health, published online: 12 november 2026; doi:10.1038/s44220-026-00758-7 the evolution of psychiatric neuromodulation aims to precisely modulate dysfunctional brain circuits for therapeutic benefit yet lacks direct comparative trials and consensus criteria. this perspective presents evidence that neuromodulation tools engage shared neural networks, proposing an evidence-based framework for optimizing circuit-based therapies and shaping future mental health care. nature mental health

alcohol and other drug use, psychological distress, and occupational functioning in australian public safety personnel purpose this study aims to examine rates of severity of alcohol and other drug (aod) use risk and psychological distress and their association with occupational functioning (absenteeism and presenteeism) among australian public safety personnel (psp). design/methodology/approach an online self-assessment of aod use risk was completed by 238 psp between march 2024 and march 2025 as part of a pilot implementation trial of a psp-tailored aod use intervention. this study analysed cross-sectional baseline data from that trial. rates and severity of aod use risk (alcohol, smoking and substance involvement screening test) and psychological distress (k10+) were examined and a series of hurdle negative binomial regressions were used to examine their associations with absenteeism and presenteeism. findings moderate-to-high levels of alcohol use risk, other drug use risk and psychological distress were prevalent in the sample. higher alcohol use risk [odds ratio (or) = 1.03], other drug use risk (or = 1.09) and psychological distress (or = 1.14) were associated with increased odds of absenteeism. however, only psychological distress was associated with the frequency of absenteeism [incidence rate ratios (irr) = 1.10]. for presenteeism, psychological distress was associated with both increased odds (or = 1.11) and frequency (irr = 1.06). other drug use risk was associated with increased odds of presenteeism, particularly at lower levels of psychological distress. neither alcohol nor other drug use risk was significantly associated with the frequency of presenteeism. originality/value findings show that psychological distress is the most consistent correlate of occupational impairment, while aod use risk is associated with occupational impairment in ways that differ across contexts and substance classes. advances in dual diagnosis

two roads to competence? how cognitive and affective individual differences reach applied performance by different routes individual differences predict applied competence, but the routes by which they do so are rarely modelled. drawing on investment and aptitude theory for cognitive resources and on appraisal theory for affective orientations, we propose an appraisal-correspondence principle: the closer an individual-difference variable stands to the outcome in its level of self-appraisal, the more directly it should act; the further away it is, the more mediation should be required. we tested the principle on pre-service teachers’ competence to teach with generative artificial intelligence (ai-tpack), using a latent-variable model on cross-sectional data from 164 pre-service primary-school teachers in türkiye. ai readiness (cognitive) and ai competence anxiety (affective) served as antecedents and generative ai literacy and ai self-efficacy as mediators. fit was good, χ2(139) = 181.44, cfi = 0.978, tli = 0.973, rmsea = 0.045, and srmr = 0.061, with 45.8% of ai-tpack variance explained. readiness produced a strong total effect (β = 0.600, 95% ci [0.444, 0.738]), half of it indirect; model comparison indicated that generative ai literacy, rather than self-efficacy, carries the mediated share, although the literacy → ai-tpack path itself was only partially supported. competence anxiety predicted neither mediator, and its direct path to ai-tpack was small (β = −0.105, ci [−0.266, 0.059]) and not significant in any of 16 pre-specified data-handling variants. the cognitive road is robust; the affective road, as predicted by the principle, bypasses the mediators but leaves only a faint and uncertain trace. full scalar invariance held across year of study and use frequency. we state the principle as a hypothesis for performance-based tests rather than as an established mechanism. journal of intelligence

psychometric properties of the spanish version of the university student stressors questionnaire (ussq): structure, reliability, validity, and measurement invariance the scarcity of psychometrically robust instruments limits the assessment of academic stressors among spanish university students. this study aimed to adapt the university student stressors questionnaire (ussq) to the spanish context and evaluate its psychometric properties in a sample of undergraduate and postgraduate students. an instrumental, cross-sectional census survey design was used to evaluate the psychometric properties of the instrument. a total of 4925 students from a spanish public university participated. exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, measurement invariance analyses (by sex, gender, and study level), and convergent validity analyses with measures of depression, anxiety, and stress (dass-21) and psychological well-being (ryff’s pwb) were conducted. the final 27-item, seven-factor model demonstrated optimal fit and adequate reliability (mcdonald’s omega: 0.73–0.89). partial measurement invariance was achieved for sex and gender, and full invariance for study level. convergent validity was supported through positive correlations with psychological distress and negative correlations with well-being. the university student stressors questionnaire (ussq) is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing academic stressors in the spanish university population. “fear of failure” emerges as the most prominent factor associated with psychological distress. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

prevalence of anorexia nervosa in population-based studies: a systematic review and meta-analysis background: reported prevalence of anorexia nervosa (an) varies across populations, diagnostic systems, and reference periods. methods: a systematic review of population-based prevalence studies was conducted using pubmed, embase, scopus, web of science, psycinfo, lilacs, and scielo. methodological quality was assessed using the nine-domain joanna briggs institute checklist. compatible adult and adolescent survey estimates were synthesized using random-effects inverse-variance meta-analysis with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and modified hartung–knapp confidence intervals. results: a total of 21,316 records were identified, of which 105 reports met the eligibility criteria. five publications provided data for four meta-analyses stratified by age group, diagnostic criteria, and prevalence period. among adults, pooled lifetime prevalence was 0.34% (95% ci < 0.01–43.67%; k = 2) based on dsm-iv criteria and 0.48% (95% ci 0.09–2.44%; k = 3) when a dsm-5 estimate was included. among adolescents, pooled lifetime prevalence was 0.39% (95% ci 0.01–9.18%; k = 2), whereas 12-month prevalence was 0.19% (95% ci 0.01–4.05%; k = 2). conclusions: although the pooled point estimates were low, their substantial uncertainty limits generalization. more consistent ascertainment and reporting of survey-specific precision are needed to improve comparisons across populations. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

ratings of musical hooks in unfamiliar pop music are influenced by repetition and distraction popular music’s widespread appeal has often been attributed to its use of ‘hooks’ – musical or lyrical phrases that are salient and easily remembered. this paper reports two experiments examining the role of attention and familiarity in shaping judgements of the salience and memorability of unfamiliar pop music. in experiment 1, participants listened to unfamiliar pop songs either once or five times, while either attending to the music or completing sudoku puzzles, before using continuous self-report (csr) to rate the salience and memorability of the full song. the results found that participants more familiar with the song after repeated listening rated it more highly, but that sudoku puzzles were not significantly distracting enough to affect ratings. experiment 2 largely replicated experiment 1, except with a verbal task as distraction, and involved providing post-listening ratings of song excerpts. findings suggest that familiarity led to higher ratings of the excerpts, while attentional distraction led to lower ratings. collectively, these results indicate that both attention and familiarity contribute to the cognitive processing of hooks in popular music. this research suggests that self-report ratings are an effective tool for psychologically investigating hooks and provide a foundation for future research on how they may influence the experience of earworms. psychology of music

distributed bias: a distributed cognition approach to the emergence of institutional bias academic abstract prejudice and discrimination operate at individual and systemic levels, yet much remains unknown about how bias transcends from the individual to shape the behaviors and cognitions of social systems. distributed cognition theory offers a needed perspective in this gap, positing that cognition is not confined to individual minds, but rather is distributed across individuals and environments throughout time. as such, system-level outcomes are not directly predictable from the cognitive properties of individuals but instead emerge from interactions of individuals with one another and with their environments. here, a distributed bias approach is proposed, such that individuals within institutions and broader social systems interact with each other and the complex array of tools in their environments, transforming the cognitive processes involved in group-based discrimination, consequently propagating systemic institutional bias. this approach offers a new mechanistic foundation for the emergence of institutional bias and proposes several avenues for future research and application. public abstract social prejudices and acts of discrimination are typically considered to exist within individual hearts and minds. however, these attitudes and practices are also woven into the neighborhoods where we live, the organizations that employ us, and the schools in which our children learn. they color the fabric of society itself. how does personal bias grow into something larger, shaping entire institutions and social systems? this work proposes that prejudice emerges not only from the minds of individuals, but also from people interacting with each other and the structures around them. the proposed perspective helps explain why bias on this higher level persists even when some individuals may not intend harm. by understanding these hidden mechanisms, we can better identify ways to interrupt bias at these different levels, creating more equitable policies and social institutions. personality and social psychology review
women’s political representation and intimate partner violence: evidence from 28 low- and middle-income countries journal of family violence

optimal linear combinations from multidimensional behavioral measuring instruments: can we obtain the best from the whole and from its parts? 多维行为测量工具的最优线性组合：能否从整体及其各部分获得最优结果？ a covariance structure analysis procedure is outlined that can be used for estimating optimal linear combinations of the components of behavioral scales measuring two or more underlying dimensions evaluated by corresponding subscales. the method provides a set of optimal weights for the linear combination of all scale components that possesses highest reliability, and a set of such weights with respect to each subscale. the approach is relevant when for validity and construct representation reasons researchers decide to use complex structure measuring instruments and are substantively interested in subject performance on the overall scale as well as on each of the subscales. the procedure is readily applied with freely available software and is illustrated on multidimensional scale data. educational and psychological measurement

construct overlap between two widely used self-report measures of dispositional mindfulness: evidence from stress and anxiety control outcomes. researchers commonly conceptualise dispositional mindfulness as a multidimensional construct comprising attentional awareness, present-moment focus, and acceptance. however, widely used measures differ considerably in the dimensions they assess, raising questions regarding the extent to which they demonstrate construct overlap and can be considered interchangeable. the present study evaluated the psychometric functioning, construct overlap, and associations of the mindful attention awareness scale (maas) and the freiburg mindfulness inventory (fmi) with stress and anxiety control outcomes. a community sample of 1,498 uk adults completed the maas, fmi, perceived stress scale, and anxiety control questionnaire. confirmatory factor analysis (cfa), exploratory structural equation modelling (esem), rasch analysis, and structural equation modelling (sem) evaluated measurement properties and examined associations with stress and anxiety control outcomes. esem provided superior fit relative to cfa for multidimensional measures, while rasch analyses indicated satisfactory measurement functioning across mindfulness measures. contrary to expectations, despite satisfactory psychometric performance, the maas demonstrated near-zero correlations with the fmi total score and its presence and acceptance facets, indicating that these measures were essentially independent in this sample rather than showing substantial dimensional overlap. structural models further revealed distinct patterns of association, with acceptance showing the strongest relationships with coping and emotion control, whereas mindfulness awareness displayed the strongest associations with threat control and stress control. findings are consistent with multidimensional conceptualisations of mindfulness and demonstrate negligible convergence between the maas and fmi, indicating that researchers should not assume that these instruments are interchangeable. more broadly, the findings highlight the importance of empirically evaluating construct overlap when selecting scales intended to assess the same psychological construct. psychological reports

the unity and diversity of social cognition subdomains in adults: a latent variable analysis. social cognition has been postulated to comprise three subdomains: perception, understanding, and regulation. however, empirical research into the factor structure of social cognition is limited. this hampers theoretical understanding and the development of sensitive neuropsychological measures for clinical application. the primary objective of the present study was to examine the extent to which the three postulated social cognition subdomains are unified or distinct based on currently available measures. in this cross-sectional study, 201 healthy adults (mean age = 43.4 years, sd = 18.9) completed up to 10 social cognition measures. the structure of social cognition was investigated by fitting six confirmatory factor analysis models that assumed varying degrees of unity. model comparisons revealed that a two-factor model distinguishing perception and a combined understanding-regulation factor fitted the data best relative to model complexity. the secondary objective was to examine the contributions of the observed factors to performance on a serious game designed to measure theory of mind. in a subsample (n = 68), four latent regression path models were fitted. the model with a single path from the combined understanding-regulation factor to the serious game provided the best fit relative to model complexity. the primary findings suggest that social cognition comprises at least two highly related yet partially distinct subdomains. these findings are consistent with a distinct perception subdomain, but indicate that the assigned measures did not form a distinct regulation factor, which may reflect measurement limitations, the breadth of the regulation construct, or regulation not being a separable subdomain. acta psychologica

intelligence as a powerful catalyst of job performance: evidence from highly educated workers this investigation tested the hypothesis that psychometric intelligence, as measured by iq tests, is relevant for job performance in brazil, particularly for more skilled occupations. thus, a hypothetical-deductive, cross- sectional study was conducted among 134 brazilian adult workers with a higher education degree or higher, using brief measures of iq, personality, and leadership traits, as well as a sociodemographic and work-life questionnaire. statistical analyses using the canonic test, spearman’s correlation, and logit regression indicated that intelligence was positively correlated with self-rated job performance (rho = .17), with individuals scoring 111+ showing a substantially higher likelihood of above-par performance in more qualified positions (71.7% vs. 41.7%). at this higher level of intelligence, duration of employment also showed stronger associations with job position (rho = .40 vs. .08) and income (rho = .53 vs. .40). after controlling for personality, workload, and quality of working life, iq remained the strongest independent predictor of above-par performance (or = 8.774). overall, the findings suggest that, among workers with higher education, intelligence constitutes a highly significant and independent component of workplace performance and occupational success. acta colombiana de psicologia

detecting therapist burnout and flourishing from brief speech: a machine‐learning approach abstract background burnout is pervasive among therapists and is associated with impaired well‐being and reduced clinical effectiveness. although flourishing and character strengths may function as protective factors, intervention implementation is limited by a lack of feasible, scalable methods for monitoring therapist well‐being. machine‐learning (ml) approaches may be suited to address these limitations. aims this proof‐of‐concept study examined the use of a transformer‐based natural language processing (nlp) model to detect therapist burnout, flourishing, mental health continuum, employee engagement and character strengths (humility, gratitude and forgiveness) from automatically transcribed therapists' verbal responses. materials and methods participants ( n = 365) included licensed and training therapists, who completed self‐report measures of burnout, flourishing, mental health continuum, employee engagement and character strengths (humility, gratitude and forgiveness). a transformer‐based roberta model was trained, tuned and evaluated using separate training, validation and test sets, with performance assessed using spearman rank correlations with permutation tests. results moderate correlations were observed for burnout ( ρ = 0.456), mental health continuum ( ρ = 0.46) and flourishing ( ρ = 0.387). discussion these findings suggest that transformer‐based nlp models might be able to detect therapist burnout, flourishing and some positive functioning indicators relevant to organisational well‐being models. limitations include the relatively small and potentially unrepresentative cross‐sectional sample, possible transcription and prompt‐related measurement error, and the absence of external validation, warranting cautious interpretation of these findings as preliminary evidence of feasibility rather than as definitive estimates of detection performance. research should also examine ethical concerns related to privacy, bias, misclassification and potential misuse. conclusion this study provides preliminary evidence supporting the use of transformer‐based nlp models for the detection of therapist burnout, flourishing and other positive functioning indicators. counselling & psychotherapy research

taming the groove: an experienced professional drummer’s use of goal setting for the enhancement of neglected performance skills the aim of this theory-driven single case study was to investigate the role of goal setting in a professional drummer’s deliberate practice routines. despite extensive research on goal setting within performance psychology, its application to performance science and professional music practice remains limited. there is a clear need for more research on how well-established expert musicians continue to develop their skills. across two 30-day action cycles, the drummer set hierarchical performance goals to strengthen identified weaknesses – most notably left foot control, speed and fluency in groove and improvisation excerpts – which had been deliberately neglected in earlier practice. the two cycles were systematically planned, executed and analysed through the lens of goal-setting theory and principles of self-regulated learning. continuous feedback from the drummer himself, an expert mentor and selected practice tools (e.g., journal, video recordings and central drumming literature) informed ongoing adjustments of goal difficulty and specificity. findings indicated that continuous self-monitoring, expert guidance and feedback-driven goal setting helped the drummer identify relevant areas for improvement, supporting higher-quality practice, persistence and the refinement of technical aspects of drumming. importantly, the study demonstrates that a well-established professional musician was able to target and overcome long-standing weaknesses, even at advanced stages of expertise, through deliberate goal-oriented practice. the findings provide examples of how the combination of domain-specific didactical knowledge and strategic planning can facilitate growth, motivation and technical renewal in a middle-aged professional drummer. musicae scientiae

‘heroes, taking one for the team, rule britannia’: supporting racist riots in online discussions abstract this study addresses online responses to the riots that followed the southport murders in the united kingdom in summer 2024. these riots occurred in a context of anti‐migrant and anti‐muslim sentiment in the united kingdom. while the riots were widely condemned, this analysis focuses on online debates and in particular those that praised people involved in the riots. to do this, the study drew on online user comments following two news articles on the daily mail website (sampled from 1 august 2024 to 15 august 2024, on the daily mail website and via google, totalling 847 unique comments) and analysed them using critical discursive psychology. the analysis identified three main arguments that were used in support of the riots: (1) (un)fairness in justice, (2) debating whether migrants are not wanted and (3) presenting rioters as heroes. it is shown how these arguments could justify and even glorify the riots despite their violent and racist undertones. journal of community & applied social psychology

guardians of the past: presidents and memory in el salvador and colombia this study provides an analysis of presidential discourses, both domestic and international, that support or oppose transitional justice and historical memory in el salvador and colombia. its aim is to explore how narratives of past conflicts and peace agreements are embedded within elite discourse. through political discourses, we examine how populism shapes historical memory, assessing its influence on accountability efforts. the corpus consists of 16 key texts delivered by the presidents of both countries between 2014 and 2024. these texts span various contexts, including commemorative speeches, election victory addresses and legislative assembly speeches. this research highlights the distinct challenges each country faces in relation to memory, shedding light on the complexities of transitional justice processes. in el salvador, the analysis reveals a populist reinterpretation of history, while in colombia, recent presidents appear more focused on rhetorically framing peace than on addressing victims’ needs. memory studies
the effect of social norms and model types on young chinese children’s helping decisions early child development and care

beyond symptom severity: prognostic information from subjective person‐specific problem networks in young people abstract background person‐specific network models are increasingly proposed to support personalized assessment and psychotherapy, but it remains unclear whether the information they contain is prospectively informative in young people. we tested whether characteristics derived from a brief perceived causal network (pecan), particularly its perceived relational structure, provided prognostic information about subsequent psychopathology beyond baseline symptom severity. methods participants were 361 children, adolescents, and young adults assessed by self‐report or parent‐report. at baseline, participants selected personally relevant problems, rated their severity, and indicated how they perceived these problems to be related. psychopathology was assessed with the pediatric symptom checklist (psc‐d) at baseline and approximately 4, 8, and 12 weeks later. linear mixed‐effects models examined prospective associations of pecan characteristics with psychopathology. exploratory post hoc analyses additionally examined problem breadth, defined as the number of personally relevant problems selected. results global characteristics of perceived problem relations showed little consistent incremental prognostic information beyond baseline psychopathology and problem breadth. mean perceived causal strength and maximum normalized weighted outdegree were not associated with subsequent psychopathology, while an inverse association with network density emerged only in self‐report and was not robust across sensitivity analyses. in exploratory analyses, greater problem breadth was associated with higher subsequent psychopathology in both self‐report and parent‐report, and these associations remained essentially unchanged after adjustment for conventional psc‐d symptom breadth. conclusion the first prospective evaluation of pecans provided limited support for incremental prognostic information contained in global perceived relational characteristics. exploratory analyses nevertheless identified problem breadth as a potentially informative compositional characteristic of personalized problem representations. these findings suggest that different components of person‐specific models should be evaluated separately and highlight the need for confirmatory replication before they inform personalized clinical decisions. jcpp advances

ecological assessment of executive functions and reasoning in colombian children: cross-validation and measurement invariance of the spanish core-6/10. ecological assessment of executive function (ef) in children relies heavily on informant-report instruments that rarely include logical-abstract reasoning, while culturally grounded measures developed originally in spanish for latin american populations remain scarce. this study examined the psychometric structure, internal cross-validation, and measurement invariance of the core-6/10, a spanish-language informant-report instrument for children aged 6-10 years assessing five executive domains and two naturalistic reasoning dimensions: verbal-logical and perceptual-analytical reasoning. validation used non-overlapping calibration and confirmation subsamples ( = 391; efa: = 195; cfa: = 196), polychoric matrices, parallel analysis, uls oblimin efa, and wlsmv cfa; invariance was tested across sex, age, and informant type. the seven correlated-factor model was retained as the best-fitting admissible solution (cfi = .940, tli = .935, rmsea = .049, srmr = .081). an exploratory bifactor analysis suggested substantial general-factor saturation (ωh = .71; ecv = .50), although estimation anomalies precluded treating it as a primary confirmatory model. internal consistency was adequate (ordinal α = .76-.87), with change-based evidence consistent with approximate scalar invariance across comparisons (|δcfi| ≤.005). reasoning dimensions showed general-factor loadings (.476-.735) comparable to core ef domains, suggesting shared variance with general executive functioning while retaining domain-specific variance. findings support the empirical relevance of reasoning within this ecological measurement framework and the core-6/10 as a promising culturally grounded instrument for research in colombian children, with potential future applications in school-based screening pending independent replication, multimethod validation, normative development, and evidence of classification accuracy. child neuropsychology
direction in person-centered psychotherapy person-centered and experiential psychotherapies

parental bonding and the recognition and preference for one's own child's body odour previous research has shown that parents can recognise and positively evaluate their infant's odour, but the extent to which these processes relate to individual differences in bonding remains unclear. addressing this gap, we examined whether parent-reported bonding difficulties are associated with odour recognition accuracy and hedonic evaluation of a child's body odour. a sample of 86 parent–child dyads (children aged 3 months to 3 years) participated in a body odour assessment paradigm. bonding was measured using the postpartum bonding questionnaire (pbq). odour identification involved selecting the child's odour from six samples, including the child's own odour, four odours from other children and a blank sample. pleasantness was rated for each sample on a visual analogue scale ranging from 0 to 100. logistic and linear regression analyses were conducted, controlling for parent sex, parent age and child age. higher pbq scores, indicating greater parent-reported bonding difficulties, were associated with a higher likelihood of correctly identifying the child's odour, and this effect remained significant after controlling for other covariates. in contrast, bonding difficulties were not associated with the child's body odour pleasantness ratings. these findings suggest that parental olfactory processing comprises at least two partially dissociable components: offspring recognition and hedonic evaluation, which may serve distinct functions in parent–child relationships. evolutionary psychology
sexuality, gender, and the transformative potential of ayahuasca: a naturalistic inquiry psychology & sexuality

infants generate structured sequences during self‐directed object exploration abstract whilst decades of carefully‐controlled developmental research have told us much about the myriad variables that affect infants' early cognitive development, the relationship between infants' real‐world, self‐directed interaction and their learning is poorly understood. one theoretical account of such organization comes from computational work on curiosity‐driven learning. previous literature predicted that when engaged in curiosity‐driven exploration, infants should impose structure on their learning environment, with this systematicity unfolding dynamically as infants move from stimulus to stimulus, generating an intermediate level of task complexity. this prediction motivated the present investigation of whether infants' self‐directed object exploration exhibits comparable sequential organization. we tested this prediction in a free play task where we quantified infants' active tactile object selections as a window into their self‐generated learning curriculum. twelve‐, 18‐ and 24‐month‐old children ( n = 53) were allowed to freely play with three novel object categories, across six trials (two per category). exemplars in each category were drawn from continua in which neighbouring objects varied systematically in similarity, enabling us to quantify sequence complexity in terms of similarity relationships between sequentially touched objects. infants were first presented with a prime object drawn from one extreme of the continuum, followed by the remaining four objects presented together. analyses of infants' first touches following removal of the prime demonstrated a systematic preference for the perceptually most distant object; however, this preference depended on prime identity and stimulus set. cluster analysis of touch sequences further suggested that infants generated systematic sequences of overall intermediate complexity. convergent with the computational predictions, this work demonstrates for the first time that when engaged in free interaction with the physical environment, infants are neither passive learners nor random explorers; rather, they are capable of directing their own timetable for learning by imposing structure on their physical sampling of the environment. infant and child development

are digital health interventions acceptable and effective at improving medication adherence in paediatric patients with asthma? a mixed-mode systematic review, narrative synthesis, and behavioural analysis health psychology and behavioral medicine

play and games as artistic reflections: an essay on childhood transformation in cultural-historical psychology through the anthropomorphizing reflection this article argues that children’s play and games constitute an anthropomorphizing artistic reflection, whose developmental power resides in their rules as a dialectical unit. drawing on vygotsky’s psychology and lukács’s marxist aesthetics, we address a gap in cultural-historical psychology: the artistic role of play and its implications for development. as a first step in exploring this marxist aesthetic field, we demonstrate how play evolves into essentially artistic behavior. we present a genetic analysis of this behavior, showing how play, understood as a reflection, gains autonomy from everyday life and thereby becomes a source of development—creating social situations of development through the very process of disentangling rules. by analyzing rules as play’s dialectical unit, we demonstrate how they engender these social situations and potentiate zones of proximal development. we argue that the ‘cathartic’ resolution of contradictions within play—a micro-genesis of perezhivanie —is fundamental for internalizing social meanings and developing higher psychological functions. thus, this study not only bridges vygotsky and lukács but reframes play as a core psychological mechanism through which artistic, anthropomorphizing reflection drives subjective development in childhood. culture & psychology

representing a future with unconditional basic income: capitalist realism and the social construction of (un)feasibility amid deteriorating labour market conditions and increasing income insecurity, unconditional basic income (ubi) has been a widely debated proposal for guaranteeing a dignified future for all. yet, in a context of pervasive capitalist realism, perceptions of ubi’s unfeasibility constitute a major barrier to its political realisation. while central to public debate, previous literature has paid little attention to how such perceptions are socially constructed. drawing on integrative frameworks combining social representations theory on collective futures with the pragmatic sociology of engagements, this study examines how people reason and argue about the future, and how this shapes the social construction of ubi’s (un)feasibility. based on a pragmatic discourse analysis of 26 interviews conducted in the basque country, we identified three main representations of the future: (1) the collapse scenario, (2) the strategic planning scenario, and (3) the realisable utopia scenario. within each representation, participants proleptically mobilised distinct images of the past, as well as different modes of engaging with the future, to advance specific political objectives concerning the implementation of ubi. we discuss the implications for understanding how collective futures are socially represented and engaged with, offering insights for resisting the imaginative constraints of capitalist realism. culture & psychology

i will not give you a straight answer: context-dependent protective effects of ambiguous responses / no voy a responder de forma directa: efectos protectores de las respuestas ambiguas en función del contexto previous research has shown that people providing ambiguous responses to questions are seen as less likable than those who provide responses that are specific or precise. however, the present research, comprising six studies involving chinese samples ( n = 1,842), demonstrates that ambiguous responses can yield more favorable outcomes than absolute denial in certain contexts. specifically, compared with outright denial, ambiguous responses elicited less negative moral evaluations and higher support intentions, suggesting a positive protective effect that helps individuals maintain their moral reputation while managing sensitive information. moreover, this protective effect was consistently observed across both student and employee samples. however, we also identified contextual boundaries: ambiguous responses lost their protective advantage in pre-election contexts, when one’s plans were known in advance, and in competitive situations. under these conditions, ambiguity was perceived to be as hypocritical as absolute denial. this research deepens our understanding of the social perception of honesty and helps explain the persistence of ambiguous responses in everyday social communication. future cross-cultural research is needed to examine the generalizability of these findings. international journal of social psychology

development and validation of the japanese version of the adhd stigma questionnaire ( asq ‐j): cultural adaptation and psychometric properties in japan abstract this study aimed to develop a japanese version of the adhd stigma questionnaire (asq‐j) and examine its reliability and validity. we surveyed 248 individuals aged 18 years and older (117 diagnosed with adhd and 131 without adhd). the results of a confirmatory factor analysis supported a three‐factor structure comprising 26 items: “disclosure concern,” “negative self‐image,” and “concern with public attitudes,” with acceptable fit indices. the asq‐j demonstrated good internal consistency, test–retest reliability, and construct validity. although partial support for construct validity was observed through associations with self‐esteem, further research is needed to confirm the construct validity more comprehensively. future studies should increase the sample size and include a broader age range—particularly younger individuals—to reassess the scale's reliability and validity, including its construct validity. japanese psychological research

psychotherapism: an analytical tool for a political and epistemological critique of the psychotherapy apparatus the article critically examines psychotherapy’s sociopolitical role through the concept of psychotherapism , seen as both an analytical tool and a set of effects related to the expansion of the psychotherapy apparatus . drawing on castel’s psychoanalysm, critical theory, and liberation psychology, it identifies four main, though non-exhaustive, iatrogenic outcomes: clinical harm, social stratification, symbolic individualization, and erosion of collective bonds. the analysis exposes psychotherapy’s alignment with neoliberal governance and challenges its presumed neutrality. it advocates for a decolonial, justice-oriented praxis that reclaims non-commodified, community-based care. journal of humanistic psychology

disrupting cisheteronormativity: recovering historical memory in service of liberation psychology this conceptual article examines cisheteronormativity as a structural organizing logic through which colonialism, white supremacy, and capitalism have historically regulated sex, gender, sexuality, kinship, and psychological life. drawing on liberation psychology as both a framework and method, the article brings queer theory, indigenous feminist scholarship, black feminist thought, and related critical traditions into dialogue to recover the historical conditions through which contemporary sexual and gender norms became institutionalized and came to appear natural. this genealogy traces how these systems operate through colonial governance, racialized constructions of gender and sexuality, patriarchal sexual scripts, cultural representation, and psychological knowledge and classification. the article concludes by considering implications for critical reflexivity, clinical practice, graduate education, and institutional transformation. recovering the historical and structural organization of sexuality expands the knowledge available to psychology for understanding psychological suffering and human flourishing in service of developing a praxis oriented toward liberation. journal of humanistic psychology
childhood victimization, cognitive distortions, and denial among men who have sexually offended against minors journal of child sexual abuse

next-gen futures cultivated through positive youth development: a narrative review of challenges and opportunities amid rapid social changes today’s youth live in a rapidly changing, global, and digital world characterized by climate change, social inequality, and social polarization. such issues can both trigger their civic engagement and undermine their mental health. in the present paper, we discuss the need for a contemporary positive youth development (pyd) framework that would live up to its theoretical roots in the relational developmental systems (rds) theory and adequately consider the challenges and opportunities of today’s youth. based on expert discussions by the cross-national positive youth development network, the following social change indicators were identified as most pressing: (i) digitalization, (ii) inequality and marginalization, (iii) polarization and radicalization, and (iv) climate change. applying a critical narrative review, we assess the current research trends in youth development and suggest a way forward regarding how the pyd framework can accommodate the challenges and opportunities of today’s youth. specifically, we suggest adding a social justice lens more explicitly to the current framework, while considering digital context and natural environment as two additional interactive layers of contextual influences. lastly, we support the inclusion of critical consciousness as a new c in the pyd framework to expand our understanding of the different forms of (non)contribution among today’s youth. review of general psychology

associations between self-identity, romantic relationship quality, and mental well-being among sexual minorities in china cogent psychology

the minority privilege: how male psychologists perceive their gender in the therapeutic encounter the demographic profile of psychology in south africa has undergone a conspicuous shift, with men now accounting for only one-fifth of registered psychologists. although existing research has shown that men often benefit from gendered advantage in female-saturated professions, this work has largely focused on career trajectories rather than on therapeutic practice. similarly, research on gender in psychotherapy has predominantly examined clients’ perceptions of the therapist’s gender, leaving male psychologists’ own understandings largely unexplored. situated within a social constructionist paradigm, this qualitative study examined how six male psychologists perceived their maleness in the therapeutic encounter. we conducted semi-structured interviews, which were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. in this article, we explore shared maleness as a therapeutic resource, with two related facets: (a) relatability and the ‘powerful position’, in which participants construed their gender as conferring both standing with clients and ease of engagement with men and (b) modelling a different kind of man, in which they positioned themselves as offering male clients an alternative form of masculinity. these findings extend the concept of minority privilege beyond occupational advantage, suggesting that masculine privilege may also operate relationally within therapeutic practice. the study highlights the importance of reflexive supervision in helping male psychologists critically examine how gender shapes therapeutic processes and outcomes. south african journal of psychology

a moderation examination of the effects of a mindfulness-based intervention on primary school students’ symptoms of inattention, depression, and anxiety abstract the number of mindfulness-based interventions (mbis) has proliferated in the last decade, as accessible evidence-based practices, to improve children’s mental health in school settings. however, some studies suggest that mbis do not offer distinct advantages over other mental health promotion interventions. these inconsistent findings may be explained, at least in part, by the lack of a clear definition of what constitutes a mbi, inconsistencies in intervention length and facilitator training, and importantly, the limited examination of moderating variables––particularly dispositional mindfulness, emotional regulation, and social competence––that may influence intervention effectiveness and mental health outcomes (inattention, anxiety, and depression). the present study was therefore interested in the potential benefits associated with a case of this type of intervention and aimed to explore whether dispositional (i.e., trait) mindfulness and mental health indicators evolved over time in primary school children. a secondary objective meant to evaluate whether receiving a mbi could moderate the relationship between changes in mindfulness and changes in mental health indicators. contrary to our hypothesis, results showed that mindfulness levels were linked with indicators of mental health. specifically, changes in mindfulness were associated with increases in inattention, anxiety and depression using structural equation modelling. moreover, the association between changes in mindfulness and inattention differed by intervention group, with greater increases in mindfulness associated with greater increases in inattention in the control group but not in the intervention group. results thus lend support to exercising caution when aiming to only foster mindfulness abilities, without ensuring that children also learn the emotion regulation skills that are required to deal with the increased awareness of their difficulties. clinicaltrials.gov trial registration number nct06346002; trial registration date: april 3rd, 2024. discover mental health

feasibility, acceptance, user satisfaction, and differences between users and non-users of an online-based support service for university students abstract mental health problems among university students have increased markedly in recent years. despite their prevalence, help-seeking remains low, highlighting the need for accessible, low-threshold support. digital interventions, including online counselling and app-based tools, may help bridge this treatment gap. this study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of the digital mental health platform “enhance” as a low-threshold support service for university students, with a particular focus on characterizing counselling users and examining differences between users and non-users. a pragmatic, self-selected survey-based cohort study was conducted across six german universities. students voluntarily registered and completed standardized assessments at baseline (t0) and post-intervention (t1). the platform included a mental health app and individual counselling via chat, video, or email. overall, 447 students completed baseline assessments (mean age = 24.15 years; 76.5% female). moderate anxiety and depression levels were reported. of these, 343 downloaded the app, 117 engaged in at least one counselling session, with 41% choosing video counselling for their first contact. satisfaction was high (zuf-8: m = 20.14); 95.9% reported improved well-being after sessions, and 78.4% found the intervention helpful. most sessions addressed mental health concerns and resulted in referral recommendations (80.9​%). higher eating disorder symptoms and having a parent with a migration history were associated with lower counselling uptake. findings suggest that “enhance” is a feasible and well-accepted low-threshold intervention, however, only 26% of the baseline sample engaged with at least one counselling session, warranting further research on long-term effectiveness and integration into university support systems. discover mental health
