telehealth training for autism support using behaviour analytic strategies: a systematic review and quality appraisal abstract using telehealth to remotely train staff in behaviour analytic techniques has become an increasingly popular method of providing services to support autistic individuals and their families. this systematic literature review has identified studies which utilised this platform to remotely train staff across the education, health and social care sectors. in total, 20 studies met the inclusion criteria to be included in the review. training was provided to 101 participants across a variety of vocational backgrounds (e.g. behaviour analysts, speech and language therapists and teachers). multiple training methods were utilised, most commonly these involved techniques found in the behaviour skills training package, such as modelling of skills, opportunities for rehearsal and the provision of feedback. the training provided was effective at increasing trainee capabilities in conducting behaviour analytic assessments (e.g. functional analyses) and skill teaching (e.g. strategies to increase social communication). however, despite most research being viewed favourably by trainees and meeting minimum quality standards, it should be considered as in its infancy. many gaps do exist, especially around international culturally diverse demonstrations of effectiveness. by investigating such applications and filling these gaps, future researchers can begin to explore the true potential telehealth has in reducing global inequalities in evidence-based services. behavior analysis in practice

infliction v. affection abstract: introduction: “hate” (the desire to harm another) can be stigmatizing, so people (especially those with a vested interest) may deflect the label by redefining hate or focusing on a benign ultimate goal. aim: thus, we hypothesized that intimate “partners” (versus relationship “outsiders”) would be less likely to label tethering – a type of hate wherein harm’s ultimate goal is to keep the partner close – as “hate.” methods: canadian undergraduates ( n = 189) randomly assigned the role of “sending” partner, “receiving” partner, or “receiver’s friend” (i.e., outsider) rated whether tethering-congruent items reflected, love, hate, or something else, and whether love and hate are best understood in emotional, motivational, or behavioral terms. results: broadly consistent with predictions, senders who conceptualized love as emotion-not-behavior labeled tethering as “love,” and receivers saw tethering as “love” if love is about what someone wants, not what they do. in contrast, although outsiders labeled tethering “love” when love was about motivation, they labeled it “hate” when conceptualizing hate in motivational terms. discussion/conclusion: these results suggest that self-protective motives and vested interests in relationship maintenance can lead to (the sometimes willful) failure to recognize hate and its harmful consequences. european journal of psychology open

evidências psicométricas da versão curta da escala de crenças acerca da violência sexual la violencia sexual contra las mujeres es un problema de salud pública y de derechos humanos. el objetivo fue validar para el contexto brasileño la presente medida, con la particularidad de ser una versión corta. para ello, se realizaron dos estudios. el estudio 1 (n = 301) incluyó análisis de tri y afe. el estudio 2 (n = 301) llevó a cabo análisis confirmatorios y de validez convergente. los resultados demostraron que la presente medida presenta una buena adecuación del modelo unifactorial y validez convergente. además, se verificó que los hombres aceptan más las creencias sobre la violencia conyugal en comparación con las mujeres. en general, el conjunto de validaciones refuerza la validez general de la escala de creencias sobre la violencia sexual (ecvs), versión corta, convirtiéndola en una herramienta confiable y útil para la investigación y las prácticas clínicas, jurídicas y educativas. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

psychometric properties of the climate change anxiety scale in a sample from mexico in recent years, the effects of climate change on mental health have been acknowledged. among the most prominent consequences is anxiety associated with climate change. behavioral and cognitive impairments have been mapped within the climate change anxiety scale (ccas). the international community has widely used this psychological instrument to explore prevalence across different populations worldwide. the factor structure has been shown to vary by culture. although the scale has been translated into spanish, its factor structure has not yet been assessed in mexico. the current pre-registered study investigated the psychometric properties of the ccas in a northwestern mexican community sample using confirmatory factor análisis (cfa). it also assessed convergent and divergent validity using average variance explained (ave) and its square root (save) compared with self-report climate change coping strategies. internal consistency was further assessed using cronbach’s alpha, mcdonald’s omega, and the average interitem correlation. finally, using data from the present study and a previously published sample, consistency across samples was evaluated using the tucker congruence index. both one- and two-factor models showed acceptable goodness of fit after excluding three items (2, 7, and 12). this 10-item version additionally exhibited acceptable reliability coefficients. finally, the northern mexican sample showed congruence with a separate student sample from central mexico. the present study provides initial evidence of the validity of a 10-item version of the ccas in a northwestern mexican sample. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

the power of polo: an exploration of the effects of a novel polo-based residential intervention programme for vulnerable youth populations abstract background : equine-assisted activities (eaa) involve structured interactions with horses outside of formal therapeutic contexts and have been associated with psychosocial benefits for vulnerable youth populations. however, research has yet to explore how ridden, sport-specific activities, such as polo with its distinct social and cultural meanings, may shape young people’s experiences. this study explored vulnerable youths’ perceived psychosocial experiences of a polo-based eaa programme. methods : thirty-three participants (m = 21, f = 12, 12–25 years old) were interviewed up to three times during residential polo programmes between 2015 and 2019 about their experiences. results : thematic analysis identified three themes: (1) psychological benefits; (2) social benefits; and (3) the power of polo. participants described perceived improvements in self-perception, confidence, teamwork, communication, and mindset. these experiences were shaped by equine interactions, opportunities for skill development, team-based participation, and feelings of social acceptance within an unfamiliar and prestigious sporting environment. conclusions : findings suggest that polo-based eaa may offer a distinctive context in which horse-human interaction, sport, achievement, and social symbolism combine to support meaningful psychosocial experiences for vulnerable youth. further research should examine the longer-term significance of participation and the specific mechanisms through which ridden, sport-based equine programmes influence young people’s identity, confidence, and social relationships. human-animal interactions

to keep or not to keep: exploring why companion dog owners relinquish abstract background : the relinquishment of companion dogs can have negative repercussions for both dogs and their owners. previous research has largely focused on categorising reasons for companion dog relinquishment, with less attention paid to the experiences of owners who are considering relinquishment, or the support needed to reduce relinquishment. to help address these gaps, this study aimed to identify (1) the most common reasons which contribute to the consideration of relinquishment; (2) which of these are most likely to result in the keeping of vs the relinquishment of companion dogs, and (3) what types of support may be most effective in helping owners who are considering relinquishment to keep their dogs. methods : survey data were collected from two groups: those who considered relinquishment and ultimately relinquished their dogs (n = 178) and those who considered relinquishment and kept them (n = 145). respondents were asked to provide all reasons for considering relinquishment from an extensive list, as well as all supports or circumstances that contributed to their decision to keep the dog, or that may have allowed them to keep their dog. results : results demonstrated that considering relinquishment was typically driven by multiple reasons, with 23% (n = 73/323) of respondents indicating a combination of both dog behaviour and human/household related reasons. while some specific reasons were more often associated with relinquishing or keeping, these associations were not significant after controlling for multiple comparisons. among those who kept their dogs, 57% (n = 82/145) agreed that they were able to do so due to receiving behavioural, emotional, financial, and/or housing support. of those who relinquished but would have preferred to keep their dogs, 73% (n = 110/150) agreed that receiving one of these supports could have helped them keep their dog. conclusion : we suggest that effectively reducing relinquishment, both at the population level and in individual cases, may require holistic approaches. while results indicate that diverting relinquishment is possible in many cases, we identify which areas of support may be most effective across different scenarios. human-animal interactions

long-term training continually fine tunes motor memories 长期训练持续微调运动记忆 nature human behaviour, published online: 11 november 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02637-8 humans’ rapid adaptation to new dynamics is a crucial ability for interacting with the world. by combining the controlled manipulations of sensorimotor adaptation studies with the long-term learning approach of complex tasks, this study shows that the learned motor memory is continually tuned, and that retention increases with long-term training. 习得的运动记忆被持续微调，且保持随长期训练而提高；摘要未给出效应量或统计不确定性。 nature human behaviour

terrorism frays morality: the effects of the 2022 istanbul bombing on moral foundations, generosity, and cooperation terrorism aims to fray the moral fabric of society. we conducted the first preregistered study to assess the impact of real terror threats by combining pre–post comparisons with an experimental threat reminder, examining moral judgments and behaviors of 222 participants before and after the 2022 istanbul bombing. endorsement of binding moral foundations increased following the attack, yet this rise in group-oriented moral concerns did not translate into greater prosocial behavior. generosity decreased from pre to post, and experimentally heightening the threat reduced cooperation. changes in individualizing foundations followed an ideology-related pattern, with larger declines among conservative individuals, revealing a culture-specific ideological asymmetry in reactions to threat. our study challenges the generalizability of terror-response models developed in western societies and highlights the need for cross-cultural research on morality and behavior. social psychological and personality science

when success feels authentic: a feasibility-based account building on evidence that authenticity reflects both self-congruence and self-enhancement, this account predicts that these influences are interdependent, such that positive outcomes feel most authentic when they are experienced as realistically achievable given one’s domain-specific beliefs. across three within-person experiments ( n s = 97, 143, 146), participants imagined successful or unsuccessful behavior in domains varying in self-relevance and evaluated its authenticity. in all studies, imagining successful behavior increased perceived authenticity, but the magnitude of this effect reflected alignment with domain-specific self-beliefs; success felt more authentic in domains where participant perceived higher standing. this pattern generalized across multiple operationalizations of self-beliefs (self-potential, anticipated others’ evaluations, and personality traits) and was not explained by social desirability. alignment effects were associated with perceived behavioral difficulty, consistent with a feasibility-based account. together, the findings suggest that authenticity judgments reflect whether anticipated behavior plausibly originates from oneself. social psychological and personality science

sociodemographic, educational, and motivational correlates of multidimensional empathy among croatian vocational nursing students: a multicentre cross-sectional study background: evidence on multidimensional empathy in secondary-level vocational nursing education is limited. this study tested prespecified differences in perspective taking (pt), fantasy (fs), empathic concern (ec), and personal distress (pd) by reported sex, educational year, residence, socioeconomic status (ses), and motivation. methods: this multicentre cross-sectional study included 879 third- and fifth-year students from nine croatian nursing schools. hypothesis-aligned welch contrasts and hedges’ g were followed by simultaneous hc3 models and 4999-permutation multivariate block tests. holm correction controlled four-outcome families. results: in adjusted analyses (n = 858), sex (pillai trace = 0.047, p < 0.001), educational year (0.019, p = 0.003), residence (0.020, p = 0.024), and intrinsic/altruistic motivation (0.021, p = 0.001) were associated with the iri profile; ses was not (p = 0.124). female students reported higher pt, fs, ec, and pd. contrary to the hypothesis, fifth-year students reported lower pt and ec. the rural–urban hypothesis was unsupported; the residence result mainly reflected higher pd among suburban than urban students. intrinsic/altruistic motivation was associated with higher pt, ec, and pd. conclusions: prespecified hypotheses received mixed support. cross-sectional year differences do not demonstrate educationally caused change, and pd must not be interpreted as uniformly adaptive empathy. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

psychometric properties and measurement invariance of a torrance-inspired test of creative thinking in primary school pupils creative thinking is increasingly recognised as an essential educational competency, yet psychometrically robust measurement tools validated for specific cultural contexts remain scarce. this study evaluates the structural validity, internal consistency, discriminant validity, and measurement invariance of a torrance-inspired test of creative thinking (tct) among primary school pupils (n = 302, ages 5–12). confirmatory factor analyses demonstrated adequate fit for a four-factor structure (fluency, flexibility, elaboration, originality) for the figural component of the battery. however, discriminant validity analyses revealed high inter-factor correlations among fluency, flexibility, and elaboration, suggesting they operate as closely coordinated facets of divergent thinking, whereas originality demonstrated psychometric independence. multigroup analyses established scalar invariance across biological sex, indicating equivalent measurement functioning between male and female pupils. conversely, metric invariance failed across age cohorts. multiple-indicator multiple-cause (mimic) modelling identified significant uniform differential item functioning (dif) across several indicators, suggesting that developmental differences influence task interaction. the findings provide psychometric support for assessing creativity in primary education but caution against direct score comparisons across diverse age groups without accounting for developmental measurement variance. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

how discrimination and preference parameters affect block option selection in multidimensional forced-choice tests 歧视与偏好参数如何影响多维迫选测验中的区组选项选择 the effectiveness of multidimensional forced-choice (mfc) assessments depends not only on the measurement model but also on how options are paired into blocks. this simulation study evaluated four block option selection (bos) strategies for fixed-form mfc assessments under the multi-unidimensional pairwise preference model with two parameters: an option discrimination parameter and an option preference parameter. the study explicitly compared the separate and joint contributions of option discrimination and option preference parameters to the accuracy of latent trait estimates. the four algorithms were based on discrimination only (∏α), preference only (δβ), and two joint algorithms that used both discrimination and preference information (∏α + δβ and ∏α/δβ). a fully crossed 2 × 3 × 4 design manipulated trait mean distinctness, inter-trait correlation, and bos algorithm. results showed that the δβ and ∏α/δβ algorithms consistently produced the two lowest mean absolute error values across all five traits and six trait-profile conditions. inter-trait correlation was a stronger contextual factor than trait mean distinctness: as correlations increased, the advantage of algorithms using preference information over ∏α became larger. these findings suggest that option discrimination and preference parameters make distinct contributions to bos and that incorporating option preference information, either alone or jointly with discrimination information, can improve the accuracy of latent trait estimates in fixed-form mfc assessments. educational and psychological measurement

can we drop a group of study participants from analyses and modeling of behavioral scale data? a note on an application of the benjamini-hochberg method 能否将一组研究参与者从行为量表数据的分析与建模中剔除？——关于benjamini-hochberg方法应用的一点说明 this note discusses a procedure for evaluating whether a group of subjects in a larger study could be dropped from analyses of data obtained with a behavioral measuring instrument when pursuing research questions of initial concern. recent decades have witnessed notable facilitation of data collection processes in educational and psychological research, leading at times to comprehensive data sets containing one or more groups of respondents that may not be relevant to substantive queries regarding a population of interest. the outlined approach helps scholars to avoid potentially seriously biased parameter and reliability estimates, standard errors, and hypothesis testing results in empirical studies, which yield misleading substantive conclusions. the described procedure is readily employed with widely available software and is illustrated using data from a child development questionnaire. educational and psychological measurement

how motion curves shape time perception in progress bars: a bayesian adaptive psychometric approach. this study quantitatively examined users' time perception of progress bars controlled by different motion curves using an adaptive bayesian psychometric approach (quick estimate of slope and threshold-quest). user interface (ui) animations incorporate various motion curves, particularly variable-speed forms such as slow-down, speed-up, bézier, and elastic curves. despite their widespread use in modern ui design, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how they influence perceived duration. to investigate how different motion curves influence users' duration perception, we measured the point of subjective equality (pse) between constant-speed and four 5-s variable-speed progress bars. in each trial, participants compared a constant-speed progress bar with a variable-speed progress bar and judged which appeared shorter in duration. the quest algorithm adaptively adjusted the constant-speed bar's duration based on individual responses across 40 trials to estimate the pse. eye-tracking data were also collected. results indicated that constant-speed and speed-up progress bars were perceived as shorter. the findings suggest that the final phase of a progress bar may play an important role in subjective time perception, potentially reflecting end-phase attentional processes and anchoring-related judgment effects. eye-tracking results indicated that longer perceived durations were associated with lower eye blink rates, suggesting stronger attentional engagement and blink suppression during viewing. based on the research findings, when perceived waiting time is a critical dimension of user experience, designers may benefit from prioritizing constant-speed or speed-up motion curves in animation design. the study also adds to time perception research by showing how subtle visual dynamics can shape users' temporal judgments in interactive contexts. perception

beyond movement behaviours: unravelling the prospective links between 24-hour behavioural composition and affective dynamics in adolescent athletes. background: while the full spectrum of 24-h movement behaviours - encompassing sleep (slp), screen-based sedentary behaviour (screen-sb), light physical activity (lpa), structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (s-mvpa), and unstructured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (us-mvpa) - is consistently linked to daily affective states in adolescent athletes, existing literature has rarely examined these behaviours as an interdependent time-use composition, and largely fails to disentangle the distinct effects of structured versus unstructured mvpa subdomains on emotional outcomes.
materials and methods: using a repeated-measures prospective daily design, this study included 161 adolescent athletes (101 males and 60 females). accelerometers were used to quantify 24-h movement behaviours. four affective dimensions were assessed through ecological momentary assessment (ema): high-arousal positive affect, low-arousal positive affect, high-arousal negative affect, and low-arousal negative affect. bayesian multilevel compositional models were used to estimate between- and within-person associations, while isotemporal substitution analyses evaluated the estimated effects of reallocating time between behaviours on next-day affect.
results: associations between 24-h behaviour compositions and next-day affect were more evident at the within-person level. a higher relative proportion of lpa was associated with higher high-arousal positive affect (0.305, 95% bayesian credible interval [cri] 0.255 to 0.354) and low-arousal positive affect (0.292, 95% cri 0.245 to 0.338), and lower high-arousal negative affect (-0.231, 95% cri -0.260 to -0.203) and low-arousal negative affect (-0.210, 95% cri -0.236 to -0.185). in 30-min substitution analyses, reallocating time from other behaviours to lpa generally showed more favourable associations with next-day affect at both between- and within-person levels, although the associations varied across substitution pairs and affective dimensions. these findings highlight lpa as the behaviour most consistently associated with favourable next-day affect.
conclusions: daily 24-h movement behaviour composition was prospectively associated with next-day affect in adolescent athletes. lpa showed the most consistent favourable associations with next-day affect, particularly when replacing sb. promoting lpa may represent a feasible strategy for supporting affective wellbeing without adding to existing training demands. psychology of sport and exercise

identifying significant correlates of adolescent online gambling using a random forest approach: a cross-sectional study. online gambling is increasing among adolescents. machine learning methods can be used to identify and rank classification-relevant predictors among a large set of variables. this study identified and ranked factors associated with online gambling among high school students in canada using a random forest (rf) approach. this study used repeat cross-sectional data from year 6 (2017-18) to year 8 (2019-20) of the compass study, including n = 103,008 students in grades 9 to 12 from 151 schools in 4 canadian provinces. students reported engaging in online gambling in the past 30-days, biological factors (i.e., socio-demographic characteristics), personality factors (e.g., mental health), social factors, and behavioural factors (e.g., movement behaviours, substance use). a rf algorithm identified and ranked factors associated with online gambling. the prevalence of past 30-day online gambling was 3.5%-3.8% across the three years. across 25 iterations, the rf identified mental health factors (flourishing score, symptoms of depression, emotional regulation, symptoms of anxiety), physical activity time in the past week, and screen time behaviours (time spent texting/watching tv/surfing the internet/playing video games per day) as factors consistently associated with online gambling in the past 30-days. the average mean decrease in accuracy of the top 10 factors ranged from 47.7 to 34.6. mental health factors and screen time behaviours were consistently ranked among the top factors associated with online gambling among canadian adolescents, suggesting that these may be important factors to include in future studies of adolescent online gambling. future studies should investigate predictors of online gambling using prospective study designs. journal of gambling studies

psychological predictors of teachers' willingness to become school principals: the role of big five personality traits and motivation to lead. despite growing concerns regarding the declining pool of candidates for school principalship, the psychological and organizational determinants of leadership aspiration remain under-explored in non-western, centralized education systems. this study investigates the predictive role of big five personality traits, perceived institutional support (pis), and motivation to lead (mtl) on teachers' willingness to become a school principal (wbsp). data were collected from 417 primary school teachers in ankara, türkiye, and analyzed using hierarchical regression and bootstrapping mediation. pis was unrelated to wbsp at the zero-order level and in no model showed the positive association predicted by social exchange theory; the small negative coefficient it acquired under statistical control is read as suppression. this pattern is consistent with a structural decoupling between school-level support and centrally governed career advancement. openness to experience was a significant positive predictor when the big five were entered, and neuroticism a significant negative predictor once mtl was controlled, in line with findings from decentralized systems. mtl was the strongest predictor and was positively associated with wbsp, supporting the decentralized expectation rather than the competing decoupling hypothesis. no indirect effect through mtl was statistically significant. the motivational and dispositional antecedents of aspiration to the principalship thus appear to operate in a centralized system much as in decentralized ones, whereas institutional support does not, with implications for leadership succession in centralized educational systems. psychological reports

gaze semantics: a scoping review of how gaze conveys and constrains meaning in social contexts abstract humans rely on gaze to encode information and signal to others. gaze may indicate where someone is attending, but its contribution extends beyond spatial orientation. evidence is scattered across different research traditions. this scoping review synthesizes 361 publications on gaze as a meaningful social cue. gaze semantics describes the systematic contribution of gaze to conveying and constraining social meaning. a cross‐domain synthesis identified four recurrent operations: gaze orients by making objects, people or locations socially relevant; addresses by positioning people as recipients or interaction partners; qualifies by modifying how other cues are interpreted; and coordinates by organizing participation and unfolding action. these functional contributions can co‐occur within a single gaze event. gaze interpretation is inferential, shaped by five categories of contextual factors: signal properties; interactional availability; multimodal and sequential embedding; cultural, social and activity frame; and gazer and observer states and interactional history. we propose a gazer–observer model of gaze understanding that integrates these findings to describe the dynamic relation between gaze production and interpretation. the same gaze pattern may support different interpretations across situations yet allow a relatively specific interpretation within a particular encounter. gaze can therefore systematically affect social interpretation while remaining semantically underdetermined to varying degrees. british journal of psychology

an ecological model of recognition: diagnosis as a relational process among survivors of childhood sexual abuse. while the diagnostic overlap between complex post-traumatic stress disorder (cptsd) and borderline personality disorder (bpd) has received increasing scholarly attention, there remains a limited understanding of how adult women survivors of childhood sexual abuse (csa) interpret psychiatric diagnoses within the relational contexts that shape their self-recognition and meaning-making processes. this study investigated the processes by which adult women survivors of csa, diagnosed with cptsd and/or bpd, understand their experiences of abuse, interpret their psychiatric diagnoses, and integrate these distinct yet interconnected aspects of their lived experience. semi-structured interviews were conducted with 19 adult women survivors of csa, and the resulting data were analyzed employing interpretive description and reflexive thematic analysis. this analysis identified a central theme: making sense of the abuse and its consequences over time. this theme encompassed four subthemes: fragmented memory, containment, and silence; internal struggles of recognition and interpretation; familial validation and invalidation; and institutional responses that either connected or failed to connect trauma to its consequences. across these domains, psychiatric diagnoses served as relational frameworks, with their meaning being negotiated across intrapsychic, familial, and institutional contexts. these findings propose a preliminary socioecological framework that extends kelley et al.'s model of traumatic stress to the concept of recognition itself, herein conceptualized as relational and dynamically unfolding. clinically, these findings underscore the importance of trauma-informed diagnostic communication that collaboratively explores possible links between current difficulties and abuse history while attending to safety, pacing, and readiness. they also highlight the importance of institutional practices that integrate trauma-related information across services and into clinical formulation. journal of interpersonal violence

meeting oneself in the virtual reality environment: a single-case experimental study investigating effects on mood, meaning, and self-compassion in adults with depressive symptoms abstract the sense of self plays an important role in psychological well-being and it is often targeted by perspective-taking interventions in psychological treatments. the present study investigated the effects of a virtual reality (vr) intervention in which participants got to see themselves from an outside perspective while their relating to self was assessed. a single-case experimental design was applied with participants ( n = 7) having depressive symptoms. changes in mood, sense of meaning, and self-compassion were assessed by daily surveys 7–10 days before and 9 days after the vr intervention. in addition, participants’ self-ratings of wellbeing and experience of the vr intervention were investigated. the perspective-taking approach in combination with vr was experienced as meaningful with great impact and appeared to positively influence mood, sense of meaning, and/or self-compassion for some participants. these findings suggest that the vr intervention has the potential to be a beneficial tool in psychological treatments for depression. psychological record

enhancing social well‐being? a comparative analysis of psychological egoism and virtue ethics as foundations for social psychology interventions abstract the disciplinary aim distinguishing applied social psychology from basic social psychology is the use of theory to develop interventions for social and practical problems. however, many applied social psychologists have failed to adequately consider the pre‐investigatory philosophical assumptions about human nature in their theories and the sort of flourishing social life such assumptions actually encourage. the aim of this analysis is to demonstrate why applied social psychologists should more carefully consider the conceptual and practical fit between their (often unexamined) assumptions of psychological egoism and instrumentalism and the kind of thriving social and relational life they intend their interventions to foster. in so doing, we offer a comparative analysis of the vision of social life and flourishing implied by psychological egoism and instrumentalism, particularly as exemplified in the social exchange theory (set), and an alternative vision grounded in an aristotelian philosophical anthropology. we argue that the aristotelian vision of human nature and social life is preferable to the one egoistic and instrumentalist one commonly assumed by many applied social psychologists because it offers a greater possibility of attaining and encouraging the sort of vibrant and flourishing social life that applied social psychologists actually intend to promote. journal for the theory of social behaviour

from lucky events to durable social consequences: a taxonomy of propagation mechanisms abstract sociological research increasingly treats luck as consequential chance rather than as a personal trait. existing work has established that random events can shape life‐course outcomes, inequality and cumulative advantage, but it remains less clear how the consequences of a lucky event are transmitted through time. this article develops a taxonomy of five propagation mechanisms: direct positional transmission, actor‐mediated conversion, relational validation, institutional embedding and compensatory buffering. the mechanisms differ in whether interpretive uptake or actor action is required, in the social carrier of the event effect, in expected temporal persistence and in the empirical designs needed to identify them. the framework therefore separates the occurrence of luck from its subsequent social fate: a lucky event may be amplified, preserved, attenuated, dissipated or reversed. psychological beliefs about personal luck are treated as optional feedback mechanisms. the taxonomy extends existing work on cumulative and compensatory advantage by decomposing the downstream effect of consequential chance into analytically distinct pathways. an application to the matthew effect illustrates how similar aggregate persistence can arise through different social mechanisms. the framework provides a basis for comparative empirical research on when chance becomes durable inequality and when institutions prevent it from doing so. journal for the theory of social behaviour

psychometric properties of the perinatal assessment of paternal affectivity in peru: a screening measure for the risk of paternal perinatal psychopathology. this study examined the psychometric properties of the perinatal assessment of paternal affectivity (papa) in peru. the sample comprised 406 fathers of infants aged 0-17 months attending growth and development services in metropolitan lima; 58.1% were first-time fathers. they completed the papa, the patient health questionnaire (phq-9), the parental stress scale (pss), and the relationship assessment scale (ras). mean symptom levels were low, with a mild-to-moderate floor effect expected in a community sample. confirmatory factor analysis supported a unidimensional structure with moderate-to-high loadings and good fit after allowing one residual correlation. the scale showed adequate internal consistency (ordinal α = 0.87; α = 0.81; ω = 0.86). multi-group analyses supported strict measurement invariance across socioeconomic status and parity. convergent and concurrent validity were supported by positive correlations with depressive symptoms (phq-9) and parental stress (pss), and negative correlations with satisfaction with the baby and relationship satisfaction (ras). roc analysis indicated excellent discriminative capacity for depressive symptomatology (auc = 0.87; optimal cutoff = 6.5; sensitivity = 0.80; specificity = 0.82). findings support the papa as a brief, reliable, and valid screening measure for paternal perinatal psychopathology in community settings, with caution advised regarding cutoff use until replicated in peruvian clinical samples. key findings: the papa demonstrated a clear unidimensional structure with good model fit in a peruvian community sample. the scale showed strong convergent and concurrent validity through its associations with depressive symptoms, parental stress, and relationship satisfaction. the papa exhibited excellent discriminative capacity for depressive symptomatology, with an optimal cutoff score of 6.5. statement of relevance: this study examines the psychometric properties of a screening tool for the risk of paternal perinatal psychopathology in peru, an overlooked aspect of early childhood mental health. identifying paternal affective difficulties allows practitioners to anticipate risks for infants' socioemotional development. the measure performed equivalently across economic conditions and parity groups, supporting its use with diverse families. this work contributes to the field by expanding assessment practices beyond maternal factors and by strengthening early detection within peruvian community and primary care settings. infant mental health journal-infancy and early childhood

tracing the impact of maternal communication deviance on joint engagement: the mediating role of maternal supportive behaviors. communication deviance is a disorganized communicative style that can disrupt shared meaning-making in parent-child interactions and is considered a risk factor for later mental health difficulties. this longitudinal study, conducted in the uk, examined whether maternal communication deviance assessed during pregnancy predicted joint engagement and related processes. participants were 229 mothers (95.9% white british; m = 27.6 years, sd = 6.1). maternal communication deviance was assessed antenatally, and mother-child dyads were observed during play at 30-months. communication deviance predicted lower total joint engagement, including supported (β = -.18, p = .007), coordinated (β = -.17, p = .016), and symbol-infused joint engagement (β = -.24, p < .001), and was associated with reduced supportive behaviors (β = -.40, p < .001) and dyadic attunement (β = -.31, p < .001). mediation analyses indicated that supportive behaviors accounted for the associations between communication deviance and joint engagement outcomes. these findings suggest that communication deviance may constrain children's opportunities for shared attention and meaning making. the study supports developmental models that highlight early communicative processes as foundational to socio-cognitive and relational development and identifies supportive behaviors as a potential target for interventions promoting early mental health and parent-child interaction. key findings: higher maternal communication deviance during pregnancy predicted less total, supported, coordinated, and symbol-infused joint engagement at 30 months. reduced maternal supportive behaviors fully explained the link between communication deviance and lower joint engagement and dyadic attunement. maternal communication deviance may act as an early environmental risk factor, highlighting the importance of supporting maternal responsiveness to promote healthy development. statement of relevance: this study examines how maternal communication deviance measured during pregnancy predicts joint engagement and dyadic attunement at 30 months, processes central to early socio-cognitive and relational development. by identifying maternal supportive behaviors as a key mechanism linking communication deviance to interactional quality, the research highlights a modifiable target for early intervention. findings advance understanding of early environmental risk factors and inform strategies to support parent-child interactions, directly addressing foundational processes relevant to child and early childhood mental health. infant mental health journal-infancy and early childhood

indigenous child wellness: measurement considerations and assessment development guided by an indigenous community council abstract there is a need for culturally aligned wellness measures for indigenous children, youth and families of turtle island (canada). following an identified community need, we co‐developed a semi‐structured discussion and arts‐based measure with the guidance of an indigenous community council. this study involved 12 adult community members, 11 of whom identify as first nation and one of whom identifies as métis. two members were first nations elders. all members of the council held knowledge related to mental health, wellbeing, social work, traditional knowledge, policy development and/or indigenous governance. indigenous community council facilitated small group meetings were conducted online due to social‐distancing pandemic requirements to develop a culturally grounded wellness assessment suitable for use with indigenous children, youth and families. analyses suggest conversational and arts‐based methods to be most culturally relevant in keeping with traditional values of relational wellbeing and storytelling. additional themes of importance included reciprocity related to providing resources and tangible supports to those who interact with the wellness assessment. wholism, a limited focus on numeracy, and a strengths‐based approach were also revealed to be critical. these results produced the core questions to be used within the wellness assessment created in fulfilment of study aims. the purpose of the development of this tool is to meet the wellness needs of indigenous children and families through traditional values and metrics of wellbeing. this approach is used to promote autonomy for indigenous families by creating a means for understanding wellness developed by indigenous people, for indigenous people. the impact of this research will span across community, policy and practice to contribute to health and wellness sovereignty for indigenous peoples in support of intergenerational family thriving. journal of community & applied social psychology

childhood conduct problems and adult sexist attitudes: indirect associations through adolescent peer processes abstract sexist attitudes are linked with negative outcomes during adolescence, but research has not examined how modifiable risk factors such as conduct problems or social processes associated with conduct problems are linked with the development of these problematic gender attitudes. the present longitudinal study examined (a) the association between childhood conduct problems and the later endorsement of sexist attitudes, and (b) the mediating role of peer rejection and peer delinquency in adolescence in this association. participants ( n = 564; 49.4% women) were drawn from a study oversampling children with conduct problems in elementary schools in québec, canada, of whom 58.3% met criteria at baseline (t1; m age = 8.43, sd = 0.93). peer rejection was assessed in early adolescence (t2; m age = 13.27, sd = 0.95), peer delinquency in mid‐adolescence (t3; m age = 14.33, sd = 0.95), and benevolent and hostile sexism in early adulthood (t4; m age = 18.93, sd = 0.97). childhood conduct problems were directly associated with higher levels of endorsement of both hostile and benevolent sexism. mediation analyses also identified significant indirect associations through peer rejection and affiliation with delinquent peers, with distinct patterns across the two forms of sexism. these patterns of associations did not differ by gender. findings underscore peer influence as a potential intervention target for preventing sexist attitudes in at‐risk youth. social development

ecologically valid assessment of infant physical aggression: a pilot feasibility study abstract physical aggression (pa) in infancy represents an important area of study for understanding the development of externalizing behaviors. current methodologies for assessing infant pa rely primarily on parent‐report measures or brief structured laboratory observations, each with inherent limitations. this pilot feasibility study ( n = 31) evaluated a multi‐day, home‐based observation protocol for capturing infant pa in children aged 11–24 months using wearable and stationary cameras across 5 days. parents recorded an average of 2.5 h/day across 5 days, demonstrating high compliance and successful capture of infant pa. observed pa occurred more frequently than parent‐reported pa, with modest concordance between methods ( β = 0.24). nearly half of observed aggression was preceded by conflict, underscoring its contextual relevance. parent‐reported laxness was associated positively with parent‐reported pa ( r = 0.38). findings suggest that naturalistic observations provide an ecologically valid assessment approach that captures pa behaviors that may go unreported or unnoticed by parents. this methodology holds promise for improving understanding of early pa development and addresses a gap in the measurement of naturalistic, home‐based observations that capture pa behaviors in ecologically valid contexts. social development

influences of self‐regulation, moral identity, and justice sensitivity on prosocial behavior in adolescence: a 10‐year longitudinal study abstract self‐regulation–a multitude of competences which enable individuals to manage behavior, cognitions, and emotions in line with moral values‐may promote prosocial behavior, but longitudinal research into adolescence is sparse. self‐regulation may also promote justice sensitivity and moral identity, which have positively been linked to prosocial behavior as well, suggesting potential mediating effects. the present study investigated how nine sr competences (e.g., inhibition, flexibility, emotion regulation, planning behavior) across middle childhood (t1–t3) relate to self‐ and parent reported prosocial behavior in adolescence (t4), and whether justice sensitivity and moral identity (t4) mediate these relations in a german sample of 1657 participants (t1: 6–10 years, 52% female; t2: 7–11 years, 52% female; t3: 9–13 years, 52% female; t4: 16–21 years, 53% female, 2% genderqueer/other). in a latent model, each sr competence was indicated by its t1–t3 measurements. t4 justice sensitivity and moral identity were included as mediators. all predicted t4 prosocial behavior while controlling for stability of prosocial behavior (t1–t3). in the total group, only altruistic sensitivity was associated with self‐ and parent‐rated t4 prosocial behavior beyond prosocial behavior stability. results varied by sex, with additional effects of some sr competences and victim sensitivity. the findings indicate the relevance of concurrent justice sensitivity as a moral‐related trait for adolescent prosocial behavior beyond prosocial behavior stability as well as sex‐specific long‐term influences of sr competences on prosocial behavior. interventions should target justice sensitivity and flexibility, as well as planning behavior in boys and emotion regulation in girls. social development

mindreading with kindness: recruiting theory of mind for benevolent social orientation abstract children's social information processing is known to be related to various behavioral and social outcomes, but most developmental research has traditionally focused on maladaptive processes, such as a defensive view of the social world, hostile attributions, negative interpretation of others’ actions, and aggressive responses, and their close associations with antisocial outcomes. by contrast, adaptive processes, such as a benevolent worldview, benign attributions, positive interpretations, and prosocial responses, and their childhood antecedents, remain relatively underexplored. the current longitudinal study investigated theory of mind (tom) and prosocial moral values at preschool age as predictors of benevolent social orientation at school age. specifically, we tested the interaction effects between tom and prosocial moral values, assuming that tom is a morally neutral tool that can be used either prosocially or antisocially. participants included 200 low‐risk, typically developing children from the u.s. midwest. at 4.5 years, tom was measured using a series of false‐belief tasks, and prosocial moral values were assessed using hypothetical dilemmas. at 6.5 years, benevolent social orientation was measured using a set of vignettes depicting ambiguous situations. results supported significant interactions: higher tom was associated with more benevolent social orientation for children with higher prosocial values and lower self‐interested values. these findings supported the view of tom as morally neutral and highlighted the critical role of early internalization of moral values in guiding children to use their abilities of social understanding for a positive view toward the social world. social development

acting together: an integrative look into team interdependence team interdependence is foundational to teamwork, yet conceptualized inconsistently. reviewing 144 studies (1999–2025), we identify three conceptual emphases—task, goal, and emergent interdependence—and show how conceptual choices shape measurement and interpretation. we distinguish structural interdependence (designed inputs) from emergent interdependence (an emergent state), clarifying misalignment that impedes cumulative knowledge. small group research

living in the margins: a qualitative study of epistemic delinking among feminist critics of attachment theory this study examines how feminist scholars experience and navigate exclusion from mainstream citation networks in developmental psychology, focusing on attachment research. drawing on narrative interviews with twelve feminist scholars who critique the canonical bowlby, ainsworth, and main framework, we use interpretative phenomenological analysis to examine epistemic delinking: the severing of a contribution from the intellectual genealogy to which it belongs through forms of acknowledgment that contain, minimize, or reattribute it despite apparent inclusivity. we developed three superordinate themes. the first, the architecture of invisibility, captures participants’ recognition that their work was being decoupled from mainstream intellectual genealogies. the second, the labor of speaking and the cost of being heard, traces the emotional, relational, and professional toll of producing critique within a field that acknowledges feminist insight without integrating it. the third, counterpractices and alternative genealogies, documents how participants built alternative scholarly communities. we propose an integrative framework treating delinking as recursive rather than linear, working through institutional rules and relational encounters at once. understanding citation as a lived, relational practice, not a quantitative trace, opens avenues for disciplinary reflexivity and epistemic justice. feminism & psychology

technoference in the home: development and preliminary feasibility testing of an animated child‐report measure abstract parental technoference is increasingly recognised as a common aspect of contemporary family life, yet no existing measures allow young children to directly report on parental technoference. this study developed and preliminarily tested the child‐report measure of technoference in the home, an animated, scenario‐based measure designed to assess parental technoference using children as informants. across two phases, we (1) reviewed and prioritised existing technoference items with experts and co‐designed animated technoference scenarios with children and (2) conducted pilot testing with 45 children aged 5–9 years. children demonstrated high engagement and comprehension across animations, and most emotion faces used in the response format were accurately identified. in the pilot, 91% of children reported parental technoference in at least one scenario. sadness was the most frequently reported emotional response. younger children (5–6 years) reported higher prevalence and frequency than older children (7–9 years). boys reported higher frequency in one scenario depicting parent‐initiated technoference. no other age and sex differences were found. these findings indicate that young children can meaningfully engage in the co‐design and testing of developmentally appropriate child‐report measures. children aged 5.5–9 years were able to use the animated scenarios to report on both the occurrence and perceived emotional impact of parental technoference in the home, demonstrating the feasibility of this measure. directions for future validation, refinement and broader application in research and practice are discussed. infant and child development

multiple routes to affiliation: children give greater weight to shared preferences affording broader relational benefits abstract while it is well‐established that similarity drives affiliation, not all similarities afford the same relational benefits. using a third‐party friendship inference task, we found that elementary‐age children in japan ( n = 65; age 6 to 11; 32 female) were sensitive to how widely shared preferences are when making affiliative judgements. specifically, children were shown a character with two preferences, each shared with a different potential friend. the more widely shared children perceived one preference to be relative to the other, the more likely they were to expect the character to befriend the person who shared that preference ( b = 0.23, se = 0.04, p < 0.001, or = 1.26). because widely shared similarities can connect individuals to larger social circles offering greater acceptance, networks, and resources, children may view these affiliative pathways as more strategic than those based on narrowly shared similarities, which may signal deeper compatibility but offer fewer relational benefits overall. infant and child development

the effect of life review intervention on perception of aging in old women background aging perception significantly influences mental health in later life, yet effective interventions targeting this multidimensional construct remain underexplored. aim this randomized controlled trial examined the effect of life review therapy on aging perception among older women. methods thirty older women (15 intervention and 15 control) were recruited from comprehensive health centers in larestan county, iran. random allocation was performed using randomized blocks. the intervention group received six weekly 1.5‐hour life review sessions based on haight and webster′s protocol; the control group received no intervention. aging perception was assessed using the validated persian version of the aging perception questionnaire (apq) at baseline and postintervention. between‐group differences were analyzed using independent t ‐tests, and within‐group changes were evaluated with paired t ‐tests. results baseline demographic characteristics were comparable between groups ( p > 0.05). in the intervention group, significant improvements were observed in control positive (12.40–14.13, p = 0.015; between‐group p = 0.008) and consequences positive (11.73–13.80, p = 0.009; between‐group p = 0.017). significant reductions were found in negative emotional representations (17.80–13.07, p = 0.026; between‐group p = 0.013) and negative consequences (29.00–22.60, p = 0.047; between‐group p = 0.010). the control group showed no significant changes across any dimension ( p > 0.05 for all). conclusion life review therapy significantly enhanced positive aging perceptions and reduced negative cognitive and emotional responses to aging in older women. this structured, time‐limited intervention offers an effective nonpharmacological strategy for promoting healthy aging and warrants integration into routine geriatric care. trial registration: iranian registry of clinical trials: irct20250819066915n1 mental illness

feasibility of the self‐reporting questionnaire‐20 (srq‐20) as a niche‐targeted psychiatric screening tool for survivors of intentional poisoning in a resource‐limited setting: a single‐center cross‐sectional study background ensuring timely and effective psychiatric care is crucial for patients with intentional poisoning. given resource constraints in countries like bangladesh, a screening tool for this patient group can effectively identify appropriate cases and ensure timely care. this study is aimed at assessing whether the who‐developed self‐reporting questionnaire‐20 (srq‐20) scale can serve as a psychiatric screening tool, compared with the diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders, fifth edition (dsm‐5), as the gold standard, and determining its cutoff score. result this cross‐sectional study, conducted in one of the largest tertiary medical college hospitals in bangladesh, included 105 patients who survived following intentional poisoning. most of the intentional poisoning survivors were in the age group of 20–29 years, female gender, having a secondary level education, being married, and belonging to a rural area. using the dsm‐5 criteria, this study found that around 91% of them had psychiatric conditions, with depressive illness being the most prevalent. the mean difference in srq‐20 scale scores between the groups of having and not having psychiatric disorders was 5.053 (±0.71), and it was statistically significant. the roc analysis revealed that the optimal srq‐20 cutoff score for predicting having any psychiatric disorders among patients with intentional poisoning was ≥ 6, with a sensitivity of 93.7% and a specificity of 100%. conclusion at a cutoff of ≥ 6, the srq‐20 scale, as a screening tool in resource‐limited hospital settings in bangladesh, showed promising diagnostic accuracy for identifying dsm‐5‐diagnosable psychiatric disorders among intentional poisoning survivors. however, its validity, reliability, prognostic utility, and optimal thresholds should be further evaluated. mental illness

effects of autonomy‐supportive music instruction on student wellness: a cluster‐randomized test of psychological need satisfaction and autonomous motivation as motivational mechanisms abstract this study examines the effects of autonomy‐supportive music instruction on student wellness and investigates the underlying motivational mechanisms through which such instruction may promote wellness in university music education. drawing on self‐determination theory, a cluster‐randomized experimental design was implemented among undergraduate music students in china. intact classes were randomly assigned to an autonomy‐supportive instructional condition or a control condition. data were collected at three time points using paper‐based questionnaires, and multilevel analyses were used to account for the nested structure of students within classes. the results indicate that autonomy‐supportive music instruction increased students' psychological need satisfaction and autonomous motivation. in turn, both psychological need satisfaction and autonomous motivation were positively associated with post‐intervention student wellness. multilevel mediation analyses using bootstrapping revealed significant indirect effects of autonomy‐supportive instruction on student wellness through both psychological need satisfaction and autonomous motivation, whereas the direct effect was no longer significant after the mediators were included. overall, the findings provide experimental evidence that autonomy‐supportive music instruction can promote student wellness by shaping students' motivational experiences. the study extends self‐determination theory to a performance‐oriented, non‐western music education context and highlights psychological need satisfaction and autonomous motivation as distinct motivational pathways linking instructional practice to student wellness. psych journal

human verification statements under article 50 of the eu ai act may raise credibility without improving calibration abstract article 50(4) of the eu ai act introduces transparency obligations for ai-generated or ai-modified public-interest text while allowing visible disclosure to be omitted in specified cases of human review or editorial control combined with editorial responsibility. this raises a question of calibrated trust: does a ‘human-verified’ statement help readers distinguish reliable from unreliable content, or does it simply increase trust regardless of accuracy? in this comment, we propose the ‘human-verification premium’ as a testable psychological hypothesis, distinguish origin, verification, and accountability as separate cues, and outline how signal detection theory could be used to test whether verification statements improve sensitivity or merely shift the response criterion. we therefore propose testing whether human-verification claims that specify what was checked and who was responsible improve calibration relative to generic verification claims. their effectiveness should be judged by improved discrimination between accurate and inaccurate content, rather than by higher average credibility. by separating the effect of a verification cue on overall credibility from its effect on accuracy discrimination, the framework makes the psychological consequences of human-verification claims empirically testable and may inform reader-facing disclosure and editorial policy. discover psychology

the effects of the three good things intervention on subjective well-being in chinese first-year college students abstract subjective well-being (swb) is a core indicator of mental health. chinese first-year college students suffer increased stress, which negatively impacts their swb during the critical university adaptation period. existing research on the three good things (tgt) interventions is mainly rooted in western culture. moreover, the moderating effects of autonomy and intrinsic motivation on the tgt intervention have not yet been explored. the present study had two main targets. one is to test the effectiveness of the tgt intervention in improving swb among chinese first-year college students. the other is to explore the moderating roles of autonomy and intrinsic motivation in intervention effects. we conducted an experiment with 183 participants, using a 2 (autonomy: autonomous/non-autonomous)×2 (intrinsic motivation: high/low) between-subjects design. the results showed the tgt intervention significantly improved swb in the intervention group (t = -8.457, p < 0.001), with a significant time × group interaction (f = 22.296, p < 0.001). both autonomy (f = 5.565, p = 0.020) and intrinsic motivation (f = 8.693, p = 0.004) had significant positive main effects on changes in swb (δswb). a significant interaction between the two factors was also found (f = 4.560, p = 0.035). this study confirms the effectiveness of the tgt intervention among college students in an eastern culture and stresses the importance of autonomy for boosting intervention effects, especially for students with low intrinsic motivation. our findings supply empirical support for cross-cultural effectiveness and the personalized design of tgt intervention for college students. discover psychology

how can i trust you again? repair behaviours and trust recovery after romantic betrayal abstract trust recovery after romantic betrayal is a central concern in couple therapy, yet little is known about which behaviours are most strongly associated with partners' perceived trust repair. we present the results of an online survey of betrayed partners who had attempted reconciliation after romantic infidelity ( n = 263). using hierarchical regressions, we tested for the effect of dispositional predictors (attachment anxiety, attachment avoidance, propensity to trust) and betrayed partners' perceptions of five post‐betrayal repair behaviours (transparency, monitoring, remorse, explanation, reconnection) on trust recovery (i.e., differential of trust in the betraying partner now compared to after having discovered the infidelity). repair behaviours explained substantially more variance in trust recovery than dispositions, which had, at best, rather indirect effects. more specifically, perceived remorse, reconnection, and explanation uniquely predicted trust recovery, whereas transparency and monitoring did not account for additional unique variance once other behaviours were included. these findings suggest trust repair is chiefly associated with what partners do , more than with stable predispositions. journal of marital and family therapy

self-defining memories in head and neck cancer patients and control group objective this exploratory study examined whether self-defining memories (sdm) differ in specificity, integration, and emotional valence between individuals treated for head and neck cancer (hnc) and matched controls. an exploratory thematic analysis examined cancer-related sdm. methods twenty-one patients with hnc and 22 controls reported five sdm each (215 memories). memories were coded for specificity, integration, emotional valence, and thematic content. intraclass correlation coefficients and multilevel logistic regression models examined group differences and associations between emotional valence and integration. cancer-related sdm were additionally examined thematically. results no group differences were found in specificity or integration (ps > .80). positive and mixed sdm were more likely to be integrated than negative or neutral sdm. four themes emerged: diagnostic uncertainty and delays; cancer diagnosis and disclosure; interpersonal relationships and cancer; and consequences of hnc treatment. conclusions sdm integration was associated with emotional valence rather than cancer status. qualitative findings highlighted diverse and personally meaningful representations of cancer experiences. health psychology open

establishing persistence in manding for information in children with autism abstract individuals with autism spectrum disorder (asd) may require explicit instruction to learn how to mand for information when they encounter missing or unknown information. the current study expands the previous research on mands for information by assessing the persistence of mands (i.e., resistance to extinction). three children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder were taught to perform two behavior chains and mand for information in a variety of ways. eo and ao trials were interspersed to ensure appropriately discriminated responding. during eo trials, an item was missing that was required to complete the chain. each participant was required to mand “where is the [item],” obtain the item, and complete the chain to access the terminal reinforcer. during ao trials, all items needed to complete the chain were present; therefore, no mand for information was necessary. training began using one item, in chain one. after responding met the mastery criterion, generalization probes were conducted on the untrained item in chain one and both items in chain two. mands for information generalized to the untrained item and the untrained chain for all three participants. behavioral interventions

development of a patient satisfaction measure for primary care behavioral health (pcbh) settings: a delphi study. studies of patient satisfaction with primary care behavioral health (pcbh) services are limited, and those that exist have either used general satisfaction measures not specific to integrated care or researcher-developed, unvalidated measures. development of a psychometrically validated measure of patient satisfaction that captures unique elements of this model would support clinical quality improvement efforts and enable more rigorous evaluation of the pcbh model. this study gathered expert feedback using delphi methodology to inform the development of a measure of patient satisfaction specifically for pcbh settings. purposive sampling was used to identify experts (n = 20). participants rated possible measure items on a scale of (1) "very irrelevant" to (5) "very relevant" as an indicator of patient satisfaction with pcbh and provided open-ended feedback on item wording across two delphi rounds. the resulting measure of patient satisfaction includes 20 items that capture key aspects of both visit satisfaction and pcbh model satisfaction. next steps include assessing the psychometric properties of this measure in a sample of pcbh patients. through the development, validation, and dissemination of this measure, we hope to add to the pcbh patient outcome literature, an area that is currently lacking in our field. journal of clinical psychology in medical settings

from family emotional insecurity to youth‐to‐parent aggression: the role of stress and bullying abstract youth‐to‐parent aggression (ypa) is a growing concern due to its harmful effects on families. this study aimed to expand the understanding of ypa by analysing the relationships between emotional insecure strategies (preoccupation and disengagement), perceived stress, bullying aggression and ypa using a longitudinal design. the sample included 591 adolescents (45.8% girls) from xxx, aged 13–18 years ( m = 14.71; sd = 0.90). results showed that emotionally insecure strategies at time 1 (t1) were linked to higher stress and bullying aggression at t1 and to increased ypa at time 2 (t2). moreover, these strategies indirectly affected ypa through stress and bullying, which served as mediators. the relationship between insecure emotional strategies and later ypa was serially mediated by stress and bullying. overall, the findings highlight key risk factors for ypa and contribute to the development of prevention and intervention approaches to address this form of family violence. journal of investigative psychology and offender profiling

a narrative review of psychological distress and psychosocial burden in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis abstract purpose adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (ais) is commonly managed as a structural spinal condition, but mental health and psychosocial concerns have also been reported in affected adolescents. this review aimed to summarize these outcomes and examine associated biological, psychological, and social factors within a conceptual biopsychosocial framework. methods pubmed/medline and google scholar were searched for relevant studies, and reference lists of relevant articles were screened for additional literature. studies reporting mental health, psychological, psychosocial, psychiatric, or related health-related quality-of-life outcomes in adolescents with ais were considered. findings were summarized narratively. results studies suggest that some adolescents with ais may experience anxiety and depressive symptoms, psychological distress, psychiatric conditions, body- and self-image concerns, and reduced health-related quality of life. the frequency and severity of these outcomes varied across study populations and assessment methods, and associations with radiographic severity were inconsistent. body and self-image, pain, and treatment-related stress were commonly associated with mental health outcomes. catastrophizing, coping, resilience, social support, and treatment experience were also examined, although the evidence was less extensive. evidence for altered pain modulation and metabolic or neuroendocrine factors was limited or inconsistent. conclusion mental health problems may affect a subset of adolescents with ais and may not be fully reflected by curve severity alone. biological, psychological, and social factors may all be relevant, although their relative contributions remain unclear. a biopsychosocial framework may help organize the available evidence and support a more comprehensive assessment of adolescents with ais. clinical trial registration not applicable. discover mental health
