influence of cross-modal load on cognitive processing and decision-making 跨通道负荷对认知加工与决策的影响 abstract thoughtful design of multitask scenarios alleviates some competition for limited attentional resources. however, tasks that demand separate perceptual resources may still result in processing overload. in this experiment, participants completed a visual search task and auditory n-back task (absent, 1, 2, 3) in isolation or together via a within-subjects, randomized, and factorial paradigm. we assessed cross-modal influence using summary statistics, a nonparametric metric of efficiency, and complementary evidence accumulation models. as predicted, we found dual-task deficits in both tasks when paired, and further declines in performance with increased task load. further, our modeling results indicated a reconfiguration in decision-making architecture as cross-modal load increased—lower response caution in one task (thresholds) to compensate for the unavoidable degradation of processing quality in another (drift rates). overall, our results suggest that dual-task capacity limits not only govern the amount of information humans can process, but impose (in)stable decision-making strategies across competing resources streams. 两任务配对完成时均出现双任务缺陷，且随任务负荷增加表现进一步下降。 建模结果显示，随跨通道负荷增加，决策架构发生重构：一个任务降低反应谨慎性（阈值）以补偿另一任务加工质量（漂移率）不可避免的下降。 作者据此提出双任务容量限制不仅约束可加工的信息量，还在竞争的资源流之间施加（不）稳定的决策策略。 cognitive research-principles and implications

some assembly required: self-testing alone is not an effective way to build broader understanding abstract extensive research has demonstrated that testing enhances long-term memory by strengthening retrieval processes for the tested memory traces. such memory models explain why learners benefit from repeated testing, but they do not account for how learners construct understanding across multiple ideas. in contrast, theories of discourse comprehension emphasize the construction of inferences, whereby learners actively connect ideas into a coherent mental representation. these two perspectives make distinct predictions about what learners retain and understand. the present study tested these predictions by comparing a test-only procedure, in which learners encountered the material exclusively through questions and corrective feedback and never read the source text, against self-explanation and reading, measuring both fact memory and inference performance. in experiment 1 (n = 254), despite superior retention of individual facts, test-only learning produced lower inference performance than self-explanation. experiment 2 (n = 68) was a preregistered replication with a minimum 24-h delay between learning and test sessions, and which repeated the learning phase in two blocks, enabling participants to retrieve from memory the answers they had encoded. the introduction of retrieval practice improved recall of facts but did not facilitate inference performance. a mixed-methods analysis revealed that generating inferences during learning specifically predicted inference performance, whereas noting facts predicted fact recall, providing converging evidence that these strategies produce different mental representations. furthermore, participants generated fewer inferences when self-explaining science texts compared with narratives, highlighting domain differences in knowledge integration. together, these results demonstrate that while test-only learning strengthens memory for discrete information, it does not foster the integrative processing necessary for comprehension. cognitive research-principles and implications
“now mum understands the same as the therapist”. children’s experiences of stepping together for children after trauma, a parent-led, therapist-assisted trauma treatment cognitive behaviour therapy

art without a single definition: how laypeople define and categorize artworks this study explored how laypeople define artworks and categorize items as artworks. results from an ontology questionnaire revealed that participants held complex views with most agreeing that original artworks possess a unique aura, suggesting a belief in artworks as more than just physical objects. in terms of intension (the criteria that define a term), participants consistently emphasized intentionalism as central to their concept of artworks. in terms of extension (the set of things that fall under a term), ai-generated items emerged as particularly informative borderline cases. notably, ai items were more often seen as artworks by physicalists and participants who valued functionalism or historicism. while laypeople's theoretical beliefs do influence their categorizations of items as artworks, the findings suggest that the extension emerges from the flexible interaction of multiple partially independent intensions rather than from a single coherent definition. these findings highlight the challenges in empirically investigating art concepts. empirical studies of the arts

joke's on you: a social relations analysis of humor styles in friendships abstract humor plays an important role in the formation and maintenance of close relationships, yet little is known about how people come to perceive their friends as funny or as using different humor styles. the present study examined perceptions of funniness and humor styles in 185 naturally occurring friendship groups ( n = 740). in the context of the social relations model, friends demonstrated modest consensus regarding humor styles and funniness, indicating that humor is sufficiently observable to generate shared impressions. at the same time, substantial perceiver and relationship variances suggested that humor judgments are also shaped by individual tendencies and the unique dynamics of particular friendships. self‐other agreement and assumed similarity were also evident across humor styles. finally, adaptive humor styles and general funniness were associated with greater friendship satisfaction, while aggressive and self‐defeating humor were associated with poorer friendship quality. these findings position humor as both an individual characteristic and an interpersonal perception that emerges through close relationships. personal relationships

psychometric properties of the spiritual attitude and involvement list short form (sail-sf) and its moderating role between threatening experiences and posttraumatic growth in spanish people with chronic pain journal of spirituality in mental health

fentanyl-induced postural changes across species: behaviors, mechanisms, and translational implications this narrative review summarizes fentanyl-induced postural effects across species, focusing on a postulated cerulospinal noradrenergic connection linking rodent catalepsy models to human wooden-chest syndrome (wcs). this could have possible translational relevance for fentanyl overdose and its clinical management. a review of english-language literature was conducted using pubmed and embase. reference lists of retrieved articles and prior reviews on the topic were searched for additional sources. the evidence supports that fentanyl-induced postural effects are centrally mediated to a significant extent through µ-opioid receptor (mor) activation in the locus cœruleus, with downstream engagement of cerulospinal noradrenergic projections onto spinal α 1 -adrenoceptors. further, this integrated pathway is subject to modulation by nitric oxide and glutamatergic signaling, striatal dopaminergic–medium spiny neuron circuitry, and pontine respiratory nuclei. phenomenology differs substantially across species, dose, and route of administration, but a phylogenetically conserved mor–cerulospinal–noradrenergic pathway, modulated by nitric oxide and dopaminergic circuitry, appears to underlie fentanyl-induced postural disturbances across species, from cataleptic immobility in rodents to wcs in humans. the conserved mechanism is expressed as species-specific chest-wall mechanics that are a determinant of clinical severity, and helps to understand the potential role of α 2 -adrenoceptor agonists as being mechanistically rational for overdose management. behavioural pharmacology

depresión y ansiedad según riesgo suicida en jóvenes colombianos: análisis secundario con metodología mixta this study analyzes the differences in language used to describe symptoms of depression and anxiety in 440 young colombians (18-30 years old) with or without suicidal risk. a secondary analysis of data from previous studies was conducted using a mixed-methods design with a transformative approach. this included responses to a sociodemographic questionnaire, an open-ended questionnaire on symptoms of depression and anxiety, the depression, anxiety, and stress scale (dass-21), and the plutchik suicide risk scale. the procedure included corpus normalization, vectorization using the fasttext model, and dimensionality reduction using the t-sne algorithm. the results confirmed that repetitive, focused negative thinking was prevalent among all participants. furthermore, greater intensity and severity of symptoms were observed in participants with suicidal risk, regardless of the specific symptom type. using this methodology within the transdiagnostic framework offers a useful empirical approach for qualitatively exploring the structure of emotional distress. the findings suggest that suicide risk is not an isolated or disconnected linguistic pattern, but rather may emerge within the context of repetitive negative thinking understood as experiential avoidance. universitas psychologica

positive sporting experience and life purpose: is the association explained by motivation? this cross-sectional study examined motivation’s mediating role in the association between positive sporting experience and life purpose. the sample comprised 473 brazilian young athletes who participated in the youth school games. data were collected using the purpose in life test, youth experience survey for sport, and sports motivation scale. structural equation modeling indicated adequate data fit for the final model (χ2/df = 2.96; cfi = 0.95; rmsea = 0.06; srmr = 0.05) and explained 27% of the variance in existential realization and 15% of the variance in existential emptiness. intrinsic motivation was positively associated with existential realization and negatively associated with existential emptiness. the findings indicate that intrinsic motivation mediates the association between positive sporting experience and life purpose among young brazilian athletes and is related to stronger feelings of existential realization. because of the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. in practice, the results suggest that coaches and parents should promote environments that foster positive sporting experience and support self-determined motivation for practice. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

do resources buffer job demands? evidence from firefighters’ burnout and well-being this cross-sectional study, grounded in the conservation of resources theory, examined the role of personal (psycap) and organizational resources (learning opportunities) in relation to job demands and their association with occupational health among brazilian military firefighters. the study involved a sample of 1,327 participants, 92.46% operational firefighters and 7.54% officers, recruited from 19 brazilian states via an electronic survey. two alternative theoretical models were tested: one examining a linear relationship and the other testing moderate effects between resources and demands. the findings were more consistent with the linear model, indicating that psycap was negatively associated with burnout and positively associated with well-being, while learning opportunities were associated with lower burnout levels. however, moderated effects were not statistically significant, suggesting that resources were directly related to occupational health outcomes rather than buffering the relationship between demands and outcomes. the results highlight the relevance of psycap as a personal resource associated with occupational health. the study also underscores the role of organizational context and work design in shaping the effectiveness of learning opportunities. these findings suggest that interventions aimed at strengthening personal and organizational resources may improve occupational health indicators among high-risk professionals. the research emphasizes the need for context-sensitive approaches given the unique challenges faced by firefighters. by advancing the understanding of resource-based processes, this study contributes to the broader literature on burnout and well-being in high-risk occupations. acta colombiana de psicologia

when treatment isn’t working: transitioning an adolescent from individual to family therapy this case report illustrates the difficulty of deciding when to shift therapeutic focus for a 12-year-old girl who presented with depression, self-harm behaviors, and suicidality. routine outcomes monitoring (i.e., weekly risk assessments and biweekly self-report measures) revealed a progressive worsening of symptoms during the first episode of care as well as ongoing issues with substance use, prompting a timely transition from individual to family therapy. the change highlighted how patient characteristics, treatment components, and delivery methods interact to influence progress, and demonstrated the critical role of systematic outcome tracking in detecting early deterioration. framing the intervention within the family system brought to light underlying dynamics that were pivotal to resolving the adolescent’s difficulties, thereby strengthening the therapeutic alliance and quickening progress towards a successful treatment outcome. the case underscores the necessity for clinicians working with adolescents to establish clear expectations and boundaries around patient and family confidentiality and to routinely evaluate suicidal ideation and health-risk behaviors, using structured outcome data to guide timely treatment adjustments. clinical case studies

from trauma reenactment to reciprocal connection in the human–animal bond abstract background: judith herman describes “trauma” as an affliction of the powerless. research shows that animal trauma similarly reflects helplessness. the parallels between human and animal trauma suggest that the human–animal bond holds significant therapeutic potential – even with animals that have not experienced explicit trauma but live in environments perpetuating helplessness or objectification. these partnerships serve as crucial therapeutic bridges for individuals with impaired human relationships. case presentation and clinical approach: this case report illustrates key perspectives for fostering partnerships that facilitate relational trauma therapy (also termed “reciprocal therapy”) in the presence of animals. it outlines a novel therapeutic framework for post-trauma intervention that integrates the animal’s lived experiences, aiming to prevent trauma reenactment by strictly rejecting the objectification of one being for the benefit of another. conclusions: moving toward relational-reciprocal approaches can create a safe space for mutual emotional and physical healing for both human and animal participants. human-animal interactions

development and preliminary validation of the japanese version of the existential gratitude scale: evidence from a post‐disaster context in fukushima abstract existential gratitude refers to the capacity to experience gratitude in the midst of adversity, yet no validated measure exists in japanese. the present study aimed to develop and validate the japanese version of the existential gratitude scale (egs‐j). following established cross‐cultural adaptation procedures, an 8‐item japanese version was created. study 1 ( n = 56) examined the factor structure using exploratory factor analysis and provided preliminary evidence of internal consistency and expected correlational patterns. study 2 ( n = 222) evaluated the scale using confirmatory factor analysis and examined its associations with well‐being, meaning in life, and posttraumatic growth. results supported a unidimensional structure with good model fit and high internal consistency. existential gratitude was positively associated with well‐being, meaning in life, and posttraumatic growth. no significant differences were observed between disaster‐affected and control groups. however, exploratory analyses within the disaster‐affected group indicated that relocation and job change were significantly associated with existential gratitude. these findings suggest that the egs‐j demonstrates acceptable reliability and validity and may serve as a useful tool for examining existential gratitude in the context of adversity. japanese psychological research

ease of retrieval determines the psychological distance from bodily sensations abstract this study investigated the role of ease of retrieval in forming psychological distance from bodily sensations. in body‐oriented psychotherapies, such as focusing, an appropriate subjective distance from one's internal experiences has been associated with feelings of therapeutic success and relaxation. on the basis of previous studies, we hypothesized that more easily recalled experiences are perceived as psychologically closer, and we examined this hypothesis through a pilot study and a main experiment. in the experiment, 155 participants were assigned to either an easy or a difficult retrieval condition. after completing a task in which they recalled bodily sensations, their perceived psychological distance from the sensations was measured. the results showed that participants in the easy‐retrieval condition perceived their bodily sensations to be significantly closer than those in the difficult retrieval condition. this finding was supported by multiple regression analyses. these results suggest that the ease of retrieval may contribute to the perceived psychological distance from bodily sensations. the theoretical and practical implications for developing safer and more agentic engagement with bodily sensations are discussed. japanese psychological research

evaluating the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of virtually delivered dialectical behaviour therapy skills groups among emerging adults in india abstract research from high‐income countries has demonstrated the effectiveness of dialectical behavioural therapy (dbt) in reducing a range of psychiatric symptomatology, with limited research on efficacy in low‐and middle‐income countries. the purpose of this study was to examine acceptability, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy of an eight‐week group dbt skills training (dbt‐st) delivered via synchronous video teleconferencing by student therapists in india. individuals who indicated an interest in participating in a virtual skills program were invited to participate in the study. those who provided consent were randomized into a virtual dbt‐st group ( n = 43) or a waitlist comparison group ( n = 41). participants completed self‐report measures of emotion dysregulation, coping, anxiety, and depression at baseline, after 4 weeks of virtual dbt‐st groups, and after 8 weeks of virtual dbt‐st groups. participants in the virtual dbt‐st group also responded to open‐ended questions regarding acceptability and feasibility and rated treatment acceptance. feasibility was demonstrated by the retention of 71.8% of participants. dbt‐st was rated as acceptable. efficacy was partially supported: participants in the dbt‐st group reported lower depressive symptoms than the comparison group at post‐assessment. there were no significant differences in emotion dysregulation, dysfunctional coping, or anxiety. international journal of psychology

multi‐omics mendelian randomization prioritizes candidate druggable genes for major depressive disorder abstract this study aimed to prioritize candidate druggable genes for major depressive disorder (mdd) using mendelian randomization (mr) integrated with expression (eqtl) and protein quantitative trait loci (pqtl) data. we conducted a systematic mr analysis combining cis ‐eqtl and cis ‐pqtl data from blood and brain tissues to assess the causal effects of druggable genes on mdd, using finngen r9 gwas summary statistics. bayesian colocalization analysis confirmed shared genetic variants, while sensitivity analyses (mr‐egger, weighted median, mr‐presso) tested robustness. a phenome‐wide mr (phe‐mr) assessed broader trait associations. to evaluate translational potential, we mapped candidate genes to known drugs using drugbank, chembl, and clinicaltrials.gov.six candidate druggable genes (mapk3, psmb9, siglec9, mst1, btn3a1, and tapbp) showed significant associations with mdd across multiple eqtl and pqtl datasets. these genes are involved in biological processes related to neuroinflammation, immune regulation, and apoptosis. colocalization analyses supported shared genetic signals between the identified genes and mdd, while phenome‐wide analyses identified associations with additional diseases and traits that may be relevant for future translational research. through mr analysis, six candidate druggable genes were prioritized from 6889 potential druggable genes as significantly associated with mdd. among them, mapk3, mst1, and siglec9 showed consistent evidence across multiple analyses and emerged as genetically supported candidate targets for future investigation. genes brain and behavior

daily subjective nearness to death and well-being among older adults in samples from four countries subjective nearness to death (sntd), referring to how close one perceives oneself to death, relates to various health outcomes. while daily variations in views of aging have been demonstrated, whether sntd fluctuates and covaries with well-being over short-term time frames remains unclear. whether country-based recruitment contexts modify these daily associations also remains underexplored. respondents ( n = 197, mean age = 64.30, range = 50–90) who participated in the subjective ages (subjective aging within global everyday ecological studies) consortium rated sntd and psychological, cognitive, and physical well-being indices, including negative affect, memory failures, and somatic symptoms, across 14 consecutive days. we recruited participants as convenience samples in israel, türkiye, the united kingdom, and the united states. sntd showed significant daily fluctuations. furthermore, on days when participants felt closer to death than usual, they reported higher negative affect, more memory failures, and more somatic symptoms. secondary exploratory analyses indicated stronger daily covariation between sntd and well-being indices in the israeli sample and weaker covariation in the american sample. these findings indicate that sntd exhibits significant daily fluctuations that align with older adults’ daily experiences. the primary findings support daily sntd-well-being coupling. the differences across the country samples are preliminary and suggest a need to examine contextual moderators in future research. international journal of behavioral development

building confianza, sharing consejos: a grounded theory study of latine mothers' socialization of coping abstract adolescence is a critical developmental period characterized by common stressors such as academic pressures and changing family and peer dynamics that may be exacerbated by additional stressors, such as acculturative stress, language barriers, and discrimination, for latine youth. cultural values of familismo (familism; loyalty to family) and respeto (respect; obedience, deference to authority) may play an important role in latine parents' socialization of coping (soc) messages about how to manage stressful situations, with implications for latine youths' coping and well‐being. yet, culturally specific approaches to parents' soc in the literature are scarce. toward theory building via grounded theory methods, this study focused on how latine parents socialize youth to cope with interpersonal and academic stressors with a sample of 23 majority mexican‐origin participants: 12 mothers ( m age = 40.08 years) and 11 adolescents ( m age = 14.36 years; 18% boys, 82% girls). mothers and adolescents each participated in a one‐time, 1.5‐h semi‐structured interview (spanish or english). mothers shared their experiences in providing advice regarding coping with interpersonal and academic stress. the resulting analysis presents a theoretical model of how latine mothers guide youth to cope with stress and the role of cultural values (familismo, respeto) in this process. results highlight the central role of fomentando confianza (building trust) as a foundational relational context enabling latine mothers to guide their adolescents in managing stressors and mothers' advice of prioritizing relational harmony, refocusing expectations, encouraging effort, and redefining agency, all of which are embedded within cultural values. this grounded theory model refines existing theories of parenting and coping socialization and advances understanding of relational contexts and cultural processes that may support latine adolescent well‐being. journal of research on adolescence
spatial geographies of biphobia and resilience among school-going lesbian, bisexual, and nonbinary girls with visual impairment in south africa journal of homosexuality

body posture and divergent thinking in sport-major and non-sport-major university students: an embodied cognition perspective objective: to explore divergent thinking under open and closed seated postures and its association with educational background. methods: thirty university students (15 sport-major and 15 non-sport-major students) completed an alternative uses task under both posture conditions. originality and flexibility were scored with transdis and analyzed using mixed-design anovas and additional frequentist and bayesian analyses. all analyses were exploratory. results: originality was higher in the closed condition in both groups, f(1, 28) = 111.68, p < .001, partial η2 = 0.800. sport-major students also showed higher originality overall. the posture × group interaction was nominally significant (p = .031), but the evidence for moderation was not fully convergent across sensitivity, bayesian, and predictive analyses. flexibility showed a less conclusive posture contrast (nominal p = .045); neither this term nor the originality interaction survived a six-test multiplicity adjustment. conclusions: the findings identify a context-specific association between seated posture and semantic-distance originality. the unusually large contrast in this small exploratory sample warrants replication with standardized manipulation checks and fluency metrics. journal of intelligence

human and ai judgment in efl speaking assessment: psychometric dependability, feedback quantity and coverage, and exploratory teacher perspectives this study examined human-ai judgment in efl speaking assessment as a measurement problem relevant to research on individual differences: how consistently do expert raters and repeated ai sessions preserve between-person differences in a complex performance? thirty oral-performance samples from first-year chinese university english majors were evaluated by four experienced efl teachers and by chatgpt-4o across four repeated sessions using the same holistic and accuracy-fluency-complexity framework. score distributions were summarized descriptively; human-rater intraclass correlations and generalizability-theory g- and d-studies evaluated dependability. feedback quantity and thematic coverage were summarized descriptively, and post-results interviews with the same four teacher-raters were analyzed as exploratory participant reflections. teachers produced more dependable single ratings. holistic phi coefficients were 0.54 for one chatgpt-4o session and 0.65 for one teacher, increasing to 0.83 and 0.88 with four assessments. analytic single-assessment coefficients ranged from 0.54 to 0.56 for chatgpt-4o and 0.61 to 0.65 for teachers. across holistic and analytic scoring, a phi coefficient of at least 0.80 was reached with four repeated chatgpt-4o sessions but three independent teachers. chatgpt-4o’s analytic dimensions showed limited differentiation from its holistic scoring: accuracy matched the holistic score in all 120 ai ratings, while fluency and complexity differed in only three and four ratings, respectively. chatgpt-4o also produced more rubric-relevant comments descriptively, while the four teacher-raters emphasized human oversight for contextual and interpersonal interpretation. the study contributes to intelligence research at the level of psychometric measurement and human-ai judgment: assessor systems can differentially preserve observed individual differences in complex performance. efl speaking was not treated as an intelligence test, and unmeasured cognitive mechanisms were not inferred from the score patterns. journal of intelligence

longitudinal interrelations of career adaptability dimensions among students in general upper secondary school this study utilized a cross-lagged panel analysis to examine the longitudinal interrelations among the four dimensions of career adaptability—namely, concern, control, curiosity, and confidence—during general upper secondary education and to examine their association with intentional gap year planning at the end of upper secondary school. the participants (214 boys and 243 girls) were finnish general upper secondary school students from six different schools who completed questionnaires at three time points across their three-year academic program. the results revealed moderate stability and strong concurrent associations among the assessed dimensions, but relatively few cross-lagged effects (i.e., concern predicting later curiosity, control predicting later confidence). there were also dynamic, partly reversing associations identified between concern and control across time. in the final year of the academic program, higher career control was associated with a greater likelihood of planning an intentional gap year. taken together, these findings suggest that career adaptability operates as a dynamic system of interacting resources whose role in career-related decisions varies across time and decision-making contexts. journal of career assessment

executive function impairment in depression? – estimating the role of socioeconomic influences through mixed-model meta-analyses abstract previous research syntheses have found cognitive impairment in depression—even in the remitted stage. open questions pertain to the influence of socioeconomic status (ses) differences and to the role of aging. our research synthesis focuses on executive function (ef) impairment and investigates the extent of ef impairment in younger individuals (adolescents, young adults) diagnosed with depression, and whether family ses exerts an influence. literature searches in bibliographic databases (medline/ovid and wos up to april 2025) yielded k = 93 observed effects (k = 30 pertaining to inhibitory control [ic], k = 30 to working memory [wm], and k = 33 to cognitive flexibility [fl]) from 58 case–control studies. we used random-effects models and tested the moderator effects of adjustment for indicators of family ses through mixed-effects models (prospero: crd420251024704). the overall weighted mean effect sizes (hedges’ g) were: -0.35 (ci95%: -0.48, -0.22), -0.56 (ci95%: -0.73, -0.40), -0.24 (ci95%:-0.45, -0.03) for ic, wm, and fl, respectively. the moderator effect of adjustment for family ses was significant for ic (p = .026) and wm (p = .003). within the subsample of studies that adjusted for ses differences, mean effects were small (ic: -0.22 [ci95%: -0.37, -0.082] k = 10, wm: -0.28 [ci95%: -0.48, -0.08] k = 8) and not heterogenous (i.e. cochran’s q test was not significant). relative to healthy individuals, adolescents and young adults with depression primarily show wm problems. however, relative to healthy individuals with a comparable family ses background, they do not show substantial ef impairment. neuropsychology review
the path to recovery: treatment adherence mediates the effect of subjective age on rehabilitation outcomes in older adults psychology & health

meaning in life and physical health in middle-aged and older adulthood: a narrative review as populations age, identifying psychological resources that support healthy aging and preserve physical functioning has become increasingly important. although meaning in life (mil) has been associated with better health and well-being, its associations with objective physical health outcomes and the mechanisms underlying these associations remain incompletely understood. this review synthesized recent evidence on the associations of mil and purpose in life (pil) with physical health and examined potential underlying mechanisms. overall, higher mil and pil were generally associated with favorable physical health outcomes, including indicators of slower biological aging, better physical functioning and quality of life, and lower mortality risk. however, much of the evidence, particularly for mortality, physical functioning, and biological indicators, was derived from studies assessing pil, limiting the generalizability of these findings to the broader construct of mil. moreover, these associations were heterogeneous and context-dependent, varying across health outcomes and study populations. behavioral, psychosocial, and biological pathways have been proposed as potential mechanisms underlying these associations, although their interrelationships and causal sequences have not been sufficiently established. to integrate these findings, this review proposes a hypothetical conceptual cascade framework encompassing multiple levels of health, ranging from biological states and subjective health to physical functioning and survival. taken together, the findings suggest that mil and pil may be conceptualized as upstream psychological resources associated with multiple dimensions of physical health. nevertheless, further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and causal directions of these associations. health psychology research

associations of job satisfaction and job stress with personality changes across the retirement transition: a conceptual replication of schimanski et al. (2026a). the workplace is an important context for adult development. consequently, retiring causes profound shifts in social interactions, daily routines, and personal identity. nevertheless, there is limited research on how specific work-related factors are related to personality changes, particularly during the retirement transition. the present study is a conceptual replication of schimanski et al. (2026a) examining associations of preretirement job satisfaction and job stress with big five personality trait changes across the retirement transition. using data from the 2006 to 2016 waves of the health and retirement study (hrs), we identified 771 individuals (44-83 years at baseline,= 60.95 years,= 5.59; 60% women) who retired within this period. we additionally identified a propensity-score-matched control group of 771 individuals who continued to work (42-82 years at baseline,= 60.72,= 5.91; 61% women). multigroup latent change score models were calculated based on the last wave before and first wave after retirement or two consecutive waves of continued employment, respectively, with the two waves being 4 years apart. in both groups, neuroticism decreased significantly, while openness decreased only among retirees. preretirement job satisfaction and job stress were significantly related to baseline personality trait levels but not to changes. the results are consistent with schimanski et al. overall, our findings suggest that retirement has minimal long-term effects on personality, and job satisfaction and job stress do not shape personality changes during this transition. the discussion focuses on implications for future studies regarding methodological approaches and possible predictors of change. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). psychology and aging

the more, the better? evidence of parallel growth in intergroup contact quantity and quality over time. intergroup contact is a central feature of intergroup relations, yet research has largely examined its quantity and quality as separate, static predictors of intergroup attitudes, leaving relatively little known about how these dimensions themselves develop over time. we examine this question in four longitudinal studies across contexts and age groups, each including both majority and minority group members. study 1 followed white british and asian british adolescents undergoing a school merger in the united kingdom (= 660, three waves). study 2 involved catholic and protestant youths participating in a peacebuilding program in northern ireland (= 592, three waves). study 3 tracked british and international students transitioning to university (= 527, four waves), and study 4 followed catholic and protestant children in northern ireland from the start of their secondary education (= 3,057, three waves). using latent growth modeling, we tracked how contact quantity and quality changed over time and how these trajectories were linked. across all studies, we observed significant cogrowth with steeper increases in contact frequency corresponding with greater improvements in interaction quality. when positive and negative valence were measured separately (studies 3 and 4), growth in contact quantity was associated with increased interaction positivity, while changes in negativity remained minimal and nonsignificantly related to contact frequency. these findings suggest that intergroup contact is itself a dynamic experience: changes in how frequently people engage in contact are systematically related to changes in how positively they experience that contact. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). journal of personality and social psychology

application of a brief, personality-based intervention for borderline personality disorder for a patient with intersecting identities: a bpd compass case study. borderline personality disorder (bpd) is a heterogeneous condition characterized by emotion dysregulation, interpersonal dysfunction, impulsivity, identity disturbance, and elevated rates of co-occurrence with other mental health conditions. criterion b of the alternative model of personality disorders (ampd) conceptualizes bpd symptoms as manifestations of dimensional personality traits, particularly negative affectivity, antagonism, and disinhibition. bpd compass (cognitive-behavioral modules for personality symptoms) is an 18-session modular cognitive-behavioral intervention designed to target these higher-order personality dimensions and their underlying maintenance mechanisms. this article presents a detailed case study illustrating the application of bpd compass with a 25-year-old bisexual appalachian woman diagnosed with bpd, persistent depressive disorder, binge eating disorder, and subclinical social anxiety disorder. treatment integrated values clarification, cognitive flexibility, behavioral skills, and mindfulness strategies tailored to the patient's cultural and identity-related experiences. throughout treatment, interventions were personalized to address the impact of appalachian cultural norms, minority stress related to sexual identity, emotional avoidance, interpersonal mistrust, and impulsive coping behaviors. by posttreatment, the patient demonstrated substantial reductions in bpd symptom severity, with zanarini rating scale scores decreasing from 23 to 6. she no longer met criteria for binge eating disorder or clinically significant social anxiety symptoms and reported meaningful improvements in emotion regulation, interpersonal functioning, and impulse control. journal of clinical psychology
longitudinal associations between positive life events and depression: the roles of optimism and self-schemata. journal of psychopathology and clinical science
evidence of limited biases in probed language-based assessments. journal of psychopathology and clinical science
the impact of health care access, resilience, and social support on health among older sexual minority women with disabilities. psychology of sexual orientation and gender diversity

a pilot study of brief school-based cognitive–behavioral therapy with defusion exercises for students with behavioral inhibition system dominance: preliminary evidence for temperament-tailored stress intervention. international journal of stress management

why would others help me?: how people explain why they can (or cannot) rely on family and friends most people count on family and friends to assist them in times of need; this study asks why people think that they can count on them. we coded about 1,100 respondents’ open-ended explanations for why they could—or could not—rely on relatives and friends in a crisis, yielding about a dozen main themes. respondents largely explained that relatives would help because of affection, secondarily because of relatives’ past support or norms of obligation. the small minority who doubted relatives’ help said that they had no kin ties, pointed to practical impediments, or claimed no need for relatives’ help. respondents explained friends’ help in similar ways. three master themes emerged: sentiment, exchange history, and practical impediments. younger respondents emphasized sentiment to explain family help, women more often cited past exchanges, and the better-educated stressed exchange history with relatives but sentiment with friends. the heavy emphasis on personal affection departs from main accounts in the social support literature. social psychology quarterly

psychological treatment utilization following motor vehicle accident exposure: an exploratory longitudinal study background: motor vehicle accidents (mvas) are associated with elevated psychological distress, yet many affected individuals do not seek psychological treatment, despite it being generally available within the health care system. objective: this exploratory prospective cohort study examined psychological distress, psychological treatment utilization, and perceived barriers over 12 months among individuals with and without mva exposure. methods: individuals with (n = 60) and without (n = 108) mva exposure completed two online surveys 12 months apart. psychological distress was assessed using the brief symptom checklist and the posttraumatic stress disorder checklist for dsm-5. utilization of psychological treatment and perceived barriers were also measured. analyses compared distress between groups, examined associations between distress and treatment utilization, explored an indirect association of mva exposure with treatment utilization via baseline distress, compared perceived barriers, and examined continuity in treatment utilization over time. results: mva-exposed individuals reported higher distress than unexposed individuals (d = 0.53, confidence interval [ci]: 0.14–0.92). mva exposure was not associated with treatment utilization (b = −0.10, ci: −0.74–0.55), but it was indirectly associated through elevated baseline distress (b = 0.25, ci: 0.05–0.45). no group differences emerged in perceived barriers. previous psychological treatment was associated with treatment utilization during follow-up independent of baseline distress (b = 2.43, ci: 1.04–3.99). conclusion: mva-exposed individuals reported persistently elevated psychological distress but were no more likely than unexposed individuals to receive psychological treatment. these exploratory findings suggest that specific factors may limit help-seeking following mvas despite elevated psychological distress. future research should identify these factors using larger samples and more comprehensive barrier assessment. health psychology research
trajectories of emotional and social intelligences and internalizing symptoms in primary school children across a post-pandemic school year discover psychology

understanding perceptions of school climate among asian-indian american adolescents asian-indian americans represent among the largest asian subgroups in the usa. nevertheless, studies of the school experiences of asian-indian american (aia) youth are limited. whereas within-group differences in school climate perceptions have been investigated for other minoritized racial-ethnic groups, no such studies have been conducted with aia youth with origins in india. more importantly, limited studies have examined response patterns with minoritized ethnic populations. the present study utilized latent class analysis (lca) to identify classes of school climate perceptions among 10th-grade aia students ( n = 460) in california as well as to provide insight into how aia youth respond to school climate items. the results of the lca suggested five categories and revealed that about 60% of aia students perceived their school climate positively. notably, more than two-thirds of respondents reported negative perceptions of meaningful participation at school. relative to their reports in other areas of school climate, aia students also reported feeling less involved in making decisions and advocating for themselves within the school system. the discussion of results explores similarities and differences in findings as compared with other student populations; it also considers implications for further scholarship and practice. school psychology international

icon arrays: a key to pictures that effectively aid statistical reasoning abstract statistical reasoning is often aided by a picture illustrating the data, but why pictures help is a matter of both empirical and theoretical debate. to help resolve both types of debates, this research compared identical reasoning tasks with pictures of the same overall shape but different internal features. experiment 1 found that the best performances occurred when people were given clearly distinct icons (either organized or scattered), followed by overlapping icons, and the worst performance was with a picture of solid fields (no icons). experiment 2, with a different and more complex reasoning task, found the best performances again with distinct icons (organized or scattered) and the poorest performance with the solid field picture (slightly below a control condition of no picture). experiment 3 further replicated and extended these findings across different texts, icons, and colors. participants also completed measures of numerical literacy, visuospatial ability, set reasoning ability, graph literacy, and nonmathematical cognitive reflection. all were correlated with bayesian reasoning performance, as well as each other, but only numeracy showed consistent predictive ability. in addition to practical implications for effective communication of quantitative information, these results support a view that the mind is designed to more effectively use discrete individuated items in statistical reasoning. journal of behavioral decision making

psychological distress and mental health support in a cohort of south africans living with diabetes diabetes mellitus (dm) affects millions of people worldwide. the international diabetes federation (idf) estimates that nearly 60 million south africans will be affected by 2050. diabetes is one of the most complex chronic conditions, and the burden of the disease extends beyond the physical and adversely impacts emotional and psychological well-being. limited mental health resources are often dedicated to dm treatment. this study intended to describe the psychological distress of people living with diabetes (plwd) and their views regarding the accessibility and quality of mental health support. the study was conducted with a south african sample using a cross-sectional research design with a survey method for data collection. participants were recruited using purposive sampling via facebook diabetes support groups, and 253 participants ( n = 253) completed a demographic questionnaire and the patient health questionnaire (phq-9). the findings show that 23.7% presented with moderate depression, 19.4% presented with moderately severe depression and 13% presented with severe depression. there were significant differences between younger and older participants in relation to their phq-9 scores. in relation to mental health support, 41.9% of participants indicated a preference for in-person mental health support and 49.8% of the sample advocated that mental health support must be tailored for people with diabetes. participants also highlighted the unaffordability of mental health support. the research highlights the mental health challenges faced by plwd, and the findings can be used to guide the development of quality and accessible mental health interventions for dm patients in a multicultural context where health disparities are evident. south african journal of psychology

the associations between depressive symptoms, excessive reassurance‐seeking, and the quality of romantic relationships in young adult couples: a dyadic longitudinal mediation model abstract this study used a dyadic mediation model to examine actor and partner effects in the associations between depressive symptoms and the quality of romantic relationships, both directly and indirectly via excessive reassurance‐seeking. a total of 105 heterosexual young adult couples participated in a three‐wave longitudinal study (waves 1‐month apart) through the prolific platform. participants completed measures of depressive symptoms, excessive reassurance‐seeking, and multiple dimensions of romantic relationship qualities at each time point. after controlling for autoregressive and reciprocal effects, several direct and indirect actor and partner effects emerged. direct actor effects were only significant for men (not women), showing that when men reported higher depressive symptoms at time 1, they experienced greater companionship, intimate disclosure, and emotional support at time 3. direct partner effects were significant for both women and men, indicating that when women reported higher depressive symptoms at time 1, their partners experienced less companionship and satisfaction at time 3. however, when men reported higher depressive symptoms at time 1, their partners reported receiving less criticism at time 3. in terms of indirect effects, depressive symptoms in men at time 1 predicted their higher reassurance‐seeking at time 2, which, in turn, predicted increased partners' perceptions of being criticized and excluded at time 3 (actor–partner effects). conversely, depressive symptoms in women at time 1 predicted higher partners' reassurance‐seeking at time 2, which, in turn, predicted decreased women's perceptions of being criticized and excluded at time 3 (partner–partner effects). these findings highlight the complex interpersonal dynamics of depressive symptoms in young adult romantic relationships and suggest that men's excessive reassurance‐seeking may be one potential pathway linking individuals' depressive symptoms with their own and their partners' perceptions and behaviors within romantic relationships. personal relationships

prenatal sars‐cov‐2 infection, covid‐19 vaccination, and preschool neurodevelopment: a confounder‐adjusted cohort study abstract background the impact of maternal sars‐cov‐2 infection and covid‐19 vaccination during pregnancy on child neurodevelopment remains unclear, with most studies limited by small samples and short follow‐up periods. this prospective cohort study assesses internalizing, externalizing, total problem behaviors, and social responsiveness in children prenatally exposed or unexposed to maternal sars‐cov‐2 infection or covid‐19 vaccination. methods the study leveraged a large nyc pregnancy cohort with detailed information on maternal infection and vaccination during pregnancy. outcomes included parent‐reported cbcl and srs. analyses were adjusted for key sociodemographic and clinical factors, including race/ethnicity, maternal mental health condition, and child age at assessment. results the study included 675 children (mean age = 3.2 years, sd = 0.8, 50.7% male), comprising 118 children prenatally exposed to sars‐cov‐2 and 557 unexposed. regression analyses showed no significant associations between prenatal sars‐cov‐2 exposure and cbcl internalizing ( β = 0.04 [95% ci: −0.85, 0.88]), cbcl externalizing ( β = −0.31 [95% ci: −1.41, 0.87]), cbcl total problems ( β = −0.50 [95% ci: −3.46, 2.51]), and srs ( β = −0.60 [95% ci: −4.09, 3.17]) scores. comparing children prenatally exposed ( n = 68) and unexposed ( n = 607) to covid‐19 vaccination revealed no significant associations with cbcl internalizing ( β = 0.41 [95% ci: −0.52, 1.44]), cbcl externalizing ( β = 1.42 [95% ci: −0.32, 2.95]), cbcl total problems ( β = 2.13 [95% ci: −1.22, 6.15]), and srs ( β = −3.65 [95% ci: −7.93, 0.32]) scores. sociodemographic covariates, such as race/ethnicity and educational attainment, were significantly associated with all neurodevelopmental outcomes. conclusion prenatal exposure to sars‐cov‐2 infection or covid‐19 vaccination was not associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in preschool children. sociodemographic factors showed stronger associations than infection or vaccination, underscoring the importance of confounder adjustment. findings provide reassurance to pregnant individuals regarding potential long‐term neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring following sars‐cov‐2 infection or covid‐19 vaccination during pregnancy. jcpp advances

the adaptive‐innovative ambidexterity framework: a qualitative exploration of ambidextrous technology use and adaptive outcomes the covid‐19 pandemic accelerated digitalisation across higher education (he), compelling employees to adapt rapidly to online work environments. more specifically, it explains how crisis‐induced improvisations were either left as temporary workarounds or, through learning, transformed into sustained, digitally enabled work practices and microinnovations. this qualitative study examines how employees in australian he administration engage in adaptive ambidextrous technology‐use behaviours, balancing the exploitation of familiar tools and the exploration of new functionalities, underpinned by bricolage and adaptive performance. using an interpretive qualitative approach, 38 semistructured interviews were thematically analysed with nvivo. the findings reveal that bricolage served as a catalyst for ambidextrous technology use, whereas adaptive performance behaviours and self‐directed and peer‐supported learning pathways mediated the sustainability of this use. these behaviours enhanced work‐related outcomes, including job satisfaction, productivity, error reduction, turnaround speed and task completion time. the study identifies innovative work practices as a novel outcome, where employees developed ‘microinnovations’ by reconfiguring workflows, automating tasks and integrating digital tools in new ways. this insight extends adaptive performance theory into the domain of creativity, bridging ambidexterity research with innovation management. the resulting adaptive‐innovative ambidexterity framework refines prior conceptualisations by situating bricolage as a catalyst, learning pathways as mediators and innovation as a distinct outcome. the study contributes theoretically by advancing microlevel understanding of adaptive ambidextrous technology use, and practically by highlighting how organisations can design digital strategies that foster both adaptation and innovation in postpandemic digital workplaces. human behavior and emerging technologies

differential biomarker associations of anxiety dimensions: a psycho-biological network analysis with external validation abstract introduction: anxiety involves dysregulation across peripheral biological systems, yet associations with specific dimensions remain unclear. we constructed a psycho-biological network linking anxiety dimensions with biomarkers spanning inflammation, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (hpa) axis, the sympathetic-adrenal-medullary (sam) axis, and metabolic regulation. methods: we conducted a cross-sectional network analysis using the midlife in the united states (midus) 3 biomarker project data (n=747). four network estimation approaches were compared, with ebicglasso selected as the primary model. an a priori psycho-biological mask was applied, and edge stability, bridge centrality, and community structure were assessed. the pipeline was validated in midus 2 (n=1,255) and midus refresher 1 (n=863). results: anxious arousal (masq(aa)) showed the strongest cross-system connectivity. the masq(aa)–c-reactive protein (crp) association was the only significant edge in the primary network (p=0.022, 95% ci [0.019, 0.164]) but was not replicated in validation cohorts. four candidate cross-system connectors were identified (masq(aa), crp, glucose, and tnfa), yet only masq(aa) was replicated across validation cohorts. inflammatory and metabolic interfaces showed limited reproducibility; hpa-axis and peripheral catecholaminergic biomarkers did not form stable cross-system bridges. network architecture showed poor reproducibility (jaccard=0.172 and 0.121; spearman ρ=0.296 and 0.225 for midus 2 and refresher 1, respectively), with limited community preservation. conclusion: anxiety dimensions showed differentiated but only partially reproducible psycho-biological connectivity. anxious arousal represents the most reproducible cross-system dimension, whereas the broader organization of anxiety-related peripheral biology is cohort-dependent. these findings support dimensional network analysis and the need for external validation and longitudinal investigation. neuropsychobiology

behavior analysis and game design: the contingencies of video game genres abstract this article proposes an integrated conceptual framework for analyzing video games through functional analysis, arguing that game design is fundamentally the arrangement of reinforcement and punishment contingencies. video game genres are functional systems defined by reinforcement schedules, operant punishment, and temporally extended consequences programmed in game environments. to illustrate this behavioral interpretation of video games, we conduct a functional analysis of the contingencies operating in three illustrative commercial genres: platformers (focused on precision and modeling), metroidvanias (based on conditional discrimination and interconnection of repertoires), and turn-based rpgs (governed by rules and chaining). furthermore, the game features that continue to shape player behavior were examined, including aesthetic elements and cross-genre metasystems, such as achievements, leaderboards, and loot boxes. the analysis demonstrates that successful game design is also successful contingency design. finally, we discuss the ethical implications of monetized metasystems (such as loot boxes) and propose that the principles of behavior analysis can be used to "reverse engineer" game design to illustrate how both experimental and applied domains can benefit from the consilience between behavior analysis and game design. perspectives on behavior science

peer review guidance to address selective reporting in single-case experimental design research abstract questionable research practices (qrps) inject bias into single-case experimental design (sced) research. a prominent qrp is selective reporting, the omission or selective depiction of data or research procedures to inflate the appearance of positive experimental effects. open and transparent research practices, including clear and appropriate research questions, transparent procedural reporting, and unbiased outcomes reporting, provide evidence that researchers have taken steps to avoid selective reporting in sced. peer reviewers have substantial influence in evaluating whether submitted articles reflect these practices. we provide explicit guidance for peer reviewers to appraise how sced research articles submitted for publication reflect open and transparent reporting as well as describe ways in which clear and constructive feedback to authors can reduce qrps in behavior science research. perspectives on behavior science

ethical dilemmas in contemporary school psychology practice: a descriptive survey of critical incidents abstract ethical decision making is a central component of contemporary school psychology practice, yet relatively little descriptive research has examined how practitioners evaluate ethically challenging situations across multiple dimensions of professional decision making. the present study provides a practice-focused descriptive examination of ethical critical incidents encountered in school psychology. participants included 159 practicing school psychologists and graduate trainees in the united states who completed a survey consisting of 29 ethical critical incident scenarios. for each scenario, participants rated the likelihood of encountering the situation in practice, perceived ethical severity, probability of harm, legal implications, and difficulty of determining an appropriate ethical course of action. results indicated that practitioners differentiated ethical situations across these dimensions rather than viewing them as uniformly problematic. boundary-related situations were among the most frequently encountered but were generally perceived as involving relatively low ethical severity and limited potential for harm. in contrast, incidents involving professional competence, confidentiality, discrimination, and parental rights were perceived as substantially more serious, more harmful, and more likely to involve legal implications despite occurring less frequently. situations involving competing professional responsibilities, compromised professional effectiveness, and access to student records were perceived as particularly difficult to resolve. these findings suggest that ethical complexity in school psychology extends beyond identifying ethical violations alone and reflects the interaction of ethical, legal, contextual, and professional considerations. by documenting practitioners’ perceptions across multiple dimensions of ethical decision making, the present study provides practice-relevant evidence that may inform ethics education, supervision, consultation, and continuing professional development for school psychologists. contemporary school psychology

diferencias de género en el desempeño matemático en los primeros años de escolaridad en colombia international studies show a relatively early emergence of a gap favoring boys over girls in various tests of mathematical skills. this gap tends to appear in the first years of primary school and continues to grow throughout the years of schooling. the current study sought to examine the performance of colombian girls and boys on several tests of specific mathematical skills that are foundational in the development of mathematical knowledge. additionally, it aimed to examine the possible role of contextual variables, such as parental occupational level, in differences in mathematics performance. to these ends, we used a database from a previous study that recorded the performance on various mathematical skills of a sample of students (n = 96) from first and second grade in the city of cali, colombia. the analyses revealed significant differences favoring boys on the number comparison, number line, and number facts tasks, but not on arithmetic and geometry tasks. parental occupation only influenced performance on the number comparison task. these results indicate that in first and second grade, performance differences are specific to certain mathematical skills. the article discusses the educational implications of these findings. universitas psychologica

empirical development of the volitional apathy scale: a brief measure of behavioral initiation and maintenance. objective: apathy, a clinical symptom commonly found in many brain conditions, is characterized by quantitative reductions in goal-directed behavior. although apathy is widely conceptualized as multidimensional, existing measures vary in how its behavioral aspect is operationalized, limiting precision in the assessment of initiation and maintenance of goal-directed behavior. this study aimed to develop and validate a brief, behaviorally specific measure of apathy that addresses this inconsistency by capturing observable reductions in initiation and maintenance of goal-directed behavior.
method: candidate items were systematically reviewed from established scales against a behavior-focused operational definition of apathy. six items proceeded to exploratory factor analysis in a mixed sample of individuals with neurodegenerative brain disorders and healthy controls (sample 1;= 173). confirmatory factor analysis was subsequently conducted in an independent, transdiagnostic clinical sample including neurological and psychiatric conditions (sample 2;= 148). reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity were examined using well-established functional, motivational, and cognitive measures.
results: the scale development process resulted in a parsimonious, four-item "volitional apathy scale" with a unidimensional structure. the scale demonstrated good model fit, acceptable-to-strong internal consistency across samples (α = .75-.88; ω = .76-.88), and robust convergent validity with independent measures, controlling for the effects of age, education, and global cognition.
conclusions: the volitional apathy scale is a brief measure of the behavioral expression of apathy, capturing observable reductions in the initiation and maintenance of goal-directed activity. the scale offers a precise, parsimonious, and psychometrically supported transdiagnostic tool for apathy assessment in clinical and research contexts. group‐based schema therapy for difficult‐to‐treat depression: a qualitative evaluation of active ingredients abstract objectives difficult‐to‐treat depression (dtd) is characterized by persistent symptoms despite adequate prior treatment. group‐based schema therapy (gst) is increasingly used in this population, yet empirical knowledge of its active ingredients remains limited. design this qualitative study explored patients' perspectives on factors facilitating or hindering recovery during gst. methods semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 13 patients with dtd after completing gst and analysed using inductive thematic analysis. transcripts were independently coded by different researchers until consensus and data saturation were reached. results facilitating factors included group processes such as cohesion, mutual support and experiencing recognition, experiential techniques, including imagery and chair work, and therapists' active engagement. increased awareness of maladaptive schema modes, particularly the critical mode, and strengthening adaptive modes were also perceived as beneficial. barriers included difficult group dynamics, the burden of homework and the complexity of the schema model. beyond common group therapeutic factors, patients identified experiential techniques as central to gst effectiveness. conclusions by altering dysfunctional patterns, evoking corrective emotional experiences and promoting the healthy adult mode, gst supported recovery in patients with dtd. these findings are consistent with previous research on (group) st for other disorders and offer guidance for further refinement and tailoring of gst for dtd. british journal of clinical psychology

lack of heterogeneous study samples in farm animal cognition research. farm animals have received limited attention in animal cognition research, despite their numbers and biomass surpassing all other mammalian species, including humans. nevertheless, studying farm animal cognition can yield benefits for both fundamental and applied research. first, in a comparative context, cognitive research on farm animals and their wild counterparts can provide insights into how domestication has shaped the evolution of the brain, including our own. second, in an applied context, understanding the cognitive processes of farm animals can improve our knowledge of how they perceive their environment and how their environment shapes their cognitive development, helping to inform better husbandry practices that meet their abilities and needs. to examine the characteristics of farm animal cognition studies, we conducted a scoping review of the cognition literature on cattle, pigs, sheep, and goats, focusing on potential biases in study samples. these species were well represented across different cognitive task types (learning, physical, social, and other), though learning tasks and pig studies were slightly overrepresented. most studies were conducted on single breeds at single sites (which were most often research sites), with an overrepresentation of females and young animals (i.e., under one year), limiting the generalizability of findings and our interpretation of fully developed cognitive capacities in these species. geographically, the majority of studies originated from north america or europe, restricting international representation and limiting insights into local breeds across the globe. these sample biases reduce diversity, compromise generalizability, and can hinder broader understanding of farm animal cognition - knowledge that is crucial for understanding the impact of domestication on the brain and for improving husbandry practices to meet farm animals' perceptual and cognitive needs. we conclude by proposing strategies to achieve more diverse and representative study populations in farm animal cognition to mitigate the above-mentioned shortcomings. topics in cognitive science

spelling profile assessment (spa): a new spelling test for english primary school children; standardization. 拼写能力评估（spa）：一种面向英国小学儿童的新型拼写测验及其标准化 we present the construction, psychometric evaluation, and administration of a new single-word spelling battery that includes: a. irregular (e.g., yacht) and regular (e.g., trap) words and pseudowords (e.g., knep) (n = 87), and b. a morphological spelling test with real words (20 affixes/seven suffixation rules) and pseudowords (mirroring the rules of the real words) (n = 40). after the pilot phase, the final battery was standardized on 1053 children (year_r to year_6 f = 514). the battery across tasks presents outstanding reliability (.97 to .99), and criterion and convergent validity were compared with the wechsler individual achievement test-third uk edition (wechsler, 2009) spelling subtest. the spelling profile assessment (spa) battery provides standard scores (mean = 100, sd = 15) per subtask, a total composite standard score for each test (a and b) and 95% confidence intervals. we calculated age-based standard scores using a continuous developmental trajectory rather than assigning individuals to fixed age groups. we model gradual developmental change to provide a more precise score. the test also includes a stopping rule, which streamlines its administration and reduces stress for children who can only spell a limited number of items. additionally, we automated every step of the standardization process and made it available under open access, ensuring transparency, reproducibility, and ease of adaptation. this tool contributes to the spelling literature by offering a comprehensive battery for assessing phonological, orthographic, and morphological spelling skills in primary-age children. it can serve as a valuable tool for educators/clinicians to gauge students' progression and tailor their spelling instruction accordingly. behavior research methods

when do missed prompts matter? a simulation and empirical sensitivity study of structured nonresponse in intensive longitudinal assessment. 遗漏提示何时重要？密集纵向评估中结构化无应答的模拟与实证敏感性研究 inference in intensive longitudinal assessment depends on whether observed prompts adequately represent the construct or phenomenon under scrutiny. when missed prompts are systematically related to unobserved momentary states, response rate summaries and missing data-adjusted estimates may underestimate clinically meaningful outcomes. using suicidal ideation as a high-stakes exemplar, this project evaluated structured nonresponse in two linked studies. study 1 used monte carlo simulation to examine recovery of complete-schedule momentary suicidal ideation prevalence across response mechanism (missing completely at random, missing at random, symptom-dependent missing not at random [mnar], disengagement-driven mnar), target response rate, and volatility-dependent missingness. simulation parameters were determined based on empirical research and calibration to varied mnar assumptions. six estimators were evaluated: observed response mean, last observation carried forward, g-computation, inverse probability weighting, augmented inverse probability weighting, and targeted maximum likelihood estimation. under missing completely at random and missing at random, estimators were approximately unbiased or modest with coverage deterioration in lower response and volatility-dependent conditions. under mnar mechanisms, all estimators underestimated complete-schedule prevalence. study 2 applied a delta-shift sensitivity analysis to an open ecological momentary assessment data set. even with 90.3% item observability, stronger outcome-enrichment assumptions for missed prompts increased estimated complete-schedule prevalence from 5.94% to 7.24%. findings indicate that high response rates and robust estimators do not guarantee valid intensive longitudinal assessment when nonresponse is structured by unobserved risk states. simulation and empirical illustration results should be considered in the context of study parameters and calibration decisions. design-stage planning and delta-shift sensitivity analyses can help researchers evaluate, reduce, and transparently report potential bias from structured nonresponse.
