ai ‘slop’ is a social judgement nature human behaviour, published online: 09 november 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02639-6 artificial intelligence (ai)-generated content increasingly saturates our information environment. efforts to detect and remove it are failing. we propose that calling ai-generated content ‘slop’ is best understood as a social judgement: what a community recognizes as unwanted ai content. studying ai slop this way makes it tractable, measurable and governable. nature human behaviour

cultural impacts on memory and their applications in legal, clinical and political settings 文化对记忆的影响及其在法律、临床和政治情境中的应用 nature reviews psychology, published online: 09 november 2026; doi:10.1038/s44159-026-00637-z memory construction is inextricable from culture and has critical consequences for one’s identity, actions and mental health. in this review, wang et al. synthesize the intersections between culture and memory, focusing on memory for specific events and highlighting legal, clinical and political settings. 记忆建构与文化不可分割，并对个体身份、行动和心理健康具有重要后果。 nature reviews psychology

algorithmic item generation of spatial ability items: a cognitive design system approach item generation based on the item model approach can efficiently produce a large number of items at a low cost, but fails to guarantee and evaluate the construct validity of the generated items. to achieve more scientific item generation and validity testing for spatial ability, this study developed an item generation algorithm for spatial ability based on the cognitive design system (cds) approach and evaluated the construct validity of the generated items. a total of 624 mental rotation items were efficiently generated via the algorithm and administered to 3846 primary and secondary school students. the results indicate that the four construct-relevant design variables formulating the algorithm all significantly affected item difficulty, accounting for 72.6% of the variance in item difficulty. furthermore, the nomothetic span analysis revealed that scores of the developed mental rotation test significantly correlated with scores from tests measuring visuospatial working memory, paper folding, and mathematics. in contrast, statistically significant correlations were not detected between the mental rotation test and the tests measuring cognitive processing speed and chinese language. these findings provide initial evidence supporting both the rationality of utilizing the cds approach to generate mental rotation items and the construct representation of the generated items, while offering tentative empirical observations regarding their nomothetic span. journal of intelligence

longitudinal changes in adolescent e‐cigarette use intentions: risk and protective factors abstract e‐cigarette use among adolescents in guam, a u.s.‐affiliated pacific island in the western pacific, is more prevalent than in the u.s. overall. this disparity underscores the importance of understanding why and how adolescents in guam intend to use e‐cigarettes. using data from a three‐wave survey collected over 4 months in middle schools, we examined risk and protective factors associated with longitudinal changes in the intention to use e‐cigarettes ( n = 538; 10–15 years old, m = 12.45, sd = .94, 52% male, 48% female). in parallel process latent growth curve modeling (pp‐lgcm), the results showed that, at the intercept and slope, e‐cigarette social influence, e‐cigarette peer influence, perceived permissiveness of e‐cigarette use, and depressive symptoms positively predicted the intention to use e‐cigarettes across time, while parental support negatively predicted it. additionally, latent growth mixture modeling (lgmm) revealed three groups of adolescents with different trajectories of e‐cigarette use intentions: high‐increasing, low‐decreasing, and moderate‐increasing. the results also indicated that peer influence regarding e‐cigarettes predicted membership in the high‐increasing group more strongly and membership in the low‐decreasing group less strongly than membership in the moderate‐increasing group. social influence and depressive symptoms predicted membership in the high‐increasing or moderate‐increasing group more strongly than membership in the low‐decreasing group. the results and their implications are discussed in the context of pacific island culture. journal of research on adolescence

enhancing relationship strengths in immigrant and refugee families: examining the feasibility and acceptability of the anchor parenting program abstract supportive parent–child relationships enable adolescents to navigate developmental transitions, respond to discrimination, strengthen ethnic‐racial identity, and maintain well‐being. yet migration‐related stressors, including systemic barriers, economic insecurity, parent–child acculturation gaps, and shifts in family roles, can strain these relationships. this paper reports a single‐group pre‐post evaluation of anchor (advancing newcomer caregivers' harmony, openness, and resilience), a strength‐based, community‐informed program designed to support immigrant and refugee caregivers of adolescents. grounded in attachment‐based relational processes, anchor aims to strengthen parents' ability to serve as a secure base and source of guidance throughout adolescence. across 11 program deliveries involving 116 caregivers, 96 completed satisfaction surveys and provided qualitative feedback and 48 also completed pre‐ and post‐program assessments of parenting and relationship strengths. among caregivers with pre‐post data, repeated measures analysis of covariance (ancovas) indicated significant increases in parenting efficacy, parental empathy, and parent–child congruence. reflexive thematic analysis identified perceived improvements in emotionally attuned communication, appreciation of children's perspectives, confidence in supporting adolescents' needs and navigating a new sociocultural context, and trust and connection within parent–adolescent relationships. caregivers also emphasized the importance of a supportive group process that centered cultural strengths. these results suggest that anchor is a feasible and acceptable intervention for immigrant and refugee caregivers (82.3% women) and provide preliminary evidence of improvements in parenting confidence, empathy, and parent–adolescent relationships. further evaluation using more rigorous controlled designs is warranted. journal of research on adolescence

investigating causal relationships between major mental disorders and hypertension subtypes and their complications: a mendelian randomization study abstract the association between major psychiatric disorders (major depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia) and hypertension has long been of clinical and research interest. using publicly available summary data from large‐scale genome‐wide association studies (gwass), we selected, quality‐controlled, and clustered eligible genetic variants for the three psychiatric disorders and hypertension‐related outcomes. the inverse variance weighted (ivw) method was applied as the primary analysis, with a suite of sensitivity analyses including mr‐egger regression, weighted median estimator (wme), and leave‐one‐out analysis performed to assess result robustness and detect potential horizontal pleiotropy. false discovery rate (fdr) correction was implemented to multiple testing. bidirectional two‐sample mendelian randomization (mr) identified a reciprocal causal association between major depression and essential hypertension. genetically predicted major depression was significantly associated with an increased risk of essential hypertension [ivw: odds ratio (or) 1.247, 95% confidence interval (ci) (1.117–1.393), p < 0.001; wme: or 1.243, 95% ci (1.127–1.371), p < 0.001]. conversely, genetic predisposition to essential hypertension also increased the risk of major depression (ivw: or 1.028, 95% ci (1.007–1.050), p = 0.008), which remained significant after fdr correction. we found that bipolar disorder was causally associated with essential hypertension, hypertensive heart disease, and hypertensive renal disease ( p < 0.05). in contrast, no causal associations were observed between schizophrenia and any hypertension subtypes or complications ( p > 0.05). all sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary effect estimates, with no evidence of significant horizontal pleiotropy or influential outliers. in conclusion, our study, conducted under the mr framework from the perspective of genetic susceptibility, supports a bidirectional causal relationship between major depression and essential hypertension. genes brain and behavior

implications of economic hardship for child well-being in active and reserve component u.s. military families: applying the family stress model. the family stress model has guided examinations of how economic hardship is linked to child outcomes with various populations, including military families. however, many studies have relied on smaller convenience samples with insufficient variation to address unique aspects of the military community context that may moderate the associations. military families' duty status (i.e., full-time versus part-time service) is one such consideration because it can shape access to military-provided financial supports and may have implications for relational processes that are linked to hardship. grounded in the family stress model, this study leveraged national data from 5529 military families who participated in the u.s. census bureau household pulse survey to assess the prevalence of economic hardship, how economic hardship was associated with economic pressure, parent psychological distress, and child mental health, and whether these patterns differed between active-duty (n = 3128) and national guard/reserve families (ng/r; n = 2401). on average, active-duty and ng/r respondents similarly reported few economic hardships (m = 0.74 out of 8 for both). support for the family stress model was observed for both groups. greater economic hardship was associated with greater economic pressure, while economic pressure was related to more parent psychological distress, and, ultimately, more child mental health symptoms. notably, parent psychological distress was more strongly associated with child mental health symptoms among active-duty than ng/r families. findings provide further support for the utility of the family stress model in studying military families while underscoring the importance of considering contextual differences. family process

the impact of therapist mind wandering on session quality in in‐person and online counselling sessions: an experimental pilot study abstract background despite individuals spending at least one‐third of their awake time mind wandering and the anecdotal issue of therapist mind wandering, especially in online sessions, no research has yet examined the impact of therapists' mind wandering on the session quality. in the present study, we examined the impact of therapists' spontaneous and deliberate mind wandering on counselling session quality in in‐person and online settings, using a novel experimental study paradigm. method two therapists conducted standardised university counselling sessions (one online and one in‐person) with 29 clients in total. therapists and clients completed post‐session measures of session quality, the therapeutic relationship, the therapeutic presence and positive and negative affect as well as a pre‐session sleepiness measure. results we found that therapists' spontaneous (but not deliberate) mind wandering was negatively associated with therapist, but unrelated to client session evaluations, and that even though therapists reported similar mind wandering in both formats, mind wandering in online sessions appeared more detrimental to therapist‐perceived session quality. conclusion this study supported the significance and feasibility of studying mind wandering in counselling research. the findings indicate that spontaneous and deliberate mind wandering may have different roles in counselling sessions, with only the former showing a negative link with session quality. future research should establish the impact of mind wandering on longer therapeutic processes. counselling & psychotherapy research

pyramidal training and coaching to implement cw-fit in elementary general education classrooms: a participatory action research study teachers serve as key practitioners to implement tier 1 positive behavior supports. using a participatory action research approach, this study examined the effects of a pyramidal training and practice-based coaching (pbc) framework to support general education teachers’ implementation of class-wide function-related intervention teams (cw-fit). two school-based coaches were trained to fidelity in cw-fit and pbc and participated in all phases of the project, including research design, training, implementation, analysis, and dissemination. using a multiple-baseline design, we examined the effects of school-based coach-delivered training and coaching on four general education teachers’ procedural fidelity of cw-fit, rates of bsp and reprimands, and whole-class student on-task behavior. results demonstrated a functional relation between pyramidal training and coaching, and teacher implementation and increases in rates of bsp. subsequently, whole-class on-task behavior improved across all four classrooms. social validity data indicated cw-fit and pyramidal training and coaching to have high acceptability and feasibility. behavior modification

school refusal assessment scale–revised children and parent: validation of the greek version in greece, no assessment scales specifically measure school refusal. the school refusal assessment scale–revised for children (sras-r-c) and the school refusal assessment scale–revised for parents (sras-r-p) are widely acclaimed scales for assessing school refusal. the aim of this study was to validate the sras-r-c and sras-r-p in the greek population. a total of 125 primary school students and their parents, and 124 middle school students and their parents, participated in this study. exploratory factor analysis identified six factors for each scale. variations in the subscales across the four developed scales (for primary and middle school students and their parents accordingly) suggest that separate validation may be necessary for primary and secondary school students, as well as for their parents. journal of emotional and behavioral disorders

self-actualization in the capitalist work place: a case study in appropriation capitalism, defined as unlimited capital accumulation, is and remains a contested system. in its search for growth and expansion, it succeeds in encapsulating and capitalizing on ever more areas of life, not only in the physical world, but also in the world of ideas and concepts. variously called appropriation, incorporation, or co-optation, it refers to how expressions of protest, revolution, and dissent are domesticated and deradicalized so as to conform to the purpose of the corporation. in this paper, i discuss the appropriation of the concept of self-actualization, as developed by abraham maslow. holding out the promise of a decentralized, nonhierarchical, and nonauthoritarian work place, it became central to the “human relations” school in management in the 1950s and 1960s. however, in subsequent translations by mainstream scholars, self-actualization became sanitized of its original humanist connotations. it was turned into a “pyramid,” a management tool for production and performance, and into the figure of the economic “entrepreneur of the self,” totally contravening maslow’s original intentions with self-actualization at work. journal of humanistic psychology

violet light and a hum: existential dimensions of trauma in kurt vonnegut’s slaughterhouse-five and psychotherapeutic discourse this paper positions literary fiction as a complementary site through which the existential dimensions of trauma may be brought into view. engagement with such representations may enrich psychotherapeutic discourse, particularly where the complex reverberations of trauma remain elusive or conceptually peripheral. the study advances an interdisciplinary approach by employing hermeneutic phenomenology to engage directly with kurt vonnegut’s slaughterhouse-five . through a close reading of the protagonist’s descent into suspended modes of being that resist integration, the analysis demonstrates that existential disclosure does not necessarily culminate in meaning-making. rather, traumatic affect, as rendered in this narrative form, emerges as paradoxical, temporally dislocated and resistant to therapeutic teleology. by bringing trauma-fiction into textual conversation with existential psychotherapy literature, the paper seeks to deepen theoretical understandings of existential upheaval as it may manifest in the wake of trauma. therefore, it contributes to contemporary discourse on trauma as capable of catalysing ontological reconfiguration. journal of humanistic psychology

investigating the equivalence and test-retest reliability of wais-5 test results between telehealth and in-person assessment modalities wais-5远程医疗与面对面评估方式的等价性及重测信度研究 administering cognitive assessment via telehealth could expand service access, but home-based telehealth assessment is under-explored. we examined the feasibility, acceptability, equivalence and test-retest reliability of the wechsler adult intelligence scale – 5th edition (wais-5 a&nz ) in this format. excluding unusable cases, 98 english-speaking participants (47 male, 51 female, m age = 47.1 years) across all age bands completed each subtest via videoconference. a matched in-person comparison group was drawn from the wais-5 a&nz normative sample. attrition and material losses were low, and post-assessment surveys indicated telehealth acceptance. differences in group performance were within equivalence margins for full-scale iq and all core indices except verbal comprehension, and all but two of the subtests for which we could not infer equivalence were related to this index score. however, since they were slower in these untimed subtests, telehealth participants may have simply given more considered responses due to feeling less rushed in our extended sessions. test-retest reliability was similar at the full-scale iq (icc telehealth = .81, icc in-person = .84), index (range telehealth = [0.62, 0.93], range in-person = [0.64, 0.89]), and scaled subtest levels (range telehealth = [0.40, 0.93], range in-person = [0.40, 0.86]). our sample included only cognitively healthy volunteers in australia and new zealand, which may limit generalisability somewhat. nevertheless, these results offer promising support for home-based telehealth assessment, as well as guidance for future research. assessment

the theory of rhythmic synergy in caregiving for older adults living with dementia abstract this manuscript sets forth a theory of rhythmic synergy to depict the dynamic and adaptive process of communication and sensemaking that caregivers experience when caring for someone living with dementia. the theory emerged from in‐depth, semi‐structured interviews with 31 adult family caregivers of a person living with dementia. rhythmic synergy refers to a higher‐order, relationally entrained state in which the caregiver perceives an implicit knowing of their person living with dementia and how to interact with them. it is developed over time through a process where the caregiver iteratively responds to the person living with dementia and strategically engages in adapting their verbal and nonverbal communication behaviors (i.e., rhythms) and sensing a kind of togetherness or presence (i.e., relational synergy) that fosters positive outcomes for the caregiver and person living with dementia. the theory also addresses the ways in which members of a care partner network can enhance or disrupt the process of developing rhythmic synergy. importantly, the theory helps explain how temporality is crucial in understanding communication in dementia caregiving, including symptom progression, increasing care demands, and changes in the network of care partners over time. personal relationships

the drawing‐a‐line method: a new method to measure social distance with a ratio scale abstract social distance describes how close an individual feels to another, and it is related to altruism. however, it is typically measured on an ordinal scale, hindering its precision and comparison with other phenomena. although the open‐field procedure effectively converts social distance to a ratio scale, some issues remain. in this study, we developed the drawing‐a‐line (dlm) method to solve them. we asked participants to identify people in positions 1, 2, 20, 50, and 100 on their social distance list and to complete a social discounting task. then, for each person, participants drew a line to represent how close they felt to that person and we calculated the lengths to obtain a social distance value on a ratio scale. results show that the dlm produced minimal variability in raw social distance at lower positions, reduced the s value in the distance function, and maintained a good fit of the data to the hyperbolic social discounting model. we discuss the results in terms of the strengths of the dlm, the methodological and conceptual significance of the decrement of the s value, and the limitations of the new method. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

an updated systematic review of routine outcome measures for use in couple therapy abstract this paper updates macintosh and butters' previous systematic review of outcome measures used in couple therapy. embase, pubmed, psychinfo, cinahl and eric databases were searched from january 2012 to november 2025 for couple therapy outcome studies. eight hundred and twenty‐three records were screened; 320 full texts were assessed for eligibility; and 24 papers were selected for review. selected studies were published in 17 different journals. the journals that published the greatest number of selected studies were the journal of consulting and clinical psychology , and the international journal of fertility and sterility. the studies were conducted in nine countries, with the greatest number being conducted in the usa and iran. a total of 1362 couples participated in the 24 studies in this review. twenty were randomised controlled trials. relationship distress was the most common primary presenting problem, and other main concerns were sexual dissatisfaction, infidelity, infertility, cancer‐related distress, substance and alcohol use, anxiety, depression, ptsd, gambling and child abuse. behavioural couple therapy and emotionally focused couple therapy were the most commonly evaluated models. the dyadic adjustment scale (das), used in over half of the reviewed studies, was the most frequently used measure of relationship satisfaction and couple relational functioning to evaluate couple therapy. twenty‐one other measures of couple functioning were used, and each in only one study. the beck depression inventory was the most frequently used measure of individual functioning. journal of family therapy

the use of team treatment reviews in eating disorder‐focused family therapy: why, when and how? abstract this article explores the use of team treatment reviews in eating disorder‐focused family therapy. it examines how this approach may enhance therapeutic engagement, relational understanding and change processes, especially when progress in treatment feels stalled or ‘stuck’. drawing on systemic, dialogical and relational theories, team treatment review sessions are conceptualised as a way of understanding and addressing dominant problem narratives, disrupted engagement and therapeutic ruptures, amplifying multiple perspectives, and softening entrenched interactional patterns commonly observed in eating disorder‐focused family therapy. the article outlines core principles for the use of team treatment reviews, including careful attention to safety, containment, power dynamics and the emotional impact of treatment both on the family and on the treating systems. consideration is given to the use of review meetings in working with adolescents, where issues of shame, secrecy and control are often prominent. the article concludes by discussing potential risks, ethical considerations and areas for future development. team treatment reviews are proposed as a flexible and potentially powerful addition to eating disorder‐focused family therapy when used thoughtfully and reflexively. australian and new zealand journal of family therapy

factor structure and psychometric properties of the intolerance of uncertainty scale-12 in multiple sclerosis. 不确定性不耐受量表-12在多发性硬化症中的因子结构与心理测量学特性 despite the high prevalence of anxiety disorders in multiple sclerosis (ms) and the inherent uncertainty associated with the disease, it is unclear whether current measures of intolerance of uncertainty (iu) are appropriate for people with ms. in this study, we describe the psychometric features of the short-form intolerance of uncertainty scale (ius-12) in a mixed sample of 2,084 participants (244 ms, 1,840 non-ms controls). a bifactor model best represented the ius-12 in the ms group. the ius-12 appeared suitable in ms, demonstrating good construct validity and moderate test-retest reliability over the 6-month survey period. measurement invariance was found across ms and non-ms participants. of note, iu scores were comparable between groups, but iu showed stronger associations with anxiety-related pathologies in participants with ms than non-ms controls. routine assessment incorporating the ius-12 may help clarify factors underpinning anxiety and inform the development of targeted psychological interventions for people with ms. assessment

stability of school academic composition and student achievement profiles: a multilevel latent transition analysis school academic composition (sac) describes the distribution of students across achievement levels within schools and provides an important perspective on academic differences between schools. however, few studies have followed the same student cohort to examine the temporal stability of sac and transitions in student achievement profiles (saps) across initial school types. using a two-wave longitudinal design, we analyzed individually matched examination records for 16,522 students from the same cohort across 48 high schools in a city in central china. these records linked students’ scores on the 2018 academic test for junior high school students (atjhss) and the 2021 national unified examination for admissions to general universities and colleges (nueaguc). we first identified saps from standardized scores in chinese, math, and foreign languages using a longitudinal mixture model. multilevel latent profile analysis then identified sac types from the within-school proportions of these profiles. separate analyses estimated transitions between school types and sap transitions conditional on initial school type and initial sap. the models identified four saps and five sac types with distinct combinations of these profiles. modal class assignments indicated that 45 schools (93.75%) retained the same type across waves, while the remaining three transitioned to adjacent types. estimated conditional retention probabilities for the predominant initial sap within each initial school type ranged from 78.85% to 95.10%. the models also identified transitions to higher- and lower-score saps. these findings indicate that relative stability in sac can coexist with changes in students’ relative academic standing. they provide descriptive evidence to inform sac monitoring and assessments of student support needs. journal of intelligence

development of the self-perceived capability for human–ai collaborative spoken english learning scale and its preliminary application among secondary school students grounded in bem’s self-perception theory and the aied bloom’s taxonomy model, this study developed the self-perceived capability for human–ai collaborative spoken english learning scale, following the procedure of theory-based construction, item generation, scale validation, and preliminary application. from an initial pool of 36 items, expert review, cognitive interviews, item analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis yielded a 30-item scale covering four dimensions: acquisition and adjustment, scenario simulation, analysis and diagnosis, and evaluation and creation. a preliminary application among secondary school students showed that their capability was overall moderate and clearly differentiated by activity type: scenario simulation was strongest, analysis and diagnosis and acquisition and adjustment were intermediate, and evaluation and creation was weakest. students with longer cumulative duration of ai use scored significantly higher than those with shorter duration on all four dimensions, and three learner profiles were identified: the well-balanced type, the simulation-dominant type, and the overall developing type. the scale demonstrated good construct validity and reliability; it can be used to diagnose learners’ level and capability profile for human–ai collaborative spoken english learning and to inform differentiated instruction and targeted intervention. journal of intelligence

the power of collective efficacy: sources, interventions, and outcomes for diverse students although self-efficacy theory has emphasized individuals’ beliefs in their capabilities, collective efficacy may operate through similar processes. understanding these mechanisms may be particularly important for promoting equitable pathways into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (stem) careers among students from underrepresented groups. using a deductive qualitative analysis approach, this study examined how the four sources of self-efficacy (i.e., performance accomplishments, vicarious experiences, social persuasion, and physiological and emotional states) contribute to the development of collective efficacy during collaborative stem learning. focus groups with diverse eighth-grade students and semistructured interviews with their teachers explored students’ experiences working collaboratively on a multimedia stem project. findings indicated that all four sources of self-efficacy contributed to students’ shared belief in their groups’ ability to accomplish collective goals. furthermore, proximal contextual supports, including peer collaboration and teacher support through problem-solving, modeling, and tolerance for mistakes, helped students navigate barriers, facilitating persistence toward shared goals and skill development. findings extend the application of self-efficacy theory and social cognitive career theory by highlighting collective efficacy as a potentially important mechanism in collaborative career development and stem engagement. implications for practice, study limitations, and directions for future research are discussed. journal of career assessment

the architecture of wisdom in interpersonal conflict: structure and trait, state, and cultural expression across world regions abstract objective how do individuals across diverse cultures navigate interpersonal conflicts, and what drives variation in their use of wisdom‐related strategies? method in two studies spanning eight world regions ( n = 4445), we examined the factor structure of five wisdom‐related strategies (intellectual humility, others' perspectives, acknowledgement of multiple outcomes, search for compromise, outsider's view), their individual‐difference correlates, and trait–state variance. results in study 1 (autobiographical recall), we identified a three‐factor structure— perspectival metacognition , conflict resolution , and outsider's view —that showed approximate measurement invariance across cultures. in study 2 (standardized scenarios), we replicated this structure and partitioned trait, state, and cultural variance. cross‐cultural differences accounted for about 4% of variance in expressed wisdom, whereas within‐person variation across situations explained the largest share: people expressed less wisdom in reflections on conflicts involving trust betrayal than social rejection, an effect linked to greater emotional reactivity to betrayal. at the individual level, need for cognition and relational‐interdependent self‐construal showed small‐to‐moderate positive associations with each wisdom‐related feature, whereas a sense of uniqueness was positively related to conflict resolution. conclusions wisdom in reflections on interpersonal conflict appears organized around three metacognitive themes that replicate broadly across cultures, with situational affordances (vs. cultural or trait dispositions) accounting for most variation in its expression. journal of personality

effectiveness of verbal fluency tests for detecting cognitive decline in adults with alzheimer’s dementia and frontotemporal dementia: a three-level meta-analysis abstract as our population ages, the prevalence of dementia, including alzheimer’s dementia (ad) and frontotemporal dementia (ftd), is increasing. early dementia diagnoses facilitate access to interventions when they are most effective for prolonging and improving life. verbal fluency tests (e.g., fas and animal fluency) can aid in the diagnosis of ad and ftd through detecting declines in executive functioning and language. these tests may be particularly useful for diagnosing the behavioural variant of ftd (bvftd), which is associated with declines in executive functioning. a systematic search of embase, psycinfo, pubmed, medline, cinhal, and ageline identified 127 peer-reviewed studies published from january 2010 to july 2024, which compared fas and animal fluency test performances of people with ad or ftd to cognitively-healthy controls. hedges’ g effect sizes determined the effectiveness of three common score types (total, intrusion, perseveration) for ad/ftd combined, ad and combined ftd subtypes, and ad and ftd subtypes (e.g., bvftd). fas and animal fluency total scores were the most reported and effective for detecting cognitive decline in these dementias combined ( g = -1.31 and g = -1.95, respectively), but similar effects were seen for ad and bvftd. the pattern of effects was not influenced by patient characteristics and remained consistent when only low risk-of-bias studies were analysed. however, significant publication bias may have inflated the effects for ad. overall, the fas and animal fluency total scores can effectively detect cognitive decline in both ad and ftd, although they cannot be recommended for differentiating between ad and bvftd. neuropsychology review

existential positive psychology as an integrative evidence-based paradigm: theory, advances, and future directions abstract in memory of the recent passing of prof. paul t. p. wong, this article synthesizes the current state of existential positive psychology as part of his profound legacy in the field of psychology. the primary aim is to present existential positive psychology as a unique evidence-based paradigm of vital relevance to today’s global challenges. to this end, the paper reconceptualizes the entire paradigm and its six foundational pillars, while reviewing the existing body of research supporting their significance for well-being. these pillars are: (1) life is viewed through a realistic existential lens that integrates both life’s bright and dark aspects; (2) personal suffering is approached with a positive mindset that accepts and makes meaning of vulnerability; (3) dialectical coping is crucial for resilience and flourishing; (4) meaning in life is central to well-being amid adversity; (5) meaning in life is inherently relational and grounded in self-transcendence; and (6) existential well-being takes the form of mature happiness and culminates in authentic flourishing and fructification (a novel construct proposed in this paper). these pillars capture the fundamental assumptions that underpin an existential positive psychology approach to human nature, theory, principles, models, and methodology. the article further proposes an integrative process model and outlines promising future directions for this emerging psychological paradigm. with its integrative and cross-cultural foundation, existential positive psychology provides a unifying framework for guiding scientific inquiry across psychology and the broader field of human flourishing. journal of happiness studies

error patterns in the cross-tangled-finger illusion under visual and tactile cueing the cross-tangled-finger illusion occurs when observers view their crossed wrists and interlaced fingers and attempt to raise a visually indicated finger but instead raise another. we quantified response errors under visual and tactile cueing. tactile cueing sharply reduced errors. under visual cueing, raising the corresponding digit on the opposite hand was the most frequent error. nevertheless, different-digit errors accompanied 31% of opposite-hand responses but only 3% of correct-hand responses, suggesting an association between hand-laterality and digit-identity errors. i-perception

breakage and uncertainty: how potters visually engage with cracks and faults given the ubiquity of ceramic materials in human history, much archaeological research focuses on understanding how people learn about pottery craftwork in social settings and the material consequences of this process. a crucial, yet often overlooked, aspect of pottery making is knowing where breakage can occur and how to respond, as highlighted in an anthropological theory of breakage. cracks and faults arising from wheel-thrown pottery manufacture create visually distinct features, providing stimuli through which differences in visual attention across levels of expertise can be studied. we hypothesised that, as potters gain experience, their knowledge of faults becomes integrated into the generative model of the object, shaping how they visually explore it. to test this hypothesis, we drew on research on visual perception, attention, and eye guidance in complex, naturalistic visual scenes, recording eye movements from over 40 participants while they viewed images of vessels with or without typical cracks and faults in both a free-viewing and a task-based viewing experiment. participants also performed a drawing task and answered structured questions about their craft knowledge. results show clear differences between experts’ and non-experts’ visual responses, reflecting how experience shapes generative models guiding visual attention. i-perception

the moderating role of environmental communication in the relationship of factors influencing tourists’ pro-environmental behavior abstract this study is a novel research integrating relevant theories of subjective well-being, reciprocal altruism, and social cognitive theory to provide a comprehensive description of the influences of psychological well-being, social well-being, indirect reciprocal altruism, and pro-environmental behavior in the context of tourism. a survey was conducted based on a sample of 529 domestic and international tourists who participated in and conducted eco-friendly tourism activities at green tourism destinations in vietnam. selecting individuals with sufficient experience to answer the questionnaire was necessary to measure the actual impact, not the intention. the collected data were cleaned and analyzed using smartpls software to assess the model fit, reliability, and structural equation modeling (sem) to test the relationships of the research model. the results indicate that all research hypotheses are supported at a significance level of p < 0.05 (95% confidence). the study’s core contribution lies in elucidating the functional distinction between psychological well-being (an intrinsic driver) and social well-being (a normative driver), while confirming that environmental communication plays a crucial moderating role in translating intrinsic well-being into specific pro-environmental actions. these findings offer significant managerial implications for destination managers regarding the design of communication messages and the optimization of sustainable tourism experiences. discover psychology

the long-term impact of bullying victimization on intraindividual change of school experience abstract bullying victimization and school experience are closely linked constructs that significantly influence students’ well-being and school engagement. while research has established associations between peer victimization and negative school experience, little is known about how bullying victimization changes students’ perceptions over time. this study investigates whether bullying victimization predicts intraindividual changes in students’ perceptions of school experience across two time points during early adolescence. using data from 273 students ( m age = 12.93, sd = 1.36), we examined different dimensions of school experience (e.g., positive affect, social integration, exclusion) and bullying victimization using validated self-report measures. we applied autoregressive models to assess the stability of school experiences and true intraindividual change (tic) models to identify predictors of within-person change, an approach which allows to estimate baseline levels and latent change analysis over time. autoregressive models indicated moderate to high temporal stability across all school experience dimensions. tic models showed that bullying victimization significantly predicted lower baseline levels of school experience indicators, particularly negative affect at school and social exclusion. moreover, bullying victimization predicted intraindividual change in negative affect and, contrary to our hypotheses also an increase in social integration, over time. the findings suggest that bullying victimization can act as a disruptive social experience that alters students’ perceptions of their school environment. by applying tic models, the study highlights the importance of modeling intraindividual change to better understand how social harm translates into shifts in school experiences. contemporary school psychology

who verifies and who continues? personality and physiological predictors of anomaly-responsive oversight in ai-supported navigation. 谁在验证，谁在继续？ai辅助导航中异常响应性监督的人格与生理预测因素 intelligent systems increasingly place humans in oversight roles, yet users exposed to the same anomaly warning do not respond uniformly. across two studies using an ai-supported navigation task, we examined whether warning design, focal hexaco traits and trial-level physiology explained anomaly-specific evaluation and verification/override behaviour. both studies used a 2 × 2 manipulation of warning salience and explanation style. study 1 combined eye tracking and pupillometry; study 2 used electrodermal activity. prominent and especially explanatory warnings produced the largest behavioural and evaluative effects. personality showed smaller effects, with behavioural increments sensitive to model specification; conscientiousness was most consistently associated with verification, whereas emotionality was associated with evaluative and physiological responsiveness. repeated participant-level validation showed substantial incremental prediction from pupil features and smaller gains from electrodermal features, including under temporally restricted sensitivity analyses. the findings support a differentiated person-centred account of anomaly-responsive oversight while separating subjective trust from behavioural reliance and verification. 凸显尤其是解释性警告产生最大的行为与评估效应。 人格效应较小，行为增量对模型设定敏感；尽责性最稳定地与验证相关，情绪性与评估及生理反应性相关。 重复的被试水平验证显示瞳孔特征带来显著增量预测，皮肤电特征增益较小，在时间受限的敏感性分析下亦然。 结果支持区分化的以人为中心的异常响应性监督解释，并将主观信任与行为性依赖和验证区分开。 ergonomics

beyond the male prototype: a systematic review of female psychopathy in forensic populations. objective: this systematic review examines the assessment of psychopathy in female populations, critically analyzing the psychometric performance of traditional instruments compared to newer dimensional models, while exploring the distinct phenotypic and behavioral characteristics of psychopathy in women.
method: a comprehensive literature search was conducted to identify empirical studies evaluating psychopathy in women across forensic and correctional settings.
results: the evidence reveals that traditional behavioral and criminal indicators-such as those operationalized by the psychopathy checklist-revised (pcl-r)-systematically yield lower scores in women. this has often resulted in the controversial and potentially arbitrary lowering of diagnostic cutoff scores for female samples. furthermore, the review identifies key differential characteristics in female psychopathy, noting that women tend to exhibit higher rates of relational aggression, verbal hostility, and emotional dysregulation over overt physical violence. conversely, alternative dimensional frameworks, such as the psychopathic personality traits scale (ppts), the comprehensive assessment of psychopathic personality (capp), and the dsm-5 alternative model for personality disorders (ampd), demonstrate robust validity. these models successfully capture the core personality traits, emotional dysregulation, and high cluster b comorbidity characteristic of female psychopathy without relying on explicit antisocial history.
conclusion: traditional instruments present limitations in reflecting how psychopathy manifests in women. transitioning toward dimensional personality frameworks is essential to ensure gender-sensitive and clinically useful assessments. acta psychologica

two-stage least squares as a mean and covariance structure estimator: reconciling econometric and psychometric formulations. 两阶段最小二乘作为均值与协方差结构估计量：调和计量经济学与心理测量学表述 instrumental variables regression is increasingly used in psychology and is the basis of model-implied instrumental variables structural equation modelling (miiv-sem), yet econometric and psychometric formulations use different statistical representations and terminology. we develop a general theory of multi-stage weighted least squares estimation for mean and covariance structures and show that classical two-stage least squares (2sls) is the second stage of a three-stage procedure. the first stage estimates predictive equations for the explanatory variables; the second estimates the structural intercept and regression coefficients; and the third estimates the remaining disturbance variance and covariances, propagating uncertainty from earlier stages. for structural parameters, the normal-theory and asymptotically distribution-free covariance estimators reduce exactly to conventional homoscedastic and heteroscedasticity-robust 2sls estimators. with model-based covariance matrices, browne's normal-theory goodness-of-fit statistic equals sargan's overidentification statistic, and its adf counterpart equals wooldridge's heteroscedasticity-robust score statistic. third-stage disturbance covariances quantify endogeneity and yield wald tests asymptotically equivalent, under the null, to the hausman ols-2sls contrast and wooldridge's robust exogeneity test, respectively. the results place miiv-sem estimators, standard errors, and tests within a coherent multi-stage statistical theory. british journal of mathematical & statistical psychology

“everyday i learn something new about myself”: applying happenstance learning theory to a career course this study examines how a u.s. college career course shaped students’ career identities and workplace readiness using krumboltz’s happenstance learning theory (hlt) as a guiding framework. reflexive thematic analysis of student interviews identified five interrelated themes: (a) evolution of professional identity, (b) enhanced professional confidence, (c) recognition of transferable skills, (d) real-world preparedness and long-term utilization of course knowledge, and (e) motivation for lifelong learning. together, these themes reflect three core hlt processes: engaging in exploratory actions that enable individuals to benefit from unplanned events, remaining open-minded about future opportunities, and developing skills that enable them to seize opportunities when they arise ( krumboltz, 2009 ; mitchell et al., 1999 ). findings suggest that structured career preparation courses foster attitudes, skills, and mindsets that enable students to leverage chance events, build resilience, and make meaning of evolving career paths. implications for career education and the design of college career courses are discussed. journal of career development

beyond performance scores: directed functional connectivity as a brain-based biomarker for tracking motor skill learning and retention abstract surgical motor skill acquisition requires prolonged training and durable retention, yet standard behavioral metrics capture performance changes without revealing the neural mechanisms of learning. here, we validate directed functional connectivity (dfc)—computed from electroencephalography across five cortical regions using nonlinear granger causality—as a brain-based biomarker for tracking motor learning and retention. twenty-five trainees completed a 15-day laparoscopic suturing program followed by six-week retention testing; an untrained control group ( n = 27) and 15 expert surgeons served as behavioral and autonomous-stage references. dfc was evaluated using subtask-level decomposition, change-point detection, and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network benchmarked against the fundamentals of laparoscopic surgery (fls) score. dfc classified pre- versus post-training trials with 94.4% accuracy, outperforming the fls-based classifier (84.5%), while matching fls on pre- versus retention discrimination (87.5% vs. 88.5%). notably, dfc identified the cognitive-to-associative transition one day later (day 6) than behavioral metrics (day 5), consistent with sleep-dependent neural consolidation. neither measure changed further from post-training to retention, and controls exhibited no adaptation. individual-level dfc measures tracked behavioral cumulative sum (cusum) trajectories. overall, dfc provides a subtask-level, longitudinally stable biomarker of neural adaptation that complements behavioral metrics and holds potential for brain-informed surgical training. npj science of learning

poetry in motion: the dance between input modality and creative tendency in chinese efl learners’ l2 writing l2 poetry writing performance is shaped by both situational factors and learner internal traits. this study examined the impact of situational input modality (control, audio-only, visual-only, audio-visual) and learners’ creative tendency (high, low) on l2 english poetry writing. sixty-five chinese efl learners wrote 260 english quatrains, assessed by chatgpt across nine dimensions, including personal voice, audience awareness, organization, tropes, schemes, l2 linguistic conventions, thematic consistency, poetic creativity, and general writing quality. results showed: (1) input modality significantly enhanced multiple aspects of poetic writing, with audio visual input showing advantages across several measures, though statistical significance was largely confined to contrasts against the audio only condition; (2) creative tendency alone had no significant effect; (3) a significant interaction effect revealed that audio-visual input enhanced poetic creativity, especially in low-creative learners, outperforming high-creative peers under unimodal conditions. these findings highlight the value of multimodal input, particularly for low-creative learners, and offer insights for l2 poetry instruction. empirical studies of the arts

cortisol, perceived stress, and schema modes in adolescents: a biopsychosocial perspective abstract schema modes represent adaptive or maladaptive responses to life situations, integrating emotional, cognitive, and behavioral dimensions. adolescence is a critical developmental stage marked by increased stress due to biological, psychological, and social changes. this study aimed to examine whether perceived stress and salivary cortisol are associated with the activation of schema modes in adolescents. a total of 73 participants aged 15–19 were divided into two groups: group 0 ( n = 37), without symptoms of perceived stress, and group 1 ( n = 36), with perceived stress symptoms. the findings confirmed that adolescents with higher perceived stress exhibited significantly greater activation of maladaptive schema modes. additionally, elevated cortisol levels were associated with specific maladaptive modes. in contrast, healthy schema modes, particularly the happy child mode, were linked to lower levels of both perceived stress and cortisol. the perception of stress symptoms emerged as a key predictor for most of the schema modes that showed statistical significance, highlighting the importance of subjective stress appraisal in adolescent psychological functioning. these results underscore the relevance of stress perception in the activation of schema modes and suggest that strengthening healthy modes may be beneficial for promoting mental well‐being in adolescents. developmental psychobiology

(2026). ethics in psychotherapy and counseling: a practical guide, 7th edition (wiley). 560 pp. $99.95 (paperback). isbn: 9781394312924. psychology of women quarterly

supporting learning during educational adaptation: supervisor autonomy support, basic psychological need satisfaction, and academic achievement in international graduate students international graduate students must learn while adapting to an unfamiliar academic and cultural environment, yet the instructional conditions that sustain that learning remain poorly specified. grounded in self-determination theory (sdt) and in research on the non-intellective correlates of academic performance, this study examined whether supervisor autonomy support—an aspect of teacher cognition and instructional decision-making—is associated with academic achievement through the satisfaction of basic psychological needs, which sdt treats as the proximal motivational condition for self-regulated learning. because self-regulated learning and metacognition were not measured, this study tests the motivational preconditions of cognition rather than cognitive processes themselves. a cross-sectional online survey was completed by 95 international graduate students enrolled in chinese universities, who responded to the supervisor autonomy support scale, the basic psychological needs scale, and the graduate student academic achievement scale. after demographic controls, supervisor autonomy support positively predicted need satisfaction (b = 0.232, β = 0.421, p = 0.001) and academic achievement (b = 0.474, β = 0.541, p < 0.001) and need satisfaction positively predicted academic achievement (b = 0.373, β = 0.234, p < 0.01). structural equation modelling with 5000 bootstrap resamples indicated that need satisfaction carried part of this association (indirect effect = 0.112, bias-corrected 95% ci [0.045, 0.207]; direct effect = 0.572, 95% ci [0.438, 0.706]); the mediation is therefore partial, and the width of the indirect-effect interval indicates that its magnitude is estimated imprecisely. given the cross-sectional, single-source design and the self-reported nature of academic achievement, these findings are interpreted as associations consistent with the hypothesised mediation rather than as evidence of an established causal mechanism. autonomy-supportive supervision is therefore a low-cost, trainable route for establishing the cognitive-motivational conditions that support learning during educational adaptation, with implications for the assessment and design of graduate supervision. journal of intelligence

academic pressures, generative ai use, and academic behaviors and perceptions among university students: an empirical study this study draws on cognitive offloading theory and self-regulated learning theory to investigate why chinese university students use generative ai (genai) and what academic correlates are observed. using a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 500 university students and analyzed through structural equation modeling (sem) and bootstrap mediation analysis. the results show that academic workload, time pressure, and sensitivity to grades are positively associated with genai usage, whereas sensitivity to quality is not. in addition, genai usage is positively associated with procrastination and self-reported memory difficulties. regarding the competing hypotheses on creative engagement, genai usage was positively associated with creative engagement, which may indicate that students may use genai for ideation rather than answer retrieval. mediation analyses confirm that genai usage significantly mediates the associations between academic workload, time pressure, sensitivity to grades, and the three outcomes. however, the indirect effects of sensitivity to quality on the three outcomes were not significant, consistent with the unsupported hypothesis. the study highlights the need to strengthen students’ ai literacy training, manage academic workload, and redesign assessment methods so as to balance responsible use with academic integrity. future research should employ longitudinal designs, multi-method measures, and explore these relationships in diverse educational contexts to gain a more comprehensive understanding. journal of intelligence

trauma-informed lactation care following perinatal loss: a scoping review of core components of care background: lactation following perinatal loss is often an overlooked aspect of bereavement care. mothers may experience physical discomfort alongside grief, emotional distress, changes in maternal identity, and decisions about lactation suppression, expression, or milk donation. trauma-informed care may provide a framework for addressing these intersecting needs. objectives: to map evidence on lactation care following perinatal loss and identify care components that can inform trauma-informed lactation practice. methods: a scoping review was conducted to identify evidence on lactation experiences, management, and support following perinatal loss. evidence was charted and inductively synthesized, followed by interpretation through a trauma-informed care lens. results: a total of 26 peer-reviewed sources were included. four interrelated core components were identified: (1) recognition, validation, and emotional safety; (2) maternal autonomy, choice, and individualized decision-making; (3) timely lactation information, education, and professional competence; and (4) integrated, continuous, and family-centred maternity and bereavement care. lactation was experienced variably, ranging from physical and emotional distress to connection, maternal identity, meaning-making, and milk donation. key gaps included inadequate anticipatory information, limited professional knowledge and confidence, inconsistent communication, fragmented care, and insufficient follow-up. conclusions: lactation following perinatal loss should be integrated into routine maternity and bereavement care rather than addressed solely as a physiological process requiring suppression. trauma-informed care should prioritize emotional safety, maternal autonomy, timely and competent information, and coordinated continuity of care. further research is needed to evaluate the implementation and effectiveness of these approaches. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

teacher emotional competence and school climate: sel implementation pathways within sel-oriented educational contexts the present study examined the associations among teachers’ emotional competence, sel implementation practices, and school climate perceptions within schools involved in ruler-related professional development initiatives. drawing on ecological and implementation-oriented perspectives of social and emotional learning (sel), this study proposed an observed-variable path model in which emotionally competent educators would report greater implementation of sel-related practices and more positive perceptions of school climate. participants were 1185 educators from 44 spanish-speaking educational institutions collaborating with the yale center for emotional intelligence and universidad camilo josé cela. after listwise deletion of cases with missing data on the variables included in the path model and unavailable school identifiers, the primary path analyses were conducted with 1022 educators nested within 44 educational institutions. participants completed multidimensional self-report measures assessing emotional competence, emotional growth mindset, sel implementation practices, and school climate perceptions. observed-variable path analysis was conducted using composite scores derived from the study measures. results indicated that emotional competence showed the strongest positive associations with both sel implementation and school climate perceptions. sel implementation demonstrated statistically significant indirect associations linking emotional competence with school climate perceptions. complementary analyses additionally indicated that emotional growth mindset demonstrated comparatively weaker, although statistically significant, associations with sel implementation and school climate. the findings highlight the relevance of teachers’ emotional competence and sel-related implementation practices within emotionally supportive educational environments. this study contributes to the literature by examining sel implementation as a potential implementation-related pathway linking teacher emotional competence with school climate perceptions within large sel-oriented educational contexts. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

building bridges to the future of vocational psychology: introduction to the special issue this special issue reflects a collective effort to re-examine vocational psychology amid major shifts in the modern landscape of work and careers. since the 2001 journal of vocational behavior special issue on the field’s future, edited by mark savickas, economic restructuring, technological acceleration, and widening socioeconomic inequalities have reshaped how people experience work across the lifespan. the 2025 society for vocational psychology conference in lausanne, switzerland, adopted “bridges” as its theme to highlight needed connections across conceptual, disciplinary, methodological, geographical, and intergenerational divides, while bridging the field’s science and practice. building on the bridges theme, the eight focal articles in this issue highlight opportunities for disciplinary renewal. these contributions span theoretical frameworks, sociopolitical realities, research methodologies, social justice views, technological advancements, assessment and intervention approaches, and professional identity. this introduction outlines the rationale for the special issue, establishes the bridge metaphor as an organizing frame, and previews the eight articles. our closing article reflects on the varied perspectives offered by the eight articles to outline next steps for reenergizing and advancing the field. journal of career assessment

the dual-process motivational perspective on anti-american attitudes: evidence from russia in this paper, we explore the psychological motivations of anti-american attitudes from the perspective of the dual-process model that emphasizes two basic human motivational goals: security (with the resulting perception of threat) and superiority (with the perception of competition). among established measures in social psychology, the former most closely corresponds to authoritarianism, whereas the latter is captured by social dominance orientation (sdo). we analyze the case of russia where grievances against the united states featured prominently in the justification of the 2022 invasion of ukraine. in study 1, we find that political and cultural grievances against the united states, as well as anti-american attitudes and support for confrontation, are more strongly and consistently predicted by authoritarianism than by sdo. in study 2, we replicate this result and also show that anti-american attitudes in the russian public are motivated by perception of threat rather than perception of competition. group processes & intergroup relations

setting the tone: the effect of leaders' mental health disclosure on follower perceptions and intentions. amid rising global mental health challenges among employees and leaders, this research examines how leader mental health disclosure-sharing sensitive information about a mental health condition-shapes followers' perceptions of the leader and the quality of their relationship. across two vignette-based experiments involving more than 1500 employees, we find that leaders who self-disclose a mental health condition are perceived as more moral, though not more sociable, and elicit greater psychological safety and greater follower willingness to self-disclose about their own mental health. these effects extend in an attenuated form to less personal disclosures about a close other's mental health challenge. despite mental health stigma and prototypical leader expectations of strength and competence, self-disclosure did not diminish perceived leader competence or sociability, except in the case of alcohol addiction (in study 2). exploratory analyses reveal that these findings are consistent across men and women leaders and followers. this research frames leaders' mental health disclosure as a health-oriented leadership behavior with direct reputational implications and demonstrates that such leader openness can foster psychological safety, reduce barriers to help-seeking, and thus contribute to destigmatizing mental health in organizational settings. applied psychology-health and well being

a socio-reflective dimension of intelligent functioning: linking theory of mind and metacognition intelligent adaptation in social contexts can require people to assess their own knowledge while representing what others know, believe, or misunderstand. self–other mental coordination is proposed as a context-dependent functional relation between these processes. the framework distinguishes other-oriented mental-state representation associated with theory of mind from self-oriented monitoring and regulation associated with metacognition. it organizes their proposed coordination across three interacting functional levels: mental-state representation, monitoring and regulation, and social-adaptive use. these levels describe functions rather than fixed developmental stages. a tentative process account specifies how information about one’s own uncertainty and another person’s informational position may guide comparison, response revision, and help seeking. developmental predictions concern reduced dependence on comparison prompts, selective adjustment when informational roles change, and transfer to new partners or content requiring the same comparison. the evidence comes chiefly from childhood and educational contexts; adult functioning requires separate testing. the framework adopts neo-piagetian constraints on processing capacity and cognizance as boundary conditions and uses developmental cycles to order the predicted changes. testing requires longitudinal, measurement-invariant latent models combined with experimental manipulations that separate coordination from its components and shared resources. its explanatory value for a socio-reflective dimension of intelligent functioning remains unestablished. journal of intelligence

neural reorganization and the identity of mental states: the case of visuospatial neglect abstract this review examines whether recovery of spatial neglect reflects reinstatement of previously lost cognitive states or context-dependent reorganization. although substantial remission is well documented, converging evidence indicates that recovery is highly sensitive to how it is measured. across structured neuropsychological tasks, dual-task paradigms, ecological assessments, and functional connectivity analyses, different operationalizations yield systematically different conclusions about recovery. the present review suggests a pattern across the neglect literature: performance often normalizes under controlled conditions, while deficits re-emerge under increased cognitive load or ecological complexity, and recovery is accompanied by large-scale network reorganization. rather than reflecting empirical inconsistency, this pattern suggests that different paradigms may probe distinct dimensions of cognitive function. the review argues that this method-dependence constrains how recovery should be interpreted and highlights the need for multi-level accounts linking behavioral performance, robustness, and neural organization. theoretical frameworks, including the reorganization of elementary functions model, the multiple generator hypothesis, and predictive processing, are discussed as possible ways of integrating these findings. spatial neglect is thus presented as a case in which recovery cannot be understood independently of how it is operationalized, with implications for both neurorehabilitation research and theories of cognitive organization. neuropsychology review

acute effects of brief mindfulness inductions on executive function performance: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis abstract evidence regarding the acute effect of brief mindfulness exercises (mindfulness inductions) on cognitive performance and executive functions (efs) is mixed. this meta-analysis aimed to estimate the overall effect on the component of efs (i.e. inhibitory control, working memory and cognitive flexibility) and investigate if the level of induced state of mindfulness explains this effect. the current pre-registered, three-level meta-analysis and systematic review included 66 published studies with 187 effect sizes, including a total of 2,503 participants in the experimental groups and 2,511 participants in control groups. standardized mean differences were calculated for the post-test difference between the mindfulness and the control condition. results from three-level meta-analytic model revealed that there is a small but significant effect of mindfulness inductions on overall efs ( k = 66, g = 0.09 95% ci [0.03, 0.16], p < 0.01). moderator analyses did not indicate significant differences across ef components (working memory, inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility); descriptive subgroup analyses yielded larger pooled estimates for inhibitory control than for cognitive flexibility and working memory. no evidence that the level of induced state mindfulness predicts effect sizes. it should be noted that moderator analysis might have been underpowered so these non-significant results should be interpreted with caution. brief mindfulness exercises do not seem to improve overall efs substantially. we conclude that the practical relevance of these null to small effect sizes is very limited. neuropsychology review
