the “unburned bridge”: a conceptual analysis of the roles of literature in b. f. skinner’s life and work abstract b. f. skinner’s engagement with literature has often been portrayed in dismissive terms. in biographical accounts, literary activity is frequently described as a marginal episode associated with an unsuccessful attempt to pursue a writing career, whereas theoretical interpretations have often suggested that literature lies beyond the explanatory scope of skinnerian psychology. challenging these interpretations, this article argues that literature constituted an organizing dimension of skinner’s intellectual trajectory, encompassing both biographical and epistemological aspects. the first section examines the biographical dimension of this engagement, arguing that literary practice functioned as a mediating element in skinner’s transition from literary aspirations to scientific work, while contributing to the formation of his intellectual identity. rather than representing a failed career path, literary engagement is examined as a formative experience that shaped his epistemological and conceptual orientations. the second section analyzes the theoretical dimension, identifying three functions of literature within skinner’s philosophical-scientific project: as a philosophical interlocutor that contributed to his epistemological reflections and critique of mentalism; as an analytical resource for the contextual interpretation of psychological concepts such as self and personality; and as a resource for cultural design, informing his reflections on educational and governmental practices involved in the maintenance and transformation of cultural practices. the analysis suggests that literature constituted an enduring and integrative dimension of skinner’s intellectual development, connecting biography, philosophy, behavioral science, and social reflection, and contributing to a more comprehensive understanding of the scope and ambitions of his philosophical-scientific project. analysis of verbal behavior

caregiving-related early adversities and parental context effects on adolescents' momentary emotion differentiation. emotion differentiation - the ability to identify specific experienced emotions - correlates with psychological health. although theorized to develop through caregiving experiences, contextual effects on emotion differentiation in developmental populations have rarely been investigated, particularly among youth who have experienced disruptions in early caregiving. here, we examined how adolescents' momentary emotion differentiation varies across socio-emotional contexts and whether these patterns differ following exposure to severe caregiving-related early adversities (creas). adolescents aged 10-17 years with or without creas (= 81; mean age = 13.49, sd = 1.97; 53% male/47% female; 9%-asian american, 28%-black/african american, 34%-white/european american, 28%-other) completed a 7-day ecological momentary assessment protocol (4-5 surveys/day), reporting emotions and social contexts. at the trait level (spanning all contexts), after controlling for covariates, there were no significant group differences in emotion differentiation. at the momentary level, negative momentary emotion differentiation decreased following negative parent-related contexts compared to other contexts. however, the momentary emotions' standard deviation indicated more differentiated phasic intensification of a few negative emotions. importantly, exposure to creas attenuated these contextual effects,(3, 2,317) = 3.06/3.75,= .027/.011. these findings provide initial evidence linking severe creas to affective dynamic processes and raise the hypothesis that early caregiving disruptions attenuate momentary parental modulation effects on emotion differentiation. development and psychopathology

the italian version of the benevolent childhood experiences scale: psychometric properties and incremental validity in predicting resilience beyond adverse childhood experiences. background: positive childhood experiences are increasingly recognized as developmental resources that may promote psychological adaptation beyond the absence of adversity. this study examined the psychometric properties of the italian version of the benevolent childhood experiences scale (bces) and its incremental contribution to resilience beyond adverse childhood experiences (aces).
methods: a community sample of 644 italian adults (68.94% women; m_age = 28.22, sd = 9.78) completed the bces, ace-q, and brief resilience scale. item endorsement rates, internal consistency, confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance across gender, correlations, and hierarchical regression analyses were conducted.
results: item endorsement was high, and a one-factor confirmatory factor analysis using wlsmv showed overall acceptable model fit. internal consistency was moderate (kr-20 = 0.63; ω = 0.66), and gender invariance was partially supported. bces were negatively associated with aces and positively associated with resilience. in hierarchical regression analyses, bces made a small but statistically significant incremental contribution to the prediction of resilience beyond age, gender, and aces (δr² = 0.017).
conclusions: findings provide initial support for the italian bces as a brief measure of benevolent childhood experiences and suggest a modest incremental contribution of bces to perceived resilience beyond adverse childhood experiences. bmc psychology

the association between parental chronic physical illness and adolescent functional somatic symptoms abstract parental chronic physical illness is a significant yet underrecognized psychosocial stressor with measurable consequences for adolescent health. this narrative review synthesized 54 quantitative, qualitative, and systematic studies drawn from a search of pubmed, embase, scopus, and psycinfo to examine how parental illness contributes to functional somatic symptoms (fss) in adolescents. drawing on the biopsychosocial model, family stress theory, and stress‐coping frameworks, we identify maladaptive stress‐appraisal and emotional parentification as principal mediators, moderated by adolescent female sex and parental illness severity. mechanism‐targeted interventions—particularly cognitive‐behavioural therapy and space‐adapted systemic approaches—demonstrate promising outcomes. clinically, findings support proactive biopsychosocial screening within paediatric primary care. at the policy level, integration models such as the uk's ‘think family’ mandate and co‐located whole‐family health clinics within adult chronic care settings are proposed to interrupt intergenerational health transmission. journal of family therapy

increasing support for humanitarian aid to palestinian civilians during the israel-gaza war through ideologically tailored social-media campaigns. promoting support for humanitarian aid to an adversarial outgroup is difficult during active war. we introduce a digital field-experimental approach that embeds psychologically grounded interventions in people's actual social-media environments. during the israel-gaza war, 6,105 adult jewish israeli facebook users were assigned to a no-study-campaign control condition, a humanitarian-moral campaign emphasizing humanitarian obligation, or an instrumental-security campaign presenting aid as advancing israeli security. days after the campaigns ended, 4,784 participants completed the follow-up survey. support for humanitarian aid declined in the control condition but increased under both campaigns, suggesting that psychological social-media interventions can buffer or reverse erosion of humanitarian attitudes during acute conflict. political ideology moderated relative effectiveness: the instrumental-security campaign was especially effective among conservatives, whereas liberals responded positively to both. these findings provide partial support for ideological message matching and offer a scalable, ecologically valid framework for testing intergroup interventions in real-world settings. personality and social psychology bulletin

validation of the sexual inhibition/sexual excitation scales with sexual arousal measures in men objective. to provide validity evidence for the spanish version of the sexual inhibition/sexual excitation scales(sis/ses) by examining the associations between its dimensions and self-reported and laboratory-based measuresof sexual arousal. method. the sample comprised 72 spanish men aged 18-30 years, of whom 50% reportedpredominantly heterosexual behavior and 50% reported predominantly gay behavior. participants completedthe sis/ses and measures of sexual functioning (sexual arousal and erection) and sexual arousal assessed in alaboratory setting (rating of sexual arousal, rating of genital sensations, and genital response). pearson correlationanalyses were conducted to examine associations between continuous scores of the four sis/ses dimensions:sexual excitation (ses), sexual inhibition due to the threat of performance failure (sis1), sexual inhibition dueto the risk of being caught during sexual activity (sis2), and sexual inhibition due to the threat of performanceconsequences (sis3). additional comparisons across tertile groups were conducted to facilitate the interpretationof significant associations. results. ses scores were positively associated with ratings of sexual arousal in thelaboratory, whereas sis1 scores were negatively associated with genital response. no significant associations wereobserved for sis2 or sis3. tertile-based analyses supported the association between sis1 and genital response, butdid not reveal significant differences in ratings of sexual arousal across ses groups. conclusions. the findingsprovide partial validity evidence for the spanish version of the sis/ses. specifically, the results support therelevance of ses for subjective sexual arousal and of sis1 for physiological sexual responding. these findingscontribute to the understanding of the differential role of sexual excitation and inhibition in male sexual response. international journal of psychological research

writing plain language summaries: can b.sc. students communicate scientific evidence as effectively as trained psychologists? plain language summaries (plss) aim for effective, evidence-based science communication by reporting scientific results in a generally understandable language. here, we investigated whether students can produce plss of high quality, using guidelines of the project klarpsy, which hosts german-language text plss of psychological meta-analyses freely accessible in the web. after a pre-screening of eligible meta-analyses and a pilot rating (e.g., of interest and social relevance), b.sc. students in psychology ( n = 18) each wrote a pls about a self-suggested meta-analysis as part of their b.sc. thesis. in the explorative evaluation study, we tested competing predictions on how author expertise might affect text quality. independent participants ( n = 232; mostly non-psychologists) rated one randomly drawn student-written pls and one expert-written pls (from the existing klarpsy collection). the perceived understanding and empowerment were both rated lower for the student texts; this is theoretically in line with an expert-superiority effect. yet, small effect sizes and the high overall text quality suggest that, even before completing their academic degree, with clear guidelines and minimal additional support from lecturers, students’ writing plss not only trains the communicative skills of future scientists and practitioners but can also provide direct outcomes of social and practical relevance. psychology learning and teaching-plat

beyond methodological constraints: a multilevel framework for evaluating scientific credibility the current replication and credibility crises are often traced to flexibility in research methods and analyses, which can leave room for questionable research practices, inadvertent biases, and methodological and statistical errors. in response, reform efforts have emphasized stricter methodological and procedural constraints, such as preregistration and confirmatory designs. in this article, we develop an alternative, multilevel framework for evaluating scientific credibility. we examine factors that influence the credibility of research findings across levels of inference, including background assumptions, theory, methodology, and data. we argue that the credibility of results depends on interactions across these levels rather than adherence to a particular methodological approach. our framework draws on two conceptions of evidential strength: logical and methodological severity. logical severity concerns the strength of the inferential relation between theoretical claims and empirical evidence, whereas methodological severity concerns the capacity of research procedures to rule out error. we argue that, when relevant severity criteria are satisfied, credible results can be obtained through diverse methods, including both confirmatory and exploratory approaches. our framework seeks to provide room for methodological pluralism while supporting core science reform goals, including credibility, replicability, and scientific informativeness. review of general psychology

learning from groups and learning about groups: a counseling psychology journey groups have been central to my personal development and scholarship. extending my leona tyler award address, i tell two interdependent stories: what i have learned from groups and what i have learned about groups. family, mentors, editorial teams, international collaborators, psychotherapy trainees, students, and colleagues taught me about presence, love, possibility, challenge and support, balance, vulnerability, empowerment, and savoring. my research career suggests three phases in understanding counseling groups: viewing groups as treatment settings, understanding groups as systems of mutually influential members, and conceptualizing groups as configurations with emergent properties that cannot be reduced to averages. i illustrate this third phase using distributions of working and resisting group climate and extend the idea to distributions of real relationship inventory item responses. across these personal and scientific lessons, the central conclusion is that groups transform people through relationships, and understanding those relationships requires attention to interdependence and configuration. counseling psychologist

recognition of intentional eye-movement behaviors for assistive human–robot interaction for individuals with limited limb function, conventional manual control methods such as joysticks are not readily applicable to assistive robot operation, highlighting the need for a hands-free control method. eye movements, as natural signals of human intention, offer advantages in intuitiveness and accessibility and are particularly suitable for such scenarios. however, prior studies have primarily focused on fixation-based gaze interaction, and relying solely on fixation is inadequate for human–robot interaction tasks that involve both robot movement and target selection. this paper presents an assistive human–robot interaction (hri) system based on eye-movement behavior recognition. first, an eye-movement dataset named gazerobdb containing four eye-movement behavior classes was constructed. representative eye-movement features were then extracted and analyzed to support eye-movement behavior classification. next, a feature-based recognition approach using machine-learning classifiers was developed to distinguish the four eye-movement behavior classes—fixation, saccade, intentional fixation, and intentional movement. among the evaluated classifiers, random forest (rf) achieved the highest overall classification performance and was combined with the extracted eye-movement features to form the eye-movement behavior recognition module of the proposed hri system. the recognized intentional fixation and intentional movement behaviors were then mapped to target selection and robot movement control, respectively. the resulting system was evaluated with 10 participants. these results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework for hands-free robot control under the evaluated conditions and highlight its potential for assistive human–robot interaction. journal of eye movement research

eye-tracking corpus research on reading cognition: progress, challenges, and future directions eye-tracking corpora integrate authentic linguistic materials from natural reading contexts with eye-movement data. they provide a new methodological paradigm for investigating cognitive processing during reading with relatively high ecological validity. at present, significant progress has been made internationally in both the development and application of eye-tracking corpora. in china, however, research in this area began relatively late. a clear and comprehensive understanding of this field is still lacking, which has constrained the further development of related research in china. therefore, this article systematically reviews the basic characteristics of eye-tracking corpora, major research advances, and key methodological issues. it also discusses future directions for the field. the review aims to provide researchers in china with a comprehensive overview of the field and methodological guidance for developing eye-tracking corpora for chinese and minority languages spoken in china, while drawing on these regional examples to illustrate broader international challenges in data harmonization, cross-linguistic comparability, and reproducibility. journal of eye movement research

specifying innateness in infant development: a framework for theory‐building based on co‐determination abstract infant research has often treated early neural and behavioral expression as a privileged window into the initial state of the mind, with early‐emerging capacities sometimes uncritically taken as broad evidence of innate knowledge. this paper evaluates the strength of such inferences through four intersecting lenses: genetics and epigenetics, cultural evolution, definitional precision, and historical and contemporary standards of scientific explanation and falsifiability. it distinguishes among several non‐equivalent forms of innateness, including claims about representational content, architectural or processing biases, developmental canalization, and maturational timing. in place of broad or underspecified appeals to innateness, it advances greater specificity in accounts of co‐determination as a framework for theory‐building that encourages delineation of biological constraints, experiential inputs, cultural ecologies, developmental timing, and interactive mechanisms proposed to produce a given outcome, as well as patterns of variation that would support or challenge those claims. the central aim is to provide a more tractable and testable basis for theorizing about the initial state of the infant mind. infancy

rasch analysis of the korean internet social capital scales abstract internet‐based ties increasingly function as social resources, but item‐ and category‐level evidence for the korean internet social capital scales (k‐iscs) remains limited. this study evaluated the 18‐item, 7‐point k‐iscs using rasch measurement in a nationwide online panel of korean adults ( n = 1500). residual‐based dimensionality diagnostics supported the theoretical distinction between online bonding and bridging social capital; therefore, the main analyses were conducted separately by subscale. both subscales showed generally acceptable item fit, ordered category functioning, high person reliability and separation, and precisely estimated item difficulty hierarchies within the calibration sample. item 4 in the bonding subscale and item 18 in the bridging subscale showed underfit, indicating the need for closer review of the emergency‐loan and frequent‐new‐contact items. person–item maps and test information functions showed that both subscales measured most precisely near the center of the latent continuum, with lower precision at the tails. dif was mostly negligible across gender and age groups, although item 18 showed slight‐to‐moderate gender‐related dif. overall, the findings support interpreting the k‐iscs as two related but distinct subscales for assessing perceived online bonding and bridging resources in korean adults, rather than as an undifferentiated total score. personal relationships

tears for better, for worse: typology and measure of crying in romantic relationships abstract people typically cry in the presence of their romantic partners, yet the social functions of this behavior within couples remain unknown. drawing on the social glue model of tears and prior research on manipulative crying, we identified five distinct types of crying in romantic relationships and created the crying in romantic relationships questionnaire (crrq) to measure them. the crrq was developed and validated across three studies in polish and uk samples ( n = 849). in the preliminary study, individuals described real‐life situations in which people might cry in the presence of their partners. based on their answers, we created an initial item pool. study 1 examined the psychometric properties of the pool, revealing that the crrq comprises five factors, each representing a different type of crying: relationship discomfort, relationship comfort, other‐oriented concern, emotion regulation, and manipulation. the results also supported the scale's reliability and validity. study 2 provided further evidence for the five‐dimensional structure of the crrq and its good psychometric properties. overall, the results indicate that the crrq is a reliable and valid measure of five distinct types of crying in romantic relationships. personal relationships

graphic development and its relations to verbal language in the french elfe nationwide birth cohort abstract this study investigated the association between graphic and language skills in 5329 children (2651 girls and 2678 boys) from the french elfe birth cohort, considering the influence of environmental factors. at 3.5 years, children completed the draw‐a‐person test and parental reports at 2 years provided data on language production (lexical and syntactic levels), sociodemographics and activities. sex‐stratified zero‐inflated poisson regression models, controlling for child sex and family socioeconomic status, were utilized for analysis. the results showed that greater language skills (estimated through macarthur–bates communicative development inventory language score—continuous or in quartiles—and making two‐word sentences at age 2) were associated with a lower likelihood of a null drawing score in both boys (or = 0.89, 95% ci = 0.86; 0.93) and girls (or = 0.88, 95% ci = 0.83; 0.93). additionally, higher language skills correlated with a higher drawing score, but this was only significant in girls ( β = 0.01, 95% ci = 0; 0.02). in conclusion, higher language skills are linked to a greater probability of completing the draw‐a‐person test for both sexes, while the relationship between language skill and drawing complexity was specific to girls in this cohort. infant and child development

rural-urban inequalities in access to early childcare and education and the availability of head start programs abstract background the supply of early childcare and education (ece) in the united states is insufficient compared to anticipated demand, with disparities in availability and features across communities. one of the core assumptions for federal funding for local head start programs is likely that these programs will alleviate a possible shortage of ece in low-income and remote communities. while head start policy encourages strategically placing head start awards in potential supply-gap areas, it is unclear how head start programs can help address such supply gaps across geographic locations. objective this study compares disparities in access to center-based ece opportunities and examines the impact of public head start programs on improving access to ece opportunities across rural-urban geographic locations, determined at the zip code tabulation area (zcta) level. methods this study employs an ecological causal-comparative, or ex post facto, design to evaluate inequalities in access to ece between rural and urban areas, using multiple data sources based on the state of tennessee, including the american community survey (acs), the tennessee department of human services (tdhs), and federal head start websites. results the finding indicates a significant difference in the demand: supply ratio across geographic locations. the finding also supports that rural areas had lower access to center-based ece opportunities than urban areas. while descriptive statistics indicate unequal head start capacity, the analysis finds no substantial evidence of differential availability of head start slots and providers across geographic locations. furthermore, the analysis of differences in demand: supply ratios with and without head start slot capacity also shows that the availability of head start slots significantly contributes to improving ece capacity and reducing supply gaps (9% to 12%) across geographic locations. conclusion the protective role of head start slots in reducing disparities in access also supports the need for increased federal funding to reduce geographic disparities in early learning opportunities and childcare infrastructure. these findings also support the need for ongoing or increased federal funding to reduce geographic disparities in ece access, not just as an early learning intervention but also in policy discourse as a childcare equity and infrastructure program. child & youth care forum

brief stimulus changes signaling extinction enhance resurgence 简短刺激变化预示消退可增强复发 abstract resurgence is the return of a previously reinforced and extinguished target response when conditions worsen for an alternative response. several studies examined resurgence when brief stimulus changes/instructions accompanied phase transitions in standard three‐phase procedures, which confounded the effects of worsening with extinction and stimulus changes. subsequent research found resurgence was greater when a 1‐s stimulus change preceded both phase changes compared with groups experiencing more frequent or no stimulus changes. the purpose of the present study was to evaluate whether presenting identical versus different stimuli prior to both phase changes influenced resurgence in experiment 1 and a stimulus only prior to extinction testing was sufficient to observe enhanced resurgence effects in experiment 2. we found no differences in resurgence whether the brief stimulus changes (1) between phases were identical or different or (2) occurred before phases 2 and 3 or only before phase 3; however, resurgence was greater when preceding only phase 3 with a stimulus change versus no stimuli between phases or a stimulus only before phase 2. these findings suggest stimuli signaling transitions to extinction testing enhance resurgence effects. we discuss whether brief stimulus changes are functionally similar to contextual changes accompanying phases previously shown to produce renewal and enhance resurgence. 刺激在两次阶段间相同或不同，未造成复发差异。 刺激出现在阶段2和3之前还是仅在阶段3之前，未造成复发差异。 仅在阶段3前呈现刺激变化时，复发大于无阶段间刺激或仅在阶段2前呈现刺激的条件。 作者据此认为，预示向消退测试转换的刺激会增强复发效应。 journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

knowledge structure and research frontiers of smartphone addiction across bibliographic environments (2004–2024) abstract smartphone addiction (sa) has developed into a broad and increasingly differentiated research field, but its knowledge structure and temporal evolution across different bibliographic environments remain incompletely characterized. we conducted a comparative bibliometric analysis of research indexed in the web of science core collection (wos) and china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki) from 2004 to 2024. after screening, 1,128 publications were included, comprising 733 wos-indexed and 395 cnki-indexed records. publication trends, research participation, keyword co-occurrence, thematic clustering and keyword bursts were analysed using r and citespace. publication output increased in both databases, although wos continued to rise and reached its highest level in 2024, whereas cnki peaked in 2021 and subsequently declined. the two datasets shared a substantial psychological and behavioural research core but differed in thematic organization. wos-indexed research covered psychological resilience, sleep, mental health, fear of missing out, social media and academic performance, whereas cnki-indexed research was more strongly organized around student populations, mobile phone dependence, loneliness, depression and mediating processes. recent research frontiers also differed: wos bursts included intervention, sleep and perceived stress, whereas cnki bursts included self-control, social anxiety, parental behaviour, anxiety and physical exercise. these findings show that smartphone addiction research contains shared thematic concerns while its knowledge organization and temporal priorities are represented differently across bibliographic environments. discover psychology

relationship mindfulness profiles and their association with personal and relational well‐being: a person‐centered analysis at individual, dyadic, and program levels abstract this study adopted a person‐centered approach to identify profiles of relationship mindfulness at individual and couple levels and examine their associations with personal and relational well‐being, demographic characteristics, and responses to couple relationship education (cre). using 1181 different‐gender couples, latent profile analyses identified three individual profiles (high, average, and low) and two dyadic profiles (generally high and discrepantly low). across both levels, profiles were primarily distinguished by overall levels. individuals and couples in the high‐mindfulness profiles reported the highest well‐being, whereas those in the low‐mindfulness profiles showed the lowest. gender and parental status were significantly related to profile membership. couples in the discrepantly low mindfulness profile showed greater improvements in well‐being following cre than those in the generally high profile. overall, the findings suggest that relationship mindfulness acts as a relatively unified construct within individuals, and partners tend to show broad concordance in their overall levels of relationship mindfulness. journal of marital and family therapy

practitioner perspectives on social justice and systems-level indirect services via individual interviews, we investigated school psychology practitioners’ ( n = 8) perspectives on implementing systems-level indirect services using a social justice lens. practitioners participated in interviews where we prompted them to consider how their practice includes domains 5–7 of the national association of school psychologists (nasp) model for comprehensive and integrated school psychological services (i.e., school-wide practices to promote learning, services to support safe and supportive schools, family, school, and community collaboration) and how social justice principles are infused in these practices. qualitative analyses indicated that practitioners encounter several barriers in implementing socially just indirect services. some identified issues included role capacity, understanding social justice definitions, and community involvement and influence. given our findings, we offer recommendations for practitioners including the importance of following nasp position statements, involvement in policy work, and embedding multicultural, liberation, and anti-racist theories and practices in school psychology training. school psychology international

prevalence and associated factors of depression, anxiety, and stress among university athletes in bangladesh abstract background university athletes face substantial academic, physical, and psychosocial pressures that may heighten vulnerability to psychological distress, despite the perceived mental health benefits of sports participation. this study aimed to determine the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress among university athletes in bangladesh and to examine how these conditions are associated with lifestyle and sociodemographic factors. methods this cross-sectional study was conducted from march to september 2025 among 249 university athletes aged 18–26 years at six randomly selected universities in bangladesh. data were collected online and in person. psychological distress was assessed with the depression, anxiety, and stress scale-21 (dass-21), and health-promoting lifestyle behaviors were evaluated with the health-promoting lifestyle profile ii (hplp-ii). descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, mann–whitney u tests, spearman’s correlations, and binary logistic regression analyses were conducted. results the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress was 42.6%, 42.6%, and 43.8%, respectively. depression, anxiety, and stress were significantly associated with relationship status, fatigue, socioeconomic status, smoking, sleep duration, sports participation frequency, and satisfaction with sports (all p < 0.05). participants with depression, anxiety, and stress had significantly lower scores across all hplp-ii domains (all p < 0.01). higher physical activity was independently associated with lower odds of depression (or = 0.462, 95% ci: 0.286–0.746), anxiety (or = 0.756, 95% ci: 0.677–0.845), and stress (or = 0.773, 95% ci: 0.677–0.882). better stress management and stronger interpersonal relationships were also significantly associated, whereas other factors were not. conclusions depression, anxiety, and stress were highly prevalent among university athletes in bangladesh and strongly associated with modifiable lifestyle factors. these findings support integrated, athlete-centered mental health strategies emphasizing physical activity, stress management, and psychosocial support. however, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and determination of the directionality of these associations. clinical trial number not applicable. discover mental health

a narrative review of the accuracy and clinical readiness of artificial intelligence methods for detecting depression abstract depression is a leading cause of disability worldwide, yet it remains frequently under-recognised because diagnosis relies on self-report and clinical interviews that are subjective, stigma-sensitive and resource-intensive, particularly in low-resource settings. this narrative review examines artificial intelligence (ai) approaches for detecting depression from text and clinical records (including large language models), speech and acoustic signals, facial behaviour, electroencephalography (eeg) and multimodal combinations. pubmed/medline, embase, psycinfo, scopus, ieee xplore and the acm digital library, supplemented by the acl anthology, arxiv and citation searching, were searched for studies published between january 2015 and august 2026, and studies were appraised for sample size, data modality, reference standard and validation strategy. across modalities, many studies report accuracies above 80%, and multimodal fusion often outperforms single modalities. however, the highest figures (93–100%) come mainly from small case–control or benchmark datasets of 30–200 participants evaluated with internal validation, whereas studies with several hundred to almost 15,000 participants report substantially more modest performance (area under the curve or balanced accuracy of approximately 0.69–0.78 for language, speech and record-based models, and 54–61% accuracy for neuroimaging). most models are trained against self-report scales such as the phq-8 rather than diagnostic interviews, external validation is rare, widely used benchmarks contain demographic and interviewer-prompt biases, and no study has yet shown that ai-based detection improves patient outcomes. large language models extend text-based assessment but show variable, prompt-dependent performance, particularly when restricted to locally deployable models, and eeg offers objective biomarkers whose near-perfect accuracies in small samples have not been replicated at scale. ai therefore offers plausible added value for scalable pre-screening, continuous monitoring and triage where specialist capacity is limited, but it should currently be regarded as a clinician-supervised adjunct rather than a diagnostic replacement. progress will require larger and more diverse datasets, interview-based reference standards, external and prospective validation, transparent reporting, fairness auditing and privacy-preserving design. discover mental health

re-examining the intent to stay scale: evidence from generation z employees in indonesia orientation: employee retention remains an important concern in organisational and industrial psychology as generation z becomes increasingly visible in the workforce. in indonesia, the applicability of established retention measures requires empirical examination. research purpose: this study examines the psychometric properties of the indonesian version of the intent to stay scale (its) among generation z employees in indonesia, specifically internal consistency reliability and convergent validity. motivation for the study: although intent to stay is widely used as an indicator of employee retention, evidence regarding measurement properties across contexts remains limited. this is particularly relevant for generation z employees in indonesia. research approach/design and method: a structured contextual harmonisation and pre-testing process was followed by field testing and psychometric evaluation. data were collected through an online survey from 461 generation z employees in indonesia who met the criteria and passed response-quality screening. item-level analyses were conducted using jamovi, while the reflective measurement model was evaluated using pls-sem with smartpls 3. main findings: all six its items demonstrated acceptable outer loadings, ranging from 0.739 to 0.897. the scale demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency reliability, with cronbach’s alpha of 0.915, rho_a of 0.923, and composite reliability of 0.934. the average variance extracted was 0.704, providing evidence of convergent validity. intent to stay scale 6 showed the lowest loading but remained above the threshold and was retained. practical/managerial implications: the findings suggest that the indonesian its may provide useful information when assessing intention to stay among generation z employees. contribution/value-add: this study provides preliminary, context-specific evidence regarding the measurement properties of the indonesian its among generation z employees in indonesia and highlights the importance of evaluating retention measures within contexts. sa journal of industrial psychology

effect of oral proprioceptive stimuli on auditory–visual integration abstract proprioception contributes to body position, balance, movement control, sensory spatial localization and multisensory integration. interactions between the stomatognathic and visual systems through trigeminal afferents have been demonstrated. this exploratory study investigated whether oral proprioceptive stimulation influences visual perception and modulates sound-induced visual changes under binocular dissociation. thirty-eight healthy adults participated. the vertical maddox test (vm), which induces binocular dissociation and increases reliance on ocular proprioception, assessed visual perception during four experimental phases: baseline without stimulation, sound stimulation, simultaneous sound and oral proprioceptive stimulation, and oral proprioceptive stimulation alone. oral proprioceptive stimuli (ops) comprised combined oral stimuli (cos), involving tongue and lip positions, and dental stimuli (ds), consisting of controlled pressure or traction applied to the incisors. none of the participants reported visual pseudo-scotomas (vs; i.e., small, transient visual losses) at baseline, whereas 89.5% (95% ci [75.9, 95.8]) reported vs under at least one experimental condition. vs was reported by 60.5% (95% ci [44.7, 74.4]) during sound stimulation and by 81.6% (95% ci [66.6, 90.8]) under at least one oral proprioceptive condition. among participants with sound-induced vs, 78.3% (95% ci [58.1, 90.3]) achieved vs elimination with at least one oral proprioceptive stimulus while sound continued. elimination was achieved with ds only in 21.7% (95% ci [9.7, 41.9]), with cos only in 8.7% (95% ci [2.4, 26.8]), and with both in 47.8% (95% ci [29.2, 67.0]). among participants who responded to both stimulus types, complete, partial, and no concordance between anatomically equivalent stimulations were observed in 45.5% (95% ci [21.3, 72.0]), 45.5% (95% ci [21.3, 72.0]), and 9.1% (95% ci [1.6, 37.7]), respectively. these exploratory findings support functional sensory interactions between the visual and stomatognathic systems and suggest that oral proprioception may influence visual perception and modulate sound-induced visual changes. they also suggest broader oral sensory contributions to central sensory processing. multisensory research

the role of cognitions and emotional processes in ptsd severity among young people seeking treatment for ptsd and substance use purpose cognitive models emphasise trauma-related appraisals in relation to post-traumatic stress symptoms. cognitive-emotional processes may also shape symptom presentation, yet these processes are rarely examined together. this study aims to address these gaps by examining the associations between overall and cluster-specific ptsd severity and the severity of trauma-related beliefs (i.e. negative post-traumatic cognitions about the self, others and the world) and transdiagnostic processes (perseverative thinking, emotion regulation and distress tolerance) in treatment-seeking youth. design/methodology/approach data were drawn from 55 adolescents and young adults (m age = 19.49, sd = 3.27; 38 female) enrolled in a randomised controlled trial evaluating an integrated treatment for co-occurring ptsd and substance use. participants completed baseline assessments of trauma-related beliefs, perseverative thinking, distress tolerance, emotion regulation and ptsd symptom severity. findings ptsd severity was strongly associated with the severity of trauma-related cognitions. beliefs about a fragile self and perceptions of permanent disturbing change evidence the strongest associations with overall ptsd severity, and re-experiencing, negative cognitions/mood and hyperarousal. no variables were significantly associated with avoidance. rumination, emotion regulation and distress tolerance were not significantly associated with ptsd severity once trauma-related cognitions were included in the models. these findings highlight associations between maladaptive trauma-related beliefs about the self and the world and ptsd severity. originality/value to the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to examine trauma-related cognitions and cognitive-emotional processes in youth with ptsd and substance use. it advances existing research by examining their associations with overall and cluster-specific ptsd severity and highlights the need to examine temporal and mediating pathways in future work. advances in dual diagnosis

graduate family therapy training for first nations practitioners: transformations of self abstract objective in light of limited teaching resources and the essential need for indigenous‐focused learning material, this study sought to contribute to the development of culturally appropriate support for first nations students training as family therapists. drawing on the wisdom and experience of graduate students of an integrated family therapy training program that embeds australian aboriginal culture and aboriginal wisdom within mainstream curriculum, we explore the transformative elements of course curriculum and teaching process. method as part of the course, first nations students prepared reflective essays on their learnings related to culturally adapted systemic frameworks for working with australian indigenous families, including ethics of practice, and impacts for self. these essays ( n = 9) were subject to grounded theoretical analysis. results findings highlight students’ perceptions of the transformative impact of the graduate program on their personal and professional development. this impact was reflected across three key domains: (i) personal and professional growth, (ii) takeaway learnings, (iii) application of learning in family therapy practice. conclusion when taught within a culturally safe process, our findings show the powerful, recursive alignment of indigenous ways of knowing and western systemic approaches to family therapy. this integration is not only perceived as professionally enriching by students but also appears to support their personal growth and in turn their capacity to work respectfully and effectively with first nations families. by embedding these respectful, integrated pedagogies into tertiary clinical training, students and supervisors can contribute to building sustainable practice capacity within first nations communities, ultimately strengthening family and community wellbeing. journal of clinical psychology

stress, displacement, and early‐life aging: telomere length in middle eastern immigrant and refugee mother–child dyads abstract telomere length (tl) is a biomarker of cellular aging and stress exposure. early‐life tl is linked to long‐term somatic and psychiatric diseases. children of immigrant and refugee mothers may be vulnerable to biological effects of stress due to maternal psychological distress. this study examined associations between maternal acculturative stress and psychological symptoms (depression and post‐traumatic stress), maternal tl, and child tl in immigrant and refugee middle eastern mother–child dyads. in a cross‐sectional design, 6‐ to 24‐month‐old children and their mothers ( n = 165 dyads) were recruited from a midwestern us community between 2022 and 2024. maternal psychological distress symptoms were assessed via standardized self‐report measures. buccal swab samples were collected from mothers and children to measure tl. multivariate linear regression was used for the analysis. maternal tl and child gestational age at birth were positively related to child tl. among immigrant families, higher maternal post‐traumatic stress was significantly related to shorter child tl, whereas for refugee families, higher depressive symptoms were significantly associated with longer child tl. these findings suggest that biological indicators of maternal aging may offer an explanatory power for early‐life stress effects in addition to self‐reported psychological distress. developmental psychobiology

cognitive-professional resource configurations for ai-mediated teaching: perceived teacher-education support and intelligent professional action ai-mediated teaching requires teachers to evaluate uncertain information, respond to changing conditions, and integrate ai with pedagogical judgment. this study examined four cognitive-professional resource domains relevant to intelligent professional action: digital literacy, digital resilience, ai-mediated epistemic agency (amea), and ai-tpack. variable-centered and person-centered analyses drew on a cross-sectional survey of 942 youshi plan preservice teachers at one chinese university. perceived structured teacher-education support was positively associated with all four resources. self-reported teaching innovation competence was positively associated with jointly higher digital literacy and digital resilience, with the response surface primarily reflecting their combined level. four resource profiles mainly differed in overall level and showed graded differences in perceived teaching innovation competence. higher perceived support was also associated with membership in higher-resource profiles. together, these findings connect perceived teacher-education support, cognitive-professional resource configurations, and self-reported teaching innovation competence, positioning the latter as a domain-specific perceived capability relevant to intelligent professional action in ai-mediated teaching. journal of intelligence
