self‐ratings, partner perceptions, and ideal partner preferences of gelotophobia, gelotophilia, and katagelasticism in couples: congruence and associations with relationship satisfaction abstract objective how people deal with ridicule and being laughed at plays a role for romantic relationships. gelotophobia (fear of being laughed at), gelotophilia (joy in being laughed at), and katagelasticism (joy in laughing at others) describe individual differences in dealing with laughter. we studied how differential perceptions among partners' traits and their profiles converge to address the description and effects of congruence. method we collected data from 286 opposite‐gender couples (relationship duration: m = 6.8 years), who provided self‐ and partner ratings and ideal partner preferences for these laughter‐related dispositions. we analyzed the congruence between different types of perceptions of the laughter‐related dispositions and whether this congruence was associated with relationship satisfaction. we computed profile‐based congruence analyses and conducted supplementary dyadic response surface analyses. results we found that perceptions are interdependent within and between partners and that profile congruence between partner perceptions and ideal partner preferences is associated with greater relationship satisfaction above and beyond actor, partner, and stereotype effects. conclusion self‐, partner‐, and ideal partner perceptions are differentially interrelated and congruence in their distinctive profiles relates to couples' satisfaction. we discuss the findings from the perspective of the ideal standards model and encourage further research on perceptions less across traits. journal of personality

therapeutic processes in virtual reality‐based avatar therapy for treatment‐resistant major depressive disorder: a qualitative analysis of patients' experiences abstract the therapeutic benefits of virtual reality‐based avatar therapy (vrt) compared with conventional psychotherapies remain unknown in individuals with treatment‐resistant major depressive disorder (trd). accordingly, this study aimed to explore patients' lived experience of vrt to identify perceived therapeutic processes and benefits, better understand how virtual reality and dialogue with an avatar contribute to therapeutic change and examine how these experiences differed from those associated with conventional psychotherapeutic approaches. a total of 12 individuals with trd who had completed 8–12 weekly vrt sessions (mean 10.75 sessions) after previously receiving at least two conventional psychotherapies were selected from a clinical trial. semi‐structured interviews conducted following completion of the vrt were analysed using an inductive qualitative content analysis approach. six themes describing the therapeutic processes underlying vrt were identified: immersive role‐play, putting theory into practice, the structure of therapy, emotional investment, an atypical therapeutic stance and externalization of internal processes. in addition, three perceived benefits emerged from these processes: integration of therapeutic concepts into daily life, development of mentalization capacities and enhanced self‐determination. finally, confrontation emerged as a transversal theme linking both the therapeutic processes and their perceived benefits. these findings suggest that vrt combines therapeutic processes common to conventional psychotherapies with distinctive features that may influence how benefits are experienced by patients. future research should examine whether these distinctive processes account for vrt's added therapeutic value and contribute to clinical improvement. clinical psychology & psychotherapy

nevertheless, we resist: exploring the joint occurrence of critical agency and critical action classes among black adolescents abstract youth's beliefs in their ability to impact racially oppressive systems (i.e., critical agency) are important for understanding the actions they engage in (i.e., critical action), but findings examining this relationship have been mixed. the current study utilized latent class analysis to examine the nuances in youth's critical agency and critical action behaviors and how these patterns co‐occur. participants were 522 black adolescents from across the united states. unique classes of critical agency (disempowered competence, gaining confidence, and agentic) and critical action (high interpersonal low communal, high, moderate, and low) emerged. results demonstrate that youth engage in critical action behaviors regardless of their perceived levels of agency, with the majority of youth belonging to the moderate action or high action classes. further, girls were more likely to be in the high action class while boys were more likely to be in the low action class. findings highlight that youth may engage in actions to resist racism regardless of how prepared they feel to do so or the amount of power they perceive having. implications for supporting black adolescent critical consciousness development within the context of well‐being are discussed. american journal of community psychology

“i picked myself up through prayer and soups”: factors impeding and enhancing long covid recovery among latinos in south texas abstract aims we aimed to understand what factors have impeded and enhanced long covid recovery among latinos in south texas. methods through community partners, 78 participants were part of seven focus groups. we analyzed the data following braun and clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. results factors that impeded recovery were: (1) working while ill due to labor needs, expectations, and limited safety nets, (2) mistrusting health care due to invalidating systemic barriers, (3) grieving former self, and (4) obsessing over the known and unknown. factors that enhanced recovery were: (1) focusing on a conscious fight to preserve life, (2) leveraging cultural knowledge to reconnect with their sense of wholeness as a person, (3) choosing western medicine as one method of healing, and (4) relying on god and trusted ones. conclusion long covid recovery interventions among south texas latinos must account for structural and social determinants of health and cultural ways of healing. journal of community psychology

unpacking the link between adult attachment and social anxiety: a serial mediation model of emotion dysregulation and self‐esteem abstract attachment insecurity has been linked to social anxiety, yet the correlates underlying this association remain unclear. this study examined whether emotion dysregulation and self‐esteem account for indirect associations between insecure attachment orientations and social anxiety symptoms. using cross‐sectional survey data from a community sample of turkish adults ( n = 631), the model tested indirect pathways from attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance to social anxiety via emotion dysregulation and self‐esteem. both attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance were positively associated with greater emotion dysregulation. in turn, greater emotion dysregulation was associated with lower self‐esteem, and lower self‐esteem was associated with higher social anxiety. indirect associations emerged through emotion dysregulation, through self‐esteem, and through the serial pathway linking emotion dysregulation to self‐esteem, although the self‐esteem pathway for attachment avoidance was not statistically significant. indirect associations were consistently larger for attachment anxiety than for attachment avoidance. these findings suggest that emotion dysregulation and self‐esteem are important correlates of the attachment–social anxiety link, with a more pronounced indirect pattern for attachment anxiety. scandinavian journal of psychology
can motivational behaviours be trained online? acceptability and effectiveness of a self-determination theory-based interaction training for physical activity professionals psychology & health

a systematic review of studies using network analysis to examine the relationship between antisocial behavior and self-regulation in school-aged children and adolescents the association between antisocial behavior and self-regulation is well established, but their developmental interplay remains insufficiently understood. network analysis has increasingly been used to explore these relationships. we conducted a systematic review (prospero: crd420251161642) of studies applying network analysis to examine these connections in youth aged 6 to 18 years. following preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses guidelines, five databases were searched. fourteen studies met the inclusion criteria ( n > 24,000; 64% longitudinal). results showed that externalizing networks, including antisocial symptoms, were organized into distinct, interconnected clusters. at the symptom level, anger, temper, and arguing were the most central oppositional symptoms, whereas impulsive symptoms (difficulty waiting, blurting out, interrupting) functioned as bridge nodes linking externalizing clusters. at the process level, impulsivity emerged as a transdiagnostic bridge, whereas inhibitory control and emotion regulation were key central processes. developmentally, three potential intervention targets emerged: behavioral impulsivity in childhood, inhibitory control and attention dysregulation in early adolescence, and emotion dysregulation and irritability in mid-adolescence. these findings highlight the value of network approaches for understanding developmental pathways linking self-regulation and externalizing behavior and may inform developmentally targeted interventions. international journal of behavioral development

a psychometric examination of digital stress in adolescents digital stress is increasingly recognized as a correlate of adolescent internalizing symptoms, yet evidence on reliable and culturally appropriate measurement remains limited in chinese samples. we evaluated the factor structure, reliability, test–retest stability, convergent validity, and measurement invariance of the digital stress scale (dss). a total of 2,191 adolescents (ages 11–17) from three chinese cities completed measures of digital stress, depression, anxiety, and short-form video addiction. the sample was randomly split for cross-validation. exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a four-factor dss-16, with the original fear-of-missing-out facet not retained. the dss-16 showed strong internal consistency and moderate 6-month test–retest reliability. convergent validity was evidenced by positive associations with depression, anxiety, and short-form video addiction. multigroup models indicated metric and scalar invariance across sex, school level, urban–rural residence, only-child status, and paternal and maternal education level. the dss-16 is a brief, reliable, and invariant measure of adolescent digital stress in china, suitable for equitable screening and research in mental health contexts. international journal of behavioral development

beyond translation: a multi-evidential validity argument for the school-adapted arabic ktk. background: performance-based motor assessments are frequently transferred across cultural and educational contexts under the assumption that translation alone preserves score meaning. however, school-based adaptations may alter the score-generating process and, consequently, the interpretations that can be supported. using the körperkoordinationstest für kinder (ktk) as an empirical case, this study examined how a school-adapted arabic version should be interpreted within a validity-argument framework.
methods: a multi-evidential psychometric evaluation was conducted with 316 saudi primary-school boys from eight schools. evidence based on internal structure was examined using efa, cfa, and split-sample replication, alongside reliability and measurement precision (, icc, sem, mdc₉₅), measurement invariance, grade-related differentiation, practice effects, and preliminary external associations.
results: results supported a replicable one-factor coordination structure (cfi = 0.979), satisfactory composite reliability ( = 0.796), and good temporal stability (icc = 0.870). the battery showed strong differentiation across grade levels ( = 0.419). metric invariance was supported, whereas full scalar invariance was not, indicating that structural replication did not automatically justify unrestricted score comparisons. systematic practice effects were observed for several subtests and the composite score, limiting straightforward interpretation of repeated measurements. the composite mdc₉₅ was 0.80 composite-score units. because age and anthropometric data were not recorded, grade differences indicate cross-sectional grade-group differentiation rather than developmental change.
conclusion: the findings extend beyond linguistic adaptation of the ktk by showing that performance-based assessments should be evaluated in terms of the score interpretations they support within a specific context. the school-adapted arabic ktk supports a coherent coordination construct and bounded use of the composite score, but does not justify direct application of the original german motor quotient classifications. more broadly, the study shows how evidence based on internal structure, reliability, measurement error, and measurement invariance can be considered together when defining defensible score use across cultural contexts. this shifts the focus of cross-cultural adaptation from translation alone to the validity of the inferences drawn from adapted scores. frontiers in psychology

initial examination of the need for chaos (revised) scale in german. the termrefers to an individual's mindset demonstrating a desire for the destruction of the established order and the societal structures. this novel construct may be of relevance for forensic, legal, and safety matters as well as politics. to measure differences in individuals' need for chaos, the seven-items nfcscale was developed in english. later two items were added to create the recently proposed nine-items nfcscale. in the present study ( = 817), we present german adaptations of those two scales and an initial examination of their psychometric properties. for the german seven-items nfcscale, we found a two-dimensional structure with the factorsandwhich were strongly and positively interrelated. the semantic content of the two additional items of the german nine-items nfcscale and the statistical analyses suggest that these items capture yet another construct (i.e.,). furthermore, results preliminary indicate sufficient reliability and validity of both german adaptations. dark personality measures (e.g., dark core, psychopathy), left-wing authoritarian antihierarchical aggression, radicalism intention (i.e., the intention to use illegal and violent means for political ends), and the inclination to justify political violence emerged as substantial correlates of the need for chaos in our german-speaking sample. frontiers in psychology

spatial iris chromaticity disparities as phenotypic correlates of harm avoidance temperament in a korean sample. introduction: the human iris has a complex developmental origin, with neural crest-derived cells contributing to the formation of the iris stroma and its melanocyte population. although ocular visual features have been linked to personality traits in western cohorts, whether quantitative spatial chromaticity disparities in the iris are associated with temperament dimensions in korean individuals remains understudied.
methods: digital iris images from 100 korean adults included in the final analytic sample were normalized using daugman's rubber-sheet model and partitioned into an eight-subregion polar coordinate grid. commission internationale de l'éclairage*** chromaticity metrics and spatial disparity indices-directional (superior-inferior, δsi; nasal-temporal, δnt) and radial (inner-outer, δio)-were extracted along the corresponding color axes. personality temperaments were assessed using the korean temperament and character inventory-revised short version (k-tci-rs). hierarchical regression analysis and 5,000-iteration nonparametric bootstrapping were performed. a benjamini-hochberg false discovery rate (fdr) correction was additionally applied across the 12 temperament-chromaticity models as a sensitivity analysis for multiplicity.
results: global mean iris chromaticity parameters were not significantly associated with the examined temperament dimensions. among the 12 temperament-chromaticity models examined, only the harm avoidance (ha)-* model showed a significant incremental contribution of the spatial disparity block, which was associated with an additional 14.7% of the variance in ha scores (δ = 0.147, = 0.001) and remained statistically significant after fdr correction (fdr-adjusted = 0.012). specifically, nasal-temporal disparity (δ*; = -0.210, = 0.039) was negatively associated with ha, whereas the inner-outer radial gradient (δ*; = 0.291, = 0.006) showed a positive association.
discussion: among the models examined, spatial iris chromaticity disparities along the yellow-blue (*) axis showed an incremental association with ha beyond global mean chromaticity in this korean sample. these exploratory findings support further investigation of spatial iris colorimetry in relation to temperament and require replication in independent populations. frontiers in psychology

when social change feels threatening: multiple pathways to reactionary politicized identification and collective action abstract efforts to recognize gender diversity have become sites of political conflict, mobilizing progressive support and reactionary resistance. understanding this resistance requires identifying which grievances arise during social change and explaining how they correlate with reactionary politicized identities and collective action. we argue that societal change becomes psychologically consequential through multiple identity‐related threats. study 1 ( n = 1160) demonstrates that perceived threats to identity‐relevant aspects of social change—changes to gender and sexuality categories, one's gender identity and the societal order—uniquely correlate with stronger identification as an opponent of gender diversity, which mediates their associations with collective action against gender‐inclusive language. study 2 ( n = 619) replicates these results, controlling for perceived aesthetic quality of gender‐inclusive language, and extends them to identification as an opponent of the queer movement and opposition to transgender inclusion. these findings highlight multiple identity‐related pathways linking social change to reactionary politicized identification and collective action. european journal of social psychology

disgust at tainted souls: testing the character hypothesis of disgust through descriptions of dark personality traits abstract disgust is commonly reported in response to socio‐moral violations, but whether and how it differs from anger in these contexts is often debated. preliminary evidence that disgust tracks the bad character of actors has left unanswered the question of which observable actions, other than visibly harming other people, lead to such character judgements. we tested the character hypothesis of disgust using a novel idea: that the perception of dark personality traits could be an important cue to bad character without direct harm. our three pre‐registered experiments ( n s = 191, 180, 157) tested participants’ emotional responses to observable behavioural signals of sadism, narcissism and machiavellianism respectively. harmful consequences were also manipulated in two of the experiments. results further supported the character hypothesis of disgust, shedding light on the difference between the two often intertwined moral emotions and the multi‐faceted concept of bad moral character. european journal of social psychology

waking up to the working day ahead: a diary study on the role of flow in linking morning anticipatory appraisals to recovery abstract in this diary study, we investigated how employees’ morning anticipatory appraisals relate to their flow experiences at work and their subsequent recovery after work. drawing on transactional stress theory, we explored how four types of morning anticipatory appraisal—positive, challenge, threat, and hindrance—predict daily flow at work, and whether flow, in turn, is associated with energy in the evening and affective rumination at bedtime. a total of 102 employees completed three daily surveys across ten consecutive working days. the results from multilevel mediation analysis revealed that morning anticipatory challenge and positive appraisal were positively related to daily flow, while anticipatory threat appraisal was negatively associated with flow. flow, in turn, predicted lower affective rumination at bedtime and mediated the effects of morning anticipatory appraisals on this outcome. contrary to expectations, flow was not significantly related to evening energy levels and did not mediate the effects at the within-person level. in conclusion, our results suggest that morning anticipatory appraisals formed before the working day are meaningfully related to employee well-being by shaping the likelihood of experiencing flow at work and the extent of work-related rumination at bedtime. in doing so, this study advances stress and recovery theory by identifying flow as a key mechanism linking early-day cognitive expectations to evening recovery outcomes, and by highlighting the anticipatory phase as a promising target for interventions aimed at improving employees’ day-to-day functioning. journal of happiness studies
longitudinal dynamics of inner peace: a 2-wave outcome-wide assessment of its association with 55 other flourishing variables in the global flourishing study journal of happiness studies

the social transmission of linguistic alignment: the role of observational reinforcement learning abstract people align their linguistic use in conversations, and it has been proposed that such linguistic alignment facilitates mutual understanding and social rapport. however, the mechanisms through which perspective alignment is socially transmitted across individuals remain unclear. here, we combined behavioural experimentation and computational learning models to investigate whether, and if so, how observing aligned and unaligned responses in others affects people's perspective alignment in subsequent language use. participants completed a three‐session design. first, in a baseline session, they played a picture matching and naming game with a child interlocutor, in which they took turns with the child participant (in fact, just recordings) to name and match pictures. second, in an observational learning session, on each trial, they first observed the child and an adult (a demonstrator) describing pictures from an appearance perspective or an occupation perspective, with the adult often or rarely using the same perspective as the child; in particular, participants were asked to explicitly predict the expression of the adult. afterwards, they played a round with the child themselves. finally, in the generalization session, they played the same picture matching and naming game as in the baseline session, but with a new child. observing high alignment increased observers' own alignment, whereas observing low alignment decreased it, and these changes carried over to the new child, indicating a communicative strategy that generalizes across interlocutors of the same category rather than a partner‐specific adjustment. to identify the underlying mechanism, we modelled behaviour trial by trial. a rescorla–wagner model first confirmed that participants learned to predict the demonstrator's choices. we then used bayesian model comparison to adjudicate three accounts of how alignment changed. a model driven by observational prediction errors (i.e. the discrepancy between participants' predictions and the demonstrator's actual choices) outperformed both an imitation account (copying the most recent choice) and a priming account (the cumulative frequency of the demonstrator's aligned responses). in the high alignment group, both positive and negative prediction errors in the second half of the observational learning session predicted alignment changes, whereas in the low alignment group, negative prediction errors predicted decreased alignment. exploratory analyses further suggested that alignment may function as a social signal: observers rated high‐alignment demonstrators as more perspective‐taking than low‐alignment demonstrators. together, these findings show that perspective alignment can be socially transmitted through prediction‐error‐driven observational learning, neither passive copying nor mere exposure, and offer a computational account of how communicative strategies spread across individuals. british journal of psychology

parental mindful parenting and adolescent athletes’ social-emotional competence: a dyadic and latent profile analysis of profile-specific associations international journal of sport and exercise psychology

pathways of positive youth development, hope, and life satisfaction: a multi‐country study among southeast asian youth abstract positive youth development (pyd) has gained prominence through models such as the 7cs—competence, confidence, connection, character, caring, contribution, and creativity—yet relatively little is known about how these dimensions function in southeast asian contexts, where young people navigate diverse cultural values, socio‐economic structures, and access to resources. further, although pyd attributes are linked to life satisfaction, limited work has explored mechanisms that may explain these associations. this study investigated the direct and indirect relations of the 7cs with life satisfaction via hope among youth from six southeast asian countries. participants included 1967 emerging adults (aged 18–25) from indonesia, malaysia, the philippines, singapore, thailand, and vietnam. a series of confirmatory factor analyses and structural equation modeling were conducted to examine the direct and indirect associations of the 7cs with life satisfaction via hope, while accounting for gender, age, and education. controlling for the covariates, results showed that confidence, connection, and creativity had indirect associations with life satisfaction through hope. country‐specific models revealed culturally distinct associations, such as the significant indirect role of character in the philippines, and the nonsignificant relations of confidence and creativity with well‐being outcomes in thailand and singapore, respectively. together, these findings advance the understanding of the 7cs in southeast asia, highlight hope as an important mechanism linking pyd to life satisfaction, and underscore the importance of culturally relevant approaches to youth development in the region. journal of research on adolescence

building capacity for engagement: a scoping review of informal and formal research training for indigenous youth abstract community‐based research approaches, including community‐based participatory action research (cbpar), are a research design that engages communities as active collaborators by offering training and support throughout the research process. these approaches, including cbpar, have gained traction in work with indigenous youth, as they build research capacity and foster equitable partnerships between community members and researchers. as an underrepresented population in cbpar, indigenous youth offer critical perspectives that can deepen understanding of community needs and inform culturally responsive approaches. to explore the uptake in community‐based research approaches and youth inclusion, this scoping review analyzed 37 research articles detailing 33 research training programs for indigenous youth engaged in research in canada, the united states, aotearoa (new zealand), and australia. training programs ranged from providing a brief overview of the research process (42%) to teaching youth specific research skills (27%). youth involvement also varied across training programs, from being included as study participants (15%) to extensive youth co‐researcher partnerships (48%). key themes were extracted from the articles to highlight the limitations and strengths of the research training programs. the programs demonstrated variability in delivery and youth involvement, with limited capacity to sustain research advancement post‐project. these findings support the need for a guide on wise practices for meaningfully engaging indigenous youth in research and for building community capacity. journal of research on adolescence
value of a human mind: how perceived ai-authorship shapes willingness to pay for cultural goods creativity research journal
dying is easy. comedy is hard: how gay comix navigated the aids crisis journal of homosexuality

same stimulus, different ideas: prior knowledge and the integration of ai-generated stimuli in creative ideation external stimuli can expand the conceptual space during creative ideation, yet individuals may incorporate the same stimuli differently depending on the knowledge and experience available to them. this issue bears on the information-processing mechanisms of creativity and on the use of generative artificial intelligence as a source of stimuli. nine groups (221 participants) from three educational and sociocultural contexts (indigenous and afro-descendant community members holding traditional knowledge, rural school students, and university students) took part in ideation workshops to design agro-industrial products. stimuli were generated with a large language model. semantic and conceptual embedding similarity and topic modelling were used to compare initial ideas, stimuli, and final ideas. topic models of these very short texts were unstable. in the community and school groups, conceptual integration generally stayed close to the initial proximity between ideas and stimuli, whereas the university groups more often exceeded it, a tendency that held across alternative representations but not in every group. coffee-domain groups, whose ideas and stimuli shared the vocabulary of the raw material, combined high persistence with high integration. three exploratory forms of integration are proposed: conceptual reinterpretation, expansion, and transformation. the analyses are descriptive, and prior knowledge was not measured directly. journal of intelligence

enhancing creative thinking in primary school students through a structured experiential practice course: a quasi-experimental test of the open teaching model this study introduces and evaluates open, a structured teaching model that translates thinking-based instruction into a coherent sequence for creativity-oriented experiential learning. by integrating origin, plan, explore, and narrate, the model connects problem identification and collaborative planning with evidence-based inquiry, revision, and communication—processes often addressed separately in primary-school practice. we examined open in a 12-week class-level quasi-experimental study involving 400 students in grades 3–4 across 10 intact classes in one primary school. five classes received the open course, while five received a regular practice course with comparable instructional time and thematic resources. standardized and curriculum-based measures assessed creative thinking and related practical performance before and after the intervention. to reflect the nested classroom design, class-level change scores and small-sample-corrected cluster-robust estimates served as the principal basis for inference, with student-level mixed anovas providing complementary analyses. student-level analyses indicated gains in selected creative-thinking and performance indicators. cluster-aware estimates for the four theory-prioritized outcomes were positive, although imprecise. the study offers an ecologically grounded test of how a clearly specified instructional model can be embedded in routine primary-school practice. open provides a replicable framework for aligning creative-thinking goals, teacher scaffolding, inquiry, and student products, and offers a foundation for more rigorous multi-school evaluation of creativity-focused teaching. journal of intelligence

cognitive predictors of ai-related textual change in upper-intermediate l2 russian writing: working memory, attention control, and critical thinking generative artificial intelligence (ai) can alter final second-language (l2) texts, yet cognitive differences may shape which changes emerge. this exploratory study examined 38 upper-intermediate learners of russian who each produced one composition with ai assistance and one without it. working memory, attention control, and critical thinking were measured continuously, and 11 textual outcomes were calculated from paired compositions. ai-assisted texts showed higher lemma-based lexical-diversity values, longer words, more connectives per 100 words, and substantially fewer first-person markers, while total word count, sentence measures, and formulaic-expression rate did not differ in the full sample. the higher pos-based content-word density was attenuated after first-person forms were excluded, suggesting a contribution from the change in person marking. exploratory models suggested negative working-memory associations with lexical-diversity and connective-rate change, and negative attention-control associations with lexical-diversity change. the positive working-memory coefficient for word-count change was sensitive to hc3 estimation and leave-one-out refitting. critical thinking showed no clear independent association in the primary change-score models, while positive coefficients for mattr and hd-d appeared in the outcome-conditioned models. under this supervised, student-mediated procedure, ai assistance was associated with lexical, discourse-marking, and stance differences in completed l2 texts. journal of intelligence

the extrinsic motivational mechanism of creativity: the moderating role of creative problem‐solving requirements and creative self‐efficacy abstract this study examines how extrinsic motivation influences employee creativity by distinguishing between creativity quantity and creativity quality. using data from 183 independent employee–manager dyads, we found that extrinsic motivation directly predicted creativity quantity, but not creativity quality. however, extrinsic motivation indirectly predicted both creativity outcomes through employees' engagement in creativity‐relevant processes. overall, its effect was more pronounced for creativity quantity than for creativity quality. we further found that the relationship between extrinsic motivation and creativity‐relevant processes was stronger when creative problem‐solving requirements were lower or when creative self‐efficacy was higher. these findings contribute to the motivation and creativity literature by clarifying how and when extrinsic motivation supports employee creativity, particularly creativity quantity. they also underscore the importance of a balanced approach that integrates both intrinsic and extrinsic motivational drivers to foster creativity in organizations. journal of creative behavior

unlocking the collective paradoxical frame in creativity: the role of inter‐group competition abstract the present study examined how collective paradoxical frame training and intergroup competition influence virtual team creativity. a sample of 159 students collaborated in small groups of 3–4 to complete a creative task. groups were trained on developing a collective paradoxical frame using images and examples from multicultural (highly conflicting ideas) or single–culture (moderately conflicting ideas) contexts. a control group condition received no exposure or training. both the multicultural and single culture conditions were further primed with instructions either to compete or not to compete with other groups. the multicultural exposure groups generated more ideas and more original ideas than the single culture exposure or the control condition. also, groups in the competition condition produced more elaborations than the non‐competition group. mediation analyses indicated that competition predicted higher fluency and originality indirectly through the mechanism of elaboration. finally, competition interacted with paradoxical frame training such that the novelty of ideas was highest when groups received multicultural paradoxical framing and were primed to compete, suggesting that competition can unlock the creative potential of a collective paradoxical frame. these findings have implications for designing training programs in the management of virtual teams and educational settings, encouraging the integration of paradoxical framing to promote creative outcomes. findings further show that intergroup competition can be constructive when it channels effort into deeper elaboration of ideas. journal of creative behavior

from pretend play to design: affordance‐based reinterpretation for conceptual design ideation abstract this study explores the relationship between pretense and the conceptual design process, challenging the traditional view that pretense is exclusive to childhood. within the framework of affordance‐based design creativity, it argues that affordance‐based pretense can play an important role in conceptual design. by linking pretense to creative thinking in design, the study examines how affordance‐based reinterpretation processes observed in pretend play can inform conceptual design ideation. the research draws conceptual parallels between children's pretend play and the early stages of the design process, where creative problem‐solving relies on reinterpreting forms and generating alternative possibilities. through a review of existing literature and experimental simulation of an “affordance‐based pretense process” with both design and non‐design students, how pretense—or the ability to “see as if”—affects creative performance during the initial form‐giving phase of design is examined. the findings suggest that affordance‐based reinterpretation supports creative performance and highlight the interaction between cognitive generation and engagement with external design representations during conceptual design. exploring these relationships, the study contributes to design creativity research by demonstrating how reinterpretation processes derived from children's pretend play can be meaningfully adapted to an adult conceptual design context. journal of creative behavior

correlates and predictors of binge eating disorder in male populations: a systematic review abstract objective this prisma‐compliant systematic review synthesises empirical literature on correlates and predictors of dsm‐5/dsm‐iv binge eating disorder (bed) in male populations (prospero: crd420250644500). method eligible studies used male‐only samples, sex‐stratified analyses, or comparisons involving men with bed. psycnet, ebscohost, pubmed and web of science (english, peer‐reviewed, full‐text) were utilised, with the final search conducted in march 2026. risk of bias was assessed using joanna briggs institute critical appraisal checklists. a structured, narrative synthesis is presented. results most of the 27 included studies were cross‐sectional and conducted in the united states. age ranged from birth to 18 years in longitudinal child/adolescent samples, and 18–74 years in adult samples but precise data for male bed subsamples was lacking. studies identified a range of factors associated with bed in male populations, including childhood/intergenerational trauma, eating and weight‐related cognitions/behaviours, psychiatric diagnoses, psychopathology, neurodevelopmental difficulties, biological health indicators, and epigenetic factors. risk of bias was low to moderate. conclusions the literature is constrained by a lack of studies that examine male bed presentations, including both within‐group analyses and sex‐based comparisons. adequately powered studies of men with bed are needed to clarify risk factors and establish a robust, integrated evidence base for clinical practice. european eating disorders review

childhood trauma and apoeε4 are associated with patterns of developmental frontal alpha connectivity, posttraumatic stress, and alcohol‐related outcomes abstract childhood trauma affects neurodevelopment and lifelong risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (ptsd) and alcohol use disorder (aud). changes in brain structures and function are observed in young carriers of apoeε4 , the genetic factor most associated with alzheimer's disease. longitudinal studies of apoeε4 , childhood trauma, and neural connectivity in adolescence have not been explored. we studied 837 trauma‐exposed participants (53% female) from the collaborative study on the genetics of alcoholism prospective sample, using latent growth curve models to assess associations of childhood trauma and apoeε4 on repeated measures of frontal alpha eeg coherence (eegc) throughout adolescence and young adulthood. young adult aud and ptsd symptoms were also examined. results indicate childhood sexual assaultive trauma (csat) and apoeε4 are linked to neural connectivity, with effects differing by brain region and direction. csat was associated with a higher eegc baseline but less growth in three eegc pairs, while apoeε4 associated with lower left frontocentral (lfc) eegc baseline and higher slope. eegc patterns and symptoms of ptsd and aud were robustly associated. a significant interaction between csat‐by‐ apoeε4 interaction also emerged, such that among apoeε4 carriers, childhood sexual assaultive trauma was associated with higher baseline pfi and diminished growth in pfi and lfc eegc. no significant direct links between apoeε4 and ptsd or aud were observed. findings highlight how eegc may help explain connections between genetics, trauma, and psychopathology, guiding at‐risk group identification and informing prevention strategies. genes brain and behavior

filial piety and subjective well-being across adult age groups: evidence from vietnamese adults background this study examines the relationship between filial piety and subjective well-being (swb) among adult children in vietnam, addressing the limited body of research that has compared the psychological implications of filial piety across different stages of adulthood. participants and procedure drawing on the dual filial piety model, two developmental cohorts were investigated: emerging adults aged 18-23 and adults aged 29-59. data were collected from a sample of 1,085 participants and assessed using the dual filial piety scale (dfps) and the mental health continuum–short form (mhc-sf). results the findings indicated that both reciprocal filial piety (rfp) and authoritarian filial piety (afp) were positively associated with, and served as meaningful predictors of, overall swb as well as its three constituent domains, namely emotional well-being, psychological well-being, and social well-being. these results suggest that filial piety continues to function as an important value orientation that is associated with positive psychological functioning among vietnamese adults. further-more, notable age-related differences emerged. older adults reported higher levels of both rfp and afp than emerging adults, indicating a stronger endorsement of filial values in later stages of life. in addition, the associations between filial piety and well-being were more pronounced among older adults, suggesting that the psychological benefits of filial piety may strengthen with age and life experience. conclusions while filial piety remains a relevant moral compass across adulthood in vietnam, its contribution to well-being appears to be most substantial when these values are deeply internalized and integrated into individuals’ sense of self. the findings are discussed within vietnam’s sociocultural context, and directions for future research are proposed to further clarify the devel-opmental and cultural dynamics underlying the link between filial piety and well-being. health psychology report

student mental health profiles in poland and vietnam: multigroup latent profile analysis using asr-derived dimensions background mental health difficulties are a growing concern among university students, particularly during emerging adulthood. given the potential role of cultural context, this study aimed to identify latent profiles of psychological functioning among stu-dents in poland and vietnam and examine their demographic and educational correlates. participants and procedure the study included 1,753 university students from poland and vietnam (m_age = 20.45, sd = 4.77), predominantly women. measures included the adult self-report (revised seven-factor model), school burnout inventory, utrecht study engagement scale, and questions on sleep and learning-related values. analyses comprised exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, measurement invariance testing, and latent profile analysis. results four profiles emerged in both countries, reflecting varying severity of co-occurring internalizing and externalizing symptoms. profiles differed across countries, with membership associated with gender in vietnam and year of study and study-work status in poland. educational burnout and study engagement differentiated profiles in both samples. conclusions the findings reveal broadly similar patterns of co-occurring psychological difficulties across both countries, but differences in severity and correlates. as sociocultural mechanisms were not directly assessed, these differences cannot be attributed to specific cultural processes. the findings support person-centered approaches to psychological functioning and underscore the need for further research on sociocultural influences. health psychology report

how university students think about the next fifty years: future orientation and career decision-making future orientation predicts career decision-making, yet its temporal extension—how far ahead people project—is rarely varied. this study asked 15 higher-education students at a regional turkish university to reflect on their lives fifty years hence, an intentionally over-extended horizon chosen to make the handling of extension observable. interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. four domains were examined: the framing of the distant future, anticipated regret, the relation between present circumstances and future possibility, and the appraisal of one’s own effort. nine participants answered at the horizon as posed, in registers ranging from aspiration to enumerated uncertainty; three declined it, two substituted a nearer frame, and one gave an answer that could not be classified with confidence. positive distant-future images did not uniformly ease decision-making, and anticipated regret appeared in four distinguishable regulatory forms. implications for career counseling are advanced as hypotheses. journal of career development

bridging strength: comparing the strong black woman schema in black adolescent girls and emerging adult women the strong black woman (sbw) schema describes expectations of resilience, self-reliance, and emotional restraint placed on black women and has been linked to anxiety and depression. although extensively studied among adult women, limited research has examined how the schema operates during adolescence or across development. using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, this study examined sbw schema endorsement and internalizing symptoms among 94 black adolescent girls (ages 12–17) and emerging adult women (ages 18–25) and explored how participants understood and experienced strength. quantitative findings showed comparable sbw endorsement and internalizing symptoms across age groups; greater sbw endorsement was associated with internalizing symptoms, and age did not moderate this relationship. qualitative findings indicated that both groups viewed strength as a mostly unquestioned cultural expectation. however, adolescents described strength as compatible with emotional expression, whereas emerging adults more often equated strength with suppressing vulnerability and experienced the strength label as burdensome. these findings suggest that the emotional meaning of strength may differ across adolescence and emerging adulthood, highlighting the need for culturally responsive intervention and future longitudinal research. journal of black psychology

characteristics of tier 3 behavior intervention plans for autistic students this study investigated the characteristics of tier 3 behavior intervention plans (bips) for autistic students in two public schools in the u.s. state of california. guided by three research questions, we examined (a) what types of behaviors and functions of behaviors are included in bips, (b) which evidence-based practices (ebps) are most commonly embedded, and (c) how many ebps are included per plan. using a descriptive design, we analyzed 120 de-identified bips that scored “adequate” or above on the behavior support plan quality evaluation guide (bsp-qe). dependent variables included the target behaviors, hypothesized behavioral functions, and number and type of ebps coded across plan sections. results indicated that aggression (44%) and off-task/disruptive behavior (43%) were most frequently targeted, with escape/avoidance (95%) as the most common function. on average, bips contained 7.4 ebps, most often reinforcement, antecedent-based interventions (abi), functional communication training, prompting, response interruption/redirection, and visual supports. findings suggest that these high-frequency ebps could be embedded as tier 1 or tier 2 supports within multi-tiered systems of support (mtss), reducing the need for intensive tier 3 interventions and promoting more inclusive educational environments. journal of positive behavior interventions

when stereotypical inferences prevail in polysemy processing: explaining fallacies of equivocation this paper develops and examines the first psycholinguistic explanation of fallacies of equivocation. on this basis, it addresses questions about polysemy processing. the paper proceeds from a case study on fallacies involving polysemous appearance verbs. three studies provide evidence that subordinate uses of these verbs are interpreted through selective suppression of features from an event knowledge schema that overspecifies the relevant information, and that a comprehension bias interferes with the execution of this strategy and prevents the contextualisation of stereotypical inferences from the verbs. these contextualisation failures result in fallacies of equivocation, for example, in philosophically influential “arguments from illusion”. mind & language

familiarity and concentration- based intensity shape spatial patterns of odor-evoked brain activation abstract olfactory perception is shaped by both the physical properties of odorants and prior odor experience. odor familiarity and concentration-based perceptual intensity are known to influence neural responses; however, less is known about how odor-evoked brain activation varies across conditions that differ in familiarity and perceived strength. using functional magnetic resonance imaging, fmri, we examined condition-specific activation patterns and brain-behavior relationships during passive odor perception. sixty-three healthy young women participated in a 2 × 2 factorial fmri experiment including familiar and unfamiliar odors presented at low- and high-intensity concentrations. odors were delivered birhinally using a computer-controlled olfactometer, and participants provided in-scanner ratings of perceived odor intensity and odor-evoked memory intensity. whole-brain analyses were used to describe condition-wise activation maps and direct between-condition contrasts, while region-of-interest analyses focused on canonical olfactory, limbic, and memory-related regions. all odor conditions elicited activation across olfactory, limbic, frontal, parietal, and cerebellar regions. direct contrasts showed that low-intensity unfamiliar odors elicited greater activation than low-intensity familiar odors in frontal and parietal regions, suggesting increased evaluative processing when weak odor input could not be readily matched to established odor representations. low-intensity unfamiliar odors also elicited greater activation than high-intensity unfamiliar odors in precuneus and supramarginal/angular regions. brain-behavior analyses showed significant associations only for familiar odors presented at low intensity, where subjective memory intensity was negatively correlated with bilateral parahippocampal activation. these findings suggest that odor familiarity and concentration-based intensity contribute to condition-specific patterns of odor-evoked brain activation, with low-intensity familiar odors revealing a selective relationship between odor-evoked memory experience and medial temporal responses. behavioral and brain functions
do parents experience stress differently in response to children’s externalizing and internalizing behaviours? early child development and care

older and wiser or is age just a number? observations of recruitment, attainment and career aspirations in mature trainee psychological wellbeing practitioners (pwps) abstract widening participation in psychological wellbeing practitioner (pwp) training by targeting mature candidates has the potential to bring greater diversity of life experience into the profession, as well as address retention challenges. this paper presents observations on recruitment interest, academic performance, and career aspirations among mature pwp trainees (aged 35 years and older), in comparison with those of traditional pwp trainees (aged under 35 years). participants were recruited from pre-training events and training cohorts at the university of surrey. the study utilised a cross-sectional survey to understand the age profiles of trainees recruited into training, an analysis of routinely held participation and academic attainment data, and a longitudinal survey to explore future career aspirations between mature and traditional trainees. the findings showed that mature candidates attended recruitment events in proportionally higher numbers, but this did not necessarily translate to securing places on training. mature trainees achieved lower class awards and exhibited higher withdrawal and termination rates compared with traditional trainees. mature trainees reported higher intentions to stay in a pwp-related role than their traditional counterparts; however, both groups expressed concerns about poor progression opportunities and the risks of burnout. the implications of these findings for clinical services and university providers, along with recommendations for future research, are discussed. key learning aims (1) to outline the rationale for widening participation in pwp training, specifically focusing on mature candidates. (2) to outline interest for pwp training, academic attainment and career aspirations in mature pwp candidates and trainees. (3) to consider the implications of these findings for talking therapies services and university training providers, with regard to recruitment practices, training support and retention. cognitive behaviour therapist

understanding a digital community page of migrant women from turkey as a counterspace digital platforms increasingly shape how migrant women form communities and make sense of transnational lives. although women's and migrants’ engagement with social media have been extensively studied, less attention has been paid to how digital communities of migrant women can operate as counterspaces, understood as responses to distress caused by experiences of marginalization. in this study, migrant women , a public instagram page created by and for migrant women from turkey living abroad with over 20,000 followers, is examined. the aim is to understand how multiple subject positions become grounds for a digital counterspace and how care and solidarity are enacted here. drawing on counterspace scholarship, reflexive thematic analysis is adopted, examining multimodal content shared on migrant women between 2019 and 2024, including posts, captions, hashtags, co-posts with members, and curated story highlights. the findings identify three interrelated themes whereby migrant women can be defined as a counterspace: (1) making migrant womanhood a shared subject position, (2) community care as gendered psychosocial infrastructure, and (3) belonging through solidarity and the selectiveness of “we.” this study highlights the possibilities of this counterspace for and beyond the community, especially regarding the reconfiguration of community through the digital mediation and transnational reimagination of a counterspace. feminism & psychology

within‐person dual‐pathway model linking optimism to depression: a random‐intercept cross‐lagged panel study of cognitive bias and loneliness among chinese university students abstract this 1‐year longitudinal study applied a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (ri‐clpm) to examine how optimism influences depression through negative cognitive bias and loneliness among chinese college students, disentangling within‐person processes from stable between‐person differences. 886 college students completed the beck depression inventory, optimism scale, negative cognitive bias questionnaire and ucla loneliness scale at three time points over 1 year. (1) all four variables (optimism, negative cognitive bias, loneliness, depression) were significantly correlated across three time points (p < .001). (2) ri‐clpm revealed: within‐person surges in optimism predicted lower negative cognitive bias ( β = −.28, p < .001) and loneliness ( β = −.35, p < .001) at the next wave; these reductions predicted lower depression ( β = .36 and .41, p < .001). mediation was partial through negative cognitive bias (indirect β = −0.11, 95% ci [−0.18, −0.05]) but complete through loneliness (indirect β = −0.15, 95% ci [−0.23, −0.08]). optimism at t1 negatively predicted negative cognitive bias and loneliness at t2, which positively predicted depression at t3. after accounting for between‐person variability, within‐person increases in optimism predicted subsequent decreases in depression through two concurrent pathways: negative cognitive bias and loneliness. british journal of developmental psychology

testing the factor structure and psychometric properties of the toronto alexithymia scale-20 among a sample of individuals diagnosed with eating disorders abstract alexithymia is implicated in eating disorder phenomenology. the toronto alexithymia scale-20 (tas-20) is a commonly used measure of alexithymia, which has been used to investigate associations between alexithymia and eating disorders. however, the tas-20 has never been validated among individuals across the eating disorder spectrum. the purpose of this study was to test the factor structure and psychometric properties of the tas-20 in a sample of patients with eating disorders. participants were 710 patients admitted to a partial hospitalization program for eating disorder treatment. participants completed self-report instruments at admit and one-month into treatment. analyses tested the three-factor structure of the tas-20 using confirmatory factor analyses (cfa) and measurement invariance across eating disorder diagnosis. next, analyses tested the psychometric properties (i.e., convergent validity, internal consistency and test-retest reliability) of this model. cfa determined that the original three-factor structure of the tas-20 fit the data after removal of five items in the externally oriented thinking factor. this structure was invariant across diagnoses. the tas-20 showed strong test-retest reliability, good internal consistency (excluding externally oriented thinking), and moderate convergent validity. this structure of the tas-20 may be more appropriate to use in future clinical work and research among those with eating disorders. journal of psychopathology and behavioral assessment
negotiating normativity: a phenomenology of orientation. journal of theoretical and philosophical psychology

development and validation of the dishonesty in intimate relationships scale (dirs) abstract: dishonesty occurs in romantic relationships and can undermine relational functioning. existing measures typically focus on specific behaviors separately – such as infidelity or lying – rather than capturing dishonesty in romantic relationships more broadly. addressing this gap, based on three studies with over 3,300 participants overall, we introduce the dishonesty in intimate relationships scale (dirs). dirs is a 10-item measure grounded in a comprehensive framework of dishonesty in romantic relationships, consisting of two dimensions: deception (e.g., lying, withholding information) and infidelity (e.g., emotional and sexual unfaithfulness). study 1 ( n = 1,448) used exploratory factor analysis to identify the two-factor structure. study 2 ( n = 1,000) supported the structure with confirmatory factor analysis. study 3 aimed to substantiate the reliability and validity of the dirs across two measurement occasions ( n = 965 at first, n = 898 at second measurement occasion), including considering its factorial, convergent, discriminant, criterion, and incremental validity. next to partial support for dirs’ discriminant validity, results provided support for its convergent and criterion validity, including associations with relationship outcomes (e.g., ambivalence, authenticity, closeness, trust), beyond other dishonesty measures and basic personality dimensions. in sum, dirs offers a brief, reliable domain-specific tool for assessing dishonesty in romantic relationships. european journal of psychological assessment

beyond rater agreement on students’ behavior abstract: over the past decades, there has been increasing interest in the multi-informant assessment of students’ behavioral problems. the current study uses the strengths and difficulties questionnaire ( goodman, 1997 ) to investigate the consistency and specificity between self-reports, parent reports, and teacher reports of secondary students’ externalizing and internalizing problems ( n = 1,326 students). findings from a ct-c[m-1] model indicated moderate to low consistency between student reports and teacher or parent reports. as expected, gender and special needs status predicted specificity in other reports of students’ behavior to some extent, particularly for hyperactivity. overall, the results highlighted the vital role of multi-informant approaches in assessing students’ behavior problems. european journal of psychological assessment

an examination of future anxiety among vocational school students in relation to sociodemographic variables abstract aim this study aimed to examine future anxiety among vocational school students and to determine whether its dimensions differ according to sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics. materials and methods this descriptive cross-sectional study included 255 vocational school students aged 18–35 years. data were collected using a sociodemographic data form and the future anxiety scale in university students. the cronbach’s alpha coefficient of the total scale was .93 in the present study. descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, and one-way analysis of variance (anova) were used for data analysis results the mean total future anxiety scale score was 55.47 ± 15.26. significant differences were observed in selected dimensions of future anxiety according to age, marital status, economic status, regular hobby engagement, regular exercise, family financial support, academic department, and dietary habits. poor perceived economic status was associated with higher fear of the future and hopelessness about the future scores. conclusion selected sociodemographic, economic, and lifestyle characteristics were associated with specific dimensions of future anxiety among vocational school students. the findings highlight the importance of psychosocial and career-support services for students experiencing economic and future-related uncertainty. discover psychology

negative partner perceptions as an indirect pathway between critical adverse experiences and negative communication in adult romantic relationships. adverse experiences, distressing or harmful lived events, affect multiple domains of functioning and are consistently linked to poorer relational functioning. however, cognitive mechanisms linking adverse experiences to communication behaviors in romantic relationships remain understudied. "critical" adverse experiences (caes) involving interpersonal harm or mental health concerns may be especially impactful. drawing on cognitive and stress-based frameworks, this study examined whether caes were indirectly associated with negative conflict behaviors through negative partner perceptions. self-report data from 2814 individuals across three waves of the german family panel were analyzed using longitudinal structural equation modeling. greater exposure to caes was associated with more negative partner perceptions, which in turn predicted subsequent negative communication behaviors. the indirect effect was significant but small, supporting a temporally ordered cognitive pathway. findings extend cross-sectional research by demonstrating three-wave longitudinal associations and highlight the impact of caes across the lifespan. implications for clinicians and researchers are discussed. journal of marital and family therapy

association between help seeking, motivation, and relationship satisfaction in couples post traumatic brain injury. traumatic brain injury (tbi) presents significant challenges for couples, affecting communication, emotional regulation, and overall relationship dynamics. this study examines the association between help-seeking, motivation, and relationship satisfaction in couples where one partner has experienced a tbi. specifically, we investigated (a) how self-stigma for help-seeking influenced motivation for mental health service engagement in both partners and (b) whether these associations varied by relationship satisfaction. using the actor partner interdependence model (apim), we assessed 160 couples to explore the interdependence of help-seeking stigma on both motivation and perceived relationship quality. results indicated that there was a statistically significant difference in perceived relationship quality between tbi and non-tbi partners. actor and partner effects were not statistically significant in this sample. however, the findings highlight the complexities of relational dynamics in tbi-affected couples and emphasize the need for further research on tbi related help-seeking stigma and relational support mechanisms. journal of marital and family therapy

the history of the rcmas‐2 and its reliability and validity (factor structure) examined in an irish context this paper reviews the psychometric properties of the revised children′s manifest anxiety scale—second edition (rcmas‐2) in irish children ( n = 912) aged 8–12 years with a view to examining its validity (factor structure) and its reliability. confirmatory factor analysis was conducted to describe the factor structure of the rcmas‐2. more specifically, it examined whether the original two‐factor structure was preferable to three‐factor or five‐factor structures. the results show that different indices favour different models, and that no single model provided a best fit to the data. the two‐factor model contained (a) an overall anxiety measure and (b) a defensiveness scale. the three‐factor model contained (a) anxiety: worry and oversensitivity, (b) anxiety: physiological and (c) anxiety: fear/concentration. the five‐factor model contained three anxiety and two defensiveness factors. in this study, the rcmas‐2 demonstrated good internal consistency, similar to the values reported in the manual, with an overall cronbach′s alpha coefficient of 0.92, and values of 0.75, 0.88 and 0.82 for the physiological anxiety, worry and social anxiety subtests. educational and clinical implications of the findings for those who work with children are discussed, and suggestions for further research are proposed. new directions for child and adolescent development

capability–opportunity–motivation–behavior (com-b) correlates of physical activity in people with multiple sclerosis who have analogue generalized anxiety disorder abstract background generalized anxiety disorder (gad) is prevalent, yet poorly managed among people with multiple sclerosis (ms). physical activity (pa) may be a potential lifestyle, behavioral approach for managing gad in ms. as a foundational step in developing pa behavior change interventions, this study applied the capability–opportunity–motivation–behavior (com-b) model for explaining pa behavior in people with ms who have analogue gad (agad). methods participants ( n = 320) prescreened for agad completed online surveys regarding pa (godin leisure time exercise questionnaire (glteq), physical activity staging questionnaire (pasq)) and com-b constructs. participants were categorized into current pa groups based on glteq scores, and long-term pa groups based on pasq scores. multivariate analysis of variance and discriminant function analysis (dfa) identified com-b constructs that differentiated pa groups. results all com-b constructs significantly differed among current and long-term pa groups. dfa identified action control, intention, self-efficacies (action, maintenance, recovery), action and coping planning, and goal setting as primary constructs differentiating pa groups. conclusion this study identified factors within the capability and motivation domains of the com-b model as primary correlates of pa in persons with ms and agad. such results might guide the development of behavior change interventions for increasing pa and perhaps treating gad in ms. international journal of behavioral medicine

resilience in psychotherapy with sexual and gender-diverse clients: a scoping review this scoping review examined how resilience theory can be applied in psychotherapeutic work with sexual and gender-diverse (sgd) clients, addressing a gap in both south african and international psychology literature. while sgd research has largely focused on adversity, stigma and minority stress, less attention has been given to strengths-based therapeutic approaches. resilience is commonly conceptualised as a dynamic process arising from interactions between individuals and their social environments that enables adaptation in the face of adversity, offering a useful lens for affirmative and culturally competent psychotherapeutic practice. following the arksey and o’malley framework and prisma extension for scoping reviews (prisma-scr) guidelines, 11 databases, two search engines and reference lists were searched. of 62 records identified, seven published between 2012 and 2024 met inclusion criteria. inductive thematic analysis revealed four patterns: a shift from deficit-based to strengths-oriented approaches; a socio-ecological understanding of resilience across individual, family and community contexts; recognition of unconventional resilience strategies; and the central role of affirmative practice and cultural competence in resilience-informed therapy. notably, no south african records were identified. the review highlights the need for local empirical research and for integrating resilience-informed, affirmative approaches into psychological training and practice to advance equitable and meaningful mental health care for sgd clients. south african journal of psychology

spanish translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and psychometric validation of the catq-s and fatq-s: assessing motivational functions of online and face-to-face aggression in secondary school students. background: peer aggression, both face-to-face and online, is a growing public health concern that affects adolescents' emotional wellbeing, social participation, and academic functioning. understanding the motivational functions that sustain these behaviours is essential for designing effective school-based interventions.
objective: this study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate the short spanish versions of the cyber aggression typology questionnaire (catq-s) and the face-to-face aggression typology questionnaire (fatq-s), which assess four motivational functions of aggression in secondary school students.
methods: an instrumental, cross-sectional design was used. following international guidelines for translation and cross-cultural adaptation, the instruments were translated, back-translated, and reviewed by an expert committee. comprehensibility and perceived difficulty were examined in a sample of 96 secondary school students (ages 12-16). psychometric validation was conducted in a separate sample of 1443 compulsory secondary education students (ages 11-16) from public schools in extremadura, spain. confirmatory factor analyses, internal consistency indices, convergent validity, and measurement invariance across gender were assessed.
results: both the catq-s and fatq-s replicated the original four-factor structure with acceptable to good fit indices. internal consistency and ave-based convergent validity were satisfactory across factors, whereas discriminant validity was not uniformly supported because of substantial overlap between some motivational dimensions. multigroup analyses showed configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance by gender, indicating that the instruments function equivalently for boys and girls.
conclusions: the spanish versions of the catq-s and fatq-s are brief, conceptually grounded instruments showing generally adequate psychometric properties for assessing motivational functions of peer aggression in spanish-speaking secondary school students. their use may support research and educational assessment of the motives underlying aggressive behaviour in school settings. acta psychologica
ambiguous loss and meaning reconstruction following dementia nursing home placement journal of loss & trauma

ai-anxiety, hope, and techno-subjunctivity: expanding psychoanalytic identity for the ai age this article recognizes that the artificial intelligence (ai) age is reconfiguring conditions for intimacy, clinical care, and psychoanalytic professional identity. beginning with ai-anxiety as a response to transformative change and technological peril, it highlights hope, not as optimism but as an active way of being that permits sustained engagement. against the reassuring claim that machines can never do what psychoanalysts do, the article distinguishes performance from process: relational ai may soon replicate expert clinical behavior without replicating human subjectivity, embodiment, or unconscious life. what remains irreducible is the meaning-making context of human care, including the fact that analytic speech acts derive meaning and force from being offered by a vulnerable, invested human other. the article then introduces techno-subjunctivity to describe the new relational field created by anthropomorphic ai: an illusion of intimacy in which users oscillate between feeling recognized by a responsive other while knowing they are interacting with a machine without interiority. psychoanalytic identity, the article concludes, must expand to include ai-fitness. such direct experience with ai’s relational pull along with critical psychoanalytic reflection will enable clinicians to accompany patients and students through techno-subjunctive life without denial, shame, or surrender. journal of the american psychoanalytic association

acting out traumatic hysteria at the salpêtrière hospital: performance and practice in jean-martin charcot’s clinic this article reexamines neurologist jean-martin charcot’s (1825–1893) clinical work at the salpêtrière hospital in paris and reassesses how he diagnosed and treated patients with traumatic hysteria. departing from scholarship that views charcot as a positivist nosologist or a clinical performer, this study demonstrates that his clinical practice cannot be reduced to either nosological classification or theatrical spectacle alone. drawing on photographic documentation, clinical lessons, recorded physician-patient interactions, and a first-person testimony, the study advances three main arguments. charcot’s clinical practice was defined by embryonic versions of psychological concepts (autosuggestion, transference, acting out, dissociation, idées fixes , abreaction, and motor reeducation) that foreshadowed janet’s and freud’s psychoanalytic theories. moreover, the performative nature of charcot’s clinical theater also created, perhaps inadvertently, a setting in which patients could explore their unconscious and act out their trauma. finally, rather than viewing patients’ somatic expressions as exclusively symptoms of suffering (or worse still, as malingering or forms of clinical manipulation), they are interpreted as posttraumatic protests directed, consciously or unconsciously, at the traumatic event(s) and the social, institutional, and medical conditions that pathologized and silenced their expressions. journal of the american psychoanalytic association
