childcare arrangements, family cognitive stimulation, and early academic skills among young children in china: a latent transition analysis early child development and care
distinct domain-specific links to early symbolic mathematics: comparing numerical and geometric processing in preschoolers early child development and care

effectiveness of psychosocial and therapeutic interventions for children and adolescents with adverse childhood experiences: a systematic review and meta‐analysis abstract background adverse childhood experiences (aces) are important risk factors for a range of mental health conditions among children and adolescents. this meta‐analysis examined the effectiveness of psychosocial and therapeutic interventions on anxiety, depression, post‐traumatic stress disorder (ptsd), and psychosocial functioning among children aged ≤18 years with documented ace exposure. methods we systematically searched randomized controlled trials (rcts) published between january 1, 2000 and september 17, 2026 that evaluated psychosocial and therapeutic interventions and reported relevant mental health outcomes among children and adolescents with documented ace exposure. searches were conducted in eight electronic databases (pubmed, medline [ovid], embase, psycinfo, cinahl, cochrane library, web of science, and ebscohost). study quality was assessed using the cochrane risk of bias 2.0 tool. pooled effect sizes (hedges' g ) were estimated using random‐effects meta‐analysis. subgroup analyses were conducted by intervention modality, duration, setting, country income level, and reported ace exposure characteristics. results after duplicate removal, 6087 records were screened, and 21 rcts involving 2450 children from nine countries were included. eleven studies were found to have low risk of bias, and 10 had some concerns, with no studies assessed as high risk of bias. meta‐analysis of six rcts showed that cognitive behavioral therapy (cbt), trauma‐focused and resilience‐building interventions significantly reduced anxiety symptoms (hedges' g = −0.46; 95% ci −0.86 to −0.06). particularly, trauma‐focused interventions demonstrated significant reductions in anxiety in subgroup analyses (hedges' g = −0.90; 95% ci −1.66 to −0.14). meta‐analysis of four rcts indicated that cbt and resilience‐building interventions lasting ≥8 weeks significantly reduced depressive symptoms (hedges' g = −0.26; 95% ci −0.44 to −0.07). no significant pooled or subgroup effects were observed for ptsd or broader psychosocial outcomes. conclusion cbt‐based, trauma‐focused and resilience building interventions effectively reduce anxiety and depressive symptoms among children with documented ace exposure. integrating evidence‐based psychological interventions with trauma‐informed principles may strengthen the delivery of mental health care for children and adolescents with documented ace exposure and mental health needs. jcpp advances
describing people’s orgasm experiences: a qualitative interview study psychology & sexuality

fear of missing out and adolescent sleep quality: a moderated mediation model background: fear of missing out (fomo) has been associated with poorer sleep among adolescents, but the psychological processes underlying this association remain unclear. objective: this study examined whether fomo was indirectly associated with poorer sleep quality through emotion regulation difficulties and whether regulatory emotional self-efficacy (rese) moderated this indirect association. methods: this cross-sectional study included 412 seventh- and eighth-grade students from one junior middle school in wuhan, china. participants completed measures of fomo, emotion regulation difficulties, rese, and sleep quality. process models 4 and 7 were used to test mediation and first-stage moderated mediation, controlling for gender and grade. results: higher fomo was associated with greater emotion regulation difficulties and poorer sleep quality. the standardized indirect association estimate for the pathway from fomo to poorer sleep quality through emotion regulation difficulties was 0.15 (95% bootstrap confidence interval [ci] [0.09, 0.21]). rese moderated the association between fomo and emotion regulation difficulties (β = −0.12, p = 0.005), with the association becoming weaker at higher rese levels. the index of moderated mediation was −0.036 (95% bootstrap ci [−0.065, −0.012]). conclusion: emotion regulation difficulties may help explain the association between fomo and poorer sleep quality among adolescents, whereas rese may serve as a potential protective resource by weakening the association between fomo and emotion regulation difficulties. health psychology research
parent-mediated consultation using proactive prompting for children with school attendance problems: two practical case studies child & family behavior therapy
age-related resistance to speed pressure in lexical decision: high error costs and a conservative response gating aging neuropsychology and cognition

intergroup contact and chinese cultural identity: a three-wave study of taiwanese students enrolled at universities in mainland china. objective: this study addressed inconsistent findings regarding cross-strait integration and the limited application of time-lagged, mechanism-focused approaches. it examined whether intergroup contact was prospectively associated with chinese cultural identity among taiwanese students in mainland china, focusing on cultural adaptation and personality traits.
method: a six-month, three-wave time-lagged survey was conducted with 286 taiwanese students at universities in mainland china. data were collected at three measurement points using validated self-report instruments to assess intergroup contact, cultural adaptation, openness to experience, and chinese cultural identity. baseline identity (t1) was controlled when predicting identity at t3. mediation and moderation analyses were conducted using process.
results: positive intergroup contact significantly predicted stronger chinese cultural identity at t3，controlling for baseline levels. results supported an indirect association through cultural adaptation, but not a full test of longitudinal mediation. openness to experience did not significantly moderate the association.
conclusions: sustained, high-quality intergroup contact was associated with increased cultural identity among taiwanese youth. the observed temporal ordering is consistent with a possible indirect pathway through cultural adaptation, although the present study does not constitute a full longitudinal test of mediation. rather than extending intergroup contact theory, the findings offer context-specific support for its applicability in an east asian setting. given that the sample was drawn from three universities in two provinces, generalizability is limited. the results further suggest that supportive social and educational environments may be more influential than broad personality traits in fostering integration. australian journal of psychology

relational spacetime: a systemic conceptual framework for couples therapy abstract contemporary couple relationships are negotiated within increasingly complex temporal and spatial conditions shaped by different contexts like work, caring responsibilities, social acceleration and digital connectivity. this paper proposes relational spacetime as a clinical and conceptual framework for examining how time and space become mutually organised within couple relationships. drawing on systemic therapy, distinctions between clock‐time and lived time, temporal desynchronisation, attachment theory, structural perspectives on relational space and sociological accounts of social acceleration, the framework examines how partners may inhabit different temporal and spatial worlds while negotiating their positions. relational spacetime is presented as a sensitising framework rather than as a new theory of time and space in therapy, bringing together temporal and spatial dimensions of recursive couple patterns. it extends the milan‐influenced tradition of attention to lived time, and its distinctive contribution lies in holding temporal and spatial organisation together within a single relational field. the paper also considers the therapist's use of questions, interruptions, silence, rhythm and advanced strategic tasks as interventions in relational time and space. particular attention is given to the relationship between second‐order systemic reflexivity and advanced strategic therapy. drawing on cecchin's curiosity and irreverence, on second‐order cybernetics (von foerster, 2003), and, critically, on smith's (2023) concept of 1.5‐order therapy, the paper argues that strategic directiveness need not imply first‐order epistemological certainty, that it can be practised from a fully second‐order position without appeal to an intermediate order and that therapeutic strategy can involve intentional and directive action while remaining tentative, provisional, reflexive and open to the revision of the hypotheses through the couple's response. relational spacetime is therefore offered as a question‐generating framework for exploring how temporal and spatial patterns, social arrangements and therapeutic interventions shape the possibilities for connection, distance and change. journal of family therapy

metáforas de act y mindfulness frente al uso tecnológico problemático en adolescentes este estudio evaluó los cambios pretest-postest asociados a una intervención basada en metáforas de la terapia de aceptación y compromiso (act) y mindfulness sobre eluso problemático de nuevas tecnologías (upnt) en adolescentes. se realizó un estudio cuasiexperimental (marzo-abril de 2024) en dos colegios privados de ibagué, colombia. mediante muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia, participaron 146 estudiantes de 13 a16 años (grados 9.º-11.º). el upnt evaluó la muestra completa; el aaq-ii (acceptance and action questionnaire-ii) y el baft (the believability of anxious feelings and thoughts questionnaire), la condición act (n=47); y el maas (mindful attention awareness scale), la condición mindfulness (n=63). se observaron reducciones significativas en las puntuaciones de internet (w=1881.50, p=.02, rb=.32), móvil (w=2123.00, p<.001, rb=.49)y upnt total (w=2971.00, p<.001, rb=.45), así como un aumento en la atención plena(w=419.00, p<.001, rb=-.57). el aaq-ii y el baft no mostraron cambios significativos. los resultados sugieren la utilidad de la intervención, aunque la ausencia de grupo control limita las inferencias causales. international journal of psychological research

predicting victimizing events in the colombian armed conflict from sociodemographic variables using a neural network model introduction: colombia has endured over 60 years of armed conflict. objective: this study addressed the issue of victims of the colombian armed conflict through data analysisutilizing deep learning (dl) tools. method: the dataset used is colombia’s registro único de víctimas (n = 173,994 records), which includes various types of violent events. a neural network model was employed to analyze and predict patterns observed in these situations, focusing on aspects such as the type of event, ethnicity, gender, and disability status. results: the model achieved an overall accuracy of 79.38% on the test set. the results reveal how these variables are distributed among victims, providing a deeper understanding of the unique characteristics of each group. discussion: the results visualize the magnitude of the impact on each population group and show how factors such as ethnicity, sex, disability status, and life stage are related to victimization in the colombian armed conflict.conclusion: these findings have significant implications for the formulation of policies and support actions aimed at mitigating the impact of the conflict on vulnerable populations. international journal of psychological research

the effect of a seven-week online mindfulness intervention on the relationship between menstrual symptoms and mental health - a non-randomized controlled trial. background: menstrual symptoms are common among physically active women and may affect their well-being and performance. moreover, symptom frequency has been associated with mental health in previous studies. although mindfulness-based interventions (mbi) have shown beneficial effects on psychological and physiological health outcomes, their potential role in the relationship between menstrual and mental health remains unclear. therefore, this study examined whether participation in an mbi was associated with changes in this relationship.
methods: 39 physically active students were split into an experimental group (eg; n = 14; 22.68 ± 2.23 years) and a control group (cg; n = 25; 22.76 ± 4.88 years), which conducted a baseline and post-intervention measurement, including a psychometric screening. the cg received no intervention during the study and was offered access to the intervention materials afterwards. assessed constructs included the 21-item version of the depression anxiety stress scale and the menstrual symptom index (msi). the mbi was developed based on mindfulness-based stress reduction, incorporating the dimensions of acting with awareness, non-judgmental acceptance, and present-moment attention.
results: at baseline in the control group, msi scores were positively associated with anxiety (b = 0.16; p = .004) and depression (b = 0.14; p = .012). no significant group × time interactions were observed for depression or stress. for anxiety, the group × time interaction was significant at the grand-mean msi score (b = - 3.30; 95% ci [- 6.50, - 0.11]; p = .043), whereas the three-way interaction was not significant (p = .054).
conclusion: the results indicate that menstrual symptom frequency is associated with mental health outcomes in physically active students. participation in the mbi was associated with changes in anxiety over time. however, the non-significant three-way interaction provided no conclusive evidence of moderation. these preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of mbi for anxiety in menstrual health context. future studies should investigate programs that explicitly address menstrual-related aspects.
trial registration: this study was registered as 'impact of an online mindfulness intervention on sleep quality in physically active students' in the german clinical trials register (drks) under the identifier drks00038462 on 13 november 2025. retrospectively registered. bmc psychology

the interplay of neural networks enabling social interaction: protocol of a multi-level, mixed-methods study of empathy and theory of mind. background: the quality and frequency of social interactions are among the best predictors of long-term mental and physical health. so how do good social interactions arise? social neuroscience has focused on a number of affective and cognitive functions including empathy and theory of mind (tom) as potential "building blocks" of social interaction. however, utilizing mainly simplistic and passive paradigms, we still fail to describe how actual, live social interactions emerge. here, the concept of "building blocks" may have become an impediment to progress. recent evidence suggests that in more complex experimental tasks, socio-affective and -cognitive processes are not simply stacked up, but are dynamically working together, just as the underlying neural networks seem to engage in lively interplay. the main objective of the study presented here (interact) is to understand how adaptive social interactions emerge by elucidating the interplay of networks and processes.
methods: using a combination of methods and across data levels, interact will move from the comprehensive investigation of behavioral and neural interaction patterns of social affect and cognition in controlled lab settings to completely free social interactions in people's everyday lives. first, we adapt an established, behavioral and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fmri) task measuring empathy and tom (empatom) to study the conjoint effects of both functions (cempatom) by manipulating their dependencies. second, we set up an interactive task version (iempatom) for hyperscanning functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fnirs) in which participants engage in a conversation with another participant that elicits empathy and tom. third, we implement a multi-agent ecological momentary assessment (ema) setup in which participants and a close social partner complete daily questions about their social interactions triggered by digitally detected physical proximity. lastly, each of these assessments includes measures of prosocial behavior to investigate how prosociality is impacted by empathy and tom interactions.
discussion: combining a novel experimental approach with single and dual neuroimaging (hyperscanning) and multi-agent ema, interact will shift from a modular to a complex systems study of actual social interaction. interact aspires to develop an interdisciplinary model of social interactions that expands our knowledge and applies it to real-world settings. bmc psychology

the imaginal as temenos for moral reckoning in israel‐palestine abstract the individual psyche in israel is under tremendous pressure to merge with a collective field of attitudes and self‐perceptions stemming from archetypal enmity, victimhood and denial of the collective’s implication in war atrocities. this dense field of denial, obfuscation, projection and self‐justification makes it enormously difficult for individual israelis to face their moral injury and implication in the moral transgressions involved in the occupation, subjugation and killing of palestinians. a clinical case showcases the unique role that the imaginal plays in approaching such reckoning. through working with literary figures, a sand tray scene and a dream series, a former israeli soldier comes into increasing conscious contact with his own moral implication and the ways it got entangled with lifelong, pervasive unconscious guilt. the author also considers how her own political and cultural positioning, intersecting with her patient’s, impact the analytic field. this process echoes and amplifies jung’s call for individuals to engage in self‐reflection and personal change as a way to contribute to ethical and moral reckoning on the part of the collective. journal of analytical psychology
affect regulation and the therapeutic movement relationship in dance movement therapy: a scoping review body movement and dance in psychotherapy
dostoevsky’s devils: a study in evil psychoanalytic inquiry
alone across cultural worlds: internal homelessness and borrowed belonging psychoanalytic inquiry

remaking “the unconscious” paradigm, act i: ...the gap” between subliminal processing and the unconscious “mind... abstract the notion of subliminal processing often refers to perception that takes place below the threshold of conscious visual awareness. this is suggested to lead to behavioural and emotional changes with spontaneous and actionable evolutionary-survival and/or social-adaptation response value. therefore, it has been suggested that the presentation of imperceptible visual elicitors can lead to responses, such as skin-conductance and heart-rate, and facial-emotional, and participant behavioural and self-report changes without conscious awareness. in a series of experiments, we disproved this theory. we showed that individually-adjusted, truly imperceptible elicitors did not induce any of these changes, when using null-hypothesis-testing, and, furthermore, provided evidence for null responses, when using bayesian analyses. we proceeded to a series of novel and exploratory experiments on unconscious theory. we tested whether behavioural and emotional responses were reported to precede conscious awareness using overt presentations of visual-emotional elicitors. we showed evidence that the experience of physiological-emotional responses was reported to precede conscious awareness of a perceived visual-emotional content. these early responses were automatic and involuntary; they did not involve or require conscious access, or accessibility, and deliberation, and could not be physiologically restrained by conscious instruction for inhibition. we proposed that responses that can be termed unconscious, but not subliminal, are preceding, spontaneous and conditionally uninhibited experiential components of exposure to perceived, but not imperceptible, emotional elicitors. we extended that they involve genuine evolutionary-survival and social-adaptation value, compared to so-called subliminal processes, because they enable spontaneously-occurring, and progressively-intentional and intended behavioural and emotional adjustments, and readjustments, and adapting refinements. integrative psychological and behavioral science

identifying variable relations using relevance logic abstract in data analysis that is based on methods from the generalized linear model, variables are related to each other, and predictions are made in which variables are linked. issues of discussion concern strength of relation and direction dependence. relations are of the regression type. in this article, the discussion focuses on type of relation. based on relevance logic, conjunctive, disjunctive and implicative relations are discussed, in particular with respect to their applicability in data analysis. it is illustrated how these relations can be distinguished from each other in cross-classifications of empirical data. it is also shown how predictions can be made of type of relation instead of variables themselves. empirical data examples illustrate these predictions. possible extensions are discussed in which relations of the type ‘if and only if’ are used. integrative psychological and behavioral science

developing standards for research in animal-assisted services (aas), human-animal interactions (hai), and the human-animal bond (hab): an international and interdisciplinary approach abstract background: the fields of animal-assisted services (aas), human-animal interaction (hai) and the human-animal bond (hab), over recent decades, have expanded in practice and research. however, acceptance of the area as one worthy of robust scientific enquiry has been limited. this reluctance is due to a range of issues including inconsistent use of methodological terminology and fidelity, publication bias, and paucity of a collaborative approach to addressing the research-practitioner gap. the complex nature and unique characteristics of many aas/hai/hab necessitate specific considerations in the planning, execution, and reporting stages of research, particularly in respect of ethical considerations concerning humans and animals involved and/or impacted. methods: given these concerns, the international association for human-animal organizations (iahaio) initiated and disseminated a call for an international, collaborative process to develop minimum standards for research in the field. the current article describes the latter nearly 3-year process – which involved over 50 researchers, practitioners, and educators – resulting in the 2025 publication “minimum standards for research involving people and/or animals in the field of aas, hai and/or the hab”, referred to as the standards . the latter living, iterative, collaborative document is positioned within a one welfare approach, taking a dynamic and relational systems approach to the interconnections between involved humans, non-human animals, and the wider physical and social environments. a systems approach is novel in the field and underscores the paramount importance of ensuring the welfare and well-being of humans, non-humans, and the environment, as all aspects are intertwined and can affect research validity, practice efficacy, and ethical stance. results and conclusion: this article summarises the key contents and objectives of the standards and discusses their relevance within current academic, professional, and educational perspectives, and extracts meaning and implications for the field. hence it provides avenues for future research, discussion, and further engagement of researchers, practitioners, and educators in improving understanding of and engagement in aas/hai/hab. human-animal interactions

executive function, balance, and eeg connectivity following hippotherapy in four children with adhd: an exploratory case-series study abstract background : this proof-of-concept case series examined the cognitive, motor, and neurophysiological correlates of hippotherapy in four 11-year-old female quadruplets with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (adhd). hippotherapy combines rhythmic equine movement with ground-based human-animal interaction, such as grooming and leading the horse, and was used here to examine whether equine-assisted activity was descriptively associated with changes in executive functioning, balance, and resting-state brain connectivity as a basis for future controlled research rather than a test of treatment efficacy. methods : participants completed 16 hippotherapy sessions over 6 weeks. pre- and post-intervention assessments included executive function (ef) tasks (stroop test, wisconsin card sorting test [wcst], corsi block-tapping test, and tower of london), the berg balance scale (bbs), and resting-state electroencephalography (eeg), including power spectral density (psd), theta-beta ratio (tbr) and theta-delta ratio, and directed phase transfer entropy (dpte). given the exploratory design and very small sample, analyses emphasized within-subject change and descriptive effect sizes, using an average-variance formulation of hedges’ g. results : post-intervention improvements were observed across all ef measures: stroop reaction times decreased across congruent, incongruent, and interference conditions; wcst completed categories increased (from 2.25 to 3.25), and perseverative errors decreased (from 29.75 to 24.25); corsi block span scores improved (from 3.60 to 4.10); and tower of london move counts decreased (from 68.50 to 62.25). effect sizes were descriptively large across measures (absolute hedges’ g range: 1.14–1.70), interpreted cautiously given a sample of four; inferential statistics were not conducted, as n = 4 precludes meaningful interpretation of p-values. balance also improved (bbs: from 38.50 to 41.00; hedges’ g = 0.97). eeg analyses descriptively indicated increased delta and theta activities in right frontal and parietal electrodes and elevated posterior alpha power, along with a shift toward stronger frontal-to-posterior delta-band and posterior-to-frontal gamma-band dpte connectivity. these findings are descriptive only and require statistical validation. conclusions : as a proof-of-concept case series, this study shows that a multimodal assessment framework can feasibly capture a convergent pattern of behavioral, motor, and neurophysiological changes temporally associated with hippotherapy in these four children with adhd. findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited, non-independent sample of quadruplet siblings and the uncontrolled design and should not be read as evidence of treatment efficacy. larger, controlled studies, ideally able to separate the horse’s movement from ground-based human-animal interaction, are needed to confirm these observations and clarify the underlying mechanisms. human-animal interactions

humane training and ethical guidelines in equine-assisted services abstract equine-assisted services (eas), which fall under the umbrella of animal-assisted services (aas), involve complex dynamics and considerations for specialty practice. the inclusion of an additional sentient being into therapeutic work creates ethical responsibilities that extend beyond human safety and clinical effectiveness. although aas standards increasingly recognize animal welfare, many equine-specific guidelines remain less operationalized regarding training, handling, and consent to participation. further operationalizing equine-specific standards may benefit the field of eas to move beyond broad commitments to welfare and establish behaviorally specific expectations that promote mutually beneficial human-animal relationships. human-animal interactions

studying in environments that reflect who we are: personalisation, representativeness and their relationship with motivation and academic performance among university students / estudiar en lugares que nos representan: personalización, representatividad y su relación con la motivación y el rendimiento en estudiantado universitario personalisation and satisfaction with one’s environment are key concepts in environmental psychology, traditionally studied in workplace settings, while motivation and performance are more frequently analysed in academic settings. this study examined the relationship between representativeness, personalisation of study spaces, satisfaction with the environment, motivation and subjective academic performance among 236 university students. the descriptive results indicated that personalisation is based on categories such as pictures/posters (47.5%) and mementos (40.7%). significant differences were found in terms of representativeness according to the type of space ( x ² = 14.7; p < .001), with higher levels in private spaces ( m e = 4.00) than in shared spaces ( m e = 3.00). furthermore, representativeness correlated positively to satisfaction with the environment (τ = .337; p < .001), motivation and subjective performance, although this relationship lost statistical significance in public spaces ( p > .05). the conclusion drawn is that the representativeness of the environment, facilitated by privacy, is a key factor associated with satisfaction and academic processes. these findings suggest the importance of designing flexible educational environments that enable students to express their identity. psyecology-bilingual journal of environmental psychology-revista bilingue de psicologia ambiental

adaptive semantic prediction in dynamic linguistic environments: computational-neural insights from hierarchical bayesian inference abstract real-world language processing unfolds in environments of volatility and uncertainty, requiring comprehenders to continuously adapt semantic predictions as environmental statistics change. however, the fundamental computational-neural mechanisms supporting such hierarchical adaptive prediction remain incompletely understood. critically, our goal was to examine how comprehenders update their beliefs about high-level environmental reliability as evidence accumulates across trials, and how this update modulates low-level semantic prediction. here, we introduce a paradigm that extends traditional filler-based designs and allows for the examination of trial-by-trial adaptation and corresponding neural responses. we further implemented a computational neural analytical framework based on the hierarchical gaussian filter to model the trial-by-trial hierarchical inference process. we showed that environmental statistical regularities systematically modulate multiple neural signatures, from the well-established n400 to later erp components, such as late anterior positivity (lap) and p600, as well as cortical oscillatory components in the theta and beta bands. model-based analyses showed that distinct computational variables were reflected in dissociable neural signatures. at the erp level, n400 activity was associated with both high-level belief states and precision-weighted prediction error (pwpe2), whereas lap was more strongly associated with pwpe2. at the level of neural oscillations, theta-band activity was associated with high-level belief states, whereas beta-band activity selectively tracks prior belief2. together, these findings indicate that distinct neural signatures are differentially associated with complementary components of hierarchical bayesian inference, supporting the ongoing estimation of the environmental statistical structure. more broadly, our results provide model-based evidence that hierarchical predictive coding operates in advanced language comprehension under uncertainty. neurobiology of language

dissociating phonological tuning from reading skill: evidence from the temporoparietal cortex in deaf and hearing adults abstract phonological processing is widely considered central to reading development in hearing individuals, with the temporoparietal cortex (tpc) regarded as essential for encoding phonological information from print. hearing people who struggle to read show altered activation and less precise phonological representations in this region. notably, skilled deaf readers show this same profile, suggesting that precise phonological representations in the tpc are not necessary for proficient reading. this raises the question of what the tpc encodes when phonological access differs. using fmri, we compared skilled deaf and hearing readers viewing real words (rws), pseudowords (pws), and pseudohomophones (phs)—letter strings that are orthographically novel but phonologically identical to rws (e.g., brane). because phs carry no lexical or semantic identity, they can isolate whole-word phonological representations accessed through print. we examined bold signal differences within individually localized tpc rois. deaf and hearing readers showed distinct response patterns. hearing readers showed equivalent responses to phs and rws, both greater than pws ([rw = ph] > pw), indicating that lexical-level phonological representations were accessed from print. deaf readers showed the largest response to rws and equivalent responses to phs and pws (rw > [ph = pw]), indicating that whole-word phonological forms were not reliably accessed from print. these findings suggest that, in skilled deaf readers, phonological information from print is encoded with reduced precision and/or less automatically, supporting the proposal that deaf readers achieve literacy through a potentially unique reading architecture where the direct orthographic-to-semantic pathway carries the primary functional load. neurobiology of language

scene-conditioned general gaze following in static images with uncertainty-preserving geometry given a static image and a selected person, general gaze following predicts the person’s likely gaze target. ambiguous head cues can leave several geometrically plausible targets. we develop a scene-conditioned localization framework that retains directional uncertainty instead of collapsing it into one gaze direction. building on a fixed, previously published geometry-guided reference, distribution-guided query interaction (dgqi) refines direction–distance candidates using scene evidence, the distribution-conditioned localization decoder (dcld) adjusts the reference heatmap through residual prediction, and selective teacher-margin ranking preservation (stmrp) protects selected correct spatial rankings during training. on the gazefollow official test set, the final model reaches a pooled/global auc of 0.9190, an original-resolution per-image auc of 0.9342, and a normalized distance error of 0.1289 compared to the published baseline values of 0.9066, 0.9214, and 0.1423, respectively. within-reference controls distinguish module effects from cross-generation changes in the scene backbone. dcld yields the clearest localization gains; dgqi contributes a smaller discrimination gain; and stmrp improves per-image auc at a localization cost. this separation has revealed that discrimination and peak localization need not improve together. zero-shot experiments on videoattentiontarget and a coverage-limited childplay subset expose further domain sensitivity. these results motivate protocol-aware, multi-metric evaluation of gaze predictions. journal of eye movement research

exploring the lived experiences of lgbtqia + young people with visible differences: being ‘ double different ’ abstract objectives existing research suggests young people with visible differences can experience a range of psychosocial challenges, such as low self‐esteem and increased anxiety and depression. however, young people from minoritised groups are not well represented in visible difference research. this includes lgbtqia+ young people, who experience both mental and physical health inequalities and may be at greater risk of negative body image than their cisgender/heterosexual peers. while it can be argued that lgbtqia+ young people with visible differences may be at greater risk of negative psychosocial outcomes compared to their cisgender/heterosexual counterparts, little research explores the unique experiences of this population. therefore, this study aimed to explore the lived experiences of lgbtqia+ young people (aged 15–28 years) with visible differences. design this study used an inductive, qualitative design. the research was underpinned by a critical realist/contextualist perspective. methods data were generated using online qualitative surveys and 75 young people with a range of gender identities, sexualities, and visible differences took part. reflexive thematic analysis was used to analyse the data. results one overarching theme, the weight of multiple marginalisation , was generated that encompassed two themes: (1) dual identities , dual stigma and (2) hiding to prevent hurting . conclusions analysis suggested that lgbtqia+ young people with visible differences face unique challenges not accounted for by generic support. however, some experienced personal growth and described feeling accepted by lgbtqia+ people. tailored, co‐produced interventions are needed to effectively support this population and reduce the health and social inequalities they face. british journal of health psychology
the effectiveness of reality therapy in improving academic achievement, achievement motivation, and happiness in students educational and developmental psychologist
a self-determination theory-based group intervention for academic motivation and well-being: a quasi-experimental study with turkish middle school students educational and developmental psychologist

stability in infant rule‐learning? abstract we tested the stability of infants' rule learning in an independent 6‐month follow‐up of infants originally assessed as part of manybabies3. valid data were available from infants at each measurement occasion (t1: 5–12 months; t2: 11–18 months) and from infants for the longitudinal analyses. infants completed a gaze‐contingent eye‐tracking adaptation of the aba/abb syllable‐triplet task. rule learning was measured as a novelty preference (greater looking times in rule‐inconsistent than rule‐consistent trials). bayesian analyses provided no evidence of rule learning at either measurement occasion and no clear evidence for longitudinal stability. infancy
parenting school-aged autistic children: a systematic review review journal of autism and developmental disorders

meta-analysis of longitudinal total brain volume trajectories in autism abstract early brain overgrowth is well-documented in autism spectrum disorder (asd); however, longitudinal brain development has not been systematically charted. we performed a meta-analysis of longitudinal total brain volume (tbv) trajectories in asd compared to controls, including 6 studies, 453 asd and 3,510 controls aged 6 months to 18 years. cross-sectional tbv was larger in asd than controls (hedges’ g = 0.22, p = 0.014). meta-regressions showed larger tbv was specific to early childhood, with reduced tbv in late adolescence in asd (f(2, 13) = 37.51, b=-0.06, p <0.001). longitudinally, tbv growth was reduced over time in asd versus controls (g=-0.09, p = 0.06). in summary, tbv alterations in asd are age dependent, it remains unclear whether alterations persist into adulthood due to a lack of studies beyond age 18. review journal of autism and developmental disorders

parents consistently underestimate their children's prejudices. prejudice begins in childhood, and parents have a crucial role to play in mitigating its development. the present study examined the accuracy of parents' estimates of their children's prejudices. specifically, this study investigated whether accuracy varied across (1) diverse parents and (2) diverse forms of prejudice (race, class, weight, disability, sexual orientation), and explored (3) why parents underestimated children's prejudices. a diverse sample of 130 parent-child dyads from across the united states (children ages 6.0-9.9 years, 59f/71 m/0nb, 54 white/71 of color, and their parents) participated between october 2023 and may 2025. parents predicted their children's selections on a playmate preference task and then children completed the task. results indicated that parents severely underestimated their children's prejudices overall (cohen's d = .83). underestimates were consistent across diverse parents (across political views, educational backgrounds, income brackets, and anti-prejudice motivations) and across several forms of prejudice (class, weight, and disability). exploratory analyses indicated that parents predicted above-chance rates of prejudice overall (i.e., did not hold "tabula rasa" beliefs), raising the possibility that parents may hold other intuitive misconceptions about the processes driving prejudice development. parents' potentially inflated sense of the degree to which ingroup membership or intergroup contact can buffer against prejudice development is discussed. child development

us–china differences in children's reasoning, visual attention, and social cognition abstract outward differences between cultures are very salient, with western and east asian cultures as a prominent comparison pair. a large literature describes cross‐cultural variation in cognition, but relatively less research has explored the developmental origins of this variation and those findings that are reported have not typically been replicated. this study helps to fill this empirical gap by replicating four prominent findings documenting cross‐cultural differences in children's relational reasoning, picture description, causal attribution, and uniqueness preference in a cross‐sectional sample of 240 3–12‐year‐olds from the united states and china. we observed cross‐cultural differences in picture description, causal attribution, and uniqueness preference, though the uniqueness preference result was in the opposite direction of the predicted direction. performance in each task followed a different developmental trajectory, but we did not observe interactions between age and cultural differences. we also did not observe strong associations in performance across tasks, or between task performance and a range of demographic factors. overall, these results suggest that existing developmental measures may be insufficiently precise to support strong mechanistic inferences about cognitive differences across cultures. topics in cognitive science

when looking away means looking inward: contextual interpretation of gaze aversions determines their attentional value. eye movements are typically understood as supporting outward orienting, directing attention toward locations of interest in the external environment. however, not all eye movements reflect outward orienting. gaze aversions, the common tendency to look away during effortful cognitive processing, serve as social signals of inward-oriented attention and ongoing processing. because observers continuously monitor others' eye movements and use gaze-related cues to guide their own behavior, distinguishing between outward-oriented gaze-shifts and inward-oriented gaze aversions is a basic challenge in human interaction. here, we examine the hypothesis that this distinction depends on the context in which gaze shifts appear. while participants reorient their attention following an outward-oriented gaze shift, they withhold doing so when the context suggests that the gaze shift reflects inward-oriented processing. to test this hypothesis, we relied on the gaze cueing effect (gce), an attentional orienting to observed gaze shifts that is known to be modulated by top-down context and interpretation. in two pre-registered experiments (total n = 90), participants performed a gaze-cueing letter-discrimination task while viewing identical gaze shifts within different contexts. one group was led to interpret the gaze shifts as occurring during effortful thinking, whereas the other group received no thinking-related context. across both experiments, attentional orienting was significantly reduced when gaze shifts were perceived as reflecting internal cognitive processing rather than attention shifts. these findings demonstrate that gaze aversions function as communicative signals that dynamically regulate interpersonal attention, and that gaze following depends fundamentally on the inferred social meaning of the observed eye movement. cognition

the relations between types of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and life satisfaction in early adolescence in indonesia: exploring the moderating role of parenting and peer social support loneliness in early adolescence is linked to poor well-being, including higher depressive symptoms and lower life satisfaction. this study examined whether maternal and paternal strength-based or unsupportive parenting, and peer social support, moderated the effects of social and emotional loneliness on depressive symptoms and life satisfaction. each loneliness type was studied within family and peer contexts. data from 761 indonesian adolescents (54.3% girls; m = 12.68, sd = 0.43) shows that paternal and maternal unsupportive parenting intensified the negative impact of social loneliness in family relationships on depressive symptoms. peer social support buffered the effects of both types of loneliness in peer contexts on depressive symptoms. strength-based parenting showed no moderating effects, and no significant findings emerged for life satisfaction. these findings underscore the need to differentiate types and relational contexts of loneliness and provide insights into the role of peer support, maternal and paternal parenting in adolescent mental health in indonesia. journal of early adolescence

attributional lag: structured choice and the conditions of personal accountability abstract several influential approaches to responsibility already recognise that agency is causally, socially and institutionally conditioned. this article begins from that shared baseline and identifies a different problem: attributional lag. institutions may acknowledge the social formation of agency when explaining how choices arise yet continue to treat a prior choice as a sufficient warrant for concentrating durable consequences on the individual. i distinguish token‐action moral responsibility from institutional personal accountability and develop three diagnostic dimensions for evaluating this mismatch: epistemic access, practical accessibility and temporal revisability. practical accessibility is not a revival of the principle of alternative possibilities; it asks whether alternatives invoked by institutions were realistically available rather than merely formal options. temporal revisability does not imply costless reversal; it asks whether later learning can be given proportionate weight in institutional decisions. attributional lag therefore names a mismatch between an institution's explanation of agency and its later use of choice to justify consequences. journal for the theory of social behaviour
an object relations perspective on emergency psychiatry psychodynamic practice

lexical‐semantic properties of freely generated everyday emotion labels and self‐reported alexithymia: a preregistered secondary analysis abstract alexithymia—difficulty identifying and describing one's feelings—is thought to involve emotion language, and reviews indicate the two are related; however, the relation varies with what aspect of language is measured. whether the meanings of the emotion words people spontaneously use in daily life relate to alexithymic difficulties remains unclear. in an existing dataset, 50 adults freely generated words for their current feelings across roughly 14 days of ambulatory experience sampling and completed the toronto alexithymia scale (tas‐20) before and after. labels retained by a preregistered lexicon filter were assigned external norm ratings of how strongly a word's meaning is typically experienced through sensations inside the body, plus action‐effector strength, and concreteness. a corpus‐based index of association with independently defined interoceptive terms covered a subset. these are properties of words, supplied by independent norming samples and corpora, not measures of participants' own interoceptive ability. values were averaged within participants, weighted by how often each label was used, and related to the tas‐20 difficulty‐identifying‐feelings and difficulty‐describing‐feelings subscales, adjusting for vocabulary quantity, valence, and arousal. all eight primary estimates were negative, but none survived correction for multiple testing. the clearest concerned difficulty describing feelings; participants reporting greater difficulty tended to repeatedly use labels with somewhat lower norm‐rated interoceptive strength (standardized β ≈ −0.27). confidence intervals spanned associations close to zero as well as those of potentially meaningful magnitude. the pattern changed substantially when each distinct word was counted once rather than weighted by frequency of use, including changes in direction for the interoceptive‐strength estimates. in this small sample, the meanings of everyday emotion labels showed a suggestive but uncertain relation to self‐reported difficulty describing feelings. the findings describe properties of the words people use—not their capacity to sense bodily signals—and show that such conclusions depend on how vocabulary is aggregated. scandinavian journal of psychology

bridging the green attitude-behavior gap: development and validation of the multidimensional sense of environmental responsibility scale. the green attitude-behavior gap remains a barrier to sustainability initiatives in higher education. to distinguish the sense of environmental responsibility (soer) from broader environmental responsibility, this study developed and validated the multidimensional sense of environmental responsibility scale (soers) among chinese university students. across three studies, principal component analysis suggested, and confirmatory factor analysis and item response theory provided further support for, an 11-item, three-factor representation comprising cognition, affective response, and behavioral intention. the scale showed good internal consistency, test-retest reliability, discriminant validity, and concurrent criterion validity. item response theory supported satisfactory item performance, and scalar measurement invariance was established across gender; female students reported higher soer levels. the soers offers a psychometrically sound tool for assessing individuals' sense of environmental responsibility and provides a measurement foundation for future intervention research examining whether changes in soer are associated with a narrower attitude-behavior gap. acta psychologica

risks of counter-stereotypical ai when it replaces human contact artificial intelligence (ai) agents are often designed with stereotype-consistent social cues-such as feminized voice assistants in service roles or masculine security robots-to increase acceptance and interaction fluency. yet these same design choices may reinforce the stereotypes they draw on. recent work, however, proposes a more optimistic possibility: counter-stereotypical ai-for example, a female-coded technical chatbot or male-coded care robot-may reduce prejudice by functioning as synthetic intergroup contact, repeatedly exposing users to agents that serve as proxy members of social groups and challenge familiar stereotypes. we build on this account but argue that its implications depend critically on whether ai supplements or replaces human interaction. when counter-stereotypical ai adds exposure to underrepresented groups, it may challenge stereotypes by broadening the range of people users associate with particular traits or domains. when it substitutes for humans, however, its effects become more ambivalent. we identify three risks of counter-stereotypical ai as replacement: non-integration, when users treat the agent as a designed persona rather than revising beliefs about people; substitution, when synthetic contact displaces the reciprocal and agentic qualities of human contact; and illusion of inclusion, when visible ai representation is mistaken for institutional inclusion. we position replacement by counter-stereotypical ai as a critical boundary condition for theories of synthetic contact and representational ai, and as a key context for future research on prejudice, technology, and social change. current opinion in psychology

changing brains and minds on a changing planet nature mental health, published online: 04 november 2026; doi:10.1038/s44220-026-00763-w brain health and mental health are shaped by the environments we inhabit. the earth–brain–health commission argues that climate, ecological and urban transformations are integral to brain health across the lifespan, offering a new framework for uniting neuroscience, psychiatry, public health and environmental science around shared challenges and solutions. nature mental health

integration of children’s wellbeing practitioners into a specialist paediatric psychology service: a non-randomised effectiveness study abstract children and young people (cyp) living with long-term physical health conditions (ltcs) have a higher prevalence of mental health conditions but report barriers in accessing mental health interventions. one way to increase access to such interventions is through children and young person wellbeing practitioners (cwps) who deliver low-intensity cognitive behavioural therapy (li cbt). this non-randomised study evaluates the effectiveness of li cbt delivered by cwps integrated in a specialist paediatric psychology service. thirty-six cyp aged 3‒23 years receiving li cbt interventions were included in the evaluation. outcome measures included the revised children’s anxiety and depression scale (rcads) and goal based outcomes (gbos), which were administered at the beginning and end of the intervention. feedback from participants was also gathered to complement quantitative data. analysis of pre- and post-intervention data highlighted a reduction in symptoms across all rcads subscales with notably large effect sizes observed when comparing total rcads scores ( d = 0.86) and low mood scores ( d = 0.99). gbo data similarly reflected progress towards personal goals with a large effect size reported ( d = 1.44). participants provided positive feedback, emphasising improvements in symptom control and emotional understanding. the integration of cwps into paediatric hospitals demonstrated preliminary effectiveness in reducing anxiety and depression symptoms among cyp with ltcs and significant progress towards their personal goals. these findings suggest that li cbt delivered by cwps could fill a critical gap within paediatric settings, although further research with a larger sample size is warranted. key learning aims (1) to understand the mental health needs of children and young people with long-term physical health conditions. (2) to learn how low-intensity cognitive behavioural therapy (li cbt) delivered by children and young people’s wellbeing practitioners (cwps) can be integrated into paediatric healthcare settings to improve mental health outcomes. (3) to explore the preliminary effectiveness of cwp-delivered interventions through clinical outcome measures and participant feedback, and consider implications for future service development and research. cognitive behaviour therapist
clinical decision-making and barriers to change in adhd assessment: australian psychologists’ perspectives australian psychologist

predictors of parenting stress in a national matched sample of children with/without chronic pain abstract background parents of children with chronic health conditions demonstrate elevated parenting stress. literature has focused on how parenting behaviors amplify their child’s pain; less research has examined parents’ emotional needs. objective using national data (usa), this study examined parent and child factors that may influence parent stress. method analyses were conducted in a sample of parents of children with/without chronic pain ( n = 3080, m child age = 11.7, 55.6% female, 50.1% with pain). results results indicated lower parenting efficacy ( t = − 21.98, b = − 1.45, se = 0.07, p < .001) and more severe child anxiety and depression symptoms ( ps < 0.001) each significantly predicted higher parenting stress. social support and financial resources were not significant predictors. there was a significant main effect of chronic pain on parenting stress across models (parent efficacy: t = 3.77, p = .002, b = 0.27, se = 0.07; social support: t = 6.24, p < .001, b = 0.47, se = 0.07; financial resources: t = 6.27, p < .001, b = 0.48, se = 0.08). conclusions parenting stress was higher for parents whose children had chronic pain, in children with higher anxiety and depression symptoms, and for parents with lower parenting efficacy. child & youth care forum
spontaneous attention to people impairs change detection in natural scenes journal of cognitive psychology

trait social anxiety and cardiovascular responses to acute stress: the mediating effects of perceived hostility and rejection in interpersonal relationships the current study aimed to (1) examine the association between trait social anxiety and cardiovascular reactivity and recovery to an initial psychological stress exposure, as well as cardiovascular response adaptation to repeated acute stress, and (2) determine whether self-reported perceptions of negative social relationships mediate the association between social anxiety and cardiovascular stress responses. the current study employed a quasi-experimental observational design, whereby participants (n = 137) completed a standardized cardiovascular stress adaptation protocol with systolic blood pressure (sbp), diastolic blood pressure (dbp), and heart rate (hr) monitored throughout. participants ( m age = 19.54, sd = 1.53, ages 18 -26) included healthy young adults who were free from cardiovascular conditions. a total 72 (52.6 %) participants were women, 63 (46 %) were men, and 2 (1.5 %) were non-binary. participants also completed measures assessing trait social anxiety (social interaction anxiety scale) and self-reported perceptions of negative social relationships which measures perceived hostility and rejection from one’s social network (nih social distress scale). the results indicated that greater perceptions of hostility from others significantly mediated the association between trait social anxiety and both diminished hr reactivity, b = -.03, 95% ci [-.070, -.001], and poorer hr recovery, b = .03, 95% ci [-.07, -.001] to acute psychological stress. given that both blunted hr reactivity and poorer hr recovery have been associated with future health outcomes, these findings may suggest a potential psychophysiological pathway linking social anxiety and negative social relationships to adverse cardiovascular health outcomes. health psychology open

mechanisms of distractor filtering in visual working memory space: evidence from attention capture visual working memory (vwm) is a cognitive system responsible for the active maintenance of visual representations to support ongoing processing. given its limited capacity, the filtering of task-irrelevant distractors is critical for optimal performance. traditional accounts propose that such filtering primarily occurs prior to the formation of distractor representations in vwm. however, emerging evidence suggests that filtering may also operate within vwm itself. the present study investigated the mechanisms of distractor filtering in vwm space. through two experiments, we employed a dual-task paradigm combining attention capture and working memory tasks to examine whether distractors enter vwm and how their representations evolve over time. the results showed that distractors captured attention immediately after the disappearance of the memory array, but not at later stages, suggesting that filtering occurs after distractors have already entered vwm in the task. notably, a relatively high rate of identity misjudgment in the working memory task further indicated that these distractors were not fully eliminated from vwm. collabra-psychology
epistemic authority in contemporary psychoanalytic supervision psychoanalytic psychotherapy
meditation attenuates the ownership–identification link: a mechanism for decentering in self-referential processing journal of general psychology

does a moral injury framework enhance our understanding of ocd? abstract background: obsessive-compulsive disorder (ocd) is characterized by intrusive thoughts that are appraised as signalling harm, evoking distress and efforts to reduce distress and/or prevent harm. it has long been observed that obsessions often reflect moral themes and that many people with ocd experience strong moral emotions, particularly guilt and shame. aims: drawing on social functionalist models of moral emotions and the literature on moral injury (mi), we propose that in some people with ocd, symptoms can be conceptualized as an mi. method: we reviewed leading theoretical models of ocd, moral emotions, and mi, and identified areas of overlap in phenomenology, development, and persistence. results: when an obsessional thought is itself a moral transgression, and/or failure to resolve the obsessional concern via the compulsion is viewed as a moral transgression, it evokes moral emotions and threatens social standing, reputation, and trust. this increases the stake in avoiding the obsession and in ensuring the compulsion is done properly. conclusions: the integration of moral injury concepts with established cognitive behavioral models may enhance case formulation, reduce treatment ambivalence, and support recovery processes that extend beyond symptom reduction to restoration of moral coherence and self-trust. clinical implications are discussed. behavioural and cognitive psychotherapy
cognitive profile, autistic traits, visual perception, and visual evoked potential findings in silver–russell syndrome applied neuropsychology-child

preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries nature human behaviour, published online: 04 november 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02583-5 lou et al. find that eligibility for preprimary education is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing across low- and middle-income countries. nature human behaviour
the role of artificial intelligence in spirituality and mental health journal of spirituality in mental health
intersectionality of mindfulness and eating disorders among gender and sexual diverse individuals: a scoping review journal of lgbtq issues in counseling
correction to ock and oswald (2018) journal of personnel psychology

an experiment investigating the interaction of feedback framing and self-perception in the labor market abstract: performance feedback is a critical driver of motivation, development, and advancement, yet gender differences in how feedback is internalized remain underexplored. across an experimental vignette study with 280 full-time employees, we investigate gender differences in expected disappointment after critical feedback and whether the tone of delivery effects men and women asymmetrically. results show that women report higher disappointment than men following negative hypothetical evaluations. this gender disparity disappears when feedback is communicated in a communal tone as men increase in their self-disappointment. these findings suggest that communal framing differentially shapes men’s and women’s emotional responses to feedback, eliminating the gender gap in disappointment. implications include rethinking managerial communication, training supervisors in inclusive feedback delivery, and recognizing the impact of feedback tone on employee self-perception, motivation, and career trajectories. journal of personnel psychology

assessing the impact of psychosocial factors on perceived personal and social risk in the face of climate change / evaluando el impacto de los factores psicosociales en la percepción del riesgo personal y social ante el cambio climático climate change is a critical challenge for contemporary society. in response, theoretical frameworks such as the climate change risk perception model (ccrpm) have been developed, explaining risk perception through cognitive, experiential and sociocultural factors, as well as sociodemographic variables. the main objective of this research was to validate this model by introducing two significant modifications: firstly, to distinguish between the perception of personal risk and that of social risk; secondly, to break down the cognitive factor into six specific variables that separate true and false beliefs about the causes, consequences and solutions to the phenomenon. a total of 367 university students took part in this study by completing a questionnaire. confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling were used to assess the impact of these dimensions on perceived personal and social risk. the results confirm that the modified model fits both dimensions of risk well, with highly satisfactory explanations of variance in line with the literature. the conclusion is that theoretical significance is achieved by treating true and false cognitive factors separately. studies in psychology

digital self-regulation before sleep and emotional control among adolescents: a multilevel cross-national study of canada and hong kong using pisa 2022 using pisa 2022 data from canada and hong kong, we examined bedtime notification management, a single-item indicator of pre-sleep digital self-regulation, and emotional control. the corrected complete-case sample included 18,884 students in 996 schools: 14,630 students in canada and 4254 in hong kong. two-level survey-weighted models distinguished within-school and between-school associations and adjusted for country, gender, socioeconomic status, school socioeconomic composition, home possessions, and school belonging. notification management was positively associated with emotional control within schools (b = 0.0377, 95% ci [0.0281, 0.0474]) and between schools (b = 0.0989, 95% ci [0.0511, 0.1466]). the within-school association was weaker in hong kong. gender moderation was nonsignificant under population-oriented weighting (p = 0.281) but significant under equal-system weighting (p = 0.032), indicating sensitivity to pooling. the individual association was small, and these observational findings do not establish causal benefits or the effectiveness of educational interventions. adolescents

eye-gaze allocations during facial emotion recognition in middle childhood: unique and shared links with cu traits, adhd symptoms, and conduct problems research on child and adolescent psychopathology

structural precarity, psychosocial risks, and anxiety among mexican young workers: mixed-methods study grounded in an integrated framework, this mixed-methods study examined relationships among anxiety, self-determination, and psychosocial risk in mexican young workers (n = 276; m = 23.77; 20–29), and a nested qualitative subsample (n = 71), including structural precarity as a contextual factor. three instruments were used: generalized anxiety disorder-7 (gad-7), basic psychological needs satisfaction at work scale (bpns), and nom-035-stps-2018. spearman correlations showed a positive association between anxiety and psychosocial risk (rs = 0.378, p < 0.01) and negative between psychosocial risk and bpns (autonomy rs = -0.558, competence rs = -0.668, relatedness rs = -0.528, all p < 0.001). anxiety correlated negatively with autonomy (rs = -0.451, p < 0.001) and competence (rs = -0.329, p < 0.05). initially, mann–whitney test indicated gender differences in competence. however, after multiple-comparison corrections (fdr), no statistically significant gender differences were found. in addition, the bpns competence subscale demonstrated low reliability (cronbach’s a = 0.41), requiring caution when interpreting findings. qualitative findings highlighted communication, supervisory support, and coping strategies. results support an integrated model, with implications for organizational interventions and regulatory compliance in early-career populations. universitas psychologica

executive functions among kindergarteners in the capital of laos: relations with socialization practices and later mathematics skills abstract executive functions (efs), conceptualized as conscious, goal‐directed control processes of thought, action, and emotion, develop rapidly during early childhood and predict various developmental outcomes. previous research has linked socialization practices to early efs and efs to mathematics achievement, yet has largely focused on weird (western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic) contexts. this study examined efs’ associations with socialization practices and later mathematics skills in the capital of laos, a rapidly shifting sociodemographic context within a united nations‐designated least‐developed, agricultural, and traditionally collectivistic country. in study 1, 66 kindergarteners ( m age = 54.8 months) performed ef and language tasks, and their caregivers reported on socialization practices (autonomy support and intrusive control). in study 2, 35 children were followed up one year later to assess their mathematics performance. the results showed that kindergarteners’ efs predicted later mathematics skills, providing additional evidence consistent with the possibility that this association extends across diverse sociodemographic contexts, while offering essential baseline data to support local mathematics education. in contrast, moderate evidence for a null association of intrusive control and anecdotal evidence for a negative association of autonomy support with children's efs were found, consistent with the possibility that socialization‐ef relations may vary across sociocultural contexts rather than following universal patterns. together, these findings suggest that efs represent an important cognitive capacity for later mathematics achievement, tentatively highlighting the value of considering sociocultural contexts when modeling early socialization‐ef relations. developmental science
issue information developmental science

cultural adaptation in extreme and unusual environments when psychologists study the role of the environment in shaping culture, they rarely consider the extreme and unusual environments (eues) in which some humans live and work. from space to antarctica to aircraft carriers, eues are settings in which survival depends upon deliberate preparation, specialized technology, and sustained coordination. these environments offer a unique context for examining how cultural systems emerge in response to recurrent ecological and social demands. in this review, i argue that three cultural features—interdependence, tightness, and hierarchy—may be especially adaptive in eues. drawing on cultural psychology, evolutionary theory, anthropology, and research on teams in extreme settings, i describe how cultural practices and values can develop as responses to environmental demands and opportunities. specifically, i outline how interdependence may facilitate task specialization, tightness may reduce costly errors under conditions of severe threat, and hierarchy may support rapid coordination when decisions must be made under time pressure. however, each of these adaptations may carry costs, such as the enforcement of problematic norms, which must be considered. though extreme and unusual, eues offer informative case studies of how environmental demands can shape cultural orientations and a setting for testing the scope of cultural theories. journal of cross-cultural psychology

feeling young and old together: daily subjective age in a dyadic context subjective age fluctuates considerably within persons across different contexts. the present study examined (a) whether older adults’ daily subjective age is associated with their respective romantic partner’s subjective age, and (b) whether such subjective age covariation is moderated by how everyday problems are appraised and approached. during a 10-day daily diary study, 67 older couples from canada (age range 60–89 years) individually provided parallel ratings of how old they felt each day. they also reported their most bothersome problem that day and how they dealt with the problem together with their partner (collaborative problem solving). as predicted, multilevel regression analyses showed evidence for dyadic covariation in daily subjective age; changes in older adults’ subjective age were significantly associated with concurrent changes in their partners’ subjective age. subjective age covariation was weaker on days when older adults reported higher severity problems and stronger on days when collaborative problem solving was higher. this moderation was specific to taking joint actions, and it did not emerge for emotional support. our findings highlight the importance of social contexts for subjective age by providing insights into the circumstances under which individual subjective age covaries with the respective partner as couples engage in their daily lives. international journal of behavioral development

evaluation of a six-item second-order academic engagement model in ecuadorian university students. introduction: academic engagement is a key determinant of students' wellbeing and academic success. although the utrecht work engagement scale for students (uwes-s-9) is one of the most widely used instruments to assess this construct, previous studies have reported inconsistent evidence regarding its factorial structure, particularly in latin american populations. this study examined the psychometric properties of the uwes-s-9 and evaluated whether a more parsimonious higher-order model could better represent academic engagement among ecuadorian university students.
methods: a cross-sectional study was conducted with 1,732 university students from three ecuadorian universities. the sample was randomly divided for exploratory and confirmatory analyses. exploratory factor analysis (efa), confirmatory factor analysis (cfa), measurement invariance across sex, age, and university type, internal consistency, convergent validity, and nomological validity through associations with external psychological constructs were assessed.
results: among eight competing models, the six-item three-factor model and its second-order counterpart showed the most favorable relative fit indices (cfi = 0.992, tli = 0.980, srmr = 0.022), although the rmsea remained elevated (rmsea = 0.105), indicating mixed evidence of overall model fit. the scale showed excellent reliability ( = 0.905; cr = 0.958), adequate convergent validity (ave > 0.68 for all dimensions), and full configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance across sex, age, and university type. associations with psychological capital, academic satisfaction, perceived stress, psychological inflexibility, and symptoms of anxiety and depression occurred in the theoretically expected directions, providing evidence of nomological validity.
conclusion: the refined six-item second-order uwes-s provides a brief and reliable representation of academic engagement in ecuadorian university students. its hierarchical structure offers a theoretically coherent and parsimonious representation of the construct, with favorable incremental and residual fit indices, although the elevated rmsea warrants caution in interpreting overall model fit. these findings support the six-item model as a promising candidate for research and educational assessment; however, independent replication is needed before it can be considered an established alternative to the uwes-s-9. frontiers in psychology

heightened fear memory retention during infancy, but not number of separation‐induced ultrasonic vocalizations, predicts a fearful phenotype in a diverse cohort of rats abstract past work using male rats, unexposed to early life adversity, suggests that number of separation‐induced ultrasonic vocalizations (usvs) and retention of an aversive association during infancy predict later individual differences in fear behavior. the present study examined these associations using male and female rats that were either exposed or unexposed to early life adversity to test the generalizability of these findings. separation‐induced usvs were measured early in infancy. animals were then subjected to pavlovian fear conditioning later in infancy, and individual differences in retention were measured 6 days later. in adulthood, individual differences in learned (contextual fear conditioning) and innate fear (light–dark box performance) were assessed. exploratory factor analysis revealed that these adulthood measures loaded onto a single factor (fearfulness). heightened memory retention of an aversive association during infancy positively predicted adulthood fearfulness, but number of usvs emitted was not a significant predictor. neither sex nor exposure to early life adversity affected the size, nor direction, of these relations. these results suggest that heightened fear memory retention during infancy is a better predictor of adulthood fearfulness than separation‐induced usvs, and that these relationships generalize across sex and early life adversity exposure. developmental psychobiology
