parent-child facial expression recognition: the role of familiarity in interactive contexts. the ability to express and understand emotion is fundamental to social communication, and develops through early parent-child interactions. across two studies, we examined parents' and children's recognition of emotional expressions during a structured interactive task. in study 1, parent-child dyads (n = 33, children aged 4-9 years) took turns producing facial expressions in response to emotion-eliciting objects while their partner guessed the eliciting object. videos of children were shown to naïve adult raters (n = 88) completing the same task. study 1 provided initial evidence for a familiarity effect, with parents outperforming naïve raters at recognising their child's expressions. study 2 (n = 45 dyads, children aged 4-12 years) extended this by testing whether recognition accuracy reflects familiarity with a specific partner or general parenting experience. participants completed the task with each other and with videos of unfamiliar partners. naïve parents (n = 69) and non-parents (n = 68) also rated the children's expressions. study 2 confirmed a bidirectional familiarity advantage: both parents and children were more accurate with their familiar partner than with unfamiliar individuals, suggesting the effect is specific to the parent-child relationship rather than reflecting a general ability to read adult or child faces. recognition accuracy was not strongly predicted by age, suggesting familiarity may account for more variance in performance than developmental changes in expressive clarity alone. these findings support the view that the unique parent-child bond plays a meaningful role in emotional understanding. journal of experimental child psychology

testing the parasocial contact hypothesis through stand-up comedy abstract: the study examined how humorous parasocial contact can reduce prejudice toward outgroups. study predictions were tested in an experiment ( n = 301) comparing the effects of a comedy stand-up by a muslim comedian (hasan minhaj or mohammed amer) to a control condition a stand-up from a non-muslim comedian (brian regan or jim gaffigan). results indicated that humorous parasocial contact was effective at facilitating parasocial relationships in all conditions. consistent with study predictions, when participants were exposed to the mediated intergroup contact with a muslim comedian, parasocial relationships – mediated through intergroup anxiety – were positively associated with willingness for contacts with muslims (i.e., negatively associated with social distance) and negatively associated with endorsement of muslim stereotypes. in contrast, these mediational relationships were not observed when mediated intergroup contact occurred with a white comedian. these and other results are discussed along with implications, limitations, and future research directions. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

from communication anxiety to psychological reliance abstract: grounded in self-determination theory (sdt), this study investigates how communication anxiety and psychological need satisfaction relate to the use of large language model (llm)-based chatbots, specifically chatgpt, for communication tasks (e.g., writing emails, drafting messages, and preparing scripts). using a three-wave panel survey of participants from the united states and south korea, we examined both between- and within-person dynamics. results showed that individuals with higher trait-level communication anxiety tended to use chatgpt more frequently for communication tasks, whereas within-person fluctuations in anxiety did not predict greater use. chatgpt use was positively associated with the satisfaction of basic psychological needs – autonomy, competence, and relatedness – and this need satisfaction, in turn, was associated with greater psychological reliance on chatgpt. importantly, need satisfaction further mediated the relationship between chatgpt use and psychological reliance at both within- and between-person levels. cultural comparisons revealed that us participants exhibited stronger momentary effects, while korean participants showed more stable, trait-based patterns. these findings highlight the role of llm-based chatbots as need-supportive communication tools that may become integrated into users’ communication practices over time, with implications for theories of ai-mediated communication, cross-cultural research, and the design of human-ai communication systems. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

condagree: an r package for ability-conditioned inter-rater agreement in constructed-response scoring condagree：用于构答反应评分中能力条件化评分者间一致性的r包 inter-rater agreement for constructed-response items is usually reported as one index per item, which cannot show whether scoring is less consistent for some examinees than for others. condagree is an r package that estimates agreement as a function of examinee ability and uses a latent-category rater error model to separate a score-opportunity effect from a residual ability effect. in simulations, conditioning on the operational score rejected a true null hypothesis in up to 68% of replications, whereas the latent-model test rejected in at most 8.5%. in 14,708 double-scored pirls 2011 responses from indonesia, kappa fell from .97 to .88 across achievement quintiles, a gradient explained mainly by score opportunity. applied psychological measurement

grmrt: an r package for joint modeling of likert responses and response times under the distance-difficulty hypothesis grmrt：距离-难度假设下likert作答与反应时间联合建模的r包 computer-administered questionnaires record item response times, yet these timings rarely inform scale evaluation. we introduce grmrt, an r package that jointly models likert responses with the graded response model and log response times with an inverted-u function of the person-item distance (the distance-difficulty hypothesis). the package estimates the model by marginal maximum likelihood, offers student-t errors for noisy web-survey timings, and tests the distance effect item by item as a diagnostic of item functioning. in 11,605 respondents to the ipip big-five markers, 48 of 49 timed items showed the expected pattern; the exception, “i insult people,” was among the least discriminating items. applied psychological measurement

assessing the "epileptic personality". this article traces the historical development, conceptualization, and assessment of the theory of the epileptic personality, with particular attention to the contributions of hermann rorschach, françoise minkowska, and leopold szondi. the theory of the epileptic personality characterized individuals with epilepsy by heightened emotionality, difficulties in social adaptation, egocentricity, sexual deviance, increased aggression and violence, and, in many cases, pronounced susceptibility to religious experience. as a rich and long-standing component of 19th-century medical thought, the theory of the epileptic personality continued to exert influence well into the 20th century, including its impact on the development of personality assessment tools. rorschach and szondi explicitly assessed the notion of the epileptic personality through their respective tests. subsequent research has, however, demonstrated that neither instrument measures a personality uniquely linked to epilepsy; rather, both capture broader psychodynamic patterns. the historical persistence of the theory of the epileptic personality reflects the influence of constitutional frameworks and their potential for stigmatization, offering enduring insights into the complex interplay among psychiatry, psychology, psychometrics, and medical and social perceptions. one dance, two partners: session-to-session therapist-client rating configurations and outcomes. this study identified session-level patterns of therapists' and clients' perceptions of the therapeutic alliance and treatment progress and examined whether these patterns were associated with client-reported outcomes. data included 15 therapist trainees, 86 clients, and 1035 session ratings. after each session, therapists and clients separately provided ratings, and clients rated their personal functioning and psychological symptoms. a multilevel latent class analysis identified five session patterns: "all-high" (53.3%), "bond-focused" (16.3%), "goals/tasks-focused" (3.3%), "client-low" (18.5%), and "all-low" (8.5%). longitudinal multilevel models revealed lower current personal functioning after client-low sessions, than after all-high or bond-focused sessions, and higher current psychological symptoms after client-low sessions than after all-high sessions. clients reported higher next-session symptoms after client-low sessions than after all-high or bond-focused sessions. no difference was detected in outcomes between all-low or goals/tasks-focused sessions and the rest. this study has significant implications for treatment planning, monitoring of the therapeutic alliance, and supervision of therapists-in-training. journal of marital and family therapy

associations among body image, exercise behavior, and relationship quality in cancer patients and survivors the current study examined associations between body image and relationship quality among cancer patients and survivors and tested whether exercise moderated these associations. participants were 71 cancer patients and survivors who were at least 18 years old, currently in a romantic relationship, and had completed an online survey assessing body image dissatisfaction, body image concerns, body appreciation, relationship satisfaction, commitment, and exercise behavior. results indicated that body image dissatisfaction and body image concerns were negatively associated with relationship satisfaction, whereas body appreciation was positively associated with relationship satisfaction and commitment. exploratory interactions illustrated moderations of vigorous and moderate exercise between body image and relationship quality, although these effects were modest. findings suggest that body image perceptions are associated with romantic relationship experiences among cancer patients and survivors, and that exercise may be relevant to understanding these associations. these findings provide implications for supporting relationships involving a cancer patient or survivor. health psychology open

animal fluency networks and item‐based trajectories in people with parkinson's disease before and after deep brain stimulation surgery abstract consistent decline in animal fluency occurs in people with parkinson's disease (pd) post‐surgery for deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus (stn‐dbs). recent findings indicate that patients produce fewer words after (vs. before) surgery. also, they produce smaller clusters of related animals, fewer switches between clusters, and more frequent (lexical frequency) and earlier‐acquired words. in this paper, we further investigated difficulties in lexical retrieval by reporting on word networks (to study the structure of the mental lexicon) and item‐based trajectories (to understand how the linguistic characteristics of the task change as the task progresses) of 61 dutch‐speaking individuals diagnosed with pd before and post‐surgery for stn‐dbs and 40 age and education‐matched healthy controls. word networks contained a higher number of edges and nodes for healthy controls relative to people with pd post‐surgery (adjusting for differences in sample size). also, patients before surgery produced a network with a lower cluster coefficient relative to healthy controls, as well as to people with pd post‐surgery. item‐based trajectories showed that both healthy controls and people with pd produced words of increasing complexity as they proceed with the task (e.g., less frequent, acquired later, of higher length). also, healthy controls showed a steeper increase in the age of acquisition of words across the first ten responses compared to pd post‐surgery. the re‐emergence of structure (clustering) in word networks post‐surgery for stn‐dbs and the differences in item‐based trajectories (vs. healthy controls) represent novel markers of lexical retrieval that are affected by surgery for stn‐dbs and pd. journal of neuropsychology

efficacy of acceptance and commitment therapy on anxiety, self-criticism, and body image in adolescent female athletes: a randomised controlled trial this randomised controlled trial evaluated an eight-session, school-adapted acceptance and commitment therapy (act) intervention among 62 adolescent female athletes from vocational high schools in ahvaz, iran. participants with high competitive anxiety and low body image satisfaction were randomly assigned to the act group ( n = 31) or a waitlist control group ( n = 31). a pretest-posttest design with 3-month follow-up was used. measures included the sport anxiety scale-2, forms of self-criticising/attacking and self-reassuring scale (short form), multidimensional body-self relations questionnaire appearance scales, and avoidance and fusion questionnaire for youth. repeated-measures anova showed significant group × time interactions for all primary outcomes ( p < .001, partial η 2 = .33–.44). the act group exhibited reductions in competitive anxiety and self-criticism and improvements in body image satisfaction at posttest and follow-up. exploratory mediation analyses indicated that intervention-related changes in psychological inflexibility were associated with changes in the outcomes; however, temporal precedence cannot be established and these findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating a causal mechanism. these results provide preliminary evidence that a brief, contextually adapted act programme was associated with improved psychological flexibility, reduced sport-related distress, and enhanced body image. practical implications for school-based interventions are discussed. journal of psychologists and counsellors in schools

metakognitive überzeugungen bei posttraumatischer belastungsstörung zusammenfassung trotz therapien wie kognitiver verhaltenstherapie und emdr haben viele ptbs-patient:innen anhaltende symptome. metakognitive modelle gehen davon aus, dass die bewertung und kontrolle von gedanken mit der ptbs-symptomatik zusammenhängen, besonders negative überzeugungen über gedanken und das bedürfnis nach gedankenkontrolle. ziel dieser studie war, zu prüfen, wie gut metakognitive überzeugungen (mcq-30) die ptbs-symptome (pcl-5) vorhersagen. insgesamt nahmen 165 erwachsene mit ptbs-symptomen (pcl-5 > cut-off) an einer online-umfrage teil. der zusammenhang zwischen ptbs-schwere und mcq-30-subskalen, alter und geschlecht wurde mittels multipler linearer regressionen untersucht. zur sicherstellung der modellgüte wurden prüfungen auf linearität, homoskedastizität, normalverteilung der residuen und multikollinearität durchgeführt. alle mcq-subskalen korrelierten positiv mit der ptbs-schwere. am stärksten waren die zusammenhänge für gedankenkontrolle (nc; r = 0,66), negative überzeugungen zu unkontrollierbarkeit/gefährlichkeit (neg; r = 0,63) und kognitive selbstaufmerksamkeit (csc; r = 0,61). die ergebnisse sind mit zentralen annahmen des metakognitiven modells vereinbar. die ergebnisse können ansatzpunkte für ein standardisiertes metakognitives profiling (mcq-30) und die priorisierung von mct-modulen (z. b. att, detached mindfulness) sein, um cas-prozesse zu reduzieren und die wirksamkeit traumafokussierter therapien zu steigern. psychotherapie

treating the whole person: clinical psychologist logan harvey on comorbidity in practice purpose the purpose of this viewpoint is to demystify common misconceptions clinicians may hold about working with people experiencing co-occurring anxiety or trauma and substance use conditions. it aims to provide clear, actionable guidance for therapists and clinicians supporting this population. design/methodology/approach this viewpoint presents an interview conducted by drs. tara gückel and jayden sercombe with experienced clinical psychologist logan harvey. a narrative analysis approach was applied to synthesise key themes and recommendations for clinical practice. findings this viewpoint highlights a transdiagnostic approach and evidence-based treatments, including eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing therapy, for addressing co-occurring mental health and substance use concerns. drawing on over a decade of clinical experience, logan offers practical insights and emphasises that many clinicians already possess the core skills needed to work effectively with this population. originality/value this paper challenges a persistent barrier in the field – the assumption that individuals with substance use concerns should be excluded from mental health treatment until their alcohol or other drug use is resolved. by presenting interventions that are appropriate and effective for co-occurring presentations, this viewpoint promotes integrated care and reinforces clinicians’ existing capacity to support this population. it offers a timely, practice-focused contribution that reframes comorbidity treatment as both accessible and achievable within routine clinical work. advances in dual diagnosis

who am i? mothers’ self-uncertainty, identification, and conformity in online maternal groups on social media abstract: research on the epistemic motivation that attracts individuals to anonymous online groups, particularly regarding early childhood mothers undergoing significant life transitions, remains limited. this study explores the self-uncertainty experienced by these mothers and investigates its connection to their identification with online maternal groups and adherence to group norms. using national survey data from 639 south korean mothers, this study, guided by uncertainty-identity theory (uit) and the social identity model of deindividuation (side), sheds light on how these mothers often internalize intense group norms. findings underscore the importance of considering mothers as members of a distinct social group (vs. individuals), enriching our understanding of motherhood dynamics. both uit and side effectively explain these complex phenomena. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

when entertainment media pull at the heartstrings abstract: given that music remains relatively understudied in eudaimonic media effect research, the present study investigated the effect of music video consumption on eudaimonic emotions and prosocial outcomes. a pre-registered experiment ( n = 326) was conducted to examine the associations between eudaimonic music consumption, emotions, prosocial motivations, and donation willingness. findings showed that participants viewing the eudaimonic music videos reported significantly higher eudaimonic emotions and corresponding physical reactions compared to those who viewed hedonic music videos. path analysis results revealed the associations between music video consumption and prosocial orientation and willingness to donate to a worthy cause. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

consistency of user’s sexism impacts the likelihood of confrontation on social media abstract: despite the proliferation of equality-focused actions on social media, such as the black lives matter and #metoo movements, discrimination is still prevalent on these platforms. while confronting prejudice may reduce future discrimination (i.e., counter-speech), several factors limit confrontation within face-to-face interactions (i.e., social costs, perceived effectiveness, self-efficacy). intervention is also more likely when others’ actions are driven by situational factors (i.e., external attribution) than stable features of personality (i.e., internal attributions). yet, whether these antecedents of face-to-face confrontation parallel online confrontation is unclear. participants ( n = 120) viewed a sexist or neutral social media profile manipulated to be consistent or inconsistent (i.e., facilitating internal and external attributions, respectively) and were asked to respond to the user’s recent post. inconsistently sexist profiles were more likely to be confronted than consistently sexist profiles. however, participants exhibited more effort in responding (i.e., number of characters) to sexist than neutral prompts, regardless of the user’s consistency. higher self-efficacy increased confrontation of sexist profiles, with larger effects emerging for inconsistent sexist behavior. contrary to expectations, heightened social cost (i.e., perceived risks of confrontation) increased response effort for sexist profiles. these counterintuitive results indicate cognitive appraisals for online counter-speech might differ from face-to-face confrontation, potentially driven by partial anonymity, physical distance, and temporal delay of feedback observed in social media interactions. while results provide partial support for the role of attribution and individual differences for online confrontation, additional research is needed to understand antecedents of counter-speech on social media. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

emotion regulation strategies are associated with differential responses to the news abstract: for some, negative news increases negative affect, harms mental well-being, and reduces news consumption. others, however, cope better with recurring news negativity. we propose that differences in emotional regulation strategies explain, at least partly, these varied responses to negative news. in a preregistered, longitudinal intensive diary study (7 days) with a diverse, predominantly western european sample ( n = 120), we examine to what extent emotion regulation strategies are associated with negative affect, mental well-being, and news use frequency. our findings indicate that cognitive reappraisal and selective attention effectively down-regulate negative emotions arising from news use. however, distraction and suppression showed no statistically significant effects on affect, well-being, or news consumption. this study provides initial evidence that emotion regulation strategies help explain individual differences in responses to negative news and lays the groundwork for a research agenda in communication science exploring the role of emotion regulation in media effects. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

validation of the manga attachment scale (mas) for measuring attachment to manga – japanese comics abstract: manga – japanese comics – is a central pillar of japanese culture and an expanding global phenomenon, yet little research has examined how individuals form and maintain meaningful connections with this medium. while previous studies conceptualized manga attachment as a multidimensional construct, no validated measures exist. this study refines and validates an existing set of manga attachment items, and introduces the manga attachment scale (mas), a psychometric tool assessing emotional, cognitive, and behavioral engagement with manga. across three independent studies, the mas was tested for factor structure, reliability, and validity. study 1 ( n = 328) used exploratory factor analysis (efa) to refine the original item set, resulting in a 14-item, four-factor structure: safe haven, separation distress, secure base, and proximity maintenance. study 2 ( n = 588) confirmed this structure via confirmatory factor analysis (cfa), demonstrating strong model fit. study 3 ( n = 511) evaluated predictive, construct, convergent, and discriminant validity, showing significant relationships between the mas, reading frequency, and manga’s perceived importance, while distinguishing it from other manga engagement measures. the mas provides a validated framework for assessing manga attachment, contributing to media attachment research and extending attachment theory. this tool facilitates future investigations into manga’s role in well-being, identity formation, and media engagement. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

mad scientists, bad impressions? abstract: although research suggests that popular media can shape adults’ perceptions of scientists, studies with younger audiences remain scarce. in this preregistered online experiment, children aged 8–12 ( n = 256) viewed an animated television program that featured women who varied in their character role (i.e., superheroes vs. supervillains) and character description (i.e., labeled vs. not labeled as scientists). children reported high levels of epistemic trust in scientists overall. however, viewing a villainous woman who was labeled (vs. not labeled) as a scientist led to slight reductions in epistemic trust. furthermore, habitual exposure to superhero television negatively predicted one dimension of epistemic trust (i.e., perceived benevolence). we discuss the theoretical implications of these findings and offer practical suggestions for content design. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

is a fish in the mouth worth two in the water? some, but not all, beluga whales indicate that it is. this essay begins by noting that the adage goes goes, "a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush." unless you are a beluga whale. then, neither option is worth much because there are not too many birds, hands, or bushes in your world. but, "a fish in the mouth might be worth two in the water," especially if those two are an unsure prospect in an unsure world. so, what would a beluga whale choose in such a spot, and more importantly, would the choices of one beluga whale align with the choices of another? the study in this issue by m. h. babb et al. (see record 2027-52608-001) focuses on these questions. the present author concludes that individual differences seem to be the key outcome from this study. the question is what one can learn from those. babb et al. offered that these could reflect personality traits (something also proposed for the demonstrated individual differences in risk-related decisions in other whale species. with only four individuals in this study, it is hard to make any strong claims, especially when those individuals were all females. that said, individual differences are not merely noise obscuring phenomena of interest. antiracism self-efficacy: motivating individuals toward racial justice we integrate existing research on racial justice allyship and antiracism with social cognitive theory to develop our understanding of why and how individuals who identify as white in the context of the us may initiate and sustain antiracist behavior at the individual level. in study 1a, we define the concept of antiracism self-efficacy and develop a seven-item measure. we then examine the extent to which the seven-item scale exhibits convergent and discriminant validity in study 1b. in study 2, we demonstrate that antiracism self-efficacy predicts a broad range of antiracist behavioral intentions and behaviors above and beyond racial attitudes and beliefs. study 3 extends this argument using a bias-confrontation paradigm, demonstrating that antiracism self-efficacy predicts bias-confrontation outcomes above and beyond other motivational constructs and general self-efficacy. overall, this work identifies and explores antiracism self-efficacy as an important concept that motivates individuals toward racial justice allyship and antiracist behavior at a micro (i.e., day-to-day) level. we posit that including antiracism self-efficacy in motivational models addressing allyship and antiracist behavior will help guide future empirical work on antiracism at the individual level, in addition to having important practical implications for racial justice/antiracism education, training, and other related initiatives within organizations. group processes & intergroup relations

temporal stability of vagally-mediated heart rate variability over a one-year period: a latent state-trait examination. vagally-mediated heart rate variability (vmhrv) is widely proposed as a biomarker for physical and mental health, but its utility hinges on psychometric robustness, particularly temporal stability and consistency across measurement contexts. prior reliability studies have been constrained by small samples, short retest intervals, and analytic approaches that cannot disentangle stable individual differences from situational fluctuations and measurement error. the present study examined the temporal and transsituational stability of vmhrv over a 1-year interval in a large, population-based sample (n = 175) from the dresden burnout study. short-term inter-beat-interval (ibi) recordings were obtained at two annual assessments under two conditions: recumbent recovery following venipuncture and seated rest. four cardiac and hrv-derived parameters, the established vmhrv indices root mean square of successive differences (rmssd), percentage of successive rr intervals differing by more than 50 ms (pnn50), and high-frequency power (hf power), complemented by mean rr interval (rr) as a general cardiac timing parameter, were analyzed using single-trait-multistate-method-minus-one [stmsm(m-1)] models within the latent state-trait (lst) framework, with recovery specified as the reference condition and resting modeled as a condition-specific method factor. reliability ranged from 0.650 to 0.903, and trait specificity ranged from 0.375 to 0.773. rr and rmssd showed the most consistent trait-like profiles across occasions and conditions. pnn50 showed the highest individual trait-specificity estimate, but also greater heterogeneity across occasions, whereas hf power showed comparatively lower trait specificity and greater occasion-specific variance. method specificity was small (0.034-0.087), indicating that stable condition-specific deviations from recovery accounted for a limited proportion of variance. these findings support the interpretation of vmhrv, particularly rmssd and pnn50, as mainly trait-like indicators of cardiac vagal function, while also showing that single short-term assessments contain meaningful occasion-related variance. standardized assessment conditions and repeated measurements remain essential for biomarker applications of vmhrv. psychophysiology

association between physical activity and cognitive function among community-dwelling older adults in delhi ncr: a cross-sectional study age-associated decline in physical and cognitive functioning is one of the most significant health problems associated with healthy ageing. this study aimed to evaluate the association between physical activity (pa) level and cognitive functioning among the older indian population residing in delhi-national capital region (ncr), india. a cross-sectional study was conducted among community-dwelling adults aged 50-65 years using the international physical activity questionnaire-short form (ipaq-sf) and montreal cognitive assessment (moca). the total number of respondents was 400 (mean age: 56.3 ± 5.8 years), with 67% female and 33% male. 70% of respondents were moderately active, with a mean moca score of 21.3 ± 3.8 and 77% had mild cognitive impairment. there was a significant positive correlation (r = .32, p < .01) between physical activity and cognitive function, with higher activity levels resulting in better moca scores. older adults’ physical activity remains below who guidelines, highlighting the need for regular activity to maintain cognitive health. neuropsychological trends

working memory, awareness of choice (aoc) and awareness of action (aoa) in the decision-making process in a professional frame working memory significantly influences decision-making effectiveness and decisionmaking awareness encompasses awareness of choice (aoc) and awareness of action (aoa). additionally, internal (i.e., personality traits, expertise) and external factors (i.e., time pressure, incentives) influence the quality of decision-making. this study investigated behavioural correlates of two professionals’ groups performing a novel dual task to explore aoc and aoa accuracy (acc). 117 healthy individuals, divided into next-generation (n=75) and experienced professionals (n=42), completed the task, followed by the 10-item big five inventory and maximisation scale. findings indicate that experienced professionals have lower acc than next-generation and that aoc turns out to be more difficult and cognitively demanding compared to aoa, maybe because thought processes are abstract and difficult to monitor and control. the lower awareness in experienced professionals, instead, could be attributed to work experience and work environment itself, that required to make complex, intuitive, and rapid decisions. moreover, personality traits correlate differently with acc in next-generation and experienced professionals, highlighting different personality patterns. neuropsychological trends

effect of music-based training on cognitive function in older adults with and without neurological impairment: a systematic review aging is associated with progressive decline in cognitive skills. combining music-based interventions has been proposed as a strategy to enhance cognitive processing in older adults. the objective of the study was to review the effects of music-based training on cognitive outcomes in healthy and neurologically impaired older adults. a comprehensive literature search was conducted. randomized controlled trials investigating music-based training (dual, multi-task) and reporting cognitive outcomes were included. methodological quality and risk of bias was evaluated. data were synthesized qualitatively. seven randomized controlled trials were included. interventions included music-based dual-task, and multitask musicmovement programs with durations from single-session to 12-month protocols. methodological quality ranged from fair to good, while cochrane rob2 assessments indicated some concerns in allocation and outcome reporting. most studies reported improvements in specific cognitive domains. music based intervention shows promise for improving cognitive domains in older adults. larger, high-quality studies with standardized protocols and longer follow-up required. neuropsychological trends

a theoretical and methodological proposal for m-self: an identity-activation and cross-role transfer protocol for life transitions life transitions can compress the working self into a single salient identity, muting resources from other roles. the identity activation and cross-role transfer protocol (mself) is a brief, modular protocol that maps roles to traits and emotions, translates traits into universal behaviours (ubs), and rehearses small, situated cross-role transfers; an optional light-touch heart rate variability (hrv) and electroencephalography (eeg) layer provides formative state feedback. pragmatic implementations in four cohorts: maternity return-to-work (11,527 mothers reached; 2024 mixed-audience survey n = 715), women nearing release from prison (n = 12), young-women mentorship (analytic n = 500; programme enrolment = 555), and an eating-disorder programme (n = 85), show within-person pre-post signals of higher self-efficacy and transfer frequency and lower perceived stress. making identity complexity visible and transfer feasible may convert transitions into developmental opportunities. evidence is exploratory, nonrandomized, and largely self-reported; randomized and longitudinal studies are needed. neuropsychological trends

beyond cold control. a neuroscientific perspective on hot executive functions in gambling and gaming disorder research on executive functions (efs) in behavioural addictions (bas) has predominantly focused on the cold domain, whereas the hot domain has received comparatively limited attention. this theoretical contribution examines gambling disorder (gd) and internet gaming disorder (igd), arguing that the social dimension of hot efs represents a major gap in current research and intervention approaches for bas. we discuss the strengths and limitations of existing interventions and highlight the need for a more socially grounded perspective. furthermore, because traditional neuroscience paradigms often isolate individuals from their social environment—despite the central role of social interactions in hot efs—we discuss the promise of socially situated decision-making scenarios and a hyperscanning approach as a possible answer to investigating the social dimension in this field of study. this perspective may provide a more ecologically valid assessment of efs and inform the development of innovative neuroenhancement interventions for individuals with gd and igd. neuropsychological trends

psychometric evaluation of the process model of emotion regulation questionnaire in the portuguese context validated instruments capturing the full complexity of emotion regulation remain scarce. grounded in gross’s process model, this study examined the psychometric properties of the portuguese version of the process model of emotion regulation questionnaire (pmerq). in a cross-sectional design, the translated 83-item pmerq was administered online to two independent quota-based samples of portuguese adults (study 1: n = 254; study 2: n = 270; mean age about 46 years; about 50% male; about 48% with higher education). in study 1, exploratory factor analyses indicated a six-factor solution reflecting broad regulatory domains, while a 12-factor solution reproduced the theoretical dimensions with partial overlap among adjacent strategies; internal consistency was acceptable to good. in study 2, the theoretical 12-factor structure was tested through confirmatory factor analysis. after data-driven refinement, a 45-item version showed adequate fit and acceptable to good reliability, with measurement invariance across gender (configural, metric, scalar). associations with emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, well-being, distress, and aggression supported convergent and concurrent criterion validity, and associations with personality partially supported nomological validity. these findings provide preliminary support for the pmerq in the portuguese context. journal of intelligence

associations between 24-h movement behaviors and executive function in chinese children: a cross-sectional study based on compositional data analysis executive function (ef)—higher-order cognitive control processes (inhibitory control, working memory, cognitive flexibility)—is related to, yet distinct from, general cognitive ability. ef develops rapidly in childhood and is sensitive to daily movement behaviors; compositional evidence from chinese school-aged children is scarce. in 441 chinese children aged 6–8 years (five regions; 252 boys, 189 girls), we examined cross-sectional associations of 24-h movement behaviors with ef—assessed via the stroop, corsi block-tapping, and wisconsin card sorting tasks—and quantified expected ef changes under isotemporal substitutions involving moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (mvpa). wrist-worn accelerometers measured the behaviors over 7 days. compositional isometric log-ratio regression and 15 min substitution models, adjusted for sex, age, school, and anthropometrics, showed that relative to other behaviors, greater mvpa was associated with higher forward recall and fewer perseverative responses. reallocating 15 min/day to mvpa from sb, lpa, or slp was associated with fewer perseverative responses (b = −0.60 to −0.82; robust to outcome-stratified multiple comparison correction) and, in the lpa and slp pairs, with higher forward recall (b = 0.16–0.22; not robust to correction). mvpa was the movement behavior component most consistently associated with executive function; reallocating time from sb, lpa, or slp to mvpa may be associated with fewer perseverative responses. journal of intelligence

unethical generative ai use and academic procrastination in higher education: a cross-sample examination of epistemic laziness and cognitive offloading the increasing use of generative artificial intelligence (genai) in higher education has raised concerns about maladaptive academic behaviors. using cross-sectional data from two independent university student samples, this study examined whether unethical genai use (ugaiu) was related to academic procrastination directly and through sequential indirect associations via epistemic laziness and cognitive offloading. turkish-speaking students were surveyed in classrooms (n = 243) and english-speaking students online via prolific (n = 213). because the samples differed in several respects, they were treated as independent samples rather than as proxies for language or culture. the newly developed measures showed configural and metric invariance (only tentatively for epistemic laziness). structural equation models controlling for gender, age, and daily genai use showed that ugaiu was positively associated with epistemic laziness and cognitive offloading in both samples. in the turkish-speaking sample, ugaiu was indirectly associated with procrastination, mainly through cognitive offloading; in the english-speaking sample, only the direct association was significant. path-specific multigroup tests provided weak evidence of a between-sample difference only for the cognitive offloading–procrastination path, which was not robust to multiple-comparison correction or partial invariance. given the cross-sectional design, the findings describe associations rather than temporal or causal ordering. journal of intelligence

associations between pass cognitive processes and early literacy skills in preschool children this study examined associations between planning, attention, simultaneous processing, and successive processing (pass) cognitive processes and early literacy skills in 150 preschool children attending two public schools in istanbul, türkiye. cognitive processes were assessed using the cognitive assessment system (cas), and early literacy was assessed using the early literacy test (erot). zero-order and age-adjusted spearman correlations showed consistently strong positive associations between cas and erot scores; age-adjusted correlations ranged from ρ = 0.640 to 0.846, with the cas total–erot total association remaining ρ = 0.846. the four pass process scores were also strongly intercorrelated (pearson’s r = 0.732–0.882), indicating substantial overlap among the cognitive-process measures. in hierarchical regression, the four pass processes accounted for substantial additional variance in erot total performance beyond age (δr2 = 0.756), with the full model explaining 75.9% of the variance. attention (β = 0.376, p = .007) and successive processing (β = 0.329, p = .015) showed statistically significant conditional associations in the full sample. complementary dominance analysis indicated the largest average relative contribution for attention, although overlapping bootstrap distributions did not support a clearly differentiated hierarchy among the four pass processes. after false discovery rate (fdr) correction across 28 pass coefficient-level tests from seven subtest-specific regression models, seven process–skill associations remained statistically significant in the full sample, compared with two in the previously screened sensitivity sample (n = 138). at the subtest level, the simultaneous processing–letter knowledge association remained significant after fdr correction in both analytic samples, whereas the attention–functional knowledge association met the fdr-adjusted significance criterion only in the screened sensitivity sample (n = 138). overall, broad pass–early literacy associations were robust, whereas process-specific patterns were more sensitive to analytic specification. given the cross-sectional design and substantial shared variance among the pass processes, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal or exclusive process–skill relationships. journal of intelligence

self-regulatory resources and academic dishonesty in digital learning environments: the mediating role of ability-protective self-handicapping and dysfunctional beliefs research on intelligence in education has shown that how students interpret and protect their perceived ability shapes their responses to evaluative threat, yet this perspective has rarely been applied to academic dishonesty, a problem intensified as assessment moves into digital learning environments. the present study examined whether learned resourcefulness, an acquired repertoire of self-control skills, is associated with academic dishonesty through two ability-protective strategies: self-handicapping, which shields perceived ability by supplying an alternative explanation for failure, and dysfunctional beliefs, which make self-worth contingent on demonstrated success. cross-sectional data from 1045 university students (71.6% female; mean age 22.0 years) were analyzed using latent-variable structural equation modeling with robust maximum likelihood estimation. the model fit the data adequately and accounted for a substantial share of the variance in dishonest behavior. dysfunctional beliefs and self-handicapping showed the strongest associations with dishonest behavior. learned resourcefulness was associated with dishonesty mainly through these two strategies; its direct association was not significant on the raw metric but reached significance under a log transformation. dishonest behavior and attitude toward dishonesty showed divergent predictor patterns, with external locus of control most strongly associated with attitude. a latent profile analysis identified an at-risk profile with the highest dishonesty. the findings suggest that academic dishonesty can be understood, in part, as an ability-protective response to evaluative threat, extending research on non-cognitive individual differences and beliefs about ability from achievement to academic integrity. journal of intelligence

filial piety expectations, ethical values, and flourishing among filipino emerging adults filial piety is valued in many collectivist contexts worldwide, and may become increasingly relevant to emerging adults as they take on more familial roles and responsibilities. these expectations can be considered a source of meaning or pressure and thus affect emerging adults’ flourishing in divergent ways. in this study, we examine how ethical values of autonomy, community, and divinity may provide meaning frames that moderate this relationship between filial piety expectations and flourishing. analysis of responses from 218 filipinos aged 18-29 revealed nonsignificant moderation effects. instead, filial piety expectations, and endorsement of the ethics of autonomy and divinity directly predicted flourishing; the ethic of community was nonsignificant. exploratory mediation analysis additionally showed indirect effects of autonomy on the relationship between filial piety expectations and flourishing. we discuss limitations in measuring the three ethics in the filipino context, implications of these results, and recommendations for future research. emerging adulthood

“you’re lucky if you sleep” : narratives of perceived psychosocial influences and consequences of sleep behaviors among emerging adults from sociodemographic minority groups in the u.s. the purpose of this qualitative study was to explore perceptions of psychosocial influences and consequences of sleep; assess the perceived role of sleep self-efficacy; and evaluate the impact of the covid-19 pandemic on sleep health among a sample of university-attending emerging adults from sociodemographic minority groups in the u.s. participants ( n = 14; 68.5% racial-ethnic minority, 43.8% first-generation) completed online interviews. results of thematic analysis showed consistency between the psychosocial factors that reportedly affect sleep (i.e., perceived influences) and the factors that were affected by sleep (i.e., perceived consequences): academics, mental health, social adjustment, physical health, and daily schedules. themes regarding sleep self-efficacy and the perceived impact of the pandemic revealed variable approaches in how participants negotiate sleep needs in relation to the competing developmental tasks of emerging adulthood. emerging adulthood

identity‐based victimization and identity coherence among minoritized adolescents in the netherlands: the role of ethnic identity, school belonging, and family emotional support abstract this cross‐sectional study examined how identity‐based victimization was associated with adolescents' sense of identity coherence in the dutch sociocultural context. guided by an integrated phenomenological variant of ecological systems theory (pvest) and resilience‐informed framework, we examined whether perceived discrimination and hate crime victimization were directly associated with identity coherence, whether these associations were indirect through ethnic identity achievement and school belonging, and whether family emotional support moderated the direct associations. using data from 1032 adolescents with a migration background (ages 13–18; 52.8% female) from the dutch fourth wave of the international self‐report delinquency study, we estimated an observed‐variable path model within the sem framework. neither perceived discrimination nor hate crime victimization was directly associated with identity coherence. instead, two distinct indirect patterns emerged, running in opposite directions. perceived discrimination was indirectly associated with higher identity coherence through higher ethnic identity achievement. hate crime victimization was indirectly associated with lower identity coherence through lower school belonging, which showed the strongest positive association with identity coherence. family emotional support did not moderate the direct associations between identity‐based victimization and identity coherence. although the cross‐sectional design precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causal processes, the results indicate that different forms of identity‐based victimization relate to adolescents' identity coherence through different proximal resources. these findings contribute to a limited european evidence base on identity‐based victimization and identity coherence among minoritized adolescents. journal of research on adolescence

establishing the structural validity, language-based performance, and convergent validity of the caregiver strain questionnaire-short form 11 within a latinx sample. caregiver strain or stress resulting from caring for a child with emotional/behavioral problems-can negatively impact the psychological health of caregivers and may underly decisions to seek mental health services for their youth. the caregiver strain questionnaire-short form 11 (cgsq-sf11) was developed to assess caregiver strain, but a spanish language form has yet to be evaluated, limiting its utility with latinx families. this study evaluated the cgsq-sf11 as a tool for assessing caregiver strain among latinx caregivers. the sample included 511 latinx caregivers of youths aged 6-18 who self-selected into english (n = 275) or spanish (n = 236) questionnaires. in general, caregivers reported moderate levels of caregiver strain, and caregivers who completed the spanish survey reported significantly lower youth mental health problem severity and caregiver strain relative to those in the english survey. confirmatory factor analyses suggest that a three-factor structure fit the data better (i.e., objective, subjective internalized, and subjective externalized strain) than a global factor. however, a bifactor model suggested that the variance in the total score was best represented by a unidimensional structure. the cgsq-sf11 achieved metric invariance, which suggests that the latent variable and strength of factor loadings for the global scale were similar across language forms. finally, we provide evidence of convergent validity through associations between the cgsq-sf11 global scale and measures of youth internalizing and externalizing problems. our findings support the use of cgsq-sf11 english and spanish language forms with latinx caregivers. family process

the fat‐body secreted neuropeptide ccha2 signals insulin‐producing cells in the brain to promote sleep abstract sleep is a fundamental behavior regulated by diverse environmental and physiological cues. while the central mechanisms underlying sleep regulation have been investigated in detail, far less is known about how nutrient signals from the periphery are communicated to the brain to modulate sleep. here, we perform a targeted rnai screen of genes enriched in the fat body and regulated by feeding state to identify genes that function in the fat body to regulate sleep in drosophila . this analysis found that fat body‐specific knockdown of ccha2 significantly reduced sleep duration and sleep depth in fed flies, phenocopying sleep in starved flies. ccha2 ‐deficient flies exhibited reduced glycogen stores and diminished feeding drive. analysis of single‐cell transcriptomic atlases confirms that the ccha2 receptor (ccha2‐r) is selectively expressed in insulin‐producing cells (ipcs) of the fly brain. we find that knockdown of ccha2 ‐ r in ipcs recapitulates the sleep loss phenotype of ccha2 mutants, supporting a role in adipose‐brain signaling. further screening of genes identified in single cell atlases as being enriched in ipcs led to the identification of numerous genes that function in ipcs to regulate sleep, including modulators of wnt and insulin signaling. together, these findings identify a fat body‐ipc axis that is a critical modulator of sleep duration and intensity. genes brain and behavior

a latent profile and network analysis of kinesiophobia in patients after total joint arthroplasty purpose: based on the stress-multifactorial system, this study aimed to classify heterogeneous subgroups of kinesiophobia in patients following total joint arthroplasty using latent profile analysis, and to identify the key constructs associated with kinesiophobia within each subgroup through network analysis.
patients and methods: the present study employed a cross-sectional survey design, conducted between april 2025 and july 2026, involving 250 patients after hip or knee arthroplasty at an orthopedic center. latent profile analysis was performed to identify subgroups of kinesiophobia. network analysis was conducted to examine the associations among kinesiophobia, pain intensity, pain catastrophizing, rehabilitation self-efficacy, and social support, with the total scores of each scale represented as a node.
results: in 250 patients after hip or knee arthroplasty, the mean kinesiophobia score was 37.65 ± 4.45, with a prevalence of 48.8%. two distinct subgroups were identified: the "low kinesiophobia-activity acceptance group" (73.6%) and the "high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance group" (26.4%). binary logistic regression showed that longer daily pain duration [or = 2.196,= 0.003], higher oswestry disability index scores [or = 1.155,=0.002], and negative coping style [or = 1.322,= 0.013] were associated with greater odds of membership in the high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance group, whereas higher rehabilitation self-efficacy was associated with lower odds of membership in this group[or = 0.857,< 0.01]. in the "high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance group", pain catastrophizing (pcs) showed the highest centrality (r= 1.424, r= 1.224, r= 1.565). conversely, in the "low kinesiophobia-activity acceptance group", rehabilitation self-efficacy (ser) showed the highest centrality (= 1.609,= 1.007,= 1.095). network comparison tests revealed a statistically significant difference in network structure between the two subgroups (= 0.29,= 0.022), but no significant difference in global strength (= 3.27,= 0.078).
conclusion: patients after total joint arthroplasty display heterogeneous patterns of kinesiophobia across latent profiles, with differences in psychological network structures between subgroups rather than in overall connectivity strength. in the high kinesiophobia-fear avoidance subgroup, pain catastrophizing shows the highest centrality, whereas rehabilitation self-efficacy shows the highest centrality in the low kinesiophobia-activity acceptance subgroup. psychology research and behavior management

measuring moral pluralism and prioritization in a global world: introduction to special section on ethical values assessment (eva) this article introduces the special section on research that used the ethical values assessment (eva). the eva measures endorsement of numerous values based on the ethics of autonomy, community, and divinity (on a likert scale), and prioritization of values (rank ordering one’s top three values). while the eva may be used with diverse age groups, the present articles focused on emerging adults. exploring values pertaining to ideology, love, and work are necessary tasks in emerging adulthood as is deciding upon priorities. the present articles, which included diverse socio-economic samples from the philippines, sub-saharan africa, thailand, and the u.s., show that the aspiration for autonomy is remarkably widespread. autonomy is the ethic of globalization, but divinity is also boosted by globalization in some cultures. depending on culture, autonomy together with either community or divinity predicts flourishing and narrating a reflective worldview. the methods employed were quantitative and mixed-methods, and cross-sectional as well as longitudinal. emerging adulthood

autonomy, community, and divinity among emerging adults in sub-saharan africa: new and renewed ethical values in a globalizing world this study used the ethical values assessment (eva) to examine the extent to which emerging adults (n = 2,316) in sub-saharan africa (ssa) rated autonomy, community and divinity values as important and prioritized them as core values in their lives, and how their values were affected by globalization. participants strongly endorsed all three values, reaffirming ubuntu as a distinguishing concept in ssa. unexpectedly, they prioritized autonomy—as do emerging adults in increasing parts of the world. globalization in the form of internet access, but not urban residence, boosted autonomy, which fits with recent literature that has termed autonomy the globalization ethic. surprisingly, globalization also boosted divinity, which may reflect a surge of religiosity unique to emerging adults in ssa, especially among those living in urban areas. several future research directions are proposed to encourage studies in ssa, a severely understudied region that has much to contribute to psychological science. emerging adulthood

making room for autonomy: longitudinal patterns of moral prioritization and pluralism among thai youth globalization is linked to rising autonomy values among youth, yet little is known about how moral priorities change longitudinally in rapidly globalizing contexts. this study tracked 40 thai adolescents (20 rural, 20 urban) over 10 years, with 32 retained in emerging adulthood. early socialization context (rural, urban) served as a proxy for early globalization exposure. at both time points, participants completed the ethical values assessment (likert ratings, forced-choice task, open-ended prompt). statistical analyses revealed parallel increases in autonomy centrality, modest declines in community, and a sharp decline in divinity importance alongside stable divinity prioritization. although all three ethics were endorsed, prioritization increasingly centered autonomy. persistent rural–urban differences reflected the enduring influence of early socialization context. qualitative analysis of write-in responses converged, with emerging adults emphasizing autonomy-oriented values and adolescents referencing a broader range of values. findings differentiate endorsement and prioritization, and illustrate how globalization and early socialization shape moral reconfiguration from adolescence to emerging adulthood. emerging adulthood

how emerging adults understand their worlds: ethical values, meaning-making, and worldview formation in a contemporary american context the mixed-study examines how ethics and values, measured by the ethical values assessment (eva; jensen & padilla-walker, 2015) shape worldview formation and meaning-making in a sample of 31 emerging adulthood (m = 21.87 years) living in the u.s. data was collected following the 2024 u.s. presidential election, creating an important socio cultural political context. using theories that span the areas of narrative meaning-making, moral development, and worldview formation to ground our interpretations. findings suggest that the integration of autonomy and community ethics was associated with a more expansive and coherent worldview, including the ability to make sense of and find significance in experiences. in contrast, those prioritizing only autonomy or only community showed limited engagement with broader societal structures or personal reflection, and those low in both dimensions lacked a developed worldview. our findings support previous literature but also expand the understanding of worldview formation and emerging adulthood development. emerging adulthood

from anorexia nervosa onset to treatment initiation: experiences of parents and young people abstract objective to explore how young people (yp) with anorexia nervosa (an) and parents experience the period from illness onset to treatment initiation, focussing on perceived impacts on family life. method an exploratory qualitative study employing 15 interviews with yp (aged 13–17 years) and 20 interviews with parents analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. results four themes were developed. evolving doubt captured parents' uncertainty and doubts, from normalising early signs of an to uncertainty about help‐seeking and managing healthcare‐related barriers. living an ordinary and busy life before an described family life before an as structured and activity‐oriented, frequently framed by parents as ‘normal’. from trust to tension reflected relational shifts following an onset, commonly marked by strain and emotional distance, though some families experienced increased closeness. making sense of the emergence of an highlighted how parents and yp sought explanations, with parents drawing on broader interpretations and perceived vulnerabilities, whereas yp offered more concrete accounts related to body image or health. conclusions the four themes portray how family life develops from taken‐for‐granted normality and trusting relationships, through parental doubt and ambiguity, towards conflict and mistrust, and how both yp and parents strive to make sense of these changes. european eating disorders review

the global measure of masturbation satisfaction (gmmast): scale development and preliminary validation. solo masturbation is a common sexual behavior, but its role in well-being is poorly understood. one reason is that the extant literature has generally focused on how engagement in masturbation (e.g., in the past 4 weeks) relates to well-being while neglecting how the subjective experience of masturbation (e.g., as valuable and positive or not) might impact well-being. this report describes the development of the brief, 5-item global measure of masturbation satisfaction (gmmast). the measure was developed using a sample of 2,486 adults who had masturbated in the past month, drawn from the masturbation and sexual health survey, a u.s. national survey. exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses and tests of measurement invariance suggest the scale has strong psychometric properties. associations with related constructs (e.g., positive and negative masturbation attitudes, masturbation motives, receipt of sexual education) provide preliminary evidence of validity. journal of sex & marital therapy

nurturing resilient minds in nursing students: purpose in life, resilience, and personality-based substance use risk-a descriptive correlational study. background: nursing students face sustained academic and clinical stressors that may affect mental health and personality-based substance use vulnerability. evidence remains limited in saudi and other middle eastern nursing-student populations on whether purpose in life and resilience relate differently to the four substance use risk profile scale (surps) personality profiles. this distinction is relevant to profile-specific prevention and student-support services. the study examined relationships among a study-specific modified purpose in life (pil) score, resilience, and the four surps profiles and explored associations with demographic characteristics.
methods: we conducted a descriptive correlational study with 915 undergraduate nursing students at a university in saudi arabia using an online english-language survey. the pil test was administered in a study-specific 20-item, 5-point online response format rather than the conventional 7-point semantic-differential format; consequently, the resulting pil score was treated as a modified within-sample measure and not as psychometrically equivalent to the conventional pil. surps was scored as four separate personality profiles with the positively worded hopelessness items reverse-scored, and cd-risc-25 responses were recoded to the standard 0-4 metric before summation.
results: mean scores were 60.55 ± 19.94 for the study-specific modified pil, 16.32 ± 4.49 for hopelessness, 13.06 ± 3.88 for anxiety sensitivity, 12.56 ± 3.75 for impulsivity, 15.36 ± 4.49 for sensation seeking, and 54.28 ± 24.60 for resilience. the modified pil score correlated negatively with hopelessness (r = -0.763) and positively with resilience (r = 0.737); resilience correlated negatively with hopelessness (r = -0.770) and positively with anxiety sensitivity, impulsivity, and sensation seeking (r = 0.688, 0.612, and 0.683, respectively; all p < 0.001). male students had slightly higher impulsivity and sensation-seeking scores, while age and academic-level differences were nonsignificant. demographic models explained very little variance (r= 0.006-0.012).
conclusion: corrected surps scoring revealed a profile-specific pattern, but the large correlations and the use of a nonvalidated 5-point pil response format require cautious interpretation. hopelessness was strongly inversely associated with the modified pil score and resilience, whereas anxiety sensitivity, impulsivity, and sensation seeking showed positive associations whose substantive meaning cannot be separated from possible construct overlap or shared-method effects in this cross-sectional self-report dataset. the findings support separate surps-profile interpretation rather than an aggregate score, while replication using the conventional pil format, culturally validated instruments, direct behavioral outcomes, and formal construct-validity testing is needed before stronger clinical inferences are made. brain and behavior

the impact of cladribine tablets on cognition over one year in patients with multiple sclerosis: a preliminary study. introduction: cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (ms), affecting >40% of patients. cladribine tablets are a high-efficacy ms disease-modifying therapy to prevent relapses and limit disease progression. our previous study showed cortical gray matter lesion stability over one year after the start of cladribine, though its effect on cognition is not well known. this study aimed to investigate the one-year impact of cladribine tablets on cognition in multiple sclerosis.
methods: fourteen ms subjects [age (mean ± sd) 50.2 ± 10.8, 7.14% men, 57.1% relapsing-remitting ms (n = 8), 42.9% secondary progressive (n = 6), expanded disability status scale 4.1 ± 2.1] were administered the brief repeatable battery of neuropsychological tests (brb-n) and the stroop color and word test (stroop) at an average of 1.5 months from cladribine start. the brb-n measures information processing speed (symbol digit modalities test, paced auditory serial addition test [pasat]), verbal memory (selective reminding test [srt]), visual-spatial memory (10/36 spatial recall test), and verbal fluency (word list generation). stroop assesses processing speed and executive function. when available, alternate versions of the individual cognitive tests were used at follow-up to reduce practice effects. paired t-tests compared within-subject baseline and follow-up data.
results: after one year, no worsening was noted on any cognitive test. furthermore, both pasat 3-second total correct and srt total delayed recall trended toward improved scores on-study, with an average 3.4 (p = 0.07) and 1.1 (p = 0.05) point increase, respectively.
conclusion: in this preliminary study, no clear decline in cognitive performance was detectable over one year in patients newly started on cladribine tablets. brain and behavior

intrinsic activity reductions and cerebello-cortical diaschisis-like mechanism in friedreich ataxia: an falff resting-state fmri study. background: friedreich ataxia (fa) is characterized by progressive degeneration of the cerebellum and its output pathways, particularly the dentato-thalamo-cortical system, leading to motor impairment and the cerebellar cognitive affective syndrome (ccas). resting-state fmri studies in fa have focused on alterations of long-range functional connectivity, but little is known about how intrinsic regional neural activity is affected within cerebello-cortical networks.
methods: twenty-eight adults with genetically confirmed fa and 28 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent resting-state functional mri. intrinsic brain activity was quantified using the fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (falff). whole-brain comparisons were performed between controls and patients, and between patients with definite ccas (fa-cog) and cognitively preserved patients (fa-nocog). within the fa group, voxelwise regressions assessed associations between falff, motor severity (scale for the assessment and rating of ataxia [sara]), and cognitive performance (cerebellar cognitive affective syndrome scale [ccas-s]), adjusting for age, sex, head motion, and cerebellar gray matter volume.
results: compared with controls, patients exhibited reduced falff in medial and lateral prefrontal regions. higher sara scores were associated with lower falff in occipital, sensorimotor, posterior cingulate, and cerebellar regions, whereas higher ccas-s scores correlated with higher falff in bilateral prefrontal and cerebellar cognitive networks. compared with fa-nocog, fa-cog patients showed lower falff in bilateral frontal and insular regions.
conclusions: resting-state falff reveals downstream dysfunction of distributed cerebello-cortical networks in fa. associations with motor severity and cognition, together with additional fronto-insular dysfunction in patients with definite ccas, support progressive cerebello-cortical disconnection consistent with a diaschisis-like mechanism. brain and behavior

age-related changes in memory for gist and details: new perspectives on the representational quality of episodic memory. substantial heterogeneity in adult age-related declines in episodic memory within and across tasks and individuals has prompted extensive theoretical debate about the source of these variations. today, many theories assume that age-related changes in the representational fidelity of memory and the degree to which a test demands the retrieval of specific details of past experiences underlie much of this variability. this special issue ofpresents 19 contributions from researchers from around the world that together aim to enrich our understanding of the representational basis of age-related memory change. these contributions explore several interrelated themes related to measuring, predicting, and, at times, counteracting age-related declines in memory specificity while extending representational accounts to new tasks, more naturalistic contexts, and populations spanning the adult lifespan as well as individuals with neurocognitive impairment. the breadth of coverage spans multiple research domains with rich histories in the field of cognitive aging, including recognition memory, autobiographical memory, event memory, decision making, comprehension, and computational modeling. collectively, the diversity of questions posed by the articles and the varied methods they advance to addressing them highlight the value of integrating findings across different research traditions to develop a more unified framework for studying age-related changes in memory specificity. task-evoked pupillary responses reveal a role for attentional intensity in auditory discrimination. sensory discrimination has long been theorized to reflect a core cognitive function underlying intelligence. building on this tradition, we examined whether task-evoked pupil responses, as an index of mental effort, relate to attention control (ac) and auditory discrimination ability. using a large data set (n = 336), participants completed three adaptive auditory discrimination tasks (pitch, duration, loudness), a cognitive battery assessing ac, working memory capacity, and fluid intelligence, and pupillometry during task performance. structural equation modeling confirmed that ac predicted auditory discrimination thresholds and fully mediated the relationship between task-evoked pupil dilation and performance. trial-level multilevel models revealed that higher task difficulty and errors were associated with larger pupil dilations, especially in demanding tasks. crucially, individuals with greater ac exhibited steeper increases in pupil dilation with rising task difficulty and were more resilient to performance declines. for high-ac individuals, large pupil responses predicted preserved accuracy; for low-ac individuals, they signaled compensatory effort with diminished success. these results suggest that ac governs both the extent and efficacy of mental effort, determining whether high arousal facilitates or fails to improve performance. this work refines classic resource models by demonstrating that cognitive effort, indexed via pupillometry, supports perception most effectively when guided by strong ac. findings support a hierarchical model in which ac serves as the functional bridge between arousal, sensory discrimination, and higher order cognition.
