the mental health system caught my sister each time she fell but never saw her coming nature mental health, published online: 30 october 2026; doi:10.1038/s44220-026-00736-z in this world view, mental health researcher lucas murrins marques draws on his research and personal experience of suicide loss within his family to argue that mental health systems are designed to manage illness and crisis but often fail to detect the gradual erosion of wellbeing that precedes them. nature mental health

amplitude–frequency characteristic as a novel eye-tracking diagnostic feature: a pilot study on an open adhd dataset the frequency characteristic of biological systems is a sensitive tool for describing physiological dynamics, yet it has been virtually unused in pupillometry. a novel eye-tracking feature is proposed—the amplitude–frequency characteristic (afc) of the “stimulus–pupil size” system—and evaluated as a candidate diagnostic marker on an open adhd dataset. after quality control, 61 sessions (18 controls, 27 unmedicated adhd, 16 on-medication adhd) were analyzed. the afc of the raw diameter signal reveals a systematic elevation of afc amplitude in adhd across the 0.5–30 hz range, strongest in the 20–30 hz band (cohen’s d = +0.995, p = 0.0034). this is a pilot and methodology- and reproducibility-focused study. at the individual diagnostic level, a normative composite z-score of three bands (10–15, 15–20, 20–30 hz), computed relative to the control group with fixed weights and no training, reaches an roc-auc = 0.788 (ctrl vs. off-adhd: p = 0.0012). at the group level, a linear discriminant projection of the eight-band profile reaches an roc-auc = 0.854. the inter-individual variability of within-subject afc stability is reduced by a factor of 2.97 in unmedicated adhd (p = 0.0085) and normalizes under methylphenidate (paired wilcoxon p = 0.0067, n = 17). the widely used ratio of high- to low-frequency afc amplitude yields an inflated roc-auc of 0.865 on the pre-filtered signal, but only 0.63 on the raw signal. all diagnostic claims are exploratory. the proposed normative feature is simple, interpretable, requires no training set, and can be computed from a single pupil recording. journal of eye movement research

navigating a system not built for us: a qualitative investigation of mental health care access barriers for black youth and their families the sharp rise in suicide rates among black youth underscores the urgent need for equity-driven, culturally responsive approaches to improving mental health care access and engagement. despite increased availability of mental health resources, black families experience persistent disparities due to systemic and cultural barriers. this qualitative study examined the perspectives of black parents/guardians and community stakeholders in a large urban city in california regarding access to pediatric mental health care. semi-structured interviews and one focus group were conducted, and data were analyzed using grounded theory. five themes emerged as primary barriers: (1) delayed treatment and institutional indifference, (2) relational harm and therapeutic mistrust, (3) cultural misalignment and emotional labor, (4) racialized surveillance and stigma, and (5) institutional signals of exclusion. participants also identified community-informed recommendations, including community-based destigmatization, partnerships with trusted community institutions, workforce representation and black provider recruitment, and structural investment and resource equity. findings highlight the need for culturally grounded approaches to reduce disparities and inform policy, practice, and future research within the black community. journal of black psychology

cross-cultural comparison of fear, sadness and anger: british english versus polish abstract a major novel focus of our investigation was to employ three complementary methodological paradigms—grid, online emotions sorting and corpus linguistics—to investigate previous findings that sadness was rated higher than its polish equivalent, smutek , on the arousal and power dimensions (lewandowska-tomaszczyk & wilson, 2024) and that fear was rated higher than its polish equivalent, strach , on the power dimension (lewandowska-tomaszczyk, wilson & niiya, 2013). convergent evidence from all three methodologies supported hypothesis two, showing that smutek and strach are conceptualised as having greater conceptual proximity than their british english equivalents, sadness and fear . the salience of sadness in polish culture suggests that the relatively lower power of strach may reflect the low power associated with smutek . corpus findings also revealed a strong association between british english fear and anger , suggesting that the high power of anger may contribute to the salience of high power in fear . online emotions data showing stronger co-occurrences between sadness and british english anger -cluster concepts than between smutek and polish anger -cluster concepts support hypothesis three. however, hypothesis one was not supported: british english anger was not rated higher than polish złość ‘anger 1’ and gniew ‘anger 2’ on arousal and power . language and cognition

embodied resistance and epistemic sovereignty: rethinking knowledge production in disability studies abstract this article develops a theoretical framework to examine how knowledge about disability is produced, legitimised and challenged within contemporary power structures. it poses the following question: how does the bodily experience of exclusion generate alternative forms of knowledge that challenge dominant epistemic structures? drawing on critical disability studies, feminist theory and southern epistemologies, the article introduces the concepts of ‘embodied resistance’ and ‘epistemic sovereignty’ as interconnected analytical tools. it argues that neoliberal discourses on resilience function as mechanisms of normalisation that individualise structural inequalities and shift the responsibility for inclusion onto people with disabilities. in contrast, embodied resistance is conceptualised as a set of situated, often subtle, practices through which people with disabilities maintain their autonomy within disciplinary environments. epistemic sovereignty refers to the relational capacity to participate in shaping the concepts and interpretive criteria through which lived experience is understood and institutionally addressed. thinking from the wound names the process through which embodied experiences of exclusion can inform critical interpretation, without treating suffering as a guarantee of knowledge. the framework is articulated through four dimensions—guiding, tactical, methodological and political—and the chilean context is used as an analytical site to illustrate how inclusion can reproduce epistemic asymmetries despite formal advances in participation. in doing so, the article contributes to disability studies and broader social theory by repositioning embodied experience as a site of conceptual production and by clarifying the relationship between knowledge, agency and social behaviour. journal for the theory of social behaviour

shared pain, shared decisions: effects of empathic engagement on social conformity and decision processes, with physiological and visual-attentional associations. empathy enables individuals to attune to others' experiences through shared affective, sensorimotor, and neural representations. although central to emotional understanding, empathic engagement may extend beyond affective resonance to shape higher-level cognitive processes. in particular, empathic engagement may promote social alignment, biasing individuals to adjust their decisions toward others'. however, it remains unknown whether experimentally induced empathic-engagement instructions influence conformity in decision-making and whether conformity under this condition is associated with physiological responses, visual attention, and individual differences in socio-emotional traits. here, 73 participants completed an empathy-for-pain task and performed a modified random-dot task in which they interacted with empathy targets. physiological signals were recorded during the empathy manipulation, while eye movements were tracked throughout the task. using switching rate as a measure of conformity, we found that feedback from empathy targets increased conformity. computational drift-diffusion modeling showed that the empathic engagement condition was associated with stronger decision bias toward targets and altered drift rate. depending on the context, visual attention to the eyes and mouth was associated with greater conformity. larger increases in phasic skin conductance from the detached-observation to empathic engagement condition were associated with greater decision conservatism and reduced decision bias. finally, alexithymia and autistic traits moderated the relationship between empathy and conformity separately, but not jointly. these findings show that the effects of empathic engagement instructions may extend beyond affective resonance to influence subsequent decision-making. more broadly, they suggest that social alignment may be related to socio-emotional traits, with exploratory associations involving physiological arousal and visual attention. acta psychologica

parietal tdcs and tactospatial working memory: evidence for a behavioral benefit in a sham-controlled crossover study. the posterior parietal cortex (ppc) contributes to spatial working memory (wm), but whether parietal transcranial direct current stimulation (tdcs) can modulate tactospatial wm remains unclear. thirty-two adults completed a double-blind, sham-controlled, within-subject crossover study with two counterbalanced visits comprising baseline, intervention, and post-intervention phases of a retro-cued tactospatial delayed match-to-sample task. during the intervention phase, active tdcs (2ma, 15min) or sham tdcs (30-s ramp-up followed by ramp-down) was applied with a left-parietal anode and right-supraorbital cathode. a sliding-window analysis identified a temporally localized active-sham improvement during the later part of the task. this contrast was significant under the hypothesized directional test (p = 0.041), but not under two-sided testing across the primary temporal search interval (p = 0.083). a supplementary analysis using narrower common temporal bounds yielded a significant two-sided result. the corresponding condition difference was not significant when averaged across the complete intervention phase. baseline accuracy was negatively associated with the selected stimulation response (r = -0.327), consistent with the directional hypothesis, although this relationship and the covariate-adjusted analyses did not reach significance under two-sided testing. together, these findings point to a possible behavioral benefit of parietal tdcs in tactospatial wm, while indicating that its magnitude, temporal characteristics, and relationship with baseline performance require further confirmation. behavioural brain research

does it take two to benefit from self‐expansion? dyadic response surface analyses of self‐expansion and relationship satisfaction in daily life abstract relational self‐expansion—the process of broadening one's self through novel and exciting experiences with a romantic partner—is important for relationship maintenance. although theory and empirical research suggest that self‐expanding experiences enhance relationship satisfaction, it remains unclear whether partners need to experience similarly elevated levels of self‐expansion on a daily basis or similarly high levels of self‐expansion across time for these benefits to emerge. in four daily diary studies ( n = 512 couples), we assessed both partners' relational self‐expansion and relationship satisfaction across 21 consecutive days. dyadic response surface analyses revealed no evidence that matching in daily fluctuations of self‐expansion or matching in heightened self‐expansion across time predicted greater relationship satisfaction. instead, couples who reported higher self‐expansion reported higher satisfaction, and actor effects were consistently stronger than partner effects. novel to this investigation, daily relationship satisfaction was lower only when self‐expansion was low, with moderate and high levels yielding similarly high satisfaction. these findings suggest that the overall level of self‐expansion of each partner's experiences, rather than similarity between partners, plays an essential role in sustaining relationship satisfaction. personal relationships

preliminary findings on the role of the mental health and wellbeing practitioner within a psychological therapies for severe mental health problems (pt-smhp) service abstract it has long been recognised that there is a cohort of service users who typically fail to meet criteria for specialist secondary mental health services, yet their needs are considered too complex for talking therapies services. as a result, new psychological practitioner roles, including mental health and wellbeing practitioners (mhwp), were introduced to support implementation efforts, including for newly commissioned psychological therapies for severe mental health problems (pt-smhp) programmes. this study aimed to explore the impact of the newly commissioned mhwp role’s deliverance of low-intensity cbt-informed interventions on service user outcome measures across three time points during psychological intervention within a primary care-based pt-smhp service in the east of england. repeated measures-anovas found significant improvement in all outcome measures, and further post-hoc pairwise comparisons generally found significant improvements in measures across each of the three time points. these preliminary findings provide initial evidence that the role of mhwps are making a difference in community-based primary care services and positively impacting service user outcomes. further studies are needed to investigate efficacy of the role with a larger sample, including across other mental health settings such as secondary care to ensure external validity. key learning aims (1) to introduce the role of a mental health and wellbeing practitioner in a primary care-based psychological therapy service for severe mental health difficulties. (2) to examine preliminary outcomes of mental health and wellbeing practitioners in the treatment of individuals presenting with a personality disorder. (3) to consider what further research may be needed in relation to the mental health and wellbeing practitioner role. cognitive behaviour therapist

developing a psychological wellbeing intervention for psychological professional trainees: a collaborative and theory-informed intervention development process abstract there is recognition of the need to design wellbeing interventions in contextually sensitive ways, and report systematic, theory-driven approaches to intervention development. however, many intervention studies in the burgeoning literature on psychological professional trainee wellbeing do not include information on processes or theory surrounding the development of interventions tested. this theory- and stakeholder-informed intervention development study was guided by the mrc framework for developing and evaluating complex interventions and underpinned by the com-b. evidence and theory were used to support an initial intervention outline. meetings were subsequently held to gather stakeholder perspectives, to address unknowns of intervention design, and to support development of a theory of change. stakeholder (trainees and professional training staff) perspectives and relevant theory were used to inform the design of an acceptance and commitment therapy (act) based intervention, to address key stressors experienced by trainees. the intervention was delivered in a group setting, over the course of four sessions spaced 1–3 weeks apart. collaboratively constructed com-b analyses identified target behaviours and shaped intervention design. a comprehensive theory of change was developed, outlining key assumptions and setting out hypothesised pathways of change. an evidence-informed act-based intervention for psychological professional trainee wellbeing has been developed with key stakeholder collaboration. an acceptability and feasibility evaluation of this intervention is underway. key learning aims (1) to understand the processes through which a tailored wellbeing intervention for psychological professional trainees was developed in collaboration with key stakeholders. (2) to consider how an acceptance and commitment therapy (act) based intervention was adapted to address specific challenges encountered by psychological professional trainees. (3) to understand the pathways through which an adapted act intervention is anticipated to support trainee wellbeing. cognitive behaviour therapist

psychological wellbeing practitioners’ experiences and perspectives of complexity in talking therapies for anxiety and depression abstract psychological wellbeing practitioners (pwps) deliver high-volume, low-intensity psychological interventions for mild to moderate mental health problems within nhs talking therapies (formerly iapt). however, anecdotal reports suggest they are working with clients presenting with more complex needs, including moderate to severe mental health difficulties, severe and enduring mental health problems, high-risk levels, and facing co-occurring social or systemic challenges. this qualitative study examines the experiences and perspectives of pwps on working with complexity in clinical practice. an online questionnaire was completed by 104 pwps working within nhs talking therapies services. data analysis utilised qualitative content analysis. seven themes were identified, highlighting a range of factors contributing to complexity, including psychological, social, physical, and systemic issues. pwps also described the emotional toll of managing complex cases and emphasised the need for improved supervision, training, and leadership. the findings underscore a growing disconnect between the intended role of pwps and the realities of clinical practice. pwps are routinely expected to manage complexity, high level of risk, and co-occurring social problems. while some practitioners find ways to navigate these demands with adequate support, the overall picture points to significant strain on individuals and services alike. future research should refine the conceptualisation of complexity, evaluate the proposed decision-making tools, and explore the perspectives of pwps and clients to inform service development. key learning aims (1) gain insight into pwps’ experiences and perspectives on managing complexity in clinical settings. (2) examine the impact of working with complex or inappropriate presenting problems or multiple needs on pwps’ professional wellbeing and clinical efficacy. (3) contribute to the limited research on pwp and low-intensity psychological interventions by expanding understanding of its use, challenges, and the impact of complexity within ttad. cognitive behaviour therapist

‘i’m not sick. i’m burnt out’: a narrative inquiry into productivity and trauma among canadian women academics filling a gap in the literature on women's trauma and productivity, this research offers insightful knowledge about women's mental health and well-being. given that more than 50% of women have experienced trauma and women are twice as likely as men to develop posttraumatic stress disorder, there is an urgent need for ongoing systematic research on women's experiences with trauma. despite the prevalence of trauma, especially among women, very little research exists regarding how women academics cope with trauma. utilizing narrative inquiry and a feminist theoretical framework, this qualitative study provides insight into the nexus between productivity, women's mental health, and trauma within the context of academia. semi-structured interviews with a range of academic women ( n = 12) from ontario, canada, university campuses situate productivity as a gendered, empowered form of resistance and as an incredibly complex trauma response. analyses of the qualitative data contribute to theoretical discussions around the multidimensional and gendered nature of women's trauma, productivity, and mental health within academia. feminism & psychology
sensory profiles for young males and females with adhd and autistic characteristics child neuropsychology

an individually calibrated task to induce cognitive fatigue and assess fatigability in children: the tloaddchild. cognitive fatigue is predominantly investigated in adults but remains understudied in school-age children, despite being a frequent condition in their daily lives. in this proof-of-concept study, we present a new task designed to induce cognitive fatigue in children: the time-load dual task for children (tloaddchild). this dual-task combines a continuous performance task (cpt-x), and a binary choice task based on shape discrimination (round vs. pointed shapes). the task can be calibrated to allow individual adjustment of high (hcl) and low (lcl) cognitive load levels. the task also enables the investigation of underlying decision-making processes using the drift diffusion model. a total of 43 typically developing french-speaking children (7-12 years old) completed the tloaddchild under both hcl and lcl conditions. we showed that the tloaddchild successfully induces cognitive fatigue in children and that cognitive load, manipulated through the hcl and lcl conditions, modulates both attentional performance and underlying decision-making processes. these findings provide evidence supporting the use of the tloaddchild to investigate the effects of cognitive load manipulation (hcl vs. lcl) on performance, cognitive fatigue, and underlying decision-making processes in school-age children. child neuropsychology

subtypes of somatic symptom disorder: a secondary analysis of a multicenter cross-sectional study background: somatic symptom disorder (ssd) is common and has high heterogeneity. objective: this study aimed to identify subtypes of ssd based on a multicenter cross-sectional study in china. methods: we analyzed data from 235 patients diagnosed with ssd. exploratory graph analysis (ega) was used to identify dimensions of somatic symptoms. latent profile analysis (lpa) was then applied to classify patients into subtypes based on their symptom profiles across these dimensions. finally, bayesian network analysis was employed to explore the distinct patterns of relationships among psychological characteristics within each subtype. results: ega revealed a four-dimensional structure of somatic symptoms: gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, cardiopulmonary, and neurological/general. lpa classified patients into two distinct subtypes: a generalized somatic symptom subtype (gss-type), with symptoms spanning all four dimensions, and a localized somatic symptom subtype (lss-type), with symptoms not covering all dimensions. patients in the gss-type group reported significantly higher levels of anxiety (t = 5.482, p < 0.001), depressive symptoms (t = 6.576, p < 0.001), health-related anxiety (t = 6.266, p < 0.001), and disability (t = 4.282, p < 0.001), alongside poorer physical (t = −4.766, p < 0.001) and mental quality of life (t = −3.646, p < 0.001) compared to the lss-type. bayesian network analysis indicated that in the lss-type, somatic symptoms and their psychological characteristics were the potential origin of depressive symptoms and anxiety, whereas in the gss-type, depressive symptoms were the potential central driver influencing both anxiety and somatic symptoms. conclusion: ssd patients can be categorized into clinically distinct subtypes based on their somatic symptom distribution. the differing psychopathological mechanisms between the gss and lss subtypes suggest the need for tailored treatment strategies. these findings warrant further validation in larger, prospective studies. health psychology research

the association between changes in health behaviors and depressive symptoms among chinese older adults: a national cross-sectional study background: depressive symptoms are common in older adults. however, few studies have assessed changes in health behaviors during the pandemic and gender differences among chinese older adults. objective: to examine the association of changes in health behaviors with depressive symptoms among chinese older adults during the pandemic, and gender differences. methods: the data were obtained from the 2020 china health and retirement longitudinal study, which included 7,947 older adults. binary logistic regression examined associations between changes in health behaviors and depressive symptoms, and subgroup analyses assessed gender differences in effects of physical activity, smoking, and alcohol consumption changes on depressive symptoms. results: the prevalence of depressive symptoms among older adults in china was 39.37% during the covid-19 pandemic in 2020. female (odds ratio [or] = 1.790, 95% ci: 1.578–2.031), unmarried (or = 1.438, 95% ci: 1.266–1.634), rural residency (or = 1.479, 95% ci: 1.321–1.657), and two or more chronic diseases (or = 1.472, 95% ci: 1.253–1.729) were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. decreased intense activities (or=1.301, 95% ci: 1.133–1.493) and decreased smoking (or = 1.500, 95% ci: 1.183–1.903) were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. subgroup analyses revealed a significant interaction between gender and changes in alcohol consumption on depressive symptoms. conclusion: the study found that decreased intense activities and decreased smoking were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. health administrators should develop policies based on the relationship between changes in health behaviors and depressive symptoms among older adults of different genders. health psychology research
issue information infant and child development

young children's help‐seeking expectations in teacher–child interactions: the effects of teachers' familiarity and response valence abstract effective help‐seeking is essential for young children's adaptation in early childhood education settings, yet little is known about how they selectively seek help based on different social cues. this study examined how young children integrate teachers' familiarity and response valence when predicting a protagonist's help‐seeking behaviour. across two studies, 90 han chinese children aged 4–7 years (45 boys) completed a third‐party task simulating teacher–child interactions. in study 1, familiarity was manipulated using photographs of each child's real teachers, whereas study 2 employed standardized cartoon figures and verbal cues to indicate familiarity. the results showed that children tended to expect that the protagonist would seek help from familiar teachers, especially those who responded positively. meanwhile, they hesitated to expect that the protagonist would seek help from unfamiliar teachers, regardless of their response valence. this pattern indicates that familiarity consistently exerted a stronger influence than response valence, as children consistently prioritized familiarity when anticipating support. together, these findings highlight how young children flexibly integrate multiple social cues when forming help‐seeking expectations and offer practical implications for fostering secure, responsive teacher–child relationships in early education. infant and child development

associations among peer bullying, self-esteem, and self-care agency in high school students in istanbul abstract this descriptive, cross-sectional study examined associations among peer bullying, self-esteem, and self-care agency in high school students in istanbul, türkiye. data were collected at a public high school in istanbul between march 1 and may 31, 2025. the study population consisted of 2,140 students, and the sample included 350 students selected using a stratified sampling method. data were collected using a personal information form, the peer bullying identification scale (pbis), the self-care agency scale (scas), and the rosenberg self-esteem scale (rses). strong negative correlations were identified between self-esteem and bullying victimization, particularly for total pbis–victim scores ( r = − 0.792, p < 0.01). mediation analysis indicated that self-esteem partially mediated the relationship between bullying victimization and self-care agency. higher bullying victimization scores were associated with lower self-esteem and self-care agency, whereas higher self-esteem was associated with greater self-care agency. these findings support the potential value of school-based mental health and nursing interventions that promote self-esteem, adaptive coping, and self-care agency among adolescents exposed to bullying. discover psychology

ai facilitation and affective dynamics of online deliberation abstract artificial intelligence systems are increasingly used to facilitate online group discussion, yet their influence on the affective conditions of collective interaction remains poorly understood. existing research has largely focused on participation, efficiency, or content quality, leaving the emotional dynamics of ai-mediated deliberation underexamined. this paper investigates how ai facilitation relates to the expressed sentiment in online group discussion, understood as one measurable dimension of its affective dynamics. drawing on two empirical studies conducted in different discussion settings in afghanistan, one involving a rule-based facilitator and the other a large language model-based facilitator, we analyze differences in expressed sentiment between ai-facilitated and non-ai discussions. across both datasets, participant sentiment was modestly higher under ai facilitation, although the mixed-effects analyses did not establish statistically significant condition differences. in addition, ai-generated facilitation messages exhibited higher sentiment than participant-authored messages, with a statistically reliable overall gap in both studies and a consistent direction across all five city-specific boards in the first study and all four ai-facilitated groups in the second, suggesting that ai facilitators introduced more positive affective signals into the discussion environment. rather than treating increased positivity as an unqualified improvement, we interpret these findings as suggesting that ai systems may act as affective mediators, potentially influencing the emotional norms and tone of collective interaction. this raises normative questions about emotional regulation, power, and democratic deliberation, particularly regarding whether affective smoothing may constrain disagreement or reconfigure deliberative agency. by foregrounding affect as a dimension of ai-mediated discussion, this study contributes empirical evidence to debates on the societal implications of ai facilitation and highlights the need for greater attention to the affective norms and expressive patterns introduced by ai facilitation. discover psychology

cross-cultural validation of the morality-as-cooperation questionnaire in brazil morality-as-cooperation provides a framework for understanding how moral behaviors and values are rooted in cooperative social interactions – a fundamental aspect of human evolution. to advance our understanding of moral psychology, particularly to test whether mac is a universally valid construct, it is important to examine it across different countries and cultures. the present investigation is among the first to extend this theory to brazil. in study 1 (n = 223), we translated, adapted, and validated the morality-as-cooperation questionnaire for brazilian portuguese, assessing its structural validity, reliability, convergent validity, and measurement invariance with the original u.s. sample. relevance showed good reliability and model fit, with strongest invariance support at the configural and metric levels under subscale-specific models; judgment showed acceptable reliability but weaker and less stable properties. additionally, an important and novel finding was that both subscales correlated moderately with dispositional gratitude, providing evidence of convergent validity while also suggesting a shared cooperative foundation linking moral evaluation and gratitude. in study 2 (n = 590), we examined discriminant and concurrent validity using a brazilian general population sample. relevance again showed good reliability and strongest invariance support at the configural and metric levels across brazilian and u.s. samples; judgment showed acceptable reliability but persistent psychometric instability. scalar and strict invariance received mixed or insufficient support. together, these findings suggest that morality-as-cooperation offers a useful framework for studying morality in brazil and beyond, although refinement of the judgment subscale is needed to ensure robust cross-cultural applications. collabra-psychology
beyond the universal and the culturally determined human: reframing the biosocial problem under neo-structuration integrative psychological and behavioral science

a scoping review of the literature on prompt‐dependent behavior in learners diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder abstract although prompt‐dependent behavior is mentioned in the literature, only a few studies have evaluated assessments or interventions for this behavior. the current study consists of a scoping review of the literature on prompt‐dependent behavior. this review aimed to identify variables responsible for the acquisition of, the types of assessments to identify, and the types of interventions employed to decrease prompt‐dependent behavior in learners with autism spectrum disorder (asd). we identified 29 articles for this review, 12 of which were empirical studies that assessed and/or employed an intervention for prompt‐dependent behavior of individuals diagnosed with asd. results indicated that although various theories exist that hypothesize how prompt‐dependent behavior is acquired, empirical support is lacking. most studies conducted indirect assessments (e.g., caregiver nomination) to identify individuals with prompt‐dependent behavior, and outcomes indicated that contingency mapping, shaping combined with prompting, and differential reinforcement were effective at decreasing prompt‐dependent behavior for certain individuals. we conclude with a summary of the limitations of the current literature on prompt‐dependent behavior, recommendations for future research, and clinical implications. behavioral interventions

a case study of early-emerging prosopometamorphopsia. prosopometamorphopsia (pmo) is a rare perceptual disorder characterized by facial distortions. this report presents the first thorough study of early-emerging pmo. zed, who was 15 years old when first tested, has experienced lifelong, dynamic facial distortions in which features move, droop, disappear, expand, and rotate. he also experiences identity misrecognitions, perceiving familiar faces as strangers and vice versa. behavioural assessments indicate zed's distortions persist across different viewpoints, visual field positions, picture-plane orientations, and visual angles. neuropsychological testing revealed deficits in face identity recognition, yet zed performed normally on tests requiring fine-grained perception of facial age and sex. while structural mri showed no lesions, mri revealed reduced face-selectivity in right posterior face-selective areas, and diffusion tensor imaging indicated lower white matter integrity in the left inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus. this case offers novel insights into the manifestations of early-emerging pmo, its co-occurrence with other face-processing disorders, and its underlying neural correlates. cognitive neuropsychology

learning to code dyadic parent–child interaction: an exploratory study abstract objective diagnostic assessment through the dyadic parent–child interaction coding system (dpics) is inextricably linked to parent–child interaction therapy (pcit), an evidence‐based parent management programme. however, there is a paucity of research on factors that may promote or hinder dpics learning, including workshop format characteristics, trainee variables, and the quantity and complexity of verbalisations captured through dpics coding. this study aims to bridge this gap. methods to do this, this study used an exploratory, quasi‐experimental design to identify workshop and trainee characteristics that influence effective learning of dpics coding. data for this study were collected across 14 cohorts of 40‐h pcit basic training workshops including 82 participants. results the findings of this study suggest that the basic pcit workshop format (one‐stage vs. two‐stage workshop), primary psychotherapeutic orientation, pre‐workshop dpics coding experience, preparation time for dpics coding before the workshop, attitude towards dpics coding importance, dpics coding confidence or time spent on dpics homework during the workshop do not exert a significant influence on dpics coding competency as assessed by the dpics inter‐coder agreement (ica). in contrast, fewer years of pre‐workshop clinical practice and native speaker status were statistically significantly associated with higher ica. conclusion implementing a systematic plan for dpics training throughout the pcit training process seems to be highly advisable, particularly for non‐native‐speaker trainees and trainees with extensive pre‐workshop clinical experience. to further elucidate the factors influencing pcit training outcomes, multi‐centre studies with more participants are needed. counselling & psychotherapy research

the seen anxiety: psychotherapists' classification of text‐described observable anxiety markers across three‐ and five‐level rating formats abstract introduction anxiety is central to the psychotherapy process, yet psychotherapists routinely infer a client's anxiety intensity from observable behaviour rather than from formal measurement, with no widely accepted framework to organise which observable markers indicate which levels of anxiety. this exploratory study examined how therapists make such classifications. method ninety‐one mental health professionals were randomly assigned to classify 41 text‐described behavioural and physiological markers using either a 5‐level or a simplified 3‐level category system, both derived from an integrated model of state anxiety in psychotherapy. results response distributions departed significantly from uniformity for nearly all markers in both formats, and the rank ordering of markers by intensity was highly consistent across formats, suggesting that therapists may share broad intuitions about relative marker intensity. which markers elicited agreement, however, was far less reproducible, depending substantially on the response format. convergence also depended on where the agreement criterion was set, declining from 90.2% to 51.2% of markers in the 3‐level format and from 63.4% to 22.0% in the 5‐level format as the criterion rose from > 0.50 to > 0.70. the 3‐level format yielded more classifiable markers at every criterion, although this advantage was not consistent across indices, whereas the 5‐level format elicited fewer ‘insufficient to determine’ responses. markers placed at the highest intensity levels were classified most consistently. discussion these findings offer preliminary groundwork for research on marker operationalisation, contextualised rating tasks and the development of training materials for psychotherapy process research. counselling & psychotherapy research

exploring counselling students' actual and intended usage of artificial intelligence through interpretative phenomenological analysis abstract objective the integration of artificial intelligence (ai) into counselling and counsellor education is expanding rapidly, yet little is known about how counselling students engage with these tools. this qualitative study explored counselling students' actual and intended uses of ai across multiple professional and academic roles. method two master's and seven doctoral students from us counselling programs participated in two in‐depth semi‐structured interviews, which were analysed using interpretative phenomenological analysis to examine their lived experiences and meaning making with ai. results four main themes emerged: ai usage as students, counsellors, supervisors and course instructors. participants described actual uses for language enhancement, statistical learning, brainstorming and clinical documentation, while envisioning future applications in multicultural training, supervision feedback and ai‐simulated counselling role‐plays. conclusion findings reflected both enthusiasm for ai's creative and practical benefits and concerns about ethical use of ai in counselling and counsellor education. counselling & psychotherapy research

culturally responsive group counselling in indonesian secondary schools: challenges and professional support needs this study explored school counsellors’ experiences, implementation challenges, and professional support needs related to culturally responsive group counselling in secondary schools in north sumatra, indonesia. data were collected through open-ended questionnaires completed by 389 school counsellors and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. three themes emerged: the underuse of group counselling for preventive and developmental purposes; challenges in facilitating intercultural interaction and managing multicultural group dynamics; and the need for contextually relevant counselling models and practical guidance. the findings indicate that culturally responsive practice requires both professional development for school counsellors and organisational support. practitioners need clear, accessible guidance, while schools and professional organisations can facilitate implementation through appropriate resources and opportunities for planning. this study provides practice-oriented evidence on counsellors’ experiences and support needs in north sumatra. the findings may inform practice in other settings, although their transferability depends on local cultural, educational, and organisational conditions. journal of psychologists and counsellors in schools

international journal of evidence based coaching and mentoring: a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis 2013–2022 since 2003, the ijebcm has bridged scholarly inquiry and professional practice in coaching and mentoring. while hodge documented the journal's first decade, its second decade remained unexamined. this study addresses the gap by integrating a systematic literature review (slr) with three bibliometric techniques (citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, co-word analysis) applied to 274 articles published between 2013 and 2022. the findings reveal intellectual maturation: publication output stabilised while citation influence accelerated after the journal's inclusion in scopus and web of science. intellectual influence was distributed across conceptual, methodological, and practice-oriented contributions drawing on interdisciplinary foundations. the corpus resolved into five interconnected thematic clusters, and conceptual analysis confirmed that coaching and mentoring function as distinct yet integrated scholarly communities. the study terms this relationship differentiated integration, where each practice retains a scholarly identity while drawing on, and contributing to, a common evidence base. the study concludes by mapping emerging and neglected research frontiers. international journal of evidence based coaching & mentoring

vygotsky's legacy in brazilian inclusive education: (trans)formation and singularity context and relevance. the study investigates the contributions of lev vygotsky's cultural-historical theory to brazilian special/inclusive education, particularly regarding the constitution of the subject with autism in school contexts. the theoretical framework is grounded in the concepts of drama, freedom and singularity, understanding the schooling process as a privileged pathway of human (trans)formation. objective. to analyse how pedagogical knowledge impacts the constitution of the child with autism, based on the notion of constitutive singularity. hypothesis. the schooling process anchored in critical-emancipatory pedagogical knowledge operates as a promoter of the subject's humanisation, in opposition to traditional clinical approaches that reduce the subject to diagnosis and to ableist perspectives that position them in a state of devaluation. methods and materials. the research, adopting a cultural-historical approach, was configured as intervention-research with an eight-year-old student with autism, enrolled in the second year of primary education. video recordings, audio recordings, photographs, field diaries and interviews with the teacher, the child and his mother were utilised. data were analysed through the microgenetic approach. results. the analysis of two paradigmatic episodes of story retelling through illustration and physical education class evidences that the child, upon inserting personal elements into school tasks, manifests his will and singularises himself, expressing the drama of the social personality as a struggle for existence. conclusions. understanding singularity as a dialectical, historical, cultural and dramatic process allows us to overcome pathologising views and to recognise that disability is not a destiny, but a condition that, in relations with others and with culture, can be transformed into potentiality. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

forgiveness toward parents and internalizing symptoms: divergent patterns across gender and maltreatment backgrounds / perdón hacia los padres y síntomas internalizantes: patrones divergentes en función de sexo e historial de maltrato emerging adulthood is marked by heightened vulnerability to internalizing symptoms. however, whether forgiveness moderates the associations between parenting and internalizing symptoms remains unclear, particularly across parent–child gender dyads and perceived parental maltreatment histories. data were drawn from a cohort of 834 emerging adults who completed an online survey assessing parenting, forgiveness toward parents, internalizing symptoms, and perceived parental maltreatment history. participants also described hurtful experiences involving their mothers and fathers in separate open-ended questions. approximately 70% of participants described at least one hurtful experience involving a parent, while 26.4% self-reported a perceived parental maltreatment history. among those with perceived parental maltreatment histories, forgiveness moderated associations involving parental warmth in mother–daughter dyads and overparenting in father–son dyads. among those without perceived parental maltreatment histories, significant moderation effects were found for overparenting in mother–daughter dyads and for both parental warmth and overparenting in father–daughter dyads. these findings highlight the diversity of hurtful experiences involving parents and suggest that the role of forgiveness varies across parent–child gender dyads and perceived parental maltreatment histories. studies in psychology

secure base leadership, role stress and intention to change assignment in a sample of spanish military personnel / liderazgo de base segura, estrés de rol e intención de cambio de destino en una muestra de militares españoles secure base leadership (sbl) is a novel theoretical perspective grounded in bowlby’s attachment theory that emphasises leaders’ impact on their subordinates’ well-being and performance. given its potential relevance in military settings, this study analyses the relationship between the perceived leadership style of superiors and role stress (ambiguity and conflict) and turnover intention (change of assignment) among 136 spanish military personnel (53.7% men; m = 41.9 years). the study considered affective organisational commitment as a mediator. using structural equation modelling (pls-sem), the results revealed the crucial role of affective commitment, which fully mediates the relationship between sbl and role ambiguity and turnover intention, and partially mediates the relationship between sbl and role conflict. turnover intention was also positively related to role conflict. this study shows that sbl, operating through organisational commitment, is an effective model that helps to prevent role stress and turnover intention among military personnel. studies in psychology

the proliferation of ai among college students: a replication and 2-year follow-up background the proliferation of artificial intelligence (ai) has impacted most aspects of life and sparked debate over its responsible use. objective as higher education grapples with how to leverage ai's benefits while accounting for its potential detriments, it is necessary to examine how undergraduates use and perceive ai. method a replication, following the same methodology as golding et al., examined how college students’ use and perceptions of ai differ from those of a comparable cohort 2 years ago. students were from the same five universities and were predominantly women, white, hispanic, or black. results familiarity and prevalence of ai use were higher, and perceptions of cheating were lower. open-ended data on motivations for (not) using ai and perceptions of (not) cheating suggested that students conceptualize ai through a nuanced lens. conclusions the use of ai has grown substantially. many students view ai as an instructional aid to guide their learning and emphasize the importance of how ai is used when determining whether it qualifies as cheating. teaching implications students’ largely positive perceptions of ai suggest that ai's use is not slowing. educators face the challenge of how best to leverage ai to enhance learning while not facilitating cheating or overreliance. teaching of psychology

a quasi-mixed methods investigation of adolescents’ coping with social status insecurity and its mediation role in relation to health problems the present study employed a quasi-mixed methods approach to explore adolescents’ coping strategies for social status insecurity and further examined the mediation roles of positive and negative coping in the relationships between social status insecurity and physical health outcomes, specifically subjective health complaints and sleep problems. participants were 134 (71 girls) sixth to eighth graders from a suburban public middle school in the midwestern united states. they completed measures assessing social status insecurity, coping strategies, and health outcomes. in addition, they answered an open-ended question describing their coping approaches to managing social status insecurity for quantitative analysis. the results indicated that social status insecurity was correlated with greater health complaints and sleep problems. the mediation results showed that after accounting for gender and self-rated status, these significant associations were mediated through negative coping only. the qualitative findings complemented the quantitative findings with a more detailed picture of adolescents’ use of coping strategies in response to social status insecurity. in summary, social status insecurity was linked to increased health problems through greater use of negative coping strategies. these findings highlight the importance of explicitly addressing negative coping behaviors in interventions aimed at helping adolescents manage insecure feelings related to their peer social status. adolescents

instagram-based education for gender-based violence prevention among indonesian adolescents: a quasi-experimental study of knowledge, attitude, and self-empowerment outcomes background/objectives: gender-based violence (gbv) is a major adolescent health problem in indonesia, yet instagram-based gbv prevention and its effect on self-empowerment remain understudied. this study examined an instagram education programme for knowledge, attitude, and self-empowerment regarding gbv prevention. methods: a quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control-group study with pre-test/post-test measurement included 236 high school students (118 intervention, 118 control) in ciputat sub-district; intact classes within each school were allocated to the arms without randomisation. the intervention group received 8–10 instagram posts over two weeks; controls received no structured content. pilot-tested questionnaires (cronbach’s α 0.75–0.95) were analysed using wilcoxon signed-rank and mann–whitney u tests. results: both groups improved significantly in knowledge, attitude, and self-empowerment (all p < 0.001). control-group scores were significantly higher than intervention-group scores at both time points (p ≤ 0.026); this gap was present at baseline and reflects pre-existing differences between the non-randomised groups, not an intervention effect. conclusions: the programme was followed by significant within-group gains, supporting its feasibility as a potential educational adjunct. however, the control group also improved, and the groups were non-equivalent at baseline, so the findings do not show superiority over usual school conditions or an effect attributable to the programme. future trials should use school-level randomisation, an active control condition, and covariate adjustment. adolescents

when faces shape places: person trustworthiness influences contextual threat social perception rarely occurs in isolation: people and places mutually shape one another's meaning. prior research has shown that threatening contexts can bias impressions of facial trustworthiness, suggesting that evaluative meaning flows from the environment to the person. here, we consider the reverse causal direction, testing whether individuals' trustworthiness can alter evaluations of environmental threat. across three preregistered experiments (total n = 367), participants judged the threat level of ambiguous visual contexts that included individuals varying on perceived trustworthiness. experiment 1 showed that untrustworthy faces increased perceived contextual threat relative to neutral or absent faces, an effect that correlated with attributing danger to the target individual. experiment 2 revealed that this effect was contingent on perceiver perspective: untrustworthy faces heightened threat only when participants evaluated the context from their own viewpoint, not when adopting the target's perspective. experiment 3 showed that this face-to-context influence emerged when faces varied in trustworthiness but not competence, indicating that it does not reflect a general negativity bias. together, these findings establish face-context integration as a process in which social meaning propagates dynamically between person and environment, revealing a fundamental mechanism of relational meaning construction in social cognition. cognition & emotion

pain, but not hypermobility, is associated with borderline personality disorder symptoms among individuals diagnosed with eds or g-hsd. research examining borderline personality disorder (bpd) in individuals with ehlers-danlos syndromes (eds) and generalized hypermobility spectrum disorder (g-hsd) is limited, despite overlap between core bpd features (e.g., emotion dysregulation) and common eds/g-hsd conditions (e.g., chronic pain). this study examined associations between bpd symptoms and eds/g-hsd features. data were from a retrospective chart review of patients evaluated at the goodhope eds clinic between 2019-2021. patients diagnosed with eds or g-hsd (n=205) completed self-report measures of bpd symptoms and eds/g-hsd features (i.e., pain severity/interference, autonomic symptom burden). clinicians assessed joint hypermobility. an anova examined group differences between individuals scoring above the recommended bsl-23 threshold (i.e., ≥ 1.5) and below the cut-off. a linear regression examined associations between eds/g-hsd features and bpd symptom severity. forty-five participants (22%) scored above the recommended bsl-23 threshold, indicating elevated bpd symptoms. these individuals reported greater pain severity, pain interference, and autonomic symptom burden compared to those below the cut-off score. in a linear regression, pain interference was the only eds/g-hsd feature associated with bpd symptom severity; pain severity, joint hypermobility, and autonomic symptom burden were not significant. greater pain interference was associated with more severe bpd symptoms among individuals with eds/g-hsd. further research is needed to clarify these relationships, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and improve interventions for this population. journal of clinical psychology in medical settings

linkshänder, gaucher or lefty: does left-handedness identity need to be considered when expanding handedness classifications? understanding the meanings of handedness is important when defining and labelling different handednesses. although the majority group of right-handers may not consider their handedness often, this is not the case for left-handers. human environments are constructed to facilitate ease for the majority, reinforcing privilege and making handedness somewhat "under the radar" for right-handers, whilst left-handers, as a minority group, have a long history of being oppressed and discriminated against. social psychology, particularly social identity theory, tells us that categories are powerful psychological constructs. humans are intrinsically drawn towards identifying with groups and becoming members, with resultant influences of membership on individuals. group identity plays an important part in people's lives and can have a psychological impact or influence. due to structural barriers and cultural influences, how we investigate differences between individuals from separate groups can be important depending on how they view the saliency of that membership. empirical evidence shows that left-handers regard their handedness as more meaningful, central and important than right-handers. we suggest that researchers consider the influence of (handedness) categorization on individuals and that the overt nature of handedness makes an everyday binary split of right and left a powerful entity and especially meaningful to left-handers. laterality

momentary emotion regulation and executive function in daily life emotion regulation (er) strategies are theorised to impose differing cognitive demands. however, little is known about the momentary association between er strategy use and executive function (ef) in daily life. to address this issue, 224 young adults (= 22.59, = 3.52 years) completed an experience-sampling protocol (4x/day for 7 days), reporting use of engagement (positive reappraisal, acceptance) and disengagement (detached reappraisal, distraction) er strategies, as well as positive and negative pre-regulation emotional intensity for the focal event. at each sampling occasion, participants also completed ef tasks assessing the core components of inhibition, updating, and shifting. we tested whether er strategy use would be negatively (depletion account) or positively (facilitation account) linked to fluctuations in ef performance. consistent with the facilitation account, findings indicated that, at the within-person level, use of engagement er strategies was associated with better ef performance. conversely, the within-person use of disengagement er strategies was not linked to ef. however, on occasions when participants reported high (but not low) pre-regulation positive emotional intensity, greater use of disengagement strategies was associated with better ef performance. these findings suggest that momentary shifts in both er strategy use and emotional intensity jointly relate to ef in daily life. cognition & emotion

differentiating negative emotions in ourselves and others: associations with internalising symptoms and social functioning negative emotion differentiation (ned), or the ability to precisely describe negative emotional states, is linked to positive individual and interpersonal outcomes. although ned has typically been defined as understanding one'semotional states (personal ned), precisely describing howare feeling may likewise facilitate social functioning and mental health. however, no validated lab measures exist to assess how precisely one labelsdiscrete negative emotions (personal ned). across four online studies, participants completed a novel task rating another person's emotions in videos. interpersonal ned was computed using intraclass correlation coefficients (consistent with intrapersonal ned conventions). participants completed self-report questionnaires assessing mental health and social functioning and, in studies 1 and 2, completed an intrapersonal ned task. intrapersonal and interpersonal ned were consistently correlated with each other. contrary to hypotheses, associations between interpersonal ned and either mental health or interpersonal outcomes were weak and inconsistent across studies, except for perceived social support, which demonstrated a positive aggregated association with interpersonal ned meta-analyzed across studies. unexpectedly, intrapersonal ned was also unassociated with outcomes of interest across studies. although results were not as anticipated, our rigorous, pre-registered measurement approach lays the groundwork for future research to develop methods for assessing interpersonal ned. cognition & emotion

investigating the relationship between personality priorities and depression, anxiety, and stress in turkish college students: the mediating roles of coping styles this study investigated how adlerian personality priorities are associated with depression, anxiety, and stress through coping styles among turkish college students. data were collected from 482 participants and analyzed using path analysis with bootstrapping. results from the post hoc, exploratory reduced model indicated that personality priorities were directly and indirectly associated with mental health outcomes. notably, helpless coping was a central statistical mediator in the associations of higher pleasing and comfort, and lower control, with greater psychological distress. in contrast, seeking social support was associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, and stress. these findings underscore the importance of coping processes in understanding the associations between personality dynamics and mental health. by providing evidence from a non-western context, this study extends research on adlerian personality priorities to turkish college students. practical implications for counseling interventions targeting maladaptive coping strategies are discussed. psychological reports

factors associated with treatment dropout among individuals with gambling disorder: a retrospective cohort study. background and aims: gambling disorder (gd) is a behavioral addiction frequently comorbid with mental health and substance use disorders. its substantial individual and societal burden, explained by the impact of gd on multiple domains that include health, relationships, work or education, is compounded by high treatment dropout rates. evidence on predictors of gd treatment dropout largely derives from controlled research settings, limiting generalizability to real-world contexts. this study is novel in evaluating service use and quality-of-care predictors of gd treatment dropout, alongside sociodemographic, clinical, and gambling-related factors, within a large public healthcare system.
methods: patients were eligible if they were diagnosed with gd between april 1, 2009, and march 31, 2021, and received at least one gd treatment episode in an addiction treatment center (atc) in quebec, canada, during this period. the index date was the end date of the last treatment episode. atc data were linked to provincial administrative health databases. multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aor) for treatment dropout.
results: among 1,719 patients, the dropout rate during the index treatment episode was 46%. prior treatment dropout (aor=5.65), bipolar disorder (aor=1.57), and residence in semi-urban or rural areas (aor=1.33) were associated with higher odds of dropout. factors associated with lower odds of dropout included history of homelessness or social issues (aor=0.66), more than two gd treatment episodes (aor=0.68), treatment duration longer than six months (aor=0.45), and high intensity (aor=0.62) or regularity (aor=0.70) of outpatient care.
discussion and conclusions: enhancing access for individuals in non-urban areas through internet-delivered interventions, and providing intensive, regular outpatient care that fosters treatment motivation and a strong therapeutic alliance, may reduce dropout and improve outcomes. journal of gambling studies

reading skills and reading anxiety symptoms in youth. many children who experience reading challenges develop co-occurring mental health difficulties, such as reading anxiety. the current study tested the relationships between specific reading skills (decoding, fluency, and comprehension) and reading anxiety symptoms. participants were 230 twins between 8 and 13 years old. multi-level linear regression models were used to account for family relationships and covaried for age and sex. age was positively associated and sex was not associated with reading anxiety. lower decoding (β = -0.19, p < .001), reading fluency (β = -0.22, p < .001), and reading comprehension skills (β = -0.22, p < .001) were significantly associated with higher reading anxiety symptoms. when testing whether each reading skill contributed to reading anxiety after controlling for others, reading comprehension (β = -0.15, p = .010) remained significantly associated with reading anxiety symptoms, whereas decoding (β = 0.01, p = .90) and reading fluency (β = -0.13, p = .08) were no longer significant. model comparisons followed a similar pattern indicating that reading comprehension (and to a lesser extent fluency) accounted for significant variance in reading anxiety over and above other reading skills, while decoding did not. secondary analyses covarying for clinical anxiety and adhd symptoms showed that the association between reading skills and reading anxiety could not be accounted for by these co-occurring symptoms. this study is among the first to examine relationships between specific reading skills and reading anxiety symptoms and highlights the need for improved identification and treatment of reading anxiety symptoms in struggling readers. research on child and adolescent psychopathology

supporting children of parents with mood disorders, anxiety or substance use problems: a systematic review and meta-analysis of psychosocial interventions abstract psychosocial interventions for children of parents with mood disorders, anxiety and/or alcohol and substance use problems may reduce their vulnerability to negative developmental outcomes and strengthen their resilience. however, existing studies vary in quality, making it difficult to identify best practices. to address this gap, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled studies evaluating psychosocial interventions for children (aged 0–18) of parents with mood disorders/anxiety and/or alcohol/substance use problems. a total of 34 studies, involving 3205 children (51.7% female), identified through pubmed, psycinfo, and scopus, met the inclusion criteria. results showed that these interventions are effective in reducing internalizing symptoms both in the short ( g = − 0.25) and long term ( g = − 0.21), and in decreasing externalizing symptoms in the short term ( g = − 0.16). however, there was insufficient evidence for significant effects on theoretical mechanisms such as family related factors or children’s coping skills. furthermore, program effectiveness did not differ based on the type of intervention or its underlying theoretical framework. these findings support the general efficacy of psychosocial interventions in improving mental health outcomes in at-risk children, regardless of program type or approach. clinical child and family psychology review

from little kids, big kids grow: the development of emotion regulation abilities from childhood to adolescence abstract less effective emotion regulation abilities during childhood represent a significant factor of risk for healthy child development. however, despite much research into less skilled emotion regulation abilities, findings about the outcomes of emotion regulation ability trajectories in adolescence are inconsistent. this may reflect methodological challenges in undertaking prospective longitudinal research, or a lack of clarity about factors that influence developmental outcomes. therefore, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the prospective relation between early childhood (ages 3–6) emotion regulation abilities and adolescent outcomes (ages 13–16). peer reviewed prospective longitudinal research studies published in english since 2015 were included in the review if they examined emotion regulation abilities in early childhood; assessed subsequent outcomes in adolescence; and examined risk, protective, or promotive factors associated with emotion trajectories. statistical analyses utilized random effects models and reported pooled effect sizes within groups. of 27,490 records identified, 16 studies were included in the systematic review, and 10 in the meta-analysis. early emotion regulation abilities that were less adaptive predicted subsequent less adaptive regulation, psychiatric difficulties, academic concerns, and social challenges in adolescence. risk and promotive factors for early childhood emotion regulation abilities included pregnancy-related factors, parental mental health, socioeconomic status, child characteristics, cognitive and behavioral traits, and family dynamics. this highlighted the complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors. there was conflicting evidence about sex, suicidality, and externalizing behaviors, and quantitative analyses revealed high heterogeneity among the studies. the findings offer insights about the identification of youth at risk, and the development of targeted clinical interventions to enhance adolescent developmental outcomes. clinical child and family psychology review

does trauma-focused psychotherapy alter pre-existing memories? a survey of german psychotherapists little is known about how pre-existing trauma memories change under trauma-focused therapy. we surveyed 224 german therapists trained in trauma therapy regarding observed memory changes, therapeutic practices, and beliefs about trauma and memory. most reported using trauma-focused interventions primarily for ptsd, although some reported using them to complete fragmented memories (49%) or recover inaccessible memories (19%). most agreed that traumatic experiences are usually remembered, but some endorsed scientifically questionable beliefs about inaccessibility or recovery being a therapeutic goal. many reported observing memory changes (82%), and among these, a substantial proportion reported the emergence of new traumatic memories (81%), although such experiences were relatively uncommon overall (12% reported them as occurring "often" or "very often"). memory changes usually involved emotional meaning, narrative expression, and retrospective reappraisal. problematic changes, such as alterations in temporal-spatial context (39%) and substantial changes in core event details (18%), were less frequent. reports of recovered memories, but not of changes in existing memories, were associated with potentially problematic beliefs and attempts to complete or recover memories, and such patterns were more common among psychodynamic therapists than among cognitive-behavioural therapists. taken together, these findings add to the complex picture of how trauma-focused interventions may affect memory and diverge from laboratory evidence generally indicating no effects on memory. they highlight the importance of evidence-informed training on trauma, memory, and suggestibility, as well as longitudinal research on trauma memory changes during therapy. memory

autonomy satisfaction and bedtime procrastination among generation z university students: the serial mediating roles of general self-efficacy and ai dependence. background: with the rapid integration of artificial intelligence (ai) into higher education, university students' daily behaviors are increasingly shaped by technology use. bedtime procrastination has emerged as a common self-regulation problem among generation z students. however, the psychological mechanisms linking environmental resources and technology-related behaviors to sleep outcomes remain insufficiently understood. this study examined the associations between autonomy satisfaction and bedtime procrastination and the mediating roles of general self-efficacy and ai dependence.
methods: a cross-sectional survey was conducted among 717 chinese university students using cluster sampling. standardized self-report measures assessed autonomy satisfaction, general self-efficacy, ai dependence, and bedtime procrastination. data were analyzed using spss 26.0 and mplus 8.0. structural equation modeling and bias-corrected bootstrap (5000 resamples) were employed to test direct and indirect effects.
results: autonomy satisfaction was positively associated with general self-efficacy and negatively associated with ai dependence and bedtime procrastination. general self-efficacy was negatively associated with both ai dependence and bedtime procrastination, while ai dependence was positively associated with bedtime procrastination. mediation analysis revealed that both general self-efficacy and ai dependence served as significant mediators, with ai dependence accounting for a larger proportion of the indirect effect. a significant serial mediation pathway was also observed.
conclusions: the findings suggest that autonomy satisfaction was associated with bedtime procrastination through both cognitive and behavioral mechanisms. ai dependence plays a particularly important role as a proximal behavioral pathway. these results highlight the need to promote balanced ai use and strengthen students' self-regulation in technology-rich learning environments. acta psychologica
journal of addictions & offender counseling journal of addictions & offender counseling

embodied regulation and connection in equine-assisted services: advancing a somatic and relational informed model within a one health and one welfare framework abstract background : horses inspire, a phase-based curriculum that integrates therapeutic horseback riding and ground-based equine-assisted psychotherapy (eap), is informed by somatic-based psychotherapy theories, with one health and one welfare principles guiding equine welfare and horse-human interaction. methods : this exploratory mixed-methods pilot program evaluation examined changes in body awareness, self-esteem, and resilience among trauma-exposed adult women participating in a 12-session equine-assisted services (eas) intervention integrating therapeutic riding and eap. the study puts forward the n-model of embodied relational integration in animal-assisted services (aas), a practice-informed theoretical framework developed within eas. unlike existing frameworks in eas or aas, the n-model is distinguished by its explicit integration of somatic, relational, ecological, dei lens and ethical dimensions within a unified one health and one welfare framework. where many models focus primarily on the human participant’s outcomes or position the animal as a therapeutic adjunct, the n-model can provide an overlay of “narrative knowing” over other models to center reciprocal processes of regulation and healing between human and horse, recognizing both as active agents whose well-being and engagement are mutually influential. this systems-based approach advances theoretical understanding by situating therapeutic change as an emergent property of dynamic, multispecies relationships rather than as a unidirectional intervention. informed by interpersonal neurobiology (ipnb), attachment theory, polyvagal theory, constructivism, experiential learning, and animal welfare science and situated within an overarching one health and one welfare framework, the model conceptualizes therapeutic change as an embodied, reciprocal, and multispecies process. the model proposes that healing emerges through the interrelated developmental processes of attunement, attachment, affirmation, and affect regulation, while recognizing that equine agency, positive welfare, and ethical multispecies relationships are integral to therapeutic engagement. results : given the small sample size and the significant medical, psychosocial, and life stressors experienced by participants, the findings should be interpreted with caution. nevertheless, outcome measures demonstrated steady improvements in self-esteem and individualized changes in body awareness, including shifts in felt sense, posture, and movement during both mounted and groundwork activities. these changes are consistent with enhanced autonomic regulation and increased somatic awareness, suggesting movement toward resilience as a dynamic, embodied, and context-specific process rather than a fixed outcome. qualitative findings highlighted themes of somatic awareness, relational attunement, body image, and experiences of being “seen” within the human-horse relationship. conclusions : this exploratory program evaluation provides preliminary support for the proposed n-model of embodied relational integration in aas as a phase-based, somatically informed framework for eas. although the small sample size and participants’ complex medical and psychosocial stressors limit generalizability, the findings suggest that integrating therapeutic riding and groundwork may support individualized, embodied pathways of change through attachment, affirmation, attunement, and affect regulation. by conceptualizing therapeutic change as a reciprocal interspecies process grounded in one health and one welfare principles, the model offers a novel framework to guide future research and clinical practice. human-animal interactions
