correlational links between professional identity and learning engagement among chinese college students: the potential mediating role of positive emotions. against the backdrop of mass higher education in china, the quality of talent cultivation in local universities has become a major concern. the study was based on self-determination theory and social cognition theory, aimed to examine the relationship between professional identity and learning engagement among college students, as well as the mediating role of positive emotions in this relationship. the research sampled undergraduate students from four public universities in a central southern region of china. a total of 482 valid questionnaires were collected via an online survey. descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, one-way anova, pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression combined with bias-corrected bootstrapping were employed for data analysis. the results indicated that participants reported moderate-to-high levels of professional identity, learning engagement, and positive emotions. significant gender, grade, major, hometown, and family socioeconomic status differences were observed across the three constructs (all < 0.001). professional identity significantly and positively predicted both learning engagement and positive emotions. positive emotions, in turn, positively predicted learning engagement and partially mediated the relationship between professional identity and learning engagement. the findings clarify the intrinsic mechanisms linking professional identity, positive emotions, and learning engagement, enrich empirical research on local university students, and provide practical implications for optimizing talent cultivation in regional higher education contexts. frontiers in psychology

a multidimensional structure of digital anxiety in older people with scale development and validation. inroduction: as digital technologies become increasingly embedded in everyday life, older people may experience persistent psychological challenges when engaging with complex and evolving digital systems. this study examines digital anxiety as a multidimensional construct in later life and develops a corresponding measurement scale. drawing on technostress theory and related gerontological perspectives, digital anxiety is conceptualized as comprising four dimensions: operational learning anxiety, technological risk anxiety, ability-based exclusion anxiety, and privacy and institutional anxiety.
methods: data were collected from three independent samples. the main sample (= 691) was split for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. additional model comparisons were conducted to examine alternative factor structures. reliability and validity were evaluated through internal consistency, test-retest reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, and associations with external constructs.
results: exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a correlated four-factor structure with acceptable model fit. additional model comparisons indicated that the substantial covariance among ability-based exclusion anxiety, operational learning anxiety, and privacy and institutional anxiety could also be represented by a partial second-order factor, whereas technological risk anxiety remained a separate first-order dimension. the scale demonstrated high internal consistency, satisfactory test-retest reliability, acceptable convergent validity, and generally supportive but not unequivocal evidence of discriminant validity. criterion-related validity was supported through associations with technostress-related constructs and weak correlations with life satisfaction.
discussion: the findings provide a psychometrically promising instrument for examining digital anxiety among older people. the results support the multidimensional conceptualization of digital anxiety while highlighting the need for further examination of the relationships among its constituent dimensions. frontiers in psychology

a self‐focused perspective on generative ai usage and adaptive performance: the roles of self‐expansion and perceived genai–self similarity abstract existing research has primarily conceptualized generative artificial intelligence (genai) as an instrumental technology that enhances employees' task capabilities and work outcomes, leaving unclear whether and how interactions with genai may shape employees' sense of self. this question is important because genai may influence not only what employees accomplish but also how they perceive their own knowledge and capabilities, which are critical for adapting to changing work demands. drawing on self‐expansion theory, we propose that genai usage enhances employees' adaptive performance by fostering self‐expansion and that perceived genai–self similarity strengthens this process. we tested the proposed model using a three‐wave time‐lagged survey of 220 full‐time employees in china. results showed that genai usage fostered self‐expansion, which subsequently enhanced adaptive performance, and this indirect effect was stronger among employees with higher genai–self similarity. by highlighting self‐expansion as a process through which genai‐enabled knowledge, perspectives, and capabilities can become incorporated into employees' self‐concepts, this study provides a self‐expansion perspective on human–genai augmentation and identifies perceived genai–self similarity as an important boundary condition of this process. journal of applied social psychology

managing first impressions: the role of acknowledgment strategies in reducing hiring bias against individuals with visible facial differences abstract although past research has established that people with visible facial differences encounter hiring discrimination, less is known about how this bias may be mitigated. in this paper, we draw on the social identity impression management theory and behaviors from intergroup affect and stereotypes (bias) map to examine whether the manner in which applicants acknowledge their facial difference can impact their hiring evaluations. this research consisted of a between–participants experimental study with 205 working adults based in india. we found that participants evaluated a job applicant with a visible facial difference more favorably when she acknowledged her facial difference through de‐categorization (de‐emphasizing group membership, while emphasizing some other information about herself) and integration (reframing her stigmatized identity in positive terms) compared to when she did not acknowledge her facial difference. additionally, we found that admiration reactions mediated the effect of de‐categorization and integration on hiring evaluations. furthermore, we found that this effect varied across different job types. relative to no‐acknowledgment, de‐categorization led to more positive evaluations through admiration only for the high‐customer‐contact job, whereas integration was effective for both low and high customer contact jobs. the results have implications for individuals with visible facial differences seeking employment, vocational trainers, and organizational stakeholders. journal of applied social psychology

countermanding saccades in children abstract the countermanding saccade task is a widely used test of reactive inhibitory oculomotor control. the test comprises “go” trials, in which saccades are directed towards target onsets, interspersed with “stop” trials, where a signal sometime after target onset indicates that a saccade should be withheld or “countermanded”. computational models of the task assume a race to threshold between internal go and stop processes, the outcome of which determines whether a programmed response is cancelled. in this study, 181 typically developing primary-school-aged children completed child-friendly versions of the task. three experiments examined the effect of task instruction (either to countermand saccades or ignore stop signals), stop signal characteristics (with and without an overlapping fixation cue) and practice (one versus two blocks). children often failed to make saccades even when they were instructed to ignore the signal and make a response to the target on every trial. saccade reaction times were longer on stop compared with correct go trials and significant “dips” (reductions in expected response frequency within discrete time bins) were observed in reaction time distributions associated with the change in the colour of the fixation stimulus that served as a stop signal. it is concluded that visual stop signals exert an exogenous inhibitory effect on saccades which decreases with increasing age. as such, care should be taken in interpreting the oculomotor stop signal task as a straightforward test of developing inhibitory control or the maturation of an internal stop process. open access statement experiment task code, raw trial-level data, and analysis files for all experiments are available via the open science framework: https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/q4pgh . the study protocol was not preregistered. attention perception & psychophysics

cycling relationships: an empirical typology and its implications for relational functioning cycling relationships are typically defined as committed romantic partnerships that have dissolved and reunited at least once in their history. these couples are relatively common and of growing empirical interest. however, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings about cycling relationships due, in part, to operationalizations that treat them as a homogeneous category, potentially obscuring meaningful variation in how different types of cycling relationships operate. to explore this possibility, the current work applied a two-step cluster analysis to individuals reporting on a current or previous cycling relationship ( n = 261) and compared the emergent groups against each other and to a non-cycling sample ( n = 161) on various relationship and individual characteristics. three clusters emerged with qualitatively different profiles: a “deliberate” other-seeking group reported no contact with the cycling partner during long splits wherein they actively sought alternative partnerships. an “exclusive” cluster evidenced short splits, frequent communication with their cycling partner but without physical intimacy, no other-seeking, and the highest levels of relational certainty. lastly, a cluster of “uncertain” other-seekers reported short splits comprising outreaches to alternative partners despite continued sexual intimacy and contact with their cycling partner during splits. this final group had the highest levels of uncertainty and the most dysfunctional relationships. they largely drove observed cycler versus non-cycler differences. psychological aggression was the only variable that differentiated all three cycling groups from non-cyclers. our findings suggest that cycling reflects qualitatively distinct relational configurations and that prevailing operationalizations may obscure theoretically consequential heterogeneity within this population. journal of social and personal relationships

the social origins of identity and bias: language models, accumulated meaning and positioning abstract this paper develops a social psychological interpretation of distributional language models, algorithmically learned representations of natural language. within these models, words are positioned according to patterns of usage, and the resulting embeddings can be interpreted as maps of cultural associations available for learning. this cultural‐learning account explains how patterned meanings become available to individual cognition but leaves open how those meanings are socially produced. drawing on social identity theory, discursive psychology and a stigmergic–dialogical model of communication, the paper argues that identity and bias emerge through social interaction and the accumulation of linguistic traces. as people take positions, respond to others and circulate formulations, they produce patterns of meaning that locate actors relationally and make alignments and differences recognizable. bias emerges when this accumulation is uneven, making associations, evaluations and distinctions differentially available across communities. from this perspective, embeddings map patterns accumulated through social activity. their geometry captures relations through which identities become recognizable and groups distinguishable. the paper extends this approach with speaker landscapes, which locate speakers by their language use and show how groups become differentiated. the result is a framework for studying how meaning, identity, bias and group differentiation are socially produced at scale. british journal of social psychology

expressive priority and goal structure and complexity during collegiate, faculty, and professional chamber music rehearsals the purpose of this study was to discover the artistic conceptualizations and priorities of collegiate, faculty, and professional musicians during the moment-to-moment decision-making of a rehearsal. we utilized musicians’ verbalizations during chamber music rehearsals as a vehicle for exploring their thought processes. analysis 1 investigated the rehearsal targets ensembles prioritized as a percentage of total rehearsal time allocated to each. analysis 2 investigated the complexity and form of professional, faculty, and collegiate chamber musicians’ goal structures as they attended to musical targets in relation to one another. professional chamber ensembles prioritized the expressive targets of character and phrasing above all others, and significantly more as a percentage of rehearsal time than did collegiate chamber ensembles. goal complexity increased with each level of experience from collegiate to professional ensembles; faculty and professional ensembles pursued elemental and technical goals in service of paramount expressive ends such as character and phrasing. we discuss the possible causes for this phenomenon, implications for music education, and recommendations for further research in these areas. we also recommend that teachers consider crafting music learning experiences to facilitate learners’ focus on expressive ends and pursual of proximal goals in service of artistic aims. psychology of music

implications of self-recording of audition performances in opera singers: a multiple case study this qualitative multiple case study investigated the potential benefits of audio self-recording during university opera auditions. while commonly employed in individual practice, self-recording remains rare in formal audition settings, possibly hindering performers’ ability to critically evaluate their performance. five classical university voice students participated in semi-structured interviews after completing an audio-recorded opera audition. each student reflected on the audition both before and after listening to their recording. thematic analysis revealed the following three primary themes: (a) self-recording as a tool for recalling specific details of the audition, (b) shifts in self-perception after listening, and (c) reduced post-audition rumination. these findings underscore the need for further research and highlight the potential of audio self-recording as a cost-effective, pedagogically valuable intervention that may support reflective learning, emotional regulation, and more effective audition preparation within higher education settings. psychology of music

does self-compassion moderate the association between music-specific stress and internalizing symptoms? music students are a high-risk population for mental health challenges due to the unique sources of stress they encounter. previous work indicates that these music-specific stressors are associated with higher levels of internalizing symptoms (i.e., depression and anxiety). consequently, further attention to protective assets and resources for music students is crucial. one construct that has garnered attention from scholars is self-compassion. prior studies have documented benefits of self-compassion in reducing and attenuating the link between stress and internalizing symptoms. yet, no study to date has considered whether self-compassion and its six subscales moderate the association between music-study stress and internalizing symptoms. the current study explored whether self-compassion and its six subcomponents moderate the relationship between music-study stress and internalizing symptoms among student musicians. participants were 151 music students at a public university in the united states. we found a positive association between music-study stress and internalizing symptoms. in addition, results revealed that self-judgment and isolation moderated the link between music-study stress and anxious symptoms, such that at higher levels of self-judgment and isolation, music-study stress evinced stronger associations with anxious symptoms than at lower levels of the two. we discuss the rationales for our findings and practice implications. psychology of music

living criteria: co-construction of evaluative criteria in creative collaboration in the primary classroom research with both professional musicians and children shows that during creativity, evaluations – such as liking, novelty and structure – shape decision-making. less is known about how these evaluative processes operate in collaborative classroom settings where creativity also supports learning. this study examined how primary school students evaluate ideas during collaborative creative tasks, particularly in relation to their musical decisions. a qualitative case study was conducted with 18 students (aged 9–10) in a primary classroom across five integrated arts lessons centred on composing and performing rhythmic ostinati. classroom observations, peer-feedback forms and student interviews were analysed thematically. findings showed that students co-constructed a ‘living criteria’: a shared, dynamic evaluative system guiding idea generation, selection and refinement. this system comprised three components: task-specific congruence (judging ideas by task fit and clarity), emerging aesthetic evaluation (linking humour, enjoyment and ‘liking’ with perceived quality) and collaborative sensitivity (balancing idea quality with group harmony). although limited by its small sample and single-class context, the study demonstrates how children integrate aesthetic, practical and social considerations when working together musically and creatively. the concept of ‘living criteria’ offers a framework for understanding how evaluative judgement develops through collaboration, with implications for music pedagogy and creative learning research. psychology of music

a lasting impression: performance memory persists after a single musical exposure despite the centrality of memory to music reading and performance, little is known about incidental long-term memory retention of music that is performed at sight. in this study, 19 undergraduate pianists sight-read a series of short, unfamiliar pieces, and then returned 1–3 weeks later to perform the same pieces, without opportunities to see or practise the music in the interim. pitch, rhythm, and metre errors were all found to decrease in the second reading, with error counts dropping on average by 13% from reading 1 to reading 2, while error types and sizes tended to persist across readings. no significant differences were found between those who had a 1-, 2-, or 3-week gap between readings, suggesting that a single brief encounter with a score can have a long-term priming effect. these findings illustrate how robust musical memory can be and may have implications for our understanding of how motor and memory systems support long-term retention in skilled performance. psychology of music

exploring musicians’ perspectives on decent work, creativity, and well-being this study, grounded in the psychology of working theory (pwt) and self-determination theory (sdt), examined how working conditions shape musicians’ experiences of decent work, intrinsic motivation, artistic identity, creative engagement, and psychological well-being. sixteen in-depth interviews were conducted with portuguese musicians, including both freelancers and those with stable contracts. reflexive thematic analysis identified four overarching themes: (a) job security and precarity, (b) intrinsic motivation, autonomy, and creative engagement, (c) artistic identity and purpose, and (d) well-being and mental health. the findings show that freelance instability undermines security, constrains creative risk-taking, and increases stress, whereas financial and institutional stability supports intrinsic motivation, reinforces artistic identity, and enables creative exploration. features associated with intrinsic motivation, voluntary engagement, persistence, and psychological investment in creative tasks were observed across both groups. autonomy itself sustained engagement for some freelancers, highlighting personal resilience and self-directed creativity. the results underscore the interplay between structural conditions (pwt) and individual motivations (sdt), showing that sustainable work environments foster well-being and high-quality creative output. the study provides practical implications for policies, education, and organizational strategies to support healthier, more productive artistic ecosystems. psychology of music

exploring patterns of resilience among adolescents with experiences of parental incarceration: insights from two countries parental incarceration presents significant risks to adolescent development and well-being. however, most research has focused on deficits rather than protective factors and has mainly been limited to high-income western contexts and caregivers’ reports. this study examined how contextual conditions impact the lives of adolescents with experience of parental incarceration (api) from south africa and canada. multigroup structural equation modelling (sem) compared api with sex- and age-matched peers who had not experienced parental incarceration on indicators of health, behaviour, risk, and resources, and identified common and country-specific predictors of api mental and physical health. across countries, api showed poorer health and behavioural outcomes than their peers. south african api ( n = 54, m age = 18.70; 50% female) reported higher family adversity but no resource differences, whereas canadian api ( n = 73, m age = 18.34; 60.3% female) showed disadvantages across multiple risk and resource domains compared with their peers. being male was a consistent protective factor in both countries, and low family adversity and more benevolent childhood experiences were associated with better mental health in canada. these findings underline that api represent a uniquely vulnerable, yet under-researched and underserved population. the results highlight the need for context-sensitive and gender-responsive supports for these young people. international journal of behavioral development

the work needs satisfaction scale in brazil: psychometric evidence and differences by gender and race/color this study examined the psychometric properties of the brazilian version of the work needs satisfaction scale and investigated differences in work-related need satisfaction across gender and race/color groups, informed by an intersectional perspective. participants were 1521 brazilian adults (67.2% women; mean age = 35.09 years), recruited across three independent waves of data collection. confirmatory factor analyses, multi-group invariance tests, and comparisons across gender and race/color groups were conducted. the five-factor structure, survival, social contribution, competence, relatedness, and autonomy showed adequate fit (cfi = .94; rmsea = .07) and high internal consistency (α = .79–.92; ω = .83–.94). invariance analyses indicated metric and scalar equivalence across gender and race/color based on practical fit-index criteria. group comparisons revealed a significant main effect of race/color, with black participants reporting lower levels of satisfaction in survival, social contribution, competence, and autonomy than white participants; the gender-by-race/color interaction was not significant. these findings indicate that, although the scale’s structure remains psychometrically stable, work-related need satisfaction is unequally distributed, reflecting persistent structural inequalities in the brazilian labor market. the study extends the application of the psychology of working theory within a brazilian context situated in the global south and reinforces the importance of reliable measures for research and promoting social justice and equity in the workplace. journal of career assessment

the grassroots of fertilizer use: norms and attitudes toward lawn care in coastal counties nutrient runoff reduces water quality and contributes to eutrophication in u.s. estuaries, highlighting the need to reduce nutrient inputs. lawn fertilizers contribute substantially to nutrient pollution in runoff. understanding the social drivers behind fertilizer use can support strategies to lower nutrient loads. we surveyed residents in two adjacent counties with different urbanization levels to identify factors influencing homeowner fertilization decisions. participants were asked about neighborhood norms, lawn care attitudes, environmental beliefs, proximity to waterbodies, and demographics. overall fertilizer use did not differ significantly between the more urbanized and more rural counties or with proximity to waterbodies. instead, income and homeowners association membership were the strongest predictors of fertilizer use. fertilization frequency was also positively associated with perceptions of neighborhood fertilization, indicating strong social norms favoring manicured lawns. recognizing the complex personal and institutional factors shaping landscaping decisions can inform efforts to encourage more sustainable practices and reduce residential nutrient runoff. environment and behavior

network analysis of adhd and autism spectrum disorder symptoms in clinic-referred adolescents abstract background attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adhd) and autism spectrum disorder (asd) often co-occur and share overlapping cognitive, emotional, and social characteristics, but the symptom-level processes underlying this comorbidity remain unclear. method using regularised partial correlation network analysis (ebic-glasso), this study examined the structure, centrality, and connectivity of dsm-5-tr adhd and asd symptoms in a clinic-referred sample of 942 adolescents (aged 11–17), based on parent ratings. results the network showed clear separation between adhd and asd symptom clusters, with stronger internal connections among adhd symptoms and weaker cross-condition associations. hyperactive–impulsive symptoms demonstrated the highest centrality overall. the most central symptoms were “has a strange way of relating to other people” (asd1), “has trouble sitting still or staying in my seat” (adhd11), and “distracted even when someone is speaking to them” (adhd3). the strongest bridge symptoms linking the adhd and asd symptom clusters were “gets frustrated when i have to wait my turn to do things” (adhd17), “is unaware of, or takes no interest in, other people’s feelings” (asd4), and “gets fixated on things” (asd12). conclusions overall, results suggest that co-occurrence may be shaped by specific highly influential symptoms, particularly hyperactivity-impulsivity and select social-emotional or restrictive/repetitive features, highlighting the value of targeting central and bridging symptoms in assessment and intervention. cognitive therapy and research

assessing the relevance of test of memory malingering (tomm) trial 2 performance after failure of trial 1 among veterans with self-reported histories of mild traumatic brain injury despite empirically established cut scores for trial 1 of the test of memory malingering (tomm), the interpretive significance of failing trial 1 while passing trial 2 remains equivocal, possibly due to the original manual's emphasis on trial 2. this study examined whether individuals with a trial 1 fail/trial 2 pass pattern demonstrate cognitive profiles more similar to individuals who fail both trials or pass both trials.participants were 203 veterans with a history of self-reported mild traumatic brain injury (mtbi) who completed a comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation in a multicenter study. based on tomm performance, participants were classified into pass-pass, fail-pass, and fail-fail groups. standardized measures of learning and memory, attention/processing speed, executive functioning, and additional performance validity tests were examined. one-way analyses of variance were conducted to compare cognitive performance across groups.the fail-pass group did not differ from the fail-fail group and performed significantly worse than the pass-pass group across learning and memory, attention/processing speed, executive functioning, and overall performance. similarly, the fail-pass and fail-fail groups demonstrated comparable rates of failure on at least one additional independent performance validity test, with both groups exhibiting significantly higher failure rates than the pass-pass group.veterans who fail tomm trial 1 but pass trial 2 demonstrate cognitive and performance validity profiles more consistent with those who fail both trials than those who pass both trials. consequently, trial 2 pass status does not negate the clinical significance of trial 1 failure in those with a history of self-reported mtbi. clinical neuropsychologist

executive function and language as predictors of clustering and switching in semantic verbal fluency: does the semantic category matter? introduction: clustering and switching scores have been shown to provide information about strategic processes involved in semantic memory search and may contribute to the assessment of executive and language impairments in developmental disorders. however, differences across semantic verbal fluency (svf) categories in their cognitive and linguistic correlates highlight the importance of understanding how category characteristics may influence the interpretation of these scores. this study investigated the associations of linguistic abilities and executive functions with clustering and switching scores in the animals, fruits, and clothes categories.
method: a sample of 111 typically developing brazilian children performed a one-minute svf task. participants also completed measures of working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, higher-order executive functions, and linguistic measures (vocabulary, rapid automatized naming, and phonological awareness). multiple regression analyses were conducted to examine the contribution of strategic scores to total word production and the independent associations of cognitive and linguistic measures with these scores.
results: the findings revealed differences in strategic scores across semantic categories. clustering and switching predicted total word production across all categories, while mean cluster size was an additional predictor in clothes. the pattern of associations with executive and linguistic measures varied depending on the strategic score examined and the semantic category. rapid automatized naming was significantly associated with clustering and switching in animals and fruits. inhibitory control was additionally associated with clustering and switching in animals, although these associations did not remain independently significant in the regression models. in clothes, clustering was independently associated with phonological working memory and higher-order executive functions.
conclusions: these findings are discussed in light of differences in animacy and in the breadth and organization of semantic networks across categories. the results underscore the importance of interpreting clustering and switching as complementary indices, as their cognitive and linguistic associations vary across svf categories. journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology

masculinity contest cultures and job satisfaction: better to be competent or embedded? abstract measures of masculinity contest culture (mcc) examine the degree to which workplace norms align with traditional tenets of masculinity. past research suggests mcc is negatively related to job satisfaction. informed by theories of mcc, we begin to unravel the moderating variables through which this relationship is attenuated or strengthened via testing gender and two forms of perceived success at work (in-role competence and social embeddedness), informing on whether mccs relate to lesser job satisfaction for all employees or primarily among subsets of those who perceive they perform poorly within them. hypotheses were tested using a three-timepoint survey with a sample of 408 full-time employed adults. results from a 5,000 bootstrap linear regression suggest the relationship between mcc and job satisfaction is moderated by gender. the relationship is strongest among men with lower perceived social embeddedness and is not statistically significant among men with higher perceived social embeddedness. in contrast, the relationship is not significant among women who report social embeddedness scores that approach the minimum but is consistently negative otherwise. moreover, there was no evidence that social embeddedness was a moderator absent gender. additionally, there were no moderation effects associated with perceived in-role competence, potentially reflecting that in-role performance may not buffer employees against the potential harms of mcc environments. implications for employee wellbeing, employee performance, and theories of masculinity contest culture are discussed. journal of business and psychology

italian guidelines for speech and language therapy in patients with stroke or primary progressive aphasia. recommendations from the italian neuropsychological society background: aphasia can be frequently observed after left hemisphere stroke, but also in neurodegenerative diseases, as in primary progressive aphasia (ppa). aphasia strongly impacts on quality of life, and rehabilitation of people with aphasia (pwa) presents clinicians with complex challenges.
aims: an ad-hoc scientific panel, including 20 members (neurologists, physiatrists, psychologists, therapists, nurses, pwa representatives), selected 4 questions not addressed by current international guidelines: (1) effectiveness of slt for post-stroke aphasia provided by professionals vs non-specialized personnel; (2) effectiveness of slt in the chronic phase vs no treatment; (3) effectiveness of non-invasive neuromodulation combined with slt vs stand-alone slt for pwa after stroke; (4) effectiveness of non-invasive neuromodulation combined with slt vs stand-alone slt for ppa patients.
methods: the scientific panel and experienced methodologists followed common guidelines for systematic reviews and the pico framework for scrutinizing several databases (last search: march 2023). recommendations were based on evidence analysis according to the grade methodology.
key findings: the scientific panel suggested one strong and three conditional recommendations, although quality of evidence was low or very low.
conclusions: the present guidelines, published by the italian higher institute for health on december 19, 2023, supplement the most recent international guidelines, particularly in tackling ppa. neuropsychological rehabilitation

heterogeneity in depression and suicidality risk among vitiligo patients: a meta‐analysis of adolescent complexity and subgroup stratification abstract patients with vitiligo are known to have a markedly increased burden of psychological comorbidities compared with the general population. however, a comprehensive and up‐to‐date assessment of the association between vitiligo, depression, and suicidality is lacking. this study aimed to quantitatively evaluate the association between vitiligo and the risks of depression and suicidality. a systematic search of pubmed, embase, web of science, and the cochrane library was conducted from inception to 25 july 2025. pooled odds ratios (ors) and standardized mean differences (smds) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (cis) were calculated. seventy‐three studies were included. the pooled prevalence of depression among patients with vitiligo was 0.37 (95% ci, 0.30–0.45). compared with non‐vitiligo controls, vitiligo patients exhibited significantly higher risks of depression (or = 1.60, 95% ci [1.05, 2.43]) and suicide‐related outcomes (or = 1.22, 95% ci [1.05, 1.41]), with suicidal ideation showing the greatest increase (or = 2.05, 95% ci [1.08, 3.90]). however, the unadjusted preliminary analysis of continuous depression scores showed an increase, but it was not significant after publication bias correction. female patients represented a particularly vulnerable subgroup, whereas adolescent patients showed a dual risk profile depending on the reference group: compared with age‐matched non‐vitiligo controls, adolescents with vitiligo had a significantly higher risk of depression (or = 2.84); however, within the vitiligo patient population, adolescents showed a lower depression risk than adult patients (or = 0.20). the risk of depression was higher than that in the general population but lower than that observed in psoriasis. vitiligo is significantly associated with elevated risks of depression and suicidality. these findings highlight the need for heightened clinical awareness and integrated psychological care to improve patients' overall well‐being and quality of life. stress and health

academic stress and depressive symptoms in high school students: a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model and cross‐lagged panel network analysis abstract despite evidence linking academic stress and depressive symptoms, cross‐sectional designs cannot reveal their developmental dynamics, and total‐scale scores obscure symptom‐level complexity and intervention targets. we applied the random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (ri‐clpm) and cross‐lagged panel network (clpn) analysis to 307 chinese adolescents (58.63% female) to examine the relationship between academic stress and depressive symptoms from the aggregate to the symptom level and to identify key nodes. results from the ri‐clpm indicated a positive association between academic stress and depressive symptoms at the between‐person level. at the within‐person level, time‐1 academic stress predicted a reduction in time‐2 depressive symptoms. clpn results revealed complex reciprocal influences: ‘people were unfriendly’ and ‘i felt hopeless about the future’ were initially vulnerable and later progressed to ‘i felt sad’ and ‘i thought my life had been a failure’. early drivers included ‘i thought my life had been a failure’ and ‘i felt that people dislike me’, whereas over time ‘i was unhappy’ and ‘i felt hopeless about the future’ gained predictive importance. the study revealed temporal relationships between academic stress and depressive symptoms and identified potential targets, providing evidence and implications for prevention and intervention. stress and health

the cognitive developmental cascade at different timescales: relationships among intrasubject variability, processing speed, working memory, and fluid intelligence in children aged 8 to 14 years. according to the developmental cascade model (fry & hale, 2000), accelerations in processing speed (ps) throughout childhood lead to improvements in working memory (wm) which in turn result in increased fluid intelligence (). decreasing intrasubject variability (isv) of reaction times has been proposed to play a crucial role within this cascade. while most of the evidence supporting the developmental cascade is derived from cross-sectional studies, longitudinal studies are scarce, with heterogeneous findings. moreover, longitudinal analysis of correlational patterns may produce biased results, if within-person changes (development within the studied timeframe) are not separated from between-person variance (stable differences and long-term changes beyond the studied time frame). to overcome these limitations,= 173 children aged 8-12 years at baseline (±: 10.01 ± 1.11, 51% female) were tested five times within 2.5 years using a computer-based testing battery including choice reaction time tasks to measure ps and isv as well as span, operation span, and coordination tasks to measure wm. cattell's culture fair test was administered to measure. separating between-person variance from within-person developmental changes using a cross-lagged panel model with random intercepts, the postulated close relationships between ps, isv, wm, andwere observed at the level of between-person differences on a long-term timescale alongside no evidence of the expected associations of within-person changes for a time frame of 2.5 years. thus, associations consistent with the developmental cascade model may reflect stable between-person differences rather than short-term within-person changes. this has important implications for developmental theory and methodology. processing speed, not multitasking, drives expert decision-making under pressure. the cognitive mechanism underlying high performance during decision-making under pressure-such as in first-person shooter games-is still unclear: advantages in multitasking or general processing speed? to resolve this, we classified= 230 players (16-34 years) of the video game counter-strike into four expertise clusters (novice, skilled, emerging, and expert), assessing their processing speed and task-switching performance. to better understand the source of expertise effects, we used drift-diffusion modeling to estimate nondecision and decision components of performance. experts exhibited significantly faster reaction times than novices, but no specific multitasking advantage was observed. the drift-diffusion modeling revealed that this speed advantage was driven by higher drift rates and shorter nondecision times. no expertise-related differences were found in boundary separation, the strategic component of decision-making. findings suggest that expert performance in decision-making under pressure is characterized by advantages in general processing speed rather than being associated with greater multitasking capabilities. general versus specific: investigating the structure of individual differences in post-error slowing across time. erroneous actions are typically followed by behavioral slowing, known as post-error slowing (pes), along with other post-error adjustments. these effects emerge on the first trial following an error and can persist across subsequent trials. while pes has been extensively studied experimentally, less attention has been given to inter-individual variability. evidence suggests that the mechanisms underlying individual differences in pes are largely domain-general, spanning multiple tasks. however, as time elapses from the point of error, task-specific processes may increasingly influence these individual differences. in this study, we applied latent variable modeling to two large samples of participants who completed three canonical inhibitory control paradigms. our findings indicate that individual differences in pes reflect both domain-general and task-specific abilities, with the influence of the domain-general factor seeming to decrease over time following error commission. cognition

unlocking early math skills: contributions of working memory to game-based learning of early mathematical skills. this study evaluated the effects of linear board games differing in mathematical demands (spanning number ranges from 0 to 20 vs. 0 to 30) on the development of children's early mathematical skills. given the influences of domain-general skills such as working memory on the development of early mathematical skills, we were particularly interested in whether learning gains were associated with children's working memory. unlike most previous studies, we employed an experimental design. in a pre-post follow-up intervention design, 149 german children aged around 6 years (73 girls, 76 boys) were randomly assigned to either a control group or one of two intervention groups playing board games in four 15-20-min sessions over the course of a week. we assessed early mathematical skills, such as counting, cardinality understanding, and basic arithmetic, as well as visual, verbal, and central executive components of working memory. results indicated a significant improvement in overall early mathematical skills irrespective of participant group. importantly, working memory (components) significantly predicted learning gains overall but also differentially for participant groups. in particular, the central executive component, as assessed at pretest, was a significantly stronger predictor of early mathematical skills learning gains at follow-up for the group playing the more demanding game version. these results provide the first experimental evidence on the relevance of working memory for mathematical learning and its association with demands of the learning content. further studies are needed to substantiate these findings. social sprouts: evaluating a play-based classroom intervention to improve peer interactions in early childhood education teaching prosocial skills in early childhood education settings has beneficial outcomes on immediate behavior change and long-term social-emotional and academic outcomes. however, early childhood educators are in need of effective, efficient, and feasible strategies to explicitly teach and reinforce young children’s prosocial skills, especially those who already struggle with social skills. using a non-concurrent multiple baseline design, the research team investigated the effects of a novel intervention, social sprouts, on an individual child’s and class-wide display of positive peer interactions and disruptive behavior. social validity data were also collected to better understand the teachers’ perceptions of feasibility, effectiveness, and acceptability. results indicated an increase in both individual children’s and class-wide display of positive peer interactions, with less pronounced effects for disruptive behaviors. all three implementing teachers perceived social sprouts to be acceptable, feasible, and effective. these results highlight a promising and feasible class-wide intervention to be implemented in head start settings. journal of positive behavior interventions

theoretically informed analysis of teacher commitment to implement pbis this study applies the theory of planned behavior (tpb) to an analysis of teacher responses in the u.s. to interview questions about commitment to implement tier 1 positive behavior interventions and supports (pbis). qualitative thematic analysis resulted in 24 codes that were assigned to three themes derived from tpb: (a) attitudes toward pbis, (b) normative beliefs about pbis, and (c) perceived behavioral control of pbis implementation. results were also analyzed by commitment levels reported prior to interviews. the high-commitment group reported perceptions of improved relationships with students and no concerns about peers or leadership. the mid-commitment group reported concerns about their own knowledge of pbis but a belief that they gain competence through experience and exposure. the low-commitment group reported concerns about the lack of positive student outcomes and perceived inequities in implementation. results are discussed in terms of development of implementation strategies to support implementer commitment through alignment with previous work in tpb. journal of positive behavior interventions

learning judo in physical education: combined video modeling and video feedback are more effective when self-controlled this study investigates how granting students control over the timing and type of video resources affects skill acquisition of the uchi-mata technique in judo, contributing to best practices in physical education (pe). twenty-four male secondary school studentswere randomly assigned to either the self-control (sc) group or the yoked (yk) group. the sc group controlled both the timing of their viewing and the type of video resources used (choosing between video modeling, video feedback, or a simultaneous split-screen view), while the yk group was restricted to viewing the resources simultaneously at predetermined times. pre-tests (t0) and post-tests (t1) were conducted before and after a four-session uchi-mata learning unit, with a retention test (t2) 2 weeks later. three judo experts assessed technical execution, while participants self-reported perceived competence using a custom-designed instrument. the statistical analyses revealed significant improvement in technical performance for the sc group at t1 and t2. the yk group exhibited improvement only at t1. a significant difference at t2 favored the sc group, demonstrating greater long-term learning effects. the sc group showed lasting improvements in perceived competence from t0 to t1 and t2. in contrast, the yk group had initial gains from t0 to t1, but these declined at t2. in conclusion, this study reveals that the combined view is not always necessary, supporting the importance of allowing students to choose when to view a video model, when to review video feedback, and crucially, when to watch them simultaneously on a split screen. behavior modification

making trouble tellable: negotiating accountability in immigrants' narratives to majority‐group recipients abstract this article examines how immigrants' experiences of problematic interactions with majority‐group members are crafted into tellable narratives when shared with a majority‐group recipient. drawing on twenty‐four interviews between immigrants and a finnish majority‐group interviewer, we analyse immigrants' narratives of problematic interactions with finns using bamberg's (1997, 2004) narrative positioning framework. we argue that when recipients share a cultural group membership with story antagonists, making narratives tellable requires the collaborative negotiation of accountability between narrators and recipients. this involves establishing the narrative as legitimate, the narrator as reasonable, and, importantly, the recipient as unimplicated in wrongdoing. our results show how these accountability demands are managed through responsibility attribution and narrative positioning. responsibility for problematic interactions was attributed to situational influences, practices of particular social categories, or broader societal patterns. through this process, narrators were positioned as reasonable and competent in the majority culture, while the recipient was positioned as empathetic and unimplicated in the problematic conduct. while this accountability work rendered problematic experiences tellable and preserved rapport, it also redirected attention away from their seriousness and social significance. the findings demonstrate how accountability work makes problematic experiences tellable across cultural groups while simultaneously limiting opportunities to recognize and challenge the broader inequalities implicated in them. journal of community & applied social psychology

artificial intelligence in autism assessment: a conceptual framework for multimodal artificial intelligence integration 人工智能在自闭症评估中的应用：多模态人工智能整合的概念框架 artificial intelligence (ai) may be increasingly positioned to strengthen autism spectrum disorder (asd) assessment by improving scalability, consistency, and workflow efficiency across settings that serve children. traditional diagnostic tools such as the autism diagnostic observation schedule, second edition (ados-2) and autism diagnostic interview-revised (adi-r) require extensive clinician preparation and are difficult to implement in many contexts, which contributes to delays and uneven access. this article provides a detailed review of how ai methods can be embedded within existing evaluation procedures. computer vision, speech analysis, natural language processing, predictive modeling, and multimodal fusion techniques are examined as tools that can support observation, interviewing, scoring, and documentation. a central contribution is a conceptual framework organized around structured signal extraction, interpretable and modular models, and strong safeguards that guide responsible use. key challenges include bias, variation in data quality, and appropriate alignment with clinical judgment. the article offers a foundation for clinicians and researchers seeking to integrate ai within asd assessment workflows. assessment

item response modeling of situational judgment tests with items nested within scenarios 情境判断测验中题目嵌套于情境的项目反应建模 situational judgment tests (sjts) are widely used to evaluate decision-making and problem-solving skills. these tests present respondents with situations (scenarios), and possible actions in response to each situation, which they must rate based on effectiveness or appropriateness. despite having high face and criterion-related validities, these tests involve complex cognitive processes, and their construct validity has been notoriously difficult to establish. this is particularly challenging when several questions relate to the same scenario, thus creating local dependencies in item responses after controlling for the overall ability. finding a suitable measurement model for sjts would address the operational challenges of test development, maintenance, scoring, and equating the scores across multiple test forms and/or testing years. we propose to use a variant of the continuous response model (crm; samejima, 1973 ) to describe points gained at the level of scenario, regardless of the number of questions asked about the scenario. a simulation study testing the performance of this scenario-level model on data generated from categorical items nested within scenarios found that crm fits well under a wide range of realistic conditions and resembles the true score better than a summated test score. we illustrate the proposed approach with an sjt presenting clinical dilemmas with several possible actions, each scored using four ordered categories. the sjt was completed by n = 2,740 examinees in operational assessment settings. the proposed crm variant fitted the data well and was effective for assessing dimensionality, modeling and scoring responses, and evaluating test reliability. implications for other operational uses such as form linking and pre-equating are discussed. educational and psychological measurement

colonial residues and toxic aftermaths: necropolitics and the matter of memory in grenfell by steve mcqueen (2023) this article examines steve mcqueen’s commemorative film grenfell (2023) as confronting the necropolitics of the grenfell tower fire and its toxic aftermaths. drawing on environmental memory studies, critical posthumanism and new materialism, the film is read as reorienting commemoration towards material conditions and toxic afterlives. in considering the longue durée of colonial governance, racial capitalism and institutional neglect, it examines how mcqueen’s durational aerial footage resists interpretive closure and aesthetic sanitisation. this is read as making present the materially and politically embedded legacies of british imperialism. in attending to the commemorative vitality of matter, the article then locates grenfell within an anthropocenic memorial landscape. memory studies

feminist theory in feminism & psychology (part ii): power and subjectivity substantive scholarship related to theorizing power and subjectivity throughout the history of feminism & psychology supports the claim that these are (or should be) central concepts within feminist psychology (and the discipline of psychology more broadly). the articles included in this virtual special issue span four decades from 1991, when the first issue of the journal appeared, to the present. they represent a rich body of relevant work and reflect the shifting theoretical terrain within feminism during this period, as well as the events of the day. linking the personal with the political has been a consistent feminist project, reinforced by theory that draws attention to the relationship between power and subjectivity. questions about how best to understand agency, resistance, and empowerment have also been addressed. attention to differences has entailed the incorporation of queer, intersectional, and decolonial theoretical perspectives. this introduction includes a selective review of the broader theoretical context for the feminist work appearing in the articles selected for the special issue, as well as an overview of the main theoretical contributions. in a supplementary document, there are section introductions to each decade detailing the contributions of individual articles and additional, suggested reading. feminism & psychology

sleep quality and quality of life among nursing students in bangladesh: a cross‐sectional study background sleep quality is an important determinant of health and well‐being. nursing students may be particularly vulnerable to sleep‐related problems because of demanding academic and clinical responsibilities. this study assessed sleep quality and quality of life (qol) among nursing students in bangladesh and explored the association between individual pittsburgh sleep quality index (psqi) items (sleep disturbances, sleep‐medication use, and daytime dysfunction) and qol. methods a cross‐sectional study was conducted among 345 nursing students at ibn sina nursing institute, dhaka, bangladesh, between january 2024 and april 2025. participants were recruited using purposive sampling. data were collected using a self‐administered bengali questionnaire incorporating the psqi and whoqol‐bref. a psqi score > 5 was defined as poor sleep quality. descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics. twelve item‐level associations with dichotomized qol were examined as exploratory analyses using pearson chi‐square tests, with exact tests, chi‐square tests for linear trend, and holm‐adjusted p values to account for multiple comparisons. statistical significance was set at p < 0.05 (adjusted p < 0.05 for item‐level inference). results the participants had a mean age of 20.71 ± 1.663 years, and most were female and unmarried. overall, 66.6% (95% ci 61.5–71.4) of participants had poor sleep quality, and 49.3% were classified as having poor qol. difficulty breathing comfortably was associated with qol ( χ 2 = 14.50, df = 3, p = 0.002; holm‐adjusted p = 0.028; trend p = 0.003) and remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. trouble staying awake during driving, eating, or socializing showed a nominal association ( χ 2 = 9.11, p = 0.03) that did not remain significant after correction (holm‐adjusted p = 0.31) and showed no linear trend ( p = 0.21). no other item (nighttime awakenings, sleep‐onset difficulty, bathroom use, coughing or snoring, feeling too cold or hot, bad dreams, pain, sleep‐medication use, or difficulty maintaining enthusiasm) was significantly associated with qol. conclusion poor sleep quality was common among nursing students. in this exploratory, unadjusted analysis, difficulty breathing comfortably was the only psqi item that remained associated with qol after multiplicity correction, no consistent dose–response pattern was observed, and the relationship between overall psqi score and qol domains was not examined; these findings are hypothesis‐generating and do not establish causation. nursing institutions could consider sleep‐health education, early identification of persistent sleep problems, and appropriate student‐support services as potential implications for student well‐being. mental illness

developmental trajectories of psychotherapist trainees’ experiences of clinical practice: global and specific aspects of change in a multinational longitudinal sample objective: to study, in a multinational sample, how psychotherapist trainees develop in their professional self-experience over the course of a year.
methods: in the spr interest section on training and development (spristad) longitudinal study, 168 therapist trainees from 11 countries filled out the comprehensive therapist work involvement scales (twis) at 6-month intervals at least 3 times. the twis assesses therapist trainees' i) role-performance; ii) role-identity; and iii) overall global experience of therapeutic work as either healing or stressful. mixed linear modeling was used to test for statistically significant change in these facets of work experience.
results: trainees' experienced both their basic relational skills and more nuanced professional expertise to improve. professional self-doubt, negative personal reactions to patients, and anxious in-session feelings with patients decreased significantly. however, the trajectories differed markedly based on trainees' initial profiles. about half of the trainees experienced a stable, effective practice. others started either distressed or disengaged, both of which showed improvement. some trainees also experienced a decline in therapeutic self-efficacy.
conclusion: this study demonstrates the generally beneficial impacts of therapist training. however, these impacts depend much on where the trainees start from. in particular, the determinants of decline in therapeutic self-efficacy call for further research. psychotherapy research

negative emotional responses to media are associated with lower psychological wellbeing among adults in the kurdistan region of iraq abstract introduction in conflict-affected societies, media may provide information and social connection while also exposing individuals to emotionally distressing content. objective to examine whether dominant emotional response valence and total daily media-use duration were independently associated with psychological well-being among adults in the kurdistan region of iraq. methods in this cross-sectional study, trained interviewers administered a structured questionnaire to a convenience sample of 239 kurdish adults recruited across multiple cities. participants reported media-use patterns and their single dominant emotional response to media and completed the who-5 well-being index. the primary multiple linear regression adjusted for age, gender, education, employment status, and preferred media content. results the sample reported low average well-being (mean who-5 raw score = 10.96, sd = 3.97, on a 0–25 scale); 64.0% scored below the conventional screening cutoff of 13. in the primary adjusted model, reporting a dominant negative emotional response (sadness, anger, fear, or pessimism) was associated with a 2.17-point lower who-5 score than reporting optimism or indifference (95% ci [− 3.31, − 1.03]). total daily media-use duration was not independently associated with who-5 scores. conclusion in this conflict-affected context, lower psychological well-being was associated with negative emotional responses to media whereas total media-use duration was not independently associated with well-being. however, the cross-sectional design cannot establish whether media-related emotion preceded lower well-being or instead reflected prior mood, personality, content selection, or recall. longitudinal and experience-sampling studies using validated measures of media content and affect are needed. discover psychology

“ i finally felt my identity existed in therapy ”: a qualitative study of transgender-diverse patients’ psychotherapy experiences in chile research on psychotherapy for transgender and gender-diverse (tgd) individuals remains limited, particularly regarding barriers to care and patients' own accounts of treatment. this study explored how tgd adults in chile describe the contextual determinants, relational and procedural characteristics, and perceived consequences of their psychotherapeutic experiences. eight tgd adults who had received psychotherapy in chile participated in semi-structured interviews. data were analyzed using constructivist grounded theory, with the generic model of psychotherapy as a sensitizing framework. participants identified four contextual determinants of their therapeutic experiences: the sociocultural context, their experiences as tgd patients within the health system, varying levels of family support, and therapist characteristics. they described fragmented treatment histories marked by financial instability, discrimination, and frequent changes of therapist, which often left them feeling lost. in contrast, beneficial therapy was characterized by consistent validation of identity, including the use of chosen names and pronouns; a safe space to discuss gender experiences; regular weekly sessions; and trauma-informed, gender-affirming practices. participants attributed improvements in body affirmation, emotional regulation, and self-compassion, as well as reduced internalized stigma, to trans-affirmative psychotherapy. they also linked positive therapy experiences to less perceived stigma from peers and greater acceptance from family members. these findings underscore the need for trans-competent psychotherapy that acknowledges personal histories and gender realities while addressing sociopolitical barriers to care. clinicians should develop competencies in gender diversity and trauma-informed care. future research should include more diverse samples across gender identities and age groups, as well as comparative evaluations of care models, to inform evidence-based guidelines for tgd-affirming practice. journal of homosexuality

childhood exposure to interparental conflict and adolescent mental health difficulties: the mediating role of self-regulation difficulties. interparental conflict (ipc) in early childhood is associated with mental health difficulties in adolescence. general psychological processes such as self-regulation that may underpin this relationship are important to understand during this developmental stage. the aim of the study was to investigate whether indicators of self-regulation difficulties in middle childhood, including (a) difficulties with persistence, (b) emotional reactivity, (c) behavioral disinhibition, and (d) sleeping difficulties, mediated the relationship between ipc in early childhood and mental health difficulties (anxiety and depressive symptoms; antisocial behavior) in adolescence. a second aim was to determine whether child sex moderated the associations between ipc, self-regulation difficulties, and mental health difficulties. structural equation modeling using data from a population-based australian sample (= 9,476) supported a mediation model where higher ipc at age 4-5 years was associated with higher indications of self-regulation difficulties at age 10-11 years, which in turn predicted higher depressive symptoms, anxious symptoms, and antisocial behavior at age 14-15 years. evidence of moderation by child sex was found. the relationship between ipc, indicators of self-regulation difficulties, and antisocial behavior was stronger for males than females, while the relationship between indicators of self-regulation difficulties and internalizing outcomes was stronger for females compared to males. these results are interpreted using perspectives on biopsychosocial development, and implications for intervention at multiple time points are discussed. “are we there to determine what happened or not?”: a thematic analysis of psychiatrists’ lived experiences supporting minors who are victims of incest. objective: minors who are victims of incest experience long-lasting psychological distress and are more likely to require inpatient treatment in child and adolescent mental health services. while psychiatrists have a critical position in mental health care delivery, they report difficulties identifying and working with these situations. we aimed to explore psychiatrists' lived experiences supporting minors who are victims of incest and suggest solutions to their specific needs.
method: we conducted a reflexive thematic analysis of 11 semistructured interviews with psychiatrists working in various settings across two cities in southwestern france. we involved a qualitative research group to gather multiple perspectives on the data, refine the study's design, and organize triangulation sessions during coding and definition of themes.
results: our analysis produced three main themes. first, the barriers and factors facilitating the identification of incest in everyday practice, with professionals striving to create a safe environment to foster the therapeutic relationship rather than systematically assessing the occurrence of incest. second, the doubt and uncertainty psychiatrists aim to manage by distancing themselves from the search of an objective truth. third, the necessity to share information to ensure the victims' safety and foster health care delivery while supporting the patients through unwanted consequences of their disclosure.
conclusions: providing psychiatrists with sufficient time to receive young persons and their families, assessing traumatic exposure in other family members, supporting early detection, increasing medical training on incest, and facilitating the availability of social and legal services constitute first steps toward a better health care delivery in this population. is existential nihilism a risk or a refuge? its paradoxical role in psychological adjustment among emerging adults emerging adulthood is a developmental period marked by heightened identity exploration and existential questioning, particularly when individuals encounter adverse life events that challenge their sense of meaning and direction. drawing on a sample of 1,811 chinese emerging adults, this study examined the mediating role of existential nihilism in the associations between negative life events and psychological adjustment. results from path analysis indicated that greater exposure to negative life events was significantly associated with stronger existential nihilistic beliefs. existential nihilism partially mediated the associations between stressful life events and both psychological outcomes. interestingly, nihilism displayed a paradoxical pattern: it was associated with lower well-being but also with fewer depressive symptoms, suggesting that nihilism may be associated with a form of emotional disengagement. these findings highlight the complex associations between nihilistic beliefs, life stress, and psychological adjustment among emerging adults, particularly within high-pressure sociocultural contexts such as contemporary chinese emerging adults. journal of humanistic psychology

csemirt: an r package for bootstrap-validated conditional standard errors of measurement in polytomous item response theory models csemirt：用于多级评分项目反应理论模型中经bootstrap验证的条件测量标准误的r包 marginal reliability summarizes measurement precision across the full latent trait distribution in a single coefficient, obscuring how precisely a scale measures at different trait levels. the conditional standard error of measurement (csem) addresses this limitation, but the csem profile is itself an estimate and depends on the item response model chosen. this paper introduces csemirt, an r package for csem analysis under the graded response model, the generalized partial credit model, the partial credit model, and the graded and rasch rating scale models. the package places all csem profiles on a common latent metric, quantifies their sampling uncertainty with delta-method and bootstrap confidence bands, tests pointwise whether competing models imply different measurement precision, and reports the trait regions in which a target conditional reliability is reached. three simulated datasets are included. csemirt is applicable to any polytomous scale development and validation context and is freely available via github. applied psychological measurement

evaluating large language models versus human therapists in generating interventions for patients with depression in psychodynamic psychotherapy. objective: recent advances in artificial intelligence, especially the rise of large language models (llms), hold great promise for transforming mental health care, but their growing integration also raises pressing questions about their ability to deliver meaningful therapeutic interventions. this study compared the capabilities of llms to those of human therapists in producing context-sensitive psychotherapy responses within 16-session supportive-expressive psychodynamic psychotherapy for patients with depression. specifically, it compared llm and human therapists on (a) the frequency and typicality of their intervention choice and (b) the quality and general helpfulness of their interventions.
method: we developed an llm-based framework composed of four specialized llm agents, each representing a different therapeutic dimension, and a judge-llm that selects the most appropriate intervention for a given context. a sample of 300 therapy session segments, each containing both human- and llm-generated responses, served as the evaluation data set. expert clinical judges assessed interventions for typicality and quality.
results: llms and human therapists relied on broadly similar intervention types. however, the contextual choice of when to use a specific type differed. human interventions were rated as generally more helpful. specifically, humans produced higher quality meaning-making interventions, while no differences were found for supportive, directive, or exploratory interventions.
conclusions: the findings suggest that under the specific locally deployed multiagent configuration tested, llms can generate a range of context-sensitive therapeutic responses but showed limitations in producing high-quality meaning-making interventions. these findings highlight both the promise and the current boundaries of such systems as supervised therapeutic adjuncts. longitudinal associations between romantic relationship involvement and quality, depression, and suicidal ideation among bisexual women. bisexual women have an increased likelihood of experiencing suicidal ideation (si) and depressive symptoms than both heterosexual and lesbian women. evidence suggests romantic relationship involvement may lead to worse mental health outcomes for bisexual individuals, even though it is frequently cited as a protective factor among heterosexual and lesbian/gay individuals. it is currently unknown whether romantic relationship involvement is associated with si among bisexual women and whether other aspects of the romantic relationship (e.g., quality, partner gender) influence mental health in this population. the present study used up to eight waves of data from bisexual young women (= 390 across waves) who participated in a longitudinal cohort study and identified as bisexual during at least two consecutive waves (range = 2-8 waves;= 3.96,= 1.93). multilevel modeling was used to assess concurrent and lagged associations between relationship involvement, quality, partner gender, and mental health. relationship involvement was not significantly associated with depression or si in concurrent or lagged analyses. in contrast, at the between-person level, participants who reported higher relationship support (on average) reported lower depressive symptoms, and participants who reported having a female partner more often (on average) reported lower depressive symptoms and si in concurrent analyses. the present findings suggest that relationship quality and partner gender, but not relationship involvement, are associated with depressive symptoms and si among bisexual women. as such, relationship quality may be a useful intervention target to improve the mental health of bisexual women. turning recommendations into action: a post-evaluation psychological service model to support families in pediatric care. pediatric psychological evaluations generate recommendations intended to guide treatment, educational planning, and service access; however, health systems often lack structured mechanisms to support families in implementing these recommendations. this study utilized a retrospective, observational design to describe the naturalistic clinical workflow of a post-evaluation psychological service model. a structured follow-up program, designed to address barriers to follow-through and enhance continuity of care within a pediatric assessment setting, was implemented and staffed by supervised postdoctoral fellows. the service provided caregiver-focused follow-up visits tailored to referral questions from evaluating psychologists and family-identified needs. medical records and referral forms were reviewed and coded for referral targets, family-reported barriers, and clinician-provided services. between september 2023 and april 2025, a total of 154 families participated (patient age = 8.29 years,= 3.59), with common diagnoses including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, language disorders, and anxiety. overall, families were referred for follow-up across diverse domains, most frequently troubleshooting service access (72%), educational programming (68%), current concerns (56%), and medication management (45%). caregivers reported at least one barrier to recommendation implementation in 83% of cases, with the most common challenges involving access to behavioral/mental health services (52%) and educational supports (41%). clinicians addressed multiple areas per family, most often providing guidance on educational programming (61%), symptom management (60%), assessment of current functioning (56%), and referral coordination (51%). these findings highlight substantial unmet service needs following pediatric psychological evaluation and demonstrate the feasibility of a structured follow-up psychological program embedded within a larger pediatric health care system. integrating post-evaluation support into pediatric assessment programs may improve care coordination, reduce implementation barriers, enhance the practical utility of recommendations, and improve
