toward the operationalization of self-compassion: a behavior analytic conceptual framework for practitioner development abstract burnout, compassion fatigue, secondary traumatic stress, and attrition represent significant and growing challenges in applied behavior analysis. these challenges all collectively impact practitioner well-being, yet strategies to support such well-being initiatives have received limited systematic attention in the behavior-analytic literature. in this discussion, i posit that the concept of self-compassion represents an important gap in supporting practitioner well-being. self-compassion, as defined by neff, includes three interrelated components: (1) responding to personal suffering with kindness rather than self-judgment, (2) recognizing struggle as part of the shared human condition, and (3) maintaining balanced awareness of difficult emotions. across health, education, and psychology fields, self-compassion has demonstrated strong empirical support as a protective factor against burnout, emotional exhaustion, anxiety, experiential avoidance, and compassion fatigue. drawing on neff’s model and translating its components into behavior-analytic terms grounded in radical behaviorism, relational frame theory, and acceptance and commitment training, in this article, i describe a conceptual foundation for self-compassion within applied behavior analysis, propose a four-component training framework, and offer directions for future research. behavior analysis in practice

animals in behavior analysis: considerations for effective and ethical research, teaching, and practice abstract behavior analysis has a long history of using nonhuman animals in basic research, classroom teaching, and applied practice, yet discipline-specific guidance for competent and ethical animal work remains limited. this paper reviews historical and contemporary trends in animal use within behavior analysis, including the decline of traditional animal laboratories, growing interest in invertebrate models, and expansion of behavior-analytic work into homes, shelters, zoos, and other applied settings. we argue that although behavioral principles are broadly applicable, competence in animal work requires more than general behavior-analytic training. in the absence of integrated guidance for developing and evaluating that competence, behavior analysts may face serious risks to animal welfare, human safety, the relationship between behavior analysis and the broader animal behavior community, and the field’s ability to advance a comprehensive science of behavior. in response, we propose a set of six minimum standards for animal-focused work in behavior analysis: (1) interdisciplinary knowledge of animal behavior, (2) species-specific knowledge, (3) skill fluency, (4) ethical conduct, (5) safe practices, and (6) appropriate mentorship strategies. a practical self-assessment tool accompanies these standards to help professionals determine their scope of competence. we hope these standards initiate a needed conversation about what is required to work with animals competently in behavior analysis and support the development of guidelines as structured, explicit, and carefully maintained as those established for human-focused work. behavior analysis in practice

inhibitory control assessed by neuropsychological tests in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review of the western and central european literature. background: inhibitory control (ic) is a core executive function impaired in both attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (adhd) and autism spectrum disorder (asd). no systematic review has yet synthesized ic profiles across both disorders using standardized neuropsychological tasks in western and central european pediatric populations.
objectives: the objective of this study was to map ic deficits across four inhibitory domains in children and adolescents with adhd and/or asd. all cross-disorder observations reflect indirect comparisons from separate bodies of literature, as no included study directly compared both disorders within the same sample.
methods: pubmed and scopus were systematically searched (2000-2025). two independent reviewers screened 129 records following preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (prisma) 2020 guidelines. quality was appraised using the newcastle-ottawa scale and the joanna briggs institute (jbi) checklist. a narrative synthesis was conducted due to substantial heterogeneity across paradigms and populations.
results: ten studies met inclusion criteria (7 adhd, 3 asd; ≥ 667). adhd was linked to response disinhibition, elevated reaction time (rt) variability, and impaired post-error adaptation. asd showed difficulties in prepotent response suppression and self-monitoring, with motor inhibition largely preserved.
conclusions: the separate adhd and asd literatures suggest potentially different inhibitory profiles based on indirect evidence. these findings support multi-domain ic assessment and provide an empirical baseline for future cross-cultural research in non-western populations. applied neuropsychology-child

a scoping review of wellbeing measures for culturally and linguistically diverse high school students this review article critically examined the psychometric instruments available for assessing the wellbeing of culturally and linguistically diverse (cald) high school students within school settings. drawing on a scoping review methodology, an extensive search of embase, psycinfo, scopus and web of science identified 40 wellbeing measures published between january 2000 and april 2023. these instruments assessed various domains of wellbeing, including academic, cultural, emotional, mental health, physical, social and trauma-related aspects, in students from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds (cald), aged 10 to 18. the review highlighted the relevance, reliability and validity, and cultural suitability, appropriateness and sensitivity of these tools for use with cald populations. findings offered psychologists and counsellors working in schools, and allied health professionals a comprehensive resource to guide the selection and application of appropriate assessment tools, inform intervention planning and support the psychosocial adjustment of cald students. this synthesis also identified gaps in current measures and outlined directions for future research and culturally responsive tool development in educational contexts. journal of psychologists and counsellors in schools

mental health problems and internet usage characteristics among adolescents who have experienced cybervictimization / problemas de salud mental y características del uso de internet entre adolescentes víctima de ciberacoso the internet provides various opportunities but also presents risks, such as cybervictimization. this cross-sectional study aimed to examine internet usage characteristics and mental health problems among adolescents who had experienced cybervictimization. based on the cyber victimization scale (cvs), the sample included 42 cybervictims and 42 non-victim controls. all participants were administered the internet addiction scale (ias), screen for child anxiety-related emotional disorders scale (scared), child depression inventory (cdi), child behavior checklist for ages 6–18 (cbcl/6–18), and ksads-pl-dsm-5. cybervictims had significantly higher ias, scared, and cdi scores, as well as higher cbcl internalizing, externalizing, and total problem scores. additionally, major depressive disorder (mdd) was significantly higher in the cybervictim group. the study showed that good peer relationships and a later age at the onset of internet use were associated with a reduced risk of cybervictimization, while daily internet use of three hours or more was associated with an increased risk of cybervictimization. consequently, this study contributes to understanding the internet usage characteristics and mental health problems of cybervictims and emphasizes the importance of developing prevention and intervention programs for cybervictimization. studies in psychology

a cross-national comparison of physical fitness, physical activity, and motivational climate among adolescent girls in iran and hungary this study compared physical fitness, physical activity, and motivational climate among adolescent girls in iran and hungary within the frameworks of self-determination theory and achievement goal theory. a cross-sectional study was performed among 539 girl students aged 13–15 years (mean age = 13.93; sd = 0.82 years). data were analysed using factorial anova, independent t-tests, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modelling. hungarian students demonstrated higher performance in most physical fitness tests and had higher body mass index values (p = 0.002). physical activity levels differed only at age 14 (p = 0.019, r = −0.18), with no significant differences at other ages. iranian students reported higher perceptions of motivational climate dimensions. the measurement model showed good fit (χ2(143) = 1.81; cfi = 0.99; tli = 0.99; srmr = 0.03; rmsea = 0.039), and structural equation modelling indicated that only task-involving climate was positively associated with physical activity (β = 0.325, p = 0.003), while other motivational dimensions were not significant. the findings demonstrated that although physical fitness and motivational climate dimensions differed across both countries, physical activity levels remained relatively similar among groups. this implies that intrinsic motivational climate may be related to physical activity participation. however, differences in physical activity levels in each country could be attributed to other variables such as education, culture, socioeconomic status, environment, among others. task-involving climate emerged as the only dimension of motivational climate associated significantly with physical activity, suggesting a potential association between task-involving climate and active lifestyles among adolescent girls. adolescents

adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the appearance- related social media consciousness scale (asmc) in argentina the widespread use of social media has raised concerns about its impact on body image,particularly through the internalization of appearance ideals. this study aimed to adapt andevaluate the psychometric properties of the appearance-related social media consciousness(asmc) scale for the argentine population. a total of 751 adults participated. the scalewas translated, culturally adapted, and examined through exploratory and confirmatoryfactor analyses. results supported a one-factor structure consistent with the original scale,with adequate internal consistency and marginal model fit even after adding theoreticallyinformed modifications. only configural invariance across gender was supported; metricinvariance was not established. this adapted version of the asmc scale shows promiseas a reliable tool for assessing appearance-related consciousness in social media contextsin argentina, though further refinement and validation work is warranted. these findingsemphasize the importance of considering digital environments when evaluating bodyimage concerns and provide a foundation for future research and interventions. the studycontributes to cross-cultural research on the psychological effects of social media andhighlights the need for locally validated instruments in global media contexts international journal of psychological research

factors associated with appearance-based social comparison in brazilian college women objective. the aim of this paper was to examine the association between appearance-based social comparison and eating disorder symptoms, body satisfaction, depressive symptoms, drive for muscularity, self-esteem, and physical activity in brazilian college women. method. the participants were 542 college women aged 18 to 30. a questionnaire was used to collect information on appearance comparisons, eating disorders symptoms, body satisfaction, depressive symptoms, drive for muscularity, self-esteem, and physical activity. a multiple linear regression was conducted adjusted by age, marital status, body mass index, and economic level. results. the model that best explained the appearance comparisons scores variation included eating disorders symptoms (β= .385; p< .001), body satisfaction (β= -.200; p< .001), depressive symptoms (β= .169; p< .001), and drive for muscularity (β= .091; p< .05). conclusion. eating disorders, depressive symptoms, drive for muscularity, and body satisfaction were associated with appearance comparisons. actualidades en psicologia

learning about social inequalities increases children's moral and prosocial actions to support marginalized groups. drawing on intergroup contact theory and the social reasoning developmental model, these studies investigated how perceiving (study 1) and learning about (study 2) social inequalities involving immigrants in the u.s. informed 8- to 11-year-old american children's moral and prosocial actions to support immigrant peers and families. in study 1 (n = 132, 64% girls, 61% white, in 2024), children with stronger perceptions of inequalities, and in some cases children with more positive attitudes about immigrants, took more moral and prosocial actions (βs .24-.70). in study 2 (n = 458, 49% girls, 42% white, in 2024-2025), children received either evidence of inequalities via stories about immigrant families navigating social systems (critical contact), evidence of cooperative relationships via stories about intergroup friendships (positive contact), or both types of evidence via stories combining family and friendship (critical + positive contact). critical contact increased children's perceptions of inequalities (βs = .19) with positive effects on actions (βs .18-.28). although positive contact did not change children's intergroup attitudes, these attitudes were also associated with actions (βs .13-.72). overall, children who learned about inequalities in their societies through developmentally tailored stories subsequently took more moral and prosocial actions to support marginalized groups. child development

early erp processing of self-referential language processing in voluntary and involuntary action contexts: n170 and epn abstract understanding how the brain differentiates self from others through language represents an important topic in psychology, linguistics, and social cognition. within an embodied cognition framework, the present eeg study investigated early neural responses to isolated german pronouns varying in self-relatedness (self-, other-, and self/other-related) and grammatical type (personal vs. possessive). forty right-handed native german speakers silently read visually presented pronouns while eeg activity was recorded. two task contexts were employed, involving voluntary and involuntary keypress responses following stimulus presentation. event-related potential (erp) analyses revealed significant modulations of the n170 and early posterior negativity (epn) components. n170 amplitudes varied as a function of pronoun type and self-relatedness, with self-related and other-related pronouns eliciting different responses from ambiguous second-person forms. epn amplitudes differed across self-reference categories, with additional interactions involving hemisphere and pronoun type. together, these findings suggest that even minimal linguistic stimuli such as pronouns engage early neural processes sensitive to self-relatedness and linguistic context. task conditions also differed in early erp amplitudes; because responses in the immediate-response condition overlapped the erp measurement intervals, these differences are reported without functional attribution. psychological research-psychologische forschung

the relation between mindfulness and mentalizing among individuals with borderline personality disorder: a controlled study. mentalizing-the capacity to consider mental states-is a core human ability, yet processes related to it remain poorly understood. mindfulness has been proposed as functionally related to mentalizing, but the nature and direction of this relation remain unclear. although both are relevant to borderline personality disorder (bpd), research has rarely examined them together. this study examined group differences in and associations between dispositional mindfulness and mentalizing among individuals with bpd, psychiatric controls (pcs), and healthy controls (hcs). participants were 153 adults (51 per group) completing diagnostic and laboratory assessments. mindfulness was measured with the five facet mindfulness questionnaire, and mentalizing with the mentalization scale and reflective functioning scale applied to the brief reflective function interview. the bpd group showed markedly lower mindfulness than pcs and hcs (= 0.80-2.40,< .001). self-reported mentalizing differences were smaller: bpd participants scored lower than hcs (= -0.51), but not pcs. observer-rated mentalizing showed no overall group effect; the bpd group scored lower than pc in planned comparisons. mindfulness was positively associated with self-reported mentalizing (< .001), but not with observer-rated mentalizing (= .03,= .69). mindfulness impairments were particularly pronounced in bpd, whereas mentalizing differences were smaller and varied across methods. self-reported mindfulness and mentalizing were positively associated, underscoring the value of examining directionality and functional relations while explicitly integrating mindfulness into theoretical models of bpd. the role of temperament and personality traits in the development of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adhd) from late childhood through adolescence. individual differences in temperament and personality traits may shed light on the presentation and development of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adhd) across adolescence. the present study used multimethod, longitudinal data from a large sample of mexican-origin youth (= 674; 50% girls) to examine associations between adhd symptoms (including combined, hyperactive-impulsive, and inattentive subtypes) and a wide range of temperament and personality traits assessed via self-, mother-, and father-reports and coded observational data. first, we found moderate 1-year rank-order stabilities of combined, hyperactive-impulsive, and inattentive adhd symptoms (rs ranging from .27 to .51) but relatively low 8-year rank-order stability from age 10 to 17 (= .19 for combined); 8-year stability was higher for boys than girls. second, hyperactive-impulsive and inattentive symptoms were both negatively correlated with concurrent effortful control and conscientiousness and positively correlated with impulsivity, negative emotionality, and neuroticism; in addition, hyperactive-impulsive symptoms were positively associated with surgency and extraversion. third, bivariate latent growth curve models showed that the levels and slopes of effortful control (and its facets) and negative emotionality (particularly the frustration, aggression, and depressed mood facets) were significantly related to the levels and slopes of adhd symptom trajectories. findings from random-intercept cross-lagged panel models showed that temperament domains and adhd symptoms had meaningful between- and within-person associations but no significant cross-lagged associations. associations were stronger for adolescent self-reports of temperament/personality than for mother-reports. overall, findings highlight connections between temperament and personality traits with adhd symptoms across adolescence. the ontogenetic roots of understanding others: how action anticipation develops in infancy. anticipating others' goal-directed actions is a core component of social cognition, yet its developmental trajectory and underlying mechanisms remain debated. in this longitudinal eye-tracking study, 107 infants were assessed at 6, 10, and 14 months. spontaneous (first-trial) and experience-based (trial-by-trial) action anticipation were distinguished during repeated goal-directed grasping actions, and associations with motor development and maternal sensitivity were examined. spontaneous anticipation increased with age, with highest response rates at 14 months, whereas experience-based changes in anticipation were evident in 10-month-olds. individual differences in motor abilities-particularly fine motor skills and action-perception integration-were linked to changes across trials (experience-based anticipation), whereas maternal sensitivity was not significantly associated with spontaneous or experience-based anticipation. the findings provide novel longitudinal evidence that individual variability in motor competence and action-perception integration relates to the development of action anticipation in infancy. people underestimate how much dissimilar others want to connect. people systematically underestimate the extent to which dissimilar others are interested in socially connecting, a phenomenon we refer to asacross six experiments, in the lab (= 795), online (= 2,681), and in the field (n = 457), we document this pessimism across multiple kinds of dissimilarity, including age, race, personality, job type, and sociocultural background. we explore two psychological processes that appear associated with these effects: greater uncertainty about how interested others are in connecting, relative to one's own interest in connecting; and a tendency for the thoughts that spontaneously come to mind about an interaction to skew negative when imagining how a partner might perceive them. we also find that people's overly pessimistic beliefs are associated with their choice of whom to approach, identifying a previously underappreciated antecedent of "homophily," people's tendency to associate with similar others. in other words, people may avoid dissimilar others not because they themselves are uninterested or because they lack the opportunity-the two explanations most commonly offered in the literature-but because they mistakenly believe dissimilar others are uninterested in them. finally, we conduct a field experiment in collaboration with mystery minds, an organization dedicated to connecting employees across differences, and find that this pessimism emerges before naturally occurring workplace conversations, even among people who had opted into meeting dissimilar colleagues and personally welcomed the interaction. together, these findings advance our understanding of metaperception, intergroup interaction, homophily, and the social cognition of conversation. context matters, doesn't it? the role of context in everyday emotion regulation strategy use. a common maxim holds that "context is everything." this perspective transformed the field of emotion regulation, which evolved from understandingregulation strategies people use, to understandingstrategy use varies by context (i.e., strategy-situation fit). theoretical accounts suggest contextual features are crucial in guiding strategy use. however, empirical evidence is isolated in piecemeal studies with inconclusive results. to comprehensively explore context-dependent emotion regulation, we need data on emotion regulation across many contexts, at scale. combining up to 11 experience-sampling data sets collected from belgian and australian samples in an integrative analysis (= 500-1,696,= 27,023-101,114,= 25.38 years, 71% women), we examined how regulation-strategy use varies as a function of three theory-derived contextual features-,, and(i.e., the presence and closeness of others). we found limited support that context matters for daily emotion-regulation strategy use. our study provides a well-powered foundational step to test a theory central to emotion-regulation research and highlights the complexity of capturing strategy-situation fit in daily life. psychological science

the memory integrated language test: cross-validation of a web-based performance validity test. 记忆整合语言测试：一项基于网络的绩效效度测试的交叉验证 the memory integrated language test (mil) is a novel web-based performance validity test (pvt) with promising initial psychometric properties. this study cross-validated the mil in a diagnostically diverse clinical sample using a criterion-grouping design. three aims were examined: (a) evaluate classification accuracy for identifying performance invalidity and determine cut scores maximizing sensitivity (≥.50) while maintaining specificity ≥.90; (b) examine psychometric properties across diagnostic groups and levels of cognitive impairment; and (c) assess construct validity. participants were 177 adults (= 35.68;= 15.20; 63% female; 33% non-hispanic white; 23% hispanic; 26% black/african american; 11% asian; 7% other). based on five independent criterion pvts, participants were classified as valid (≤1 pvt failure,= 154) or invalid (≥2 pvt failures,= 23). the valid group was further categorized into mild cognitive impairment (= 28), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (= 59), and psychiatric (= 52) groups. in the overall sample, the mil demonstrated outstanding classification accuracy (a significant area under the curve = .96), with a cutoff score of ≤44 (96% sensitivity/91% specificity). across diagnostic groups, the mil maintained outstanding classification accuracy (area under the curve = .90-.97) with strong sensitivity and specificity. convergent validity analyses indicated expected associations with other memory-based pvts, while discriminant validity analyses yielded weak associations with executive function and memory domains. supplemental analysis using a ≥1 pvt failure threshold yielded acceptable classification accuracy (area under the curve = .78), with a cutoff score of ≤44 (53% sensitivity/96% specificity). findings indicate that the mil is a psychometrically robust freestanding pvt. the body acceptance by others scale-2: an examination of its psychometric properties in adults from greece the 13-item body acceptance by others scale-2 (baos-2) measures generalised perceptions of body acceptance by others. here, we examined the psychometric properties of a novel greek translation of the baos-2. we asked 1009 greek adults (age range 18-72 years) to complete the baos-2, alongside additional validated measures used to assess construct validity. exploratory factor analysis in a first split-half subsample (n = 505) showed that a unidimensional model with all 13 items had acceptable fit. this model also had acceptable fit when examined using confirmatory factor analysis in a second split-half subsample. composite reliabilities were adequate in both subsamples (ω = .95) and the unidimensional model evidenced complete measure invariance across subsamples. however, we found evidence of differential item functioning (dif), with age, body mass index (bmi), and gender identity affecting responding to about half of the items in total. in addition, younger age and higher bmis were associated with lower body acceptance by others. our results also supported the convergent (positive associations with body appreciation, negative associations with internalisation of appearance ideals and social appearance anxiety), concurrent (positive associations with self-esteem, compassionate self-responding, and perceived social support), and discriminant validity (weak association with social desirability) of the greek baos-2. finally, incremental validity was supported insofar as a body acceptance by others predicted body appreciation over-and-above internalisation of appearance ideals. these results suggest that the greek baos-2 had adequate psychometric properties, although future users of this instrument should be cautious about dif for group-based comparisons. body image

siren: a python package for automated psychometric scale shortening using document embeddings. siren：使用文档嵌入自动缩短心理测量量表的python包 siren (semantic item reduction engine) is an open-source python package that shortens unidimensional and multidimensional scales from item text alone, without respondent data. items are encoded as transformer-based embeddings, and scale reduction is framed as constrained optimization over the resulting similarity matrix: retained items maximize within-dimension coherence or coverage while minimizing between-dimension similarity, subject to user-specified item counts per dimension. ant colony optimization is the default search, with slsqp, genetic algorithm, and simulated annealing alternatives. diagnostic functions report coverage of dropped items, benchmark any short form against random subsets, and flag redundant items. siren runs on windows, linux, and macos and is installable from pypi. applied psychological measurement

scheitern auf probe: reallabore zwischen experimenteller offenheit und politischen zielvorgaben zusammenfassung dieser beitrag in der zeitschrift „gruppe. interaktion. organisation. (gruo)“ diskutiert spannungen zwischen experimenteller offenheit und politischen zielvorgaben in der aktuellen reallaborpraxis. einerseits zielen politische bestrebungen (z. b. vorgegeben durch nachhaltigkeitsziele) auf sozial-ökologische transformationen, andererseits impliziert der experimentcharakter offenheit für überraschungen und nichtlineare dynamiken, die mit zielharmonisierung in konflikt geraten können. der beitrag nutzt historische perspektiven zur entstehung des konzepts der realexperimente, um diese ambivalenz zu verdeutlichen, und analysiert exemplarisch verschiedene ausführungen aktueller „reallabore“. dabei zeigt sich, dass praktiken der akzeptanzbeschaffung gewöhnlich vorrang vor ergebnisoffenen experimenten erhalten. der beitrag plädiert für eine reflexive reallaborforschung, die das scheitern, den eigensinn der stakeholder sowie die damit verbundene demokratische legitimation ernst nimmt und die experimentelle offenheit als eigenständiges gemeinwohlziel einstuft. gio-gruppe-interaktion-organisation-zeitschrift fuer angewandte organisationspsychologie

interkulturelle kompetenzentwicklung in der polizei: kurzfristige prä-post-veränderungen im basismodul eines flächendeckenden organisationsentwicklungsprogramms zusammenfassung dieser beitrag in der zeitschrift „ gruppe. interaktion. organisation. (gio)“ untersucht kurzfristige prä-post-veränderungen nach dem basismodul eines flächendeckenden interkulturellen qualifizierungsprogramms der landespolizei sachsen-anhalt. das programm ist als mehrstufiges organisationsentwicklungsvorhaben angelegt. in einer theoriegeleiteten explorativen evaluation wurden sieben kognitive, motivationale, affektive und sozial-affektive indikatoren erhoben ( n = 870 prä-messungen; n = 532–541 gematchte paare). nach holm-korrektur für multiples testen zeigten sich statistisch belastbare veränderungen beim flexiblen denken ( d = 0,24, 95 %-ki [0,15; 0,33]) und bei der interkulturellen selbstwirksamkeit ( d = 0,16, 95 %-ki [0,07; 0,24]); nur der erste befund erreicht nach den vorab verwendeten konventionen die schwelle eines kleinen effekts. für kulturelle sensibilität, die drei empathiedimensionen und interpersonales vertrauen ergaben sich keine robusten prä-post-unterschiede. das design erlaubt weder eine kausale attribution zum basismodul noch aussagen zu verhaltenstransfer oder organisationalen wirkungen. der beitrag diskutiert daher vor allem, wie training, führung, supervision und evaluation in einer bürokratisch strukturierten polizei zu einer werteorientierten und lernenden organisationsentwicklung verbunden werden können. gio-gruppe-interaktion-organisation-zeitschrift fuer angewandte organisationspsychologie

experimentieren zwischen stabilität und wandel zusammenfassung dieser beitrag in der zeitschrift „gruppe. interaktion. organisation. (gio)“ untersucht anhand einer empirischen fallstudie aus dem inqa-projekt „agilkom“ die rolle experimenteller organisationsentwicklung in der öffentlichen verwaltung. im fokus stehen organisationale experimentierräume als geschützte lern- und erprobungsräume, in denen neue formen von zusammenarbeit, führung und arbeitsorganisation getestet werden können, ohne die stabilität der gesamtorganisation zu gefährden. die ergebnisse zeigen, dass solche experimentellen settings helfen können, spannungsfelder zwischen stabilität und veränderung sowie kontrolle und selbstorganisation produktiv zu bearbeiten. hervorgehoben wird insbesondere die bedeutung von führung als legitimierende und schützende instanz für explorative prozesse. zugleich wird personalentwicklung als zentrale vermittlungsinstanz sichtbar, die organisationale veränderungsprozesse moderiert und begleitet. ziel des beitrags ist die diskussionen zu experimenteller organisationsentwicklung und ambidextrie um die perspektiven zur führung und veränderungsfähigkeit in der öffentlichen verwaltung zu erweitern. gio-gruppe-interaktion-organisation-zeitschrift fuer angewandte organisationspsychologie

experimentelle organisationsentwicklung in institutionellen kontexten: spannungsfelder und gestaltungslogiken der inqa-experimentierräume zusammenfassung dieser beitrag in der zeitschrift „gruppe. interaktion. organisation. (gio)“ zeigt anhand der inqa-experimentierräume, wie experimentelle organisationsentwicklung in institutionellen kontexten gelingen kann. im mittelpunkt stehen die vom bundesministerium für arbeit und soziales geförderten inqa-experimentierräume, die organisationen einen finanziell abgesicherten und zugleich geschützten rahmen bieten, um neue formen der zusammenarbeit, beteiligung und anpassung zu erproben. wir beschreiben den aufbau dieses rahmens sowie den zugrunde liegenden prozess und verdeutlichen, wie experimentieren als strukturierter lernmodus in transformationsprozessen wirken kann. dabei wird insbesondere herausgearbeitet, dass die förderung nicht nur einzelnen beteiligten unternehmen zugutekommt, sondern durch gezielten breitentransfer kleine und mittlere unternehmen in ganzen branchen und regionen erreichen kann. so entstehen über den einzelfall hinaus impulse für die verbreitung innovativer arbeits- und organisationspraktiken. es werden indes auch konzeptimmanente spannungsfelder sichtbar. insgesamt leistet das beispiel einen beitrag zum verständnis, wie organisationen durch experimentelle, beteiligungsorientierte entwicklungsformate ihre resilienz in transformationsprozessen stärken können. gio-gruppe-interaktion-organisation-zeitschrift fuer angewandte organisationspsychologie

acceptance and commitment therapy integrated with feminist therapy following intimate partner violence: a case study posttraumatic stress disorder (ptsd) is a debilitating mental health concern following the experience of a traumatic event, such as sexual assault. acceptance and commitment therapy (act) and feminist therapy have each demonstrated promise in the treatment of ptsd, particularly in survivors of sexual assault and intimate partner violence (ipv). there is nascent theoretical support for the integration of act and feminist therapy for ptsd due to their shared contextual conceptualization of suffering. the present study describes the integration of act and feminist therapy with luna, a young woman recovering from sexual assault in an abusive romantic relationship. quantitative outcomes, including percentile ranks and percent changes are presented alongside luna’s self-described outcomes. at the end of treatment, luna reported quantitative improvements in anxiety, depression, eating concerns, and distress. she also described improvements in values-based action, psychological flexibility, and personal empowerment. limitations, including the brief course of treatment and measurement considerations, are discussed. future research should continue to explore the integration of act and feminist therapy for the treatment of ptsd for ipv. clinical case studies

holding the tension: reflections of a presidency in a division at an inflection point in this address, i offer reflections on my year as president of the society of counseling psychology amid political backlash, institutional uncertainty, and organizational change. i explore how overlapping threats to education, research, and human dignity reshaped the priorities of my presidency, the field, and the division. the resultant lessons reflect the challenges of balancing vision with care, urgency with sustainability, and advocacy with stewardship. i invite us to consider what it means to remain faithful to our values when the conditions for putting them into practice change. ultimately, this is an invitation to counseling psychologists to ask what this moment requires of our science, training, practice, leadership, and relationships with the communities we serve and represent. i proffer holding tensions as a shared responsibility: remaining connected, confronting difficult truths, and building a profession capable of meeting the demands of an uncertain future. counseling psychologist

the moderating role of anger rumination and self-control in the day-to-day associations between irritability and sleep in male adolescents: an exploratory experience sampling method study. background: irritability is highly prevalent in adolescents and may be exacerbated by sleep disturbances, with sleep patterns undergoing significant changes during this developmental period. reciprocally, poor sleep may generate an increase in anger dysregulation. this exploratory study investigates the day-to-day associations between sleep and irritability, as well as the moderating effects of maladaptive (i.e., anger rumination) and adaptive (i.e., self-control) emotion regulation (er) strategies.
methods: fifty-six male adolescents aged 12-18, with diverse sleep and emotional problems, participated in a 9-day experience sampling method study. participants also completed self-report questionnaires assessing irritability, sleep quantity and quality, and maladaptive and adaptive er strategies. linear mixed effect models with lagged covariates were used to test associations and moderating effects.
results: at the within-person level, sleep quality was associated with next-day irritability (std = -0.92, 95% ci [-1.31, -0.53). higher daily anger rumination (std = 0.25, 95% ci [0.17, 0.34]), and daily self-control (std = -0.18, 95% ci [-0.27, -0.10]) were directly associated with higher next-day irritability. at the between-person level, lower self-control was also associated with higher next-day irritability (std = -0.52, 95% ci [-0.77, -0.27]). interactions between daily sleep quality and between-person anger rumination ( = 0.18, 95% [0.07, 0.30]), and self-control ( = 0.75, 95% ci [0.38, 1.12]) were related with irritability. reciprocally, lower irritability from the day was associated with better sleep quality the following night (std = -0.11, 95% ci [-0.20, -0.01]).
conclusion: these preliminary findings suggest that sleep may be related to next-day irritability in adolescent boys and may vary as a function of anger rumination and self-control. additionally, irritability also showed a potential association with subsequent sleep. however, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small, all-male adolescent sample. future studies including larger and more diverse adolescent samples are needed to assess their generalizability and robustness. jcpp advances

sexual distress and function in sexual and gender minorities: a finnish population-based study. sexual and gender minorities consistently report worse physical and mental health compared to the majority population. differences in sexual health have been studied less, especially among smaller minority subgroups such as asexual and non-binary people. we explored sexual function and distress in a finnish population-based survey from 2019 ( = 8,589), comparing sexual and gender minorities with one another and with the heterosexual and cisgender population. sexual distress was highest among bisexual men and women and lowest among asexual women, emerging identity men, and heterosexual men. sexual desire was highest among bisexual women and gay men, and lowest among asexual men and women. lesbian women had the highest sexual arousal and satisfaction, and the lowest rates of pain and orgasm difficulties of all women. gay, asexual, and emerging identity men experienced less early ejaculation than heterosexual men. sexual distress did not differ significantly between cisgender and gender minority people even though trans men and trans women had the highest mean distress. we found no indications that queer, pansexual, demisexual, non-binary, or asexual people suffer from more problems with sexual distress and function than the majority population. our findings highlight the heterogeneity regarding sexual health in the lgbtq+ population. journal of sex & marital therapy
