“that’s what shapes who i am”: identity development and importance among diverse youth with lgbtq+ parents in the u.s identity processes, such as identity development and identity importance, can help mitigate the negative outcomes associated with stigma among youth with marginalized identities. this study qualitatively investigated identity development and importance among diverse youth with lgbtq+ parents. fifty-one youth (ages 12–25 years old) with at least one lgbtq+ parent in the united states participated. semi-structured interviews were held from december 2018 to february 2020, with questions about parent-child communication and identity. using thematic analysis, a trained team coded participants’ transcribed interview responses deductively into identity type and then inductively into five themes: function of appearance and perception of identity, feelings of representation responsibility , intersections among personal and parent/family identity , community impact on identity , and intersection of personal identities . themes support and extend previous findings on the importance of parent, family, and community contexts to identity processes among youth with lgbtq+ parents and inform law, policy, and practice. journal of adolescent research

from directive to shared leadership: the context of virtual teams building on bell and kozlowski’s (2002) framework, this study proposes that formal leaders in virtual teams can foster shared leadership by using directive behaviors that establish structural support systems. a 10-week field study of 392 team members from 70 teams across two fortune 500 companies supports the proposed model: directive leadership enhances shared leadership indirectly through team empowerment. this indirect effect is amplified when location diversity is high and perceived media richness is low. the findings contribute to the virtual teams and leadership literatures and offer practical recommendations for leaders managing distributed work. small group research

the future of eye tracking in teacher competence research: towards in-action, multimodal, mixed-methods and more theory-driven research in education mobile eye tracking has opened up new possibilities for studying teachers’ visual attention as it unfolds in authentic classroom settings, yet the field continues to face important theoretical and methodological challenges. this reflective study revisits three empirical studies, all stemming from a single large-scale mobile eye-tracking project in early childhood education, in order to develop a new theoretical framework, methodological insights, and recommendations for future eye-tracking research in education. across the three studies, quantitative eye-tracking data, stimulated recall interviews, and multimodal conversation analysis were combined to examine how teachers distribute their visual attention among children, how they reason about their own gaze behaviour, and how gaze relates to patterns of classroom interaction. these three empirical studies jointly show that linguistically vulnerable children are overlooked and that this cannot be explained with a strict dichotomy between intentional and unintentional processes, but instead operates along a continuum shaped by teachers’ expectations, beliefs, and biases. building on these insights, this study proposes adaptations to existing theoretical frameworks on teacher attention and professional vision, rendering them eye-tracking-informed, and argues for a shift towards in-action, multimodal, mixed-methods, and theory-driven eye-tracking research in educational settings. implications for future research design on data triangulation and technological development are discussed. journal of eye movement research

the impact of patient weight status on healthcare students' attitudes: two experimental studies in midwifery and dental students abstract background weight stigma refers to prejudice and discrimination based on body weight. healthcare professionals often hold negative attitudes towards patients with overweight, which can negatively affect patient care and health outcomes. however, weight stigma is yet to be explored in midwifery and dental students. methods two online experimental studies using hypothetical patient vignettes were conducted in midwifery ( n = 281; study 1) and dental and non‐dental students ( n = 528; study 2). participants were randomly assigned to view a healthy‐weight, overweight or obese patient vignette and then reported their attitudes, predicted time, advice they would provide and beliefs about obesity. data were analysed using anova and logistic regression. results in study 1, midwifery students held significantly more stigmatizing attitudes towards patients who were overweight than healthy‐weight patients; however, there was no significant difference in attitudes towards patients with obesity. predicted time spent with patients did not significantly differ as a function of patient weight status. in study 2, dental and non‐dental students reported more stigmatizing attitudes towards overweight and obese patients compared to healthy‐weight patients. predicted time spent with patients did not differ significantly. dental and non‐dental students were more likely to offer lifestyle‐related advice to overweight and obese patients. there was no significant relationship between beliefs about obesity and attitudes towards treating patients. conclusions weight stigma is evident among healthcare students and can affect healthcare advice. increased awareness of potential biases in midwives and dental students is needed and should form formal training to improve equitable healthcare delivery. british journal of health psychology

the relationships between career adaptability, psychological capital, social capital, and personality traits: a network analysis abstract with the effects of globalization and digitalization, the business world and labor markets have undergone massive changes in recent decades, including the skills and abilities that individuals in the workforce need to possess. career adaptability therefore, has attracted growing attention from researchers as an important internal resource that may help individuals adapt to these changing conditions. it is well‐established in the available literature that individuals’ career adaptability is closely associated with their other dispositional, psychological, and social resources, but little is known about how these major factors interact within a system to shape outcomes. employing a network analysis approach, the present study aimed to examine the associations among career adaptability, psychological capital, social capital, and personality traits. a total of 648 undergraduates (52.3% female) from two universities in türkiye were surveyed with the measures of career adaptability, the big five personality traits, psychological capital, and social capital. ebicglasso network results demonstrated that components of psychological capital, particularly self‐efficacy and resilience, occupied the center of the network, while other nodes spread relatively peripherally. in addition, significant associations were found among the components of career adaptability, psychological capital, social capital, and personality traits. these results emphasize the importance of understanding the different roles played by each construct in the career adaptability process and underline that psychological capital resources may play a central role. career development quarterly

safety, trust, and connection with horses: adults’ lived experience of group equine‐assisted psychotherapy in substance use treatment abstract talk‐based interventions are the standard of care in substance use residential treatment, yet little is known about how adults experience alternative approaches like equine‐assisted psychotherapy (eap). this hermeneutic phenomenological study explored how 12 adults experienced group eap sessions during residential substance use treatment at three facilities in the united states, and what meaning the experience held in their overall recovery journeys. analysis of semistructured interviews yielded six themes: nervous system regulation, authentic connection, present‐moment awareness, experiential learning, transcendent meaning, and transformed perception of treatment. participants’ accounts described two facets of the horse–human encounter: experience in the arena (reset, relief, practice) and meaning in recovery (acceptance, hope, freedom). participants’ lived experience suggested that eap engaged preverbal, somatic, and relational dimensions of the recovery process. implications for clinical practice, eap practitioner training, and treatment program design are considered. journal of counseling and development

climate change anxiety and pro-environmental behavior: a systematic review of motivational and inhibitory pathways climate change anxiety (cca) is a growing psychological response to perceived and anticipated environmental threats, encompassing cognitive, emotional, and functional impairments. while cca has the potential to both motivate and hinder pro-environmental behavior (peb), its relation with sustainable action remains complex. this systematic review was conducted in accordance with prisma guidelines and synthesized empirical evidence on the relation between cca and peb. searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, pubmed, psycinfo, and ebsco for peer-reviewed english-language studies published between january 2020 and february 2026. a total of 59 empirical studies met the inclusion criteria. most studies employed cross-sectional designs with self-report measures, with some incorporating longitudinal, experimental, or cross-national approaches. results indicate that moderate levels of cca often predicted sustainable behaviors, particularly if supported by adaptive coping strategies, environmental knowledge, and high self-efficacy. conversely, high levels of anxiety may reduce engagement through eco-paralysis, especially when individuals perceive low personal or collective efficacy. several studies also identified mediating and moderating mechanisms such as environmental identity, coping strategies, future self-continuity, and climate efficacy beliefs. these findings suggest that cca can function as both a motivational and inhibiting emotional response, highlighting the importance of interventions that strengthen coping resources and perceived agency to transform climate concern into sustained environmental action. ecopsychology

the paradoxes of a pre‐reflective will to interpret: a critical comment on junghun oh's idea of ‘embodied moral reflexivity’ abstract in her recent publication in this journal, junghun oh offers an alternative reading of pierre bourdieu's notion of the habitus by invoking the ideas of ‘the will to interpret’ and ‘embodied moral reflexivity’. oh premises her analysis on the idea that there are inner interpretive processes or re‐evaluations that the habitus is assumed to allow. my main line of critique in this comment is, first, that this approach is similar to past inconsistent efforts by other authors to reconcile the irreconcilable ideas of bourdieu's habitus and self‐reflection; and, second, that, in the absence of an ontological stratum that can enable the emergence of the reflective interpreter that oh assumes, the idea that bourdieu's habitus allows for subtle reinterpretations of personal values and dominant norms is theoretically unintelligible and leads to paradoxical imageries. journal for the theory of social behaviour

rapid fear detection predicts prosocial giving abstract prosociality is fundamental to human social life, yet individuals vary widely in their willingness to incur costs for others. what drives this variation? we tested four preregistered hypotheses about whether the speed of detecting specific social stimuli (faces vs. cars, infant vs. elderly faces, fearful vs. angry faces, trustworthy vs. untrustworthy faces) is associated with prosocial giving. participants (n = 200) completed visual detection tasks, personality assessments, a director task measuring theory of mind, and two economic games: the dictator game, indexing costly giving in the absence of strategic pressure, and the ultimatum game, indexing giving under strategic constraints. one hypothesis received partial support: faster detection of fearful faces was associated with greater giving, an effect that was most robust in the dictator game and was significant in the primary analyses. robustness checks confirmed the dictator game finding across analytic approaches, while the ultimatum game effect was attenuated in analyses using robust standard errors and ordinal logistic regression. neither detection of other social stimuli, big five personality traits, facial width-to-height ratio, nor theory of mind performance reliably predicted giving. these findings suggest that absolute speed of detecting distress signals reliably predicted prosocial giving, that this effect did not reflect general processing speed, and that general social attunement, vulnerability sensitivity, and higher-order social cognition did not reliably predict giving. affective science
overprotection and stigma by compassion in mental health professional practice discover mental health

self-efficacy fluctuation and training engagement in adolescent athletes: online social feedback and the moderating role of comparison orientation. introduction: this study treats adolescent athletes' self-efficacy as a dynamic process rather than a fixed quantity, asking how its fluctuations arise in online social settings and how that volatility shapes training engagement.
methods: we recruited a stratified sample of 320 youth athletes across sport discipline, competitive tier, and sex, and combined ecological momentary assessment with weekly follow-up over 8 consecutive weeks, using instruments released under open licenses and open-source software throughout. two dispersion indices, the intraindividual standard deviation and the root mean square of successive differences, summarized fluctuation at the person level, while absolute occasion-to-occasion change indexed momentary instability at the event level. we fitted multilevel linear models, a two-level dynamic structural equation model, latent growth curve models, and multilevel structural equation models, with each path labeled by its level of analysis.
results: momentary self-efficacy showed genuine within-person temporal dependence rather than independent scatter, and its trajectory was phase-linked to the competitive calendar and unevenly distributed across individuals. between persons, fluctuation amplitude tracked the intensity of negatively valenced comparison rather than the sheer volume of feedback, and comparison orientation amplified that association on the negative arm alone. within persons, negative comparison enlarged momentary instability both immediately and at a one-occasion lag, whereas positive signals steadied confidence only briefly. amplitude was negatively associated with all three engagement facets beyond mean efficacy, most strongly for absorption, although a formal equality test separated absorption from dedication but not vigor. the direct reach of negative comparison into engagement proved facet-specific: vigor and absorption were affected, dedication was not, so the facet-by-facet hypothesis holds only in part. sensitivity analyses adding competitive-calendar phase, splitting the series by season phase, partialling the person mean and the person-specific autoregression out of the amplitude index, entering competitive tier as a covariate, and checking participant-coded valence against automated sentiment scoring left the pattern intact.
discussion: the findings extend social cognitive theory's vicarious and persuasive sources into a temporally dense digital regime and point toward protective coaching and self-regulation strategies. frontiers in psychology

pornography violence exposure scale: a graded bifactor measure of exposure to violent pornographic content. introduction: research on associations between pornography viewing and sexual violence has been limited by the absence of validated instruments that differentiate exposure along a violence continuum within pornographic practices, with existing measures focused on consumption frequency or problematic patterns rather than on the specific content consumed. the pornography violence exposure scale (pves) was developed to assess exposure to pornographic content graded across three violence levels: non-violent material and domination-without-pain (level 1), coercive content (level 2), and explicit physical aggression (level 3).
methods: a cross-sectional study with 2,181 spanish young adults aged 18-35 years who reported viewing pornography examined factor structure, measurement invariance across sex and age, convergent, nomological, and incremental validity, and discriminative capacity for sexual violence outcomes via receiver operating characteristic (roc) analysis.
results: a bifactor model demonstrated good fit (cfi = 0.978, tli = 0.957, rmsea = 0.076), with a dominant general factor (ωh = 0.84, ecv = 0.81) capturing graded exposure to violent content. strict measurement invariance was supported across sex and age groups. convergent correlations with sexual violence outcomes (mean || = 0.24) substantially exceeded near-zero nomological associations with sexual function and partner-evaluation indicators (mean |r| = 0.03), and the general factor produced significant incremental validity for both victimization (δ = 0.088) and perpetration (δ = 0.200), with acceptable discrimination for perpetration (auc = 0.753).
discussion: the pves is the first psychometrically validated instrument for measuring differentiated exposure to violent pornographic content, enabling more precise investigation of content-specific associations with sexual violence outcomes. frontiers in psychology

does consumer education with responsibility content improve drivers understanding, confidence, and use of adas after an over-the-air update objective this study explores whether consumer education (ce) with and without driver responsibility content improves drivers’ understanding and use of advanced driver-assistance systems (adas). background research suggests that ce with responsibility content may improve driver understanding; however, how other forms of learning interact, such as experiential learning, remains unclear. method eighty drivers (21–76 years) participated in a ce study using a traffic jam assist adas. the study was conducted as a 2 (ce content: ce with responsibility content and ce without responsibility content) x 2 (driver engagement instructions: hands-free and hands-on) x 3 (timing of mental model assessment (mma): pre-ce, post-ce, and post-drive). results ce with responsibility content did not significantly enhance mma understanding or confidence beyond ce without responsibility content in this study ( p > .05). regardless of responsibility content, drivers who received hands-on instructions consistently scored higher compared to hands-free instructions ( p < .01). mma confidence rating decreased at post-ce for all conditions but only returned to baseline levels at post-drive ( p < .05) for drivers who received hands-free instructions. conclusion drivers who received hands-on instructions scored higher than hands-free at all; however, other forms of learning (e.g., experiential learning) may be necessary when the system substantially changes the driver’s role. application ce may be enough to improve drivers’ understanding if an update does not alter how a driver interacts with the system, or how it aligns with their initial mental model. human factors

differences in reporting suicidality among autistic girls: comparing parent-, child self-, and clinician-rated child self-reports between distinct measures abstract purpose suicidality in autistic girls is an emerging albeit understudied concern, driven by elevated internalizing symptoms, socio-emotional challenges, and limited autism-sensitive assessments. this study examined diagnostic (autistic vs. non-autistic), informant (parent-, written child self-, clinician-rated child self-report), and measure (written self-report (cdi-2) vs. verbal interview (c-ssrs and k-sads)) differences in suicidality. it was hypothesized that (1) suicidality would be reported more in autistic than non-autistic girls, and (2) written child self-report would yield the highest suicidality endorsement rate, followed by parent- and clinician-rated child self-report. methods participants consisted of 213 autistic ( n = 112) and non-autistic ( n = 101) girls aged 6–13. suicidality was assessed using the kiddie schedule for affective disorders and schizophrenia (k-sads; parent-report), the children’s depression inventory, second edition (cdi-2; written child self-report), and the columbia suicide severity rating scale (c-ssrs; clinician-rated child self-report). results across informants/measures, autistic girls had three times greater odds of endorsing suicidality than non-autistic peers (or = 3.05, 95% ci [1.64, 5.67], p < 0.001). written child self-report yielded the highest endorsement, while parent- (or = 0.51, 95% ci [0.32, 0.82], p = 0.006) and clinician-rated child self-report (or = 0.39, 95% ci [0.24, 0.64], p < 0.001) were less likely to capture suicidality. conclusions findings highlight the role of child self-report in detecting suicidality among autistic girls and suggest that multi-informant, autism-informed approaches utilizing both written and verbal response methods can reduce underestimated risk and facilitate timely intervention. journal of autism and developmental disorders

autistic student well-being indicators at school: parent, educator, and therapist perspectives abstract purpose autistic students experience high distress and unmet support needs at school, yet there is limited school‑based evidence to guide how their well‑being is understood in everyday educational contexts. this study aimed to address this gap by examining school‑based indicators of autistic student well‑being across multiple dimensions. methods a two‑phase, multi‑informant design was used. in phase 1, qualitative data were collected from caregivers, educators, and school‑based therapists (n = 41) to identify externally observable indicators of high and low well‑being. in phase 2, a separate sample (n = 36) evaluated the perceived reliability of the most frequently identified indicators by participants in phase 1. results inductive content analysis identified 94 indicators of high well‑being and 99 indicators of low well‑being. three key findings emerged. first, indicators varied substantially in how they were expressed across students, highlighting the importance of interpreting change relative to individual baselines rather than normative expectations. second, many indicators reflected specific dimensions of well‑being and did not function as global markers across contexts. third, indicators most frequently reported were not always those judged to be most reliable, underscoring limitations of frequency‑based approaches. conclusion these findings demonstrate that autistic student well‑being at school is multidimensional, context‑dependent, and individually patterned. by clarifying how well‑being indicators are identified and interpreted in school settings, this study provides a foundation for future practice‑focused tools, professional learning, and research that supports more responsive and inclusive approaches for autistic students. journal of autism and developmental disorders
knowledge of childhood autism and care experiences in critical settings: a survey among italian nurses journal of autism and developmental disorders

interpersonal cardiac synchrony during emotional sharing between strangers abstract interpersonal physiological synchrony is well documented in close relationships, where it supports social bonding and emotion regulation; however, little is known about whether cardiac synchrony emerges during emotional interactions between strangers. here we examined interpersonal cardiac synchrony in pairs of strangers during an emotional sharing task. eighty participants (40 dyads) engaged in 15 min of emotional sharing, during which one participant recounted a negative personal experience while the other provided support. we assessed cardiac synchrony as the cross‐correlation of residualized inter‐beat interval (ibi) time series from synchronized electrocardiogram (ecg) recordings. results showed that greater mutual liking, gender match, and shared emotional perception were linked to stronger cardiac synchrony, suggesting that interpersonal synchrony reflects social and emotional alignment even between strangers. additionally, the similarity between the heart rate variability (hrv) of each interaction partner predicted greater synchrony, indicating that physiological compatibility may facilitate alignment. we also examined whether a brief mindfulness induction given to the support provider enhanced synchrony and interaction quality. however, the mindfulness induction had no significant effect, suggesting that a brief self‐regulation practice may not influence physiological alignment in first‐time interactions. these findings extend research on interpersonal cardiac synchrony beyond established relationships, identifying key factors that shape physiological alignment during emotional sharing in first‐time interactions. psychophysiology

uncertainty avoidance moderates the association between parenthood and well-being parenthood is associated with both psychological rewards and costs, and prior research has identified conditions under which it relates to higher or lower well-being. this study examines whether the relationship between parenthood and subjective well-being is moderated by uncertainty avoidance, a cultural dimension reflecting the extent to which societies respond to uncertainty. using data from 331,480 individuals across 82 countries, we found that in countries with high uncertainty avoidance, parents reported lower subjective well-being than nonparents, whereas this association was not significant in countries with low uncertainty avoidance; a similar moderation pattern was observed when the number of children was examined. these effects persisted after controlling for individual-level factors (e.g., income), country-level socioeconomic indicators (e.g., gross domestic product [gdp] per capita), and other cultural dimensions (e.g., individualism). although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, the findings suggest that the association between parenthood and subjective well-being varies across cultures and is moderated by uncertainty avoidance. social psychological and personality science
joint trajectories of maternal autonomy support and psychological control: spillover from marital satisfaction and work-family gains journal of youth and adolescence

social identities and long covid abstract social identity research has often overlooked the experiences of people with chronic health conditions and disabilities. people with long covid, who comprise over 5% of the adult population of the united states, are one such group. the present study leverages data from a sample of 10,576 adults in the united states to ask: to what degree do people with (and without) long covid identify as “disabled,” “a long hauler,” and “a covid survivor”? people with long covid ( n = 1059) identify more strongly with each of these identities than people who had recovered from long covid ( n = 1576) and those who never developed long covid ( n = 8124). in addition, while most individuals do not identify as “disabled” or as a “long hauler,” people who actively had long covid and those who had recovered from long covid identified as “covid survivors.” moreover, people who had recovered from long covid identified more strongly as “disabled” than people who never developed long covid in the first place. stronger identification with all three identities is related to greater depression. results suggest that long covid can have lasting impacts on individuals' self‐concepts and social identities. the article includes suggestions for researchers and discusses ways in which future research in this area can benefit both individuals with long covid and social psychological theory. social and personality psychology compass

leaving religion: the nature and consequences of religious deidentification research on religious deidentification is accelerating. this article summarizes the nature and consequences of leaving religion. first, i describe a theoretical model of religious deidentification. second, i review the nature of leaving religion by exploring who leaves religion, how they deidentify, and what motivations impel their decision to depart. third, i explore the consequences of leaving religion through two primary mechanistic responses: religious residue and religious reactance . “religious residue” refers to the persistence of religious cognitions, emotions, and behaviors after religious deidentification—the tendency for features of religion to continue to linger among “religious dones” (i.e., formerly religious individuals). “religious reactance” refers to the tendency to respond in attitudinally countervalenced ways after leaving religion, providing important boundary conditions for religious residue. fourth, i examine how religious dones are perceived by others and the potential intrapersonal and interpersonal costs of religious deidentification. testable hypotheses to guide future empirical research are presented. current directions in psychological science

predicting university students' intention to apply investment strategies: integrating theory of planned behavior and self-determination theory. behavioral intention is central to investment-related decision making, but belief-based predictors and motivational need satisfaction should not be conflated. this quantitative cross-sectional study examined 512 undergraduate students in jiangxi province, china, drawing on the theory of planned behavior (tpb) and self-determination theory (sdt). multiple regression tested attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control as predictors of intention to apply investment strategies; descriptive statistics and correlations separately characterised autonomy, competence, and relatedness. the tpb model explained 55.2% of the variance in intention. all three tpb predictors were statistically significant, with perceived behavioral control having the largest unstandardized coefficient (b = 0.36, p < .001). the sdt constructs had moderately high means and positive intercorrelations (r = 0.68-0.73), describing a motivational profile rather than a tested contribution to intention. the two-item subjective norm measure showed modest reliability (cronbach's α = 0.584), requiring caution in interpreting its coefficient. demographic characteristics were available for 310 respondents because institutional permissions differed, limiting assessment of the representativeness of the full analytical sample. no sdt-to-intention paths or incremental effects beyond tpb were estimated; thus, the proposed tpb-sdt integration is theoretical and interpretive, not a statistically validated joint model. the study contributes a transparent distinction between proximal tpb predictors and complementary sdt-related motivational experiences in university investment learning, while identifying the need for future joint predictive and longitudinal tests. acta psychologica

aging reshapes the response to subchronic lps: cognitive and neuroinflammatory resilience with selective amyloid vulnerability and reduced responsiveness to l-theanine and aerobic exercise. aging alters the brain's inflammatory profile, which may influence vulnerability to neuroinflammatory insults and the effectiveness of neuroprotective interventions. this study investigated whether prophylactic administration of l-theanine (lt) and aerobic exercise could attenuate behavioral and molecular changes induced by subchronic systemic lipopolysaccharide (lps) exposure in aged rats. three- and eighteen-month-old male wistar rats received lt, exercise, or both prior to repeated lps administration. behavioral assessments included working, recognition, and spatial short-term memory, followed by hippocampal analyses of inflammatory cytokines, the pcreb/creb ratio, and aβ₁-₄₂ expression. both aging and lps administration in 3-month-old rats impaired working memory, spatial short-term memory, and motor activity compared to young adult controls. unlike young adult animals, subchronic lps exposure did not impair cognitive performance in aged rats. lps exposure resulted in reduced body weight and increased aβ₁-₄₂ levels, while il-1β, tnf-α, and the pcreb/creb ratio remained unchanged in aged rats. prophylactic lt and/or aerobic exercise produced modest behavioral improvements, enhancing working memory in the y-maze, but did not significantly alter hippocampal inflammatory cytokines, the pcreb/creb ratio, or aβ₁-₄₂ expression in old rats. in conclusion, aged rats exhibited relative resistance to lps-induced cognitive and inflammatory effects but remained susceptible to amyloid-related changes. behavioural brain research

aquaporin-4 antagonist protects against acute alcohol-induced behavioral impairment. binge drinking rapidly triggers acute neurological dysfunction through direct and indirect effects on the brain. although widespread, the most affected regions govern planning and decision-making, coordination, and impulse control. here we suggest that the rapid alcohol induced behavioral impairment is mediated by water transport across the blood brain barrier. since aquaporin-4 (aqp4) channels mediate most water transport into the brain, we examined how pharmacologically inhibiting aqp4 affects behavioral output. thirty-three adult sprague dawley rats were placed into 3 conditional groups (saline, ethanol, and a&e). each group performed the same battery of behavioral assessments. spatiotemporal recordings of animal behavior were video recorded and analyzed using custom matlab scripts. acute ethanol exposure altered behavioral performance in a task-dependent manner across open field, object recognition, and elevated zero maze assays compared to saline-control trials. ethanol increased open-field center time (14.92 ± 3.37 vs 2.23 ± 0.79 s), object discrimination index (-0.03 ± 0.13 vs 0.51 ± 0.03), and zero-maze open-zone time (293.31 ± 69.60 vs 82.60 ± 19.31 s). aqp4 inhibition attenuated the ethanol induced behavioral effects for both the open field test and elevated zero maze by 81.6% and 75.3%, respectively. however, aqp4 inhibition did not protect against ethanol induced impairment for the object recognition test. our findings suggest that blocking aqp4-mediated water transport may protect against alcohol-induced disruption of context-sensitive risk-guided behavior. future studies may aim to investigate the extent to which water transport into the brain after alcohol exposure alters the neural activity associated with risk-guided behavioral output. behavioural brain research

olfactory context modulates recognition and directed forgetting of emotional faces: a chemosensory-cognitive perspective abstract olfaction has privileged access to limbic and memory-related brain regions, yet how ambient odor valence influences memory for emotional faces remains poorly understood. this study examined the effects of pleasant odor, unpleasant odor, and odorless condition on recognition accuracy, reaction time, and directed forgetting of emotional faces. in experiment 1 (study-recognition, n = 31), unpleasant odor significantly impaired recognition accuracy relative to pleasant odor and odorless condition (ps < .01) and slowed reaction times (p < .01); negative faces were recognized more accurately than positive faces (p < .01). in experiment 2 (item-method directed forgetting, n = 33), a three-way interaction (p < .05) showed that odor valence selectively modulated directed forgetting depending on face type. under pleasant odor, positive faces showed a robust directed forgetting effect (p < .01), whereas neutral faces exhibited a marginally reversed effect (p = .052). under unpleasant odor, neutral faces demonstrated a significant directed forgetting effect (p < .01). no directed forgetting was observed for negative faces across all odor conditions. these findings provide novel behavioral evidence that olfactory contexts do not simply enhance or impair memory globally but selectively tune intentional forgetting in a valence-specific manner, advancing our understanding of how chemosensory environments shape cognitive control over socially relevant emotional information. chemical senses
consensual unwanted sex and body dissatisfaction among cisgender heterosexual women and queer women/gender expansive individuals journal of sex research
prevalence of sexual acts and materials provided for financial compensation among young adults in the united states journal of sex research

temporal comparisons elicit greater pride, lower shame, and stronger improvement orientation among chinese children abstract background upward social comparisons are widely used to encourage effort, yet they often lead to negative emotions. temporal comparisons may support self‐improvement while preserving positive self‐experience. this study investigates whether temporal comparisons offer these potential benefits for chinese children. methods two between‐subjects experiments were conducted with chinese primary and secondary school students (aged 8–16 years) in autumn 2024. we manipulated comparison type and comparison direction through reading‐writing tasks. study 1 ( n = 632, 51% girls) used writing tasks involving comparisons with better or worse peers or past selves, alongside a no‐comparison control. study 2 added 285 participants (51% girls) who imagined and wrote about better or worse future selves, sharing the social‐comparison and control groups from study 1. after the tasks, participants reported pride, shame, improvement goals, and superiority goals. results past‐self comparisons elicited greater pride, less shame, and a higher improvement‐to‐superiority goal ratio than social comparisons and no comparison; comparing with a better past self elicited greater pride and lower shame than comparing with superior others. future‐self comparisons elicited greater pride, less shame, and a higher improvement‐to‐superiority goal ratio than social comparisons; comparison with a worse future self preserved greater pride than comparison with superior others. conclusions temporal comparisons, including both past‐self and future‐self comparisons, showed emotional and motivational advantages among chinese children. journal of adolescence
when the self becomes a dataset: datamaxxing and the psychology of ai-assisted self-monitoring cyberpsychology behavior and social networking

when do environmental attitudes lead to action? contextual moderation in everyday laundry practices in france this study examines when and how environmental attitudes translate into sustainable household behavior by analyzing everyday laundry practices in france. drawing on the attitude–behavior–context (abc) model and practice-oriented approaches to domestic energy use, we conducted in-depth interviews with 13 french adults. the analysis identifies four interrelated contextual moderators: temporal constraints, cleanliness norms, infrastructural limitations, and institutional trust. these factors shaped whether pro-environmental attitudes became consequential for laundering practices or were weakened, displaced, or blocked by competing domestic commitments. the findings show that the attitude–behavior gap is not simply a matter of insufficient motivation or information, but a patterned outcome of everyday practices whose material, temporal, normative, and institutional arrangements make some actions easier than others. the study contributes to environmental behavior research by specifying how contextual moderation operates in a high-frequency, culturally embedded household practice and by clarifying the abc model’s heuristic value alongside practice-oriented approaches. environment and behavior
the effect of (un)certainty appraisal on rule-based versus similarity-based categorization processes motivation and emotion

searching for the core of conspiracy belief systems: the relationship between specific beliefs and generic mentality abstract conspiracism is commonly measured through specific conspiracy beliefs and generalized conspiracy mentality, a broad tendency to suspect conspiracies behind events. researchers often assume that these measures are psychometrically distinct and that mentality accounts for correlations among beliefs. we evaluate the cross‐sectional statistical implications of these assumptions using psychological network analysis in three comparative studies spanning nearly 30,000 respondents, 17 country samples and multiple validated scales. mentality and beliefs are generally distinguishable, but their structural relationship varies across measurement strategies. with a comparative cross‐national belief battery, study 1 falsifies the mentality‐centred account in seven of eight countries; the belief‐centred account is supported in france and falsified nowhere. study 2, using salient us‐specific beliefs, points towards the mentality‐centred account, although both tests are inconclusive. with country‐specific beliefs, study 3 falsifies the mentality‐centred account in six countries and the belief‐centred account in all eight. these findings challenge the view that conspiracy mentality consistently organizes beliefs and underscore the importance of how both constructs are measured. european journal of social psychology

does the gender equality paradox in personality manifest at the within-country regional level? insights from germany, russia, and the united states the aim of this study was to contribute to the understanding of the gender equality paradox by examining within-country variation in the size of the gender gap in five-factor model (ffm) personality traits across regions in three geographically large and socially diverse countries, and to explore whether this variation was associated with various regional-level indicators. multilevel analyses were conducted to assess regional gender differences in ffm personality trait scores using data from germany (four datasets), russia (one dataset), and the us (two datasets). samples ranged from 6,476 to 29,398, with data collected between 2005 and 2017. when the size of gender differences varied across regions, we examined whether this variation was associated with regional indices of human development (shdi) and its subcomponents, gender equality, individualism/collectivism, and survival/self-expression values. regional variation in gender differences was most consistent for neuroticism, openness, and conscientiousness. in several datasets, regions with higher educational attainment, health, and individualism showed larger gender differences in these traits, consistent with the direction of the gender equality paradox observed across countries. these findings suggest that societal and contextual factors may contribute to gender differences in personality not only across countries but also across regions within countries. european journal of personality
surviving, belonging, and being recognized: a critical reappropriation of quality of life in older trans women in chile journal of homosexuality

psychological resilience profiles and associated factors in adolescents with depression and suicidal ideation: a latent profile and variable selection approach abstract to explore the heterogeneity of psychological resilience in adolescents with depression and suicidal ideation and to identify psychosocial factors associated with different resilience profiles. a total of 286 hospitalised adolescents diagnosed with depressive disorders and suicidal ideation were consecutively enroled. psychological resilience was assessed using the adolescent resilience scale. latent profile analysis (lpa) was conducted to identify resilience profiles. least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (lasso) regression was used to select variables associated with membership in the low‐ and moderate‐resilience profiles, using the high‐resilience profile as the reference category. bootstrap resampling was performed to assess the stability of variable selection. lpa identified three psychological resilience profiles: low resilience‐vulnerable (22.0%), moderate resilience‐cognitive advantage (66.8%), and high resilience‐tenacious (11.2%). social support, problem‐focused coping, and emotion‐focused coping were selected in both profile‐comparison models and showed relatively high bootstrap selection frequencies. neglectful parenting was selected only in the comparison between the low resilience‐vulnerable and high resilience‐tenacious profiles and showed comparatively lower selection stability. psychological resilience showed substantial heterogeneity among adolescents with depression and suicidal ideation. social support and coping strategies were consistently associated with resilience profile membership, whereas the association with neglectful parenting was less stable. these findings may inform future research on profile‐based psychological assessment and differentiated support strategies; however, longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal and causal relationships. stress and health

does treating maternal depression affect maternal and child hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis activity? six‐year follow‐up of a cluster randomized trial in rural pakistan abstract perinatal depression is a risk factor for adverse long‐term outcomes in both mothers and children, including stress system dysregulation. yet, it is unclear whether treating perinatal depression has lasting intergenerational effects on biological stress regulation. this study evaluated the effects of a psychosocial intervention programme initiated during the perinatal period and sustained throughout the child's early childhood (up to 5 years of age) on hair‐derived measures of hypothalamic pituitary adrenal (hpa) axis activity in mothers and their children. mothers with prenatal depression were recruited during their third trimester of pregnancy and randomly assigned to a peer‐delivered psychosocial depression intervention ( n = 283) or control ( n = 287). at six years postpartum (one year after the conclusion of the intervention), hair samples were collected from mothers ( n = 392) and children ( n = 366) and analysed for cortisol, cortisone, and dehydroepiandosterone (dhea). additionally, 584 mothers without prenatal depression were recruited during pregnancy, of which 426 mothers and 389 children provided hair samples at six years. mixed models showed no evidence of intervention effects on maternal hpa axis activity or child cortisone and dhea. in contrast, children whose mothers received the intervention exhibited higher cortisol levels relative to children in the control group, bringing them closer to cortisol levels observed in the non‐depressed group. there was also an interaction between the intervention and baseline maternal depression severity, with stronger intervention effects on cortisol among children whose mothers experienced more severe depressive symptoms during pregnancy. results suggest that treating prenatal depression can lead to durable improvements in stress system regulation in children, especially among those whose mothers had the highest symptom burden prenatally. stress and health
issue information no abstract is available for this article. social and personality psychology compass

perceived discrimination, loneliness, social anxiety, and smartphone addiction among rural left‐behind children in c hina: a two‐wave longitudinal cross‐lagged panel study abstract this study examined prospective associations between perceived discrimination (pd) and smartphone addiction (sma), and the mediating roles of loneliness and social anxiety, using a two‐wave longitudinal cross‐lagged panel design. a sample of 1773 rural left‐behind children (aged 10–15 years, mean age = 13.37, sd = 1.44; 822 boys [46.4%] and 951 girls [53.6%]) was assessed at two waves separated by 6 months. results showed that pd at t1 exhibited significant cross‐lagged associations with sma, loneliness, and social anxiety. loneliness and social anxiety each independently mediated the prospective pd–sma association. bidirectional prospective associations were observed between loneliness and social anxiety. bootstrap analyses identified two sequential contemporaneous–prospective indirect pathways: (a) concurrent pd–loneliness covariation at t1 prospectively predicting social anxiety t2, which in turn predicted sma t2 ( β = 0.008, 95% ci [0.004, 0.013]), and (b) concurrent pd–social anxiety covariation at t1 prospectively predicting loneliness t2, which in turn predicted sma t2 ( β = 0.010, 95% ci [0.007, 0.015]). taken together, the findings indicate that perceived discrimination is prospectively associated with smartphone addiction through indirect pathways involving loneliness and social anxiety. practical implications for school‐based interventions targeting left‐behind children are discussed. international journal of psychology

scrolling for a purpose: a relationship between social media use and meaning in life with self‐concept clarity as a moderator abstract this cross‐sectional study examines the relationship between social media use (frequency and goals of use) and the purpose dimension of meaning in life and explores the moderating role of self‐concept clarity (scc). we hypothesize that while social media offers a wide range of opportunities for identity exploration, purpose in life derived from its content and activities may be especially appealing to individuals who lack a clear and stable sense of self. an online study was conducted on a nationally representative sample of 1113 polish respondents aged 18–81. the results revealed that while the frequency of social media use was not significantly associated with purpose in life, information‐seeking and self‐presentation goals positively predicted it. furthermore, the positive relationship between social media use and purpose in life was stronger among individuals with low and medium levels of scc. finally, socioeconomic status and age further moderated the role of scc in the associations of self‐presentation and social interaction goals with purpose in life. we conclude that social media may shape purpose in life, especially when used for information seeking and self‐presentation, and particularly for those with low self‐concept clarity. targeted interventions—rather than restricting social media use—should foster scc itself—through counseling that supports self‐reflection and value articulation—complemented by media literacy programs and by strengthening offline sources of purpose. scandinavian journal of psychology

brain atlas selection for developmental dyslexia: a comparative study of gcn classification based on graph-theoretical and topological feature fusion abstract developmental dyslexia (dd) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder, and abnormalities in the functional brain network structure are suggested to be closely related to dysregulation of connections between brain regions. however, the applicability of different brain atlas segmentation strategies in dd brain network modeling has not been systematically evaluated. to this end, this study constructed brain functional networks using three brain atlases (aal, craddock, and power) for comparative analysis and built a graph convolutional network (gcn) classification framework that integrates traditional graph-theoretic features and higher-order global topological features extracted using persistent homology. the results of the experiment show that the aal template performs best in dd recognition, with a classification accuracy rate of 83.31%. additionally, by converging cross-threshold topological feature stability analysis with grad-cam model attribution, we identified a set of brain regions that exhibited both robust intergroup differences across multiple sparsity levels and high importance in the gcn’s decision-making process, thereby jointly pinpointing the core neural substrates of dd. our results provide a theoretical basis for brain atlas selection and functional connectivity modeling, and offer a new path for optimizing dd-assisted recognition methods. neurobiology of language

semantic distance differently modulates fpvs-eeg responses to words and pictures abstract the organization of semantic knowledge within the brain has long been studied through various theoretical frameworks and is still a matter of debate. many studies that have helped advancing our knowledge about this topic have approached it in the context of its deterioration, notably in patients with semantic dementia. in healthy subjects, the question whether and how semantic distance between concepts represented by picture or word stimuli influences brain responses remains understudied. in this study with 24 healthy subjects, we used eeg recordings coupled with a fast periodic visual stimulation (fpvs) approach, for the first time, to assess the semantic distance effect with different stimulus modalities. picture or word stimuli from a reference category (birds) appeared every fourth item among a 4-hz stream of either man-made objects (forming the high distance [hd] condition) or other animals (low distance [ld] condition). within a few minutes of recording, eeg responses were observed at the predetermined frequency of the reference category presentation (at 1 hz), suggesting its exemplars were activated at least sufficiently to be automatically discriminated from different superordinate (hd) and basic (ld) categories, for both pictures and words. pictures and words elicited a different pattern of response to semantic distance, with larger amplitudes in the hd than in the ld condition for pictures but a reversed pattern of somewhat greater amplitudes in the ld than in the hd condition for words. our findings support a similarity-based structure of semantic representations and provide evidence for a differential mapping between semantic and picture/word surface representations. neurobiology of language

how to practice open science: a cookbook for clinical psychology and psychotherapy research. even though open science practices advance the credibility and accessibility of knowledge gained through research, they are not yet as common in clinical psychology as in other subfields of psychology. this paper presents an overview of how to implement open science practices in clinical psychology and psychotherapy research. we will address frequently encountered challenges and present different ways to deal with sensitive topics within the specific field. we explain open science practices while planning a study, during data collection and preparation of a publication, and for the publication of results. finally, we will show options for how to structure a whole research group in support of open science practices. with different types of actions - of varying degrees of complexity and openness - we can continually and ethically move toward more open science, which will strengthen clinical research and is therefore essential for people with lived experiences of psychological symptoms, patients, psychotherapists, and for investments in psychological treatments. journal of clinical psychology

sensory processing patterns and their associations with dementia worry among community-dwelling older adults background: changes in sensory input, such as declines in visual and auditory function among community-dwelling older adults, rather than sensory processing characteristics themselves, have been the focus of previous studies. changes in sensory processing may influence the mental health of older adults. objectives: to examine the association between sensory processing patterns and dementia worry among community-dwelling older adults. methods: a self-administered questionnaire survey was conducted among 186 community-dwelling older adults. sensory processing characteristics were assessed using the adolescent and adult sensory profile (aasp). dementia worry was assessed using the dementia worry assessment scale (dwas). sensory processing patterns were extracted using cluster analysis. multiple regression analysis was conducted using dwas scores as the dependent variable and sensory processing patterns as independent variables. results: two clusters were identified based on the four aasp quadrants: the “lower aasp score group” and the “higher aasp score group.” in the multiple regression analysis, using the lower aasp score group as the reference, the higher aasp score group was significantly associated with higher dwas scores (standardized β = 0.182, p = 0.011). conclusion: these results suggest that individual differences in sensory processing characteristics may be associated with psychological reactions to dementia in older adulthood. relatively higher scores for low registration, sensory sensitivity, and sensation avoiding were associated with higher levels of dementia worry. health psychology research

perceived blue space restorativeness and subjective vitality among coastal tourists: a cross-sectional moderated mediation study background: blue spaces may support psychological recovery, yet the processes linking perceived restorativeness to subjective vitality and the role of digital engagement remain unclear. objective: this study examined the indirect associations between perceived blue space restorativeness and subjective vitality involving psychological detachment and cognitive restoration, and whether online vigilance moderated the restorativeness–detachment association. methods: we used a cross-sectional online survey of 384 adult chinese tourists who had recently visited a coastal site. latent-variable structural equation modeling was used to estimate the proposed associations. bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals were applied to the indirect effects, and moderation was examined through a product-indicator latent interaction. results: perceived blue space restorativeness was positively associated with psychological detachment (β = 0.466) and cognitive restoration (β = 0.318), while psychological detachment was positively associated with cognitive restoration (β = 0.312). psychological detachment (β = 0.257) and cognitive restoration (β = 0.316) were both positively associated with subjective vitality. the sequential indirect association was significant (β = 0.046). online vigilance negatively moderated the restorativeness–detachment association (β = −0.179), and indirect effects involving psychological detachment were not significant at high online vigilance. conclusion: the findings suggest that perceived blue space restorativeness is associated with greater subjective vitality through psychological detachment and cognitive restoration, while online vigilance may weaken this restorative process by constraining psychological detachment. these results extend understanding of psychological recovery in blue space environments and highlight the importance of reducing digital attentional demands during restorative leisure experiences. health psychology research
virtual reality therapy is a feasible and tolerable adjunct to ketamine treatment for ptsd and depression discover mental health

family accommodation and preschool dysregulated fear interact to predict child anxiety abstract family accommodation, or behaviors that parents enact to alleviate or prevent child anxiety, has been linked to child anxiety severity. accommodation has also been implicated in the etiology and maintenance of child anxiety. preschool children, who may show early anxiety symptoms, may be particularly impacted by accommodation when they show temperamental predisposition towards anxiety. dysregulated fear, characterized by displays of fear and shyness in low-threat contexts, has emerged as a temperamental construct that highlights risk for anxiety. typically studied in toddlerhood, dysregulated fear has not been operationalized in preschool children. the current study examined whether dysregulated fear, measured observationally at child age 4, moderated the longitudinal relation from family accommodation at age 4 to change in child anxiety from age 4 to age 5. the sample included 138 children (44.5% female, 83.9% white/european american, 3.6% hispanic/latino) and their mothers. dysregulated fear was coded as shyness and withdrawal during stranger approach and compliments tasks deemed “low threat” in comparison to a speech task. mothers reported family accommodation at child age 4 and child anxiety at child ages 4 and 5. controlling for age 4 anxiety and maternal age, there was an interaction between family accommodation and dysregulated fear in predicting child anxiety. family accommodation related to child anxiety across values of, but most strongly at high, dysregulated fear. these results expand evidence of environment-temperament interactions in predicting child anxiety to include dysregulated fear in the preschool developmental period, which is aligned with evidence-based child anxiety prevention programs. research on child and adolescent psychopathology

enfoques teóricos de la adolescencia en la psicología y su comprensión del adolescente en la actualidad este ensayo explora el concepto de adolescencia desde una perspectiva teórica, identificando los diferentes enfoques o perspectivas que han surgido en la psicología y algunos saberes afines en torno a él. el objetivo principal es comprender la adolescencia como un fenómeno bio-psico-social, tomando como referencia las definiciones y características sobre la adolescencia, provenientes de los enfoques bioevolutivos y los psicosociales que han modelado la comprensión del desarrollo adolescente, e integrarlos con los factores sociales y culturales contemporáneos como la juvenilización y la influencia de los medios de comunicación. se concluye que la adolescencia hoy es un período de transición marcado por la emergencia de cambios bioevolutivos, la construcción de identidad, la elaboración de conflictos inconscientes por la pérdida de la infancia y la adaptación a un contexto sociocultural que exalta la juventud. se alude a cómo las dinámicas de consumo y la tecnología han transformado las prácticas juveniles, configurando un yo adolescente fragmentario pero adaptativo y una identidad centrada en el reconocimiento social y la autoexpresión. revista costarricense de psicologia

serial homicidal behavior: a research question. this festschrift contribution identifies a research question that i believe most needs to be addressed in the near future in understanding, preventing, and responding to serial killers of interpersonal violence. although there has been an upsurge of research on sexual homicide over the years, there is still much we do not know. the dilemma is: how can we add to the collective knowledge of killers? what role, if any, does early-life social isolation contribute to the development of serial homicidal behavior, and how does it interact with other known risk factors such as trauma, personality disorders, and cognitive/neurological abnormalities? journal of interpersonal violence

psychobiological correlates of bullying in juvenile offenders: personality traits, psychopathic features, and platelet mao-b activity. bullying behavior among youth is linked to long-term psychosocial and criminological consequences and is particularly prevalent yet understudied in juvenile justice settings. stable individual differences, including personality traits, early psychopathic traits, and biological markers, may provide a framework for understanding bullying among young offenders. the present study examined whether these factors, both individually and cumulatively, were associated with bullying behavior among 370 male adolescents aged 14 to 19 years detained in a juvenile detention center in northern russia. bullying behavior was evaluated using the kiddie schedule for affective disorders and schizophrenia - present and lifetime version. data were available for subsets on personality traits measured with the temperament and character inventory ( = 320), early psychopathic traits assessed with lynam's childhood psychopathy scale (self-report = 136; teacher report = 154), and platelet monoamine oxidase b (mao-b) activity ( = 178). associations between bullying, personality traits, psychopathic traits, and mao-b activity were examined using independent-samples-tests, linear and logistic regression models. all analyses were conducted using available cases and adjusted for smoking. a cumulative risk index was created to examine the combined contribution of multiple risk factors, based on the top 20% in novelty seeking, psychopathic traits, and low mao-b activity. bullies differed from non-bullies on nearly all personality traits, showing higher novelty seeking and lower self-directedness and cooperativeness. bullies also exhibited higher psychopathic traits (self- and teacher-rated) and lower mao-b activity, although the mao-b association weakened to a trend when adjusting for smoking. the likelihood of belonging to the bullying group increased with the accumulation of risk factors across personality, psychopathic traits, and mao-b activity. we conclude that, within an already high-risk offender population, bullying is associated with the cumulative presence of personality characteristics, psychopathic traits, and biological markers, supporting a multidimensional framework of risk. journal of interpersonal violence

the prediction and mediating role of lifetime and daily aggressive sexual fantasies: an experience-sampling study aggressive sexual fantasies (asf) have consistently been associated with different sexual-aggression measures and mediated the effects of other risk factors on sexual aggression. little, however, is known about the predictors of asf and whether they should be considered as an independent risk factor for sexual aggression or rather an expression of aggression-related sexual interests. the present study, therefore, assessed lifetime asf cross-sectionally ( = 422; = 28.14; = 9.76) and over a 14-day experience-sampling period ( = 230; = 27.38; = 9.08). of the participants, 87% reported to have experienced asf at least once in their lives; 11% reported asf during the experience-sampling period. psychopathy, violent pornography consumption, sexual interest in sexual sadism, and the interactions between hypersexuality and sexual-abuse experiences, machiavellianism, and sexual interest in sadism were associated with higher lifetime asf. sexual interest in sadism positively predicted asf during the experience-sampling period, but only in men. lifetime asf were the strongest predictor of sexual aggression and mediated the cross-sectional associations between sexual interest in sadism, hypersexuality, and violent pornography consumption and sexual aggression. these findings support the notion that asf are an important cognitive risk factor for sexual aggression, partially independent from sexual interest, and require stronger attention by research and practice. journal of sex research

impact of epileptiform abnormalities on functional phenotype in a cohort of autism spectrum disorder patients with or without epilepsy: a monocentric retrospective study purpose: autism spectrum disorder (asd) and epilepsy frequently co-occur, suggesting shared neurobiological underpinnings. while no specific seizure type or epilepsy syndrome is consistently associated with asd, epileptiform abnormalities (eas) are commonly observed in affected individuals, though their clinical significance remains unclear.
methods: this study examined the impact of eas and epilepsy on the functional phenotype of 338 individuals with asd, assessed through video-eeg (v-eeg) and standardized psychometric tools (ados-2, leiter-r, wisc-iv, vabs).
results: results showed that asd individuals with epilepsy exhibited significantly lower cognitive performance compared to those with asd alone or with eas. additionally, greater symptom severity was observed in the asd-+ea group. however, no significant differences emerged in adaptive functioning or language abilities.
conclusion: these findings highlight the potential influence of epileptiform activity on cognitive and behavioral outcomes in asd. further longitudinal research is warranted to elucidate the prognostic implications of eas in asd and better characterize its impact on functional profile. journal of autism and developmental disorders
