is love gone or are you stressed? examining daily associations between non-relationship stress and love, passion, and intimacy in couple relationships non-relationship stress refers to external stressors that originate outside of the romantic relationship and can include heavy workload, financial problems, conflict with colleagues, and more. non-relationship stress is related to lower relationship satisfaction; however, other important variables, such as love, passion and intimacy, have not been thoroughly examined in this context. the objective of this preregistered study was to examine the links between daily non-relationship stress and feelings of love, passion, and intimacy. using a 14-day daily experience dataset of 100 couples, we hypothesized that on days when a person’s (actor effect) and their partner’s (partner effect) non-relational stress is higher (vs. lower), their own love, passion, and intimacy would be lower that day compared to other individuals (between-person effects) and their typical levels (within-person effects). we expected these patterns to hold controlling for daily mood, relationship duration, and prior-day levels of the outcome. however, our confirmatory models revealed that only one’s greater non-relationship stress predicted one’s lower feelings of love, passion, and intimacy. implications of these results for researchers and professionals working with couples are discussed. journal of social and personal relationships

transition to parenthood and changes in wellbeing and relationship quality: a propensity score matching approach does becoming a parent enhance or undermine wellbeing and relationship quality? mixed findings along with methodological challenges do not provide clear answers. drawing from nationally representative data in new zealand collected across 2012–2024, we extended prior studies by using propensity score matching to compare changes in both wellbeing and relationship quality of people who became parents ( n = 1,260) to matched controls who did not become parents ( n = 1,260) but were similar in key socio-demographics and baseline wellbeing and relationship quality. on average, parenthood had small wellbeing benefits. matched controls experienced small steady declines in life satisfaction and increases in psychological distress. by contrast, people who became parents sustained higher life satisfaction for 2 years following the transition before declining to the same levels as matched controls 4 years later. new parents also did not show increases in psychological distress, but differences to matched controls were small and mostly nonsignificant. parenthood was also accompanied by relationship challenges. both matched controls and people who became parents experienced significant declines in relationship satisfaction across time, and these trajectories did not significantly differ. however, new parents reported significantly stronger increases in conflict across the following 4 years compared to matched controls. the results strengthen evidence that parents may experience small life satisfaction benefits, and indicate that declines in relationship satisfaction may not be as unique to the transition to parenthood as prior studies assume, but reveal that new parents may encounter increases in relationship conflict that likely challenge relationship satisfaction and wellbeing. journal of social and personal relationships

indicators of mental health among u.s. military service members with eating disorders with and without co-occurring trauma-related diagnoses. objective: active-duty service members (adsms) may be at particular risk for eating disorders (eds), posttraumatic stress disorder (ptsd), and sexual assault (sa). this study aimed to determine the prevalence and mental health care complexity of adsms with eds, with and without co-occurring trauma-related diagnoses.
method: this retrospective adsm cohort study utilized military electronic medical records and tricare insurance claims between 2016 and 2023. those with ed-related, 10th revision, clinical modification codes were stratified by the presence of trauma-related care and evaluated for psychiatric comorbidity and psychotropic prescriptions.
results: of the 7,758 adsms with an ed, 28% had ptsd, 3% sa, and 8% both. among those with ed only, 58% had an anxiety disorder, 54% had a mood disorder, and 61% were prescribed a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (ssri). in multivariable logistic regression analysis adjusting for sex, service, rank, age, ed diagnosis, race/ethnicity, enrollment length, and body mass index, compared with those with ed alone, those with ptsd or ptsd and sa were significantly more likely to have anxiety disorder (a= 3.02 and 3.04, respectively), mood disorder (a= 3.54 and 4.58, respectively), or ssri prescription (a= 2.70 and 4.68, respectively); those with sa without ptsd were more likely to have an anxiety disorder or ssri prescription (s < .01).
conclusions: approximately 40% of adsms with an ed had a trauma-related diagnosis. trauma-related diagnoses were associated with odds of mood/anxiety disorders or ssri prescriptions up to fivefold higher than those with eds alone. clinicians treating individuals with eds should be well-versed in trauma-informed care and ensure access to specialty services for adsms with eds to mitigate psychological stress and promote recovery. posttraumatic stress disorder evidence-based psychotherapy utilization among lesbian, gay, bisexual, and queer veterans receiving care in the veterans health administration. objective: the aim of the study was to evaluate sexual orientation-based differences in utilization of cognitive processing therapy (cpt) and prolonged exposure therapy (pe) among veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder receiving care in the veterans health administration.
method: data were extracted from the veterans health administration electronic health records of veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder identified as lesbian, gay, bisexual, or queer (lgbq) or heterosexual. veterans were matched 3:1 using propensity score matching, yielding an analytic sample of 114,372 veterans (25% lgbq). the odds of utilizing cpt or pe and achieving the minimum dose (i.e., eight or more sessions), adjusting for service connection, military sexual trauma, and charlson comorbidity index score, were examined.
results: lgbq veterans had higher rates of military sexual trauma, higher charlson comorbidity index scores, and a lower likelihood of being service-connected at 51%-100% compared to heterosexual veterans. lgbq veterans had higher odds of any cpt utilization (adjusted odds ratios = 1.13, 95% ci [1.06, 1.20],< .001) and pe utilization (adjusted odds ratios = 1.24, 95% ci [1.11, 1.37],< .001). in adjusted analyses, there was no relationship between sexual orientation and achievement of minimum dose of cpt or pe.
conclusions: lgbq veterans are accessing evidence-based treatments for posttraumatic stress disorder in the veterans health administration at higher rates compared to heterosexual veterans, but receipt of a minimum dose for either treatment is low for both lgbq and heterosexual veterans. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). psychological trauma-theory research practice and policy

mental health experiences of frontline health workers in sierra leone: a qualitative study using the framework method. background: frontline health workers in sierra leone have endured pandemics and recurrent infectious and maternal emergencies under chronic under-resourcing, yet the psychological burden they carry remains poorly understood. this study explored how they experience and cope with mental health challenges during and after emergency response.
methods: a qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 42 purposively sampled frontline health workers across three districts and eight professional cadres. sample size was guided by information power rather than saturation. data were analysed using the framework method, indexing all transcripts into a matrix of 42 participants by 17 categories. reporting followed the consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research.
results: charting produced 17 categories under four themes: the weight of witnessing, stigma and social fracture, coping in the margins, and institutional abandonment. distress was patterned rather than uniform: accounts of stigma between cadres came mainly from burial and laboratory staff, and accounts of enforced family separation from those deployed away from home. two categories, both specified in advance, were populated across the whole sample: fear of infection, and absent or token formal support; no participant described employer-provided psychosocial support as adequate and sustained.
conclusions: frontline health workers in sierra leone described heavy and largely unaddressed psychological burdens, and asked directly for prompt hazard pay and sustained recognition. read with the conceptual frameworks and literature, their accounts make a case for building structured psychosocial support into emergency preparedness and universal health coverage planning, as an obligation to the workforce and a condition of its retention. acta psychologica

the great eft schism: testing johnson's and greenberg's alternative models of what drives couple satisfaction abstract emotion‐focused therapy for couples (eft‐c) is organized around two theoretical accounts: johnson's (2019) attachment‐based model, which treats attachment as the primary motivational system in romantic relationships, and the greenberg–goldman (2008) multi‐motivational model, which adds regard and attraction to attachment as three co‐equal systems. their relative explanatory power has not been directly compared. the present study tested whether the multi‐motivational model explains more variance in relationship satisfaction than an attachment‐only model in a non‐clinical community sample. a nationally quota‐representative sample of 1090 individuals nested in 545 couples completed measures of relationship satisfaction (csi‐16), attachment behaviors (bare), interpersonal attraction (ias), and level of regard (blri). hierarchical regression and relative weights analysis compared model performance, with generalized estimating equations and cluster‐bootstrap confidence intervals accounting for non‐independence within couples. the attachment‐only model explained 47% of variance; adding attraction and regard increased this to 70.5% (δ r 2 = 0.235, cohen's f 2 = 0.80). contrary to expectations, regard emerged as the dominant predictor (41.3% of explained variance), followed by attraction (29.8%) and attachment (29.0%). perceived partner regard uniquely predicted satisfaction ( p < 0.001), whereas self‐reported regard for partner did not ( p = 0.663). conclusions about clinical mechanisms cannot be drawn from this cross‐sectional, non‐clinical design. nonetheless, the findings are inconsistent with the strong form of the attachment primacy hypothesis and consistent with the greenberg–goldman multi‐motivational account. comprehensive assessment of distressed couples may benefit from attending to regard and attraction alongside attachment. family process

how social identity relates to stress appraisal at work: integrating the social identity approach with the transactional model of stress abstract drawing on the social identity approach and the transactional model of stress, this study examines how individually perceived group identification (ipgi) relates to the primary and secondary appraisal of stressful situations. we hypothesized that stronger ipgi would be associated with framing stressors from a more collective rather than an individual perspective during both appraisal phases. the study combined a survey assessing employees' ipgi with an online interview conducted 3 weeks later, in which participants described a recent stressful work event. data were collected from employees across diverse industries and occupational contexts in germany ( n = 114). interview transcripts were coded for collective and individual pronoun use during primary and secondary appraisal. stronger ipgi was associated with more collective pronoun use in both phases of appraisal but was not related to less individual pronoun use, suggesting that identification with the group adds to, rather than replaces, individual appraisal. these findings offer initial evidence that identification with the group is linked to a more collective linguistic framing of stressful work experiences and provide a basis for further research on the role of ipgi in the appraisal of stress within team‐based contexts. journal of applied social psychology

more than words: lay perceptions of mental health terminology across context and severity. mental health terminology has evolved and proliferated, yet it remains unclear how laypeople-particularly young adults-perceive and understand common terms. this has far-reaching implications, for instance, on normalization of mental health experiences, stigma, help-seeking behavior, and clinician-patient communication. the present study included 693 young adults (= 21 years old) in southern california who completed an online survey about five mental health terms: (a) mental illness, (b) mental disorder, (c) mental health concern, (d) psychological issue, and (e) psychological distress. participants completed a variety of complementary questions, including assigning study terms to 57 mental health experiences, symptoms, and disorders; responding to evaluative questions (e.g., how stigmatizing the term was); and providing open-ended feedback regarding term rejection. "mental health concern" was the most broadly applied and least rejected term. conversely, "mental illness" and "mental disorder" were reserved for clinical conditions and viewed as more stigmatizing, severe, and in need of treatment. qualitatively, "mental illness" was twice as likely to be rejected than "mental disorder." gender and personal/family history of a mental disorder moderated evaluative judgments. the findings suggest that mental health terms are not interchangeable and instead represent a continuum of perceived severity, clinical weight, and social acceptability. the study revealed important nuances (e.g., between "mental illness" and "mental disorder") that have implications for scientific communication, clinical practice, and public understanding of mental health. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). psychological services

visual attention: defining the origin of the current terms of engagement abstract our environment bombards the mind with far more visual information than can be processed. because of this overload of information, our minds focus on only a subset of the visual inputs that land on our retinas. the visual attention mechanisms of the brain select which inputs we process to the level of awareness, store in memory, and act upon. here i provide an overview of the topics, tasks, and methods that researchers have developed to study visual attention and conclude by discussing continuing controversies. finally, weaknesses in our understanding of the brain’s limited capacity ability to process visual information are identified as potential targets for future study. attention perception & psychophysics

the visibility bargain: the psychological costs of sustained public climate communication abstract: as climate change has moved from a scientific concern to a highly visible societal and political issue, climate scientists have increasingly been called upon to serve as public interpreters of climate risk. expectations that scientists engage with media, counter misinformation, and participate in public debate have expanded alongside their existing research, teaching, and administrative responsibilities. yet despite the growing normalization of public engagement as a professional obligation, the psychological consequences of sustained scientific visibility remain insufficiently theorized within psychology. this article provides a conceptual synthesis of psychological and interdisciplinary research to examine the consequences of sustained public climate communication. integrating research on emotional labor, moral injury, and occupational stress, it introduces the concept of the visibility bargain: an implicit institutional arrangement through which expectations of public engagement redistribute emotional and ethical burdens from institutions to individual scientists. drawing on qualitative research, case studies, and communication scholarship, the article argues that for climate scientists, sustained public visibility may be associated with cumulative emotional strain, ethical dissonance, exposure to harassment, and career vulnerability. the visibility bargain is proposed as an integrative framework that explains how these distinct forms of strain become concentrated within individual scientists under conditions of expanding public visibility and limited institutional support. the article outlines implications for psychological research, institutional design, and climate communication practice, emphasizing the need to move from visibility-driven models of public engagement toward sustainability-oriented approaches that integrate communication into workload recognition, professional role design, and institutional support structures. by conceptualizing climate communication as a shared institutional responsibility rather than solely an individual professional obligation, the article contributes a psychologically grounded framework for understanding the human consequences of public climate communication. european psychologist

creative project teams’ adaptive responses to task alterations at different points in time abstract how does a project team’s response to the timing of task alterations affect its receptiveness to these alterations? in addition, what role do creative team processes play in determining the team’s response? the purpose of the present research is to explore answers to these questions. we start our theoretical analysis with the assumption that creative project teams facing a deadline progress through varying levels of divergent and convergent team processes, manifesting in process-specific trajectories. in study 1a, we empirically demonstrate these trajectories for 20 creative project teams. we then examine how creative project teams respond to task alterations at two times of heightened readiness—early or at the temporal midpoint of a team project (study 1b). in a sample of 68 creative project teams, we find that optimal information integration requires teams to recalibrate some of those processes that are disturbed when a task alteration occurs. specifically, midpoint (relative to early) intervention teams integrated more novel information when they engaged in idea implementation right after the task alteration, whereas early (relative to midpoint) intervention teams integrated more novel information when they engaged in problem formulation. higher levels of information integration, in turn, predicted creative outcomes. we discuss implications for team creativity and team adaptation. journal of business and psychology

psychosocial pathways of etomidate misuse among chinese youth in drug rehabilitation institutions background: etomidate, an ultra-short-acting gamma-aminobutyric acid type a anesthetic, has been widely misused across east and southeast asia. by 2024, it became the most frequently misused anesthetic or psychotropic substance in china, with 86.4% of users younger than 35. objective: this study explored how young people recruited from chinese drug rehabilitation institutions initiated and sustained etomidate vaping, attempted to stop, and understood the psychosocial factors associated with continued use and return to use. methods: semi-structured interviews were conducted with 103 participants (aged 15–35) with a history of etomidate misuse, recruited from drug rehabilitation institutions. transcripts were analyzed using codebook-oriented thematic analysis. results: five themes concerned uninformed initiation, motivational pathways, device-related habituation, harms, and cessation attempts followed by returning to use. nearly half were initially unaware that the product contained etomidate. a rapid, short-lived effect was described as promoting repeated inhalation, and negative emotion regulation was the most common motive for continued use. device portability and concealability were associated with use across settings and everyday urges. commonly self-reported harms included cognitive and motor difficulties, emotional changes, and hazardous driving. cessation strategies included distraction, avoiding other users, and changing environments; however, online peer contact and drug-related digital content were described as re-evoking urges and contributing to return to use. conclusion: among young users in drug rehabilitation institutions in china, self-reported etomidate vaping experiences were characterized by limited risk awareness, emotion-regulation motives, device affordances, and digital social exposure. these findings suggested the potential value of emotion-regulation-focused interventions and platform-level governance. health psychology research

the differential role of physical activity intensity and intrinsic motivation on children’s well-being background: negative life events are associated with lower well-being in children, and this association may vary with physical activity and motivational quality. objectives: this study examined gender differences in negative life events, physical activity, motivation, and well-being and tested whether moderate and vigorous physical activity moderated the association between negative life events and well-being. it further explored whether intrinsic motivation extended this moderating relationship. methods: this cross-sectional study included 752 children aged 8–14 years (335 boys, 417 girls; mean = 10.36 years) and their parents. parents reported negative life events and physical activity; children reported well-being and intrinsic motivation. moderation analyses were conducted separately by gender, alongside formal tests of gender differences. results: parents rated negative life events more severe for girls. girls also reported lower vigorous physical activity, intrinsic motivation, and well-being. greater event severity was associated with lower well-being in boys and girls. formal gender differences in moderations were significant for vigorous but not for moderate physical activity. follow-up gender-stratified analyses showed that, among girls, higher moderate activity was associated with a weaker negative association between event severity and well-being, whereas higher vigorous activity was associated with a stronger negative association. no interactions were observed among boys. the three-way interactions involving intrinsic motivation were non-significant. conclusion: a statistically significant difference in moderations was observed for vigorous but not for moderate physical activity. thus, gender-stratified findings for moderate activity should be considered exploratory. given the cross-sectional design and subjective assessment of physical activity intensity, findings should be interpreted as associative. health psychology research

spurious multidimensionality in psychological measures: disentangling measurement-model misspecification from persistent secondary variance psychological measures frequently exhibit secondary factors that may reflect substantive dimensions, systematic response processes, measurement-model misspecification, or combinations of these sources. we focus on spurious multidimensionality arising when the functional form linking a latent variable to its indicators is misspecified. using a height inventory administered to 11,979 participants (51% women), we compared dimensionality based on pearson and polychoric correlations and estimated continuous and ordinal one-factor and bifactor models. we additionally examined item-level response-function fit, nonlinear dependence between general- and specific-factor estimates, shared residual patterns, and item endorsement. polychoric and ordinal modeling strengthened several indicators of general-factor dominance, markedly improved correspondence between model-implied and empirical item-response functions, and nearly eliminated nonlinear dependence between general- and specific-factor estimates. these findings indicate that treating ordinal responses as continuous introduced systematic construct-related variance into the specific factor. however, a strong specific factor remained under ordinal modeling, continued to substantially improve model fit, and showed a highly similar loading pattern across continuous and ordinal specifications. its loadings were only partly accounted for by shared residual patterns and were systematically related to item endorsement. the results therefore suggest that a single secondary factor can simultaneously capture spurious variance caused by measurement-model misspecification and persistent systematic variance potentially arising from response processes. secondary factors should consequently not be treated as necessarily substantive or wholly artifactual; their sources should be investigated by comparing alternative measurement specifications and examining item-level response functions and residual structure. collabra-psychology

juvenile psychopathy and its relation to immaturity: maturational growth mediates associations between adolescent and adult psychopathy scores. psychopathic traits tend to decline from adolescence to adulthood, which could be attributed to aging out of inherently "juvenile" characteristics that resemble psychopathy (e.g., parasitic lifestyle, impulsivity, lying, reward sensitivity). simultaneously, maturity of judgment (moj) improves over this period, with components of such (e.g., emotional maturity, consideration of others, future outlook) resembling psychopathy-related deficits. this study assessed the co-development of psychopathy and moj through a parallel process model, and in a separate mediation model, tested whether advances in moj partially explained variance between adolescent and young adult psychopathy scores. by examining data from the pathways to desistance, a longitudinal study of 1170 justice-involved males (mage = 16, range = 14-17) who were interviewed across 11 waves spanning 7 years following a serious offense, we found the growth of psychopathy (shown to decline across the study) was significantly related to the growth of moj (increased across the study). we found significant indirect pathways linking adolescent psychopathic traits to young adult psychopathic traits 7 years later (i.e., callous-unemotional, grandiose-manipulative, impulsive-irresponsible) through the moj trajectory (p < .05), such that gains in maturity explained variance in psychopathic traits from adolescence to young adulthood. our results suggest that developmental changes in maturity may contribute to individual differences in the continuity and expression of psychopathic traits across adolescence and young adulthood. findings have implications for interpretability of juvenile assessments, treatment opportunity, and legal decision-making considerations. journal of research on adolescence

recursos protectores del uso del condón en hombres con vih desde una perspectiva ecológica el uso consistente del condón continúa siendo una estrategia fundamental para prevenir la transmisión del vih y otras infecciones de transmisión sexual. no obstante, la mayor parte de la investigación se ha centrado en los factores de riesgo asociados a su uso inconsistente, mientras que los recursos protectores han recibido menor atención, particularmente en hombres que viven con vih. el objetivo de este estudio fue comprender, desde las experiencias de hombres que viven con vih, los recursos protectores que favorecen el uso del condón utilizando el modelo ecológico como marco analítico. se realizó un estudio cualitativo mediante entrevistas semiestructuradas a 31 hombres con una edad promedio de 26 años y un tiempo promedio de 2.6 años desde el diagnóstico de vih. la información fue analizada mediante análisis temático con apoyo del software atlas.ti e interpretada de acuerdo con los niveles del modelo ecológico. los resultados identificaron recursos protectores en el microsistema (educación sexual familiar, comunicación con la pareja y experiencias derivadas del diagnóstico), el mesosistema (amistades, educación sexual escolar y contexto de la relación de pareja), el exosistema (servicios de salud y políticas públicas) y el macrosistema (normas culturales, valores de autocuidado y conciencia social sobre la salud sexual). los hallazgos muestran que el uso del condón constituye una práctica construida mediante la interacción de múltiples contextos, lo que evidencia la utilidad del modelo ecológico para comprender el autocuidado sexual y orientar intervenciones multinivel dirigidas a hombres que viven con vih. calidad de vida y salud

comparación de la satisfacción corporal, estilo y calidad de vida de adultos por índice de masa corporal el objetivo fue comparar el estilo de vida, la calidad de vida y la satisfacción corporal en adultos por índice de masa corporal (imc). se empleó un diseño empírico-analítico, con una muestra de 400 adultos de entre 30 y 54 años, residentes del valle de toluca, méxico. los participantes fueron agrupados en tres categorías por imc: peso normal, sobrepeso y obesidad. se utilizaron tres instrumentos: escala de estilo de vida para mexicanos, el cuestionario iwqol-lite y las siluetas de stunkard. se aplicaron prueba de kolmogorov-smirnov, análisis de varianza de una vía (anova), prueba de kruskal-wallis, prueba de levene y medidas de tamaño del efecto (η² y ε²). los resultados mostraron diferencias significativas en los factores de actividad física (f = 5.54, p < 0.01), alimentación no saludable (f = 4.03, p < 0.05) y estilo de vida total (f = 3.83, p < 0.05). en cuanto a la calidad de vida, solo la dimensión de estado físico presentó diferencias significativas (h = 23.27, p < 0.001), siendo mayor en personas con obesidad (m = 17.83) que aquellas con peso normal (m = 14.30). se hallaron diferencias estadísticamente significativas en la satisfacción corporal (h = 44.46, p < 0.001). calidad de vida y salud

la idea del hombre en el corredor de ultra trail el presente trabajo tiene como objetivo establecer un diálogo entre las concepciones del hombre propuestas por scheler (1969) y diferentes dimensiones presentes en el corredor de ultra trail. se plantea como un ensayo teórico sustentado en una revisión narrativa de literatura filosófica, antropológica y científica vinculada con la evolución de la carrera de resistencia, el trail running y el ultra trail running. a partir de las cinco concepciones desarrolladas por scheler, se analiza al corredor desde diferentes perspectivas: la trascendencia y la búsqueda de sentido; la razón implicada en la planificación y la toma de decisiones; la dimensión biológica e instintiva vinculada con la carrera de resistencia; la fragilidad que puede emerger ante el esfuerzo prolongado; y la conciencia, libertad y responsabilidad asociadas a la elección de afrontar el desafío. esta articulación permite aproximarse al corredor más allá de sus capacidades fisiológicas, atendiendo también a dimensiones psicológicas y existenciales de su experiencia. asimismo, se consideran las posibles implicaciones de la práctica para el bienestar y la calidad de vida, así como el aporte de la psicología del deporte en el acompañamiento del corredor. el ultra trail puede constituirse así en un escenario en el que cuerpo, mente, límite y elección se encuentran y en el que alcanzar una meta puede adquirir un significado que excede el resultado deportivo: quizá no conquistar el mundo, sino, de alguna manera, conquistarse a sí mismo. calidad de vida y salud

determinantes de la calidad de vida en estudiantes de medicina de universidades privadas en paraguay: un estudio transversal antecedente: la calidad de vida es un concepto complejo, influenciado por factores físicos, mentales y sociales. la calidad de vida es esencial, especialmente para los estudiantes de medicina, quienes enfrentan una carga académica elevada. objetivo: evaluar la calidad de vida de los estudiantes de medicina de universidades privadas de ciudad del este y presidente franco, en paraguay. se utilizó el cuestionario whoqol-bref para evaluar cuatro dominios: salud física, salud psicológica, relaciones sociales y medioambiente, con el fin de obtener un perfil detallado del bienestar de estos estudiantes. metodología: este estudio es cuantitativo, de alcance descriptivo y transversal. se empleó un muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia, utilizando la técnica de bola de nieve para reclutar a los participantes. se recogieron los datos mediante un cuestionario digital (google forms®) en junio de 2023. el cuestionario whoqol-bref incluye 26 ítems distribuidos en cuatro dominios. para garantizar la fiabilidad del instrumento, se calculó el coeficiente alfa de cronbach (α=0.89), lo que indica una excelente consistencia interna. se llevaron a cabo análisis descriptivos y correlacionales entre los dominios evaluados. resultados: participaron 135 estudiantes, con una edad promedio de 28 años. la mayoría fueron mujeres (56.3%), y el 54% de los estudiantes ya tenía una carrera universitaria previa. en cuanto a la calidad de vida, los resultados mostraron que la percepción general de salud física fue baja (media de 2.83), especialmente entre los estudiantes con patologías crónicas. en términos de salud psicológica, los problemas de sueño y falta de concentración fueron comunes, con una media de 3.23 en este dominio. las relaciones sociales y el medioambiente también mostraron percepciones regulares, con medias de 3.24 y 3.11, respectivamente. se hallaron correlaciones significativas entre salud física, salud psicológica y relaciones sociales, lo que sugiere que la mejora en un dominio puede influir positivamente en los otros. conclusión: el estudio demostró que los estudiantes de medicina de las universidades privadas de ciudad del este y presidente franco tienen una calidad de vida promedio, con áreas críticas en salud física y psicológica. la salud física fue la dimensión con las puntuaciones más bajas, especialmente entre los estudiantes con patologías crónicas. se recomienda implementar intervenciones y programas de mentoría, talleres de gestión del tiempo y técnicas de estudio para mitigar el estrés. también sería beneficioso ofrecer atención psicológica y nutricional en los servicios para mejorar el bienestar estudiantil. las futuras investigaciones deben considerar el impacto de estas intervenciones y explorar cómo la actividad física puede mejorar la calidad de vida de los estudiantes. calidad de vida y salud

experiencias y representaciones sociales en la atención familiar de niños y niñas con trastorno del espectro autista: un estudio exploratorio en un centro educativo terapéutico de la provincia buenos aires (argentina) las experiencias familiares vinculadas con el cuidado de personas con autismo evidencian un cruce entre la esfera de lo colectivo cultural y lo individual. la noción de representación social, acuñada por moscovici (1979) y profundizada por jodelet (1986), resulta fructífera para pensar este proceso de interacción o interfase entre lo individual y lo colectivo. estos sistemas cognitivos de sentido común guían y decodifican nuestra forma de ver el mundo. y en esto tiene un lugar fundamental el deber ser, las expectativas y la norma, pero también los valores, las motivaciones y los propósitos. el objetivo del presente artículo consiste en realizar una primera aproximación a la problemática vinculada con las experiencias familiares en la atención de niñas y niños con trastorno del espectro autista (tea). se trata de una investigación incipiente, radicada en el mismo centro en donde se llevó a cabo la experiencia. se aplicó un cuestionario estructurado a una población compuesta por 20 personas que están vinculadas al cuidado de niños y niñas con autismo que asisten al centro. por tratarse de una investigación incipiente, los resultados se presentarán de forma descriptiva y se identificarán algunas problemáticas a profundizar a futuro. calidad de vida y salud

evaluación no patologizante en la psicología escolar: una revisión sistemática sobre prácticas en la educación secundaria este estudio presenta una revisión sistemática de la literatura, basada en las directrices prisma, sobre la evaluación psicológica en el contexto educativo amazónico desde una perspectiva no patologizante, con énfasis en el ámbito de la psicología escolar. la búsqueda se realizó en las bases de datos scielo y dialet y el portal de periódicos capes, considerando estudios publicados entre 2017 y 2025. tras el proceso de identificación, selección y elegibilidad, se incluyeron investigaciones que abordaban prácticas de evaluación psicológica en contextos escolares vinculados a poblaciones amazónicas y/o ribereñas. los resultados evidencian la predominancia de enfoques tecnicistas y psicométricos, centrados en la medición individual del rendimiento y del comportamiento, con limitada incorporación de variables socioculturales, territoriales y comunitarias. asimismo, se observa una escasa producción teórica explícitamente orientada a una perspectiva de evaluación psicológica no patologizante, aunque algunos estudios indican avances hacia enfoques más críticos, institucionales y contextualizados. se concluye que persiste una brecha entre las prácticas tradicionales de evaluación psicológica escolar y las demandas de contextualización cultural en la amazonía. en este sentido, se destaca la necesidad de desarrollar modelos evaluativos críticos, situados y sensibles a las realidades ribereñas que contribuyan a procesos educativos más inclusivos y socialmente comprometidos. calidad de vida y salud

creencias sobre la infidelidad en adultos entre 25 y 35 años de la ciudad autónoma de buenos aires el presente estudio busca indagar sobre las creencias asociadas a la infidelidad en individuos de 25 a 35 años que residen en la ciudad autónoma de buenos aires. se tiene como objetivo explorar las conductas infieles, sus motivaciones, las creencias y las consecuencias percibidas sobre la infidelidad. para esto, se llevó a cabo un estudio descriptivo de corte transversal cualitativo, entrevistando a 50 personas, 25 hombres y 25 mujeres, analizando sus creencias, tipos de infidelidad, causas, el rol de la tecnología de la comunicación y las atribuciones predominantes en la muestra seleccionada. los participantes debían residir exclusivamente en buenos aires y tener entre 25 y35 años. tras el análisis de las entrevistas, se observan diferencias significativas en las causas y percepciones de la infidelidad según el género. las mujeres mencionan el aburrimiento y la búsqueda de nuevas experiencias, mientras que los hombres lo asocian más a problemas de comunicación y monotonía en la relación. ambos grupos coinciden en que la comunicación es crucial para el mantenimiento de las relaciones. los efectos emocionales de la infidelidad incluyen tristeza, decepción y pérdida de confianza, con diferencias en la forma de buscar afecto fuera de la relación: las mujeres tienden a involucrarse en infidelidades emocionales y físicas, mientras que los hombres prefieren la infidelidad física y virtual. la percepción de la infidelidad como ruptura de un contrato es más común en hombres. estos resultados resaltan la influencia de las creencias culturales en la interpretación de la infidelidad y en las crisis de pareja. calidad de vida y salud

ansiedad en el entorno laboral: análisis de caso clínico e intervención con terapia estratégica breve la ansiedad social se caracteriza por miedo intenso a la evaluación negativa y puede afectar el desempeño interpersonal, académico y laboral. el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar la evolución clínica asociada a la aplicación de la terapia breve estratégica (tbe) en un caso clínico de ansiedad social con predominio en situaciones evaluativas laborales. la metodología correspondió a un estudio de caso clínico único, de enfoque cualitativo con apoyo de indicadores clínicos de autorreporte, mediante evaluación inicial, seguimiento intratratamiento y evaluación final. la intervención se desarrolló en ocho sesiones organizadas en cuatro fases terapéuticas. los resultados evidenciaron una evolución clínica favorable, reflejada en la reducción del indicador subjetivo de estrés (ise), que pasó de 8 en la evaluación inicial a 1 al finalizar la intervención, aunque con fluctuaciones intermedias. asimismo, se observó mayor seguridad para expresar opiniones, fortalecimiento de la asertividad y disminución clínicamente referida de síntomas físicos asociados a la ansiedad. se concluye que la tbe se asoció con síntomas clínicos favorables; los hallazgos deben interpretarse con cautela debido a las características metodológicas del estudio, particularmente su diseño de caso único, la modalidad virtual de intervención y el uso de autorreporte. calidad de vida y salud

covid-19 related risk communication strategy regarding the use of face masks in the argentine republic background: during the covid-19 pandemic, face mask use became one of the most recommended interventions to reduce viral transmission however, the effectiveness of mask policies depended on the quality of governmental risk communication. objective: to explore governmental risk communication strategies regarding face-mask use in argentina during the first phases of the covid-19 pandemic using capability, opportunity and motivation (com-b) framework. methods: a qualitative content analysis was conducted of public available communication strategies disseminated between march 2020 to march 2021. sources included national governmental publications, and reports from international organizations. communication material was analysed according to the com-b framework. results: governmental communication campaigns strongly addressed the capability component promoting mask use. the opportunity dimension was enhanced through coordinated governmental communication, however, socioeconomic inequalities limited opportunities for adherence among vulnerable populations. motivation evolved through pandemic. during the initial stages, fear of infection and uncertainty contributed to high adherence to masking recommendations. overtime, prolonged restrictions, and behavioral fatigue reduced public motivation. contradictory behaviors by political leaders, highly publicized events involving inadequate compliance with preventive procedures, and the spread of misinformation on social media further weakened trust and may have undermined adherence. conclusion: argentina implemented extensive communication strategies that contributed to public awareness and early adoption of face masks during covid-19 pandemic. analyses using the com-b framework demonstrated that communication efforts addressed behavioral capability and opportunity, but faced increasingly challenges in sustaining motivation over time. the findings highlight the importance of transparent, evidence-based communication, as well as the need for political role modeling and attention to socioeconomic barriers. future public health emergency responses should integrate behavioral science frameworks with communication strategies tailored to vulnerable populations and changing social contexts. calidad de vida y salud

fatiga por compasión en los profesionales de la intervención social: estrategias de afrontamiento y satisfacción por la compasión como factor determinante la investigación sobre la fatiga por compasión se ha centrado principalmente en los profesionales de la salud, mientras que el conocimiento sobre los trabajadores de la intervención social es limitado. estos trabajadores atienden a personas en situaciones de extrema vulnerabilidad, estrés y violencia, lo que puede provocar altos niveles de estrés y fatiga por compasión. el objetivo de este estudio fue determinar el nivel de fatiga por compasión en estos profesionales y probar un modelo mediacional en el que las estrategias de afrontamiento, a través de la satisfacción por compasión, la reducen. los participantes fueron 400 profesionales de la intervención social de diferentes comunidades autónomas españolas, con una media de 10 años de servicio. la evaluación de la fatiga por compasión se realizó con el proqol y las estrategias de afrontamiento con el csi. también se midieron variables organizativas y laborales. las variables organizacionales y laborales mostraron diferencias significativas en la fatiga por compasión: ésta aumentó con más de 15 años de trabajo y con malas condiciones laborales. la satisfacción por compasión actuó como mediador entre las estrategias de afrontamiento y la fatiga por compasión. la autocrítica se muestra como la estrategia más relevante para aumentar la fatiga, ya que elimina el efecto de la satisfacción por compasión. es necesario formar a los profesionales en el manejo adecuado esta problemática y evitar culpabilizarlos (autocrítica) en su actividad profesional. también es necesario introducir una cultura de cuidado organizacional en las administraciones. calidad de vida y salud

diseño y validación inicial de la escala creeai-6: un instrumento para medir creencias sobre capacidades de la ia en el contexto argentino este artículo presenta el diseño y la evaluación psicométrica inicial de la creeai-6, una escala breve de seis ítems para evaluar creencias sobre capacidades específicas de la inteligencia artificial (ia) en el contexto argentino. los ítems fueron desarrollados a partir de investigaciones previas sobre representaciones sociales de la ia en argentina (becerra, mezzadra & movía, 2025), cubriendo seis áreas de contenido: decisiones justas, respuestas certeras, orientación psicológica, compañía emocional, investigación científica y enseñanza/aprendizaje. la escala se administró a una muestra de 426 adultos argentinos usuarios de ia. los resultados mostraron una consistencia interna adecuada (α = .804; ω = .811). el análisis factorial exploratorio (afe) mostró una solución compatible con una estructura predominantemente unifactorial, que explicó el 42% de la varianza total, con cargas factoriales que oscilaron entre .553 y .767. no obstante, los índices de ajuste global del modelo fueron subóptimos (rmsea = .152; tli = .807), por lo que la unidimensionalidad de la escala debe considerarse preliminar y requerirá confirmación mediante análisis factorial confirmatorio en muestras independientes. como evidencia de validez basada en la relación con otras variables, la creeai-6 presentó una correlación positiva y moderada con la actitud general hacia la ia (aias-4; ρ = .487, *p* < .001) y diferencias significativas en función de la frecuencia de uso de ia y del sexo, en línea con lo esperado teóricamente. se discuten las implicancias de contar con un instrumento breve con indicadores psicométricos iniciales adecuados para medir creencias sobre capacidades de la ia en población argentina y se sugieren futuras líneas de investigación para ampliar la evidencia de validez del instrumento. calidad de vida y salud

educación democrática y neoliberalismo: una revisión sistemática en el contexto iberoamericano este artículo presenta una revisión sistemática de la literatura académica iberoamericana publicada entre 2021 y 2025 sobre la relación entre las nociones de educación democrática y neoliberalismo, desde una perspectiva crítica e interdisciplinaria que articula aportes de la psicología, la filosofía y la educación. el estudio parte del reconocimiento del neoliberalismo como una racionalidad política que transforma no solo las instituciones educativas, sino también las formas de subjetividad, y se interroga frente a ello por las posibilidades de una educación democrática. la investigación se desarrolló conforme al protocolo prisma 2020, aplicando criterios rigurosos de inclusión, exclusión y análisis de contenido, a partir de un corpus de 21 artículos seleccionados en las bases dialnet, scielo y doaj. el análisis permitió identificar cuatro enfoques teóricos predominantes —denominados pedagógico-crítico, filosófico-político, psicoanalítico de la subjetividad y socioeducativo—, así como una serie de patrones comunes, convergencias y tensiones teóricas, junto con vacíos significativos y áreas emergentes en la literatura revisada. finalmente, se destaca el lugar aún marginal que ocupa el pensamiento de jacques rancière en el corpus analizado, pese a su potencia crítica para repensar la educación democrática desde una lógica igualitarista y emancipatoria. calidad de vida y salud

producción científica en salud mental: una revisión de alcance este estudio de revisión de alcance buscó sistematizar y analizar la producción académica en salud mental publicada entre 2016 y 2024, con el fin de identificar tendencias, enfoques metodológicos y vacíos en la investigación, ante el reto que representa organizar un cuerpo de conocimiento en constante crecimiento. siguiendo la declaración preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analyses (prisma), se consultaron seis bases de datos académicas (scopus, sciencedirect, latindex, redalyc, pubmed y scielo) mediante descriptores como salud mental, bienestar, normalidad y funcionalidad, en español, inglés y portugués. se incluyeron 55 estudios, agrupados en tres ejes temáticos: metodológico (14%), centrado en las estrategias investigativas empleadas; práctico (53%), orientado a la aplicación clínica y de política pública; y conceptual (33%), enfocado en la definición de la salud mental en relación con la normalidad, el bienestar y el funcionamiento. esta distribución evidencia que la producción reciente privilegia la aplicación práctica y la discusión conceptual por encima de la reflexión metodológica, un desequilibrio que esta revisión permite cuantificar de forma sistemática. los hallazgos resaltan el carácter multidimensional de la salud mental y la necesidad de un abordaje interdisciplinario e integrador que articule las estrategias investigativas, las aplicaciones prácticas y las definiciones conceptuales del campo. calidad de vida y salud

predictors and clinical outcomes of pretreatment length in an outpatient veterans affairs dialectical behavior therapy program. dialectical behavior therapy (dbt) pretreatment is a standard component of dbt designed to prepare patients for treatment, identify treatment goals, and build commitment. examination of dbt pretreatment is of particular importance in naturalistic clinical settings, where clinical resources are limited, such as veterans affairs medical centers, where dbt has become more widespread. eligible veterans (= 89) were enrolled in an outpatient dbt program at a midwestern veterans affairs medical centers. thirteen potential predictors (spanning demographic, health care utilization, and clinical factors) of dbt pretreatment length, operationalized as pretreatment duration and number of pretreatment sessions, were examined. partial least squares regression was used to identify latent components. the relationship between pretreatment length and treatment outcomes was also examined. a significant one-component solution explained 29.10% of the variance in pretreatment duration. borderline personality disorder symptoms, past suicide attempts, past inpatient days, and past psychiatric emergency room admissions were positively associated with pretreatment duration. a significant one-component solution, consisting of the same predictors, with the exception of past suicide attempts, and the addition of race, sex, and psychiatric comorbidity, explained 18.10% of the variance in number of pretreatment sessions. neither pretreatment duration nor number of pretreatment sessions was related to treatment attendance, completion, or symptom severity. indicators of clinical severity and complexity predict number of days and sessions spent in dbt pretreatment. non-white race, male sex, and psychiatric comorbidity predict greater number of dbt pretreatment sessions. deviation from the standard four-session pretreatment approach may be needed for some veterans. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). psychological services

social cognition and parenting among black caregivers: linking public regard to racial and emotion socialization. among black families, cultural racism necessitates adaptations in emotion socialization to prepare children for navigating racialized environments. black caregivers with high negative public regard, or the belief that others view black americans negatively, may engage in racial barrier socialization and discourage their children's expression of negative emotions. however, no studies have directly tested associations among negative public regard, racial barrier socialization, and emotion socialization practices. the present study employed a social-cognitive framework to examine direct and indirect associations between negative public regard, racial barrier socialization, and suppressive emotion socialization practices among black caregivers. it was hypothesized that negative public regard would be associated with higher racial barrier socialization and, in turn, greater use of distress, minimizing, and punitive emotion socialization practices. black caregivers (= 100;= 43.57 years,= 7.75; 91% female) completed self-report measures of racial identity, racial socialization, discrimination, and emotion socialization. controlling for child sex, caregiver emotion dysregulation, and prior discrimination experiences, we found a significant indirect effect of negative public regard on minimizing (but not punitive nor distress) emotion socialization through racial barrier socialization. these findings incrementally advance extant literature, which contends that black caregivers' racial barrier socialization and minimizing emotion socialization may operate in tandem to prepare black youth for others' negative prejudicial beliefs and anti-black racism in broader society. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). journal of family psychology

adolescents’ in vivo emotional responses to digital and in-person peer experiences: differences by context and links to daily life depressive symptoms abstract the rise of digital media has raised questions about potential links to adolescent depression, especially among girls. this study investigated whether affective responses to daily peer interactions, and depressive symptoms, varied by context – digital media or in-person. a sample of 110 adolescents assigned female at birth, aged 12–17 ( m = 15.30, sd = 1.51; 83.6% white and 96.7% non-hispanic) and enriched for risk for depression and suicidality, participated in 30 days of ecological momentary assessments over 3 months. participants reported their most recent “worst” and “best” peer interactions, the context of these interactions (digital media or in-person), their affective responses to these interactions, and depressive symptoms. multilevel models revealed that greater negative affect during negative interactions was associated with higher depressive symptoms, regardless of context ( b = 0.02, p < .001). in contrast, positive in-person interactions were associated with higher positive affect than digital interactions ( b = −2.01, p = .02), which, in turn, was associated with lower depressive symptoms ( b = 0.08, p = .01). findings highlight the protective role of positive in-person experiences in adolescent emotional well-being, and challenge assumptions that negative digital experiences are the primary causes of depressive symptoms. development and psychopathology

designing fulfilling and productive workdays: effects of task meaningfulness sequences on daily engagement and performance. given the importance of experiencing fulfilling and productive workdays, scholars have focused on ways to boost employees' daily engagement and performance, suggesting this may be accomplished by increasing meaningfulness of their work tasks. however, an alternative approach may be needed in multifaceted work contexts where employees need to complete sets of varied tasks each day, including tasks that lack meaningfulness. to address this issue, we integrate the workday design perspective with research on residual engagement to examine implications of strategically sequencing tasks in terms of their meaningfulness. we theorize that because of a process we refer to as engagement cascade, performing the day's most highly meaningful tasks earlier and in a concentrated manner will tend to produce higher levels of daily engagement relative to sequences in which the most highly meaningful tasks occur later or are disbursed. we use agent-based modeling to formalize the engagement cascade process and generate specific predictions regarding how daily engagement is impacted by different task meaningfulness sequences. findings from an intensive longitudinal design study with national aeronautics and space administration and russian space agency crew members (study 1), an experience sampling field experiment with full-time employees (study 2), and two controlled laboratory experiments with undergraduates (study 3 and supplement to study 3) provide support for our hypotheses. specifically, the decreasing task meaningfulness sequence engendered higher levels of daily engagement and, in turn, daily performance, relative to the increasing, inverted u-shaped, and u-shaped sequences. measuring the need for solitude in emerging adulthood: development and validation of the need for solitude (nfs) scale. the need for solitude is of increasing public interest now that individuals can be constantly connected with others through digital technology. yet despite its timeliness, the need for solitude still lacks a valid conceptualisation and measure in our digital society. to address this gap, we conceptualise the need for solitude and develop a self-report measure to capture individual differences in need strength in two preregistered online survey studies among emerging adults (18-25-year-olds). in study 1, we establish the 14 items and unidimensional structure of the need for solitude (nfs) scale (n = 224) and confirm its structural validity, convergent validity, discriminant validity, internal consistency, and test-retest reliability (n = 303) in student samples in the netherlands. in study 2, we replicate its psychometric properties and establish its measurement invariance in a community sample of emerging adults in the netherlands and the united kingdom (n = 841). combined, the results suggest that the nfs is a distinct and measurable trait that aligns with but also deviates from conceptually related traits (e.g., loneliness). overall, the nfs scale provides a robust foundation for studying individual differences in the need for solitude in our digital society. acta psychologica

the italian certainty about mental states questionnaire: validation and links to schizotypy and psychoticism 意大利心理状态确定性问卷：验证及其与分裂型人格和精神病性的关联 mentalization deficits have been linked to schizotypy, a multidimensional construct indexing liability to schizophrenia-spectrum psychopathology. traditional self-report measures often fail to capture the full breadth of mentalizing content. we validated the italian version of the certainty about mental states questionnaire (camsq), which assesses perceived mentalizing about the self and others across feelings, thoughts, motives, and intentions. in a community sample ( n = 496), we tested factor structure, internal consistency, measurement invariance across binary gender groups, and convergent validity, supporting the expected psychometric model. we then examined associations between camsq scores, psychoticism, and schizotypy indicators (cognitive-perceptual, interpersonal, and disorganization). higher psychoticism and some schizotypal features, particularly disorganization, were associated with lower self-certainty coupled with higher other-certainty, suggesting an imbalance in perceived access to one’s own versus others’ mental states. findings provide preliminary evidence that perceived mentalizing relates systematically to schizotypy in nonclinical samples and support the camsq as a useful tool for assessing self-perceived mentalizing capacities. implications for assessment research are discussed. assessment

growing through it: a longitudinal examination of body dissatisfaction, mental health, and resilience during adolescence. introduction: research indicates adolescence, specifically puberty, is a critical period of psychological and physiological development. it is well known that body image is a key aspect of developmental psychology impacting mental health. yet little is known about the buffering effects of resilience to moderate the relationship between body image and mental health over time. the present study investigated the effects of body mass index (bmi), higher age, and early pubertal status as risk factors predicting subsequent changes in body dissatisfaction and body esteem longitudinally. the study also sought to explore body dissatisfaction, body esteem, and resilience as independent variables in the prediction of future changes in depressive symptomology.
methods: following a retrospective longitudinal observational research design stemming from a larger research project, 228 adolescents aged 10-16 completed physiological and psychosocial measures across 2 years (baseline (year 0) and follow-up (year 2)). measures used in this study included the tanner stages of development (pubertal development); harpenden stadiometer, michelli gse 460 scale, center for disease control (cdc) bmi equation, and cdc 2022 extended growth charts (bmi and bmi percentile); body image assessment procedure for pre-adolescents (bia-p; body dissatisfaction); body esteem scale for adolescents and adults (bessa; body esteem); short mood and feelings questionnaire (smfq; depressive symptomology); and connor davidson resilience scale, 10-item short-form (cd-risc 10; resilience).
results: multivariate regression analyses indicated that early puberty status predicted significant increases in body dissatisfaction over time, while bmi and age were not significant predictors. additionally, bmi, age, and puberty status did not demonstrate any significant predictive associations with body esteem at follow-up. baseline body dissatisfaction and body esteem were then examined as independent predictors of changes in depressive symptomology, and analyses evaluated whether resilience moderated these associations. among adolescents reporting no change or decreases in resilience, higher levels of body dissatisfaction at baseline predicted greater increases in depressive symptomology at follow-up; however, this association was not observed among adolescents with increases in resilience, indicating a significant moderating effect of resilience on this relationship (p = 0.0080). body esteem at baseline did not significantly predict depressive symptomology at follow-up, nor was this relationship moderated by changes in resilience (p = 0.3972).
conclusions: findings provide a deeper understanding of risk and protective factors associated with depressive symptomology in adolescents, highlighting resilience as an important independent variable that may buffer the impact of body dissatisfaction on mood outcomes. these results may help researchers and clinicians better conceptualize how resilience functions in adolescents navigating puberty and body image and support its consideration in interventions aimed at mitigating mood disturbances. journal of adolescence

coaching approach behavior and leading by modeling (calm) program for treating early childhood anxiety: a case study anxiety disorders onset earlier than most mental health conditions, with preschool-age children showing prevalence rates comparable to children ages 5 to 17 years. yet, there are limited treatment options suitable for preschool-age children that account for still-developing abstract thinking and metacognition. the coaching approach behavior and leading by modeling (calm) protocol was adapted from parent-child interaction therapy (pcit) to target a broad range of anxiety disorders in children ages 3 to 8 years. this case study outlines the implementation of a 10-session calm treatment protocol for a 5-year-old female presenting with generalized anxiety disorder (gad). the treatment implemented pride skills through parent coaching, followed by exposure-based sessions. post-intervention assessments indicated significant improvement in anxiety symptoms measured by the preschool anxiety scale (pas) and high parent satisfaction measured by the therapy attitude inventory (tai). these findings support early intervention through parent-coaching as a viable alternative to cognitive therapies for young children with anxiety disorders. clinical case studies

the challenges of challenging: development and validation of the barriers to challenging scale. although therapist challenges can be useful to help clients break through defenses and gain awareness about maladaptive thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, many therapists are hesitant to use them (hill, 2020). to be able to assess such hesitance, we conducted two studies to develop the barriers to challenging scale (bcs) and assess its psychometric properties and relations with related constructs. in study 1, 286 therapists, therapists-in-training, and undergraduate helping skills students completed the 34-item pilot measure. an exploratory factor analysis revealed a three-factor structure of the final 15-item bcs: client reactions, negative beliefs, and lack of skills. acceptable test-retest reliability and high internal consistency were found for all scales. the bcs was negatively correlated with self-efficacy for using challenges and positively correlated with barriers to using immediacy and conflict-avoidant communication style, supporting its validity. in study 2, 358 therapists, therapists-in-training, and undergraduate helping skills students completed the 15-item bcs. confirmatory factor analyses supported the stability of the bcs's multidimensional three-factor structure; high internal consistency was found for all scales. measure invariance tests indicated that undergraduate and graduate students and practicing therapists interpreted items similarly. the bcs was positively correlated with attachment anxiety, further supporting its validity. participants scored higher on the bcs subscales compared to parallel subscales on a measure of barriers to using immediacy, indicating that therapists perceive more barriers to using challenges than to using immediacy. limitations and implications are discussed. parental reflective functioning in attachment-based family therapy for lgbtq+ young adults and their nonaccepting parents. parental rejection significantly impacts the mental health of sexual and gender minority young adults and can undermine parent-child relationships. attachment-based family therapy for sexual and gender minorities aims to repair these ruptures by facilitating "corrective episodes," where parents listen to their young adult's experience of feeling rejected and respond with empathy and validation rather than defensiveness. parental reflective functioning (prf) is thought to be a necessary precursor to such productive enactments. this study examined whether prf during individual preparatory sessions with parents predicted parents' observed behaviors toward their young adult during subsequent conjoint sessions. participants included 45 parents of israeli lgbtq+ young adults who participated in an open clinical trial of attachment-based family therapy for sexual and gender minorities. prf was observationally coded using a modification of the reflective functioning scale. parents' behaviors were coded using the parent-child interaction coding system. consistent with our preregistered hypothesis, higher levels of prf in individual sessions with parents predicted a greater frequency of constructive parent behaviors toward their young adult, including validating the young adult's experience and soliciting their emotional reactions, during subsequent conjoint sessions. conversely, higher prf predicted significantly lower frequencies of parents' patronizing and judgmental behaviors. contrary to our hypothesis, parents' defensiveness was not associated with prf. notably, prf in the final preparatory session with parents remained a significant predictor of their behaviors in subsequent conjoint sessions, even when controlling for initial parental reflective functioning, suggesting that fostering mentalization immediately prior to conjoint sessions is a crucial therapeutic task. bidirectional affective influences in psychotherapy: a linguistic case analysis of therapist-client moment-to-moment emotional tones and session outcome. focusing on emotion is a defining feature of psychodynamic theory; however, few studies have examined emotional synchrony at a fine-grained temporal level and linked these processes with session outcomes. this single-case study investigated turn-by-turn emotional tone synchrony between client and therapist across 38 sessions of open-ended psychodynamic psychotherapy conducted in a community clinic. emotional tone was operationalized as the ratio of positive to negative emotion words, derived from 2,929 therapist and client speaking turns using the linguistic inquiry and word count system. dynamic structural equation modeling was used to estimate within-session autoregressive effects and cross-lagged parameters indexing therapist-to-client and client-to-therapist emotional influence. results indicated significant bidirectional emotional synchrony, with therapist emotional tone predicting subsequent client emotional tone and client emotional tone predicting subsequent therapist emotional tone, controlling for autoregressive effects. at the between-session level, stronger therapist-led synchrony was associated with higher client-rated session outcomes, whereas client-led synchrony was not. in addition, greater therapist emotional granularity, operationalized as variability in therapist emotional tone across speaking turns, was associated with higher client-rated session outcomes. these findings provide idiographic support for dynamic emotional synchrony in a manner consistent with psychodynamic models of affective attunement. moreover, the use of a language-based index of emotional synchrony highlights clinically observable and potentially modifiable emotional processes because therapists can intentionally shape their emotional language while directly observing the emotion words used by clients. implications for psychotherapy process research, training, and clinical practice are discussed. a conceptual framework for understanding intelligent behavior in fungal mycelia. fungi exhibit remarkably complex behavior through their mycelial networks, which consist of thread-like structures known as hyphae. recent research on saprotrophic fungi has demonstrated that their mycelium behaves in ways that indicate memory, learning, decision-making, and problem-solving based on spatial pattern recognition-all of which are considered intelligent features. i present a framework to study the behavior of fungal mycelia as an emergent entity from decentralized control of numerous simple reactions at the hyphal level. the framework is based on the concept of swarm intelligence, for which internal communication is the key mechanism. consistent with trewavas' definition, the intelligence of a mycelium is evaluated purely in terms of its behavior and does not presuppose any form of consciousness. the paper also reviews recent findings that support the potential role of electrical signal transfer across the mycelial network as the mechanism that enables fungal mycelia to engage in intelligent behavior. the fungal mycelial network therefore provides a useful model for studying intelligent behavior in non-neural organisms and its evolution from unicellular to multicellular systems. topics in cognitive science

gut consciousness: a perspective on visceral phenomenal awareness abstract the proposition that the enteric nervous system sustains a form of consciousness is seldom entertained in mainstream neuroscience, yet it follows from a disciplined reading of contemporary theories of mind. we argue that the 400–600 million neurons embedded in the mammalian gastrointestinal wall, taken together with the vast interoceptive surface they supervise, the enteroendocrine–immune interface, and the microbial community they co-regulate, constitute a substrate that satisfies, on several of the leading theories of consciousness, the criteria those theories use to attribute experience elsewhere. we synthesize evidence on enteric autonomy, chemo- and mechanosensory resolution, vagal and humoral signalling, self/non–self-discrimination at the epithelial–immune boundary, comparative data from invertebrates whose nervous systems are dominated by gut-like plexuses, and convergent clinical signatures (irritable bowel syndrome, food intolerances, psychedelic nausea, glucagon-like peptide-1 signalling) that are difficult to accommodate under a purely sensorimotor account. throughout we distinguish two claims that are easily conflated: that the gut makes a large and underappreciated contribution to the single consciousness of the whole animal, and that enteric processing constitutes a second, much simpler locus of experience of its own. most of the available evidence bears on the first, and we set out five lines of investigation that would discriminate between them. we conclude that gut consciousness is a testable hypothesis, likely corresponding to an ‘animal’ mode of consciousness dominated by interoceptive feel, drive and affect, and we propose empirical directions for its further investigation. neuroscience of consciousness

from structure to experience: a spinozist framework for consciousness rooted in critical brain dynamics abstract the study of consciousness is divided between mechanistic accounts that overlook subjective experience and phenomenological approaches limited to neural correlates. we propose a unified framework by grounding our concrit model of consciousness and critical brain dynamics within spinoza’s ontological monism. spinoza’s principle of psycho-physical parallelism—mind and body as attributes of one substance—provides a metaphysical basis to dissolve the explanatory gap between neural processes and lived experience. within this framework, three properties which are maximized near criticality correspond, under spinoza’s parallelism, to mental dimensions: entropy corresponds to experiential richness—the diversity of idea under the attribute of thought, internal susceptibility to reflexive capacity or degrees of autonomy, and scale-free dynamics to the structural alignment with the common order of nature that, under the attribute of thought, is expressed in adequate ideas. thus, we propose that brain activity near criticality under the attribute of extension is the very same phenomenon that, under the attribute of thought, is conscious experience. this synthesis reinterprets leading theories—including integrated information theory, global neuronal workspace theory, and the entropic brain hypothesis—as complementary views of a shared underlying reality. by situating concrit within spinoza’s monism, we argue that consciousness is not emergent or epiphenomenal but the parallel manifestation of universal organizational principles, offering a conceptually unified and interpretively transparent framework for neuroscience. neuroscience of consciousness

is it possible to make unconscious inferences? the limits of the influence of unconsciously perceived stimuli on conscious decisions. stimuli presented outside conscious awareness can influence behavior, yet the extent to which such information supports complex decision-making remains unclear. the present study examined the limits of unconscious influence across three levels of decision complexity. participants made decisions based on stimuli presented using sandwich masking. stimulus presentation parameters were held constant across conditions, while decision requirements varied. simple decisions required no contextual integration, intermediate decisions required the integration of masked information with consciously presented context, and complex decisions additionally required logical inference. the results showed that decision accuracy decreased with increasing complexity: it was highest in the simple condition (58%, with strong bayesian evidence for above-chance performance), lower but still above chance in the medium condition (54%), and not reliably above chance in the complex condition. this suggests that unconscious influence can extend beyond simple decisions but becomes increasingly unreliable when decisions require more demanding integration or inferential processing. our findings indicate that one of the functional roles of consciousness may be to support the flexible use of information in higher-order cognitive processes and are broadly consistent with theoretical approaches such as the global neuronal workspace theory. neuroscience of consciousness

reconsidering pavilions as visual focal points: an eye-tracking study of viewing behaviour in classical chinese garden paintings chinese garden painting traditions have long emphasised the compositional importance of pavilions and have often treated them as visual focal points. however, whether a compositional focal point also becomes a focus of viewers’ attention during actual viewing remains an open question. this exploratory study examines five pavilion scenes from forty views of the yuanmingyuan by combining historical plan reconstruction, compositional analysis, eye tracking, and post-viewing questionnaires. thirty participants viewed the paintings while fixation timing, order, duration, and frequency were recorded. across most scenes, pavilions were not the first elements to attract attention and generally received less cumulative attention than vegetation, topography, or larger architectural groups. their visual prominence varied with spatial position, scale, and relationships with paths, water, terrain, and surrounding buildings. across scenes, pavilion fixation probability and time to first fixation did not differ significantly, whereas total fixation-duration proportion and fixation count did; jjmq exceeded each of the other four scenes on both cumulative measures. the findings suggest that pavilions function not as fixed visual centres but as conditional nodes of attention whose observed salience was associated with spatial relationships and pictorial composition in the five scenes examined. journal of eye movement research
