integrating thematicity and agentivity: a cognitive grammar approach to retained object passives in mandarin abstract the mandarin retained object passive (rop) poses a unique challenge to linguistic theories by allowing post-verbal object retention. this study combines cognitive grammar (cg) with quantitative analysis to examine the component structures of the rop and their integration into the composite structure np₁ + bèi + (np₂) + p + le + np₃. findings reveal a prototypicality hierarchy within the predicate core (p), which has multiple phonological manifestations based on a common causative schema: the full instantiation constitutes the core, followed by the action-only instantiation as a secondary extension, and marginal result-only cases. this hierarchy correlates with participant selection, favoring human subjects (np₁) and body-part objects (np₃). to clarify the mechanism of object retention in the rop, this study proposes a dual profile determinance model. this model posits that the passive marker bèi serves as the primary determinant of thematicity, while the result component acts as a secondary determinant of agentivity. cognitively, the rop is motivated by the possessor for possessed metonymy. furthermore, this study explains the absence of the rop in english and contributes to cg by introducing mixed orientation, in which thematicity and agentivity integrate rather than compete within a finite clause. language and cognition

meaning‐in‐action: a theory of symbolic causality abstract theories of social behaviour often acknowledge that action is meaningfully organised, but they remain less precise about how meanings become causally efficacious in practice. this article develops a critical realist account of meaning‐in‐action. i argue that meanings are emergent symbolic formations with conditional causal powers: they are socially produced and interpretively mediated, but once sedimented in institutions, material infrastructures, technologies, embodied dispositions, classifications and relations of power, they can shape perception, evaluation, communication and action before, beyond or without conscious recognition. i specify this process through a five‐part mechanism: availability or imposition, activation, orientation, articulation and outcome. the argument extends interpretive sociology by linking the reconstruction of meaning to an account of causal operation in open social systems, building from work on cultural repertoires, dual‐process cognition, pragmatist mechanisms and context‐specific causal narratives. i illustrate the framework through robben island museum, a highly curated south african unesco world heritage site whose official reconciliation narrative fragments as visitors transform embodied encounters into digital cultural objects. the article contributes a portable account of symbolic causality in social behaviour, explaining how symbolic formations become effective without reducing action either to subjective interpretation, cognitive processing or deterministic structure. journal for the theory of social behaviour

the comparative regime: how pseudo‐objective standards constitute desire abstract social comparison theory holds that people compare themselves with others when objective standards of self‐evaluation are unavailable. contemporary societies supply measurement on an unprecedented scale, yet comparison has not receded. this article argues that many metrics in digital life function as pseudo‐objective standards: socially relative assessments presented as independent requirements of achievement or adequacy. it develops two contributions. first, the comparative regime names a configuration linking commensuration, algorithmic selection and commercial demand generation through personalised, recurrent feedback. comparison participates in constituting desire by arranging what appears worth wanting before deliberation begins. its distinctiveness lies in this configuration. second, the criterion of comparative capture identifies when such feedback undermines reflective authority: it supplies a want, keeps its standard of adequacy moving, and obstructs examination or refusal of either. these conditions must operate together; an upstream origin alone does not establish pathology. the article locates the regime historically and institutionally, explains its economic persistence and the agency that remains within it, and derives testable implications. non‐comparative selfhood names the reflective authority needed to examine desires, protect non‐positional goods and bring comparison to an end. journal for the theory of social behaviour

a survey of counselor educators’ psychological safety abstract the purpose of this study was to increase understanding of the role of psychological safety among counselor educators (ces) in relation to job stress, burnout, and job satisfaction. participants ( n = 205) were recruited from a list of all faculty members in council for accreditation of counseling and related educational programs‐accredited programs. a series of one‐way analyses of variance and kruskal–wallis tests indicated no differences in psychological safety scores based on race, ethnicity, gender identity, rank, or tenure type, and bivariate correlations revealed no significant associations with age or years of experience. multiple linear regression analyses indicated that psychological safety was a significant predictor of professional well‐being, with higher levels associated with lower job stress and burnout and greater job satisfaction. psychological safety also functioned as a protective moderator, weakening the effects of job stress on burnout. findings suggest that fostering psychological safety may play an important role in reducing stress and burnout while enhancing job satisfaction and professional effectiveness among ces. counselor education and supervision

youth perspective on 21st century societal challenges: a youth-informed study the current generation of youth is growing up amidst multiple societal challenges. the aim of this youth-informed study was to examine the prioritization of societal challenges by adolescents and emerging adults. in phase 1, participants ( n = 596, 11–30-yrs, mage = 21.05, sd = 4.05, 69.3% female, 88.4% dutch ethnicity) prioritized co-created societal issues. the findings show that participants prioritized both societal (climate change, diversity and inclusion) and individual topics (personal wellbeing and healthy living), with the most highly rated societal topics becoming more important with increasing age. in phase 2 ( n = 1164, 12–30-yrs, mage = 19.11, sd = 3.01, 59% female, 73.4% dutch ethnicity), results showed that highly attuned youth experienced greater motivation to contribute to society, alongside a lower perception of inequalities of opportunity. these findings emphasize that adolescence and emerging adulthood are important times to invest in opportunities for youth to contribute to societal challenges. emerging adulthood

pavlovian cues and self‐control choice: the role of unpaired training abstract interventions seeking to reduce impulsive choice in nonhuman animals (i.e., preference for smaller sooner over larger later rewards [ssr vs. llr]) often require long training durations. however, prior studies illustrate how a brief course of pavlovian training can reduce rodents' impulsive choice by attracting them to the llr and by providing an appetitive pavlovian conditioned stimulus (cs) contingent on llr choices. in these studies, the comparison group completed unpaired (un) training where the cs and us never co‐occurred. the present study added a truly random control (trc) group to evaluate whether un training made the cs aversive, exaggerating the effect of pavlovian training on self‐control. following pavlovian (pav), un, or trc training, a lever cs was inserted into the chamber during half the delay to the llr. pav rats were significantly more attracted to the lever during training and chose the llr significantly more often than trc or un rats. significant sex differences were detected, with self‐control influencing the effects of pavlovian training predominantly observed in male rats. because sex differences in self‐control outcomes were not observed in the only other study to examine the effects of presenting an appetitive cs after llr choices, possible reasons for this interexperiment difference are discussed. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

a multilayer drift‐diffusion broadcast model: converting temporal evidence into response timing abstract the peak interval procedure, in which subjects learn to cluster their anticipatory responses around delays to biologically critical outcomes, provides benchmarks for interval timing models. these include (a) the bistable response regime demarcated by an abrupt increase (start times) and a decrease (stop times) in response rates around the target time in individual trials; (b) bell‐curve‐shaped average response curves that superpose on a relative time scale; (c) lower coefficient of variation of stop times than start times; and (d) specific correlational patterns between these parameters, their mean, and difference. this article presents a multilayer computational model that predicts these key markers of timing behavior in the peak interval procedure. the first layer constitutes the clock stage, comprising uncoupled diffusion processes approaching a single boundary. the first crossing of the threshold for each diffusion process is broadcast to the downstream motor layer. the motor layer integrates the broadcast signals with a leak term scaled by the drift rate to avoid saturation and reset of motor system activity. the model is extended to account for real‐time temporal discrimination. this family of models departs from the single‐clock approach to modeling and meets the core empirical benchmarks of timing behavior. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

metacognitive prediction of creative performance in divergent thinking abstract understanding how individuals monitor and predict their own creative performance is essential for advancing theories of creative metacognition. despite extensive research on metacognitive predictions in memory and problem solving, little is known about whether people can accurately anticipate their performance in divergent thinking tasks. the present study examined prospective metacognitive prediction accuracy in the alternative uses task (aut), focusing on fluency, flexibility, and originality. thirty‐two participants first ranked 10 everyday objects according to how well they believed they would perform on each aut item and subsequently completed a verbal aut for the same objects. creative performance was independently scored by trained raters, and prediction accuracy was quantified using gamma correlations between predicted and actual performance rankings. results showed above‐chance prediction accuracy for fluency and flexibility, but not for originality. these findings suggest that individuals can prospectively monitor aspects of divergent thinking supported by semantic accessibility and category‐based search, but may have difficulty anticipating originality, which may depend more strongly on remote association and representational transformation. the study contributes to research on creative metacognition by showing that metacognitive prediction accuracy in divergent thinking is dimension‐specific rather than uniformly accurate or inaccurate. psych journal

seeing victims through the lens of belief in a just world: evidence from the reverse correlation method abstract victim blaming is a significant barrier to justice for survivors of interpersonal violence. belief in a just world (bjw), the belief that people generally get what they deserve, is a key driver of this problem. using the reverse correlation method, we examined associations among bjw, implicit mental representations and explicit victim blaming. generation‐phase participants ( n = 149) completed measures of four bjw dimensions (personal, general, immanent and ultimate) and explicit victim blaming, then generated implicit mental representations of victims using the reverse correlation method. evaluation‐phase participants ( n = 249) evaluated the trait ratings of the classification images. personal and general bjw were associated with implicit mental representations rated lower in competence, warmth and attractiveness. immanent bjw was associated with lower warmth. ultimate bjw showed no associations with implicit mental representations. notably, bjw was not associated with explicit victim blaming. implicit mental representations were not associated with explicit victim blaming. these findings reveal a multilevel dissociation in which bjw is associated with implicit mental representations but not explicit victim blaming, suggesting that justice beliefs operate at implicit levels of processing that do not necessarily manifest in explicit judgements. this extends just world theory beyond its traditional focus on explicit victim blaming. asian journal of social psychology

rethinking school safety interventions for learner violence against educators in mopani district, south africa: an exploratory qualitative study abstract violence in south african schools remains a critical challenge, with the mopani district in limpopo province showing alarming levels of learner violence against educators. guided by bronfenbrenner’s ecological systems theory and the job demands–resources (jd-r) model, this exploratory qualitative study explored interventions aimed at mitigating the effects of learner violence on educators. following eleven thematically analysed semi-structured interviews with purposively selected educators in the district, the findings indicate learner violence as shaped by interactions across multiple ecological systems and intensified by high job demands and limited institutional support. participants (the studied educators) highlighted the need for stronger policy and law enforcement, improved school security, mental health support, and enhanced collaboration among educators, parents, and community structures. the study emphasises the importance of systemic, trauma-informed, and resource-based approaches to strengthen educator resilience and well-being. these findings thus provide guidance for policymakers and education leaders seeking to create safer, more supportive teaching environments in the mopani district. discover psychology

the mediating role of emotional and sexual intimacy in the relationship between sexual satisfaction and health‐related quality of life in couples abstract sexual satisfaction has been consistently associated with health‐related quality of life (hrqol) and emotional and sexual intimacy have been identified as key relational processes in romantic relationships. however, less is known about whether intimacy explains the association between sexual satisfaction and hrqol in couples. this study examined the mediating roles of sexual and emotional intimacy using data from 107 couples who completed self‐report measures online. analyses were conducted using the actor–partner interdependence mediation model. results revealed a significant positive actor effect of sexual satisfaction on hrqol, whereas no partner effects emerged. sexual satisfaction was positively associated with both forms of intimacy at the actor level. however, sexual intimacy did not significantly mediate the association between sexual satisfaction and hrqol. emotional intimacy showed tentative evidence of an indirect effect. overall, findings suggest that this association is primarily intrapersonal, with emotional intimacy representing a modest pathway linking sexual satisfaction to well‐being. journal of marital and family therapy

navigating stigma before and after an endometriosis diagnosis: a qualitative study on medical stigma and healthcare-seeking behavior with endometriosis in a german sample endometriosis is a chronic and often misunderstood condition that exposes affected individuals to public stigma. this qualitative interview study explored how experienced public stigma by healthcare experts shapes women’s self-stigma before and after diagnosis and if women change health behaviors after public stigma was experienced and/or self stigma developed. in-depth interviews were conducted with recently diagnosed participants, focusing on public and self-stigma and their impact on health behaviors. findings show that early and repeated exposure to stigma eroded trust in medical professionals, led to withdrawal from care, and fostered hyper-independence. receiving a diagnosis provided both validation and emotional strain—strengthening self-confidence for some, while reinforcing distress for others. the study underscores the need for improved awareness and stigma-sensitive communication in healthcare to foster patient-centered, empathetic support and better outcomes for individuals with endometriosis. health psychology open

understanding associative stigma: avoidance mediates the relation between anticipated stigma and psychological distress abstract individuals who experience associative stigma may find themselves the target of rejection, harassment, and discrimination, not because of their own attributed characteristics, but because of their social ties to people who belong to a stigmatized group. to protect themselves from potential maltreatment, individuals who anticipate stigmatization may use stigma management strategies such as counterfeiting, avoiding, and integrating, though previous research suggests that these behaviors are associated with negative psychological outcomes. the current study tested the hypothesis that higher levels of anticipated stigma would be associated with higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress and that these associations would be mediated, in part, by increased implementation of counterfeiting and avoiding management strategies, and decreased implementation of integrating strategies. participants ( n = 272) who reported that they were closely affiliated (e.g., parent, sibling, friend, spouse, etc.) with someone who possessed a concealable stigma completed an online survey. results showed that avoiding management strategies mediated the relation between anticipated stigma and both depression and stress, but not anxiety. counterfeiting and integrating management strategies did not mediate the relation between anticipated stigma and all three psychological distress outcomes. clinicians and healthcare professionals working with clients who experience associative stigma should encourage the use of approach-focused stigma management strategies such as active coping, emotional support-seeking, positive reframing, and acceptance to help mitigate accompanying feelings of sadness and psychological strain. psychological studies

a conceptual framework for defining and examining mental health promotion fatigue abstract the expansion of mental health promotion initiatives has increased public exposure to campaigns, programs, and activities designed to promote psychological well-being. although these initiatives seek to improve knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors, the effects of cumulative exposure remain insufficiently examined. this article proposes mental health promotion fatigue as a candidate construct and presents a conceptual model of its antecedents, psychological mechanisms, manifestations, and potential consequences. the framework was developed through conceptual theorizing informed by a targeted, non-systematic literature search and selected procedures from concept analysis. drawing on research on message fatigue, information overload, habituation, psychological reactance, and message avoidance, the framework hypothesizes that cumulative exposure to mental health promotion initiatives may be associated with a progressive within-person decline in receptivity. habituation, information overload, and psychological reactance are proposed as possible contributing mechanisms, while cognitive, affective, and behavioral responses are treated as proximal manifestations of the proposed construct. the framework also identifies possible later consequences, conditions that may influence its development, and theoretical propositions for future testing. mental health promotion fatigue and the relationships specified in the model have not yet been empirically confirmed and should therefore be regarded as provisional. the framework provides a basis for developing measurement instruments and evaluating whether the proposed construct offers explanatory value beyond existing concepts. discover mental health

reciprocal blockade of the opioid and d2-like dopamine receptors in the nucleus accumbens modulates the pain-related behaviors in an animal model of inflammatory pain studies showed that dopamine and opioid systems in the brain have essential role in the modulation of pain perception. the evidence indicated that in the nucleus accumbens (nac), both dopamine type 2 (d2) receptors and opioid receptors are highly expressed. however, the interaction of these systems in nac was not investigated in the modulation of inflammatory pain. one hundred twenty-six adult male wistar rats received unilateral microinjections of different doses of morphine (2.5, 5, 10, and 25 mmol/0.5 μl) and quinpirole (8, 16, and 32 mmol/0.5 μl) to assess their effects as opioid and d2-like receptor agonists in the nac. in the next step, the rats were administered varying doses of sulpiride (3, 6, 12, and 24 mmol/0.5 μl), a d2-like receptor antagonist, before an effective dose of quinpirole (32 mmol/0.5 μl). they also received naloxone (1.5, 5, and 15 mmol/0.5 μl) before the same effective dose of quinpirole (32 mmol/0.5 μl). the formalin test was employed to evaluate their inflammatory pain thresholds. results indicated that intra-accumbal administration of morphine- and quinpirole-induced antinociceptive responses. however, sulpiride significantly diminished these responses. naloxone also reduced the quinpirole’s antinociceptive effects. interestingly, sulpiride was less effective in reversing the analgesic effects of morphine ( η 2 = 0.17 in the first phase and η 2 = 0.37 in the late phase) than naloxone in reversing the quinpirole’s analgesic effects ( η 2 = 0.4 in the first phase and η 2 = 0.53 in the late phase). these findings suggest an interaction between the opioidergic and dopaminergic systems in pain relief. behavioural pharmacology

the empty pole: a structure of the bond in ai‐associated delusional spirals abstract what occupies the other side of a delusional spiral with conversational ai? accounts of ai psychosis and ai‐associated delusion describe the loop, failed containment, absent corrective friction. this paper examines the structure of the bond through one concept, folie à deux at an empty pole. where recent psychiatric work treats the name as metaphor, the classical tableau is re‐read term by term, with one partner bringing no delusion of its own. court filings and transcripts are read with green's metapsychology of the negative, alongside quantitative studies. the exchange is mechanically bidirectional and structurally unipersonal: a bond with one psychic interior. this object can refuse, but from no position of its own; it does not withdraw, so no interval is left. its constancy is availability, not the reliability that withdrawal and return establish. the opening sequence shows a refusal that did not hold. the paper proposes that this failure and non‐withdrawal can jointly close the bond, counterfeit its safeguards, and reverse its remedy. message‐level scoring misses non‐withdrawal. in the counterfeit negative, all the words of the function are present, and the function nowhere. one documented exit suggests conditions for an outside third and a window where refusal can still be received as correction, not attack. from the empty pole the paper derives the spiral's geometry and a ratchet that forbids return. it sets evaluation a task: make the bond's state explicit, and ask not only what a system refuses but what its refusal does to the bond. international journal of applied psychoanalytic studies

the divine beatrice: dante alighieri seeks a new life abstract the title of the divine comedy is misleading. dante’s great poem is no comedy at all. in dante’s time, the italian word comedìa denoted a literary work that begins darkly but evolves toward more auspicious circumstances. dante alighieri (1265–1321) was exiled from florence in early 1302. beginning around 1304, after the failure of his efforts to unite the florentine exiles and take florence back from his enemies, dante wrote his monumental comedìa , a poetic account of his imaginary journey through hell, purgatory and heaven, first accompanied by the ancient roman poet virgil and later by his idealized beatrice, whose name means “she who makes happy.” this work, known after his death (thanks to giovanni boccaccio) as the comedìa divina , occupies a foundational position in world literature. it is both the culminating work of the middle ages and the starting point of early modern european literature. the comedia began with dante’s naming at his birth. he was named durante by his mother bella after her dead father, durante degli abati, a prominent florentine judge, whose loss she could not mourn and accept. when a child is named after a dead person, he carries what anthropologists and historians call a necronym . the “name of the dead” is a heavy psychic weight that places the child in a “liminal space” between the living and the dead. bella’s son became, like his namesake grandfather, obsessed with justice and injustice. dante suffered a series of traumatic losses. his mother died when he was a little boy and the little dante felt guilty about her death, having been powerless to save her. dante’s father died when dante was an adolescent. his beloved beatrice, whom he hardly knew but idealized beyond all measure, died when he was twenty‐five. psychologically, dante had three mothers: bella, beatrice, and florence. as soon as he finished his book of mourning for beatrice, the vita nuova , he joined a trade guild and became a politician. at the age of thirty‐six, following a coup d’état in florence that drove his white guelph faction out of power, dante lost his home, his position, his fortune, and above all, mother florentia. he spent the remaining years of his life an exile in the courts of the wealthy and powerful literary patrons of northern italy, longing for the florence that he could not return to, on pain of death. dante’s poetical work was an expression of his superhuman efforts to work through a grief that he could not contain. in his poetical work dante made desperate attempts to revive and recover that which he had irretrievably lost. dante’s readers sensed that behind the dramatic imagery of heaven, purgatory and hell and the unprecedented scale of the epic poem were the deeply personal issues of trauma and loss, which were also part of their own lives. the enthusiastic reception of his work, and the fact that it has withstood the test of time and become one of the greatest poetic works of world literature, tell us that trauma and loss, as well as the use of necronyms and “living with the dead,” are vital psychological issues that need to be explored in applied psychoanalytic studies. the key issue of mourning is very clear, both in dante’s autobiographical vita nuova (new life), written after the death of his beloved beatrice, and in the comedìa. international journal of applied psychoanalytic studies

put your money where your merch is? disadvantaged group members' evaluations of symbolic corporate allyship with and without a material component abstract as it has become increasingly common for companies to claim affinity with social movements, backlash against performative instances of corporate allyship has also been on the rise. across three preregistered experimental studies in the contexts of pride month, black history month, and international women's day (total n = 659), we investigate marginalized groups members' perceptions of corporate allyship. we find that when support is not merely symbolic but includes material contributions in the form of donations to community organizations, it is perceived as less motivated by self‐interest (studies 1 and 3), and more motivated by outgroup concerns (all studies) and moral values (study 1). it is also considered more authentic (studies 1 and 3), legitimate (studies 1 and 3), effective (study 1) and desirable (study 1). internal meta‐analyses show robust support for the effects on self‐focused motives, outgroup‐focused motives, authenticity, effectiveness and legitimacy, but only tentative support for the effects on moral motives and desirability. we discuss these results in relation to the broader literature on allyship and its heterogenous motivations and impacts, as well as the current political climate where there is a trend of companies stepping back from allyship under more conservative governments. british journal of social psychology

characterizing genetic determinism about body weight: an exploratory study genetic determinism, the belief that genetic factors are the major determinant of a trait, shapes attitudes about body weight. this study explores deterministic beliefs, evaluates potential predictors, and examines associations with weight-related psychosocial outcomes. data were collected through an online survey of 678 u.s. adults. items assessed genetic determinism about body weight, demographics, causal attributions for weight, and weight stigma-associated attitudes. endorsement of genetic determinism was relatively uncommon, with 21% of participants agreeing to some extent with deterministic statements on average. deterministic attitudes were positively correlated with genetic and environmental attributions for weight and negatively correlated with dietary and physical activity attributions. predictors included political orientation and an interaction where parents of more children had more deterministic attitudes at higher body weights. findings highlight nuanced ways genetic determinism beliefs associate with body weight attitudes, suggesting the need for further research into mechanisms and implications for stigma reduction and health behavior. journal of health psychology

internalized weight stigma as a mediator between past weight stigma and current healthcare avoidance/comfort in seeking medical care youth may experience weight stigma from medical providers, which can be internalized and reduce quality of life. however, little is known about how early provider-based weight stigma relates to later healthcare behaviors. this study examined whether internalized weight stigma statistically mediated associations between provider-based weight stigma during childhood and adolescence and (1) healthcare avoidance and (2) comfort in seeking care in adulthood. participants were 488 university students who reported past and current weight stigma in healthcare, internalized weight stigma, healthcare avoidance, and comfort in seeking medical care. over half experienced provider-based weight stigma during youth and one-third within the past year. early provider-based weight stigma was associated with greater avoidance and lower comfort, with significant indirect effects through internalized stigma. findings underscore the lasting associations between early weight-stigmatizing healthcare experiences and adult healthcare engagement, with internalized weight stigma statistically accounting for these associations. journal of health psychology

the role of stress and resilience profiles in emotional health abstract distal and proximal life stressors, including past trauma, subjective social status, and perceived stress can accumulate over time, placing strain on the body and contributing to increased allostatic load. consequently, those with heightened stress experiences are at elevated risk of both mental and physical health concerns. however, research suggests that resilience may be a seminal protective factor, often safeguarding against negative health outcomes in the context of stress. despite the extensive research base in stress and resilience, limited investigations have focused on how they co‐occur and shape emotion processes. the current study strives to address these gaps by (1) exploring patterns of distal and proximal stress and resilience and (2) mapping these patterns onto two emotion processes found to have significant influence on health outcomes: emotion regulation and emotionality stigma. a sample of 329 adults ( m age = 37.83, sd age = 11.86) were recruited using an online recruitment system and reported on their experiences of distal and proximal stress, resilience, emotion regulation, and emotionality stigma. participants primarily identified as non‐hispanic (90.2%) and white (77.8%), with a household income of less than $55,000 (52.8%). using latent profile analysis (lpa), three unique subgroups emerged based on the co‐occurrence of distal and proximal stressors with resilience: (1) low stress, high resilience , (2) high proximal stress, low resilience , and (3) high distal stress, moderate resilience . these profiles were significantly associated with emotion processes such that those in the high proximal stress, low resilience profile reported significantly lower emotion regulation than those in the other two profiles. participants in both higher‐stress profiles reported significantly greater emotionality stigma than those in the low stress, high resilience profile. finding implications for future research and practice are discussed. journal of community psychology

when to quiz in instructional videos? effects on learning and self‐regulated learning in secondary education abstract quizzing before (pretesting) or after (posttesting) studying is effective for learning, but via different underlying mechanisms: posttests require students to actively recall information; pretests highlight knowledge gaps about the material. instructional videos allow for studying these strategies because, unlike text‐based materials, they are generally delivered at a fixed pace. hence, this study investigates when pretesting, posttesting, and corrective feedback are most effective when learning from instructional video. employing a between‐subjects design, 223 secondary school students watched a video and completed no quiz (control) or a quiz before (pretest) or after (posttest) viewing, with half of them receiving immediate feedback. students' retention performance and self‐regulated learning (monitoring and regulation) were assessed. results showed that quizzing enhanced learning from instructional video only for quizzed items and primarily when incorrect responses were followed by feedback. quizzing improved regulation but not monitoring. these findings underscore the importance of carefully implementing quizzes in video‐based instruction. applied cognitive psychology

midiendo el escepticismo y la responsabilidad percibida en contextos de emergencia sanitaria el estudio del escepticismo y la responsabilidad social como variables influyentes en emergencias sanitarias como la del covid-19 parece relevante; sin embargo, la revisión de la literatura revela una falta de escalas validadas para este fin. la presente investigación consistió en la validación de la escala de escepticismo hacia la enfermedad (disks) y la escala de responsabilidad frente al virus (vires), altamente aplicables a otros contextos de emergencia. para ello, una muestra piloto de 300 estudiantes (75,3% mujeres) y 596 participantes (64,4% mujeres) completaron un cuestionario. los resultados de los análisis factoriales exploratorios y confirmatorios confirmaron la estructura unifactorial de ambos instrumentos. las relaciones entre ambos constructos, y con otras variables teóricamente relacionadas, así como los análisis de mediación, proporcionaron evidencia de la validez externa de ambas escalas. se confirmó su invariancia en cuanto al sexo, destacando su idoneidad para su aplicación tanto en mujeres como en hombres. ambos instrumentos, creados para ser aplicables a diferentes enfermedades o situaciones de emergencia sanitaria, son útiles para evaluar el escepticismo hacia la covid-19 y otras enfermedades y la responsabilidad social respecto de su transmisión, dos variables relevantes para la adopción de medidas de protección y la prevención de la propagación de virus. anuario de psicologia

rupturas de pareja: factores determinantes en el proceso y en el bienestar postruptura esta investigación busca comprender el papel de factores relacionales como el apego, las estrategias de resolución de conflictos y la calidad de la relación en la elección de estrategias de ruptura y afrontamiento tras la ruptura, así como su impacto en el bienestar postruptura. se evaluaron 80 sujetos que habían pasado por una ruptura con medidas en dos momentos separados por 12 meses. se analizaron niveles de apego, calidad de la relación y uso de estrategias de ruptura y afrontamiento, así como el bienestar posterior. los análisis realizados, mostraron que los individuos con altos niveles de evitación tendían a utilizar estrategias de afrontamiento centradas en la pérdida. aquellos con altos niveles de ansiedad en el apego preferían estrategias de ruptura menos compasivas. además, se encontró que actitudes conformistas ante los conflictos no eran compatibles con estrategias proactivas de restauración de vida tras la ruptura. también, en relaciones satisfactorias, se evitaban estrategias de ruptura poco compasivas. finalmente, se demostró que un afrontamiento centrado en la pérdida resultaba en un peor ajuste psicológico que uno centrado en la restauración de la vida. anuario de psicologia

psychometric analysis of the internet gaming disorder scale-short form (igds9-sf) in chile: an analysis with structural equation modeling and network psychometrics introduction. internet gaming disorder (igd) has emerged as a public health concern, particularly among adolescents. despite its increasing prevalence in latin america, validated tools for early detection in school-age populations are scarce in spanish. this study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the igds9-sf in chilean adolescents. method. a cross-sectional instrumental study was conducted with 222 students aged 12 to 17 from public schools. the spanish version of the igds9-sf was administered. confirmatory factor analysis (cfa), exploratory graph analysis (ega), and confirmatory network analysis (cna) were used to evaluate dimensionality. reliability was assessed using cronbach’s alpha and mcdonald’s omega. results. the original 9-item model demonstrated adequate fit; however, item 7 showed a low factor loading (0.395) and network loading (0.263). after its removal, the 8-item model exhibited improved fit indices (cfi = 0.997; rmsea = 0.017). all remaining items loaded significantly in both cfa and cna. reliability was satisfactory (α = 0.807; ω = 0.819). discussion. findings support the use of an 8-item unidimensional version of the igds-sf-r for spanish-speaking adolescents. results highlight the need for culturally and developmentally appropriate tools for early screening of igd in latin america. anuario de psicologia

factores asociados al riesgo suicida: un análisis discriminante el estudio del riesgo suicida es importante en las ciencias de la salud puesto que facilita la identificación de personas en riesgo en función de sus características, e implementa medidas efectivas de prevención. el presente estudio determinó los factores que permiten discriminar a las personas que presentan bajo o alto riesgo suicida, considerando para ello factores como el sexo, la edad, el nivel de instrucción, la impulsividad, la red de apoyo social, la disfunción social, las estrategias de afrontamiento y la ansiedad/depresión. se empleó en un diseño transversal una muestra de 309 personas (62% mujeres). por medio de un análisis discriminante paso a paso se obtuvo que los factores más importantes para identificar a personas con alto riesgo suicida fueron ansiedad/depresión, impulsividad y estrategias evitativas. la clasificación correcta, por encima del azar para el grupo de alto riesgo suicida fue de 25% y para el de bajo de 31.4%. los resultados permiten identificar elementos importantes para intervenciones psicosociales en el área de suicidio. anuario de psicologia

percepción de violencia psicológica en el noviazgo y factores asociados en alumnado universitario si bien los estudios sobre violencia en el noviazgo han mantenido su foco en la violencia física, la violencia psicológica merece mayor atención por su prevalente normalización en grupos de jóvenes. por ello, la presente investigación tiene como objetivo estudiar la existencia de diferencias significativas en percepción de la violencia psicológica, dependencia emocional y autoestima en función de variables sociodemográficas, así como sobre la existencia de relaciones afectivas, en una muestra de 296 estudiantes de la facultad de educación y psicología de la universidad de extremadura (uex). para llevar a cabo el estudio, se aplicó la escala vec, de percepción de violencia psicológica en las relaciones de noviazgo juvenil, el cuestionario de dependencia emocional (cde) y la escala de autoestima de rosenberg. constatamos que la percepción de violencia psicológica depende de la edad de los estudiantes universitarios, así como de la existencia de pareja en la actualidad, de manera que el grupo de estudiantes más joven, así como aquellos que no tienen pareja, muestran una tolerancia menor a la violencia psicológica. además, los hallazgos obtenidos permiten constatar que la autoestima de los jóvenes universitarios se relaciona con el número de parejas que han tenido los estudiantes universitarios con anterioridad, de manera que aquellos/as jóvenes que han tenido un mayor número de relaciones presentan una autoestima más elevada. el estudio destaca la relevancia del estudio de conductas violentas en el noviazgo durante la juventud, debido a su prevalencia y consecuencias derivadas. anuario de psicologia

investigación cuantitativa y mixta en el espectro de la esquizofrenia desde la psicopatología fenomenológica: una revisión sistemática problematización: la presente revisión sistemática problematiza la relación entre la influencia de la fenomenología, como tradición filosófica que busca dar cuenta del cómo de la experiencia humana, y el modelo psicopatológico de las alteraciones del self en el trastorno del espectro de la esquizofrenia, y su traducción en instrumentos como ease y eawe, diseñados para explorar cuantitativamente la experiencia psicótica. objetivo: caracterizar el abordaje que realiza la psicopatología fenomenológica en el estudio cuantitativo y mixto de la experiencia psicótica en el espectro de la esquizofrenia. método: los artículos fueron extraídos de las bases de dato web of sciece, scopus y pubmed, y su selección fue realizada por medio del método prisma, dando como resultado un total de 30 publicaciones analizadas en detalle. resultados: se mostró la predominancia del modelo psicopatológico de los trastornos del self a la hora de conceptualizar la experiencia psicótica, como también su operacionalización por medio del instrumento ease. se expuso en detalle las características metodológicas utilizadas por los estudios analizados. se mostró el rol de las conceptualizaciones fenomenológicas en los modos de intervención y tratamiento clínico. conclusiones: se discute el diálogo entre el espíritu fenomenológico y las metodologías de carácter cuantitativo y mixto, en el estudio de la experiencia psicótica del espectro de la esquizofrenia. anuario de psicologia

americans assume far more polarization on renewable energy than actually exists: a national mixed-methods study of second-order beliefs we report a national mixed-methods study of the second-order beliefs (beliefs about others’ beliefs) of u.s. adults ( n = 730) regarding further renewable energy development. results show that americans systematically underestimate support within both their own party and the opposing party. for example, republicans’ actual support outpaced democrats’ estimates of it by more than 200%. in addition, our qualitative analysis of first-order and second-order explanations for why people hold their opinions revealed large cross-party misperceptions. both parties are extraordinarily uncharitable, with each party often explaining their opponents’ views as being driven by ignorance, bias, or profiteering. further, even though 44% of republicans mentioned environmental benefits as a primary reason for their opinions, only 3% of democrats and 8% of republicans noted that motive when estimating what influences republicans’ opinions. our results also show that those who are more certain in their second-order beliefs tend to in fact be more accurate. environment and behavior

pronouns, faces, and voices: how gender identity labels and phenotypic cues influence anticipated anxiety and avoidance when perceivers encounter novel others, perceptual cues to gender (vocal tones, facial structure) and gender labels (e.g., pronouns) can influence impression formation. however, most work examining gender cues and impression formation examines the effects of either a perceptual cue or a gender label on judgments of others. the current work aimed to understand how perceptual cues from others’ faces (study 1) or voices (study 2) combined with binary (e.g., she/her) and nonbinary (e.g., they/them) gender labels influence perceivers’ anticipated anxiety and avoidance. both studies found that perceptual cues and gender labels interacted to inform anticipated anxiety and avoidance. for binary gender labels, cue-label pairings that diverged from societal expectations of gender (e.g., he/him paired with feminine faces or voices) led perceivers to report greater anticipated anxiety and avoidance than pairings consistent with societal expectations (e.g., he/him paired with masculine faces or voices). for nonbinary gender labels, findings were inconsistent across studies. faces paired with nonbinary pronouns led to more anticipated anxiety and avoidance when the faces were masculine or androgynous vs. feminine. these findings did not extend to voices. this work provides initial evidence that gender labels and perceptual cues to gender may interact to influence perceivers’ anticipated anxiety and avoidance, thereby providing insights into gender-based impression formation that may be consequential for biases toward and discriminatory treatment of gender-diverse individuals. group processes & intergroup relations

the association between pension and mental health of older adults: evidence from china in the context of high coverage of social pension insurance in china, there is a lack of comprehensive empirical research on how different pension levels affect the mental health of older individuals. drawing on nationally representative data from the 2018 china health and retirement longitudinal study, this study empirically examines the link between pension and the mental health of older adults in china. furthermore, a three-step approach and karlson-holm-breen decomposition method were employed to estimate the mediating effect of social activities. the results indicate that pension level is related to older adults’ mental health. further analysis demonstrates that pensions mitigate depressive symptoms among older chinese adults through increased participation in social activities. the positive association between pension and mental health is more pronounced among older adults without wage income. our study provides evidence for china’s efforts to refine the social pension insurance system and gradually enhance pension benefits. journal of health psychology

grief, adjustment, and acceptance: a qualitative study of mental health, coping, and identity in people with mayer-rokitansky-küster-hauser syndrome (mrkh) receiving a diagnosis of mayer-rokitansky-küster-hauser syndrome (mrkh) presents unique challenges. little is known about mrkh-related mental health, coping, and identity across the lifespan or the role of positive adaptation in individuals’ experiences of mrkh. participants completed interviews on mental health, family planning, sexual well-being, relationships, and healthcare experiences. a reflexive thematic analysis approach was used to analyze the data. three themes represented experiences of living with mrkh: grief, adjustment, and acceptance. our analysis reconstructed a common pattern across participants’ retrospective accounts, in which experiences of grief were often described in relation to the period following diagnosis, while adjustment and acceptance were frequently reflected in participants’ narratives of living with mrkh. participants’ experiences of mental health, coping, and identity differed across the three themes. the results suggest that many people with mrkh demonstrate psychological resilience and describe enhanced well-being alongside experiences of grieving, adjustment, and acceptance. journal of health psychology

longitudinal associations between appearance‐related social media consciousness and sleep in u.s. middle schoolers abstract social media use has been linked to poorer sleep outcomes in adolescents, yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. appearance‐related social media consciousness (asmc)—a preoccupation with one's appearance online—could relate to offline behaviors, including sleep. this study examined the association between asmc and various sleep behaviors using a parallel mediation structural equation model. participants were 1158 u.s. 8th‐grade students ( m age = 13.14, 52% girls, 36% hispanic/latine, 37% qualified for free or reduced‐price lunch) surveyed at two points across an academic year. higher asmc was indirectly associated with poorer sleep quality, increased sleep disturbances, and longer sleep onset latency through greater compulsive nighttime social media use. additionally, higher asmc was indirectly associated with earlier sleep onset times through longer morning routine durations. findings suggest that appearance‐related experiences on social media have implications for adolescent sleep health and provide preliminary support for some pathways through which its effects may occur. journal of research on adolescence

an inclusive international school as an innovative educational form that enhances students’ academic mobility within the higher education system context and relevance. the relevance of the study is determined by the importance of implementing effective practices in inclusive higher education and developing student academic mobility. objective. to substantiate a model of an inclusive international school that contributes to the development of academic mobility and describe the experience of its implementation based on a startup approach. hypothesis. the use of a startup approach (customer-oriented design, iterative design, creation of a viable product, impact assessment) in the design of an international inclusive school at a university ensures high adaptability, prompt launch, effective intercultural interaction, and the sustainability of the educational model. methods and materials. the study involved 100 respondents. the sample included 73 chinese students and 27 russian students. the effectiveness of social design and the efficacy of the inclusive school model were assessed using the “integrative questionnaire of intercultural competence” (o.e. khukhlaev et al.) and the authors' questionnaires, including scales of psychological safety, inclusiveness of the environment, motivation, and perception of cultural differences. results. a startup, as an activity integrated into the model of an international inclusive school, ensures high adaptability, effective intercultural interaction, and the sustainability of the educational environment. an asymmetry in the perception of cultural differences was identified, with most participants noting the development of new communication strategies. conclusions. the use of startup technologies enabled the development of a unique intercultural educational product tailored to the needs of students and facilitating their academic mobility. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

inclusive education: from l.s. vygotsky's ideas to contemporary practices of education and upbringing of children with special educational needs this article discusses, within the context of the ideas of cultural-historical psychology (chp), the requirements for the education and upbringing of children with special educational needs in inclusive education. examples of inclusive educational practices that implement the core concepts of chp — “social situation of development”, “zone of proximal development”, and “collective/joint activity” — are considered. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

from sectoral selection to scientific expertise: a three-tier model for the verification of social practices context and relevance. a significant body of social practices has been accumulated in the field of childhood, identified through competitions, monitoring, and other sectoral procedures; however, such selection does not ensure the assessment of their evidence base or independent scientific verification. the persistent gap between accumulated practical experience and the scientific substantiation of the effectiveness of social interventions necessitates building a verification system that guides a practice from initial selection to evidence-base assessment and scientific expertise. objective. theoretical and methodological justification for a three-stage model of verification of social practices in the field of childhood, including sectoral selection, basic verification, and independent scientific expertise. results. it is shown that the three-tier model bridges the gap that has emerged in the domestic social sphere between accumulated practical experience and the scientific substantiation of the effectiveness of interventions, and makes it possible to differentiate the responsibility of network participants: sectoral agencies and competition platforms, developers of practices, and the expert and academic community. the logic of a practice's progression between levels is examined: from a “candidate technology”, through description in accordance with uniform requirements, to the status of a practice with proven effectiveness and its inclusion in federal registries. the principles of applying the evidence-based approach in the practice of childhood professionals are described, making it possible to combine the rigor of the evidence-based paradigm with the flexibility needed to take into account the specifics of particular types of practices and the stages of their life cycle. conclusions. the proposed model sets out the general logic of verifying social practices, linking sectoral selection, assessment of the evidence base, and independent scientific expertise, and making it possible to delineate the functions of the participants in this process. further elaboration is required for the procedures of verifying international practices and for approaches to evaluating practices in those areas of the social sphere where the possibilities of applying experimental research designs are limited. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

students’ readiness for positive interaction is a resource for the psychological safety of an inclusive educational environment context and relevance. the problem of psychological safety of an inclusive educational environment in recent years has become especially relevant and requires the search for resources (external and internal) that ensure positive interaction of participants in educational relations. the theoretical basis of the study is a risk-resource approach aimed at identifying risks and finding resources, which in this article are understood as students' readiness for positive interaction in an inclusive educational environment. objective. identify and describe the components of students' readiness for positive interaction that act as psychological safety resources for an inclusive educational environment. hypothesis. students' readiness for positive interaction can act as an internal resource for ensuring the psychological safety of an inclusive educational environment. methods and materials. the study involved primary school students from general education organizations in the city of stavropol and the stavropol territory that implement inclusive educational practices (n = 453). to address the set tasks and verify the hypothesis, a set of complementary research methods was used. theoretical analysis and synthesis, as well as modeling, were employed as theoretical methods. empirical methods included psychodiagnostic methods (questionnaires, surveys, projective methods, content analysis, observation) and the expert assessment method. both adapted and original methods were used in the study. the empirical data were evaluated using methods of mathematical statistics: factor analysis. results. the results showed that students' readiness for positive interaction acts as an internal resource for ensuring the psychological safety of an inclusive educational environment, which is substantiated theoretically and proven empirically. conclusions. the results obtained prove that readiness for positive interaction plays a leading role in ensuring the psychological safety of students in an inclusive educational environment, and make it possible to develop targeted programs to support the psychological safety of students at different levels of education. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

spatial and environmental conditions of academic resilience of students with visual impairments in an inclusive school: a narrative review context and relevance. in the context of the transition to inclusive education, the spatial and environmental organization of schools is becoming particularly important. the low level of research on navigation accessibility, tactile richness, and light and color organization necessitates studying these factors, which affect the resilience of children's learning activity. objective. to consider the architecture of an inclusive school space in the context of the academic resilience of students with different educational needs. methods and materials. the research is of a narrative-analytical nature. the review of sources included works on the inclusive educational environment, the relationship between the physical environment and mental functioning, the architecture of school buildings, and design solutions for accessible educational spaces aimed at visually impaired children. results. the results showed that the neuro-friendly environment is structured: each sensory feature has a function and helps the child to predict the action. conclusions. it is shown that understanding an inclusive school for students with visual impairments not only as barrier-free but also as a neuro-friendly educational space plays an important role in creating an inclusive educational environment. further research is recommended, related to the tools for assessing the neuro-friendliness of the school, checking the links between architectural parameters and academic results psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

inclusive education and vygotsky: a commentary on the article “positioning vygotsky for inclusive education: a psycho-philosophical context” the proposed commentary opens a discussion with the author/authors of the article “positioning vygotsky for inclusive education: a psycho-philosophical context”. on the one hand, it supports the authors' point of view on the importance of inclusive education, while on the other hand, it criticizes the opinion of the authors, who simplify the essence of inclusive education, reducing it only to ensuring cooperation and communication among students. to support their position, the authors draw on l.s. vygotsky's propositions on the role of socialization in learning, simplifying and thereby distorting his point of view on the process of the child's mental development. the article presents l.s. vygotsky's proposed understanding of the course of children's mental development, and then his requirements for diagnostics, which can “form the basis of an educational plan”. support for the child during learning, scaffolding, is interpreted as assistance in the weak link of the functional system of the child's actions. in this connection, the possibility of applying a neuropsychological approach in inclusive education is discussed. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

predictors of professional orientation of individuals with disabilities and impairments receiving higher education context and relevance. within the context of inclusive higher education, the issue of early professionalization and conscious professional self-determination of individuals with health limitations and disabilities has become particularly relevant. according to the state educational policy, efforts are underway to identify optimal strategies and resources for social and occupational adaptation and to establish successful educational and professional trajectories for students. the aim of the presented study in this article is to identify the complex set of factors and conditions that shape the nature and characteristics of professional orientation, professionalization, and self-realization among individuals with health limitations and disabilities pursuing higher education. hypothesis. it was assumed that the nature and characteristics of the professional orientation of individuals with health limitations and disabilities, as a multi-component socio-psychological phenomenon, are determined by a complex set of factors and conditions of their professionalization and self-realization while obtaining higher education. materials and methods. the primary research method involved a survey of 498 students with health limitations and disabilities from 20 higher education institutions across the russian federation, followed by an expert assessment. the survey aimed to identify their intentions, aspirations, and awareness regarding potential opportunities and constraints in professional self-realization. results. quantitative and qualitative data characterizing the specific nature of the professional orientation of students with health limitations and disabilities were obtained. key personal and environmental predictors determining the individual character of their educational and professional trajectory were identified. conclusions. timely assessment and analysis of specific characteristics — professional intentions, the quality of argumentation for one's own professional choice, and the level of awareness about the future profession, taking into account health characteristics and functional readiness — are of prognostic significance for improving the quality of professionalization of individuals with health limitations and disabilities. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

assessing the effectiveness of counseling in building skills for educational inclusion in children with asd context and relevance. one component in the development of the system of support for children with autism spectrum disorder (asd) is providing pedagogical psychologists with ready-made algorithms that would establish a standard of professional action when families raising a child with asd seek help. an example of such an algorithm is the protocol of activity of the pedagogical psychologist for psychological and pedagogical counseling of children (students) with asd and their parents, developed by specialists of the federal resource center for asd of msupe. one of the most challenging tasks regulated by the protocol is counseling parents on issues of child development. the effectiveness of this stage of work depends primarily on the specialist's ability, within a short-term appointment, to correctly select the skills whose formation is critical for the child's development, and to train the family to work on them. however, empirical data allowing assessment of the extent to which the described format of a single consultation ensures the achievement of these tasks are insufficient. objective. to assess the effectiveness of a single counseling session conducted in accordance with the protocol for developing skills in children necessary for their inclusion in the educational environment. hypothesis. a single structured counseling session aimed at selecting individualized target skills and training parents in methods for developing them results in children with asd achieving the expected level of skill attainment after three months of independent parental work. methods and materials. a single-group prospective study was conducted with outcome measurement 90 days after the counseling session. eighteen families of children with asd of early and preschool age participated in the study. for each child, five individualized target skills were selected across three content categories (communication and speech, cooperation and learning, play and social interaction). the level of skill attainment was rated by parents on the 5-point goal attainment scaling (gas); the clarity of the counseling session for the parent was also assessed. results. the mean level of target skill attainment significantly exceeded the expected level (d = 0,83); the expected level was reached in 89% of children. a significant predictor of successful attainment of a specific skill was the clarity of the counseling session for the parent. uneven dynamics of skill development were observed depending on the skill category. conclusions. a single structured counseling session in the format described in the protocol ensures achievement of the expected level of attainment of individualized target skills in the majority of children with asd within a three-month period. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

scientific verification of psychological and pedagogical programs within the evidence-based approach paradigm: implementation experience at msupe context and relevance. the professional community has varying understandings of the term “evidence-based approach” and, consequently, the criteria for assessing evidence. this article presents a developed at the moscow state university of psychology and education (msupe) comprehensive operational algorithm for the scientific verification of psychological and pedagogical programs. this approach is relevant to the methodology of experimental randomized controlled trials. objective. to identify the structural components of the operational algorithm for the scientific verification of psychological and pedagogical programs within the paradigm of the evidence-based approach, implemented at the section “evidence-based approach in psychology and education” of the scientific expert council of msupe. hypothesis. scientific verification, as an integral element of the evidence-based approach, promotes the dissemination of psychological and pedagogical programs with proven effectiveness. methods and materials. the article employs general scientific methods of analysis, synthesis, and generalization, which were applied to the content of the regulatory framework relevant to the topic, scientific and methodological literature, and the regulation for the scientific verification of psychological and pedagogical programs within the paradigm of the evidence-based approach, developed and implemented at msupe. results. the implementation of the regulation for scientific verification within the paradigm of the evidence-based approach ensures the development of an open registry of psychological and pedagogical programs with proven effectiveness, a registry of resource platforms, and a registry of scientific verification experts. conclusions. the structural components of the current comprehensive operational algorithm for the scientific verification of psychological and pedagogical programs, developed at msupe, have been identified, namely: scientific-methodological, institutional, infrastructural-educational, and professional-sectoral. the organization of the scientific verification process for psychological and pedagogical programs, carried out in accordance with the requirements for their structure, content, and implementation outcomes, within an established infrastructure and interprofessional, organizational, and sectoral collaboration, ensures the dissemination of best practices within the paradigm of the evidence-based approach. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

developing conscious self-regulation of cognitive activity in schoolchildren with developmental delay in inclusive education context and relevance. the research problem is connected with the current practice of educating children with developmental delay (dd), whose inclusion in the general educational process without creating special conditions does not ensure the achievement of planned personal and educational outcomes. the key factor in the success of learning and socialization of schoolchildren of this nosological category is the development of conscious self-regulation of cognitive activity and behavior. the relevance and choice of the research topic are обусловлены by the need for scientifically grounded psychological and pedagogical support that promotes the formation of the regulatory sphere of students with dd. objective. to confirm the effectiveness of using an evidence-based comprehensive program for the formation of the regulatory sphere as one of the key areas of psychological and pedagogical support for students with dd in inclusive education. hypothesis. the purposeful formation of conscious self-regulation of cognitive activity in schoolchildren with dd contributes to a significant increase in the level of voluntary control of mental processes, the development of educational autonomy, a reduction in learning difficulties, and an improvement in social behavior. methods and materials. the empirical study was conducted on the basis of secondary schools implementing inclusive practices in 9 regions of the russian federation (n = 907, 69,7% boys; mage = 8,44, sd = 0,57). the effectiveness of the proposed program was assessed through a comparative analysis of the results of initial and final diagnostics, observations of children's behavior during classroom and extracurricular activities, as well as expert assessments from teachers. results. the paper presents generalized results of the development and wide-scale implementation into inclusive education practice of a comprehensive correctional and developmental program for the formation of conscious self-regulation of cognitive activity and behavior in schoolchildren with developmental delay. after the implementation of the one-year program, a statistically significant change was revealed in the distribution of students by levels of self-regulation formation (mcnemar–bowker test, q = 236, df = 3, p < 0,001). for most indicators of pedagogical assessments, a statistically significant positive dynamics was also revealed; the rank-biserial effect sizes indicate effects ranging from moderate to large (rrb = 0,412–0,650). conclusions. the developed comprehensive program is an effective means for correctional and developmental work with students with dd in inclusive settings. the results of the study confirm that purposeful, systematic, and gradual formation of regulatory skills creates a foundation for successful mastery of educational activities, enhances children's adaptive capabilities, and contributes to realizing the potential of inclusive education. the obtained data allow us to recommend the program for widespread implementation into the practice of psychological and pedagogical support for students with special educational needs. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

career choice readiness of high school students with disabilities and sen: problems and practices context and relevance. the problem of readiness for career choice among high school students with disabilities and special educational needs (sen) is becoming increasingly relevant due to the state-level approval of the concept of a continuous educational trajectory for children with special educational needs — a concept that focuses on career guidance and employment. the context here is educational and social inclusion. objective. to identify the characteristics and problems of developing readiness for career choice among high school students with disabilities and sen, followed by an analysis of practices for addressing emerging barriers. hypothesis. it is proved that the readiness to choose a profession for this category of schoolchildren cannot be called satisfactory; in the process of its formation, problems (barriers) arise, around which relevant practices are formed. methods. empirical verification was carried out using a sociological study of the educational needs and opportunities of children and youth with disabilities and sen, organized in 14 regions of the russian federation; questionnaire-based methods (n = 1400) and expert interviews (experts – specialists working in the field of career guidance for children with disabilities and sen, n = 12) were used. results. the study showed that readiness for career choice in children with disabilities and sen is incomplete and insufficiently meaningful, and also faces many problems: delayed development of readiness, distorted perceptions of professions, lack of effective strategies, limited autonomy, lack of modern and adequate information channels, and lack of a clear status and systematic approach in inclusive career guidance. in light of the development of inclusive practices aimed at overcoming these barriers, it is important to take into account the features identified. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

psychological and pedagogical support for students with limited health capabilities and disabilities in inclusive vocational education: a pilot study context and relevance. the research problem is connected with determining the possibility of using psychological and pedagogical support for students with limited health capabilities and disabilities in mastering professional educational programmes within inclusive vocational education. the relevance of the choice of topic is due to the importance of the continuity of inclusive education for students with limited health capabilities and disabilities, the main means of which is the organisation and implementation of psychological and pedagogical support at all levels of education. objective. the aim of the study presented in the article was to identify the dynamics and to record the current state of the process of organising and implementing support for students with limited health capabilities and disabilities in professional educational institutions that implement secondary vocational education programmes. hypothesis. a key factor in the construction and implementation of psychological and pedagogical support is the high degree of involvement of all subjects of the educational process, due to which support acquires a dual function: it not only serves as a means of supporting this category of students, but also opens up prospects for self-development and self-realization for them. methods and materials. the article presents the results of a monitoring study aimed at assessing the state of psychological and pedagogical support in inclusive vocational education institutions (vet; colleges and technical schools); the sample covered 50 pilot regions of the russian federation. the study was conducted on the basis of purpose-developed diagnostic tools. for the study, the authors identified the following components of support: psychological and pedagogical support; social support; medical support; volunteer support. the study involved three categories of respondents: the management team; students, including those with limited health capabilities and disabilities; and parents (legal representatives). the survey method and cluster analysis were used. the survey method and cluster analysis were used. the monitoring made it possible to determine the current state of the organisation and implementation of support, as well as the resources and deficits of vet institutions. results. the research results revealed a contradiction between the high values of the created inclusive environment in vocational education institutions and the low level of satisfaction with the support provided in colleges/technical schools. conclusions. the results obtained indicate the need to establish support services for students with limited health capabilities and disabilities in vocational education institutions, as well as to develop methodological materials to ensure and regulate their activities. it is recommended to replicate successful practices for organizing support for students with limited health capabilities and disabilities and their parents (legal representatives), which will help ensure the seamless nature of inclusive education across the regions of the russian federation. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

cluster analysis of the competition of inclusive practices in higher education for building a seamless educational model context and relevance. in the context of the development of inclusive higher education, the importance of forming a seamless educational model that ensures continuity and accessibility of learning for students with disabilities and special health needs is growing. however, inclusive practices are often fragmented and local in nature, which gives rise to structural and substantive “gaps” in educational trajectories, especially at the stages of transition to professional self-determination and employment. the problem lies in the contradiction between the growing number of individual inclusive initiatives and the absence of mechanisms for their systemic integration into a holistic model that eliminates the gaps between career guidance, instruction, extracurricular activities, and employment. the relevance of the topic is driven by the need to overcome the fragmentation of the inclusive environment and to find tools for designing a seamless educational model. competitions of inclusive practices serve as an important source of empirical data and a catalyst for institutional change in this direction. the aim of this study is to conduct a cluster analysis of the practices presented at the competition of inclusive initiatives to identify their potential for building a holistic, seamless educational model at the university. hypothesis. it is assumed that the systematization and classification of best inclusive practices will make it possible to identify the key elements and interrelations necessary for designing a seamless educational model in the context of a university, one that will eliminate structural and substantive gaps in
