the german emotion beliefs questionnaire: factorial validity, measurement invariance, and descriptive reference values in a population-representative sample. background: beliefs about emotions are considered a central mechanism of emotion regulation and mental health [1]. the 16-item emotion beliefs questionnaire (ebq; [2]) assesses beliefs about the usefulness and controllability of positive and negative emotions. while the original study supported a three-factor model, subsequent population-based studies favored the theoretically proposed four-factor structure. although two german-language adaptations exist, neither has been validated in a population-representative sample, and descriptive reference values, evidence for measurement invariance across key sociodemographic groups, and systematic investigations of sociodemographic correlates of emotion beliefs are still lacking.
methods: the german version of the ebq [3] was administered to a representative sample of the german general population (n = 2368; mean age = 50.3; sd = 17.13; range: 18-93; 44.7% men, 55.2% women). confirmatory factor analyses (mlr) were conducted to compare competing three- and four-factor models. measurement invariance across gender, age, and educational level was examined and descriptive reference values were calculated.
results: although the four-factor model fit better than the three-factor solution on all indices examined, the two controllability factors were very highly correlated (r = .90) and showed limited discriminant validity, indicating a largely valence-independent controllability dimension. bifactor analyses supported interpretation of the total score (ω_h = 0.792, ecv = 0.603), and the ebq further demonstrated good psychometric properties. measurement invariance was supported up to the strict level across age and gender, and approximately at the scalar level across education. educational attainment showed the most consistent associations with emotion beliefs across the total score and all subscales. descriptive percentile reference values are provided by age group and gender.
conclusions: the german ebq demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties in a representative adult sample. population-based descriptive reference values may facilitate research comparisons and preliminary clinical contextualization of individual scores. the findings support a largely valence-independent controllability dimension and highlight educational attainment as a consistent sociodemographic correlate of emotion beliefs. bmc psychology
spatial–numerical associations survive spatial frequency equalization in an adult unimanual snarc task psychonomic bulletin & review

rising from the floor: a movement analysis of older adults and individuals with parkinson’s disease parkinson’s disease (pd) is a common chronic neurological disorder leading to increased fall risk and movement difficulty. individuals with pd experience rigidity and bradykinesia limiting movement speed and quality that may compromise motor strategies with normal function. the goal of this research is to compare the timed supine to stand test (tss) speed, lower extremity range of motion (rom) and strategy type (2-3 points of contact versus 4 points of contact) between a group of older adults with pd and those without pd (wpd). data were collected using the noraxon® ultium motion analysis system via inertial measurement units (imu), ground reaction force (grf) with insole pressure sensors, and video. each participant performed one repetition of the tss. chi square analysis revealed individuals with pd preferred the 4-point contact method. manova revealed no significant difference between lower extremity range of motion or grf between groups but did demonstrate a significant difference in time to stand. controlling for age via mancova revealed no difference in range of motion, grf, or time to perform the tss. speed with the tss appeared to be a function of age rather than pd. individuals with pd prefer to use 4 points of contact while transferring from the ground. healthcare providers should tailor transfer recommendations for individuals with pd and older adults to include four points of contact. perceptual and motor skills

the application of self-determination theory to short-form video addiction: the roles of psychological needs and intrinsic motivations short-form video applications are widely used worldwide. at the same time, new concerns have been raised owing to excessive and addictive short-form video use, with significant harm to health and well-being. by self-determination theory, the present study aimed to test the effects of satisfaction and frustration of three basic psychological needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) in relation to short-form video addiction (sva) and evaluate the roles of the intrinsic motivations for passing time and entertainment underlying such relationships. the study included 367 chinese tiktok users (37.1% male) aged 18 to 62 years ( m ± sd = 20.63 ± 4.40 years), who voluntarily completed an anonymous online questionnaire without compensation. all three types of need satisfaction had significant negative associations with sva, while the three types of need frustration were significantly positively associated with sva. entertainment motivation significantly and negatively mediated the relationship between competence/relatedness satisfaction and sva while significantly and positively mediating the relationship between relatedness frustration and sva. motivation for passing time served as a risk-enhancing mediator in the relationship between competence/relatedness frustration and sva. therefore, this study identified relatedness frustration and motivation for passing time as the most salient risk factors of sva. the implications for sva interventions that focus on psychological needs and intrinsic motivation are also discussed. psychological reports

mental motivation and attentional control as predictors of academic success: evidence from high- and low-performing students attentional control and mental motivation are critical cognitive factors underlying academic success. however, their interrelationships and differential patterns across performance levels remain underexplored in higher education populations. therefore, this study examined differences in attentional control and mental motivation between high- and low-achieving university students, and assessed how gender, academic specialization, and study level relate to these constructs. total of 300 undergraduate students completed validated arabic versions of the attentional control and mental motivation scales. results showed that high-achieving students demonstrated superior attentional shifting, but did not differ from low-achieving peers in attentional focusing or mental motivation scores. critically, attentional shifting mediates the relationship between academic achievement and mental motivation, suggesting that achievement differences in mental motivation are partly explained by shifting capacity. female students reported significantly higher motivation than males; no effects emerged for academic specialization or study level. in conclusion, these findings highlight attentional shifting—not focusing—as a key cognitive mechanism in academic success. interventions targeting attentional control, particularly shifting abilities, may enhance student mental motivation and achievement outcomes. psychological reports
issue information applied cognitive psychology

how large language models weight narrative cues when detecting deception in oral accounts: a multi‐model comparison abstract lie detection research has increasingly turned to artificial intelligence, yet the application of large language models (llms) remains underexplored for transcribed oral narratives. we compared five llms (gemini‐3‐flash, gemini‐3‐pro, deepseek‐v4‐flash, gpt‐5.6‐luna, and grok‐4) in classifying truthful and deceptive statements from interview transcripts of oral travel narratives collected from 95 chinese‐speaking participants. guided by criteria‐based content analysis (cbca), reality monitoring (rm), and the verifiability approach (va), theory‐driven prompts instructed models to score five narrative cues before making binary veracity judgments. gemini‐3‐flash achieved the highest accuracy (74.74%, auc = 0.76) with 81.63% sensitivity and 67.39% specificity, and stable repeated‐run performance. for this optimal model, unusual/superfluous details served as the sole significant predictor of objective veracity even after controlling for text length. llms can detect deception above chance but show large performance heterogeneity. independent human coding, cross‐cultural replications, and adversarial robustness testing are needed before real‐world deployment. applied cognitive psychology

lying fallow: individual and contextual conditions explaining intra‐organizational career inaction abstract the changing nature of careers has implications for navigating organizational careers. an increased focus on employee agency and an erosion of clearly structured and predictable career paths mark them with ambiguity and uncertainty, thereby increasing the likelihood of intra‐organizational career inaction (i.e., insufficient action on a desire to make an intra‐organizational career transition over time). due to a one‐sided focus on the influence of organizational conditions and on realized transitions (i.e., those in which the individual has moved into a new position within the organization), individual conditions and possible discrepancies in the execution of career desires remain underexplored. this paper takes an individual decision‐making perspective to explain intra‐organizational career inaction. building on career inaction theory, we examine which configurations of individual and contextual conditions contribute to this phenomenon. this is important as intra‐organizational career transitions can build employee competences, leading to a dynamic and resilient workforce. empirically, we adopted a qualitative longitudinal research design covering 1 year, following 26 employees who expressed a desire to make an intra‐organizational career transition at the beginning of the study. qualitative comparative analysis (qca) revealed four paths consisting of different combinations of the proposed conditions. we contribute to the career literature by addressing challenges in navigating contemporary organizational careers and to career inaction theory by empirically examining its core tenets. applied psychology-an international review-psychologie appliquee-revue internationale

does work‐related information and communication technology use during daily commutes promote the speed of work engagement? a role transition perspective abstract the current study aims to address how and when work‐related information and communication technology (ict) use during daily commutes affects the speed of work engagement. based on a role transition perspective, we propose that work‐related ict use during the home‐to‐work commute (wict h‐w) has a positive indirect effect on the speed of work engagement via increased psychological detachment from home; and work‐related ict use during the work‐to‐home commute (wict w‐h) has a negative indirect effect on the next‐day speed of work engagement via increased work‐to‐home conflict. moreover, we expect general task significance to amplify these effects of work‐related ict use during commutes. using an experience sampling study with 149 employees over 10 consecutive workdays, multilevel analyses revealed that daily wict h‐w was positively related to psychological detachment from home, which, in turn, accelerated the speed of work engagement in the morning. on the other hand, daily wict w‐h was positively associated with work‐to‐home conflict; however, the relationship between work‐to‐home conflict and next‐day speed of work engagement was not significant as expected. besides, the cross‐level moderating role of general task significance was supported by our data. specifically, employees with higher task significance experienced more pronounced effects of wict h‐w on psychological detachment from home and of wict w‐h on work‐to‐home conflict. these findings highlight daily commutes as a critical role transition context and show that work‐related ict use during commutes can either facilitate or disrupt employees' daily role transitions depending on the direction of commute and the general perceived significance of work tasks. applied psychology-an international review-psychologie appliquee-revue internationale

morphological analysis when morphemes are hard to detect: evidence from infixation and reduplication abstract there is substantial psycholinguistic evidence that skilled reading involves morphological analysis, whereby morphologically complex words like teacher are recognised via constituent morphemes {teach}+{-er}. the ability to recognise morphemes is vital as it allows readers to interpret both familiar and unfamiliar words. however, over 50% of the evidence for this claim comes from studies of suffixation in english, where morphemes typically have a relatively consistent surface form across exemplars ( clean in cleaner, cleanliness ; -ed in walked , jumped ). it remains unclear whether morphological analysis is also robust when morphemes lack a consistent surface form. using the morpheme interference paradigm in tagalog, we test whether infixes and reduplicants are detected during prelexical processing. infixes are inserted within a stem and therefore reduce the consistency of its surface realisation (e.g., tawag → t-in-awag ‘called’), while reduplicants involve partial or full copying of a stem and therefore lack a consistent surface realisation (e.g., tawag and lundag become ta tawag ‘will call’ and lu lundag ‘will jump’, where ta- and lu- are instances of the same reduplicant morpheme). we found robust morpheme interference effects in both accuracy and rts. specifically, nonwords with morphological structure induced significantly lower accuracy and longer rts than nonwords without. our findings show skilled readers’ acquired sensitivity to these sophisticated morphological structures and motivate refinements to theories of morpheme learning. psychonomic bulletin & review

research on mortuary practices in han dynasty of china from the perspective of ‘rites of passage’: death, identity transformation and the reconstruction of social order death signifies not only the end of life but also a disruption of an individual’s established identities, social relationships, and continuity of social life. this study examines han chinese mortuary practices through the lens of rites of passage, exploring how death was transformed into a socially recognized event through ritual and how mortuary practices responded to changes in identity, emotion, and social relationships brought about by death. the findings show that han mortuary rituals did not merely serve to dispose of the deceased but transformed biological death into a process of social repositioning through a series of ritualized practices. mourning dress embodied both kinship relations and the expression of grief, transforming the bereaved from ordinary family members into mourners with specific ritual identities. tombs and grave goods, while spatially separating the living from the dead, preserved and reconstructed the deceased’s social identity, facilitating the gradual transformation of the deceased from a “dead person” into an individual incorporated into the ancestral realm. han chinese mortuary practices thus reveal the coexistence of “separation” and “continuity”: although death ended the bodily co-presence of the living and the dead, it did not simply terminate their social relationship. in this sense, han mortuary practices were not only institutional expressions of social order but also important cultural mechanisms for negotiating death and grief, transforming identities, and sustaining relationships between the living and the dead. omega-journal of death and dying

medical assistance in dying as a cultural conflict: conceptualizing chinese immigrants’ navigation in canada medical assistance in dying (maid) was legalized in canada in 2016 but remains illegal in china. due to distinct cultural, social, and political differences between china and canada, maid can be a cultural conflict for chinese immigrants after they immigrate to canada. to better understand their navigation of maid in canada, three theoretical lenses are adopted. confucian ethics serve as a theoretical framework for understanding how life is perceived from a collectivistic, relational, and moral perspective in chinese culture. autonomy theory is used to understand how life is understood from an individualistic, independent, and autonomous perspective in canadian culture. acculturation theory is further used to explore how chinese immigrants in canada perceive and respond to maid by adopting different strategies when they interact with these two value systems. this conceptual analysis can help healthcare professionals better understand and support immigrants’ cultural needs as they navigate maid in canada. omega-journal of death and dying

focus on the building, not the blocks abstract objectives: difficulty with word finding is a pervasive symptom in aphasia and a common target of treatment. this review explored whether therapy-induced naming gains induce improvements to everyday (naturalistic) communication. methods: online databases were searched for naming interventions that also assessed discourse or functional communication, and for studies of therapies that directly treated them. results: among the studies that found word production gains following therapy, only about half found that the gains generalized to improved discourse or functional communication. however, discourse and functional communication can be improved by therapies that target them, and often improve word finding as well. conclusions: generalization of rehabilitation is complex and difficult to achieve. if the therapeutic goal in aphasia is to improve everyday communication, then intervention research needs to shift focus from “building blocks” like word production to the building of discourse and functional communication. journal of the international neuropsychological society

normative data and change scores on the cerad word list in a robustly intact sample of older adults and preliminary validation in an impaired sample. objectives: the word list subtest of the consortium to establish a registry for alzheimer's disease (cerad) neuropsychological battery has been widely used in clinical research to identify and track cognitive disorders. however, normative data and change scores are lacking. the current study aimed to create normative data for the word list subtest.
methods: cerad word list data from 1,530 older adults diagnosed as cognitively intact, mild cognitive impairment (mci), or dementia were seen for two annual visits in a longitudinal observational study from the uniform data set of the national alzheimer's coordinating center. multiple linear regression predicted time 2 scores from time 1 scores, demographic variables (age, education, sex, and race), and retest interval. validation included comparing predicted scores to observed scores in the original sample, and additional validation across five comparison groups (cognitively intact, mci, dementia, worsening cognition, or improving cognition) and one-sample chi-square test of probabilities to compare group classification to predicted categorization based on chance alone.
results: the four demographic variables significantly predicted test scores for the six primary scores from the word list subtest. for change data, when predicted time 2 scores were compared to observed time 2 scores, there were significant differences for 4 of the 6 scores, but the effect sizes were small. significant differences were found across the five comparison groups for total recall and delayed recall (p-values < .001).
conclusions: the current study provides normative data and regression-based change scores for the cerad word list subtest for older adults. journal of the international neuropsychological society

beliefs about structural racism shape perceptions of racial economic inequality despite vast racial disparities in economic outcomes, white americans tend to overestimate their economic parity with black americans. white americans also tend to be less likely to hold an understanding of racism that is rooted in structural processes, relative to individual-level biases. across three studies ( n = 2,124 participants), the present research explored whether white americans’ misperceptions of racial economic inequality are explained, in part, by a general lack of exposure to information about structural racism. in study 1, we measured the extent to which participants conceptualized racism in terms of structural factors. in studies 2 and 3, we experimentally manipulated exposure to information about structural racism. specifically, participants listened to an audio clip discussing structural roots of racial discrimination, a comparable audio clip on implicit racial bias, or no clip at all. in each study, participants estimated black–white equality in income and wealth, then indicated their support for reparative public policies (e.g., affirmative action in hiring). across studies 1–3, holding a structural understanding of racism was correlated with perceiving lower levels of contemporary black–white economic equality and greater support for racial equity-enhancing policies. further, exposing participants to information about structural racism led them to perceive lower levels of racial economic equality (vs. interpersonal racism or control information in study 2) and express more equity-enhancing policy support (vs. interpersonal racism information in study 3). group processes & intergroup relations

racial bias masquerading as nostalgia: nostalgic longing and opposition to increased racial representation in the media racial/ethnic minority diversity in the mass media has increased in recent years, in part due to racebending—non-white performers portraying traditionally white characters. racebending is, however, frequently met with backlash, with opponents expressing nostalgia for original representations and decrying racebending as deviating from traditional portrayals. although expressing nostalgia is seemingly race-neutral, we reasoned that expressing nostalgia to decry racebending is, for some people, an indirect means of expressing biased attitudes that allows racially biased people to oppose racebending without having to appear biased. three studies ( n = 694) found that white supremacist attitudes predicted self-reported media nostalgia, which in turn predicted racebending opposition. however, nostalgia was inconsistently predictive of opposition to media changes. specifically, we found that people higher in nostalgia opposed racebending, but not other deviations from traditional presentations (i.e., whitewashing). these results suggest that nostalgia is used by some to indirectly oppose racial diversity in the media. group processes & intergroup relations

implications of self-observation for metaperceived gender salience during mixed-gender online negotiations gender salience is a core construct in theories of gender-related affect, cognition, and behavior. this research suggests a novel, subtle trigger of gender salience in mixed-gender negotiations: the self-observation typically involved in online interaction. this trigger maps onto everyday experience and is qualitatively different from other documented triggers. we reasoned that given individuals’ enduring alertness to the possibility of being viewed unfavorably by others, seeing their own image would lead them to imagine that their interaction partner was focused on their gender—a visible distinctive group membership in the interaction context. a mini meta-analysis across three studies in which mixed-gender dyads negotiated online with self-view on or off (total n = 366 dyads) indicated that overall self-observation increased women’s but not men’s metaperceived gender salience, although there was some inconsistency across the studies. analyses of indirect effects suggested that higher gender salience was associated with greater female disadvantage in negotiation outcomes. group processes & intergroup relations

how feminine and masculine do cisgender people in the u.s. think the average gender nonbinary person is? perception of gender is ubiquitous and consequential in social life. people who are perceived as women are expected to enact femininity, whereas people who are perceived as men are expected to enact masculinity. how do gender nonbinary people fit into these binary assumptions? the present work examined the perceived femininity and masculinity of nonbinary people. in particular, cisgender, primarily straight/heterosexual, u.s.-based participants reported their assumptions about the assigned sex (study 1; n = 315) or their perceptions of the femininity and masculinity (studies 2–3; n s = 216 and 277) of the average nonbinary person. no apparent bias in terms of assumed sex or perceived femininity emerged, yet participants rated the average nonbinary person as reliably below the scale midpoint on masculinity. accordingly, cisgender straight americans’ perceptions of the average nonbinary person may in part reflect a tendency to safeguard masculinity. group processes & intergroup relations

the effect of nonbinary pronouns on job candidate evaluations the increasing visibility of pronouns in professional settings raises questions about their influence on workplace outcomes, one of which is candidate evaluations in hiring. this study investigates how including pronouns on cvs affects evaluations of job candidates, focusing on competence, likeability, and suitability. in two preregistered, between-subject experiments ( n total = 408), we tested whether nonbinary pronouns (they/them) impact these evaluations differently compared with binary pronouns (he/him) or the absence of pronouns. participants reviewed a job description and evaluated cvs with manipulated pronouns. results showed a significant negative effect of nonbinary pronouns on candidate evaluations (study 2), particularly among individuals with higher levels of prejudice (both studies). these findings highlight the challenges of gender identity expression in job applications and underscore the need to address biases in hiring practices to promote workplace equality. social psychological and personality science

validation and psychometric properties of the school failure coping scale in a hungarian sample the study of coping responses to school failure situations is of particular importance from a developmental psychology perspective; however, there are few assessment tools available in hungary that specifically measure strategies related to these situations. therefore, it became necessary to conduct a hungarian-language adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the school failure coping scale (sfcs). the study involved 9th-grade hungarian students (m = 15.07; sd = 0.56; n = 526). in addition to the sfcs, we measured passive-aggressive behavior, school burnout, and the quality of school life using separate questionnaires. as a result of exploratory factor analysis (n = 250), the original 47-item scale was reduced to a 29-item, six-factor hungarian version, in which the factors anger, accepting responsibility, comfort and forgetting, seeking social support, avoidance, and disengagement were identified. confirmatory factor analysis (n = 276) indicated an adequate fit, and the reliability of the total scale was also adequate. according to the convergent validity results, reactions based on anger and avoidance are associated with less favorable school adjustment. in the network analysis, assertiveness proved to be the most important bridge between the constructs. based on these results, the hungarian version of the sfcs can be reliably used to examine coping with school failure situations and can serve as a foundation for prevention and intervention programs aimed at providing psychological support to adolescents. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

multimodal neuroimaging and behavioral characterization of aged female apoe4 knock‐in rats reveals a preclinical alzheimer's disease phenotype abstract the apolipoprotein e ε4 allele (apoe4) is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic alzheimer's disease (ad) and confers disproportionate risk in women, particularly after reproductive senescence. the brain changes preceding overt neurodegeneration in apoe4 carriers remain incompletely characterized. we conducted neuroimaging and behavioral studies in aged (18‐month) female apoe4 humanized knock‐in rats and apoe3 controls. regional brain volumes across 197 areas were quantified by voxel‐based morphometry (vbm); white and gray matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging (dti), yielding fractional anisotropy (fa) and apparent diffusion coefficient (adc). spatial memory was assessed with the barnes maze and motor coordination with the beam walk. apoe4 rats showed significantly larger regional brain volumes than apoe3 controls. dti revealed increased fa in the thalamus, brainstem, and white matter tracts, and reduced fa in the sensorimotor cortex. across most regions elevated fa was accompanied by reduced adc, an inverse relationship consistent with cytotoxic edema. behaviorally, apoe4 rats were significantly impaired on the barnes maze. aged female apoe4 knock‐in rats exhibit a preclinical ad phenotype: widespread volumetric enlargement across white matter, sensorimotor, and limbic circuits, with microstructural alterations (elevated fa in brainstem, thalamus, and white matter; reduced fa in sensorimotor cortex). this mirrors the imaging and cognitive profile of cognitively normal human apoe4 carriers in preclinical ad and validates the model as a translationally relevant platform for investigating early apoe4‐driven pathophysiology and testing preventive interventions. genes brain and behavior

calling development: a systematic review of longitudinal evidence although career calling is linked to many beneficial outcomes for both individuals and organizations, knowledge on how a sense of calling develops is limited and, in some ways, controversial. to clarify this issue, we conducted a systematic review of longitudinal studies that analyzed the temporal relation between calling and other variables in its nomological network. across 14 studies, the strongest longitudinal evidence suggests that calling is more often an outcome of career development processes rather than an initiating cause. specifically, vocational self-definition, agency, and career feedback and appraisal appear to precede calling, whereas personal resources more often follow calling, and life meaning and values appears reciprocally linked with calling. on this basis, we propose a preliminary integrative developmental framework of calling in which calling emerges through recursive cycles of career clarification, agentic engagement, contextual feedback and appraisal, and life meaning- and value-based integration. journal of career assessment

how and when artificial intelligence awareness fosters proactive career behaviors: the role of workplace impostor thoughts and future work self salience drawing on self-discrepancy theory, this study examined how and when artificial intelligence (ai) awareness promotes proactive career behaviors. we collected three-wave, time-lagged data from 329 full-time employees in the united kingdom. results showed that ai awareness was positively related to proactive career behaviors. the indirect effect of ai awareness on proactive career behaviors through workplace impostor thoughts was significant when future work self salience was high but not when it was low. future work self salience also strengthened both the relationship between ai awareness and workplace impostor thoughts and the direct relationship between ai awareness and proactive career behaviors. these findings demonstrate that technology-induced identity threats can motivate proactive career efforts and clarify how and when ai awareness translates into proactive career behaviors. implications for career counseling and organizational practice are discussed. journal of career assessment

climate emotions and pro-environmental behavior abstract: to mitigate climate change, it is essential to understand the individual predictors of pro-environmental behavior (peb). theory and research suggest that experiencing emotions related to climate change may drive engagement in peb. however, previous research has considered only relatively few climate emotions, overlooking the potentially important role of a broader range of climate emotions as well as their unique contributions. additionally, previous research largely relied on cross-sectional designs, limiting insights into potential within-person relations. building on theorizing on climate emotions and peb, we explore relations between a comprehensive set of 11 climate emotions and four dimensions of peb (i.e., conservation peb, citizenship peb, reduced meat consumption, and sustainable transportation behavior). we further address exploratory research questions regarding differences in relations depending on the dimension of peb and unique between- and within-person relations. we collected data from n = 1,313 employed adults in germany across five measurement waves with 3-month time lags. results of mixed-effects models revealed that, at the between-person level, negative climate emotions (i.e., fear, guilt, and sadness) were positively and moderately related to different dimensions of peb. regarding positive climate emotions, attentiveness was positively and moderately related to peb, whereas the other positive climate emotions yielded mixed effects, depending on the specific dimension of peb. at the within-person level, climate change–related fear was positively, albeit weakly, related to peb, whereas climate change–related joviality was negatively and weakly related to peb. european psychologist

leading in the climate crisis abstract: the escalating climate crisis demands coordinated, collective action. this review paper draws and extends the social identity model of pro-environmental action (simpea) to explore how identity leadership can foster the social and psychological foundations for effective climate mobilization. while simpea outlines the role of social identity in driving environmental engagement, we extend the model by highlighting identity leadership as a critical mechanism for building group identification, collective efficacy and sustained group action. synthesizing insights from social, environmental, and political psychology, the paper demonstrates how leaders who shape, represent, and embed shared group identities can enhance group-based processes necessary for climate action. we argue that these group-level dynamics are essential for scaling meaningful climate engagement and that dominant individual-focused (i-frame) approaches are insufficient without complementary group-based (g-frame) strategies. this integrative review offers a conceptual framework for understanding how identity leadership can mobilize collective climate action and provides practical insights for policymakers, activists, and organizational leaders seeking to foster environmentally engaged communities. by focusing on leadership as an important driver for group process, the paper advances simpea and contributes to a more psychologically grounded approach to climate leadership. european psychologist

interpersonal communication environments and counterarguing intentions toward climate misinformation: the role of personal climate discussion networks, norms, and attitudes how everyday social environments shape behavioral responses to environmental information remains a core question in environment–behavior research. this study examines how interpersonal communication environments influence individuals’ intentions to counterargue environmental misinformation. drawing on social capital theory and the reasoned action approach, we conceptualize personal climate discussion networks as routine social environments that structure subjective norms and attitudes, which in turn motivate behaviorally oriented responses. using an online survey of 525 u.s. adults exposed to three climate misinformation memes, we estimated structural equation models with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. communication frequency within personal discussion networks consistently predicted stronger pro-climate subjective norms and attitudes, which robustly predicted counterarguing intentions across stimuli. in contrast, perceived credibility neither directly predicted counterarguing intentions nor mediated the relationships between subjective norms or attitudes and counterarguing intentions. these findings suggest that corrective responses to environmental misinformation are driven less by individual-level cognitive evaluation and more by socially structured interpersonal environments that activate norms and attitudes. environment and behavior
memory-based learning disabilities: a syndrome without a pigeonhole—towards a mechanism-first assessment framework neuropsychology review
when leader perfectionism works and when it does not: the role of leader vision in shaping follower outcomes journal of business and psychology

longitudinal development of portion size estimation in patients with anorexia nervosa receiving inpatient treatment—evidence from laboratory and real‐life data abstract background food intake is highly aversive for patients with anorexia nervosa (an), and fear of weight gain is closely linked to altered eating behaviours, including reduced portion sizes. this study investigated how portion size estimation develops longitudinally in patients with an during inpatient treatment. we hypothesised that patients with an would overestimate portion sizes compared to healthy controls, with overestimation being most pronounced at treatment onset and decreasing over the course of treatment. methods 29 patients with an were assessed three times during real‐life mealtimes in an inpatient setting and in a laboratory‐based task: shortly after inpatient admission, in the middle of treatment, and shortly before discharge. 19 healthy control participants were assessed cross‐sectionally. the laboratory task was performed twice, asking participants one time to select a portion they would be ready to eat completely and a second time selecting an adequate portion for a hypothetical other person of their age and gender. results patients with an overestimated portion sizes as compared to control participants at baseline, both in the laboratory and under real‐life circumstances. patients chose larger portions for a hypothetical healthy person. as treatment progressed, patients chose larger portions they would be ready to eat in the laboratory task, while they continued to perceive the real‐life lunch portions as large, indicating that they did not adapt to usual portion sizes and continued to overestimate. discussion portion size estimation in patients with an differed depending on whether the task was implemented under laboratory or real‐life conditions, supporting the need for method combinations. a better understanding of mechanisms underlying portion size estimation is needed to advance mealtime support and other treatment approaches for an. european eating disorders review

studying multiracial adolescents' racial self‐categorization(s): conceptual, methodological, and analytic recommendations abstract when multiracial youth respond to demographic questions about their race in surveys (e.g., what is your race/ethnicity?) they must reconcile their lived experiences, consider others' expectations, and weigh various contextual factors when responding. although such racial self‐categorization choices are a fundamental aspect of multiracial realities, multiple empirical and analytic roadblocks limit the ability to study these choices quantitatively as an outcome and with a critical lens. in this theoretical and conceptual manuscript, we address such potential roadblocks by exploring various models suitable for categorical racial self‐categorization outcomes (i.e., logistic regression, multinomial logistic regression, structural equation models). we first explain the significance of racial‐self‐categorization(s) in the development as well as empirical study of multiracial adolescents. next, we describe our theoretical grounding in critical quantitative frameworks, which we use to frame our analysis of data collection and analytical modeling strategies researchers might employ when studying racial self‐categorization among multiracial youth. these insights support the field of adolescent development by improving our understanding and development of multiracial adolescents and advancing critical discourse that challenges “race‐neutral” and (mono)racist methodologies. journal of research on adolescence
perceived income inequality and life satisfaction: robust evidence from rural vietnam using an instrumental variable approach journal of happiness studies
episodic memory in immersive virtual reality environments: the role of affective context and navigation control psychological research-psychologische forschung
emotional inertia in daily life: a dynamic structural equation modelling analysis of the role of emotion regulation strategy use cognition & emotion
not everything can be counted: how awe enhances perceptions of immeasurability cognition & emotion

longitudinal associations between sleep disturbance and disordered eating: the mediating role of emotion dysregulation abstract objective accruing evidence suggests a significant relationship between sleep disturbances and disordered eating. early adolescence is a period of heightened vulnerability for sleep disturbances and disordered eating. however, the longitudinal relationship between sleep disturbance and disordered eating remains unclear in early adolescent samples. the current study aims to examine if sleep disturbance longitudinally predicts disordered eating in early adolescents 3 years later, how the odds of having clinically significant disordered eating change per each unit increase in sleep disturbance, and if emotion dysregulation mediates these relationships. methods a sample of 6,161 early adolescents between 9 and 13 years old from the adolescent brain and cognitive developmentsm study (abcd study®) was examined with data extracted from baseline, 2-year follow-up, and 3-year follow-up. participants who completed kiddie schedule for affective disorders and schizophrenia, computerized version (ksads-comp), child behavior checklist (cbcl), and sleep disturbance scale for children (sdsc) were included. a binary clinically significant disordered eating variable was created by coding participants who met criteria for present, past, or partial remission eating disorder diagnoses on the ksads-5. results results indicated that greater sleep disturbance at baseline was associated with higher levels of disordered eating and clinically significant disordered eating at 3-year follow-up, and emotion dysregulation partially mediated these relationships (all ps < .001). conclusions given that sleep is a modifiable factor, these results underscore the potential for integrating sleep-focused interventions into ed prevention and treatment programs for early adolescents. interventions targeting emotion regulation may help reduce the impact of sleep problems on disordered eating in early adolescents. journal of pediatric psychology

it happened, it's not my fault, and i can trust again”: compassionate imagery to enhance trauma‐focused cognitive behavioural therapy for complex ptsd abstract imagery is a central part of compassion‐focused therapy (cft), which teaches individuals to create affiliative motives and emotions for oneself and others in order to recover from the multiple sequelae of trauma including shame, guilt and fear of trusting others. this case illustration describes the use of imagery during an ongoing 15‐month intervention based on cft and trauma‐focused cbt for sam, a 35‐year old male with cptsd and ocd. pre‐therapy, symptoms included dissociation, nightmares and flashbacks, doubting the abuse, hyperarousal, fear of relying on others and aggressive obsessions. a series of compassionate imagery techniques were used to reduce self‐doubt, self‐blame, suppressed anger, disgust and an ongoing sense of threat. large changes were observed in suds for trauma memories and dissociation frequency, as well as in conviction in positive beliefs about self and others. ptsd symptoms reduced from severe to non‐clinical. this illustrates the potential of cft to tackle the rational‐emotional divide, whereby cognitive techniques often fail to reduce distress underpinned by early traumatic memories. journal of clinical psychology

parent–adolescent discrepancies in perceived overparenting and adolescent mental health: a multi‐informant perspective abstract parent–adolescent discrepancies in perceptions of parenting may provide important insight into adolescent adjustment. this study examined how consistency and discrepancy in perceived parental overparenting across parent–adolescent and father–mother dyads were associated with adolescent mental health problems in chinese families. participants were 860 adolescents (417 boys; m age = 10.17, sd = 1.54) and their mothers and fathers. results showed that adolescents reported higher levels of anxiety/depressive symptoms, withdrawal, and somatic complaints when both parents and adolescents perceived high levels of overparenting. discrepancies between adolescents and parents were also associated with poorer adjustment: adolescents reported more anxiety/depressive symptoms and withdrawal when they perceived higher paternal overparenting than their fathers did, and more anxiety/depressive symptoms when they perceived higher maternal overparenting than their mothers did. in father–mother dyads, adolescents showed more anxiety/depressive symptoms, withdrawal, and somatic complaints when both parents reported high overparenting, whereas interparental discrepancies were not significant. these patterns were consistent across boys and girls. findings highlight the value of considering adolescents', mothers', and fathers' perspectives simultaneously when examining overparenting and adolescent mental health. international journal of psychology

adverse childhood experiences, attachment, guilt, and mental health as predictors of positive dyadic coping following perinatal loss among women background: perinatal loss is a highly stressful life event that can profoundly affect women’s emotional well-being and couple functioning. this study examined the role of adverse childhood experiences (aces), insecure romantic attachment (attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance), guilt, and mental health problems (mhp) in predicting positive dyadic coping (pdc) among women who had experienced perinatal loss. methods: a total of 162 spanish women completed online questionnaires assessing attachment (experiences in close relationships–revised scale (ecr-r)), aces (adverse childhood experiences questionnaire (aceq)), as well as guilt and mhp using ad hoc likert-type items. data were analyzed using correlation analyses, hierarchical regression, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsqca), and mediation models (spss, process). results: hierarchical regression analysis showed that lower attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance were the strongest predictors of pdc, with the final model explaining 68.8% of the variance. fsqca indicated that no single condition was necessary for either high or low pdc; however, several sufficient configurations accounted for most cases of high pdc, particularly those characterized by low attachment avoidance combined with low attachment anxiety, low guilt, or the absence of aces. configurations associated with low pdc were primarily characterized by higher attachment avoidance and attachment anxiety, often combined with greater psychological distress or guilt. mediation analyses revealed that insecure attachment, particularly attachment anxiety, mediated the association between aces and pdc, suggesting that aces influenced coping primarily through indirect pathways rather than direct pathways. conclusions: overall, these findings highlight the central role of attachment processes and emotional regulation in promoting pdc following perinatal loss and support the utility of integrative, non-linear approaches for understanding adjustment to perinatal bereavement. behavioral psychology-psicologia conductual

targeting family accommodation of problem behavior to increase parent adherence with behavioral treatment plans conducting a functional analysis and implementing derived treatments can produce effective behavior plans for severe problem behavior (e.g., self-injury, aggression, and disruptive behavior). nonetheless, skills training and an effective plan may not be sufficient to produce parent adherence. low levels of treatment adherence may persist because parent responses that reinforce problem behavior also produce negative reinforcement for the parent response through immediate problem behavior cessation. this case study presents a contextual behavioral informed approach to target the negative maintaining contingencies supporting parent accommodation of problem behavior, and to increase adherence with behavioral treatment plans. despite parent mastery of treatment components while under direct clinical observation, accommodation of the child’s severe problem behavior persisted periodically between clinical appointments. case conceptualization highlights the borrowed concept of family accommodation as it relates to parent-child interactions that exacerbate and maintain the maladaptive behaviors of both. the course of intervention outlines strategies aimed at undermining the contingencies that maintain accommodation while providing parents with new behavioral treatment-related committed actions that are consistent with adherence. outcomes are reviewed and presented within a multiple-baseline single case design across parents. implications of the findings are discussed, along with recommendations for clinicians and students who identify parent accommodation of problem behavior within their clinical work. clinical case studies

the pursuit of valued living: applying a values targeted approach with an autistic young person persistent anxiety and repetitive, restricted behaviours are common experiences for autistic young people and can be barriers to valued living and thus the opportunity to thrive. this case study presents the use of the dna-v intervention framework, an act model, in an 18-month co-constructed, values targeted approach with an autistic young woman. outcome measures were administered at multiple time points from baseline through to 3-month follow up post discharge from the service. the young woman was observed to experience improved well-being and psychological flexibility, and in particular, engaged in an increased amount of activities that aligned with her identified values. this case study offers use of the dna-v model in practice and suggests how the importance of value identification and nurturing this skill may lead to an increase in behaviour related to enhanced psychological flexibility and well-being. the pattern observed in this case also suggests how the use of a stepped away approach in which a faded transition from intensive level to reduced involvement may link to improvements in well-being sustained over time. clinical case studies
correction to: the rhythmic embodied perception framework of breath, brain, and perception neuroscience of consciousness

eye gaze tracking for real-world systems: a systematic review eye gaze tracking has become a key feature for human-centered intelligent systems, and has wide variety of applications such as human–computer interaction, extended reality, behavioral analysis and safety-critical monitoring. despite the rapid progress made in the field by deep learning and large-scale datasets, the field is still fragmented as reported performance often does not translate into robust real-world deployment. this paper presents a systematic review of eye gaze tracking research with regard to methodological development, sensing modalities, application areas, evaluation practice and recurring limitations. following prisma guidelines, the contemporary literature involving learning paradigm and deep learning models are analyzed. this paper uses the evidence from cross-study evidence to explore the effect of dataset characteristics, evaluation protocols, and sensing choices on the reported performance. particular attention is given to bias in datasets, fragility in evaluation, failure in generalization and the gap between application aspiration and the reality of deployment. the reviewed article continues with analysis of trade-offs among rgb, infrared, depth, and physiological modalities in order to demonstrate unrealized potential and existing shortcomings of multimodal fusion. the analysis reflects that future developments in the field of gaze tracking are less correlated to the incremental refinement of architecture, and more correlated to the importance of robustness-aware evaluations of benchmarks, the longitudinal evaluation and deployment of the algorithm, and the evaluations on the model. this review is intended to provide a comprehensive understanding of the current state of the art of eye gaze tracking that can be used to guide future research towards reliable real-world systems. journal of eye movement research
digital masculinity and digital media exposure in relation to male genital self-image, mental health, and sexual health: a scoping review journal of sex & marital therapy

task-sensitive semantic-visual alignment of motion schema during incremental mandarin sentence comprehension abstract language comprehension involves dynamically integrating linguistic input into coherent event representations. a common approach to investigating this process has been to examine behavioural congruency effects between linguistic and visual information. however, it remains unclear under what conditions these effects emerge and whether they reflect embodied processing or alternative cognitive mechanisms. the present study examined semantic-visual alignment of motion schema during incremental processing of mandarin motion sentences, focusing on whether congruency effects are modulated by task demands and visual probe regions. 149 native mandarin speakers completed either a self-paced sentence-diagram verification task or a self-paced sentence-diagram viewing task. in both tasks, participants processed segmented chinese motion sentences, while schematic diagrams were presented either after the directional verb (e.g., jìn , ‘into’) or the landmark (e.g., bàn-gōng-shì , ‘office’). results revealed overall congruency effects across tasks and diagram regions. crucially, effects were stronger in the verification task than in the viewing task but remained stable across diagram regions. these findings suggest that semantic-visual alignment is sensitive to task demands but does not necessarily become stronger as the sentence unfolds. these congruency effects are open to both embodied and amodal semantic interpretations and are therefore not uniquely diagnostic of embodied processing. language and cognition

morphological processing of inclusive language in spanish: a usage-based account abstract we examine how form and usage shape the processing of the spanish gender-inclusive morpheme -e. within usage-based models, repeated exposure strengthens representations, allowing high-frequency forms to be retrieved holistically while infrequent forms remain compositionally demanding. to test these predictions, we compare the processing of the relatively frequent pronominal quantifier tod-e-s (‘everyone- inc - pl ’) with its masculine counterpart tod-o-s (‘everyone- m - pl ’) and plural inclusive adjectives such as content-e-s (‘happy- inc - pl ’) with masculine forms such as content-o-s (‘happy- m - pl ’). first-language spanish speakers completed a word-by-word self-paced reading task in which these forms referred to mixed-gender groups, followed by a sociolinguistic questionnaire. the results showed no reliable processing cost for todes relative to todos at the precritical, critical and postcritical regions. by contrast, inclusive adjectives elicited longer reading times than masculine adjectives at the critical word and spillover region. this cost appeared across most participant groups but was absent among those reporting the highest use of inclusive language. a participant-level bootstrap comparison showed that the processing burden was reliably greater for inclusive adjectives than for todes. these findings indicate that inclusive morphology is not processed uniformly across grammatical contexts. instead, grammatical categories and individual experience modulate entrenchment, suggesting adult speakers can incorporate emergent morphology into real-time processing routines through exposure. language and cognition

‘the difference is that they haven’t only observed, they’ve actually practised it’: how virtual reality is reshaping pornography’s fantasy/reality debates this study examines the relationship between the rapidly expanding genre of virtual reality pornography and the long-standing pornography fantasy/reality debates. through an in-depth literature review and interviews with key experts, the article explores how the digital landscape and emerging technological developments, such as virtual reality pornography, are reshaping this discourse, questioning the ethical implications of the virtual reality medium, including the implications for sexual violence. the findings illustrate that the fantasy/reality binary is inadequate to analyse the saturation of new pornographic forms and functions available, including immersive and participatory capabilities of virtual reality media, where fantasy and reality are co-active. using a phenomenological lens, this article introduces the new concept of ‘pornality’ as an innovative framework for examining the multiple realities of virtual reality pornography. this concept offers a way to transcend binary framings, raises new avenues of inquiry, and examines the technological capabilities of developing pornographic modalities by extending the limitations of traditional media frameworks. by opening more productive dialogues, this research illustrates how a pornality framework can reshape academic and policy discourse, enabling us to consider future-proofing in new ways. journal of gender-based violence

eating disorder risk and sexual victimization: considering the impact of lgbtq+ status a limited body of research has linked eating disorders (eds) with sexual victimization (sv) among college students. this research highlights higher ed risks for females, but how gender relates to eds and sv among lgbtq+ individuals remains underexplored. specifically, there is minimal research on the experiences of transgender, gender non-conforming and sexual minority students who experience eds and sv compared to their cisgender classmates. we examine whether lgbtq+ students who have been sexually victimized are at greater risk for eds using data from the spring 2021 national college health assessment. our findings indicate that eds are more prevalent among sexual and gender minority college students than their cisgender, heterosexual peers and that sv is associated with an increased likelihood of having an ed. however, sv did not differentially impact ed risk among sexual or gender minorities, though the predicted probability of eds is highest for sexual and gender minorities who have experienced sv. institutions of higher learning may benefit from culturally sensitive ed prevention and response programmes that also address the overlapping needs of students affected by sv, particularly among sexual and gender minorities. journal of gender-based violence

psychometric validation of the patient health questionnaire 4 items for screening anxiety and depression among returned cambodian migrant workers abstract background ultra-brief mental health screening tools are increasingly needed for large-scale surveys and resource-constrained settings in low- and middle-income countries (lmics). the patient health questionnaire-4 (phq-4) is a widely used instrument for assessing anxiety and depression; however, its psychometric properties have not been validated among returned migrant workers in cambodia. methods a cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 returned cambodian migrant workers recruited across four high-migration provinces in october 2022. internal consistency was evaluated using cronbach’s alpha. confirmatory factor analysis (cfa) compared one-factor and two-factor structural models. construct validity was evaluated by examining associations between phq-4 scores and occupational health risk factors using multivariable logistic regression. results the sample comprised 392 returned migrant workers (mean age = 34.7 years, sd = 8.9; 52% male, 48% female). the mean overall phq-4 score was 2.13 (sd = 2.24) with the majority exhibiting none to mild psychological distress. the phq-4 demonstrated acceptable internal consistency ( α = 0.78). cfa supported a two-factor structure representing distinct anxiety and depression dimensions, showing superior model fit compared to the poor fit of the one-factor model (cfi = 0.97, tli = 0.78, rmsea = 0.23, srmr = 0.028). the two-factor model demonstrated excellent fit (cfi = 0.99, tli = 0.98, rmsea = 0.035, srmr = 0.016) and the two latent factors were strongly correlated ( r = 0.79, p < 0.001). higher phq-4 scores were significantly associated with long working hours (aor = 1.45, 95% ci [1.10, 1.92]), unsafe working conditions (aor = 1.63, 95% ci [1.21, 2.20]) and hazardous work exposure (aor = 1.38, 95% ci [1.05, 1.82]) supporting exposure-based construct validity. conclusions the phq-4 is a reliable and valid ultra-brief screening tool for evaluating anxiety and depression among returned cambodian migrant workers. evidence supports its application in both occupational settings (workplace surveillance, returnee checks) and non-occupational settings (primary care, ngo community outreach). its ultra-brief format provides a low-burden, scalable instrument for rapid mental health screening by non-specialized personnel in resource-limited settings across cambodia. discover psychology

validation of the russian version of the cognitive functioning self‑assessment scale (cfss) in patients with non‑psychotic mental disorders. background: cognitive assessment is vital for detecting impairments affecting quality of life, occupational functioning, and prognosis. while objective cognitive tests are available, tools assessing subjective cognition are limited. this study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the cognitive functioning self-assessment scale (cfss) into russian and to examine its internal consistency, structural validity, and convergent validity in patients with non-psychotic mental disorders.
methods: the cfss was translated and culturally adapted into russian following international guidelines. the sample consisted of 322 consecutively recruited patients (18-60 years) with non-psychotic mental disorders. participants completed the russian version of cfss, patient health questionnaire‑9 (phq‑9), generalized anxiety disorder‑7 (gad‑7), and the cognitive facet of the world health organization quality of life instrument (whoqol‑100).
results: the russian version of cfss showed excellent internal consistency ( = 0.925; = 0.929). esem supported a one‑factor structure with acceptable fit (cfi = 0.985; tli = 0.983; rmsea = 0.072). cfss scores were associated with the whoqol‑100 cognitive facet (r = -0.67, < 0.001), phq‑9 (r = 0.55, < 0.001), and gad‑7 (r = 0.36, < 0.001). in an exploratory secondary analysis, participants with higher cfss scores differed from those with lower cfss scores in several sociodemographic and self-reported clinical characteristics.
conclusions: the russian version of cfss is a reliable, valid, and practical instrument for assessing subjective cognitive functioning in patients with non‑psychotic psychiatric disorders. further studies incorporating objective neuropsychological measures and repeated assessments are needed to evaluate concurrent/criterion-related validity and temporal reliability. applied neuropsychology-adult

boundaries and bridges: the complex alliance between counselling and learning theories abstract counselling theories have traditionally been conceptualised within psychological, therapeutic, and developmental frameworks while learning theories have largely evolved as a separate field of inquiry. although both domains are concerned with personal change, adaptation, and the development of new understandings, explicit theoretical integration between counselling and learning remains relatively limited. this article explores whether counselling may be usefully understood through the lens of learning theory and examines the extent to which key learning concepts can illuminate processes commonly associated with counselling. drawing on major traditions in learning theory, including behaviourist, cognitive, constructivist, social, experiential, transformative, and humanistic perspectives, the paper develops a conceptual framework for analysing counselling as a context in which intensive personal learning frequently occurs. rather than proposing an equivalence between counselling and learning, the analysis identifies significant areas of conceptual overlap and highlights how counselling may facilitate changes in knowledge, self-understanding, behaviour, meaning making, and identity. attention is given to the roles of reflection, experience, dialogue, agency, and relational processes in supporting learning-oriented forms of personal development. the article concludes that a learning perspective offers a valuable complementary lens for understanding counselling processes and provides a basis for strengthening interdisciplinary dialogue between counselling theory and learning theory. implications for theory development, research, and professional practice are discussed, alongside the limitations of the present conceptual analysis. integrative psychological and behavioral science
ruminative self-focus and cyberbullying in college students: the mediating role of anger rumination and the moderating role of self-concept clarity psychological studies

dual-factor mental health states and academic outcomes in chilean public schools this study examined the association between dual-factor mental health states and academic outcomes, including mathematics achievement, language achievement, and school attendance, in a large sample of students attending chilean public schools. using a quantitative, nonexperimental correlational-predictive design, mental health states were constructed based on the joint distribution of psychological symptoms and positive psychological functioning. results from multilevel linear regression models revealed a clear gradient in academic achievement. students with complete mental health demonstrated the highest performance, whereas those with possible mental health problems showed the lowest achievement. a key finding was that students classified as vulnerable (low positive psychological functioning without elevated symptomatology) exhibited significant academic impairment, highlighting functional risks that remain invisible under deficit-oriented screening. additionally, symptomatic but content (elevated symptoms and elevated positive psychological functioning) students displayed intermediate outcomes, suggesting that positive psychological functioning may partially buffer the academic impact of psychological distress. no statistically significant associations were observed for school attendance. these findings underscore the educational relevance of the positive dimension of mental health. they support integrating dual-factor screening within multi-tiered systems of support to promote more precise, equitable, and coherent school-based mental health practices in public education systems. school psychology international

modeling the dynamics of time series search interest in autism with implications for public policies purpose this study aims to examine and forecast the temporal behavior of google search interest for the term “autism” in brazil. the purpose of this study is to investigate the temporal dynamics of public attention and evaluate whether these dynamics can inform the planning of communication and inclusion policies. by linking digital attention patterns to policy timing, territorial outreach and inclusive public communication, the paper contributes to evidence-based strategies for autism awareness and social inclusion. design/methodology/approach monthly google trends data for brazil were analyzed using time series forecasting models, including arima, additive and multiplicative holt–winters specifications and additive and multiplicative prophet models. the methodological procedure considered logarithmic transformation, stationarity assessment, differencing where required, residual diagnostics, information criteria and forecast accuracy indicators. the mathematical formulations of the models were retained to clarify the meaning of the stochastic process, smoothing components, seasonal effects and forecast errors. findings the results indicate a marked seasonal pattern, with recurrent peaks in april and lower levels of relative interest in december and january. among the evaluated specifications, the additive holt-winters model achieved the most accurate forecasting performance across the main error metrics. the arima results indicate limited autoregressive persistence and a pronounced role for seasonal and short-lived innovations in the search series. the weak association between searches for “autism” and “prejudice” suggests little systematic linear co-movement between these aggregate query series; possible explanations for this pattern are cautiously discussed, as google trends does not identify individual search motivations. practical implications the results support the strategic use of digital search data for planning autism-related communication, professional training and inclusive public policies. awareness campaigns can be better timed around predictable peaks in april, while periods of lower attention can be used to prepare materials, train professionals and strengthen intersectoral coordination. regional search patterns also suggest the need for territorially sensitive strategies, especially where online information-seeking may compensate for limited access to specialized services. originality/value the study extends autism-related infodemiology from predominantly descriptive or event-centered analyses to comparative time-series forecasting of a long monthly series in brazil. by comparing arima, additive and multiplicative holt–winters and additive and multiplicative prophet specifications, the paper evaluates whether recurring patterns of public attention can be forecast with sufficient stability to inform the timing of communication and inclusion policies. advances in autism

(don’t) mind the gap? the role of current versus desired state of goal attainment in predicting sustainable behavior understanding what motivates individuals to engage in sustainable behavior is essential for advancing sustainable development goals (sdgs). drawing on the cybernetic model of behavior regulation, this research investigates how the perceived gap between one’s desired level of societal progress towards sustainability and the current societal reality stimulates individuals’ action toward sustainability. across two studies, we found that individuals’ desired state—not the current state—was the strongest predictor of both their willingness (study 1) and actual engagement (study 2) in sustainable behavior. interestingly, individuals remained highly motivated to act sustainably even when sdgs were perceived as largely achieved. these effects extended beyond environmental concern to two other sdgs: health promotion and public safety. this suggests that, within the context of our studies, sustainable behavior seems to be meaningfully driven by personal goal alignment rather than current goal achievement in a society alone. our findings offer a novel application of the cybernetic model to sustainable behavior and highlight the importance of interventions that connect sustainable actions with individuals’ personal values, aspirations, and identity. for policymakers and practitioners, this implies that fostering a sense of personal ownership and relevance of sdgs may be more effective than emphasizing societal progress alone. social psychological bulletin

plan for scale out: adapting a diabetes prevention program for implementation in rural and remote british columbia abstract background rural and remote communities in canada face a higher incidence and risk of developing type 2 diabetes (t2d) compared to urban populations (government of canada sc, 2022). small steps for big changes is an evidence-based diabetes prevention program designed to support individuals at risk of t2d in adopting and maintaining sustainable changes to their diet and exercise through the application of behavior change techniques. to expand the reach of small steps for big changes and address the significant gap in t2d prevention resources in rural and remote communities, the program was scaled out to rural and remote community organizations across british columbia. the aim of this study was to describe the process used to scale out small steps for big changes and to identify the program and implementation strategy (is) adaptations made during the pre-implementation phase to support delivery. method adoption rates were analyzed and reported according to the adoption dimension of the re-aim ( reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, maintenance ) framework (glasgow et al., am j public health 89(9):1322–1327, 1999 sep) to describe the proportion of settings willing to deliver small steps for big changes . data on adaptations were extracted from meeting notes and email correspondence. adaptations to is were identified by comparing these data to is used in a previous small steps for big changes implementation project. all adaptations were deductively coded by two independent coders using the framework for reporting adaptations and modifications to evidence-based interventions (s, wiltsey stirman et al., implement sci 14(1):58, 2019 jun 6) and the framework for reporting adaptations and modifications to implementation strategies (cj miller et al., implement sci 16(1):36, 2021 apr 7). results three organizations in the interior and two in the northern region of british columbia adopted small steps for big changes , representing adoption rates of 23% and 22%, respectively. twenty-seven program adaptations were made with a primary goal of improving program oversight and quality improvement. 15 implementation strategy adaptations were identified and an additional 15 implementation strategies were added to support scale-out in attempts to improve reach, adoption, acceptability, or fidelity of the program. conclusion these findings can inform targeted implementation efforts and guide decisions about scaling diabetes prevention programs, such as s mall steps for big changes , into diverse community settings. international journal of behavioral medicine

psychological risk, protection and support in the context of dementia nature mental health, published online: 23 october 2026; doi:10.1038/s44220-026-00748-9 marchant et al. revisit the concept of psychological debt, synthesizing evidence that risk factors such as loneliness and repetitive negative thinking, alongside protective traits including purpose in life, may shape dementia risk. the perspective highlights mechanisms, methodological challenges, and opportunities for psychologically informed dementia prevention. nature mental health

systematic review and meta-analysis of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia as a suicide prevention strategy nature mental health, published online: 23 october 2026; doi:10.1038/s44220-026-00743-0 cagdas türkmen et al. conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate whether cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia affects suicidal ideation and behaviors in adults with insomnia. by synthesizing evidence across multiple trials, the study assesses the potential role of a first-line insomnia treatment in suicide prevention. nature mental health
