from sample diversity to interpretive convergence nature reviews psychology, published online: 22 october 2026; doi:10.1038/s44159-026-00636-0 generative artificial intelligence tools are being increasingly used by scientists, especially as writing aids for researchers outside english-dominant institutions. however, these tools might narrow interpretations even when applied to increasingly diverse samples. sampling diversity will not be enough to broaden behavioural science if interpretive diversity is lost. nature reviews psychology

escala de depresión, ansiedad y estrés (dass–21): estudio de sus propiedades psicométricas en argentina introducción: el 13% de la población mundial padece un trastorno mental, siendo el 59% cuadros de ansiedad o depresión (oms, 2022a). aunque en argentina existen instrumentos validados para evaluar por separado estos cuadros, no se cuenta con una herramienta breve que evalúe de manera integrada la sintomatología de depresión, ansiedad y estrés, dimensiones frecuentemente comórbidas de alta utilidad clínica. objetivo: evaluar las propiedades psicométricas del dass-21 en adultos de argentina. metodología: la muestra incluyó 334 adultos argentinos. se calcularon el coeficiente alfa de cronbach y las correlaciones ítem-total. se realizó un análisis factorial confirmatorio (modelos de tres factores y bifactor), se analizaron las correlaciones con el phq-9, gad-7 y hscl-11, y se evaluaron diferencias entre pacientes y no pacientes de psicoterapia. resultados: se obtuvieron evidencias de adecuada consistencia interna, homogeneidad y validez de constructo, concurrente y de criterio. el modelo bifactor, compuesto por un factor general de malestar emocional y tres factores específicos, presentó el mejor ajuste (cfi = ,95; tli = ,93; rmsea = ,06; srmr = ,05). las correlaciones con el phq-9 (r = ,79), el gad-7 (r = ,83) y el hscl-11 (r = ,86) aportaron evidencias de validez concurrente, mientras que los índices de fiabilidad compuesta (cr ≥ ,77) y los coeficientes heterotrait-monotrait ratio (htmt < ,85 entre subescalas) demostraron validez discriminante. discusión: estos resultados posicionan al dass-21 como el primer instrumento breve, gratuito y válido para la evaluación integrada de sintomatología de depresión, ansiedad y estrés en población adulta argentina, aplicable tanto en la práctica clínica como en investigación. revista ces psicologia

emotional dependence scale (eds-s): development and validation of a short measure in spanish-speaking adults aged 18–50 years objective. to develop and validate the short emotional dependence scale (eds-s) in spanish-speaking adults aged 18–50 years. method. a total of 1159 peruvian adults aged 18–50 years participated. internal structure was examined under the graded response model of item response theory, relations with other variables through a structural model, and measurement invariance across sex. results. a bifactor model with three specific factors (need for affection, low autonomy, fear of abandonment) showed adequate fit (m2 = 30.186, df = 18, p = .036; rmsea = .024; cfi = .999). hierarchical omega was acceptable (ωh = .81). the structural model yielded χ²(141) = 1087.27; cfi = .961; rmsea = .076, and scalar invariance across sex was supported. the eds-s is a brief, valid, and reliable measure. actualidades en psicologia

psychological and behavioral correlates of food addiction symptoms in university students: the role of hedonic eating and food label attitudes food addiction (fa) involves addictive-like eating and impaired control over palatable food consumption. this cross-sectional study examined fa correlates among 404 university students, focusing on palatable eating motives and food label reading attitudes. sixty-six participants (16.3%) met the original yale food addiction scale (yfas 1.0) threshold of at least three of seven dsm-iv-tr criteria plus clinically significant impairment or distress. female sex, smoking, obesity, and a higher t-pems mean were associated with higher odds of meeting the threshold; the obesity estimate was imprecise because that subgroup was small. model discrimination was acceptable in-sample (auc = 0.746). the t-pems mean had a weak inverse correlation with label attitudes ( r = −0.143) that was not significant after adjustment (β = −0.10, p = 0.060; r 2 = 0.057). findings support an association between palatable eating motives and fa but limited evidence for an independent label-attitude relationship. longitudinal and multicenter studies are needed. journal of health psychology

predictors of communication skills following a peer partner intervention for young autistic children with limited or no spoken language young autistic children with limited or no spoken language present with a myriad of social and communication challenges that restrict participation in school environments. instructional approaches that include a speech-generating device (sgd) to augment speech and teaching peers to be supportive communication partners can lead to marked improvements in communication, expressive language, and social reciprocity. to inform clinical decisions and individualize approaches to meet child needs, more research is needed to identify key child-level behaviors that predict treatment response to social communication interventions. this study determined if pre-treatment levels of (1) expressive and receptive language, (2) nonverbal cognitive skills, (3) autism characteristics, and (4) peer-directed communication and reciprocity were related to child communication following an sgd intervention with peer partners. participants included n = 56 autistic children (ages 3 to 6 years) with limited or no spoken language and n = 107 non-autistic peers (1–3 for each child). peers learned to stay–play–talk, then participated in 10 play-based intervention sessions with an autistic child implemented by trained school staff. an sgd with voice output app was provided for all children. participants demonstrated significant increases in three social communication outcomes after intervention. bivariate correlations were used to assess the relationship of potential predictors with these three key communication outcomes. then, predictors with significant associations were included in multiple linear regressions to examine the contributions of child-level predictors for each outcome. all three regression models explained significant variance and had at least one significant child-level predictor (e.g., expressive language, autism characteristics, or nonverbal cognitive skills). results provide support for identifying child characteristics that are precursors for growth in peer-directed social communication, and are thus important to teach to optimize outcomes for autistic children with significant communication challenges. behavioral sciences

investigation into effective factors affecting the self-esteem of university students using a pls-sem model in this study, we investigated the associations among university students’ self-esteem, social appearance anxiety, food craving acceptance, willingness to consume a healthy diet, body mass index, subjective evaluation of weight change, and fast-food intake level. data from 387 students were collected using an individual information form, the food craving acceptance and action scale, the social appearance anxiety scale, and the rosenberg self-esteem scale, and analysed using bootstrapped partial least squares structural equation modelling (pls-sem). self-esteem was negatively associated with social appearance anxiety and positively associated with willingness to consume a healthy diet (p < 0.05). although the direct association between body mass index and self-esteem was non-significant (p > 0.05), significant negative indirect associations emerged, through willingness to consume a healthy diet and/or social appearance anxiety (p < 0.05). contrary to expectations, a significant negative association was found between food craving acceptance and willingness to consume a healthy diet (p < 0.05). self-esteem was indirectly associated with fast-food intake level and food craving acceptance negatively, and with subjective evaluation of weight change positively. despite its high complexity and low explanatory power, the model achieved medium pls predictive power, demonstrating some out-of-sample predictive relevance for the majority of indicators within the current plspredict framework. these findings are inherently exploratory, serving as a foundational framework for future longitudinal research while offering valuable insights for professionals providing health and psychological guidance to university students. behavioral sciences

retention intervals, causal connections, and the 2016 election abstract prior work has shown that memory typically gets worse over time, and narrative memory is better the more causally connected an event is within the story. here, we assessed memory for a real-world narrative event, the 2016 us presidential election, which played out over many months. people were asked to recall election-related news stories and write brief headlines. we assessed memory in terms of the amount of time that had passed since the event, as well as the degree to which an event was causally integrated into the larger story. the data from 944 participants involved 1115 distinct news events that were coded in terms of temporal delay and number of causal connections to other events. we used negative binomial regression to examine these influences. surprisingly, although the amount of time had little impact on memory overall, the number of causal connections was significantly related to memory. furthermore, memory was driven more by the number of causal consequences that followed from an event rather than those that preceded it, although these had some influence. this indicates that for complex, long-term narratives, even those that play out over many months, the role that events play in a narrative’s causal structure are better predictors of memory than temporal distance. cognitive research-principles and implications

biological correlates of psychological distress among conflict-affected youth in yemen: the association of vitamin d status and helicobacter pylori infection. background: conflict-affected youth face intersecting biological and psychosocial stressors; however, integrated data are scarce. this study examined the associations between vitamin d deficiency, h. pylori infection, and psychological distress among youth in yemen.
methods: a community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 400 young adults (18-30 years) in al-dhalea, yemen. depression, anxiety, and stress were assessed using the dass-21. serum 25-hydroxyvitamin d, h. pylori stool antigen (confirmed by urea breath test), inflammatory markers (crp, il-6, tnf-α), and morning cortisol were measured. hierarchical regression models examined independent and combined associations.
results: moderate-to-severe depression, anxiety, and stress affected 49%, 60%, and 46% of participants. suboptimal vitamin d levels (< 30 ng/ml) were present at 87.5%, and 45% had an active h. pylori infection. vitamin d showed the strongest independent association with depression (β = -0.41, 95% ci: -0.50, -0.32), anxiety (β = -0.35, 95% ci: -0.45, -0.25), and stress (β = -0.29, 95% ci: -0.39, -0.19). h. pylori infection was independently associated with higher stress (β = 0.14, 95% ci: 0.05, 0.23). an exploratory post-hoc subgroup analysis identified a high-risk subgroup (n = 68, 17.0%) with concurrent severe vitamin d deficiency, h. pylori infection, severe psychological symptoms, and elevated inflammatory markers and cortisol (all p < 0.001).
conclusion: this study identifies a clustered vulnerability pattern of psychological distress, vitamin d deficiency, and h. pylori infection among conflict-affected youth. an exploratory "triple burden" subgroup warrants investigation. these hypothesis-generating findings suggest the potential utility of integrated interventions, though rigorous evaluation is required. major limitations include unmeasured trauma, a single-governorate scope, and post-hoc subgroup analysis requiring replication. clinical data indicate a substantial trauma burden in this setting, underscoring the need for future studies with validated trauma instruments. psychology research and behavior management

affective and nonaffective neural alterations across generations in survivors and perpetrators in a post‐genocide context abstract armed conflicts are associated with profound and long‐lasting mental health consequences, including post‐traumatic stress disorder (ptsd), which has been linked to alterations in neural processing in both affective and nonaffective domains. while numerous studies have documented such alterations shortly after traumatic events, far less is known about their long‐term persistence, their intergenerational transmission, and potential differences between victims and perpetrators of mass violence. addressing these gaps, the present pre‐registered study examined neural and psychological correlates of trauma among civilian survivors and civilian former perpetrators of the 1994 genocide against the tutsis in rwanda, as well as one of their offspring. participants completed questionnaires assessing traumatic exposure and ptsd symptomatology, alongside four electrophysiological tasks targeting affective (threat processing, emotion recognition) and nonaffective (sensory gating, auditory oddball) processes. thirty years after the genocide, survivors exhibited higher ptsd symptom severity than former perpetrators, particularly for re‐experiencing, hyperarousal, and avoidance. in affective tasks, survivors showed enhanced neural responses to threat and emotional stimuli, with some alterations persisting into the next generation. these effects were less pronounced or absent in former perpetrators and their offspring. in contrast, nonaffective tasks revealed robust sensory and oddball effects but no consistent associations with ptsd in either group. overall, the findings suggest that long‐term neural alterations following genocide are more prominent in affective processing and are especially evident among survivors, the primary targets of the violence. the study further highlights selective intergenerational transmission of trauma‐related symptomatology and demonstrates the feasibility of conducting electrophysiological research in post‐conflict, non‐western contexts. psychophysiology

less is more: why and when having less signals competence living with less has become increasingly popular in contemporary culture. it can simplify people’s lives and enhance their well-being. beyond these intrapersonal benefits, we document a novel, interpersonal benefit of having less: individuals who own fewer possessions are perceived as more competent than those who own more. this effect arises because observers infer that they rely more on reasoning rather than feelings in decision-making. we further develop a three-condition descriptive model specifying that the effect emerges when having fewer possessions appears voluntary, when the possessions are primarily non-hedonic, and when the quantity of possessions is sufficient to meet minimum needs. this research extends the literature on the benefits of having less from an intrapersonal to an interpersonal perspective and identifies possession quantity as a new cue for perceived competence. personality and social psychology bulletin

implicit prejudice differentially predicts placement into valuable and scarce opportunities racial excellence gaps persist, partly due to unequal participation in advanced learning opportunities. guided by the opportunity hoarding framework, this research investigates whether white americans’ pro-white/anti-black prejudice differentially predict simulated advanced placement (ap) course admission decisions, and under what conditions—when the opportunity is valuable, scarce, or both. across two experiments, we observed an unexpected overall pattern in which black students were placed into higher priority tiers than white students. nonetheless, greater implicit prejudice predicted larger white–black differences in placement decisions, explained by placing black students into lower tiers rather than white students into higher tiers. critically, we found preliminary evidence that this pattern emerges only when ap participation was described as both valuable and scarce. explicit prejudice showed less consistent associations with differences in placement decisions across studies. the valuable and scarce nature of advanced learning opportunities may amplify the effect of implicit prejudice in deciding who deserves access. personality and social psychology bulletin

the effects of foreign accent syndrome on bilingual speech production: multilevel evidence from a controlled-case study. foreign accent syndrome (fas) is a rare motor speech disorder with altered speech patterns perceived as a foreign accent. the effects of fas on the first (l1) and second-acquired (l2) languages in bilinguals have not been examined in depth and knowledge about its neural correlates is limited. additionally, possible disruptions in auditory-motor feedback processes supporting speech monitoring and voice adaptation are rarely assessed. this study reports on p1, an l1 catalan- l2 spanish bilingual with fas. we sought to characterize fas in her two languages using a multilevel approach combining perceptual, phonetic, neuropsychological, sensorimotor adaptation to auditory feedback and structural neuroimaging analyses. results showed that p1's l1 and l2 speech production were perceived as foreign by native bilingual listeners. phonetic analyses revealed segmental and suprasegmental disturbances in both languages resulting from focal left motor cortex damage. voice adaptation to auditory noise revealed an abnormal pattern, with differences between l1 and l2, suggesting altered auditory-motor integration. notably, p1's speech rate, fluency and eloquence were more affected in her l1, suggesting decreased automaticity in this language. she also presented domain-general executive control deficits and increased l1 to l2 switching, as she found l2 production easier. these findings suggest differential effects of fas on the l1 and l2 speech production of p1, with increased l1-l2 switching as a potential compensatory strategy to decrease executive control burden in l1 production and facilitate more fluent communication. our findings highlight a potential role for disrupted auditory-motor speech and voice integration in the manifestation of bilingual fas. cortex

development and validation of the ai-empowered visualization teaching competency scale. this study took primary and secondary school teachers in western china as participants. grounded in the ai-tpack framework and integrating visual literacy, data literacy, and relevant learning and development theories, it constructed a five-dimensional theoretical framework for teacher visualization teaching competency under ai empowerment. drawing on item analysis, exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, reliability testing, measurement invariance testing, and criterion-related validity testing, the study developed and validated the ai-empowered teacher visualization teaching competency scale (ai-vtcs). the results show that ai-vtcs comprises five dimensions-design and creation, awareness and interpretation, decision-making and collaboration, ethics and safety, and professional development-with a total of 31 items. the cronbach's α coefficients of the five subscales ranged from 0.911 to 0.934, and that of the overall scale was 0.967. both the first-order and second-order five-factor models achieved good fit, and the moderate-to-high correlations among the five dimensions support the hierarchical nature of the construct. measurement invariance from configural to strict invariance was established across gender, school type (public/private), and teaching stage (primary, middle, and high school). convergent validity, discriminant validity, and criterion-related validity all met psychometric standards. this study not only fills the theoretical gap in existing teacher competency frameworks regarding ai-empowered visualization teaching, but also provides a reliable and valid standardized measurement instrument for teacher education institutions to assess and precisely enhance teachers' ai visualization teaching competency. frontiers in psychology

the arabic leary impostorism scale: initial psychometric evaluation in a university student population. background: the leary impostorism scale (lis) is a brief established instrument designed to assess impostorism; however, no validated arabic version is currently available. this study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the arabic lis among university students.
methods: a cross-sectional validation study was conducted among arabic-speaking university students in saudi arabia. participants completed the arabic lis and comparator measures of impostorism, self-efficacy, and perfectionism. psychometric evaluation included internal consistency, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, construct and concurrent validity, and test-retest reliability.
results: a total of 185 participants with complete lis data were included in the psychometric analyses. the arabic lis demonstrated excellent internal consistency (cronbach's= 0.93; mcdonald's= 0.93). factorability indices supported factor analysis [kmo = 0.90; bartlett's(21) = 1536.59,< 0.001]. exploratory factor analysis based on polychoric correlations supported a single-factor structure, with factor loadings ranging from 0.81 to 0.94 and an eigenvalue of 5.45. confirmatory factor analysis showed statistically significant freely estimated loadings (< 0.001), with standardized loadings ranging from 0.78 to 1.00; global fit indices were(14) = 105.39, cfi = 0.91, tli = 0.87, rmsea = 0.19 (90% ci [0.16, 0.22]), and srmr = 0.06. strong positive correlations were observed with the cips-20 (= 0.76), cips-10 (= 0.77), and ipss-3 (= 0.66), whereas weaker correlations were found with general self-efficacy (= 0.20) and perfectionism (= 0.16-0.18). test-retest reliability was moderate among 14 participants retested after 1-4 weeks (pearson= 0.65; icc = 0.65).
conclusion: the arabic lis demonstrated high internal consistency and promising initial evidence of validity as a brief measure of impostorism among arabic-speaking university students. further evaluation of its factor structure and temporal stability in a broader population is warranted. frontiers in psychology

how personality traits and cultural value orientation moderate the pathway from musical emotional expression to group cohesion in choral rehearsal. introduction: choral singing is widely valued for building cohesion in community, educational, and well-being settings, yet the route by which emotional expression during rehearsal becomes group cohesion remains poorly specified, and most work still centers on individual feeling rather than on group-level interaction. grounded in emotional contagion and social identity theory, this study proposes and tests a dual-moderated mediation model.
methods: we surveyed 612 singers nested within 38 amateur choirs at three separated points in time and coded behavioral synchrony from audio- and video-recorded rehearsals, sampling choirs in two chinese regions chosen to maximize variation in individualism-collectivism rather than to represent two national cultures.
results: multilevel structural equation modeling supported a serial pathway: musical emotional expression raised group cohesion through behavioral synchrony and then shared affect, with monte carlo confidence intervals confirming the chain and with reversed-order and parallel-mediator models fitting less well. extraversion and agreeableness steepened the front segment from expression to synchrony, whereas cultural value orientation, measured in each singer rather than assigned by sampling site, conditioned the rear segment from shared affect to cohesion, the conversion being stronger under a collectivistic orientation. because 38 ensembles buy limited precision at the choir level, a monte carlo power analysis accompanies the estimates and marks which of them rest on firmer ground.
discussion: by giving the expression-cohesion transition an observable behavioral stage, and by locating personality and cultural moderators on distinct path segments, the study joins contagion and identity accounts. because the design separates measurements in time but manipulates nothing, the implications for choral education and group facilitation are offered as testable guidance rather than as settled practice. frontiers in psychology

relative contributions of personality, psychosocial functioning, and executive cognition to individual differences in delay discounting. background: delay discounting (dd) is a widely studied individual-difference phenotype that reflects preferences between smaller immediate and larger delayed rewards. previous studies have linked dd to demographic characteristics, personality traits, psychosocial functioning, and cognitive abilities. however, the relative incremental contribution of these domains within the same predictive framework remains unclear.
methods: we analyzed data from 1,193 healthy young adults from the human connectome project-young adult dataset. delay discounting was indexed by the area under the discounting curve for the $200 condition. participants were randomly divided into a training set (= 953) and a hold-out test set (= 240). hierarchical models sequentially incorporated demographic variables, personality and psychosocial measures, and executive cognitive measures. ordinary linear regression, elastic net, and xgboost were evaluated using apparent training performance, nested five-fold cross-validation, and hold-out testing. model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (), root-mean-square error (rmse), and mean absolute error (mae). incremental value was quantified as the change inbetween adjacent models (δ).
results: age and gender alone had little predictive value for dd. in the primary hierarchical models, the largest initial improvement occurred after personality and psychosocial measures were added, with a further increase after cognitive measures were included. the cognition-first analysis, however, showed that cognitive predictors produced similar gains when entered directly after the demographic baseline, particularly with elastic net and xgboost. thus, the apparent difference between the two predictor domains depended partly on the order in which they were entered. xgboost fit the training data substantially better than the linear models, but this advantage largely disappeared under cross-validation. in the hold-out test set, elastic net performed best (= 0.0507, rmse = 0.1976, mae = 0.1522), although overall prediction remained modest. an expanded sensitivity analysis using 257 available non-imaging predictors likewise showed low validated predictive performance.
conclusions: personality-psychosocial and cognitive measures both provided incremental predictive information beyond demographics, although their apparent relative contributions varied with predictor-block order. however, the modest validated performance indicates that delay discounting is influenced by multiple factors beyond those captured by the present models. these findings support a multidomain perspective on individual differences in delay discounting while highlighting the importance of cautious interpretation of predictive performance in large-scale behavioral datasets. frontiers in psychology

latent profiles of motivational and regulatory systems and their differential associations with problematic gaming and smoking behavior among chinese college students: a cross-sectional study background: problematic gaming and smoking are prevalent among college students, yet the extent to which they share or differ in associated psychological profiles remains unclear. this study identified latent psychological profiles based on motivational (behavioral inhibition system [bis] and behavioral activation system [bas]) and regulatory (control/impulse) systems, and examined the associative pathways through which anxiety and depression were linked to the relationships between these profiles and the two addictive behaviors. methods: this cross-sectional study was conducted between 16 and 29 march 2023. using convenience sampling, 21 universities were purposively selected from 10 provinces/municipalities in china. a total of 13,643 online questionnaires were returned, and 13,215 valid questionnaires were analyzed after excluding 428 invalid questionnaires. participants completed measures of bis/bas, self-control, problematic gaming, anxiety, depression, smoking behavior, and demographics. latent profile analysis was used to identify motivational–regulatory profiles. path analyses estimated indirect associations via anxiety and depression, and moderation analyses examined demographic moderators. all associations were interpreted cross-sectionally. results: five distinct profiles were identified: goal-oriented (4.44%), low-reactive (7.26%), moderate-conflict (16.32%), high-conflict (10.12%), and high-reactive-balanced (61.86%). all indirect associations via anxiety and depression were significant for both problematic gaming and smoking. within problematic gaming, anxiety-related indirect associations were consistently stronger than depression-related ones. within smoking, anxiety-related and depression-related indirect associations were comparable. conclusions: these cross-sectional findings indicate that the relative prominence of anxiety- and depression-related pathways may differ within each behavior. because the two outcomes were measured on different scales, no direct cross-outcome comparison was conducted. given the cross-sectional design and the measures used, no causal or mechanistic conclusions can be drawn, and the findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. behavioral sciences

the role of the dissenting voter on jury deliberation online: a pilot study. jury deliberation involves both individual judgments and interpersonal processes through which jurors exchange information, respond to disagreement, and work toward a collective decision. this mixed-methods pilot study examined individual characteristics, deliberative participation, verdict change, and dissent across seven virtual mock juries. thirty-five participants took part in pre- and post-deliberation data collection and deliberated via zoom in six-person juries that included a trained confederate operating under a conditional dissent protocol. collaborative conflict-management style was positively associated with self-reported deliberative participation, whereas openness, agreeableness, competing conflict style, and civic engagement were not; however, the overall predictor model did not significantly improve fit relative to the unconditional model. among 34 participants with complete verdict data, all six who initially selected not guilty changed to guilty following deliberation, producing a statistically significant paired shift that did not support the hypothesized direction of change. confederate-introduced dissent occurred in six juries, while dissent emerged organically in one. differences in deliberation length were therefore examined descriptively. qualitative content analysis further indicated that exchanges involving dissent included substantive engagement with competing interpretations, evidentiary ambiguity, and jurors' reasoning. these preliminary findings suggest that understanding jury decision-making requires attention not only to final verdicts, but also to how jurors participate in and respond to disagreement during deliberation. behavioral sciences

express: how error rates scale with chance rate among dogs following human pointing gestures, and why it matters humans use pointing gestures to communicate with dogs. however, efforts to study how dogs receive this communicative signal have produced ambiguous results. prior work presenting a choice between two options has shown that dogs choose the pointed-to option at above chance levels, but just barely. with only two options, the high probability of choosing correctly by chance weakens the signal. after replicating the 2-option task, we changed the task’s parameters by presenting dogs with six options. we compared two models that make divergent, quantitative predictions on how the success rates will relate on the two tasks. one model stresses that multiplying the options should reduce the number of correct choices made by chance at a higher rate than instances of genuine communication. a second model that involves no understanding of referents, but just a systematic shift in attention, predicts the effect size to remain constant irrespective of the number of options. dogs chose the location pointed to at barely above chance rates in both the 2-choice and 6-choice tasks. this pattern discourages the view that dogs understand the referential aspect of human pointing. additional patterns that become visible with more than two options bolster this interpretation. dogs chose the correct side of the arena and succeeded on second choices disproportionately more often. dogs succeeded with far and near locations at similar rates. these results challenge the view that dogs interpret human pointing as referring to a specific object, which has implications for claims that point-following evinces intentional capacities among dogs. quarterly journal of experimental psychology

express: the dynamics of cue integration in metacognitive judgments learners form judgments of learning (jols) by integrating multiple cues. however, little is known about how cue integration might change over time. to examine this, we introduced a modified cue-integration paradigm in which one cue (the context cue) remained constant across sequences of trials varying in length, while another cue (the target cue) varied randomly. this design allowed us to examine how the consistency and variability of a cue affect its use for jols and that of other available cues. in three experiments, participants studied nouns with two cues manipulated per experiment (e.g., emotionality, concreteness). in all experiments, both cues influenced jols, and the target cue’s influence remained stable across conditions, suggesting that learners used the two cues independently. in experiment 1, the context cue’s effect declined when its level was constant across multiple consecutive trials. this adaptation effect did not replicate in experiments 2 and 3. exploratory cross-experimental analyses showed stronger context cue effects immediately after than immediately before context cue levels switched. this hints at a transient increase in cue salience following a switch. together, our findings show that learners flexibly respond to changes in cue consistency and variability while maintaining their overall cue integration strategy. quarterly journal of experimental psychology
on randolph blake journal of vision

preservice mathematics teachers’ problem-solving self-efficacy, critical thinking disposition, and mathematical creativity self-efficacy: a cross-sectional path analytic study developing flexible thinking, generating alternative solution strategies, and producing original ideas are increasingly emphasized in mathematics education. this study examines the relationships among preservice elementary mathematics teachers’ problem-solving self-efficacy, critical thinking disposition, and mathematical creativity self-efficacy. drawing on a theoretically informed framework, it specifically investigates whether critical thinking disposition statistically mediates the association between problem-solving self-efficacy and mathematical creativity self-efficacy. data were collected from 554 preservice elementary mathematics teachers. analyses included descriptive statistics, pearson correlations, and bootstrap-based observed-variable path analysis to obtain robust estimates of direct and indirect associations. findings indicated that positive problem-solving self-efficacy was strongly associated with critical thinking disposition, which was, in turn, positively associated with mathematical creativity self-efficacy. critical thinking disposition also statistically mediated the association between problem-solving self-efficacy and mathematical creativity self-efficacy. a reverse-direction model showed comparably good overall fit, indicating that the observed data were also compatible with an alternative directional ordering. these findings suggest that problem-solving self-efficacy and critical thinking disposition represent complementary cognitive-affective constructs that are empirically associated with perceptions of mathematical creativity. given the cross-sectional design, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal direction. the results instead provide empirical support for a theoretically motivated model of the associations among problem-solving self-efficacy, critical thinking disposition, and mathematical creativity self-efficacy. journal of intelligence

episodic memory: dynamic modes for constructing episodes the capacity to re-experience a moment from one's past, known as episodic memory, is critical for our ability to navigate the present and plan for the future. this article reviews and synthesizes over a half century of behavioral and neuroscientific research that has shaped our understanding of how we remember past events. this work has revealed complementary truths about episodic memory: episodic memories seem to be based on traces of experience, carrying objective information about specific moments in time, and on imaginative reconstructions, built on a scaffold of prior knowledge. we propose that the tension between these perspectives can be reconciled by conceptualizing episodic memory not as a readout from a static memory system but as the outcome of two neurocognitive modes— a generative mode that facilitates schema-based inference and prediction, and a contextual mode that binds memories to context-specific anchor points. drawing from experimental findings and computational models, we describe how multiple memory modes arise from dynamic cortico-hippocampal interactions, allowing episodic memory to be at once precise and constructive. annual review of psychology

korean negative outcome expectations scale–engineering (k–noes–e): cross-cultural validation with korean women engineering students the present study aimed to validate the negative outcome expectations scale-engineering (noes-e; lee et al., 2018) among a sample of korean women engineering students. the noes-e assesses four components of negative outcome expectations in engineering: cultural-related stressors, personal life and work balance, job characteristics, and social costs. in the present study, an exploratory factor analysis ( n = 351) was conducted, and the results supported the original four-factor structure, although one item was removed. confirmatory factor analysis ( n = 355) indicated that the bifactor model provided the best fit to the data. the measurement invariance test further showed that the korean version of negative outcome expectations scale-engineering (k-noes-e) was equivalent across university location and income. in addition, convergent, discriminant, concurrent, and incremental validity were supported. these findings suggest that the k-noes-e is a useful instrument for researchers and practitioners seeking to understand negative outcome expectations among korean women engineering students. journal of career assessment

beliefs about social mobility across childhood children in the united states face declining rates of upward social mobility, yet cultural narratives such as the american dream persist, emphasizing that anyone can improve their circumstances while also distorting perceptions of opportunity and inequality. this article synthesizes emerging research on how children in the united states and china reason about social mobility. in early childhood, children view social status as malleable and recognize that opportunities for upward mobility are not equally accessible to all. with age, children increasingly explain disparities in upward mobility in terms of structural rather than individual factors and allocate resources to groups they view as less likely to experience mobility. together, this research suggests that recognizing unequal opportunities for upward mobility is associated with behavior that rectifies, rather than perpetuates, inequality. we conclude by identifying key questions about how children’s beliefs and causal explanations about social mobility vary across social and cultural contexts, what experiences shape their emergence, and whether the expression or correlates of beliefs about social mobility change from childhood to adulthood. current directions in psychological science

multidimensional emotional disorder inventory: reliability and validity in a turkish community sample. categorical diagnoses often fail to capture the comorbidity and heterogeneity of emotional disorders, and the multidimensional emotional disorder inventory (medi) offers a transdiagnostic, dimensional alternative. this study examined the psychometric properties of a turkish version of the medi. the instrument was adapted following standardized cross-cultural procedures, including forward-backward translation, quantitative expert review of content validity, and a bilingual pilot study of linguistic equivalence. a community sample (= 1011) completed the turkish medi together with convergent validity measures. the factor structure was examined in two random half-samples using exploratory structural equation modeling (esem, n = 505) and esem and confirmatory factor analysis (= 506), and esem-based measurement invariance was tested across administration mode (online vs. paper-and-pencil) and gender. esem supported the original nine-factor structure in both half-samples. all nine subscales showed good internal consistency (cronbach's α and mcdonald's ω = 0.80 to 0.88), and esem-based invariance tests supported scalar invariance across gender and administration mode, with weaker support for administration mode. each medi dimension correlated strongly with its target criterion, supporting convergent validity, and gender-stratified community reference data were established. the findings support the reliability and validity of the turkish medi for assessing transdiagnostic dimensions in community samples. its utility for clinical decision-making requires further validation in clinical samples. behavioral sciences

cinematic vr in preservice teacher education: an evaluation of classroom interaction scenarios this study evaluated cinematic virtual reality (c-vr) classroom interaction scenarios for use in preservice teacher education. final-phase preservice teachers ( n = 212) completed a standardised c-vr session with 16 psychologically demanding classroom scenarios and a post-test battery assessing affect, presence, cybersickness, perceived benefit, coping satisfaction and peer recommendation. perceived-benefit and peer-recommendation ratings were concentrated in the upper half of their four-point scales, while subgroup differences by prior teaching-related and vr experience were small and statistically inconclusive. presence was positively associated with positive affect. coping satisfaction was positively related to positive affect and negatively related to negative affect. cybersickness scores were concentrated towards the lower part of the theoretical scale range although higher cybersickness was associated with higher negative affect and less favourable appraisals of the format. overall, the findings indicate favourable post-session appraisals of c-vr classroom scenarios and identify cybersickness as an implementation-relevant constraint while not establishing instructional effectiveness or learning gains. psychology learning and teaching-plat

filial caregiving burnout in the chinese cultural context: conceptualization, scale development, and longitudinal validation abstract in china, the confucian norm of filial piety has historically framed eldercare as an important responsibility of adult children. amid rapid population aging, caregivers frequently experience profound exhaustion. while traditional assessments capture caregiver burden, they may be less sensitive to role‐ and culture‐embedded experiences such as emotional detachment, relational strain, and value dissonance arising when caregiving realities conflict with internalized obligations. although the phenomenon of filial caregiving burnout (fcb) has been recently identified, it lacks a formal theoretical definition and measurement tool. to address this limitation, we conceptualize fcb and develop a culturally grounded, multidimensional scale. using an exploratory sequential mixed‐methods design, qualitative interviews first generated the initial item pool. subsequent quantitative evaluations across three independent caregiver samples ( n = 1653) refined and validated the structure via exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, alongside measurement invariance testing. finally, a two‐wave longitudinal design assessed predictive validity. the finalized 17‐item fcb scale features a robust three‐factor structure: physical and mental exhaustion, relational detachment, and dysregulation of filial piety value. it demonstrated excellent internal consistency ( α = 0.948), acceptable model fit, and measurement invariance across gender and hukou type. longitudinally, higher baseline fcb significantly predicted lower subsequent family and job performance and higher subsequent family undermining and counterproductive work behavior. moving beyond generic burden metrics, the fcb scale captures relational and value‐laden aspects of filial caregiving burnout and provides a multidimensional tool for assessing burnout experiences among adult‐child caregivers. family process

standing before memory: experiencing memorials moves us to engage with the past abstract experiencing a memorial can affect observers beyond making the events that are commemorated salient. the present research addresses this issue by surveying and comparing participants who were in the presence of a memorial to control participants who were not. in the presence of a memorial, participants reported greater personal relevance of the topics commemorated as well as greater behavioral intentions to engage with the past ( n study 1 = 142). this association was not due to simply assuming to be in the presence of a memorial ( n study 2 = 149) and replicated ( n study 3 = 244). our findings suggest that public memorials do not merely mark a place or event but influence observers to engage with the past and may affect behavioral intentions. we discuss the role of contextual factors, individual differences, and emotional responses, highlighting the need for further research. journal of applied social psychology

threat ownership theory: toward a greater understanding of the dynamic link between threat and political attitudes abstract how do threatening events shape political attitudes? some theories argue that threat increases support for conservatism. others claim that threat reinforces preexisting political beliefs. others argue that some threats can induce support for liberalism. our theoretical approach attempts to reconcile these conflicting perspectives, proposing that people support the political ideas or entities they perceive as best able to address the threat they experience. in one meta‐analysis and one well‐powered experiment, we examined the effect of threat on political beliefs, in accordance with our theory. our meta‐analysis aligned with expectations, indicating that the type of threat influenced the direction in which political beliefs shift. in our experimental study, we again manipulated the type of threat, with some threats being both left‐ and right‐wing politicized and others not. although we anticipated results similar to our meta‐analysis, we found no consistent evidence that our manipulated threats influenced political beliefs. these findings imply the link between threat and political preferences is more tenuous than expected. journal of applied social psychology

fostering connections: how mentoring relationships can promote youth social capital abstract little is known about how mentors support mentees in strengthening social capital. it is theorized that mentors support mentees in building new connections and strengthening existing relationships (i.e., connection‐building support). this mixed‐methods study examines how connection‐building support contributes to mentee's network mobilization in pursuit of life goals. survey data were gathered from youth ( n = 122) ages 13–18 (88% youth of color; 57% female). a path model tested the association between connection‐building support and mentee goal attainment and occupational identity via network mobilization. interviews with 12 mentor‐mentee pairs further elucidated how mentors support mentee social capital. connection‐building support was indirectly associated with greater progress toward life goals and stronger occupational identity via network mobilization. qualitative findings added nuance on mentor actions that support mentee social capital. findings highlight implications for practice and offer considerations for strengthening youth social capital in mentoring relationships. journal of community psychology

christian school leaders' perspectives on student mental health: a mixed methods study abstract this convergent parallel mixed methods study examined private christian school leaders' perceptions of student mental health needs and their schools' capacity to address those needs. participants included 164 private christian school leaders who completed a survey; 10 of these leaders participated in semi‐structured interviews. we analyzed survey data with descriptive and inferential statistics, analyzed interview responses with inductive semantic thematic analysis, and integrated both data strands through mixed methods analysis. results showed that leaders perceived substantial student mental health concerns, particularly anxiety and interpersonal conflict, and reported school responses such as counseling services and family collaboration. leaders at schools with mental health professionals reported greater perceived student mental health challenges and greater perceived capacity to meet students' needs. quantitative and qualitative findings converged around leaders' self‐reported commitment to supporting student well‐being. this study contributes to the limited literature on mental health support in private christian schools and offers insight into how leaders perceive these schools' understanding of and responses to student mental health needs. psychology in the schools

boosting or blocking breastfeeding confidence? the role of online breastfeeding content in relation to mothers' breastfeeding self‐efficacy abstract mothers increasingly go online to find answers to their breastfeeding concerns, read personal experiences, or connect with breastfeeding “mommy influencers.” this study analyzes how the consultation of online platforms and breastfeeding‐related posts is linked to mothers' breastfeeding self‐efficacy, and whether this relationship is moderated by mothers' different motives (i.e., information‐seeking, entertainment, or community building) for consuming such content online within a dutch‐speaking context. drawing on social cognitive theory and the uses and gratifications framework, an online survey ( n = 354; m age = 31, 22) was conducted among dutch‐speaking mothers. participants reported their exposure to online breastfeeding content from various resources (social media, “mommy influencers,” parenting community groups), their motives for consulting these different resources, and their breastfeeding self‐efficacy. structural equation modeling (sem) reveals that online breastfeeding content consumption is not directly related to breastfeeding self‐efficacy. however, an interaction effect was found with the information‐seeking motive: mothers not using online parenting platforms for informational purposes show a more negative association between online exposure to breastfeeding content and breastfeeding self‐efficacy compared to mothers not using these platforms for informational reasons [correction added on 12 november 2026, after first online publication: the preceding sentence has been corrected]. these findings highlight the complex role of online breastfeeding content, suggesting that informational motives may shape mothers' self‐efficacy differently. scandinavian journal of psychology
masculine capital and men’s body image: managing appearance concerns and implications for health interventions psychology & health
contrapower sexual harassment: a focus on perpetrators journal of social psychology

from the intolerance of uncertainty scale–5 to the intolerance of uncertainty scale–4: psychometric evaluation and refinement of an ultra-brief intolerance of uncertainty scale in a sample of spanish adults background: intolerance of uncertainty (iu) is a central transdiagnostic vulnerability factor across emotional disorders. however, currently available scales present important limitations, particularly excessive length and factorial instability. methods: this study evaluated the psychometric properties of the intolerance of uncertainty scale–5 (ius-5) in a sample of spanish adults (n = 998) using a cross-sectional online study design with a cross-validation approach that included exploratory graph analyses, redundancy testing, confirmatory factor analyses, and assessments of reliability and convergent validity. results: network analyses supported a unidimensional structure but identified item redundancy. confirmatory analyses indicated that a four-item model (ius-4) provided the best fit to the data. the ius-4 demonstrated adequate internal consistency (ω = 0.79), satisfactory convergent validity at the construct level (average variance extracted [ave] = 0.53), moderate to large correlations with anxiety sensitivity (r = 0.53), and moderate correlations with anxiety, depressive, and obsessive–compulsive symptoms (r = 0.41–0.42). conclusions: these findings support the ius-4 as a brief, psychometrically robust, unidimensional measure of iu in the spanish population. further research is warranted to examine its applicability in clinical samples and its potential utility as a screening tool. behavioral psychology-psicologia conductual

temporal invariance and validity of the european quality of life 5 dimensions 3 level version among taiwanese older adults following hip fracture surgery background: the euroqol five-dimension, 3-level (eq-5d-3l) instrument is widely used to assess health-related quality of life (hrqol). however, its longitudinal validity among older adults after hip fracture surgery remains unclear. the present study examined the psychometric properties of eq-5d-3l, with emphasis on factorial validity, temporal invariance, and score stability. methods: a total of 719 older adults who underwent hip fracture surgery completed the eq-5d-3l at baseline and 562 completed the eq-5d-3l at 3 months postoperatively. results: confirmatory factor analysis (cfa) supported a single-factor structure at both time points (baseline: comparative fit index [cfi] = 0.988, tucker–lewis index [tli] = 0.975; 3 months: cfi = 0.997, tli = 0.993). temporal invariance was mostly supported (δcfi ≤ 0.01) across configural, metric, and scalar models. however, the correlation between baseline and follow-up utility scores was nonsignificant (r = 0.072, p = 0.052), indicating varied recovery patterns. conclusions: these findings support the eq-5d-3l as a valid longitudinal measure of hrqol among older adults following hip fracture surgery. behavioral psychology-psicologia conductual

best practices for spirituality and religion in counseling: a review of its development and implications abstract the association for spiritual, ethical, and religious values in counseling ( aservic ) last published competencies for addressing spiritual and religious issues in counseling in 2009. this article describes the 2025 revision, which reframes these competencies as best practices. key structural changes include reorganization from six categories into the ways paradigm (i.e., ways of being, ways of understanding, and ways of intervening ), an intentional shift in terminology, and explicit integration of cultural humility and intersectionality throughout the framework. the revised best practices approach emphasizes ongoing professional development rather than fixed achievement, which reflects spirituality and religion as dynamic dimensions of human experiences. supplemental documents include reflection questions, a resource guide, and guidance to support practical implementation. implications for counselor education, supervision, and professional development emphasize holistic integration rather than checklist approaches. this revision positions counseling professionals to more effectively address spiritual and religious considerations in culturally responsive and ethically informed ways. counseling and values

racial ideology cluster profiles differ by race-related stress, not sense of belonging racial ideologies reflect philosophies about how black individuals should interact and behave in society. individuals who endorse ideologies prioritizing black people and culture are commonly assumed to feel more sense of belonging to the racial group than those whose ideologies are not racially focused. yet, such assumptions are untested and inconsistent with social identity frameworks highlighting ideology and sense of belonging as unique dimensions of social identity. this study addresses this gap by investigating associations between racial ideologies and sense of belonging using self-report measures from 229 black adults. using ensemble cluster analysis, we identified three ideology profiles and compared them across race-related stress and sense of belonging. members of the nationalist and mainstream minority profiles were more likely than members of the humanist profile to report high levels of cultural race-related stress and institutional race-related stress. only members of the nationalist profile reported high levels of individual race-related stress. cluster profiles did not differ in a sense of belonging to the racial group suggesting that individuals’ philosophies and expectations are varied, but this diversity does not undermine a sense of belonging to the racial in-group. consistent with social identity frameworks, these results demonstrated that recognizing and investigating discrete identity dimensions is necessary for greater understanding of racial identity and its functions. journal of black psychology

“i am prejudiced and i do not know why”: negotiating prejudice and moral identity in everyday talk abstract relations between the roma minority and the czech majority remain shaped by persistent structural inequalities, despite the public salience of egalitarian norms. this exploratory qualitative study examines how members of the czech ethnic majority negotiate, articulate and regulate anti‐roma bias while maintaining an egalitarian moral identity. drawing on reflexive thematic analysis of two focus group discussions ( n = 14), predominantly with educated young adults, we generated three overarching themes: (1) constructing the origins of bias through structural distance and socialised caution; (2) navigating the discrepancy between spontaneous reactions, the subjective “warning light,” and self‐regulatory management; and (3) moral boundaries under pressure regarding bystander hesitation and relational constraints in the face of overt racism. rather than expressing blatant hostility, participants framed prejudice as an involuntary, socially conditioned reflex requiring ongoing internal and discursive self‐regulation. limited intergroup contact was narrated as an unchosen, structural given and reinforced by familial warnings and normalised humour. furthermore, reluctance to confront overt discrimination reflected tensions between abstract anti‐racist principles and concerns over peer cohesion. integrating frameworks on prejudice self‐regulation, motivational orientations and discursive accountability, these findings illustrate that contemporary majority prejudice functions as a dynamic moral enterprise. addressing subtle bias requires educational and community interventions that support individuals in translating private egalitarian convictions into normatively supported, active bystander practice. journal of community & applied social psychology

political identity, leftism, and guns among a national sample of lgbtq+ americans beliefs about and ownership of guns have long been politicized in the united states. although research is well-established regarding the democrat/republican divide on gun control in the general population, empirical work on lgbtq+ populations and taking into account americans with leftist politics is lacking. a national sample of lgbtq+ americans ( n = 1,170) completed the gun violence in the context of interpersonal violence experiences among sexual and gender minorities (gives) study. these studies examine gun ownership, behavior, and beliefs in the context of self-identified political identity. a substantial minority ( n = 207; 17.7%) self-identified with leftist politics via a write-in option on the survey, and therefore a new category of the political identity variable was created. study 1 found that political identity is significantly associated with gun ownership, carry/display of guns, and all measures given regarding beliefs about guns and perceptions of safety due to hate-motivated mass violence. post hoc testing revealed that although democrats and republicans were most sharply divided, there were also key differences across variables in how leftists and independents responded. study 2 investigated the leftist subgroup more closely, finding that among leftist identities endorsed, there are significant differences in ownership, beliefs about gun control, beliefs that guns make one safer, and social presence of guns. further research should aim to explore the relationship between lgbtq+ identity and leftist politics, and how americans who self-identify with leftist politics may differ in beliefs and behaviors regarding firearms. journal of social and political psychology

reconfiguring the national memory: bangladesh in the immediate aftermath of the july 2024 mass uprising in july 2024, university students in bangladesh initiated the quota reform movement , demanding a merit-based system for government job recruitment. initially ignored by the ruling awami league government, the movement sparked widespread protest. as public unrest intensified, the movement evolved into a mass uprising by mid-july, ultimately leading to the ousting of prime minister sheikh hasina on 5 august. in the wake of this upheaval, dr. muhammed yunus, an economist and nobel laureate, was appointed chief adviser of the interim government, tasked with steering the country through the crisis. this article examines the interim government’s initiatives aimed at reshaping national memory following the uprising, particularly focusing on its mnemonic recalibrations within the country’s tumultuous political landscape. it analyzes how these initiatives are crafted to shape future narratives by rendering pre-uprising national memory of bangladesh unwanted. memory studies

are there directional longitudinal associations between school reading and mathematics achievement? abstract conflicting claims exist in the literature on the direction of the effects between reading and mathematics. this study used the random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (ri‐clpm) in a larger sample to assess directional associations across grades 3, 5, 7 and 9 using longitudinal data of the national assessment program of literacy and numeracy (naplan). the population data comprised all 87,610 new south wales school students in grade 3 of 2012. the ri‐clpms showed large positive directional effects from reading to subsequent mathematics in primary school and the start of secondary school (grades 3 to 5 and 5 to 7). also, between grades 3 and 5, the models showed large positive directional effects in the opposite direction, mathematics to subsequent reading. the longitudinal studies reviewed show heterogeneity. image british journal of developmental psychology
when hormones and emotions intersect: emotionally focused therapy for women with bipolar disorder women & therapy

theorizing trust as practice: a decolonial study of everyday interethnic relations in indonesia abstract one of the important topics in decolonization is indigenization. in this article, we seek to contribute to the body of knowledge by developing situated psychological knowledge, theory and practice of trust that is aligned with local, cultural and indigenous worldviews. moving beyond euro‐american models that frame trust as an individual disposition or rational calculation, we conceptualize trust as a relational, embodied and historically situated practice, grounded in asian moral and cultural worlds. based on our immersive ethnographic fieldwork and visual narrative methods involving 35 participants across four pasar (traditional markets) in indonesia, the analysis reveals how trust is enacted through culturally meaningful routines, such as extending informal credit, navigating stereotypes, managing debt and preserving relational dignity during bargaining. these practices draw on intergenerational memory, moral obligation and spatial familiarity, while also navigating the enduring effects of colonial histories and ethnic stratification. by theorizing trust as relational interconnections of humans, materials, emotions and cultural expectations, we offer an epistemic innovation by exploring indonesian marketplace life as a site for analysis. the findings contribute to efforts to decolonize theory in social psychology by articulating a practice‐based understanding of trust that foregrounds interdependence, moral economy and the micropolitics of coexistence in plural asian contexts. asian journal of social psychology

scale development and factor analysis of the moral–civic identity scale in adolescents and emerging adults from germany and german-speaking switzerland abstract adolescence and emerging adulthood are key periods for consolidating value-based identities that motivate civic life. we introduce the moral–civic identity (german original: moralisch demokratische identität ; mdi) scale, a brief instrument that assesses the internalized centrality of moral and civic traits in the self-concept. data came from 1149 adolescents and emerging adults (16–27 years) residing in germany or the german-speaking part of switzerland, who were recruited through a professional online panel provider. participants completed 27 trait items (9 moral, 9 civic; 9 distractors). initial confirmatory factor analyses compared a one-factor model, a correlated two-factor model (moral, civic), a higher-order model, and a bifactor model. subsequent data-informed item-reduction analyses yielded a 14-item correlated two-factor solution (7 moral; 7 civic) that provided the most parsimonious and theoretically coherent representation in this present sample. the subscales showed adequate reliability, and moral and civic identity were strongly related yet distinct. multi-group cfa supported full invariance across residence (germany vs. german-speaking switzerland) and configural–scalar invariance across gender. the mdi offers a short and openly available tool for research and evaluation, with initial evidence supporting its use in germany and the german-speaking part of switzerland. discover psychology
parent-child interaction therapy: attrition and outcomes in a community-based clinic child & family behavior therapy

a comparison of stimulus‐stimulus pairing and operant discrimination training to establish conditioned reinforcers abstract individuals with developmental disabilities may be sensitive to a limited number of conditioned reinforcers. stimulus‐stimulus pairing, a common strategy used to establish conditioned reinforcers, has demonstrated inconsistent results. operant discrimination training involves conditioning reinforcers by presenting them as discriminative stimuli during operant conditioning. the effectiveness of establishing conditioned reinforcers using both methods was evaluated. eight consecutively admitted individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities participated in the study. while both methods produced stimuli that induced above‐baseline levels of responding, only four participants demonstrated moderate‐to‐high treatment effects, and no relative advantage could be established for either procedure. behavioral interventions

friendship heterogeneity in gifted adolescents: a lexical analysis of close relationships research on the socialization of gifted adolescents yields inconsistent findings, and potential heterogeneity within this population has rarely been examined. this study is aimed at qualitatively examining how gifted adolescents perceive their close friendship. we conducted semistructured interviews with 31 french gifted adolescents (11 girls and 20 boys) enrolled in middle school and analyzed the transcripts using descending hierarchical lexical analysis with iramuteq. five distinct friendship experiences emerged: ambivalent (marked by tensions between identification/differentiation and support/competition); emotionally uninvested (characterized by low affective engagement); supportive (involving mutual aid and sharing outside school); school‐based (a secure and structuring bond anchored in the school setting); and fraternal (with strong emotional closeness modeled on sibling relationships). these configurations were associated with gender, age, grade level, grade acceleration and friend status (as best vs. close friend). across configurations, perceived friendship quality varied with relational dimensions (warmth vs. opposition), emotional intensity, spatiotemporal context, and identity processes. although most participants described meaningful and functional bonds with their close friend, they reported difficulties primarily in classroom contexts. this finding underscores the value of a more comprehensive analysis of friendship networks. new directions for child and adolescent development

rethinking autism: parental narratives on diagnosis, stigma and neurodiversity purpose this study aimed to examine the lived experiences of parents raising autistic children, focusing on diagnostic challenges, social stigma and the tension between medical and social disability models. design/methodology/approach through semi-structured interviews with 40 parents from specialized support centers, the authors explore how early recognition difficulties, masking behaviors and gendered experiences shape caregiving practices. findings findings reveal that parents experience significant emotional distress during diagnosis, compounded by societal judgment and pressure to conform. research limitations/implications despite these challenges, the parents’ words emphasize emerging strengths and a call to reconceptualize autism within a neurodiversity framework. this study demonstrates that integrating clinical indicators with familial experiences is essential for refining diagnostic protocols and support systems. implications for clinical practice, policy reform and research underscore the need for inclusive approaches that view autistic traits as natural variations rather than deficits, urging revisions in practice, policy and community support. social implications beyond documenting parental difficulties, the study contributes a culturally situated interpretation of how diagnostic uncertainty, stigma, caregiving demands and neurodiversity-oriented meaning-making interact within a palestinian service context. the findings extend existing literature by showing how these processes are experienced together rather than as isolated challenges. originality/value this study offers an original qualitative exploration of palestinian parents’ lived experiences of raising autistic children, using interpretative phenomenological analysis to examine diagnostic challenges, stigma, masking, gendered caregiving and neurodiversity. unlike studies grounded primarily in clinical perspectives, it centers parental narratives to illuminate how sociocultural factors shape autism experiences in a conflict-affected setting. by integrating lived experiences with contemporary neurodiversity perspectives, the study advances understanding of autism beyond deficit-based models and provides practical implications for improving diagnostic pathways, family-centered support, professional practice and inclusive policies that promote acceptance and well-being. advances in autism

the importance given to personal values depends on whether you focus on social desirability or utility the goal of this paper is to answer the following question: what personal values are most important to people? building on dubois and beauvois’ model of social value, i try to show that the prioritization of personal values depends on the evaluative focus (social desirability versus social utility) one adopts. in two studies ( n total = 2019) asking participants to judge schwartz’s personal values when adopting the two different evaluative foci, the results showed that self-transcendence (self-enhancement) values were systematically judged as more socially desirable (socially useful) than self-enhancement (self-transcendence) ones, with openness-to-change and conservation falling in between. these results may help resolve inconsistencies observed in the literature between works showing a general preference for self-transcendence values and others pointing to the centrality of self-enhancement values in the functioning of capitalist societies. social psychological bulletin

attentional biases in dispositional mindfulness and gratitude dispositional mindfulness and gratitude are two individual differences suggested to be linked to attentional processes. the present study aimed to assess the presence of attentional biases associated with these two traits. sixty-one participants completed an emotional dot-probe task while eye movements were recorded. each of the 96 trials presented one emotional facial expression (fear, surprise, anger, sadness, disgust, or happiness) paired with a neutral face from the same encoder. attentional biases were measured using dwell time and initial orienting, in addition to traditional probe response times. results suggested that individuals high in mindfulness responded faster to probes than those low in mindfulness across all conditions, supporting the view that mindfulness enhances attentional control and cognitive flexibility. moreover, the interaction between dispositional mindfulness and gratitude significantly predicted initial orienting toward sad stimuli, suggesting a moderation effect. johnson–neyman analyses suggested that the time taken to first fixate on sadness stimuli significantly increased as one’s level of mindfulness increased, but only f or individuals with high levels of gratitude. in light of these results, we propose the hypothesis that highly grateful individuals may avoid sad stimuli as a self-preservation strategy and that this tendency becomes more efficient as attentional control improves with mindfulness. social psychological bulletin

bridging the gap in physical activity promotion for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes: a com-b study of primary care healthcare professionals abstract aims to identify determinants of physical activity (pa) promotion among healthcare professionals (hcps) caring for patients with prediabetes (pd) and and type 2 diabetes mellitus (t2dm), using the capability, opportunity, motivation–behavior (com-b) model. methods a cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 84 hcps involved in diabetes care. the questionnaire assessed pa-promotion practices, knowledge of pa recommendations, personal pa levels, and com-b model constructs. descriptive, univariate, and multivariate analyses were performed. results of the 84 participants, 56% reported promoting pa most of the time, while only 29.7% correctly identified pa recommendations. mean com-b scores on a six-point likert scale (1–6) were 4.00 for capability, 4.66 for motivation, and 3.24 for opportunity. hcps who frequently promoted pa had significantly higher scores across all com-b domains compared to non-promoters ( p < 0.05). in multivariate analysis, motivation emerged as the strongest predictor of pa promotion behavior (f = 19.7), while perceived opportunity remained comparatively low. conclusions pa-promotion in primary care for patients with pd and t2dm remains suboptimal despite relatively high perceived capability and motivation among hcps. limited opportunity- reflecting time constraints, organizational barriers, and lack of structured support may hinder implementation. interventions targeting both motivation and system-level opportunities may enhance pa promotion and improve diabetes management in primary care settings. international journal of behavioral medicine
