longitudinal trajectories of housing quality and their associations with elderly depression: a prospective cohort study based on the china longitudinal aging social survey, 2018-2023. prior studies have demonstrated the crucial role of housing quality in the mental health of older adults. however, there remains insufficient evidence regarding how longitudinal trajectories of housing quality relate to elderly depression. based on the china longitudinal aging social survey conducted from 2018 to 2023, this study used the group-based trajectory model to identify distinct longitudinal trajectories of housing quality (measured using nine housing characteristics) in chinese older adults and subsequently examined their associations with depressive symptoms, as well as potential mediations and urban-rural differences. three group-based trajectories, including "consistently high-level", "moderate-fluctuating growth", and "low-fluctuating growth", were yielded. compared with the "low-fluctuating growth" trajectory, older adults in the "consistently high-level" trajectory exhibited significantly lower depression levels (β = -0.484,< 0.001), whereas those in the "moderate-fluctuating growth" trajectory exhibited no significant changes. this association did not differ significantly between urban and rural areas. mechanism analysis indicated that, in rural areas, better physical health, stronger social support networks, and higher levels of social adaptation served as important mediators that linked elevated housing quality with reduced depression. by contrast, in urban areas, social support networks and social adaptation did not demonstrate significant mediating effects, and better physical health may mask the association between housing quality and elderly depression. these findings suggest that we should avoid staged declines in housing quality among the elderly and pay attention to urban-rural differences in the mechanisms linking housing quality trajectories with elderly depression. behavioral sciences

negotiating mental health and professional identities: an interpretative phenomenological analysis of nursing students' categorisation, disclosure, and support-seeking. this study explores how students develop, negotiate and represent their mental health alongside their professional identities. the aim is to understand how nursing students construct and negotiate their mental health identities in academic and clinical environments.using interpretative phenomenological analysis (ipa), this qualitative research employed nine nursing students enrolled in the bachelor of science in nursing (bsn) programme at king khalid university in saudi arabia. semi-structured interviews were conducted in arabic, the participants' native language, and professionally translated to english for analysis. interviews were analyzed using a six-stage ipa protocol and an integrated coding framework operationalizing concept from social identity theory, symbolic interactionism, and identity negotiation theory.the data led to five themes: (1) navigating the stigma boundary: the 'tough nurse' imperative, strategic silence or selective disclosure as identity management. (2) developing the 'mental health' label: repertoires and levels of surveillance/monitoring. (3) the clinical-classroom divide: contexts affecting identity performance and role transitions. (4) help-seeking as identity betrayal: the cost to identity of seeking formal help and preference for informal support. (5) reconciling personal and professional identities: future self-prototype construction, divergent personal-professional developments, and post-trauma story-telling.nursing students' mental health identities are socially constructed and strategically negotiated across contexts. this multi-theoretical model advances understanding beyond deficit-oriented frameworks, showing that help-seeking is limited by identity barriers. behavioral sciences

the impact of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions: an empirical examination based on chinese urban panel data. depressive emotions have emerged as a critical public health concern, with their etiology closely linked to the natural environment, particularly air quality. grounded in environmental stress theory and social support theory, this study utilizes panel data from 277 prefecture-level cities in china spanning 2011-2023 to theoretically analyze and empirically examine the effects of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions and the underlying mechanisms. the findings reveal that: first, improvements in air quality significantly reduce public attention to depressive emotions, a conclusion that remains robust across multiple robustness tests. second, the unemployment rate serves as a partial mediator between air quality and public attention to depressive emotions, while healthcare workforce allocation and public fiscal expenditure effectively buffer the adverse psychological impacts of air quality deterioration. third, the influence of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions exhibits significant urban heterogeneity, being more pronounced in eastern and central regions, cities with net population outflows, and mature and declining resource-based cities. by examining environmental public goods and social support systems, this study provides novel empirical evidence for understanding the relationship between air quality and public mental health, offering valuable insights for promoting synergy between environmental policies and social security policies. frontiers in psychology

assessment of psychological problems in children with chronic physical health conditions using dsm-oriented aseba scales: a meta-analysis. background: chronic physical health conditions (cphcs) increase the risk of mental health problems. the present meta-analysis integrates research of studies that compared dsm-oriented scores from the achenbach system of empirically based assessment (aseba) in young people with cphcs and a control condition.
methods: a systematic search in electronic databases (psycinfo, medline, google scholar, and psyndex) identified 115 studies involving 12,958 children and adolescents with cphcs and 24,638 control group members which were included in a hierarchical meta-analysis.
results: elevated scores were found on all dsm-oriented scales, with the highest effect sizes observed for somatic problems ( = 0.66 standard deviation units, confidence interval [ci] 0.56 to 0.75) and affective problems ( = 0.61, ci 0.53 to 0.69). between 8.6% (attention deficit/hyperactivity problems) and 14.3% (affective problems) of the young people with cphcs scored in the clinical range. effect sizes were larger if parent ratings rather than adolescent or teacher ratings were used, in the case of direct neurological involvement and of shorter duration of the cphcs, in older samples, and when test norms rather than healthy comparison groups were used.
conclusion: we conclude that the aseba is a recommended screening tool for children with cphcs but more direct comparisons of results from the dsm-based scales and the empirically derived aseba scales are needed to inform the choice of the scales.
systematic review registration: https://osf.io/nfvdj. frontiers in psychology

psychosocial transformation and peacebuilding: analysis of the community impact of development and peace programs in colombia. introduction: the prolonged armed conflict and the impact of its consequences following the signing of the peace treaty generated profound psychosocial impacts on colombian communities. these impacts include the fragmentation of the social fabric, distrust, and limited citizen participation. in this context, the development and peace programs were designed as initiatives aimed at promoting territorial reconciliation and strengthening social capital.
objective: the objective of this study was to analyze, through the voices of community leaders, the impact of these programs on psychosocial transformation and peacebuilding.
methods: this study used a multimodal qualitative design grounded in a hermeneutic approach and supported by analytical procedures drawn from grounded theory. semi-structured interviews were conducted with 17 community leaders with extensive experience in the selected programs. the data were analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding with the support of qualitative analysis software.
results: the results demonstrate a transition from conditions of vulnerability, isolation, exclusion, and fear to scenarios of social cohesion, citizen empowerment, and strengthening of community mental health. furthermore, the authors observed that the programs facilitated processes of collective agency and increased critical political participation. another crucial finding was the impact on the redefinition of traumatic experiences through dialogue, free expression, and trust-building.
conclusion: the programs supported processes of identity reconfiguration, psychosocial resilience, and the recovery of collective voice in the participating communities. frontiers in psychology

low-intensity mind-body exercise for mental health in ageing societies: tai chi as a scalable intervention across depression, anxiety, insomnia, loneliness, and cognitive decline. population ageing is increasing the number of older adults who experience overlapping depressive symptoms, anxiety, insomnia, loneliness, and cognitive vulnerability, often alongside multimorbidity, pain, frailty, and functional limitation. this structured narrative review evaluates tai chi as a scalable, low-intensity mind-body exercise for these interconnected problems. we synthesised 171 publications identified through pubmed and citation chaining, including tai chi-specific clinical studies, broader mind-body evidence, guidelines, and implementation literature. evidence is most consistent for reducing depressive symptoms, improving sleep, and improving balance, with possible benefits for selected cognitive outcomes. evidence is weaker for diagnosed depressive or anxiety disorders, loneliness as a primary outcome, long-term cognitive trajectories, and dementia incidence. tai chi should therefore be positioned as an adjunct to established care, not as a replacement for pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (cbt-i), or multidomain dementia-risk reduction. proposed pathways include autonomic regulation, sleep stabilisation, behavioral activation, balance confidence, cognitive-motor integration, and group participation; however, most mechanism evidence is indirect or exploratory. translation requires clearly specified protocols, active comparators, blinded outcome assessments where feasible, long-term follow-up, systematic adverse-event reporting, cost-effectiveness analyses, and equity-focused implementation. tai chi is the most credible as an adaptable component of stepped or integrated care for older adults, provided that programmes are standardised, safely delivered, and evaluated against clinically significant outcomes. frontiers in psychology

associations of self-reported physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health among civil aviation flight students: a cross-sectional study. objective: to examine the associations of self-reported physical activity at different intensities, total sedentary time, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health indicators among civil aviation flight students.
methods: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted at a civil aviation university from january 5 to 30, 2026. a total of 776 students majoring in flight technology were included, of whom 774 (99.7%) were male. because only two participants were female, the primary inferential analyses were restricted to male participants. physical activity and sedentary behavior were assessed using modified self-report items. physical activity duration represented participants' self-reported activity time on a typical activity day rather than average daily or weekly physical activity time; sleep exposure was assessed using categorical self-reported sleep duration. depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic internet use were assessed using validated scales. generalized estimating equation models were used to examine cross-sectional associations between the behavioral indicators and outcomes, with false discovery rate (fdr) correction.
results: in the fully adjusted male sample, after fdr correction, longer self-reported vigorous-intensity physical activity duration on a typical activity day was associated with lower anxiety scores; self-reported sleep duration <7 h was associated with higher depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic internet use scores; and longer self-reported total sedentary time was associated with higher problematic internet use scores. no statistically significant linear associations were observed between moderate- or light-intensity physical activity and any outcome after fdr correction. the observed associations were generally small: the association between vigorous-intensity physical activity and anxiety was approximately 0.10 outcome standard deviations, the associations between sleep duration <7 h and the corresponding outcomes were approximately 0.24-0.27 standard deviations, and the association between total sedentary time and problematic internet use was approximately 0.04 standard deviations. the directions of the main associations were generally consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses, although the strength of statistical evidence for some associations varied by outcome definition, sample restriction, and data-processing approach.
conclusion: among male civil aviation flight students, self-reported physical activity, total sedentary time, and sleep duration were cross-sectionally associated with selected mental and behavioral health indicators. given the cross-sectional design, these findings cannot establish causality, an optimal physical activity dose, a sleep intervention threshold, or time-substitution effects between behaviors. the findings suggest that behavioral indicators and mental and behavioral health status may be considered jointly in this population, but the observed associations require confirmation in longitudinal studies using objective, device-based behavioral measures. frontiers in psychology

mathematics anxiety is associated with attentional and memory‐related neural activity during numerical cognition abstract mathematics achievement can be influenced by negative emotions and expectations related to numerical tasks. individuals with high mathematics anxiety often show poorer numerical performance. this study investigated the neural mechanisms underlying different levels of numerical processing associated with mathematics anxiety using number line estimation and arithmetic verification tasks during fmri. participants were classified into high ( n = 22, age = 23.09 ± 2.22) and low ( n = 24, age = 22.67 ± 3.29) mathematics anxiety groups based on detailed screening prior to scanning. trait and test anxiety were also assessed to capture broader anxiety‐related characteristics. before the fmri session, participants completed assessments of calculation performance and digit span, and a mock mri session was used to reduce scanner‐related stress. participants completed task and control conditions for each numerical task during fmri. neuroimaging data were analyzed using 2 × 2 whole‐brain voxel‐wise anova. group differences in task‐related brain activation were further examined both before and after statistically controlling for trait and test anxiety. results showed that low mathematics anxiety was associated with greater frontal eye field activity during number‐space mapping and stronger supramarginal gyrus activity during arithmetic computation compared with high mathematics anxiety. controlling for trait and test anxiety helped clarify which neural effects remained associated with mathematics anxiety after accounting for variance shared with broader anxiety‐related factors. overall, attentional and memory‐related effects remained associated with mathematics anxiety after this adjustment, whereas additional effects involving motor processes and cognitive control were attenuated, suggesting that these effects may partly reflect variance shared with broader anxiety‐related constructs. psychophysiology

a dynamic state‐based framework for quantifying triadic autonomic synchrony during group decision‐making abstract in triadic social interaction, autonomic coordination is dynamic and may be poorly captured by session‐level synchrony estimates. we propose a state‐based framework to quantify time‐varying interpersonal synchrony during a laboratory group decision‐making task (desert survival task) using concurrently recorded electrodermal activity (eda) and ecg‐derived heart rate variability (hrv). twelve triads (36 participants) with complete physiological recordings were analyzed. signals were segmented into overlapping 60 s windows (1 s step). for each participant, window‐level features were extracted (eda: 4 features; hrv: 74 features), standardized within individuals, and converted to dyadic divergence vectors (absolute differences) for the three dyads in each triad. divergence vectors (combined eda plus hrv) were reduced with pca (95% variance retained) and clustered using a single global k ‐means model trained on pooled windows to yield five discrete synchrony states shared across triads. states were ordered along the first principal component (pc1) of the divergence space, with its orientation chosen so that state 0 corresponded to the highest‐synchrony state (hss). triad‐level state metrics quantified both prevalence and temporal stability: fractional occupancy rate (for), mean dwell time (mdt), and conditional long‐run fraction (clrf; ≥ 10 s runs). empirical triads showed a graded continuum of synchrony across states and a strong bias toward the hss. surrogate validation using a leave‐one‐fixed iterative amplitude adjusted fourier transform (iaaft) null applied at the signal level demonstrated that hss occupancy and stability exceeded chance alignment (for; p < 0.001; mdt and clrf; p < 0.001). convergent validity of the proposed state representation was further supported by continuous signal‐based benchmarks: compared with state 4, state 0 showed lower dynamic time warping distances and higher lag‐optimized physiological linkage (max r 2 ) for both eda and hrv (all p < 0.001). in contrast, group‐mean anxiety measures (spin, stai) were not reliably associated with hss prevalence or stability in this sample. these findings suggest that discrete synchrony states capture interpretable, non‐random coordination regimes in triads and provide a complementary framework for characterizing the temporal organization of autonomic synchrony beyond conventional continuous synchrony measures. psychophysiology

differential associations of executive-function components with initial status and change in chinese character reading during preschool. executive functions may contribute differently to early literacy, but it remains unclear whether their component-specific associations differ with respect to children's existing reading knowledge and subsequent growth. this question is particularly relevant in character-based writing systems, where learning to read requires children to establish and retrieve associations between visually complex written forms and their pronunciations. this one-year longitudinal study followed 131 kindergarten children across three timepoints and examined whether baseline working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive-flexibility task performance was associated with initial status and subsequent change in chinese character reading. a latent growth model was estimated with age, gender, nonverbal intelligence, and socioeconomic status as covariates. verbal working-memory performance was consistently and positively associated with initial reading status but not with subsequent change. no statistically significant unique associations were found for inhibitory-control performance. cognitive-flexibility performance was not consistently associated with initial status but was negatively associated with subsequent reading change; exploratory analyses suggested that this association was stronger among younger kindergarten children. overall, the findings indicate that different executive-function components may relate differently to existing reading knowledge and subsequent reading growth during the preschool period. they also highlight the importance of considering developmental stage, task characteristics, and measurement constraints when examining executive function and reading relations across writing systems. journal of intelligence

life satisfaction, hopelessness, and attitudes toward irregular migration among young adults: the moderating role of risk-taking. migration is an inevitable aspect of human existence, but youth attitudes toward irregular migration have recently become a growing concern among policymakers, researchers, and government officials in developing countries like nigeria, where challenging living conditions and lack of opportunities to achieve an individual's potential often influence migration-related attitudes. while previous studies have largely focused on economic and structural factors, limited research attention has been given to the psychological determinants of irregular migration attitudes. hence, this study examined life satisfaction and hopelessness as predictors of attitudes toward irregular migration among nigerian young adults, with risk-taking propensity as a moderator. a cross-sectional survey was conducted among 564 undergraduates from federal, state, and private universities in nigeria, and four standardized psychological instruments, which include the satisfaction with life scale, attitudes toward unauthorized migration scale, general risk-taking propensity scale (grips), and hopelessness scale, were used for data collection. the data collected were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (pls-sem, version 3.0). the results showed that life satisfaction had a significant negative influence on irregular migration attitudes and also indicated that hopelessness had a significant positive influence on attitudes toward irregular migration. again, risk-taking propensity had a positive influence on migration attitudes and also served as a positive moderator in the relationship between hopelessness and irregular migration attitudes among young adults. therefore, these findings indicate that hopelessness alone may not be sufficient to explain why some nigerian young adults develop favourable attitudes toward irregular migration. rather, the influence of hopelessness appears to depend on the individual's propensity to engage in or tolerate risk. in conclusion, findings of this study suggest that practical interventions aimed at addressing irregular migration among young nigerians should extend beyond economic and structural measures to incorporate psychological and behavioural components, particularly programmes that enhance life satisfaction, reduce hopelessness, and promote safer decision-making among risk-prone young adults. behavioral sciences

positive error-handling in tgfu-based basketball instruction: effects on tactical decision-making and the role of perceived classroom psychological safety. background: basketball learning involves rapid decisions and visible mistakes that may carry interpersonal risk. this study examined whether positive error-handling within teaching games for understanding (tgfu) improved tactical decision-making and whether improvements were associated with changes in perceived classroom psychological safety.
methods: sixty students (30 male and 30 female) were individually randomized within gender strata before formation of two instructional classes, with one class per condition (= 30 each). the same teacher delivered tgfu with positive error-handling (peh) or neutral error-handling (neh) over eight weeks. tactical decision-making was assessed through standardized 3-on-3 games at pretest (t0), posttest (t1), and three-week retention (t2); psychological safety was assessed at t0 and t1. passing, dribbling/driving, and shooting decisions were coded using the focused balpai rubric.
results: exploratory student-level analyses showed a condition × time interaction for decision-making,(1.583, 91.821) = 9.89,< 0.001, ηp= 0.146. peh increased from m = 1.951 (sd = 0.202) at t0 to 2.304 (0.258) at t1 and 2.295 (0.279) at t2; neh increased from 1.902 (0.179) to 2.114 (0.251) and 2.087 (0.291). psychological safety also showed a condition × time interaction,(1, 58) = 11.07,= 0.002, ηp= 0.160. peh increased by 0.462 points, whereas the neh increase of 0.129 points was not statistically significant. an exploratory within-subject mediation analysis in peh yielded a model-implied indirect effect of ab = 0.160, 95% bootstrap ci [0.100, 0.221].
conclusion: the peh class showed larger observed gains within the common tgfu curriculum, and increases in psychological safety covaried with decision-making improvements. these concurrent changes suggest a possible explanatory role for psychological safety but do not establish temporal or causal mediation. with one instructional class per condition, classroom-specific influences could not be separated from the condition effect, and inferential statistics were not adjusted for within-class dependence. future studies should include multiple classes per condition, account for within-class dependence, and assess psychological safety before subsequent decision-making outcomes to examine the proposed explanatory process. frontiers in psychology

a study of the impact of ai-employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior. introduction: with the deep integration of digitalization and generative artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence has transformed from a mere technical tool into a core collaborative partner within modern workplaces and human‑resource management. as an interdependent human‑ai working mode characterized by complementary task division, joint task accomplishment, complementary decision‑making, and continuous iterative interaction between employees and ai agents, ai‑employee collaboration is conceptually distinct from simple ai adoption, instrumental ai use, and ai‑assisted technical systems. drawing on social cognitive theory, the present study aims to investigate how ai‑employee collaboration predicts employee innovation behavior, alongside the mediating role of self‑efficacy and the moderated‑mediation boundary condition of servant leadership.
methods: three‑wave time‑lagged questionnaire data were collected from 259 employees working in internet‑service, finance, and catering industries across beijing and jinan. hierarchical regression and bootstrap approaches were adopted to test the proposed moderated‑mediation model.
results: the results show that ai‑employee collaboration exerts a significant positive predictive effect on employee innovation behavior. self‑efficacy partially mediates the relationship between ai‑employee collaboration and employee innovation behavior. moreover, servant leadership positively moderates the link between ai‑employee collaboration and self‑efficacy and further strengthens the indirect predictive effect of ai‑employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior through self‑efficacy.
discussion: this research enriches existing literature by providing incremental empirical evidence for the internal cognitive mechanism and contextual boundary of ai‑driven employee innovation. theoretically, it unpacks the cognitive "black box" connecting ai‑employee collaboration and employee innovation and identifies servant leadership as a key situational contingency factor. practically, these findings deliver concrete, actionable managerial insights for digitally transforming organizations to leverage ai tools and unlock employees' innovative potential. frontiers in psychology

legal evidence-authority dissociation in juror judgment: a multistudy reanalysis of memory contamination and ai advice. introduction: legal decision makers may remember information without using it to update a legal judgment, and may respond differently to the same recommendation depending on its attributed source. lead separates these processes into memory-entry, judgment-incorporation, and authority-deference gates.
methods: we reanalyzed three public, de-identified datasets: one jury-deliberation misinformation study and two preregistered judge-versus-artificial-intelligence sentencing studies. we compared gate-specific estimates while retaining study-specific outcomes and raw units.
results: in study 1, pro-prosecution misinformation crossed the memory-entry gate more clearly than the judgment-incorporation gate. in studies 2 and 3, mitigating case facts produced larger judgment-incorporation effects than authority-source assignment. the authority-source effect was equivalent to zero within a prespecified small-effect bound in study 2 (source experiment 1), but remained inconclusive in study 3 (source experiment 2).
discussion: lead identifies which process changed and supports cross-gate magnitude comparisons without treating unlike outcomes as identical. this secondary analysis does not estimate behavior in real courts, but it provides a transparent framework for forensic and legal psychology. frontiers in psychology

teaching and psychological associations of adolescent piano composition skills: a study on constructivist practices and reflective guidance based on teacher reports. introduction: to understand the connection between open teaching environments and musical creative performance, this study focuses on adolescent piano teaching, examining the structural associations among constructivist practices, reflective guidance, and piano composition skills, and analyzing the parallel indirect associations linked via creative self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation for composition.
methods: a cross-sectional questionnaire design was adopted, based on the analysis of 723 self-reports from teachers with adolescent piano teaching experience and their evaluation data on students' states and skills. multivariate regression and bootstrap resampling methods were used for statistical path testing, comparing group distribution characteristics under different learning purposes, and testing the boundary conditions formed by the frequency of composition teaching.
results: (1) both constructivist practices and reflective guidance showed significant positive associations with the evaluated piano composition skills; (2) creative self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation for composition presented significant parallel indirect paths in the above associations; (3) the overall differences among groups with different learning purposes on all core constructs reached statistical significance, with the descriptive means of the grading test or competition group generally being lower than those of the hobby group; (4) no significant moderating phenomenon of composition teaching frequency on the association between constructivist practices and intrinsic motivation was found.
discussion: autonomous decision-making and process scrutiny are independently and positively associated with teacher-evaluated student composition skills, respectively. these teaching practice characteristics, together with students' capability beliefs and internal willingness to participate, constitute the relevant conditions for musical practice. however, as these internal psychological states are inferred by teachers for whole groups rather than evaluated at the individual level, interpretations regarding direct psychological mechanisms remain limited. in teaching applications, compared with simply increasing the frequency of activities, improving the design quality of open and reflective tasks may be of more practical significance. frontiers in psychology

from reducing cognitive load to sustaining participation: psychological mechanisms, evidence, and stage-matched pedagogy for university tennis beginners. university tennis beginners face simultaneous technical, perceptual, tactical, and psychological demands that may exceed their attentional resources, challenge perceived competence, and diminish engagement. this mini-review synthesizes evidence on cognitive load, self-efficacy, autonomous motivation, multidimensional engagement, ecological dynamics, and beginner tennis pedagogy to explain how instructional design can support both skill acquisition and sustained participation. evidence on equipment scaling and game-based learning indicates that low-compression balls, smaller courts, simplified rules, and cooperative tasks can increase the number of playable exchanges, enjoyment, and early confidence, although direct tests of cognitive load reduction are scarce and university-specific evidence remains limited. constraints-led practice can then connect stroke production with perception, positioning, decision-making, and tactical intention, whereas selective technical instruction is most useful when a diagnosable movement feature restricts accuracy, consistency, or transfer. on this basis, this review proposes an evidence-informed, stage-matched (readiness-informed) conceptual framework that organizes individually supported instructional functions into a diagnostic, skill-specific, overlapping, and reversible structure rather than an empirically validated sequence: stage 1 reduces entry barriers and builds credible mastery experiences; stage 2 develops adaptive exploration and transfer; and stage 3 refines limiting technical features while progressively restoring standard conditions. engagement is positioned as a proposed mediating process linking psychological mechanisms to learning and participation. the framework extends evaluation beyond immediate performance toward retention, transfer, confidence under challenge, and sustained participation as an important but currently undertested outcome. controlled and longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate the proposed mechanisms, pathways, and boundary conditions across diverse university settings. frontiers in psychology

psychometric validation of the chinese physical effort scale and profiles of physical-effort approach and avoidance among chinese university students. objective: individual differences in tendencies to approach or avoid physical effort may be relevant to exercise-related psychological and behavioral characteristics. this study examined the psychometric properties of the chinese physical effort scale (pes) and investigated individual differences in physical-effort approach and avoidance tendencies and their associations with exercise-related psychological and behavioral variables among chinese university students.
methods: participants were 1,273 students from six universities across eastern, central, and western china. exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, reliability and validity analyses, and multigroup confirmatory factor analysis were used to evaluate the factor structure, reliability, validity, and measurement invariance of the chinese pes. latent profile analysis identified configurations of physical effort approach and avoidance, and bch analyses compared profiles on emotion regulation, exercise motivation, and physical activity.
results: factor analyses supported a two-factor structure comprising physical effort approach and avoidance. the scale showed high internal consistency and test-retest reliability, with evidence supporting convergent and discriminant validity and metric and scalar invariance across gender and academic year. three profiles were identified: balanced (59.07%), avoidance-oriented (14.93%), and approach-oriented (26.00%). the approach-oriented profile showed higher cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, external regulation, introjected regulation, and autonomous regulation, and lower amotivation. it also showed higher total physical activity than the other profiles and higher weekly exercise frequency than the balanced profile.
conclusion: the chinese pes showed psychometric support among chinese university students. distinct configurations of physical effort approach and avoidance were associated with emotion regulation, exercise motivation, and physical activity. frontiers in psychology

big five personality traits and subjective perceptions of adulthood abstract adulthood is often inferred from age and milestones such as marriage, parenthood, and career. this study tested whether perceptions of adulthood – subjective adult status and perceived importance of markers of adulthood – are associated with personality traits in a uk sample ( n = 714, age 18–77 years, m ag e = 39.30). regression analyses indicated that subjective adult status, or feeling like an adult, was associated with lower neuroticism and higher conscientiousness. personality independently explained 27% of variance in subjective adult status. endorsement of the markers of adulthood scale (moa) subscales had mixed associations, as the role transitions, independence, and legality markers subscales were associated with higher neuroticism and lower openness, whereas endorsement of the relative maturity subscale was associated with higher openness and higher conscientiousness. higher extraversion showed associations with endorsement of all moa subscales. these results illustrate the presence of individual differences in perceptions of adulthood and suggest that personality may shape whether we see ourselves as adults, and how we define adulthood. findings have implications for research on adult development, and for practitioners supporting young people with the transition to adulthood. journal of adult development
forty years after poodle-face palinopsia: human-to-cat and cat-to-human facial feature transfer. cortex

recognising facial identity across age: a comparison of super‐recognisers, people with developmental prosopagnosia and typical perceivers abstract recognising and matching unfamiliar faces across highly variable photographs of the same face is a challenging task, but few studies have examined the ability to group identities together across photographs depicting different biological ages. this study examined the ability to sort the identity of ambient images that depict two target individuals between infancy and young adulthood. three participant groups were examined: super‐recognisers (srs), individuals with developmental prosopagnosia (dps) and controls. srs significantly outperformed both dps and controls, making fewer overall errors in clustering the identities. furthermore, 80% of srs achieved perfect accuracy, compared with 15% in each of the other two groups. dp performance was highly variable and overall did not differ from controls, with both performing near chance‐level. these findings highlight the heterogeneity of impairment in dps and the srs' exceptional tolerance for within‐person variability, even across significant age‐related changes, offering a potential indicator for use in sr screening. applied cognitive psychology

exploring early perceptual processing of faces displaying down syndrome features from a masked priming paradigm. background: understanding how facial characteristics associated with intellectual disability are processed during early stages of perception may provide new insights into disability-related social cognition. masked priming paradigms offer a useful approach for examining how contextual information influences face recognition before conscious deliberation.
methods: digitally generated facial stimuli displaying down syndrome characteristics were developed from standardized facial photographs and validated by 66 experts and 136 participants from the general population. the validated stimuli were subsequently used in a masked priming face recognition task completed by 22 psychology students, in which reaction times (rts) and recognition accuracy were recorded across three priming conditions.
results: priming condition significantly influenced reaction times, with faster responses observed in the identity condition, in which prime and target shared both identity and facial phenotype, than under feature-based or different priming conditions. facial phenotype alone did not significantly affect reaction times or recognition accuracy. however, recognition accuracy varied according to the interaction between priming condition, facial phenotype, and stimulus type, indicating that behavioural performance depended on the experimental context rather than on facial phenotype alone.
conclusion: this exploratory study provides preliminary evidence that the recognition of faces displaying down syndrome characteristics involves early perceptual processes. the findings contribute to the emerging field of disability-related social cognition and support the use of experimental cognitive paradigms to better understand disability perception. frontiers in psychology

comprehension under threat: outgroup threat predicts perceived accent strength, ease of comprehension, and speaker evaluations. nonnative speakers, influenced by their first language, often produce accented speech that systematically deviates from that of native speakers. nonnative-accented speech is often judged more harshly than native-accented speech, in part due to increased comprehension difficulty. however, non-linguistic factors like social attitudes can bias perceptions of nonnative accent strength and comprehensibility, which in turn impacts social evaluations of speakers. grounded in intergroup threat theory, this study examines the relationship between perceived outgroup threat, speech perception, and speaker evaluations within the hong kong context. specifically, in a sample of native cantonese-speaking hong kong undergraduates ( = 691), we investigate how perceived threat from mainland chinese people influence perceived nonnative accent strength, comprehensibility, and subsequently, social evaluations of native putonghua speakers, cantonese-accented putonghua speakers, native cantonese speakers, and putonghua-accented cantonese speakers. speakers were rated in terms of competence and warmth, perceived nonnative accent strength, and comprehensibility. mediation analyses tested the mechanisms through which threat influences speaker evaluation. perceived outgroup threat was associated with lower competence ratings for putonghua-accented cantonese speakers. threat selectively biased speech perception for putonghua-accented cantonese speakers, predicting stronger perceived nonnative accent strength and lower comprehensibility, which mediated the relationship between outgroup threat and speaker evaluations. robustness checks testing the effects of outgroup threat separately by datasets and accent levels indicated perceived comprehensibility played a more consistent and pivotal role than accent strength in this model. results suggest listeners engage in social creativity strategies to yield positive ingroup distinctiveness, utilizing linguistic differentiation as a strategic mechanism to penalize speakers from threatening outgroups. frontiers in psychology

dynamic within‐person associations between problematic social media use and sleep quality among university students: the mediating role of nomophobia and the moderating role of trait rumination abstract problematic social media use (psmu) and poor sleep quality are prevalent among university students. although previous research has documented associations between psmu and sleep problems, less is known about the short‐term dynamic mechanisms underlying this relationship and the individual differences that may shape vulnerability. drawing on intensive longitudinal data and dynamic structural equation modeling, this study examined a moderated mediation model in which nomophobia (i.e. anxiety or distress arising from being unable to access or use one's mobile phone) mediated the association between psmu and poor sleep quality, with trait rumination examined as a moderator of this indirect association. a 21‐day daily diary study was conducted with 228 chinese university students. at the between‐person level, higher psmu was associated with greater nomophobia and poorer sleep quality. at the within‐person level, increases in psmu were prospectively associated with greater nomophobia, which subsequently predicted poorer sleep quality, supporting an indirect association through nomophobia. this indirect association was more pronounced among students with higher levels of trait rumination. by capturing dynamic day‐to‐day processes, these findings extend current understanding of how psmu may contribute to poorer sleep during emerging adulthood and highlight nomophobia and rumination as potential targets for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital habits and sleep. applied psychology-health and well being
artificial intelligence and systemic therapy: relational possibilities, ethical tensions, and an emerging systemic agenda international journal of systemic therapy
not so tense, but becoming boring! a study on human-machine interaction and metro drivers’ safety performance human performance
predicting daily report card treatment response in early childhood adhd: the relative importance of reward vs. punishment sensitivity journal of clinical child and adolescent psychology
executive functioning in preschoolers with adhd: the roles of disruptive behavior disorders and callous-unemotional behaviors journal of clinical child and adolescent psychology

demand-sensitive time allocation in digital reading: evidence from 25 education systems digital assessments record item-visit durations and revisiting. these traces can reveal responses to task difficulty, but achievement associations do not establish stable person-level measures. we linked digitalpirls 2021 process, response, and achievement data across 25 education systems, obtaining 121,908 students with usable process records and 116,206 complete cases for the primary achievement models. item difficulty was estimated from other students in five groups, excluding each target student’s own responses. we measured how each student’s first-visit time and revisiting changed with difficulty. more difficult items elicited longer first visits in all 25 systems, whereas the average difficulty effect on revisiting was weak. a one-standard-deviation increase in time adaptation was associated with 19.92 overall-reading points, compared with 3.19 points for revisit adaptation. effect magnitudes varied substantially across systems. repeated analyses of separate item halves showed limited stability for time adaptation (0.317) and moderate stability for revisit adaptation (0.529), after correction for test length. time adaptation estimated from four fifths of the items remained associated with performance on the remaining fifth in all 25 systems. these findings support time adaptation as a task-responsive behavioral indicator within digitalpirls. they do not establish a highly reliable trait score or identify a single cognitive mechanism. journal of intelligence

emerging technology-supported intercultural learning for cognitive, attitudinal, and behavioral outcomes: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis emerging technologies are increasingly used to support intercultural learning, yet evidence on the distinct effects of artificial intelligence (ai), augmented reality (ar), and virtual reality (vr) remains limited. this systematic review and three-level meta-analysis synthesized 17 studies published from 2020 to july 2026 (77 effect sizes) to examine cognitive, attitudinal, and behavioral outcomes. the overall effect was large and significant (hedges’ g = 0.965, 95% ci [0.580, 1.350], p < .001), although heterogeneity was substantial. ai-supported interventions also showed a significant positive pooled effect (g = 1.150, 95% ci [0.744, 1.555], p < .001). ar showed a significantly larger estimated effect than vr (β = −1.481 for vr relative to ar, p = .017), but this difference was not robust to excluding one ar study. academic level (f (1, 75) = 17.27, p < .001) and sample size (f (2, 74) = 3.873, p = .026) were significant moderators, with larger effects in k–12 and larger-sample studies. however, these exploratory comparisons involved uneven technology distributions and only two k–12 studies. outcome domain did not significantly moderate effects. sensitivity analyses supported the stability of the overall pooled effect. the findings indicate that emerging technologies can improve intercultural learning, while better-balanced comparative studies are needed to identify which technological approaches are most effective. journal of intelligence

validity evidence for the clinic screening tool for hiv (cst-hiv) addressing factors that undermine health-related quality of life in people living with hiv. background: this study evaluated the psychometric properties and clinical validity of the clinic screening tool for hiv (cst-hiv) to determine whether the cst-hiv demonstrates a reliable multidimensional structure and clinically meaningful associations with established patient-reported outcome measures (prom) and hiv clinical markers.
methods: a cross-sectional study was conducted within the spanish coris multicentre cohort, including 286 adults with hiv. participants completed the cst-hiv and validated proms. clinical indicators (cd4 cell count and percentage, hiv-1 rna viral load, and non-aids events) were collected at current and retrospective time points. analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity, associations with clinical markers, and age-group comparisons.
results: confirmatory factor analysis showed good model fit, with satisfactory internal consistency across domains (ω = 0.86-0.89). cst-hiv shows convergent validity, including psychological distress with phq-4 ( = 0.79), anticipated stigma with hiv stigma ( = 0.65), sexuality with sexual satisfaction ( = -0.74), sleep and fatigue with insomnia severity ( = 0.79), and material deprivation with social exclusion ( = 0.67) (all < 0.001). anticipated stigma (ρ = -0.16, = 0.014) and material deprivation (ρ = -0.18, = 0.005) were associated with lower cd4 counts, while material deprivation was associated with higher viral load (ρ = 0.13, = 0.046). sexual satisfaction was lower among participants aged ≥50 years ( = -0.47, < 0.001).
conclusion: the cst-hiv demonstrates strong psychometric performance, supporting its use as a valid, brief, multidimensional screening tool to inform person-centered hiv care and clinical intervention. frontiers in psychology

psychometric properties of the self-reflection and insight scale (revised) in german-speaking clinical psychology trainees. introduction: self-reflection is a core competency for clinical psychologists and mental health professionals. given its essential role in clinical practice and personal development, it is important to assess self-reflective capacity reliably and efficiently. this study aimed to translate and examine the psychometric properties of the self-reflection and insight scale-revised (sris-r) for use in german-speaking contexts.
methods: the sris-r was translated using a back-translation procedure. a total of 257 participants completed the questionnaires via an online survey.
results: both the original 14-item factor structure and revised german model solutions were tested. confirmatory factor analyses indicated that the original english factor structure could not be satisfactorily replicated in the german sample. therefore, exploratory factor analyses using polychoric correlations were conducted and suggested structural differences in the german version. based on these findings, a parsimonious revised 13-item two-factor scoring solution and a methodologically refined two-factor model including a cross-loading and a residual correlation were examined. the modified 13-item version showed improved internal consistency (α = 0.86 for self-reflection and α = 0.84 for insight). the parsimonious revised 13-item scoring solution retained the conceptual distinction between self-reflection and insight while being feasible for practical questionnaire scoring. convergent and discriminant validity evidence supported theoretical associations of self-reflection with related constructs, particularly self-insight and reflection, whereas insight showed negative associations with rumination and private self-consciousness. additional esem analyses supported a two-factor representation while indicating relevant item-level cross-loadings. the 13-item structure was subsequently tested without modification in an independent sample ( = 161), showing comparable model fit and high factorial similarity across samples. multigroup analyses further supported scalar invariance across the two samples. together, these findings provide cross-sample support for the distinction between self-reflection and insight, while indicating remaining structural complexity at the item level. given the limited support for a general factor, interpretation of the two subscale scores rather than a total score is recommended.
discussion: however, further research is needed to replicate the revised structure in broader and more diverse german-speaking samples. a culturally adapted and efficient measurement, like the one presented here, is essential for fostering and assessing self-reflective skills in clinical professionals. frontiers in psychology

an empirical investigation of the pathways model of problem gambling and the upps-p abstract while impulsivity is recognised as a central aetiological factor of problem gambling within the pathways model, limited research has examined the different dimensions of this trait and the three gambling sub-types contained within this model. thus, the current study aimed to explore the relationship between impulsivity and the three problem gambling sub-types within the pathways model. a total of 368 moderate and high-risk problem gamblers (pgsi score ≥ 5) aged between 18 and 73 ( m age = 36.95, sd age = 10.73) were recruited via the general community and prolific. participants completed an online survey containing the gambling pathways questionnaire (gpq), the short-marlowe-crowne social desirability scale (s-mcsds), the problem gambling severity index (pgsi), and the short-upps-p impulsive behavioural scale (s-upps-p). anova results showed anti-social impulsivist to report higher mean levels of positive/negative urgency than emotionally vulnerable and behaviourally conditioned gamblers. a multinomial logistic regression revealed that negative urgency more than tripled the odds of membership to the emotionally vulnerable gambling sub-type relative to the behaviourally conditioned sub-type. positive/negative urgency and sensation-seeking were also associated with significantly higher odds of membership in the anti-social impulsivist gambling sub-type compared to the behaviourally conditioned sub-type. findings reinforce the idea that problem gamblers belong to a heterogeneous population, with positive urgency and sensation-seeking potentially serving as key factors distinguishing anti-social impulsivist gamblers from behaviourally conditioned and emotionally vulnerable gamblers. discover psychology

deep learning of brain–behavior dimensions identifies transdiagnostic biotypes in youth with adhd and anxiety disorders nature mental health, published online: 16 october 2026; doi:10.1038/s44220-026-00740-3 attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and anxiety disorders often co-occur in youth, but their heterogeneity complicates treatment. here the authors use a deep learning framework to analyze functional connectivity and behavioral data, identifying brain–behavior dimensions and biotypes that clarify symptom profiles and support early risk stratification. nature mental health

association between anxiety, self-control, aggression, and internet gaming disorder among children and adolescents with elevated depressive symptoms background/objectives: internet gaming disorder (igd) has been officially classified as a gaming disorder in the icd-11, and clinical interest in it has been growing rapidly. using data from a large-scale, school-based cohort, the aim of this study was to compare the psychological characteristics of a group with elevated depressive symptoms (dsg) and a control group, and to identify the variables most strongly associated with igd within the dsg. methods: we analyzed 2093 participants (1113 in the dsg and 980 in the control group) in a school-based cohort of internet, game, and smartphone users (icure), established by the national center for mental health (ncmh). the measures included the children’s depression inventory (cdi), the trait anxiety inventory for children (taic), the self-esteem scale (ses), the self-control scale, the korean version of the aggression questionnaire (k-aq), the school bullying scale (sb), and the internet game use-elicited symptom screen (iguess). analyses of covariance (ancova) and multiple regression analyses controlling for sex were performed in r 4.4.5. results: compared with the control group, the dsg showed significantly higher anxiety, aggression, bullying, and gaming disorder symptoms, along with lower self-esteem and self-control (ancova). within the dsg, trait anxiety (β = 0.15), self-control (β = −0.275), and aggression (β = 0.111) emerged as significant correlates of igd. conclusions: these findings suggest that not only anxiety and self-control but also aggression are independently associated with gaming disorder. therefore, for the prevention and treatment of igd in emotionally vulnerable adolescents, self-regulation and anger-management programs, along with anxiety reduction, may be beneficial. adolescents
