sobrecarga del cuidador, memoria episódica y funcionamiento ejecutivo ecológico en cuidadores informales de personas mayores dependientes introducción: el envejecimiento poblacional en latinoamérica ha incrementado la demanda de cuidados informales. aunque la sobrecarga del cuidador se asocia con ansiedad, depresión y deterioro de la calidad de vida, sus correlatos cognitivos específicos continúan siendo heterogéneos. objetivo: examinar asociaciones entre sobrecarga del cuidador, salud mental, calidad de vida y funcionamiento cognitivo en cuidadores informales de personas mayores dependientes en chile. método: estudio observacional analítico de corte transversal en 59 cuidadores informales. se aplicaron la zbi, hads, whoqol-bref, mcs, m-ace iii, lassi-l y zmt. se realizaron comparación de grupos, análisis correlacionales y modelos de regresión lineal jerárquica ajustados por edad, escolaridad, ansiedad y depresión. resultados: los cuidadores con sobrecarga presentaron mayores niveles de ansiedad y depresión, junto con menor calidad de vida en los dominios físico, psicológico, social y ambiental. no se encontraron diferencias significativas en cognición global ni en la mayoría de las medidas ejecutivas evaluadas. la interferencia proactiva en recuerdo libre mantuvo una asociación negativa significativa con sobrecarga tras controlar variables sociodemográficas y emocionales. asimismo, los cuidadores con sobrecarga mostraron mayores tiempos de trazado en el zmt, sin diferencias significativas en planificación ni en número de errores. conclusiones: la sobrecarga del cuidador se asoció principalmente con una mayor vulnerabilidad emocional y detrimento de la calidad de vida. en el ámbito cognitivo, la interferencia proactiva en recuerdo libre y el tiempo de ejecución en una tarea ecológica de planificación fueron los indicadores más sensibles a la sobrecarga. estos hallazgos deben interpretarse como evidencia preliminar y requieren confirmación mediante investigaciones longitudinales. revista ces psicologia

engagement in ai-mediated informal digital learning of english: an adaptive intelligence perspective on motivational, psychological, and technological resources using adaptive intelligence as a theoretical lens, the study investigates how l2 motivational selves are associated with ai-idle engagement through psychological capital (psycap) and l2 grit and whether these indirect associations vary with ai literacy among 1025 chinese university efl learners. the proposed model was tested using structural equation modeling (sem). for the ideal l2 self, associations with engagement emerged both directly and indirectly through psycap and l2 grit, whereas the ought-to l2 self showed an indirect association through psycap and no direct association with engagement. higher ai literacy corresponded to stronger associations of both psycap and l2 grit with engagement. the two motivational self-guides were therefore associated with engagement through different psychological pathways, with ai literacy related to variation in the strength of these pathways. from an adaptive intelligence perspective, this conditional pattern indicates that the relevance of psycap and l2 grit to ai-idle engagement varies with learners’ ai literacy. these findings extend the application of adaptive intelligence to informal human–ai learning. journal of intelligence

bridging the human-ai trust gap: the mechanisms underlying perceived efficacy of ai-powered psychological counseling large language models. artificial intelligence (ai) is transforming the delivery of mental health services, yet public trust in ai-based psychological counseling remains a significant challenge. drawing on a "technology-context-trust" framework, this study recruited a total of 1000 consumers in china through credamo and conducted five between-subjects, scenario-based experiments to examine differences in perceived efficacy between llm-based psychological counseling and human experts and to investigate the mechanisms underlying these differences. perceived efficacy was the primary outcome of the study and, in experiment 1b, also served as a mediator linking counseling provider type to downstream market outcomes, including overall attitude, willingness to try, and willingness to pay. the results showed that (1) consumers generally perceived ai as less efficacious than human experts, a difference driven by the parallel mediating effects of perceived professional competence and perceived risk; (2) participants rated the ai-based service as more efficacious in the routine counseling vignette, whereas they rated the human-expert service as more efficacious in the major psychological-disorder intervention vignette; (3) disclosure of technological investment enhanced trust in ai's capabilities and mitigated negative evaluations; and (4) safety-standard disclosure reduced perceived risk, while higher perceived economic accessibility was associated with a smaller provider-related difference in perceived professional competence. these findings characterize subjective service evaluations among the recruited online consumers in china and do not establish comparative clinical effectiveness. they inform research on consumer trust while highlighting the need for further validation in more diverse samples and actual service settings. behavioral sciences

nature-based mindfulness program for parents and caregivers: a mixed-methods study. introduction: there is a growing interest in incorporating nature into mindfulness-based programs. this study is unique as it targets parents and family caregivers experiencing caregiving stress.
methods: a mixed-methods study was conducted to evaluate the outcome of a nature-based mindfulness intervention program. a comprehensive outcome measures targeting benefits of parents and caregivers, including mental health symptoms, wellbeing, physical distress, family functioning, and family conflicts, were assessed over time. the role of nature in overall outcome was investigated through the participants' perceived connectedness to nature and time spent in nature. the program consists of four sessions, totaling 8 h of contact time, held at a retreat center and social care units. a total of 95 participants were recruited, including 40 caregivers of older adults and 55 parents under stress. the study employed a time series design, with assessments conducted 1 month before the program, pre-program, post-program, and at a 3-month follow-up.
results: for caregivers, significant improvements were observed in multiple outcome measures, including anxiety, stress, physical distress, daily functioning, and wellbeing, following the program. further improvement in connectedness with nature was noted between the pre-test and the 3-month follow-up, with depression and family functioning approaching significance. for parents under stress, significant improvements were found only in wellbeing after the program. however, additional improvements in anxiety, stress, physical distress, and family conflicts (psychological aggression, corporal punishment, and physical maltreatment) were observed during the follow-up period, with depression and daily functioning approaching significance. hierarchical regression analysis indicated that connectedness to nature significantly associated with the program's effect on depression. qualitative analysis revealed that participants benefited from attention restoration, increased awareness, and insights gained from nature and mindfulness practices.
discussion: due to the limitations of the study, including the lack of control group and the use of self-reported measures, future study should verify the benefits of nature-based mindfulness programs particularly on the effects on parents and caregivers under stress and at risk of mental health conditions. frontiers in psychology

physical activity, mental health, and healthy development in adolescents: mechanisms and implications for intervention. adolescence combines heightened neurobehavioral plasticity with a steep rise in the incidence of depressive and anxiety disorders. habitual physical activity, by contrast, begins to fall much earlier, from about age seven, so adolescents enter the years of peak diagnostic risk already substantially less active than they were as children. that offset, rather than a coincidence of two curves, is the premise of this review. meta-analytic syntheses report moderate improvements in depressive (smd = -0.45, 95% ci -0.59 to -0.31) and anxiety symptoms (smd = -0.39, 95% ci -0.61 to -0.17) after exercise interventions in samples aged 5 to 18 years, yet several large pragmatic trials have detected no benefit. this mini review synthesizes recent evidence on these effects, the mechanisms proposed to explain them, and why the evidence base remains internally inconsistent. we argue that the contradiction is largely resolvable: efficacy estimates come from a heavily overlapping pool of trials and are inflated by unblinded designs, self-reported outcomes, and passive comparators, whereas universal school-based trials recruit predominantly asymptomatic students and deliver far less activity than prescribed. mechanisms span three nested levels, neurobiological, psychosocial and behavioral, but most mediation evidence is concurrent rather than temporally ordered. read through self-determination theory and acceptance-based accounts of distress tolerance, tolerable difficulty appears to be part of how participation confers benefit, with implications for injury, dropout and elite youth sport. priorities include adequately powered trials with active controls and process evaluation, compositional analysis of movement behaviors, and temporally ordered mechanistic designs. frontiers in psychology

from need satisfaction to academic achievement: pathways through wellbeing and engagement among university students across different italian institutions. background: university students face personal and academic demands that may challenge their adaptive functioning. although intrinsic goals, need satisfaction, wellbeing, and academic engagement have been distinctively linked to academic achievement, an integrated model specifying how these constructs are structurally related and associated with students' academic outcomes is lacking. the present study addresses this gap by testing models grounded in self-determination theory and previous evidence.
methods: participants were 2891 university students (= 23.22 years,= 5.25 years; 74.75% women) recruited across multiple italian universities. the online survey comprised different measures, including socio-demographic items, the basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration scale, the aspiration index, the sinapsi academic engagement scale, and the mental health continuum-short form. structural equation modeling was used to test two alternative model specifications. starting from a more general model, progressively more parsimonious models were tested by constraining selected direct effects. the final model was selected based on comparative fit, overall model fit, parsimony, and theoretical coherence.
results: the retained model specified wellbeing as antecedent to academic engagement. within this model, basic psychological need satisfaction showed indirect links to academic achievement through wellbeing and academic engagement, while intrinsic goals were related to achievement only through academic engagement. academic engagement emerged as the most proximal predictor of achievement, mediating the pathways from need satisfaction, intrinsic goals, and wellbeing.
conclusions: these findings provide an integrated account of how satisfaction of basic psychological needs, intrinsic motivations, wellbeing, and academic engagement relate to academic achievement in university students. our evidence supports a model in which psychological need satisfaction represents a relevant condition associated with wellbeing, intrinsic goals contribute more specifically to academic engagement, and academic engagement acts as the proximal mechanism linking these factors with academic achievement. beyond advancing theoretical understanding, our results may inform preventive programs and interventions nurturing students' wellbeing while also promoting their academic performance. frontiers in psychology

school-based mental health support for students with intellectual disability in the middle east and north africa: a 26-year scoping review. unlabelled: students with intellectual disability (id) in the middle east and north africa (mena) region face significant mental health challenges, yet the extent and nature of school-based support for them remain unclear. this scoping review mapped the english-language evidence on school-based mental health support for this population. six sources were searched for studies published between january 2000 and may 2026. the initial search identified 255 records, of which 210 were screened, and an update search identified one further study. six studies were included; two met all eligibility criteria and four met them in part. one study evaluated an intervention, cognitive-behavioral play therapy, and reported improved self-esteem; it was delivered in residential welfare centers rather than schools. one study reported a strong association between bullying victimization and depressive symptoms among students with mild id. four studies surveyed 1,037 practitioners in saudi arabia, qatar, and the united arab emirates, three of them in mixed disability populations. practitioners reported moderate and uneven preparedness in behavioral assessment, social skills training, trauma-informed practice, and mental health support, and self-efficacy and perceived school support were associated with teachers' attitudes toward supporting student mental health. no school-delivered intervention was identified, and no included study reported follow-up or a family component. overall, the english-language evidence identified by this review is small, heterogeneous, and geographically concentrated, and few students with id took part directly. the findings point to a need for culturally adapted school-based interventions, stronger mental health content in teacher preparation, and explicit inclusion of students with id in regional education and mental health frameworks.
systematic review registration: https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/hjqmr. frontiers in psychology

examining child stress response, parenting and relationship-related changes associated with a dyadic mindfulness and self-compassion program. introduction: interventions that dyadically equip families with self-compassion skills represent a promising approach for addressing mental health challenges, particularly during the key transitional period of middle childhood. this study examines changes and candidate processes associated with participation in the mindfulness and self-compassion for children and caregivers (msc-cc) course.
methods: twenty-three caregiver-child dyads (child,=8.78; caregiver,=41.2) participated in msc-cc, delivered remotely over six weekly group sessions. pre- and post-intervention assessments included self-report measures of parenting and relational closeness outcomes during a dyadic stressor task (behavior, reflective functioning[rf], and physiology). analyses investigated pre-post change in primary outcomes and linear mixed-effects models estimated time-related changes and baseline moderators of physiological change. significance tests identify pre-post increases in parenting and emotion-supportive beliefs.
results and discussion: physiologically, we detected significant decreases in child physiological arousal. exploratory moderation analyses suggest, among others, low levels of mindfulness and high rf at baseline predict the largest reductions in child stress physiology. while uncontrolled, the msc-cc participation was associated with increases in mindful parenting and the caregiver-child relationship and lower child physiological arousal during a dyadic challenge, most prominently in families with lower emotion-supportive beliefs at baseline. altogether, this highlights candidate processes and moderators of efficacy to be confirmed in a fully powered randomized controlled trial.
trial registration: clinicaltrials.gov,, nct05818397, registration and study start on 2023-10-16. frontiers in psychology

university physical education course experience and resilience-based psychological recovery capacity among students in chinese higher education: indirect associations through emotion regulation, exercise self-efficacy, and peer connectedness. university students face increasing psychological pressure, yet formal mental health services often remain limited in reach and depend on active help-seeking. this study examines university physical education (pe) as an educational context whose perceived qualities may be associated with psychological resources relevant to adaptation under stress. using cross-sectional survey data from 831 chinese college students, we examined whether perceived pe course experience was associated with resilience-based psychological recovery capacity and whether this association was indirectly linked through emotion regulation, exercise self-efficacy, and peer connectedness. the retained measurement specification represented pe course experience as a second-order construct comprising teacher support, mastery climate, embodied engagement, emotional release, and peer interaction. structural equation modeling indicated that pe course experience was positively associated with resilience-based psychological recovery capacity and with all three proposed indirect-linking variables. bootstrapping results supported significant indirect associations through emotion regulation, exercise self-efficacy, and peer connectedness, with exercise self-efficacy showing the largest estimated indirect association. the association remained significant after controlling for perceived stress and extracurricular exercise frequency. these findings link perceived pe course qualities with resilience-based adaptive capacity, conditional on the measured covariates. they do not isolate curriculum effects from physical-activity exposure. because the design is cross-sectional, the findings should be interpreted as theoretically grounded associations rather than causal effects. frontiers in psychology
early parenting stress, coparenting quality, and changes in the home learning environment: longitudinal links to children’s language and literacy parenting-science and practice

digital attention disruption and academic impact in adolescents: a data-driven network and machine learning analysis. academic impact associated with digital media use is a topic of considerable concern in the fields of adolescent mental health and education; however, the role of attention status in this context remains largely unknown. the present study aimed to systematically investigate the multidimensional association patterns between attention-related characteristics and academic impact among adolescents using data mining approaches. the data were derived from two publicly available cross-sectional survey datasets, and a final sample of 799 adolescents aged 19 years and below was included after age screening. the analytical framework integrated lasso regression, regularized partial correlation network analysis based on ebicglasso, xgboost predictive modeling with shap interpretation, and latent profile analysis. results showed that lasso regression identified stress level (coefficient = 0.384) and social media use duration (coefficient = 0.297) as the strongest predictors of academic impact. network analysis revealed a three-community structure, corresponding to the "digital distraction load," "psychological-academic exhaustion," and "academic engagement" dimensions, with academic impact located at the intersection of the first two communities. the xgboost model achieved an auc of 0.842, and shap dependence plots further revealed a nonlinear pattern with an inflection point at approximately 3.5 hours for daily social media use duration and a nonlinear effect of stress level. latent profile analysis identified three subgroups, among which the "high stress-exhaustion" group showed a probability of academic impact as high as 79.4%. these findings indicate that attention-related characteristics can effectively predict academic impact status in adolescents, with stress level, social media use duration, and number of notifications constituting the most influential set of predictors. the results provide data-driven theoretical evidence and practical implications for the early identification and stratified intervention of academic impact in adolescents. frontiers in psychology

what is gratitude research missing? bridging the gap between conceptualization, measurement, and intervention. does contemporary gratitude research investigate the full phenomenon described by current gratitude theories? gratitude has become a prominent construct in positive psychology, with research linking it to well-being, resilience, prosociality, and mental health. as theoretical perspectives have expanded, however, empirical approaches appear not to have broadened to the same extent. this purposive mini review examines gratitude research across conceptualization, measurement, intervention, physiology, and neuroscience. contemporary theories and measures increasingly represent gratitude as a multidimensional phenomenon encompassing interpersonal, existential, contemplative, embodied, and ecological dimensions. by contrast, dominant and influential intervention paradigms continue to emphasize reflection on benefits and benefactors, while much of the neuroscience literature reviewed here operationalizes gratitude through interpersonal, appraisal-based, and reciprocity-related scenarios. these differences suggest a conceptual-operational mismatch: relatively broad understandings of gratitude are often investigated through more narrowly focused empirical approaches. consequently, existing findings may illuminate interpersonal and benefit-focused gratitude more fully than broader forms of grateful experience. we conclude by proposing directions for developing ecologically valid, embodied, and relational methodologies capable of investigating a wider range of gratitude experiences. frontiers in psychology

emotional processing in a nap paradigm: the role of sleep stages in memory and reactivity abstract it is widely known that sleep has a role in modulating emotional processing. however, while sleep facilitates the consolidation of emotional memories, its influence on emotional reactivity remains unclear. most prior work has not fully addressed emotional reactivity, often relying solely on subjective or physiological measures, nor has it disentangled the contribution of different sleep stages. here, using a between‐subjects design, we asked participants to complete two picture‐based tasks assessing emotional memory and emotional reactivity before and after a manipulation condition (nap, n = 40; wake, n = 40), and again 2 days later. spontaneous variations in nap duration resulted in participants reaching rem sleep (rem group, n = 20) or not (no‐rem group, n = 20). emotional reactivity, assessed using an emotional picture task consisting of 28 images with different emotional contents (negative and neutral), was measured through subjective ratings and physiological responses (phasic cardiac response and skin conductance response). sleep preserved memory performance relative to wakefulness, but after 2 days, only negative images maintained a memory advantage in the nap group; however, no differences emerged as a function of rem sleep occurrence during the nap. for emotional reactivity, subjective arousal decreased after sleep in the rem group, whereas valence ratings declined only after 2 days. physiologically, heart rate habituation was greater in the no‐rem group. together, these findings indicate that sleep fosters emotional memory consolidation while modulating reactivity in ways that diverge across subjective and physiological domains, with a decrease in subjective arousal ratings and an increase in phasic cardiac response. these findings, which should be interpreted in the context of the observed differences in participants' sleep architecture, highlight the complex role of sleep in emotional processing and underscore the need for standardized experimental paradigms. psychophysiology

visual-semantic processing and reading comprehension in chinese deaf and hard-of-hearing students: roles of updating, semantic radical awareness, and daily sign language use. reading comprehension among deaf and hard-of-hearing (dhh) students may depend partly on how semantic information embedded in chinese characters is used. this cross-sectional study examined associations among working-memory updating, semantic and phonetic radical awareness, and reading comprehension, with exploratory comparisons across broad communication-mode groups. fifty-two dhh middle school students completed a 2-back task, radical-awareness measures, along with grade-specific reading tests. reading scores were standardized within grade; balanced 2-back accuracy served as the updating index. parallel and conditional indirect-association models were estimated with 5000 bootstrap resamples. updating was positively associated with both types of radical awareness but showed no significant total or direct association with reading comprehension. semantic radical awareness was positively associated with reading comprehension and showed a significant specific statistical indirect association between updating and reading comprehension. the specific indirect association via phonetic radical awareness was not significant, whereas the contrast between the two specific indirect associations was significant. exploratory moderation analyses indicated stronger associations among students who reported daily sign language use. overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence of associations between visual-semantic processing, updating, communication mode, and reading comprehension among dhh students, and may inform instruction aimed at supporting their reading comprehension. behavioral sciences

a social exchange perspective on employee performance in sierra leone's public sector: the roles of authentic leadership, participative decision-making, and trust. purpose: based on social exchange theory (set) and social information processing (sip), this research attempts to explore the effect that participative decision-making (pdm) has on the performance of employees working in sierra leone's public sector using affective trust, work engagement, affective commitment, and organizational citizenship behavior (ocb) as mediating variables in relation to authentic leadership as a moderating variable.
design/methodology/approach: the study used a quantitative and cross-sectional research design. data collection was conducted among public sector employees in sierra leone using a convenience sampling method. the study applied partial least squares structural equation modeling (pls-sem) to assess the measurement and structural model hypotheses.
findings: the empirical results reveal that participative decision-making (pdm) associate with employee performance through affective trust, which associate to work engagement and affective commitment, resulting in organizational citizenship behavior (ocb). the variable of work engagement proved itself as a better predictor of ocb than affective commitment. besides, authentic leadership moderated the relationship between affective trust and work engagement/affective commitment.
originality/value: the current research contributes to the set and sip frameworks by validating a step-by-step process leading to pdm, which ultimately influences employee performance. the study fills one of the significant gaps in the literature by providing evidence from an unexplored area of public sector employees in sierra leone. frontiers in psychology

dynamic adaptation of attentional control across bilingual interactional contexts. background/objectives: bilingual experience is thought to shape cognitive control via adaptive attentional reorganization, yet the neural mechanisms by which different interactional contexts dynamically modulate attentional control remain unclear. this study used eeg to examine how chinese monolingual, english monolingual, bilingual, and voluntary naming contexts influence attentional control in chinese-english bilinguals.
methods: thirty-five bilinguals completed picture-naming tasks in different contexts, followed by an antisaccade task with concurrent eeg. we analyzed reaction time, erps, frontal and parietal delta/theta power, and frontoparietal functional connectivity (wpli).
results: bilingual and voluntary naming contexts shortened antisaccade reaction times (all< 0.01). no significant main effect of context was found on n2 amplitudes (= 0.615). both contexts reduced parietal delta and theta power relative to the english monolingual context (all< 0.05). exploratory connectivity analysis initially suggested bilingual-context effects, but this finding did not survive homologous roi validation. these preliminary sensor-level findings await validation by source-localized eeg or fmri.
conclusions: these findings suggest that bilingual and voluntary naming contexts may facilitate attentional control through adaptive reorganization of the attentional system rather than through enhancing a specific inhibitory process. this pattern is consistent with the adaptationist perspective on bilingual cognition and provides preliminary neural evidence for the language mode theory. frontiers in psychology

the effects of tai chi on executive function and neurophysiological outcomes in college students: a systematic review and meta-analysis. background: college students face substantial cognitive demands, motivating scalable non-pharmacological approaches to support executive function. tai chi combines low-to-moderate physical activity, motor-sequence learning, postural control, breathing regulation, and sustained attention, but evidence in young adults remains uncertain.
objective: to evaluate the effects of tai chi on objective executive-function outcomes and to summarize associated neurophysiological findings in university students.
methods: following prisma 2020, pubmed/medline, web of science core collection, scopus, and cnki were searched from inception to 15 april 2026, with an english-language restriction. eligible studies evaluated structured tai chi against a concurrent comparator and reported objective executive-function and/or prespecified neurophysiological outcomes. two reviewers screened records, extracted data, and assessed randomized trials using rob 2. certainty was evaluated using grade. hedges' g was pooled using dersimonian-laird random-effects models; reml and hartung-knapp analyses assessed robustness. the present review was not prospectively registered; prospero crd420261480624 concerns a future update.
results: seven randomized trials were eligible (= 425), and four comparisons entered the primary selected-task meta-analysis (= 248). the pooled estimate favored tai chi (= 1.05, 95% ci 0.23-1.87;= 89.0%) but was dominated by one task-congruent working-memory trial and was not robust under hartung-knapp inference (95% ci - 0.56 to 2.67;= 0.130). inhibitory-control performance improved across three trials (= 193; g = 0.57, 95% ci 0.28-0.85;= 0%), although certainty was low. working memory effects were nonsignificant for the primary selected metric (= 1.00, 95% ci - 0.37 to 2.37) and correct responses/accuracy (= 0.79, 95% ci - 0.19 to 1.77). cognitive flexibility was represented by one trial (= 0.29, 95% ci - 0.20 to 0.77). neurophysiological findings were exploratory. no study reported objective academic outcomes.
conclusion: tai chi may improve short-term inhibitory-control performance in college students, but evidence for broader executive-function benefits is insufficient. larger preregistered trials using active comparators, task-neutral measures, longer follow-up, and objective academic outcomes are required. frontiers in psychology

the mid‐term impact of a hedonic aroma on psychophysiological indicators in women with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy: a randomized controlled trial abstract the study investigated the impact of essential oils on women undergoing chemotherapy (ct) treatment for breast cancer (bc), comparing an experimental group (eg) exposed to hedonic aromas with a control group (cg) receiving standard ct. a total of 112 women were randomly assigned to either a control group receiving standard chemotherapy treatment or an experimental group receiving an additional essential oil intervention during two consecutive chemotherapy cycles. the primary outcomes were quality of life (qol), anxiety, and depression whereas the secondary outcomes were emotional distress, need for help, treatment beliefs, treatment side effects, illness perceptions, self‐efficacy for coping, working memory, and cortisol. mixed‐effects models were used to analyse the differences between the two groups over time, more precisely, from the first ct session involving essential oils (t1) to two sessions later (t3), with a 6‐week interval. although no significant between‐group differences were found for the primary outcomes, variations emerged in the patterns of association between these measures and several secondary outcomes over time. specifically, in the eg, the association between baseline and subsequent anxiety remained stable, whereas this link weakened in the control group (cg). at t3, the adverse impact of higher anxiety on qol and chemotherapy necessity beliefs was weaker or absent in the eg compared to the cg. physiologically, higher pre‐session salivary cortisol at t3 was linked to better qol only in the eg, suggesting a normative acute stress response, whereas the cg showed attenuated reactivity. other secondary outcomes, such as cognitive function and treatment side effects, did not differ significantly between groups. these findings suggest that essential oil inhalation may help stabilise anxiety levels associated with chemotherapy and contribute to qol. these findings have relevant clinical implications. stress and health

social cognition in forensic psychology abstract this paper examines principles of social cognition in forensic psychology, a field that sits at the intersection of psychological science and the justice system. social cognition—the study of how people perceive, interpret, and respond to others—rests on four pillars: impression formation, stereotypes and prejudice, attribution, and attitudes. much of forensic psychology, from competency evaluations to risk assessments to testimony about eyewitness identification accuracy, implicitly involves these social‐cognitive processes. rather than a comprehensive review, this paper draws selectively on material chosen to highlight key ideas and to stimulate further reading and discourse. to that end, we present three illustrative concepts of social cognition relevant to forensic contexts: (1) disruptions in social cognition can have forensic significance, (2) social perception in legal settings is dynamic and reciprocal, and (3) evaluating expert witness testimony is especially difficult. within legal processes, judges, jurors, attorneys, parties to the case (e.g., defendants, plaintiffs), and witnesses engage in social‐cognitive dynamics that shape how justice unfolds. heuristics—such as judging credibility based on likeability, fluency, or attractiveness—can distort accuracy of perceptions. accordingly, awareness of social‐cognitive influences may be particularly important in forensic settings, where judgments about individuals can have significant implications for legal outcomes. throughout the paper, we offer a comparative reflection of overlapping concepts from social cognition and forensic psychology, highlighting underexplored connections and future directions for research and teaching. comparative work like this has potential to generate scientific advancements, to the benefit of basic theoretical breakthroughs and enduring solutions for applied problems. social and personality psychology compass

criterion‐related validity of the couple flourishing measure in a spanish population: distinguishing outpatients from community participants abstract relational (or couple) well‐being has begun to be conceived from an integrative perspective that transcends mere satisfaction or stability in couples and may include dimensions such as emotional connection, joint growth, and shared purpose. this study evaluated the criterion‐related validity of the couple flourishing measure (cfm) in comparison with the dyadic adjustment scale (das) in a spanish sample of people in affective‐sexual relationships ( n = 118; mage = 40.3, sd = 8.77). differences between participants receiving affective‐sexual therapy services ( n = 67) and community participants ( n = 51) were analyzed, as well as their discriminative ability using roc curves. the results showed that the cfm had a greater ability to discriminate between the two groups (auc = 0.81, 95% ci [0.74, 0.89]) than the das (auc = 0.71, 95% ci [0.62, 0.81]). in turn, a preliminary cutoff score for cfm was identified (61.5), with moderate sensitivity (0.64) and high specificity (0.94). these findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the criterion‐related validity of the cfm for distinguishing outpatients receiving affective‐sexual therapy from community participants without previous therapeutic experience and suggest that the measure may offer complementary information beyond traditional indicators of relationship adjustment. implications, limitations, and directions for future research are discussed. family process

latent profiles of maternal parenting stress moderate the relationship between overparenting and young children’s social–emotional competence this study examined how maternal parenting stress and overparenting are associated with young children’s social–emotional competence using both variable-centered and person-centered approaches. a total of 445 mothers of young children completed measures of parenting stress, overparenting, and children’s social–emotional competence. variable-centered analyses showed that positive experience was associated with children’s social–emotional competence through overparenting. latent profile analysis identified three maternal parenting stress profiles based on different combinations of positive experience and strain, namely disengaged, engaged–high-strain, and engaged–low-strain. children of mothers in the engaged–low-strain profile showed the highest levels of social–emotional competence, whereas those in the disengaged profile showed the lowest levels. further analyses showed that the association between overparenting and children’s social–emotional competence differed across maternal stress profiles. this association was significantly stronger among mothers with high positive experience and low strain than among mothers experiencing high strain. these findings suggest that the association between overparenting and children’s development depends on mothers’ broader parenting stress profiles. they also highlight the importance of considering the heterogeneous and two-sided nature of maternal parenting stress when examining its implications for children’s social–emotional competence. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education
retrieval-induced forgetting and facilitation across the alzheimer’s disease continuum: behavioral and neuroanatomical evidence from a recognition-based paradigm. neuropsychology

identifying future geriatric nurses: psychometric evaluation of the german willingness to work with elderly people scale among nursing students. introduction: in german-speaking countries, where geriatric care faces a persistent nursing shortage, nursing students are expected to play a key role in addressing future workforce needs. currently, there is a lack of valid and reliable instruments to assess nursing students' willingness to work with older adults. this cross-sectional study aimed to validate the german version of the willingness to work with elderly people (weps-d) scale and examine factors associated with the willingness to work with older adults to support geriatric workforce development in nursing education.
methods: a convenience sample of 207 german-speaking nursing students completed the survey, including 52 students who participated in a 4-week retest. structural validity was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis (efa), while convergent validity was assessed through correlations with the kogan attitudes toward older people scale (kaop), age stereotypes (as), and future self-views (fs). internal consistency and test-retest reliability were examined. in addition, multiple linear regression was used to identify factors independently associated with willingness to work with older adults.
results: efa identified a four-factor structure (intention, perceived behavioral control, attitude, and subjective norm) with 20 items, explaining 49.01% of the total variance. convergent validity was supported at the factor level, with factor 3 (attitude) showing a moderate correlation with the kaop (= 0.515,< 0.01), while the total weps-d score showed a lower correlation (= 0.385,< 0.01) that did not meet the pre-specified criterion. at the scale level, internal consistency (cronbach's α = 0.894, mcdonald's ω = 0.902) and test-retest reliability (icc = 0.882) were good, although factors 3 (attitude) and 4 (subjective norm) showed relatively low internal consistency. multiple linear regression showed that higher education and negative or neutral attitudes toward aging were significantly associated with lower weps-d scores compared with vocational training and positive attitudes, respectively.
conclusion: the weps-d is a valid and reliable tool for assessing nursing students' willingness to work with older adults. it can be used in schools to identify the potential workforce in geriatric nursing and guide early educational interventions. frontiers in psychology

motor action observation evaluation questionnaire: development and initial validity evidence for the scores in people with and without chronic low back pain. introduction: chronic low back pain (clbp) is highly prevalent and associated with functional limitations. although action observation is increasingly used as a cognitive-motor rehabilitation strategy, no brief instrument exists to assess how individuals appraise and understand movements during observation.
methods: the questionnaire for the assessment of motor action observation (cenoam) was developed using a sequential mixed-methods design. phase 1 involved item generation based on literature review and qualitative analysis, followed by expert content validation using aiken's. phase 2 consisted of a cross-sectional study including 280 participants (140 with clbp and 140 asymptomatic). dimensionality and psychometric properties of the cenoam scores were examined using exploratory factor analysis, complementary dimensionality methods, internal consistency (,), floor and ceiling effects, concurrent associations, and known-groups comparisons, following cosmin recommendations.
results: the final seven-item instrument showed a parsimonious two-dimensional structure, comprising familiarity and competence-demand, supported by converging evidence across multiple methods. internal consistency was high for both total and subscale scores, and no floor or ceiling effects were observed. cenoam scores were positively associated with motor imagery ability, physical activity, and pain self-efficacy, and negatively associated with fear of movement. participants with clbp showed significantly lower scores than asymptomatic individuals across all dimensions, with large effect sizes.
conclusion: the cenoam provides a brief and interpretable measure of movement appraisal during action observation. its scores show initial evidence of validity and may support the individualization of action-observation-based rehabilitation in musculoskeletal conditions. frontiers in psychology

on the inclusive environment of hospital schools and the medico-social foundations of hospital pedagogy context and relevance. the article reviews the experience of building an inclusive educational environment for children in need of long-term treatment in medical organizations of the russian federation. from 2011 to the present, the number of children with medical needs undergoing long-term treatment in medical organizations has been rising and has reached 6 million long-term pediatric hospitalizations per year. establishing a nationwide educational system for the group of children under consideration is of decisive importance for their continuous development. objective. to present the development and implementation stages of the authors' nationwide hospital school model between 2011 and 2025, along with the challenges addressed and the subsequent results. hypothesis. the development and implementation of a hospital school model in the russian federation for children requiring long-term inpatient medical care will ensure the realization of their constitutional right to accessible, high-quality education, while maintaining continuity in their psychological and social development during long-term treatment. methods and materials. a structural analysis was conducted of the implementation in the russian federation, from 2011 to 2025, of the project to develop, establish, and implement a nationwide hospital school model across various institutional settings (the “uchimznaem” russian hospital schools project; key figures: 72 hospital schools, 72 medical organizations of various profiles, and 30000 children receiving education in these organizations annually). results. despite the complexities of interagency cooperation, structural differences between medical and educational organizations, varying profiles of long-term pediatric treatment, and challenges in training specialized pedagogical and other personnel, the hospital school model implemented in the russian educational system between 2011 and 2025 has created qualitatively new conditions for the continuous education and development of children and adolescents during long-term treatment. conclusions. highlighting the issues and challenges of educating children under long-term medical care forms a foundation for distinguishing hospital pedagogy as a distinct branch within general pedagogy. it also facilitates the study of the medico-social foundations of hospital pedagogy in the context of inclusive education, the synthesis of russian and international experience, and further interdisciplinary research on this topic. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education
beyond accuracy: how humans evaluate legally correct but socially controversial legal advice from machines. technology, mind, and behavior

inner speech and the architecture of social cognition: a commentary on silvanto (2026) this commentary builds on silvanto's (2026) argument that congenital aphantasia should be recognised as a form of cognitive diversity rather than a pathology, with rehabilitation targeting underlying causes of imagery loss rather than the restoration of mental imagery. silvanto further highlights the association between visual imagery loss and emotional dysregulation. while we support this move away from pathologising aphantasia, we highlight a critical gap in the literature: the underappreciated role of inner speech in social-emotional cognition. we argue that sensory imagery (and aphantasia) should be recognized as a multifaceted process, with dissociations observed across modalities. furthermore, we propose that inner speech, whether condensed or expanded (accompanied by auditory verbal imagery), serves as a computationally efficient, resource-light alternative to sensory imagery, supporting cognition without the need for detailed sensorimotor simulation. this perspective reframes aphantasia as cognitive diversity and highlights the need for greater empirical and theoretical focus on inner speech. cortex

beyond sum scores: a network analysis of dark triad traits and nonsuicidal self-injury in emerging adults. background: previous studies have investigated the relationships between dark triad traits and nonsuicidal self-injury (nssi) based on sum scores of corresponding scales. however, this practice has hampered the fine-grained understanding of how specific dark triad traits relate to nssi at the item level. this network analysis study aimed to examine these relationships in a joint framework and identify potential intervention targets.
methods: dark triad traits and nssi were measured using the dirty dozen (dd) and the behavior subscale of the adolescent nonsuicidal self-injury assessment questionnaire (ansaq) among 1,950 emerging adults. a regularized partial correlation network was constructed, and expected influence and bridge expected influence were calculated for each node.
results: in addition to connections within each community, several cross-community edges were observed. the strongest direct edge between the dark triad traits and nssi was found between n4 "i tend to expect special favors from others" (narcissism) and b1 "intentionally pinching myself" (nssi), but this edge was small in magnitude. p1 "i tend to lack remorse" (psychopathy) and n1 "i tend to want others to admire me" (narcissism) had the highest expected influence values, whereas p4 "i tend to be cynical" (psychopathy) and p1 "i tend to lack remorse" (psychopathy) had the highest bridge expected influence values.
conclusion: these findings suggest that the item-level connections between dark triad traits and nssi are generally weak, with the most prominent associations occurring within the dark triad traits dimensions themselves. p1 and n1 appear to occupy central positions in the dark triad traits network, while p4 and p1 mainly serve as bridges among the three dark traits traits rather than as direct links to nssi. the direct association between narcissistic entitlement and intentional pinching may warrant further investigation, but its clinical significance remains unclear. future research should examine whether these specific personality characteristics and self-injury behaviors can inform targeted prevention or intervention efforts among emerging adults with dark triad traits. frontiers in psychology

preworks : a precarious work scale for the cultural and creative industries the current study proposes and validates the precarious work scale (preworks), a modular, theory-based instrument intended to encapsulate the multidimensional and idiosyncratic nature of precarious work within the cultural and creative industries (ccis). preworks was constructed through a systematic multi-step process, yielding 11 items across four dimensions: job instability, economic precarity, limited collective bargaining power, and lack of rights and protection. the scale was evaluated with a sample of 469 workers in ccis, who were categorised into five professional categories. confirmatory factor analysis corroborated the multidimensional structure, while the mimic-dif analysis provided support for the scale's overall comparability across the five groups. latent mean differences revealed significant structural inequalities within ccis. furthermore, the findings provide substantiated evidence for the construct validity of the instrument. overall, preworks emerges as a psychometrically robust instrument that is capable of capturing precarious working conditions in ccis, whilst also highlighting the uneven distribution of precariousness. empirical studies of the arts

playing the self, paying the price: a dual‐path model of avatar identification and online game consumption abstract with the rapid expansion of the online gaming market, understanding the psychological mechanisms underlying player consumption behavior has become increasingly important. this study investigates how online game players' identification with virtual avatars is associated with perceived consumption value and, in turn, with gaming experience and in‐game spending. two substudies were conducted with a total of 669 participants. study 1 employed a questionnaire‐based survey to examine the relationships among core variables. study 2 targeted players of honor of kings , a widely popular online game, to further test the proposed mediation model. the findings indicate that avatar identification significantly predicts perceived enjoyment through two mediators, specifically visual authority value and character competence value, which in turn are associated with players' consumption behaviors. furthermore, the association between identification with a specific avatar and consumption intention provides additional support for the proposed mediation pathways. this research contributes to an “identification–value–experience” framework for understanding online game consumption, suggesting that avatars serve not only as extensions of the self but also as sources of perceived value relevant to enjoyable gaming experiences and consumer decision‐making. practical implications are discussed for game developers aiming to optimize user experience and inform monetization strategies. psych journal
