registered replication report: johns et al. (2005) 注册重复报告：johns 等（2005） “stereotype threat” refers to the fear of being judged based on negative stereotypes about the performance of a certain group one identifies with. numerous published studies have found that stereotype threat might lower mathematics-test performance among women. however, many studies have used suboptimal designs and analyses, the literature might be subject to publication bias, and the cross-cultural generalizability of the effect remains unknown. in this registered replication report, we describe the result of nine direct replications (total n = 1,709) of a representative stereotype-threat study by johns et al., who found that threatened women (but not men) underperform when they are confronted with a mathematics test that is presented to measure gender differences and that this effect can be alleviated by altering test instructions. a multilevel analysis showed no significant interaction effect between stereotype-threat condition and gender and an observed gender gap only on the mathematics test, in which women performed worse than men (hedges’s g = −0.26, se = 0.11, 95% confidence interval [ci] = [−0.47, −0.05]). the stereotype-threat effect among women was virtually null and not significant ( n = 1,275, g = 0.04, se = 0.08, 95% ci = [−0.11, 0.20]) and considerably smaller than the original study ( n = 45, d = −0.82, 95% ci = [−1.45, −0.18]). secondary analyses yielded a main effect of gender composition and a random effect of lab on mathematics-test performance, but neither variable affected the interaction between stereotype threat and gender. the current results fail to replicate the stereotype-threat effect by johns et al., hence casting doubt on the generalizability of the effect of stereotype threat on women’s mathematics performance. advances in methods and practices in psychological science

preparation for bias conversations among black/african american, latinx, and asian parent‐adolescent dyads: a qualitative content analysis of observational data abstract preparation for bias conversations may be critical in raising youth awareness of racial‐ethnic discrimination, fostering a strong racial‐ethnic identity, and teaching them how to cope or respond to racialized stressors. however, the literature relies almost exclusively on survey approaches, limiting understanding of how these conversations actually unfold in real time. the present study used qualitative content analysis of observational data to describe the strategies 151 black/african american, latinx, and asian parents ( m age = 41.63, sd = 6.16) and youth aged 11–14 years ( m age = 12.16, sd = 0.91) discussed to respond to four discrimination scenarios that varied in the location, the power asymmetry, and the nature of the interaction. black/african american parents were primarily u.s.‐born whereas latinx and asian parents were predominantly first‐generation immigrants. we aimed to center participants' words to understand how they respond to discrimination in context, whether parents and youth differed, and how this may vary across racial‐ethnic groups. we identified strategies that could be categorized into ignoring the perpetrator, confronting, support‐seeking, reporting, activism, and protective compliance. unique to our analysis was the ability to distinguish how strategies were embedded in the type of discrimination stressor, the context of race/ethnicity, and youth‐ versus parent‐suggested strategies. though there was a broad range of strategies that were suggested, the findings illustrate that the context of the discrimination matters and that parents and youth also value different approaches. journal of research on adolescence

homework responsibility and parent–adolescent communication: maternal and paternal associations with academic and psychological adjustment among chinese adolescents responsibility for homework and parent–adolescent communication may have different associations with adolescent adjustment. using two waves of the china education panel survey (2013–2015), we examined these parent-specific behaviors in outcome-specific analytic samples ranging from 7457 to 7604 adolescents. ordinary least squares models included the four parental measures jointly and adjusted for corresponding baseline outcomes, covariates, and class fixed effects. the principal predictors and outcomes were measured concurrently at follow-up. maternal communication was positively associated with cognitive ability and academic achievement, whereas maternal homework responsibility had negative associations in the additive main models. communication with either parent and paternal responsibility were associated with fewer depressive symptoms. direct coefficient comparisons distinguished maternal responsibility from maternal communication across all three outcomes after multiple-testing adjustment. these associations were small and do not establish causal effects. the study adds a joint, parent-specific comparison across academic and psychological outcomes, distinguishing reported homework responsibility from communication frequency rather than treating involvement as a single behavior. behavioral sciences

disparities in social determinants of health and health outcomes among autistic individuals without intellectual disability in middle-to-late adulthood autism is increasingly recognized across the lifespan, yet little is known about how structural social disadvantage contributes to long-term health risks among autistic adults in middle and later adulthood. participants were identified from the uk biobank study, comprising 576 autistic adults with no intellectual disability and an average of 15.2 years of education, and 5,760 controls matched on age, sex, residing area, race, and educational attainment. social determinants of health (sdh) were assessed using a composite score calculated from 12 indicators that characterized economic, health care, neighborhood, and social domains. mediation analysis was performed to estimate the extent to which sdh disparities mediated the elevated mortality and chronic disease risks among autistic adults. the study sample was 66.4% male and had a mean age of 51.6 years ( sd , 8.03). autistic adults had worse sdh levels across almost all dimensions. these disparities mediated 39% of the elevated mortality risk. in addition, autistic adults showed increased incidence of cardiovascular disease, dementia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, depression, and anxiety, with sdh disparities mediating 17% to 38% of these elevated risks. these findings indicate that multifaceted disadvantage plays a substantial role in the health inequities experienced by autistic adults, underscoring the need for cross-sector interventions and policy reforms. lay abstract autistic adults face persistent disadvantage in social conditions that shape health outcomes. these disadvantages may partially explain why autistic adults face higher rates of chronic illnesses and earlier death. from a large cohort in the united kingdom, we compared 576 autistic adults with 5,760 adults without autism across 12 indicators of social determinants of health (sdh), covering economic, health care, neighborhood, and social domains. autistic adults showed disadvantage across nearly all domains. these disparities mediated 39% of excess mortality and 17% to 38% of the increased risk for chronic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, dementia, type 2 diabetes, depression, and anxiety. economic deprivation and social isolation showed relatively larger mediating effects. this study provides evidence that structural inequities in sdh substantially contribute to the long-term health trajectories of autistic adults. addressing these inequities will require policies and interventions that move beyond individual-level supports to tackle systemic barriers in employment, health care access, housing, and community participation. autism

social media usage patterns and anxiety in chinese adolescents: age-specific risks from a cross-sectional perspective. the relationship between social media use and adolescent mental health is complex and multifaceted, with recent findings suggesting that the associations vary according to the nature of social media activities, but the most common social media usage patterns among chinese adolescents remain insufficiently explored. this study explored the associations of overall social media use and social media use for entertainment and information seeking with anxiety among chinese adolescents across three developmental stages. a total of 6125 adolescents (= 14.65) from urban and suburban schools across four regions of china were included in the analyses. participants completed surveys measuring the frequency, duration, and type of social media use, anxiety symptoms, and demographic characteristics. the results showed that, in the adjusted group analyses, entertainment-oriented social media engagement was significantly associated with higher anxiety, whereas information-seeking use showed no significant association with anxiety. furthermore, age was identified as a significant moderator of the association between entertainment-oriented social media use and anxiety, with this association being particularly pronounced during early adolescence (ages 12-14). these findings may inform the development and evaluation of age-specific intervention strategies focused on entertainment-oriented social media engagement, particularly during the critical developmental window of early adolescence. behavioral sciences

understanding how multiple strengths support the mental health of adolescents and young adults in a gender-diverse sample. adolescents and young adults are facing a mental health crisis, with disproportionate burden among youth with diverse gender and sexual identities. resilience science highlights the importance of modifiable strengths and protective factors as targets for prevention. the resilience portfolio model (rpm) conceptualizes resilience as a multidimensional system of strengths across regulatory, interpersonal, meaning-making, and environmental domains that promote well-being following adversity. this secondary analysis study examined whether strengths across these domains were prospectively associated with mental health and whether these associations differed across social identity groups. data were drawn from a subsample (n = 1584) from project lift up, a national longitudinal study of 4981 adolescents and young adults (ages 13-22 years), including an oversample of sexual and gender minority youth. participants completed a baseline survey and follow-ups at six-month intervals. strengths across the four rpm domains were assessed at different waves (waves 1-4), and mental health symptoms were assessed at wave 1 and wave 5 using the dsm-5-tr cross-cutting symptom measure. multiple strengths were independently associated with subsequent global mental health symptoms after adjustment for baseline symptoms, adversity, demographic characteristics, and social determinants of health. mentoring, hope, self-compassion, and recovering positive affect were associated with lower wave 5 global symptoms, whereas self-care was associated with higher symptoms. other interpersonal and environmental strengths were not independently associated with global symptoms. evidence for moderation was limited to two exploratory interactions involving sexual minority identity, indicating that recovering positive affect and activism may operate differently for these youth. findings highlight the value of examining multiple dimensions of resilience simultaneously and suggest that regulatory, meaning-making, and selected interpersonal strengths may be particularly relevant to subsequent mental health during adolescence and emerging adulthood. behavioral sciences

social media fatigue and depressive symptoms among chinese university students: artificial intelligence anxiety as a statistical mediator and subjective socioeconomic status as a moderator. as social media and artificial intelligence (ai) become increasingly embedded in university students' learning and daily lives, fatigue arising from established digital platforms and anxiety surrounding emerging ai may constitute interrelated forms of technology-related distress. however, how these experiences are jointly associated with depressive symptoms, and whether these associations vary by subjective socioeconomic status (sses), remains insufficiently understood. drawing on conservation of resources theory and research on status maintenance, this cross-sectional study examined ai anxiety as a statistical mediator of the association between social media fatigue and depressive symptoms and further tested whether sses moderated the association between ai anxiety and depressive symptoms. survey data from 1108 chinese university students were analyzed using regression models with heteroscedasticity-consistent type 3 (hc3) robust standard errors and percentile-bootstrap confidence intervals. social media fatigue was positively associated with ai anxiety, which in turn was positively associated with depressive symptoms, yielding a significant statistical indirect association. as sses increased, the association between ai anxiety and depressive symptoms became stronger, and the corresponding conditional indirect association also increased. overall, these findings suggest that understanding university students' digital mental health requires attention to both distress arising across different technological environments and the subjective social positions from which these experiences are evaluated, offering a more context-sensitive perspective on how established and emerging forms of digital stress may be jointly associated with psychological well-being. behavioral sciences

the influence of indigenous documentary narratives on cultural resilience and mental health awareness. indigenous documentary narratives may provide culturally grounded contexts for understanding identity, resilience and mental health, yet empirical evidence linking narrative engagement with these interconnected outcomes remains limited, particularly within indigenous communities in china. this cross-sectional mixed-methods observational study examined associations among narrative engagement, perceived cultural authenticity, cultural identification, cultural resilience, mental health awareness, stigma and help-seeking attitudes among 480 adults from ethnic minority communities in yunnan and hunan provinces, china, with 36 participants contributing qualitative data. after a standardized viewing session involving four documentaries representing yi, miao, bai and tujia/miao narratives, participants completed culturally adapted measures of narrative engagement and cultural and mental-health constructs. confirmatory factor analysis supported the final 60-item, six-factor measurement model ((1,695) = 3,284.15,/df = 1.937, cfi = 0.941, tli = 0.938, rmsea = 0.044, 95% ci [0.042, 0.046], srmr = 0.048), with satisfactory reliability and convergent validity. narrative engagement was positively associated with cultural resilience ( = 0.51), mental health awareness ( = 0.44), and help-seeking attitudes, while showing an inverse association with mental health stigma ( = -0.35; all < 0.001). multivariable models explained 53.4% of the variance in cultural resilience and 34.8% of the variance in mental health awareness. covariate-adjusted statistical indirect associations were observed through cultural identification ( = 0.225, 95% bca ci [0.168, 0.291]) and perceived cultural authenticity ( = 0.114, 95% ci [0.058, 0.144]). qualitative analysis identified cultural mirroring, normalization of distress through cultural metaphors, and intergenerational dialogue as central themes. overall, the findings identify interconnected statistical associations among narrative, cultural and mental-health variables, but do not establish temporal or causal pathways. longitudinal and comparative studies are needed to examine the temporal stability and potential mechanisms underlying these associations. frontiers in psychology

monitoring patient progress and changes in patient and clinician reported symptoms with measurement informed care in a pediatric primary care mental health integration program. introduction: measurement informed care (mic) utilizes validated instruments to screen and monitor patient symptoms and has been shown to improve patient outcomes and streamline diagnostic processes. our primary care mental health integration (pcmhi) program embedded mental health clinicians in the pediatric primary care setting to increase access to mental healthcare and provide care for adolescents. the purpose of this study was to identify changes in patients' self-reported symptom severity and determine whether provider assessments of patient progress were associated with patients' completed screening scores between the initial and final visits of short-term treatment within a pcmhi program.
methods: patients were retrospective from a multisite pediatric pcmhi program. the program's standardized measures included the patient health questionnaire-9 (phq-9) and generalized anxiety disorder-7 (gad-7) for patients older than 12 years and the pediatric symptom checklist-17 (psc-17) for patients younger than 12 years. before each pcmhi session, patients completed self-reported assessments, and after the session, clinicians provided a score reflecting overall patient progress. data from treated patients were extracted from electronic medical records, and changes in patient scores were calculated and analyzed using stata 16.1 (college station, tx).
results: a total of 2,702 patients were eligible for analysis. significant reductions (95% cis) in the proportion of patients scoring above clinically relevant cutoffs were observed for the phq-9 (28.8%; 26.1-31.5%), gad-7 (25.8%; 23.4-28.4%), psc-17 attention subscale (16.5%; 14.6-18.6%), and psc-17 internalizing subscale (17.3%; 15.3-19.4%) (all < 0.001). no significant change was identified for the psc-17 externalizing subscale (11.0%; 9.4-12.8%; = 0.19). effect sizes for score change among patients above the clinical cutoff were large ( = 0.68-0.80 across the phq-9 and gad-7 severity scores), and the odds of moving below the cutoff exceeded the odds of moving above it for every measure except the externalizing subscale. cgi improvement scores were significantly correlated with the phq-9, gad-7, and each of the psc-17 subscales (all < 0.001).
conclusion: validated mental health assessments, completed by patients before their appointments, documented reductions in symptom severity over brief, short-term treatment and changes in patient- and clinician-completed assessments were significantly correlated. these results demonstrate the feasibility of using patient-provided self-assessments to monitor patient progress. frontiers in psychology

intimate partner violence and depressive symptoms among ever-partnered peruvian women: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of national surveys, 2015-2024. background: intimate partner violence (ipv) is a major public health concern associated with adverse mental health outcomes in women. we examined trends in depressive symptoms and temporal variation in their association with ipv among ever-partnered peruvian women from 2015 to 2024.
methods: we conducted a repeated cross-sectional analysis using data from 10 consecutive national endes surveys. the primary weighted analytic sample included 101,145 women aged 15-49 years. depressive symptoms were defined as a phq-9 score ≥10. survey-weighted prevalence ratios were estimated using modified poisson regression with robust variance.
results: overall, 35.3% of women reported any ipv, including physical (28.0%), emotional (24.5%), and sexual ipv (6.1%). the weighted prevalence of depressive symptoms was 7.1%. the estimated annual relative change was +2.31% (95% ci: 1.03-3.61%; < 0.001), with a non-monotonic annual pattern. any ipv was associated with higher prevalence of depressive symptoms (apr: 2.37; 95% ci: 2.18-2.58). emotional, physical, and sexual ipv were also associated with depressive symptoms (aprs: 2.32 [95% ci: 2.14-2.53], 2.21 [95% ci: 2.04-2.39], and 1.97 [95% ci: 1.80-2.17], respectively). the association varied across periods: 2015-2019, apr 2.72; 2020-2021, 1.77; and 2022-2024, 2.29 (p for interaction <0.001).
conclusion: ipv was consistently associated with depressive symptoms, although the magnitude varied over time. these findings support integrated, confidential identification of ipv alongside timely mental health assessment and referral, without establishing the effectiveness of any specific screening strategy. frontiers in psychology

mental health, academic performance, and addictive behaviors among university student carers. objectives: student mental health is an emerging global public health priority in higher education. preliminary evidence indicates that caregiving is a mental health risk factor in university students. this study investigates demographic, educational, and caregiving variables as potential risk factors for university student carer mental health (anxiety, depression), addictive behaviors, and academic performance problems.
methods: 2,533 university students in italy completed an online cross-sectional survey assessing depressive symptoms (patient health questionnaire-9), anxiety symptoms (generalized anxiety disorder-7), 10 addictive behaviors (screener for substance and behavioral addictions), and self-assessed academic performance. predictors included demographics variables (sex, age, nationality), educational variables (degree programme, residential status, enrollment status), caregiving context variables (carer-care recipient relationship, care recipient's type of health condition) and caregiving responsibilities.
results: student carers living with a family member with a serious health condition comprised 30.1% of the sample (= 762). compared with non-carers, carers reported higher depressive symptoms (= 1.83, 95% ci [1.33, 2.33]; β = 0.14), higher anxiety symptoms (= 1.32, 95% ci [0.87, 1.77]; β = 0.11), and lower academic performance (= -0.21, 95% ci [-0.39, -0.02]; β = -0.05). carer status was also associated with higher odds of problematic involvement in cannabis (or = 1.69, 95% ci [1.25, 2.28]), food consumption (or = 1.62, 95% ci [1.34, 1.95]), shopping (or = 1.39, 95% ci [1.09, 1.78]), videogaming (or = 1.29, 95% ci [1.06, 1.57]), and social-network use (or = 1.26, 95% ci [1.06, 1.50]). within the student-carer subgroup, after adjusting for all demographic, educational, caregiving-context, and caregiving-responsibility variables, caring for a family member with a mental health condition or intellectual disability was associated with higher depressive symptoms (= 1.66, 95% ci [0.54, 2.79]). greater caregiving responsibilities were associated with higher depressive symptoms (= 1.12, 95% ci [0.62, 1.62]), higher anxiety symptoms (= 1.01, 95% ci [0.57, 1.44]), and higher odds of problematic food consumption (or = 1.32, 95% ci [1.10, 1.59]), and physical exercise (or = 1.31, 95% ci [1.08, 1.59]).
conclusion: findings replicate prior evidence showing student carers are at higher risk than non-carer peers for mental health problems. results extend prior research showing student carers are also at higher risk for addictive behaviors and poorer self-assessed academic performance. findings highlight the incremental and simultaneous contributions of demographic, educational, and caregiving variables as risk factors for student carer mental health and addictive behaviors. frontiers in psychology

animation-assisted psychological intervention in pediatric care: mechanisms, clinical applications, and emerging evidence. children frequently experience fear, anxiety, and pain during medical encounters, and this distress can lead to poor cooperation, longer procedures, and lasting avoidance of care. animation, delivered as cartoons, preparation films, applications, serious games, and virtual reality (vr) scenes, has become one of the most widely deployed non-pharmacological adjuncts in pediatric settings because it is inexpensive, non-invasive, and easily standardized. drawing on a structured search of six databases through july 2026, this mini-review synthesizes randomized and meta-analytic evidence across perioperative anxiety, procedural pain, pediatric dentistry, chronic-disease self-management, and mental health promotion. it organizes the evidence around five psychological pathways: attentional competition, observational learning, exposure and inhibitory learning, narrative-affective processing, and self-efficacy. additionally, it examines a sixth, non-psychological use in which animation is used to provide therapeutic visual stimulation. evidence supports moderate short-term benefits for anticipatory anxiety and for needle- and dentistry-related distress, with weaker and less consistent effects for high-intensity procedures and physiological outcomes. we argue that the field's core issue is conceptual rather than empirical: animation refers to a delivery medium, not a treatment, and trials have compared media rather than mechanisms. this obscures three unresolved problems: discordance between self-reported and autonomic outcomes; an untheorized moderating role of the developmental stage; and a theoretical tension between distraction, which withdraws attention from the feared stimulus, and exposure, which requires engagement with it. mechanism-matched comparators, core outcome sets, developmentally stratified designs, transparent intervention reporting, and follow-up across repeated procedures are prerequisites for cumulative progress. frontiers in psychology

comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in china (campus): study protocol for a multi-center prospective cohort with planned embedded randomized intervention trials. unlabelled: university students face a rising prevalence of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and suicidal ideation that exceeds the capacity of conventional, resource-constrained campus support services. although artificial intelligence (ai)-assisted screening tools have emerged, many have evaluated selected modalities or isolated prediction tasks, and their integration with prospectively evaluated intervention pathways remains limited. this protocol describes the comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in china (campus), a multi-center research program comprising a five-year prospective cohort, eight planned embedded randomized controlled trials, and exploratory multimodal ai and multi-omics studies across seven chinese universities. longitudinal cohort enrolment commenced at henan medical university in september 2025 and is planned to expand across seven participating universities. multidimensional screening integrates psychological self-report (phq-9, gad-7, isi, bsi-cv, and others), physiological measurements (eeg, mri, fnirs, hrv, eye tracking, facial-expression analysis, erp, voice acoustics), and an exploratory biospecimen component for multi-omics profiling, potentially including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and microbiome analyses, subject to the finalization and approval of layer-specific protocols. students identified through cohort screening as potentially eligible for an intervention trial will undergo trial-specific eligibility assessment. those who meet the eligibility criteria and provide trial-specific informed consent will be individually randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or its comparator within one of eight separate two-arm, multi-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trials. a transformer-based multimodal ai framework with shap-based feature attribution will be developed and internally evaluated for questionnaire-defined risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. the initial henan medical university cohort recruitment and university-student mental-health assessment were approved by the ethics review committee of henan medical university (xyll-20250484), and written informed consent is obtained from participants before enrolment. each additional participating center will obtain local ethics approval before study activation. findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences, and policy briefs, providing evidence that may inform the design and prospective evaluation of youth mental-health programs in other university settings.
clinical trial registration: the two clinical trials were registered in the chinese clinical trial registry (chictr). the registration details and urls are as follows: chictr2500113527: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298271; chictr2500113613: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298268. frontiers in psychology

physical exercise and mobile phone addiction in college students: negative emotions and coping styles as chain mediators. background: considering the significant risks that widespread mobile phone addiction poses to the holistic health of college students, further research is essential. this article systematically explores correlational mechanisms linking physical exercise engagement to mobile phone addiction. furthermore, it evaluates how negative emotions and coping styles function as mediators in this relationship.
methods: a convenience sampling approach was employed to recruit 3,283 undergraduates across the first 3 years of college. data collection took place between april and may 2025, during which participants self-reported their engagement in physical exercise, problematic mobile phone use patterns, psychological distress (manifested as depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms), as well as their preferred coping styles. all responses were gathered through the wenjuanxing online survey platform. for the statistical analysis, spss 29.0 was utilized to compute descriptive statistics and bivariate correlations. furthermore, to evaluate the sequential mediation effect, we adopted hayes' process macro (version 4.1, model 6), implementing a bootstrapping approach with 5,000 iterations to generate bias-corrected confidence intervals for the indirect pathways.
results: students showed low physical exercise (m = 18.49 ± 14.90) and variable mobile phone addiction (m = 35.40 ± 14.78). physical exercise negatively correlated with addiction (= -0.83), negative emotions (= -0.39), and negative coping styles (= -0.39), but positively with positive coping (= 0.31). negative emotions positively predicted addiction (= 0.618). mediation analysis showed physical exercise exhibited a correlational link with lower addiction levels (direct effect = 21.54%) through three distinct indirect correlational pathways. the path through negative emotions was dominant (72.45%), while coping-related paths accounted for 1.41%-4.6%. the independent mediating contribution of positive coping styles was slightly larger than that of negative coping styles; the dominant explanatory power across both models stemmed from the pathway of negative emotions.
conclusions: correlational results preliminarily suggest that physical exercise may be negatively associated with college students' mobile phone addiction through correlational pathways including sequential serial paths involving negative emotions and two types of coping styles. the present correlational data could provide empirical reference for developing sports-based mental health interventions. frontiers in psychology

work-related distress among interpreters working in interpreter-mediated psychotherapy: a 1-year follow-up. background: interpreter-mediated psychotherapy may pose demands on interpreters, particularly in trauma-focused settings. empirical evidence on interpreters' perceived work-related distress and associated variables remains limited. this longitudinal exploratory study examined perceived work-related distress and posttraumatic stress symptoms (ptss) among interpreters participating in a trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (tf-cbt) workshop and explored associations with psychotherapy-related difficulties, trauma-informed interpreting competence, and involvement in trauma-focused psychotherapy.
method: the analytical sample comprised 68 interpreters working in psychotherapy, who contributed up to three observations each, yielding a total of 120 valid observations of perceived work-related distress. observed outcome data were available for 51 participants at baseline (t0), 37 at 6 months (t2), and 32 at 12 months (t3). perceived work-related distress was assessed using a single author-developed item, ptss using the pcl-5, and process- and content-related interpreting difficulties and trauma-informed interpreting competence using author-developed self-report items. involvement in trauma-focused psychotherapy was also assessed. linear mixed-effects models were used.
results: perceived work-related distress was moderate and did not significantly change over time. higher ptss ( = 0.22, se = 0.10, = 0.034) and greater process-related difficulties ( = 0.34, se = 0.10, < 0.001) were associated with higher perceived work-related distress. content-related difficulties, trauma-informed interpreting competence, and involvement in trauma-focused psychotherapy were not significant (all ≥ 0.137).
discussion: the findings suggest that process-related difficulties may be particularly relevant to interpreter well-being. role agreements between therapists and interpreters, structured communication, collaboration within the therapeutic triad, and training or supervision addressing process-related challenges may represent relevant areas for practice and future research. frontiers in psychology

probing executive function in the toddler data desert: a touchscreen fnirs study of working memory and adhd-related symptoms. attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adhd) is associated with early differences in attentional control and working memory (wm), yet relatively few paradigms are developmentally feasible across the toddler-to-preschool period while also distinguishing spatial from featural information use. addressing this "toddler data desert," we extended a self-ordered pointing paradigm into a touchscreen wm search task paired with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fnirs) to characterize developmental changes in search behavior and cortical recruitment. the larger study enrolled 204 children aged 2-6 years; 200 completed both set size 3 conditions, 197 completed both set size 6 conditions, and 162 completed both set size 9 conditions after a performance-based advancement criterion. children completed stationary, spatially informative and feature-informative, featural/color-informative treasure chest blocks across increasing memory loads while fnirs measured bilateral frontal, temporal, and parietal responses. behaviorally, children required fewer selections during spatial than featural search at set sizes 3 and 6, and performance improved with age; this condition difference was no longer statistically reliable at set size 9 within the selected higher-performing subset. immediate perseverative selections also decreased markedly with age. exploratory post hoc sequence analyses further showed increasingly organized spatial search under higher memory load, whereas featural search remained comparatively heterogeneous, and organization in a preceding spatial block did not reliably predict subsequent featural search. symptom-defined adhd risk did not significantly predict behavioral efficiency. neurally, spatial and featural blocks showed age-associated differences in distributed frontotemporal-parietal recruitment, and the elevated-symptom group showed broader frontal recruitment despite comparable behavioral performance. together, these findings support the treasure chest task as a toddler-feasible approach for examining developmental differences in spatial and featural working-memory search while highlighting the value of integrating behavioral sequence measures with cortical activity. neural risk-group findings should be interpreted as cross-sectional associations rather than diagnostic biomarkers. behavioral sciences

cognitive transparency and trust calibration in explainable ai systems: a psychological model of human-ai decision reliance. introduction: explainable artificial intelligence (xai) is widely expected to improve transparency and support appropriate human reliance on ai-assisted decision-making. however, the psychological processes through which explainability relates to reliance remain insufficiently understood, and explainability, transparency, and trust have largely been examined separately.
objectives: this study develops and tests a psychological model of cognitive transparency in which ai explainability, algorithmic transparency, and perceived ai accuracy are associated with human reliance on ai through cognitive understanding, cognitive trust, and trust calibration, with ai literacy as a boundary condition.
methods: a cross-sectional online survey was completed by 342 ai users in south korea in may and june 2026. each participant evaluated one self-selected ai system that they had personally used; all constructs were measured by self-report. the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (pls-sem) in smartpls 4.
results: ai explainability (β = 0.349) and algorithmic transparency (β = 0.297) were positively associated with cognitive understanding. cognitive understanding (β = 0.388) and, more strongly, perceived ai accuracy (β = 0.492) were associated with cognitive trust. cognitive trust was associated with trust calibration (β = 0.631), which was associated with human reliance on ai (β = 0.600). all hypothesized indirect effects were significant, and ai literacy strengthened the association between ai explainability and cognitive understanding (β = 0.192). the model explained 36%-54% of the variance in the endogenous constructs and showed medium predictive power.
conclusion: the findings are consistent with a sequence in which explainable ai relates to reliance through users' understanding and trust judgments. because all constructs were self-reported and measured at a single point in time, the results describe associations among users' perceptions rather than causal effects, independently verified calibration, or objectively appropriate reliance. the findings suggest that ai developers in domains such as healthcare, education, and finance, where calibrated reliance is critical, should pair user-facing explanations with information about system accuracy and with ai literacy support. frontiers in psychology

effects of structured exercise on executive function across childhood, adolescence, and later life: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis examining exercise skill characteristics. background: structured exercise may benefit executive function across childhood, adolescence, and later life, but whether effects vary by executive-function domain, developmental stage, or qualitative exercise characteristics remains uncertain.
methods: we conducted a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in non-clinical children, adolescents, and older adults. five databases were searched from inception to may 20, 2026; eligibility was restricted during screening to formally published english-language journal articles dated from january 1, 2015 to may 20, 2026. outcomes were classified as inhibitory control, working memory, or cognitive flexibility. intervention arms were coded for environmental predictability, cognitive engagement, coordination complexity, and motor skill learning demand. three-level random-effects models retained dependent effect sizes within trials, with study_id-clustered cr2 robust inference and sensitivity analyses using alternative sampling-covariance structures. the review was registered in prospero (crd420261402803).
results: forty-seven trials representing 49 independent samples and 4,195 actual participants contributed 202 effect-size estimates. structured exercise was associated with a positive average effect on executive function (hedges' = 0.412, robust 95% ci [0.284, 0.540], < 0.001). heterogeneity was substantial (total = 74.45%), and the 95% prediction interval ranged from -0.476 to 1.299. positive pooled estimates were observed for all three executive-function domains and for children, adolescents, and older adults, but neither domain ( = 0.060) nor developmental stage ( = 0.825) significantly moderated effects. environmental predictability, cognitive engagement, coordination complexity, motor skill learning demand, intervention duration, and comparator type were also not significant moderators. main conclusions were generally robust to alternative sampling-covariance assumptions and study restrictions, although stage-specific effect magnitudes, particularly in adolescents, were less stable in leave-one-trial-out analyses. small-study-effect diagnostics were inconsistent, publication bias remained uncertain, and grade certainty was low because of serious risk of bias and inconsistency.
conclusion: structured exercise was associated with better executive-function performance on average, but substantial heterogeneity and prediction intervals spanning no effect indicate that benefits are not uniform. current evidence does not identify a specific executive-function domain, developmental stage, program duration, comparator type, or broadly defined exercise skill characteristic that reliably yields larger effects.
systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/view/crd420261402803, identifier prospero (crd420261402803). frontiers in psychology

distinct visual pathways of threat retrieval in fear‐conditioned faces abstract many have demonstrated rapid (< 100 ms) visuo‐cortical differentiation of threat‐associated faces. this may go back to low‐spatial frequency (lsf) visual information originating from magnocellular pathways. yet it remains unknown whether potentially magnocellular fear signals extend beyond evolutionarily prepared emotional faces. if so, spatial frequency characteristics should modulate visual processing of faces with newly acquired threat‐relevance. furthermore, it is unclear whether sub‐bands of the visual spectrum are associated with autonomic arousal. using a differential fear‐conditioning paradigm ( n = 68), this study tested whether early visual attentional capture, indicated by the p1 event‐related potential component, face encoding, indicated by the n1 component, and autonomic arousal, indicated by skin conductance responses (scr), prioritizes lsf information of threat‐associated faces with neutral expressions during fear retrieval. additionally, correlations tested whether the same subcortical system underlies the p1 and scr. stimulus ratings and n1 amplitudes confirmed successful fear acquisition. during fear retrieval, the p1 showed a selective left‐hemispheric enhancement in response to lsf threat‐faces. by contrast, the n1 was sensitive to spatial frequency but not fear‐relevance. cs‐differentiation in the scr was not modulated by spatial frequency but longer cs presentations resulting in larger fear differentiation. amplitudes of p1 and scr were positively correlated only for safety faces. data support the notion that magnocellular‐cortical pathways adapt quickly to novel threat‐associations and facilitate rapid threat retrieval in early visual attention, but not face encoding, even for perceptually neutral faces. at least in the present paradigm, subcortical fear pathways do not associate with anticipatory arousal in scr. psychophysiology

target selection and action control in interception tasks action possibilities may emerge or disappear over time due to interactions among multiple moving objects. which action possibility and how it is actualized reflect the interplay among environmental constraints and individual capabilities and preferences. the present study aimed to identify individual and task-specific factors that predict target selection in an interception task and characterize the solutions executed by individuals to realize the chosen action possibility. we created a video game simulating team sports such as american football, in which the participant controlled the thrower attempting to intercept one of the two moving targets. near each target, there was a defender that could intercept the pass. in addition, a third defender moved from the endzone toward the thrower. we manipulated target speed and defender distance to alter both temporal and spatial constraints. our results indicated that target selection was influenced mainly by the difference between the defenders’ relative gains. throughout practice, participants also adapted all three execution variables that define the throwing outcome, with a relevant effect of target speed in scaling the values of each execution variable. this study demonstrated that during a virtual interception task with coexisting action possibilities, individuals select which target to intercept based on a high-order, relational variable and calibrate their movement according to the selected target speed. perceptual and motor skills

attentional focus, empathy and gratitude: an experimental analysis abstract empathy and gratitude are distinct but related prosocial constructs that may be shaped by attentional processes. this study examined whether attentional orientation influences situational empathic responding and whether dispositional gratitude moderates this effect. a sample of 198 undergraduate students completed a 20‐item gratitude questionnaire (g‐20) and later participated in a cooperative task under other‐focused, self‐focused, or control instructions. both active attentional conditions were associated with greater odds of reporting empathy than the control condition, whereas they did not differ from each other. expression of gratitude was negatively associated with empathic responding. gratitude in the face of suffering significantly interacted with attentional condition, although none of the condition‐specific associations reached significance. these findings suggest that directing attention either toward others or toward one's own internal experience may facilitate situational empathic responding. international journal of psychology

interrupted minds at work: how mindfulness shapes the effects of workplace interruptions abstract this study tests the interactive model of workplace interruptions, including intrusions, distractions, discrepancy detections, and breaks in task performance. specifically, we suggest that workplace interruptions exhibit an inverted u‐shaped relationship with task performance. in addition, we explore how mindfulness moderates these relationships. using time‐lagged multisource survey data from 319 supervisor–subordinate dyads working in manufacturing, retail, and service industries, our results show significant inverted u‐shaped relationships of intrusions and breaks with employee task performance. we found significant negative linear effects of distractions and discrepancy detections on task performance. furthermore, the inverted u‐shaped effects of intrusions and breaks were significantly moderated by employees' mindfulness. we confirmed that workplace interruptions may not necessarily be bad, but the frequency of interruptions, coupled with an individual's level of mindfulness, predicts employees' task performance. based on these findings, we discuss the importance of workplace interruptions and mindfulness resources for effective performance. applied psychology-an international review-psychologie appliquee-revue internationale

exploring a range of potential factors promoting and constraining ef in south african preschoolers abstract background socioeconomic disadvantage is widely associated with poorer cognitive and educational outcomes. however, emerging evidence suggests that children in low‐income contexts may demonstrate resilience in executive function (ef) development. this study examined the predictors of ef in south african preschoolers from disadvantaged communities to identify modifiable, context‐specific influences. methods 125 children (aged 3–5 years) and their caregivers were recruited from 15 early childhood centers in cape town. children completed three tablet‐based ef tasks from the early years toolbox measuring working memory, inhibition, shifting, while caregivers reported on demographic variables, household assets, child sleep, child screen time, child exposure to violence, and parenting practices. multiple linear regressions examined predictors of child ef, with exploratory analyses on a subset ( n = 22) for hair cortisol analysis. results older child age ( β = 0.37, p < 0.001), caregiver secondary education ( β = 0.22, p = 0.003), and fewer sleep difficulties ( β = –0.45, p = 0.042) significantly predicted higher child ef scores, together explaining 25% of variance. household assets, screen time, violence exposure, and parenting scores were non‐significant. in the subsample, hair cortisol concentration correlated positively with ef ( ρ = 0.55, p = 0.009), suggesting potential adaptive calibration under adversity. conclusions findings highlight that modifiable proximal factors (e.g., caregiver education and child sleep) shape ef development more strongly than socioeconomic indicators. results challenge the presumed universality of ses‐ef gradients and underscore the importance of culturally grounded, contextually validated measures for understanding resilience and early cognitive development in majority world settings. developmental science
dyadic associations between body appreciation and sexual function among cisgender heterosexual and gender and sexually diverse couples journal of sex & marital therapy

effects of mindfulness therapy on stress biomarkers and psychological symptoms in women with recurrent pregnancy loss: a randomized clinical trial abstract women with recurrent pregnancy loss (rpl) exhibit high levels of depression, anxiety, and stress, which negatively impact their quality of life. this randomized clinical trial evaluated the effects of an eight‐week online mindfulness‐based intervention (mbi), with weekly one‐hour sessions, on psychological and biological markers of stress in 35 women with rpl. participants were randomly assigned to either the mbi or standard care (control group) and assessed before and after the intervention through salivary biomarkers (cortisol, alpha‐amylase, and immunoglobulin a—iga) and the validated questionnaires depression, anxiety and stress scale‐21 (dass‐21) and psychological general well‐being index (pgwb‐i). no significant time × group interactions were observed for salivary biomarkers, including cortisol ( p = 0.672), alpha‐amylase ( p = 0.342), and iga ( p = 0.148). participants in the mbi group showed significant reductions in total dass‐21 ( p = 0.018), depression ( p = 0.026), and stress ( p = 0.015) scores, whereas anxiety did not differ significantly between groups ( p = 0.121). they also showed robust improvements in overall well‐being ( p < 0.001) and multiple pgwb‐i domains. these findings suggest that mbi may improve self‐reported psychological well‐being in women with rpl; however, as no significant effects were observed in the primary biomarker outcomes, these secondary psychological findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis‐generating. trial registration https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/rbr‐4xc76cr stress and health
the project o.c.t.o.p.u.s.: observing cyberdelic transformations of priors under simulation cyberpsychology behavior and social networking

development and psychometric validation of the amateur football tournament satisfaction scale using rasch analysis. introduction: amateur football tournaments attract millions of participants worldwide, yet no dedicated instrument exists to measure players' satisfaction with these experiences. this study developed and validated the amateur football tournament satisfaction scale in full-length and short-form versions using rasch analysis across two independent samples.
methods: in study 1, we generated an initial 30-item pool and used factor and rasch analyses with 245 amateur players to purify the items, producing a 26-item full-length scale and a 10-item short form. in study 2, we independently validated the short form with 407 participants through confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity testing, and differential item functioning analysis.
results: both studies supported a unidimensional structure, with three purification rounds yielding the 26-item scale and confirmatory factor analysis supporting the short form's structure. the short form demonstrated high internal consistency ( = 0.897) and expected correlations with training satisfaction, group cohesion, and burnout. it correlated at 0.974 with the full-length version, although this may partly reflect item overlap. most items functioned equivalently across gender and league participation groups, but a few study 1 items showed significant dif.
discussion: the amateur football tournament satisfaction scale offers a psychometrically sound instrument for assessing amateur football tournament satisfaction. the full-length version suits detailed research, while the short form provides an efficient option for routine evaluation. frontiers in psychology

adaptation of the internal political efficacy scale and its associations with empathy, mental well-being, and global citizenship: a parallel mediation model. internal political efficacy, a significant psychological variable related to individuals' perception of their ability to understand political processes and act effectively within them, has been gaining importance in the context of global citizenship. this study primarily examined whether empathy and mental well-being constitute parallel indirect pathways between internal political efficacy and global citizenship and, secondarily, evaluated the psychometric properties of the short form of the internal political efficacy scale in a turkish sample. the research used two independent samples comprising a total of 681 participants: 311 participants for the psychometric analyses of the adapted scale and 370 participants for testing the structural model. in the psychometric analyses, confirmatory factor analysis verified the proposed structure of the scale and demonstrated that the instrument possesses acceptable reliability. in the structural model analyses, internal political efficacy was positively associated with empathy, mental well-being, and global citizenship. moreover, empathy and mental well-being showed statistically supported parallel indirect pathways in the relationship between internal political efficacy and global citizenship, while the direct association remained significant. the study contributes to the global citizenship literature by integrating political efficacy, socio-emotional functioning, and mental well-being within a single psychological framework. frontiers in psychology

development and validation of the chinese acceptance scale for university students (cas) in hong kong, china. background: this paper reports the development and validation of the chinese acceptance scale (cas) as a measure of acceptance of diversity among chinese university students. integrating western and chinese conceptions of acceptance of diversity, the cas was initially conceptualized with four dimensions: "diversity of contact," "comfort with difference," "appreciation of others," and "" (tolerance of others).
methods: study 1 involved content validation by an expert panel ( = 10), which evaluated 25 items and resulted in a 20-item instrument covering the four proposed dimensions. study 2 examined the psychometric properties of the cas using two waves of data from 963 university students, assessing factor structure, measurement invariance, convergent and discriminant validity, and reliability.
results: confirmatory factor analysis provided support for the initial four-factor model. however, the results indicated that "appreciation of others" and "kuan rong" were better represented as a single factor. the revised three-factor model consisted of "diversity of contact," "comfort with difference," and "inclusive appreciation." this model showed good factorial validity, measurement invariance over time, and satisfactory reliability. convergent and discriminant validity were also supported at the total-scale level, although further examination of these properties at the subscale level is needed. overall, the findings suggest that the cas can be used to assess acceptance of diversity among chinese university students. frontiers in psychology

kinesiophobia following acl reconstruction: a qualitative netnographic study of lived experiences shared on reddit. introduction: kinesiophobia, broadly defined as fear of movement and vulnerability to (re)injury, is one of the most significant psychological barriers to functional recovery following anterior cruciate ligament (acl) reconstruction, yet its everyday, lived texture is not fully captured by structured psychometric instruments. orthopedic clinicians frequently observe that patients who have achieved objective surgical and functional recovery nonetheless remain reluctant to resume movement. this study aimed to explore this phenomenon in patients' own words.
methods: we conducted a qualitative netnographic study of 50 first-person reddit narratives shared by individuals with acl injury, spanning the rehabilitation trajectory from preoperative anxiety to chronic post-return instability. data were analyzed using braun and clarke's reflexive thematic analysis by an interdisciplinary team of orthopedic surgeons and psychiatrists.
results: three interconnected themes emerged. first, a progressive loss of trust in the injured body, in which normal postoperative sensations were hypervigilantly monitored and catastrophically reinterpreted as signs of graft failure, persisting even after objective strength testing and medical clearance. second, fear-driven disruption of functional identity and future planning, in which reinjury fear extended beyond the knee to threaten occupational continuity, financial security, and physical self-concept. third, persistent uncertainty and compulsive reassurance-seeking, fueled by inconsistent rehabilitation guidance and unfavorable social comparison with peers' recovery timelines on social media.
discussion: psychological readiness for return to activity appears to be shaped by an interacting network of bodily, identity-related, and informational factors that extend beyond fear of reinjury as traditionally measured. incorporating expectation management, structured reassurance, and psychologically informed communication into postoperative care protocols may benefit orthopedic and rehabilitation teams. naturally occurring online narratives may serve as an ecologically valid source of insight into the psychological dimensions of acl recovery, complementing structured psychometric assessment. frontiers in psychology

do you feel your body right now? ecological momentary assessment of interoceptive intensity and valence across multiple domains in everyday life. researchers usually assess interoception (i.e., the perception of inner bodily states) under laboratory conditions, once, with a focus on one organ, mostly the heart. the present study expands this research and presents findings from two independent studies, demonstrating the reliability and validity of an ecological momentary assessment (ema) approach to study interoception in different modalities at the very same time from a subjective perspective. we asked more than 250 participants to rate how intensely they feel their heart, gut, and breath at random moments in everyday life, as a measure of interoceptive attention. we further assessed the appraisal of these interoceptive body sensations by means of valence ratings. across two samples (n1 = 141, n2 = 112), we demonstrated high reliability of this assessment at the between-person level and modest reliability at the within-person level. we further examined convergent and divergent validity for both subjective measures. the study findings highlight promising psychometric properties and applicability of this novel assessment of ambulatory interoception. this method enables large-scale field studies to investigate interoceptive attention and appraisal on a momentary basis to understand the role of bodily sensations in daily functioning and health. frontiers in psychology

low caregiver-child positive escalation in childhood predicts late adolescent bpd abstract borderline personality disorder (bpd) and major depressive disorder (mdd) are highly comorbid, yet little is known about developmental family processes that distinguish between individuals who will go on to develop mdd versus bpd. using longitudinal, observational data from the preschool depression study, we tested whether caregiver behaviors and caregiver-child interaction patterns during a conflict discussion task predicted later bpd vs. mdd symptoms. caregiver-child dyads ( n = 161) completed five-minute conflict discussions at up to three timepoints across late childhood and early adolescence; these discussions were observationally coded for caregiver and dyadic behaviors. outcomes were self-reported bpd symptoms and clinical interview-based mdd symptoms assessed in late adolescence. after controlling for caregiver bpd and mdd and correcting for the false discovery rate, hierarchical linear regression models showed that lower dyadic positive escalation between caregiver and child predicted elevated bpd symptoms in late adolescence. associations with mdd symptoms were not significant. these findings suggest that maintaining or building positive affect during challenging caregiver-child interactions may be a protective interpersonal process that is more specific to risk for bpd than risk for mdd. implications for our understanding of the development of bpd versus mdd in childhood and adolescence are discussed. research on child and adolescent psychopathology

to collapse or not to collapse multiple measures of the same psychological construct: a demonstration across 14 independent studies of autistic and non-autistic children abstract large data repositories provide a valuable opportunity to combine multiple independent studies, creating large samples that can address questions not achievable within a single study. however, independent studies often use different instruments to measure the same behavior or psychological construct, such as cognitive ability, social functioning, or psychopathology. investigators often combine samples that include different instruments under the assumption that instruments assessing the same construct capture the same underlying phenomenon. yet this assumption of instrument interchangeability may be wrong. collapsing different instruments into a single variable could introduce bias. here, we established a quantitative method to demonstrate compatibility among multiple instruments with moderation analyses. we illustrate this method in domains of cognitive ability, anxiety symptoms, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptoms as exemplars that might interact with outcomes of interest (autistic features instruments). a total of 1,352 participants were included from autistic and non-autistic samples across 14 independent studies. our findings suggest that within this sample, some commonly used instruments within a domain can be acceptably combined, whereas others demonstrate discrepant relationships with outcomes of interest. more importantly, we offer a generalizable approach for scientists seeking to leverage existing datasets for secondary analyses. research on child and adolescent psychopathology

culturally aligned implementation of mindfulness programs through family, school, and community partnerships for holistic wellbeing abstract this study investigates the culturally relevant implementation of a mindfulness‐based program (mbp) in western county, focusing on the role of family, school, and community partnerships (fscps) in fostering alignment and sustainability. data were gathered through interviews, observations, and document analysis, using a qualitative case study approach. thematic analysis identified key themes related to cultural alignment and partnership‐building. findings highlight the significance of aligning mbps with community values and leveraging strong fscps for successful integration and long‐term sustainability. this study highlights the critical importance of collaboration, cultural sensitivity, and community engagement in the successful implementation of mbps. it provides practical insights for educators, leaders, and policymakers on how to customize mindfulness programs to meet the unique needs of diverse communities. by linking mindfulness practices with local cultural values and fostering strong partnerships, mbps can contribute to lasting educational and social change. the research also highlights the need for leadership that prioritizes cultural relevance and community input, offering a model for driving educational innovation through fscps. journal of community psychology

reporting-source differences in associations between student-perceived relationships with teachers and social-emotional skills: evidence from the suzhou sses 2019 sample. introduction: students' perceptions of their relationships with teachers may be associated with social-emotional functioning, but the magnitude of this association may depend on who reports the outcomes. this study examined whether student-perceived relationships with teachers were associated with five domains of social-emotional skills reported by students, parents, and teachers, and whether association magnitudes differed across reporting sources.
methods: data were drawn from 7,246 students in 151 school-by-cohort units in the suzhou sample of the 2019 oecd survey on social and emotional skills. survey-weighted fixed-effects models estimated within-unit associations, matched stacked models compared slopes across informants, and school-by-cohort-grouped cross-validation assessed incremental prediction.
results: all 15 informant-by-domain associations were positive and remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. in matched samples, student-report slopes ranged from 0.234 to 0.256, compared with 0.083 to 0.109 for parent reports and 0.080 to 0.106 for teacher reports. all student-versus-adult contrasts remained significant after correction, whereas none of the parent-versus-teacher contrasts did. the same pattern was observed in 44 of 45 skill-level tests. adding the relationship index improved out-of-fold weighted r² in all 30 prediction comparisons, although absolute predictive performance was weak, particularly for adult-reported outcomes.
discussion: student-perceived relationships with teachers showed cross-informant relevance, while the strongest observed associations occurred when both the relationship measure and the social-emotional outcome shared the student reporter. these findings suggest that reporting source should be treated as substantive information in educational assessment and that relationship ratings should be used to contextualize, rather than replace, multi-informant evidence. frontiers in psychology

the cost of misaligned roles: school climate, non‐counseling demands, and school counselors’ program implementation and work engagement abstract school counselors face persistent challenges in implementing comprehensive school counseling programs (cscps) amid complex organizational demands, yet the conditions shaping these challenges remain underexamined. grounded in job demands–resources theory and role theory, we tested a mediation model examining school climate as an organizational antecedent, non‐counseling work demands as a mediator, and cscp implementation and work engagement as dual outcomes among 530 practicing school counselors. results indicated that school climate had significant positive direct effects on both cscp implementation and work engagement. non‐counseling job demands partially mediated the relationship between school climate and cscp implementation but did not significantly mediate the climate–work engagement relationship. findings highlight school climate as a structural job resource with positive effects on school counselor professional outcomes. findings also emphasize non‐counseling duties as job demands that erode the effect of positive school climate on cscp implementation. implications for counseling practice, training, and policy are discussed. public statement : when schools create positive, supportive environments, and school counselors are better protected from being pulled away from their students by administrative tasks, substitute teaching, and clerical duties that fall outside their professional role. our research shows that this protection is the key mechanism through which school climate improves both the quality of school counseling programs students receive and the degree to which counselors remain energized and engaged in their work. journal of counseling and development

profiles of post-traumatic symptoms and well-being among young adults: associations with early adversity, psychopathology and social support post-traumatic stress symptoms (ptss) are common in young adulthood, yet symptom-based approaches provide only a partial account of mental health. the dualcontinua model conceptualizes mental health as the coexistence of psychological distress and psychological well-being (pwb), allowing diverse post-trauma configurations. this study identified ptss– pwb profiles in 2,000 nationally representative lithuanian young adults (18–29 years) and examined their associations with adverse childhood experiences (aces), depression, anxiety, alcohol misuse, and social support. participants completed validated selfreport measures, and kmeans clustering was applied to standardized ptss and pwb scores. four profiles emerged: complete mental health, vulnerable, symptomatic but content, and struggling. profiles were correctly differentiated (silhouette = .41) and differed significantly in ace exposure, psychopathology, alcohol misuse, and perceived social support (η 2 = .02– .27). notably, vulnerable and symptomatic-but-content groups showed similar psychopathology despite contrasting well-being levels. findings support heterogeneous trauma–well-being trajectories and highlight the need to address both distress and well-being in interventions. emerging adulthood

re-membering country and culture: relational liberatory praxis in an aboriginal women’s healing project blak women’s healing is an indigenous-led program developed by, for, and with aboriginal women in the west of melbourne. grounded in liberation psychology, decolonial community psychology, and indigenous studies, the program engages contemporary cultural practice and yarning to create culturally safe spaces where aboriginal women can come together to explore, understand, and support healing. this article reports on one iteration of the program, drawing on women’s stories of participating in the cultural practice workshops and the subsequent public exhibition, where further yarns took place. using a relational and culturally grounded analytic approach consistent with the program’s liberatory praxis, we examined how women narrated their experiences across these interconnected spaces. through this work, we observed the enduring impacts of historical trauma and ongoing structural violence, alongside the strength, cultural knowledge, and collective resilience mobilized by aboriginal women to (re)build pathways to healing for themselves, their families, and communities. the findings illuminate how cultural re-membering, relational connection and collective safety, and the amplification of counter-stories operate as forms of liberatory praxis. in doing so, the article contributes to scholarship on indigenous-led healing and demonstrates the transformative potential of culturally grounded, community-based approaches to supporting social and emotional wellbeing and healing. journal of humanistic psychology

domain-specific effects of men’s parental investment cues on women’s mate evaluations: increased long-term but decreased short-term mate attractiveness abstract women’s obligatory parental investment may lead women to value men’s ability and willingness to invest in future offspring when evaluating long-term mates. although men’s disposition toward parental investment has received less attention than their resource acquisition ability, several studies have shown that behavioral cues to men’s willingness to invest influence women’s evaluations. however, it remains unclear whether parental investment cues specifically influence long-term mate attractiveness or generally increase favorability. this study used text-based profiles to examine whether cues to men’s willingness to invest have domain-specific effects on women’s evaluations. female nursing school students in japan ( n = 254) were randomly assigned to read a male profile that either included or did not include parental investment cues and then evaluated the target man across long-term mating, short-term mating, and non-mating contexts. the results showed that men described as having positive attitudes toward parenting and children were evaluated as more attractive as long-term mates, but less attractive as short-term mates. no effects were observed for non-mating evaluations, namely friend attractiveness and general liking. these findings suggest that men’s attitudes toward parenting and children serve as cues to men’s willingness to invest in future offspring and influence women’s evaluations in a domain-specific manner. the study findings also suggest that parental investment cues may signal not only men’s suitability as long-term mates but also their lower suitability as short-term mates. this study provides evidence for the domain specificity of parental investment cues and highlights the importance of such cues in human mate choice. evolutionary psychological science

empathy as a dyadic process nature reviews psychology, published online: 14 october 2026; doi:10.1038/s44159-026-00624-4 empathy frequently arises in interactions between two people rather than within a single individual in isolation. in this review, genzer and perry consider the cognitive, affective and motivational aspects of empathy through a dyadic lens that considers the empathizer, the recipient and their shared experience. nature reviews psychology

dimensional asymmetries in social attention: dynamic head movements elicit opposite attentional biases in vertical versus horizontal dimensions abstract when observing a person with direct gaze but a horizontally averted head posture, attention often shifts opposite to head direction (overshoot effect). we investigated whether this effect generalizes to vertical head movements and whether it depends on gaze direction information. across four experiments, centrally presented faces shifted dynamically to averted head positions before a target appeared at a location congruent or incongruent with head direction. vertical head movements (experiments 1 and 2) produced head-congruency effects, which were stronger when the eyes were closed. in contrast, horizontal head movements (experiments 3 and 4) produced classic overshoot effects, which surprisingly were amplified when the eyes were closed. thus, direct gaze attenuated head-cueing effects but did not alter their direction. overall, these findings reveal dimensional asymmetries in social attention and demonstrate that gaze-head integration considers spatial context. implications for hierarchical, holistic, and predictive cue-integration accounts are discussed. open practices statement all four experiments were preregistered on the open science framework (osf; experiment 1: https://osf.io/qds4x ; experiment 2: https://osf.io/d6rwe ; experiment 3: https://osf.io/xe9a6 ; experiment 4: https://osf.io/3pq49 ). materials, experimental scripts, stimuli, raw data, and analysis scripts underlying the reported results are publicly available at https://osf.io/aq7zf/ and https://osf.io/j96fx/ attention perception & psychophysics

estimating stimulus-processing time via position slopes in visual search abstract existing approaches to measure the time needed to process a single stimulus have confounded the measure with other time-consuming processes, such as initiation of the response, and neglect the massively parallel processing abilities of the visual system. conversely, traditional set-size manipulations in visual search yield flawed estimates of stimulus-processing time, mainly because the number of actually processed stimuli is typically unknown. we have recently developed the systematic-search paradigm , a visual-search paradigm that overcomes this limitation and potentially provides a valid measure of stimulus-processing time. its core idea is to bring the order of search under experimental control, so that the number of processed stimuli is determined by the position of the target on the current trial. we then extract the slope of the linear function relating target position (and therefore the number of processed stimuli) to response times. with this approach, all extraneous processing times are relegated to the intercept of the function. the present study provides a further validation of this slope-measure by showing that it reflects the complexity of the visual stimuli (exp. 1), but is robust against changes in the complexity of the response (exp. 2). all raw data, analysis code, preregistrations, and research materials are available online ( https://osf.io/42mxh/ ). open practices statement in both experiments, we report how we determined our sample size, all data exclusions (if any), all manipulations, and all measures in the study. the experiments’ designs and analyses were preregistered. all trial-level raw data, analysis code, preregistrations and research materials are available online ( https://osf.io/42mxh/ ). direct links to the preregistrations are https://osf.io/tbk8s/ (exp. 1) and https://osf.io/va98q/ (exp. 2). attention perception & psychophysics
