quality of life and well-being of syrian refugees: insights from spain and jordan. syrian refugees face numerous challenges, including conflict, displacement, family separation, human rights violations, limited access to basic needs, and exposure to violence and torture. these experiences significantly affect their physical, psychological, social, and environmental quality of life (qol). the aim of this study was to assess the qol of syrian refugees in spain and jordan and to examine the association between sociodemographic characteristics, living conditions, and experiences of discrimination with different qol domains. this study used a cross-sectional correlational design in syrian refugee centers, homes, and camps across spain and jordan. a convenience sample of syrian refugees with confirmed status in the past ten years was recruited. demographic data were collected via a demographic form, and the world health organization quality of life-brief questionnaire (whoqol-bref) was used to assess their quality of life. data analysis included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, one-way anova, and independent-tests. the two hundred participants were predominantly aged 18-29 (43%), female (52.5%), married (51.5%), with secondary school education (46.5%), and unemployed (70%), with low monthly family income (60.5%). while 69% experienced low levels of discrimination, 33% were satisfied with their health, and 47.5% rated their qol as neutral. refugees in spain reported higher qol across physical, psychological, social, and environmental domains compared to those in jordan (< 0.05). the qol was related to socio-demographic factors: higher among married participants (= 0.044), urban residents (< 0.001), and recent immigrants (<5 years,< 0.001), but lower among those with low income (= 0.011). gender differences showed that males had better physical (= 0.001) and psychological (= 0.032) qol than females. lower discrimination levels and employment were associated with higher qol across multiple domains. this study highlights the lasting association of the syrian conflict on refugees' qol, emphasizing the need for holistic healthcare that addresses physical, psychological, social, and environmental challenges both before and after displacement. findings call for comprehensive support systems, including early mental health interventions, anti-discrimination efforts, and community inclusion programs, to enhance refugees' resilience and integration. the study identifies specific subgroups at greater risk of lower qol-including women, older adults, those with low income, the unemployed, camp residents, and those experiencing discrimination-providing actionable insights for policymakers to target resources and interventions effectively. tailored rehabilitation and psychological care are essential for empowering refugees to rebuild their lives and fostering social cohesion in host communities. behavioral sciences

professional future expectations and mental health in university students: a psychosocial and environmental approach. introduction: university students face heightened risks regarding mental health, with depression, anxiety, and stress being the most prevalent issues. students' mental health is associated with their academic performance and psychosocial well-being, as well as with their development and future professional trajectories.
methods: this study is part of the iberian observatory of healthy learning and youth participation (oiasp-j) and uses the healthy learning environments ecosystems instrument. the sample consisted of included 2,315 university students, of whom 65.5% ( = 1,516) were female, with a mean age of 22.9 years ( = 5.18).
results: older male students who value institutional ethics and values, demonstrate greater academic engagement, report higher levels of well-being, more effective stress management, and greater happiness, exhibit fewer psychosocial risks related to well-being and mental health. social isolation emerged as a significant factor associated with greater vulnerability in well-being and mental health. regarding professional future expectation, students with more positive expectations exhibited better individual, psychosocial, and organizational indicators than those with more negative expectations.
conclusion: we conclude that the results provide evidence for higher education institutions, health professionals, and policymakers to invest in more skills programs and mental health interventions. these programs may help students thrive academically, maintain good mental health throughout their studies, and successfully complete their training. in turn, this facilitates a smooth transition into professional life and enables students to contribute to society. frontiers in psychology

the relational and structural dimensions of wellbeing: a population‐based latent model of social conditions, mattering, perceived discrimination, and quality of life abstract mattering, the experience of feeling valued and able to contribute, is a recognized determinant of wellbeing. perceived discrimination (pd), or unfair treatment, is socially patterned and may communicate devaluation. anti‐mattering, the subjective experience of insignificance and disregard, serves as a theoretical lens on pd, not a measured construct. population‐level studies rarely examine mattering and pd together, their socio‐demographic patterning or associations with quality of life (qol). in the 2024 norwegian quality of life survey ( n = 16,396), mattering, pd, and qol were modelled as latent constructs in a structural equation model estimating direct and indirect associations with socio‐demographic predictors. socio‐demographic factors explained 11% of the variance in mattering and 31% in pd, with the largest contributions to pd observed among younger adults and those with financial difficulties, health limitations, or immigrant backgrounds. mattering was positively associated with qol ( β = 0.55, β std = 0.59) and pd negatively ( β = −0.81, β std = −0.29), both p < 0.001; the model explained 61% of qol variance. the difference in explained variance suggests that pd was more strongly patterned by the socio‐demographic factors included in the model than mattering. welfare policy and practice therefore need to address mattering and discrimination relationally and structurally. journal of community & applied social psychology

neural representation of chinese word classes: an ale meta-analysis of noun and verb processing whether nouns and verbs rely on distinct neural systems remains debated, particularly in chinese, which has limited inflectional morphology and flexible word-class use. we used activation likelihood estimation in gingerale 3.0.2 to synthesize task-based fmri/pet studies identified from three databases. twenty-three publications contributed 28 experiment-level contrast entries. the primary analyses compared 8 noun-versus-baseline and 15 verb-versus-baseline entries, using a pooled 23-entry reference; the original mixed inputs of 9 noun-associated and 19 verb-associated entries were retained as additional analyses. input maps used cluster-level family-wise error inference at p = 0.05, and final between-set contrasts used p = 0.05 with a 200 mm3 minimum cluster size. noun-related convergence was concentrated in the left parietal region, whereas verb-related convergence involved frontal and posterior regions. the primary comparison identified greater noun-related convergence in the left parietal and right claustral/insular regions and greater verb-related convergence in bilateral frontal and right posterior regions. the baseline-only conjunction yielded no suprathreshold cluster, while the additional analyses showed a broadly comparable pattern. together, these findings support partly differentiated neural processing of nouns and verbs in chinese. behavioral sciences

joint profiles and dimension-level networks of parental psychological control and problematic short-video use among chinese adolescents. problematic short-video use (psvu) is a pervasive public health concern among adolescents, yet its relationship with parental psychological control has typically been examined through variable-centered approaches that treat this relationship as uniform and combine paternal and maternal control. the present study therefore examined joint configurations of paternal and maternal psychological control and psvu, along with their dimension-level interrelations. using a two-stage design, latent profile and psychometric network analyses were applied to 2634 chinese adolescents. subgroups were first identified based on paternal psychological control, maternal psychological control, and psvu; dimension-level network structures were then compared across profiles to examine differences in the associations between parental control and psvu dimensions. the results revealed four distinct profiles: a high-control/high-dependence profile, a high-control/low-dependence profile, a low-control/low-dependence profile, and an average-control/moderate-dependence profile. the high-control, low-dependence profile reported higher control but significantly lower psvu. network comparisons indicated that the high-control, high-dependence profile exhibited significantly stronger global network connectivity than the high-control, low-dependence profile, whereas direct bridge pathways linking parental control to psvu dimensions did not differ significantly between the two profiles. these findings suggest that the parental control-psvu relationship is neither uniform nor direct, underscoring the value of integrating person-centered and network approaches. behavioral sciences

associated factors and cultivation strategies of positive social mentality among college students in the new era. background: in the context of the new era, college students' positive social mentality plays a pivotal role in their personal development and social harmony.
objective: this study aimed to examine the current status and correlates of positive social mentality among medical students, with a focus on gender, academic year, and socio-contextual factors.
methods: a cross-sectional survey was conducted with 123 undergraduate medical laboratory students using a self-developed questionnaire with strong psychometric properties (cronbach's α = 0.968; kmo = 0.883). the instrument assessed eight dimensions of positive social mentality (optimism, psychological resilience, self-efficacy, social responsibility, growth mindset, sense of belonging, value identity, and emotional regulation) and six categories of associated factors (family, school, online ecology, peer relationships, employment pressure, and policy perception). data were analyzed using t-tests, anova, and standardized multiple regression.
results: no statistically significant gender difference was found in the overall index or in any of the eight dimensions (all ≥ 0.208), and no dimension differed significantly across academic years (all ≥ 0.127); on average value identity scored highest and growth mindset lowest. standardized multiple regression revealed that school education was by far the strongest positive predictor (β = 0.68), followed by peer relationships (β = 0.18), family factors (β = 0.17) and policy perception (β = 0.16), while online ecology was negatively associated (β = -0.14) and employment pressure was not a significant predictor (β = -0.09, = 0.140); the six factors together explained 81% of the variance (r = 0.81).
conclusion: positive social mentality among medical students is associated with multiple interrelated environmental and relational factors rather than with gender or academic year. targeted, multi-level interventions addressing these factors are needed to foster students' psychological well-being and civic engagement. frontiers in psychology

beyond appearance: how clothing shapes self-confidence through self-expression and social identity in a collectivist context. using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design, this study examined how clothing relates to self-confidence among 312 bangladeshi university students (72. 4% male), testing whether the internal and external pathways described by enclothed cognition and impression management theory remain separable when the self is culturally construed as interdependent rather than independent. exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a provisional, internally cross-validated two-factor structure distinguishing self-expression and performance confidence from social identity and external influence confidence, though the two factors were strongly correlated (= 0.79), and a second-order model fit the data equivalently well. female students reported higher self-expression confidence than male students [t (310) = -3.48, p =0.001], and hierarchical regression showed that psychological predictors, social influence confidence and appearance-related academic-performance belief, explained substantial additional variance beyond demographics (δr= 0.356), together accounting for 39.4% of variance in self-expression confidence. thematic analysis of 22 interviews and 183 open-ended responses identified five themes: comfort and authenticity; clothing as context-specific "armor"; the social gaze; identity negotiation; and inner self-reliance, which converged with, complemented, and in one case qualified the quantitative findings. the strong association between internal and external confidence dimensions is consistent with self-construal theory and prior cross-cultural evidence that impression management operates more automatically for people from collectivist backgrounds, suggesting these pathways may be less distinguishable in this context than in the largely western samples on which the underlying theories were developed. the social identity dimension showed weaker psychometric performance and should be interpreted as exploratory. findings extend enclothed cognition and impression management theory to a collectivist south asian context and offer directions, rather than validated recommendations, for higher education, student counseling, career preparation, and fashion education. frontiers in psychology

does intelligence buffer or amplify personality effects? an experimental test in a brief frustration-induction paradigm. progress on the intelligence-personality interface increasingly depends on studying the processes through which the two combine. one such process is whether intelligence buffers or amplifies personality expression under stress. applied research reports such buffering for neuroticism on performance and conscientiousness on safety behavior, but not whether it extends to brief experimental contexts. we tested it with a mirror-tracing frustration paradigm with error-contingent penalties. psychology undergraduates (= 420 recruited; analytic= 334-378) completed intelligence measures, personality inventories (neo-ffi, bis/bas), and the panas pre- and post-task. the induction increased negative affect (= 0.78). neither hypothesis was supported, but the nulls are inconclusive: the design could detect only moderation well above the target magnitude, and equivalence tests could not exclude smaller effects. an exploratory analysis suggested, however, that intelligence may moderate a process rather than a trait: errors committed during frustration predicted affective change at higher levels of ability. this interaction held after residualizing errors on ability but did not survive bonferroni correction and requires confirmatory replication. the buffering-amplifying question appears underspecified as posed; we propose an agenda specifying context, process, outcome, and required sample sizes. journal of intelligence

personality profiles and self-efficacy among primary and secondary school teachers: a person-centered analysis. this study aimed to identify hexaco personality profiles among primary and secondary school teachers in china and examine their associations with teacher self-efficacy. based on data from 1895 teachers, latent profile analysis was used to identify distinct personality profiles. r3step and bch analyses were then conducted to examine the associations of demographic characteristics with profile membership and differences in teacher self-efficacy across profiles, respectively. finally, structural equation modeling (sem) was used to examine the associations between personality and teacher self-efficacy. three distinct personality profiles were identified: balanced, engaged, and resilient. teachers in the engaged and resilient profiles reported higher levels of self-efficacy than those in the balanced profile. extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, and openness to experience were positively associated with teacher self-efficacy. these findings provide empirical evidence for understanding personality heterogeneity among primary and secondary school teachers in china and its associations with teacher self-efficacy. behavioral sciences

personality traits as mediators of the relationship between affective distress and self-esteem among incarcerated youth: a parallel mediation model this study examined how affective distress, self-esteem, and personality traits are related among detained young adults, and how these factors connect to rehabilitation-relevant risk factors. the sample included 455 participants (18–25 years, m = 21.31, sd = 2.32; 97.8% male), recruited from educational, detention and prison centers. cp5f, rses, and pda were used, and analyses included mann–whitney tests, linear regression, and mediation models. the results showed that placement history predicted higher levels of depression and total distress, as well as lower self-esteem, while access to intimate visits was associated with lower levels of sadness and total distress. the diagnosis of chronic/psychiatric illness, suicide attempts, and trauma in the family of origin were associated with higher levels of distress, while diagnosis, suicide attempts, and a history of recidivism were also associated with lower self-esteem. in the regression model, depression was negatively associated with self-esteem, whereas concern showed a positive association (r2 = 0.18). in the parallel mediation model, the dysfunctional score was negatively associated with self-esteem both directly and indirectly, through extraversion, conscientiousness and emotional stability; autonomy showed no mediating effect and the indirect effect of agreeableness, significant in the individual model, became non-significant when tested alongside the other mediators. the total indirect effect and the direct effect were both significant in the parallel mediation model. the conclusions highlight the central role of affective distress in lowering self-esteem and support the need for early psychological screening and detention interventions aimed at reducing distress and strengthening emotional stability. behavioral sciences

the cost of mentalizing: executive contributions to social cognition performance in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. background: mentalizing deficits are common in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (als). performance at high-level socio-cognitive tasks may be particularly vulnerable to integrity of basic cognitive processes. however, the extent to which non-social functioning contributes to socio-cognitive impairment in als remains poorly understood. in this study, we addressed this question in a large cohort of patients.
methods: we assessed 257 als patients and 120 healthy controls using the story-based empathy task (set), which dissociates intention attribution (ia), emotion attribution (ea), and basic causal inference (ci). vectorial analyses were applied to quantify overall performance and imbalance between social and non-social components. mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the contribution of executive system integrity to social cognition performance in als.
results: patients showed significantly reduced performance across all set conditions compared to controls, with imbalance between mentalizing and basic causal inference. distinct profiles emerged across als phenotypes. als patients with behavioral changes exhibited predominant deficits in emotion attribution, whereas cognitively unimpaired als showed selective impairment in intention attribution. executive functioning was significantly associated with set performances and mediated the relationship between basic inference and both intention and emotion attribution.
discussion: mentalizing impairment in als reflects an interaction between executive processes and specialized socio-cognitive systems. the identification of dissociable profiles supports a dual-route, network-based model of als, involving socio-affective and inferential pathways, and underscores the importance of integrated cognitive assessment and more targeted interventions addressing both social and non-social cognitive domains. frontiers in psychology

racial discrimination, school climate, and black adolescents' internalizing and externalizing behaviors: a longitudinal moderation abstract using data from black adolescents in the adolescent brain cognitive development (abcd) study ( n = 1,316), we examined the moderating effect of school climate on the relationship between racial discrimination and later internalizing and externalizing behaviors during adolescence ( m age = 12.00; sd = 0.65). longitudinal regression analyses showed that positive perceptions of school climate were linked to a weaker association between racial discrimination and subsequent internalizing and externalizing behaviors. findings highlight the need to reduce discrimination that black youth face while simultaneously building safe and equitable school climates. journal of community psychology
“it’s quite a dark, long journey to the light at the end of the tunnel”: a qualitative study of children’s experiences of living with long covid psychology & health

group music activities and academic burnout among non-music-major college students with recent group music participation: a cross-sectional sem-fsqca study. academic burnout among college students is an important concern in educational psychology and student well-being. this cross-sectional study examined the associations among group music activity participation, social connectedness, collective effervescence, and academic burnout among non-music-major college students with recent group music participation. a questionnaire survey was conducted among 1027 college students in china who had participated in at least one group music activity during the previous semester. covariance-based structural equation modeling (cb-sem) was used to examine whether group music activity participation was associated with academic burnout directly and indirectly through social connectedness and collective effervescence, including a proposed sequence from social connectedness to collective effervescence. fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsqca) was further used to examine which combinations of group music activity participation, social connectedness, and collective effervescence were associated with low academic burnout. the sem results showed that higher group music activity participation was significantly associated with lower academic burnout. social connectedness and collective effervescence were involved in significant individual indirect associations, and the serial indirect association involving social connectedness followed by collective effervescence was also statistically supported. the fsqca results showed that no single condition constituted a necessary condition for low academic burnout. the joint presence of high group music activity participation, high social connectedness, and high collective effervescence formed a sufficient configuration associated with low academic burnout (consistency = 0.896, coverage = 0.647) under the present sample and analytical conditions. taken together, the findings suggest that group music participation, relational connectedness, and shared emotional experience are meaningfully associated with differences in academic burnout among non-music-major college students. these findings provide a complementary variable-centered and configurational perspective on the psychosocial correlates of group music participation and may inform future longitudinal research and campus-based student well-being initiatives. behavioral sciences

reading conflicting socio-scientific issue texts: visual and post-reading myside bias this study examined whether university students display myside bias during and after reading conflicting socio-scientific issue (ssi) texts about genetically modified foods. fifty-seven students read supporting and opposing claims while wearing eye-tracking glasses. visual myside bias, defined as greater visual attention to information consistent with readers’ pre-reading stance than to information inconsistent with that stance, was assessed using percent time spent (pts) and revisited fixation count (rfc) in myside and otherside areas of interest. prior knowledge, scientific epistemic beliefs, epistemic emotions, and a post-reading argument generation task were also assessed. students devoted significantly more visual attention to myside information on both pts and rfc, showing that myside bias emerged during reading as well as in post-reading argument generation. prior knowledge and scientific epistemic beliefs negatively predicted both visual and post-reading bias. negative epistemic emotions were positively correlated with both bias measures but were not significant after cognitive variables were controlled. longer viewing time and more frequent revisits did not necessarily indicate higher-quality informal reasoning; when directed toward myside information, they reflected stance-consistent processing. these findings provide process-based evidence of biased ssi reading and highlight knowledge and epistemic beliefs as potential supports for more balanced, evidence-oriented engagement with conflicting information. journal of eye movement research

collective future thinking over the russia-ukraine war: cross-national perspectives from poland and türkiye collective future thinking involves individuals’ imagining the future of the group they feel they belong to. in the present study, we examine how individuals from türkiye and poland, two countries with different sociocultural and geopolitical contexts, simulate the future of their own country and that of russia and ukraine in the context of the russia-ukraine war. participants ( n = 152) reported two future events that they expected to occur in russia, ukraine, and their own countries. the polish sample, which is closer to the war zone, imagined more war-related events, including energy crises and russian attacks, reflecting their negative attitudes toward russia. they also anticipated a more positive, emotionally intense future for ukraine, especially in the distant future, as poland holds a pro-ukrainian attitude. these findings suggest that perceptions and relationships between countries influence how people envision the future, shaped by socio-political and cultural factors specific to each country. memory studies

different timescales for generalized attraction and category-specific repulsion in numerosity perception the sense of number is a fundamental ability supported by dedicated neural mechanisms. because natural scenes often contain multiple object groups, numerosity may be encoded in a category-specific manner. consistent with this idea, adaptation effects are reduced when adaptor and test stimuli differ in category, particularly when category signals object identity (e.g., color but not motion). we asked whether this category-selectivity extends to other stimulus-history effects. integrating past information into current perception may support the formation of discrete object representations from continuous input. accordingly, both session-level (central tendency) and trial-level (serial dependence) biases may be category-tuned. we tested this hypothesis by manipulating color and motion features, each defining categories mapped to distinct numerosity ranges, presented either in blocked or interleaved sessions. overall, we observed a comparable pattern across color and motion. at the session level, blocked presentations revealed a perceptual effect opposite to the compression predicted by range-specific central tendency. interleaving abolished this effect and promoted convergence toward a prior shared across categories. at the trial level, the interleaved presentation provided both category repetitions and alternations, allowing us to examine how history effects unfold as a function of temporal lag and category match. we observed a characteristic temporal profile, with short-lag attraction, intermediate neutrality, and long-lag repulsion. notably, attraction was category-independent, whereas repulsion was selectively observed for category repetitions. overall, these findings show that multiple stimulus-history effects shape numerosity perception depending on the temporal and categorical structure of the environment, with category-selectivity primarily emerging in the repulsive bias. i-perception

psilocybin enhances conditioned place preference learning in planarians psilocybin has emerged as a promising therapeutic agent, with clinical benefits attributed to enhanced neuroplasticity rather than acute pharmacological effects. however, the fundamental mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. using planarians as a model system, we investigated whether psilocybin enhances associative learning using a conditioned place preference paradigm. following a single exposure to 5 µm psilocybin, planarians underwent 5 days of conditioning in which light was paired with sucrose. psilocybin-treated planarians showed a significantly greater shift in light preference compared to controls (time × group × drug interaction: f (2,38) = 3.3, p < 0.05), with effects persisting at least 6 days post-administration. these findings demonstrate that psilocybin enhances appetitive associative learning in an invertebrate model, supporting the hypothesis that psychedelic-induced neuroplasticity operates through evolutionarily conserved serotonergic mechanisms. behavioural pharmacology

predicting climate adaptation intention and collective climate action abstract: individual adaptation to climate hazards (e.g., create an emergency plan) and collective climate action (e.g., participate in a protest) arises from the interplay of numerous variables. traditional linear models often fail to capture this complexity. this study employed a supervised machine learning (ml) approach to address two questions: first, how accurately ml models – incorporating a theory-transcendent set of 94 variables ranging from trust in relevant actors to climate emotions – predict climate adaptation intention and collective climate action compared to sparse, linear models based on established theories; and second, which variables are most important for these predictions. data were collected in 2024 from 4,246 participants in the united kingdom, italy, germany, and the united states using representative quota sampling. we applied models of varying complexity, including three ml algorithms (elastic net, random forest, gradient boosted decision trees), to predict climate adaptation intention and collective climate action. the ml algorithms substantially improved predictive performance beyond linear regressions grounded in established theories, particularly due to their capacity to model numerous variables. climate emotions (particularly enthusiasm, guilt, and isolation), general coping styles and age were key predictors of both climate adaptation intention and collective climate action. additionally, media exposure to climate change and extreme weather, along with social support for these issues, emerged as important predictors. these findings underscore the complexity of predicting climate adaptation and mitigation efforts due to the large number of interacting variables. we discuss potential leverage points for future research, such as climate emotions and the social amplification of climate change impacts through media and interpersonal channels. european psychologist

counselor burnout: scope, consequences, and a five‐step intervention framework for sustainable practice abstract counselor burnout remains a persistent threat to practitioner well‐being, ethical decision‐making, and client outcomes. recent national surveys and workforce briefs document high demand, constrained capacity, administrative barriers, and growing clinician burnout, especially among early‐career practitioners. converging evidence links burnout to diminished therapeutic effectiveness and premature dropout, elevating the urgency for proactive, evidence‐informed approaches. this article synthesizes current literature and introduces reset, a pragmatic five‐step framework for counselors: (1) r ecognize early warning signs through regular self‐monitoring, (2) e valuate contributing factors including workload, systemic barriers, and personal stressors, (3) s trategize evidence‐informed self‐care and recovery strategies, (4) e ngage professional support and supervision, and (5) t ransform professional roles and reconnect with purpose. we discuss implications for counselor education and training, supervision, and organizational policy, and outline directions for research that close the research–practice gap. journal of counseling and development

the role of self-esteem in parent–child conflict and problematic smartphone use among adolescents: a three-wave cross-lagged study although prior research has linked parent–child conflict to problematic smartphone use (psu), most evidence is cross-sectional, leaving the directionality unclear. guided by the interaction of person–affect–cognition–execution (i-pace) model, this three-wave longitudinal study examined the reciprocal links between parent–child conflict and psu and the mediating role of self-esteem. chinese adolescents (n = 1368; 40% female; mage = 16.05, sd = 0.85 at baseline) completed self-report measures of parent–child conflict, self-esteem, and psu at six-month intervals. cross-lagged panel models (clpms) were the primary analysis, and random-intercept clpms (ri-clpms) served as a sensitivity analysis. clpms showed bidirectional predictions between parent–child conflict and psu, with t2 self-esteem mediating both indirect paths. ri-clpms revealed significant between-person associations among parent–child conflict, self-esteem, and psu; at the within-person level, only t1 parent–child conflict prospectively predicted t2 psu, whereas the reverse path and within-person mediation were not significant. these findings suggested that the longitudinal link between parent–child conflict and psu may partly reflect stable between-person differences, with only limited within-person prospective evidence for a conflict-to-psu pathway. behavioral sciences

object speed and distractor number affect performance but not attentional allocation in multiple object tracking abstract keeping track of multiple moving objects across dynamic real-world scenarios such as driving, team sports, or crowded social environments is a fundamental challenge for visual attention. we have previously demonstrated that as the number of tracked objects increases, the strength of attentional facilitation allocated to each individual object decreases, limiting tracking success. it is also well established that beyond the number of tracked objects, faster-moving objects and objects embedded amongst higher numbers of distractors are more difficult to track. are these effects on tracking difficulty also mediated by less effective allocation of attention to tracked targets as in the case of tracking more targets? if so, one should expect the strength of attentional modulation to drop systematically with increasing speed and total number of moving stimuli. in two experiments (total n = 70), participants were instructed to track moving targets amongst identical distractors while we manipulated object speed (experiment 1) and number (experiment 2). as expected, tracking performance declined with both manipulations. however, steady-state visual evoked potentials (ssveps) recorded during successful tracking revealed that attentional enhancement of tracked targets compared with distractors did not drop with increasing speed or object number. in summary, bottom-up changes in the stimulus display and top-down attentional manipulations affect tracking performance in independent ways, with the balance between strength of attentional allocation and bottom-up demands of the task determining successful tracking. the allocation of attention itself seems to be determined exclusively by top-down goals rather than being reactive to bottom-up display characteristics. significance statement keeping track of multiple moving objects is fundamental to navigating dynamic real-world scenarios. this ability is accomplished through multifocal attentional selection, which weakens as the number of tracked targets increases. this study asks whether other stimulus manipulations increase tracking difficulty by diluting attentional allocation. using steady-state visual evoked potentials to measure selective attention during tracking, we demonstrate that both increases in speed and distractor number impair performance, but they do not affect attentional enhancement of targets relative to distractors. this suggests that top-down attentional control operates independently from bottom-up demands. attention perception & psychophysics
the temporal dynamics of semantic guidance in scenes attention perception & psychophysics

examining racism-based police violence and mental health among black african emerging adults in the united states: the moderating roles of grit and family cohesion in the united states, black americans are disproportionately likely to experience racism-based police violence (rpv), which has led scholars and practitioners alike to call this a public health crisis. although this is not a recent phenomenon, the existing literature has limited its examination of rpv exposure and mental health trauma to the black american experience, ignoring that racial identity alone is not the only identity that is factored into racism-based violence against black african individuals. this cross-sectional study, therefore, adds to the existing literature on rpv and trauma literature by examining three forms of rpv exposure—direct victimization, in-person witnessing, and media-based exposure—and their relationship with depression, police contact anxiety, and suicidality, while exploring the buffer relationship of grit and family cohesion among first and second-generation black african emerging adults (aged 18–29). findings from this study highlight that exposure to all three forms of rpv is directly associated with police contact anxiety, with rpv-media-based exposure being significantly related to suicidal ideation. importantly, this study demonstrated the existence of generational differences. moderation analyses examining whether family cohesion and grit moderate the effects of rpv showed that, among first-generation emerging adults, neither family cohesion nor grit had a significant moderating effect on any form of rpv; among second-generation emerging adults, family cohesion had a significant association between rpv-media and police contact anxiety. the findings support the need for future research to perform longitudinal studies on rpv and mental trauma in black african emerging adults. journal of interpersonal violence

dating violence in adolescence: an exploratory study on personality traits, legitimizing attitudes and prevalence dating violence is recognized as a global priority for research and intervention. although legitimizing attitudes toward dating violence and personality traits are considered risk factors, their joint contribution to adolescent dating violence remains limited. this study aimed to characterize the prevalence of dating violence among adolescents and its associations with legitimizing attitudes, neuroticism and agreeableness. the study included 410 portuguese adolescents aged 14 to 19 years ( m = 17.18, sd = 1.39). participants completed a sociodemographic questionnaire, the conflict in adolescent dating relationships inventory–short form, the attitudes toward dating violence scale and the mini international personality item pool. results showed that 57.3% of adolescent reported perpetrating at least one form of dating violence and 58.9% reported victimization, with verbal/emotional violence being the most prevalent subtype. no significant gender, developmental stage, or interaction effects was found for overall dating violence perpetration and victimization. however, significant main effects of gender and developmental stage, as well as significant gender × developmental stage interactions, were observed for legitimizing attitudes toward psychological and physical dating violence. boys reported higher legitimizing attitudes than girls during middle adolescence, whereas no gender differences were observed during late adolescence. moreover, only boys showed a significant decline in legitimizing attitudes from middle to late adolescence. perpetration and victimization were positively associated. neuroticism and agreeableness were associated with perpetration, but only neuroticism was associated with victimization. legitimizing attitudes explained additional variance beyond traits. these findings support prevention programs targeting violence-supportive beliefs during adolescence and inform future research on the interplay among personality traits, legitimizing attitudes and dating violence. journal of interpersonal violence

school climate, victimisation and anti-bullying self-efficacy: a multilevel study of primary school students bullying is a pervasive issue in schools, negatively impacting students’ psychological well-being, academic performance and social development. understanding the factors that relate with students’ ability to cope with bullying is crucial for developing effective interventions. this study explores the relationship between bullying victimisation, school climate (broken into three factors including teacher support and fairness of rules, peer relationships and school liking and safety) and students’ anti-bullying self-efficacy in a national sample of irish primary students. data were collected from 566 primary school students through two questionnaires administered between 2023 and 2024. a multilevel linear regression was conducted to analyse the relationship of bullying victimisation and the school climate indices with anti-bullying self-efficacy, while accounting for the nested structures of the data. results revealed that bullying victimisation was negatively associated with anti-bullying self-efficacy (β = −.14, p < .01), whereas teacher support and fairness of rules (β = .13, p < .05) and peer relationships (β = .11, p < .05) were positively associated with anti-bullying self-efficacy. these findings suggest that anti-bullying programmes should not only focus on enhancing students’ individual coping resources but also prioritise fostering a supportive and inclusive school environment. journal of interpersonal violence

red culture immersion and psychological wellbeing among chinese college students: the mediating role of collective self-esteem and the moderating role of psychological resilience. introduction: red culture, the cultural legacy forged by the chinese people under the leadership of the communist party of china during revolution, construction, and reform, is increasingly integrated into university education in china. however, the psychological mechanisms through which immersion in red culture contributes to college students' psychological wellbeing remain largely unexplored. drawing on social identity theory, the present study examined whether collective self-esteem mediates the relationship between red culture immersion and psychological wellbeing, and whether psychological resilience moderates these pathways.
methods: a cross-sectional survey was conducted with 612 chinese college students (46.2% male; m age = 19.92, sd = 1.31) recruited from two universities in jiangsu province, china. participants completed validated measures of red culture immersion, collective self-esteem, psychological resilience, and psychological wellbeing. a moderated mediation model was tested using structural equation modeling with latent interaction terms and bias-corrected bootstrap analyses (5,000 resamples).
results: red culture immersion was positively associated with psychological wellbeing ( = 0.25, < 0.001), and collective self-esteem partially mediated this relationship (indirect effect = 0.13, 95% ci [0.08, 0.18]). psychological resilience moderated both the second stage of the mediation pathway and the direct pathway: the positive association between collective self-esteem and psychological wellbeing was stronger among students with high resilience ( = 0.43, < 0.001) than among those with low resilience ( = 0.19, < 0.001), and the direct effect of red culture immersion on psychological wellbeing was similarly amplified by resilience. the index of moderated mediation was significant (index = 0.10, 95% ci [0.05, 0.16]).
discussion: immersion in red culture is associated with college students' psychological wellbeing partly through stronger collective self-esteem, and this beneficial process is particularly pronounced among psychologically resilient students. these findings extend social identity theory to the domain of red culture education and carry practical implications for integrating red culture resources into university mental health education. frontiers in psychology

enhancing flexibility mindset: a randomized controlled trial using daily emotion-focused self-reflection. introduction: flexibility mindset has recently been proposed as a motivational factor that supports adaptive self-regulation during adversity, yet it remains unknown whether it can be strengthened through psychological intervention. the present randomized controlled trial examined whether a brief daily emotion-focused self-reflection intervention designed to cultivate six emotional resources (authentic pride, awe, flow, gratitude, relaxation, and vicarious joy) would increase flexibility mindset and improve mental health outcomes.
methods: forty-four university students were randomly assigned to either an intervention group or an active control group and were instructed to complete daily micro-exercises over a three-week period. assessments were conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and a two-week follow-up and included measures of flexibility mindset, depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, positive affect, and negative affect.
results: participants in the intervention group showed significant increases in flexibility mindset from pre to post (within-group= 0.91) and from pre to follow-up (within-group= 1.05), whereas no significant changes were observed in the active control group. between-group contrasts confirmed greater increases in the intervention group at both assessments. across both conditions, higher flexibility mindset was associated with higher positive affect at post and follow-up after adjustment for baseline flexibility mindset, baseline positive affect, and group, with both associations remaining significant after holm correction. depressive symptoms, anxiety, and stress decreased significantly over time across conditions, whereas no significant change in negative affect was detected.
conclusion: to our knowledge, this is the first randomized controlled study to provide evidence that flexibility mindset may be amenable to psychological intervention. the findings suggest that the deliberate cultivation of emotional resources may represent a promising pathway for strengthening motivational processes relevant to adaptive self-regulation. further research is needed to examine underlying mechanisms, long-term effects, and generalizability across populations and contexts. frontiers in psychology

integrating control-mastery theory and emdr in the treatment of attachment-related trauma: pathogenic beliefs, testing processes, and target selection. attachment-related trauma often develops through repeated relational experiences involving emotional misattunement, role reversal, inconsistent caregiving, and chronic threats to relational security. such experiences may contribute to pathogenic beliefs concerning dependency, responsibility, emotional expression, and interpersonal safety, while making the identification of clinically meaningful targets for trauma processing particularly complex. this paper proposes a clinical-theoretical integration of control-mastery theory (cmt) and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (emdr) for the treatment of attachment-related trauma. drawing on the cmt concepts of pathogenic beliefs and testing, we suggest that relational processes within therapy may provide clinically useful information about the beliefs currently organizing the patient's difficulties. observation of passive-into-active, transference, and direct tests may help clinicians formulate and refine hypotheses about the relational meanings linking present difficulties to developmental experiences. when integrated with standard aip-informed history-taking and emdr target assessment, this information may contribute to the prioritization of candidate attachment-related memories for processing. the paper also introduces the concept of relational readiness as a complementary dimension of emdr case conceptualization, referring to the extent to which pathogenic relational expectations have become sufficiently observable within the therapeutic relationship to inform target formulation, without replacing established considerations of stabilization, affect tolerance, or readiness for trauma processing. a clinical illustration is presented to demonstrate the proposed sequence from relational testing and disconfirmation to emdr target formulation and processing. the model is intended as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than an empirically validated treatment protocol, and its incremental clinical value requires systematic investigation. frontiers in psychology

health behavior, loneliness and social participation among students in a higher education institution: a community case study providing insights into health psychology. background: higher education institutions can be conceptualized asthat may facilitate individuals' health and well-being (in terms of low loneliness), health behavior, and general social participation. however, facilitating factors in individuals, their social network, and contextual factors were not researched building on theand the.
objective: in a community case study, students' health behavior, loneliness, and social participation were investigated to determine interrelations and factors that help students maintain a healthy lifestyle, reduce loneliness, and increase social participation.
method: we analyzed an online survey of 373 students using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, regression models, and exploratory curve estimation.
results: of 293 students with available loneliness data, the mean loneliness was = 2.76 (sd = 1.06; range 1-4), and 122 (41.6%) were classified as lonely. loneliness was reflected in private relationships and study-related contacts, whereas no significant association was found with studying/working from home, χ(1) = 0.11; = 0.74. lonely students differed from not-lonely students across 10 behavioral domains, including talking to a doctor, watching films, spending time in nature, interacting with others online, listening to music, drinking alcohol, eating, and shopping. for a healthy lifestyle, the regression results highlighted psychological resources and perceived health: self-efficacy predicted the healthy lifestyle indicator in step 1 (or = 2.40), and health literacy responsibility was significant in step 2 (or = 1.78), but poor subjective health was the strongest predictor in the final model (or = 0.52; = 0.21). loneliness was negatively associated with social participation (ß = -0.30), but this association weakened when further psychological and contextual factors were considered. exploratory curve estimation indicated an inverted u-shaped association between stress and social participation among not-lonely students ( = 0.09; = 0.03), whereas this pattern was not statistically significant among lonely students.
conclusion: students' loneliness should not be understood as social disconnection, but as part of a broader health-psychological pattern involving health and well-being, psychological resources, contextual factors, and social participation within the higher education community. frontiers in psychology

effects of physical activity intervention on active ageing and physical function among older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. background: although the health benefits of physical activity for older adults have attracted extensive scholarly attention, existing systematic reviews mostly focus on a single outcome domain. few studies have simultaneously performed quantitative synthesis of active ageing and physical function within a unified analytical framework.
objective: registered on (prospero registration: crd420261465400), this systematic review and meta-analysis comprehensively evaluated the effects of physical activity intervention on active ageing (global active ageing, mental health, social participation, functional health) and physical function (sppb, chair stand test, tug, gait speed, handgrip strength, balance) among older adults.
methods: three databases including pubmed, web of science and cnki were searched to retrieve peer-reviewed chinese and english randomized controlled trials (rcts) published up to july 1, 2026. the cochrane risk of bias tool was adopted to assess the methodological quality of included studies.
results: a total of 25 rcts with a combined sample size of 7,861 participants were incorporated. for the active ageing domain, global active ageing (smd = 1.38, 95%ci = [0.54, 2.22], = 0.001), social participation (smd = 1.03, 95%ci = [0.87, 1.20], < 0.00001) and mental health (smd = 0.6, 95%ci = [0.17, 1.03], = 0.006) exhibited statistically significant improvements, whereas functional health showed no significant between-group difference ( = 0.07). in terms of physical function, significant improvements were observed in sppb (smd = 0.33, 95%ci = [0.07, 0.58], = 0.01), chair stand test (smd = 0.37, 95%ci = [0.10, 0.63], = 0.006) and tug (smd = -0.68, 95%ci = [-1.16, -0.20], = 0.006). no significant effects were detected for gait speed, handgrip strength and balance. subgroup analyses provided exploratory insights into potential moderators of intervention effects. for mental health outcomes, twice-weekly interventions yielded significant within-group improvements, whereas three-times-weekly interventions did not reach statistical significance. however, formal between-subgroup comparison showed no statistically significant difference in effect magnitude across frequency strata, so these frequency-based findings remain hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger studies.
conclusion: physical activity intervention significantly improves multiple dimensions of active ageing and partial physical function indicators in older adults, yet the ameliorative effects present domain-specific and indicator-specific characteristics. these findings yield preliminary evidence for physical-activity-related benefits across select active-aging and physical-function domains, though optimal intervention modality, frequency, intensity and duration remain undefined, precluding definitive program-design guidance from current evidence. frontiers in psychology

outdoor education on the mental health of chinese children: a mini-review. children's mental health is an increasing concern in education and public health. outdoor education and related outdoor activities have therefore received growing attention. however, definitions of outdoor education remain inconsistent, and evidence concerning chinese children is fragmented. this review addresses two questions: what is outdoor education, and what potential implications may it have for the mental health of children in china? drawing on the prisma reporting framework, we searched web of science and scopus, supplemented by google scholar, and included 18 english-language empirical studies. sources were synthesized narratively: conceptual sources clarified the definition of outdoor education, whereas empirical studies were classified as direct or closely related intervention evidence or as indirect evidence concerning related outdoor and nature-based activities. outdoor education is understood as structured, goal-oriented, experience-based learning in outdoor or natural settings, often aligned with educational objectives. few studies in the retrieved english-language literature directly evaluated structured outdoor education programmes among chinese children. this apparent scarcity may partly reflect the english-language restriction and the omission of chinese-language databases, rather than the full extent of research in china. studies of related activities, including nature contact, horticultural activity, and outdoor physical activity, were considered as indirect or adjacent evidence. overall, the available evidence suggests that structured outdoor and nature-based educational activities may be associated with favorable emotional, social, and self-regulatory outcomes. by distinguishing direct from indirect evidence, this review clarifies the current evidence base and provides a foundation for contextually appropriate program development and future research in chinese children. frontiers in psychology

the longitudinal association between disability and loneliness among older adults in china: an urban-rural comparative analysis. loneliness is a major mental health concern among older adults and has been increasingly linked to functional decline in later life. this study aimed to inform targeted care strategies by exploring urban-rural differences in the longitudinal association between disability and loneliness among older adults in china. data were obtained from 6654 adults aged 60 and older across three waves (2016, 2018, 2020) of the china longitudinal aging social survey (class). disability was measured with activities of daily living (adl) scale, and loneliness was measured with self-report items. cross-lagged panel models (clpms) were constructed separately to examine the longitudinal associations for urban and rural older adults. rural older adults reported higher levels of loneliness than urban older adults, and older women reported higher levels of loneliness than older men. loneliness predicted increased disability at subsequent waves in urban and rural older adults. disability predicted increased loneliness at subsequent waves only among rural older adults, not among urban older adults. disability and loneliness were longitudinally associated among older adults in china, with notable urban-rural differences. integrated physical and psychological interventions are critical in rural areas, whereas strategies should prioritize early loneliness screening to prevent subsequent functional decline in urban areas. behavioral sciences

visualizer cognitive style modulates the operation of object-based attention in processing bindings in visual working memory. this study aims to investigate how visualizer cognitive style modulates the operation of object-based attention in processing bindings in visual working memory (vwm). two behavioral experiments and one event-related potential (erp) experiment were carried out. the revised chinese version of the object-spatial imagery questionnaire was used to divide participants into object visualizers (ovs) and spatial visualizers (svs). participants maintained bindings in vwm alongside an interpolated task consuming object-based attention. the results of the behavioral experiments showed that, compared with svs, ovs maintained bindings more stably but showed a larger cost when object-based attention was consumed. the erp results showed that for ovs, when object-based attention was consumed, the p2 was reduced during vwm encoding, and the late positive component was enhanced during performance of the interpolated task. however, these modulations were absent for svs. these findings suggest that visualizer cognitive style is associated with differences in binding stability, reliance on object-based attention, and resource engagement across vwm stages, advancing our understanding of how object-based attention contributes to the binding process in vwm. frontiers in psychology

economic status and decision-making behavior: the cost of cognitive control. economic poverty entails material deprivation and life unpredictability, imposing heavier external constraints on low-income individuals' goal pursuit than on their higher-income counterparts. we hypothesized that relative economic disadvantage fosters situation-driven decision-making among lower-income groups, which consumes cognitive resources and may impair performance in other cognitive domains. two experiments were conducted. experiment 1 (= 41) used a pre/post stroop task design around a product choice task to examine cognitive control changes; experiment 2 (n = 903, online) examined decision-making tendencies using a similar product choice task. in experiment 1, income percentile was marginally and negatively associated with post-task cognitive-control decline (i.e., lower-income participants tended to show greater decline) (= -0.31,= 0.05) and was not significantly correlated with decoy susceptibility (= -0.23,= 0.15); the directions of both associations were consistent with our predictions. because the sample was small and the study was explicitly exploratory, these results should be regarded as preliminary rather than conclusive. experiment 2 showed that lower-income participants showed significantly higher decoy susceptibility (= -0.22,< 0.001) and significantly slower decisions (= -0.24,< 0.001). taken together, the well-powered results of experiment 2, together with the directionally consistent pattern of experiment 1, indicate that economic disadvantage is associated with greater reliance on external contextual cues and greater cognitive expenditure during decision-making. because experiment 2 did not include a direct measure of cognitive control, whether such decision styles in turn impair subsequent cognitive control awaits direct testing. behavioral sciences

pupil size automatically tracks and predicts the complexity of visual information abstract stimulus complexity is a fundamental constraint on the human visual system to summarize scenes into manageable representations. although the pupil is known to reflect cognitive load, its role in processing visual complexity remains largely unexplored. in four experiments exploring orientation ensemble perception, we found that pupil size serves as a dynamic indicator of stimulus complexity, which was measured by entropy. experiment 1 showed that pupillary constriction decreased (resulting in a larger pupil) as orientation distributions became more dispersed, a change that tracked increases in behavioral adjustment errors. experiment 2 revealed that these pupillary adjustments occurred automatically during passive viewing and correlated with individual differences in perceptual sensitivity. experiment 3 showed that these automatic pupillary adjustments emerged even when participants never performed any task and purely passively viewed the bar arrays throughout the entire session. finally, experiment 4 demonstrated that the pupil adjusted predictively in response to cues signaling upcoming stimulus complexity. collectively, our findings suggest that the pupil plays an active, predictive role in visual summarization: it dilates to gather more information from complex stimuli, thereby optimizing the encoding of summary statistics at the earliest stage of the visual hierarchy. psychophysiology

baselines matter: cardiovascular baseline procedures in affective psychophysiology abstract a baseline is necessary to define biological reactivity in psychophysiological research. however, the conceptualization and implementation of baseline measurements are often underdescribed and weakly justified. this poses a problem because poor baseline decisions have the potential to introduce noise, reduce comparability across studies, and bias interpretations of data. in this article, we focus on laboratory studies using cardiovascular measures in affective psychophysiology. motivated by substantial variation and limited reporting of baseline procedures, we examined within‐baseline stabilization in two studies. study 1 analyzed 1593 baseline sessions from 1310 participants in the popane and cepav datasets. study 2 assessed generalizability using data from 2395 participants collected in a u.s. laboratory. findings suggest that although different cardiovascular indices may stabilize differently during a 5‐min baseline, this procedure is a reasonable, pragmatic choice. more broadly, findings highlight the need for stronger justification, standardization, and reporting of baseline procedures in psychophysiological research. psychophysiology
