a study on the factors associated with college students’ intention to use ai-based mental health services: the roles of trust, empathy, and privacy concern artificial intelligence technology is gradually being integrated into mental health service contexts and is increasingly discussed as a potential supplementary resource to university mental health support systems. however, ai-based mental health services involve sensitive factors such as emotional expression, personal privacy, and relational interaction. therefore, college students’ willingness to accept ai-based mental health services and the potential factors associated with such acceptance remain unclear. based on an extended technology acceptance model, this study introduces six factors—accessibility (acc), privacy concern (pc), perceived anthropomorphism (pa), perceived empathy (emp), trust (tru), and perceived usefulness (pu)—to systematically examine their relationships with university students’ behavioral intention (bi) to use ai-based mental health services. a total of 375 volunteers participated in the current study and completed relevant questionnaires. structural equation modeling was employed for data analysis. the results indicate that accessibility, perceived usefulness, and trust are all significantly and positively associated with behavioral intention. perceived empathy is significantly and positively associated with trust, whereas privacy concern is significantly and negatively associated with both trust and behavioral intention. the analysis of indirect effects shows that there is a significant sequential indirect association between perceived anthropomorphism and behavioral intention through perceived empathy, trust, and perceived usefulness. in addition, a significant negative indirect association between privacy concern and behavioral intention through trust was observed. the findings indicate that, in the highly sensitive context of mental health services, college students’ intention to use ai-based mental health services is associated with a combination of accessibility, perceived usefulness, emotional interaction experience, privacy-related evaluations, and trust. behavioral sciences

the impact of configurational fit of product and service on customer decision-making: evidence from an event-related potential experiment. artificial intelligence provides new approaches for smart product-service systems. as such, an increasing number of service-oriented manufacturing enterprises are leveraging artificial intelligence (ai) to achieve value co-creation with customers. in the process of intelligently matching additional services to products, measuring the congruity of product-service systems remains to be explored. this study employs an event-related potential (erp) methodology to examine how product-service congruity influences customer purchase intentions associated with cognitive processing. erps elicited by high-congruity product-service combinations were significantly different from low-congruity combinations. by proposing a method to determine product-service congruity, this study provides insights for matching product-service combinations in an ai-driven context. these findings can guide the delivery of enhanced personalized product-service combinations in platform economies and ai ecosystems, enabling enterprises to achieve value co-creation. behavioral sciences

the weight of junk food: smaller hippocampal, amygdala, and prefrontal volumes in adolescents—the cogni‐action project abstract most studies investigating diet–brain relationships in youth focus on single foods. whether the joint consumption of multiple food groups is associated with neuroanatomy during adolescence remains largely unexplored, particularly outside high‐income countries. in this cross‐sectional study, 61 chilean adolescents (11.6 ± 1.07 years; 42.6% girls) underwent t1‐weighted mri. volumes of total gray matter, hippocampus, amygdala, and selected prefrontal regions were extracted. dietary intake was assessed using the global food quality index questionnaire. confounder‐adjusted linear regressions examined individual food group–brain associations, with correction for multiple comparisons. canonical correlation analysis (cca) was used to identify multivariate food group–brain covariation with permutation‐based inference. univariate analyses showed a significant inverse association between pastry consumption and hippocampal volume (β = −0.402, 95% ci: −0.571 to −0.228, adjusted r 2 = 0.34). cca identified one significant multivariate mode linking higher unhealthy food consumption to brain volumes ( r = −0.70, p = .008). pastries, fried foods, and soft drinks showed the strongest contributions, whereas the corresponding brain variate was characterized by smaller hippocampal, amygdala, and anterior cingulate/prefrontal volumes. in conclusion, higher consumption of unhealthy food groups is associated with smaller limbic–prefrontal volumes in adolescents. although causality cannot be inferred from these cross‐sectional data, these findings highlight adolescence as a critical window for diet–brain health research. applied psychology-health and well being

are interpersonal relationships predictors or outcomes of psychological distress in children with special educational needs abstract psychological distress is more prevalent in adolescents with special educational needs than in typically developing adolescents. despite previous evidence and theories for the association between interpersonal relationships and psychological distress, longitudinal research is lacking to investigate the temporal association between interpersonal relationships and psychological distress. the two‐wave longitudinal study aimed to investigate the reciprocal association between interpersonal relationships and psychological distress in a sample of adolescents with special educational needs. the study involved 580 high school students in the project. students completed online inventories twice with an assessment interval of 1 year to measure adolescent‐parent relationships, peer relationships, and sibling relationships, as well as psychological distress, with the assistance of teachers. the cross‐lagged panel models suggested that adolescent‐parent relationships and peer relationships at the first wave did not predict psychological distress at the second wave. high psychological distress at the first wave predicted poor adolescent‐parent relationships and poor peer relationships at the second wave. good sibling relationships at the first wave predicted low psychological distress at the second wave. however, psychological distress at the first wave did not predict sibling relationships at the second wave. the findings suggested that for adolescents with special educational needs, adolescent‐parent relationships and peer relationships were the consequences rather than the predictors of psychological distress, and sibling relationships were the predictors rather than the consequences of psychological distress, which provided implications for theories and psychoeducational interventions for adolescents with special educational needs. stress and health
from self-regulation to character: digital well-being intervention effects on character strengths and subsequent distress journal of positive psychology

how disgust and fear influence strategic aspects of arithmetic performance in children and adolescents this study is the first to combine a strategy perspective with a typological approach to emotions to determine how disgust and fear influence arithmetic performance in children and adolescents. in experiment 1, 10–11-year-old (n = 32) and 14–15-year-old (n = 32) participants were asked to choose between two rounding strategies, whereas in experiment 2, a different sample of 10–11-year-old (n = 32) and 14–15-year-old (n = 32) participants executed instructed rounding strategies to estimate the sums of two-digit addition problems following either emotionally neutral or negative (disgust- or fear-inducing) pictures. negative emotions led participants to select the better strategy less frequently and different patterns of associations between problem characteristics and better-strategy selection were observed across emotion conditions: whereas selection was associated with the difference of deviations, a diagnostic strategy-selection cue, in the neutral condition, it was associated with problem-magnitude information in the negative-emotion condition. negative emotions also slowed strategy execution, with participants being slower under disgust than under fear. moreover, disgust reduced response accuracy relative to the neutral condition in 10–11-year-old children but not in 14–15-year-old adolescents. in contrast, the effects of negative emotions on better-strategy selection and strategy execution latencies did not significantly differ between age groups. these findings have important implications for furthering our understanding of how negative emotions influence arithmetic performance in particular, and cognitive performance in general, both in children and adolescents. journal of intelligence

self-esteem as a shared resource beyond romantic relationships: an extension into friendships and parental relationships self-esteem is an important factor in understanding relationship quality, for both the individual and their romantic partner. yet, most research has focused on solely romantic relationships, neglecting other close relationships that are at least equally important for understanding humans. in the present analysis, introductory psychology students at a canadian university and their significant other (romantic partner, close friend, or primary caregiver) completed measures of self-esteem and relationship quality ( n = 308 dyads). actor-partner interdependence model analyses replicated and extended robinson and cameron’s (2012) findings that the higher dyad members’ combined self-esteem, the higher the dyad-level relationship quality. thus, self-esteem may serve as a shared resource in romantic, friend, and family relationships. journal of social and personal relationships

cognitive disorganization in help-seeking youth: a transdiagnostic developmental formulation perspective abstract cognitive disorganization in help-seeking youth can involve difficulties with attention, task sequencing, language access, or discourse organization alongside unusual experiences and functional decline. this perspective proposes a transdiagnostic developmental approach to clinical formulation using four complementary questions: what is the young person’s developmental baseline; which functions vary within the person across load, context, and time; what is happening in the environment and how is threat interpreted; and do established clinical-risk indicators require formal assessment or referral? the questions address different assessment tasks, may be considered together, and constitute a proposed clinical heuristic. assessment of genuine environmental harm, safeguarding needs, and urgent medical or psychiatric risk takes precedence over explanatory interpretation. the synthesis distinguishes direct evidence from adjacent findings and clinical hypotheses. acute-stress research supports effects on specified executive outcomes under studied conditions; extrapolation to discourse organization, threat meanings, or reality testing in help-seeking youth remains insufficiently supported. stress sensitivity is therefore a domain-specific formulation hypothesis to test, not an established property of the presentation. the proposed contribution is to organize established assessment domains around observable difficulties and documented uncertainty. prospective studies should measure domains separately and assess reliability, incremental clinical value, and safety against explicit alternative explanations and falsification criteria. discover psychology
less care, more respect: low concern about social evaluation signals competence journal of social psychology

from hope to subjective well-being: examining the career construction model of adaptation among turkish adolescents adolescence is a crucial period for individuals to make decisions that will impact their future. in this sense, the career construction model of adaptation (ccma) can shed light on a better understanding of career development during adolescence by providing a framework for how positive career outcomes are achieved. the purpose of this study is to test the ccma by examining the relationships between hope, career adaptability, career construction behaviors, and subjective well-being as indicators of adaptive readiness, adaptability resources, adapting responses, and adaptation results, respectively, in turkish adolescents. the study was conducted with 626 adolescents (364 female, 262 male). the results of structural equation modeling revealed positive relationships between the dimensions of the model, as well as a significant sequential relationship from hope to subjective well-being, mediated by career adaptability and career construction behaviors. the findings highlight the importance of hope and career-related factors for the well-being of adolescents. journal of career development

shyness and adjustment in two cohorts of rural chinese children abstract the present study examined relations between anxiety‐based shyness and social, school, and psychological adjustment in rural chinese children at two different historical periods. participants included two cohorts (2012 and 2022) in middle childhood from southeast china ( n = 740 and 710, m age = 9.50 and 9.14). results revealed significant cross‐cohort differences in relations between shyness and adjustment. specifically, shyness was negatively associated with peer preference and academic achievement and positively associated with internalizing problems (loneliness and depression) more strongly in the 2022 cohort than in the 2012 cohort. findings suggest that as rural china undergoes rapid social change toward a competitive market‐oriented society, the adaptational significance of anxiety‐based shyness has become increasingly negative for child development. social development

from childhood to campus: trauma, mental health, and academic success previous research suggests that emerging adults with histories of childhood adversity exhibit heterogeneous patterns of psychosocial risk and resilience during the transition to college, suggesting the need for person-centered approaches that can identify distinct constellations of strengths and vulnerabilities. latent profile analysis identified four profiles of college freshmen ( n = 316) based on patterns of psychosocial and behavioral functioning: normative, struggling, stressed substance users, and thriving/resilient. students in the struggling and stressed substance use profiles reported higher childhood adversity exposure and worse mental health. significant indirect associations between aces history and anxiety and depressive symptomatology emerged through profile membership, although significant direct associations remained. stressed substance users had a higher rate of course failure, and students in the two highest-risk profiles were more likely to drop out by their sophomore year. both aces and current psychosocial functioning contribute to poor mental health and academic outcomes, suggesting that interventions should integrate skill-based supports with trauma-informed approaches. emerging adulthood
supporting change in service delivery: an instrumental case study of multilevel mentorship in school-based occupational therapy journal of occupational therapy schools and early intervention
optimising indicated prevention for child anxiety and depression: a 12-month follow-up for cluster-randomised factorial 2 x 2 x 2 trial journal of child and adolescent mental health

psychoanalysis at the edge of recognition: gaza and the colonial unconscious abstract this article examines the psychoanalytic implications of the destruction of gaza through a qualitative, interpretive longitudinal analysis of the analytic work with a young palestinian physician whose family and social world were devastated by war, displacement, and exile. drawing on clinical material across successive phases of this experience, it argues that gaza challenges psychoanalysis not only clinically but epistemologically. under conditions in which the material and social foundations of everyday life are systematically dismantled, trauma can no longer be understood as a bounded individual psychic event, but emerges as continuous, collective, and historically situated. the paper explores the analyst’s position as witness and the limits of analytic neutrality when psychic suffering is inseparable from structural violence. integrating psychoanalytic theory with decolonial thought, liberation psychology, and palestinian‐centred scholarship, it develops the notion of a colonial unconscious to describe historical structures that differentially organize recognition within psychoanalytic discourse. the clinical material suggests that testimony can disrupt inherited interpretive frameworks while transforming the analyst’s own epistemic position. the article concludes that psychoanalysis may need to extend its frame beyond the dyad, allowing historical reality, collective memory, and plural forms of witnessing to participate in the analytic field. journal of analytical psychology

a trilogy theory of moral cowardice cowardice is a lack of courage to face danger. moral cowardice occurs when the taking of a principled stand is avoided because of its risks, especially the disapproval or hostility of others. moral cowardice is the result of a set of processes that begins with the recognition of a problem and ends with cowardly action. in moral cowardice, principles of moral behavior—whether at the universal, sociocultural, or individual level—are tossed aside. and the individual invents rationalizations to explain to themselves and others why their actions are not really cowardly after all. the more persuasive the rationalizations, the more likely the individual is to behave in a cowardly manner. moral cowardice seems to be rampant in today’s world, especially among leaders. the article seeks to understand what, exactly, this moral cowardice comprises. review of general psychology

the computational functions of the inferior olive: clues from evolution abstract background cerebellum-like structures, mainly studied in weakly electric fish, act to remove the effects of the fish’s own movements on the electrical signals they receive, but do not directly control movement, nor do they have a clear error signal. in contrast, the cerebellum does directly control movement – arguably the most prominent functional difference between the two structures. anatomically, the most pronounced difference is that the cerebellum possesses an inferior olive. this conjunction suggests that the inferior olive carries out a function that is necessary for the control of movement. summary this paper compares cerebellum-like structures with the cerebellum itself to examine how the evolution of the inferior olive conveyed the capacity for direct motor control. cerebellum-like structures act as adaptive filters to remove self-generated sensory interference. however, issuing motor commands introduces a new problem, that of error. because the output of a sensory-filtering circuit is an estimate of the sensory signal, it cannot serve as an error signal to calibrate movement. we review computational, behavioural, and evolutionary evidence showing that climbing fibres from the inferior olive supply this missing error signal. in short, the evolution of the inferior olive represents a marked expansion in cerebellar competencies, transforming a sensory cancellation device into a primary controller of movement. key messages the evolution of the inferior olive resolved the fundamental computational limitation of cerebellum-like sensory filters by providing a dedicated error signal, thereby enabling cerebellar participation in motor control and the learning of internal models. empirical evidence across learning paradigms and evolutionary lineages supports the view that the primary computational function of the inferior olive is to supply the error signals required for this transformation in cerebellar function. brain behavior and evolution
ecological shaping of arab school counselors’ attitudes toward lgbtq youth international journal for the advancement of counselling

profiles of cognitive appraisal of non-suicidal self-injury scars and their clinical correlates in adults with a history of self-injury: a cross-sectional study. scars are the most durable consequence of non-suicidal self-injury (nssi), but how patients appraise them, and how appraisal dimensions combine within individuals, remains unclear. in this cross-sectional study, 234 adults with a history of nssi and at least one scar, recruited consecutively in ryazan and moscow, russia, completed the russian nssi scar cognition scale (hopelessness, shame, inner strength) and measures of suicidal ideation, social anxiety, rumination, body-image dysphoria and nssi functions. profiles were derived by cluster analysis and tested for stability. three stable profiles emerged: low-salience (55.1%), negative-dominant (28.2%) and strength-dominant (16.7%). the negative-dominant profile showed the highest suicidal ideation, social anxiety, rumination, body-image dysphoria and self-punishment; the strength-dominant profile showed suicidal ideation and social anxiety similar to the low-salience profile, intermediate rumination and body-image dysphoria, and the strongest endorsement of nssi functions. these differences persisted after covariate adjustment. scar appraisal explained a further 7.9% of variance in suicidal ideation beyond demographics, self-injury status and general distress; scar visibility explained none. in behavioural remission, the negative-dominant profile reported higher suicidal ideation than the other profiles. scar appraisal distinguishes subgroups with different clinical correlates. longitudinal studies are needed to establish whether these profiles predict outcomes or can guide treatment. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

associations between types of physical activity and mental health among korean adolescents: a cross-sectional study using data from the 21st korea youth risk behavior survey (2025). adolescence is critical for developing physical activity habits and maintaining mental health. using data from the 21st korea youth risk behavior survey (2025), this cross-sectional study examined the associations between physical activity and mental health in korean adolescents. the sample included 52,618 middle and high school students. physical activity included ≥60 min/day of physical activity, vigorous physical activity, muscle-strengthening exercise, active transportation, and physical education class participation. mental health indicators included stress perception, depressive symptoms, suicidal ideation, suicide plans, and suicide attempts; stress perception was examined descriptively, whereas depressive symptoms and suicide-related indicators were evaluated as outcomes in the multivariable analyses. analyses accounted for the complex survey design, including sampling weights, stratification, and clustering. survey-adjusted tests and complex-sample multivariable logistic regression were performed, adjusting for sex, grade, academic achievement, household economic status, living arrangement, and weight status. vigorous physical activity and physical education participation were significantly associated with all four mental health outcomes. compared with no vigorous physical activity, participation on 1-2 days was associated with lower odds of suicidal ideation (aor = 0.875, 95% ci: 0.811-0.944), suicide plans (aor = 0.810, 95% ci: 0.720-0.912), and suicide attempts (aor = 0.803, 95% ci: 0.688-0.937). physical education twice per week was associated with lower odds of all four outcomes (aors = 0.737-0.927). in contrast, several frequency categories of ≥60 min/day of physical activity and muscle-strengthening exercise were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. these findings suggest that associations between physical activity and mental health vary by activity type and mental health outcomes. behavioral sciences

prospective associations between parenting styles and adolescents' social-emotional competence: a cross-lagged network analysis. adolescence involves substantial developmental changes, with social-emotional competence (sec) serving as an important protective factor. however, how parenting styles are prospectively associated with adolescents' sec in the chinese cultural context remains unclear. a two-wave longitudinal study was conducted among 1167 middle school students in china (52.4% male; baseline m= 13.16 years, sd = 0.93). using longitudinal data and a cross-lagged panel network analysis (clpn), we examined the temporal relationships among parental autonomy support, psychological control, and sec. opinion exchange showed a positive prospective association with later self-management. adolescent self-management showed a limited adolescent-to-parent prospective association, whereas responsible decision-making showed relatively prominent incoming and outgoing prospective connectivity and may warrant further investigation in confirmatory and intervention research. these findings highlight the potential relevance of parent-adolescent communication and emotional support for adolescents' social-emotional functioning. behavioral sciences

family-school partnership as interpretive practice: educator accounts of attribution, communication, and decision-making in arab education in israel. family-school partnership is often discussed in relation to student support, yet adult interviews primarily illuminate how educators interpret family knowledge and organize professional action. this interpretivist qualitative study examined how 13 educators in arab education in israel constructed partnership when interpreting students' learning, emotional, social, or behavioral difficulties. the educator interviews were analyzed using topic-focused reflexive thematic analysis. four unmatched mother interviews, collected to explore school communication, transparency, and decision inclusion, received a separate, bounded contextual reading; they neither generated themes nor triangulated educator accounts. three educator-derived themes concerned changing the terms of engagement before crisis, treating family knowledge as capable of revising professional attributions and informing response, and attributing participation- and belonging-related meanings to coordinated adult support. a descriptive cross-case display showed how reattribution-and-response accounts were distributed across the educator interviews, including partial, ambiguous, and negative cases; these counts describe this dataset rather than estimate prevalence. the mother accounts complicated school-centered constructions by describing contact that could remain delayed, one-directional, or without influence over decisions. the findings support an adult-centered account of contact, epistemic authority, communicative accessibility, and decision inclusion; they do not demonstrate a causal pathway or student outcomes. behavioral sciences

between human and machine: university teachers’ accounts of judgment, metacognitive defense, and cognitive offloading in generative ai use generative artificial intelligence (genai) allows university teachers to delegate cognitive work while deciding how students should engage with it. using codebook thematic analysis, we examined multi-source accounts from 25 teachers recruited through an ai-focused learning community and its professional networks in china. materials comprised interviews with 22 teachers, three documentary cases, self-narratives and reflective essays. three themes organize the findings: reconstructing the teacher role, defending professional judgment, and managing teachers’ and students’ cognitive participation. participants described disciplinary expertise as a basis for evaluating ai outputs and reported practices intended to retain human engagement. instrumental and partnership orientations overlapped; descriptive comparison with later use profiles did not establish a simple relationship between partnership language and usage intensity. because the protocol introduced several focal topics, we distinguish prompted positions from volunteered formulations. the proposed belief–strategy–practice cycle is a heuristic interpretation of retrospective accounts, not a demonstrated mechanism. the study contributes an account of how teachers connect their own cognitive offloading with their reported organization of students’ learning opportunities. its claims concern this ai-engaged sample rather than university teachers generally. journal of intelligence

telework and technostress: a systematic review of risk and protective factors for workers’ well-being the consolidation of telework has introduced digital demands that may increase technostress and threaten employees’ psychological well-being and sustainable career development. grounded in conservation of resources theory, this systematic review examined psychosocial risk factors associated with technostress in telework, protective individual and organizational resources, and the contribution of digital psychological support interventions. following prisma guidelines, scopus, web of science, and pubmed were searched between june and august 2025 for peer-reviewed empirical studies published from 2022 to 2025 involving remote or hybrid adult employees. fourteen of 556 identified records met the picos-based eligibility criteria. methodological quality was assessed using joanna briggs institute critical appraisal tools. digital overload, technological complexity, work intensification, and blurred work–life boundaries were associated with poorer psychological and work outcomes. digital self-efficacy, adaptability, proactive personality, supportive leadership, trust, and communication emerged as protective resources. digital psychological support interventions may reduce emotional strain and strengthen resources for sustainable careers. australian journal of career development

“this too shall pass”—resilience factors of parental divorce during covid-19 pandemic for adolescents abstract the covid-19 pandemic had detrimental effects on the well-being of individuals across the world. for adolescent girls experiencing parental divorce during the covid-19 pandemic, the effect was exacerbated, as they had to grapple with the adversities associated with both the pandemic and divorce. nonetheless, many of them have fared well and shown resilience despite adversities. the resilience of adolescents in the face of parental divorce during covid-19 has been largely understudied, especially in south africa. the present study aimed to explore the factors that enable the resilience of adolescent girls from divorced households during the covid-19 pandemic. in alignment with qualitative research, the study employed a phenomenological research design. purposive sampling was used to recruit five female adolescents in johannesburg, south africa. data were collected using semi-structured interviews and a focus group. braun and clarke’s six steps of data analysis were used to analyse data thematically. the findings of the study grouped resilience into individual attributes (coping mechanisms, viewing divorce as a good resolution, perseverance, optimism and spirituality), relational factors (relationships with mothers, extended family, friends and partners) and contextual factors (access to mental health support and teacher support). these findings underscore that a combination of individual and social-ecological factors should anchor interventions aimed at promoting the resilience of adolescent girls whose parents divorced during pandemics. journal of child and family studies
relationships of alcohol media literacy with drinking behavior, norms, and attitudes among south korean adolescents journal of child and family studies

social anxiety symptoms and body‐focused repetitive behaviour severity in adolescents: a serial mediation analysis of shame and emotion regulation difficulties abstract body‐focused repetitive behaviour disorders (bfrbds), including trichotillomania (ttm) and skin‐picking disorder (spd), typically emerge during adolescence. these disorders have been conceptualized within emotion regulation models, in which body‐focused repetitive behaviours (bfrbs) may function as attempts to regulate aversive emotional states. although anxiety frequently co‐occurs with bfrbds, its association with bfrb severity is generally modest, highlighting the need to examine affective and regulatory processes. this cross‐sectional study examined the associations among social anxiety, shame‐proneness, emotion regulation difficulties and bfrb severity using a serial mediation model. participants were 107 adolescents aged 12–18 years (80.4% female) who met dsm‐5 criteria for ttm or spd and were recruited from a tertiary child and adolescent psychiatry clinic. diagnoses were established using semi‐structured clinical interviews. the analysis controlled for age and sex. social anxiety was positively correlated with shame, emotion regulation difficulties and bfrb severity ( r = 0.28–0.31, all p < 0.01). in the serial model, social anxiety was associated with greater shame, which was associated with greater emotion regulation difficulties; in turn, emotion regulation difficulties were associated with greater bfrb severity. the total indirect effect ( b = 0.162, 95% ci [0.038, 0.337]) and the serial indirect effect through both mediators ( b = 0.117, 95% ci [0.040, 0.257]) were significant, whereas neither single‐mediator indirect effect was significant. the direct association remained significant ( b = 0.302, p = 0.022), consistent with partial statistical mediation. these findings support the proposed theory‐based model but do not establish temporal or causal ordering. clinical psychology & psychotherapy

the reciprocal relationships between positive youth development and psychological distress in adolescents: the moderating role of gender and stress mindsets abstract although previous studies have suggested a reciprocal relationship between positive youth development (pyd) and adolescent psychological distress, the distinction between within‐person dynamics and between‐person differences remains unexamined. given the gender differences in adolescents' pyd and psychological distress, we examined gender as a moderator to test for gender‐specific developmental dynamics. additionally, early adolescence is filled with developmental challenges; therefore, we examined stress mindsets as moderators to clarify how cognitive appraisals of these challenges shape these reciprocal processes. using three‐wave longitudinal data from 2331 chinese adolescents ( m age = 13.92, sd = 0.65; 52.4% girls), we applied a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (ri‐clpm) combined with multigroup analysis and local structural equation modeling (lsem). at the between‐person level, results demonstrated a strong negative correlation between pyd and distress. at the within‐person level, increases in psychological distress significantly predicted subsequent declines in pyd, whereas the reverse pathway was not significant. these relationships were consistent across genders. lsem analyses revealed that a stress‐is‐debilitating mindset linearly moderated the autoregressive pathways of psychological distress. conversely, a stress‐is‐enhancing mindset showed no significant within‐person moderating effect. these findings indicate that protecting adolescent development requires reducing psychological distress and addressing negative stress mindsets. applied psychology-health and well being

beyond mean score differences: home language and the interpretation of cognitive test performance in china large-scale surveys often use cognitive test total scores to describe group differences, but the construct meaning of such scores depends on task content, administration, language experience, and opportunities to learn. the china family panel studies (cfps) word test is an oral mandarin character reading task with education-dependent entry and stopping rules. we analyzed 16,689 adults followed from 2010 to 2018 using the full survey strata, primary sampling units, and longitudinal weights, and contrasted baseline-adjusted, gain score, geographic overlap, propensity overlap, floor exclusion, nonlinear, and measurement error sensitivity results. the fully adjusted 2018 contrast relative to mandarin-speaking homes was −0.023 sd (95% ci [−0.077, 0.030]) for sinitic-dialect homes and −0.292 sd (95% ci [−0.430, −0.154]) for the pooled minority-language response category. the latter estimate was reduced to −0.183 sd after exact ethnicity code fixed effects and to −0.081 sd (95% ci [−0.291, 0.129]) under overlap weighting; only 49 respondents fell in the 1st–99th percentile propensity score intersection. a covariate-adjusted gain score model yielded a smaller minority-language contrast (−0.180 sd, 95% ci [−0.356, −0.005]). correcting the baseline under plausible reliability values of 0.85–0.95 produced point estimates from −0.226 to −0.277 sd. floor exclusions reduced but did not eliminate the negative contrast. these results show that the pooled minority-language coefficient is strongly estimand- and support-dependent. they support a constrained interpretation of the observed cfps score rather than a direct inference about broad crystallized intelligence or a uniform effect of minority-language use. journal of intelligence

academic resilience and behavioral patterns in a digital problem-solving task: evidence from process data digital problem-solving assessments provide process data that can reveal how students behave beyond final achievement. previous research has shown substantial individual differences in problem-solving behavior. academic resilience commonly refers to strong academic performance despite socioeconomic disadvantage, but little is known about how academically resilient students behave during problem solving. this study examined whether socioeconomically disadvantaged students classified as academically resilient showed distinctive behavioral patterns in the programme for international student assessment (pisa) 2012 ticket task. academic resilience was defined using socioeconomic disadvantage and mathematics achievement, and propensity-score matching (psm) was used to improve comparability on selected background characteristics. process data were analyzed as action sequences to identify recurring behavioral profiles. results showed that resilient students tended to follow longer action sequences and had higher backtracking proportions, whereas differences in timing indicators were not statistically significant. these findings suggest that mathematics-based academic resilience is associated with differences in the organization of task behavior. journal of intelligence

differentiated contributions of executive functions to domain-specific numerical precursors in preschool children. executive functions (efs) are well-established predictors of early mathematical development, yet whether distinct components contribute differentially to specific numerical precursors during the preschool years remains unclear. the present study examined the unique contributions of inhibitory control, verbal short-term memory (vstm), visuospatial working memory (vswm), and set-shifting to three precursors (procedural cardinality, non-symbolic quantity reproduction, and approximate number system [ans] performance) while controlling for the domain-general contributions of receptive language and rapid automatized naming (ran) and tested whether age moderated these associations. a total of 316 italian preschoolers (m = 59.85 months, range 38-76; 158 females) completed nine tasks from the dap-t tablet-based battery; hierarchical regression and moderation analyses were conducted on multiply imputed datasets (50 imputations), with holm-bonferroni correction applied to individual coefficients and complete-case sensitivity analyses performed to assess robustness. age moderation was examined through six interaction terms with bonferroni correction. age was the strongest predictor across outcomes. above and beyond age and domain-general covariates, procedural cardinality was uniquely predicted by vstm (β = 0.205); ans performance by inhibitory control (β = 0.191) and ran (β = 0.252); non-symbolic quantity reproduction by ran (β = 0.182) and age alone. ran emerged as the most consistent cross-domain predictor of numerical performance after age, with effects surviving correction on non-symbolic quantity reproduction and ans. set-shifting contributed to no outcome robustly after correction. none of the six age-moderation interactions survived bonferroni correction; a single nominal effect emerged for age × vstm on procedural cardinality (= .044), which should be regarded as exploratory. efs thus show a differentiated profile across numerical precursors, with vstm and inhibitory control as primary executive supports for procedural cardinality and non-symbolic comparison, respectively, whereas non-symbolic quantity reproduction appears to draw more on domain-general processing efficiency than on standard executive control. journal of intelligence
political emotions shape preferences for leaders’ facial traits: anger favours dominance, fear favours trustworthiness cognition & emotion

development and non-randomized pilot trial of families forward: a new program for families of autistic youth transitioning to adulthood abstract objective autistic youth and their families describe transitioning to adulthood as overwhelming. yet, there are few evidence-based, family focused transition programs broad enough to serve youths’ wide range of autism-related and background characteristics. we report on the community-engaged development of families forward (focusing on relationships, well-being, and responsibility ahead), a new family based, individualized transition planning program (phase 1) and non-randomized pilot trial findings regarding acceptability, feasibility, and clinical promise (phase 2). methods phase 1 involved qualitative interviews with autistic youth, parents/caregivers, and professionals (n = 31) regarding transition-related experiences, existing service gaps, and feedback on the families forward concept. in phase 2, 14 families participated in a trial of families forward delivered remotely by community-based coaches. families completed pre/post measures of program skills (family communication, knowledge), mechanistic targets (self-efficacy, stage of change), and outcomes (transition planning activities, perceived stress) and exit interviews. feasibility and acceptability benchmarks were specified a priori. a community advisory board of racially and ethnically diverse autistic young adults, parents, and professionals guided the research. results phase 1 identified the need for flexible, skills-based, collaborative transition programs and highlighted the relevance of proposed program skills (family communication, collaborative goal-setting, problem solving, systems navigation). in phase 2, all feasibility, acceptability, and clinical promise benchmarks were met. exit interviews highlighted how family communication and structured goal-setting improved collaborative, youth-centered planning. conclusions across racial and ethnic backgrounds and autism characteristics, families forward shows promise for improving transition outcomes. centering community input during program development likely increased relevance and feasibility. journal of pediatric psychology

design and initial psychometric evaluation of the multidimensional school social climate inventory for educational assistants (mssci-ea) in chile. educational assistants remain underrepresented in multidimensional assessments of school social climate. this study developed the multidimensional school social climate inventory for educational assistants (mssci-ea) and examined initial evidence regarding its content validity, internal structure, and internal consistency. instrument development involved a systematic review, item generation, expert judgment, and pilot testing. the main study included 871 educational assistants from 91 chilean schools. exploratory graph analysis (ega) was conducted using spearman correlations, glasso network estimation, and louvain community detection. internal consistency was estimated using cronbach's alpha and mcdonald's omega based on pearson correlations. item stability was examined through 1000 bootstrap resamples, and hierarchical ega assessed whether a unidimensional higher-order structure could support an overall score. the retained solution comprised 90 items across 12 dimensions. both alpha and omega ranged from 0.773 to 0.957. average item stability, calculated according to the final dimension assignments, ranged from 0.252 to 1.000. hierarchical ega identified five higher-order communities and did not support a unidimensional interpretation of an overall total score. these findings provide initial psychometric evidence for the mssci-ea. further evaluation of the less stable item groupings and independent confirmation of the dimensional structure are needed. behavioral sciences

physiological arousal and its effects on time perception: a systematic review abstract time perception is a fundamental aspect of human cognition, influencing motor coordination, decision‐making, and planning. unlike sensory modalities such as vision or hearing, which rely on dedicated sensory organs, the perception of time lacks a specific neural substrate, making it highly dependent on internal physiological and psychological states. research suggests that physiological arousal plays a crucial role in temporal distortions, with pacemaker‐accumulator models proposing that heightened arousal accelerates the internal clock, leading to an overestimation of time. we provide a systematic review of the available literature on the complex relationship between physiological indices of arousal and time distortion. overall while a relatively consistent association emerged between baseline cardiac autonomic activity and temporal accuracy. when physiological arousal was experimentally manipulated, its relationship with temporal distortion was substantially less consistent. these differences were observed across pain, stress, emotional, and physical‐activity paradigms and appeared to vary according to the characteristics of the eliciting stimulus. this pattern highlights the need to distinguish physiological arousal from the other cognitive processes involved and provides a basis for future research investigating also the other potential explanatory factors in the relationship between arousal and time perception. wiley interdisciplinary reviews-cognitive science

associations between loneliness, cyberloafing, and digital stress in college students: evidence from profile and network analyses this study examined the associations among loneliness, cyberloafing, and digital stress among chinese college students. drawing on data collected from 1,431 students via self-report questionnaires including the cyberloafing scale, the digital stress scale, and the loneliness scale, we employed latent profile analysis to identify profiles of loneliness, followed by profile-specific network analyses and network comparison tests to examine the organization of cyberloafing and digital stress across loneliness profiles. three loneliness profiles emerged: low-loneliness, companionship-deficit, and high-loneliness. fear of missing out showed relatively high strength centrality across the three networks, whereas connection overload was particularly prominent in the low-loneliness and companionship-deficit networks. active cyberloafing consistently showed the highest bridge strength between the cyberloafing and digital-stress communities. together, these findings highlight variation in the organization of cyberloafing and digital stress across loneliness profiles and demonstrate the value of integrating person-centered and network approaches to understand college students’ digital experiences. emerging adulthood

linking a customized employment intervention to life satisfaction of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities: the mediating role of integrated employment this study examined the effect of a customized employment (ce) intervention on the life satisfaction of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (idd) through the mediation of integrated employment (number of jobs in the past 12 months). a randomized controlled trial was conducted in spain with unemployed individuals with idd who were randomly assigned to control (n = 202) or experimental (n = 232) groups. the ce intervention took place from september 2022 to july 2023. life satisfaction and employment were measured at baseline (september–october 2022), mid-intervention, and follow-up (december 2023–january 2024). results confirmed the mediation process: individuals in the experimental group secured more jobs than controls, and this integrated employment was in turn associated with higher life satisfaction. these findings elucidate the mechanism through which ce exerts its effects, specifically by improving integrated employment, which in turn enhances life satisfaction. australian journal of career development

purpose in life and exercise task behaviors: evidence from a 10-week running task in college students this study examined associations between purpose in life (pil) and objective indicators of exercise task completion patterns among college students. participants were 547 college students (mean age = 19.71, 42.23% female) required to complete 63 km within 10 weeks for course credit. participants completed questionnaires assessing pil and demographic characteristics before the running task began. running data were tracked via a mobile app and five behavioral indicators were derived: days from task onset to initiation, days from completion to deadline, total completion time, percentage of distance in final 2 weeks, and frequency of early morning runs. multiple regression analyses revealed that higher pil significantly predicted shorter total completion time after controlling for gender, age, and bmi. pil was also associated with more frequent early morning runs, although this association was not robust to alternative model specifications. however, pil showed no significant associations with the remaining behavioral indicators. journal of health psychology

sickle cell disease and young couples: understanding the influence of shared and individual meaning on couples’ experience of illness abstract this study explored the experiences of young adult couples navigating sickle cell disease (scd), focusing on the shared and individual perspectives that inform their collective navigation of the illness. using a systemic lens, the research addressed a critical gap in understanding how this chronic condition shapes relationship dynamics. advances in scd treatment have increased life expectancy, allowing more patients to transition into young adulthood and form intimate relationships. despite this, systemic support for these couples remains sparse. as partners navigate shared coping, there is an urgent need for interdisciplinary care that integrates medical family therapy (medft) with biomedical treatment to address the psychosocial complexities of the disease. using a transcendental-phenomenological approach, researchers conducted individual interviews with both partners from nine couples ( n = 18). data were analyzed dyadically to capture how individual perceptions and shared relational realities converge to influence adaptation. six core themes were identified, indicating that effective adaptation and relational stability are fostered by couples’ ability to recognize the individual and shared experiences of living with a chronic illness. this research provides a foundation for medical family therapists to develop approaches that enhance psychosocial outcomes for young adult couples with scd. contemporary family therapy

association between physical activity and psychological resilience in older adults: an analysis of a prospective cohort study in china. background: although numerous studies have confirmed the mental health benefits of physical activity, evidence on the association between physical activity and psychological resilience-particularly longitudinal evidence that accounts for dynamic patterns of activity change-remains limited. therefore, this study aimed to examine the cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between physical activity patterns and psychological resilience among older adults in china.
methods: this study used two waves of data (2011-2014) from the chinese longitudinal healthy longevity survey (clhls) and included chinese older adults, and employed both cross-sectional and prospective analysis designs. physical activity was categorized into four patterns of change: consistently inactive, active-to-inactive, inactive-to-active, and consistently active. psychological resilience was assessed using a five-item scale and dichotomized as high or low. logistic regression and cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the associations between physical activity patterns and psychological resilience, adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and health status.
results: in the cross-sectional analysis, compared with the remain-inactive group, the inactive-to-active group (or = 0.59, 95% ci: 0.51-0.69, < 0.001) and the remain-active group (or = 0.61, 95% ci: 0.51-0.72, < 0.001) had lower odds of low pr, whereas the active-to-inactive group was not significantly associated with low pr (or = 0.94, 95% ci: 0.77-1.13, = 0.486). in the longitudinal analysis, the active-to-inactive (hr = 0.73, 95% ci: 0.56-0.96, = 0.023), inactive-to-active (hr = 0.72, 95% ci: 0.61-0.85, < 0.001), and remain-active groups (hr = 0.59, 95% ci: 0.48-0.73, < 0.001) had lower hazards of incident low pr. no statistically significant pa-by-subgroup interactions were detected.
conclusion: pa patterns characterized by current activity, regardless of past activity status, were associated with lower odds of prevalent low pr and lower hazards of incident low pr among older adults. these observational findings support further investigation of pa as a potentially modifiable factor associated with psychological resilience. frontiers in psychology

an investigation of personal and social-contextual resources as mediators of the influence of duration of covid-19 pandemic exposure and mentoring program participation on the mental health and well-being of adolescents. although a sizable body of research indicates deterioration in the mental health of adolescents during the covid-19 pandemic, the mediating processes accounting for these effects as well as the potential for community-based prevention programs to offset and/or buffer declines in mental health during this period have received limited investigation. the present study addressed these gaps using data from a randomized controlled trial of the big brothers big sisters of america community-based mentoring program in which there was naturally occurring variation in the extent to which the 18-month window between baseline and an initial follow-up assessment overlapped with the pandemic. structural equation modeling analyses revealed support for hypothesized indirect associations of pandemic exposure with negative change in mental health and well-being via co-occurring declines in levels of personal and social-contextual resources, as well as a partially offsetting indirect association of mentoring program participation with improved mental health via an increase in personal resources. mentoring program participation did not interact with pandemic exposure, and model pathways generally did not vary significantly by gender. findings suggest that declines in adolescent mental health during the covid-19 pandemic were linked to disruptions in their personal and social-contextual resources and that community-based mentoring interventions may at least partially offset pandemic-related declines in mental health. behavioral sciences

the impact of negative emotion on visual working memory under excessive cognitive load: the role of the resource-allocation stage and location information. visual working memory (vwm) enables people to temporarily store important information for use in subsequent tasks. previous studies have indicated that a negative emotional state can influence the processing of vwm; however, the direction of this influence and its underlying cognitive mechanisms remain contentious. the present study investigated the impact of negative emotion on vwm, with a particular focus on how this association was manifested across cognitive-load conditions, theoretically defined resource-allocation stages, and location-information conditions. across two experiments, negative emotion was found to exert a bidirectional effect: it impaired vwm performance under low cognitive load, whereas it produced a facilitative effect under excessive cognitive load. importantly, this facilitative effect emerged only during the early stage of resource allocation and when the locations of memory items and probe items were congruent. under these specific conditions, negative emotion increased vwm capacity (k = 3.86, se = 0.23) compared with the neutral condition (k = 3.32, se = 0.22), whereas this facilitative effect disappeared when location congruence was disrupted. these findings demonstrate that the effects of negative emotion on vwm depend on the interaction between emotional states, cognitive load, and location-information availability. this provides important evidence for understanding the boundary conditions under which emotion modulates cognitive function, and offers theoretical guidance for load-sensitive and emotion-aware cognitive system design in complex information-processing environments. behavioral sciences

when trust and privacy pull in opposite directions: consumer decision making with conversational ai drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (s-o-r) framework, this study examines how consumers’ perceptions of information quality, personalization, explainability, and responsiveness are associated with purchase intention through their relationships with perceived usefulness, algorithmic trust, and privacy concern, while considering ai literacy as a boundary condition. data from 588 chinese online shoppers who completed a standardized shopping task through direct interaction with a conversational ai shopping assistant were analyzed using structural equation modeling. the results show that all four consumer-perceived conversational-ai cues are positively associated with perceived usefulness and algorithmic trust, whereas perceived personalization is also positively associated with privacy concern. perceived usefulness and algorithmic trust are positively associated with purchase intention, whereas privacy concern shows a negative conditional association with purchase intention in the structural model. personalization shows competing indirect associations with purchase intention: positive indirect associations through usefulness and trust coexist with a negative indirect association through privacy concern. the positive trust–intention association and the negative conditional privacy concern–intention association are stronger at higher levels of ai literacy, whereas the usefulness–intention interaction is statistically compatible with practical equivalence relative to the specified study-specific bound. these findings indicate that consumer responses to conversational ai reflect competing benefit–risk evaluations rather than a uniformly positive acceptance process, and that ai literacy is differentially associated with the strength of the trust–intention and privacy concern–intention relationships. behavioral sciences

neural oscillatory and sympathetic arousal dynamics during mindfulness meditation: characterizing relaxed alertness abstract mindfulness meditation is often characterized as a state of relaxed alertness, yet the neural and autonomic processes that define this state remain unclear. this study examined concurrent electroencephalographic (eeg) oscillations and skin conductance level (scl) during brief breath‐focused mindfulness meditation, with a focus on temporal dynamics. eeg and scl were recorded during 2 min of eyes‐closed rest and a 15 min mindfulness meditation, with analyses focused on 8 min of the silent self‐guided period following instruction, divided into four consecutive 2 min segments. planned contrasts compared eyes‐closed rest with mindfulness meditation and examined changes across the meditation period, while sex‐related variability was explored. meditation was associated with greater theta (4–7.5 hz) amplitude than rest. exploratory analyses also indicated greater delta (1–3.5 hz) amplitude during meditation and a progressive increase in delta across the meditation period. alpha amplitude (8–13 hz) showed no reliable state‐related or temporal effects. scl did not differ between rest and meditation overall, although an exploratory trend analysis indicated an initial decrease followed by a later increase during meditation. global alpha amplitude was positively associated with scl during meditation, after accounting for participant differences and changes across the meditation period. exploratory sex analyses suggested a larger rest‐to‐meditation theta increase in males and greater beta and gamma amplitudes in females across states, although these findings should be considered preliminary. together, these results suggest that mindfulness meditation is not simply characterized by reduced arousal, but instead involves dynamic patterns of neural activity and sympathetic arousal that are broadly consistent with relaxed alertness. psychophysiology

how caption color perception shapes news value judgments abstract this study examines how caption hue (open caption telop, oct) shapes the evaluation of news value, including credibility, novelty, and timeliness, across affective contexts. using controlled hue manipulations based on the practical color coordinate system (pccs), participants evaluated realistic news stimuli with a continuous rating scale. results revealed significant main effects of hue and interactions with context across all value dimensions. warm hues enhanced perceived credibility and timeliness, particularly in negative contexts, whereas purple selectively increased perceived novelty. intermediate hues showed less stable effects. furthermore, certain hues facilitated integration across value dimensions, while others produced dissociative patterns. these findings demonstrate that hue functions not only as an affective cue but also as an organizing principle in evaluative judgment. applied cognitive psychology

breaking away from destructive feedback: the role of emotion regulation in negative self-verification people often favor self-verifying feedback which reinforces existing self-beliefs, a preference that can further entrench negative self-views. prior work suggests that emotional responses to the prospect of receiving non-self-verifying feedback may influence whether people engage in self-verification; however, the contribution of emotion regulation to feedback choices is unclear. the current study aimed to explore how affective processes affect whether people choose to observe feedback that is likely to either confirm or disconfirm their existing self-views. participants ( n = 202) completed an online survey to assess their self-views, emotion regulation habits, and preference for self-verifying feedback in a simulated feedback task. additional open-ended questions assessed how participants’ made their feedback choice, what they were feeling, and whether they managed their emotional response to make their decision. the qualitative results demonstrated that the choice of negative self-verifying feedback was related to the desire for subjective accuracy, consistent with existing theories of self-verification. however, our results also indicate significant relationships between emotion regulation habits and feedback choice among participants with high depression symptom severity. this study’s findings provide new insights into the cognitive and affective determinants of self-verification, suggesting that for individuals with depression, training in engagement-based emotion regulation could potentially lessen negative self-verification tendencies. psychological reports

going green in stages: psychological processes behind intention formation and action for climate mitigation abstract mitigating the climate crisis requires rapid societal change in favour of sustainability. despite widespread concern, many consumers continue with high‐emission activities. to assist behaviour change, it is useful to understand where in the process of change people currently are and what motivates the next step. in a preregistered study using a representative sample of adults ( n = 1200), we measure ‘stage of change’ for transport and diet behaviours, and test the relationship with psychological predictors of proenvironmental behaviour. for both behaviours, people who intend to change worry more about climate change and feel more morally responsible to act than people who see no need to change. by contrast, acting on intentions is associated with holding a strong environmental identity. we find little predictive value of a broad range of other variables proposed in the literature, including social norms. we also find differences between the two behavioural domains. the results show the benefit of conceptualising behaviour change as a multistage process and the necessity of considering the behavioural domain when aiming to understand predictors of change. applied psychology-an international review-psychologie appliquee-revue internationale

retro-cue alerting effects on conscious perception across different levels of target visibility abstract can alerting retro-cues improve the conscious perception of stimuli that would otherwise remain unseen? while pre-stimulus alerting is known to facilitate conscious access, the effects of retro-cues remain ambiguous due to methodological confounds in existing literature. specifically, most studies finding retro-cue benefits have relied on spatial features (such as lateralized targets or cues), which confound alerting with spatial selection. our design addresses this gap by employing central visual targets and non-lateralized auditory cues, thereby isolating the temporal boost of phasic alerting from spatial orienting. across four experiments, participants reported the presence and orientation of a central gabor patch presented at near-threshold ( $${\sim }50\%$$ detection) or higher visibility ( $${\sim }75\%$$ detection) levels. an auditory alerting tone was presented prior to, simultaneously with, or after the gabor, at various short and long stimulus onset asynchronies, with both short and long temporal ranges. results consistently showed that pre-stimulus and simultaneous cues significantly enhanced conscious perception, increasing both seen rates and (in some experiments) perceptual sensitivity. crucially, the presence of retro-cue benefits was observed at higher stimulus visibility, but not at near-threshold, suggesting a potential influence of target visibility on retro-cue efficacy. when targets were near-threshold, retro-cues did not reliably improve conscious perception, whereas tones presented 200 ms after target offset significantly increased the proportion of seen reports when target visibility was increased. these findings indicate that non-spatial auditory retro-cues can modulate conscious report when the underlying sensory trace is sufficiently robust. more broadly, they show that the timing of conscious access can be influenced by late alerting signals even in the absence of spatial information, providing a behavioural platform to refine models of how alerting and evidence strength interact in conscious perception. psychological research-psychologische forschung

linking normal-range and maladaptive personality traits and facets to personality disorders: a meta-analytic review this systematic meta-analysis ( k = 99, total n = 69,673) explored the relationships between personality disorders on the one hand, and normal-range big five traits (neuroticism, extraversion, openness, agreeableness, and conscientiousness) and the maladaptive traits assessed with the pid-5 (negative affectivity, detachment, psychoticism, antagonism, and disinhibition) on the other hand. the results revealed a positive correlation between neuroticism and all personality disorders. significant associations were also observed between extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness and personality disorders, while openness was the least predictive trait in relation to personality disorders. these results demonstrated a substantial consistency with earlier meta-analytic studies. the findings also suggested that while maladaptive traits generally showed stronger associations with personality disorders than normal-range traits, their multivariate explanatory power was weaker than expected, implying potential response bias due to item keying. additionally, while some personality disorders did not exhibit significant associations at the higher-order domain level, we identified strong correlations with specific facets within the corresponding trait domains. this statistical attenuation at the domain level likely resulted from opposing effects on different facets within the same domain. the conclusions of our study provided a comprehensive picture of the interrelations between personality disorders and big five personality domains and facets. european journal of personality

learning preference profiles and visual narratives in higher education: relevance to human intelligence research university students differ in how they approach unfamiliar information, yet learning-style labels provide a weak basis for matching instruction to individuals. this study examined learning preference profiles and visual narratives in higher education, considering their relevance and limits for human intelligence research. a convergent mixed-methods secondary analysis included 144 complete questionnaire records and 12 interpretable drawings at a colombian public university. the adapted 80-item instrument used five response categories, with frequently and always counted as endorsements. reflective scores were highest, followed by theoretical, pragmatic, and active scores (χ2(3)=158.27, p<0.001; kendall’s w=0.366). the analytic composite exceeded the action-oriented composite (rrb=0.891, p<0.001). this ordering persisted across four scoring representations, although effect sizes and tied maxima varied. drawings mainly represented learning through direction, staged progress, obstacles, and internal processing. missing participant explanations, incomplete coding records, and absent participant-level linkage restricted integration to exploratory descriptive comparison. the study offers methodological considerations for human intelligence research by distinguishing descriptive patterns from claims about cognitive capacities. neither intelligence nor metacognitive performance was assessed, and instructional implications remain hypotheses requiring prospective evaluation. journal of intelligence

topical review: a conceptual framework for diabetes distress tolerance in transitional age youth with type 1 diabetes abstract objective approximately one-third of adolescents with type 1 diabetes (t1d) experience substantial diabetes distress, which is longitudinally associated with worsened glycemic control. this is particularly consequential given the inverse relationship between diabetes distress and healthcare transition readiness. interventions for distress may seek to either reduce it or increase capacity to tolerate it; however, diabetes-specific distress tolerance remains insufficiently conceptualized in the research literature. the purpose of this topical review is to propose a conceptual framework for examining diabetes-specific distress tolerance in transitional age youth with t1d, which may further inform measure development and interventions to increase diabetes distress tolerance, enhance transition readiness, and improve longitudinal health outcomes. method we review literature on diabetes distress in transitional age youth with t1d, focusing on effective interventions to reduce diabetes distress, including relevant literature on the related construct of distress tolerance. we then integrate this literature to propose a conceptual framework of diabetes distress tolerance that may inform the development of interventions to improve transition readiness and health outcomes for transitional age youth with t1d. results existing diabetes distress interventions for transitional age youth with t1d have primarily targeted skills to reduce distress, rather than increasing capacity to tolerate it. distress tolerance is an understudied construct in relation to t1d management. conclusions we propose a conceptual framework of diabetes distress tolerance that may inform intervention development to address diabetes distress for youth with t1d. given transition-associated risks of adverse outcomes, more research is needed to address diabetes distress tolerance in transitional age youth with t1d. journal of pediatric psychology
