measuring state and trait anxiety in turkish adolescents: development and validation of the six-item short forms of the state-trait anxiety inventory. objective: although the state-trait anxiety inventory (stai) is a well-established instrument for anxiety assessment, its length may limit feasibility in large-scale, longitudinal, and time-sensitive research settings. existing abbreviated forms were mainly created for adults worldwide, including türkiye. accordingly, this study aimed to develop and psychometrically evaluate abbreviated versions of the stai-state (stai-s) and stai-trait (stai-t) for turkish adolescents.
method: a two-phase psychometric validation design was implemented across two independent cohorts. exploratory factor analysis (efa) was initially conducted in sample 1, comprising adolescents recruited from an outpatient child and adolescent psychiatry clinic ( = 420), to identify the most parsimonious item configurations. subsequently, confirmatory factor analysis (cfa) and criterion-related validity analyses were performed in sample 2, consisting of public high school students ( = 277). measurement invariance across clinical/community status, sex, and age, comparisons with alternative factor models, and receiver operating characteristic analyses against the generalized anxiety disorder-7 were examined.
results: efa supported a stable two-factor structure for both six-item scales, accounting for 53.7% of the total variance for the stai-s and 57.3% for the stai-t. internal consistency was high for both abbreviated instruments ( = 0.804). cfa indicated mixed but broadly acceptable fit for the two-factor solutions (stai-s: χ/df = 3.66, cfi = 0.979, srmr = 0.033, rmsea = 0.098; stai-t: χ/df = 3.28, cfi = 0.987, srmr = 0.028, rmsea = 0.091). standardized factor loadings ranged from 0.61 to 0.92 across models. invariance of item thresholds and factor loadings held across clinical/community status, sex, and age in analyses treating the items as ordered-categorical. the shortened versions also showed a high correlation with the original 20-item scales and preserved their criterion-related performance. concurrent validity was supported by correlations with the generalized anxiety disorder-7 and the satisfaction with life scale.
conclusion: the findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the reliability and structural validity of the six-item stai-s and stai-t in turkish adolescents. the abbreviated forms appear suitable for research use, whereas their clinical utility requires confirmation in independent samples. frontiers in psychology

construction of a digital literacy education support model and development and validation of a scale for physical education majors in china. introduction: physical education majors have a dual identity as current learners and future educators. their digital literacy is not only related to their adaptation to digital learning environments but also directly influences the development of their future competence in physical education teaching, training organization, and management practice. therefore, it is necessary to systematically identify and strengthen educational support for their digital literacy development. however, existing studies have mainly focused on digital literacy levels or single influencing factors, with insufficient attention paid to the educational support structure underlying the formation of digital literacy. in particular, standardized measurement tools tailored to the context of physical education remain limited. this study aimed to construct a digital literacy education support model for physical education majors in china and to develop and validate a corresponding scale.
methods: semi-structured interviews were conducted with 22 physical education majors and 12 university teachers and counselors. the interview data were analyzed using grounded theory through three-stage coding, which identified five main categories: personal traits, symbiotic environment, school environment, social environment, and policy and institutional system. based on these categories, an educational support model was constructed. subsequently, an initial item pool was developed through literature analysis and expert review, and item analysis, exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and reliability and validity testing were conducted using pilot and formal survey data.
results: the results showed that exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor structure, explaining 58.119% of the total variance. confirmatory factor analysis indicated good model fit (/df = 2.725, rmsea = 0.037, cfi = 0.968, tli = 0.965, ifi = 0.968). cronbach's alpha coefficients, split-half reliability, and test-retest reliability for all dimensions met recommended psychometric standards, and the scale demonstrated good convergent and discriminant validity.
discussion: the findings suggest that the development of digital literacy among physical education majors is shaped by the joint effects of multilevel support involving individual, relational, school, social, and institutional conditions. the developed 30-item scale shows good reliability and validity and can provide a theoretical basis and practical tool for universities to diagnose and improve educational support for digital literacy among physical education majors. frontiers in psychology

psychometric validation and nomological network of the amsterdam executive function inventory (aefi) in ecuadorian adolescents. executive functions (efs) are vital for cognitive self-regulation and goal pursuit during adolescence, yet validated rating scales remain scarce in latin america. this study evaluated the psychometric properties, item-level operating characteristics, and nomological network of the amsterdam executive function inventory (aefi) in an ecuadorian adolescent sample (n = 830; aged 12-18 years; m = 14.30, sd = 1.75; 52.77% female). employing a split-sample derivation and validation approach with ordinal diagonally weighted least squares estimation, the original 13-item structure yielded poor fit. following item refinement, a revised 10-item, three-factor model across attention, self-control, and planning demonstrated robust cross-validated structural fit (robust cfi = 0.970, robust tli = 0.958, robust rmsea = 0.048, srmr = 0.043) and scalar measurement invariance across early (12-14 years) and late (15-18 years) adolescence. dimension-specific graded response modelling confirmed adequate item functioning, with measurement precision concentrated across average latent trait levels (θ = -2.0 to 2.0). nomological network analyses corroborated construct validity via strong associations with self-reported behavioural dysregulation and affective disruption on the sena and pai-a, alongside expected cross-informant divergence across family and school reports and limited discriminant separation from somatic complaints. these findings establish the revised 10-item aefi as a promising, structurally invariant, and psychometrically adequate brief self-report measure for developmental and educational research in ecuadorian youth. behavioral sciences

variability of stepping characteristics in sauropods introduction: in quadrupeds, the motor repertoire of the forelimbs is typically more diverse than that of the hindlimbs due to more pronounced supraspinal control. this greater supraspinal control may manifest as lesser automaticity in forelimb movements during a relatively simple motor task, such as locomotion. the degree of automaticity can be estimated by the variability of certain movement parameters. however, such variability is rarely assessed separately for the forelimbs and hindlimbs. sauropods appear to be the only group of animals for which, based on available data, it is possible to estimate the variability of stepping parameters for both the forelimbs and hindlimbs. methods: the forelimb and hindlimb stride length and step width were measured using outline drawings of 27 relatively long sauropod trackways. their coefficients of variation were then calculated. results: an analysis of trackways revealed significant differences in the variability of step width and stride length between the forelimbs and hindlimbs for some trackways. in some cases, the stepping parameters of the hindlimbs were more variable. significant negative correlations were found between estimated walking speed and (i) the coefficient of variation (cv) of forelimb stride length and (ii) the cv of hindlimb step width. conclusions: these findings are consistent with a greater contribution of hindlimb-related mechanisms to locomotor organization in sauropods compared with several extant quadrupedal taxa. brain behavior and evolution

therapeutic alliance and predictive validity of reflective functioning in conjoint mentalization-based treatment for borderline personality disorder. objective: few studies have investigated the therapeutic alliance in treatment of patients with borderline personality disorder (bpd), particularly regarding alliance in group psychotherapy. this study aimed to investigate the development of therapeutic alliance in a 3-year outpatient mentalization-based treatment (mbt) program for bpd combining individual and group psychotherapy, and to examine whether reflective functioning (rf) predicted alliance development.
method: patients with bpd or significant sub-threshold borderline personality pathology were included, with baseline data from 47 patients and longitudinal data from 42. baseline assessment comprised diagnostic interviews, self-report measures, and interview-based measures of rf. patient-reported alliance was assessed every 6 months using the working alliance inventory (subscales bond, task and goal) for individual psychotherapy and the group questionnaire (domains positive bond, positive work and negative relationship with their respective subscales) for group psychotherapy. main statistical method was linear mixed models.
results: in individual psychotherapy, initial alliance levels were satisfactory across all subscales. over the course of treatment, the bond level remained stable, whereas task and goal showed small but statistically significant increases. in group psychotherapy, positive bond was high initially and stable during treatment. for the positive work domain and its two subscales, initial levels were below the satisfactory range. during treatment, there was a small but significant increase in agreement on tasks and goals with the other group members but not with the therapists. for the negative relationship domain and its three subscales, all estimates except one were within the satisfactory range initially. initial level of the subscale group members was outside the satisfactory range, indicating somewhat strained relationships with the other group members. longitudinally, there were no improvements for the domain or subscales. rf at baseline had no significant effect on the therapeutic alliance in either treatment modality.
conclusion: the study demonstrates overall satisfactory levels of therapeutic alliance in an mbt program for bpd but also indicates specific alliance-related challenges in the group psychotherapy component. initial level of rf may not affect the therapeutic alliance in mbt treatment.

distinctive features of phubbing behavior and being phubbed in adolescents: empathy, social cognition, interpersonal competence, and smartphone addiction. the aim of our study is to concurrently examine, within the same structural model, the effects of social cognitive functions, empathy, emotional regulation difficulties, interpersonal competence and smartphone addiction on adolescents who display phubbing behavior and those who are being phubbed. a cross-sectional study was carried out with the participation of 305 adolescents between the ages of 16 and 18. the difficulties in emotion regulation scale-short form, interpersonal reactivity index, interpersonal competence scale, generic scale of phubbing and generic scale of being phubbed, smartphone addiction scale and reading the mind in the eyes test were administered to the participants. smartphone addiction was positively associated with phubbing behavior (β = 0.775,< 0.001), whereas interpersonal competence was negatively associated with phubbing (β = -0.145,< 0.001). a significant positive indirect association between emotional regulation difficulties and phubbing behavior via smartphone addiction was observed (β = 0.273,< 0.001). interpersonal reactivity was positively associated with being phubbed (β = 0.203,= 0.001), whereas social cognition was not significantly associated with either outcome. our findings suggest that different socio-cognitive competencies and smartphone addiction may be associated with phubbing in adolescents, and that these associations may differ between phubbing behavior and being phubbed. behavioral sciences

risky riding violations among motorcycle riders through an integrated model of behavioral, psychological and workload factors risky violation behavior among motorcycle riders engaged in goods-delivery and service activities poses a significant challenge to road safety, particularly amid the growing demand for platform-based commercial motorcycle services. this research developed a unified structural model to investigate how theory of planned behavior (tpb) constructs, risk perception, personal traits and workload are associated with risky riding violations across behavioral, perceptual, individual and occupational dimensions. a survey of 1400 commercial riders working in food-delivery and ride-hailing services was conducted, with 1251 samples analyzed after screening. thereafter, the hypothesized associations among the constructs were evaluated through structural equation modeling (sem). the results suggested that perceived social pressure and personality characteristics were positively associated with risky violation behavior, whereas attitudes and workload demonstrated negative associations with risky violation behavior. furthermore, when the structural model was examined separately according to work experience, differences in the patterns and strengths of the relationships among the factors were observed. overall, risky riding violations appear to arise from a combination of behavioral, individual and occupational conditions with the strength and direction of these associations differing across levels of work experience. therefore, road safety interventions should consider the specific characteristics and experience levels of commercial riders rather than applying a uniform approach to all riders. tailored strategies addressing the distinct behavioral and contextual factors of different rider groups may contribute to more effective risk reduction and road safety promotion. behavioral sciences

interpersonal emotion regulation in middle childhood: from cognitive capacity to context-sensitive regulation. interpersonal emotion regulation (ier) requires individuals to understand another person's emotional state and adapt regulatory decisions to interpersonal goals and situational demands. across four linked studies, the present research examined age-related patterns, cognitive and social-cognitive correlates, contextual modulation, and individual differences in context sensitivity in children aged 8-10 years. ier was assessed using vignette-based strategy ratings, executive-function and social-cognitive measures, and experimental manipulations of regulatory goals and demands. across the observed age range, increasing age was associated with greater cognitive and affective engagement and lower avoidance and co-rumination, whereas distraction and suppression showed no significant age associations. executive function, empathy, and theory of mind were systematically associated with greater adaptive and lower maladaptive ier. children also altered their regulatory decisions as social goals and regulatory demands changed. person-by-context analyses showed selective effects: general cognitive-control capacity moderated responsiveness to regulatory goals, whereas social cognition moderated demand-related variation in cognitive engagement. together, the findings suggest that ier in middle childhood involves not only developing regulatory capacities but also coordinating those capacities with the goals and demands of interpersonal situations. behavioral sciences

creativity in design education: an educational psychology model of motivation, cognitive load, and self-efficacy. objective: this study examines the statistical relationships among learning motivation, cognitive load, creative self-efficacy, and expert-rated creative performance among undergraduate design students.
methods: a quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted with 428 valid responses from undergraduate students majoring in design-related disciplines. students first completed a design task, after which questionnaire data were collected and anonymized design works were evaluated by three independent experts. spss was used for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, regression-based path analysis, and bootstrap tests of statistical indirect effects; amos was used to evaluate the measurement model.
results: learning motivation and germane cognitive load were positively associated with creative self-efficacy. creative self-efficacy showed the strongest positive association with design creative performance, and germane cognitive load showed a smaller positive direct association. extraneous cognitive load was negatively correlated with creative performance at the bivariate level, but its adjusted direct path was not statistically significant; therefore, h5 was not supported. intrinsic cognitive load was not significant. bootstrap results indicated significant statistical indirect relationships through creative self-efficacy.
conclusion: the findings suggest that design creativity is associated with students' motivation, meaningful cognitive engagement, and creative self-beliefs. because the questionnaire was administered after the design task, the indirect effects should be interpreted as statistical indirect relationships rather than evidence of causal or temporal mediation. frontiers in psychology

beyond a single continuum: latent profiles of flourishing and burnout among chinese teachers. teacher flourishing and burnout have often been viewed as opposing work experiences, implying that higher levels of one should be accompanied by lower levels of the other. however, recent research suggests that these experiences can coexist within the same individual. we extend this line of research by using latent profile analysis to examine how multiple dimensions of flourishing and burnout combine in different ways among 5694 primary and secondary school teachers in china. five profiles were identified: broadly adaptive (61.19%), struggling (19.41%), engaged-strained (8.96%), unfulfilled (6.29%), and depleted-disconnected (4.16%). broadly adaptive and struggling teachers followed the expected inverse pattern between flourishing and burnout. in contrast, engaged-strained teachers maintained moderate levels of flourishing and relatively high personal accomplishment despite substantial emotional exhaustion and depersonalization; unfulfilled teachers showed favorable flourishing and low exhaustion and depersonalization but extremely low personal accomplishment; and depleted-disconnected teachers showed particularly poor emotional and social well-being alongside elevated exhaustion. these findings advance our understanding of teacher flourishing and burnout beyond a single-continuum model, although sensitivity analyses indicated that the retained profile solution was sensitive to the composition of the personal accomplishment measure, particularly for the struggling and unfulfilled profiles. rather than asking simply whether teachers are flourishing or struggling with burnout, schools may benefit from asking in what areas teachers are feeling or functioning well and in what areas they are struggling. behavioral sciences

physicians’ metacognition in medical decision-making abstract a large literature reports that physicians are overconfident when making medical decisions. however, the validity of these findings is questioned due to methodology pitfalls leading to poor ecological validity. moreover, most previous studies do not distinguish between (i) metacognitive bias, the general tendency to report high or low confidence irrespectively of actual accuracy, and (ii) metacognitive sensitivity, the capacity to discriminate between one’s own correct and incorrect decisions. here, we aim to overcome these limitations by drawing from state-of-the-art paradigms and tools from the cognitive science of metacognition. to examine overconfidence and to disentangle metacognitive bias from metacognitive sensitivity, we developed a carefully controlled set of case-vignettes of patients with headaches that was completed by 52 physicians. we found that physicians’ confidence, reliably discriminated their correct from their incorrect decisions, demonstrating genuine metacognitive sensitivity. however, physicians were also overconfident, and this overconfidence was most pronounced among the least accurate participants. moreover, the costliest errors (i.e. missed urgent cases) were held with higher confidence than unnecessary referrals. finally, unlike previous reports, we found limited interindividual variability depending on specialty, gender, or seniority level, although our study was not powered for these comparisons. highlights physicians were overconfident, replicating previous reports, yet their confidence reliably discriminated correct from incorrect decisions—genuine metacognitive sensitivity, quantified here for the first time with signal detection theory metrics. metacognitive measures showed limited variation by specialty, gender, or seniority (the study was not powered for these comparisons), though specialties differed markedly in their urgency-referral criterion. the costliest errors—missed urgent cases—were held with higher confidence than unnecessary referrals. refining medical training to assess and cultivate metacognitive sensitivity—rather than merely mitigating overconfidence—could help better align confidence judgments with diagnostic accuracy. neuroscience of consciousness

the influence of maternal representations of the child on parenting behaviors: a longitudinal study from pregnancy to 4 years postpartum abstract maternal representations of the child begin forming during pregnancy and evolve through interactions with the baby. research suggests that prenatal representations may have a more stable impact on parenting than postnatal representations, but their long‐term impact remains unclear. this study examines (1) how prenatal and 1‐year postnatal representations are associated with parenting when child is age 4 and (2) whether prenatal representations have a more enduring influence on later caregiving than postnatal representations by exploring how stability or shifts in representations across time shape parenting. one hundred fifty‐five us mothers, oversampled for intimate partner violence and low income, participated in this longitudinal study. prenatal balanced representations were significantly associated with more sensitive and less unresponsive parenting, whereas disengaged representations were linked to lower sensitivity and greater unresponsiveness. postnatal representations predicted sensitive parenting but were not significantly associated with intrusive or unresponsive behaviors. examination of changes in prenatal to postnatal representations revealed that mothers who shifted from balanced (prenatal) to non‐balanced (postnatal) representations displayed higher sensitivity than those who remained non‐balanced. results highlight the consistent impact of prenatal representations on parenting, emphasizing the need for timely interventions during pregnancy and the early postpartum period to promote positive parenting. infant mental health journal-infancy and early childhood

psychological wellbeing among university students: a biopsychosocial model of resilience, perceived stress, social support, and physical activity. introduction: drawing on the biopsychosocial model, this study examined how resilience, perceived stress, social support, and physical activity influence psychological wellbeing among university students.
methods: a cross-sectional survey was conducted with 452 undergraduate students from universities in shandong province, china. structural equation modeling (sem) was employed to test direct and mediating effects, while moderation analyses were used to examine interaction effects.
results: the results indicated that: (1) resilience had a significant negative effect on perceived stress and a significant positive effect on psychological wellbeing; (2) perceived stress significantly and negatively predicted psychological wellbeing; (3) perceived stress partially mediated the relationship between resilience and psychological wellbeing, indicating that resilience enhanced wellbeing both directly and indirectly by reducing stress; (4) social support significantly moderated the association between resilience and perceived stress, such that the stress-buffering effect of resilience was stronger at higher levels of social support; and (5) physical activity significantly moderated the relationship between perceived stress and psychological wellbeing, with higher levels of physical activity weakening the negative impact of stress on psychological wellbeing.
discussion: by integrating psychological, social, and behavioral factors within a biopsychosocial framework, this study clarifies the mechanisms underlying psychological wellbeing among university students. the findings highlight the importance of resilience development, stress reduction, social support enhancement, and physical activity promotion in university-based mental health education and intervention programs. frontiers in psychology

parental emotion regulation, psychological distress, and family involvement in education among chilean caregivers: an observed-variable analysis. this study examined the association between parental emotion regulation (er) and family involvement in education (fie), including the potential mediating role of psychological distress, operationalized through depressive, anxiety, and stress symptomatology (dass), and the moderating role of caregiver gender, while accounting for sociodemographic variables. a cross-sectional study was conducted with a sample of= 219 chilean parents/caregivers. the emotion regulation evaluation scale (re-mesacts), the depression, anxiety and stress scale (dass-21), and the family involvement in education scale (epfe) were administered. a sequential observed-variable analytical strategy combining regression, mediation with non-parametric bootstrap (5000 resamples), moderation, covariate-adjusted models, and complementary sensitivity analyses was employed. er was positively associated with fie after accounting for dass (β = 0.230,= 0.004) and negatively associated with dass (β = -0.410,< 0.001). however, dass was not significantly associated with fie (β = -0.065,= 0.365), and the indirect effect of er on fie through dass was not statistically significant (= 0.026,= 0.374). a statistically significant er × gender interaction was observed (= 0.739,< 0.001). simple-slope analyses showed a positive association among female caregivers (= 0.345,< 0.001) and a negative association among male caregivers (= -0.394,= 0.021). an exploratory complementary multigroup analysis showed that the er → fie path differed between gender groups, χ(1) = 7.90,= 0.005. most sociodemographic covariates were not significantly associated with fie; however, caregivers of students attending private fee-paying schools reported significantly higher fie than those associated with public schools ( = 3.162,= 0.045). overall, er was positively associated with educational involvement, whereas dass did not statistically mediate the er-fie association. the observed er × gender interaction suggests a potential gender-dependent pattern; however, because the male subgroup was small (= 38), the gender-specific estimates should be regarded as preliminary and require replication in larger and more gender-balanced samples. the findings highlight the relevance of parental emotion regulation for family involvement and provide a basis for further investigation of psychological and sociodemographic factors associated with educational involvement. behavioral sciences

relative deprivation and suicidal ideation among chinese college students: the mediating role of psychological pain and the moderating role of social support. suicidal ideation remains a longstanding and critical issue in mental health research due to its serious consequences for individuals' lives and well-being. although relative deprivation has been identified as an important risk factor for suicidal ideation, the mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. drawing on multiple theoretical perspectives, including the strain theory of suicide and the stress-buffering model, this study examined a moderated mediation model linking relative deprivation to suicidal ideation, with psychological pain as the mediator and social support as the moderator. a cross-sectional survey was conducted among 630 college students. participants completed self-report measures of relative deprivation, psychological pain, perceived social support, and suicidal ideation. the findings revealed that relative deprivation was positively associated with suicidal ideation and that psychological pain mediated this association (= 0.066, 95% ci = [0.028, 0.121]). moreover, social support significantly moderated both stages of the mediation process, weakening the positive effect of relative deprivation on psychological pain and the positive effect of psychological pain on suicidal ideation (= -0.130, 95% ci = [-0.190, -0.070];= -0.089, 95% ci = [-0.150, -0.028]). overall, the findings suggest that relative deprivation contributes to suicidal ideation through psychological pain and that social support serves as an important boundary condition in this process. these findings extend existing theoretical frameworks and offer practical implications for suicide prevention among college students. behavioral sciences

the psychology of learning with generative ai in foreign language education: building a theory of metacognition, trust, and human-ai co-regulation through a systematic review. generative artificial intelligence (genai) is reshaping foreign language education, yet the psychological processes underlying effective learner-ai interaction remain fragmented. this theory-building systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on metacognition, trust, and human-ai co-regulation in genai-supported foreign language learning. following prisma 2020 procedures, web of science and scopus were searched for studies published from 2022 to june 2026. after screening, 51 empirical studies were included. the findings show that metacognition shapes learners' planning, monitoring, regulation, and reflection; trust influences how learners accept, verify, modify, or reject ai-generated information and feedback; and human-ai co-regulation involves the dynamic distribution of cognitive and regulatory activity between learners and genai within teacher-mediated instructional contexts. ai literacy and learner agency further support critical evaluation, strategic ai use, and retention of human decision-making responsibility. based on these findings, the review develops the metacognition-trust-co-regulation (mtc) framework, which conceptualizes effective genai-assisted learning as an iterative process in which metacognitive regulation informs trust, trust calibrates reliance, and reliance shapes human-ai co-regulation. the framework positions genai as a cognitive partner whose educational value depends on critically informed, metacognitively regulated, and humanly governed use. frontiers in psychology

from pattern recognition to abstract representation: visual search and neural mechanisms of structured pattern processing in skilled basketball players. objective: this study employed eye-tracking and erp to investigate structured pattern processing in basketball players of different skill levels.
methods: a skill-level comparison (skilled vs. less-skilled) was adopted. participants viewed static point-light displays depicting basketball half-court configurations, with structured (typical tactical formations) and unstructured (random positions) conditions randomly presented. participants predicted offensive actions while behavioral, eye-tracking, and erp data were simultaneously recorded.
results: skilled players showed higher decision accuracy than less-skilled players under structured conditions but not under unstructured conditions, whereas they responded significantly faster under both conditions, with a larger group difference under structured conditions. for pupil diameter, skilled players showed smaller pupil diameters than less-skilled players under both conditions, while within the skilled group pupil diameter was larger under structured than unstructured conditions. eye-tracking revealed fewer total fixations and a distinct gaze distribution in skilled players-more fixations on opponents and the ball, fewer on open space-along with larger pupil diameters under structured conditions, suggesting enhanced cognitive engagement. erp data showed that skilled players exhibited larger p300 and lnc amplitudes under structured conditions, reflecting enhanced semantic mapping and schema-based retrieval.
conclusions: these findings are consistent with a theoretical perspective in which expertise may involve a shift from "pattern recognition" toward "abstract representation," rather than a reduction in neural activity. however, abstract representation, neural information density, and semantic encoding were not directly measured in the present study. the transformer architecture is therefore offered as a conceptual analogy-its multi-head self-attention corresponds to skilled players' hierarchical visual sampling, its encoder to semantic mapping (p300 enhancement), and its memory integration to schema-based retrieval (lnc enhancement). these findings provide a basis for structured situational training in sport decision-making. journal of eye movement research

the social intelligence reliance halo: perceived social understanding, epistemic trust, and reliance quality in human-ai decision making. as generative ai systems become more socially responsive, personalized, and perspective-aware, a central question is whether such features improve human-ai decision quality or simply make ai advice more influential. this study introduces the social intelligence reliance halo as a proposed social-to-epistemic spillover pattern in which perceived social understanding functions as a non-diagnostic cue for epistemic evaluation: an ai that appears to understand the user may also be granted greater epistemic authority or reliability even when the relational cue provides no evidence of factual accuracy. a randomized two-condition experiment was conducted with 462 working adults with recent generative-ai experience. participants interacted with either a high social-intelligence (high-si) relational framing package or a neutral ai across six repeated decision trials. post-interaction measures assessed perceived social intelligence, epistemic authority, epistemic reliability, suspension of critical judgment, verification behavior, and ai literacy; trial-level behavioral reliance was analyzed with generalized estimating equations. the randomized high-si package increased perceived social intelligence and increased advice-taking both when participants were initially correct and the contingent ai recommendation was wrong (or = 1.507,< .001) and when participants were initially incorrect and the recommendation was correct (or = 1.800,< .001). the condition × participant-dependent advice-correctness interaction was nonsignificant (or = 1.195,= .289), providing no reliable evidence that the randomized treatment effect differed across these two states. because recommendation correctness was mechanically determined by participants' initial accuracy rather than independently randomized, this interaction is interpreted as exploratory treatment heterogeneity across participant-dependent correctness states rather than evidence that the high-si package altered sensitivity to ai accuracy. post-interaction perceived social intelligence was positively associated with epistemic authority and reliability, and ai literacy was associated with lower suspension of critical judgment and greater verification; these associations do not establish temporal or causal mediation. the study therefore provides experimental evidence that a bundled relational framing package can amplify both beneficial and harmful reliance, while the proposed social-to-epistemic pathway and accuracy-sensitive reliance remain questions for stronger future designs. journal of intelligence

developing a workplace institutional betrayal measure using a survivor-led qualitative methodology institutional betrayal, a concept coined by jennifer freyd, has been used to understand institutional responses to sexual violence predominantly in a university setting and specific workplaces (e.g., military). the institutional betrayal questionnaire (ibq) has been essential in quantitatively measuring survivors’ experiences of institutional betrayal and understanding institutional responses, but it has not been widely applied to workplaces. additionally, most quantitative researchers create measures without input from the population they seek to study, resulting in a top-down approach to research that has been criticized, particularly when done with marginalized populations. the current study developed an adapted version of the ibq as applied to workplaces. in doing so, we directly sought input from survivors on how the original ibq may be modified to more adequately reflect their experiences with reporting sexual assault in the workplace. we identified four relevant themes from 23 interviews with participants who reported their sexual assault in the workplace. these four themes included: clarity of measure, endorsing additional measure items during the interview, suggestions for additional or revised items for the ibq-workplace measure, and other methodological considerations. we present an updated version of the ibq for workplaces based on survivor feedback and discuss future directions for survivor-led research. psychology of women quarterly

variability in preprocessing and analysis of the error‐related negativity in adult response‐conflict studies: a systematic review abstract the analysis of eeg (electroencephalography) data affords many defensible choices, creating substantial researcher degrees of freedom. while stimulus‐locked components such as the n400 show wide methodological variability and incomplete reporting, it has been unclear whether this generalizes to the response‐locked error‐related negativity (ern). we conducted a prisma‐guided systematic review of ern studies published 1995–2025. from a chronologically stratified sample of 202 studies of adults using conventional response‐conflict tasks and conventional erp analyses, we extracted preprocessing and quantification choices, assessed reporting completeness, examined temporal trends, and tested predictors of pipeline decisions (e.g., montage size, amplifier, analysis software, task). ern pipelines and order of analysis steps were highly heterogeneous, no two studies used the same workflow, and reporting gaps persisted. several analytic decisions showed modest temporal shifts, yet overall diversity remained high. sample sizes increased over time but remained insufficient for typical small‐to‐moderate sized effects, and detailed preregistrations were extremely rare. none of the 32 processing and analysis choices examined in more detail varied systematically by task, and only a subset was linked to recording parameters (e.g., montage size, amplifier, analysis software). across adult ern studies using conventional response‐conflict tasks and conventional erp analyses, we observed substantial methodological heterogeneity, limited convergence in analytic practice, and considerable potential for analytic flexibility. together this may complicate the comparison and synthesis of findings across studies. psychophysiology

inducing interpersonal closeness: effects on inter‐brain synchrony and collaborative performance abstract feeling close to another person is widely assumed to facilitate collaboration. however, causal evidence that interpersonal closeness improves collaborative behavior remains limited, and it is unclear whether any such influence is accompanied by increased synchrony at the neural level. previous studies comparing inter‐brain synchrony (ibs) and collaborative performance across relationship types (e.g., friends vs. strangers) have reported better collaboration and higher ibs in closer relationships, but these effects are confounded by familiarity and shared interaction history. to address these limitations, we experimentally manipulated interpersonal closeness in 123 dyads of strangers ( n = 246) to test its causal influence on ibs and collaborative performance. dyads were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: no interaction, small talk, or a closeness‐generating conversation. after the manipulation, dyads completed a collaborative task while undergoing mobile eeg hyperscanning. the manipulation was effective: perceived closeness increased significantly between the no‐interaction, small‐talk, and closeness‐generating conversation conditions. however, induced closeness did not affect collaborative performance or ibs during collaboration. these findings suggest that the better collaboration and higher ibs often reported for pre‐existing relationships in previous studies may originate from factors beyond momentary feelings of closeness, such as familiarity derived from prior interaction. interestingly, across all dyads, we observed a negative association between central delta ibs and collaborative performance, with ibs explaining unique variance beyond self‐reported measures. this negative link is consistent with the idea that, in this context, ibs reflects speech‐tracking and increased cognitive demands during coordination, rather than coordination efficiency. psychophysiology

cross‐cultural dimensions of communication in aging: a review and update abstract this article reviews and updates the current state of communication, culture, and aging research. although novel avenues of investigation within the discipline continue to evolve, extant research findings are categorized into three principal areas. first, and somewhat counterintuitively, evidence suggests individuals in many east asian cultures report meaningfully greater negative attitudes toward older people than those in north american, western european, and australasian samples, a finding that requires contextual interpretation regarding cultural norms and the reporting of aging perceptions. second, cultures may be becoming more similar in their perceptions of aging due to factors including modernization and cultural convergence, and third, there is considerable interregional variability (e.g., within asia) in people's perceptions of communication and aging. communication, whether mediated, face‐to‐face, or other, is central to how we relate to and interact with those of the same and different ages. topics in cognitive science

association between impulsivity, depression, and non-suicidal self-injury in youths: a study combining variable-centered and person-centered approaches youth represents a critical transitional phase from adolescence to adulthood, characterized by significant psychological changes and challenges. non-suicidal self-injury (nssi), defined as the intentional harm to one’s body tissue without suicidal intent, is increasingly conceptualized as a transdiagnostic entity that often emerges during this period. this study examines the combined effects of impulsivity and depression on nssi in youths from both variable-centered and person-centered approaches. a total of 2,292 university students were recruited for this study, in which we performed moderation and latent profile analyses. the results indicated that impulsivity and depression interact to significantly influence nssi. specifically, high levels of impulsivity and depression were associated with elevated nssi scores. furthermore, latent profile analysis identified four subtypes of impulsivity-depression, with the “high impulsivity-high depression” type exhibiting the most severe nssi. these findings highlight the importance of considering both impulsivity and depression in understanding and preventing nssi among youths. psychological reports

recreational screen use and internalizing problems from preadolescence to young adulthood in a longitudinal twin cohort with co-twin comparison abstract the mental health impact of increasing recreational screen use among youth has raised substantial concerns, yet questions about causality remain unresolved. here, leveraging a co-twin control design, we examined associations between screen use and internalizing problems from childhood to early adulthood among 21,797 swedish twins, accounting for shared familial factors. recreational screen use was associated with increased internalizing symptoms and clinical diagnosed depression and anxiety. however, these associations were substantially attenuated within discordant twin pairs and did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. these findings suggest that shared genetic and environmental factors partly explain the association between youth screen use and mental health. although co-twin estimates provided limited evidence for clear causal effects, the association between heavy interactive screen use and clinical risk highlights the need to understand potential mechanisms linking digital behaviours and youth mental health. nature human behaviour

uncovering the behavioural mechanisms underlying rebound effects of sustainability‐oriented interventions abstract despite the recognition of rebound effects (re) in offsetting potential sustainability gains, a comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms remains limited. this study contributes by uncovering the psychological determinants leading to re, while adopting an interdisciplinary approach that goes beyond the environmental sustainability domain. a systematic literature review of 135 publications resulted in the hierarchical consolidation of 30 unique behavioural rebound mechanisms. a critical evaluation highlighted their strengths and limitations in terms of addressed intervention types, outcome domains and effect types (i.e., behavioural, temporal, contextual and interpersonal). the results are inductively synthesised into a proposed novel conceptual model explaining behavioural re as the result of changes in psychological determinants related to (i) environmental perceptions, (ii) non‐environmental perceptions, (iii) intrinsic motivation and (iv) bounded rationality. the findings are translated into eight agenda points for behavioural rebound research, along with a discussion of practical implications and possibilities for preventing re. applied psychology-an international review-psychologie appliquee-revue internationale

social media exposure and anxiety and depression in young people: a systematic review and meta‐analysis of longitudinal and experimental studies abstract objectives the aim of the current review was to comprehensively synthesize the evidence for the relationship between social media use and anxiety and depression symptoms in young people using data from robust methodological designs, namely, longitudinal and experimental studies. methods psycinfo, web of science, medline, embase and scopus databases were searched for peer‐reviewed, english‐language, longitudinal and experimental studies. included studies measured smu in terms of time or frequency of use, mainly via self‐report, used standardized measures of depression and anxiety, and recruited samples ranging from 10 to 24 years of age. results screening retrieved 37 eligible studies that included 36 longitudinal observational studies and one experiment. twelve studies examined depression outcomes (pooled r = .08, 95% cis [0.04, 0.11]), and five studies examined anxiety (pooled r = 0.093, 95% cis [0.059, 0.126]), showing very small linear effects. there were no moderating effects for year of publication, duration of follow‐up or mean age of sample for the depression effects. conclusions given the very weak relationships between smu and the severity of anxiety and depression symptoms, smu is unlikely to account for the contemporary youth mental health crisis. further longitudinal research designed to examine potential non‐monotonic relationships between smu and adverse mental health outcomes is required, along with attention to other potential causes of increased prevalence of mental health problems in young people. british journal of clinical psychology

is timing everything? age-related differences in the use of temporal agency cues abstract sense of agency (soa) is the subjective experience of controlling one’s own actions and their effects. to infer soa people rely, among other cues, on temporal cues such as temporal contiguity (i.e. the closeness in time between action and effect) and temporal expectation (i.e. the match between expected and actual timing of an effect). we investigated whether the use of temporal cues and their interplay differ between younger (18–28 years) and older (65–75 years) adults. in the experiment, participants first completed adaptation blocks to form expectations regarding the timing of an effect. in adaptation blocks, actions were followed either by immediate (immediate effect condition) or by delayed (delayed effect condition) effects. in subsequent test blocks, the action-effect delay was varied, and participants soa over the effect was assessed. across both age groups, soa increased, the more the timing of the actual effect corresponded to the expected effect, indicating that temporal expectation is used as primary agency cue. however, in younger (but not in older) adults, the change in soa as a function of delay was steeper in the immediate effect condition than in the delayed effect condition. this may indicate that temporal contiguity and temporal expectation have reinforced each other in the immediate effect condition but counteracted each other in the delayed effect condition. thus, whereas both age groups primarily rely on temporal expectation, younger adults may additionally integrate temporal contiguity when inferring soa. psychological research-psychologische forschung

decoding the anxiety burden in asia and developing an xgboost‐based online screening tool using korean data abstract anxiety disorders impose a substantial burden across asia, yet comprehensive regional surveillance remains limited. in addition, the utility of the health‐related quality of life instrument with 8 items (hint‐8) for anxiety screening in the korean population has not been fully clarified. this study integrated data from global burden of disease (gbd) 2021 and korea national health and nutrition examination survey (knhanes) to comprehensively assess the prevalence, incidence, and disability‐adjusted life year (daly) rates of anxiety disorders across 48 asian countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. joinpoint regression, age‐period‐cohort modelling, decomposition analysis, and health inequality indices were employed to analyse trends and driving factors. in the korean dataset, eight machine learning algorithms were compared. shap analysis was used to interpret the results, and the best‐performing model was ultimately developed into an online prediction model. in 2021, asia accounted for over half of global anxiety cases, and age‐standardized rates increased by 14.6%–17.1% since 1990. after 2019, incidence (apc = 9.532%) and daly rates (apc = 9.157%) rose sharply. burden patterns varied by sex and age, and population growth was a major driver. in the korean dataset, xgboost showed the best performance (auc = 0.894). an 8‐feature parsimonious model performed comparably to the 17‐feature model while improving interpretability and practical feasibility. asia's growing anxiety burden demands prioritised care for women, adolescents, and middle‐aged populations and better crisis mental health services. a korean machine‐learning tool shows potential but requires broader asian validation. stress and health

psychometric properties of the childhood trauma questionnaire-short form (ctq-sf) in adolescents from the peruvian amazon. childhood trauma is a significant public health problem owing to its effects on the socioemotional development of adolescents, which calls for validated assessment instruments. this study aimed to adapt and examine the psychometric properties of the childhood trauma questionnaire-short form (ctq-sf) in adolescents from the peruvian amazon. an instrumental, cross-sectional study was conducted with 878 adolescents aged 12-17 years (m = 14.0; sd = 1.46) from public secondary schools in the san martín region, peru, randomly divided into two subsamples of 439 participants each for exploratory (efa) and confirmatory factor analysis (cfa); reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, and measurement invariance across sex were also examined. the original five-factor model did not show adequate performance. after removing items with weak loadings or redundant content, a three-factor, 18-item structure emerged-lack of perceived family support/neglect, sexual abuse, and physical-emotional abuse-which showed adequate fit (cfi = 0.958; tli = 0.951; rmsea = 0.051; srmr = 0.067) and satisfactory internal consistency (ordinaland = 0.76-0.95). convergent validity was adequate for sexual abuse and physical-emotional abuse (ave = 0.81 and 0.50) and borderline for lack of perceived family support/neglect (ave = 0.42), whereas discriminant validity was supported for all factor pairs (htmt = 0.262-0.626). full scalar invariance across sex was also established (δcfi ≤ 0.002; δrmsea ≤ 0.003). these findings indicate that the peruvian ctq-sf is better represented by a three-factor correlated structure, yielding a brief version that allows comparisons between sexes; nevertheless, because its temporal stability and external validity remain to be examined, its use should currently be restricted to research and preliminary screening purposes. frontiers in psychology

psychological impacts of exercise snacks vs. traditional exercise: a comparative study. this study conducted a 4-week randomized controlled trial to compare the psychometric profiles and adherence patterns of exercise snacks group (esg)-a high-frequency, fragmented exercise protocol-against traditional exercise group (teg)-continuous exercise-under volume-equated conditions (90 min/week at 40%). a total of 180 participants were evaluated on perceived stress (ps), decision fatigue and cognitive load (dfcl), and physical activity enjoyment (pae; reverse-scored to reflect negative psychological appraisal). the results indicated that the esg cohort experienced significantly higher levels of ps, dfcl, and lower physical activity enjoyment [higher pae inverse score, alongside a markedly higher attrition rate (15.56%) compared to the teg cohort (5.56%).] intra-group correlation analyses confirmed operational independence among psychometric indicators across both modalities, demonstrating that high-frequency protocols introduce distinct cognitive and affective costs without confounding measurement structures. these findings indicate that while esg offers a schedule-flexible approach for physical health, its high-frequency demands introduce notable "behavioral friction" and cognitive strain. consequently, practitioners and researchers must carefully balance the metabolic benefits of fragmented exercise against its psychological costs to ensure sustainable adherence for general populations. frontiers in psychology

development and initial psychometric validation of the psychological exemption zone perception scale in reverse mobility among doctoral talent. against the backdrop of market-oriented career environments and increasing performance pressure, some doctoral talent evaluate higher education institution/research work settings as comparatively stable, restorative, controllable, and meaningful career options. however, the existing research lacks a standardized instrument for measuring this subjective evaluation of work settings as psychologically protective environments. building on prior constructivist grounded-theory findings and relevant organizational psychology literature, this study developed and initially validated the psychological exemption zone perception scale (pezps) in the context of reverse mobility among doctoral talent. a multi-stage scale development procedure was adopted. thirty candidate items were generated and reviewed by nine experts, resulting in a 25-item formal scale. using data from 838 valid responses, the sample was randomly divided into an exploratory sample ( = 335) and a validation sample ( = 503). exploratory factor analysis yielded a five-factor structure: perceived institutional shelter, perceived time sovereignty, perceived boundary controllability, perceived restorative security, and perceived meaning-belonging. the five factors explained 65.8% of the total variance, and parallel analysis supported their retention. confirmatory factor analysis showed acceptable model fit,/df = 2.324, cfi (comparative fit index) = 0.943, tli (tucker-lewis index) = 0.935, rmsea (root mean square error of approximation) = 0.051, and srmr (standardized root mean square residual) = 0.041. pezps demonstrated good internal consistency, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, alongside preliminary criterion-related and incremental validity evidence. cronbach'swas 0.902 for the total scale and ranged from 0.839 to 0.881 across dimensions; cr (composite reliability) ranged from 0.834 to 0.881, ave (average variance extracted) from 0.502 to 0.597, and the maximum htmt (heterotrait-monotrait) value was 0.700. pezps total scores were significantly associated with criterion variables in theoretically expected directions and was associated with additional explained variance in reverse mobility intention beyond demographic variables and related psychological indicators. overall, this study advances psychological exemption zone from a qualitative concept to a measurable construct and provides a preliminary tool for studying psychologically protective work-setting evaluations among doctoral talent. further validation across different types of heis and broader career contexts is needed. frontiers in psychology

cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the chinese version of the reward deficiency syndrome questionnaire (rdsq-29). objective: this study aimed to translate the rdsq-29 into chinese and evaluate its reliability, validity, and cross-gender measurement invariance among chinese university students.
methods: a convenience sample of 1,628 university students in xinjiang, china, was recruited for this cross-sectional study. the translation followed the brislin model. psychometric evaluations included item analysis, exploratory factor analysis (efa) conducted in one subsample ( = 883), and confirmatory factor analysis (cfa) conducted in another subsample ( = 745). criterion validity was assessed by examining correlations with the barratt impulsiveness scale-brief (bis-brief) and the internet gaming disorder scale-short form (igdsf-9). internal consistency and test-retest reliability were evaluated, and multi-group cfa was used to assess measurement invariance across genders.
results: the chinese rdsq-29 retained the original five-factor structure (activity, lack of sexual satisfaction, social concerns, risk-seeking behavior, and general reward deficiency). cfa demonstrated excellent model fit (χ/df = 2.790, comparative fit index [cfi] = 0.968, tucker-lewis index [tli] = 0.963, root mean square error of approximation [rmsea] = 0.049). the total score showed strong positive correlations with the bis-brief ( = 0.660, < 0.001) and the igdsf-9 ( = 0.398, < 0.001). internal consistency was excellent (total scale α = 0.975; subscales α values = 0.819-0.957), and test-retest reliability was high (intraclass correlation coefficient [icc] = 0.924). full measurement invariance across genders was established (δcfi ≤ 0.003, δrmsea ≤ 0.001).
conclusion: the chinese version of the rdsq-29 demonstrated good reliability and validity and is suitable for assessing reward deficiency syndrome (rds) among chinese university students. frontiers in psychology

testing a dual-process-inspired questionnaire-primary residual framework for personality prediction: an exploratory study with static line drawings. comprehensive self-report personality inventories can impose substantial response burden, motivating the development of more efficient assessment strategies and the exploration of complementary information sources. guided by dual-process theory, this exploratory study examined a questionnaire-primary residual fusion framework in which a reduced questionnaire response vector served as the main predictive source, while static abstract line drawings were evaluated as a bounded auxiliary source of information. a total of 100 participants completed the 187-item sixteen personality factor questionnaire (16pf) and provided unprompted abstract line drawings. to account for the small sample size and reduce optimistic bias, we used participant-level repeated cross-validation, fold-local questionnaire item selection, standardized image preprocessing, cross-fitted residual learning, and nested selection of the visual correction scale. the reduced questionnaire provided a useful but imperfect held-out approximation of the full-form 16pf reference scores, with factor-level pearson correlations ranging from 0.34 to 0.78. in contrast, the static drawing modality did not provide stable incremental predictive value. nested validation selected a zero visual correction in 21 of 25 outer folds, and the fixed scale originally proposed for visual correction (0.05) produced a slightly higher mean absolute error than the questionnaire-only condition (1.2120 vs. 1.2100). an exploratory analysis using teacher-provided observer ratings likewise showed no advantage for visual fusion over questionnaire-only prediction. these findings indicate that dual-process theory can motivate a testable asymmetric framework for integrating explicit and non-verbal information, but the present data do not support static final line drawings as a reliable source of incremental personality information. future research should examine richer process-level drawing signals, including stroke timing, pauses, pressure, and trajectory dynamics, in larger independent samples. frontiers in psychology

what moves parents to recommend digital mental health tools for youth? behavioral insights and implications abstract in this study we aimed to examine behavioral determinants influencing parents' willingness to recommend digital mental health interventions (dmhis) to their youth, guided by the capability, opportunity, motivation–behavior (com‐b) model. we conducted semi‐structured interviews with 22 parents of adolescents aged 13–19 years with mental health concerns. interview transcripts were thematically analyzed using a hybrid inductive‐deductive approach. findings were mapped onto com‐b domains. capability barriers included low awareness, uncertainty about ssis, and difficulty navigating digital tools. opportunity facilitators involved embedding ssis in trusted settings and receiving endorsements from credible sources, though views on peer recommendations were mixed. motivation was shaped by alignment with parental values (e.g., safety, communication) and emotional responses such as fear or skepticism related to dmhis and privacy. results from this study highlight the need for dissemination strategies that directly address parental concerns and priorities, including culturally relevant messaging, tailored framing, and delivery through familiar and trusted community settings. journal of community psychology

an exploratory study: what can eye-movements tell us about phonological awareness in children with intellectual disabilities? word decoding as a foundational reading skill is significantly associated with phonological awareness in children with typical development as well as children with intellectual disabilities. phonological awareness is often assessed using traditional behavioral methods, which may underestimate abilities, particularly in individuals who are difficult to test due to behavioral, communication, or attentional difficulties. this study tested whether an eye-tracking “looking-while-listening” paradigm provides an additional recording option which is appropriate and potentially informative to examine the cognitive process while solving phonological awareness tasks in the assessment of children with intellectual disabilities. fifty-nine children with mild to moderate intellectual disabilities (aged 8–14 years) completed sound, syllable, and phoneme blending and segmentation tasks in paper-based and eye-tracking formats. participants were classified as proficient or non-proficient based on behavioral performance in the paper-based format. eye-tracking indices included proportional fixation duration, counts, revisits, and duration of the initial fixation (first fixation) on target, phonologically similar, and distractor images. proficient participants showed a higher proportional total fixation duration and a higher frequency of fixation on target images, as well as greater attention to phonologically similar competitors than distractors, compared to non-proficient participants, who showed no such differentiation. the findings which we obtained in our exploratory study suggest that eye tracking is a feasible, process-oriented method for assessing phonological awareness in children with intellectual disabilities and may capture cognitive mechanisms not reflected in traditional assessment procedures. this assumption should be pursued further through carefully designed experimental studies. journal of eye movement research

the longitudinal association between shyness and cognitive biases among rural chinese children: a three-wave cross-lagged analysis this study investigated longitudinal relationships between shyness and three types of cognitive biases (i.e., probability judgment bias, cost judgment bias, and threatening interpretation bias) among rural chinese children. a three-wave design (lasting 12-month) was employed with 1,112 children (61.24% boys; mage = 10.29) from gushi county, china, who self-reported their levels of shyness and cognitive biases at each wave. cross-lagged panel models revealed that shyness was moderately stable over time and significantly predicted subsequent increases in all three types of cognitive biases. probability and cost judgment biases also predicted later shyness, but only from the second to third wave, providing partial support for a bidirectional relationship. in contrast, threatening interpretation bias did not significantly predict later shyness. these findings suggested that shyness plays an important role in shaping children’s cognitive biases and highlighted the importance of early intervention targeting maladaptive cognition in shy children to prevent long-term socio-emotional challenges in chinese culture. journal of early adolescence

psychometric properties of the parental lying scenarios scale (plss): test–retest reliability, validity, and factor structure abstract most parents lie to their children. parental lying has been linked to parent–child relationship quality and children's social and moral development, underscoring the importance of accurately measuring this behavior. existing instruments primarily assess prevalence, focus on a particular subtype of parental lying only (i.e., parenting by lying), and their psychometric properties remain understudied. this study therefore introduces the parental lying scenarios scale (plss), a 40‐item self‐report instrument of parental lying prevalence and frequency across a broad range of parental lies. we assess its test–retest reliability, convergent and predictive validity, and factor structure. data were collected from dutch parents of children aged 5–12 years ( n = 247 for test–retest reliability and factor analysis; n = 316 for validity analyses). the plss demonstrated strong test–retest reliability and evidence for convergent and predictive validity. exploratory factor analyses at two timepoints consistently identified two distinct factors: lying to influence children's behavior and lying to shape children's knowledge or emotions. this study provides initial support for the plss as a reliable and conceptually meaningful instrument for capturing a broader range of parental lying. the plss thereby offers a promising methodological foundation for future research on the antecedents and socio‐moral implications of parental lying for both parents and children. social development

cognitive strategies, sensitivity, prejudice, and elements of inclusion among social workers abstract this study examines the interplay between cognitive and metacognitive strategies, environmental sensitivity, prejudice, bullying, and perceived self-efficacy in a small group of individuals working in the social sector. using a mixed-method design, standardized questionnaires assessed cognitive strategies and sensory processing sensitivity, while semi-structured interviews explored experiences of prejudice and bullying. results indicate that highly sensitive individuals often experience greater vulnerability to stress but also demonstrate enhanced emotional processing and empathy, which function as professional resources. interviews revealed the complex dynamics of bullying, the pervasive impact of prejudice on social and professional relationships, and the pivotal role of self-efficacy in sustaining motivation and resilience. the findings highlight the importance of professional training and reflective practice in strengthening cognitive and relational competencies, challenging stereotypes, and fostering inclusive environments. by emphasizing the potential of educators and practitioners as agents of social change, this study contributes to understanding how individual and collective well-being can be enhanced through culturally and socially responsive pedagogical practices. psychological studies

spiritual and auditory interventions to reduce anxiety and stress during magnetic resonance imaging (mri): a patient preference trial an elevated level of anxiety or stress during magnetic resonance imaging (mri) may disrupt both the quality of the images produced by an mri and the workflow of clinical services. the purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between different auditory conditions and post-mri anxiety/stress levels among patients undergoing mris using four different auditory conditions (holy quran, music, nature sounds, and no sound). a partially randomized, patient-preference study was conducted with 400 participants. each participant completed the anxiety and stress domains from the arabic version of the depression anxiety stress scale (dass-21). the results indicate that participants who listened to the holy quran during their mri experienced the lowest anxiety/stress levels, and participants who listened to music demonstrated the second lowest anxiety and stress scores. participants who selected the holy quran recitation or music during mri reported lower post-mri anxiety and stress scores compared to other groups. journal of health psychology

social anxiety intervention for college students: the effect of dancesport exercise prescriptions combined with group psychological counseling. objective: this randomized controlled trial (rct) was designed to evaluate the relative efficacy of a structured dancesport exercise prescription, group psychological counseling, and their combined application in reducing social anxiety symptoms among chinese university students.
methods: forty-eight university students with elevated social anxiety were recruited from the dancesport club of hefei normal university and randomly allocated to four parallel groups ( = 12 per group): a dancesport exercise prescription group (dp), a group psychological counseling group (gc), a combined intervention group (dp-gc), and a no-intervention control group. social anxiety and related psychological symptoms were assessed before and after the 12-week intervention using the symptom checklist-90 (scl-90), the interaction anxiousness scale (ias), the social avoidance and distress scale (sad), and the liebowitz social anxiety scale (lsas). group differences over time were examined using a 4 × 2 group × time repeated-measures framework, supplemented by adjustedcomparisons, effect-size estimates, and 95% confidence intervals.
results: the three active intervention conditions showed greater pre-to-post reductions in social anxiety-related outcomes than the control condition. the combined dp-gc group showed the largest improvement across the measured outcomes. however, because the combined condition integrated two intervention components within the same scheduled sessions and the sample size was small, the observed advantage is interpreted cautiously as a potential additive benefit rather than definitive evidence of a true synergistic interaction.
conclusion: dancesport exercise prescription and group psychological counseling may each reduce social anxiety symptoms among college students, with complementary scale-specific effects. the combined intervention model appears promising, but its superiority should be interpreted cautiously in light of the integrated intervention design, small sample size, and reliance on self-report outcomes. frontiers in psychology

differential pathways to depressive symptoms in students with and without special educational needs: the role of emotional reactivity and parent-teacher relationships. social and emotional competence (sec) is a core target of school-based social and emotional learning (sel), yet learner variability may alter how relational experiences and emotion-regulation difficulties are associated with mental-health outcomes. depressive symptoms were treated as clinically meaningful indicators of psychological distress and, within an sel-oriented framework, as downstream correlates of difficulties in emotional self-management; they were not treated as interchangeable with low sec. participants were 465 greek students aged 10-14 years (160 in the combined sen group-94 with documented status and 66 identified by teacher screening-and 305 without sen) and 51 teachers from 26 schools. students completed measures of emotional reactivity, perceived parental and teacher acceptance-rejection, and depressive symptoms. cluster-adjusted path models, bootstrap tests of indirect effects, covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses, and formal multigroup equality constraints were used. in students without sen, paternal rejection showed a direct association with depressive symptoms (β = 0.15), whereas maternal rejection showed indirect associations through recovery (standardized β = 0.011) and impairment (standardized β = 0.022). in the combined sen group, teacher rejection (β = 0.18) and emotional impairment (β = 0.38) were directly associated with depressive symptoms, and paternal rejection showed indirect statistical associations through emotional reactivity. in an analysis restricted to the 94 students with documented sen, the teacher-rejection and impairment associations persisted, whereas the paternal rejection-recovery estimate was similar but less statistically certain. formal multigroup tests supported differences only for maternal rejection-recovery, maternal rejection-impairment, and teacher rejection-depressive symptoms; other between-group contrasts were descriptive or inconclusive. the findings illustrate how relational and regulatory correlates may vary across heterogeneous learner groups, without establishing causal or temporal mechanisms. the teacher-rejection finding warrants further study in students with documented sen, while the paternal pathways require particular caution because the recovery association was less statistically certain in the smaller documented-only analysis. behavioral sciences

social capital, life meaning, and depressive symptoms among older adults in china: the moderating roles of digital social participation and digital social interaction. population aging and digitization are two defining trends in china, yet how digital forms of social participation and interaction condition the association between social capital and older adults' mental health remains unclear. using cross-sectional data from the 2022 china family panel studies (= 4394 adults aged 60 years and above), this study examined whether two bounded indicators of social capital-intergenerational interaction frequency and interpersonal trust-are associated with depressive symptoms, whether life meaning carries part of those associations, and whether two forms of digital social engagement moderate them. a moderated mediation model with five regression equations was estimated by survey-weighted least squares, with design-based standard errors and confidence intervals obtained by bootstrap replication of primary sampling units. both intergenerational interaction frequency (β = -0.238,< 0.001) and interpersonal trust (β = -0.756,< 0.001) were negatively associated with depressive symptoms, and the indirect associations through life meaning were -0.047 (95% ci -0.072 to -0.021) and -0.163 (95% ci -0.252 to -0.074) respectively, accounting for 19.6% and 21.6% of the corresponding total associations. both digital measures moderated associations within the model and in opposite directions: the negative association between interpersonal trust and depressive symptoms was stronger among respondents who used wechat (interaction β = -0.719,= 0.011), whereas the positive association between intergenerational interaction frequency and life meaning was weaker among those who shared more often on wechat moments (interaction β = -0.035,< 0.001). these findings suggest that digital social participation and digital social interaction are not merely independent correlates of older adults' mental health but conditions under which the associations between specific social capital indicators and mental health take different forms. behavioral sciences
