bias at scale: global disparities in the representativeness and contextualization of childhood research psychological science, including research on child cognition, behavior, and development, has traditionally relied on convenience samples drawn from a narrow range of sociocultural communities. moving beyond the simplifying weird/non-weird dichotomy, this study estimates the global representativeness of children participating in developmental research across multiple metrics of human cultural experience. a systematic review of studies published between 2016 and 2020 in five leading journals reveals a disproportionate focus on children from communities situated at the extremes of all selected metrics. this bias is coupled with a selective disregard for cultural context in research originating from these overrepresented settings, reflecting a persistent double standard in how culture is treated across the field. notably, studies involving children from underrepresented communities do not receive greater recognition (e.g., citations) unless they are embedded within larger, multinational research projects. we discuss the implications for representativeness, contextualization, and epistemic inclusion of these patterns, and we advocate for systemic change toward a genuinely global science of child development and psychological science more broadly. perspectives on psychological science

exploring dimensions of gendered racial identity development among emerging adult black women gendered racial identity plays a vital role in shaping the mental health and well-being of black women and girls. however, limited research captures how black women make meaning of their intersectional identities during adolescence and emerging adulthood, which are important developmental periods for identity, self-concept, and belonging. drawing on the established conceptual framework of black women's gendered racial identity development, this study sought to explore the dynamic, iterative process of emerging adult black women's gendered racial identity development. emerging adult black women ( n = 19; ages 21–24) living in the u.s. participated in a single time-point semi-structured interview, reflecting retrospectively on their gendered racial identity development across adolescence and emerging adulthood. data were analyzed using a modified constructivist grounded theory approach guided by black feminist and intersectional frameworks. findings revealed two primary themes: (1) critical gendered racial encounters, involving sub-themes of navigating gendered racism, receiving gendered racial socialization messages, engaging in resistance, and cultivating community; and (2) evolution of gendered racial ideologies (i.e., assimilation, defiance, pride, and empowerment), which shifted across developmental phases of hyperawareness, reflection, rejection, acceptance, and navigation. this study advances our understanding of black women's gendered racial identity by elucidating the iterative nature of identity development during adolescence and emerging adulthood. psychology of women quarterly

object details persist in visual working memory regardless of category sufficiency for search abstract when searching for objects in complex environments, performance often improves with more specific target representations. yet, sometimes a more general representation may be preferable. for example, when repeatedly searching for unique exemplars from the same object category, a shared category‐based representation could help alleviate the cognitive burden of constantly encoding and maintaining new exemplar representations. we therefore examined whether the format of target representations used for search is sensitive to the sustained preservation of object‐category membership. across two experiments, observers searched consecutively for images of real‐world objects from the same basic‐level category. we recorded contralateral delay activity (cda), an electrophysiological marker of visual working memory (vwm) maintenance, to assess whether the encoding of object‐specific details diminished across category repetitions in favor of more generalized representations. in experiment 1, we manipulated whether object‐category membership alone sufficiently differentiated each unique target from nontargets in the search array. in experiment 2, we preserved category sufficiency but allowed the targets to additionally repeat at the level of the exemplar to examine how repeatedly searching for the same object differs from repeatedly searching for the same kind of object. we found that while fewer object‐specific details were maintained in vwm when category membership was sufficient, the amount of detail only diminished across repetitions of the exact same object. moreover, observers exhibited sensitivity to the sustained preservation of the target category in the form of perceptual and semantic expectancy violations following category switches, as indexed by n2pc and n400 erp components. together, we show that, even though the sustained preservation of a target object category does not continuously reduce the encoding of object‐specific details, categorical information is nonetheless represented in parallel. we speculate that object‐specific representations principally serve attentional guidance, while categorical representations benefit target‐match decisions. psychophysiology

altered interoceptive predictive coding in functional neurological disorders abstract interoception, the processing of internal bodily signals, has been linked to the pathophysiology of functional neurological disorder (fnd), along with the theoretical concept of altered predictive coding (pc). fnd symptoms such as sensory‐motor dysfunction may arise from disrupted integration of sensory input and predictions. however, pc in the modality of interoception has not yet been investigated in fnd. using a pc paradigm, the cardio‐audio synchronization task measured electrophysiological responses to the heartbeat during omitted sounds that were temporally locked to the heartbeat (synchronous condition) or not (asynchronous control condition). patients with mixed fnd symptoms ( n = 36) were compared to sex‐ and age‐matched healthy controls (hc: n = 42) by contrasting synchronous and asynchronous heartbeat‐evoked potentials during omissions using cluster‐based permutation statistics. we further tested associations with self‐reported interoceptive variables and assessed whole‐scalp main and interaction effects in global field power (gfp) and topography. patients with fnd showed no cluster‐level differences between conditions, whereas we identified a central cluster difference in hcs. the interoceptive‐specific contrast (synch‐asynch difference waves) differed between groups and correlated with interoceptive self‐report but only when tested across groups ( r = −0.33, p = 0.012). in this paradigm, group‐by‐condition interactions in topography identified the insula as the most probable source of differences. these interactions occurred before those identified in gfp analyses, suggesting that differential networks emerge first, followed by changes in overall activity strength. these results indicate that patients with fnd use different neural mechanisms for interoceptive pc (i.e., precision‐weighted prediction errors in interoception‐guided predictions) than hcs. patients with fnd showed no difference in interoceptive pc, suggesting a dysfunctional interoceptive system. together, these findings suggest that interoceptive‐cued regularity processing in fnd is characterized by altered early network recruitment, followed by differences in overall signal strength, potentially reflecting a disrupted progression of interoceptive pc . psychophysiology

should i stay or should i go? preference for consistency predicts choice perseveration in the monty hall problem five incentivized studies ( n = 5,354) tested whether preference for consistency (pfc) predicts staying with one’s initial choice in the monty hall problem, despite the fact that switching maximizes the probability of winning. studies 1 and 2 found that higher pfc predicts staying, even after controlling for need for closure, preference for structure, intolerance of uncertainty, conspiracy beliefs, and numerical competence. studies 3 and 4 provided experimental evidence that incentives moderated the link between pfc and staying, but higher (vs. lower) pfc only attenuated rather than eliminated incentive sensitivity. study 5 identified anticipated regret over switching and losing as a mechanism underlying the effect, showing that the link between pfc and staying held across cultural contexts, although its magnitude was culturally calibrated. together, this research shows that consistency motivation governs choice perseverance in a task that is intentionally impersonal and assumed to be driven by probabilistic reasoning rather than motivational forces. personality and social psychology bulletin

social safety questionnaire: development and validation of a psychometric scale assessing social safety and social threat 社会安全问卷：评估社会安全与社会威胁的心理测量量表开发与验证 social safety theory posits that perceptions of social safety and social threat shape human health and behavior, yet no instrument exists for assessing these constructs. to address this gap, we developed and validated the 20-item social safety questionnaire (ssq) in a community sample of 503 adults (preregistration: osf.io/qaeh3). four factors were identified: social rejection, social support, social acceptance, and interpersonal trust. as expected, social safety positively related to perceived social support ( r = . 75 ) and social safeness ( r = . 81 ), and negatively to loneliness ( r = − . 53 ), psychological distress ( r = − . 64 ), and everyday discrimination ( r = − . 51 ). additionally, the ssq alone explained 41.4% of the variability in psychological distress; even after controlling for age, gender, race/ethnicity, and subjective socioeconomic status, ssq predicted lower distress (standardized β = − . 60 , p < . 001 ). the ssq is thus a concise, theoretically sound, and psychometrically robust instrument for assessing social safety and threat in research and, potentially, in clinical settings for case conceptualization, treatment planning, and patient monitoring. assessment
how physical information explains infants’ supposed psychological world nature reviews psychology

the within‐person relationship of allostasis and allostatic load with job performance abstract physiological indicators such as heart rate (hr) and heart rate variability (hrv) are frequently used in allostatic load (al) research. however, it often remains unclear whether these indicators reflect adaptive short‐term activation (allostasis), thus, represent primary mediators, or accumulated physiological burden (al), and thus, represent secondary outcomes. we propose a classification scheme specifying when physiological indicators should be interpreted as primary mediators or secondary outcomes. we tested this scheme in two longitudinal multilevel studies using different sources of job performance ratings (self, peer/supervisor, and client ratings). in study 1, participants ( n = 167–331) repeatedly measured hr and hrv under resting conditions over 4 weeks and reported job performance, resulting in 509–1001 observations. peer/supervisor ratings were additionally obtained. in study 2, counselors ( n = 11–15) measured hr/hrv before counseling sessions, and clients subsequently rated session quality (71–91 sessions). results largely supported the proposed classification scheme. when hr/hrv were interpreted as secondary outcomes, lower hr, lower lfhf, and higher hrv predicted better job performance. when interpreted as primary mediators, higher lfhf predicted better client‐rated performance. thus, the same physiological indicators may show opposite relationships with performance depending on the timing and context of measurement. our findings refine al theory by clarifying the distinction between allostasis and al, help explain inconsistent findings in the literature, and provide guidance for interpreting physiological indicators in organizational research. applied psychology-an international review-psychologie appliquee-revue internationale

the evolution of finger counting strategies in addition: a three‐year longitudinal study in young children abstract in this study, the developmental trajectory of children's finger‐based strategies for addition is described for the first time using a longitudinal design involving 207 children aged 4 ½ at the first testing point. children were observed individually twice a year over a three‐year period. the trajectory typically followed by children corresponds to the one theoretically described in the literature as supporting the gradual internalization of finger strategies and leading to the complete mentalization of the solving process. more precisely, children progressed from a modeling strategy in which each operand of an addition is represented on the fingers of each hand, through a concrete counting‐on strategy, in which both operands are still represented but enumerated in a single continuous process, to a counting‐on strategy, in which only one operand is kept in mind while the other is tracked on fingers. the frequent use of the concrete counting‐on strategy between modeling and counting‐on strategies supports baroody's proposition that it serves as a transitional step between concrete and more abstract forms of numerical representation. however, the concrete counting‐on strategy was associated with poor addition performance, suggesting that it corresponds to a reconstructive stage in which children gain new insights about numbers but lack the cognitive resources to fully capitalize on them. overall, this study provides the first detailed description of the evolution of finger‐based strategies toward the internalization of the addition solving process. developmental science

positive peer groups support preschoolers’ word learning abstract children learn language from their social partners, and differences in the behavior of these social partners can influence language learning outcomes. the literature largely focuses on adult caregivers; however, there is less clarity regarding the extent to which the social behavior of peers might also impact children's language learning. children spend a large proportion of their time with peers once they enter preschool; peers are thus an important source of input for learning. moreover, preschoolers are not just interacting with individual peers but also with groups of peers. to explore the impact of peers’ social behavior on preschoolers’ word learning, the present study manipulated peer behavior at two levels: individual peers and the peer group context. forty‐four preschoolers (36‐60 months) completed a tablet task in which they watched a series of animated videos of a classroom. participants were exposed to (1) either a positive or negative social group (manipulated between‐subjects) and (2) a positive and negative individual (manipulated within‐subjects). participants were then taught four novel object‐label pairings by the children in the video. we measured preschoolers’ accuracy in learning these novel object‐label pairs. overall, preschoolers learned the words above chance and there was no difference in learning from the positive and negative individual peers. however, participants learned words significantly better in the positive group than in the negative group. this pattern of results suggests that peer groups, and the overall affective context of children's learning environments, may play important roles in boosting preschoolers’ language learning trajectories. developmental science

visual sensitivities in toddlers’ hands provide a foundation for shape perception abstract human competencies in object recognition and category generalization implicate representations of the 3d geometry of objects. there is no accepted account of how such object‐centric representations are formed. toddlers’ manual and visual exploration of objects is strongly associated with their emerging abilities in object recognition and category generalization, although there is limited understanding of the processes that underlie this association. building on marr and nishihara's seminal theory of shape, we proposed (1) that toddlers actively select views that optimize fundamental visual sensitivities for long extents and for edges oriented horizontally and vertically and (2) that these biased views result in the axis of the object's maximum elongation, the major axis, being stably present in the variable 2d shapes projected from the object to the eye. we analyzed the visual properties of toddlers’ ( n = 90, 12–38 months) egocentric views as they manipulated objects. we observed a highly biased sampling of object views in which the major axis of the physical object is near maximal extension and oriented near horizontal or vertical, two properties that make the major axis stably determinable in the variable 2d shapes projected to the eye. the findings show how fundamental low‐level visual sensitivities may play a critical developmental role in biasing behaviors that bias the input in ways that make hard computational problems tractable. the findings also provide an empirical agenda for research focused on the development of object‐centric representations of 3d shape. summary we examined the visual properties of toddlers’ egocentric views of objects. we found that the generated views were a selective sampling of possible views that optimized foundational low‐level visual properties for shape perception. the findings implicate strong intrinsic constraints on toddlers’ visual experiences of object views. the biases in the toddler generated views are consistent with class theories of object‐centric representations of 3‐dimensional geometry. developmental science

investigation of the prolonged impact of severe socioeconomic hardship and mother's perceived social support on neurocognitive development in young children in the rural ecuadorian amazon abstract children living in conditions of severe socioeconomic (ses) hardship are at elevated risk for neurocognitive delays, yet most developmental neuroscience research has focused on children in high‐income, western populations, limiting our understanding of diverse developmental contexts. this study examined maternal perceived social support as a potential buffer against the stressors associated with ses hardship on child neurocognitive development in a longitudinal sample of indigenous families in the rural ecuadorian amazon. twenty‐eight children ( m age = 28.02 months at t1; 57.6 months at t2) participated in the study completing an assessment of early cognitive ability at t1 and an inhibition task while functional near‐infrared spectroscopy (fnirs) measured cortical activation at t2. a three‐level linear mixed model revealed a significant interaction between early cognitive ability and maternal perceived social support on functional activation. specifically, children of mothers with high social support showed no association between early cognitive ability and cortical activation, while those with low support exhibited atypical patterns (hyper‐ or hypoactivation), suggesting that increased maternal perceived social support may help buffer the risk exposure of chronic stressors associated with ses hardship. these findings underscore the importance of culturally embedded social resources in promoting resilience among children facing cumulative risk. supporting maternal social networks may be a promising pathway for improving child neurodevelopment in underrepresented, low‐resource communities and contributes to more inclusive global models of brain development. developmental science

using signature strengths for a good day: need‐based pathways to daily hedonic, eudaimonic, and social well‐being abstract using one's signature strengths is a robust predictor of well‐being, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying this association remain insufficiently understood. drawing on self‐determination theory's dual‐process model, the present study examined whether basic psychological need satisfaction and need frustration serve as parallel mediators of the relationship between daily signature strengths use (ssu) and three dimensions of well‐being, namely hedonic, eudaimonic, and social well‐being. a sample of 224 chinese college students completed daily assessments for 14 consecutive days ( n = 2491 daily observations). multilevel structural equation modeling with the 1‐1‐1 mediation framework revealed a striking level‐dependent asymmetry: at the within‐person level, need satisfaction, but not need frustration, mediated the daily ssu–well‐being relationship across all three outcomes, whereas at the between‐person level, need satisfaction mediated the associations with all three outcomes and need frustration mediated those with hedonic and eudaimonic well‐being only; the need satisfaction pathway was consistently stronger. exploratory dimension‐specific analyses suggested a tentative pattern involving competence frustration at the between‐person level, although this finding was based on a single‐item measure. these findings support the proposed role of need satisfaction as an important mechanism linking daily strengths use to multidimensional well‐being. applied psychology-health and well being

digital health interventions for psychological and cognitive care in cancer patients and caregivers: a re‐aim‐based systematic review abstract beyond physical challenges, cancer can cause psychological and cognitive challenges for patients, caregivers, and family members. digital health interventions show promise in addressing these issues. however, evidence on their applicability in daily cancer care is limited. the objective of this systematic review is to evaluate the internal and external validity of digital health interventions targeting psychological and cognitive impairments in cancer patients, caregivers, and family members, using the re‐aim framework. this systematic review was conducted following the prisma guidelines, using pubmed/medline, scopus, and psychinfo databases. data were extracted using data forms based on the re‐aim framework. the methodological quality was assessed using the quality assessment tool for quantitative studies (qatqs). a total of 191 studies involving 29.907 patients and caregivers met the inclusion criteria. included studies were randomized controlled trials and nonrandomized studies of interventions related to digital health, using an online or hybrid format. the reach, implementation, and effectiveness domains were most frequently reported, while adoption and maintenance were the most unreported domains within the re‐aim framework. despite reporting on reach, effectiveness, and implementation, limited data on external validity restricts the impact and scalability of digital health interventions in cancer care. future research should endeavor to address current challenges and improve the use of digital health interventions in cancer care. applied psychology-health and well being

a systematic review of interventions to support health, wellbeing, and job satisfaction for emergency call handlers in the ambulance, police, and fire services abstract emergency call handlers (ech) in ambulance, police, and fire services experience high levels of occupational stress which can have adverse health consequences. to systematically review interventions to support the health, wellbeing and employment of ech working in the emergency services. following prisma 2020 guidelines, academic databases and grey literature were searched [last search: 06/02/25]. studies of any design assessing physical or mental health or employment outcomes were eligible. screening and quality appraisal were conducted independently, with data extraction completed and cross checked by two reviewers. the jbi family of tools was used to assess quality and risk of bias. twelve studies met the inclusion criteria and were narratively synthesised into four categories: psychoeducation and resilience training, residential recovery programme, organisational wellbeing initiatives, and multicomponent interventions. sample sizes ranged from n = 9 to n = 4020. the majority of interventions identified aimed to improve mental health, while physical health and employment outcomes were less frequently assessed. there was significant heterogeneity in study design which limited comparability between the studies. most studies included a mixed sample of ech and first responders and the methodological quality of included studies was variable. some studies employed rigorous designs (e.g., rcts), whilst others relied on observational methods. the included studies also demonstrated organisational barriers to the delivery of interventions in these settings. there was limited evidence for the effectiveness of interventions for supporting health and wellbeing or reducing stress amongst ech. there is a need for role‐specific interventions for ech. systematic registration this systematic review was registered on prospero: crd42025639271 stress and health

the shifting lens of ostracism: exploring the impact of social exclusion on situational perception dimensions abstract does a change in situational cues directly influence how people construe a situation? this study provides experimental evidence that ostracism is associated with systematic shifts in situational perception and affective responses, and examines whether these situational perceptions account for more variance in feelings of being ignored and excluded than broad personality traits. through both between‐subject (study 1, n = 446) and within‐subject designs (study 2, n = 259), ostracism was consistently associated with greater perceived negativity and adversity and lower positivity. across both studies, situational perception accounted for more variance in feelings of being ignored and excluded than the big five traits, with positivity and negativity emerging as the most consistent predictors. primary analyses were estimated using multiple imputation, with complete‐case analyses retained as sensitivity checks. the central pattern of findings remained robust across missing‐data approaches, although some secondary effects in study 2 were less stable, highlighting the importance of measuring situational perception when examining how social exclusion shapes subjective construals and emotional responses. social and personality psychology compass

factors influencing the emergence of dependency length minimization in neural agent simulations abstract given various grammatical options, language users prefer the word order choice that reduces the overall length of syntactic dependencies, a principle known as dependency length minimization (dlm). the origins of this preference remain an open question, particularly whether it originates from constraints on efficient information processing. computational simulations provide a powerful approach to identifying the factors influencing the emergence of linguistic phenomena. however, previous simulations of dlm have not examined realistic interaction contexts and have produced mixed results. the present study investigates the emergence of dlm in artificial languages using a recently proposed language learning and communication framework based on recurrent neural networks. in this framework, agents are trained to speak and interpret artificial languages and then use these languages to communicate. using this framework, we study the impact of several factors related to processing limitations in a communicative setting, such as noise during listening, limited speaker capacity, and incremental sentence processing. our results reveal a complex interplay among these factors in shaping word order preferences in neural agents. specifically, in the full meaning space, agents regularize toward a single dominant word order, while in the half meaning space, they show a short‐before‐long preference that only aligns with dlm in verb‐initial languages. a consistent dlm preference emerges only when agents are subject to incremental processing pressure. these results suggest that limitations in human cognitive processing may indeed play a role in shaping dlm. our findings provide insights into the conditions under which neural models replicate human‐like preferences for minimizing syntactic dependency distances and highlight the challenges of designing emergent communication models that capture human cognitive biases in language processing. cognitive science

double negation without double effort: erp evidence from mandarin chinese abstract accounts of negation processing, including two‐step simulation, pragmatic, and monotonicity‐based accounts, differ in their predictions about whether double negation requires additional cognitive effort relative to affirmation. using event‐related potentials, we investigated a mandarin chinese double‐negation structure (“méiyǒu x bù y”) that is logically equivalent to its affirmative counterpart (“suǒyǒu x dōu y”). forty native speakers read context sentences (double negation vs. affirmation) followed by critical sentences containing semantically congruent or incongruent target words. crucially, the target word appeared in a separate sentence, downstream from the negation operators; the design, therefore, tests whether a pragmatically licensed double negation establishes a discourse representation functionally equivalent to affirmation at the point of propositional evaluation. at the critical word, incongruent words elicited larger n400/p600 amplitudes, and these congruency effects did not differ between contexts, indicating equivalent representations and no detectable downstream cost. post‐critical analyses, however, revealed context‐specific differences: the affirmation context showed a prolonged negativity to incongruency—plausibly reflecting sustained engagement with its more salient violation—whereas the double negation context did not. a representational similarity analysis (rsa) further showed greater neural tracking of incongruency magnitude in the double negation context at a later window (726–798 ms). together, these findings indicate that a pragmatically licensed double negation supports downstream semantic integration as efficiently as affirmation, while later processing remains context‐sensitive. because this early equivalence is also consistent with a monotonicity‐based account, we frame the early‐equivalence/late‐divergence pattern as a tentative dual‐stage characterization to be tested in future work, rather than a decisive adjudication between theories. cognitive science

more evidence for the standard account of theory of mind development: a reply to fabricius (2026) abstract fabricius argues that the results of a recent study of ours speak for a deflationary competence limitation account of theory of mind development. according to this account, children do not operate with proper mental state concepts until age 6–7 or older. however, the original findings are, in fact, incompatible with such competence limitation accounts, but compatible with the standard picture of theory of mind development: according to this picture, children acquire proper mental state concepts by age 4, but this competence is sometimes masked by performance factors. cognitive science

schema therapy for voice hearers: a case series study abstract distressing voice‐hearing experiences are frequently characterised by hostility, criticism and abuse and emerging evidence suggests that these experiences may reflect internalised dysfunctional schema modes, particularly the punitive parent mode. yet no research has evaluated a schema therapy intervention explicitly targeting schema modes. this naturalistic case series evaluated schema therapy for voices (stv) within a routine specialist psychology service. twenty transdiagnostic voice hearers started formulation‐driven stv comprising approximately 20–30 individual sessions integrating chair‐work, imagery rescripting and schema mode work. fifteen participants completed treatment. primary outcome was voice‐related distress. secondary outcomes included voice severity, voice content, negative affect, emotion regulation difficulties and schema modes. feasibility indicators were encouraging, with 83.3% of eligible clients selecting stv and 75.0% completing treatment. participants demonstrated a significant and large reduction in voice‐related distress ( d = 1.18). significant improvements were also observed in negative affect, emotion regulation difficulties and punitive parent mode. changes in voice severity, negative voice content and vulnerable child mode were in the expected direction but did not reach statistical significance, while healthy adult mode showed little change. stv appears feasible to deliver within routine clinical practice and associated with meaningful reductions in voice‐related distress. the pattern of findings provides preliminary support for a schema mode conceptualisation of distressing voices and suggests that directly targeting punitive parent, vulnerable child and healthy adult modes may represent a promising therapeutic approach. controlled trials are now required to establish efficacy and investigate proposed mechanisms of change. clinical psychology & psychotherapy
differential contributions of executive function components to antisocial behavior in arab adolescents developmental neuropsychology

neural correlates of dissociating mindfulness subdomains: a differential analysis approach abstract objectives in recent years, mindfulness has entered the scientific discourse, holding significant therapeutic potential. however, findings regarding its neurobiological basis have been inconsistent. trait mindfulness comprises distinct dimensions, two of them are presence and acceptance, but neural correlates accompanying them remain largely underexplored. this study focuses on neurostructural associations reflecting these two subdomains’ distinct patterns to explore their complex interplay, thereby contributing to a more comprehensive, neural, and psychometrically grounded understanding of mindfulness. method structural mri scans and acceptance and presence scores on the freiburg mindfulness inventory were analyzed in 261 healthy adults. correlates of both subdomains, oppositely directed, were investigated through multiple linear regression analyses of grey matter volume (gmv). threshold-free cluster enhancement (tfce) corrected whole-brain, and region of interest analyses of the amygdala were conducted. post-hoc, linear regression analyses were performed to further explore each subdomain. results an intriguing dissociation in neurostructural correlates of acceptance and presence was observed: acceptance correlated positively with gmv in the left rolandic operculum ( k tfce-fwe = 243, p fwe = 0.02) and the left postcentral gyrus ( k tfce-fwe = 17, p fwe < 0.05) and negatively with amygdala gmv ( k tfce-fwe = 40, p fwe = 0.03), while presence correlated negatively with gmv in cortical areas. conclusions acceptance may promote non-judgmental integration of emotional and sensory stimuli, while presence reflects the capacity for sustained, focused attention. to our knowledge, this is the first study addressing the distinct neurostructural correlates of these subdomains, revealing their potential complementary and compensatory roles within mindfulness at both the neurobiological and psychometric levels. preregistration this study is not preregistered. mindfulness
comparing a positive psychology intervention and cognitive behavioral therapy: a randomized trial for postpartum depression journal of happiness studies

the sequential roles of psychological flexibility and positivity in the association between post-traumatic stress symptoms and depressive symptoms among earthquake survivors in türkiye earthquakes can have substantial consequences for psychological well-being, including post-traumatic stress and depressive symptoms. drawing on acceptance and commitment therapy (act), which conceptualizes psychological flexibility as a central process in adaptive psychological functioning, this study examined the sequential mediating roles of psychological flexibility and positivity in the association between post-traumatic stress symptoms and depressive symptoms among survivors of the two major earthquakes that struck türkiye on 6 february 2023. this cross-sectional study included 834 earthquake survivors (mage = 26.7; 71.1% female) who were assessed approximately three months after the earthquakes. participants completed validated self-report measures of post-traumatic stress symptoms, psychological flexibility, positivity, and depressive symptoms. depressive symptoms were assessed using the 12-item depression subscale of the brief symptom inventory and were analyzed as a continuous variable. correlation and sequential mediation analyses were conducted, with indirect effects evaluated using bootstrapping. post-traumatic stress symptoms were positively associated with depressive symptoms and negatively associated with psychological flexibility and positivity. psychological flexibility was positively associated with positivity and negatively associated with depressive symptoms, while positivity was negatively associated with depressive symptoms. sequential mediation analysis indicated that psychological flexibility and positivity mediated the association between post-traumatic stress symptoms and depressive symptoms. these findings suggest that psychological flexibility and positivity may represent relevant psychological processes in the association between post-traumatic stress and depressive symptoms among earthquake survivors and may inform post-disaster psychological support. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

burnout and emotions at work: the moderating role of guilt in a cross-national sample burnout is a prevalent occupational phenomenon with significant consequences for employee well-being. although emotions have been studied in relation to burnout, less attention has been paid to their function as burnout outcomes and to the role of guilt as a boundary condition of this process. this study examined the relationships between burnout and positive and negative emotions at work, as well as the moderating role of guilt, from a cross-national and gender perspective. a sample of 857 employees (57.2% women; m age = 38.50 years) from spain, chile, colombia, and mexico completed validated measures of burnout (spanish burnout inventory), emotions at work, and guilt. structural equation modelling and multigroup analyses were conducted, complemented by moderation analyses using the process macro. burnout was negatively associated with positive emotions and positively associated with negative emotions. multigroup analyses supported strict invariance across gender and configural–metric invariance across countries. guilt significantly moderated both relationships, such that the associations between burnout and emotional experiences were weaker at higher levels of guilt. at comparable levels of burnout, higher guilt was associated with less favorable predicted emotional levels, indicating that guilt shapes the strength, rather than the direction, of the burnout–emotion association. these findings position guilt as a boundary condition of the burnout–emotion association, with implications for burnout prevention and employee well-being interventions. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

a systematic review of tangible reinforcers during functional communication training abstract we conducted a systematic review of the functional communication training literature to synthesize the types of high‐ and low‐tech stimuli included in functional communication training and their associated levels of social validity. our search was restricted to studies published in 2010 or later, marking the introduction of the apple ipad. we identified 116 studies comprising 250 participant‐level fct applications. we summarized participant characteristics, the types of high‐ and low‐tech stimuli incorporated into treatment procedures, assessments used to identify stimuli, the extent to which social validity was evaluated for applications with high‐ and low‐tech stimuli, and social validity outcomes. findings suggest that tablet devices were the most common high‐tech stimuli, whereas edibles were the most common low‐tech stimuli, and that applications involving these types of stimuli were associated with moderate to high levels of social validity. we discuss these findings with respect to considerations surrounding the incorporation of high‐tech stimuli in the assessment and treatment of challenging behavior. behavioral interventions

sensory hyper‐sensitivity associates with poor infant sleep and different parental sleep practices, in a uk cohort abstract sleep difficulties (e.g., increased sleep onset latency and more frequent night awakenings) are common in early development and are associated with increased parental stress. sleep difficulties have been linked to sensory hypersensitivity in typically developing infants and infants with family history of autism. in the current study, we investigate whether infant sensory sensitivity is associated with the strategies parents employ when settling infants to sleep. strategies encouraging autonomy, rather than those involving active physical comforting, have previously been shown to lead to better sleep. we report findings from a cross‐sectional uk sample of 245 infants aged 6–13 months, from which we collected online parent‐report measures of infant sleep and sensory sensitivity (itsp). we replicate previous findings showing that poorer sleep is correlated with higher infant sensory sensitivity. we then show an association between higher infant sensory sensitivity and more frequent use of all settling strategies, as well as a higher number of different strategies used. a strong correlation between infant and maternal sensory sensitivity precluded testing whether parental settling strategies are driven by infant or parental sensory sensitivity. the current findings emphasize the need to integrate information about intrinsic (e.g., infant sensitivity) and social environment factors (e.g., parental sensitivity, settling strategies) to understand infant sleep. infancy

growth is rarely a straight line: developmental path of early metacognition, role of parental metacognitive talk and influence on children's memory abstract rudimentary metacognitive skills emerge early in infancy. to date, however, little is known about the developmental course of these early skills or the factors involved in their development. to address this gap, the present study aimed to: (a) map the developmental trajectory of metacognitive uncertainty from 18 to 36 months; (b) examine whether parental metacognitive talk during play predicts this development; and (c) test the relations between these two factors and children's later memory performance. using a longitudinal design, 60 parent‐child dyads were tested every 6 months using an eye‐tracking cue fixation paradigm to estimate metacognitive uncertainty. the frequency of parental metacognitive talk was collected during a play session shared with their child. children's memory was assessed at 36 months with a cartoon‐recall task. growth curve analyses revealed a nonlinear trajectory, with a shift in metacognitive functioning around 24 months that was predicted by parental metacognitive talk. path analyses indicated that parental talk at 30–36 months and metacognitive accuracy at 24–30 months were both related to children's later memory skills. this study documents early changes in metacognition while highlighting the role of parent‐child interactions in this development. infancy

exploring cues of reciprocity in third‐party word learning abstract this study examined how toddlers learn novel words by observing two adults interact in third‐party contexts. specifically, we examined whether toddlers show stronger evidence of selective referent identification for labeled objects in third‐party contexts and how word learning may be supported by cues of reciprocity between adult interlocutors, including physical exchange of the object, verbal exchange about the object, and/or the adult listener's response to the information provided. toddlers ( n = 64, mage = 29.9 mos., sd = 1.7 mos) were assigned to one of four conditions: object exchange + action imitation, object exchange only, verbal exchange + label repetition , or verbal exchange only . in the object exchange conditions, children observed one adult speaker label and manipulate a target object and then hand it to another adult listener, who either imitated the object manipulation or held the object without manipulation. in the verbal exchange conditions, one adult speaker labeled and manipulated the target object without handing it over, and the other adult listener either repeated the label or provided a neutral verbal response. children's learning was assessed by whether they selected the target object in response to its label; preference responses were used to distinguish target selection from object preference. children showed stronger evidence of selective referent identification in the object exchange conditions compared to the verbal exchange conditions. these results suggest that physical exchange of a labeled object between adult interlocutors may help toddlers identify the interaction as referentially relevant and therefore support word learning in third‐party contexts. infancy

grmcor : an r package for range-restriction bias correction of discrimination parameters in the graded response model grmcor：等级反应模型区分度参数范围限制偏差校正的r包 the graded response model (grm) is widely used for analyzing polytomous response data from attitude, personality, and character measurement instruments. however, when response data are collected from a range-restricted sample such as selected applicants, screened participants, or high-performing students, grm discrimination parameters are systematically underestimated. no existing r package implements range-restriction bias correction specifically for grm discrimination parameters. this paper introduces grmcor , an r package that implements the truncated normal standard deviation ratio correction for grm discrimination parameters under direct range restriction. the package provides functions for estimating grm parameters from restricted samples, applying the correction, comparing restricted and corrected estimates, visualizing bias patterns, and validating the correction procedure via monte carlo simulation. monte carlo results demonstrate that grmcor substantially reduces bias in discrimination parameter estimates, with mean bias reduced from −0.64 to near zero and rmse reduced by approximately 52% under 50% range restriction. the package is freely available via github. applied psychological measurement

memoria episódica en bilingües: evidencia actual y direcciones futuras el lenguaje es una habilidad característicamente humana muy vinculada con los sistemas de memoria, en particular con la memoria episódica, entendida como la capacidad de codificar, almacenar y recuperar experiencias contextualizadas de la propia historia personal. el uso de una segunda lengua (l2) plantea exigencias adicionales a este proceso, aunque no resulta claro de qué manera la experiencia bilingüe modula la codificación, el almacenamiento y la recuperación de información episódica. mediante un enfoque de revisión narrativa sustentado en procedimientos de búsqueda sistemática, este estudio aborda dos preguntas centrales: (a) si la recuperación de memorias autobiográficas depende del idioma de codificación y recuperación, y (b) si el bilingüismo y la dominancia lingüística modulan el desempeño en tareas de memoria episódica de laboratorio (recuerdo libre, recuerdo con clave y reconocimiento). se seleccionaron catorce artículos empíricos publicados entre 2010 y 2021 (dos sobre memoria autobiográfica y doce sobre aprendizaje de listas de palabras) a partir de un conjunto inicial de 622 registros identificados en siete bases de datos. los resultados sugieren que el desempeño en memoria episódica es sensible de manera consistente al idioma de codificación y recuperación (efectos de especificidad de codificación), a la competencia en l2 y al contexto de inmersión y, de manera más tentativa, a diferencias etarias en el desempeño bilingüe. sin embargo, la marcada heterogeneidad en la definición y caracterización de las poblaciones bilingües (por ejemplo, edad de adquisición, competencia y dominancia) limita la comparabilidad de los hallazgos entre estudios y hace necesario un reporte más estandarizado en futuras investigaciones. revista ces psicologia
facing mortality: surfacing themes among four cases psychoanalytic inquiry

rethinking cognitive bias in human-ai cognitive systems: a structured conceptual mapping review. research in cognitive psychology has long shown that human judgment and decision making are systematically influenced by cognitive biases, particularly under conditions of uncertainty. as artificial intelligence (ai) systems become increasingly embedded in socially relevant decision making contexts-such as healthcare, education, communication, and governance-these cognitive dynamics do not disappear. instead, they may be reproduced, amplified, or transformed through human-ai interaction. despite the rapid growth of research on cognitive biases in ai-related contexts, existing reviews remain fragmented and heterogeneous, often focusing on single biases or specific application domains. this article reports a structured conceptual mapping review of review-level publications examining how cognitive biases are conceptualized, categorized, and addressed in human-ai interaction. a bounded search of scopus, web of science, and pubmed identified ten eligible review publications published between 2020 and 2025. using a three-level framework, the mapping distinguishes data-level, algorithmic-level, and human-interaction-level processes. within the retrieved corpus, the analysis reveals heterogeneous terminology, a predominance of healthcare applications and interaction-level analyses, and limited review-level synthesis of empirical evaluations of mitigation strategies. drawing on distributed cognition and joint cognitive systems, we propose coupled human-ai cognition as a theoretical lens rather than as an empirically established conclusion. the study provides a structured conceptual map, identifies terminological and methodological gaps, and develops propositions for future empirical research. behavioral sciences

not just feeling stressed: coping, emotional, and somatic functioning in adolescents' daily lives abstract daily stress is a pervasive experience during adolescence and is linked to emotional and physical health, yet few studies have examined multiple coping strategies in relation to different domains of emotional and somatic functioning within the same daily context. this study used a daily diary approach to examine whether coping strategies moderate associations between daily stress and adolescents' positive affect, negative affect, and somatic symptoms. data were drawn from a 7‐day daily diary study of 208 chinese adolescents. participants reported stress, affect, somatic symptoms, and coping strategies. multilevel models disaggregated within‐person and between‐person associations and tested moderation effects. at the within‐person level, higher‐than‐usual daily stress was associated with lower positive affect and higher negative affect on the same day. emotion‐focused coping amplified these associations, whereas affiliation‐focused coping attenuated them; task‐focused coping was nonsignificant. at the between‐person level, higher average stress was related to poorer emotional and somatic functioning. emotion‐focused coping amplified these associations, and task‐focused coping strengthened the association between stress and lower positive affect. lagged associations were generally weaker. these findings highlight the importance of distinguishing within‐person processes from between‐person differences in understanding adolescents' responses to daily stress. coping strategies play distinct roles in shaping emotional and physical functioning in daily life and may represent targets for intervention. applied psychology-health and well being

dual kindness, less distress: a longitudinal and dual‐paradigm study on self‐compassion, prosocial behavior, and depressive symptoms in chinese adolescents abstract self‐compassion (kindness to oneself) and prosocial behavior (kindness to others) are important protective resources against adolescents' depressive symptoms; however, their bidirectional dynamic relationships with depressive symptoms and heterogeneous trajectories of depressive symptoms remain unclear. clarifying these relationships can provide empirical evidence for precision interventions targeting adolescents' depressive symptoms. this study surveyed 1214 chinese adolescents ( m age = 15.46 ± 0.71, 60.7% male) three times (with approximately 6‐month intervals) and integrated variable‐centered and person‐centered approaches to (1) examine the bidirectional longitudinal relationships between dual kindness and depressive symptoms using the random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (ri‐clpm) and (2) identify heterogeneous developmental trajectories of depressive symptoms using the latent class growth model (lcgm) and subsequently test whether baseline dual kindness predicts trajectory membership and whether depressive symptom trajectories predict t3 kindness qualities. ri‐clpm results showed that at the within‐person level, increases in positive self‐compassion and prosocial behavior effectively buffered depressive symptoms, with positive self‐compassion and depressive symptoms exhibiting bidirectional dynamic relationships, whereas fluctuations in negative self‐compassion were unrelated to depressive fluctuations. at the between‐person level, global and positive self‐compassion as well as prosocial behavior were stably negatively correlated with depressive symptoms, while negative self‐compassion was positively correlated with depressive symptoms. lcgm identified three developmental trajectories: a low‐symptom declining group, a threshold‐symptom increasing group, and a high‐symptom remitting group. baseline self‐compassion significantly predicted trajectory group membership across all pairwise comparisons, whereas prosocial behavior predicted membership only in the low‐symptom declining group relative to the other two. different trajectory groups also showed significant differences in subsequent kindness qualities. together, the two analytical paradigms revealed the complex interplay between dual kindness and depressive symptoms at both the variable level and the individual heterogeneity level. these findings suggest that prosocial behavior may be better suited for universal prevention, whereas self‐compassion (enhancing its positive components and reducing its negative components) should serve as a core intervention target for risk groups. applied psychology-health and well being

perceptions of ai‐generated informational texts and effects of the source: an online experiment abstract artificial intelligence (ai) is becoming increasingly common for health information seeking, yet many people are still skeptical of its performance. this between‐subjects online experiment tested whether informing readers that a text was produced by ai influenced their ratings in 774 participants. they were randomly assigned to read one of six brief texts and rated trustworthiness, interest, and perceived understanding, as well as intention to act upon the received information and willingness to share the information with others. source information did not influence ratings, but only 41.5% of participants in the ai source condition noticed the source. source awareness was associated with higher education and greater nutrition knowledge. nutrition information produced by ai chatbots is generally seen as trustworthy, although source information is often ignored. our research highlights critical implications for public health messaging in the digital age as consumers may not differentiate between information generated by ai versus other sources, although future research is required to assess source perceptions in ai‐generated texts in more detail. applied psychology-health and well being

examining the potential role of respect in health disparities abstract the social factor thought to be at the heart of health disparities is social devaluation that disadvantages members of certain groups. respect is arguably the opposite of devaluation and as such may counteract social processes of devaluation that contribute to health disparities. we define respect and discuss its behavioral correlates and social function. we review the very limited direct data on whether (dis)respect is associated with physical health. we then identify candidate mechanisms that may help explain how intergroup and interpersonal experiences of respect get under the skin to influence health and conclude with discussion of whether respect may play a role in explaining racial and socioeconomic health disparities in the united states. respect is central to models of intergroup relations, and there is very preliminary evidence that respect, when examined on its own rather than as part of another construct such as discrimination, is associated with physical health outcomes such as self‐rated health, mortality, and cardiovascular disease. inconsistent associations also arise in this literature, such as interpersonal respect being more commonly reported among black and lower ses individuals in the us if measured in daily life, but showing expected associations when measured at the intergroup‐level or as a one‐time self‐report. thus, while there is logical and empirical reason to believe that respect may be good for our health, much less is known about who experiences respect, from whom, and with what consequences for racial and socioeconomic disparities in physical health in the us. social and personality psychology compass

neural cell models of specific reading disabilities: identification of cellular and transcriptome alterations abstract based on post‐mortem studies, a long‐standing hypothesis on the biological bases of specific reading disabilities (rd) has been that alterations in neuronal migration alter language neural circuits. however, there are questions concerning the original studies (small sample size, comorbidities). further, this idea has not been strongly supported by current genetic studies. in this study, we test altered neural cell phenotypes using cells derived from two pairs of siblings strongly discordant for reading—probands with severe rd and their strong‐reader siblings. we observed significant differences in neurosphere outgrowth between the neural precursor cells (npcs) from the probands compared to their strong‐reader siblings. transcriptome analyses of adherent npcs and neurons derived from the npcs identified genes differentially expressed between the probands and siblings, including genes previously identified in neurodevelopmental disorders. of note was the overexpression of the hormone igf1 and the transcription factor otx2 , responsible for the opening and closing of critical windows in development and predicted to be involved in critical windows for language acquisition. our results support altered transcriptome and cellular phenotypes in rd neural cells and suggest possible molecular mechanisms underlying the changes. genes brain and behavior

reln haploinsufficiency enhances fentanyl‐induced locomotion and dorsal striatal activity without affecting opioid reinforcement and relapse‐like behavior abstract the reln gene encodes the extracellular glycoprotein reelin that regulates synaptic plasticity and activity‐dependent gene expression with implication in several neuropsychiatric disorders, including substance use disorder. although reduction of reln expression has been associated with altered responses to psychostimulants and cannabinoids, its role in opioid‐evoked behaviors has not been investigated. here, we tested whether reln haploinsufficiency alters behavioral and molecular responses to the synthetic opioid fentanyl. heterozygous reeler ( reln +/−) mice and wild‐type littermates were assessed using complementary contingent and non‐contingent models of fentanyl exposure, including multi‐phase fentanyl intravenous self‐administration paradigm, conditioned place preference paradigm, locomotor assays, and dorsal striatal immediate early gene expression. reln haploinsufficiency did not alter acquisition, extinction, or cue‐induced fentanyl seeking during self‐administration, indicating stable opioid reinforcement and relapse‐like behavior. following acute, passive fentanyl exposure, reln +/− mice exhibited enhanced fentanyl‐induced locomotion and fos immunoreactivity in the dorsal striatum, while fentanyl conditioned place preference remained unchanged. together, these findings demonstrate that reln haploinsufficiency does not modify opioid reinforcement or cue‐driven drug seeking but enhances acute drug‐evoked neuronal activation in the dorsal striatum. these results identify reln as a modulatory factor in opioid‐responsive neural circuits rather than in the associative learning processes underlying opioid reinforcement. genes brain and behavior

cohesión familiar y riesgo de trastornos alimentarios en adolescentes, personas adultas jóvenes: una revisión sistemática esta revisión sistemática analiza la relación entre la cohesión familiar y el riesgo de desarrollar trastornos de la conducta alimentaria (tca) en adolescentes y personas adultas jóvenes, basándose en investigaciones publicadas entre 2020 y 2024. los tca son condiciones complejas, influenciadas por factores biológicos, psicológicos y sociales, donde las dinámicas familiares juegan un papelcrucial como factores de riesgo o protección. se siguieron las directrices prisma, buscando en bases de datos científicas (web of science, ebsco, pubmed, jmir y proquest) con palabras clave específicas. tras aplicar criterios de inclusión y exclusión, se analizaron seis estudios que evaluaron la cohesión familiar y los tca en adolescentes, adultas y adultos jóvenes. los estudios utilizaron variadas herramientas como también escalas de cohesión familiar, abarcando un total de 10 000 participantes en diversos contextos culturales. los resultados indicaron que niveles bajos de cohesión familiar y dinámicas parentales negativas, como la sobreprotección y la falta de apoyo emocional, aumentan el riesgo de tca. factores mediadores como pensamientos automáticos negativos y ansiedad social también influyeron significativamente. sin embargo, la literatura mostró limitaciones, como el uso de muestras no probabilísticas y la incapacidad de establecer causalidad. esta revisión resalta la importancia de abordar los tca desde una perspectiva familiar, destacando la necesidad de intervenciones que fortalezcan la cohesión familiar y mitiguen factores de riesgo. además, se identificó la escasez de estudios en contextos locales y en otros rangos etarios, subrayando áreas clave para futuras investigaciones. revista costarricense de psicologia

bridging the gap between contemporary and buddhist definitions of mindfulness: a scoping review abstract background divergent definitions of mindfulness complicate the interpretation of mindfulness-based intervention research. some scholars suggest that incorporating insights from historical models of mindfulness in buddhism may further enhance the benefits of mindfulness practices. although these recommendations converge on some points, they diverge on others, warranting systematic examination. objectives the present review identifies commonly discussed differences between contemporary and buddhist conceptualizations and synthesizes them into an integrative model of mindfulness. method a scoping review using database searches identified relevant publications in peer-reviewed journals ranked in the top quartile according to scimago journal rank. excerpts from 120 articles comparing contemporary and buddhist conceptualizations of mindfulness were analyzed using inductive content analysis. results four categories were identified, indicating that the reviewed literature commonly characterizes buddhist conceptualizations of mindfulness as (a) oriented toward ethical behavior and liberating self-transformation; (b) involving discerning awareness and wise judgment informed by recollection and insight; (c) inseparable from an interconnected system of practices; and (d) involving heedfulness and vigilant guarding of the mind, remembering one’s intentions. conclusions by revisiting and integrating these differences, we propose, as an interpretive synthesis of these contrasts, a process model of mindfulness consisting of four components: (a) sound awareness (non-judgmental awareness), (b) discerning awareness and wise judgment, (c) choice and action guided by wise judgment, and (d) heedfulness. rather than interpreting contemporary and buddhist conceptualizations as incompatible, the model incorporates the differences as complementary components within a unified account. preregistration : this review’s protocol was registered with the open science framework ( https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/4w7df ). mindfulness

joint developmental trajectories of irritability and executive function: associations with time-varying psychopathological problems among chinese adolescents existing research has established that irritability and executive function (ef) are distinct yet often co-occurring transdiagnostic symptoms, each with its developmental trajectory. however, no evidence exists on whether these two symptoms follow joint developmental patterns or on which patterns increase risk for later problems. to address this gap, the present study tracked joint trajectories of irritability and ef and linked these patterns to subsequent externalizing and internalizing problems. a seven-wave longitudinal design was employed with a sample of 491 students in china (m = 9.84 years, sd = 0.71; 48.1% boys). irritability was reported by mothers, while adolescents completed three ef tasks assessing inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility and reported their own psychopathological problems. parallel process latent growth curve modeling was used to examine joint trajectories of irritability and ef. bch auxiliary analysis was conducted to test whether externalizing and internalizing problems differed across the identified classes. four joint irritability-ef trajectories emerged: persistently high irritability, low-increasing ef, adapted, and moderate. the persistently high irritability class exhibited the highest externalizing problems, followed by the low-increasing ef class, a pattern that remained robust after multiple comparison correction. the adapted class exhibited relatively high levels of both externalizing and internalizing problems, a pattern that did not remain robust after multiple comparison correction. these findings highlight the co-occurrence and diversity of developmental patterns of irritability and ef, with distinct patterns conferring specific risks for later externalizing versus internalizing problems, underscoring the importance of early identification of at-risk trajectories for targeted intervention. research on child and adolescent psychopathology

parallel parent–child mindfulness intervention for migrant families' adaptation: a randomized controlled trial parent and child sociocultural adaptation is essential to migrant family well-being, and community-based mindfulness training may support this process. however, evidence on mindfulness interventions for migrant families remains scarce, particularly those engaging parent and child simultaneously. this study evaluates a parallel parent-child mindfulness intervention targeting sociocultural adaptation, psychological adjustment, and family relationships among chinese new-arrival families in hong kong. in a randomized controlled trial, 116 parent-child dyads were assigned to an 8-week mindfulness intervention or routine community services. outcomes were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 6-month follow-up. compared with controls, the intervention significantly improved parents' sociocultural adaptation, with attenuated effects at follow-up. it also increased parent life satisfaction and reduced parenting stress at posttest. child outcomes were largely nonsignificant, except for short-term improvements in social interaction and life satisfaction at posttest. indirect effects of the intervention through parent sociocultural adaptation were nonsignificant, with estimates in the hypothesized direction for parent life satisfaction (b = 0.94, 95% ci [-0.02, 1.90]) and psychological distress (b = -1.42, 95% ci [-2.89, 0.04]). no mediation effects were observed among children. subgroup analyses indicated that effects on parent adaptation and life satisfaction varied by child sex and family length of residence, with sustained effects observed only among parents of boys and families residing in hong kong for less than 2 years. findings suggest that parallel parent-child mindfulness interventions may support specific aspects of migrant families' adaptation, with more consistent and sustained effects for parents than for children. family process

gendered motives for group formidability among children and adults. recent decades have seen a surge of research revealing the core, early emerging psychological building blocks for navigating human societies. yet, how such core motives operate across life, undergirding political ideology, remains unknown. here we use the same kind of minimal, abstract group stimuli across the lifespan to show that gendered preferences for majority groups manifest among preschoolers and adults alike (but not among preverbal infants) and that they motivate support for sustaining intergroup hierarchies (for example, ethnic persecution, militarism and social welfare opposition) among adults. preschool (n = 317) boys, but not girls, preferred majority rather than minority members, whereas infants (n = 180) chose randomly between the two. among adults (n = 3,467), males also liked the majority more than females, and these coalitional preferences correlated robustly with political ideology. these results indicate that gendered motives for intergroup formidability are rooted in earliest childhood once children begin navigating peer relationships independently. nature human behaviour

rolle neuropsychologischer hochschulambulanzen in forschung, lehre, aus- und weiterbildung zusammenfassung: theoretischer hintergrund: die einrichtung der neuropsychologischen psychotherapie als eigenständiger gebietsweiterbildung fördert die etablierung von neuropsychologischen hochschulambulanzen an den universitäten. fragestellung: der vorliegende artikel beleuchtet die entwicklung neuropsychologischer hochschulambulanzen in den letzten 10 – 15 jahren, untermauert mit exemplarischen daten einer beispielambulanz. methode: die erfahrungen bezogen auf die umsetzung von aus- und weiterbildung im bereich der klinischen neuropsychologie (altes system) bzw. auf dem gebiet der neuropsychologischen psychotherapie (neues system) und der klinischen versorgung von patient_innen mit erworbenen hirnschädigungen im rahmen dieser strukturen werden reflektiert. ergebnisse: erfahrungen mit der bereichsweiterbildung klinische neuropsychologie unter refinanzierung von anstellung und theorie können teilweise auf die umsetzung der gebietsweiterbildung übertragen werden. behandlungsdaten einer neuropsychologischen hochschulambulanz illustrierten unterschiede aber auch gemeinsamkeiten im vergleich zu anderen psychotherapeutischen hochschulambulanzen. aufgrund der heterogenität der ätiologien und beeinträchtigungsprofile sind individuelle betrachtungen von outcomeparametern notwendig. schlussfolgerung: erfahrungen bezüglich der verzahnung von aus- und weiterbildung, wissenschaftlicher qualifikation und klinischer versorgung werden positiv subsumiert. zeitschrift fur klinische psychologie und psychotherapie

uptake, barriers, and facilitators of open science in clinical psychology abstract: open science practices (osps) aim to enhance transparency, reproducibility, and research quality, yet empirical research regarding their uptake in clinical psychology remains scarce. the present survey examined osps across clinical psychological research, teaching, and psychotherapeutic practice at universities and university clinics in german-speaking countries. based on responses from 130 participants ( m = 37.13 ± 9.75 years of age, 61.54 % female), preregistration, a priori sample size planning, and open access publishing were the most commonly reported osps. concerns regarding data protection and ethics, time constraints, and fear of mistakes were the most prominent barriers, while access to infrastructure and incentives were the most needed types of support. teaching activities addressed open science topics, whereas implementation in clinical practice remained limited. overall, the findings highlight the need for field-specific guidelines, institutional support, and aligned incentive structures to foster sustainable adoption of osps across career stages and contexts. zeitschrift fur klinische psychologie und psychotherapie

validation of the motives to use social network sites scale (motus) in argentine adults the use of social networking sites has become a daily practice worldwide, prompting the development of instruments to assess the motives underlying their use. the aim of this study was to validate the motives to use social network sites scale (motus) in a sample of argentine adults from córdoba. a total of 1,053 participants completed the spanish version of the motus along with measures of fear of missing out (fomo) and social connectedness. the internal structure was examined using confirmatory factor analysis, and additional analyses were conducted to assess gender factorial invariance, convergent validity, and reliability. results supported an eight-factor, 26-item model (robust cfi = .91; robust tli = .89; robust rmsea = .074; srmr = .051) and invariance across men and women. most subscales showed adequate reliability (ω = .73–.89), with the exception of passive entertainment, which demonstrated low internal consistency. all dimensions were positively associated with fomo, particularly the passive-use dimensions, whereas correlations with social connectedness were weak. these findings provide evidence supporting the use of the motus for assessing motives and modes of social networking site use in this population, although additional psychometric research is warranted, particularly regarding the passive entertainment dimension. revista ces psicologia

breaking the vicarious trap: two buffers against close others’ environmental influence abstract background close others' pro-environmental or anti-environmental behaviors can create a vicarious trap: good deeds trigger licensing (reducing one's own effort), and bad deeds induce identification (justifying inaction). however, how this trap can be mitigated remains unclear. methods across four studies (total n = 523), we found evidence for the vicarious trap in pro‑environmental behavior (peb) and tested two buffers: situational openness (study 2) and environmental self‑identity (studies 3–4). study 1 compared relationship types; study 4 combined a brief identity‑enhancement intervention with a 30‑day diary. results study 1 ( n = 97) showed that recalling close friends' (but not family members') environmental actions reduced subsequent peb. study 2 ( n = 180) demonstrated that situational openness—making the recalled behavior public—eliminated the trap. study 3 ( n = 180) showed that high environmental self-identity provided complete immunity. study 4 ( n = 66) provided preliminary, exploratory evidence that identity enhancement promotes an identity‑driven pathway: daily environmental self‑identity predicted next‑day peb with autoregressive controls, and mediation analyses confirmed identity as the causal mechanism. conclusions these findings identify boundary conditions and provide initial evidence for an identity‑driven behavioral pathway, with practical implications for interventions leveraging social norms and self‑concept to promote sustained peb. bmc psychology

impact of the covid-19 pandemic on mental health of parents with young children up to three years post-pandemic: a dynamic, population-based cohort study abstract background parents of young children experienced significant mental health challenges during the covid-19 pandemic, suggesting accumulation of pandemic-related stressors over time. this raises concerns about potential post-pandemic effects, specifically among those facing additional hardships. this study examines the impact of the pandemic on parental mental health up to three years post-pandemic and identifies predictors of mental health during the pandemic. methods data collected between october 2019 and january 2025 from the dynamic population-based sarphati cohort were used, including 4,319 parents whose initial measurement occurred prior to or during the pandemic. measurements were restricted to when children were aged 0–3 years. repeated measurements of psychological distress ( n = 6,595 observations), loneliness ( n = 6,595), and parenting stress ( n = 9,830) were analysed across eleven time periods (pre-, during, and post-pandemic) using linear mixed models. change in emotional well-being due to the pandemic ( n = 9,228) was analysed descriptively across pandemic periods. sociodemographic, family, household, and pandemic-specific factors were tested as mental health predictors during the pandemic. results psychological distress significantly increased during the pandemic (second lockdown: estimated marginal means (emm) = 4.83, 95% ci [4.52; 5.13] versus pre-pandemic emm = 4.41, [4.12; 4.71]), declined post-pandemic (2022), but significantly increased again from 2023 onwards (2024/2025: emm = 5.11, [4.72; 5.49]). loneliness significantly increased in the second lockdown (emm = 1.78, [1.66; 1.91] versus pre-pandemic emm = 1.40, [1.28; 1.53]) and remained elevated up to 2024/2025 (emm = 1.64, [1.48; 1.79]). parenting stress significantly increased in the second lockdown (emm = 16.3, [16.0; 16.6] versus pre-pandemic emm = 16.0, [15.7; 16.4]) and continued rising post-pandemic (2024/2025: emm = 17.4, [17.0; 17.7]). poorer emotional well-being due to the pandemic was most pronounced during lockdowns. financial difficulties, dissatisfaction with living conditions, additional childcare needs and working from home significantly predicted poorer mental health during the pandemic. conclusions parents with young children appear to face ongoing psychological burden three years after the covid-19 pandemic. this underscores the importance of continued monitoring and support for families with young children, alongside research to identify which subgroups face persistent difficulties and how these challenges affect child development. bmc psychology
