autism and homelessness: risk and protective factors in a bayesian analysis of autistic characteristics. autistic individuals are overrepresented in homeless populations, yet mechanisms driving this association remain unclear, particularly in the context of diagnostic access and structural inequities. we surveyed 333 adults in australia, assessing autistic traits (autism-spectrum quotient [aq]-50), homelessness risk factors, adaptive functioning and social support. bayesian hierarchical logistic regression models were used to estimate associations. associations between autistic traits and homelessness probability differed according to diagnostic status. among participants without a formal diagnosis, higher aq-50 scores were associated with greater estimated homelessness probability, although uncertainty remained; this association was attenuated among formally diagnosed participants. structural risk factors were credibly associated with higher homelessness probability, whereas mental health-related risk factors showed a positive posterior estimate with greater uncertainty. interaction effects involving socioeconomic status and social support suggested that associations between autistic traits and homelessness varied according to broader social context. bayesian mediation analyses explored adaptive functioning as a potential pathway linking autistic traits and homelessness; however, evidence for an indirect effect remained uncertain. findings highlight the importance of diagnostic accessibility, social support and structural accommodation for individuals experiencing elevated autistic traits and housing instability. improving access to diagnosis, autism-informed services and structural supports may represent promising targets for future interventions aimed at reducing housing instability, pending longitudinal evidence.lay abstractautistic people are more likely to experience homelessness than the general population, but the reasons for this are not fully understood. many adults with autistic traits may never receive a formal diagnosis, which can limit their access to support and services. this study examined how autistic traits, everyday functioning skills and social support relate to the risk of homelessness. we surveyed 333 adults in australia about autistic traits, factors associated with homelessness, daily living skills and social support. statistical analyses were used to estimate how these factors were associated with the probability of homelessness. adults reporting higher autistic traits without a formal autism diagnosis showed a higher estimated probability of homelessness within this sample. associations between autistic traits and homelessness differed according to diagnostic status, and stronger social support was associated with lower estimated homelessness probability. these results suggest that earlier identification of autism and improved access to support services may be associated with improved housing stability and service accessibility for autistic adults. strengthening social support networks may also be important. these findings may help inform screening practices within homelessness services and policies that improve access to autism assessment and support. autism
associations and interactions between genetic vulnerability and physical activity with mdd in the all of us research program nature mental health

facilitating mindfulness training with ultrasonic neuromodulation this randomized trial tested whether suppressive transcranial focused ultrasound (tfus) targeting the posterior cingulate cortex during mindfulness training altered equanimity and resting-state default mode-central executive network (dmn-cen) connectivity in novice meditators. thirty meditation-naive adults were randomized to active or sham tfus; 24 completed a 2-week body focus program (active n = 16; sham n = 8), including 14 daily lessons and four tfus-meditation sessions. resting-state fmri scans were acquired and the equanimity scale-16 (es-16) was administered before and after the meditation training intervention. voluntary meditation practice time was measured during four tfus-meditation sessions during training. dmn-cen connectivity showed an interaction (β = −0.118, 95% ci [−0.186, −0.050], p = 0.002), reflecting decreased connectivity in active and a nonsignificant increase in sham. greater dmn-cen decreases were associated with greater es-16 acceptance increases across participants (β = −22.93, p = 0.031). the estimated relation between connectivity change and voluntary practice duration differed in direction by condition, but the interaction was not significant (β = −51.69, p = 0.061). pcc-targeted tfus combined with mindfulness-based training was associated with resting-state connectivity differences but not differential change in the es-16 total score. replication in a larger, fully blinded trial is needed. the preregistration specified a target of 80 participants with 1:1 allocation ( https://osf.io/pe6d4/ ). resource-related changes made before outcome examination resulted in 30 randomized participants, of whom 24 completed. because the connectivity hypothesis was underspecified, the connectivity analyses and non-preregistered es-16 subscale analyses were treated as exploratory. mindfulness

stable asymmetries, fragile wordings: cross-formulation evidence on the epistemic side-effect effect the epistemic side-effect effect (esee) is the asymmetry whereby agents are more readily attributed knowledge about harmful than helpful side effects of their actions. we examine whether this asymmetry depends on the formulation of the knowledge claim. across three experiments conducted in polish and english, using between- and within-subjects designs, we tested agentive, causal, and change-of-state formulations of the knowledge probe. wording effects were limited and uneven: the harm–help asymmetry persisted across all formulations, and harm cases remained highly stable, whereas help cases showed greater variability and the only detectable formulation effects. justifications for knowledge attributions predominantly invoked consequence awareness rather than belief or evidential support, while knowledge denials in help cases drew on a wider range of epistemic and motivational considerations. the findings suggest that esee is not driven by probe wording, and that help cases are the main site of residual variability in the effect. review of philosophy and psychology

genai literacy and students’ exploitative and exploratory innovation: the moderating role of critical thinking generative artificial intelligence (genai) literacy, encompassing the knowledge, skills, and attitudes for effective use, is becoming essential in education. however, its distinct associations with exploitative versus exploratory innovation and the role of critical thinking remain unclear. grounded in social cognitive theory, this study surveyed 228 students to examine these relationships. genai literacy was positively associated with exploitative innovation and showed a u-shaped association with exploratory innovation, in which benefits emerged only after a literacy threshold; the u-shaped association was robust to correction for multiple comparisons. critical thinking negatively moderated the association between genai literacy and exploitative innovation, and this interaction was robust to correction for multiple comparisons; the hypothesized moderation of the u-shaped exploratory association, in contrast, did not reach the 0.05 level and did not receive empirical support. the findings extend theory by differentiating how genai literacy relates to distinct innovation types and offer practical guidance—drawn from the supported associations and from theoretical reasoning—for fostering balanced human–ai collaboration. because participation was voluntary, the self-selected sample may have overestimated the reported associations, and all results should be interpreted with this caveat in mind. journal of intelligence

stable across time and targets? test-retest reliability of the emotional accuracy test. the emotional accuracy test (eat) assesses performance-based emotional understanding by comparing perceivers' ratings with targets' multidimensional self-reports. prior research supports its convergent and construct validity; the present studies examined test-retest reliability. study 1 (= 27; mean interval = 25.52 days) repeated the same targets and showed rank-order stability,= .58, 95% ci [.26, .79], and absolute agreement, icc(a,1) = .59, 95% ci [.20, .80], with no systematic mean-level change. study 2 (= 62; mean interval = 17.00 days) used different target sets and showed rank-order stability,= .69, 95% ci [.53, .80], and consistency, icc(c,1) = .65, 95% ci [.49, .76]. absolute agreement was lower, icc(a,1) = .52, 95% ci [.37, .63], with higher time 2 scores. target set was confounded with occasion and scored composites differed in length (three vs. four videos), so the mean difference cannot be uniquely attributed to occasion. adjusting for mean rating intensity reduced study 2's correlation to .49, a conservative sensitivity estimate because adjustment may also remove accuracy-relevant variance. together with prior validity evidence, these findings provide additional psychometric support for using the eat in group-level and correlational research. journal of intelligence

beyond overlap: development and validation of the inclusion of ai in self (iais) scale and its moderating role in the relationship between ai identity and ai threat artificial intelligence (ai) is becoming increasingly integrated into people’s self-concepts, yet a psychometrically robust multi-item pictorial instrument for assessing the inclusion of ai in self (iais) is lacking. drawing on self-expansion theory and the ai-mediated communication (ai-mc) model, we developed and validated the iais scale. the iais comprises four pictorial items capturing overlap, distance, centrality, and size, designed as indicators of a single dimension. in study 1, chinese university students (n = 195, 56.9% male) were recruited through campus online platforms using convenience sampling. we conducted exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses (efa/cfa), examined reliability and convergent, discriminant, and criterion-related validity (the last via steiger’s z tests), and assessed gender invariance with multigroup cfa. in study 2, the scale was cross-validated in a sample of chinese employees (n = 513, 38.4% male) recruited through the credamo online research platform. in study 3, a mixed student–employee sample (n = 240, 43.3% male) completed a two-wave longitudinal survey with a 15-day interval. the moderating role of iais in the relationship between ai identity and ai threat was tested with process model 1 (5000 bootstrap resamples). results supported a replicable single-factor structure, good reliability, and convergent, discriminant, and criterion-related validity. iais significantly moderated the association between ai identity and ai threat. we conclude that iais is a psychometrically sound instrument for assessing the inclusion of ai in self, and that the negative association between ai identity and ai threat is stronger among individuals who include ai more deeply in the self. journal of intelligence

math anxiety and metacognition: how numerical content shapes confidence math anxiety is robustly linked to lower success rates in mathematical tasks, yet its relation to metacognitive aspects, such as confidence and overconfidence, remains less well understood. moreover, prior research often used tasks in which numerical content and mathematical reasoning were intertwined, making it difficult to determine whether math anxiety is triggered by computation itself or by numerical framing more broadly. to address these gaps, two experiments examined associations between math anxiety, task success rates, confidence, and overconfidence. in both experiments, participants completed a novel single-answer sudoku task (sast) and the cognitive reflection test (crt), together with anxiety-related self-report questionnaires. in experiment 1 (n = 209), the sast contained numbers, similar to the traditional sudoku. math anxiety predicted lower success rates and confidence, and greater overconfidence, in both the numerical sast and the crt, beyond relevant individual-difference variables. experiment 2 (n = 200) used a structurally identical sast, in which letters replaced numbers. while the crt results replicated experiment 1, math anxiety no longer predicted confidence or overconfidence in the letter sast. the findings suggest that math anxiety relates to impaired metacognitive monitoring when numerical content is present, even without computational demands, but not in equivalent non-numerical reasoning tasks. journal of intelligence

essentialist and nonessentialist views of cognitive aging in older age: the role of working memory, cognitive inhibition and psychological well-being. views of cognitive aging refer to how people think and believe about age-related cognitive changes with aging, including whether they perceive these age-related cognitive changes as fixed (essentialism of cognitive aging) or as potentially malleable (nonessentialism). this cross-sectional study examined the role of cognitive functioning-in particular working memory and cognitive inhibition/interference performance-and psychological well-being in explaining views of cognitive aging among older adults. a total of 237 community-dwelling older adults aged 64-85 years completed the views of cognitive aging questionnaire, along with verbal working memory, cognitive inhibition/interference tasks, and a psychological well-being questionnaire. regression analyses showed that cognitive performance and psychological well-being explained a significant, though modest, part of the variance mainly in nonessentialist (malleable) views of cognitive aging. better working memory performance was associated only with stronger generalized and personal nonessentialist views. in addition, greater cognitive resistance to proactive interference, but not inhibition, and psychological well-being were positively associated with generalized nonessentialist views of cognitive aging. these associations were more evident among adults aged 75-85 years than among those aged 64-74 years. overall, these findings suggest that cognitive performance and psychological well-being contribute differently to the views of age-related cognitive changes and are more closely related to flexible, rather than fixed, views of cognitive aging, particularly in adults 75 and older. the examination of views of cognitive aging could be included in assessment protocols aimed at promoting healthy aging. journal of intelligence

demographic-adjusted normative equations for the oculo-cognitive addition test (ocat): a foundation for individualized oculo-cognitive assessment background: many neurological and cognitive disorders have early oculomotor hallmarks. the oculo-cognitive addition test (ocat) is a quick, objective screening tool that measures eye movement and time-based biomarkers of cognitive processing during simple mental addition tasks in under two minutes. normative values for age, sex, education level, and apolipoprotein e type 4 (apoe ε4) carrier status must be established so cognitively normal populations are not misdiagnosed. methods: a total of 382 participants completed ocat, with 350 participants making up the normative cohort from which raw gaze data were processed to derive fixations, saccades, blinks, pupillary dynamics, and time-based features. separate multiple linear regression models were fitted for each feature with age, sex, education, and apoe ε4 carrier status as predictors to establish demographic-adjusted normative equations. results: processing time, fixation time, fixation size and fixation area and their variability increased progressively from the first to the third number within each addition sequence, consistent with increasing cognitive workload. demographic-adjusted multiple linear regression models generated normative equations for individual ocat features based on age, sex, education, and apoe ε4 carrier status. these models were used to derive individualized expected values, 95% reference intervals, and z-scores. conclusions: these demographic-adjusted normative equations enable individualized interpretation of ocat performance and are necessary steps towards clinical implementation. journal of eye movement research

through the looking glass: eye tracking as a cognitive benchmark for language-model semantics and observer-specific semantic alignment assessing semantic representations learned by language models remains challenging because conventional intrinsic benchmarks capture limited aspects of meaning and often correlate weakly with downstream performance. eye tracking offers complementary, cognitively grounded evidence: gaze measures recorded during reading and scene viewing index online processing and attentional selection, although they should not be treated as readouts of semantic representations. this narrative review and methodological framework synthesizes research linking distributional and contextual language representations to eye-movement behavior, focusing on semantic relatedness, predictability, surprisal, model scale, layer-dependent alignment, and model–human correspondence. evidence from naturalistic reading corpora shows that embedding-derived relatedness and language-model surprisal explain variance in fixation measures, while recent work demonstrates that cognitive alignment depends on model size, layer, tokenization, task, and measurement regime. we propose extending this approach from population-level model evaluation to observer-specific gaze-derived relational structure. for visual scenes, gaze transitions can be represented as candidate choices and relational graphs and compared with multiple semantic-relation matrices derived from language or vision–language models. because gaze transitions are influenced by spatial distance, object size, salience, task demands, context, and preprocessing decisions, these factors must be controlled and, where causal isolation is intended, manipulated independently of semantic relations. we propose combining candidate-normalized hierarchical choice models, residualized gaze relations, representational similarity analysis with reliability and uncertainty assessment, and required independent behavioral validation to characterize convergence and divergence between model semantic geometry and observer-specific relational organization. journal of eye movement research

exploring asd identification using different types of eye-tracking features eye tracking offers a non-invasive way of examining social visual attention in children and may support the objective identification of autism spectrum disorder (asd). however, small-sample studies are often affected by individual differences, inconsistent feature selection, and limited integration of different gaze representations. this study explored a dynamic and static multiscale feature fusion framework for classifying children with pre-existing clinical asd diagnoses and typically developing (td) children using eye-tracking data collected during an emotion recognition task. after quality screening, 44 children aged 4–7 years were included (18 asd and 26 td). static statistical features, dynamic sequences, early feature concatenation, and multiscale fusion were evaluated using participant-independent data partitioning, with static feature selection restricted to the training participants in each split. cnn–lstm with multiscale fusion achieved an accuracy of 0.78 ± 0.08, asd recall of 0.65 ± 0.22, f1-score of 0.71 ± 0.12, and auc of 0.76 ± 0.16. a fully nested leave-one-participant-out evaluation provided additional internal validation of participant-level classification. overall, the results indicate that different approaches to combining static and dynamic gaze representations may lead to different classification outcomes, while further validation in larger independent samples is needed. journal of eye movement research

idealised idols and body dysmorphic vulnerability in adolescent k-pop fans: do body image disturbances and self-objectification play a role? this study investigated the relationship between celebrity worship and body dysmorphic symptoms among 1,081 adolescent female k-pop fans. we examined body image disturbance and self-objectification as mediators. participants completed the body dysmorphic disorder yale-brown obsessive compulsive scale-self report, the celebrity attitude scale-23, the self-objectification questionnaire, and the multidimensional body-self relations questionnaire-as. the structural equation model demonstrated significant direct and indirect pathways among the study variables, confirming the mediating roles of both variables and the overall adequacy of model fit. this suggests that intense identification with celebrities is associated with heightened vulnerability to body dysmorphic symptoms among adolescents, reflecting the internalisation of unrealistic beauty ideals and appearance-focused cognitive and emotional processes, particularly in cultures that emphasise feminine beauty. interventions that enhance media literacy and critical thinking about beauty norms are essential, especially as societal structures intensify appearance-related pressures. international journal of adolescence and youth

the effects of agricultural education on students battling adverse childhood experiences: a qualitative case study while agricultural education has positively impacted millions of students since its inception, many of its students have experienced adverse childhood experiences. this study aimed to describe the perceptions of participating new mexico and arizona agricultural educators regarding the benefits of agricultural education for students with trauma and to outline the challenges of teaching students experiencing aces. we used a qualitative case study design to conduct interviews with 14 agricultural educators. we determined that agricultural educators frequently encounter students with aces and that agricultural education offers numerous benefits for students facing aces, including hands-on career preparation, access to a responsible role model in their teacher, and positive activities that engage them outside the home. we concluded that teaching these students can lead to challenges such as behavioural issues, teacher secondary traumatic stress, and cultural nuances that can exacerbate the effects of aces. international journal of adolescence and youth
intimate partner violence in the context of separation: prevalence and risk factors journal of family violence

gender differences in child maltreatment predictors of physical intimate partner violence victimization: a study among australian adults abstract purpose experiences of child abuse and neglect are widely acknowledged to be associated with increased risk of intimate partner violence (ipv) victimization in adulthood. this study examines whether the association between childhood abuse and neglect experiences and adult ipv victimization differs for males and females. it then goes on to examine which specific types of childhood experiences of abuse and neglect are associated with adult physical ipv victimization. methods the study draws on data collected as part of an ongoing australian prospective, longitudinal study of mothers and their offspring. logistic regression models were estimated, and model coefficient comparisons were conducted. the association between specific types of childhood experiences of abuse and neglect and adult physical ipv victimization were examined. results analyses showed that the associations between childhood experiences of abuse and neglect and adult ipv victimization varied by gender. for females, two types of abuse (sexual and emotional) and one type of neglect (emotional) during childhood were significantly associated with physical ipv victimization in adulthood. in contrast, for males, it was their experiences of physical abuse and physical neglect that were associated with physical ipv victimization in adulthood. conclusion emotional and sexual abuse and emotional neglect in childhood is significantly associated with subsequent physical ipv victimization for females, whereas childhood physical abuse and neglect is significantly associated with subsequent physical ipv victimization for males. this suggests that females and males may be affected differently by those abuse and neglect experiences in childhood, and further exploration of how this occurs will yield valuable insight into why females and males have different pathways to victimization. journal of family violence

an investigation of mental health inequalities related to race and ethnicity in psychological therapy services. objective: prior evidence suggests that people from racial/ethnic minority (rem) groups experience greater psychological distress, especially if they are isolated from their cultural ingroup. this study examined associations between rem status and psychological symptoms measured before and after therapy, as well as interactions with neighbourhood-level rem density.
method: electronic health records from 130,857 patients who accessed psychological interventions in primary care services in england were analyzed. pre- and post-treatment depression (phq-9), anxiety (gad-7) and functional impairment measures (wsas) were linked to individual-level and neighbourhood-level demographic and socioeconomic data. multilevel (mixed effect) models were used to examine associations between individual and neighbourhood socioeconomic variables with available measures of psychological distress.
results: specific (rather than all) rem groups had higher indices of psychological distress, and there was little evidence of a moderating effect of neighbourhood ethnic density in the hypothesized direction. after controlling for socioeconomic variables, consistently higher indices of distress before and after therapy were evident for patients from white-other, pakistani, bangladeshi, and "other" backgrounds.
conclusions: mental health inequalities are evident for people from specific rem groups. psychotherapy research

the role of socio-cognitive abilities in adolescent and young adult romantic relationships: a systematic review abstract high-quality romantic relationships are linked to better psychological well-being, yet adolescents and young adults vary in the quality of their romantic experiences. socio-cognitive abilities, including empathy, emotion regulation, and theory of mind, may play a role in shaping romantic outcomes. this systematic review synthesizes evidence from 26 studies to examine how these abilities relate to romantic relationship quality in adolescents and young adults, following prisma 2020 guidelines. given the limited research on theory of mind in this population, perspective-taking was additionally included as a closely related socio-cognitive process. findings indicate that the relational value of these abilities depends substantially on which subcomponent is engaged: empathic concern and cognitive reappraisal were consistently associated with higher relationship satisfaction and more constructive conflict resolution, while personal distress and expressive suppression showed the opposite pattern. perspective-taking also showed consistent positive associations. research on theory of mind in romantic contexts remains scarce, but available evidence suggests a promising role in partner well-being and emotion regulation. the review further identifies an asymmetry between actor and partner effects and addresses developmental and gender-related patterns. overall, the review highlights the possible interdependence of socio-cognitive abilities in adolescent and young adult romantic relationships and the limited evidence available on theory of mind. current psychology
smartphone addiction, fomo, and online social identity: the protective role of peer and parent attachment current psychology
randomized controlled pilot trial of a messenger-integrated self-compassion intervention (miscab-s) for individuals at risk of compulsive sexual behavior disorder current psychology
development and validation of the driving self-esteem questionnaire current psychology

the importance of the parent-clinician dyad during a neurodevelopmental assessment in a community mental health setting. although much is known about the challenges clinicians and parents face during a neurodevelopmental assessment, to date, there has been little focus on examining these differing experiences. the aim of this study was to explore the views of clinical staff and parents during an autism spectrum disorder assessment, using a mixed-method approach which involved both parents and staff completing a survey with closed and open-ended questions and/or parent one-on-one qualitative interviews or a focus group. the study highlighted the challenges faced by both clinical staff and parents during the assessment process. despite the emotional challenges, parents felt supported; however, staff were self-critical about aspects of the process. it became clear that there is a need for a strong alliance between staff and parents throughout the process, which requires a holistic, adaptive, and collaborative approach. staff challenges can be managed through a supportive multidisciplinary team, while provision of clear expectations prior to the assessment may alleviate parental stress. behavioral sciences

situated student sense of belonging in higher education: the importance of context and engagement. while the benefits of student sense of belonging in higher education are well established, lower levels of belonging among minoritized ethnic students and fluctuations over time are frequently reported. however, most research focuses on the wider institution, overlooking the department as the primary setting for meaningful interpersonal interactions that foster belonging. using students' 'home' department as the principal context for belonging, this longitudinal study employed psychometric measures across the first year of study to examine situated sense of belonging, exploring differences by ethnicity and changes in belonging over time. relationships between belonging, involvement, and engagement were also explored. contrary to previous findings, ethnicity had no effect on belonging. however, both belonging and involvement declined over time, whereas engagement remained stable. engagement, but not involvement, emerged as a significant predictor of belonging. the absence of previously reported differences according to ethnicity highlights the importance of context, supporting the situated nature of student belonging and suggesting that departments may have greater potential than institutions to foster belonging, mitigate inequality, and support student wellbeing and success. the reported decline in students' belonging signals the need for sustained interventions that promote engagement and belonging beyond the initial stages of the students' entry into higher education. behavioral sciences

fair learning environment and financial well-being as resources for students’ academic engagement: basic psychological need satisfaction as a common motivational pathway academic engagement is associated with the resources available to students, yet it remains unclear through which psychological processes resources of different origins are related to academic engagement. bringing together basic psychological needs theory and the study demands–resources framework, this study examined whether autonomy, relatedness, and competence satisfaction mediate the associations of an institutional resource, a fair learning environment, and a resource rooted outside the academic environment, subjective financial well-being, with academic engagement. the measures were first evaluated using data from 278 university students. the structural model, specifying the three needs as parallel mediators, was then tested in a subsequent, non-overlapping sample of 741 students in türkiye. both resources positively predicted all three need satisfaction dimensions, whereas academic engagement was predicted only by autonomy (β = 0.43) and competence satisfaction (β = 0.36); relatedness satisfaction made no significant unique contribution. neither resource was directly associated with academic engagement. the total indirect effects were β = 0.31 for a fair learning environment and β = 0.13 for subjective financial well-being. the model explained 47.4% of the variance in academic engagement. resources of different origin were indirectly associated with academic engagement through the same two needs, autonomy and competence satisfaction. behavioral sciences

supporting chinese american youth mental health through culturally responsive parenting workshops and youth social-emotional learning. chinese american youth and their immigrant parents face multiple challenges, including discrimination and acculturative stress, which negatively affect their social-emotional development and mental health. despite elevated needs, chinese american youth are less likely than their white peers to access school-based or community-based mental health services. we partnered with chinese language schools to deliver two interventions: parent-child connect, a culturally responsive parenting workshop, and the culturally adapted version of merrell's strong kids socio-emotional learning (sel) curriculum to support youth mental health. a total of 49 chinese american parents (= 44.88 years,= 4.94; 90% mothers) participated in the six-week parent-child connect workshop. thirty youth (4th grade to 8th grade, 70% girls) participated in the six-week culturally adapted strong kids sel program. parents reported significant increases in positive parenting after the intervention, including warmth (= 0.40), reasoning (= 0.34), autonomy granting (= 0.38), parent-child communication (= 1.44), and perceived parenting competence (= 1.11), along with a significant decrease in their own mental health difficulties/general distress (= 0.33). parents also reported a significant increase in youth prosocial behavior (= 0.46). youth reported significant increases in sel knowledge, social-emotional competencies, and resilience (= 0.99) and a marginal increase in emotion-focused coping (= 0.43), after the intervention. qualitative feedback suggested that parents and youth found the culturally tailored and interactive activities engaging, sought additional opportunities to practice coping strategies, and reported developing strategies for responding to discrimination. findings suggest that culturally adapted parenting and sel programs are feasible and potentially beneficial for chinese american families when delivered in collaboration with language schools and community organizations. we discuss implications for how school psychologists, counselors, and educators can adapt interventions to better support immigrant families, promote youth social-emotional development, and improve mental health outcomes. behavioral sciences

risk and protective factors for the development of career resources: results of the “empower peers 4 careers” intervention study the transition from school to work represents a key developmental challenge during adolescence. career resources—personal, social, and identity-related factors that support career orientation and preparation—are crucial for navigating this transition. from a resilience perspective, the question arises under which risk and protective conditions such resources develop, are maintained, or are jeopardized. this study examines the relationship between psychosocial difficulties, a career-orientation-focused positive peer culture (ppc) intervention, and the development of career resources. the study used a quasi-experimental pre-post design with an intervention and a control group. the sample consisted of 234 lower secondary school students from regular and special education schools who participated at both measurement points. career resources were assessed with the career resources questionnaire, and psychosocial difficulties with the strengths and difficulties questionnaire. linear regression analyses were conducted while controlling for baseline values and relevant sociodemographic variables. exploratory subscale analyses and a process evaluation of the ppc group meetings were also conducted. the results showed no significant overall effect of the ppc intervention on career resources. however, psychosocial difficulties at baseline were a significant negative predictor of career resources in ninth grade. at the subscale level, an association with “importance of work in life,” reflecting a motivational and value-related aspect of career development, emerged at the unadjusted level; however, this association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing and should therefore be considered exploratory. the process evaluation indicated predominantly positive group experiences, particularly collaborative problem-solving and mutual support, but also challenges regarding participation and implementation within the school schedule. the findings highlight the relevance of psychosocial difficulties for career development and suggest that the role of peer-based social support in career preparation warrants further investigation. behavioral sciences

the effects of psychological counseling types on stress, athlete burnout, and resilience in athletes: ai chatbot vs. face-to-face counseling this study examined the effects of artificial intelligence (ai) chatbot counseling and face-to-face counseling on perceived stress, athlete burnout, and resilience among athletes. in this three-arm quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study, 73 athletes participated in ai chatbot counseling, face-to-face counseling, or a control condition over a 12-week intervention period. nonparametric longitudinal analyses revealed significant group-by-time interactions. after adjustment for multiplicity, significant group-by-time interactions were observed for perceived stress and reduced sense of accomplishment, a sub-variable of athlete burnout. perceived stress significantly decreased in the face-to-face counseling group, whereas reduced sense of accomplishment significantly decreased in the ai chatbot counseling group. for supportiveness, a sub-variable of resilience, the group-by-time interaction was significant before multiplicity adjustment but did not remain significant after adjustment. these findings indicate different patterns of change across the counseling conditions and psychological outcomes. given the quasi-experimental design and baseline differences among the groups, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and further investigation is needed to clarify the potential roles of ai chatbot counseling and face-to-face counseling in supporting athletes’ psychological well-being. behavioral sciences

the development of mandarin-speaking children’s comprehension of irony this study examined age-related differences in irony comprehension among 168 mandarin-speaking children aged 6–10 years. each child watched four illustrated stories with prerecorded audio: one literal, one deception, and two irony stories. for each irony story, children judged the speaker’s satisfaction, identified praise or criticism, and explained the remark. their answers were then classified into four ordered performance levels. age-group and irony-condition effects were tested with a generalized ordinal gee clustered by child, and explanation errors were examined descriptively. performance differed significantly by age group but not by irony condition. six-year-olds identified the speaker’s dissatisfaction and intended criticism in 40.4% of their classifiable story responses, compared with 83.3% among 10-year-olds. yet only about two in five responses from 10-year-olds included a correct or near-correct explanation. children who misjudged both attitude and meaning usually understood the remark literally and treated it as sincere. when children recognized dissatisfaction and criticism but could not explain the irony, most responses contained no relevant explanation, while some explained the remark as an attempt to conceal dissatisfaction or avoid direct criticism. together, these findings show age-related differences in recognizing ironic criticism and in performance on the explanation task. they also suggest that some awareness of the speaker’s strategy may be present before children can explain irony adequately. behavioral sciences

the mediating role of resilience in the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms among college students at a hispanic-serving institution in a u.s.-mexico border region. anxiety and depressive symptoms are prevalent concerns among college students, yet less is known about the role of resilience in their association among students in u.s.-mexico border regions. this cross-sectional study examined whether resilience statistically mediated the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms while controlling for sociodemographic factors and year of data collection. participants were a convenience sample of 857 college students attending a hispanic-serving institution in a u.s.-mexico border region from 2021 to 2025. anxiety, resilience, and depressive symptoms were measured using the generalized anxiety disorder-7, brief resilience scale, and patient health questionnaire-9, respectively. mediation analysis was conducted using process model 4 with 5000 bootstrap samples. higher anxiety was associated with lower resilience (= -0.056,< 0.001), and greater resilience was associated with lower depressive symptoms (= -1.379,< 0.001). the indirect association of anxiety with depressive symptoms through resilience was significant (= 0.077, 95% bootstrap ci [0.052, 0.103]). the direct association remained significant (= 0.700,< 0.001), indicating partial statistical mediation. these findings suggest that resilience is an important factor in the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms and may inform comprehensive student mental health initiatives. behavioral sciences

emotion regulation and brain mechanisms: a transdiagnostic perspective on neural circuits, individual differences, and clinical translation. emotion regulation (er) difficulties are now firmly established as a transdiagnostic feature of psychiatric and stress-related disorders. large-scale meta-analyses published in 2026 confirmed er impairments across fifteen diagnostic categories, shifting the key question from whether er is transdiagnostic to how this knowledge can inform diagnosis and treatment. this perspective argues that er should be conceptualized as a transdiagnostic neurocognitive dimension rather than a disorder-specific deficit. to support this view, three complementary studies are integrated: neuroimaging studies of prefrontal-limbic and large-scale brain networks involved in cognitive reappraisal; evidence of er-related neural alterations across mood, anxiety, trauma-related, personality, and addictive disorders; and research on individual differences and neuromodulation that explain variability in regulatory capacity and treatment response. er is framed within a broader executive-function model, operating as a "hot" executive process alongside "cool" cognitive-control functions. building on this evidence, a layered transdiagnostic model of emotion regulation (ltm-er) is proposed. the model includes a shared transdiagnostic core circuit (layer 1), disorder-specific neural signatures (layer 2), and individual moderators such as developmental history, dispositional traits, regulatory strategies, and stimulation parameters (layer 3). five testable predictions are derived from the model, highlighting how multimodal biomarkers and personalized interventions may advance precision approaches to emotion dysregulation across psychiatric disorders. behavioral sciences

climate-related distress: latent profiles of eco-anxiety, ptsd and cptsd symptoms and associated resilience and vulnerability factors in a portuguese sample. climate change is increasingly recognized as a significant stressor affecting well-being, yet responses to climate-related distress are heterogeneous and may reflect the interplay of eco-anxiety and trauma-related symptoms. this study used latent profile analysis to identify patterns of climate-related distress and examined their associations with environmental identity, developmental adversity, attachment, prior psychopathology, demographic characteristics, and direct exposure to climate-related events. a sample of 917 portuguese adults completed measures of eco-anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) symptom clusters, disturbances in self-organization (dso) symptoms, environmental identity, childhood adversity, and attachment. correlates were examined using multinomial logistic regression and manova. a five-profile solution was identified, ranging from minimal symptom endorsement to severe, co-occurring elevations in eco-anxiety, ptsd, and dso symptoms. profiles differed in protection of nature, but not connectedness with nature. higher-distress profiles were associated with greater direct exposure to climate-related events, childhood adversity, insecure attachment, prior psychopathology, younger age, and female sex, whereas lower-distress profiles were more strongly associated with secure attachment and the absence of previous mental health difficulties. these findings support a person-centered conceptualization of climate-related distress and highlight heterogeneity in the co-occurrence of eco-anxiety and trauma-related symptoms. climate-related distress may be embedded within developmental, psychological, demographic, and socioecological contexts. behavioral sciences

task-evoked whole-brain functional connectivity predicts post-training go-choice bias after food go/no-go training individual responses to food go/no-go training vary substantially, but the task-evoked network correlates of this variability remain unclear. this study tested whether large-scale functional connectivity during food choice predicts individual differences in post-training go-choice bias. a behavioral sample of 172 young women completed food go/no-go training in which go and no-go cues were paired with value-matched food items, followed by an in-scanner binary food-choice task; usable task-based fmri data were available for 162 participants. task-modulated connectivity among 268 brain regions was estimated using generalized psychophysiological interaction analysis, and connectome-based predictive modeling with repeated 10-fold cross-validation was used to predict post-training go-choice bias. participants selected go items above chance after training (59.3%). whole-brain go—no-go connectivity showed modest cross-validated concurrent prediction of post-training go-choice bias (combined network: mean ρ = 0.408, rmse = 0.169, p < 0.001; positive network: ρ = 0.325, rmse = 0.174, p < 0.001; negative network: ρ = 0.394, rmse = 0.169, p < 0.001). positive predictive edges prominently linked medial frontal and frontoparietal systems with the motor network and connected regions within the default mode network; medial frontal–salience connections were prominent in the distributed negative network. these findings identify candidate predictive connectivity patterns associated with individual variability in post-training go-choice bias that require independent validation. behavioral sciences

routes into single motherhood, normative family beliefs, and perception-based indicators of psychosocial vulnerability among women recruited through ecuadorian public university networks: an exploratory study single motherhood may begin through a self-reported decision to raise a child alone or through circumstances such as paternal irresponsibility, partner abandonment, and family constraints. guided by the stress-process model and perspectives on stigma and self-determination, this exploratory cross-sectional study examined associations among the reported route into single motherhood, normative beliefs about the indispensability of fathers, perceived labor inequity, and two perception-based indicators: endorsement of fear of judgment and endorsement of changes in self-esteem/self-concept. participants were recruited through purposive networks coordinated by one faculty or administrative contact at each of the six public universities in coastal and andean ecuador. the resulting non-probability analytic sample comprised 157 women who provided consent and identified as single mothers. of these respondents, 51 (32.5%) selected the decision-based response (“she decided to do it alone”), and 106 (67.5%) selected one of the three circumstance-based responses. fear of judgment was endorsed less often in the decision-based group than in the circumstance-based group (9.8% vs. 25.5%; exploratory p = 0.022). in secondary exploratory logistic regressions, both membership in the decision-based group (aor = 0.25, 95% ci 0.08–0.77) and student status rather than faculty status (aor = 0.18, 95% ci 0.06–0.55) were associated with lower within-sample odds of fear-of-judgment endorsement. the reported route was not independently associated with changes in self-esteem/self-concept. this indicator was associated with considering a father indispensable (aor = 2.91, 95% ci 1.41–5.99) and with greater perceived inequity in labor (aor = 1.57 per index point, 95% ci 1.15–2.13). among these respondents, the selected indicators varied according to reported route, normative beliefs, and perceived labor inequity. because the sample was non-probability-based and the outcomes were derived from individual questionnaire responses, the findings are not population estimates. they identified questions for larger studies using stronger sampling designs and validated multidimensional measures, as well as potential areas for university assessment, including stigma, caregiving accommodations, and employment equity. behavioral sciences

cognitive outcomes following neurosurgery for frontal intracerebral tumors: a systematic review and meta-analysis abstract objective: neurosurgical resection of frontal lobe tumors poses specific challenges to the patients. even when lesions involve the so-called “non-eloquent” areas, such as the prefrontal cortex, neurosurgery can still affect critical functions, because the prefrontal regions are essential for executive functions and other complex cognitive processes. the aim of this study is to systematically review the literature and quantitatively assess the impact of frontal lobe tumor resection on patients’ cognitive functioning. methods: in the present systematic review and meta-analysis, we synthesized data from 50 studies that included pre- and post-neurosurgery neuropsychological assessments. in addition, we conducted a meta-analysis of a subset of studies ( n = 15) including sufficient data to quantitatively evaluate the cognitive effects of frontal lobe tumor resections. results: we found that cognitive performance, after neurosurgery, was not significantly changed compared to pre-neurosurgery performance. we also identified several limitations in the literature, including variability in neuropsychological assessment protocols, differences in follow-up time points, inconsistent reporting of baseline cognitive functioning, and underpowered sample sizes. conclusions: in future studies, researchers should adopt standardized, comprehensive assessments, with well-powered cohorts and long-term follow-ups, to better characterize post-neurosurgical cognitive outcomes, including those regarding “non-eloquent” frontal regions. a multidisciplinary and harmonized approach remains crucial for understanding the cognitive impact of frontal lobe tumor neurosurgery and for improving patient care. journal of the international neuropsychological society

bigger between-language than within-language stroop effects in young and older deaf american sign language-english bilinguals abstract objective: the present study investigated stroop interference effects in young adult and older deaf american sign language (asl) and english bilinguals with asl and english stimuli. method: deaf asl-english bilinguals (n = 108; aged 21–88) signed their responses in two computerized stroop tasks, one with asl videos of color signs and one with printed english color words. participants saw 120 trials in each language with 84 congruent and 36 incongruent trials. results: even though participants responded in asl in both tasks, stroop effects were larger with english than with asl stimuli in both response times (rts) and errors, a pattern of results not typically seen in spoken-language bilinguals (in which stroop effects are often smaller between-languages than within-languages). older participants showed larger stroop effects than younger participants, especially in english rts. aging effects in error rates were not significant in either language. conclusions: the finding of larger stroop effects in deaf signers with english rather than asl stimuli suggests a possibly critical role for modality of presentation in eliciting stroop effects. additional work is needed to determine why english is more sensitive to aging effects in deaf signers, and which language will be most sensitive for detecting cognitive impairment in this population. journal of the international neuropsychological society

spirituality as a resilience anchor for parents raising children with spastic cerebral palsy abstract parenting children with spastic cerebral palsy (scp) presents significant emotional, physical and financial challenges, often exacerbated by social inequalities, stigma and limited support systems, particularly in under‐resourced settings like south africa. this qualitative, phenomenological study utilised semi‐structured interviews to collect data from eight mothers of children with scp attending a selected lsen school in soweto, south africa. the interviews explored participants' lived experiences in raising children with scp. the findings of this study reveal that spirituality serves as a resilience anchor, enabling parents to reframe challenges, regulate emotions and sustain hope. practices such as prayer, worship and scripture reading were identified as vital coping mechanisms, fostering emotional stability, peace and gratitude. parents described their caregiving roles as a divine purpose, which instilled meaning and empowered them to persevere despite adversities. this study contributes to understanding resilience as a dynamic and socially embedded process, offering valuable insights into the intersection of spirituality and caregiving in resource‐limited settings. journal of community & applied social psychology

retrospective accounts of femme lesbian, bisexual and queer women’s contextual safety in childhood and adolescence in australia lesbian, bisexual and queer (lbq) women are under increasing threat. the combined nature of patriarchal misogyny, femmephobia and queerphobia contributes to high levels of sexual violence and harassment. current literature focuses on biomedical health – stis and pregnancy – and interventions targeting youth behaviour. sociocultural factors are often treated as secondary. here, we focus on contextual safety (cs) – the relationships, discourses, and interpersonal behaviours of others that afford risk, harm, or safety. through a critical feminist lens, we explored lbq femme-women’s retrospective accounts of cs. a reflexive thematic analysis of repeated interviews with 10 femme- and lbq-identified australians provided insight into experiences and what can be done to protect young people. pervasive masculine entitlement, with the media’s sexualisation of lbq femininity, were key contributors to harm. left with little choice, subject to feminine devaluation, participants often self-sabotaged in response to sexual threats through feigning and fawning. participants’ experiences displayed stereotype incompatibility and confusion, leading to behaviours which validate either queer identity or a feigned cis-het identity in equally risky ways. participants urged families and schools to minimise risk through community education. we must continue to push against the status quo to afford more safety in sexual exploration. psychology & sexuality
an alternative behavior of organisms: a review of baum’s (2024) introduction to behavior: an evolutionary perspective perspectives on behavior science

to whom national culture matters: an analysis of mentions of countries in titles and abstracts in social and personality psychology and related fields from 1990 to 2020. culture significantly influences human psychology, making it essential for psychological research, particularly in social psychology, to acknowledge its importance. however, the majority of psychological research ignores or marginalises culture and context. this is problematic because, despite representing a small portion of humanity (specifically western, educated, industrialized, rich and democratic (weird) populations) mainstream psychology is published as if it represented the whole humanity. among the subfields of psychology, social psychology is arguably the one in which this issue should be least prevalent. to investigate this, we conducted a study on titles and abstracts of articles from 69 social psychology journals published between 1990 and 2020, examining how cultural diversity and awareness of its importance changed over time. the results indicate that cultural awareness is more prominent in journals focused on culture, international or local issues; while remaining almost entirely absent in journals focused on theory, reviews and business. furthermore, cultural awareness displays an imbalance regarding culture: while weird mentions remain most common, mentions of other regions appear to be disproportionately represented or 'inflated' in specific contexts. the generalizability of psychological theories will remain impossible if culture is not integrated as a central factor in research. international journal of psychology

a cross-cultural study of attachment and depression: the role of pride. greater attachment anxiety and avoidance are linked to more depressive symptoms. however, this association may present differently based on one's country of membership and expression of pride. in contrast to the eurocentric definition of pride in the united states, pride means both pleasant and unpleasant/disengagement emotions in chinese culture. this cross-cultural study aimed to examine the moderating effect of pride in the association between attachment anxiety/avoidance and depressive symptoms in both the united states and china. adults (n = 770) from china (n = 410) and the united states (n = 360) completed self-report measures. the results of moderation analyses (process model 1) indicated a marginally significant interaction effect of attachment insecurity × pride in predicting depressive symptoms among chinese individuals, but not among us individuals. specifically, greater attachment insecurity significantly exacerbated depressive symptoms for chinese individuals who expressed heightened levels of pride. the role of attachment on depressive symptoms may vary significantly by levels of pride among chinese individuals. this study highlights the importance of considering culturally congruent emotions such as pride when examining attachment-based mental health. international journal of psychology

between fire and electricity: a cultural-historical analysis of activity, sense formation, and energy transition among wayuu indigenous women abstract energy transitions are typically framed as technical processes of infrastructure replacement. this study challenges that framing by examining how wayuu indigenous women from the uriana clan in la paz–manaure (la guajira, colombia) form personal sense within culturally mediated activity systems as electricity gradually enters their territory. drawing on cultural-historical activity theory, we analyse the hearth as a central mediating artefact that integrates embodied knowledge, intergenerational transmission, matrilineal authority, and the reproduction of collective life within the desert ecosystem. through repeated ethnographic fieldwork (2022–2024), guided by zemelman’s methodological orientation toward totality, displacement, and epistemic reorientation, we reconstruct two partially overlapping activity systems, fire-based and electricity-based, and examine the contradictions that arise at their intersection. the analysis shows that the introduction of the electric stove simplifies operations at the surface while reconfiguring motive–object relations, altering temporal and sensory structures of activity, and transforming the conditions under which personal sense is formed. these findings contribute to cultural-historical psychology by showing how technological change in marginalised indigenous territories works as a dialectical transformation of activity, a process that exceeds the neutral substitution of tools, through which consciousness, identity, and intergenerational continuity are reorganised. the study calls for culturally situated approaches to energy transition that engage with the historically constituted forms of activity through which collective life and human subjectivity are reproduced. human arenas

addressing the “pseudo” in pseudoscience: a pilot study of the cognitive bias correction intervention we live in a post-truth era where misinformation is prevalent and the demarcation between scientific evidence and pseudoscience has become more ambiguous. pseudoscience leverages the epistemic and cultural authority of science. for people who are more prone to cognitive biases, pseudoscience can appear as accurate as empirical science. this study explored whether a cognitive bias correction (cbc) program could modify a person’s thinking style and reduce cognitive bias. individuals who were more likely to endorse pseudoscience had an intuitive thinking style and showed poorer ability to integrate evidence. those exposed to the cbc intervention became less willing to accept implausible hypotheses and showed an overall tendency to better integrate evidence on the bade task. these findings are consistent with the growing evidence that misbeliefs are linked to biased thinking styles, and that psychoeducational interventions targeting these biases may be effective in overcoming misinformation. journal of cognitive psychology

prevalence, determinants and spatial patterns of marital dissolution among ever married women in tanzania using population-based survey data abstract background marital dissolution, encompassing divorce and separation, poses critical social, economic, and health challenges. this study maps the prevalence and determinants of marital dissolution among ever-married women in tanzania, employing a multilevel mixed-effects model to capture individual and community-level influences and using geospatial analysis to identify regional patterns. methods this population-based study utilized data from the 2022 tanzania demographic and health survey (tdhs-mis), which employed a stratified two-stage cluster sampling design. a total of 10,837 ever-married women aged 15–49 years were included. socio-demographic and contextual variables were analyzed. a mixed-effects multilevel logistic regression models were used to assess factors associated with marital dissolution, while geospatial analyses, including spatial autocorrelation, were conducted to examine geographic patterns across tanzania. results marital dissolution was reported by 15% of respondents. geospatial mapping indicated pronounced regional disparities, with the highest rates in the southern zone, particularly in lindi (25.56%) and mtwara (23.84%). significant individual determinants included older age (aor = 1.05, 95% ci 1.04–1.06), cash employment (aor = 2.73, 95% ci 2.23–3.35), and lower educational attainment. community-level factors, such as community-level household wealth and urban residence, also influenced marital dissolution, with urban women nearly twice as likely to experience dissolution compared to rural women. conclusion the findings indicate that marital dissolution is a notable concern among ever-married women in tanzania, with important implications for family stability and social well-being. the results highlight the complex interplay of demographic, socio-economic, and regional factors associated with marital dissolution. spatial analysis further identifies geographic disparities, with higher concentrations observed in specific regions such as the southern zone, suggesting the need for context-specific interventions. these findings underscore the importance of integrating social and public health strategies to support stable family structures in tanzania’s evolving socio-economic environment. discover psychology

psychological support in prenatal diagnosis: the parental perspective abstract the communication of a diagnosis of fetal malformation is a very complex event for the parental couple to experience. the aim of the study is to report a planned evaluation of an ongoing psychological support within a prenatal diagnosis clinic, examining the extent to which it represents a source of support service for parental couples. an ad hoc semi-structured questionnaire was administered to couples who had received a prenatal diagnosis of fetal malformation, regardless of whether they had received psychological support. descriptive analyses were performed on quantitative items, while an inductive thematic analysis was applied to open-ended responses to identify recurring themes. the results show that the majority of couples who used the support reported being satisfied with it. the ultrasound examination and specialist consultation were considered by the majority of the participants to be the most appropriate moments to receive the counseling. on the other hand, 41.38% of the couples who did not receive support would have liked to have received it. finally, the majority of the couples, regardless of whether they received psychological support, would recommend that couples in similar situations seek psychological support and that other hospital facilities integrate such services. the results show that among couples who have received psychological support, most reported having benefited from it. in the absence of the psychologist within the multidisciplinary team, however, only a few participants have actively requested it. the findings are discussed in terms of the clinical relevance of psychological support at the time of fetal diagnostic assessments and specialist consultation. journal of clinical psychology in medical settings

association between mental well-being, body composition, and physical activity among adolescents in the eastern cape, south africa background: adolescence is a critical developmental period during which health behaviours are established and may influence physical and mental well-being across the life course. however, evidence on the associations between body composition, physical activity, and mental well-being among south african adolescents remains limited.
aim: the study aimed to determine the association between mental well-being, body composition, and physical activity among adolescents in the eastern cape, south africa.
method: adolescents (= 266, mean age = 15 years, sd = 1.238 years; female = 58.27%) from two districts in the eastern cape were randomly selected to participate in this quantitative cross-sectional study. we collected data through anthropometric measurements, bioelectrical impedance analysis, the international physical activity questionnaire, and the mental health continuum short form. data were analysed using spss version 28. statistical significance was set at< 0.05 with a 95% confidence interval. logistic regression was used to examine the association between metabolic risk and mental well-being, as well as to assess the extent to which body composition components and physical activity predict mental well-being.
results: most participants (65.4%) fell in the normal body mass index (bmi) category. an average of 502.70 minutes (sd = 574.20 minutes) per week of physical activity was displayed by the total sample. body fat percentage emerged as the only statistically significant predictor of mental well-being.
conclusions: although most adolescents exceeded the recommended 300 minutes of physical activity per week, neither physical activity nor bmi predicted mental well-being. instead, body fat percentage was the only significant predictor, indicating that higher body fat was associated with poorer mental well-being. these findings suggest that body composition, rather than overall physical activity levels or bmi alone, plays a critical role in adolescent mental well-being. journal of child and adolescent mental health

school-based digital mental health interventions: a scoping review introduction: globally, the mental health of children and adolescents is a public health concern. schools are a primary access point for youth mental health support, yet traditional delivery models remain constrained by limited resources, shortage of specialised professionals, and high counsellor caseloads. digital mental health interventions may help address these gaps by offering scalable, accessible, and less-stigmatising support.
aim: this review aimed to map and characterise school-based digital mental health interventions for children and adolescents by examining intervention characteristics, implementation, and intervention outcomes.
methods: a comprehensive search of peer-reviewed studies (2008-2025) was conducted across psycnet, eric, and pubmed, using the prisma-scr checklist. eligible studies evaluated a digital mental health intervention delivered in a school setting among k-12 students and reported at least one implementation and/or mental health outcome.
results: across 40 studies, most were conducted in high-income countries and used randomised designs. web-based, structured cognitive behavioural therapy (cbt) modules in classroom settings predominated. intervention delivery ranged from teacher-led to self-directed use, with some hybrid clinician-supported models. findings were heterogeneous for internalising symptoms (e.g., depression and anxiety), with evidence of benefit in some cbt-oriented interventions but mixed effects in universal programmes. in contrast, mental health literacy, stigma, and well-being outcomes showed more consistent positive effects. engagement and implementation quality appeared closely linked to effectiveness.
conclusion: school-based digital mental health interventions can improve mental health literacy and stigma-related outcomes when grounded in cbt. future research should prioritise standardised outcome measurement (e.g., fidelity, adoption), theory-to-component linkages, co-design elements, and hybrid effectiveness-implementation, particularly in low-and middle-income settings. journal of child and adolescent mental health

simplicity, complexity, and the inkblot puzzle abstract: hans zulliger’s three-card inkblot test was created in the 1940s to function as a short-form of rorschach’s inkblot method. despite having been continually published and used, the zulliger has undergone less stringent research than the rorschach. we administered both tests to 101 psychiatric outpatients using the rorschach performance assessment system (r-pas) as the basis for administration and coding, to investigate the zulliger test’s convergent validity and utility of assessment. in this study, we focused on complexity and simplicity, as these constructs represent a fundamental dimension of rorschach data. we conducted a principal component analysis on 13 variables from both tests to compare their underlying structure. to assess linear correspondence and between-method agreement, we analyzed complexity (as standard scores) and f%, along with two study-derived proportion variables: fluency (r/per card) and density (complexity per response). we employed scatterplots with loess smoothing, pearson correlations, t tests, predictive performance metrics, and bland–altman analyses for these four variables. the underlying structure of r-pas and zulliger data showed convergence, confirming our hypothesis that data from the two tests are generated in a comparable manner. further, we found that zulliger provides unbiased measures of complexity, f%, fluency, and density. however, bland–altman analyses revealed wide limits of agreement for complexity and f%, indicating potential limitations in clinical utility at the individual level. predictive performance metrics showed satisfactory specificity and negative predictive values (npv), but sensitivity and positive predictive values (ppv) varied widely and were poor at some thresholds. overall accuracy ranged from 71% to 85%, suggesting moderate to strong agreement between r-pas and zulliger scores. rorschachiana

social markers in the care of intrafamilial child sexual abuse: a socio‐representational approach and its theoretical and methodological implications abstract professionals responding to intrafamilial child sexual abuse (csa) must assess ambiguous situations shaped by emotional tension and social knowledge. this research investigates the socio‐cognitive logic guiding their judgements and intended practices in the french context, where legal and institutional reforms have strengthened expectations for identification and protection of csa. it draws on social representations theory to shed light on how responses are shaped by socio‐symbolic meanings. a two‐step methodology was implemented. study 1 developed a contextualised vignette reflecting the ambiguity in intrafamilial csa disclosures. thirty interviews with the general population were analysed to identify interpretative frameworks activated in evaluation, informing vignette operationalisation and assessment measures. study 2 used this material to examine the influence of victims' social markers (age: 8 vs. 14 years; socioeconomic background: advantaged vs. disadvantaged) on judgements among 380 professionals‐in‐training in healthcare and social work. results showed that these social markers affected severity assessments, responsibility attribution to the minor and alleged perpetrator and decisions regarding protective interventions. findings highlight socio‐representational logic related to age and social class that orient interpretation and decision‐making. this work underscores the need for reflexive training to reduce influences in csa responses and demonstrates the value of contextualised methodological approaches for advancing research and practice. british journal of social psychology

conventional mri markers and cognitive dysfunction in multiple sclerosis: an exploratory pilot study. background: cognitive impairment is a common and disabling manifestation of multiple sclerosis (ms), yet its structural correlates remain incompletely understood in routine clinical practice. although advanced neuroimaging has improved our understanding of the underlying mechanisms, its limited accessibility restricts widespread clinical implementation. we aimed to investigate whether conventional mri markers are associated with domain-specific cognitive impairment in patients with ms.
methods: in this exploratory cross-sectional study, 25 adults with clinically confirmed multiple sclerosis underwent cognitive assessment using the standard persian montreal cognitive assessment (moca), version 7.1, and conventional 1.5-t brain mri. conventional mri measures included lesion burden, lesion topography, and visually rated cortical atrophy. associations between mri markers and moca-derived cognitive domains were assessed using spearman rank correlation with false discovery rate adjustment for multiple testing.
findings: twenty-five patients with clinically confirmed ms completed cognitive and mri assessments. mean age was 42.4 ± 9.1 years, 56% were women, and the mean moca score was 22 ± 7. periventricular (88%) and juxtacortical/cortical (84%) lesions were the most frequent mri findings, total t2/flair lesion burden showed only weak correlations with cognitive performance (ρ range -0.02 to 0.29; all fdr-adjusted p > 0.65). the largest lesion-based association was observed between infratentorial lesions and concentration (ρ = -0.48, unadjusted p = 0.018; fdr-adjusted p = 0.405). among atrophy measures, gca showed the strongest association with visuospatial performance (ρ = 0.51, unadjusted p = 0.012; fdr-adjusted p = 0.405), with additional moderate trends for concentration (ρ = 0.40, p = 0.052) and executive function (ρ = 0.40, p = 0.052). no mri marker remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons.
interpretation: although no mri-cognitive association remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons, several unadjusted associations showed moderate effect sizes and may warrant further investigation. the strongest exploratory associations involved infratentorial lesions and concentration (ρ = -0.48) and global cortical atrophy and visuospatial performance (ρ = 0.51). the absence of consistent relationships between overall lesion burden or individual regional mri markers and cognitive performance suggests that focal structural measures alone may not fully capture the neural substrates of cognitive dysfunction in ms. this pattern provides a rationale for further investigation of distributed, network-level mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction, while the present findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. conventional mri may therefore provide complementary structural information in the clinical assessment of cognitive dysfunction in ms. larger, adequately powered studies using comprehensive neuropsychological assessment and quantitative, network-sensitive mri measures are needed to determine whether these observed patterns are reproducible and clinically meaningful. brain and behavior
