high-stakes bouts and performance under competitive pressure in mixed martial arts abstract: this study examines the impact of competitive pressure on performance in mixed martial arts using ultimate fighting championship data from 2010 to 2021 (3,694 fights; 1,478 fighters). fixed-effects logit models estimate how win probability changes after consecutive losses, controlling for ranking differences, physical characteristics (height, reach, age), and fighter fixed effects. the fighters were more likely to win after prior defeats. the odds of winning were 1.23 times higher after one loss ( p < .01) and 1.46 times higher after two consecutive losses ( p < .01), compared to fighters not on a losing streak. this pattern is consistent with adaptive adjustment under pressure. gender differences emerged in the magnitude of these effects, although the small female subsample limits the generalizability of the gender-specific findings. the results suggest that performance under pressure reflects a combination of psychological, physical, and contextual factors. these findings may have implications for psychological preparation in high-stakes competition. journal of applied sport and exercise psychology-zeitschrift fur sportpsychologie

fear-avoidance responses and return-to-sport duration following injury in elite adolescent field hockey players abstract: this study examined the association between fear-avoidance responses and return-to-sport duration across various injury types in elite adolescent field hockey players. i prospectively monitored elite adolescent athletes following injury, assessed their fear-avoidance using the athletes’ fear avoidance questionnaire (afaq), and recorded the return-to-sport duration. to account for the nested structure of repeated injuries within individual athletes, i used linear mixed-effects models, with injury type, afaq score, age, and sex as fixed effects and athlete identity as a random effect. the results showed significant variation across injury types, with ligament injuries associated with the highest fear-avoidance scores and longest return-to-sport duration. higher fear-avoidance scores were significantly associated with longer return-to-sport duration after accounting for injury type, age, and sex. these findings suggest that fear-avoidance may be an important factor associated with return-to-sport duration, highlighting the potential value of addressing psychological responses during adolescent sports rehabilitation. journal of applied sport and exercise psychology-zeitschrift fur sportpsychologie

the effects of imagery and self-talk on bouldering performance abstract: olympic bouldering combines high physical demands with complex cognitive and psychological requirements, making both physical and psychological performance factors relevant for success. while most studies on bouldering performance have investigated the role of several physiological determinants, research on psychological aspects remains limited. imagery and self-talk (st) are two well-established psychological techniques recommended for optimizing performance in several sports, yet there is limited empirical evidence investigating their effectiveness in bouldering. the aim of this study was to examine the effects of a pettlep imagery intervention and st on bouldering performance, and to determine whether imagery ability moderates the effects of the imagery intervention on performance. in total, 58 experienced climbers ( n = 17 female, m age = 31.47, sd age = 9.26) were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: an imagery condition using pettlep imagery, an st condition practicing motivational and positive st, or a non-treatment control condition (cc). performance was measured by the number of completed moves (bouldering points, bps) and bouldering time (bt) on a kilter board. imagery ability was assessed using the vividness of movement imagery questionnaire-2 (vmiq-2) and mental chronometry. results from a mixed anova revealed that the imagery condition significantly increased bps on the kilter board from the first to the second measurement time, whereas no significant improvements were observed in the st condition or cc. no significant effects were found regarding changes in bt. multiple regression analyses showed that mental chronometry scores predicted improvements in bps after the imagery intervention, and both the mental chronometry and vmiq-2 scores predicted changes in bt. in summary, the findings provide preliminary evidence that pettlep imagery may have the potential to enhance bouldering performance, particularly among climbers with higher imagery ability. journal of applied sport and exercise psychology-zeitschrift fur proaction or procrastination? the double-edged sword effect of perceived overqualification abstract: research has extensively investigated the impacts of perceived overqualification (poq), while few studies have explored the conditions under which these effects may be either beneficial or detrimental. drawing upon cognitive appraisal theory, this study investigates when and how future work self-salience (fwss) shapes employees’ distinct responses to poq. using data from 239 employees across the sichuan and jiangxi provinces in china, we constructed a latent moderated structural model and demonstrated that, for employees with higher fwss, poq fosters proactive career behavior through problem-solving pondering. in contrast, for those with lower fwss, poq leads to work procrastination through affective rumination. both theoretical and practical implications are provided. journal of personnel psychology

from affect to rules: a conceptual model of compensation in prodromal behavioral frontotemporal degeneration. behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvftd) is typically described in terms of progressive loss of social and behavioral control. however, the earliest stages of the disease may also involve active, developed forms of compensation that remain largely invisible to standard assessment. these strategies are rarely characterized, yet they may offer a unique entry point into the mechanisms by which social functioning is temporarily preserved despite emerging degeneration. here, i report a longitudinal single-case study of a young c9orf72 repeat-expansion carrier followed from the prodromal stage to established moderate bvftd. based on more than a dozen hours of semi-structured interviews initiated at symptom emergence, thematic analysis identified five compensatory subthemes. together, these strategies suggested a coherent shift in the architecture of behavioral control that remain largely invisible to standard medical or neuropsychological assessment. as implicit, flexible, and internally sustained regulation became less reliable, functioning appeared to rely on control processes that were more explicit, environmentally distributed, routine-based, and effortful. these observations can be organized around three broader principles: explicitation, externalization, and stabilization. the case suggests that early preservation in bvftd may reflect not only residual capacities, but also an active and fragile reorganization of social and behavioral control. by foregrounding the patient's own compensatory work, this study provides a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework for understanding how everyday functioning may be maintained during the prodromal-to-dementia transition, and highlights qualitative longitudinal single-case designs and participatory research as a powerful tool for identifying hidden forms of adaptation in neurodegenerative disease and refine theoretical models of social behavior. cortex

an english list of personality items with social desirability and observability ratings abstract: desirability and observability are crucial factors that can influence the validity of personality measurement. the current research aims to provide the desirability and observability ratings of close to 800 personality items. we found that the most desirable dimensions were conscientiousness and agreeableness. the least desirable dimensions were extraversion and openness. in terms of observability, extraversion and agreeableness were the most observable dimensions, whereas openness and honesty-humility were the least observable. item length and scale type also influenced the two characteristics, with shorter personality items and scales using adjectives and adverbs as items showing higher desirability and observability. we observed significant variation in desirability across personality scales, with certain scales possibly being more prone to social desirability responding than others. the rating list, with its desirability and observability ratings, can be an invaluable resource for users of personality scales: helping those researchers to select suitable items or scales for specific research needs. finally, we found that developing items with more detailed content and avoiding the use of adjectives and adverbs as personality items may help reduce desirability bias. journal of individual differences

too little, just right, or too much: individuals’ evaluations of their conscientiousness and associated outcome abstract: recent research suggests that a majority (75%) of individuals perceive they have “too much” conscientiousness. although possessing high levels of conscientiousness is commonly associated with desirable outcomes, some theorizing suggests that possessing too much may be undesirable. the current series of preregistered studies seek to replicate prior findings that a majority of individuals report having “too much” conscientiousness (studies 1, 2, and 3) and examine the outcomes – desirable and undesirable – associated with possessing “too much” conscientiousness (studies 2 and 3). counter to expectations, results revealed that, across all three studies, a majority of participants (75% study 1; 68.9% study 2; 70.8% study 3) perceived their conscientiousness levels as “just right”; whereas, a much smaller percentage perceived their conscientiousness levels as “too much” (9% study 1; 19.1% study 2; 22.1% study 3). perceiving “too much” conscientiousness yielded consistently positive outcomes, including less anxiety, less burnout, more grit, and more academic or career success (studies 2 and 3). implications and directions for future research are described. journal of individual differences

personality traits and hormonal correlates in women undergoing ivf treatment abstract: this study examined the associations between alternative five-factor model (affm) personality traits and hormonal indicators in women undergoing in vitro fertilization (ivf), and compared personality profiles between women with female-factor infertility and those in male-factor infertility couples. the sample consisted of 76 women assessed using the zuckerman–kuhlman–aluja personality questionnaire (zka-pq). hormonal data (lh, fsh, prolactin, tsh, ft4, estradiol, and progesterone) were obtained from routine clinical analyses. correlation analyses revealed selective and modest associations between personality traits and hormonal levels. estradiol showed the most consistent pattern, being positively associated with sensation seeking, neuroticism, activity, and aggression. progesterone was primarily related to activity and aggression, whereas tsh and fsh were negatively associated with extraversion. other hormones showed limited or domain-specific associations. facet-level analyses indicated that these relationships were more differentiated at lower levels of personality structure. group comparisons indicated that women in male-factor infertility couples reported higher levels of neuroticism, particularly anxiety and low self-esteem, compared to women with female-factor infertility, while no differences were observed for other traits. overall, findings support the view that hormone–personality relationships are indirect, modest, and most evident for biologically proximal traits. the results highlight the value of integrating biologically grounded personality models in reproductive health research and underscore the importance of considering both endocrine and psychosocial factors in understanding infertility. journal of individual differences

weaponizing the bond: pet abuse as a mediator of ipv victimization and mental health symptomology. the purpose of the current study was to understand how the perpetration of pet abuse (i.e., dog and cat), in the context of intimate partner violence (ipv), contributes to victims' mental health outcomes. we were specifically interested in examining 1) the relationship between a partner's pet abuse perpetration and depression, anxiety, and ptsd and 2) how pet abuse might mediate the relationship between ipv victimization and mental health outcomes.participants (= 1,173) were recruited online via testset and responded to items related to ipv victimization, their partner's maltreatment of dogs or cats, and current mental health symptomology. separate path models estimated the direct and indirect effects of physical, psychological, and sexual ipv victimization on depression, anxiety, and ptsd symptoms, with a partner's cat and dog abuse specified as mediators.psychological ipv victimization and pet abuse consistently emerged as the strongest direct predictors of mental health symptomology across all models. dog and cat abuse significantly mediated the relationships between physical and sexual ipv, but not psychological ipv, on victims' depressive, anxiety, and ptsd symptoms.pet abuse is a significant risk marker for ipv and psychological distress. pet abuse warrants both legal recognition as a form of domestic violence and clinical recognition as a distinct source of trauma. psychosocial intervention

prevalence and perpetration contexts of sexual violence among cisgender lgbq+ adults in australia this article analyses the lifetime and 12-month prevalence of sexual violence victimisation in a sample of 5,267 cisgender lesbian, gay, bi/pansexual, queer or other non-heterosexual participants in australia. the study explores three research questions in relation to cisgender lgbq+ respondents: (1) the prevalence of sexual violence among respondents and differences by gender and sexuality; (2) the gender of perpetrators of sexual violence against respondents and variations by respondent gender and sexuality; and (3) the relationship contexts in which sexual violence occurred for respondents and differences by gender and sexuality. data was collected from a cross-sectional, australia-wide online survey of lgbtq+ health and well-being. the findings demonstrate significant disparities in sexual assault experiences across gender and sexual identity groups, with queer and plurisexual individuals reporting the highest rates. we also identify distinct patterns in perpetrator gender and relationship contexts, emphasising the importance of disaggregating data by gender and sexual identity. we find that the gendered dimensions of sexual violence are co-constituted by sexual identity and relational contexts for cisgender lgbq+ participants. these findings underscore the need for tailored research, policy responses and support services that address the needs and experiences of diverse lgbq+ groups, moving beyond homogeneous assumptions about sexual violence in lgbq+ communities. journal of gender-based violence

reframing informal disclosures of sexual violence as ‘an ongoing conversation’: how victim-survivors discuss victimisation with friends, family and partners sexual violence (sv) is more likely to be disclosed to friends, family members and partner(s) (ons, 2021), though less is known regarding these informal disclosure experiences compared to formal disclosures (for example, to the police). this victim-survivor-led study explored the ways in which victim-survivors of sv disclosed and discussed victimisation with friends, family and partners. semi-structured interviews were carried out with 31 victim-survivors of child sexual abuse, sexual assault and rape in the uk, demonstrating the gradual nature of disclosure. the findings highlight the various ways in which victim-survivors make others aware of their experiences, including: disclosing as memories emerge, disclosing as awareness emerges, disclosing multiple aspects of victimisation, disclosure gradually becoming limited, partially disclosing, attempting to disclose, and enlisting the support of others to disclose to specific people. in addition to disclosing victimisation experiences, victim-survivors also discuss the impact of victimisation, including the ways in which they were responded to by others. various factors influence the way in which victim-survivors disclose, including victim-survivor identities, victimisation experiences, acknowledgement status, previous responses and feared responses. the findings indicate that informal disclosure is a complex and ever-shifting process through which victim-survivors attempt to speak about victimisation and impact(s) via numerous conversations with multiple people, potentially over the life course. journal of gender-based violence

depressive and anxiety symptoms associated with icu admission in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a prospective cohort study. background: hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (hdp) are a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in latin america. depression and anxiety are frequent during pregnancy and may influence hdp severity, yet their impact on clinical outcomes remains unclear.
objective: to determine whether depressive and anxiety symptoms are associated with obstetric intensive care unit (icu) admission and hospital length of stay among women with hdp.
methods: a prospective cohort study was conducted at a colombian tertiary-care referral hospital (july 2024-january 2025). women aged ≥16 years in their third trimester hospitalized for hdp completed the edinburgh postnatal depression scale (epds) and generalized anxiety disorder-7 (gad-7). multivariable firth penalized logistic regression and cox regression models assessed associations with icu admission and length of stay results: among 234 participants (median age 25 years), 61.1% required icu care; only 14 of the 143 icu patients (9.8%) were assessed before icu transfer. an epds score ≥10 or a positive response to item 10 was independently associated with icu admission (or 4.83 , 95% ci 1.56 -14.94, p=0.006) and longer hospitalization (hr 0.69 , 95% ci 0.48 -1.00, p=0.048). in an exploratory finding, a gad-7 score ≥10 showed an inverse association with icu admission (or 0.29, 95% ci 0.09-0.88, p=0.029). hemoglobin <11 g/dl and a post hoc mean arterial pressure threshold ≥102.5 mmhg were also significantly associated with icu admission.
conclusions: depressive symptoms were associated with obstetric icu admission and prolonged hospitalization in patients admitted for hdp, whereas anxiety appeared protective, which seems counterintuitive and requires future research to confirm its association; however, because most assessments took place after icu transfer, causality could not be established. integrating mental health screening into hdp management may improve maternal outcomes. journal of the academy of consultation-liaison psychiatry

suicide ideation and lgbtq+ felt sense of belongingness and internalized shame: an investigation through the lens of the integrated motivational volitional model of suicide in lgbtq+ adults in the u.s. and the u.k. introduction: lgbtq+ populations experience elevated suicide risk, yet the psychosocial mechanisms contributing to this disparity remain understudied. drawing on the integrated motivational-volitional (imv) model of suicide and stigma-based health disparities frameworks, we tested whether defeat relates to suicidal ideation (si) indirectly through internal and external entrapment, and whether lgbtq+-related shame and belongingness moderate these pathways. methods: lgbtq+ adults from the united kingdom (n = 302; 76% female, 69% cisgender) and the united states (n = 469; 62% female, 75% cisgender) completed an online cross-sectional survey. results: in the u.k. sample, defeat was indirectly associated with si through both internal and external entrapment, consistent with imv predictions. in the u.s. sample, defeat predicted si via internal, but not external, entrapment, and lgbtq+ shame moderated the defeat to internal entrapment association. discussion: these findings highlight entrapment as a key psychological mechanism linking minority stress to suicidal ideation in lgbtq+ adults and suggest potential cross-national variability in how shame processes contribute to suicide risk. implications for theory refinement and clinical assessment of entrapment in stigmatized populations are discussed. journal of social and clinical psychology

interpersonal processes in daily life: within-person dynamics of experiential avoidance, responsiveness, vulnerability, and momentary loneliness introduction: loneliness is increasingly recognized as a critical public health concern, yet its moment-to-moment determinants remain poorly understood. from a contextual behavioral perspective, loneliness may emerge as a downstream consequence of patterns of interpersonal behavior shaped by experiential avoidance and disrupted intimacy processes. methods: the present study examined a contextual behavioral science-based model of loneliness grounded in the interpersonal process model of intimacy using ecological momentary assessment. participants (n = 31) completed surveys (n = 1201) three times daily for up to 14 days assessing experiential avoidance, interpersonal processes (vulnerability and responsiveness), perceived connection, loneliness, and mental health. results: results indicated that both the quantity and quality of social interactions were associated with momentary loneliness, with perceived connection demonstrating a stronger association than interaction frequency. momentary feelings of connection were predicted best by provided and experienced responsiveness rather than expressed or received vulnerability. efforts to control emotions, conceptualized as experiential avoidance, were not associated with the number of social interactions but was indirectly associated with connection through increased vulnerability, suggesting its role in shaping the quality rather than quantity of interpersonal engagement. although strong concurrent associations were observed across variables, lagged effects were largely nonsignificant, indicating that these processes may operate primarily at a momentary level. in contrast, mental health predicted subsequent loneliness, whereas loneliness did not predict later mental health. discussion: results highlight the importance of targeting interpersonal processes and psychological flexibility to reduce loneliness and suggest that loneliness may be best understood as a dynamic, context-dependent process unfolding in daily life. journal of social and clinical psychology

how and why?: perceptions of people with terminal illnesses’ suicides as a function of suicide method and motive introduction: we quantitatively assessed how third-person perceptions of people with terminal illnesses’ suicides vary as a function of situational factors related to the suicide as well as participants’ individual differences. method: vignettes were used in between-groups designs to manipulate a target person’s suicide method (study 1) and primary motive (study 2). results: on average, participants reported generally favorable attitudes toward this phenomenon across studies. in study 1, medical methods (e.g., physician-assisted death) were perceived more favorably than traditional methods (e.g., hanging), but minimal differences in perceptions emerged across various suicide motives (e.g., mental health concerns, wanting control over death) in study 2. masculine honor beliefs were positively associated with stigmatizing attitudes toward the target. self-directed and other-directed fear of death yielded contradictory effects. suicide acceptability was consistently positively associated with favorable attitudes toward this phenomenon. discussion: overall, this program of research has important implications for understanding nuances in third-person perceptions of this phenomenon as a function of relevant situational factors (e.g., method, motive) and individual differences, while advancing suicide theories to be more comprehensive and inclusive of physical health. journal of social and clinical psychology

emotion regulation and mental distress following a romantic breakup introduction: romantic breakups are common, yet for some individuals they pose a serious threat to their mental health. this two-wave prospective study examined how specific emotion regulation (er) strategies and the balance between maladaptive and all er strategies (the maladaptive er ratio) relate to post-breakup mental distress. methods: adults (n = 95) with lovesickness, who had experienced a breakup within the past 3 months completed online questionnaires at study intake (t1) and 3 months later (t2). er was assessed at t1 with two instruments. post-breakup mental distress index (pmdi) composite scores were formed, summarizing breakup distress, lovesickness, and general psychopathology at t1 and t2. results: cross-sectional analyses indicated that rumination, catastrophizing, and experience suppression were associated with higher pmdi, whereas acceptance predicted lower pmdi. prospectively, rumination, catastrophizing, and putting into perspective predicted higher pmdi at follow-up. maladaptive er ratios predicted pmdi at t1, whereas only the hferst maladaptive er ratio predicted pmdi at t2 beyond baseline pmdi. discussion: findings highlight the beneficial concurrent association with acceptance and the detrimental short- and long-term influence of rumination and catastrophizing. the context-specific nature of er was highlighted, as the putatively adaptive strategy of putting into perspective predicted higher distress at follow-up. a greater relative predominance of maladaptive strategies within the er repertoire was strongly associated with concurrent post-breakup distress, while its prospective relevance differed between the two measures. reducing rumination and catastrophizing while fostering a more balanced er repertoire may facilitate post-separation adjustment. journal of social and clinical psychology

longitudinal effects of parental drinking problems and depression on adolescent social adjustment: mediating roles of constructive and destructive marital conflict, emotional security, and parental psychological control abstract this study investigates how parental depressive symptoms and drinking problems during early adolescence are linked to adolescents' social adjustment through family‐level mechanisms, including marital conflict, psychological control through guilt, and emotional insecurity. drawing on emotional security theory and a three‐wave longitudinal design, data were collected from 281 families beginning when adolescents were in seventh grade and followed annually over 3 years. structural equation modeling revealed that parental depressive symptoms and drinking problems at time 1 predicted increased destructive conflict and decreased constructive conflict at time 2. these distinct forms of conflict were, in turn, associated with parenting and emotional processes: destructive conflict was positively associated with adolescents' emotional insecurity and psychological control through guilt, whereas constructive conflict was negatively associated with psychological control through guilt. emotional insecurity and psychological control through guilt significantly mediated the associations between marital conflict and adolescent social maladjustment at time 3, after accounting for baseline maladjustment. these results illuminate both family risk and protective factors of early adolescent social adjustment, informing preventive programs of potential underlying mechanisms likely to be intervened upon. by identifying differences between constructive and destructive conflict, this research also constitutes an effort to understand parental adjustment's role in adolescent social outcomes through family dynamics. family process

intrinsic rewards guide visual resource allocation via reinforcement learning abstract humans and other animals prioritize visual processing of stimuli that signal rewards. while previous research has focused on tangible incentives (for example, money or food), the effects of intrinsic incentives—such as perceived competence—are less well understood. here, across a series of visual estimation experiments, we manipulated observers’ subjective sense of confidence in their judgements using either deceptive trial-by-trial feedback or real discrepancies in stimulus reliability. we found that observers prioritized encoding of stimuli associated with lower uncertainty or error, benefiting performance for stimuli already estimated accurately, while further impairing performance for those estimated poorly. these reward-driven biases, while potentially adaptive, impaired overall accuracy in the present tasks by causing resource allocation to deviate from the error-minimizing strategy. to account for these findings, we supplemented a normalization model of neural resource allocation with a simple reinforcement learning rule. intrinsic and external rewards cumulatively shaped the values assigned to different stimuli by the model, and the resulting discrepancies biased resource allocation and thereby estimation error, quantitatively matching the data. these findings reveal how intrinsic reward signals can shape resource allocation in ways that are both adaptive and counterproductive, offering a computational basis for the motivational biases underlying cognitive performance. nature human behaviour

selfish and prosocial individuals both distort their actions’ impact, but selfish distortions can be more contagious abstract people often act without knowing exactly how their actions impact others. here, across nine preregistered online experiments ( n = 8,769 adults, predominantly us residents), we tested whether people exploit this ambiguity to make themselves look good. on average, selfish individuals inflated the social benefit of their choice while downplaying that of the alternative, reporting the two options as more similar than prosocial individuals did (experiment 1a: b = 0.24, 95% confidence interval 0.14–0.34). prosocial individuals portrayed their choice as comparatively more socially beneficial; they also inflated their implied relative sacrifice, although less consistently. we observed distortions even before people made a choice and when choices were forced, consistent with distortions reflecting social preferences rather than mere justification. while people differed in whether and how they distorted, distortions favouring selfishness showed evidence of contagion: others adopted them and became more selfish (experiment 6, selfish-serving versus no-distortion: b = 0.49, 95% confidence interval 0.10–0.88). these findings offer a psychological foundation for why polarized positions about the social impact of one’s actions may emerge. when social consequences are open to interpretation, people may predictably form divergent interpretations. nature human behaviour

the reference frame of the flashed-face distortion effect the flashed face distortion effect (ffde) is a visual illusion in which faces presented rapidly in the visual periphery appear grotesquely distorted. previous studies have suggested that the ffde may involve higher-level mechanisms of face perception that integrate information across temporally and spatially adjacent stimuli. however, the effect may also arise from lower-level visual processes, such as encoding local edges or orientations. to provide further insight, the present study examined whether the ffde is represented in retinotopic or spatiotopic coordinates, which are often associated with different stages of visual processing. participants made a saccadic eye movement during the sequential presentation of face stimuli. across the saccade, faces were presented either at the same retinal location (retinotopic coordinates) or at the same screen location (spatiotopic coordinates). the subjective strength of the ffde for postsaccadic faces was measured using a seven-point rating scale. the results showed that the ffde was pronounced in retinotopic coordinates but was substantially reduced in spatiotopic coordinates. these findings suggest that the ffde is primarily mediated by relatively low-level visual processing mechanisms, similar to classical visual aftereffects. perception

empirische arbeit: systematisierung von transferprozessen im schulischen kontext: ein integratives transferprozessmodell im rahmen von transferprozessen sollen innovationen im schulischen kontext initiiert, umgesetzt sowie verbreitet und somit veränderungen bzw. verbesserungen herbeigeführt werden. dabei bleiben die verortung einzelner aktivitäten im gesamtprozess und die interaktionen der relevanten akteur:innen aus bildungsforschung, -praxis, -administration und -politik jedoch häufig unspezifisch. der vorliegende beitrag systematisiert daher anhand eines integrativen transferprozessmodells zum einen vier miteinander verzahnte transferphasen – entwicklung und initiierung, implementation, scaling-up sowie reflexion. zum anderen integriert das modell die hauptsächlich in den jeweiligen transferphasen anzutreffenden forschungstypen – anwendungsorientierte grundlagen- und entwicklungsforschung, implementations-, scaling-up- und synoptische forschung – in einem gemeinsamen heuristischen rahmen. das modell soll eine systematisierung liefern, anhand dessen transferaktivitäten verortet, verknüpft und geplant werden können. außerdem soll das modell transparenz über die phasenabhängigen uni-, bi- oder multidirektionalen interaktionsmöglichkeiten mit den relevanten akteur:innen schaffen. anhand des integrativen transferprozessmodells werden methodische zugänge, empirische beispiele sowie zentrale herausforderungen von transferprozessen diskutiert. psychologie in erziehung und unterricht

empirische arbeit: versuch einer synoptischen evaluation: transferprozess eines programms zur schulentwicklung transferprozesse im kontext von schule sind so gewünscht wie herausfordernd. pant und kolleg:innen (2026) haben ein integratives transferprozessmodell vorgestellt, das es ermöglicht, innovationen im schulischen kontext forschungs- bzw. evidenzbasiert zu planen, umzusetzen und zu skalieren, wobei die relevanten stakeholder berücksichtigt werden. zugleich wird der transferprozess selbst als forschungsgegenstand verstanden. der vorliegende beitrag illustriert dieses modell anhand des transferprozesses einer beispielhaften programmlinie zur schulentwicklung beginnend mit impakt schulleitung über das perspektivschul-programm, s4 – schule stärken, starke schule und ganztagsschule gemeinsam gestalten bis hin zum kontext von startchancen. dabei werden die entwicklungs- und initiierungsphase sowie die implementationsphase, aber auch die scaling-up-phase nachgezeichnet. abschließend wird beispielhaft eine synoptische evaluation skizziert, die den gesamten transferprozess nochmals zusammenfassend reflektiert und evaluiert. psychologie in erziehung und unterricht

stichwort: systemische transformation im bildungssystem der beitrag geht von der grundlegenden these aus, dass die aktuellen anforderungen an das bildungssystem nicht durch vereinzelte reformen, sondern nur durch eine systemische transformation bewältigt werden können. diese wird vor dem hintergrund des bestehenden steuerungsgefüges im bildungssystem diskutiert, das durch ein komplexes mehrebenensystem mit unterschiedlichen institutionellen logiken, zuständigkeiten und professionellen orientierungen geprägt ist. systemische transformation wird als ko-konstruktiver und langfristiger entwicklungsprozess konzipiert, der die koordinierte zusammenarbeit von bildungspolitik, bildungsverwaltung, bildungsforschung und bildungspraxis voraussetzt und auf die entwicklung gemeinsamer handlungsfähigkeit im bildungssystem zielt. im mittelpunkt stehen spannungsfelder zwischen den akteursgruppen, anforderungen an kohärente governance sowie die bedeutung von systementwicklungskapazität als voraussetzung gemeinsamer verantwortungsübernahme und abgestimmten handelns. abschließend wird herausgearbeitet, dass nachhaltige transformation nur durch geteilte verantwortung, gemeinsames lernen, professionelle brückenarbeit und die entwicklung neuer kooperations- und steuerungsformen gelingen kann. psychologie in erziehung und unterricht

hot topic: professionelles und institutionelles lernen sichtbar machen: chancen für transferforschung im startchancen-programm lernziele und lernfortschritte prozessbezogen sichtbar zu machen, ist der empirisch nachweislich wirksame kern diagnosegeleiteter förderung für fachliches lernen von kindern und jugendlichen. im startchancen-programm wird er unterstützt durch lernprozessbegleitende checks und fördermaterialien zu basiskompetenzen für lehrkräfte und lernende. die digitale erfassung der checks ermöglicht zugleich auch forschenden, aus vielen schulen gleichzeitig typische verläufe, gelingensbedingungen und wirkungen der fachlichen lernprozesse empirisch zu identifizieren. datengestützte unterrichtsentwicklung umfasst darüber hinaus zwei weitere ebenen: das professionelle lernen von lehrkräften und das institutionelle lernen von schulen. der kurzbeitrag skizziert, wie im startchancen-programm beides sichtbar gemacht wird und welche prozess-einsichten dadurch für transferforschung über professionelle und institutionelle lernprozesse ermöglicht werden. psychologie in erziehung und unterricht

editorial: transfer im schulischen kontext: interaktion von forschung, politik und praxis die frage, wie wissenschaftliche erkenntnisse zur verbesserung von bildungsprozessen beitragen können, hat in den vergangenen jahren zunehmend an bedeutung gewonnen. angesichts aktueller herausforderungen des bildungssystems – von der förderung grundlegender fachlicher und digitaler kompetenzen lernender bis zu fragen der bildungsgerechtigkeit in einer sich stets wandelnden gesellschaft – wird verstärkt diskutiert, wie bildungsforschung, -praxis, -politik und -administration nachhaltig zusammenwirken können. dabei wird deutlich, dass der transfer wissenschaftlicher erkenntnisse nicht als linearer prozess verstanden werden kann, in dem in der forschung wissen produziert wird, das in der praxis umgesetzt wird. vielmehr erfordert ein erfolgreicher transfer von fundierten wissenschaftlichen erkenntnissen die vertrauensvolle zusammenarbeit unterschiedlicher stakeholder, die gemeinsame ziele aushandeln, an die grenzen ihres jeweiligen wissens gelangen und gemeinsam neues wissen generieren, um so transferprozesse im schulischen kontext effektiv zu gestalten. psychologie in erziehung und unterricht

empirische arbeit: from knowledge transfer to learning by expanding together: creating new hybrid forms of activity through research-practice partnerships across the globe, the influence of education research on policy and practice is limited by the fragility of connections among researchers, policy makers, and educators. research-practice partnerships are a relational and systemic approach to promoting knowledge transfer that can support mutual learning across boundaries, though the approach differs from traditional, linear approaches to dissemination. this paper explores how one partnership’s activities supported a large school district’s process for adopting instructional materials in a way that integrated ideas and findings from research related to science teaching and learning. the paper explores how boundary crossing through boundary spanners, boundary practices, and artifacts supported the hybridization process. the analysis illustrates and helps theorize how successful knowledge transfer in research-practice partnerships entails transformation of activities through hybridization, rather than direct transfer of intact research-based practices into new settings. psychologie in erziehung und unterricht

toward a post‐jungian cosmopsychism: entropy, information, and the inhibitory dynamics of consciousness abstract this paper advances a model of the psyche as a thermodynamic–informational organism that modulates entropy to let symbolic life emerge and evolve. building on jungian metapsychology, complexity theory, and contemporary predictive‐processing and oscillation neuroscience, i introduce the acceleration–expansion–gravity (aeg) model of psychic dynamics. acceleration marks entropy spikes and archetypal flooding, expansion the elaboration of symbolic complexity, and gravity the integrative forces that restore coherence. central to these rhythms is the “inhibitory membrane” of consciousness: an explicitly metaphorical construct with physiological anchors, instantiated by oscillatory brain dynamics that regulate the permeability between unconscious potentials and conscious awareness. the model illuminates clinical phenomena such as trauma, psychosis, creativity, and individuation as recurrent cycles of entropy modulation. framing psyche and cosmos alike as self‐organizing, entropy‐regulating systems, this post‐jungian cosmopsychism offers both a clinical map of transformation and a cosmological vision of how meaning coheres at the edge of chaos. journal of analytical psychology

transitioning to the business of a session in collaborative-dialogic meetings: a conversation analysis abstract psychotherapy meetings contain a transition from the opening phase of greetings/small-talk to the official business. we examine how this transition is managed by therapists and families following a collaborative-dialogic approach to family therapy. using conversation analysis, we analysed the openings of 10 meetings from a public child and youth mental health service in western sydney, australia. therapists introduced the official business of the session using a turn characterised by pauses, re-starts, self-repairs, and a question form of “what would be useful/important to talk about?” in response, there was a lack of uptake from families as they negotiated both the topic and who would speak. therapists responded by proposing topics that families could either accept or decline or by nominating the next speaker though gaze, thereby prompting that person to speak. while promoting family discussions about topics may have therapeutic utility though transferring responsibility from therapist to family, a more active speaker nomination by the therapist may minimise disruption and transition more quickly to therapeutic topics. contemporary family therapy

digital co-regulation and dysregulation in romantic relationships: a systemic model of technology-mediated emotional processes abstract technology has become an integral context through which romantic relationships are initiated, maintained, and experienced globally. while prior research has emphasized communication and connection, less attention has been given to how technology functions as a mechanism of emotional regulation within relationships. in the current qualitative study, we examined how individuals use technology to navigate relational processes across cultural contexts. semi-structured interviews were conducted with 31 participants and analyzed using the constant comparative method, an iterative process in which data are coded and continuously compared within and across interviews to identify and refine emergent themes. findings revealed expected patterns in the use of technology during relationship initiation and termination, but also an emergent pattern highlighted the role of technology in processes of digital co-regulation and dysregulation. these findings suggest that technology operates as an embedded regulatory mechanism within romantic systems. implications are discussed for systemic theory, cross-cultural research, and clinical practice. contemporary family therapy

the revised american psychological association guidelines for clinical supervision: rationale, revisions, and implications for practice and scholarship. clinical supervision is foundational to the training of psychologists and protection of public welfare, yet concerns about its quality have persisted across decades of psychotherapy scholarship and practice. the american psychological association (2014, 2015) guidelines for clinical supervision in health service psychology provided the first comprehensive, competency-based framework for supervision practice in psychology. after a decade of its adoption, supervision research has advanced, and important additions to the original guidelines were introduced in 2025 to address these developments. this article describes the rationale for these revisions and articulates the changes across its six domains: supervisor competence (domain a), multicultural orientation (domain b), supervisory relationship (domain c), teaching and learning strategies (domain d), professional competence problems (domain e), and ethical, legal, and regulatory considerations (domain f). revisions include the introduction of group supervision as a distinct supervisory competency, reframing of diversity competence as multicultural orientation, an expanded emphasis on the pedagogy of supervision, and new guidance on attending to the intersection of supervisee identities and professional competence concerns. implications for practice, training, and future research are discussed. brain structure correlates of circulating endocannabinoids and related lipids in early adolescents abstract the endocannabinoid (ecb) system underlies many biological processes and is thought to be critical in adolescent brain development. however, the ecb system’s contributions to brain morphometry during adolescence remains understudied. here we investigated cross-sectional associations between brain structure and circulating ecbs and related lipids in a subsample of adolescents ( n = 294, ages 10–14, 44.5% female, 65.3% white) from the adolescent brain and cognitive development (abcd) study utilizing a structural equation modeling approach. after accounting for sex and age, significant covariance between circulating ecbs and related lipids and cortical thickness, surface area, and volume in brain regions throughout the cortex were revealed. while the mechanisms underlying these associations need further research, these results suggest that the ecb system likely plays a critical role in early-adolescent brain development. future work should determine underlying mechanisms, evaluate these associations longitudinally, and consider sex differences and the modulatory effects of pubertal hormones. development and psychopathology

mediating role of emotion regulation and sibling relationship quality among young adult siblings of individuals with and without autism spectrum disorder abstract purpose siblings of autistic individuals (asd-sibs) report, on average, significantly less closeness and warmth in sibling relationships than siblings of non-disabled individuals (nd-sibs). however, findings on other aspects of life satisfaction on well-being between asd-sibs and nd-sibs is more mixed. therefore, understanding some potential mechanisms by which aspects of the sibling relationship relate to well-being for asd-sibs and nd-sibs is needed. in particular, understanding how aspects of emotion regulation may relate to the sibling relationship may provide pathways for future support strategies. methods the current study compared 42 non-disabled young adult siblings of autistic individuals to 145 non-disabled young adult siblings of non-disabled individuals. participants completed an online survey with measures of sibling warmth and closeness, emotional reappraisal and emotional suppression, gratitude, life satisfaction, distress, and optimism. moderated mediation analysis examined whether pathways amongst variables differed between asd-sibs and nd-sibs. results the asd-sibs reported significantly lower levels of warmth and closeness and significantly higher levels of distress. asd-sibs also reported greater use of emotional suppression. both emotional suppression and reappraisal partially mediated the relationships between the sibling relationship and well-being variables, though such relationships did not significantly differ by group. conclusion the current results indicate that strategies of emotional regulation may impact the relationship between sibling closeness/warmth and well-being among asd-sibs. more research is needed to determine how changes in emotional regulation may help improve both the relationship and well-being. journal of autism and developmental disorders

national prevalence and sociodemographic correlates of potential depression, anxiety, and suicidality among the young population in kazakhstan: a national population-based study. background: mental health disorders are the primary driver of the global disease burden among young people, yet nationally representative data for central asia remains scarce. this study aimed to determine the prevalence and sociodemographic correlates of potential depression, anxiety, and suicidality among the young population in the central asian nation of kazakhstan.
methods: a cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the 2024 kazakhstan multiple indicator cluster survey (mics), a nationally representative, multi-stage probability sample. potential depression and anxiety were screened using the phq-2 and gad-2 instruments (cut-off ≥ 3), while suicidality was assessed via self-reported thoughts (past two weeks) or attempts (past 12 months). weighted prevalence estimates were calculated, and modified poisson regression models identified independent sociodemographic risk factors. population attributable fractions (pafs) were estimated to quantify the impact of associated risks.
findings: we included 5,079 individuals aged 15-24 years. the weighted national prevalence was 1.70% (95%ci = 1.31-2.08) for potential depression, 1.59% (95%ci = 1.23-1.96) for potential anxiety, and 0.96% (95%ci = 0.65-1.27) for potential suicidality among the population aged 15-24 years. in adjusted analyses, female sex was the strongest predictor of both potential depression (adjusted risk ratio [arr] = 2.72, 95%ci = 1.55-4.79) and anxiety (arr = 2.80, 95%ci = 1.58-4.96). non-kazakh ethnicity was also significantly associated with an increased risk of depression (arr = 1.88, 95%ci = 1.17-3.02) and anxiety (arr = 1.99, 95%ci = 1.28-3.11). pafs indicated that female sex accounted for 45.6% and 46.8% of the risk for depression and anxiety, respectively. no significant sociodemographic correlates were identified for suicidality.
conclusion: these findings provide the first nationally representative benchmarks for youth mental health in kazakhstan. while prevalence rates are lower than global averages, the marked disparities by sex and ethnicity highlight the need for targeted, culturally sensitive mental health interventions. strengthening early detection and resource allocation for these vulnerable subgroups is essential to meet national and sustainable development goal targets. bmc psychology

the role of rumination and planning in climate anxiety, worry, and pro-environmental behaviour among young adults: evidence from two studies abstract background climate anxiety is a common psychological response to climate change among young people. although cognitive emotion regulation (cer) strategies are thought to shape how individuals cope with climate-related distress, their associations with climate anxiety and pro-environmental behaviour remain insufficiently understood. employing a sequential two-study design, the present study examined the role of selected cer strategies and evaluated brief interventions aimed at targeting them. methods two studies were conducted among slovenian young adults. study 1 used a cross-sectional design ( n = 442; 18–24 years; 75.8% female) to examine associations between rumination, catastrophising, positive refocusing, refocus on planning, climate anxiety, and pro-environmental behaviour. study 2 was a randomised controlled trial ( n = 89; 18–24 years; 92.1% female) comparing expressive writing, expressive writing plus planning, and a control condition. climate anxiety, climate worry, pro-environmental behaviour (or pro-environmental behavioural intentions), rumination, and planning were assessed across repeated measurements. results in study 1, rumination emerged as the strongest correlate of climate anxiety, while refocus on planning was the strongest correlate of pro-environmental behaviour. in study 2, neither intervention led to significant changes in rumination and refocus on planning, reduced climate anxiety or climate worry, nor increased pro-environmental behaviour (or pro-environmental behavioural intentions). however, both interventions produced short-term increases in climate worry immediately after the exercises. exploratory analyses indicated that increases in rumination, across all conditions, were associated with increases in climate anxiety and climate worry over time. conclusions the findings suggest that cer strategies show nuanced associations with climate-related outcomes. rumination appears to be a consistent correlate of climate distress, while planning may accompany both climate concern and pro-environmental engagement. brief self-guided interventions were insufficient to produce meaningful changes in these outcomes. bmc psychology

the mediating role of alexithymia in the relationship between family belonging and psychological resilience in english language teaching students abstract this study examined the associations among family belonging, alexithymia, and psychological resilience and the statistical mediating role of alexithymia among english language teaching (elt) students. a sequential mixed-methods design was employed. quantitative data were collected from 177 elt students and analyzed using structural equation modeling (sem). for the qualitative strand, 30 volunteers were randomly selected from the quantitative sample and interviewed using a semi-structured protocol; the data were analyzed through qualitative content analysis. the structural model demonstrated an overall acceptable fit ( χ² /df = 2.17, rmsea = 0.082, srmr = 0.055, cfi = 0.98, gfi = 0.94). family belonging was positively associated with psychological resilience and negatively associated with alexithymia, while alexithymia was negatively associated with psychological resilience. the direct association between family belonging and psychological resilience was not statistically significant after alexithymia was included in the model ( β = −0.03, p > .05). a supplementary bootstrap analysis with 5,000 resamples showed a statistically significant indirect association through alexithymia ( b = 0.096, bootse = 0.019, 95% ci [0.061, 0.136]). the qualitative findings complemented these results by contextualizing participants’ experiences of family belonging, emotional awareness and expression, and coping and recovery. overall, the findings provide context-specific insight into the interrelationships among these constructs among elt students and may be particularly relevant to university students in similar educational and cultural contexts. given the cross-sectional design, the indirect association should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal or temporal mechanism. bmc psychology

associations among affective valence, intrusive thoughts, and prospective memory abstract prospective memory (pm), the ability to remember to carry out intended actions, is influenced by cognitive and emotional factors. this study investigated how changes in affect influence pm by experimentally manipulating mood (negative, neutral, and positive) in young and older adults using a within-subject design. valence was assessed at baseline (t1), post-induction (t2), and post-task (t3), producing indices of induction-related (t2-t1) and task-related affective change (t3-t2). pm performance improved with more positive affect and declined with more negative affect. perceived control over intrusive thoughts significantly predicted pm. in an associational indirect-effect analysis, post-induction and post-task affect change were each indirectly associated with pm performance through perceived control over intrusive thoughts. these effects were consistent across age group. findings support capacity-based accounts, suggesting that negative affective states increase distraction via intrusive, task-unrelated thoughts, impairing pm. positive affect may enhance pm through performance-related affective processes. by examining when and how affective valence is associated with pm, this study provides a nuanced account of affect–pm coupling and highlights the role of intrusive thoughts. motivation and emotion

using features of dynamic networks to guide treatment selection and outcome prediction: the central role of uncertainty. 利用动态网络特征指导治疗选择与结果预测：不确定性的核心作用 multivariate time-series models are commonly used in psychology to investigate person-specific associations between multiple variables. they are often represented and interpreted as dynamic network models, where features such as the centrality of nodes can potentially guide treatment selection and outcome prediction. researchers typically rely on point estimates of specific network features while ignoring estimation uncertainty, which can lead to wrong inferences and overoptimistic claims. we introduce a one-step bayesian approach for estimating multilevel vector autoregressive (mlvar) models (bmlvar), which enables uncertainty quantification for person-specific network features and the regression of external outcomes on such features. in a preregistered simulation study, we compare the new model with several popular methods for network estimation. we also apply all methods to empirical data to highlight their differences. our simulation results indicate that all methods perform mediocrely in estimating different centrality measures in practically relevant settings. bmlvar model still outperforms the other methods in many simulation conditions, especially regarding the statistical power to detect associations with an outcome. however, estimating the model properly can be challenging with limited data. overall, all methods require a lot of data or very large effects to produce reasonably accurate results. thus, although centrality measures based on dynamic networks have been widely used, our simulation study suggests they are unlikely to work well for achieving major goals of interest, such as guiding treatment selection and outcome prediction. we provide a new model that incorporates estimation uncertainty into the modeling process, thereby protecting against premature conclusions. infantile amnesia: the forgetting that shapes our identity infantile amnesia, the adult loss of autobiographical and episodic-like memories from early childhood, has long been a fascinating mystery. how, as many studies suggest they do, can forgotten early-life memories influence an individual's life? numerous investigations have concluded that this memory loss results from the immaturity of the infant hippocampus- or medial temporal lobe–dependent system, which lacks the ability to consolidate, store, or retrieve memories. based on our studies, we proposed a novel view of infantile learning and memory: the infant hippocampus-dependent memory system actively consolidates long-lasting, latent childhood memories and mental schemas that facilitate relearning and new, congruent learning throughout life. childhood experiences shape and mature the structure and abilities of the hippocampus during a critical period. this view provides a biological explanation for individual differences, personality trait development, and the impact of early interventions in preventing or reversing cognitive and developmental delays due to neglect, deprivation, and trauma. annual review of developmental psychology

integrating cultural and critical perspectives in positive youth development: a framework for out-of-school time programs the field of positive youth development (pyd) has its origins in community-based organizations designed to support youth development. recently, pyd scholars and leaders have increasingly called for approaches that foreground social justice, culture, and attention to the discriminatory contexts of growth and development. this article reviews culturally informed and critical community youth programs designed to foster pyd outcomes that expand beyond academic and behavioral indicators typically explored to include those that might be particularly salient for minoritized youth such as racial-ethnic identity, culture, and their interplay with other aspects of socioemotional development. we also highlight liberatory approaches that partner with youth in cocreating programs that empower inquiry and action. building on this literature, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes four approaches to integrating cultural and critical perspectives within out-of-school time programming: culturally supportive, informed, grounded, and engaged. these approaches reflect increasing attention to youths’ identities and lived experiences, from providing high-quality and affirming developmental settings to adapting programming to cultural contexts, centering community knowledge and practices in program design, and intentionally cultivating critical consciousness and youth agency. we describe and exemplify these distinct approaches and explore what critical and liberatory conceptualizations mean for future research and practice. annual review of developmental psychology

psychological reparations: healing the harms of racism. the field of psychology can offer much in the realm of internal healing and symbiotic repair. when i was an early career psychologist, i considered tools, like therapy and racial socialization, or the communication between parent and child about race and racism, which could contribute to redressing racial stress and trauma for black families. and yet now, as a clinical psychologist who approaches midcareer status interrogating these tools, i am deeply vested in how my training and advocacy can be applied to go beyond solely individual or familial interventions. as such, i am investigating reparations-a policy-oriented tool that can help bring both material and mental health advances to black americans-as a fundamentally psychological practice in nature. through this autoethnographic text, i ask how we can support the reparations movement to benefit more from psychological strategies and how our field can lend tools to advance the current momentum more favorably into public and private sectors. although my focus on black american individuals, families, and communities intends for them to be the beneficiaries of psychological reparations in this introductory prose, advancing reparations policies and practices through a psychological lens can provide much-needed pedagogy, research, and programming that purports to generate subsequent change for all americans. virtual nature and seasonality: exploring the influences of time of year and virtual season on stress, affect and nature connectedness outcomes—a randomized trial immersive virtual nature (ivn) has emerged as a promising tool to promote well-being and nature connectedness, though little is known about potential seasonal influences. to address this gap, this single blind randomized trial with parallel groups explores possible influences of the seasonal theme of virtual scenarios and time of year when the exposure occurs on psychological responses to ivn experiences. 108 university students (inclusion criteria: ≥ 18 years old, normal or corrected to normal sight) were recruited in early spring (march 18 – april 9) or early autumn (september 28 – october 17) and randomized to view a 360° nature video of the same environment with either a summer ( n = 27 and 26, respectively) or winter theme ( n = 27 and 28, respectively). outcomes included affect, perceived stress, nature connectedness, intention to perform green exercise, and intention to visit the location depicted in the videos. all participants were included in the analysis. two-way anovas found significant pre-post improvements for most outcomes (e.g., perceived stress: f (1,104) = 35.64, p < 0.001) except positive affect and intention to perform green exercise. no significant pre-post by “theme” interactions were observed for any of the outcomes. a significant pre-post by “cohort” interaction was found only for perceived stress ( f (1,104) = 7.32, p = 0.008), with greater reductions in the spring cohort compared to the autumn cohort. ivn depicting either summer of winter seasonal themes can elicit similar psychological responses. however, the magnitude of some responses may vary across the year. journal of environmental psychology

climate anxiety is associated with increasing distress and diminishing returns in pro-environmental behaviours: a cross-sectional study of australian youth growing evidence points to significant positive relationships between climate anxiety and psychological distress; however, there is also evidence that climate anxiety is associated with much-needed climate action. we aimed to assess whether there is a ‘goldilocks zone’ of climate anxiety wherein climate action is maximised at the lowest levels of psychological distress—a critical knowledge gap in youth, who report the greatest climate anxiety of any age group. in a large sample of australian youth (n = 869), we investigated the relationships amongst climate anxiety, individual and collective pro-environmental behaviours, and psychological distress. a series of analyses of variance showed large main effects between climate anxiety quintiles on measures of both individual and collective pro-environmental behaviours. upper climate anxiety quintiles showed significantly higher psychological distress; the highest climate anxiety quintile was at 9- to 12-fold higher odds for moderate (i.e., clinically significant) depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms. our curve-fitting analysis revealed better fit for non-linear models, with s-curves having the lowest error. broadly, the results could not identify a ‘goldilocks zone.’ instead, we observed that at higher levels of climate anxiety, there were consistently higher levels of distress but diminishing returns in pro-environmental behaviours, both individual and collective. we urge caution in promoting climate anxiety as a necessary motivating factor for climate action, as actual action tapers off while psychological distress continues to increase at higher levels of climate anxiety. journal of environmental psychology

covariation among higher-order psychopathology dimensions is driven by nomorbidity and not comorbidity abstract emerging classification frameworks claim that covariation among psychopathology dimensions reflects comorbidity. we scrutinized this claim by applying bayesian change point models to four waves of the adolescent brain cognitive development study data ( n = 11,868 youths; 48% female) and examined associations among higher-order psychopathology dimensions. covariation between psychopathology dimensions was driven by nomorbidity, not comorbidity: we observed strong positive associations among psychopathology dimensions at relatively extreme low (asymptomatic) levels (for example, when three to five symptoms were endorsed) and weak positive associations at higher levels. for instance, at wave 1, a 1-point increase in internalizing was associated with a 32% increase in externalizing at nearly asymptomatic levels ( b = 0.28), compared with only a 7% increase at higher levels ( b = 0.07). these findings challenge existing assumptions about comorbidity in nonclinical samples, suggesting that covariation is more accurately explained by the absence of symptomatology rather than shared psychiatric conditions. nature mental health

rdoc mechanisms underlying bodily symptoms in psychiatry: a scoping review abstract: somatic or bodily symptoms are shared among various psychiatric disorders. across the mood, anxious, dissociative and psychotic spectra, common and perhaps specific mechanisms for these debilitating symptoms need to be clarified. we propose here a scoping review of studies published until may 2025 focusing on primary research in adult populations about bodily symptoms, psychiatric disorders, and neurobiological mechanisms connecting them, based on the research domain criteria (rdoc) matrix. our review follows the prisma-scr checklist and included 73 articles. studies focusing solely on psychosomatic disorders were excluded. in the included studies, the most represented somatic symptoms were general symptoms such as pain or unspecific somatic symptoms, whereas anxiety and mood disorders accounted for the majority of psychiatric disorders. in terms of mechanistic links between somatic symptoms and psychiatric disorders, somatosensory perception and self-knowledge were the most studied rdoc subconstructs. when combined together, the most common triad associating somatic symptom, rdoc construct and psychiatric disorder was pain - perception - borderline personality disorder, occurring in 11 articles. this work also identifies knowledge gaps in the literature about mechanistic links between somatic symptoms and psychiatric disorders. for example, specific functional syndromes, dissociative disorders and interoception and their interactions are interesting concepts for future primary research studies. alternatively, the most studied associations suggest topics to be covered by systematic reviews. altogether, our results emphasize the need for more interdisciplinary research, taking advantage of recent advances in neuroscience that could help to uncover the complex mechanisms at play between psychological and bodily symptoms. keywords: psychosomatic, bodily symptoms, psychiatric disorders, rdoc, scoping review, biopsychosocial psychology research and behavior management

distinct roles of reward in target detection and search termination: evidence from static and dynamic visual search abstract reward has been shown to facilitate visual search, yet it remains unclear whether this benefit reflects enhanced search efficiency or changes in the decisional processes underlying target detection and search termination. the present study examined how reward affects visual search termination in both static (experiment 1) and dynamic (experiment 2) contexts. in both experiments, reward availability, target presence, and set size were manipulated. the color of the search array signaled reward availability for a given trial. participants were rewarded for correct responses faster than their baseline performance in the reward condition, while no reward was provided in the no-reward condition. across both experiments, reward facilitated target-present responses but did not improve target-absent performance. in static search, reward influenced both search efficiency and decisional processes, whereas in dynamic search its effects were primarily confined to decisional processes. specifically, reward altered search efficiency only in the static search, while computational modeling consistently indicated reduced decision caution for target-present responses across both search contexts. in contrast, the influence of reward on target-absent decisions was weaker and depended on the search context. together, these findings suggest that reward effects on decisional processes were more consistent across the two visual search contexts examined in the present study, whereas reward effects on search efficiency appeared to depend more strongly on search context, and that target detection and search termination are differentially influenced by motivational incentives. cognitive research-principles and implications

ethnoracial discrimination and subsequent cognitive functioning among adolescents: a 2‐month follow‐up study abstract introduction ethnoracial discrimination is a persistent risk factor for adolescents' developmental problems, yet limited research has examined its prospective association with adolescents' cognitive functioning. the current research employed a two‐wave design to investigate whether ethnoracial discrimination predicted subsequent adolescent cognitive functioning and to explore whether these associations differed between white adolescents and adolescents from ethnoracially minoritized backgrounds. methods the sample consisted of 113 adolescents (mean age = 14.85 years, sd = 0.41 years; 36% boys, 63% girls, 1% non‐binary; 35% non‐hispanic white, 65% ethnoracially minoritized) in the midwestern united states from 2018 to 2020. using a two‐wave follow‐up design with assessments 2 months apart, adolescents completed self‐report measures of perceived ethnoracial discrimination and executive functioning as well as performance‐based cognitive tests. results higher perceived ethnoracial discrimination was associated with greater self‐reported executive‐functioning problems and worse speeded set‐shifting over time, after adjustment for baseline cognitive functioning and demographic covariates. both associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction. however, interaction and stratified analyses did not provide robust evidence that the associations differed between white adolescents and adolescents from ethnoracially minoritized backgrounds. conclusions taken together, the findings highlight the detrimental role of ethnoracial discrimination for adolescent cognition, underscoring the urgency of combating ethnoracial discrimination and supporting adolescents who are impacted by discriminatory environments. journal of adolescence

observed effects of improvisational theater on personal growth: a scoping review abstract drama has long been used as a modality for promoting personal growth; still, new approaches continue to emerge. this scoping review aimed to chart evidence on the administration of improvisational theater (a form of unscripted performance) for personal growth and to identify directions for future research and practice. conducted in line with joanna briggs institute (jbi) guidelines, this review included empirical studies examining the effects of theatrical improv on personal growth, with no limitations on participants, regions, or publication periods. systematic searches of four databases (psycinfo, pubmed, scopus, and web of science) were conducted on june 29, 2026. the reference lists of included studies and citing articles identified through citation tracking were then manually searched. two independent reviewers screened and selected studies, and discrepancies were resolved through discussion and mutual consensus. study characteristics, primary outcomes, intervention design, and study design were extracted and analyzed descriptively. the review included 73 studies. mapped onto a framework structured by the bio‐psycho‐social‐spiritual (bpss) model and erikson's psychosocial developmental stages, outcomes were predominantly concentrated in the psychological and social domains, particularly among young adults, whereas the biological and spiritual domains were sparsely represented. across all age groups, each population demonstrated specific thematic patterns. positive effects were reported in the majority of studies, though notable heterogeneity in intervention and study designs was observed. theatrical improv showed preliminary positive effects on personal growth—particularly in communication, creativity, and well‐being—supporting its use as a low‐intensity, adaptable foundation for specialized applied improv programs beyond psychotherapy and education. applied psychology-health and well being

testing transfer effects of domain-general cognitive abilities to domain-specific decision making in soccer: are basic cognitive abilities related to creativity and intelligent decision making? a frequently investigated question is how domain-general cognitive abilities are related to domain-specific performance. the present study addresses several shortcomings of earlier research on the hypothesized positive relationship between domain-general cognitive ability tests and domain-specific cognitive skills (i.e., decision making) in soccer. by measuring both domain-general cognitive abilities (attentional breadth, multiple object tracking, working memory, and inhibition) and domain-specific performance (creative and intelligent decision making) on continuous scales (n > 100 participants [competitive soccer players] for every pairwise correlation), we avoid the common pitfalls of cross-sectional, between-group comparisons in this field. the results reveal only a small-to-medium correlation between multiple object tracking and intelligent decision making in soccer and a small correlation between attentional breadth and creative decision making, with no other significant associations found in the remaining six hypothesis tests. in addition, playing level was not associated with domain-general cognitive abilities. taken together, these findings contribute to the growing skepticism regarding the role of domain-general cognitive abilities in explaining team-sport expertise. psychology of sport and exercise
