shifting distribution and lethality profile of suicide methods in türkiye before, during, and after the covid-19 pandemic: a nationwide forensic epidemiological study background/objectives: the impact of the covid-19 pandemic on suicide method distribution and lethality profiles remains insufficiently studied, particularly in the post-pandemic period. this study aimed to examine temporal changes in suicide methods and lethality profiles in türkiye across three distinct periods: pre-pandemic (2016–2019), pandemic (2020–2022), and post-pandemic (2023–2025). methods: national suicide statistics published by the turkish statistical institute (turkstat) for 2016–2025 were retrospectively analyzed. suicide methods were classified as high-lethality (case fatality rate [cfr] > 50%) or low-lethality (cfr < 50%). chi-square tests, cramér’s v, and linear regression were applied. methods without available cfr data (train/vehicle collision, self-immolation, other) were excluded from lethality analyses. results: a total of 38,498 suicide deaths were recorded. the crude suicide rate increased from 4.03 to 5.36 per 100,000 (r2 = 0.909; p < 0.001), reaching its highest level in 2025. firearm use declined during the pandemic (30.0% to 26.9%; p < 0.001), whereas jumping from height increased during the pandemic and remained elevated post-pandemic (12.1%, 13.9%, and 13.6%, respectively; p < 0.001). chemical substance use temporarily increased during the pandemic (4.8% to 6.3%; p < 0.001), while natural/liquefied gas use increased post-pandemic (0.7%; p = 0.002). conclusions: the crude suicide rate increased during the study period; however, this increase was not accompanied by a sustained shift toward higher-lethality methods. post-pandemic suicide prevention strategies should be maintained, with particular attention to means restriction and sex-sensitive surveillance and prevention strategies. behavioral sciences

fairness views, equal sharing, and contributions in team production previous research has documented heterogeneity in individuals’ fairness views regarding how jointly produced output should be distributed. using a public goods game as a simplified representation of collective production, we report three experiments examining whether individuals’ fairness views are associated with their contributions under an equal-sharing rule (experiment 1), whether fairness-related prompting can affect contributions (experiment 2), and whether the procedure used to determine participation under the arrangement affects rule acceptance and contributions (experiment 3). experiment 1 shows that participants with more egalitarian fairness views contributed more under the equal-sharing rule, while experiment 2 provides causal evidence that fairness-related prompting affected subsequent contributions: participants asked to generate reasons why equal sharing is fair contributed more than those asked to generate reasons why it is unfair. experiment 3 shows that, compared with a procedure in which participation was imposed, a procedure in which participation was determined by group voting resulted in higher contributions and greater acceptance of the equal-sharing rule. exploratory analyses further suggest that the effects of voting may be stronger among participants with less egalitarian initial fairness views. our findings indicate that individuals’ fairness views and the procedures used to determine participation are relevant to understanding contribution behavior under an equal-sharing rule. behavioral sciences

the arabic classroom participation questionnaire: validation with d/deaf and hard of hearing university students the classroom participation questionnaire (cpq) was developed with school-aged d/deaf and hard of hearing (d/dhh) students, but no arabic version exists for university populations. this study adapted the cpq into arabic, extended it to d/dhh university students, and examined its internal structure, reliability, and the associations of communication understanding with communication-related positive and negative affect. in total, 135 d/dhh students at saudi public universities completed the 26-item arabic cpq. internal consistency was excellent (α = 0.91–0.96). positive- and negative-affect items formed clear, separate factors, whereas instructor- and peer-understanding items were highly interrelated (r = 0.83) and were combined into one composite; a four-factor confirmatory model showed acceptable fit (cfi = 0.90, rmsea = 0.089). communication understanding was strongly associated with positive affect (r = 0.69) and weakly with negative affect (r = 0.24), and the two affective dimensions were largely independent (r = 0.16). female students reported more positive and less negative affect; hearing-device use added no independent association. the arabic cpq functioned reliably in this population. because the understanding and positive-affect subscales share communication-specific content, their strong association partly reflects item overlap; the independence of the two affective dimensions suggests that accessibility and psychosocial support address distinct needs. behavioral sciences

dungeons & dragons in schools: an underexplored opportunity for early anxiety support. adolescent anxiety presents a growing challenge for schools, with emotional difficulties affecting educational engagement, attendance and wellbeing before some pupils meet thresholds for specialist mental health support. this creates a need to investigate accessible and non-stigmatising forms of early support within schools. emerging ttrpg research has described experiences involving social connection, confidence, self-expression and emotional exploration, but direct evidence concerning secondary-aged pupils experiencing emerging or subthreshold anxiety remains limited. this opinion paper brings together findings from existing ttrpg research, mechanisms identified in broader psychological theory and related narrative approaches, and propositions concerning how these may operate through school-based ttrpg participation. its contribution is a conceptual model linking components of ttrpg participation with five overlapping proposed mechanisms: narrative distance; psychological safety and social connectedness; intrinsic motivation and agency; identity exploration and self-efficacy; and cognitive flexibility and emotional regulation. the paper also outlines an illustrative school-based delivery model and a staged agenda for future research. these pathways are theoretically plausible rather than empirically established, and ttrpg participation should not be assumed to reduce anxiety or replace specialist assessment or treatment. initial research should establish feasibility, acceptability and safety, including potential adverse experiences, before psychological or educational outcomes are evaluated. behavioral sciences

a possible social support paradox in adolescent digital risk: online hate exposure, cyberviolence acceptance, and divergent peer–family contexts social support is generally assumed to protect adolescents from digital risk, yet its associations may differ by source and context. using national data from 9296 south korean adolescents, this study examined associations among online hate exposure (ohe), cyberviolence acceptance (cva), online risk behavior (orb), online peer support (ops), and perceived family support (pfs). ohe was positively associated with cva and orb, with a significant indirect association between ohe and orb through cva. ops was positively associated with orb, whereas pfs was negatively associated with orb and attenuated the ops–orb association. the negative pfs–orb association was weaker at higher cva. however, explained variance was modest and both interactions were very small. the findings suggest a possible social support paradox but require longitudinal replication. behavioral sciences

uncanny valley in conversation? effects of internal and external human-likeness on intimacy and trust conversational agents built on large language models increasingly converse like humans, expressing emotions and disclosing their own experiences. human-likeness, however, has been studied largely as a matter of appearance—how human an agent looks. language now also lets an agent display internal human-likeness by conveying an inner life, raising the question of how deeply an ai should express its own experiences—and whether that depends on its appearance. in a 2 (appearance: machine-like vs. human-like) × 3 (self-disclosure: none vs. low vs. high) between-subjects experiment, 193 university students completed a single, brief, fully scripted counseling session with an ai counselor prototype and evaluated it on six measures, controlling for prior mind perception. the effects of disclosure depth depended on appearance: with the machine-like counselor, intimacy and social presence peaked at low and declined at high disclosure, with trust and perceived authenticity showing the same direction—an uncanny valley-like pattern—whereas with the human-like counselor evaluations generally rose with depth. deeper disclosure was not judged more inappropriate, and moderated mediation analyses showed that deepening disclosure from low to high reduced anthropomorphism—and, through it, intimacy and trust—only for the machine-like counselor. internal and external human-likeness were read together: how deeply an ai should speak about itself cannot be decided apart from how it looks. behavioral sciences

a multilevel mental health intervention with latine newcomers: the feasibility and mixed methods results of a community-based participatory pilot study. latine immigrants in the u.s. face discrimination, a lack of access to resources, fear of deportation, family separation, and a lack of understanding of the complex factors that have led them to seek safety and survival in a new country, factors that critically impact their mental health. academic and community partners implemented the immigrant well-being project (iwp), a mental health intervention that partners community-based organizations (cbos) and universities to bring latine immigrants and university students together to engage in mutual learning and social change efforts. we assessed the feasibility of the iwp model and preliminary outcomes from a pilot implementation with three cohorts of latine immigrant adults (n = 54) between 2018 and 2021. employing a within-group longitudinal, mixed-methods design with qualitative interviews and quantitative surveys over 12 months (pre-intervention, post-intervention, and 6-month follow-up), we examined engagement and the impact of the 6-month intervention, as well as explored feasibility/acceptability and participants' experiences. multilevel growth modeling revealed significant decreases in depression and anxiety symptoms and difficulty accessing resources, with dosage and cohort significantly moderating intervention effects on these variables. some cohorts also experienced significant decreases in ptsd symptoms and increases in satisfaction with resources. qualitative results revealed that having student and cbo support navigating services positively impacted mental health, which highlights the importance of connecting immigrants to existing community resources. findings are discussed in the context of covid-19 and hostile immigration policies, emphasizing the importance of addressing social-structural determinants of mental health for immigrants. behavioral sciences

school-based intervention programs: conceptual, empirical, practical, and equity-focused considerations across development, implementation, evaluation, and dissemination school-based intervention programs play an essential role in promoting students’ academic, behavioral, and social–emotional development. achieving meaningful and equitable outcomes, however, depends on more than the availability of intervention programs. it also requires high-quality intervention work across the interconnected domains of intervention development, implementation, evaluation, and dissemination. substantial scholarship exists within each domain, yet relevant concepts, considerations, and practical guidance are often distributed across separate studies and frameworks, making it difficult for intervention scientists and intervention adopters to develop an integrated understanding of intervention work. this paper provides a functional conceptualization of intervention work by synthesizing foundational concepts, empirical and practical considerations, and guiding questions across its four primary domains. rather than proposing a new intervention framework, the paper complements existing frameworks by clarifying what each domain is intended to accomplish, the knowledge and products it generates, and how activities within one domain can inform and improve decisions made throughout the others. collectively, the paper argues that high-quality intervention work depends not only on excellence within each domain, but also on intentionally designing activities within each domain so that the resulting knowledge and resources contribute to the broader system of intervention research and practice. the paper is written for two primary audiences: (a) intervention scientists engaged in developing, implementing, evaluating, or disseminating intervention programs, and (b) intervention adopters responsible for selecting, implementing, evaluating, and making continued-use decisions about programs in educational settings. three primary contributions are provided. first, the paper clarifies foundational concepts, essential considerations, and key questions associated with each domain. second, it illustrates how the four domains collectively contribute to the development, implementation, evaluation, dissemination, adoption, and sustained use of high-quality intervention programs. third, it translates this conceptual perspective into practical guidance through tables, 12 key questions and considerations, and separate reflection guides designed to support professional judgment, high-quality intervention science, and evidence-driven intervention adoption and use. behavioral sciences

the temporal relationships between non-suicidal self-injury and social anxiety: a cross-lagged panel study empirical evidence increasingly supports an association between non-suicidal self-injury (nssi) and social anxiety symptoms among chinese adolescents, although their temporal relationship remains inadequately established. to address this gap, the present study employed a cross-lagged panel design to examine the longitudinal relationships between nssi and social anxiety symptoms. the final analytic sample consisted of 614 chinese adolescents aged 13–18 years (53.09% girls), who completed three waves of assessments at six-month intervals using standardized self-report measures of nssi, social anxiety, and rejection sensitivity. longitudinal analyses controlling for prior symptom levels and gender showed that social anxiety at time 1 significantly predicted subsequent nssi at time 2. a reciprocal relationship between social anxiety and nssi was also observed across subsequent measurement waves. furthermore, rejection sensitivity showed a significant indirect effect in the longitudinal association between social anxiety and subsequent nssi. these findings highlight the longitudinal and reciprocal associations between social anxiety and nssi among chinese adolescents and suggest that rejection sensitivity may represent an important psychological pathway linking social anxiety to subsequent nssi. intervention strategies targeting nssi may therefore benefit from considering co-occurring social anxiety symptoms and rejection sensitivity. behavioral sciences

relationships between instructor leadership styles, self-efficacy, and exercise adherence intention among recreational badminton participants this study examined the relationships between perceived badminton instructors’ leadership styles (training and instruction, democratic, positive feedback, and social support behaviors), self-efficacy, and exercise adherence intention. data were collected through a questionnaire survey from late august to early october 2025, yielding 186 valid responses from 210 distributed questionnaires. frequency and reliability analyses were conducted and structural equation modeling was performed. training and instruction behavior was positively related to self-efficacy, whereas democratic, positive feedback, and social support behaviors were not significantly related to self-efficacy. positive feedback behavior was positively related to exercise adherence intention, while training and instruction, democratic, and social support behaviors were not significantly related to exercise adherence intention. self-efficacy was positively related to exercise adherence intention. self-efficacy significantly mediated the relationship between training and instruction behavior and exercise adherence intention, whereas no significant mediation was found for democratic, positive feedback, or social support behaviors. this study identifies the structural relationships between perceived badminton instructors’ leadership styles, self-efficacy, and exercise adherence intention. the findings provide practical implications and evidence for developing effective coaching strategies to support exercise adherence intention among recreational badminton participants. behavioral sciences

neural-discursive dynamics in collaborative spatial problem solving: evidence from fnirs hyperscanning and accountable talk high-quality collaboration cannot be inferred simply from how much students talk or how strongly their brain activity is synchronized during joint work. this study examined relations among accountable talk, inter-brain synchrony (ibs), and group task performance in fifth-grade students’ collaborative mathematical problem solving. forty-nine students worked in 15 groups and completed two collaborative spatial design tasks, yielding 30 group × task records. functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fnirs) data and video recordings were collected simultaneously; discourse was coded using accountable talk indicators, and group design products were scored as task performance. mixed-effects models showed that higher task performance was associated with more accountable talk turns, shorter mean turn duration, and higher accountable talk density, but not with longer total accountable talk duration. ibs showed channel-group-specific associations with task performance, suggesting that overall synchrony alone did not fully characterize collaborative activity. temporal-window analyses showed that the within-window association between accountable talk density and ibs differed according to task performance level. these findings suggest that, within the present collaborative tasks, productive collaboration was associated with dense task-relevant accountable discourse and performance-dependent behavioral–neural associations rather than talk quantity or overall neural synchrony alone. behavioral sciences

associations between interoceptive awareness, psychological state, and physical performance in sport-science students: a cross-sectional study background/objectives: interoceptive awareness may support stress regulation in sport, but its association with objective physical performance remains unclear. this study examined relationships between self-reported interoceptive awareness, perceived stress, anxiety, sleep quality, and field-based performance in sport-science students. methods: eighty-five students (54 men, 31 women; 20.65 ± 2.43 years) completed the maia-2, pss-10, stai, and psqi and performed handgrip, countermovement-jump, sit-and-reach, and bilateral y-balance tests. analyses included pearson correlations, welch tests with false-discovery-rate correction, hc3-robust hierarchical regression, and exploratory age- and sex-adjusted bootstrap indirect-effect models. results: the maia-2 composite was inversely associated with perceived stress (r = −0.461, 95% ci [−0.614, −0.275], p < 0.001) but showed no detectable association with physical performance (r = −0.003 to 0.136; all q ≥ 0.961); equivalence testing indicated that four of the five performance correlations were statistically equivalent to zero within a ±0.30 bound. women reported higher stress and anxiety, whereas men showed greater handgrip strength and jump height. individual-sport participants reported higher state anxiety than team-sport participants (g = −0.886, q = 0.004). interoceptive awareness did not significantly increase explained variance in any performance model, and exploratory indirect-effect confidence intervals all included zero. conclusions: self-reported interoceptive awareness was related to perceived stress but was not detectably related to brief field-based performance in this sample. longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to test temporal and causal mechanisms. behavioral sciences

end-of-life expectations and meaning-making among first-year medical residents: a phenomenological study in a mexican general hospital. end of life is a profound and culturally charged human dimension. bioethics and palliative medicine have promoted a shift from the traditional biomedical model toward person-centered care that preserves dignity through the dying process. physicians-in-training live in continuous contact with illness and death, yet are rarely invited to reflect on their own finitude. reflection on one's own mortality has been linked to greater comfort discussing prognosis, more patient-centered end-of-life decision making, and reduced avoidance behaviors in clinical encounters with dying patients; however, most training programs address death only as a technical or bioethical topic, rarely as a personal experience requiring processing. this study explored the end-of-life expectations and meaning-making of first-year medical residents at a mexican general hospital, considering the influence of medical culture and sociocultural discourse. a qualitative phenomenological design was used. data were collected through asynchronous, self-recorded video interviews guided by five open-ended questions addressing illness and death, family, autonomy, medical care at the end of life, advance directives, and euthanasia. purposive sampling included twenty-eight first-year residents (2024-2025 cohort) who had previously completed coursework in medical ethics, giving the final sample of twenty-eight participants. data were analyzed using an interpretive phenomenological approach supported by atlas.ti. open coding of experiential meaning units was followed by iterative hermeneutic interpretation. participants described the end of life through two tensions: an idealized, peaceful death surrounded by family, and a pragmatic view shaped by clinical exposure to suffering and futile treatment. participants uniformly favored palliative care and expressed a preference for dying at home in the case of a terminal illness. attitudes toward euthanasia ranged from support as an individual right to religious/ethical opposition, frequently anchored in personal grief experiences. advance directives were positively valued but rarely formalized. emotional overflow, including tears, occurred in some interviews. despite clinical experience, medical residents are not immune to the emotional and existential tensions surrounding death. findings suggest that integrating reflective, narrative-based pedagogical strategies into residency training may help to process death-related distress and strengthen person-centered, dignity-preserving end-of-life care. behavioral sciences

beyond general prosocial behavior: nature connectedness, authenticity, and instrumental prosocial behavior in late childhood research linking nature connectedness to prosociality has rarely distinguished motivationally specific forms of helping. the present study examined the associations of nature connectedness with general prosocial behavior and the more specific instrumental prosocial behavior during late childhood, with authenticity examined as an associational variable. using a cross-sectional design, the final analytic sample comprised 281 grade 4 and grade 5 students aged 9–12 years who were recruited through convenience sampling from two primary schools in yantai, china. path analyses using factor scores adjusted for differential item functioning were interpreted within an associational variable analysis framework. nature connectedness was positively associated with authenticity and general prosocial behavior, with a significant positive indirect association involving authenticity. in contrast, authenticity was negatively associated with instrumental prosocial behavior. nature connectedness showed a positive direct association with instrumental prosocial behavior after accounting for authenticity but a negative indirect association involving authenticity, resulting in a nonsignificant total association. the positive direct association differed by sex and was significant among boys but not girls. these findings underscore the importance of distinguishing instrumental from general prosocial behavior and suggest that authenticity may help differentiate their associations with nature connectedness in late childhood. behavioral sciences

behavioral activation and mobile phone addiction in chinese university students: the chain-mediating effects of perceived social support and negative cognitive emotion regulation behavioral activation refers to specific behavioral responses generated by individuals when exposed to reward stimuli in order to obtain reward satisfaction, and continuous rewarding experiences may lead to addictive tendencies. to understand the relationship between behavioral activation and mobile phone addiction tendency among chinese college students, as well as the chain mediating roles of perceived social support and negative cognitive emotion regulation, a questionnaire survey was conducted among 648 students randomly sampled from a university in fuzhou, fujian province, china, to investigate the relationships among behavioral activation, perceived social support, negative cognitive emotion regulation, and mobile phone addiction tendency. the results showed that: (1) behavioral activation negatively predicted mobile phone addiction tendency among chinese college students (β = −0.11, t = −2.92, p < 0.001); (2) negative cognitive emotion regulation partially mediated the relationship between behavioral activation and mobile phone addiction tendency; and (3) perceived social support and negative cognitive emotion regulation played a chain mediating role between behavioral activation and mobile phone addiction tendency. these findings suggest that behavioral activation can negatively predict mobile phone addiction tendency through perceived social support and negative cognitive emotion regulation in chinese college students. behavioral sciences

quantifying the diagnostic contribution of neuropsychological evaluation using natural language processing objective: diagnostic clarification is regarded as a core function of neuropsychological evaluation, yet its impact has rarely been quantified because diagnoses are typically embedded within unstructured narrative reports. this pilot study quantified the diagnostic contribution of neuropsychological evaluation by examining diagnostic reclassification and diagnostic clarification using a novel natural language processing (nlp) pipeline. method: a retrospective observational study was conducted using 220 adult outpatient neuropsychological evaluation reports from the national neuropsychology network. a rule-based nlp pipeline extracted and harmonized pre-evaluation referral diagnoses and post-evaluation clinician diagnoses from reports in the ucla electronic health records into structured diagnostic profiles. diagnostic reclassification, diagnostic specificity gain, and changes in diagnostic category distributions were quantified. exploratory analyses examined demographic correlates of diagnostic clarification. results: diagnostic reclassification was common following neuropsychological evaluation. overall, 87.7% of patients received at least one new diagnosis, 55.0% had at least one preexisting diagnosis not retained, and 84.5% demonstrated increased diagnostic specificity. among patients with nonspecific cognitive symptom codes, 90.1% transitioned to formal psychiatric, neurological, or neurocognitive diagnoses. collectively, these changes shifted diagnostic profiles away from nonspecific cognitive diagnoses toward more specific formal psychiatric and neurocognitive diagnoses (all p < .001). exploratory demographic associations were modest. conclusions: neuropsychological evaluation provides substantial incremental diagnostic information beyond referral documentation by increasing diagnostic specificity and refining diagnostic formulation. these pilot findings establish diagnostic clarification as a measurable clinical outcome and demonstrate the potential of nlp to transform routine neuropsychological reports into scalable metrics for evaluating the clinical impact of neuropsychological services. clinical neuropsychologist

collective nostalgia widens the gap between obsessive and harmonious passion in support for political violence abstract collective nostalgia—a longing for a group's shared past—carries both a sweet pull toward ingroup connection and a sour potential for outgroup hostility. we propose that these divergent associations depend on the form of passion people hold for their political cause. drawing on the dualistic model of passion, we distinguished obsessive passion, a pressured form of ideological involvement tied to self‐worth, from harmonious passion, freely endorsed and integrated with other commitments. in a cross‐sectional survey of u.s. democrats ( n = 263) and republicans ( n = 154), participants reported their passion for their party, collective nostalgia for its past, ideological commitment, and support for political violence against the rival party. in both subsamples, obsessive passion was associated with greater support for political violence, whereas harmonious passion was not. collective nostalgia moderated both associations in opposite directions: at higher levels of nostalgia, the obsessive‐passion link was stronger, whereas the harmonious‐passion link turned negative, predicting lower support for political violence. these patterns held across parties, controlling for ideological commitment. collective nostalgia thus appears not uniformly radicalizing; longing for a shared past accompanied greater support for political violence at higher levels of obsessive passion but lower support at higher levels of harmonious passion. journal of applied social psychology

strengthening the wise-and-competent mode: effects of group schema therapy for children abstract background this pilot study evaluated the effects of a group intervention based on an extended schema therapy framework designed to strengthen the wise-and-competent mode in children, an adaptive psychological resource associated with flexible emotional regulation and healthy copings. methods a quasi-experimental 2 (group: intervention vs. control) × 2 (time: pre-intervention vs. post-intervention) mixed design was used. the final sample included 41 students aged 10–12 years (21 intervention, 20 control). participants completed measures of emotional intelligence, anxiety, and coping strategies before and after the intervention. the protocol consisted of 25 sessions organized across six stages. data were analyzed using mixed-design anova. results results supported all study hypotheses. compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant increases in emotional intelligence and functional copings, and significant reductions in anxiety and dysfunctional copings. no comparable changes were observed in the control group. conclusions the findings suggest reduced use of maladaptive coping modes and lower anxiety levels, alongside enhanced adaptive coping modes associated with emotional regulation, supporting the potential effectiveness of group schema therapy interventions in children. cognitive therapy and research

effects of rumination on state shame in adolescents: an online experimental investigation abstract purpose adolescence is a vulnerable period for the experience of shame and the development of ruminative habits. we sought to examine whether and how rumination potentiates shame, a risk factor for psychopathology. cognitive research in adults has proposed that the impact of rumination on emotion depends on its processing style, but this has been tested mainly for basic (e.g. sadness) but not complex emotions (e.g. shame). we predicted that abstract rumination (e.g. focusing on “why”) would increase shame to a greater extent than concrete rumination (e.g. focusing on “how”) and distraction. methods adolescents ( n = 128; 16–19 years old) underwent an online study. they were instructed to focus on a past event that caused feelings of shame (by retrieving a vivid memory). participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups prompting engagement in abstract rumination, concrete rumination, or distraction. self-report measures assessed state shame before and after the experimental manipulations. trait self-critical rumination (scr) was also measured at baseline. results we found a significant reduction in state shame in the distraction group, but not in concrete or abstract rumination groups, nor significant differences between the rumination groups. trait-scr did not predict levels of state shame following rumination. conclusion unlike prior research predominantly in adults and primary emotions, abstract and concrete rumination did not have different consequences for shame in adolescents. rather than focussing solely on changing processing style, interventions for adolescent shame may need to interrupt rumination more broadly. models of rumination derived from adult samples may require refinement for adolescent shame. however, future research is required to replicate and extend these effects with additional design improvements. cognitive therapy and research

experiences of oppression among partner‐abusive men: perspectives of immigrant latino intervention program participants and staff abstract this study explored how systems of oppression influence intimate partner violence (ipv) among immigrant latinos in the united states enrolled in battering intervention programs (bips). utilizing a critical community psychology perspective and latino critical theory, focus groups were conducted with bip participants and providers to understand participants' experiences and perceptions of oppression in the united states as they relate to ipv. thematic analysis identified a number of key aspects in their experiences as follows: (1) the coerced silence of immigrant latino participants, (2) the criminal legal system's role in perpetuating oppression, (3) multifaceted disenfranchisement and barriers to resources, (4) financial hardship and economic stress linked to ipv, (5) power and control as binding oppression to ipv and (6) the gendered cultural socialization of latinos. the findings challenge dominant narratives by highlighting the importance of structural factors in ipv among latinos and in immigrant communities globally. given the limited and inequitable availability of culturally appropriate ipv resources for latinos, battering intervention programs that incorporate an understanding of oppression into their programming can more effectively support latinx communities impacted by ipv. journal of community & applied social psychology

gossip sharing willingness in primary school children: the role of competition and potential allies abstract the present study conducted two experiments to investigate chinese children's willingness to share positive and negative gossip, as well as the roles of competition and potential allies in gossip sharing among children aged 8 to 12 years. in experiment 1 ( n = 242), vignette‐based scenarios were used to examine differences in children's willingness to share gossip with different valences in competitive and non‐competitive contexts. in experiment 2 ( n = 246), we further explored how the presence of potential allies influenced children's gossip‐sharing willingness within a competitive context. the results showed that: (1) children were generally more willing to share positive gossip than negative gossip; (2) children's willingness to share positive gossip was lower in competitive contexts than in non‐competitive contexts; (3) children were less willing to share negative gossip about competitors with potential allies than about those without potential allies; and (4) willingness to share negative gossip increased significantly with age, whereas willingness to share positive gossip showed a nonsignificant decline. these findings highlight the valence preference and context dependency of children's gossip‐sharing willingness and provide insights for future research on how interaction contexts and interpersonal factors shape children's gossip behavior in school settings. social development

anxiety and depression symptoms in chinese male patients with substance use disorder: independent and comorbid networks anxiety and depression are prevalent among patients with substance use disorder (sud), yet the mechanisms of their symptom-level interactions remain insufficiently understood. this study investigated 1586 male sud patients (mean age = 35.91) in a chinese drug rehabilitation center, using network analysis and directed acyclic graphs (dags) to analyze their anxiety and depression. results showed that fear and dizziness were the most central symptoms in the anxiety network and confusion was the most central symptom in the depression network. in the comorbidity network, apprehension was the key bridge symptom, and dag further indicated mental disintegration as a triggering symptom for both anxiety and depression. these findings may indicate fear , dizziness, confusion , apprehension , and mental disintegration as relatively important symptoms, providing potential directions for future intervention research aimed at reducing comorbidity of anxiety and depression in sud patients. journal of health psychology

relating object memory to word learning: data from a new test of toddlers' object recognition abstract learning names for concrete objects, which dominate early vocabularies, relies on visual processes such as object recognition and memory for previously named objects. we examined the relation between memory for pairs of familiar and novel objects and early vocabulary development. we tested 52 14‐ to 24‐month‐olds (26 girls) in a preferential‐looking object recognition task. analysis of data from 44 toddlers suggested memory performance was based on whether the stimuli were from categories known to children in this age range and a vocabulary percentile score based on age and gender, rather than just age or total productive vocabulary. we found some evidence that toddlers with higher vocabulary percentile scores remembered familiar but not novel object pairs. we discuss possible reasons for differences in memory for familiar and novel objects, limitations of our task and how our findings fit with proposals on the relations between memory, visual processing and variability in vocabulary development. image british journal of developmental psychology

linking employees' boundary‐spanning behaviour to leadership emergence: a social exchange theory perspective abstract this study examined the links between employees' boundary‐spanning behaviour and leadership emergence, focusing on the mediating role of prestige and the moderating roles of coworker support and relational‐interdependent self‐construal. two studies were conducted to test the hypotheses. study 1 (experimental survey, n = 208) tested the mediation hypotheses. study 2 (questionnaire study, n = 691) extended study 1 by examining the moderated mediation model. the results show that employees' boundary‐spanning behaviour is positively related to leadership emergence, which is mediated by prestige. additionally, coworker support and relational‐interdependent self‐construal moderate the relationship between employees' boundary‐spanning behaviour and prestige. based on the social exchange theory, this study revealed the mechanisms and boundary conditions of leadership emergence, enriching the literature and expanding the theory's application to organisational behaviour. it suggested that organisations and managers should encourage employees to engage in boundary‐spanning behaviour. this would break down departmental barriers and promote a supportive, collaborative atmosphere, enhancing employees' prestige and leadership emergence. international journal of psychology

decoding diversity: are there patterns in the organization of grooming movements in domestic cats? abstract grooming is crucial for mammalian health and hygiene, serving diverse functions such as parasite defense, removing dirt, and thermoregulation. grooming is not purely reactive but integrated into daily routines and regulated endogenously. in rodents, it has been shown to follow a sequential structure with predictable patterns, often interpreted as reflecting pattern‐generating neurological programs. in this study, we examined the temporal and spatial structure of self‐grooming sequences in cats to test whether grooming in this species follows similarly predictable patterns. grooming performance in 17 cats was recorded, and 40 sequences were analyzed to discern the allocation of grooming time to different body areas. pattern analyses reveal the temporal order in which body areas were cleaned. oral grooming occupies the largest portion of grooming time, whereas face washing and scratching were less frequent. high individual variation was found in the distribution of grooming time across body areas and in the spatiotemporal order of sequences, challenging the idea of strict patterns and grooming rules in cats. instead, our analyses indicate that grooming is structured by probabilistic transitions between spatially adjacent body regions. we conclude that grooming sequences in cats are primarily determined by the spatial proximity of grooming targets and movement efficiency. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

qualitative markers of reflective functioning: exploratory psychometric examination in community participants meeting or not meeting borderline personality disorder criteria 反思功能的定性标记：在符合或不符合边缘型人格障碍标准的社区参与者中的探索性心理测量检验 reflective functioning (rf) is the capacity to understand oneself and others in terms of mental states. it is central to intra- and interpersonal functioning, as impairments in rf are associated with psychopathology, and especially borderline personality disorder (bpd). the reflective functioning scale (rfs), the gold-standard measure of rf, requires the identification of qualitative markers, but their specific contribution to the global score and whether the prevalence of these markers differs among proxies of clinical samples has rarely been examined. participants who met the criteria for bpd ( = 51), other psychiatric disorders ( = 49), or healthy controls ( = 51) were interviewed for rf using the brief reflective functioning interview, which was coded with the rfs. positive markers were stronger predictors of rf scores than negative ones, though both uniquely contributed to the prediction of rf. qualitative categories did not predict the global rf scores beyond the prediction by marker valence. groups differed in marker prevalence, with bpd displaying higher rates of distorted, self-serving markers of rf. findings suggest that qualitative markers of rf add unique insight into mentalizing, informing theoretical and clinical endeavors, but that the current set of markers may be redundant and requires reconsideration. journal of personality assessment

pre-service science teachers’ anxiety levels about artificial intelligence applications the objective of this study is to ascertain the levels of anxiety experienced by pre-service science teachers in relation to the utilization of artificial intelligence applications. a mixed research method was employed in the study. one of the mixed research method designs, the sequential explanatory design, was employed in the study. in the quantitative section of the study, a survey design was employed, while a case study design was utilized in the qualitative component. the population of the quantitative component, which constitutes the participants of the study, consists of 208 pre-service teachers enrolled in the science department of the faculty of education at a state university. the study sample consisted of 162 pre-service science teachers. the sample was selected through the use of simple random sampling. in the qualitative component of the study, eight prospective science educators, selected for their maximum diversity, were the subjects of investigation. in the course of data collection for the study, the scale was administered to 162 pre-service science teachers. subsequently, semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight pre-service science teachers. in the data analysis phase of the study, quantitative and qualitative data were analyzed separately. descriptive statistics and inferential statistics were employed to analyze the quantitative data, while content analysis was utilized to analyze the qualitative data. the findings revealed that the level of artificial intelligence anxiety among the pre-service science teachers was moderate, as indicated by the scale administered to this group. the interviews revealed that pre-service teachers with high and low levels of artificial intelligence anxiety had similar responses. both groups agreed that artificial intelligence cannot replace the teaching profession. based on these findings, the research team proposed two recommendations: first, to provide pre-service teachers with the necessary training on artificial intelligence, and second, to offer an artificial intelligence course to all pre-service teachers. discover psychology

pilot test of the relationship and financial education together program for lgbtq+ people in relationships abstract financial stress negatively impacts health and relationships and relationship stress undermines financial management. lgbtq+ individuals face additional stress from discrimination, yet no known programs address both relationship and financial stress for lgbtq+ people. we pilot‐tested the adaptation of together, an evidence‐based relationship and financial education program, for lgbtq+ people in relationships by assessing its acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility using mixed methods. we collected quantitative data on program satisfaction and usefulness through surveys completed anonymously by 31 participants and qualitative data through three focus groups with program participants ( n = 12) and one focus group and six interviews with program staff (three case managers and 6 facilitators). findings supported the adaptation's acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. participants noted high program satisfaction and usefulness, but also offered ways in which the curriculum could be strengthened and even more focused on lgbtq+ people in relationships journal of marital and family therapy

musical episodic modulation of human functioning: anticipation mechanisms, personal sense, and emotional recall abstract this article develops a theoretical and exploratory account of musical episodic modulation of human functioning, with special attention to emotional recall. it responds to a recurrent limitation in the psychology of music: although music’s effects on attention, emotion, memory, motivation, and performance have been widely documented, these domains are often examined separately rather than as mutually organized dimensions of lived episodes. the article proposes that music may function as a modulating agent of human functioning when its temporal, affective, and semantically open structure becomes coupled with ongoing activity through anticipation mechanisms. drawing on activity theory, phenomenology of temporal consciousness, floating intentionality, entrainment, and appraisal theory, the paper conceptualizes anticipation mechanisms as the dynamic relations among anticipators, the anticipated, and horizonality. these mechanisms explain how musical signals may organize salience, attention, affect, readiness, and possible next actions over time. the argument is illustrated through a phenomenologically oriented self-study in which the same song contributed to opposed emotional episodes during two recall activities: hopelessness, yearning, and sadness in relation to the memory of a deceased father, and excitement, hope, and joy in relation to an anticipated romantic encounter. the contrast suggests that musical valence does not determine emotional outcome by itself. rather, emotions emerge through projection-appraisal loops involving objects of thought, personal sense, belief systems, previous experience, and the unfolding music. the article concludes by outlining limitations, future research directions, and distinguishing the more specific phenomenon analyzed from the broader account of musical modulation of human functioning. integrative psychological and behavioral science

training and professional development in treatment intensity recommendations among practicing behavior analysts: a preliminary investigation abstract although there is strong support for the use of interventions based on applied behavior analysis (aba) with individuals with autism spectrum disorder (asd), there is also evidence of heterogeneity in response to intervention. treatment intensity recommendations represent consequential clinical decisions that directly influence patient outcomes, resource allocation, and effectiveness of interventions. however, little is known about how behavior analysts develop the competencies required to determine treatment intensity in practice. we surveyed behavior analysts about their professional development experiences related to making these recommendations ( n = 559). results indicated that most respondents received training through in‐field observation and shadowing provided by their employer. implications for training and supervision to better prepare behavior analysts for this aspect of treatment planning are discussed. behavioral interventions

speaking black queer grief(s): toward transformative care for black tlgbqia2s+ communities while literature has spoken to the wealth of loss experienced by black and queer communities separately, limited empirical literature has focused on how people living at the intersection of these identities grieve and make meaning of these losses. moreover, when examined, these experiences overwhelmingly highlight physical death and exclude the pervasive impact of nondeath losses facilitated by confluent anti-black and heterosexist systems. as such, the present work is guided by critical and liberation frameworks to understand how structural violence shapes the way that black queer communities diversely experience grief. using semi-structured interviews, the present qualitative study explored how 10 black queer adults (range 18–41) made meaning of their grief experiences through a critically conscious lens. an inductive thematic analysis revealed three main themes: body, mind, and spirit—naming and claiming grief as disempowerment across dimension and beyond binaries , severance—grieving separation as “the other” within the collective , and defiant reconstruction—world building in the aftermath of loss through new imaginings . authors provide grief-informed considerations for transformative liberational practice with black queer communities. journal of humanistic psychology

from hopelessness to despair: psychological states after the loss of hope recent psychological and philosophical research has placed emphasis on aspects of hope that were left unnoticed by earlier attempts to define hope through a set of necessary and sufficient conditions. this development has been coupled with making distinctions between different psychological states that share some of hope’s features. less attention has been given on applying analogous distinctions to the examination of hope’s loss and to the psychological states that result from it. the essay aims to bridge this gap, by offering a description of the psychological states connected with the loss of hope and of the effects that these states have. it begins by discussing some prominent features of hope, focusing on its complexity. it then gives an account of hope’s abandonment and of its absence. concentrating on three distinct states, hopelessness, desperation and despair, the essay examines cases where one can experience despair or desperation without experiencing hopelessness and vice versa. the essay’s claim is that elements of hope remain even in cases where one’s attitude is no longer hopeful and that these elements can affect one’s beliefs and actions in significantly diverse ways. journal of humanistic psychology

exploring illness perception classes in the general population: a latent class analysis. objectives: this study aimed to identify classes of illness perceptions in the danish general population and examine their association with physical and mental health outcomes.
method: latent class analysis was conducted on 4,999 participants using the brief illness perception questionnaire (bipq) to identify distinct illness perception classes. cross-sectional and five-year follow-up analyses explored associations between illness perception class and outcomes including symptom severity, physical functioning, anxiety, depression, and screening for functional somatic disorder (fsd).
results: three distinct illness perception classes were identified:,, and. theclass showed positive illness perceptions and favourable outcomes. theclass showed low perceived control and symptom coherence but did not differ significantly from theclass in outcomes. theclass showed negative perceptions of consequences, concern, timeline, and emotional responses and had the poorest health outcomes both at baseline and follow-up, even when adjusting for baseline scores. class membership was significantly associated with all outcomes cross-sectionally and longitudinally.
conclusions: illness perception class membership was associated with long-term physical and mental health. membership to theclass predicted poorer outcomes and higher fsd risk, suggesting that negative illness perceptions may precede negative health outcomes and represent a target for intervention. psychology & health

development of dual systems constructs during childhood: sexual abuse variety as a predictor of differential development the dual systems model has risen to prominence as a developmental framework because of its capacity for understanding adolescents' high propensity for risky behaviors during this period of the life-course. while development of impulse control and sensation-seeking mainly occurs during adolescence, childhood and exposures during childhood may lead to long-term impacts on development during this period of the life-course. sexual abuse in childhood may be a particularly relevant predictor of differential development of these constructs. this study addressed these gaps in the literature by examining sexual abuse as a predictor of differential development of impulse control and sensation-seeking during childhood and early adolescence. the adolescent brain cognitive development data were analyzed. group-based trajectory modeling was used to identify developmental heterogeneity in impulse control and sensation-seeking. multinomial logistic regression was used to examine sexual abuse variety as a predictor of differential development. results indicated that a four-group model of impulse control development (high impulse control, moderate impulse control, declining impulsivity, high impulsivity) and a three-group model of sensation-seeking development (high sensation-seeking, moderate sensation-seeking, low sensation-seeking) best fit the data. greater sexual abuse variety predicted increased risk of assignment to the high sensation-seeking group, but did not predict impulse control development. journal of child sexual abuse

‘the one place where i can come and not get in trouble’: emotional safety and epistemic trust in brief psychosocial intervention for adolescent depression epistemic trust – trust in interpersonally communicated knowledge – has recently gained attention in psychotherapy research, yet its operation within therapeutic relationships remains insufficiently understood. this study examined how relational and epistemic processes developed within a single case of brief psychosocial intervention (bpi) and the extent to which they were accounted for by the three-communication-systems model of epistemic trust. a theory-building single-case study design was employed using complete transcripts from 11 therapy sessions with a 14-year-old female with depression. iterative deductive, inductive, and abductive analysis indicated that the case broadly followed the processes described by the existing three-communication-systems model. however, the analysis also distinguished emotional safety in communicating vulnerable experiences from epistemic openness to communicated knowledge, with indicators of emotional safety evident before more explicit epistemic openness towards the therapist. the case further supported understanding therapeutic learning as a collaborative process in which patients actively contribute to the construction of therapeutic understanding. these findings do not establish emotional safety as a necessary precursor to epistemic trust, but suggest potential refinements to existing accounts of epistemic trust and generate propositions for further psychotherapy process research. counselling psychology quarterly

gender dysphoria among 46,xx patients diagnosed with congenital adrenal hyperplasia in childhood: a case series most research on gender identity in individuals with 46,xx congenital adrenal hyperplasia (cah) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency (21-ohd) is focused on severe forms of cah, commonly termed "classic cah." much less is known about gender identity outcomes in milder, non-classic/late-onset cah, and how gender dysphoria may impact clinical care and management decisions. this case series presents four pediatric patients with 46,xx karyotype who were diagnosed with cah in early-to mid-childhood and represents a varying spectrum of cah severity. in each case, patients had female-typical genitalia or their genital variation was not appreciated and further evaluated by the care team at birth; thus, all patients were assigned female at birth without targeted discussion on gender development. each patient later experienced gender dysphoria and identified as male, transitioning socially and/or medically. this case series reflects on commonalities across cases, intentional non-adherence to cah medication to allow for desired increased androgen levels, as well as mental health concerns. this case series highlights the importance of interdisciplinary care for youth with 46,xx cah, and in particular, the benefits of collaboration with behavioral health providers to improve care for patients with cah throughout childhood and young adulthood. journal of clinical psychology in medical settings

color discrimination in action: high-throughput measurement in immersive vr. precise measurement of color discrimination across color space is limited by the time and effort required to collect large psychophysical datasets. we investigated whether immersive virtual reality (vr) can support high-throughput measurement of color discrimination without compromising data quality. a standard four-alternative forced-choice odd-one-out task was embedded in an interactive vr environment inspired by the rhythm game beat saber, in which participants indicated the location of a chromatic target by slicing approaching cubes. stimuli were presented on a color-calibrated vr headset, and chromaticities were specified in dkl space. discrimination thresholds were measured for hue and chroma shifts around two reference colors. participants sustained response rates of approximately one trial per second while maintaining stable performance. thresholds replicated established asymmetries in color discrimination: hue thresholds were lower than chroma thresholds, and the hue-chroma ratio differed between color quadrants. a control experiment comparing vr-based slicing responses with matched keyboard responses revealed comparable psychometric fits and threshold estimates, indicating that motor engagement did not degrade measurement precision. questionnaire measures further showed significantly higher intrinsic motivation, enjoyment, and stimulation in the immersive condition relative to a classic static psychophysical task, without increases in reported pressure or discomfort. these results demonstrate that calibrated immersive vr can yield reliable color discrimination measurements at substantially increased throughput, providing a scalable approach for mapping the metric structure of color space. journal of vision

the near-death experience, an instance of higher-dimensional phenomenal consciousness? phenomenal consciousness has no satisfactory explanation in the strict natural scientific physicalist framework. this may be an indication of consciousness not being a causal outcome of neurophysics at all. if this is the case, there would be no grounds for postulating that the collapse of neurophysical structures at death would dissolve consciousness and its constituent elements. if consciousness does not disappear when neurophysical functions terminate, the near-death experience could be an indication of the continuation of consciousness after the collapse of brain functions. this would be in line with the proposal that higher spatio-temporal dimensionality is involved in the emergence and maintenance of phenomenal consciousness, even after death. journal of consciousness studies

the metaphysics of self-causality this article proposes an idealist/panpsychist metaphysics which connects the integrated information theory of consciousness (iit) with the work of the philosopher arthur schopenhauer: both frameworks describe the whole universe as consisting of different forms of auto-causation — or, as schopenhauer termed it, ‘the will’. iit proposes that consciousness is self-causality: the ‘information’ being measured in a system (e.g. a set of neurons in the brain) is causality (that is, any difference that makes a difference in the future), while ‘integrated’ means the system ultimately has causal power over itself. schopenhauer, too, claimed that all matter and energy consists of this kind of conscious self-causality, which makes sense according to charles darwin’s idea that what is extant is always that which self-perpetuates. the ‘is–ought problem’ is resolved in this article by explaining causality as valence, or the subjectively-experienced difference between good and bad (understood within this theory as satisfaction vs. frustration of causality from its own perspective). journal of consciousness studies

clearing the air about psychedelic spirituality psychedelic-assisted therapy occasions mystical experiences and their intensity often predicts therapeutic outcomes. owing to their spiritual import, psychedelics have been linked to supernatural thinking, religions, and cults. several authors within the psychedelic field argue these associations render the field scientifically and ethically questionable, with some calling for the ‘mystical framework’ of therapy to be replaced. this paper examines the controversy surrounding psychedelic spirituality to diagnose the issue and offer proposals for easing tensions. we argue that the question of the veracity of mystical insights is the primary source of controversy, but is a philosophical rather than scientific question and can, for now, be bracketed. we also argue that despite the charge of guruism and cultishness, researchers should be free to hold personal beliefs about the truth of these insights. given their profession, however, they ought to remain agnostic about such insights and maintain values and views inherent to the ethos of science in their professional conduct. journal of consciousness studies

how meaning turns out-of-body experiences into life change: a phenomenological qualitative study out-of-body experiences (obes) are vivid and extraordinary events that may lead to psychological transformation, though not all individuals who report them undergo lasting change. this qualitative study explores when and how obes become transformative. semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten healthy adults who had experienced spontaneous obes. thematic analysis focused on three variables: frequency, phenomenological complexity, and subjective interpretation. findings suggest that transformation occurred only in those who reported complex obes involving both displacement and entities) and interpreted them within a transcendental framework. participants with simple obes or a psychological interpretation showed no major change. all reported difficulties sharing their experience, often fearing disbelief or judgment. this highlights the importance of creating non-pathologizing environments where individuals can make meaning of such experiences, since interpretation appears to mediate their transformative impact. journal of consciousness studies

cross-modal experiences and the problem of phenomenal overlap mehta’s (2014) phenomenal overlap argument claims that successful cross-modal perception of one and the same object can, from the subject’s point of view, lack any shared element that presents that object, thereby challenging naã¯ve realism’s prediction that the same object should give rise to non-trivial phenomenal overlap. morgan (2017) replies by appealing to spatiality, arguing that vision and touch are at least alike in how they locate objects in space. this paper distinguishes an object’s intrinsic spatial properties from its relational spatial properties that obtain between object and subject, and argues that the similarity morgan invokes concerns, at best, the latter. it is too thin and too abstract to meet naã¯ve realism’s demand for relevant phenomenal overlap. more broadly, despite the range of proposals considered, cross-modal experience is systematically heterogeneous, and current forms of naã¯ve realism lack a clear account of how the same object could ground such pervasive intermodal differences. journal of consciousness studies

representational adequacy, natural selection, and quantum ontology: against a three-dimensionally spatial reality we human cognizers represent reality as three-dimensionally spatial. however, despite appearances to the contrary, i contend that the likelihood that reality is three-dimensionally spatial in accordance with our spatial representations is either low at worst or inscrutable at best, if these representations are the results of evolution. the key reason is that natural selection is interested primarily in fitness and not specifically in truth per se. dimensional veridicality of our spatial representations — i.e. the property of veridically representing the true dimensionality of space — is not required for adaptive behaviour. dimensional veridicality per se confers no additional evolutionary benefits. representational adequacy with respect to the relevant structure of reality suffices for evolutionary fitness without dimensional veridicality. independent considerations of quantum ontology — e.g. wave function realism — also challenge the common view that reality is three-dimensionally spatial. there are serious considerations that counsel agnosticism: we do not know, and hence should suspend judgment about, the true spatial dimensionality of reality. journal of consciousness studies

emotion, consciousness, and the heart–brain connection: a quantum biological perspective understanding human consciousness and emotion requires an interdisciplinary approach that can involve topics from neuroscience, physiology, and even quantum biology. this article proposes an integrative theory in which emotion is defined broadly as a concept that can capture different phenomena arising from brain activity, from instinctual affective responses to higher cognitive feelings, and considers how similar principles may apply to the heart’s intrinsic nervous system. we review evidence that the heart, with its own network of neurons, communicates with the brain to influence emotions and conscious experience. in this view, consciousness is considered as a complex phenomenon arising from the brain’s neurons and from a dynamic brain–heart system in which bodily states (especially cardiac signals) are represented in the brain to influence the creation of feelings of self and sentience. we further explore recent quantum biology perspectives on consciousness, which suggest that quantum-level processes in neurons (e.g. microtubule quantum states or nuclear spin dynamics) might contribute to the emergence of mind. preliminary connections to the philosophy of mind are examined, particularly how the exposed ideas address the ‘hard problem’ of consciousness and revive dual aspect and panpsychist interpretations. we discuss how heart–brain interactions and quantum processes together might provide new connections with conscious experience — including the age-old intuition of the ‘heart’ as an organ of wisdom and emotion. journal of consciousness studies

depressive symptoms mediate relationship of social support sources and loneliness among portuguese and immigrant population the present study proposed a model analysing the indirect effect of depressive symptoms in the relationship between social support sources (family, friends and significant other), and loneliness among portuguese and immigrant population. survey data sample consisted of 300 participants (150 portuguese and 150 immigrants) adults residing in portugal. the bootstrap result for indirect effect of depressive symptoms was significant, indicating that social support sources (family, friends, and significant other) had a significant effect on loneliness through the role of depressive symptoms. portuguese participants reported higher levels of depressive symptoms, perceived social support sources from friends and significant other compared to immigrant population. no gender differences were found between male and female participants and perception of the aforementioned variables. moreover, participants in the portuguese sample with age ranging from 18 to 30 years manifested higher levels of depressive symptoms and loneliness. meanwhile, individuals with secondary education in both samples reported higher levels of depressive symptoms. this research advances our understanding of social support sources from family, friends and significant other among portuguese and immigrant population while providing empirical data on the effect of depressive symptoms in the relation of social support and loneliness. psychological reports

attributional bias in the assessment of emotions. this study examined whether individuals display an attributional bias when identifying the source of their emotions. specifically, do people favor situational over dispositional explanations when attributing their negative emotions? sixty-eight participants completed two assessments to identify the cause of emotions-one evaluating their own emotions and another evaluating someone else's. dispositional and situational attributions were measured for both positive and negative emotions. the findings show that individuals tend to attribute their own negative emotions more to situational factors than to dispositional ones, but this pattern does not apply to others' emotions. this same asymmetry was not observed for positive emotions. this study broadens previous research on attributional bias to include personal emotional experiences. the work indicates that self-reports of the source of negative emotions could be biased. psychological reports

how much of a choice is physical inactivity? situated agency and institutional responsibility in public health the persistent gap between health intentions and actual behavior calls into question accounts of physical inactivity that treat it as a uniformly rational and freely chosen preference. this theoretical article draws on a non-systematic narrative synthesis of research on action initiation, individual differences relevant to physical activity, and public health ethics. action-initiation paradigms show that neural activity can precede reported awareness of simple actions and, in some cases, predict aspects of ensuing choices, but they do not establish that such activity causally determines complex behavior or explains physical activity maintained over time. evidence from behavioral genetics and developmental research indicates that self-regulatory characteristics and physical activity are partly shaped by heritable and early-life factors. we therefore develop an account of situated agency in which deliberation retains a meaningful role but operates under biological, developmental, and environmental conditions that are unequally distributed. within this framework, individual and institutional responsibility are complementary, with greater prospective responsibility falling on institutions where they can modify avoidable barriers while preserving individual choice. success should therefore be assessed not by equalizing individual capacity or increasing average population physical activity alone, but by whether improvements in access, uptake, and sustained participation extend to people facing greater baseline barriers. psychological reports

school-based creative arts therapists’ understanding of their perceived professional roles and pathways to systems integration school-based creative arts therapies are practiced across the united states (u.s.) and supported by an emerging literature base demonstrating their utility as youth mental health interventions. yet limited research has examined creative arts therapists’ (cats) experiences of professional integration, role clarity, or systems navigation in school settings, particularly within a u.s. context. this qualitative study explored how school-based cats understand the ways their work is perceived by professional peers, integrated into school systems, and sustained over time. nine credentialed cats, recently or currently working in u.s. schools, participated in two semi-structured focus groups via videoconference. transcribed data were derived from focus group discussions and analyzed across braun and clark’s six phases of thematic analysis within a contextualist epistemological framework. findings suggested that participants perceived their work as having contributed meaningfully to students’ socio-emotional functioning, provided inclusive support, and reduced systemic stress. participants also described challenges with professional recognition, misconceptions of their work, and structural constraints. participants further reported active advocacy via stakeholder education and relying on mixed peer support networks. implications suggest the need for collaborative efforts on multidisciplinary school teams as well as greater clarity in professional role and institutional functioning. arts in psychotherapy

an interdisciplinary framework integrating management, global occupational health, and neuroscience for workplace well-being workplace well-being is a critical determinant of global public health and organizational productivity. despite awareness of psychosocial risks and mental health in workplace, issues such as presenteeism, burnout, and chronic non-communicable diseases (ncds) continue to rise. we propose a multidisciplinary, theoretical framework that integrates organizational management, global occupational health, neuroscience, and positive psychology to assess and improve workplace environments, thereby benefiting both individual health and the common good. the goal is to foster effective, healthy, and efficient work. global occupational health supports the systematic assessment of workers’ capacities and vulnerabilities, the early identification of psychosocial risks, and the prevention of chronic ncds across diverse working populations. basic and applied neuroscience address the complexity of human emotions and cognition with their underlying neural mechanisms. evidence clarifies the neural circuits underpinning feelings, motivation, stress responses, and interindividual variability in coping with stress and job demands. positive psychology research provides non-pharmacological strategies—such as mindfulness, strengths-based approaches, and gratitude or meaning-centered interventions—that might reduce distress and enhance resilience when implemented according to scientific and ethical standards. integrating these domains allows policymakers, stakeholders, managers, occupational health professionals, and workers to design multi-level interventions that improve decision-making and promote healthier organizations. such an interdisciplinary approach offers a promising pathway to protect and promote workers’ well-being by designing evidence-informed strategies to prevent workplace-related mental disorders, accidents, and avoidable mortality. discover mental health

impact of multilingualism on cardiac autonomic activity, working memory and trait anxiety: a pilot study abstract recent years have witnessed a growing interest in how multilingualism modifies executive functions. heart rate variability (hrv), a noninvasive and innocuous indicator of cardiac autonomic function, can also capture individual differences that link cognitive performance with physiological and emotional profiles. this pilot study aimed to analyze the association of multilingualism with cognitive, autonomic, and emotional regulation during working memory (wm) tasks, while also considering trait anxiety (trait-a). nineteen young adults were classified as a monolingual group (mon, n = 9) or a multilingual group (mul, n = 10). participants completed the state‑trait anxiety inventory (stai) and the neuropsychological battery of executive functions and frontal lobes (banfe‑3). they then performed an n-back task at three difficulty levels while hrv linear and nonlinear indices were computed. mon exhibited high trait‑a, whereas mul showed moderate trait‑a. no significant differences were observed in the banfe-3 subtests, but mul achieved greater accuracy at the 2-back level of the n-back task. hrv indices showed a load-dependent decline in both groups; within-group analyses, however, revealed that mon and mul participants showed different within-group autonomic response patterns to cope with the rising cognitive load. these findings suggest that sustained multilingual experience may be associated with differences in autonomic–cognitive responses and attenuated anxiety-related disruptions, underscoring the value of hrv in characterizing individual variability in physiological and behavioral responses. cognitive processing
