body and mental health; a reflection and report of the indian association of dance movement therapy’s inaugural symposium abstract in recent years, notable progress has been made in the evolution of mental health care in india, with the enactment of the mental healthcare act, (2017) and the introduction of the national commission for allied and healthcare professions act, (2021). however, dance/ movement therapy (dmt) providers and consumers continue to experience common systemic issues. within this socio-political context, this article presents a discourse on the inaugural symposium of the indian association of dance movement therapy (iadmt), which aimed to position dmt as a distinct and significant part of the indian healthcare ecosystem. this landmark event focused on examining the role of the body in mental health and promoting somatic and other creative approaches across psychology, education, neuroscience, and policy. the manuscript summarizes contributions made by national and international presenters who offered diverse perspectives on culture, decolonization, legislation, the global landscape, and the body in mental health. the speakers offered actionable steps, including urging engagement in research to illustrate the effectiveness of dmt; inviting delegates to participate in their respective professional associations actively; asking government bodies to form a national council with representatives from all creative arts therapies’ associations; and the need for a standardized curriculum for all creative arts therapies. this article also reflects on the overarching themes that emerged from speakers and their exchanges with delegates, including a sense of belonging, professional identity, and advocacy. american journal of dance therapy

sociodemographic risk factors and wisc-iv cognitive profile in children with specific learning disorder: a case-control study specific learning disorder (sld) stems from genetic, environmental, and cognitive factors; however, their relative contributions and the diagnostic validity of cognitive measures remain unclear. this case-control study compared 35 children aged 8-12 diagnosed with sld according to dsm-5-tr criteria with 35 healthy controls of comparable age and sex. sociodemographic characteristics, developmental history, and wechsler intelligence scale for children-iv (wisc-iv) profiles were examined using t-tests, chi-square analysis, receiver operating characteristic (roc) analysis, and firth-penalized logistic regression. children with sld scored significantly lower on all wisc-iv indices, with large effect sizes (cohen's d = 0.84-1.39). these differences were maintained after adjusting for age, sex, and socioeconomic status. among the four factor indices, the working memory index had the highest discriminatory power (auc = 0.805). four independent predictors-age at first sentence production, a family history of sld, maternal education below college, and the absence of regular extracurricular activities-explained 78.0% of the variance and yielded an 88.6% classification accuracy. these findings indicate that genetic predisposition, environmental disadvantage, and early language delay converge in sld risk and support working memory assessment as a clinically useful diagnostic indicator. applied neuropsychology-child

viewpoint on hierarchical organization of multisensory integration and segregation abstract in this viewpoint, christoph kayser, uta noppeney, and tim rohe highlight the central role of normative bayesian frameworks, in particular bayesian causal inference, for explaining how the brain decides whether sensory signals should be integrated or segregated and how they are weighted by their reliabilities. in parallel, the multisensory correlation detector model is emphasized as a mechanistic proposal for how the brain computes spatial and temporal relations across sensory channels. together, these developments have shifted the field from merely locating multisensory processing in the brain to characterizing the specific computations implemented across cortical hierarchies. the authors outline current trends, such as model-based analyses of neuroimaging and neurophysiological data, increasing use of artificial neural networks to study multisensory processing at larger scales, and emerging work in naturalistic, real-world settings. they discuss ongoing controversies surrounding the influence of attention and tasks on multisensory integration, the limits of bayes optimality, and the role of neural oscillations, especially alpha rhythms, in shaping multisensory binding. they further advocate for stronger open-science practices and systematic replication of influential findings to consolidate the empirical and theoretical foundations of the field. finally, they encourage early-career scientists to develop strong methodological skills, cultivate their own conceptual ‘angle’, and actively engage with the multisensory community. multisensory research

aphantasia: a coaching case study in 1880, sir francis galton was the first to describe a condition where individuals were unable to create mental images. this condition, aphantasia, has many different definitions including as a total congenital absence of visual imagery. there is debate about whether it is a visual processing impairment only or a cluster of broader cognitive ones. this structured composite case study describes a senior executive with aphantasia who came to coaching wanting to improve her self discipline. it presents the client and coaches reflections on the utility of coaching and contains implications for coaching practice in this unusual area. international journal of evidence based coaching & mentoring

group-related psychosocial working conditions and individual health impairment: a multilevel approach that reflects intragroup agreement abstract: psychosocial job characteristics are typically examined at the individual level, whereas psychosocial risk assessment (pra) relies on group-level averages to evaluate work-related health risks. this study investigates how group-level averages of psychosocial risk factors, collected in the context of pra, relate to individual health risks. using data from 9,238 employees across 32 organizations, we applied a three-level generalized mixed model to estimate associations between group-level psychosocial risk factors and individual burnout and explored whether within-group agreement influences these associations. group-level demands and resources showed meaningful associations with individual burnout, whereas the effects of within-group agreement were inconsistent. these findings suggest that aggregated workplace-group scores reflect relevant aspects of psychosocial risk and can inform pra. incorporating group-level perspectives extends current theoretical and methodological considerations beyond individual data and may support a more nuanced interpretation of pra results when identifying areas that could benefit from targeted preventive measures. zeitschrift fur arbeits-und organisationspsychologie

working alone but together: the relationship between social support and radical and incremental creativity in coworking spaces abstract: individuals working in coworking spaces (i. e., coworkers) benefit from a professional office and like-minded people to escape the loneliness of working from home. social support in coworking spaces may play an important role in two forms of creativity: radical and incremental. the present study investigated whether social support by coworkers is positively related to both forms of creativity and whether this relationship is stronger for extraverted coworkers and those who spend more workdays in the coworking space. a total of 127 coworkers from austria, germany, and switzerland participated via an online questionnaire. hierarchical linear regression analyses revealed a positive association between social support and radical creativity. however, no such association was found with incremental creativity. the extent of coworking (i. e., number of workdays in a coworking space) moderated the relationship between social support and incremental creativity. we discuss practical implications for creativity in coworking spaces. zeitschrift fur arbeits-und organisationspsychologie

job boredom: a systematic literature review abstract: work-related boredom is a topic of increasing interest, and a growing amount of empirical research has investigated its correlates over the last few decades. this article extends previous research by providing a systematic review of the literature on job boredom, examining the applied definitions and measures, its most common correlates, antecedents, and outcomes as well as the processes linking job boredom to these correlates. the results revealed significant inconsistencies at the most fundamental levels, in terms of conceptual, theoretical, and methodological divergence among studies. based on the findings of this systematic literature review, we provide an overarching definition of job boredom and integrate it into a general model of workplace well-being, thus contributing to the development of an integrative theoretical framework of job boredom. we specifically offer a systematic overview of psychological processes underlying the experience of job boredom and its associations and provide future research directions. zeitschrift fur arbeits-und organisationspsychologie
an invaluable resource for group therapists: the second edition of the clinical practice guidelines international journal of group psychotherapy

multiculturalism and social justice themes in group counseling research: a latent dirichlet allocation analysis of published abstracts the importance of multicultural competence for effective group therapy practice has been widely acknowledged. gaining an understanding of trends in the canon of group therapy scholarship and identifying gaps has implications for future research and practice. as such, the present study examined trends in the scholarly literature on multiculturalism (e.g., culture, ethnicity, identity) and social justice (e.g., redressing inequities, systemic oppression, and privilege) in group psychotherapy. method: we conducted a psycinfo search for peer-reviewed, scholarly journal articles with keywords related to group counseling and multiculturalism and social justice. we analyzed the abstracts of the resulting 277 english-language articles published from 1947-2020 using latent dirichlet allocation (lda), a topic modeling approach. we present themes and discuss implications for future scholarship, as well as study limitations. international journal of group psychotherapy

einsamkeit im kontext von bindungsorientierungen zusammenfassung hintergrund einsamkeit und unsichere bindungsorientierungen sind eng miteinander verbunden und spiegeln schwierigkeiten wider, grundlegende bedürfnisse nach nähe und intimität zu erfüllen. einsamkeit resultiert dabei nicht allein aus einem mangel an kontakten, sondern ist häufig auch mit beziehungserwartungen und interpersonellen verhaltens- und regulationsmustern verbunden, die ebenso für bindungsunsicherheit relevant sind. ziel der arbeit (fragestellung) es wird dargestellt, wie unsichere bindungsorientierungen mit dem erleben von einsamkeit in verbindung stehen, und was über die längsschnittliche dynamik zwischen beiden konstrukten bekannt ist. außerdem wird aufgezeigt, wie psychotherapeutische interventionen an zentralen prozessen des interpersonellen erlebens und verhaltens ansetzen können. material und methoden in dieser narrativen übersicht werden zentrale konzepte, potenzielle wirkmechanismen und empirische befunde beschrieben. zudem werden klinische implikationen anhand ausgewählter therapeutischer ansätze und fallvignetten konkretisiert. ergebnisse und diskussion zahlreiche studien belegen einen zusammenhang zwischen höherer bindungsunsicherheit und einsamkeit. theoretische überlegungen sprechen für bidirektionale zusammenhänge, die empirisch bislang jedoch nur eingeschränkt belegt sind, da längsschnittliche befunde kein klares bild der zeitlichen dynamik liefern. therapeutisch erscheint es sinnvoll, an sozialen kognitionen, emotionsregulation und interpersonellem verhalten anzusetzen und dabei bindungssensitiv vorzugehen, um neue beziehungserfahrungen zu fördern. psychotherapie

einsamkeit im spannungsfeld zwischen stabiler eigenschaft und vorübergehendem zustand zusammenfassung hintergrund mit der konzeption psychologischer merkmale als stabile eigenschaften (traits) oder aktuelle zustände (states) sind zahlreiche theoretische und praktische implikationen verbunden. der vorliegende beitrag fasst diese implikationen für einsamkeit zusammen und bettet sie in die empirische befundlage ein. ziel der arbeit (fragestellung) der beitrag diskutiert, inwieweit trait- und state-perspektiven auf einsamkeit angemessen sind, sowie welche fragen und implikationen sich aus den jeweiligen perspektiven ergeben. material und methoden auf grundlage aktueller forschung wird erörtert, inwiefern einsamkeit die kriterien eines trait bzw. state erfüllt. ergebnisse die gesichtete literatur legt nahe, dass einsamkeit sowohl trait- als auch state-charakteristika aufweist und daher nicht als reiner trait oder reiner state verstanden werden kann. vielmehr bewegt sich einsamkeit im spannungsfeld zwischen diesen polen. gleichzeitig zeigt sich, dass dieses spannungsfeld bislang unzureichend untersucht ist, insbesondere im hinblick auf wechselwirkungen zwischen trait- und state-aspekten. diskussion einsamkeit stellt ein komplexes phänomen dar, das eine entsprechend differenzierte theoretische und empirische betrachtung erfordert. eine ausschließliche einordnung als trait oder state greift daher zu kurz. psychotherapie

flow and similar attentional states in autism and adhd: a scoping review of similarities and differences flow is a state of optimal engagement. autistic individuals and individuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adhd) might have variations in flow-like experiences, such as hyperfocus, autistic inertia, and monotropism, that diverge from traditional or typical definitions. following the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses extension for scoping reviews (prisma-scr) guidelines, we systematically reviewed 43 publications, including empirical studies, reviews, and other literature, to examine these constructs. results showed that attentional experiences associated with neurodivergence overlap with, but also differ notably from, typical flow. autistic inertia hinders task initiation and transitions, in contrast to flow’s seamless engagement. monotropism involves rigid, directed focus and repetitive, tenacious engagement, whereas flow allows for flexible adaptations to challenges. hyperfocus is like flow regarding intense concentration and immersion but is often involuntary, lacks clear goals, and is associated with emotional dysregulation. although commonalities exist across these attentional experiences, the greatest overlap occurs within autistic inertia, monotropism, and hyperfocus. attention in autistic and adhd individuals might be more dynamic than previously believed, with potential for transitions between these experiences. this fluidity can enhance focus and productivity but may also lead to negative outcomes, such as overly rigid fixation or difficulty engaging with and disengaging from tasks. clarifying these differences and overlaps can inform tailored interventions and supports, helping neurodivergent individuals manage focus, reduce task-related stress, and optimize productivity. perspectives on psychological science

dyadic: a scalable platform for research on human–human and human–ai conversation dyadic：面向人际与人机对话研究的可扩展平台 conversation is ubiquitous in social life, but the empirical study of this interactive process has been thwarted by tools that are insufficiently modular and unadaptive to researcher needs. to relieve many constraints in conversation research, in the current tutorial, i present an overview and walkthrough of a new tool, dyadic ( https://www.chatdyadic.com ), a web-based platform for studying human–human and human–artificial intelligence (ai) conversations using text-based or voice-based chats. dyadic is distinct from other platforms by offering studies with multiple modalities, ai suggestions (e.g., in human–human studies, ai can suggest responses to a participant), live monitoring (e.g., researchers can evaluate chats between communicators in real time), and survey deployment (e.g., likert-type scales, feeling thermometers, and open-ended text boxes can be sent to humans for in situ evaluations of the interaction), among other consequential features. no coding is required to operate dyadic directly, and integrations with existing survey and participant-recruitment platforms are offered. advances in methods and practices in psychological science

why most stereotypes are negative. stereotypes are a foundational construct in psychological science, often defined as beliefs concerning characteristic group attributes. we present a cognitive-ecological theory of social perception that predicts and explains why such characteristic attributes are likely negative, that is, why most stereotypes are negative. the theory assumes that, cognitively, people characterize groups by attributes that distinguish them from other groups. ecologically, positive social information is more frequent (i.e., positivity prevalence), and negative social information is more diverse (i.e., negativity diversity). if negative attributes are less frequent and more diverse relative to positive attributes, then they must be more likely to distinguish one group from another. consequently, the attributes people see as characteristic of a group are likely to be negative. we illustrate the predicted stereotype negativity across two studies and two existing data sets. we then formalize the theory and illustrate it with simulations showing that rare attributes can be highly diagnostic of group membership while applying to only a minority of group members. thus, the theory explains why most stereotype content is likely negative, despite the well-documented positivity prevalence, and why stereotypes may be diagnostic and comparatively accurate, despite being descriptively inaccurate. the theory explains stereotype negativity without requiring motivational derogation, essentialist group differences, or a general negativity bias, and it clarifies when positive stereotypes should occur. we also discuss the theory's relation to dimensional models of stereotype content and consequences for interventions aimed at reducing stereotype negativity. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). psychological review

carving stories at their natural joints. over the past three decades, psychology has documented the recurrence of specific themes in stories across cultures (e.g., love, alliances, monsters, and imaginary worlds) and linked them to identifiable motivational mechanisms (e.g., mate choice, cooperation, threat detection, and exploration). yet this body of work has remained fragmented, organized around individual themes rather than integrated into a unified account of what makes narrative content psychologically engaging. here, we propose the motivational-ingredient framework. we identify a set of motivational ingredients: core narrative features, each defined by the specific motivational mechanism it activates. drawing on evolutionary psychology, affective neuroscience, and the study of human motivation, we compile a comprehensive table of ingredients grounded in the current understanding of human motivational architecture. this framework offers a theory-driven, cross-culturally applicable foundation for the empirical study of narrative content, with implications for fields ranging from media psychology and computational humanities to education and public policy. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). psychological review

life strategies of loneliness among older people: constructs for developing a psychological diagnostic tool for assessing levels of experience context and relevance. the acceleration of population aging on a global scale and the complex of socio-psychological problems caused by this process actualize the creation of a methodological basis for positive life strategies for the elderly and a radical revision of existing psychological diagnoses, taking into account their reorientation to a prosperous old age. objective. the aim of this study is to provide a theoretical justification for the conceptual framework of psychological diagnostics of the levels of experiencing loneliness among elderly people, from the perspective of the prospects for its application in developing positive life strategies for addressing loneliness among elderly people. methods and materials. the methodological basis of the study consists of the ideas and concepts of scholars related to the experience of loneliness in older adults, which made it possible to build a theoretical foundation for developing a life strategy for addressing loneliness. in the development and implementation of the diagnostic process, the following approaches were used: a cognitive approach — to assess cognitive distortions and define diagnostic criteria; a psychodynamic approach — to develop diagnostics for measuring experiences of loneliness; an existential approach — to carry out differential diagnostics; ideas from symbolic interactionism and radical constructivism — to construct criteria and indicators of the levels of experiencing loneliness; and conceptual modeling of the levels of experiencing loneliness. results. the theoretical foundations and key concepts of the life strategy of loneliness have been developed, aimed at improving diagnostic procedures for psychologists in terms of developing life strategies for older people, assessing their readiness to overcome difficulties in the social sphere, supporting the consciously chosen strategy of dealing with loneliness, correcting maladaptive states, and preventing risks associated with extreme forms of experiencing loneliness. the criteria and levels of experiencing loneliness by older people have been identified in relation to the choice of life strategies and taking into account the “successful” and “unsuccessful” types of aging. conclusions. theoretical generalizations and the author’s conceptual framework for psychological diagnostics of the levels of experiencing loneliness are applicable for the development of positive life strategies and programs of psychological support and assistance for older people. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

development and validation of the questionnaire “metacognitive ability to program activities” context and relevance. in modern social conditions, the problem of studying the metacognitive abilities and skills of an individual engaged in various activities remains relevant, as the degree of awareness of one's own thinking strategies and methods of achieving effectiveness can significantly influence both the success of an individual's activities and the overall success of their self-realization. objective: to develop and test the validity and reliability of the questionnaire “metacognitive ability to program activities”, based on the understanding that the effectiveness of activities (educational and professional) is determined by the developed metacognitive abilities that allow an individual to timely assess and manage their own intentions and actions in order to achieve the goal of the activity. methods and materials. the study involved 1785 participants (m = 20, sd = 1.9, 77% women and 23% men). to test the reliability of the questionnaire, the following methods were used: the reflexivity questionnaire by a.v. karpov, the self-efficacy questionnaire (by j. maddox and m. scheier, adapted by a.v. boyarintseva), the general self-efficacy scale (by r. schwarzer and m. jerusalem, adapted by v.g. romek), the self-regulation style questionnaire (by v.i. morosanova), and the action control questionnaire (by j. kuhl, adapted by s.a. shapkin). statistical data analysis was performed using the r programming language (v.4.3) in the rstudio environment (v. 2023.12.1+402 “ocean storm”). reliability analysis (cronbach's alpha) was conducted using the “ltm” package functions, and confirmatory factor analysis was implemented using the “lavaan” package functions. graphical support was provided using the “semplot”, “ggplot2”, and “patchwork” packages. results. a questionnaire was developed and tested, the expediency of which was confirmed by a confirmatory factor analysis performed using the maximum likelihood method: gfi = 0.957, agfi = 0.943, cfi = 0.971, tli = 0.966, srmr = 0.025, rmsea = 0.049; checking the internal consistency of statements used in the questionnaire using the kronbach coefficient, (α = 0.943), convergent validity (links were found between the metacognitive ability to program activities and reflexivity, indicators of the ability to self-regulate, types of self-efficacy and control over actions (in the field of implementation and failures), where r ≥ 0.138 at p < 0.0001, as well as a test of discriminant validity, which revealed the absence of correlations with an indicator not included in the construct under study (involuntary control over the action during planning)). thus, construct validity can be considered pronounced. conclusions. the tested questionnaire includes 18 items, rated on a 5-point likert scale, which were developed based on the theoretical model of self-assessment of metacognitive behavior by d. lacosta. the questionnaire can be used to analyze the formation of metacognitive ability to program activities, as an element of metacognitive awareness of an individual, its social and intellectual maturity, as well as the possibility of forecasting, based on its application, the potential success of mastering educational and professional activities. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

approbation of a comprehensive time-to-contact test: factors influencing task performance context and relevance. the ability to extrapolate movement is the basis for successful interaction with dynamically changing objects in the environment. to perform such tasks, individuals may rely on either cognitive motion extrapolation or cognitive clocking based on a previously estimated time interval. objective: to probe a comprehensive implementation of time-to-contact tasks aimed at assessing the ability to extrapolate movement, to evaluate the effect of the implemented task types on response accuracy, and to study the effect of learning on task performance. methods and materials. the study sample consisted of six people aged 32 to 44 years. participants completed an experimental protocol consisting of different types of tasks in the morning and evening hours for at least 5 days (total number of measurements 10 to 28, m = 21.83, sd = 8.21). the task included seven levels reflecting different aspects of experimental tasks on extrapolation of movement. from level to level, the complexity of the movement trajectory, the ability to track movement (hiding the trajectory or its part), as well as orientation to the timing (fixed time of the ball's movement) sequentially varied. results. task performance accuracy varied significantly between the implemented levels, with the greatest difficulty being caused by complicating the movement trajectory and concealing it, while the fixed duration of the object’ movement did not facilitate task performance. no learning effect was observed across multiple test repetitions during the study. conclusions. the results indicate the leading role of the motion tracking mechanism, rather than the timing strategy, in the success of extrapolation. the proposed paradigm provides a sensitive tool for studying the cognitive mechanisms of contact time estimation. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

empathy ability in patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders: subjective assessment and experimental study data context and relevance. empathy is a multifactorial ability that determines the quality of interpersonal relationships and the level of social adaptation. research on empathy in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (ssd) yields mixed results: some studies show significant deficits, while others do not confirm these differences. a possible explanation for these contradictions is the limitations of self-report methods in measuring empathic abilities, with a noted lack of both domestic and international studies in which self-report data are compared with results from experimental measures of empathy. the relevance of such studies is determined by the need to identify the most accurate methods for assessing empathy in individuals with ssd and to highlight empathy deficits that are specific to this group. objective: to compare subjective assessments of empathic ability with data obtained from experimental research. hypothesis. indicators of empathic abilities in patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder, measured using questionnaire-based methods, are higher than those obtained through experimental approaches, as patients with rsd often underestimate their level of empathic deficit. methods and materials. the study involved 53 participants: 36 patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders and 17 mentally healthy controls, aged 21 to 50 years (mean age: m = 30.1, sd = 8.8 for patients; m = 30, sd = 7 for controls). the sample included 30 males and 23 females. to achieve the research aim, the following instruments were used: the symptomatic questionnaire scl-90, the hospital anxiety and depression scale (hads) for assessing psychopathological symptoms, the davis interpersonal reactivity index (iri), and the modification of fyodor vasilyuk and elena sheryagina’s technique of “comforting strategies” for evaluating empathic ability. results. no significant differences were found between the groups in empathy indicators measured via the iri questionnaire: patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders assessed their capacities for perspective-taking, compassion, and empathic concern at levels comparable to healthy controls (p > 0.05). the only significant difference was in empathic distress: during interpersonal situations involving others' feelings in crises, patients with rsd experienced more intense anxiety than controls. in the “comforting strategies” task, patients with schizoaffective disorder more frequently employed responses related to formal or counter-support (i.e., responses not aimed at normalizing the emotional state of the other person and even exacerbating their discomfort). their ability to provide reflexive and emotional support was lower than that of the control group (p < 0.01). conclusions. empathy indicators obtained via questionnaire methods in patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder are higher than those derived from experimental assessments. patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders more often than healthy individuals provide unproductive support, indicating that they tend to underestimate their level of empathic deficit. questionnaire-based methods are insufficiently effective for assessing empathic ability in these patients, as they fail to reveal existing deficits in empathic responsiveness to the emotional states of others. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

experimental study of the effect of fonts on fluency and word recall in a second language context and relevance. previous studies have identified changes in cognitive processes when disfluency is introduced (increased metacognitive estimates of cognitive processing difficulty). however, these studies have scarcely examined the effects of disfluency on second language learning. objective. the present study focuses on experimentally testing the effects of font on fluency and foreign language word memorisation. methods and materials. the study was conducted in a group of participants (n = 304; 62% female; mean age = 18.28) learning english as a foreign language. the participants' task was to memorise pairs of english words presented in either easy (arial and arial bold) or hard-to-read fonts (sans forgetica, a specially designed font that disrupts perceptual fluency by removing parts of letters and slanting). the participants were asked to reproduce the pairs by the first word a few minutes after memorisation and 2 weeks after memorisation. the number of correctly reproduced pairs was recorded. results. the findings indicated that participants preferred the easy font over the hard-to-read font, suggesting a preference for ease of processing. however, the study revealed that the font did not influence the memorisation of foreign language words. conclusions. the study's findings are consistent with those of previous disfluency research conducted on native language materials. at this stage, the use of hard-to-read fonts in educational practice is not recommended for disfluency induction. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

“the short dark tetrad questionnaire”: a russian adaptation in light of the general factor hypothesis context and relevance. this article presents a russian adaptation of the short dark tetrad (sd4) methodology, alternative to previously published by kornienko et al. (2022). the instrument expands the dark triad concept by including a fourth factor — everyday sadism. addressing the question of the independence of dark traits, various approaches to their conceptualization and diagnostics are analyzed: despite discrepancies between models, all directions indicate a pronounced overlap of these constructs and the existence of a common foundation or core. methods and materials. the study involved 826 participants aged 18 to 63 years (m = 36.58; sd = 9.82; 77% women) and, in addition to the sd4, utilized the dark factor (d70) instrument to assess individual traits as manifestations of a general dark factor, as well as the mini-ipip for the big five. results. confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency and reliability. results consistent with the literature were obtained: narcissism is positively associated with extraversion and openness, sadism negatively correlates with agreeableness; men exhibit higher scores on all scales except narcissism. the observed negative association of machiavellianism with openness requires additional empirical verification due to discrepancies in existing research. conclusions. despite moderate correlations between similar scales across different instruments, contradictory patterns of interrelationships between scales were found. the necessity for a deeper analysis of theoretical and operational differences in dark trait models is discussed, especially considering existing contradictions in the literature. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

experience of using the fifth edition of the wechsler intelligence scale for children (wisc-v) on a sample of russian children context and relevance. timely and adequate diagnostics of children's cognitive abilities is an important and urgent task facing psychologists working in the field of education and health care, as well as providing psychological counseling. the version of the wisc, currently widely used for quantitative diagnostics of intelligence in russia, is significantly outdated and is an adaptation of the first edition of the test, released in the middle of the last century. cognitive tests created without taking into account the developmental characteristics of children may not include an assessment of abilities relevant to the current situation of development and significantly distort the diagnosis. obviously, it is more appropriate to use more modern methods in assessing the intelligence of children of the alpha generation. objective. this study describes and analyzes the experience of using the fifth edition of the wechsler intelligence scale for children (wisc-v) on a sample of modern russian children. hypothesis. this version of the wechsler test for children is more consistent with modern requirements for assessing the intelligence in children. methods and materials. the sample of the present study consisted of 182 children living in moscow and the moscow region, age m = 107.5 months; sd = 26.4 months (48% boys). all children were tested for intelligence using the wisc-v. results. a data normality check, an analysis of mean values for subtests and indices, as well as correlation and factor analyses were conducted. the results indicated that the distribution of the full scale iq did not deviate from normality. all subtest scores demonstrated significant correlations with the primary index scales. however, the mean values for both subtests and primary index scales were higher compared to the data from the american sample. conclusions. the fifth edition of the wechsler intelligence scale for children (wisc-v) aligns more closely with contemporary psychodiagnostic standards, providing a comprehensive assessment of various cognitive characteristics, including fluid intelligence, working memory, and processing speed. however, for full adaptation of the test in russia, an expansion of the sample and clarification of the norms is required. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

locus of control as a factor in the structural organization of professionally important qualities of programmers context and relevance. one of the most important personal qualities — locus of control is studied in the context of its activity status and significant role — as a professionally important quality. objective. the research is aimed at identifying and explaining the specifics of the relationship between the locus of control and the effectiveness of information activity and the structural organization of its subject determinants, as well as its impact on them. hypothesis. the study is based on the hypothesis that there exists an initial link—characterized by a deterministic influence—between the locus of control and the structural organization of the core professionally significant quality of programmers, who serve as the most representative examples of the subject-information class of activities. methods and materials. the study design included the implementation of the methodology of structural-psychological analysis, the method of polar groups, and a set of psychodiagnostic methods aimed at determining the individual measure of the locus of control, as well as the basic professionally important qualities. the sample included a total of 288 people (215 men and 73 women; aged 18 to 58 years; m = 32.82, sd = 3.39); it specialists (programmers). results. there is a correlation between the individual measure of internality and the performance of programmers, which is represented at the level of a tendency, indicating a complex and indirect influence on performance. the locus of control has a priority influence on the degree of structural organization of professionally important qualities, and through it, that is, indirectly and significantly on the effectiveness of activity in general. this influence manifests itself in the fact that the measure of integration — the structural organization of these qualities in internals is significantly higher and, therefore, their total functional potential is also greater. conclusions. the hypothesis about the existence of a significant deterministic influence of the locus of control on the structural organization of the main professionally important qualities of information activity has been verified. it has been proven that the integration of the professionally important qualities of programmers' activity is significantly higher among internals than among externals; this pattern is one of the main factors that determine the differences in the effectiveness of the activity itself. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

does non-symbolic and symbolic representation depend on visual-spatial working memory across school education? context and relevance. representation of quantitative information is an integral component of understanding the world around us and underlies academic success in stem disciplines. at the same time, the accuracy of quantitative perception presented in various formats is dependent to varying degrees on visual-spatial working memory throughout school education, and both are considered a “double deficit” of cognitive resources in learning. objective: to study the specifics of the dependence of the accuracy of both non-symbolic and symbolic representation on visual-spatial working memory in schoolchildren at the primary (grades 4) and secondary (grades 9) school. methods and materials. the study involved 1,013 schoolchildren, including 511 fourth-grade students (mage = 10.7, sd = 0.5; 49.2% girls) and 502 ninth-grade students (mage = 15.9, sd = 0.5; 52.2% girls). the non-symbolic and symbolic representations were used by “number sense” and the “number line” tests, respectively (tikhomirova, malykh, 2022). visual-spatial working memory was assessed using the “corsi block test” (tikhomirova, 2025). results. the accuracy of non-symbolic representation is moderately and directly proportional to visual-spatial working memory; and this relationship is observed at both primary and secondary school, with a significant increase at the end of schooling. the accuracy of symbolic representation is less dependent on working memory and is observed only at the primary school. conclusions. the dependence of the accuracy of non-symbolic and symbolic representations on visual-spatial working memory is mediated by the format of quantity presentation and has a pronounced age-related character. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

interpersonal communication and subjective well-being of pregnant women: the role of communication channels context and relevance. pregnancy is accompanied by significant changes, which can place women at risk of experiencing poor subjective well-being (swb). communication with close people has been recognized as an important factor in promoting psychological well-being, but there is a lack of research on how different aspects of communication and the nature of the relationship are related to social support (ss) and swb for women during pregnancy with their first child. objective: to study how the volume of communication and the structure of a social network (in terms of communication channels, degree of emotional closeness and social category of contacts) are related to three aspects of swb (life satisfaction, well-being, richness of life). hypotheses. ss, life satisfaction, and who-5 are associated with communication with emotionally close people, while richness of life is associated with communication with less close people. face-to-face communication is associated with all indicators of swb and ss during pregnancy. methods and materials. the study involved 55 first-time expectant mothers at 3 to 8 months of pregnancy, working or studying at the time of the study (21—36 years old, m = 28 ± 4.4). an interview reconstructing a week-long experience of communication (directed communication) in three channels (calls, messengers, face-to-face). it also includes questions about the degree of emotional closeness of contacts on a scale from 1 to 10 and the social category of the contact. swb was measured using the scales: who-5 — index of general well-being, “life satisfaction” by e. diener and “psychological richness of life” by s. oishi, and the questionnaire of “social support” by s. cohen. results. the results showed that computer-mediated communication, unlike face-to-face communication, does not have a positive effect on swb and ss in pregnant women, with the exception of a positive effect on the richness of life. conclusions. it is shown that the key importance for swb is not the amount of communication, but their emotional closeness and channel of communication. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

the experience of happiness: the role of internal contradictions in the system of personal values context and relevance. happiness is one of the fundamental human experiences, yet its relationship with the internal consistency of personal values remains understudied. the theoretical framework of the study integrates d.v. kashirsky's concept of personal values, l. festinger's theory of cognitive dissonance, and the ideas of v. frankl and a.n. leontiev on the nature of happiness. objective: to identify the relationship between the experience of happiness and internal contradictions in the system of personal values (the discrepancy between the importance of a value and its realization). hypothesis. the experience of happiness is determined by the absence of pronounced internal contradictions in the system of personal values: the lower the level of dissonance between the importance of values and their realization, the higher the happiness index. methods and materials. the sample consisted of 94 students from moscow universities (86.2% female, age 17—39 years, m = 20.95; sd = 3.43). the following instruments were used: the kvs-2 personal values inventory (kashirsky, 2014) and the oxford happiness questionnaire (ohq) adapted by a.m. golubev and e.a. dorosheva (2017). pearson's correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis (backward method) were applied. results. significant negative correlations between the happiness index and internal contradictions were found in 19 out of 25 life domains. the strongest associations were revealed for the domains of freedom (r = –0.426), harmonious life (r = –0.411), and stability (r = –0.400). the regression model identified contradictions in the domains of love (β = –0.209), freedom (β = –0.284), and stability (β = –0.212) as significant predictors of happiness, explaining 24.9% of its variance. conclusions. the findings confirm that the experience of happiness is closely related to the internal consistency of personal values, particularly in the existentially significant domains of freedom, love, and stability. the results substantiate a two-level approach to psychological practice: harmonizing key value domains through concrete actions and fostering internal readiness for change. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

features of the influence of affective stimuli on human emotional activity objective: to study the autonomic correlates of emotional reactions when viewing affective images based on the theory of information representations/images, and to determine their relationship with the level of emotional maladjustment. methods and materials. the event-related telemetry method was used to assess the dynamics of the subjects' functional state. the level of emotional maladjustment was assessed using the grigoriev and tkhostov projective technique. the sam self-assessment test was used to analyze the subjects' subjective emotional response to stimulus images. results. two types of autonomic responses were identified among participants who demonstrated a standard subjective evaluation of affective stimuli according to the self-assessment manikin (sam). in 53% of the participants, an adequate autonomic response was observed, in which positive stimuli were associated with an improvement in functional state, reflected by an increase in adaptive potential and a decrease in the stress index. in the remaining 47% of the participants, a paradoxical autonomic response was identified, in which positive stimuli were associated with a deterioration of functional state. an association was found between the type of autonomic response and the level of emotional maladjustment, particularly with respect to the need for safety. conclusions. the results suggest that the nature of the autonomic response to stimuli is related to the level of emotional maladjustment in the subjects. this approach allows for the assessment of the dynamics of functional state within a single experimental session by continuously recording physiological indicators using event-related telemetry. this enabled the recording of changes in the state of each subject in response to the presentation of stimuli of different valence without the need for repeated measurements on different days. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

psychological resources of readiness for professional self-determination: meta-analysis context and relevance. a noticeable trend in the latest studies of sustainable professional development of the individual is the search and analysis of its psychological resources. despite the large amount of accumulated empirical data, the problem of their fragmentation actualizes the prospects for complex studies that could deeply and comprehensively reveal the specifics of relationship between various aspects of professional development and the resources that provide it. objective. the study had its purpose to use meta-analysis methods to consider how various psychological resources influence students’ readiness for professional self-determination. methods and materials. searching for publications for the period from 2019 to 2024 was conducted in 4 databases (researchgate, google scholar, sciencedirect, elibrary); 49 works were selected (8 in russian and 41 in english) with a total of 25,843 subjects. the random-effects model was used for evaluating the effect sizes of psychological resources of readiness for professional self-determination at the level of individual studies. meta-regression analysis was implemented for a generalized assessment of the contributions of various psychological resources to the students’ readiness for professional self-determination. results. the meta-analysis demonstrated a significant influence of regulatory, motivational and emotional resources on the students’ readiness for professional self-determination. the effects and contribution of self-positioning, according to the effect size analysis and meta-regression, were insignificant or, in the case of certain aspects of professional self-determination, had moderate significant values. conclusions. the study confirmed the effects and general contribution of psychological resources to the students’ readiness for professional self-determination. the most significant predictors of readiness for professional self-determination are, first of all, regulatory, personality, emotional and motivational resources. prospects for further research may be associated with implementing narrow meta-analyses focused on studying the specific effects of certain psychological resources in relation to particular aspects of professional self-determination of an individual. eksperimentalnaya psikhologiya

delayed bereavement in early adulthood: a new perspective background and relevance. a comparative analysis of the psychological consequences of natural versus sudden, violent loss of a significant close person during early adulthood is being conducted. the research design, aimed at assessing the severity of traumatization, comorbid psychopathological symptoms considering the type and time since loss, as well as the effectiveness of personal resources, creates an opportunity to examine the role of posttraumatic stress in the period of adaptation to loss. the relevance of the study is determined by the need for systematic clarification of the differential diagnostic criteria of complicated grief and posttraumatic stress. objective. to analyze the psychological consequences of experiencing different types of loss and to identify arguments supporting the differentiation between manifestations of the grieving process and symptoms of posttraumatic stress at different time intervals following the traumatic event. hypothesis. the severity of psychological consequences following the loss of a close person is determined by the type of loss, the time elapsed since the event, and the presence or absence of emotional-cognitive resources that facilitate the completion of the grieving process and the reduction of posttraumatic stress symptoms. methods and materials. the study sample consisted of young adults (18 to 32 years old, m = 22,3) with a history of losing a significant close person (n = 103), subjectively assessed as the most traumatic event in their personal experience. to test the research hypothesis, the following set of measures was used: the posttraumatic stress disorder check list (pcl-5), adapted in 2017 at the institute of psychology of the russian academy of sciences (tarabrina, kharlamenkova, padun, et al., 2017); symptom check list of psychopathological symptoms in the russian adaptation (tarabrina et al., 2007); c. ryff's scale of psychological well-being, adapted by l.v. zhukovskaya and e.g. troshikhina (2011); the behavioral control questionnaire (e.a. sergienko, g.a. vilenskaya, i.i. vetrova); and the questionnaire «age-of-me» (barak, 2009), adapted by e.a. sergienko (2011). results. it was demonstrated that the pattern of psychological consequences of losing a significant close person in young adulthood is determined by a combination of factors, including the cause of death, the time elapsed since the event, as well as the degree of availability and utilization of emotional-cognitive resources necessary for integrating the experience of loss. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

level and main factors of distress of participants of the special military operation hospitalized for acubarotrauma objective. to assess the severity of ptsd symptoms and the level of psychological distress among participants of the special military operation hospitalized with acoustic-barotrauma; to identify the primary clinical and socio-psychological factors contributing to distress; and to determine key stress-coping resources in order to enhance the effectiveness of rehabilitation and psychological intervention programs. methods. the study was conducted at the national medical research center for otorhinolaryngology of the fmba of russia, with the support of the "defenders of the fatherland" foundation, between february 2025 and may 2026. a total of 102 male respondents aged 29 to 73 years (m = 51 years, sd = 10) participated. the study was carried out in a single phase, during which participants completed a personal questionnaire to gather anamnestic and socio-demographic data, the pcl-5 questionnaire to screen for ptsd symptoms, and a modified version of holland’s "distress thermometer" to assess the level and factors of subjective distress. results. a high level of psychological trauma is observed among participants of the special military operation who have sustained acoustic trauma. between 18.4% and 27.6% of patients exhibit pronounced symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) at a clinical level, indicating a need for professional assistance from specialists—specifically clinical psychologists and, in some cases, psychiatrists. mean scores for subjective distress associated with the identified hearing impairments reach 3.4 out of 10. more than half of the respondents express serious concerns regarding their future, employment prospects, and financial well-being due to hearing loss caused by acoustic trauma. key stress-coping factors for these individuals include both external sources of support (family, friends, medical staff, financial aid) and internal resources (positive mindset, humor, religious beliefs, and prior experience coping with adverse events). marital status is a statistically significant factor determining the level of psychological distress; unmarried participants exhibit significantly higher levels of distress. notably, while marital status influences the overall level of distress, it does not affect specific ptsd symptoms, suggesting that these phenomena have distinct underlying natures. conclusions. psychological distress in this group of patients is pronounced and is driven not only by current clinical symptoms but also by anxiety regarding long-term life prospects—factors that must be taken into account when designing rehabilitation pathways. these findings justify the need to integrate psychological assessment and psychosocial rehabilitation into the standard treatment and rehabilitation protocol for patients with acoustic barotrauma, starting from the time of hospitalization. in approximately one-quarter of the patients examined, ptsd symptoms reach a clinically significant level, highlighting the need to involve mental health specialists in their care. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

the role of maternal stress and parenting style in the development of child stress in the context of armed conflict context and relevance. the mental health of mothers and children in the context of armed conflict is a critically important issue. research indicates that maternal stress and maladaptive parenting styles are key mediators in the transmission of the psychological consequences of trauma from mother to child, even in the absence of the child's direct exposure to combat. however, the nature of the influence of distance from the conflict zone on these processes and the unique contribution of maternal stress and parenting practices to child stress, after accounting for the regional factor, remain unclear. objective. to assess the influence of proximity to the combat zone on the level of maternal stress, parenting styles, and child stress, as well as to determine the unique contribution of maternal stress and parenting practices to the level of child stress after controlling for the influence of the regional factor. hypotheses. 1) distance from the combat zone is negatively associated with the level of maternal stress, negative parenting styles, and the level of child stress. 2) maternal stress and parenting style make a unique contribution to the child's stress level that cannot be explained solely by the adverse regional environment. methods and materials. the study involved 3544 mothers of preschool-aged children (maternal ages: m = 35.87, sd = 5.43) residing in the donetsk people’s republic (dpr), the republic of crimea, and other regions of russia. russian-language versions of questionnaires were used: the perceived stress scale (assessment of maternal stress), the perceived stress scale for children (mother's assessment of child stress), and the parenting practices questionnaire (identification of parenting types: positive, inconsistent, use of punishments). data analysis employed descriptive statistics, cluster analysis, analysis of variance (anova), and hierarchical regression. results. the level of maternal stress decreased linearly with increasing distance from the conflict zone. the level of child stress and the use of a punitive inconsistent parenting style were significantly higher in the dpr but did not differ between crimea and other regions. hierarchical regression analysis showed that maternal stress and, especially, the punitive inconsistent parenting style make a unique and significant contribution to the level of child stress, exceeding the influence of the regional factor. conclusions. parenting styles are an independent and the most powerful risk factor for the development of child stress. the obtained results emphasize the necessity for comprehensive interventions aimed simultaneously at reducing maternal stress and correcting parenting practices, both in active conflict zones and in relatively prosperous regions. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

hardiness and psychological adjustment of children, adolescents and their parents undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (hsct) context and relevance. hsct is currently curative therapy for several life-threatening diseases in children and adolescents. due to the high stress-inducing nature of this treatment, the increase in the number of patients receiving it, psychological adjustment of patients to hsct as well as support during the treatment and subsequent rehabilitation are increasingly acute. objecive. the aim was to investigate the role of resilience of patients and their parents in psychological adaptation to stress during hsct. methods and materials. the study was conducted on patients (8-18 years aged) with onco-hematological, hematological and immune diseases, as well as their caring parents (n=47). the set of questionnaires was presented to the subjects 3 times during hsct (at the conditioning stage, on +3 and +12 weeks after hsct). results. the results revealed a key role of hardiness in the composition of the individual resources of patients and their parents for less distress during hsct, higher quality of life, subjective well-being and productive copings. conclusions. the level of hardiness determines the difference in the success of psychological adaptation to hsct both for children and their parents. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

from intrusion to hallucination: an integrative psychological model of traumatic memory transformation in ptsd context and relevance. ptsd involves not only intrusions and flashbacks but also multimodal hallucinations, previously read as a manifestation of comorbid psychosis, which hindered the development of a unified model linking hallucinations to traumatic memory mechanisms. objective. to formulate an integrative model of the intrusion-to-hallucination transition in ptsd and its specificity in combat trauma. methods and materials. a theoretical synthesis of research on traumatic memory and neuro-metacognitive correlates of perceptual decompensation. results. a cascade model is proposed: the intrusion-to-hallucination pathway as phase transitions driven by traumatic memory disintegration, dissociation, metacognitive dysregulation, and dominance of traumatic priors over sensory input; combat trauma catalyzes multimodality via cumulative exposure and moral dissonance. conclusions. hallucinations are the peak of the re-experiencing continuum, transitioning into a discontinuum (a dissociative register). the cascade model integrates neurocognitive and psychological levels of analysis of hallucinatory experience and provides a phase-specific map of therapeutic targets. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

youth coping in the context of the stress-inducing impact of the special military operation's information environment context and relevance. young people in modern russia find themselves in the complex context of a military conflict and the associated information impacts. in this regard, the task arises of searching for mechanisms to mitigate the risks of deterioration in the psycho- emotional health of young people against the background of specific stress. the theoretical basis of the study was a contextual approach to the study of stress in young people who found themselves in conditions of varying territorial proximity to the special military operation (smo), as well as the dispositional theory of coping. the aim of the study was to identify and analyze the general and specific features of coping with the stressful impact of the information context of a special military operation in young people with different territorial proximity to the military conflict zone. methods and materials. the study involved 582 people aged 17 to 36 years (m = 20.9; sd = 6.3). methodological complex: a semi-structured questionnaire processed using the method of content analysis; an abbreviated version of the russian-language method for assessing coping strategies (cope- 30), a non-situational version (m.a. odintsova, n.p. radchikova, l.a. aleksandrova, 2022); self-assessment scales for indicators of personal existential security; self-assessment scales for prevailing emotions arising in response to incoming information. results. the level of stress associated with the information context in young people varies depending on their territorial proximity to the svo, manifesting itself most acutely among residents of the border zone and crimea. young people from active combat zones are characterized by emotional blunting and decreased existential security; residents of border areas demonstrate higher levels of negative emotions. quantitative data indicate a generalized tension in the use of coping strategies, which indicates a destabilization of psychological regulation. the most common coping strategies were limiting information exposure and distraction/switching, while at the dispositional level, resilience to information overload is associated with proactive coping strategies. conclusions. young people's coping with stress associated with the information context in the context of the svo is complex, but often tense and internally contradictory. high activity in the use of coping strategies serves not so much as an indicator of successful adaptation as a symptom of the destabilization of psychological regulation mechanisms under the influence of a chronic stressor. the findings highlight the importance of considering the territorial context, including the paradoxical effects of adaptation to extreme conditions, and developing targeted psychological support programs aimed at developing flexible and effective information hygiene and emotional self-regulation skills. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

theoretical analysis of scientific approaches to the problem of psychological trauma context and relevance. the problem of psychological traumatization has become especially relevant due to contemporary events associated with multiple societal crises and extreme situations such as military conflicts, socioeconomic instability, terrorist attacks, natural disasters, widespread severe illnesses, and the aftermath of pandemics. objective. to systematize key modern approaches to understanding psychological trauma within both russian and international academic literature. methods and materials. this paper employs theoretical analysis and synthesis of scientific publications addressing psychological traumatization from the last twenty years. results. the article outlines contemporary russian and foreign scientific perspectives on psychological trauma. the approaches to post-traumatic stress by n.v. tarabrina, the procedural model by n.e. kharlamenkova, the multiresource coping model by d.a. leontiev, the psychodynamic approach by n.s. khrustaleva, m.m. reshetnikov, the crisis approach by a.g. karayani, yu.s. shoigu, the medical approach by yu.a. alexandrovsky, k.a. idrisov, and others are considered; the basic concepts, theories, and diagnostic tools are defined. additionally, it reviews psychodynamic and cognitive-behavioral approaches prevalent in international psychology. the primary research areas concerning psychological trauma and continuous traumatic stress are also explored. conclusions. in the most generalized form, psychotrauma can be considered as the result of a complex interaction of personality and unfavorable environmental conditions. psychological trauma is a natural but extreme adaptive reaction to a stress level exceeding the resources of the psyche. further research requires a detailed description of the mechanisms of its occurrence, the study of sustainability resources, complex cases and ways to overcome. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

artificial intelligence in psychotherapy: a review of the effectiveness and risks of using ai chatbots context and relevance. the growing implementation of artificial intelligence (ai) in sychotherapeutic practice is driven by the increasing need for effective, scalable, and accessible tools to support individuals with mental health conditions, including post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd). objective. this literature review aims to synthesize international empirical studies evaluating the effectiveness of ai chatbots in psychotherapy. methods and materials. the analysis included 25 english-language publications examining these systems from clinical, methodological, and ethical perspectives. results. the first thematic cluster addresses the therapeutic effectiveness of ai chatbots used either independently or alongside in-person therapy. numerous studies report short-term reductions in symptoms of depression, anxiety, and ptsd, as well as increased patient engagement and emotional resilience. adaptive and personalized ai systems, as well as hybrid models combining ai with human therapist involvement, are considered particularly promising. the second cluster highlights limitations, such as methodological heterogeneity, lack of long-term data, superficial diagnostic interactions, and potential safety risks in crisis situations. issues of privacy, trust, the limits of ai autonomy, and the distribution of responsibility are also discussed. conclusions. overall, the review demonstrates the significant potential of ai chatbots in psychotherapy while emphasizing the need for further development, clinical validation, and ethical regulation to ensure their safe and effective use. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

the effect of post-traumatic stress on the dynamics of emotional state in patients with cerebral meningioma after stereotactic radiosurgery context and relevance. cerebral meningioma is the most prevalent benign tumor of the central nervous system. despite favorable outcomes following stereotactic radiosurgery (srs), a considerable proportion of patients continues to experience significant psychological distress. post-traumatic stress symptoms play a key role in the formation and chronification of emotional disadaptation, being associated both with the current illness situation and with prior traumatic experience. the persistence of emotional disadaptation symptoms, including post-traumatic ones, in the absence of tumor progression points to their predominantly psychogenic nature and highlights the need to examine the role of pts in the dynamics of adaptation to the disease. objective. to examine the longitudinal dynamics of emotional disadaptation, including post-traumatic stress symptoms, in patients with сerebral meningioma, identify individual adaptation trajectories, and determine the role of prior traumatic experience in their formation. methods and materials. sixty-two patients with cm (91% female, mean age 57,8 years) underwent repeated psychological assessment six months after srs. the assessment battery included the modified distress thermometer (holland), pcl-5, beck depression inventory, spielberger—hanin anxiety scale, ruminative response scale, and the somatosensory amplification scale. statistical analyses comprised paired-sample t-tests, repeated-measures anova, hierarchical cluster analysis, and binary logistic regression (ibm spss statistics 23). results. at six months post-srs, pts symptoms remained at baseline levels (p = 0,583); statistically significant improvement was observed only for state anxiety (p < 0,01). cluster analysis identified three adaptation trajectories: improvement (43,5%), stability (40,3%), and deterioration (16,1%). logistic regression revealed three significant predictors of an unfavorable trajectory: prior traumatic experience (or = 6,49; p < 0,01), elevated rumination (p < 0,01), and younger age (p < 0,05). conclusions. the findings demonstrate the persistence of pts symptoms after successful cm treatment and confirm the key role of prior traumatic experience in the chronification of emotional disadaptation. patients with a traumatic history are 6,5 times more likely to show deterioration (or = 6,49; p < 0,01). the results support the need for targeted pts screening and differentiated psychological support incorporating trauma history assessment at the pre-srs stage. konsultativnaya psikhologiya i psikhoterapiya-counseling psychology and psychotherapy

positioning vygotsky for inclusive education: a psycho-philosophical context inclusion has its roots in two foundational ideas: equity and a rights-based perspective on education, as articulated in national and global policies. however, inclusion, in its true sense, has been misunderstood as helping learners adjust to the mainstream. this misleading idea has raised serious concerns about the essential role of diversity in inclusion. in its narrow terms, the physical arrangements for learners with disabilities have been accepted as inclusion, thereby overlooking the underlying assumptions about development, learning, and diversity that actually shape the discourse of inclusive educational practices. this makes it imperative to lay out the theoretical and philosophical foundations of inclusive education. vygotsky, while avoiding individualistic and deficit-driven approaches, reframes cognitive engagement as socially mediated and culturally situated processes. considering diversity an opportunity rather than a barrier in the classroom, vygotsky emphasises dialectical materialism and the social origins of higher mental processes as vital to cognitive practices. in this context, this discourse analysis-based article revisits the core constructs of vygotskian theory, such as co-construction, mediation via cultural tools, internalisation, perezhivanie, the zone of proximal development, and the shaping of thought with language, to conceptualise inclusive education within this framework. this conceptualisation indicates the positioning of certain essentialities, such as dialogue, scaffolding, collaboration, and interaction with peers, in creating inclusive educational opportunities for all learners. the article also explores the potential to apply vygotsky’s ideas to pedagogical processes, assessment, and teacher preparation, focusing on teachers' roles as mediators in developing supportive, collaborative learning environments. the article concludes by establishing the strength of vygotsky’s theoretical framework in shaping the scope of inclusive education. psikhologicheskaya nauka i obrazovanie-psychological science and education

afterword to the correspondence between luria and piaget the correspondence between artur luria and jean piaget began in 1929, following their meeting at the 9th international congress of psychology in new haven. this article examines the history of their academic and personal relationship, their joint projects involving lev vygotsky which never came to fruition, and the history of the english translation of “thinking and speech”, with a foreword by piaget. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

specific features of communicative interaction between a psychologist and a virtual client in psychotherapeutic speech skills training context and relevance. the quality of psychotherapeutic speech is a key predictor of therapeutic effectiveness and the strength of the therapeutic alliance. the development of ai simulator for training psychotherapists requires evaluating their ecological validity. the study is theoretically based on models of therapeutic discourse analysis. objective. to describe the specific characteristics of verbal interaction between a psychologist and an ai simulator and to identify the limitations of such interaction. a secondary goal is to propose a methodology or a set of metrics for evaluating this interaction. hypothesis. the text of the training sessions will exhibit all structural and thematic features inherent in psychotherapeutic sessions in general. methods and materials. the study involved 10 practicing psychologists (8 female, age m = 35, sd = 2). the corpus consisted of 16 text dialogues with a standardized synthetic client, “anna”. data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and content analysis with coding of speech acts according to the verbal response modes (vrm) taxonomy. the frequency of intervention types was recorded. results. the most frequent speech acts were “directive instruction” (48,9%) and “exploratory question” (23,7%). a significant portion consisted of alliance-building interventions, particularly “validation and empathy” (16,9%). however, speech acts related to client resistance were completely absent (0%). conclusions. the significance of the “zone of proximal development” concept for training psychotherapists is highlighted. the dialogue in a simulated environment was confirmed to be authentic but functionally limited. it corresponds to real practice in technical execution but lacks relational skills due to the “ideal”, compliant behavior of the synthetic client. future ai trainers should include non-compliant behavior scenarios. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology
review on the book “dialogs on l.s. vygotsky” kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

russia in the representations of young belarusians: the image of the country and attitudes towards integration cooperation context and relevance. the significance of preserving cooperation between russia and belarus dictates the need to study young people's attitudes towards this cooperation with the aim of identifying possible socio-psychological barriers to its development. objective. examining young belarusian students' perceptions of russia and their attitudes towards closer relations between the two countries. research question. what are the preconditions of belarusian youth’s attitude towards integration cooperation between russia and belarus in the current context, and to which psychological factors might they be related? methods and materials. in may 2025, an online survey was conducted among 106 belarusian students (m = 19,0, sd = 1,72, 57% male) aged 18-25 using open-ended questions developed by the authors. results. most of the students interviewed had a positive image of russia. while a positive attitude towards closer relations between the two countries prevails, awareness of the scope of cooperation between belarus and russia is low among many students. most respondents view russia as a non-threatening state for belarus. however, one-tenth of the students think that a threat does exist. conclusions. the results of the study show that there are favorable socio-psychological grounds for maintaining a positive attitude towards closer relations between belarus and russia among most young belarusians. at the same time, most students are unaware of the extent of cooperation between the two countries, and many do not consider it to be significant. some students express fears about belarus potentially losing its sovereignty as a result of closer ties with russia. all of these factors could hinder the development of effective cross-country engagement between belarus and russia. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology
