artificial intelligence as a cultural tool: heuristic potentials and limitations of the metaphor context and relevance. the large-scale adoption of artificial intelligence systems in education, professional activity, and everyday life challenges established psychological conceptions of development, mediation, and subjectivity. within cultural-historical psychology, ai is most often analyzed through the metaphor of a cultural tool, which appears to preserve theoretical continuity but may obscure the fundamentally novel nature of digital sociotechnical systems. objective. through theoretical analysis, to identify the advantages and disadvantages of considering artificial intelligence as a cultural tool within the logic of cultural-historical psychology. hypothesis. the cultural tool metaphor has significant heuristic potential for analyzing the mediation of activity involving ai; however, its explanatory capabilities are limited and, when applied uncritically, lead to conceptual reductions. theoretical framework. the study is based on a reconstruction of key tenets of the cultural-historical and activity traditions, as well as on interdisciplinary work in the philosophy of technology, the anthropology of digital technologies, and critical ai studies. results. it is shown that ai radically breaks the link between the mediation of activity and the mediation of development, redistributes agency and responsibility, and also generates effects of reverse mediation, influencing the subject's way of thinking and self-evaluation. it is revealed that the language of the cultural tool carries a latent normative effect, contributing to the naturalization of technological change. conclusions. artificial intelligence represents the first mass cultural means introduced without a cultural-psychological project of subject development. this positions ai not merely as an object of analysis but as a challenge to cultural-historical psychology itself, necessitating a reconsideration of key concepts. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

theoretical and applied psychology of communication context and relevance. the year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the birth of the renowned russian psychologist, philologist, and educator alexei alekseevich leontiev (1936-2004). in keeping with established scientific tradition, events dedicated to this anniversary celebrate the scientist's ideas through the lens of the current state of science and practice. publications aimed at drawing attention to the scientist's legacy occupy a prominent place among these scientific events. this article discusses the collection of scientific papers “psychology of communication” (moscow: smysl, 2026), published for the anniversary and addressed to a wide range of readers in the humanities. objective is to briefly introduce the works of a.a. leontiev included in this collection, as well as to explore the rationale for collecting these works under one cover and presenting them as a coherent whole. hypothesis. an analysis of a.a. leontiev's scientific legacy in the field of communication studies provides grounds for considering the results of his research from various perspectives—linguistic, psychological, and pedagogical—as reflected in relevant publications. methods and materials. the method used was a historical and methodological analysis of a.a. leontiev's works based on the publications included in the publication under review. results. the evolution of communication research is demonstrated, and the logic of the author's scientific research is traced, beginning with works in the field of psycholinguistics and ending with general publications on the psychology of communication, which suggest the possibility of applying an activity-based approach to communication processes. conclusions. an analysis of a.a. leontiev's research on communication issues demonstrates the development of an original, interdisciplinary approach to the study of communication. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology
a book in dialogue: l.s. vygotsky’s ideas a century on kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

subject agency in the context of digital childhood: possibilities for its emergence and suppression context and relevance. the main challenge posed by the digitalization of education, which involves the use of neural networks and artificial intelligence, is the need to restore the student’s own subject agency when solving educational tasks. subject agency in activity is the most important condition for organizing the processes of developing the intellectual abilities of students and teachers. objective. determine the conditions under which ai is used by students as a means of solving tasks that ensure the initiation of subject agency in educational and project‑based activities. hypothesis. the initiation of students' subject agency will be brought about by a special reconstruction of the digital systems used by master's students — search engines, ai systems — in order to transform them into a means of organizing their own activity for solving specially posed tasks. such tasks, implemented in the process of students' learning, will make it impossible for master's students to directly handle digital system. results the authors associate the solution of the research tasks formulated by them with a change in the forms of teaching in their specific work with master's students based on the creation of special educational tasks. the most important type of task is the task that initiates subject agency in educational work. conclusions. the most important condition for restoring students' subject agency when using ai is the use of tasks in which students themselves identify the limitations of the answers offered by ai systems. in this case, the student is faced with the need to justify their new solution, which does not coincide with the answers offered by the ai. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

verbal-logical thinking and reading skills: a cross-lag analysis of mutual influence at the stage “kindergarten—primary school” context and relevance. the relevance of a longitudinal analysis of cause-and-effect relationships between verbal-logical thinking and the acquisition of reading skills stems from the need to address a fundamental problem in psychology—the relationship between mental development and learning. in practical psychology, this research is associated with the search for early individual psychological markers of potential learning difficulties. the processes of mental development and learning to read are closely interrelated throughout general education, but the direction and strength of these causal relationships may change during the transition from preschool to the initial stage of general education. objective. this study examines the interplay between verbal-logical thinking and reading skills during the transition from kindergarten to the first grade of primary school. methods and materials. a total of 260 children (50,1% female) participated in the study at two time points: during their preschool preparatory groups (mage = 6,82, sd = 0,3) and one year later, following the completion of their first year of primary education (mage = 7,83, sd = 0,3). verbal-logical thinking was assessed using a mental development test measuring abstraction, classification and generalization, and analogical reasoning. reading proficiency was evaluated according to reading method, ranging from non-reading to reading in whole words. data were analyzed using cross-lagged panel structural equation modeling. results. the analysis of cross-lagged relationships revealed a bidirectional nature of the relationship between verbal-logical thinking and reading proficiency during the transition from preschool to primary school. the most pronounced direct proportional effect was observed in the direction where the level of reading proficiency achieved by the end of the preschool period influences the subsequent development of cognitive operations—abstraction, classification and generalization, and analogical reasoning—at the onset of formal schooling. conclusions. the specific nature of the causal relationship between the development of verbal-logical thinking and reading acquisition was identified and interpreted within the framework of cultural-historical psychology. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

correspondence between a.r. luria and j. piaget 1930–1966 years the letters exchanged between the renowned 20th-century psychologists aleksander luria and jean piaget reveal the intricate and sensitive process of fostering collaboration between scholars from two distinct and frequently opposing social “camps”. the unseen participant (and probably the initiator) of these exchanges was lev vygotsky. this correspondence is being published for the first time. notes by a.d. maidansky and e. yu. zavershneva. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

the gamification dilemma in education: a compromise model between extrinsic motivation and existential well-being context and relevance. gamification is widely introduced into higher education as a means of enhancing academic motivation, yet its effects are contradictory: short-term gains in engagement are often accompanied by increased anxiety, burnout, and alienation. existing approaches assess effectiveness mainly through instrumental metrics, ignoring students' subjective experiences and existential well-being. this contradiction and the theoretical vacuum around it determine the relevance of the study. objective. to identify the contradiction between extrinsic motivation and the existential well-being of students in a gamified environment and to develop a theoretical compromise model. hypothesis. the gamification dilemma is a systemic property arising from the contradiction between the external nature of its stimuli and the internal conditions of well-being; there are “critical points” in the design, the management of which allows a compromise to be found. methods and materials. the study involved 180 undergraduate students of lipetsk state technical university (age 18–23, m = 20,2; sd = 1,3; 60% female), selected by purposive convenience sampling through the online platform yandex forms, who systematically encountered elements of gamification in their academic courses. the authors' scales for assessing the perception of gamification elements were used, along with validated questionnaires on academic motivation, anxiety, impostor syndrome, and academic cynicism. results. the key predictor of increased anxiety, impostor syndrome, and learning disengagement is the subjective perception of gamification as a system of external control, rather than its mere presence; public comparison and the perception of bonus points as a mandatory race are the most destructive. conclusions. the gamification dilemma has been empirically confirmed. the developed model identifies an “incompatibility zone”, a “managed compromise zone”, and four “critical points” for design. it is recommended to redesign educational environments, shifting the focus from external control to supporting students' autonomy, competence, and meaningfulness. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

ai assistants and recommender systems as agents of algorithmic socialization context and relevance. in contemporary digital culture, ai assistants and recommender systems increasingly mediate access to information, communication, and cultural models, making it necessary to examine them as new agents of socialization. objective. the article offers a theoretical and methodological analysis of ai assistants and recommender systems as mediators involved in the shaping of cognitive practices, communicative experience, value orientations, and identity. hypothesis. algorithmic systems are assumed to operate not only as technical tools, but also as distinctive mediators of cultural experience that influence the internalization of social norms, patterns of social comparison, and forms of self-presentation. methods and materials. the study is based on a theoretical-analytical review of the literature. the methodological framework includes conceptual analysis, comparative theoretical analysis, thematic synthesis, and interpretive integration of scholarship in the psychology of socialization, cultural-historical psychology, human—ai interaction, digital ethics, and platform studies. results. the analysis shows that ai assistants acquire a quasi-social status, shaping communicative expectations, trust, and cognitive habits, while recommender systems participate in constructing social reality, normative understandings, and algorithmically mediated identities. on this basis, the concept of algorithmic socialization is theoretically elaborated. conclusions. ai should be conceptualized not simply as a tool, but as a new socializing infrastructure and a specific semiotic-technical means that mediates personality development, the formation of higher mental functions, and the internalization of norms in digital culture. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

shame-proneness and authenticity in emerging adulthood context and relevance. authenticity is associated with well-being and is one of the conditions for the full functioning of the personality. however, maintaining authenticity may be associated with social risks. shame, as a self-conscious emotion directed at the self and associated with the fear of social isolation, may restrict the expression of authenticity. the challenges of searching for the self and the consequences of shame-proneness are especially important in emerging adulthood, when decisions taken can critically affect life. objective. to identify the presence and specific features of the relationship between personal authenticity and shame-proneness in emerging adulthood. hypothesis. the level of personal authenticity is interconnected with shame experience, while the relationships of such experience with the various components of authenticity will be ambiguous. methods and materials. the study involved 133 young people aged 18 to 29 (m = 23,8, sd = 2,9, 41,4% male). authenticity, shame-proneness and the expression of traits in emerging adulthood were assessed using a battery of questionnaires (moscow authenticity scale, authenticity scale, tosca-3, gasp, inventory of the dimensions of emerging adulthood). results. divergent relations of moderate strength were identified between shame-proneness and the components of authenticity, taking into account the traits of emerging adulthood. shame-proneness is positively associated with self-alienation and accepting external influence, and is negatively related to authentic living. for authenticity measured with the moscow authenticity scale, a negative relation was found between shame-proneness and the aspects of authenticity related to knowing and accepting oneself. conclusions. the identified connections are weak or moderate in strength, which suggests that the consequences of a tendency to experience shame can be offset by an authentic person's ability to accept their imperfections and their high capacity to follow their purpose and accept life's circumstances. kulturno-istoricheskaya psikhologiya-cultural-historical psychology

psychology of culture change: the power of situations returns. creating inclusive cultures with equal opportunity and belonging is a goal of most communities and organizations, but achieving that goal has been uneven at best. many attempts at inclusive culture change have not worked, while others have backfired. one reason is that these attempts have exclusively emphasized individual efforts and underestimated the power of situations in nudging individuals' beliefs, behaviors, interactions, and relationships, which together create local culture. this article disaggregates the power of situations into four distinct types of situational forces, by integrating research from social psychology and adjacent disciplines, to illustrate how some situational forces shift beliefs, behaviors, social interactions, and relationships toward greater inclusion and equality while other situational forces move in the opposite direction. an important goal is to illuminate how individual beliefs and behaviors connect to higher-order changes in local cultures and to identify where research is lacking to chart a future research agenda. annual review of psychology

vrrec: a zero-coding open-source vr body-motion capture tool for behavioral research. vrrec：一款用于行为研究的零编码开源vr身体动作捕捉工具 we present vrrec, an open-source, motion-tracking and recording tool for pc-based virtual reality (vr). the tool addresses a persistent gap in vr-based experimental research by enabling real-time capture of head, hand, and optional body-tracking data without the need to code. vrrec runs discreetly in the background, collecting positional and rotational data as researchers engage participants with third-party vr applications. this design lets researchers use flexible paradigms that leverage off-the-shelf vr content, eliminating the need to build or modify custom software. however, because vrrec does not read application-level events or object states from the target vr software, it does not directly support paradigms that require synchronization with in-app events or distances to dynamic virtual objects or avatars. vrrec still allows manual event marking for contextual annotation. the resulting data are stored as plain text, which can be imported into various analysis pipelines to derive behavioral metrics in fields such as social psychology, rehabilitation, and consumer research. evaluations show consistent and stable recording performance with minimal impact on system resources, while also indicating some limitations for study designs that require millisecond-accurate timing precision. by streamlining vr motion data acquisition, vrrec broadens the range of feasible vr study designs and reduces technical barriers, making vr-based behavioral research more accessible. both the source code and the executable version of vrrec are freely available on github. behavior research methods

cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the levenstein perceived stress questionnaire in both temporal versions in a sample of ecuadorian adults objective: this study aimed to linguistically and culturally adapt levenstein's perceived stress questionnaire (psq) into ecuadorian spanish and to examine the psychometric properties of both its general (past 1-2 years) and recent (past month) temporal versions.
methods: a five-phase instrumental design was implemented across four independent samples (total n = 1386). phase 1 involved standardized translation, back-translation, and expert review, followed by an initial pilot administration (n = 300) using non-probability convenience sampling to identify comprehension and cultural-adequacy issues, with predominant representation of health and education professionals. phase 2 (n = 300) evaluated the resulting linguistic adjustments prior to the factorial analyses. phase 3 conducted exploratory factor analysis (efa; n = 395) using principal axis factoring with oblimin rotation, with factor retention determined by parallel analysis. phase 4 performed confirmatory factor analysis (cfa; n = 391) evaluating model fit and internal consistency via cronbach's alpha and mcdonald's omega. phase 5 evaluated multigroup factorial invariance by biological sex.
results: the adaptation yielded two refined versions of the psq. the general version retained 22 items in a three-correlated-factor structure: perceived overload and pressure, well-being and personal resources, and alienation and relational disconnection (efa variance explained: 40.44%). the recent version comprised 23 items across four factors, with pressure and worry emerging as a distinct dimension (efa variance explained: 54.97%). both versions demonstrated excellent internal consistency (general: α =0.891, ω = 0.907; recent: α = 0.911, ω = 0.918) and satisfactory confirmatory fit indices (general: cfi = 0.950, rmsea = 0.064; recent: cfi = 0.950, rmsea = 0.061). configural, metric, and scalar invariance across sex groups, re-estimated with wlsmv, showed negligible fit deterioration (δcfi ≤ 0.005) in both versions, now on configural baselines with good absolute fit (cfi = 0.949 general; cfi = 0.946 recent); residual (strict) invariance was not separately testable under this ordinal estimator. evidence of convergent and discriminant validity was not obtained in the present study, representing a primary limitation.
conclusions: the psq-593 demonstrates adequate structural validity and internal consistency for assessing perceived stress across two temporal frames in the ecuadorian population. its dual temporal structure offers differentiated utility for epidemiological research, longitudinal studies, and intervention evaluation. future research should establish convergent, discriminant, and predictive validity, and replicate the factorial structures in samples more broadly representative of the ecuadorian population. acta psychologica

alignment of natural language processing-derived rdoc scores with depression, anhedonia, and anxiety in psychiatric electronic health records. traditional categorical diagnoses often fail to capture the dimensional nature of psychiatric disorders such as depression and anxiety. natural language processing (nlp) offers a promising approach to extract dimensional constructs relevant to psychopathology from clinical documentation. in this cross-sectional study, we analyzed clinical notes from 358 psychiatric patients treated at mclean hospital and enrolled in the "psychometrics at mclean" (pam) study to examine the alignment between nlp-derived research domain criteria (rdoc) constructs and psychometric assessments of depression, anhedonia, and anxiety. rdoc scores for positive valence systems (pvs) and negative valence systems (nvs) were extracted using nlp methods previously validated at the group level and compared with standardized clinical assessments: positive valence systems scale (pvss), quick inventory of depressive symptomatology (qids), snaith-hamilton pleasure scale (shaps), and generalized anxiety disorder-7 (gad-7). significant associations were observed between depression (qids) and both pvs (β = -0.42, p = 0.008) and nvs (β = 0.45, p = 0.015); anhedonia (shaps) and both pvs (β = -0.39, p = 0.005) and nvs (β = 0.36, p = 0.030); and anxiety (gad-7) and nvs (β = 0.29, p = 0.049), but not anxiety and pvs. these results are consistent with theoretical accounts in which both pvs and nvs are implicated in depression, whereas anxiety primarily involves nvs. these findings demonstrate that nlp-derived rdoc scores align with established clinical measures, providing evidence of convergent validity with symptom-based measures and of discriminant validity, most notably the selective association of anxiety with nvs. nlp-derived rdoc scores may offer a scalable approach for characterizing dimensional psychopathology; however, longitudinal and predictive validation will be required before applications such as treatment-response monitoring can be supported. npp - digital psychiatry and neuroscience

associations between sleep quality and well-being among nurses: the serial mediating roles of psychological resilience and adversity coping background promoting nurses’ well-being is important for mental health and workforce stability. poor sleep quality is common among nurses and has been associated with lower general well-being. psychological resilience and adversity quotient may serve as protective personal resources, but their roles in this association remain unclear. objectives this study examined the association between sleep quality and general well-being among chinese nurses from the perspective of conservation of resources theory, focusing on the independent and serial mediation of psychological resilience and adversity quotient. methods this multicenter cross-sectional study enrolled 1,149 nurses from 22 tertiary medical institutions in zhejiang province, china, between september and november 2025. data were collected using the pittsburgh sleep quality index, the adversity quotient scale, the connor-davidson resilience scale, and the general well-being schedule. descriptive statistics, pearson correlation analysis, and common method bias tests were conducted for the study variables. confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were used to evaluate the measurement and hypothesized structural models, respectively. indirect effects were tested using bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. results sleep quality, psychological resilience, adversity quotient, and general well-being were all significantly correlated ( p < 0.001). psychological resilience and adversity quotient significantly mediated the association between sleep quality and general well-being. the total indirect effect accounted for 41.6% of the total effect. all three indirect effects were significant: (1) sleep quality → psychological resilience → general well-being (β = −0.137, p < 0.001, 22.2% of the total effect), (2) sleep quality → adversity quotient → general well-being (β = −0.070, p < 0.001, 11.2% of the total effect), and (3) sleep quality → psychological resilience → adversity quotient → general well-being (β = −0.051, p < 0.001, 8.2% of the total effect). conclusion sleep quality was associated with chinese nurses’ well-being both directly and indirectly through psychological resilience, adversity quotient, and their serial mediation effect. nursing managers may consider sleep quality improvement and targeted strategies to strengthen psychological resilience and adversity quotient as potential approaches to supporting nurses’ general well-being. frontiers in psychology

occupational stress, moral dilemmas, and decision-making confidence among chinese police officers: the mediating role of emotional exhaustion police officers routinely make consequential decisions in emotionally demanding and morally ambiguous situations, yet how chronic occupational stress and moral strain relate to the confidence with which officers reach those decisions remains poorly specified. this cross-sectional study examined whether the associations of occupational stress and moral dilemmas with decision-making confidence among chinese police officers are statistically accounted for by emotional exhaustion within a hypothesized mediation model. a convenience sample of 412 active-duty officers from three municipal police bureaus in henan province, china, completed validated chinese versions of the operational police stress questionnaire, a six-item moral dilemma scale, the emotional exhaustion subscale of the maslach burnout inventory-general survey, the 12-item general health questionnaire, and a five-item decision-making confidence scale. structural equation modeling with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples showed that both occupational stress (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) and moral dilemmas (β = 0.27, p < 0.001) were positively associated with emotional exhaustion, which was in turn negatively associated with decision-making confidence (β = −0.38, p < 0.001). the indirect effects of occupational stress (indirect effect = −0.16, 95% ci [−0.21, −0.11]) and moral dilemmas (indirect effect = −0.10, 95% ci [−0.15, −0.06]) through emotional exhaustion were both statistically significant, whereas the direct effects of the two antecedents were non-significant. the model explained 38% of the variance in emotional exhaustion and 15% of the variance in decision-making confidence. these findings are consistent with resource-based interpretations grounded in conservation of resources theory, and they identify emotional exhaustion as a potentially modifiable correlate of officers’ self-evaluated decisional capacity; whether reducing burnout also benefits decision-making itself remains to be established with longitudinal and experimental designs. frontiers in psychology

fathers’ experiences singing to their infants: an interpretative phenomenological analysis background infant-directed singing (id singing) is a powerful phenomenon with well-established clinical applications for infants and parents. existing research, however, focuses primarily on mothers, leaving a critical gap in the literature. methods this study explores fathers’ experiences singing with their infants, specifically examining how fathers engage in and perceive singing to their infant; the factors that influence fathers’ singing; and how, if at all, singing influences father-infant bonding. semi-structured interviews with thirteen fathers were analyzed using interpretative phenomenological analysis (ipa). results fathers in this study sang intuitively, expressively, and responsively to their infants. they perceived singing as a predominantly positive experience that regulated their emotions, although they also described occasional challenges with singing. fathers’ singing was influenced by their heritage, spouse, and fatherhood role. while fathers expressed some uncertainty regarding singing’s immediate influence on father-infant bonding, many hoped music could help them relate to their child in the future. discussion though findings align with previous research on maternal id singing, participants’ accounts highlighted distinct aspects of their id singing experiences. in order to meet fathers’ unique needs and promote equitable family-centered care, interventionists must account for fathers’ experiences when designing music interventions. implications for music interventions and recommendations for future father-infant musicality research are discussed. frontiers in psychology

development and validation of the civil aviation occupational gender stereotype scale and its impact on professional identity and self-efficacy among chinese civil aviation majors introduction this research aimed to develop and validate the civil aviation occupational gender stereotype scale (ca-ogss) and investigate its associations with professional identity and self-efficacy among chinese civil aviation majors, thereby providing an empirical foundation for fostering gender equality in the field. methods in study 1, an initial 15-item pool was generated and refined through a literature review, interviews, and expert evaluation; its factor structure and reliability were examined using exploratory factor analysis (sample 1, n = 707) and confirmatory factor analysis (sample 2, n = 1,465). in study 2, the finalized 10-item ca-ogss, alongside established measures of professional identity and self-efficacy, was administered among 830 civil aviation majors to test a moderated mediation model. results the ca-ogss demonstrated a stable two-factor structure, explaining 73.12% of the total variance in efa. the final cfa model showed acceptable fit comparative fit index = 0.995; tucker–lewis index = 0.989; root mean square error of approximation = 0.072 [90% ci: 0.062, 0.084]; standardized root mean squared residual = 0.013), although the χ 2 / df value (6.77) exceeded the conventional cutoff. reliability was acceptable. path analysis revealed that gender stereotypes were associated with self-efficacy through professional identity, and this indirect association was moderated by gender. simple slope analysis suggested that the association was negative among women but positive among men; the indirect association via professional identity was stronger among men than among women. discussion the findings indicate that ca-ogss is a valid and reliable tool and underscore the importance of gender stereotypes in relation to the outcomes of civil aviation students, suggesting that future interventions to promote gender equality must account for these differential effects across genders. frontiers in psychology

interpersonal emotion regulation in daily life: a comparison of individuals with and without depressive disorders background emotion dysregulation is strongly linked to depressive disorders, yet distinctions between interpersonal and intrapersonal forms remain underexplored in daily life. this study examines emotion dysregulation in depression during close interpersonal interactions, comparing individuals with depression and healthy controls (hc), and exploring associations with alexithymia and childhood maltreatment. methods participants (18 hc, 17 with depression) reported three emotion regulation (er) strategies (cognitive reappraisal, social sharing, suppression) during interpersonal interactions over 2 weeks (3 prompts/day). group (depression vs. hc) was the independent variable, and er strategies the dependent variables. alexithymia, childhood maltreatment, and depressive symptoms were assessed at baseline. data were analyzed using two-level hierarchical linear modeling. results no group differences in er strategy use were observed, and depressive symptom severity was not associated with strategy intensity. post-hoc analyses showed that alexithymia was positively associated with depressive severity across the full sample and negatively associated with social sharing within the depressed group. cognitive reappraisal showed heterogeneous associations with childhood maltreatment subdomains. conclusion interpersonal emotion dysregulation did not differentiate depressed from healthy individuals. given the small sample size, these null findings should be interpreted cautiously. nevertheless, alexithymia and childhood maltreatment appear relevant for er in close relationships, highlighting their importance in depression research. frontiers in psychology

early detection of problematic internet use among university students: psychometric validation of the piuq-9 background university students extensively use the internet for academic, social, and recreational purposes, increasing the risk of developing problematic internet use (piu). although several instruments exist, there is a need for brief, psychometrically sound screening tools capable of identifying individuals at risk and detecting related conditions such as internet gaming disorder (igd) and online gambling disorder (ogd). objectives this study aimed to examine the reliability and validity of the 9-item problematic internet use questionnaire (piuq-9) in a sample of first-year university students and to explore its screening performance for piu and its potential utility for identifying increased risk of related conditions such as internet gaming disorder (igd) and online gambling disorder (ogd). methods a cross-sectional study was conducted with n = 273 university students [180 women (65.9%), 93 men (34.1%); mean age 19.5 years, sd 1.9]. participants were recruited from university settings and completed a self-administered battery of validated instruments assessing piu, addictive behaviors, impulsivity, emotion regulation, and general psychopathology. construct validity was examined using confirmatory factor analysis. internal consistency was assessed using mcdonald’s omega. convergent validity was evaluated through pearson correlation coefficients with related constructs. test–retest reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (icc) and weighted kappa statistics. receiver operating characteristic (roc) curve analyses were conducted to determine empirically derived screening threshold for identifying high risk of piu, igd, and ogd. results confirmatory factor analysis supported a unidimensional structure of the piuq-9. the scale demonstrated good internal consistency (ω = 0.82) and explained 38.5% of the total variance. convergent validity was supported by moderate to strong correlations with related measures, including risk of internet/social network addiction ( r = 0.666; 95%ci: 0.594–0.727), impulsivity ( r = 0.369; 95%ci: 0.262–0.467), emotion regulation difficulties ( r = 0.382; 95%ci: 0.276–0.479), and psychological distress ( r = 0.312; 95%ci: 0.201–0.415) (all p < 0.001). test–retest reliability was good ( icc = 0.753; 95%ci: 0.650–0.830), with item-level agreement ranging from moderate to substantial (weighted kappa = 0.435 [95%ci: 0.278–0.593] to 0.698 [95%ci: 0.593–0.803]). the area under the roc curve was 0.824 (95% ci: 0.768–0.881). roc analyses identified an empirically derived screening threshold of 9 for high risk of piu, 11 for increased risk of igd, and 13 for increased risk of ogd. these thresholds showed variable discriminatory performance, with lower specificity and positive predictive values for igd and ogd. conclusion the piuq-9 is a brief, reliable, and valid instrument for assessing piu among university students. this study extends previous research by providing evidence of its accuracy in identifying related behavioral addictions, such as igd and ogd, within a population highly vulnerable to piu yet still underrepresented in the scientific literature. the findings support its utility as an efficient screening tool in both research and applied settings, facilitating early detection and targeted prevention strategies in young adult populations. frontiers in psychology

co-residence with both parents, attitudes toward parents, and psychological difficulties among chinese secondary school students: indirect associations through social adaptability background this cross-sectional study examined whether co-residence status and students’ attitudes toward parents were associated with psychological difficulties directly and indirectly through social adaptability. method a regional census cluster survey distributed questionnaires to 39,739 students in 20 secondary schools in one district of chongqing, china. the analytic sample comprised 34,097 valid responses (85.80%). psychological difficulties were represented by continuous scores from 35 mental health test items covering academic anxiety, self-blame, and impulsivity. two separate observed-variable path models were estimated with school-level clustering, maximum likelihood estimation, 5,000 cluster-bootstrap draws, and adjustment for sex and grade. results more positive attitudes toward parents were associated with fewer psychological difficulties through social adaptability (standardized indirect association = −0.148, bias-corrected 95% ci [−0.170, −0.129]); the total association was −0.196 [−0.228, −0.162]. compared with students living with both parents, students living with others showed a small positive indirect association with psychological difficulties (0.034 [0.022, 0.050]) and a small total association (0.049 [0.033, 0.070]). conclusion the findings were compatible with indirect associations through social adaptability, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal or causal mediation. co-residence findings should be interpreted cautiously because the retained dataset did not preserve the original nonparental living-arrangement categories. frontiers in psychology

parental reflexivity and latent psychological violence among urban parents in kazakhstan and kyrgyzstan: an exploratory study introduction parental reflective functioning (prf) has been associated with less harmful parenting behavior and a lower likelihood of intergenerational continuity of violence. however, little is known about whether the association between parental reflexivity and psychologically harmful parenting differs between fathers and mothers in central asia. this study examined parental reflexivity, measured using a. v. karpov’s reflexivity scale as an operational proxy for prf, and its association with latent psychological violence among urban parents in kazakhstan and kyrgyzstan. methods a cross-sectional multi-city study was conducted in almaty, shymkent, turkestan, and bishkek. the analytical sample ( n = 400), drawn from a larger dataset ( n = 500), included 158 fathers and 242 mothers. measures included reflexivity, aggression, empathy, latent psychological violence (ilv), uyat intensity, and family-of-origin violence. analyses comprised parent-group-specific regressions, bootstrap coefficient comparisons, hierarchical moderation models with a prf × parent-group interaction, and robustness analyses using recruitment-site fixed effects, robust standard errors, the full sample, parent-group weighting, and additional family-context covariates. results reflexivity was strongly inversely associated with latent psychological violence in both parent groups. the prf–ilv slope was descriptively steeper among fathers than mothers ( b = −0.900, r 2 = 0.485 vs. b = −0.779, r 2 = 0.417), but the difference was not statistically significant ( z = −1.27, p = 0.204; 95% bootstrap ci [−0.320, 0.067]). the prf × parent-group interaction was also nonsignificant (δ r 2 = 0.002, p = 0.201). among highly reflective parents with family-of-origin violence, none of five fathers met the exploratory high-ilv threshold (ilv ≥ 70), compared with 1 of 7 mothers; this difference was nonsignificant ( p = 1.000). family-of-origin violence was associated with lower reflexivity among both fathers ( d = 0.64) and mothers ( d = 0.74). discussion parental reflexivity showed a robust inverse association with latent psychological violence, but formal analyses provided no evidence that this association differed between fathers and mothers. the descriptively steeper father association should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of a father-specific effect. these findings support further longitudinal and intervention research in urban central asian populations. frontiers in psychology

effects of psychological skills training on self-control, perceived physical self-defense capacity, and mental toughness in elite female wrestlers: a randomized controlled trial background self-control, self-defense self-efficacy, and mental resilience are fundamental psychological determinants of performance and competitive endurance in combat sports. however, scientific evidence on structured, evidence-based psychological intervention programs for professional female wrestlers remains limited. this study examined the effects of a psychological skills training (pst)-based intervention on self-control, self-defense self-efficacy, and mental resilience in professional female wrestlers. methods a randomized controlled pre-test–post-test design was employed. thirty-six professional female wrestlers (aged 18–25) were randomly assigned to a pst group ( n = 18) or a control group (cg; n = 18). the pst group completed an 8-week structured psychological intervention alongside regular training, while the cg continued routine training only. self-control, self-defense self-efficacy, and mental resilience were assessed pre- and post-intervention using valid and reliable psychometric scales. data were analyzed via repeated-measures anova, with effect sizes calculated. results significant group × time interactions were observed across multiple outcomes. a highly significant interaction emerged for perceived physical self-defense capacity (sp; f (1,34) = 56.525, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.624) and for dp scores ( f (1,34) = 9.360, p = 0.004, ηp 2 = 0.216). among self-control subscales, significant interactions were found for inhibition ( f (1,34) = 8.172, p = 0.007, ηp 2 = 0.194) and, more strongly, for initiation ( f (1,34) = 14.157, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.294). for mental resilience, highly significant interactions were detected for confidence ( f (1,34) = 59.976, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.638), control ( f (1,34) = 32.486, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.489), and persistence ( f (1,34) = 32.709, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.490). overall, the intervention demonstrated medium-to-high effect sizes across psychological performance indicators. conclusion these findings suggest that pst may serve as a useful complementary approach for enhancing self-control, perceived physical self-defense capacity, and mental toughness in professional female wrestlers. however, results should not be interpreted as evidence of improved competitive wrestling performance, technical success, or objectively measured physical self-defense ability, as these outcomes were not directly assessed in this study. frontiers in psychology

ignoring a noisy metronome during dyadic drumming introduction this study investigated how the tonal and rhythmic properties of a “noisy metronome” and the opportunity for visual contact would affect drumming partners' abilities to synchronize with each other. method participants' task was to drum a regular beat in synchrony with their partner at a prescribed tempo. they heard a metronome while drumming that they were instructed to ignore. we manipulated the noise profile of the metronome so that it contained long-range autocorrelations, short-range autocorrelations, or white noise. we also manipulated its pitch so that it formed a consonant or dissonant chord alongside the participants' drum tones. we assessed the effect of this noisy metronome on participants' synchronization stability, tempo, and body motion. results our findings showed that the noisy metronome impaired synchronization between partners but improved tempo-keeping. manipulations of the metronome's rhythmic and tonal properties had no effect on any of the outcome variables. the noisy metronome prompted increased head and hand motion from the participants (measured in terms of motion speed); head motion was also greater among active musicians than inactive/nonmusicians, and hand motion was greater among partners who knew each other. visual contact improved synchronization and participants moved their drumming hand more when they could see each other than when they could not. discussion our findings have implications for our understanding of how people process and respond to competing rhythms and the strategies they use to (co-)regulate the timing of their movements. frontiers in psychology

skin color and mental health in peru: the mediating role of experiences of discrimination among university students objective this study aimed to examine the mediating role of experiences of discrimination in the association between skin color and mental health among university students. methods a cross-sectional correlational design was used. the sample comprised 603 university students aged 18 to 38 years from metropolitan lima. skin color was assessed using the perla color palette, experiences of discrimination were measured using the experiences of discrimination scale, and mental health was assessed using the mental health inventory-5 (mhi-5), considering its two-dimensional structure of psychological well-being and psychological distress. the analyses included descriptive statistics, spearman’s rank correlations, linear regression models with hc3 robust standard errors, and mediation models with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals based on 5,000 resamples. results darker skin tones were significantly associated with greater discrimination. in turn, discrimination was associated with lower levels of psychological well-being and greater psychological distress. no significant direct associations were found between skin color and either psychological well-being or psychological distress. the mediation analysis showed a significant indirect effect of skin color on psychological distress through experiences of discrimination, whereas the indirect effect on psychological well-being was not significant. overall, the findings suggest that discrimination constitutes an important psychosocial pathway linking darker skin tones to greater psychological distress. conclusion in this sample, skin color was not directly associated with mental health; however, it acquired psychosocial relevance through its association with greater exposure to experiences of discrimination. these findings suggest that phenotypic hierarchies may be associated with the mental health of peruvian university students through greater exposure to discrimination. addressing discrimination within university settings may help reduce psychological distress and promote students’ mental health. frontiers in psychology

psychometric validation of the positive youth development scale–short form in peruvian university students introduction evidence on the psychometric performance of the positive youth development scale–short form (pyd-sf) in spanish-speaking university populations remains limited. this study examined evidence based on internal structure, measurement invariance across sex, internal consistency, the empirical distinctiveness of the five dimensions, and relations with purpose in life for pyd-sf scores in peruvian university students. methods a cross-sectional instrumental study was conducted with 1,015 peruvian university students aged 18 to 30 years. confirmatory factor analysis was performed using the diagonally weighted least squares (dwls) estimator for ordinal data. measurement invariance across sex, internal consistency, the empirical distinctiveness of the five dimensions, and relations with purpose in life were also assessed. results the findings supported a correlated five-factor structure consistent with the theoretical 5cs model. strict measurement invariance across sex was established. internal consistency coefficients were generally acceptable, although the categorical omega coefficient for caring was marginal. heterotrait–monotrait ratios remained below 0.85, and all five dimensions showed positive and statistically significant correlations with purpose in life. conclusion the findings provide evidence based on internal structure, internal consistency, measurement invariance across sex, the empirical distinctiveness of the five dimensions, and relations with purpose in life for pyd-sf scores in peruvian university students. these results support their use for group-level research in comparable university populations. frontiers in psychology

the trans-cultural geometry of liberation: convergent topologies across independent soteriological traditions article i of iii: the comparative anatomy of liberation structures this article demonstrates that diverse soteriological traditions across six civilisational contexts (hindu, buddhist, christian mystical, islamic sufi, kabbalistic jewish, and graeco-roman philosophical) instantiate a shared structural grammar of liberation despite having developed their models within substantially different philosophical, linguistic, and institutional contexts. a five-element template is identified: a conditioned principle (current self), an unconditioned principle (ultimate ground), a perceived gap between them (the structural definition of bondage), a method of resolution (path), and a final stabilised state (liberation). this template resolves into exactly three topological types: closed identity (gap recognised as illusory, endpoint: stillness), open-relational (gap refined and preserved, endpoint: sustained intensity), and disentanglement (gap recognised as natural original condition, endpoint: witness-detachment). the convergence of these three types across traditions constitutes the primary evidence presented. a critical methodological finding is introduced: the invariance test, which demonstrates that liberation is characterised not by observable transformation but by its absence: the liberated person continues with their work as before, neither celebrating, advertising, nor restructuring identity around the event. the article refrains from offering a causal hypothesis for the convergence, reserving that analysis for article iii in this series. frontiers in psychology

can artificial systems become conscious?—recursive embodied closure as an integrative framework recent advances in artificial intelligence, connectomics, and computational neuroscience increasingly raise the question of whether artificial systems—or even pure computer simulations—could become conscious. contemporary theories emphasize embodiment, predictive processing, homeostatic regulation, and continuous interaction between cognition, body, and environment rather than isolated computation. we propose recursive embodied closure as an integrative framework linking embodied, predictive, functionalist, and dynamical approaches to consciousness. rather than replacing existing theories, the framework identifies a shared organizational principle: the continuous recursive coupling of cognition, bodily regulation, action, and environmental feedback. we argue that consciousness may, in principle, emerge in artificial systems, including computational simulations, for three reasons. first, consciousness may depend on recursively closed loops linking cognition, body, and environment, and such loops could also be realized in robotic, neuromorphic, or virtual embodiments. second, evidence from comparative neuroscience, convergent evolution, neurotechnology, and philosophy of mind suggests that the mechanisms relevant for consciousness are largely substrate-independent and may therefore be implemented in both biological and artificial systems. third, although unknown physical mechanisms cannot be excluded, there is currently no empirical evidence for biological processes that are uniquely necessary for consciousness. taken together, these considerations support the view that consciousness is best understood as an emergent property of recursively embodied, environmentally embedded cognitive systems rather than of biological matter itself. if so, biological brains, artificial neural networks, neuromorphic hardware, and even virtual agents may constitute plausible candidates for future artificial consciousness. frontiers in psychology

legal precarity as culturally situated acculturative stress: social support and psychological security among akha-hani cross-border wives in southwest china this article examines how legal precarity becomes acculturative stress and how relational support shapes psychological security among akha-hani cross-border wives in southwest china. existing acculturation research has established that migration involves psychological and sociocultural adjustment, but less is known about how stress develops when substantial cultural proximity coexists with legal and administrative uncertainty. based on prolonged field engagement between 2022 and 2024 and formal ethnographic data collection from july to september 2024 in xishuangbanna, the study draws on 28 in-depth interviews, four focus group discussions involving 29 additional participants, and participant observation. the findings show that shared akha-hani language, kinship, and ritual familiarity reduced some forms of interpersonal and cultural distance, but did not remove stress associated with documentation, public procedures, mobility, and family futures. legal precarity became psychologically consequential through uncertainty, dependence on others, restricted agency, and reduced predictability in everyday family life. mandarin was important mainly in public and institutional settings rather than as a general barrier within akha-hani households. emotional, practical, and informational support from husbands, relatives, peers, and local networks helped women manage these pressures and strengthen psychological security. however, support was sometimes ambivalent when immediate assistance also maintained dependence on particular family relationships. the study contributes to cultural and migration psychology by showing how institutional insecurity can generate acculturative stress even under conditions of substantial cultural proximity. frontiers in psychology

how do virtual exercise technology and social presence influence motivation to exercise? introduction virtual technology offers a promising tool for encouraging engagement in exercise, as it can provide the user with enhanced visual stimuli and accessible metrics; however, the specific features within that technology that contribute to motivation and participation require further investigation. this study examined how different visual displays and the presence of a second rider influenced motivation to exercise using virtual technology. methods twenty-four young adults completed a 3-km cycling course on the same virtual track under three counterbalanced conditions including (a) a metrics-only ride, where a screen in front of the rider displayed only standard performance variables (e.g., power, cadence), (b) a solo-virtual ride, which was identical to the previous condition, but with the addition of the participant being depicted on the screen as an avatar amongst virtual scenery, and (c) a paired-virtual ride, that contained the same elements as the previous two conditions, but with the addition of a second rider represented on the screen as an avatar. results the quantitative results, which included performance-related variables (cadence, power, speed, and heart rate), measures of intrinsic motivation, and ratings of perceived exertion, revealed significantly higher values for the paired-virtual condition compared to both the metrics-only and the solo-virtual conditions. differences between the metrics-only and the solo-virtual conditions were isolated to interest-enjoyment and effort-importance. brief interviews with participants indicated that the paired-virtual condition produced heightened levels of enjoyment and competitive drive which motivated participants to exert more effort. the solo-virtual condition was reported to be relaxing, but it was also reported as the least engaging. the metrics-only condition provoked negative emotions due to the absence of distractions and a heightened focus on internal cues. discussion the results highlight the psychological mechanisms that influence motivation and engagement when using virtual exercise technology. frontiers in psychology

the associations between wearable device feedback perception and athletes’ training load management behavior: the chain mediating role of physiological data literacy and recovery self-regulation introduction despite the rapid proliferation of wearable devices in sport, athletes vary considerably in their ability to interpret device-generated physiological feedback, and the psychological pathways linking feedback perception to training load management remain insufficiently understood. this study introduces physiological data literacy (pdl) as a content-specific form of data literacy and examines whether pdl and recovery self-regulation (rsr) sequentially mediate the association between wearable device feedback perception (wfp) and training load management behavior (tlm). methods using a cross-sectional design, 357 active athletes (189 males and 168 females; mean age = 22.76 years, sd = 3.68) completed the wearable device feedback perception scale, physiological data literacy scale, recovery self-regulation scale, and training load management behavior scale. path analysis with bias-corrected bootstrapping (5,000 resamples) was conducted. results wfp showed a positive total association with tlm ( β = 0.511). significant specific indirect associations were observed through pdl (standardized indirect effect = 0.083, 95% ci [0.032, 0.136]) and rsr (standardized indirect effect = 0.085, 95% ci [0.048, 0.128]). a significant sequential indirect association was also observed for the theoretically specified wfp → pdl → rsr → tlm ordering (indirect effect = 0.065, 95% ci [0.040, 0.098]). the direct wfp–tlm association remained significant after inclusion of both mediators. however, the reverse sequential model yielded identical aic and bic values. discussion the findings are statistically compatible with a theoretically motivated sequential framework linking wfp, pdl, rsr, and tlm, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal precedence or causal direction. pdl represents a conceptually distinct competency that, together with rsr, warrants further examination in longitudinal and intervention research on wearable-supported training. frontiers in psychology

synergizing strengths of four trauma-focused treatments in a highly intensive integrated program for posttraumatic stress disorder: rationale and two case descriptions background various evidence-based trauma-focused psychotherapies for posttraumatic stress disorder (ptsd) are available and several commonalities have been identified. yet, these trauma-focused psychotherapies also have important differences. this raises the question whether several trauma-focused methods can be combined in one treatment format. thus far, systematic efforts to combine multiple trauma-focused treatment methods have been limited. objective to describe the rationale, structure, and application of a highly intensive treatment format integrating four trauma-focused psychotherapies, illustrated by two case presentations. the study was descriptive and was not designed to evaluate clinical effectiveness. method description of a structured treatment format that integrates prolonged exposure (pe), eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy (emdr), brief eclectic psychotherapy for ptsd (bepp) and narrative exposure therapy (net) in a highly intensive dose. sessions were performed twice a day over the course of 1 week. this format was conceptualized in the context of a documentary series on an online ongoing education platform for therapists. results a combat veteran with ptsd and a survivor of long-term physical and sexual abuse with ptsd completed the 1-week program. their treatment courses illustrate how the components of pe, emdr therapy, bepp, and net can be organized and applied within a single intensive format. in non-standardized interviews conducted for the accompanying documentary, both participants described different functions and perceived contributions of the 4 treatment approaches. conclusions the case descriptions demonstrate that the proposed integration of four trauma-focused approaches could be applied as planned in two individual treatment trajectories of patients with severe ptsd. patients' reflections were not collected or analyzed as formal qualitative data and cannot be used to establish treatment effectiveness, safety, or general feasibility of the treatment format. prospective studies incorporating standardized outcome assessments, systematic adverse event monitoring, and formal qualitative evaluations are required to systematically investigate the treatment program. frontiers in psychology

network analysis of the interrelationships among stigma, resilience, and self-esteem in lung cancer patients stigma is a significant psychosocial challenge for patients with lung cancer and is closely related to psychological resilience and self-esteem. however, most existing studies have examined these factors in isolation, overlooking the complex interrelationships among their specific dimensions. this cross-sectional network analysis investigated 248 patients with lung cancer using validated measures of stigma, resilience, and self-esteem. a regularized partial correlation network comprising 11 dimensions was estimated using the ebicglasso algorithm. expected influence (ei) and bridge expected influence (bei) were used to assess overall and cross-community connectivity, respectively. “hope for the future” showed the highest observed ei (ei = 1.91), closely followed by “support and coping,” while “self-negation” showed the highest observed bei (bei = 0.517). these findings characterize the interconnected structure of stigma, resilience, and self-esteem and highlight future-oriented hope and negative self-evaluation as potentially relevant dimensions for psychosocial assessment and intervention development, although their roles should be further examined in longitudinal studies. frontiers in psychology

exploring factors associated with self‐reported parental spanking and hitting out of anger: cross‐sectional and longitudinal analyses using national panel data abstract more than one in three us parents use corporal punishment to discipline their children. the objective of this study is to add to a greater understanding of factors associated with self‐reported corporal punishment, based on two survey items: one that asked about use of spanking and one that asked about hitting out of anger. the second objective was to examine the longitudinal relationship between parents' self‐reported use of spanking at age 35 and their self‐reports of hitting out of anger 5 years later. to accomplish these objectives, national us monitoring the future panel study data were used as follows. objective 1: data collected in 1993–2020 from parents age 35 with child(ren) ages 2–12 at home. objective 2: data collected in 1998–2020 from parents age 40 with child(ren) ages 7–17 at home. we conducted multinomial logistic regression to accomplish the objectives. most factors significantly associated with increased odds of reporting spanking at age 35 differed from the factors associated with increased odds of reporting hitting out of anger at age 35. reporting spanking at age 35 was associated with greater odds of reporting hitting out of anger at age 40 (aor = 2.10, 95% ci: 1.71, 2.58). depressive symptoms (aor = 1.24, 95% ci: 1.09, 1.40) and disordered alcohol use (aor = 1.55, 95% ci: 1.14, 2.11) were associated with greater odds of reporting hitting out of anger. future research should continue to examine whether different types of corporal punishment have different determinants, whether and in what ways corporal punishment may escalate over time, and whether measurement error may impact this research. family process
issue information family process

who is [not] expected to use singular them? evidence from real-time language processing abstract this article presents the results of an experiment that investigates how knowledge of a speaker’s beliefs modulates people’s expectations of linguistic choices that person would make, specifically the use of the gender-neutral pronoun them to refer to a known and specific entity. as the use of gender-neutral pronouns is associated with more gender-progressive individuals, it was hypothesized that the use of them would be more surprising if coming from someone more conservative and that this expectation would manifest in real-time processing. the experiment is a self-paced reading task in which participants read sentences from a fictitious “speaker” using a gender-marked ( him/her ) or gender neutral ( them ) pronoun to refer to different types of nouns: those that mark gender definitionally (e.g., saleswoman), those that mark gender stereotypically (e.g., plumber), and those that do not have any strong gender associations (e.g., pedestrian). the results provide evidence that a speaker’s ideological beliefs do influence real-time processing of their utterances: participants demonstrated a processing advantage when a progressive speaker used gender-neutral them following a neutral noun antecedent compared to the same usage from a conservative speaker. results are discussed in the context of past work on social meaning and speaker-specific language processing effects. journal of cultural cognitive science

introducing ai to an online petition platform changed outputs but not outcomes nature human behaviour, published online: 30 september 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02580-8 corpus et al. examine how the introduction of an ai writing tool impacted change.org petitions, finding that it increased petition homogeneity but did not improve petition outcomes. nature human behaviour

augmenting the hypnotic imagination: practical applications of artificial intelligence for clinical hypnosis. artificial intelligence (ai), particularly large language models (llms), offers clinical hypnotists a powerful and immediately accessible set of tools for enhancing practice. despite growing interest at the intersection of ai and mental health care, virtually no practical guidance exists for clinicians seeking to integrate ai into hypnotherapy. this article addresses that gap. written by practicing clinicians in active engagement with an ai system, it provides concrete, demystified, and clinically grounded examples of how ai can augment clinical hypnosis: from generating individualized hypnotic scripts and tailored therapeutic metaphors to synthesizing research evidence, adapting interventions across cultural contexts, designing between-session self-hypnosis resources, supporting clinical training, and generating research hypotheses. ethical considerations - including the american psychological association's recent ethical guidance for ai use, informed consent, data privacy, and the clinician's irreplaceable role as curator of all ai-generated material - are discussed. the article concludes with a practical step-by-step guide, including sample prompts ready for immediate clinical use. american journal of clinical hypnosis

approaches to the study of intergenerational conflicts in organizations and their classification context and relevance. the simultaneous presence of three to five age cohorts within a single organizational space makes intergenerational tension in contemporary organizations increasingly systemic, raising the need for a theoretical understanding of the nature and mechanisms of intergenerational conflicts. objective. the article aims to provide a theoretical analysis of the phenomenon of intergenerational conflicts in modern organizations. methods and materials. the study is based on methods of conceptual analysis, generalization and a systems approach to understanding theoretical concepts of intergenerational conflicts. results. a multidimensional classification of types of intergenerational conflict is proposed, based on five criteria. in addition, the determinants of such conflicts are systematized across three levels of analysis: macrosocial, organizational-managerial, and socio-psychological. conclusions. the findings are of practical relevance for the development of hr tools aimed at diagnosing and managing generational heterogeneity in contemporary organizations. psychology and law

functional catamnesis (longitudinal functional outcomes) in recipients of inpatient social services who were recognized as legally capable or having restricted legal capacity context and relevance. among legally incapacitated individuals who were subsequently recognized as legally capable or having restricted legal capacity, over 75% lived in inpatient social service facilities when their civil-legal status was upgraded. no prior functional outcome assessment in this cohort has been conducted. objective. to evaluate functional catamnesis in recipients of inpatient social services after upgrade of civil-legal status. methods and materials. the cohort comprised 96 individuals (62 males, 34 females) from 6 inpatient social service facilities in the moscow and vladimir regions (54 with restricted legal capacity, 42 legally capable). catamnesis duration: m = 4.6; sd = 3.47. methods included longitudinal dynamic assessment (n = 40), analysis of objective data, and evaluation of overall improvement using the cgi-s and cgi-i scales. frequency analysis and k-means cluster analysis were applied to process the results. results. after the upgrade of their civil-legal status, 76 % of the participants continued to receive social services in an inpatient form, 2 % received services in a non-inpatient form, for 22 % social services were discontinued after discharge. depending on the severity of the mental disorder and the dynamics of overall improvement in clinical status and social functioning, 6 clusters of participants were identified. the functional catamnesis was favorable in 77 % of the participants and uncertain in 16 %. conclusions. functional catamnesis success depends on clinical features, personality characteristics, and whether the individual receives a sufficient volume of social support. following the upgrade of civil-legal status, some individuals retain the need for inpatient social services. psychology and law

big data technology and its influence on the personal well-being of students: psychological risks and legal solutions context and relevance. the application of big data in university education opens wide opportunities for personalizing learning but is accompanied by psychological risks: impaired perception of autonomy, erosion of trust in the university, increased anxiety, emotional alienation, and reduced student psychological well-being. mitigating these risks is possible through the integration of psychological and legal aspects, which would ensure a balance between innovation, data protection, and psychological comfort. objective. to identify the psychological consequences of big data application in higher education (he) and propose solutions that minimize risks and ensure student psychological well-being. methods. an interdisciplinary approach: student surveys (likert scale — anxiety, perception of monitoring); interviews (alienation, trust); content analysis; analysis of federal law no. 152-fz (on personal data); synthesis of successful practice experience; comparative analysis; triangulation. results. established psychological risks include: dehumanization (62% of respondents feel like "data objects"), emotional alienation, loss of autonomy (67% of respondents), anxiety (3.5 on the likert scale). successful practices (informed consent, psycho-ethical codes) reduce anxiety (to 2.1) and strengthen trust (+70%). addressing legal gaps reduces psychological risks and enhances student psychological well-being. conclusions. psychological risks associated with big data use can be mitigated through transparency in data analytics processes, implementation of psycho-ethical codes, and mandatory faculty involvement in data interpretation. harmonizing legislation with international standards and conducting regular algorithm audits are necessary to compensate for student feelings of insecurity and anxiety, enhance trust in data analytics, and thereby promote student psychological well-being. psychology and law

assessment of the semantic sphere in clinical practice: adaptation and differential-diagnostic potential of j. nuttin's motivational induction method context and relevance. modern forensic psychological and psychiatric examination requires a systemic analysis of the individual's semantic sphere, which serves as the highest level of behavioral regulation. hypothesis. the modified version of j. nuttin's motivational induction method (mim) is a reliable and valid tool capable of identifying nosology-specific features of the motivational-semantic sphere in individuals who have committed unlawful acts. objective. to analyze the psychometric properties of the adapted method and to explore the features of the semantic sphere in personality disorders (pd) and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (ssd). methods and materials. the study involved 148 male participants, including individuals with personality disorders (pd), schizophrenia spectrum disorders (ssd), and mentally healthy individuals. to assess the motivational-semantic structure and time perspective, j. nuttin’s motivational induction method (mim) and v.e. milman’s motivational structure assessment technique were used. method modification. to solve the set tasks, j. nuttin’s mim was modified and translated into a quantitative assessment system: the temporal code was used to encode responses regarding the moment of the illegal act; the list of "persons" was divided into three groups in the assessment of the content of motivation; the assessment of the content of motivational objects was modified to reflect the goals and objectives of the expert assessment of the semantic perception of a legally significant situation. results. psychometric analysis confirmed the reliability and validity of mim. factor analysis revealed qualitative differences in the structure of the groups' meaning sphere, enabling the empirical substantiation of the method's differential-diagnostic potential: individuals with pd demonstrate temporal ambivalence, a dominance of hedonistic motives, and a passive-dependent social stance. meanwhile, examinees with ssd were characterized by a narrowed future perspective, contradictory self-reflection, and semantic fragmentation. conclusions. mim is a reliable tool for clinical psychodiagnostics. the method allows for the objectification of the characteristics of the meaning sphere and possesses high differential-diagnostic potential in distinguishing between pathocharacterological and endogenous types of response. limitations and future prospects. a necessary step toward integrating mim into forensic psychiatric expert practice is the addition of variables related to legally relevant circumstances, as well as expanding the sample and the nosological spectrum of the participants. psychology and law

the relationship between aggressive behavior and perceptions of parental attitudes among adolescents context and relevance. the issue of parent-child relationships and the education system, as well as their influence on a child's behavior, still remains relevant in modern psychological and educational research. at the same time, the results of studies on the connection between children's views of their parents' behavior and the displays of aggression in adolescents often contradict each other. objective. determining the presence and quality of the connection between an adolescent's view of their parents' attitude and how they show aggression. hypothesis. the manifestation of aggression in an adolescent's behavior is linked to the specific characteristics of their subjective perception of their parents' attitude toward them. methods and materials. the study involved 104 students from a comprehensive school in moscow (56 boys and 48 girls) aged 13-14 years. to assess the level of aggressive behavior, the following instruments were used: the "buss-perry aggression questionnaire (bpaq-24)" (adapted by s.n. enikolopov and n.p. tsibulsky) and the "aggressive behavior" scale (e.p. ilyin and p.a. kovalev). adolescents' perceptions of parental attitudes were assessed using the "adolescents about parents" test (l.i. vasserman, i.a. gorkovaya, and e.e. romitsyna). results the presence and quality of the connection between the adolescent’s perception of parental attitude and his manifestation of aggression was established. conclusions. it has been shown that there is a significant inverse relationship between an adolescent’s perception of his parents’ positive attitude towards him and the characteristics of his aggressive behavior. at the same time, a direct link was found between forms of aggressive behavior in children and a hostile or detached attitude towards them on the part of both parents, as well as an inconsistent attitude on the part of the mother. psychology and law
