the restorative process in restorative justice programs for juvenile offense situations context and relevance. restorative justice programs for juvenile offenses demonstrate a fundamental difference from conventional responses to unlawful behavior, which accounts for their effectiveness. recognition on this fact and the expansion of the restorative approach in the field of childhood has led to the widespread use of this term, while simultaneously blurring and distorting perceptions of the essence of the restorative paradigm in dealing with criminal and conflict situations. as a criterion of classifying practices under this paradigm, the concept of “restorative process” is proposed, the main characteristic of which is the specific transformations occurring in participants and in the relationships between them. objective. to construct a working concept of the “restorative process in restorative justice programs” and to identify the conditions, forms of manifestation, and characteristics of the restorative process in restorative justice programs for juvenile offenses. key research question: what constitutes the restorative process in restorative justice programs for juvenile offenses and what are its forms of manifestation? methods and materials of empirical research. the study employed qualitative methods of data collection and analysis: an analysis of seven case studies of restorative programs for juvenile offenses and semi-structured interviews with four facilitators of restorative programs. results. a working concept of the “restorative process” is formulated, its key characteristics, conditions, and obstacles to its implementation are identified, as well the specific features of the restorative process involving minors. conclusions. theoretical distinction between the concepts of “restorative program” and “restorative process” and phenomenological description of the restorative process and its characteristics made it possible to identify the transformations occurring in participants during a restorative program and to render visible, at the micro-level, the changes in human relationships that underlie the broader social meaning of restorative justice as a paradigm. psychology and law

hostility and social distrust as predictors of deviant affiliation in adolescents context and relevance. according to the prosecutor general's office, juvenile crime in russia increased by 10% between january and november 2025, reaching 25,900 cases. more than half of these teenagers committed crimes as part of groups. during the same period, 89,600 children in our country became victims of crime. according to the investigative committee of the russian federation, 2,000 children suffered from domestic violence in 2024. however, it was noted that domestic violence is a latent phenomenon—children experiencing violence do not seek help, and the actual situation is many times higher than the reported crime statistics. objective. to identify and analyze specific intrapersonal and intrafamily psychological characteristics of adolescents associated with the risk of developing deviant behavior and affiliation with destructive groups. hypothesis. the link between negative intra-family relationships and the risk of deviant affiliation in minors is mediated by high levels of hostility and distrust towards the social environment. methods and materials. the study involved 142 adolescents aged 12 to 18 years (m = 15.12, 56% boys, 44% girls), students in grades 5—11 of schools and gymnasiums in ufa. a range of methods was used: the buss—durkee hostility inventory (a. buss, a. durkee) was used to assess aggression and hostility; projective techniques such as "unfinished sentences" (j. sachs, s. levy; modified by v. mikhal) and " unfinished sentences, the child's attitude to violence" (j. sachs, s. levy; modified by e.n. volkova) were used to study the underlying attitudes of adolescents to their immediate environment; and the "antivitality and resilience" questionnaire (o.a. sagalakova, d.v. truevtsev) was used to analyze negative experiences and assess the family climate, as well as the tendency to antisocial behavior. results. a statistically significant phenomenon of frustrated aggression was identified, in which high levels of hostility are combined with reduced overall aggression. a sharp contrast was found in emotional attitudes toward parents: a positive attitude toward the mother, compared to an extremely negative perception of the father. thirty-seven percent of respondents experienced abuse, 17% experienced emotional violence in the family, and 48% of minors lack trust in society due to fear of betrayal. the dominant coping strategy is forced independence, characteristic of 63% of respondents. a model of the relationship between family dysfunction and the risk of deviant affiliation in minors was empirically tested. correlation and regression analysis revealed that hostility and mistrust of the social environment (measured as a combination of loneliness and mistrust) are direct predictors of a tendency toward antisocial behavior and susceptibility to deviant groups. the influence of factors such as negative attitudes towards the father and the experience of abuse on the tendency to deviance is mediated by the formation of these psychological characteristics in adolescents. conclusions. a psychological risk syndrome, including mistrust of society and latent hostility associated with dysfunctional parent-child relationships, forms a complex of characteristics in adolescents that contribute to the development of a psychological profile sensitive to deviant affiliation. psychology and law

addictive personality attitude as an integrative feature of drug-addicted convicts determining their personal and behavioral characteristics in places of imprisonment context and relevance. the relevance of the chosen topic is due to the significance of studying the addictive personality attitude of drug-addicted convicts and its influence on their personal and behavioral characteristics. objective. the goal is to identify the impact of addictive personality traits on the personal and behavioral characteristics of drug-addicted convicts. methods and materials. the empirical study was conducted on the basis of correctional facilities of the federal penitentiary service of russia in the udmurt republic. the study involved 224 drug-addicted convicts. personal and behavioral characteristics were assessed using the following psychodiagnostic tools: " method for studying life sense orientations" (d.a. leontiev); "scale of addictive attitudes" (r. mcmalin, p. geilhar); questionnaire "life style index" (r. plutchik, g. kellerman, g. conte); questionnaire "propensity to search for sensations" (m. zuckerman); "questionnaire of coping methods" (t.l. kryukova, e.v. kuftyak); " method of self-attitude research" (v.v. stolin, s.r. pantileev); " method of character accentuation research" (g. shmishek); questionnaire "level of subjective control" (e.f. bazhin et al.). results. the structure of the addictive personality attitude of drug-addicted convicts was established, and significant interrelations of the personal and behavioral elements of the structural components of the addictive personality attitude were revealed. conclusions. drug-addicted convicts have an addictive personality trait as an integrative personality feature, which is a set of addictively conditioned personality and behavioral characteristics that determines the unconscious readiness to use drugs and initiates certain (aimed at obtaining strong emotional sensations) types of behavior in drug-addicted convicts in places of detention. psychology and law

features of attitudes towards family relationships in convicted men who previously served prison terms context and relevance. the rise in crime, which has reached its peak in the last decade, requires a thorough analysis of the root causes of various criminal acts in order to develop effective measures to prevent recidivism and successfully rehabilitate individuals who have served their sentences in correctional institutions. objective. to study attitudes towards family relationships in men convicted of violent and non-violent crimes who have previously served prison terms. hypotheses. men convicted of violent and non-violent crimes who have previously served prison terms are characterized by a disunited type of family cohesion and a rigid type of family adaptation; men convicted of violent crimes who have previously served prison terms do not have a structured type of family adaptation; men convicted of violent and non-violent crimes tend to have negative family attitudes: low cohesion, a desire for independence among family members, emotional detachment, a lack of common interests in spending free time, minimal support for each other, and an increased sense of anxiety when trying to establish communication or discuss problems. methods and materials. the questionnaires “family adaptation and cohesion scales”, faces-3, d. olson et al., adaptation by e.g. eidemiller, m.yu. gorodnova; “measuring attitudes in a married couple” by yu.e. aleshina et al.; semi-standardized interview. the empirical study was conducted in penal colonies of the territorial bodies of the federal penitentiary service in the vologda and sverdlovsk regions, the trans-baikal territory. results and conclusions. men convicted of violent crimes predominantly demonstrate hierarchical attitudes, which contribute to the belief that dominance and control over others are necessary. convicted men who have committed non-violent crimes often demonstrate a spontaneous desire for immediate gratification in their family life, while ignoring their obligations. psychology and law

social identity and stigmatization in the context of coping behavior among prisoners: а theoretical model context and relevance. in this paper, coping behavior of convicted individuals is examined through the lens of stigmatization as a key stress factor. social identity acts as a dual mechanism determining the choice of coping strategies: it can serve as a resource that mitigates the effects of stigmatization, or as a factor that reinforces destructive behavioral patterns. objective. to present a theoretical analysis of the role of social identity in the processes of coping with stigma-related stress in the penitentiary environment. theoretical framework. stigmatization is conceptualized as a form of identity threat that triggers processes of cognitive appraisal and coping. social identity, following h. tajfel's definition, is understood as the individual's knowledge of their membership in social groups, combined with the emotional and value significance attached to that membership. the stigmatization model is integrated into a modified transactional model of stress. results. it is demonstrated that convicted individuals, as a stigmatized group, face a dual challenge: external stigma and internal self-stigmatization. identification with the group of convicted individuals can perform both a "healing" and a "cursing" function. concealable stigma creates an additional stressor context associated with the need to manage information about one's group membership. conclusions. the problem of integrating the construct of stigmatization into research on coping behavior of convicted individuals is formulated, and directions for addressing it are proposed, with an emphasis on the multiplicity of social identities and the quality of group ties as a buffering mechanism. the novelty of the proposed approach is substantiated, lying in the integration of a modified coping-with-identity-threats model and a multiple-identity model to explain the choice of coping strategies in the penitentiary environment. psychology and law

coping strategies in dealing with the pathology of loneliness and the destruction of time experience in conditions of long-term solitary confinement (review of foreign experience) context and relevance. solitary confinement is systematically practiced in penal systems around the world despite the lack of scientifically proven criteria for its admissibility and clear evidence of its irreversible destructive effects on human psychophysiological health. as a result, it makes full resocialisation and reintegration impossible, increases the risk of recidivism, and reduces public safety. objective. systematisation of coping strategies used by convicts to deal with pathological loneliness and destructive time experience in long-term isolation, aimed at developing prevention and rehabilitation programmes for (former) prisoners. hypothesis. pathological loneliness and destructive time perception are not individual pathologies, but rather a systemic reaction of a healthy psyche to a violation of basic anthropological living conditions; at the same time, the psyche has adaptive potential that can be realised through specific coping strategies. methods and materials. the research methodology is based on the method of thematic analysis of scientific publications and phenomenological synthesis of data in the study of autobiographical evidence of convicts. the theoretical framework is made up of ideas from existential psychology and the theory of stress and coping. results. the components of ontological trauma caused by solitary confinement have been identified: 1) the historically conditioned transformation of humanistic reform into forms of psychological violence; 2) the universal pathology of loneliness as a biopsychological reaction to the destruction of human social nature; 3) the destruction of time experience. coping strategies have been systematised and described. conclusions. the systematisation and detailed development of coping strategies to deal with the traumatic experience caused by long-term solitary confinement is seen as the basis for preventive and rehabilitation programmes, providing opportunities for the gradual humanisation of penal practices and contributing strategically to strengthening and stabilising security in society by reducing recidivism rates. psychology and law

age and gender peculiarities of the relationship between malevolent creativity and cognitive personality characteristics context and relevance. the manifestation of malevolent creativity (mc) in fraud, corruption, disinformation, and conspiracy theories leaves the study of the relationship between creative thinking and behavior relevant. objective. to study and analyze the relationship of mc with cognitive personality traits. hypothesis. 1. the tendency to display malevolent creativity in harmful behavior is negatively associated with constructive thinking and positively associated with destructive thinking styles and difficulty processing incoming information; 2. this relationship has features depending on gender and age. methods and materials. the sample consisted of 424 people, including students from moscow universities n=156 people (m = 20.1, sd = 1.04, 49% of them girls) and adults n =266 people (m = 34.9, sd = 13.76, 59% of them women). the following methods were used: "behavioral features of malevolent creativity" (adaptation by meshkova et al.), s. epstein's constructive thinking questionnaire (adaptation by yenikolopov and lebedev), the bpaq-24 hostility scale (adaptation by yenikolopov and tsybulsky), "characteristics of the information and semantic field" (zlokazov et al.). results. the following patterns were identified: significant correlations of mc: 1. positive — with destructive thinking styles, hostility and the total indicator of the information and semantic field of personality (imf), 2. negative - with the scale of general constructive thinking (gct). differences in the strength of the association of mc with cognitive characteristics by gender and age have been revealed. men have significantly stronger bonds with gct and mc than the female. the connection between mc and imf is significantly stronger among young people compared to adults. differences between the samples by gender and age have been established: young people and men have lower imf and higher gct compared to adults and women; young people and women have higher categorical thinking compared to men and adults. conclusions. 1. people with a high propensity for mc have the following cognitive profile: low constructive thinking combined with high hostility, developed destructive thinking styles, impairments in the information and semantic field of personality, i.e. they do not know how to adjust their way of thinking to the requirements of the situation in order to act effectively, see the world only in black and white categories, are subject to generally accepted superstitions, believe in various omens, are insufficiently critical of incoming information, are more focused on avoiding failures, are suspicious, have difficulty processing incoming information because of its dynamism, redundancy, and heterogeneity. 2. mc is not the result of any one destructive style of thinking, but only one developed constructive thinking does not protect a person from having mc. here, a balance is important not only for constructive and destructive styles of thinking, but also for other cognitive features. men have the most developed component compared to women, constructive thinking, and, consequently, instability to stress, plays the greatest role as a predictor of high mc. in young people, the inability to navigate incoming information and choose constructive solutions (violations in the information and semantic field of personality) is the least developed compared to adults, but it has become a predictor of a tendency to behavior in which mc is realized. 3. the established differences and general patterns of cognitive characteristics between the samples by gender and age (youth and men have a lower total index of the information and semantic field and higher overall constructive thinking compared to adults and women; women and youth have a more developed destructive style in the form of categorical thinking compared to adults and men), as well as correlations with destructive thinking styles, allow us to identify those thinking styles that are not risk factors for the association of malevolent creativity and behavior in the age groups we studied (up to 50 years) — this is the naive optimism thinking style. psychology and law

creative competence of a legal psychology instructor as a resource for burnout prevention and student motivation background. teaching legal psychology courses involves a continuous analysis of destructive and criminal behavior, creating risks of emotional exhaustion among university teachers and a decrease in students' intrinsic academic motivation. traditional reproductive teaching methods in this subject area demonstrate limited effectiveness. objective. empirical verification of the influence of a teacher's creative competence (implemented through project-game and simulation technologies) on reducing professional burnout among educators and increasing academic motivation among students of the faculty of legal psychology. methods. formative experiment with a control group. sample: 14 university teachers (teaching experience 11.4 years) and 86 students (2nd—3rd years). diagnostic instruments: maslach burnout inventory (mbi, adapted by n.e. vodopyanova, e.s. starchenkova), academic motivation scale (ams, adapted by t.o. gordeeva et al.), semi-structured interviews, feedback questionnaire. statistical analysis: mann—whitney u test, wilcoxon t test. results. a statistically significant reduction in teachers' emotional exhaustion by 18.5% (p < 0.05) and depersonalization by 14.2% (p < 0.05) was recorded in the experimental group; the increase in students' intrinsic academic motivation reached 23% compared to the control group (p < 0.01). a 31% reduction in students' fear of professional errors was revealed. conclusions. creative educational technologies ("con_cretely about conflict creatively!", "psychological moot court", "narralaw") serve as an effective bilateral resource, simultaneously mitigating teacher burnout and enhancing student professional-oriented motivation. psychology and law

analysis of professional standards: normative model of professional activity of psychologist (part 1) context and relevance. in the absence of a unified federal law on psychological assistance, professional standards serve as the primary regulator of psychologists' activities. however, the disparity of standards adopted over the years complicates understanding the normative content of the profession, creating the risk of formalism in the training and employment of specialists. objective. to analyze the content of professional standards as a set of idealized notions of activity and to define the normative model they propose. hypothesis. existing professional standards vary in the elements of their activity system (from the breadth of coverage of clients' psychological problems to the demands placed on the individual and the environment) and reflect the internal contradictions of the profession, particularly between its declared subjectivity and the strict regulation of procedures. methods and materials. we used j. engeström's activity system model, which allows us to identify the following elements of activity: object (client problems), tools (methods), rules (regulatory framework), division of labor (interaction), community, and subject. the empirical base consisted of 15 current professional standards, selected based on their relevance to the psychological field. results. a lack of a unified terminological and functional framework was established: widespread types of activities (diagnosis, counseling, development) have been identified, while psychotherapy, supervision and expertise remain in the "gray zone". the tendency towards universality of activities in a number of standards has been revealed, as opposed to narrowly functional administration in others. conclusions. the normative model of a psychologist's activity in russia is characterized by high variability and systemic gaps: specialists in different fields are characterized by accents on different elements of activity. psychology and law

diagnostics of dispositions of violent extremism — short version context and relevance. violent extremism remains a significant problem in the modern world (radicalization and deradicalization, 2025). this article presents the results of the validation of an abbreviated version of the methodology for diagnosing violent extremism dispositions in adolescents and young adults. objective. to analyze and test the factor structure of the methodology for diagnosing violent extremism dispositions in a sample of young adults. hypothesis. there is an acceptable factor structure for the methodology of diagnosing dispositions of violent extremism. methods and materials. the adaptation of the methodology involved 715 students from russian universities. the bass-perry aggression questionnaire was adapted by s.n. enikolopov and n.p. tsibulsky, and the s.n. enikolopov and n.p. tsibulsky legitimized aggression questionnaire was used to assess socially acceptable aggression. results. when checking the external validity, statistically significant associations between the dispositions of violent extremism and the scales of legitimized aggression were found. when checking the factor structure of the methodology on both samples using confirmatory factor analysis, it was revealed that the six-factor structure is acceptable. conclusions. the paper presents a new model of a shortened methodology consisting of six scales: "dehumanization," "mysticalism," "acceptance of violence," "readiness for violence," "reductive maximalism," and "openness and peacefulness" as a counterfactor. the resulting model proved to be reliable and valid (internal and external validity). psychology and law
how couples sustain active friendship in intimate relationships: a grounded theory study of relational processes contemporary family therapy

the role of perceived social support in the psychological well-being of forced migrants context and relevance. the multiple consequences of forced migration lead to the need for a comprehensive study of the factors of psychological well-being of migrants. objective. to assess the relationship between psychological well-being and perceived social support (pss) among forced migrants. hypothesis. pss is significantly related to such well-being components as positive emotions and relationships. methods and materials. 75 women (23,5 ± 10,0) and 125 men (20,5 ± 5,2) participated in the study. two extreme groups (each n = 51) were identified based on pss level. we used a short version of depression, anxiety, and stress scales (lovibond, lovibond, 1995), modified dembo-rubinstein method (shaigerova et al., 2019), subjective life satisfaction scale (cantril, 1965), modified semantic differential method (molchanov, almazova, pоskrebysheva, 2023), intersectional day–to–day discrimination index (scheim, bauer, 2019), ucla loneliness scale-3 (russell, 1996), multidimensional scale of perceived social support (zimet et al., 1988), subjective effectiveness of various coping strategies in daily life (shaigerova et al., 2024), frequency of seeking help from various categories of people (ushkov et al., 2020). results. respondents with high pss were more likely to seek help from close individuals, relied on a wider range of coping strategies, and demonstrated better indicators of emotional state and self-esteem. participants with a low pss were more likely to seek help from members of a "secondary support group", relied on maladaptive coping strategies. an interaction effect between gender and pss was found in subjective effectiveness of certain coping strategies. conclusions. pss level is related to components of psychological well-being among forced migrants, which is essential in developing programs for adaptation and resocialization in a new sociocultural environment. social psychology and society

attitudes towards digital educational technologies among international and russian students at multinational university: motivational and personality predictors context and relevance. internationalization and digitalization are the most important trends in modern higher education. in russian psychology, there is a lack of research on the psychological predictors of international students' attitudes towards digital educational technologies (dets) in the context of intercultural adaptation issues. objective. to identify the characteristics of attitudes towards the dets and its motivational and personality predictors among international students from cis and non-cis countries compared to russian students of russian multinational university. hypotheses: (1) international students, especially from non-cis countries, have a less positive attitudes towards the dets than russian students; (2) types of academic motivation are more often significant predictors for attitudes towards the dets compared to personality traits in all students’ groups; and (3) personality traits are more often significant predictors for attitudes towards the dets among international students compared to russian students. methods and materials. the study involved 480 students from a multinational russian university: 223 international university students (71,7% female) from 40 countries aged 17 to 39 years (m = 22,34; sd = 3,44) and 257 russian university students (71,2% female) aged 17 to 36 years (m = 19,86; sd = 2,05). for diagnostics, the author's "attitudes towards dets scale for university students", a short russian-language version of the five-factor questionnaire, and the "academic motivation scale" were used. results. intercultural differences were confirmed both in the severity of attitudes towards dets and its components, and in their relationships with motivational and personality factors among university students from asian cis countries and non-cis countries compared to russian students. conclusions. it is necessary to develop programs to increase the interest, awareness, and practical skills of international students for working with the dets of a particular university, taking into account the identified cultural, motivational, and personality characteristics, which will contribute to better adaptation to education in russia in university students from different countries. social psychology and society

the specificity of the relationship between resilience and civic and ethnic identity and strong-willed qualities among buryat, yakut and russian youth context and relevance. in the context of multinational russian society, the problem of the relationship between resilience and civic and ethnic identity and strong-willed qualities acquires particular significance.objective. to identify and compare the structure of the relationships between resilience components, civic and ethnic identity and strong-willed qualities in students of buryat, yakut, and russian ethnicities.hypothesis. there are significant positive links between resilience components, indicators of civic and ethnic identity and strong-willed qualities in the groups studied; the structure of these relationships has an ethnocultural specificity, manifested in the strength and configuration of the correlation constellations in buryats, yakuts and russians. methods and materials. the study involved 397 students from the trans-baikal territory, the republic of buryatia, and the republic of sakha (yakutia) aged 16 to 24. diagnostics were carried out by the following methods: the test “resilience of an adult” (a.v. makhnach), child and youth resilience measure (cyrm-28) (in adaptation of a.v. makhnach and a.i. laktionova), the questionnaire of strong-willed qualities of personality (m.v. chumakov), the civic identity express assessment scale (a.n. tatarko, n.m. lebedeva), the ethnic identity express assessment scale (n.m. lebedeva). spearman's rank correlation coefficient was used for data analysis. results. in all three groups, family and social ties have appeared as the universal resource of resilience. purposefulness, energy, initiative, and responsibility have formed the universal regulatory core of strong-willed qualities. spirituality demonstrated three cultural patterns: integrative in russians, regulatory in buryats, and contextual in yakuts. the ethnic identity certainty proved to be more significant for the overall resilience of yakuts; the positivity of civic identity is more significant for russians. independence is not related to resilience in any group, while among the buryats a negative association with spirituality was found. conclusions. family and social ties are strongly associated with overall resilience in subjects, regardless of nationality. identity (ethnic and civic) is included in the system of personal resilience resources, but the nature of the relationships is culturally specific. spirituality plays different roles in the three cultures. independence is not associated with resilience components in the study groups. social psychology and society

two terms for one concept: why the duplication? the article proposes continuing the discussion initiated in the paper by n.n. tolstykh and a.v. makhnach “on the doubling of the term: zhiznesposobnost and/or resilience?” (tolstykh, makhnach, 2026), regarding the use of two concepts: individual resilience of parents (denoted as “rezilentnost’” in russian) and the corresponding family-level construct (denoted as “zhiznesposobnost’” in russian), as presented in the article by o.a. ulyanina et al. “family as a resource for overcoming difficult life situations in children affected by hostilities” (ulyanina et al., 2025). the article under discussion also employs other ambiguous concepts related to the issue. the authors argue for using the term “resilience” in russian-language academic papers both in relation to the individual and to the family. their argumentation is grounded in the principle of unambiguous terminology, which ensures the effectiveness of scientific language. they note that the constructs of individual resilience (“rezilentnost’”) for parents and the corresponding family-level construct (“zhiznesposobnost’”) denote similar essential features. social psychology and society

adaptation of the russian-language version of the dual filial-piety scale (dfps-ru) context and relevance. against the backdrop of global growth in life expectancy and population ageing, the study of intergenerational relations is becoming increasingly pertinent. however, russian scholarly discourse lacks a universal diagnostic instrument for examining the variability of care for older adults. objective. to adapt for russian-speaking populations a contemporary version of the 'dual filial-piety scale', originally developed by asian scholars. methods and materials. the scale was translated and subsequently administered to 363 respondents from the karachay-cherkess republic (karachay students, including 225 women and 138 men; mean age = 20,64 years). results. psychometric evaluation of the russian adaptation yielded significant results confirming the replicability of the original measure's two-factor structure — authoritarian and reciprocal respect toward elders. the findings demonstrate good psychometric properties, evidenced by structural model parameters and scale reliability indices. confirmatory factor analysis (cfa) indicated a good fit for the original two-factor model. furthermore, this study extends the application of the eastern filial piety construct to western cultural contexts while accounting for sample-specific cultural characteristics. conclusions. the adapted russian version demonstrates satisfactory psychometric properties and can serve as a valid research instrument for investigating respect towards elders and intergenerational communication phenomena. social psychology and society

the relationship between intercultural competence and prosocial and antisocial creativity in russian students context and relevance. intercultural competence is one of the key competencies that modern universities cultivate in their students. its high level is associated not only with more effective intercultural interaction but can also stimulate creativity. however, creativity should be considered not only in terms of originality but also in the context of its social orientation. objective. to identify the relationship between intercultural competence and prosocial and antisocial creativity in students at russian universities. materials and methods. the study involved 214 undergraduate and graduate students from russian universities (m = 21,99; sd = 3,47, 83,65% women). the study questionnaire included the cultural intelligence scale (cqs), the malevolent creativity behavior scale (mcbs), and the positive creativity engagement scale. the representation of students from other cultures in the study group and the relationship between educational profile and intercultural communication were also recorded. results. the results showed that the motivational and behavioral components of intercultural competence were positively associated with prosocial creativity; the metacognitive component was negatively associated with antisocial creativity in the form of lying, and the behavioral component was negatively associated with antisocial creativity in the form of harm, but at the level of a statistical trend. conclusions. specific relationships between the components of intercultural competence and student creativity were identified. while they can serve as a resource for supporting prosocial creativity, antisocial creativity is not reducible to a competency deficit and requires consideration of additional factors. social psychology and society

assessing the social skills of migrant students: a theoretical model and the development of a diagnostic tool context and relevance. psychological and pedagogical support for students with a migration background requires theoretical conceptualization of social skills as a component of adaptation in the educational environment, as well as the development of a diagnostic tool to assess these skills. objective. to propose a theoretical culturally specific model of migrant students’ social skills that reflect their successful acculturation in the russian educational environment, and to develop a diagnostic tool for their assessment. methods and materials. multidimensional scale of school students’ life satisfaction; achenbach questionnaire; brief sociocultural maladjustment scale. results. the developed social skills questionnaire for migrant children demonstrated high internal reliability (cronbach's alpha > 0,9), factor analysis revealed three scales ("behavior in educational situation," "interaction with peers," "compliance with school rules"). significant correlations were found between social skills, psychological well-being, and successful sociocultural adaptation. conclusions. social skills were found to form a single construct comprising three distinct groups, each of which is relevant to migrant students' adaptation to the russian educational context and applies universally across all school levels: skills related to classroom behavior, peer interaction, and adherence to school rules. a diagnostic instrument to assess these skills was developed and pilot-tested. social psychology and society

ecosystemic diagnosis of social integration among forcibly displaced children from artsakh context and relevance. forcibly displaced children from conflict zones like artsakh face profound challenges in social integration due to the rupture of social ties and continuous existential insecurity. existing individual-level diagnostic tools inadequately address this complexity, failing to reflect the dynamic interaction between the child's internal resources and the multilayered environment. purpose. this research aims to fill the diagnostic gap by operationalizing and empirically validating a multilevel socio-pedagogical ecosystemic diagnostic model (spedm) to objectively assess integration risks for forcibly displaced children. hypothesis. the primary hypothesis posits that the mesosystem (social ties) will function as the primary structural mediator, linking distal exosystemic resources (institutional support) to the social integration outcome, rather than the exosystem having a direct independent effect. materials and methods. a comparative, mixed-methods design was employed, collecting data from 300 forcibly displaced children (fdcg, aged 7—15) from artsakh and a matched non-displaced comparative group (ndcg). structural equation modeling (sem) was used to test the measurement and structural models. results. the spedm demonstrated excellent goodness-of-fit (cfi = 0,965; rmsea = 0,051), confirming the structural consistency of the constructs. the combined ecological factors explained of the variance (r2 = 0,64). a critical finding was that the exosystem's influence was not direct but exhibited a strong indirect association statistically mediated by the mesosystem, which showed the strongest direct association with integration (β = 0,40). conclusions. the study validates the structural necessity of relational mediation under displacement conditions. the derived socio-pedagogical ecosystemic index (sei) translates these findings into a standardized quantitative metric, shifting case management from intuition-based assessment to targeted socio-pedagogical intervention planning. social psychology and society

psychological and sociocultural adaptation of forced migrants in the krasnodar region: problems and resources for overcoming them context and relevance. forced migration leads to mental health problems, existential uncertainty, and high sensitivity to the attitudes of the host society. a study of forced migrants' adaptation in specific regions with a large number of migrants is particularly important. the krasnodar krai, a historically multicultural region, has become home to tens of thousands of people from conflict zones. objective. to study the psychological and sociocultural adaptation of forced migrants in the krasnodar krai.research questions. what are the most common problems forced migrants face during their adaptation to a new sociocultural environment? what are the main strategies and resources forced migrants use to overcome difficulties in psychological and sociocultural adaptation? methods and materials. the sample consisted of 25 forced migrants from the territories of the new constituent entities of the russian federation and from ukraine. the study was conducted using a qualitative design (thematic data analysis) and semi-structured interviews. results. the need to overcome trauma is realized through involvement in helping practices and a focus on supporting others in similar situations. the cultural and linguistic proximity of migrants to the host society can increase feelings of psychological alienation. migrants rebuild symbolic and social boundaries to preserve their identity in a context where external similarities mask profound differences in lived experience. conclusions. the adaptation of forced migrants is a contradictory process where post-traumatic stress coexists with an active search for new sources of stability in life. social psychology and society

co-occurrence of post-traumatic stress disorder and substance use disorder among out patients in a nigerian general hospital purpose this paper aims to investigate the prevalence and relationship between post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) and alcohol and other substance use disorders in a clinical population in nigeria, a low- and middle-income (lami) country. there exists evidence that ptsd increases vulnerability to both the onset and persistence of substance misuse and often complicates treatment outcomes, though there is data paucity in lami countries. design/methodology/approach a cross-sectional study was conducted among 285 patients attending the outpatient clinics of karu general hospital over a seven-month period. participants were selected using systematic random sampling. data were collected using a socio-demographic questionnaire and the ptsd, alcohol use disorder (aud) and substance use disorder modules of the mini international neuropsychiatric interview. findings ptsd was diagnosed in 40 participants, representing a prevalence of 14%, although only 1.4% had been previously identified with the condition. non-alcohol substance use disorder was highly prevalent (88.1%), while aud was present in 22.5% of participants. participants diagnosed with aud were almost three times more likely to have ptsd compared with those without aud [odds ratio (or): 2.74, 95% confidence level [ci]: 1.25–5.83; p < 0.001]. similarly, participants with other substance use disorders (suds) were over three times more likely to be diagnosed with ptsd than those without such disorders (or: 3.38, 95% ci: 1.34–8.02; p < 0.01). originality/value the results contribute to the sparse evidence regarding comorbidity between ptsd and suds in lami countries. advances in dual diagnosis
conceptualization and perspective-taking in narrative discourse: cross-linguistic event and entity management in syrian arabic and french (l1/l2) discourse processes

improving employees’ job-stress mindset with an online micro-intervention: a randomized controlled study we tested the effectiveness of an online stress-mindset micro-intervention specific to job stress in a sample of 120 employees. we examined whether the intervention improves stress mindset, well-being, and cognitive appraisal. we randomly assigned participants to an intervention or control condition (i.e. alternative treatment or passive control group). participants took part in the intervention at the beginning of the study and filled out another survey two weeks later. the intervention included a video about the benefits of stressful situations and a writing task. one half of the intervention group received a booster session after one week (intervention group with booster) and one half did not (intervention group without booster). regression analyses showed that the intervention improved stress mindset right after intervention and two weeks later. we did not observe a fade-out effect. both intervention groups reported reduced exhaustion and hindrance appraisal. participants in the intervention group without booster reported a less pronounced decrease in work engagement and, contrary to expectations, a decrease in challenge appraisal compared to the passive control group. our results imply that employees’ stress mindset can be improved with an online micro-intervention and that this intervention reduces employee exhaustion and hindrance appraisal. european journal of work and organizational psychology

transitions in preschool children's internalizing and externalizing symptoms before and during the covid-19 pandemic: the role of family disruptions in singapore. the covid-19 pandemic disrupted family routines, economic security, and caregiving contexts, with potential consequences for children's mental health. however, less is known about heterogeneity in preschool children's changes in internalizing and externalizing symptoms from before to during the pandemic and about how pandemic-related family disruptions predicted these transitions. this study examined symptom transitions among 2,601 preschool children from the singapore longitudinal early development study, using pre-pandemic data from 2018-2019 and during-pandemic data from 2021 (age = 4.92 years,= 1.18; 50.17% girls). latent profile analysis identified three groups at both waves: low, mild, and severe symptoms. random intercept latent transition analysis revealed four transition patterns: stable low symptoms (63.40%), worsening symptoms (22.30%), stable mild symptoms (6.23%), and improved symptoms (7.73%). compared with the stable low symptoms group, older children and those from families negatively impacted by the pandemic in work and family function were more likely to experience stable mild or worsening symptoms. ethnic differences were also observed, and pandemic-related financial stress was associated with both worsening and improved symptom patterns. these findings highlight heterogeneous symptom transitions among preschool children and underscore the importance of considering demographic characteristics and family-level disruptions when supporting children's mental health following large-scale crises. development and psychopathology

perceived family instability, involvement in interparental conflict, and depression in adolescents abstract family instability and involvement in interparental conflict have long been identified as risk factors for adolescent depression; however, adolescent perceptions may be an underexamined measure of family instability which could produce cascading effects toward depressive symptoms. altered perceptions due to cognitive maturation and puberty may make adolescents particularly attuned to deviations in the stability of the family system. moreover, their involvement in parents’ conflicts may further amplify their vulnerability to these stressful environmental experiences and increase their likelihood of depression. therefore, perceived family instability, involvement in interparental conflict, and depressive symptoms were examined in 296 adolescents (50.3% female, mostly white) across three annual waves starting at age 13 years. using autoregressive latent trajectory modeling, between-person results showed that adolescents with higher initial levels of perceived family instability tended to show higher initial depression levels, and some adolescents’ involvement in their parents’ disputes increased faster than others over this three-year period. within-person results indicated that adolescents experiencing higher-than-usual perceived family instability at age 14 exhibited significantly higher depressive symptoms at age 15, pointing to the unfolding emotional cost of instability for early-to-middle adolescents. findings emphasize modeling enduring vulnerabilities and intra-individual fluctuations in family and emotional processes during adolescence. development and psychopathology

the long shadow of social withdrawal: the impact of social withdrawal in adolescence on adult developmental outcomes – the trails study abstract social withdrawal in late childhood and adolescence is linked to long-term developmental challenges, yet its unique impact on adult adaptive functioning remains understudied. this trails study ( n = 1,798 in the population cohort, m ( sd ) age at t1: 11.1 (0.6), 49% boys, 86.5% ethnically dutch, m ( sd ) age at t7: 28.9 (0.6); n = 405 in the high-risk cohort, m ( sd ) age at t1: 11.1 (0.5), 66% boys, 97.6% ethnically dutch, m ( sd ) age at t7: 29.6 (0.7)) examined whether social withdrawal during the ages of 11 to 16 predicted the achievement of developmental milestones by age 29, including romantic competence, residential autonomy, friendship satisfaction, work competence, and financial competence. higher levels of social withdrawal consistently predicted lower likelihood of having achieved these milestones by age 29 (median or = 0.76 in both cohorts), even after controlling for peer victimization, cognitive abilities, and family background measured in early adolescence. these effects were consistent across cohorts and gender. sensitivity analyses that accounted for genetic confounding and clinical conditions (e.g., autism, depression) further supported the findings. these results highlight social withdrawal as a critical risk factor for developmental disadvantages, urging early interventions to foster social engagement and mitigate long-term maladjustment. development and psychopathology

the adolescent reward system: longitudinal brain–behavior dynamics and pandemic effects abstract adolescence is a critical period of brain development characterized by heightened reward sensitivity, which influences behavior and emotional regulation. major life events, like the covid-19 pandemic, may affect reward system development. this longitudinal study integrates self-reported behavioral activation system (bas) measures with fmri data from the adolescent brain cognitive development study® to examine reward processing during versus before the pandemic. 5,405 participants (m age = 9.92, sd = 0.62) completed the monetary incentive delay task during fmri scanning and bas assessments at baseline and year 2. participants were grouped by whether their year 2 follow-up occurred before or during the pandemic. generalized linear mixed models examined changes in bas subscales (drive, fun-seeking, reward responsiveness); fmri analyses assessed neural activation in key cortical/subcortical regions. brain network analysis evaluated functional connectivity across reward and executive networks. results revealed a decline across all bas subscales at year 2 compared to baseline, with more pronounced reductions in bas drive among those assessed during the pandemic. network analysis showed cohesive executive but variable reward network changes, especially in the right hemisphere. developmental changes in reward sensitivity were accompanied by shifts in activation in core reward regions (e.g., nucleus accumbens, caudate, putamen, thalamus), which also varied by age and sex. findings show declines in reward sensitivity over time, and reveal subtle but meaningful adaptations in reward-related brain function in relation to the pandemic, highlighting the need to consider individual differences during adolescence, especially under stress. development and psychopathology

differences in perceived experiences of ai-based versus human psychological support among dual users: paired comparisons, hierarchical regression, and repeated-measures sensitivity analysis bmc psychology
development and validation of a scale for measuring irrational behavior in undergraduate students’ online discourse bmc psychology

effectiveness of cognitive behavioural therapy on anxiety and depression symptoms in naturalistic settings for patients with and without personality disorders. objectives: personality disorders (pd) are often considered a negative prognostic factor for cognitive behavioural therapy (cbt) in anxiety and depression, yet evidence from real-world settings with rigorous diagnostic assessment remains limited. this study examined whether pd diagnosis influences cbt outcomes using data from intherapy, an italian cbt service integrating systematic outcome monitoring with structured diagnostic assessment (scid-5).
methods: patients receiving cbt for anxiety and/or depression were classified according to the presence or absence of a pd and assessed on anxiety, depression, and psychosocial functioning. treatment effectiveness was evaluated through symptom change, reliable and clinically significant improvement (rcsi), and recovery rates. mixed-effects growth curve models examined outcome trajectories, and regression analyses tested the role of pd diagnosis, treatment exposure, and dropout status.
results: cbt was associated with a rcsi rate of 50%, with moderate-to-large pre-post effect sizes for anxiety (d = .77), depression (d = .76), and functioning (d = .63). although patients with pd presented with higher baseline severity and lower recovery rates, pd diagnosis did not independently predict outcomes when baseline severity, dropout status, and number of sessions were controlled for. symptom trajectories were nonlinear and largely comparable across groups. notably, patients with pd who dropped out late showed greater functional impairment at discharge than late dropouts without pd.
conclusions: these findings suggest that standard disorder-specific cbt is effective for patients with comorbid pd in real-world practice. apparent poorer outcomes primarily reflect greater initial severity, underscoring the importance of adequate treatment duration and strategies to prevent late dropout. british journal of clinical psychology

host country nationals’ acculturation preferences: the interplay of social dominance, stereotype content, perceived threats and benefits, and diversity ideologies host-country nationals’ (hcns’) acculturation preferences are critical in understanding how immigrants acculturate. therefore, previous research has examined how different theoretical models and approaches, along with their corresponding intercultural elements, are associated with hcns’ acculturation preferences. among the most prevalent intercultural elements are social dominance orientation from social dominance theory, perceived social structures and stereotypes from the stereotype content model, perceived threats and benefits from the threat-benefit model, and diversity ideologies from the intergroup diversity ideologies model. however, there seems to be less clarity as to which of these elements, when competing together, are most associated with hcns’ acculturation preferences in private and work settings, particularly toward hispanic immigrants in the u.s. we address this question using a latent profile analysis and logistic regression in a sample of 647 hcns in the u.s. our results indicate that most hcns preferred some sort of integration in both private and work settings, with only a few adopting an “indifference” acculturation preference in which hcns have no definitive acculturation preference. moreover, when competing together, we found that hcns reporting higher levels of perceived symbolic benefits, multiculturalism, and polyculturalism were more likely to prefer a form of integration as opposed to an “indifference” acculturation preference. journal of cross-cultural psychology

cultural tightness increases lay theory of learned prejudice incorporating research on lay theories of prejudice and culture, the present research ( n total = 1,912) investigates cultural tightness-looseness as an antecedent of a lay theory of learned prejudice. studies 1 and 4, recruiting across nine countries (united states, mexico, germany, israel, chile, france, greece, south africa, and japan), demonstrated that people who lived in tighter societies more strongly believe that prejudice is learned. studies 2 and 3 experimentally showed that u.s. participants who imagined themselves in a tight (vs. loose) society endorsed this lay theory more, regardless of the prejudice level in the simulated society. notably, lay theory of learned prejudice was associated with greater support for educational activism and policies (studies 3 and 4). together, these findings expand the understanding of how people conceptualize the origins of prejudice, while advancing a cultural psychology of lay theories. journal of cross-cultural psychology

aging language: understanding how human cognition changes as we grow old abstract language lies at the core of human nature. it is, therefore, not surprising that it has long been investigated as a privileged domain for understanding how human cognition is structured and organized. because language is not monolithic across the lifespan, examining how it changes at different life stages has become a powerful means of advancing our understanding not only of language itself, but also of other cognitive functions—and of cognition as a whole—in light of the transformations it undergoes at specific developmental and aging phases. topics in cognitive science

longitudinal associations among teacher–student relationships, academic self-efficacy, and prosocial behavior in chinese left-behind adolescents: a three-wave ri-clpm study journal of youth and adolescence

‘for the first time, i felt seen’: understanding what helps autistic emerging adults feel safe and included on social media social media is a prominent part of everyday life and is used regularly to connect users with a diverse network of content and people from around the world. research on social media among autistic individuals has largely focused on online risks (e.g., cyberbullying) among children and adolescents, with limited attention to the perspectives of autistic emerging adults (i.e., aged 18–29), particularly regarding social media safety and inclusion. the aim of this qualitative study was to understand what helps autistic emerging adults feel safe and included on social media, focusing on their lived experience and recommendations for improvement. data was collected from 50 autistic emerging adults ( m age = 24.57, sd = 3.01) through an online open-ended survey. using reflexive thematic analysis, we generated three key themes: (a) welcomed by a community of allies, (b) curating my experience and (c) communicating in ways that work for me. the findings offer insight into the features and strategies used by autistic emerging adults to feel safe and included when using social media, and provides practical recommendations to foster a safer and more inclusive online environment for neurodivergent individuals. lay abstract social media is a part of everyday life and is used by many people to connect with others around the world. to our knowledge, no research has looked at what helps autistic emerging adults (people aged between 18–29 years) feel safe and included on social media. we wanted to understand this. we created an online survey with open-ended questions about social media use, asking 50 autistic emerging adults questions regarding their thoughts on what helps them to feel safe and included when using social media. we also asked for their ideas about what could be improved. we used a type of process called reflexive thematic analysis to look at patterns in what people said. we created three themes that we feel represented these patterns, which we called (a) welcomed by a community of allies, (b) curating my experience and (c) communicating in ways that work for me. participants spoke about feeling seen and accepted among others who shared they were autistic online. they also spoke about strategies they used to control what they experienced, and appreciated the different ways in which they could interact with others using social media. participants felt more autism education was needed online, and made suggestions relating to more safety and custom settings on social media platforms. the findings of this study give insight into what helps autistic emerging adults feel safe and included when using social media. autism

indirect genetic effects on psychosocial development and the potential role of genetic nurture environmentally mediated parental influences can inflate estimates of genetic effects by producing indirect genetic effects: associations between relatives’ genotypes, often parents’, and an individual's phenotype after accounting for the individual's genotype. renewed efforts to study indirect genetic effects involved showing that parental alleles not inherited by the child (non-transmitted alleles) still predict offspring outcomes, a pattern sometimes labeled genetic nurture. in this review, we describe several alternative mechanisms that may give rise to indirect genetic effects: sibling effects, assortative mating, dynastic processes, and population stratification. we synthesize how extended twin and family models, parent–offspring trio designs, sibling comparisons, and adoption studies can detect indirect genetic effects. we then summarize research on indirect genetic effects across developmental domains, highlighting robust indirect genetic effects for education and limited or context-dependent effects on psychopathology and personality. we outline priorities for future multigenerational designs that clarify the sociocultural transmission of psychosocial development within families. annual review of developmental psychology

three‐year‐old children make explicit metacognitive judgments – if asked appropriately abstract metacognition—the capacity to represent and reflect upon our knowledge and its sources—is fundamental for higher cognition and learning. developmental research suggests that the ability to make explicit metacognitive judgments emerges surprisingly late, not before school age. however, this research has assumed that metacognition is optimized for private reflection and therefore tested children's metacognitive judgments in individual settings. in contrast, recent theoretical approaches propose that explicit metacognition may have a primarily social function and should therefore become most evident in socio‐communicative contexts. we tested this proposal across four pre‐registered studies ( n = 195). first, we conducted two studies in which 3‐ and 5‐year‐old children participated in a social version of a well‐established metacognition task ( partial ignorance task ). children had to communicate their uncertainty towards a cooperative partner who relied on their advice. even 3‐year‐olds provided accurate metacognitive judgments under these conditions: they spontaneously and explicitly reported uncertainty when they were partially ignorant, but not when they were knowledgeable. two control studies yielded mixed evidence regarding the question whether the enhanced metacognitive performance in the first two studies was indeed mainly due to the socio‐communicative context rather than other factors. overall, the current findings suggest that explicit metacognition manifests earlier in development than previously assumed and may be boosted in some—particularly socio‐communicative—contexts. developmental science
beyond asexuality as a single category: sexuality-related profiles and differential perceived stigma-related impairment across the ace spectrum journal of sex research

stability and transitions in positive youth development profiles among adolescents: the role of interpersonal relationships abstract adolescence is a period of significant developmental plasticity, offering opportunities to foster positive strengths. research has suggested that positive youth development (pyd) varies across individuals and cultures; however, there is still limited understanding of how pyd evolves over time, particularly in non‐western cultural contexts. to address this gap, the current study employed latent profile analysis and latent transition analysis to identify distinct pyd profiles, examine transitions between profiles, and investigate the predictive roles of interpersonal relationships. a total of 1680 chinese adolescents (45.9% male, m age = 15.42 years) participated in assessments at three time points with 6‐month intervals. the results identified three profiles: asset‐poor, moderate, and prosperous. the asset‐poor subgroup exhibited the highest probabilities of transition, whereas the prosperous subgroup exhibited the greatest stability. both the asset‐poor and moderate subgroups showed a tendency to transition toward more adaptive profiles. multivariate logistic regression analyses revealed that parent–child relationships and school interpersonal relationships exerted different effects on transitions in pyd profiles. these findings highlight the value of developing tailored interventions that strengthen adolescents' inherent strengths in line with their specific patterns, thereby supporting all adolescents in achieving optimal development. applied psychology-health and well being

a longitudinal network analysis of parental responses to adolescents' negative emotions and adolescent social media doomscrolling abstract parental emotion socialization has been closely linked to various adolescent risk behaviors on social media; however, the interactive mechanisms between parental responses to adolescents' negative emotions (pr) and social media doomscrolling (sd) remain unclear. a network analysis method considering time‐varying effects was used to describe the structural characteristics and dynamic interactions between pr and sd. a total of 2873 adolescents participated at both measurement occasions. cross‐sectional network analysis indicated that emotion‐focused response was the most central node in the pr network, tolerance emerged as the central node in the sd network, and conflict functioned as a key bridge node in the contemporaneous network of pr and sd. cross‐lagged network analysis revealed that earlier punitive responses predicted increases in subsequent parental distress reactions and adolescents' withdrawal symptoms during doomscrolling. furthermore, higher levels of earlier salience were associated with increased tolerance and relapse and reduced parental expressive encouragement at the later time point. these findings enrich the understanding of the topological features and temporal associations between pr and sd, offering implications for family‐based interventions to address doomscrolling in the digital era. applied psychology-health and well being

mindfulness buffers the effect of negative affect on rumination: a daily diary study during a mindfulness‐based intervention abstract negative affect automatically triggering rumination is a core pathological mechanism underlying emotional distress. while mindfulness is hypothesized to buffer this process, few studies have dynamically tracked these effects during systematic interventions. the study employed a single‐arm daily diary design during an 8‐week mindfulness‐based intervention (mbi) to investigate whether daily mindfulness buffers the effect of negative affect on rumination. a sample of 116 participants with emotional distress completed daily assessments of mindfulness, negative affect, and state rumination during the mbi. data were analyzed using linear mixed models (lmms) and dynamic structural equation modeling (dsem). lmm results showed that following the mbi, participants' daily mindfulness significantly increased, while daily negative affect and state rumination significantly decreased. given the single‐arm pre–post design without a control group, these pre–post changes should be interpreted cautiously and cannot be attributed solely to the intervention. dsem results indicated that higher daily mindfulness buffered the effect of daily negative affect on state rumination. additional analyses further suggested that different mindfulness components played distinct roles in the onset and maintenance of rumination. these findings highlight the protective role of mindfulness in weakening maladaptive rumination, thereby promoting overall psychological well‐being. applied psychology-health and well being

mental health symptoms do not increase risk for distressing experiences during intensive mindfulness meditation training: evidence from a prospective matched-control intervention study abstract objective we aimed to test whether mental health problems are associated with distressing experiences during intensive meditation training and with the impact of these experiences following intensive training. method we conducted a preregistered prospective matched-control study comparing 6-day insight mindfulness meditation retreats ( n = 89) to daily living among matched controls ( n = 44). results unexpectedly, lower, and not higher, pre-retreat depression and anxiety symptoms were associated with greater endorsement of distressing experiences during the retreats compared to daily living among matched controls. moreover, at 2-week follow-up, retreat participants with low and those with high pre-retreat anxiety symptoms reported more positive than negative impact of distressing experiences endorsed during the retreat. conclusions the findings challenge claims that depression and anxiety symptoms are a risk factor for heightened distressing experiences during intensive meditation training or the adverse effects of these meditation-related experiences. preregistration the study was preregistered at clinicaltrials.gov (identifier: nct04749264; 20 december 2020). mindfulness

learning how: a “mindless” procedure alone gives rise to contextual cueing—a weakly supervised connectionist model of statistical context learning in visual search abstract because our environment is not random, it is beneficial to assimilate the statistics of sensory impressions and improve performance, such as visual search for a target object in a cluttered array of nontarget objects (contextual cueing [cc] effect). computational models of cc have so far focused on predicting the target location from a particular configuration of nontarget items. this contrasts with recent findings according to which display repetitions train human participants’ general procedures for the search task. here, we test the latter idea by employing a connectionist model of visual search that exclusively learns a search procedure without acquiring any individual display-layout information. we show that an instance of a “learning how” mechanism not only proposes a viable alternative account to existing “learning that” mechanisms, but also generates more plausible key behavioral metrics and exhibits a central bias as an emergent phenomenon of learning-induced plasticity. these findings have implications for models of visual search and artificial intelligence: learning a procedure from leveraging a task’s structure alone can mimic the effects of top-down modulation of attention while also reducing the need for supervision in learning, thereby making computational models that leverage procedural learning behaviorally more plausible and easier to train. psychonomic bulletin & review

when care hurts or disappears: the consistency of emotional abuse and neglect and adolescents' internalizing problems: the mediating role of personal and general beliefs in a just world abstract previous research on childhood maltreatment has predominantly focused on the independent effects of emotional abuse (ea) or emotional neglect (en), providing limited insight into how combinations of these co‐occurring subtypes are associated with adolescent adjustment. based on shattered assumptions theory, this longitudinal study examined how combined patterns of ea and en were associated with adolescents' internalizing problems, as well as the indirect associations involving personal belief in a just world (pbjw) and general belief in a just world (gbjw). a total of 484 chinese adolescents (51.03% girls; m age ± sd = 12.77 ± 0.72, range age = 11–16) were followed over a six‐month interval. polynomial regression and response surface analyses revealed that: (1) when ea and en increased simultaneously, adolescents reported higher levels of internalizing problems; (2) when ea and en were imbalanced, internalizing problems became more severe as the discrepancy between them widened, particularly when ea exceeded en; and (3) pbjw, but not gbjw, accounted for significant indirect associations between joint ea–en patterns and internalizing problems. these findings reveal the complex role of combined emotional maltreatment experiences in relation to psychological distress and highlight the stronger association of active emotional abuse, relative to passive neglect, with internalizing problems. this study extends the understanding of maltreatment patterns and offers insights for interventions that aim to strengthen adolescents' personal just world beliefs. journal of research on adolescence

development beyond information: human becoming in the age of ai discussions of artificial intelligence in education increasingly equate development with the acquisition and deployment of information. this article argues that such accounts rest on false assumptions. development is better understood not as an informational state but as a relational, historical process of becoming through which persons emerge and continue to change. drawing on vygotsky, on ilyenkov's distinction between living and petrified ideality, and on the enactive approach to cognition, we characterise development through four features: its historicity, its dependence on reciprocal sense-making, its mediation by others who orient the learner, and its cultivation within relations of care. large language models operate over the sedimented products of these processes without participating in them. as objectifications of human purposes, such systems may mediate human development or foreclose it. we conclude by considering what this account implies for education. human development

the evolved nest in childhood: relation to adult well-being and social capital across cultures abstract evolved nests are species-specific developmental systems that support biological, psychological, and social needs. the human evolved nest includes practices such as responsive care, self-directed play, and extensive affectionate touch. previous studies have linked childhood experience of these practices to both child and adult well-being. here we assessed whether recall of evolved nest experiences during childhood (age 0–18) was related to three dimensions of adult well-being and social capital (personal well-being, social relationships, and general prosociality) in three countries (usa, uk, japan). recalled evolved nest experience was positively associated with multiple measures under each dimension across cultures after controlling for demographic factors ( n = 1,401). in contrast, it was not found to be associated with incentivised measures of prosociality (elicited via a series of economic games) in any country. exploratory factor analyses revealed that experiences of evolved nest practices clustered together under two common factors in each country: positive and negative experiences. these factors were independently associated with multiple indicators of adult well-being and social capital in each country, and these associations were generally stronger for positive (vs. negative) experiences. our findings are consistent with the hypothesis that childhood experience of the evolved nest has long-term benefits for individual and societal well-being regardless of cultural differences. journal of happiness studies

multiple elevations on symptom validity indicators embedded in psychopathology screening measures improves specificity when classifying invalid symptom overreporting 心理病理筛查工具中症状效度指标的多次升高可提高无效症状过度报告分类的特异性 traditional symptom validity tests (svt) are crucial yet costly components of routine evaluations. embedded overreporting svt cutoffs in commonly used psychopathology screeners exist, but it is unclear how multiple elevations across these measures impact detection accuracy. this study explored if the convergence of elevations across three embedded svts, beck depression inventory-second edition, beck anxiety inventory, and posttraumatic stress disorder checklist for dsm-5, improves invalidity detection accuracy using preselected and sample-derived cutoffs. individual screeners demonstrated high specificity but low sensitivity, and each screener uniquely predicted validity status. using conservative/preselected cutoffs, elevating ≥2 embedded svts significantly improved specificity to >99% with modest sensitivity (32%), while ≥3 elevations using liberal/sample-derived cutoffs resulted in 98% specificity but an improved sensitivity of 41%. multiple elevations across embedded svts can identify noncredible responding/symptom endorsement on psychopathology screeners, thus signaling that more robust validity testing can be discontinued. however, given the lower sensitivity of this approach, these embedded svts may better rule in rather than rule out noncredible responding when elevated. assessment
agency, emotion, and memory in forgiving collective agents review of philosophy and psychology

the dynamics of student engagement in cooperative science learning: a multimodal approach student engagement is critical for effective cooperative learning, but engagement is hard to measure due to its multidimensional and implicit nature. here, we applied video coding, microanalysis, and neural measures to examine how students engage in group work. nine groups of high school students (four students per group) participated in a cooperative learning task, in which they collaboratively created a model of a cell while their electroencephalogram (eeg) brain activity was being recorded. the whole session was also videotaped, transcribed, and coded offline. analysis of video recordings revealed that students alternated between on-task, off-task, and idle states every 10–30 s on average. the duration of time students were on-task significantly predicted test performance. eeg analysis revealed that both theta (4–7 hz) and alpha activity (8–12 hz) during idle states were indistinguishable from off-task states but significantly different from on-task states. our findings point to the complexity of assessing student engagement in group work and to the need for interdisciplinary work that considers both brain and behavior as complementary information sources. npj science of learning
