collaborators and successors; attachment and relation: a discussion of david tuckett’s paper “revolution and its (unwitting) discontents: did kohut’s ideas enhance or undermine american psychoanalysis?” the author overviews david tuckett’s substantial and innovative approach to examining psychoanalysis which sheds new light on the suppositions that underlie and organize analysts’ understanding of analytic process and reviews his application of that methodology to kohut’s work. the author will suggest that while tuckett’s methodology of unearthing the implicit suppositions that analysts bring to their clinical work and data are profoundly illuminating, this work itself is organized by his own supposition that the core of psychoanalysis is the discovery and uncovering of an extant unconscious structure that he terms “x.” leaning on neville symington, the author illustrates how tuckett’s suppositions and consequent conclusions regarding kohut’s innovation of self psychology—and much contemporary psychoanalysis—is based on a conflation of the primary with the secondary and manifests an attachment to classical psychoanalysis rather than being in relation to it. the author illustrates how many contemporary psychoanalysts are concerned with a wider range of phenomena than the revelation of the underlying template or “x” and will conclude that kohut’s contributions have advanced psychoanalysis rather than undermining it. journal of the american psychoanalytic association

a brief measure of life satisfaction: psychometric properties and measurement invariance of the polish three-item satisfaction with life scale (swls-3). background: the satisfaction with life scale-3 (swls-3) is a brief three-item version of the five-item satisfaction with life scale (swls), but it has not been validated in poland. this study examined its psychometric properties, structural validity, measurement invariance across sex and between the polish and original uk samples, and convergent validity with well-being, gratitude, awe, and forgiveness.
participants and procedure: a total of 506 polish-speaking adults (= 27.70,= 7.72; 58.1% women) completed an online survey including the swls, the world health organization five well-being index (who-5), the gratitude/awe questionnaire, and the toussaint forgiveness scale. structural validity was assessed by testing the fit of the hypothesized model. measurement invariance across sex and samples was examined. internal consistency was evaluated using cronbach's alpha (α) and mcdonald's omega (ω). convergent and discriminant validity were assessed through associations with related constructs.
results: the swls-3 demonstrated good model fit. it showed configural, metric, and scalar invariance across sex. across samples, metric invariance was supported, but scalar invariance was not achieved. internal consistency was acceptable (α = .78, ω = .79). scores were positively associated with well-being, gratitude and awe, and forgiveness.
conclusions: the swls-3 is a reliable and valid brief measure of life satisfaction, suitable for large-scale research, including cross-cultural research on associations, although caution is needed when comparing mean scores across countries. current issues in personality psychology

the roles of social support and sense of community in promoting psychological health at work orientation: the garment industry remains labour-intensive and exposes workers to psychological risks that are often overlooked in social compliance systems. research purpose: the study examined how support from colleagues, supervisory support and sense of community shape psychological distress among garment workers in ghana. motivation for the study: prior research has largely focused on wages, physical safety and compliance, while the psychological health of workers in the garment industry has remained underexplored. research approach/design and method: a quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted on 416 garment workers in ghana’s free zone hub. data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. main findings: support from colleagues and supervisors strengthened a sense of community at work. supervisory support and sense of community significantly reduced psychological distress, while the direct effect of colleague support on distress was not significant. sense of community mediated the relationship between social support and psychological distress. practical/managerial implications: factory managers should train supervisors in supportive communication and create workplace systems that promote belonging, peer interaction and community-building. contribution/value-add: grounded in positive psychology, the study extends psychosocial health literature by showing that workplace relational resources, especially supervisory support and sense of community, are critical for reducing distress among garment workers. sa journal of industrial psychology

sustaining women’s executive leadership tenure in south africa’s private sector: a relational sustainability framework orientation: despite improvements in women’s representation in executive leadership, tenure sustainability remains uneven, particularly within transformation-driven contexts such as south africa’s private sector. research purpose: this study explored how structural, cultural and developmental dynamics shape the sustainability of women executives’ leadership tenure following appointment. motivation for the study: industrial and organisational psychology (iop) scholarship has predominantly focused on barriers to leadership access rather than executive tenure durability. in south africa, legislated transformation has improved representation; however, sustained executive presence has not increased proportionately, suggesting a sustainability gap requiring theoretical and practical examination. research approach/design and method: an interpretivist qualitative design using interpretative phenomenological analysis was adopted. in-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight senior women executives who voluntarily exited c-suite or equivalent roles across south african private-sector industries. main findings: executive tenure sustainability emerged as a function of relational alignment across three interdependent domains: structural legitimacy, cultural belonging and developmental continuity. misalignment produced cumulative relational strain, increasing vulnerability to voluntary exit despite demonstrated competence and formal authority. practical/managerial implications: the study introduces the executive sustainability diagnostic model, enabling organisations to assess governance integration, leadership climate architecture and talent mobility systems to proactively manage executive tenure risk. contribution/value-add: the study advances relational sustainability as a mid-range iop framework, shifting leadership scholarship from pipeline-access metaphors to systemic analysis of executive tenure durability. sa journal of industrial psychology
validating a sexual assertiveness questionnaire with college students in the united states sexual and relationship therapy
effects of dual-site transcranial direct current stimulation on cognitive flexibility in children with specific learning disorders applied neuropsychology-child

the primacy of autonomy: grounding counseling ethics in libertarian moral philosophy abstract counselor values impact ethical judgments and clinical practice. contemporary approaches to counseling ethics are informed by dominant liberal/progressive values. this article proposes an alternative ethical framework grounded in libertarian moral philosophy. libertarianism is introduced through the axioms of self‐ownership and moral separateness , from which emerge the principles of autonomy, non‐coercion, and voluntariness. by prioritizing client autonomy above other ethical principles, the libertarian‐oriented counselor seeks to protect the authenticity of the existential–humanistic encounter by holding moral space and guarding against values imposition. implications include greater counselor transparency in informed consent, avoidance of subtle paternalism, and an obligation to scale back professional social advocacy. issues of impaired autonomy, public protection, and suicidality present challenging cases requiring further examination. integrating moral philosophy and psychology in training and supervision may broaden moral diversity in counseling, deepen counselors’ moral self‐awareness and skill in navigating value conflicts, and inform consideration of optionality within ethics codes. journal of humanistic counseling

influencers and fatphobic aesthetic moralism: the digital pedagogy of adolescent body ideals this study examines how adolescents internalize fatphobic body norms through sustained exposure to influencer-driven aesthetic narratives of health. the term “fatphobic aesthetic moralism” is used as an interpretive framework to describe how influencer-driven content may transform aesthetic and health-related body norms into moral evaluations, whereby thinness, muscularity, and visible self-discipline become associated with responsibility, self-control, and personal worth. drawing on survey data from 1,032 spanish adolescents aged 12-17 years and semi-structured interviews with educators, health professionals, and social workers, the results show that adolescents who identify influencers as role models for health and beauty show a higher prevalence of elevated fatphobic attitudes. quantitative results distinguish the greater overall frequency of peer referents from the higher prevalence of elevated fatphobic attitudes among adolescents selecting influencers, while qualitative results reveal how influencers function as informal pedagogues whose authority derives from algorithmic visibility and affective proximity. professionals emphasized that these narratives naturalize fatphobia by framing bodily conformity as evidence of effort and virtue, while deviation signals irresponsibility or failure. within this framework, influencer culture can be understood as a digital pedagogy through which body norms may become moralized via aesthetic codes, producing enduring hierarchies of worth that extend beyond beauty ideals into the evaluation of the self and others. psychology society & education

rendimiento matemático de estudiantes con discapacidad intelectual en educación primaria: una revisión sistemática los estudiantes con discapacidad intelectual enfrentan importantes desafíos para participar y aprender matemáticas, muchos de los cuales derivan de visiones segregadoras sobre sus posibilidades de logro en esta disciplina escolar. esta revisión sistemática examinó la investigación disponible acerca del rendimiento matemático de este alumnado en educación primaria. el estudio siguió las orientaciones prisma 2020 para la recopilación y síntesis de evidencias empíricas. la búsqueda electrónica se realizó en mayo de 2025 en las bases de datos web of science, scopus y scielo. tras los procesos de identificación, selección y cribado, se analizaron 71 artículos publicados entre 1999 y 2025. los resultados indican un predominio de estudios centrados en estudiantes con discapacidad intelectual leve y una prioridad por el análisis de factores pedagógicos mediante intervenciones con enfoques cuantitativos. se observan avances en el ámbito de los números y las operaciones básicas, de carácter mayoritariamente procedimental. además, se identifica un creciente interés por examinar variables individuales, con especial énfasis en las habilidades cognitivas de dominio general y específico, que no se traducen de forma sistemática en intervenciones orientadas a su desarrollo. desde una perspectiva práctica, los hallazgos sugieren la necesidad de orientar la investigación hacia el fomento del conocimiento conceptual y la resolución de problemas, integrando la evidencia disponible para favorecer oportunidades equitativas y de calidad en las matemáticas. psychology society & education

risk factors for romantic breakup in emerging adulthood: a systematic review couple relationships and breakups are frequent during emerging adulthood, a stage characterized by social exploration and instability in various developmental areas. however, there is no frame of reference from which to approach the main risk factors for these breakups during this period, despite the significant impact that such experiences can have on the mental health of those involved. therefore, the aim of this systematic review is to examine the variables that recent studies have identified as key risk factors associated with breakup in emerging adulthood. following prisma guidelines, a structured search was performed in the web of science and scopus databases. a total of 1,779 articles published between 2007 and 2024 were reviewed, with 23 meeting the inclusion criteria. the results show that breakups are influenced by individual factors (e.g., age or substance use), relational factors (e.g., low commitment and satisfaction), and contextual factors (e.g., work and income). these findings offer a foundation for designing psychoeducational interventions aimed at fostering healthier romantic relationships. psychology society & education

not all psychological capital is equal: a scoping review of psychological capital profiles psychological capital (composed of self-efficacy, hope, optimism, and resilience) is a malleable, state-like psychological resource, positively linked to well-being, health, and performance across applied domains. moving beyond traditional variable-centered research, this scoping review maps person-centered empirical studies to identify psychological capital profiles and examine the variables that differentiate them. following prisma-scr guidelines, 20 studies (21 empirical studies) published between 2019-2026 were reviewed. the results revealed that the number of profiles identified ranges from 2 to 7. some studies reported profiles that differ only in terms of psychological capital intensity (level-based), while others identified more complex combinations across dimensions (shape-based). also, profiles were distinguished by significant differences in several variables (e.g., well-being, outcomes, socio-demographic characteristics). these findings support the relevance of a person-centered approach to better understand the multidimensional nature of psychological capital and provide a solid basis for developing tailored interventions to enhance individual well-being and performance. psychology society & education

autolesión y su relación con factores asociados al uso de redes sociales: revisión sistemática la autolesión no suicida constituye una problemática relevante de salud mental que, en el contexto digital actual, ha adquirido nuevas formas de expresión, exposición e interacción a través de las redes sociales. el objetivo fue analizar la evidencia reciente sobre la relación entre autolesión no suicida y el uso de redes sociales. se aplicó el preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses para búsqueda y selección de artículos en las bases scopus, ebscohost y proquest, utilizando criterios de inclusión de estudios en inglés y español. finalmente, se analizaron 13 artículos con diseños principalmente mixtos y transversales, centrados en plataformas como x, instagram, tiktok, youtube y whatsapp. los resultados mostraron que las redes sociales pueden funcionar como factores de riesgo, al favorecer la exposición y normalización de la autolesión, pero también como espacios de apoyo y contención emocional. se concluye que la interacción digital constituye un entorno ambivalente, que requiere políticas de moderación más eficaces y estrategias preventivas con enfoque en salud mental y alfabetización digital, así como estudios que prueben modelos para esclarecer el espacio digital. psychology society & education

association between emotional intelligence and prosocial tendencies in young adults: the mediating role of empathy emotional intelligence and empathy have been consistently associated with prosocial behaviors in children and adolescents; however, empirical evidence in young adults remains limited, particularly on how these variables relate differently to types of prosocial motivation. likewise, little is known about empathy’s mediating role in the relationship between emotional intelligence and prosociality. this study examined the direct and indirect pathways linking emotional intelligence to prosocial tendencies, with empathy as a mediator, in a sample of young adults. the study used a cross-sectional observational-analytical design and included 514 young people aged 18 to 35 (m = 21.13, sd = 3.71). the trait meta-mood scale, the interpersonal reactivity index, and the prosocial tendencies measure-revised were used. data were analyzed using path models. emotional intelligence and empathy together explained 14% of the variance in prosocial tendencies (r² = .14). emotional repair, empathic concern, and personal distress showed different associations across prosociality dimensions. mediation analyses indicated that empathy, particularly empathic concern and perspective taking, statistically mediated the association between emotional intelligence and prosocial tendencies. the findings expand the empirical evidence on prosociality in young adulthood and highlight empathy as a socioemotional correlate within the association between emotional self-awareness and prosocial helping. psychology society & education

un modelo explicativo de la soledad y la ideación suicida en adolescentes peruanos: el rol mediador de la autolesión no suicida el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo examinar el rol mediador de la autolesión no suicida en la relación entre la soledad (social y emocional) y la ideación suicida en adolescentes peruanos. se desarrolló un estudio explicativo de corte transversal con una muestra de 434 adolescentes, con edades entre 14 y 17 años, provenientes de tres instituciones educativas públicas. se emplearon instrumentos validados para evaluar la soledad, la ideación suicida y la autolesión no suicida, y se analizó el modelo propuesto mediante ecuaciones estructurales con el estimador de máxima verosimilitud robusta (mlr). los resultados evidenciaron que la soledad social y emocional se asociaron positiva y significativamente con la ideación suicida; asimismo, la autolesión no suicida desempeñó un rol mediador en ambas relaciones. en cuanto a las diferencias según género, las mujeres presentaron puntuaciones más elevadas en soledad emocional, autolesiones e ideación suicida. se concluye que los adolescentes que experimentan soledad pueden recurrir a la autolesión no suicida como mecanismo de afrontamiento desadaptativo, lo que se asocia con una mayor ideación suicida. psychology society & education

preventing work-related loneliness: a cross-cultural qualitative study of 30–60-year-old people living alone the aim of this study was to identify strategies to prevent and mitigate loneliness associated with work, and based on this, develop recommendations for workplaces. the participants were 30–60-year-olds living in one-person households across finland, new zealand, and the united kingdom. the data were collected through an international online survey (n = 396) and interviews with 19 participants residing in finland. in previous research, work loneliness refers to a perceived lack of meaningful relationships at work. work-related loneliness denotes feelings of loneliness that emerge from work circumstances and may extend beyond the immediate workplace. the previous research suggests that work-related loneliness can be reduced by supporting core psychological needs of belonginess, autonomy, and competence, and by fostering social connection through adaptive practices, supportive cultures, and personal resource development. the main research findings were formulated as participant-identified challenges and their solutions for work-related loneliness. key challenges were: 1) hyper-efficiency and individualism, 2) work-induced disruption of social life and well-being, and 3) inequality and limited awareness of loneliness. the corresponding solutions were: 1) promoting belonging and teamwork, 2) promoting work–life balance and well-being, and 3) promoting inclusion and intervening in loneliness. the research findings can be connected to the needs of relatedness, autonomy and competence at work. the solutions offer a comprehensive approach to mitigating work-related loneliness and can contribute to a more inclusive workplace culture while potentially reducing costs associated with loneliness. nordic psychology

social-cognitive frameworks for understanding the connection between social isolation and psychosis risk. increasing evidence demonstrates an association between social isolation and psychosis risk. in this perspective, we attempt to account for why that is. drawing from work in social psychology, social neuroscience, and clinical psychological science, we present two frameworks for understanding the association between social isolation and psychosis risk: the "social-needs" framework and the "social-processing" framework. social needs states that because of people's inherent social needs, isolation produces increased social attention, perception, and thought to fill the social void, resulting in the perception of anomalous social information and social meaning. social processing states that the lack of exposure to social stimuli during isolation diminishes social processing (i.e., social thought, social perceptions) and may lead isolated individuals to turn their attention inward, blurring internal and external worlds and intensifying self-focus in a way that creates reality-monitoring disturbances and anomalous self-experiences. conveniently, these frameworks can be empirically arbitrated. we review the literature connecting social isolation to psychosis, describe the frameworks, their empirical support, and the predictions they make, and discuss clinical implications. ultimately, a better accounting of isolation's pro-psychotic effects might lead to better efforts at psychosis prevention. perspectives on psychological science

la aparente apatía de las juventudes ante la crisis climática: conductas proambientales en un grupo de jóvenes el artículo aborda parte de los resultados obtenidos en la tesis titulada “percepciones acerca del cambio climático y acciones proambientales en personas jóvenes costarricenses de la gran área metropolitana. un estudio cualitativo” (fernández, 2023). este trabajo de corte cualitativo y alcance exploratorio-descriptivo indagó dichas conductas y los factores que inciden en ellas. para ello, se realizaron 21 entrevistas semiestructuradas a personas universitarias entre los 18 y los 30 años habitantes de la gran área metropolitana, procesadas posteriormente mediante análisis temático reflexivo. los principales hallazgos señalan que las acciones más reportadas fueron aquellas que requerían la menor cantidad de esfuerzo o intención; rutinas ya integradas que no causaban una disrupción importante. esto es coherente con la visión de los informantes, quienes atribuyen la crisis climática a las grandes compañías y a los sectores de mayor poder adquisitivo. dicha perspectiva los llevaba a considerar que el impacto individual es mínimo y que, por lo tanto, no vale la pena actuar. finalmente, se observó que el contexto juega un rol importante al ejecutar acciones proambientales. las personas participantes señalaron barreras estructurales que les desincentivaban a optar por conductas más sostenibles. revista costarricense de psicologia

artificial intelligence interventions for resilience and mental health in older adults: a systematic review background: as global population ages, the supply-demand imbalance in geriatric mental health services has become increasingly pronounced. in this emerging field, artificial intelligence (ai)-driven interventions for geriatric mental health remain fragmented. this systematic review synthesizes the application process of ai interventions and dissects the disciplinary knowledge structure of existing studies to unlock ai potential and facilitate evidence-based interventions. methods: guided by the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (prisma) framework, a systematic search of seven databases was performed from january 1, 2005 to november 5, 2025. this review includes a total of 95 studies in english and chinese on ai-based interventions for geriatric mental health. these studies were categorized by basic characteristics, intervention processes, and thematic clustering. results: the field has evolved from an initial exploratory phase to a period of rapid growth. these ai interventions encompass four core dimensions, involving seven ai technology types, nine intervention pathways, and seven key acceptance-influencing factors. research topics focused on clinical efficacy and risk management of ai interventions, as well as psychological assessment and human-computer interaction. this study summarized interdisciplinary, comprehensive research on ai-based geriatric mental health interventions. furthermore, it establishes an explanatory model emphasizing multidisciplinary synergy, which provides a framework for future theoretical and practical development. conclusions: there remains a notable gap between technology design and the psychological characteristics of older adults in ai mental health interventions, and interdisciplinary research is still insufficient. future efforts should strengthen collaboration across clinical medicine, psychology, sociology, and computer science, embed elderly psychological traits into closed-loop technology design, increase policy support, enhance ai accessibility in community and family settings, and improve caregivers’ technical literacy. only through these steps can human-centered ai technology sustainably and equitably address the unmet mental health needs of older adults in the context of global aging. registration: the study has been registered on https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ (registration number: crd420261287044; registration link: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/view/crd420261287044). behavioral psychology-psicologia conductual

personality traits and affective argumentation style as factors in perceived argument strength in natural conditions of competitive debating. the role of psychological matching of speaker and listener. a pilot study in this pilot study, we investigate whether there exists a relationship between affective argumentation style and big five personality traits in the context of perceived persuasive strength, and whether the psychological matching of speaker and listener affects the evaluation of argument strength. the study took the form of a structured natural experiment, conducted during a summer school for students of the faculty of psychology and cognitive science at adam mickiewicz university. the aim of the summer school was to provide an opportunity to practice persuasive skills through competitive debates, based on the british parliamentary format. the neo-ffi personality test was used to diagnose costa and mccrae's big five traits, and zhao et al.'s perceived argument strength scale was used for evaluation of the strength of arguments. transcripts of the debates were subjected to sentiment analysis, in which the speaker's specific argumentation style was identified. the results suggest that the key insight does not lie simply in the absence of statistically significant linear matching effects, but in the substantial heterogeneity observed in persuasive behaviour and evaluation. this heterogeneity highlights the limitations of simplified matching models and points towards a more contextual, dynamic, and person-sensitive understanding of persuasion. acta psychologica

associations between music teachers' big five personality traits and their stereotypical beliefs about students gifted for music teachers' beliefs about gifted students may influence instructional practices and students' educational development. while previous research has focused primarily on beliefs about intellectually gifted students, little is known about beliefs regarding students gifted for music and their relation to teacher characteristics. the present experimental vignette-based online study investigated whether music teachers' big five personality traits are associated with their beliefs about students gifted for music. a sample of 392 (prospective) music teachers evaluated a fictitious student presented in a case scenario on achievement-related, socio-emotional, and behavioral characteristics to assess their beliefs. to this end, the student's musical success in a well-established music competition was manipulated to elicit teachers' assumptions about whether the student was musically gifted or of average musical ability (post-hoc classification). multivariate regression analyses with teachers' personality traits as predictors, students' ascribed musical ability level as a moderator, and teachers' beliefs about students' characteristics as outcomes showed that teachers' beliefs were primarily associated with students' ascribed musical ability level. compared to average-ability students, students gifted for music received higher ratings of intellectual abilities, musical abilities, and performance and motivation. in addition, subsequent univariate analyses showed that higher teacher agreeableness was associated with higher social skills ratings for average-ability students, whereas higher teacher conscientiousness was associated with higher intellectual ability ratings for students gifted for music. no significant interaction effects emerged for teachers' openness, extraversion, or neuroticism. these findings suggest that teachers' beliefs about students gifted for music are primarily associated with students' perceived ability level, while teacher personality traits show small additional associations. acta psychologica

[endometrial cancer: current clinical issues, unmet needs, and future research directions]. the annual meeting of the society of gynecologic oncology (sgo) is one of the most influential academic conferences in the international field of gynecologic oncology, playing a pivotal role in driving clinical research progress and standardizing clinical practice. this article systematically reviews the endometrial cancer-related research presented at the 2026 sgo annual meeting. integrating current clinical practice, it provides a comprehensive analysis of research hotspots, unmet clinical needs, and future trends in this field, aiming to outline a clear academic framework for clinical and pharmaceutical professionals, facilitating their understanding of the frontiers of research. overall, molecular classification has become an essential foundation for risk stratification, yet it still faces significant challenges in quality control, result interpretation, and clinical integration. adjuvant therapy for early-stage patients is shifting toward biomarker-driven individualized strategies, while her2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (adc) are gradually moving into earlier lines of treatment, and intensified adjuvant therapies for high-risk populations continue to be explored. advanced and recurrent diseases have entered an era of concurrent treatment options, highlighted by immunotherapy and adc. however, patient selection, sequential therapy, and toxicity management remain to be optimized. surgical treatment exhibits a trend toward minimally invasive approaches and precise staging centered on sentinel lymph node (sln) mapping, with its rational integration with neoadjuvant and systemic therapies, emerging as a new research focus. future efforts should rely on high-quality prospective studies and real-world evidence to further advance the application of molecular classification in treatment decision-making and to refine multidisciplinary collaborative management systems. zhonghua yi xue za zhi

segmental sternal resection for metastatic ovarian cancer: surgical technique and clinical outcome. isolated sternal recurrence from ovarian cancer is exceptionally rare, and its optimal surgical management remains poorly defined. in selected patients with a prolonged disease-free interval and a solitary metastatic lesion, radical resection may provide durable local control while preserving chest stability and respiratory function. this video tutorial describes the surgical technique and clinical outcome of segmental sternectomy performed for a single-site sternal recurrence of ovarian cancer occurring after a disease-free interval of 12 years. following comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation and staging confirming isolated disease, an en-bloc segmental resection of the involved sternum was performed. chest wall reconstruction was achieved using a rigid methyl methacrylate prosthesis, restoring anterior thoracic stability while protecting the mediastinal structures without compromising respiratory mechanics. the postoperative course was uneventful, with satisfactory functional recovery and stable chest wall integrity. at 1-year follow-up, contrast-enhanced computed tomography positron emission tomography demonstrated no evidence of local or distant recurrence. this video tutorial highlights the feasibility and safety of segmental sternectomy with prosthetic reconstruction for highly selected patients with isolated sternal metastasis from ovarian cancer, and emphasizes the importance of individualized multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of uncommon late recurrences. multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : mmcts

validation of a dual 2-back task as an effective method for inducing acute mental fatigue. this study proposes a novel dual 2-back task involving updating of visuospatial working memory, which was designed to induce acute mental fatigue. the dual 2-back task was itself embedded in a protocol designed to overcome common limitations of time on task studies, such as learning effects, confounding effect of boredom, and an absence of psychophysiological index of mental effort. seventy-three healthy young adults were required to continuously update visual information for 30 min without any rest intervals, ensuring sustained high cognitive demand. during the dual 2-back task, multiple measures were collected, including self-reported fatigue and sleepiness, signal detection performance (d'), eeg markers (p300 amplitude, frontal theta and posterior alpha power density) and cardiac pre-ejection period (pep) reactivity. participants reported a significant increase in fatigue and sleepiness, and exhibited reduced ability to detect a match, indicating a decline in performance. concurrently, eeg indices reflected fatigue-related changes, with a decrease in p300 amplitude and an increase in alpha power. in contrast, frontal theta and pep reactivity, two markers of mental effort, did not vary significantly over time. interestingly, participants did not report increased boredom, and the changes in performance and eeg markers persisted even when controlling for boredom. overall, these results confirm that the dual 2-back task is an effective method to induce mental fatigue. however, given the considerable interindividual variability observed, future studies should adopt analytical approaches that consider the strategies participants use to cope with mental fatigue (e.g., effort disengagement versus compensatory effort). acta psychologica

effects of abortion bans on the physician workforce. objective: to examine physicians' experiences providing early pregnancy care under abortion bans and perspectives on how these bans affect the reproductive health workforce.
methods: from may 2024 to may 2026, we conducted semistructured interviews with obstetrician-gynecologists, family medicine physicians, and emergency medicine physicians practicing in states with total or near-total abortion bans. participants were recruited with purposive and snowball sampling. interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed with an inductive thematic approach.
results: fifty-five physicians from 14 states participated, including 25 obstetrician-gynecologists, 21 emergency medicine physicians, and 9 family medicine physicians. abortion bans introduced uncertainty that reshaped the boundaries of clinical decision making and narrowed the services physicians felt able to provide, leading to increased referral to specialists for care previously managed by nonspecialists. participants described tensions between professional obligations and personal well-being, as well as disruptions to core professional values, including commitments to patient autonomy, beneficence, and nonmaleficence. perceived effects on the training pipeline included loss of expertise, barriers to physician and trainee recruitment, and diminished preparedness for independent practice among trainees in abortion-ban states. professional burnout emerged as both a consequence of these changes and a factor shaping professional decision making.
conclusion: physicians across multiple specialties involved in early pregnancy care reported that abortion bans affected scope of practice, physician training, recruitment and retention, and workforce participation. these findings suggest that abortion bans may affect not only abortion provision but also the broader reproductive health care workforce and access to early pregnancy care. o&g open

from early adversity to lifespan mental health: the interplay of metabolism, genetics, and brain plasticity. early life adverse experience, whether prenatal or postnatal, is a prevalent risk factor for altered trajectories of biological development, often culminating in comorbid metabolic and psychiatric disorders in adulthood, which represent a substantial public health burden. in this article, we review evidence that adversity-induced metabolic reconfiguration, specifically involving insulin sensitivity and glucose homeostasis, disrupts developmental processes in neural circuits governing stress regulation, reward learning, and executive control. we discuss how this "metabolic embedding" contributes to specific psychiatric phenotypes, with an emphasis on immuno-metabolic depression. furthermore, we examine how genomic information can be leveraged to enhance individual-level prediction of at-risk subjects, moving beyond static polygenic risk scores toward biologically informed metrics such as expression-based polygenic scores. we propose a lifespan framework that integrates metabolic, neurobiological, and genomics to advance precision prevention. annual review of psychology
mindfulness and cognitive-based interventions show promise for university students, but evidence certainty remains limited. evidence-based nursing

u.s. veterans and psychedelics: prevalence of use and policy preferences. veteran issues in the united states often figure prominently in policy debates and media coverage surrounding psychedelic substances, such as psilocybin mushrooms and ibogaine. this is partially driven by the need to improve access and efficacy of treatments for mental health conditions, especially conditions (such as posttraumatic stress disorder) that are more common among veterans than nonveterans. in this study, the authors present new data from the 2025 rand psychedelics survey. the study focuses on the use of specific psychedelic substances and policy preferences among u.s. veterans and compares them with nonveterans. the study also includes data on veterans' willingness to try these substances and their attitudes about u.s. department of veterans affairs (va) policies on certain psychedelics. rand health quarterly

the kush drug epidemic in sierra leone: public health implications, socioeconomic drivers and health system responses. background: kush, a synthetic drug combining cannabinoids and nitazene opioids, has emerged as a major public health concern in sierra leone, with reported prevalence and clinical severity increasing markedly as it was first identified. this review examines the health consequences of kush use, the socioeconomic and structural drivers underpinning its spread, and the adequacy of health system and policy responses across the mano river basin.
methods: a narrative review was conducted using structured searches of pubmed/medline, scopus, web of science and google scholar (2016-2025). grey literature, including government policy documents, reports from international organisations, civil society publications and credible media sources, was systematically reviewed. eligible sources addressed kush or related synthetic drug use in sierra leone and the wider west african subregion, with emphasis on health outcomes, socioeconomic determinants, health system capacity and policy responses.
results: kush exhibits unpredictable toxicity and high dependence potential, with documented associations including acute psychosis, cognitive impairment, severe morbidity and rising mortality. weak surveillance systems likely underestimate its burden. structural drivers include entrenched youth unemployment, poverty, rapid urbanisation, post-conflict trauma and limited access to education and mental health services. regional dynamics across sierra leone, liberia, guinea and the gambia reinforce its transnational spread. responses since 2024 have intensified but remain disproportionately focused on law enforcement, whereas prevention, treatment and workforce development remain critically under-resourced.
conclusion: the kush crisis exemplifies a complex, cross-border public health emergency. addressing it requires integrated, evidence-informed strategies that strengthen health systems, expand community-based interventions, improve toxicological surveillance and enhance regional coordination under ecowas frameworks. public health challenges

the association between coach-athlete relationship and self-reported task, contextual, and overall athletic performance among university student-athletes introduction the coach-athlete relationship is a fundamental psychosocial factor associated with athlete performance. however, its associations with self-reported task performance, contextual performance, and overall athletic performance have not been sufficiently examined within a single model. drawing on theoretical frameworks such as the 3c model and self-determination theory, this study aimed to investigate the associations between the coach-athlete relationship and two performance sub-dimensions (task performance and contextual performance) and their composite overall score (athletic performance), with overall athletic performance operationalized as a composite score reflecting athletes' global self-perceived performance. method this quantitative study employed a correlational survey design with 276 university student-athletes (154 male and 122 female) competing in individual and team sports. the coach-athlete relationship scale and the athletic performance scale (comprising task performance and contextual performance sub-dimensions and an overall composite score) were used. hierarchical regression analysis was conducted to examine the statistical association of the coach-athlete relationship with self-reported performance dimensions after controlling for demographic variables. results the coach-athlete relationship was positively and significantly correlated with task performance (r = 0.412, p < 0.001) , contextual performance (r = 0.465, p < 0.001) , and overall athletic performance (r = 0.461, p < 0.001) . hierarchical regression analysis showed that the coach-athlete relationship demonstrated a significant statistical association with task performance ( β = 0.514, p < 0.001) , contextual performance ( β = 0.563, p < 0.001) , and overall athletic performance (β = 0.560, p < 0.001) , after controlling for demographic variables. conclusion a high-quality coach-athlete relationship is positively associated with athletes' self-reported task performance, contextual performance, and overall athletic performance. these findings suggest that the coach-athlete relationship may be important in relation to athletes' social, cooperative, and team-oriented behaviors. however, as all measures were self-reported, the results reflect perceived rather than objective performance. frontiers in psychology

beyond physical isolation: behavioral correlates and potential neurobiological mechanisms of functional social isolation functional social isolation (fsi) describes a proposed form of social disconnection in the digital era, wherein individuals are physically co-present yet psychologically detached during pervasive digital immersion. this review examines how everyday digital immersion may contribute to persistent social disengagement, outlines its behavioral correlates and potential neurobiological pathways, and discusses its implications for public health and behavioral psychology. by synthesizing emerging literature on co-present digital immersion, social buffering, and neuroendocrine regulation, we identify five behavioral correlates relevant to fsi: attentional fragmentation, habitual or problematic online engagement, emotional volatility, avoidance of offline social interaction, and reduced practice of offline social skills. we also consider evidence concerning oxytocin, dopamine, norepinephrine, endocannabinoids, serotonin, and cortisol, alongside models of internet-related behaviors. these systems may represent candidate pathways linking digital immersion, attentional capture, affective regulation, and reduced engagement with available social partners. however, current neurobiological evidence is largely indirect and is not specific to fsi; similar patterns may arise from traditional social isolation, chronic stress, sleep disturbance, anxiety, or depression. we therefore present a hypothetical multi-system framework intended to generate testable predictions rather than establish an fsi-specific neurochemical state. fsi may be modifiable through interventions that reduce digital interruptions during face-to-face interaction and support meaningful synchronous engagement. future research should validate its measurement, test causal pathways, and evaluate interventions across populations and social contexts. frontiers in psychology

sculpting the developing brain: a review of neural mechanisms linking physical activity to executive function and emotion regulation in youth childhood and adolescence are a critical period for brain development, yet global physical inactivity threatens this neurodevelopmental trajectory. this review synthesizes the past decade of evidence on how physical exercise modulates executive function and emotional brain circuitry in youth. behaviorally, moderate-intensity aerobic exercise may enhance inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility. however, effect sizes are consistently small-to-moderate, and not all cognitive domains show uniform benefits, with working memory effects being smaller and more variable, and high-intensity exercise sometimes impairing performance. neuroimaging findings reveal enhanced prefrontal-amygdala functional connectivity, strengthening top-down emotion regulation. mechanistically, acute exercise appears to enhance cognition via transient neurochemical and hemodynamic changes, while chronic exercise may induce longer-lasting neuroplasticity through bdnf-related pathways, although these mechanisms remain largely inferred and peripheral bdnf is an imperfect surrogate for central activity. cognitively engaging activities yield superior benefits, with the most consistently supported protocols involving approximately 45-min sessions, three times weekly, sustained for 12 weeks or longer. these parameters represent modal characteristics of successful interventions rather than precisely established optimal prescriptions, and substantial heterogeneity across studies precludes highly specific, universally applicable recommendations. notably, neurodevelopmental populations like adhd exhibit distinct or amplified responsiveness. key limitations include methodological heterogeneity, fragmented causal inference, small sample sizes in neuroimaging studies, and limited evidence for clinical populations. future work must advance precision exercise prescriptions based on individual neural profiles and translational research bridging laboratory findings with real-world educational contexts. frontiers in psychology

ai-assisted multimodal analysis of digital media-enabled intergenerational transmission of regional musical intangible cultural heritage: evidence from blind ballad artists' narrative singing in jindongnan and the taihang mountains digital media has expanded the dissemination of regional musical intangible cultural heritage (ich), but online visibility does not necessarily lead to intergenerational transmission. this study proposes an ai-assisted multimodal framework to examine the digital dissemination and transmission pathways of blind ballad artists' narrative singing traditions in jindongnan and the taihang mountains. the dataset comprises 2,136 online videos, 184,572 interaction records, 412 youth questionnaires, and 36 field interviews. to avoid target leakage, normalized 30-day dissemination effectiveness was predicted using only content-intrinsic features, creator metadata, and 24-h early engagement indicators. the heritage-aware explainable dissemination framework integrates textual, visual, audio, platform, and field-informed cultural features. across five creator-level splits, it achieved an mae of 0.412 ± 0.014, an rmse of 0.552 ± 0.018, and an r 2 of 0.706 ± 0.020. shap analysis identified early engagement, cultural embeddedness, youth-oriented interpretation, inheritor visibility, subtitles, and village scenes as key predictors. pls-sem further identified a significant statistical indirect pathway linking digital exposure with transmission intention via emotional resonance, cultural identity, and learning participation. given the cross-sectional questionnaire design, these relationships are interpreted as associations rather than temporal or causal effects. the findings indicate that stronger transmission-oriented digital engagement is associated with culturally embedded representation, interpretive accessibility, and participatory learning. frontiers in psychology

extracurricular activities and refugee students in turkish educational settings: a systematic review turkey hosts the world’s largest refugee population, and extracurricular activities have increasingly been positioned as potential supports for refugee students’ psycho-social adjustment, school belonging, and peer integration. however, a comprehensive synthesis of eca-related outcomes for refugee students in turkish educational settings remains absent from the literature. this systematic review examined the associations between extracurricular activity participation and refugee student outcomes across psychological, social, and educational settings-related domains. following prisma guidelines, studies were evaluated using the mixed methods appraisal tool (mmat), and findings were integrated through the systematic what is known (swim) framework. findings suggest that ecas are associated with potential improvements in school attachment, perceived social wellbeing, and aspects of psychological adjustment; however, outcomes varied substantially across studies and participant groups, and the overall certainty of evidence remained low to very low. the findings further suggest that many extracurricular activities operate primarily within an integration-oriented framework, producing individual-level benefits without consistently addressing relational and structural barriers to equitable participation. the review highlights the importance of culturally responsive facilitation, inclusion-oriented programme design, and greater attention to refugee students’ own perspectives in future research and practice. overall, extracurricular activities appear promising but insufficiently understood mechanisms for supporting refugee students’ inclusion and psycho-social adjustment within educational settings. systematic review registration open science framework (osf), https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/eg4x8 . frontiers in psychology

bamboo anthropomorphism and sustainable behavioral intention: evidence from bamboo as a substitute for plastic in china background bamboo, as a sustainable alternative to plastic, offers nature-based solutions to global plastic pollution and public health crises, advancing the united nations sustainable development goals (sdgs). however, the cognitive mechanisms of the public's sustainable behavioral intention toward bamboo as a substitute for plastic are still not well known. methods drawing on the hierarchy of effects (hoe) model, this study proposes an integrative cognition–affect–intention framework in which bamboo anthropomorphism is associated with sustainable behavioral intention through place attachment and environmental guilt. structural equation modeling (sem) and multi-group analysis (mga) were conducted using 926 valid responses collected from 31 provincial-level administrative regions in china. regional differences and social norms are added as grouping variables to assess cross-group stability and heterogeneity of the structural relationships. results bamboo anthropomorphism was not significantly directly associated with sustainable behavioral intention. significant indirect associations were observed through place attachment, environmental guilt, and their sequential mediation, with the indirect effect through environmental guilt being the largest. multi-group analyses indicated overall structural stability, with exploratory path-specific differences across regional and social-norm groups. conclusion this study refines the application of the hoe model by distinguishing place-based relational affect from self-conscious moral emotion within the cognition–affect–intention process. the findings suggest that bamboo anthropomorphism is associated with sustainable behavioral intention primarily through indirect affective and moral pathways. exploratory group comparisons further suggest pathway-specific contextual heterogeneity, providing preliminary implications for differentiated environmental communication promoting bamboo-based plastic substitution and supporting the sdgs. frontiers in psychology

psychometric validation of the chinese generative artificial intelligence acceptance scale among university students introduction generative ai use has become widespread among chinese university students, but use does not necessarily indicate acceptance. this cross-sectional psychometric validation study adapted and evaluated the 20-item generative artificial intelligence acceptance scale for use in china. methods following translation, back-translation, expert review, and pilot testing, data were collected from a convenience sample of 604 university students at six institutions in yunnan, anhui, and zhejiang provinces. participants were randomly divided into exploratory and confirmatory subsamples of 302 each. results corrected item–subscale correlations ranged from 0.555 to 0.774. exploratory factor analysis and parallel analysis supported four dimensions—performance expectancy, effort expectancy, facilitating conditions, and social influence—and the unrotated four-factor solution explained 52.22% of the total variance. the correlated four-factor cfa model fitted the second subsample well, scaled χ 2 (164) = 180.41, p = 0.180, robust cfi = 0.993, robust tli = 0.992, robust rmsea = 0.020, and srmr = 0.035, and fitted significantly better than the three-factor alternative, δχ 2 (3) = 102.11, p < 0.001. a second-order model showed comparable fit. cronbach’s alpha ranged from 0.757 to 0.873, mcdonald’s omega from 0.810 to 0.905, and composite reliability from 0.773 to 0.888. ave ranged from 0.494 to 0.615, with performance expectancy marginally below 0.50. htmt estimates ranged from 0.542 to 0.775, and none of their bootstrap confidence intervals included 1.00; however, the fornell–larcker criterion was not fully satisfied, and the upper confidence limit for pe–fc was 0.868. measurement invariance across gender was supported. conclusion the findings provide preliminary support for primarily using the four subscales in similar chinese university samples; a total score should be limited to broad descriptive use. frontiers in psychology

the relationship between university students’ future work self and career decision-making difficulties: the mediating role of learned helplessness and the moderating role of social loafing background university students often report notable career decision-making difficulties in competitive employment environments. research has established a positive link between an individual’s future work self and their career development, while learned helplessness and social loafing relate to greater career decision-making difficulties. this study examines the associations among future work self, learned helplessness, social loafing, and career decision-making difficulties, focusing on the mediating role of learned helplessness and the moderating role of social loafing. methods 611 university students responded to the future work self scale, learned helplessness scale, social loafing tendency questionnaire, and career decision-making difficulties scale. the analysis used smartpls 4.0 with partial least squares structural equation modeling (pls-sem). results future work self was negatively associated with career decision-making difficulties ( β = −0.571). learned helplessness partially mediated this relationship ( β = −0.055), and social loafing significantly moderated the association between future work self and learned helplessness ( β = 0.290). the model explained 45.3% of the variance in career decision-making difficulties and 48.7% of the variance in learned helplessness. conclusion the findings indicate that future work self relates to lower levels of learned helplessness and career decision-making difficulties, while higher social loafing corresponds to a weaker association between them. frontiers in psychology

is empathy-driven teaching effective in cultural product design? an empirical study on students’ empathy and design creativity introduction cultural product design (cpd) education concerns not only students’ extraction and translation of traditional cultural elements, but also their understanding of the cultural contexts behind cultural artefacts and the experiences of potential users. empathy is considered to help designers understand needs, emotions, and contexts from the perspectives of others; however, its role in cpd education remains insufficiently examined through empirical research. this study introduced an empathy-driven instructional approach to examine its associations with students’ empathy and design creativity. methods the participants were 79 undergraduate students from two intact classes in a cpd course. the two classes were assigned at the class level to either the empathy-driven instructional approach or the traditional instructional approach. the empathy-driven group received systematic guidance based on the empathy-driven instructional approach, whereas the traditional group received the traditional instructional approach. both groups completed design tasks based on designated cultural artefacts. results the results showed that students in the empathy-driven group demonstrated higher levels of empathy than those in the traditional group. the analyses also identified significant indirect associations through empathy between the instructional approach and the novelty and quality of design outcomes, a pattern consistent with partial mediation. discussion these findings suggest that the empathy-driven instructional approach in cpd education can help students develop a more integrated understanding of the relationships among artefact contexts, user experiences, and contemporary product experiences, and may support the generation of design outcomes with greater novelty and quality. this study provides preliminary empirical evidence for incorporating empathy training into cpd education. frontiers in psychology

perceived parenting styles and creativity among chinese college students: the multiple mediating roles of self-efficacy and psychological resilience introduction creativity is a fundamental driver of economic growth and societal transformation. the development of creativity can be viewed as a function of the dynamic interplay between environmental contingencies and individual dispositions. research has explored the association between perceived parenting styles and creativity, but few studies have focused on the mediating pathways that explain this relationship. the aim of this study is to examine whether self-efficacy and psychological resilience play a mediating role between perceived parenting styles and creativity. methods a cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 750 chinese college students using convenience sampling from march to may 2025. data were collected using the egna minnen beträffande uppfostran (embu), the general self-efficacy scale (gses), the connor-davidson resilience scale (cd-risc) and the william creativity assessment test (wcat). correlation analysis and mediation tests were performed using spss 22.0 and process macro 3.3 with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals (5000 resamples) to test indirect effects. results correlation analysis revealed significant relationships among perceived parenting styles, self-efficacy, psychological resilience, and creativity. further mediation analysis revealed that perceived parenting styles were associated with college students' creativity through three indirect pathways: via self-efficacy, via psychological resilience, and via both sequentially. discussion this study concludes that perceived parenting styles are directly associated with college students' creativity, and are also indirectly associated with it through the mediating roles of self-efficacy and psychological resilience, as well as through their chain mediating role. these findings identify self-efficacy and psychological resilience as potential targets for future research on creativity enhancement in college students. frontiers in psychology

genai-mediated immersive dialogue practice in liaison interpreting: a mixed-methods investigation of cognitive-affective outcomes and interactional processes introduction liaison interpreting competence encompasses working memory management, executive control, self-efficacy, and affect regulation, yet its development remains constrained by the linguistic inconsistency and variable cognitive-affective demands of conventional peer role-play. drawing on an integrated framework, this quasi-experimental mixed-methods study investigates whether generative ai (genai)-mediated immersive dialogue practice can create a more cognitively authentic and affectively facilitative practice environment for interpreter-learners. method seventy undergraduate students from two intact classes in a chinese university were assigned to an experimental group ( n = 35) practicing with a voice-enabled genai tool simulating bilingual interlocutor personas, or a control group ( n = 35) engaged in traditional peer role-play over 8 weeks. because only one class was assigned to each condition, the between-group comparisons are exploratory. data included interpreting performance scores, anxiety and engagement questionnaires, coded interaction transcripts analyzed through epistemic network analysis (ena), and semi-structured interviews examined via reflexive thematic analysis. results and discussion the experimental group scored significantly higher than the control group in overall interpreting performance, particularly in informational accuracy and interactional management. genai-supported practice was also associated with significantly lower interpreting-related anxiety with a large effect size. learning engagement did not differ significantly, indicating that the two modalities may sustain engagement through different psychological mechanisms. interaction analysis revealed a hub-and-spoke network centered on meaning transfer, with clarification requests and self-repair reflecting active metacognitive monitoring. this pattern represents the aggregate structural profile of interaction across the intervention period rather than a developmental trajectory. qualitative findings identified psychological safety and repeatable mastery opportunities as key affordances, alongside role instability and limited corrective feedback as constraints, with students exercising psychological agency through prompt negotiation and self-directed scaffolding. these findings offer preliminary empirical support for genai as an affectively facilitative practice partner whose effects are theoretically consistent with predictions derived from cognitive load theory, processing efficiency theory, and self-efficacy theory, although the underlying cognitive and motivational mechanisms remain to be directly tested. frontiers in psychology

childhood maltreatment and appearance-related social media consciousness: the moderating role of gender and social media use time objective appearance-related social media consciousness (asmc) has emerged as an important construct for understanding appearance-related vulnerability in social media contexts, yet its developmental antecedents remain underexplored. this study examined the associations between retrospectively reported childhood maltreatment and asmc and tested whether these associations varied by gender and social media use time. methods participants were 405 chinese university students recruited from two universities. they completed measures of asmc, childhood maltreatment, social media use time, and demographic characteristics. path analysis, multi-group analysis, and moderation analysis were conducted, with body mass index (bmi) controlled. results emotional abuse ( β = 0.12, p = 0.040) and sexual abuse ( β = 0.12, p = 0.014) were positively associated with asmc, whereas physical neglect was negatively associated with asmc ( β = −0.13, p = 0.047). the overall pattern of maltreatment–asmc associations differed by gender, δ χ 2 (5) = 11.50, p = 0.042. direct wald tests indicated that only the sexual abuse–asmc association differed significantly between males and females, χ 2 (1) = 9.61, p = 0.002. conclusion these findings suggest that retrospectively reported childhood maltreatment is associated with asmc, with different maltreatment subtypes showing distinct patterns of association. the sexual abuse–asmc association differed significantly by gender, whereas no significant moderating effect of social media use time was found. frontiers in psychology

earthquake preparedness in higher education: institutional resilience, risk perception, and psychosocial mechanisms among academic staff introduction seismic hazards generate psychosocial and organizational consequences, while effective preparedness depends on the translation of institutional resources, risk perception, and resilience mechanisms into functional procedural knowledge. objectives and hypotheses this study tested an integrative model of earthquake preparedness among academic staff, examining institution-related perceptions, seismic risk perception, cognitive resilience, psychological resilience, adaptive resilience, preparedness engagement, and knowledge of intervention procedures. hypotheses addressed direct associations, mediation, moderated mediation, and serial mediation. methodology the sample included 235 academic staff members employed in higher education institutions. data were collected through an online multidimensional questionnaire assessing institutional, cognitive, psychological, and adaptive resilience, risk perception, preparedness engagement, and procedural knowledge. exploratory factor analysis, internal consistency coefficients, inter-construct correlations, and multicollinearity diagnostics were used to examine the instrument's psychometric properties and the empirical overlap among the resilience dimensions. statistical analyses included linear regression, mediation, moderated mediation, and serial mediation using the process macro for spss, with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. results institutional resilience was significantly associated with engagement in preparedness activities. cognitive resilience statistically explained the association between seismic risk perception and procedural knowledge, indicating that perceived risk becomes more functionally relevant when supported by cognitive processing capacities. psychological resilience moderated this mechanism, showing that the indirect association varied according to emotional regulation capacity. serial mediation did not support a fully sequential cognitive–adaptive pathway; instead, adaptive resilience accounted for a significant indirect association between institutional functioning and procedural knowledge. conclusions earthquake preparedness in higher education emerges as an integrative psychosocial and organizational process shaped by institutional mechanisms and individual cognitive, psychological, and adaptive resources. the findings support evidence-based preparedness programs that strengthen institutional communication, cognitive processing of risk information, psychological resilience, and adaptive capacities for emergency response. frontiers in psychology

teacher autonomy support and music learning engagement: conditional associations of self-efficacy and discrete achievement emotions among university music students objective university music learning requires sustained engagement under demanding instructional and practice conditions. this study examined whether perceived teacher autonomy support, music learning self-efficacy, and discrete achievement emotions showed distinguishable associations with multidimensional engagement when considered simultaneously among chinese undergraduate music students. methods cross-sectional survey data were collected from 500 undergraduate music students enrolled at three universities in southern china. participants reported on one current core music course and its primary instructor. covariance-based structural equation modeling was used to evaluate the measurement and structural models, with music learning engagement specified as a higher-order construct comprising behavioral, cognitive, and agentic engagement. indirect associations were estimated using 5,000 case-resampling bootstrap replications with 95% bias-corrected confidence intervals. results the measurement and structural models showed good fit. perceived teacher autonomy support was positively associated with music learning self-efficacy and retained a small positive conditional association with engagement. self-efficacy was positively associated with enjoyment and negatively associated with anxiety and boredom. when all variables were modeled simultaneously, enjoyment was positively associated with engagement and boredom was negatively associated with engagement, whereas anxiety and self-efficacy showed no statistically distinguishable direct associations with engagement. the theoretically ordered indirect associations through self-efficacy and enjoyment [ β = 0.209, 95% ci (0.099, 0.359)] and through self-efficacy and boredom [ β = 0.042, 95% ci (0.011, 0.087)] were statistically distinguishable from zero, whereas the corresponding anxiety pathway was not. the model explained 29.5% of the variance in engagement. conclusion perceived teacher autonomy support, competence-related beliefs, and discrete achievement emotions were differently associated with music learning engagement. in particular, enjoyment and boredom retained distinct associations with engagement after the other constructs were considered simultaneously. these findings support examining instructional support, self-efficacy, and discrete emotional experiences together rather than treating them as interchangeable correlates of university music learning engagement. frontiers in psychology

revising the measurement of eriksonian ego identity in contemporary italian adolescents: the epsi-it introduction the identity subscale of the erikson psychosocial stage inventory (epsi) is the most widely used brief measure of eriksonian ego identity, but it carries a historically situated gender item and has no published italian validation. instruments inherit the assumptions of the era that produced them, and an item can lose validity as those assumptions shift. methods in two waves of an italian school cohort in rome (2025, n = 3,068; 2026, n = 2,896), we examined the original epsi and developed the revised epsi-it. results among the models compared, a bifactor solution fit best in both waves (epsi-it ω h = 0.64, ecv = 0.54), though absolute fit was moderate; the structure supports a total score complemented by a synthesis subscale, whereas clarity (reverse-keyed confusion) adds little beyond the general factor. the 11-item epsi-it showed a coherent structure and a theory-consistent nomological network, and the harmonized core was invariant across groups and waves in terms of the loading level, with a minor intercept-level decrement. across-wave criterion attenuation appeared equally on the constant harmonized items, arguing against an explanation specific to the revision. the gender item did not function as an ego-identity indicator and was removed. discussion we recommend the total score as the primary index, complemented by the synthesis subscale, and report preliminary grade-specific reference values for research use. more broadly, a historically situated item—here gender-related certainty used as a marker of ego identity—can come to function as separable content in a contemporary cohort. frontiers in psychology

extracurricular multilateral training incorporating cognitive–motor activities and its effects on motor proficiency, cognitive ability, and problematic internet use in adolescents background after-school physical activity programs may enhance adolescents’ motor and cognitive development, but evidence regarding their effects on problematic internet use (piu) remains limited. objective this study examined the effects of a 12 week extracurricular multilateral training (emt) program incorporating cognitive–motor activities on motor proficiency (mp), cognitive ability (ca), and problematic internet use (piu) among indonesian adolescents, while accounting for baseline outcomes, daily physical activity, gender, and parental education. methods this parallel-group randomized controlled trial included indonesian junior high school students participating in a 12-week emt program delivered twice weekly. mp, ca, and piu were prespecified as the three primary outcomes and were assessed pre- and post-intervention. ancova compared post-intervention outcomes between the emt and control groups, adjusting for the corresponding baseline score, daily physical activity, gender, and parental education. pearson correlations examined associations among baseline outcomes. results the emt group demonstrated significantly higher post-intervention mp and ca scores and a significantly lower piu score than the control group after adjustment for the corresponding baseline outcome, daily physical activity duration, gender, and parental education (all p < 0.001; ηp 2 = 0.163–0.422). at baseline, ca was positively associated with mp and negatively associated with piu in both groups, while mp was negatively associated with piu only in the emt group (all p < 0.05). conclusion a 12 week extracurricular multilateral training program incorporating cognitive–motor activities improved motor proficiency and cognitive ability and reduced problematic internet use among indonesian adolescents. these findings support the inclusion of structured, cognitively engaging multilateral training in school-based after-school physical activity programs to promote adolescents’ physical, cognitive, and behavioral health. frontiers in psychology

psychological resilience and psychological status among community-dwelling older adults: a cross-sectional study in china introduction in aging societies, promoting psychological well-being among older adults is crucial. while psychological resilience is known to benefit mental health, less is understood about how external resources—specifically cultural and environmental resilience—influence psychological status (life satisfaction and depression) via resilience pathways in older populations. this study investigated these associations and their cross-sectional indirect associations through psychological resilience. methods a cross-sectional survey was conducted with 508 community-dwelling adults aged ≥60 in wenzhou, china (july–september 2024). validated scales measured life satisfaction (swls), depression (ces-d-10), psychological resilience (brs), cultural resilience (chinese cultural beliefs of adversity scale), and environmental resilience (community walkability). control variables included demographics, health, and financial strain. data were analyzed using correlation, regression, and mediation analysis (process macro, model 4) with bootstrapping (95% ci). results psychological resilience partially mediated the relationships between both cultural resilience and environmental resilience with life satisfaction. cultural resilience had a significant total effect on life satisfaction, with 28.9% of its effect mediated by psychological resilience. environmental resilience’s total effect on life satisfaction was mediated by psychological resilience by 19.9%. however, psychological resilience did not mediate the relationships between either cultural or environmental resilience and depression. conclusion psychological resilience serves as a significant mediator linking external resources (cultural and environmental resilience) to life satisfaction, but not depression, among older adults. longitudinal research is needed to confirm causality. frontiers in psychology
