coach behaviors, coach–athlete relationships, and competitive psychological processes in elite sport: a temporal narrative synthesis background research on coach behavior, coach–athlete relationships, and competitive psychological processes has developed in partly separate literatures, limiting understanding of how these domains interact across an elite competitive cycle. aims this review examined how these domains are represented across foundation building, competitive maintenance, peak competition, and post-competition transition, while distinguishing direct temporal evidence from interpretive phase placement. methods web of science, sportdiscus, and scopus were searched for peer-reviewed english-language studies published from january 2016 to 22 june 2026. of 645 records identified, 481 unique records were screened, 205 underwent eligibility assessment, and 30 empirical studies were included. results evidence was strongest for competitive maintenance and peak competition. repeated-measures, diary, prospective, and event-based studies linked coaching behavior and relationship-related judgments with motivation, well-being, perceived justice, burnout, appraisal, coping, affect, confidence, and perceived performance. evidence for foundation building was limited, while direct evidence on post-season evaluation and cross-cycle carryover was largely absent. conclusion the proposed temporal framework should be viewed as an evidence-informed research architecture rather than an established causal sequence. it highlights phase-specific hypotheses for future research, coach education, and psychological support. frontiers in psychology

how teacher support, peer connection, and embodied meaning-making interact in drama-based social-emotional learning in higher education drama-based social-emotional learning has gained increasing attention in higher education, yet participation in embodied activities does not in itself ensure sustained engagement or social-emotional development. less is known about how teacher support, peer interaction, and embodied participation become interconnected in classroom practice, or about the conditions under which this process may be disrupted. this multisite interpretive qualitative study was conducted across four universities in eastern china. data were generated through interviews with 24 students and eight teaching staff, supplemented by 24 reflective journals, 24 classroom observations, and 16 course documents. reflexive thematic analysis produced three themes: participatory safety and bounded autonomy supported by teacher scaffolding; peer connection and group belonging developed through embodied collaboration; and emotional resonance and self-awareness emerging through embodied meaning-making. safety, responsiveness, and a sense of meaning were associated with students’ willingness to participate, whereas unclear boundaries, limited peer responsiveness, and excessive emotional intensity were associated with reduced participation. the findings conceptualize drama-based social-emotional learning as interconnected classroom processes involving teacher scaffolding, peer connection, embodied participation, and reflective integration. frontiers in psychology

emotional intelligence and life satisfaction among health sciences students: a cross-sectional study background perceived emotional intelligence has been associated with psychological wellbeing and may be particularly relevant among health sciences students exposed to academic and interpersonal demands. this study examined the association between perceived emotional intelligence and life satisfaction among health sciences students. methods a cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in january 2023 among 334 undergraduate students enrolled in medicine, nursing, nutrition, and physiotherapy at an ecuadorian university. perceived emotional intelligence was assessed using the 24-item trait meta-mood scale (tmms-24), and life satisfaction was assessed using the five-item satisfaction with life scale (swls). age, sex, and academic program were included as covariates in the adjusted model. group differences were examined using non-parametric tests, the association between the study variables using spearman's rank correlation, and adjusted associations using multiple linear regression. results perceived emotional intelligence was positively associated with life satisfaction (ρ = 0.383, p < 0.001). in the adjusted model, perceived emotional intelligence remained positively associated with life satisfaction ( b = 0.194, 95% ci 0.125–0.263, β = 0.292, p < 0.001). female students reported lower life satisfaction than male students ( b = −2.145, 95% ci −3.982 to −0.308, p = 0.022), whereas no significant sex difference was observed in perceived emotional intelligence. no statistically significant differences in either construct were detected across academic programs or ethnic groups. the adjusted model explained 10.7% of the variance in life satisfaction ( r 2 = 0.107). conclusion perceived emotional intelligence was positively associated with life satisfaction among ecuadorian health sciences students after adjustment for age, sex, and academic program. the modest variance explained by the model supports a multifactorial interpretation of life satisfaction. given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal relationships. frontiers in psychology

when does chatgpt help or hinder? a scoping review of influencing factors in college efl learners' affective and cognitive experiences existing reviews have established the overall direction of chatgpt's effects on college english as a foreign language (efl) learners' affective and cognitive experiences but have not systematically addressed under what conditions these effects arise. this scoping review maps the influencing factors reported in 26 empirical studies examining chatgpt and closely related llm-based generative ai tools as shaping these experiences. a systematic search of web of science, scopus, and eric following prisma-scr guidelines and the ( arksey and o'malley, 2005 ) framework yielded 829 records, with 26 studies meeting inclusion criteria after deduplication and two-stage screening. influencing factors were extracted from each study and organized into learner-level, instructional-level, and technology-level categories based on the cognitive-affective theory of learning with media. ten types of influencing factors were identified. evidence density varied markedly across the three levels, with learner-level factors supported by the largest body of research and technology-level factors by the smallest. self-efficacy showed consistent mediating pathways across eight studies, while metacognitive awareness produced the most clearly documented conditional differentiation between strategic and surface-level chatgpt use. structured instructional integration was the factor with the most consistently positive effects across the three studies that examined it. the influencing factor mapping table reveals that the effects of chatgpt on efl learners are not uniform but contingent on the interaction among learner characteristics, instructional design, and technology use patterns, supporting differentiated rather than uniform approaches to chatgpt integration in college efl instruction. frontiers in psychology

occupational burnout in women schoolteachers in kazakhstan: psychometric evaluation and psychosocial correlates within the job demands-resources framework background teaching combines intense interpersonal demands with administrative and digital workload, and in kazakhstan more than four fifths of schoolteachers are women, which makes burnout in this group a gender-relevant occupational health and wellbeing concern. evidence from central asia remains scarce, and the performance of the russian-language maslach burnout inventory-educators survey (mbi-es) in this population had not been formally examined. methods in a cross-sectional study conducted between october and december 2025, 323 women teachers recruited by convenience in general education schools in three kazakhstani cities completed the mbi-es, the state scale of the spielberger state–trait anxiety inventory, and a structured questionnaire covering employment, workload, social-psychological, lifestyle, and digital factors. we split the sample at random, examined the structure in one half and confirmed it in the other, compared the three-factor model against one-factor, two-factor, and bifactor alternatives, tested measurement invariance, and fitted hierarchical regression models built on the job demands-resources framework. results the correlated three-factor model outperformed one-factor and two-factor alternatives and fitted the validation subsample well ( χ 2 /df = 1.69; cfi = 0.955; rmsea = 0.065; srmr = 0.080). a bifactor model fitted better on global indices but yielded a degenerate exhaustion-specific factor and negative general loadings for accomplishment items, so we retained three factors. loadings and intercepts were invariant across the random halves; across cities loadings held but intercepts did not. subscale reliability was high (α 0.918 to 0.963). job demands added 35.1% of explained variance in emotional exhaustion beyond background characteristics, resources a further 6.6%; perceived work stress, state anxiety, and low physical activity remained independent correlates in the full model (adjusted r 2 = 0.630). depersonalization was associated with conflict, work stress, isolation, and an unfavorable collegial climate (adjusted r 2 = 0.443), and personal accomplishment gave the weakest model (adjusted r 2 = 0.170). demographic and formal workload characteristics contributed little. conclusion the russian-language mbi-es performs acceptably in women schoolteachers in kazakhstan. in this convenience sample, burnout was associated more closely with appraised psychosocial working conditions than with formal job parameters. the cross-sectional design supports no causal inference, and the findings apply to women teachers in three urban settings. frontiers in psychology

the impact of ai chatbot service quality on consumer purchase intention: the cognitive and affective mediating mechanisms introduction the increasing prevalence of artificial intelligence chatbots in e-commerce raises questions about how the service quality dimensions of ai chatbots may influence consumer purchase intentions. drawing on expectation-confirmation theory, the information systems success model, and the technology acceptance model, this study proposes a conceptual framework to examine these relationships. methods survey data were collected from 493 chinese consumers with prior experience using ai chatbots. the study examined perceived personalization, social presence, information quality, and human-ai service continuity as possible antecedents of purchase intention. perceived usefulness and satisfaction were treated as mediating variables. partial least squares structural equation modeling was used for the analysis with 5,000 bootstrapped resamples. results perceived personalization, social presence, information quality, and human-ai service continuity were associated with perceived usefulness. additionally, perceived personalization, information quality, and human-ai service continuity were positively associated with satisfaction. conversely, social presence did not show a significant direct effect on satisfaction. both perceived usefulness and satisfaction are linked to purchase intention, with satisfaction having a stronger direct connection. the mediation analysis revealed that perceived usefulness and satisfaction mediate the relationship between ai chatbot service quality and purchase intention. the only exception was the indirect effect of social presence through satisfaction, which was not statistically significant. discussion this study seeks to contribute to understanding how the service quality of ai chatbots influences consumers’ purchase intentions through perceived usefulness and satisfaction. the results indicate that information quality is the most significant among the service quality dimensions in ai-mediated interactions. the lack of a significant direct impact of social presence on satisfaction suggests that, in utilitarian-oriented e-commerce environments, consumers are more likely to prioritize functional service features over social–emotional factors when assessing ai chatbot services. these findings may inform e-commerce practitioners seeking to improve ai-driven customer service by emphasizing information accuracy and completeness, enhancing personalization, and fostering seamless human-ai service continuity to drive purchase conversions. frontiers in psychology

dynamic associations among exercise self-efficacy, extracurricular exercise involvement, and perceived physical fitness in chinese undergraduates: a three-wave ri-clpm study inroduction university students often experience difficulties maintaining regular extracurricular exercise, yet less is known about how exercise-related confidence, involvement, and perceived fitness unfold within individuals over time. this three-wave longitudinal study examined the dynamic associations among exercise self-efficacy (ese), extracurricular exercise involvement (eei), and perceived physical fitness (ppf) in chinese undergraduates using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (ri-clpm). methods undergraduate students aged 18 years or older from eight universities in sichuan province, china, participated in offline surveys at three waves with approximately eight-week intervals. the baseline (t1) analytic sample included 1,673 students; 1,543 provided valid follow-up data at t2, and 1,455 provided valid follow-up data at t3. manifest mean scores of ese, eei, and ppf were analyzed in mplus 8.3 using robust maximum likelihood and full-information maximum likelihood for missing data. results the free-lag ri-clpm showed excellent fit and was retained as the final model. at the within-person level, higher-than-usual ese predicted higher-than-usual eei at the subsequent wave across both intervals. higher-than-usual eei also predicted higher-than-usual ppf across both intervals. in addition, eei at t2 positively predicted ese at t3; individual between-interval path differences did not survive multiplicity adjustment. in contrast, ppf did not significantly predict later ese or eei. the specific indirect association from ese_t1 to ppf_t3 through eei_t2 was small (b = 0.02250; standardized estimate = 0.02038) and received tentative support from the 95% bias-corrected bootstrap interval [0.004, 0.051], while the wald test was marginal ( p = 0.055). discussion these findings identify exercise self-efficacy and the quality of extracurricular exercise involvement as candidate targets for experimental research on university students’ perceived fitness. frontiers in psychology

from childhood trauma to functional impairment in borderline personality disorder: the mediating role of emotion dysregulation and impulsivity background borderline personality disorder (bpd) is characterized by severe psychosocial dysfunction and high rates of adverse childhood experiences. emotion dysregulation and impulsivity are core bpd features that may mediate the impact of childhood trauma on functioning. methods a total of 203 outpatients with bpd (mean age = 24.4 years; 84.7% women) completed the childhood trauma questionnaire (ctq), difficulties in emotion regulation scale (ders), barratt impulsiveness scale (bis-11), and functioning assessment short test (fast). associations between childhood trauma (ctq total and subscales) and psychosocial functioning were examined, testing the serial mediating role of the two mediators (process model 6; percentile bootstrapping, 5,000 resamples; adjusted for gender and age). results ctq total was associated with poorer functioning in the covariate-adjusted mediation model, with a significant direct effect. the total indirect effect through the mediators was significant, but no single pathway, including the serial ctq → ders → bis-11 → fast pathway, reached significance. among trauma subtypes, emotional abuse and emotional neglect showed significant total and direct effects, and the serial pathway was significant for both neglect subtypes; sexual and physical abuse were not associated with functioning. when the five trauma subtypes were entered simultaneously, none showed a unique association. conclusion childhood trauma is associated with poorer psychosocial functioning in bpd, partly through emotion dysregulation and impulsivity, although much remains unexplained. the absence of unique subtype effects points to the cumulative nature of childhood adversity (polyvictimisation). being cross-sectional, these findings support trauma-informed therapeutic approaches only as hypotheses for future research. frontiers in psychology

dual-pathway processing of ai-generated chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, eeg, and artistic expertise ai-driven generative art is changing the scope of artistic creation, but the principles behind its aesthetics and the perception of its outcomes remain relatively unexplored, especially concerning culturally specific art forms. the present study investigates how viewers cognitively, affectively, and evaluatively process ai-generated chinese ink paintings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. we introduce the concept of expressive expansion as a viewer-perceived psychological effect — the tendency for ai-generated ink works to elicit higher ratings of expressiveness and dynamic tension than traditional counterparts — and examine its neural and behavioral correlates using a multimodal paradigm. stimuli generated using a pre-trained stable diffusion architecture were assessed according to three aesthetic metrics along with traditional and digital non-ai artworks by 120 respondents equally split into professional artists and non-artists. multidimensional measurement based on eye-tracking, semantic differential rating, and eeg showed that, under blind viewing conditions, ai-generated stimuli yielded significantly greater scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional and digital non-ai works, suggesting that they engaged broader attentional exploration and increased attentional engagement as indexed by implicit behavioral and neural measures. professional and non-professional evaluators agreed on expressiveness evaluation scores but differed considerably in their cultural authenticity perception, suggesting a dissociation between aesthetic appeal and cultural validity. these findings are consistent with a dual-pathway interpretive framework in which perceptual-affective and cultural-evaluative responses can dissociate as a function of artistic expertise — an account advanced as consistent with the observed dissociation rather than as a mechanism established by the present data — and contribute to the emerging empirical literature on audience responses to ai-generated art in culturally specific domains. all conclusions are restricted to the selected stimulus sets under the present experimental conditions. the source code, lora model weights, and experimental datasets will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/15100376058/ink-painting-ai-expressive-expansion (doi: 10.5281/zenodo.20540420). frontiers in psychology

from leadership to innovation: the psychological pathways of intrinsic motivation and creative process engagement introduction although responsible leadership (rl) has attracted increasing attention from the academic community, the correlation mechanism between it and employee innovative behavior (eib) has not been fully clarified. based on the data of high-tech enterprises in china, this study explores how intrinsic motivation (im) and creative process engagement (cpe) explain the relationship between responsible leadership and innovative behavior. method this study uses spss 27.0 and amos software for statistical analysis. the data is collected on the credamo platform. after routine data screening and cleaning, 344 valid replies are used for follow-up analysis. result the results showed that rl was positively related to eib, with im and cpe independently mediating this relationship. besides, the sequential indirect effect of rl on eib through im and cpe was also significant. discussion the findings indicated that im and cpe serve as two interconnected mechanisms linking rl with eib. drawing on self-determination theory and social information processing theory, this study further illustrates how employees interpret responsible leadership-related information, develop im, and remain engaged in creative activities. frontiers in psychology

the effect of perceived organizational support on safety compliance in libyan public hospitals: a cross-sectional study of the mediating role of proactive personality background perceived organizational support (pos) reflects employees’ beliefs that their organization values their contributions and cares about their well-being. although pos has been linked to desirable workplace outcomes, less is known about the psychological processes through which it is associated with safety compliance behavior among healthcare employees, particularly in under-examined developing-country contexts. objective this study aims to evaluate proactive personality as an individual-level mechanism underlying the association between pos and safety compliance behavior in healthcare personnel. methods a hospital-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 309 healthcare employees working in public hospitals in ajdabiya, libya. data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (pls-sem) with smartpls 4. reliability and validity of the measurement model were assessed before testing the direct and indirect relationships using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples (bias-corrected and accelerated, bca). results pos was positively associated with proactive personality ( β = 0.242, p < 0.001) and safety compliance behavior ( β = 0.217, p < 0.001). proactive personality was also positively associated with safety compliance behavior ( β = 0.554, p < 0.001), the strongest path in the model. proactive personality was also associated with a significant indirect association between pos and safety compliance ( β = 0.134, p < 0.001), consistent with complementary partial mediation. the structural model accounted for 41.2% of the variance in safety compliance behavior and 5.9% of the variance in proactive personality. conclusion the findings indicate that proactive personality is associated with a stronger direct relationship with safety compliance behavior than organizational support is among healthcare workers in this sample. the study extends organizational support theory within the healthcare context by showing how individual differences relate to safety-related behavior. given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted causally; the findings nonetheless suggest that healthcare organizations may benefit from combining organizational-support practices with efforts that support proactive engagement among staff. as a primary goal, the abstract should render the general significance and conceptual advance of the work clearly accessible to a broad readership. references should not be cited in the abstract. leave the abstract empty if your article does not require one – please see the “article types” on every frontiers journal page for full details. frontiers in psychology

a process-oriented interpretation of perfectionism: error, uncertainty, and the principles of organization contemporary dimensional models have substantially advanced the psychological understanding of perfectionism. however, growing theoretical and empirical evidence suggests that understanding the phenomenon may also require consideration of additional process-oriented perspectives. rather than proposing a new definition of perfectionism, the present perspective introduces a complementary process-oriented interpretative framework that focuses on the principles of organization underlying the phenomenon. particular attention is directed toward individuals’ relations to error, uncertainty, and performance-related self-evaluation, as well as to the experiential organization associated with these processes. within this framework, perfectionism is interpreted as a psychological configuration in which flawlessness functions as a normative reference point, organizing self-evaluation, anticipatory regulation, and the interpretation of action. the paper further argues that characteristics commonly associated with perfectionistic strivings may, in some cases, reflect striving for excellence rather than perfectionism itself, suggesting that these forms of functioning may be organized according to different psychological principles. a phenomenological analysis illustrates how anticipation of mistakes may influence attentional focus, temporal experience, self-monitoring, and the lived experience of action. the proposed perspective is not intended to replace existing dimensional models but to complement them by offering an additional process-oriented level of interpretation. at the theoretical level, this framework contributes to a more differentiated understanding of perfectionism, while at the empirical level it highlights new directions for investigating error anticipation, regulatory flexibility, conditional self-evaluation, and other dynamic psychological processes that may not be fully captured by traditional trait-based measures. frontiers in psychology

left dorsomedial prefrontal cortex hyperactivation reflects early compensation for emerging social cognition difficulties in multiple sclerosis background social cognition (sc) has emerged as a relevant neurocognitive domain in people with multiple sclerosis (pwms), given its impact on everyday functioning. however, the neural mechanisms supporting sc performance in pwms remain underexplored, highlighting the need for ecologically valid assessment paradigms capable of capturing both behavioral and neural aspects of social-cognitive functioning. in this study, we addressed this gap by investigating the clinical application of an fmri-adapted version of the edinburgh social cognition test (escot) to explore the neural correlates of sc functioning in pwms. methods in total, 59 subjects (27 pwms, mean edss = 3.74, and 32 healthy controls) were enrolled in this study and underwent a comprehensive neuropsychological assessment, including sc tests, and the fmri-adapted version of the escot. results no significant between-group differences were observed during the fmri task performance. across groups, the paradigm elicited activation within a network involving the bilateral middle temporal poles, left dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and precuneus, regions consistently implicated in social-cognitive processing. within the pwms group, a significant association was identified between neural activation and behavioral sc performance (rho = −0.447, p = 0.032), linking poorer sc performance with greater activation of the left dorsomedial prefrontal cortex. conclusion the findings support the applicability of the escot as an ecologically valid neuropsychological paradigm for capturing the neural processes underlying sc abilities in a clinical population. the observed relationship suggests that increased activation of an executive neural hub may support sc proficiency in pwms, potentially reflecting an early compensatory strategy. frontiers in psychology

comparing physical education course satisfaction between students with hearing and visual impairments in mainland china: a revised importance—performance analysis introduction this study examined physical education satisfaction among chinese university students with hearing and visual impairments using revised importance-performance analysis (ripa). methods a cross-sectional survey was conducted with 449 students from 10 universities in guangdong province, china, including 251 students with hearing impairments and 198 students with visual impairments. the study assessed perceptions of instructional content, teaching practices, learning outcomes, and overall physical education experiences. results the findings revealed distinct patterns of needs and satisfaction between the two groups. students with hearing impairments placed greater importance on instructional clarity, communication accessibility, and individualized support, whereas students with visual impairments prioritized course accessibility, activity safety, and support for sustained physical activity engagement. across both groups, immediate participation experiences and inclusive learning environments were valued more highly than long-term physical fitness outcomes. discussion these findings indicate that physical education satisfaction among students with sensory impairments is shaped by disability-specific needs and educational experiences. accordingly, universities should adopt disability-specific physical education strategies by strengthening communication accessibility and individualized instructional support for students with hearing impairments, while emphasizing activity accessibility, safety, and sustained physical activity engagement for students with visual impairments. frontiers in psychology

multimodal art intervention for flourishing in lonely university students: psychological and exploratory neurophysiological outcomes introduction loneliness is highly prevalent among university students and is associated with reduced positive functioning. however, evidence concerning multimodal art interventions for flourishing-related outcomes in this population remains limited. this study examined whether an eight-week, group-based multimodal art intervention could improve psychological flourishing, state positive affect, aesthetic experience, and exploratory wearable electroencephalography (eeg) indices among lonely university students. methods sixty students with elevated loneliness (20-item ucla loneliness scale score ≥ 44) and below-flourishing mental health, as assessed using the mental health continuum–short form, were randomly assigned to either the intervention group ( n = 30) or a wait-list control group ( n = 30). the intervention comprised eight weekly group sessions integrating guided music listening, visual creation, movement or role-play, and group sharing. outcomes were assessed over time and analyzed for group × time interactions. results significant group × time interactions were observed for flourishing, f (2, 112) = 4.57, p = 0.012, partial η 2 = 0.075; positive affect f (2, 112) = 19.45, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.258; aesthetic experience f (2, 112) = 24.37, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.303; and the relaxation index f (2, 112) = 3.30, p = 0.040, partial η 2 = 0.056. the group × time interaction for the attention index was not significant. discussion the findings provide preliminary evidence that a group-based multimodal art intervention may enhance aesthetic engagement, positive affect, psychological flourishing, and alpha-based relaxation among lonely university students, although attention-related eeg indices remained unchanged. multimodal art programs may offer a feasible and accessible approach to supporting university students’ well-being. frontiers in psychology

navigating the systemic labyrinth: the dual-track breakthrough of student-athletes under china's “integration of sports and education” introduction although dual career (dc) development has received growing international attention, the psychosocial experiences of high-level student-athletes (hlsas) within china's evolving integration of sports and education (ise) context remain underexplored. methods this study adopted an interpretivist qualitative design and used reflexive thematic analysis to examine retrospective developmental accounts from 19 chinese hlsas admitted to university through the high-level sports team pathway. results athletic achievement expanded access to higher education but did not automatically secure stable competence, legitimacy, or belonging across academic and athletic settings. effort often remained within hlsas' control even when its returns became uncertain because of injury, bodily limits, competitive conditions, and fluctuating performance, requiring athletes to recalibrate causal expectations and perceptions of what could still be changed. institutional support, recognition, and opportunities also varied with athletic standing, making the quality of integration psychologically consequential beyond the formal coexistence of sport and education. discussion these findings conceptualize dc as a process of conditional inclusion. chinese hlsas navigate a systemically structured but psychologically experienced labyrinth, in which breakthrough occurs when athletic achievement is transformed from an entry credential and performance identity into a broader basis for competence, belonging, self-redefinition, and future possibility. effective ise therefore requires developmental conditions that allow sporting achievement to open educational opportunities without defining the limits of student-athletes' subsequent academic, personal, and career development. frontiers in psychology

the association of high school male teachers’ physical education classroom environment with academic buoyancy among female students: a chain mediating role of positive academic emotions and learning engagement introduction this study aimed to examine the associations of high school male teachers’ physical education classroom environment with female students’ academic buoyancy, and to examine the chain mediating role of positive academic emotions and learning engagement. methods using the perceived physical education classroom environment scale, the academic buoyancy scale, the academic emotions scale, and the learning engagement scale, a survey was conducted among 630 female high school students from five high schools in northeast china, yielding 601 valid questionnaires. data were analyzed using pearson correlation, multiple regression, and mediation analysis with bootstrapping (process model 6). results (1) high school male teachers’ physical education classroom environment was significantly positively correlated with female students’ academic buoyancy ( r = 0.363, p < 0.01), positive academic emotions ( r = 0.274, p < 0.01), and learning engagement ( r = 0.298, p < 0.01); positive academic emotions were significantly positively correlated with learning engagement ( r = 0.314, p < 0.01) and academic buoyancy ( r = 0.341, p < 0.01); learning engagement was significantly positively correlated with academic buoyancy ( r = 0.313, p < 0.01). (2) physical education classroom environment was positively and significantly associated with female students’ academic buoyancy, with a direct association of 0.2525, accounting for 69.60% of the total effect. (3) in the relationship between physical education classroom environment and academic buoyancy, positive academic emotions and learning engagement showed both independent mediating effects and a chain mediating effect, with effect sizes accounting for 16.50, 10.70, and 3.20% of the total effect, respectively. conclusion high school male teachers’ physical education classroom environment is positively correlated with female students’ academic buoyancy, and shows a positive indirect association not only through the independent mediating roles of positive academic emotions and learning engagement but also through their chain mediating role. given the cross-sectional self-report design, these findings should be interpreted as correlational evidence rather than causal conclusions. frontiers in psychology

source-based morphometry analyses yield associations between large-scale structural brain networks and psychopathic traits in incarcerated adolescents studies commonly report that youth with elevated psychopathic traits exhibit deficits within limbic and paralimbic regions, including reduced gray matter volume (gmv) in the amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex (ofc), and temporal pole. however, studies have also reported additional structural abnormalities in regions extending beyond limbic and paralimbic regions among youth with elevated psychopathic traits, including the middle frontal gyrus (mfg), inferior frontal gyrus (ifg), precuneus, inferior parietal lobule (ipl), and fusiform gyrus. this suggests youth with elevated psychopathic traits may be associated with deficits within large-scale structural networks. the current study investigated whether youth with elevated psychopathic traits were associated with such deficits through the use of source-based morphometry (sbm), a multivariate analysis of structural magnetic resonance imaging data. sbm uses independent component analysis (ica) to identify distinct sets of brain regions that form different large-scale structural networks. we investigated whether youth psychopathy scores, assessed via the hare psychopathy checklist: youth version (pcl:yv), were associated with sbm loading coefficients among n = 413 incarcerated boys. compared to participants scoring low on the pcl:yv, participants scoring high on the pcl:yv contributed less (i.e., exhibited reduced gmv) to large-scale structural networks containing limbic and paralimbic regions (e.g., the amygdala, insula, ofc, temporal pole, and posterior cingulate) and additional regions (e.g., the ifg, precuneus, ipl, and fusiform gyrus). through the use of multivariate sbm analyses, the current study helps further improve our understanding of structural abnormalities among youth with elevated psychopathic traits. frontiers in psychology

when inclusive leadership meets supervisory interaction pressure: explaining innovative behavior among public employees introduction public organizations increasingly depend on employees to identify service failures and implement improvements, yet immediate supervisors combine developmental support with evaluative authority. drawing on job demands-resources theory and integrating psychological contract and public service motivation research, this study examines how inclusive leadership is associated with innovative behavior and when supervisory interaction pressure constrains this relationship. methods cross-sectional survey data were collected from 4,511 tax civil servants across a provincial tax administration system in china and analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and moderated sequential mediation analyses. results inclusive leadership was positively associated with innovative behavior directly, and the observed indirect association was consistent with the proposed ordering of psychological contract and public service motivation. supervisory interaction pressure weakened the positive relationships between inclusive leadership and both psychological contract and innovative behavior. however, the moderated mediation tests did not provide sufficient statistical evidence that supervisory interaction pressure significantly weakened the indirect or ordered sequential indirect relationships. inclusive leadership nevertheless remained positively associated with both outcomes at higher levels of supervisory interaction pressure, indicating that interaction pressure constrained rather than eliminated its benefits. discussion the study contributes to public personnel management research by showing how the relational conditions surrounding supervisory interaction shape the use and interpretation of inclusive leadership as a job resource. it further explains how supportive supervisory conduct is associated with perceived reciprocity, public service motivation, and innovative behavior. frontiers in psychology

negative school gossip, self-esteem, and exercise intention among chinese adolescents: a mediation model purpose this study examined the associations among negative school gossip, self-esteem, and general exercise intention among chinese adolescents, with particular attention to the mediating role of self-esteem and the relevance of these associations to physical education (pe) and school-based movement contexts. methods a cross-sectional online questionnaire survey was conducted among 1,713 junior middle school students in china. negative school gossip, self-esteem, and exercise intention were assessed using established self-report scales. data were analyzed using latent-variable structural equation modeling in mplus 8.3. common method bias, reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and model fit were examined before testing the mediation model. bias-corrected bootstrap analysis with 2,000 bootstrap samples was used to test the indirect association. a sensitivity analysis was conducted by controlling for gender, grade, region, parental education, only-child status, and family economic status. results the three-factor measurement model showed better fit than alternative measurement models, and the measures demonstrated acceptable reliability and validity. in the main structural model, negative school gossip was negatively associated with self-esteem ( β = −0.157, p < 0.001) and exercise intention ( β = −0.063, p = 0.031), while self-esteem was positively associated with exercise intention ( β = 0.240, p < 0.001). the standardized indirect association from negative school gossip to exercise intention through self-esteem was significant [ β = −0.038, 95% bootstrap ci (−0.055, −0.024)], accounting for 37.62% of the total association. the pattern remained stable after controlling for demographic covariates. conclusion negative school gossip was associated with weaker general exercise intention among chinese adolescents, and self-esteem partly accounted for this association. although exercise intention was not measured specifically for pe lessons, the findings are relevant to pe because school movement contexts are highly visible and peer-evaluative settings in which reputation-based exclusion and stigma may reduce psychological safety. the results therefore suggest that supportive peer climates and protection from gossip-related exclusion may be important for inclusive pe and equitable participation in school-based physical activity. frontiers in psychology

from need to action: exploring the motivations of women entrepreneurs through the triple-driver framework of women’s entrepreneurship introduction women’s entrepreneurship has received increasing scholarly attention in recent years; however, research has largely overlooked women entrepreneurs whose ventures are specifically dedicated to addressing the needs of other women. existing conceptualizations of women’s entrepreneurial motivations are primarily theoretical and have not been extensively validated using empirical data.this study aimed to explore the motivations of women entrepreneurs who established ventures addressing women’s needs and to develop an empirically grounded framework for understanding these motivations. methods a qualitative design was employed, involving in-depth semi-structured interviews with 60 israeli women entrepreneurs. data were analyzed using explanatory content analysis, guided by the competency-based framework. results the findings resulted in the development of the triple-driver framework of women’s entrepreneurship, comprising three interrelated domains: personal drivers (e.g., lived experience and personal passion, justice-oriented values, autonomy), relational drivers (family and friends, role models), and ecosystem drivers (recognition of unmet societal needs, institutional support). discussion this study advances the literature by proposing an empirically grounded framework that broadens the theoretical understanding of women-centered entrepreneurship. the findings offer practical implications for policymakers and organizations seeking to foster women’s entrepreneurship and provide a foundation for future quantitative validation and cross-cultural research. for policymakers and organizations seeking to support women’s entrepreneurship, the triple-driver framework provides a roadmap for understanding the personal, relational, and ecosystem-level pathways through which women are motivated to initiate and develop ventures. this understanding can inform the development of support efforts that are better aligned with women entrepreneurs’ motivations. for women entrepreneurs themselves, recognizing these motivational drivers may provide a clearer understanding of the factors shaping their entrepreneurial actions, helping them more intentionally define, direct, and develop their initiatives. frontiers in psychology

a cross-cultural empirical investigation of aesthetic responses to an iranian dance style the empirical aesthetics of dance is a relatively recent field of investigation, and most research has been focused on the aesthetic experience of observers when perceiving different western dance styles. it is well-known from other domains that prior exposure and familiarity modulate value formation and aesthetic judgment. dance cultures vary considerably with regard to emotional expressivity and types of movements used. therefore, we hypothesised that culturally-dependent emotional expressivities and the choice of movements within a choreography would modulate observers’ aesthetic experience. across three experiments, with a total of 242 iranian and english participants, we investigated cross-cultural aesthetic judgment to dance movements of an iranian dance style. we asked how culture group, intended emotional expressivity, type of movement, motion energy and luminance interacted in aesthetic judgments of expressivity, beauty and liking. taking advantage of a newly developed iranian dance movement library, we found a general effect of culture and of emotion. iranians generally rated the stimuli higher than english participants did, and joyful movements were preferred overall. iranians found lower body and staccato movements more beautiful than english participants did – likely due to the subtle role of lower body movements, unfamiliar to english observers, in iranian dance. while motion energy (but not luminance) had some influence on aesthetic judgment, intended emotion and movement type were stronger modulators of expressivity, beauty and liking judgments. this iranian dance style is a largely unknown dance genre in many parts of the world and holds great promise as a subject for empirical aesthetics. perception

implementación de dos programas virtuales de mindfulness en docentes universitarios y su asociación con resultados en la ansiedad, la depresión y el burnout la depresión y la ansiedad son trastornos que pueden afectar a personas en cualquier ocupación, incluyendo a los profesores universitarios, impactando su bienestar emocional y desempeño laboral. esta investigación estudió cambios en las variables emocionales y de burnout en una muestra de docentes universitarios de facultades de psicología asociados a dos condiciones de intervención basadas en mindfulness. treinta y tres profesores fueron divididos aleatoriamente, un grupo recibió la intervención de mindfulness basada en el protocolo unificado (pu) de barlow en sesiones virtuales (n =18), el otro lo hizo a través de la aplicación headspace (hs) con el programa básico (n = 15). se encontró una asociación en las dos condiciones de intervención (pu y headspace) con una disminución en los niveles de depresión y una de las escalas de consciencia emocional. sin embargo, el puntaje de eficacia del burnout solo aumentó en el grupo que recibió el módulo del protocolo. esta investigación destaca que la práctica de mindfulness, ya sea a través de una aplicación o en sesiones guiadas por profesionales, puede tener un impacto positivo en la salud emocional y el bienestar de profesores universitarios, con beneficios notables en la reducción de ansiedad y depresión. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

the body imagines: soma in the intersubjective field 1 abstract this article offers a contemporary perspective on the psychosomatic field in analysis wherein the psyche and body exist as a unified whole. from this perspective, the body is one of several channels for the emergence of unconscious material, which is to be understood and engaged like any other manifestation of the unconscious. hence, bodily symptoms or sensations are embraced as dreams which inform us about the unconscious processes of the patient, the analyst, and their shared intersubjective field. the manifestations of somatic experience are understood as providing a window into the mind/body field. through the integration of jungian and bionian thought, with supporting research from neuroscience, metaphor, implicit experience, and primary affects, this article offers a contrast to the traditional jungian perspective which emphasizes visual image and narrative over sensory, somatic, and affective experience. journal of analytical psychology

sixteen years later: revisiting cultural complexes and the roots of archetypal thematic analysis (ata) 1 abstract written as a letter to my 28‐year‐old self, this paper explores the development of my engagement with cultural complexes . on august 18, 2009, i finished a chapter applying cultural complexes to a history of china, complete with elaborate charts that seemed to confirm a process by which cultural complexes are formed, and how china’s then recent actions during the beijing olympic games (i.e., utilising 7‐year‐old yang peiyi’s vocals yet refusing to allow her to perform at the opening ceremony, opting instead for the lip‐syncing of 9‐year‐old lin miaoke and the initial cover‐up of classical dancer liu yan’s accident during rehearsals) seemed to confirm the constellation of emotional and behavioural patterns that could be usefully assembled under the concept. while this paper is an opportunity to reflect on my critical assessment of cultural complexes, it is equally an example of autoethnographic study and a meditation on personal archival practices within a post‐ and neo‐jungian framework. crucially, an autoethnographic approach has facilitated an understanding of how the development of archetypal thematic analysis (ata) (in collaboration with ann yeoman) stems from my thinking around, and appraisal of, cultural complexes. ata is offered as a complement to cultural complex theory (cct) in the hopes that a mobilisation of both can produce a methodological expression of a ‘third way’ or what paul preciado calls a mutant psychoanalysis . journal of analytical psychology

a jungian psychology perspective on cultural hatred and african american women jungian psychology as developed from the work and theories of c.g. jung has not been without issues related to racism and raciality. the development of jung’s theories carries historical references to people of color, particularly africans and african americans, that are racially negative. as american jungian psychology has evolved, there is a deeper questioning as to jung’s theories related to africanist people. in the reflection of applicability of a jungian lens to clinical work with the african diaspora, it must initially be noted that there is a cultural bias in the original lens that views those of african descent. this paper explores the ego; cultural and collective consciousness of african american women as related to cultural hatred. african american women experience psychological issues unique to them based on being black/brown bodied individuals. this paper discusses these issues, in understanding the double consciousness of being african and american, with consideration of a racialized jungian psychology theoretical model. psychoanalytic inquiry

media coverage of novel sustainable products in portugal: representations of bioplastics in the news / cobertura mediática de productos sostenibles nuevos en portugal: representaciones de los bioplásticos en las noticias bioplastics offer a promising alternative to conventional plastics, reducing environmental impacts and dependency on fossil resources, and promoting the transition to the circular economy. however, their success depends heavily on consumers’ acceptance, which is often shaped by how the media portray these products. this study examines how bioplastics have been represented in portuguese media and how these narratives may influence consumer beliefs and acceptance. a total of 133 online news articles from major portuguese outlets with mentions to bioplastics, published between 2010 and 2024, were identified. this resulted in 650 coding units with specific mentions to bioplastics that were coded by two independent judges into five categories: definitions, types/feedstocks, uses, properties, and impacts of bioplastics. overall, media coverage emphasised positive impacts and properties of bioplastics, while also highlighting challenges, such as production issues and limitations in replacing conventional plastics. misconceptions often stemmed from confusion around biodegradability, reinforcing false beliefs that bioplastics can naturally degrade in the environment. future communications should promote an alignment between industry and consumers’ conceptualisation of biodegradability, clarifying bioplastics definitions, characteristics, and benefits. psyecology-bilingual journal of environmental psychology-revista bilingue de psicologia ambiental

gender-role attitudes and sleep among full-time employed mothers and fathers in taiwan: a three-wave longitudinal study abstract background gender-role attitudes may shape how employed parents understand work and family roles, but their implications may depend on social position. we examined whether these attitudes were associated with subsequent sleep quality among full-time employed mothers and fathers, and whether this association differed by parent gender. we hypothesized that more traditional attitudes would be associated with poorer subsequent sleep to a greater extent among mothers than among fathers. methods participants were 523 full-time employed taiwanese parents of at least one child aged 12 years or younger, assessed at baseline and approximately 3 and 6 months later. primary linear mixed models included 478 participants with at least one follow-up assessment and complete covariate data and predicted follow-up pittsburgh sleep quality index scores from baseline gender-role attitudes, parent gender, and their interaction, adjusting for baseline sleep and demographic covariates. ordered-categorical analyses examined measurement properties and cross-gender comparability of the attitude items. results after accounting for sleep quality at study entry, the association between gender-role attitudes and later sleep differed between mothers and fathers in the hypothesized direction (b = 0.126, p = .028). the estimated associations ran in opposite directions, although neither was statistically significant on its own in the primary model. this difference was near zero without accounting for sleep at study entry and, on average, across all three assessments. the attitude items were not fully comparable between mothers and fathers. conclusions a hypothesized mother–father difference in the association between gender-role attitudes and later sleep was observed after accounting for sleep at study entry. this exploratory pattern was not consistent across longitudinal approaches, and limited comparability of the attitude items across groups leaves its substantive meaning uncertain. these findings leave open a question worth pursuing: whether the same attitudes relate to sleep differently depending on the everyday work and family circumstances in which they are held. future studies can test this by directly measuring how daily caregiving and household work are shared—a promising next step for research on parental sleep. bmc psychology
