prevalence of depression in iranian premenopausal and postmenopausal women and its association with sex hormone levels abstract background despite the global interest in depression as a disorder, few studies have been conducted on the association of female sex hormones and depression across different reproductive ages, and the findings have not been consistent to date. this study aimed to investigate the prevalence of depression in premenopausal and postmenopausal women in southeast iran and its association with sex hormone levels. methods this cross-sectional study included 952 women aged 18–65 years, recruited randomly across four socioeconomic regions of kerman, southeast iran, in 2024. depressive symptoms were assessed using a validated persian language version of the beck depression inventory-ii (bdi-ii), a self-report screening instrument, with a cut-off score of > 14 to identify women with elevated depressive symptoms. serum levels of progesterone, prolactin, estradiol, and testosterone were measured. demographic variables such as body mass index (bmi) and age were also recorded. multivariable logistic regression models were stratified by menopausal status to examine hormone-depression associations. results the overall prevalence of elevated depressive symptoms was 40%; separately, 39% in premenopausal and 41% in postmenopausal women. in the adjusted multivariable models, lower estradiol levels were independently associated with greater odds of depressive symptoms in premenopausal women (adjusted or = 0.63, 95% ci: 0.18–0.92, p = 0.038) and postmenopausal women (adjusted or = 0.61, 95% ci: 0.23–0.88, p = 0.034). older age and higher bmi were also independently associated with elevated depressive symptoms in both groups. divorced or widowed marital status was an additional significant predictor in premenopausal women (adjusted or = 1.36, 95% ci: 1.17–1.59, p = 0.043). there were no significant associations between progesterone, prolactin, or testosterone with elevated depressive symptoms after adjustment. conclusions our findings on women in southeast iran suggest that postmenopausal women are slightly more likely to experience elevated depressive symptoms than premenopausal ones. additionally, women with elevated depressive symptoms had significantly lower estradiol levels than those without. in both premenopausal and postmenopausal groups, older age, higher bmi, and lower estradiol levels were independently associated with greater odds of elevated depressive symptoms. divorced or widowed marital status was an additional significant predictor in premenopausal women. bmc psychology

internet addiction disorder and cybersecurity risk: a neurobiological and behavioral review. internet addiction disorder (iad) has attracted substantial clinical and scientific interest over the past two decades. although the condition remains outside formal diagnostic frameworks in the fifth edition of the diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders, accumulating neuroimaging evidence demonstrates that compulsive internet use is associated with disruptions in dopaminergic reward circuitry and prefrontal cortical function that closely parallel those observed in substance use disorders. these neurobiological changes, encompassing impaired executive function, elevated impulsivity, and heightened reward sensitivity, may carry implications for cybersecurity. available evidence suggests that individuals exhibiting addictive patterns of internet use show reduced compliance with security protocols, increased vulnerability to social engineering, and elevated engagement in risky online behaviors, although directionality cannot be established with confidence given the predominantly cross-sectional evidence base. the present narrative review synthesizes evidence from addiction neuroscience, clinical psychology, and cybersecurity research to propose a mechanistic account of the iad-cybersecurity risk relationship. the review identifies impaired prefrontal inhibitory control as the central neurobiological mediator linking iad to cybersecurity vulnerability, mediated primarily through impulsivity and compounded by the attentional and affective characteristics that render addicted individuals susceptible to social engineering. drawing on literature spanning 2017-2026, the review also situates this account within a contemporary regulatory context, including the documented acceleration of problematic internet use during the covid-19 pandemic, australia's landmark social media minimum age legislation, and an influential 2026 civil verdict in which a u.s. jury found major platform operators liable for harms arising from addictive design. clinical, organizational, and policy implications are discussed. cyberpsychology behavior and social networking

parent–child play and media addiction in adolescence: a three-wave longitudinal study although media addiction is a recognized public health concern, the theoretical framework surrounding its longitudinal development remains relatively underdeveloped. this study addresses that gap by evaluating a developmental model that traces a path from early parent–child play at age 6 to adolescent media addiction at age 14, with executive function and peer attachment at age 10 examined as parallel mediators. we used three waves of data from a representative sample of 1,130 parent–child dyads in the panel study on korean children. early parent–child play at age 6 significantly predicted higher executive function at age 10, which subsequently predicted lower media addiction at age 14. this indirect path via executive function was statistically significant. conversely, the indirect effect through peer attachment was not significant, as peer attachment was unrelated to both early play and subsequent media addiction. the direct effect of parent–child play on adolescent media addiction was nonsignificant, demonstrating that the protective influence of early family play operates through cognitive mechanisms rather than social bonds. these findings shift the clinical focus from proximal adolescent factors to early prevention, emphasizing middle childhood as a critical therapeutic window for bolstering executive function to mitigate later media addiction risks. cyberpsychology behavior and social networking

ai-mediated mental health support: the role of attachment orientation and psychological distress. general-purpose generative ai (genai) models are increasingly serving as quasi-social agents, representing a novel form of informal ai-mediated help-seeking. this study examined associations between adult attachment orientations (experiences in close relationships-relationship structures questionnaire), psychological distress (depression anxiety stress scales-21), and the use of genai for mental health support. in a nonprobability sample of 584 israeli adult genai users, 29.3 percent reported having turned to these models at least once for emotional support, coping advice, or mental health assistance; the proportion reached 47.0 percent among those reporting severe distress. these self-reported figures reflect any such contact, from a single exchange to sustained use. hierarchical logistic regression identified distress as the strongest psychological correlate of use. younger age and female gender predicted use. attachment anxiety was associated with use, but this association did not remain significant once distress was included, a pattern consistent with the shared variance between the two constructs. attachment avoidance was negatively but nonsignificantly associated with use. findings position general-purpose genai as an accessible, low-barrier resource disproportionately used by distressed individuals. the high uptake among severely distressed users (47.0 percent) points to potential safety concerns and to a need for systematic evaluation of the safety, crisis-response quality, and clinical-displacement risks of consumer-facing ai use. cyberpsychology behavior and social networking

decent work for older adults in south korea: a social justice perspective this study used the concept mapping methodology to explore the perceptions of decent work among individuals aged 65 years and older from low socioeconomic backgrounds in south korea. nineteen participants were selected to represent a broader older population with income as the criterion. through in-depth interviews and participant engagement in sorting and rating statements, this study revealed a perceptual structure of decent work, with nine clusters organized into three dimensions : rewards, well-being, and integration. these findings extend the existing literature on decent work and the psychology of working theory, providing valuable theoretical insights and practical implications for enhancing counseling practices, informing policies, guiding education and training, and advancing theories on older adults’ work. this study underscores the importance of addressing systemic barriers and developing tailored interventions that reflect the specific needs and aspirations of older adults in the workforce. 초록 본 연구는 한국에서 낮은 사회경제적 배경을 지닌 65세 이상 고령층이 인식하는 괜찮은 일(decent work)의 의미와 구조를 탐색하기 위해 개념도 방법(concept mapping methodology)을 적용하였다. 소득 수준을 기준으로 고령층 인구를 폭넓게 대표할 수 있도록 총 19명의 연구참여자를 선정하였다. 심층 면접, 진술문 분류 및 평정 절차를 통해 분석한 결과, 괜찮은 일은 보상(rewards), 웰빙(well-being), 통합(integration)의 세 가지 차원과 이에 속한 아홉 개의 군집으로 구성된 지각적 구조인 것으로 나타났다. 이러한 결과는 괜찮은 일 및 일의 심리학 이론에 관한 기존 논의를 확장하는 동시에, 상담 실제의 개선, 정책 수립을 위한 근거 제공, 교육 및 훈련 프로그램 개발, 그리고 고령층의 노동 경험에 대한 이론적 발전에 대해 중요한 이론적·실무적 시사점을 제시한다. 나아가 본 연구는 노동시장에서 고령층이 직면한 구조적 장벽을 해소하고, 이들의 고유한 요구와 열망을 반영한 맞춤형 개입을 개발하는 것이 중요함을 시사한다. counseling psychologist
reactivating logic? age-dependent effects of intuitive debiasing training thinking & reasoning

unpacking the antecedents and consequences of resilience to socioeconomic risks: changes from mid- to late adolescence. poverty-related risks exact detrimental effects on young people's development, highlighting the need to understand the processes through which youth sustain resilience. this study examined the proximal contextual antecedents and developmental consequences of socioeconomic risk and resilience in middle (9grade) and late adolescence (12grade). using survey data from a large longitudinal study (= 738; 54% female; 42% white, 32% latino/a/x, 12% biracial or multiracial, 8% asian, and 6% black), youth were classified as above or below the 75th percentile on socioeconomic risk and psychological resilience, yielding four risk and resilience groups: a) high-risk and high-resilience, b) low-risk and high-resilience, c) high-risk and low-resilience, and d) low-risk and low-resilience groups. in middle adolescence, the school and family contexts were particularly salient for distinguishing risk and resilience groups; however, by late adolescence, the family context remained the only consistent resource differentiating resilient youth. in middle adolescence, youth who were resilient in the face of economic stress had better mental and physical health than their less resilient peers. in contrast, socioeconomic risk regardless of resilience was problematic for academic achievement. in later adolescence, only the advantages in mental health persisted for youth resilient in the face of socioeconomic risk. findings from the current study highlight potential targets in proximal contextual resources to improve supports for youth experiencing socioeconomic disadvantage. international journal of behavioral development

depression screening tools for non- and minimally speaking autistic adults: feasibility, psychometrics, and wider validity depression remains underdiagnosed in non- and minimally speaking (nms) autistic adults, despite caregiver concerns suggesting high rates of mood-related difficulties, as such this study evaluates the validity, reliability, and feasibility of three established caregiver-report depression measures (anxiety, depression, and mood scale-adams; glasgow depression scale–caregiver supplement-gds-cs; mood, interest, and pleasure questionnaire-mipq) with 160 caregivers of nms autistic adults. participants completed surveys, and a subset engaged in cognitive interviews to assess content validity and usability. psychometric analyses included confirmatory factor analyses, internal consistency estimation, and exploratory cut-off scores based on parent-reported concern about depression. results indicated that the gds-cs had the strongest support, showing acceptable model fit, fair reliability, and high caregiver acceptability. the adams also demonstrated strong psychometric properties and feasibility, with the added benefit of capturing related symptoms such as anxiety. the mipq, while designed for individuals with limited language, showed poor model fit and lower caregiver usability. findings support the use of the gds-cs and adams as promising tools for screening depression in nms autistic adults and highlight the need for further validation and tailored mental health assessment approaches for this underserved population. lay abstract some autistic people do not use speech to communicate, even when they become adults. these individuals are called minimally speaking (or nonspeaking; nms). many parents think their nms autistic adult children may be depressed, but few have a diagnosis from a doctor. one reason for this is that most ways doctors check for depression ask about feelings using spoken words. this does not work well for people who do not speak. this study asked 160 parents of minimally speaking autistic adults to fill out three surveys that may help identify depression. the surveys were the adams, the gds-cs, and the mipq. the parents answered questions about how their adult children behave, how often certain things happen, and whether they think their child is depressed. some parents also talked in interviews about how easy or hard the surveys were to understand and complete. the results showed that two of the surveys, the adams and the gds-cs, worked pretty well and were quick to fill out. parents said the gds-cs was the easiest to understand. the third survey, the mipq, was harder for parents to use and did not work as well. this study shows that it is possible to screen for depression in autistic adults who do not speak by asking caregivers the right kinds of questions. it also shows that more research is needed to make sure these tools work for everyone. doctors and caregivers can use these tools to find people who may be feeling depressed and need more help. this is an important step toward making sure all autistic adults, including those who don’t speak, get the mental health care they need. autism
deep brain stimulation for major depressive disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis nature mental health

reconstructing mental representations of block towers: a new bias for physical stability in visual working memory abstract recent studies have explored the perception of physical properties (such as mass and stability) in psychology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence (ai), and perhaps the most popular stimulus from such studies is the block tower – since such displays (of stacked rectilinear objects) evoke immediate vivid impressions of physical (in)stability. previous work has studied how people make higher-level decisions about such towers, often with explicit questions (“which way will it fall?”), and limited to those tower properties that are systematically manipulated as explicit independent variables. here, in contrast, we explored how such stimuli are spontaneously encoded into visual working memory in the first place. using a novel drag-and-drop reconstruction task in a custom three-dimensional interface, observers briefly viewed randomly generated block towers, and then simply reproduced them from memory – without ever being asked about stability, per se. by simulating both the original and reconstructed towers in a physics engine, we discovered a novel bias: observers reliably remember towers as more stable than they originally were, even when the reconstructions are otherwise accurate. this reveals for the first time how visual memory is structured (and biased) not only by how scenes are segmented into objects, but also by how those objects are physically related to each other – all without ever asking anyone anything about physics. psychonomic bulletin & review

grateful for what and whom? how gratitude list content varies and is associated with affective responses a gratitude list activity, whereby one recalls and writes down things they are grateful for, is a well-studied intervention known to confer an immediate and even prolonged boost in well-being. however, the specific content people reflect on, and how it relates to affective evaluations and the impact of the intervention, remains underexplored. using data from a global online study ( n = 19,265), we applied natural language processing to examine the content of gratitude lists, identifying 16 thematic clusters, with the most common one focused on social relationships. next, we examined and found various sociodemographic and psychological differences in people’s gratitude list content. further, mentioning themes related to family or nature was associated with greater increases in positivity following the activity. overall, our findings highlight individual differences in what people naturally think of during this popular intervention and suggest opportunities for personalized modifications to enhance adherence to and effectiveness of the intervention. personality and social psychology bulletin

state racial and lgbtq+ equality: moderators of prospective suicide risk pathways among young ethnoracially minoritized lesbian and bisexual women and nonbinary individuals. ethnoracially minoritized lgbtq+ young people demonstrate greater suicide risk than their non-hispanic white peers, yet limited research exists examining state equality protective factors that can reduce risk, especially among lesbian and bisexual women/nonbinary individuals assigned female at birth (lbwnbi). guided by a strengths-based approach and integrated theoretical model, we used an observed variable path analysis to examine moderating effects of state racial and lgbtq+ equality, and interactions between these factors and individual- and interpersonal/community-level protective factors, on prospective associations between intersectional minority stressors and entrapment, and entrapment and suicidal ideation. the analytic sample included 486 ethnoracially minoritized lbwnbi in the national queer women's mental health cohort longitudinal study (m = 22; 40% hispanic/latine, 38% black/african american, 18% asian; 51% bisexual) who completed baseline (t1), 3-month (t2), and 6-month (t3) surveys. intersectional minority stressors at t1 led to greater suicidal ideation at t3 via entrapment at t2. conjoined state racial and lgbtq+ equality moderated the relationship between t1 intersectional minority stressors and t2 entrapment to reduce t3 suicidal ideation. this effect was also moderated by individual protective factors, proving especially important for lbwnbi living in states with low equality. suicide prevention efforts with this population should involve multi-faceted, multi-sectoral policies and interventions that effect transformative change to redress historical and contemporary structural-level oppressions, injustices, and inequities. journal of research on adolescence

assessing individual differences in adult theory of mind through mental state language: human and artificial intelligence approaches. 通过心理状态语言评估成人心理理论的个体差异：人类与人工智能方法 theory of mind is central to human social behavior, yet empirical studies rely largely on biased measures with limited ecological validity. we propose and evaluate the use of mental state language as a spontaneous indicator of theory of mind expressed in social interaction. among research participants (334 undergraduate students, 63.8% non-hispanic white, 74.3% female) engaged in a dyadic cooperative task with an unfamiliar peer, mental state language demonstrated strong convergent validity with established measures of theory of mind and, when compared to established measures, superior predictive validity for interpersonal functioning. fine-tuned transformers and open-source generative large language models reliably replicated human coding of mental state language, enabling scalable assessment. these findings offer promising initial construct-validity evidence for mental state language as a measure of theory of mind, and motivate its extension to naturalistic, dynamically unfolding social interactions. assessment

representational realism is not the default position of cognitive neuroscience abstract mental representations figure prominently in cognitive neuroscience, and this prominence is often taken to imply an underlying commitment to robust representational realism: the view that representations are real neural entities bearing determinate content grounded in their physical properties. the present paper challenges this assumption on two fronts. first, i argue that robust realist approaches face principled limitations, such as overgeneralization, and struggle to accommodate the diversity and context-sensitivity of neuroscientific data. second, i claim that robust realism is neither required nor typically presupposed in scientific practice, as researchers rarely adopt such strong ontological commitments. moreover, i present an alternative position, representational pragmatism, which treats representations not as discrete entities but as idealized epistemic artefacts, namely modelling tools that enable intelligibility, guide experimentation, and support prediction. i contend that this approach is more consistent with both neuroscientific practice and empirical data. to illustrate these points, i articulate a set of widely accepted constraints on representational attribution and examine varitel semantics, a leading contemporary robust realist framework. i argue that it fails to meet these desiderata and cannot reconcile its commitments with empirical findings. this, i maintain, exemplifies a broader difficulty of robust realism: the fallacy of misplaced concreteness, whereby methodological abstractions are mistaken for literal features of neural architecture. finally, i defend representational pragmatism as a more viable and scientifically grounded stance that also fares better on representational desiderata. i conclude that if there is a “default scientific position”, it appears more pragmatist than robust realist. review of philosophy and psychology

gender and interracial relationship dissolution: evidence from a decade of roommate outcomes using a natural experiment at an elite college (1982–1991), we analyze roommate choices following random first-year assignments, during a period when the asian-student population doubled. this design allows us to test how shifting demographics affect interracial tie dissolution. focusing on white-asian dyads, we find a significant gender divide: women exhibit consistently high rates of interracial relationship dissolution regardless of population composition, whereas men's interracial ties are affected by population shifts, with tie dissolution increasing as minorities have more same-race outside options. these findings shift the study of intergroup contact from relationship formation to durability, demonstrating that opportunity structures shape interracial relationship dissolution in a setting largely free from self-selection processes that characterize most naturally occurring ties. social psychology quarterly

impact of social network ties on subjective well-being: exploring structural conditions of weak ties this study clarifies how the structural properties of social networks are associated with subjective well-being. specifically, this study defines and classifies social network ties into three types (weak, mixed, and strong) based on network transitivity and examines the differences in the impact of social network ties on individual subjective well-being among the three types. i implemented a computer simulation to estimate the effects of social network ties and analyzed data from a pro-sociality and personal network survey conducted in japan in 2024 (n = 1,000). the computer simulation and statistical analyses reveal that mixed ties (weak ties combined with strong ties) were the most effective social network ties and that weak ties were the least effective social network ties for attaining a high level of subjective well-being. this suggests that weak ties are the most effective in attaining a high level of subjective well-being only if they are connected to strong ties. if weak ties are isolated from strong ties, they may lose their positional advantage in social networks. social psychology quarterly

too useful to avoid, too uneasy to accept: cognitive dissonance among language majors in the genai era this study examined the formation and regulation of cognitive dissonance among 30 undergraduates majoring in english, chinese, japanese, thai, and vietnamese through semi-structured interviews and grounded theory analysis. the findings identified cognitive dissonance as the core category, four dissonance-generating categories—competence development disconnect, ethical-normative conflict, devaluation of language majors, and educational inertia—and one regulation-related category, dissonance regulation. a square-pyramid model was developed to explain the process from dissonance generation to regulation. the study shows that students’ genai use cannot be understood as simple acceptance or rejection, but as conflicts among beliefs, emotions, values, and behaviors around ai and language learning. it also raises concerns that early or excessive ai use may reduce opportunities for sustained practice and language competence development. this study extends the application of cognitive dissonance theory to ai-mediated language education and offers implications for language programs to strengthen ai literacy, ethical guidance, human–ai collaboration, and competence-oriented assessment. journal of intelligence

the silence in a radical field abstract this first‐person account interrogates the silence of mainstream community psychology in the face of the ongoing genocide in gaza. we confront the gap between the field's stated commitments to social justice, prevention, and liberation, and its complicity through inaction. silence is not neutrality but alignment with power, reflecting the colonial foundations and whiteness that structure mainstream psychology. drawing on the tradition of bearing witness as a critical research methodology, we came together through a conference session and developed this account through collective dialogue, iterative exchange, and transnational solidarity. organized thematically, the article asks four central questions: (1) what does mainstream community psychology's silence on palestine say about our commitments, values, and usefulness?; (2) why is palestinian resistance pathologized as deviance rather than recognized as dignity?; (3) what is the purpose of theory if not applied in moments of urgent crisis?; and (4) what will mainstream community psychology claim it stood for when genocide was broadcast in real time? we ground our critique in lived realities across west asia, africa, europe, and exile. the account is a refusal of complicity, a challenge to measure the field's worth not by rhetoric but by courage and solidarity in the struggle for liberation. american journal of community psychology

multivariate genetic analyses test for the presence of a general ‘ n ’ factor underlying neurodevelopmental conditions abstract background neurodevelopmental conditions often emerge early in life and have substantial genetic influences. there are significant genetic correlations between neurodevelopmental conditions, such as between autism spectrum disorder (autism) and attention deficit‐hyperactivity disorder (adhd), and they are listed together in diagnostic manuals. here we assess whether there is a single underlying genetic neurodevelopmental (‘ n ’) factor for neurodevelopmental conditions. methods genetic summary statistics of neurodevelopmental conditions, or their proxy traits, were used to model the genetic relationship between neurodevelopmental conditions. summary statistics contain the effect sizes of each variant's association with a neurodevelopmental condition from a genome‐wide association study. single and multiple common factor models were fitted to the data using genomic structural equation modelling. results a single common factor model did not provide a good fit for the genetic architecture of neurodevelopmental conditions. a two‐factor model fitted the data best. it was also found that the common genetic variation associated with a trait representing motor development, namely age at onset of walking, was negatively and positively associated with adhd and autism, respectively, suggesting some genetic differentiation between these two common neurodevelopmental conditions. conclusion these results provide insight into the genetic architecture of neurodevelopmental conditions and their inter‐related structure. data on measured common genetic variation, as discovered from recent genome‐wide association studies, does not support the hypothesis that all neurodevelopmental conditions fall into a single ‘ n ’ factor. jcpp advances

sound flexibly interacts with dual‐format templates to optimize visual search abstract previous studies indicate that the dual formats of templates recursively operate in tandem during visual search tasks. the guiding template with coarse features supports target localization, whereas the target template with precise features supports target identification. however, whether a sound that provides target‐consistent identity information would flexibly interact with these two templates to optimize search behavior remains unclear. across two experiments, event‐related potentials (erps) were recorded while participants searched for and identified a visual target letter (“v” or “k”). in experiment 1, visual targets were presented in isolation (v) or synchronously with a speech sound that was congruent (avcon) or incongruent (avincon) with the target; experiment 2 additionally paired the target with a sound unrelated to both potential targets and distractors (avun). behaviorally, converging findings across experiments indicated that relative to avun and v conditions, congruent sounds improved accuracy and shortened response times, whereas incongruent sounds prolonged response times. erp results revealed early cross‐modal interactions, reflected in amplitude modulations of the occipital p195 and centroparietal n270 components in the avcon and avincon conditions relative to summed unimodal erps (exp. 1); these interactions were reduced in the avun condition, in which the sound was uninformative about potential targets (exp. 2). cross‐condition multivariate pattern analysis (mvpa) showed higher target‐presence decoding accuracy in the avcon condition than in the avincon, avun, and v conditions. peak‐to‐peak improvements in the avcon–avincon and avcon–v comparisons, but not the avcon–avun comparison, were positively correlated with corresponding improvements in behavioral accuracy. these findings suggest that the interaction between sounds and the dual formats of templates is contingent on the usefulness of available information. when the guiding template is relatively efficient, task‐irrelevant sounds may generally interact with the entire visual search array. subsequently, congruent sounds selectively enhance target‐template processing, potentially contributing to improved target identification. psychophysiology

sexual distress, concerns about sex life, and successful sexual aging: an exploration in older partnered german adults although research on older adults’ sexual functioning and sexual health has increased in recent decades, there is a lack of systematic assessments of the role of sexual distress in positive sexual aging. this study examined associations between sexual distress, concerns about sex life, and positive sexual aging, and whether these associations differ by gender. data were drawn from a 2024 online survey of partnered, sexually active german adults aged 65 years and older (n = 598). positive sexual aging was assessed using the successful sexual aging scale (ssas). structural equation modeling controlling for age showed that distress about sexual functioning was strongly and negatively associated with successful sexual aging in both women and men. concerns about sex life were additionally and uniquely associated with lower ssas scores among women. findings underscore the importance of assessing sexual distress and gender-specific concerns in older adults’ sexual health care. journal of sex & marital therapy

working memory and vocabulary knowledge sustain activation of the literal meaning of metaphors during sentence comprehension abstract metaphors convey meanings beyond their literal interpretation, requiring individuals to rely on linguistic and cognitive resources beyond those used for literal language. models of metaphor comprehension propose different routes to deriving metaphorical content. the indirect-access model suggests that literal meaning is accessed first and then rejected if context demands, whereas the direct-access model argues that metaphorical content is retrieved automatically without an initial literal interpretation. however, previous research has yielded mixed findings on this issue. we examine whether individual differences in metaphor processing explain these inconsistencies. we hypothesize that individuals may differ in their ability to retrieve metaphorical content or inhibit literal meaning directly. in experiment 1, participants read sentences such as john is an early bird so he can... and were slower and less likely to select a target continuation (e.g., attend ) when it was paired with a distractor related to the literal meaning of the metaphor (e.g., fly ) compared to an unrelated distractor (e.g., cry ). this literal awakening effect was more pronounced in individuals with higher vocabulary knowledge and working memory capacity. in experiment 2, we examined whether the effect persisted when distractors were no longer grammatical in context (e.g., attend versus flying or crying ). the literal awakening effect remained but was no longer modulated by individual differences. these findings suggest that, under semantic and syntactic competition, individuals with higher vocabulary knowledge and working memory capacity may attempt to reinterpret the related distractor as an elaboration of the metaphor, indicating that activation of the literal meaning of metaphors is sustained by vocabulary knowledge and working memory capacity. memory & cognition

misinformation resistance in memory reports of one instance of a repeated event: post-warnings reduce misinformation endorsement in recognition abstract previous research shows that remembering repeated events differs from remembering single events, yet little research has examined suggestibility in adults’ memory for repeated events. in the present experiment, we investigated the effects of eyewitness misinformation and the role of a warning against misinformation in a repeated-event scenario. we examined how different types of misinformation – entirely new items versus items present in non-target instances – influence reporting. three hundred and nine participants watched four surveillance-mission videos that shared a general story structure but differed in key details. participants were later exposed to pieces of misinformation in a video narrative of someone else reporting the first mission. reporting was measured using free recall, cued recall, and recognition. we replicated the standard misinformation effect in the repeated-event context. we found that the warning reduced misinformation reporting, but the effect was present only in the recognition task. based on the source-monitoring framework, we expected it would be easier to resist external (entirely new) misinformation than misinformation consistent with what was present in non-target instances, and this was also true. the warning’s lack of efficacy may be accounted for in two ways. first, the inherent difficulty of attributing details to specific instances of repeated events may have overshadowed the potential effects of the warning. second, ours was a general warning; it might not have been strong enough to restore an adequate understanding of a memory task distorted by misinformation. memory & cognition
investigating the role of affective valence and arousal in exposure therapy for anxiety and related disorders cognitive behaviour therapy

what is the impact of coercive control on children exposed to domestic violence? moving beyond traditional frameworks focused on physical violence, the article adopts a comprehensive definition of coercive control as encompassing psychological abuse, isolation, stalking, and the systematic denial of autonomy, and argues that its effects on children are distinct and deeply harmful, often persisting long after direct exposure ends. three key mechanisms of harm are identified: (1) credible threats , which compel children and mothers to constantly modify their behavior to avoid punishment, creating a chronically stressful environment akin to “walking on eggshells”; (2) hypervigilance , a state of continuous environmental scanning that depletes cognitive resources needed for learning and healthy social development; and (3) disruption of developmental milestones , including secure attachment, self-regulation, and social competence. understudied areas require future research, including children’s recovery trajectories after separation from a coercive parent, the use of children as surveillance tools by abusers post-separation, and “litigation abuse” whereby legal systems are used to maintain control and destabilize families. the author concludes that effectively protecting children requires recognizing coercive control as a systematic erosion of autonomy and safety, not merely a series of violent incidents, and calls for research to better inform therapeutic interventions and legal policy. journal of interpersonal violence

a cycle of gendered vulnerability: understanding violence, poverty, and systemic failure among refugee women in malawi gender-based violence (gbv) is an urgent global health and social problem. gbv has implications for women’s health outcomes and causes disruption to an individual’s ecosystem, including their educational attainment, economic stability, and safety. refugee women are an underserved subpopulation of women who experience extreme vulnerability related to gbv and poor maternal health outcomes. the primary aim of the study was to gain foundational knowledge about the relationship between gender inequality and gbv in the lives of childbearing-aged refugee women in malawi, including healthcare utilization. specifically, we sought to (a) explore women’s perspectives on the gendered nature of violence, poverty, and vulnerability in the refugee camp context, (b) understand women’s experiences and perceptions of health and social services for gbv survivors, and (c) identify structural factors that facilitate or impede women’s access to justice and support. guided by the sustainable development goals (sdgs), we conducted a qualitative analysis reporting on the qualitative sub-study of a larger mixed-methods project. a total of 50 women were interviewed using focus group discussions from a refugee camp in malawi on their health, well-being, and experiences with gbv. data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. the findings revealed a cycle of gendered poverty, vulnerability, and a gendered system response. the following three subthemes were identified: (a) single motherhood and abandonment as drivers of poverty, (b) marriage as a gendered survival strategy, and (c) the constraining effect of children and caregiving. poverty is gendered, driven by abandonment, enforced through survivalist marriages, and cemented by caregiving constraints. systemic responses often replicate the very power imbalances that enable gbv, further perpetuating the cycle. these findings underscore the need for culturally appropriate policies and integrated interventions to address the intersecting social and structural factors contributing to gendered violence, poverty, and vulnerability among refugee women. journal of interpersonal violence

conflict-related sexual violence against males in ukraine—first insights on forms, perpetrator characteristics, and (non)disclosure sexual violence is a common but often neglected phenomenon of armed conflict. while conflict-related sexual violence (crsv) is often framed as affecting women and girls, increasing evidence highlights crsv against males; however, empirical data remain scarce. between november 2023 and december 2024, an online survey targeting male survivors of crsv in ukraine was distributed via social media using a convenience sampling approach. the questionnaire assessed different forms of crsv, context and perpetrators’ characteristics, (non)disclosure, and fear of anticipated stigma. descriptive statistics were computed for participants who reported at least one event of crsv; analyses of disclosure and anticipated stigma were based on the available valid data. in total, 67 participants, aged 18 to 58 years, reported multiple and often repeated forms of crsv. the most frequently reported experiences were sexual touching ( n = 52; 77.6%), forced undressing ( n = 48; 71.6%), threats of sexual violence ( n = 44; 65.7%), and rape ( n = 42; 62.7%). perpetrators were most often male soldiers, police officers, and prison staff, frequently acting in groups. more than half of the participants had not disclosed their experiences of crsv and reported anticipated stigma, including fear of blame, loss of masculinity, social exclusion, and disbelief. the study contributes to the limited empirical evidence on crsv against males in conflict settings and highlights anticipated stigma as a potential barrier to disclosure and help-seeking. although the findings are not generalizable to the wider population, they underscore the need for further research, trauma-informed survivor-centered support services, and stigma-reduction strategies. journal of interpersonal violence

post-traumatic growth and depreciation among women exposed to intimate partner violence: the predictive role of core beliefs and resilience traumatic experiences can lead to negative changes in an individual’s evaluations of themselves, others, and the world by disrupting their belief systems. the purpose of this study is to examine post-traumatic depreciation (ptd) and post-traumatic growth (ptg) in women exposed to physical violence by an intimate partner, as well as the psychological factors potentially associated with these variables. the research was conducted with 72 female participants aged 19 to 63 reached through purposeful sampling. findings indicated that psychological resilience has a strong protective effect on ptd, whereas the disruption of core beliefs is a risk factor that significantly predicts ptd. contrary to expectations, no significant relationship was found between the disruption of core beliefs or psychological resilience and ptg. this result suggests that in chronic and interpersonal traumas, the shattering of the belief system does not spontaneously lead to ptg; instead, it may contribute to ptd when the disruption remains unrepaired. these findings indicate that in clinical interventions for survivors of violence, targeting ptg alone may not be sufficient; interventions aimed at strengthening psychological resilience and repairing disrupted core beliefs play a critical role in preventing ptd. journal of interpersonal violence

men’s experiences with image-based sexual abuse in the united states: victimization contexts, emotional experiences, and perceived vulnerabilities image-based sexual abuse (ibsa) is a growing form of technology-facilitated sexual violence, with increasing prevalence across the globe and significant psychological and social consequences. this study explores the unique experiences of united states men victim-survivors of ibsa using a transcendental phenomenological approach to examine how they interpret the interpersonal contexts surrounding their victimization, the forms of abuse they experience, their emotional responses, and the factors they perceive as shaping their vulnerability. findings highlight the role of intimate partner dynamics in facilitating abuse, with victimization commonly occurring following relational conflict. participants also described blackmail and retaliatory dissemination as the primary forms of abuse and reported profound emotional consequences following their victimization. socioeconomic circumstances and social identities also emerged as perceived vulnerability factors. this study underscores the importance of addressing the gendered nature of ibsa, where men (stereotypically framed as perpetrators) are increasingly recognized as victims of this form of abuse. the results call for a reexamination of societal norms around sexual violence and the legal system's response to ibsa, emphasizing the need for more inclusive support structures and policies that account for the unique experiences of male victims. journal of interpersonal violence

patterns in mother-child and father-child mutually responsive orientation during mealtimes: correlation with martial satisfaction marital relationship and parent-child interaction have been found to be correlated. using observational data from family mealtime interactions, this study examined mother-child and father-child mutually responsive orientation (mro) among toddlers (18-24 months) during mealtime and its association with mother-reported marital satisfaction. mro refers to a positive, reciprocal, and cooperative parent–child relationship that serves as a foundation for early socialization. our final sample consisted of 71 families. latent profile analysis identified a four-class solution. class 1 reflected moderately high interaction quality for both father–child and mother–child relationships. class 2 was characterized by moderate father–child interaction quality coupled with low mother–child interaction quality. class 3 demonstrated comparatively lower father–child interaction quality and high mother–child interaction quality. finally, class 4 represented high-quality interactions for both fathers and mothers across domains. findings further indicated that families characterized by lower-quality father–child interactions alongside higher-quality mother–child interactions reported the lowest levels of maternal marital satisfaction. in contrast, when fathers demonstrated moderate or high-quality interactions with their child, mothers reported higher marital satisfaction, regardless of the quality of mother–child interactions. these results underscore the importance of father–child interaction quality in shaping mothers’ perceptions of marital satisfaction. journal of social and personal relationships

teacher responses to bullying: an examination of socially ostracized youth’s emotions and help-seeking intention using a virtual reality experiment teacher responses to bullying may shape victimized youths' emotions and help-seeking. the current study used a virtual-reality experimental paradigm of social exclusion, cyberball-vr, to examine how different types of teacher responses influence early adolescents’ help-seeking intention and emotions following social exclusion. youth participants (n = 123) ages 10-14 (61% male) were randomly assigned to a teacher response condition (i.e., active, passive, ignoring) after experiencing social exclusion. the final analytic sample included 104 participants. participants self-reported eight discrete emotions (i.e., anger, embarrassment, frustration, shame, fear, satisfaction, happiness, hope) and help-seeking intention during cyberball-vr. teacher response condition significantly moderated change in satisfaction and fear. active teacher response was associated with an increase in both satisfaction and fear. when teachers actively address bullying, such as social exclusion, victimized youth may feel more satisfied because their plight has been noticed, and yet also fearful of possible negative social consequences of teachers becoming too involved. journal of early adolescence

ecological theory in early literacy assessment: a preschool teacher-focused scale (etelas-pt). early literacy development in preschool is shaped by children's individual skills and environmental contexts, including classroom practices, family routines, peer relationships, and cultural influences. while children's engagement with literacy is embedded in daily interactions, most assessment tools remain focused on child outcomes, providing limited information about teachers' practices and their engagement with the ecological theory that supports early literacy development. based on bronfenbrenner's ecological theory, this study developed the ecological theory early literacy assessment scale (etelas-pt) to assess preschool teachers' practices and awareness related to supporting children's early literacy development within an ecological framework. scale development involved a literature review, analysis of existing early literacy assessment instruments, and teacher interviews. the items were refined through expert review and pilot testing with nine teachers. the resulting instrument was administered to 221 preschool teachers (96.8% female; 56.9% with ≥10 years of experience) in public and private institutions. psychometric analyses revealed a four-factor structure: mesosystem, exosystem, macrosystem, and chronosystem, with 25 items. factor analysis showed high sampling adequacy (kmo = 0.894) and significant sphericity (χ(300) = 3727.006,< 0.001), with the four-factor structure explaining 64.35% of the total variance. confirmatory analysis demonstrated an acceptable model fit (cmin/df = 2.241; rmsea = 0.069; srmr = 0.075; cfi = 0.909; ifi = 0.910). the scale showed high internal consistency (α = 0.923; ω = 0.932). by identifying the ecological dimensions important to both early literacy development and preschool teachers' practices and awareness, the etelas-pt provides a psychometrically supported tool that could be used for professional support as well as contextualized approaches towards early literacy practice in preschool. behavioral sciences

sex differences in aggressive traits and superior temporal cortical responses to monetary loss background: individuals vary in aggression traits. here, we investigated how individual aggression is associated with altered reward and punishment processing in the brain and the neural bases of sex differences. methods: aggression was assessed by the achenbach adult self-report. we curated the human connectome project dataset and modeled the bold signals to identify regional responses to reward and punishment blocks in the gambling task (n = 981, 473 men) as well as responses to the identification of negative emotional face in a target-matching task (n = 885, 436 men). whole-brain statistical significance was assessed at the voxel-level p < 0.001 (uncorrected) with cluster-level family-wise error (fwe) correction at p < 0.05. for regional responses identified in men or women alone, we conducted slope tests to examine the sex differences in their relationships with individual aggression. results: whole-brain regression showed higher activation of the left superior temporal gyrus (stg) during gambling loss in men. we extracted the left stg response to reward versus baseline (stg-win β) and to loss versus baseline (stg-loss β), where β is the glm contrast estimate. left stg-loss β was significantly correlated with aggression score in men but not in women, and a slope test confirmed the sex difference (z = 3.54, p < 0.001). stg-loss β but not stg-win β was significantly correlated with aggression score in men, and a slope test confirmed the specificity of this valence-related correlation (z = 3.66, p < 0.001). further, the correlations of stg-loss β and of stg response to negative emotional faces versus shapes with aggression score differed in men (z = 2.70, p = 0.007). conclusions: stg response to loss represents a neural correlate of aggression in men but not in women. the stg-loss response did not reflect a broader relationship between aggression and negative emotion. behavioral sciences

dark empaths and intimate partner violence: a latent profile analysis of dark tetrad traits and empathy dimensions in face-to-face and cyber violence perpetration. intimate partner violence (ipv) has been consistently linked to dark tetrad traits (narcissism, machiavellianism, psychopathy, and sadism), typically associated with reduced empathy. however, cognitive empathy may be used instrumentally rather than protectively, giving rise to a "dark empath" profile-elevated dark traits alongside preserved empathetic mechanisms-which remains understudied in ipv perpetration. the present study used latent profile analysis to identify personality profiles based on dark tetrad traits and empathy and examined differences in face-to-face and cyber ipv perpetration. participants (= 324; 70.4% women; 82.1% based in spain) completed measures of the dark tetrad, empathy, and face-to-face and cyber ipv perpetration. four profiles emerged: empathic non-dark, typical, dark cognitive empath, and dark non-empathic. the dark non-empathic profile showed the clearest elevations in face-to-face physical and psychological violence. for cyber monitoring/control, the dark cognitive empath profile showed the highest estimated score and was significantly higher than the empathic non-dark and typical profiles, but did not differ significantly from the dark non-empathic profile. these findings provide preliminary evidence that preserved cognitive empathy alongside elevated dark traits may be associated with elevated cyber monitoring/control, although this pattern was not unique to the dark cognitive empath profile. the findings further suggest that cognitive and affective empathy should be distinguished when examining ipv perpetration. behavioral sciences

social media exposure and helping intentions toward stray animals: a moderated mediation model of empathy and responsibility attribution abstract the global stray animal population presents a pressing challenge for animal welfare, public health, and social governance. social media has become a primary context in which individuals encounter animal‐related content, yet the psychological mechanisms linking such exposure to helping intentions remain underexplored. drawing on the empathy‐altruism hypothesis and attribution theory, this study examined whether animal empathy mediates the association between social media exposure and helping intentions toward stray animals, and whether responsibility attribution moderates this indirect pathway. two new scales—the social media exposure scale and the stray animal helping intentions scale—were developed and validated in a pilot study ( n = 280). the main study surveyed 744 young chinese adults ( m age = 20.18 years, primarily college students) using measures of social media exposure, animal empathy, responsibility attribution, and helping intentions. results indicated that social media exposure was positively associated with helping intentions, both directly and indirectly through animal empathy. responsibility attribution moderated the social media exposure–empathy link, such that the positive association was stronger among individuals with lower levels of responsibility attribution. these findings suggest that emotionally evocative, anthropomorphized social media content may serve as a low‐cost tool to promote engagement in stray animal welfare among young adults, particularly among individuals who do not strongly attribute the plight of stray animals to human action. journal of applied social psychology
from stressful life events to depressive symptoms: the roles of negative automatic thoughts and positive-attentional discrepancy in college students cognitive therapy and research

optimizing naloxone education abstract: message sensation is commonly used in educational messaging to capture attention, yet its impact on cognitive learning appears paradoxical. drawing on the activation model of information exposure and the limited capacity model of motivated mediated message processing, this study examines how message sensation influences memory and knowledge improvement. an in-person 2 (death imagery: absent vs. present) × 2 (sound effects: absent vs. present) × 2 (animation: talking-head vs. action) between-subjects experiment was conducted among 603 us adults. path modeling revealed that the need for activation moderated the effects of perceived message sensation on visual encoding and retrieval: as this need decreased, the association between perceived message sensation and memory accuracy (visual encoding and retrieval) shifted from positive to negative. these findings advance media psychology by showing how message features and individual traits interact to shape learning in high-stakes public health contexts. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

time matters: temporal concepts in developmental science developmental science typically emphasizes two key dimensions of data: variables and persons. the third dimension – time – has received comparatively less attention. this article highlights the critical role of timing in developmental research and encourages to utilize known dynamic concepts of development in research questions more often, such as the life stage principle, the phase transition perspective, and dynamic concepts derived from puberty research. the life stage perspective emphasizes how age-graded transitions and social timing shape development. the phase transition perspective focuses on discrete shifts or life changes that can influence mechanisms of individual functioning. the pubertal timing perspective provides concepts that help capturing variability in the onset and progression of developmental changes. to illustrate the utility of these perspectives, i present empirical evidence primarily drawn from acculturation research. this field is particularly informative for understanding dynamic developmental processes because it highlights the co-action and interaction between developmental and acculturation-related change, particularly among immigrant and minoritized youth. adding timing as a central analytic dimension of analysis and practice promises to improve intervention designs, can enhance predictions of adaptation, and supports positive developmental trajectories across diverse contexts. european journal of developmental psychology

intergroup contact, acculturation, behavioural tendencies and collective action in newly arriving and established immigrants abstract two preregistered studies, longitudinal study 1 with african immigrants in italy ( n = 253) and cross‐sectional study 2 with second‐generation vietnamese in czechia ( n = 311), investigated whether immigrants' intergroup contact (positive vs. negative) with members of the host society associates with immigrants' acculturation preferences (original culture maintenance vs. host culture adoption) and relevant intergroup outcomes (behavioural tendencies towards host society members and support for collective action on immigrants' behalf). in both studies, positive contact with host society members was associated with more positive behavioural tendencies towards them. in the newly arriving immigrants (study 1), positive intergroup contact further predicted lower preference for immigrants' original culture maintenance, whereas negative contact predicted higher preference for original culture maintenance, intention to engage in collective action and, unexpectedly, immigrants' preference for host culture adoption. in the established immigrants (study 2), positive intergroup contact was not only associated with positive behavioural tendencies to members of the host society but also with immigrants' preference for host culture adoption, whereas negative contact was associated with preference for original culture maintenance and collective action. overall, positive and negative intergroup contact with members of receiving societies is key for immigrants at all stages of their adaptation, while other factors may depend on the particular stage. trial registration: the authors have pre‐registered this research with an analysis plan prior to conducting the research at: https://osf.io/36unt/ journal of community & applied social psychology

what autobiographical memory researchers might learn from literary autobiographers: the cases of jean-jacques rousseau and elias canetti in recent years, several psychologists have emphasised the importance that literary autobiographies have for a better understanding of memory phenomena. however, their arguments were limited to a general recognition of the potential role played by these works taken as a whole. in the present article, i briefly explore the autobiographies of two great men of letters – that is, the writer and philosopher jean-jacques rousseau and the nobel prize in literature winner elias canetti – from an autobiographical memory researcher’s point of view. based on the analysis of a handful of excerpts from their works, i argue that literary autobiographies are useful tools for investigating the metacognitive knowledge that autobiographers gain about their memory, while providing ground for indirect testing of scientific findings that contemporary psychologists have acquired about autobiographical memory. in the conclusions, i provide some tentative suggestions to future researchers who wish to delve into the empirical study of literary autobiographies. memory studies

towards a memory justice: statues as epistemic battlegrounds this article proposes an analysis of recent statue toppling events and their debates through the lens of epistemic injustice, against a background of theories and modes of cultural memory, in application to two case studies, one in the united kingdom, and one in france. through an analysis of the events surrounding the toppling of the edward colston statue in bristol, uk, and the defacing, but ultimate non-removal of the jean-baptiste colbert statue in paris, france, against a backdrop of their respective nations’ heritage policies, the work will assess the extent to which the exploration of the epistemic battlegrounds of statues can be used to aim towards a memory justice. memory studies

intergenerational trauma ‘in reverse’: a critique of the modes of circulation of combatants’ memories in colombia this article rethinks intergenerational trauma through the problem of directionality and the social forms through which war memories circulate. scholarship on intergenerational trauma has often relied on a descendant, family- and blood-based model in which traumatic content travels vertically from older ‘carriers’ to younger ‘recipients’. drawing on colombian post-conflict materials on ex-combatants’ family ties – especially mothers’ experiences around recruitment, disappearance, reunion, stigma and responsibility, as well as adoptive and extended kin configurations shaped by war – this article argues that traumatic memory frequently circulates relationally and multidirectionally, including ascendant trajectories (from children to parents) and transfilial trajectories (beyond consanguinity and nuclear kin). conceptually, the article shifts the analytic focus from transmission as inheritance/succession to circulation as role-based, mediated and politically contested. it further situates intergenerational trauma within a broader ecology of traumatic circulation by clarifying its relationship to secondary and vicarious traumatisation, and by foregrounding the work of silence, secrecy and affective responsibility in shaping what can and cannot be remembered. the article concludes by proposing a vocabulary for analysing war memory beyond unidirectional descent, with implications for memory research in other post-violence settings. memory studies

memory, ideology and power: towards a materialist framework this article critically interrogates the theoretical foundations of memory studies, foregrounding the field’s long-standing neglect of marxist ideology theory and the consequences of this omission. while constructivist and postmodernist paradigms have shaped memory studies by emphasising subjectivity, narrativity and epistemological plurality, this article argues that these approaches have frequently attenuated materialist critique and obscured the structuring role of institutions, power and hegemonic interests in the production of collective memory. by re-examining foundational figures – above all maurice halbwachs – and by engaging critically with the theoretical frameworks of jan and aleida assmann, astrid erll and their successors, the study exposes the idealist assumptions that underpin dominant cultural memory discourse and highlights the systematic misreadings through which its depoliticised canon has been consolidated. it contends that a renewed engagement with ideology critique can recover the material, institutional and political dimensions of how memory is produced, contested and mobilised within specific socio-economic formations. in doing so, the article offers a substantive intervention into memory studies, advocating for a historically grounded, politically engaged materialist framework capable of reinvigorating critical analysis within the field. memory studies

the effects of correlated color temperature on risky decision-making in fatigued individuals: an event-related potential study objective this study investigated the effects of correlated color temperature (cct) on risky decision-making in fatigued individuals and the potential neural mechanisms underlying these effects. background underground facilities (ugfs) are increasingly utilized as military shelters, but the environmental stressors within them can easily lead to mental fatigue among commanders. the blue component within polychromatic white light, as indexed by cct, has been shown to enhance alertness and cognition through non-visual pathways mediated by intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (iprgcs). however, it remains unclear whether cct can benefit risky decision-making in fatigued individuals during the day. method we examined the effects of varying ccts (4000 k, 6500 k, 8500 k, 12,000 k) on fatigued individuals using a within-subjects design ( n = 21) and assessed subjective alertness and mood, behavioral performance in attention and risky decision-making, and event-related potentials (erp), including feedback-related negativity (frn) and the p300 component. results the results showed that 12,000 k led to more favorable decisions, reflected by a lower risk ratio, more cash-outs, and higher revenue. erp analyses revealed larger frn and p300 amplitudes under 12,000 k, indicating that higher cct enhanced cognitive control and promoted more conservative decision-making, enabling beneficial feedback-based decisions even under fatigue. conclusion blue-enriched white light improves alertness, mood, and decision-making in fatigued individuals, promoting gain-maximizing and risk-minimizing decisions. application the current findings demonstrate that cct may serve as a key parameter for light-based interventions aimed at alleviating fatigue in risky decision-making in ugfs. human factors

state authenticity and interpersonal dominance and affiliation in daily life self-determination theory (sdt) suggests that state authenticity occurs in social interactions conducive to autonomy and affiliation. however, few studies have investigated associations between state authenticity and interpersonal context. using methods from contemporary integrative interpersonal theory, we investigated state authenticity during social interactions as rated on smartphone surveys by a large community sample of adults (n = 493; 21,299 observations). results from multilevel structural equation models showed that higher state authenticity was associated with higher ratings of one’s own dominance, affiliation, and positive affect, and lower negative affect. also, higher state authenticity was associated with higher ratings of others’ affiliation and positive affect, lower dominance and negative affect, and higher interpersonal complementarity. associations between authenticity and interpersonal characteristics held when controlling for affect. results support sdt that state authenticity is associated with social situations in which the individual’s agency and affiliation are complemented by others’ submissive and affiliative behavior. self and identity
emergent stigma: the collateral damage that ‘karens’ cause to people named karen self and identity

psychological capital and our mental health crisis critics both inside and beyond the academy have denounced the growing spread of “therapy speak” and self-diagnosis, especially over online platforms. this discourse has been connected in unclear ways to a widely perceived mental health crisis in different ways. for some, this talk is an accurate index of worsening mental health, while others contend this vocabulary is an engine driving it. this article turns to the sociologist pierre bourdieu’s ideas about the multiple forms of capital to make social, cultural, and historical sense of this phenomenon. building on bourdieu’s reflexive approach to sociology, a redefined understanding of “psychological capital” is proposed. this is contrasted with the existing definition as well as social science theories of human, social, cultural, and symbolic capital. psychological capital is more than a set of traits or social-cognitive skills an individual possesses. it is a form of acquired knowledge about self and others as well as a way of relating to them. psychological capital can be readily exchanged for other goods in contemporary culture, bestowing considerable value. the article outlines some of the reasons individuals invest in their psychological capital at this historical juncture, as well as describing some of the personal and social costs of accumulating this form of wealth as self-worth. theory & psychology

association of sarcopenia with global, motor, cognitive, and swallowing function prognosis in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta‐analysis abstract objective sarcopenia has been demonstrated to correlate with the prognosis of stroke. this study aimed to systematically evaluate the impact of sarcopenia on global, motor, cognitive, and swallowing function outcomes in stroke patients. methods relevant studies investigating the association between sarcopenia and multidimensional prognostic outcomes in stroke were retrieved from the pubmed, embase, web of science, cochrane library, and scopus databases. the primary outcome was the risk of poor global functional prognosis assessed by the modified rankin scale (mrs). secondary outcomes included motor function scores (functional independence measure‐motor, fim‐motor), cognitive function scores, and the risk of swallowing dysfunction. results a total of 36 cohort studies were finally included. pooled results indicated that stroke patients with comorbid sarcopenia faced a notably elevated risk of poor global functional prognosis (mrs, or = 2.43, 95% ci: 1.95 to 3.03, p < 0.001). the motor function scores (fim‐motor, smd = −0.94, 95% ci: −1.11 to −0.77, p < 0.001) and cognitive function scores (fim‐cognition or montreal cognitive assessment, smd = −0.95, 95% ci: −1.22 to −0.69, p < 0.001) in the sarcopenia group were significantly lower than those in the non‐sarcopenia group, while the risk of swallowing dysfunction showed a notable but non‐significant elevation (endotracheal intubation or functional oral intake scale, or = 1.45, 95% ci: 0.94 to 2.25, p = 0.09). subgroup analyses indicated that the patient populations, cut‐off value of mrs, follow‐up duration, stroke type, and diagnostic criteria for sarcopenia were the main sources of heterogeneity. sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results. egger's test suggested the presence of publication bias, but the conclusions remained valid after correction using the trim‐and‐fill method. conclusion sarcopenia is an important risk factor for poor global, motor, cognitive, and swallowing function prognosis in stroke patients. in clinical practice, sarcopenia screening should be incorporated into the routine assessment of stroke patients, and individualized interventions should be promptly implemented for high‐risk populations to improve long‐term prognosis. brain and behavior

the c‐reactive protein–triglyceride–glucose index and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke patients following endovascular thrombectomy abstract background and purpose the c‐reactive protein–triglyceride–glucose index (cti), capturing insulin resistance (ir) and systemic inflammation, is related to stroke prognosis in general, but has not yet been studied with respect to functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (evt). methods a retrospective analysis was carried out on individuals with acute ischemic stroke (ais) experiencing evt (september 2018–december 2024). cti is measured as: 0.412 × ln (c‐reactive protein) (mg/l) + ln [fasting triglyceride (mg/dl) × fasting glucose (mg/dl)]/2. the endpoint was unfavorable functional outcomes, characterized by a modified rankin scale (mrs) score of 3–6 at 90‐day follow‐up. restricted cubic splines (rcs) and logistic regression (lr) analysis were utilized to estimate the link between the cti and clinical outcomes. results among 813 patients, a high cti level was significantly correlated with unfavorable functional outcome ( p < 0.05). compared with patients in the lowest quartile (q1) of cti, those in the highest cti quartile (q4) demonstrated an increased likelihood of unfavorable outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aor] of 2.04, 95% confidence interval (95% ci) of 1.17–3.54). rcs modeling, after adjustment for significant variables identified in the univariate analysis, confirmed that there was no nonlinear connection between cti levels and the probability of unfavorable functional recovery. stratified analysis indicated that these associations were more significant among elderly and non‐smoking patients. conclusion the cti is an independent indicator of functional outcomes in individuals with ais undergoing evt, underlining its potential clinical value as a readily accessible marker for risk stratification and individualized prognostic assessment. brain and behavior

comparing demographic and clinical features of obstructive sleep apnea patients with and without sleepiness: a cross‐sectional study abstract background excessive daytime sleepiness (eds) is a common but variable symptom in obstructive sleep apnea (osa), with unclear associations with disease severity and clinical features. this study aimed to compare demographic and clinical characteristics of osa patients with and without eds in an iranian population. methods in this cross‐sectional study, 117 patients aged 18–65 years with polysomnography‐confirmed osa were recruited at rasoul akram hospital, tehran, iran, from april 2022 to march 2023. eds was assessed using the epworth sleepiness scale (ess ≥ 10). data on demographics, anthropometric measures, clinical variables (e.g., ahi), and medical history were collected. statistical analyses included spearman correlations, t‐tests, mann‐whitney u tests, and chi‐square tests. results of 117 patients (63.2% male, mean age 38.18 ± 2.43 years), 42.7% had eds. no significant correlation was found between ahi and ess ( ρ = 0.121, p = 0.194), nor differences in osa severity (mild, moderate, severe) between sleepy and non‐sleepy groups ( p = 0.998). ahi correlated with age, weight, bmi, neck, and waist circumference ( p < 0.05); ess correlated with height, weight, and neck circumference ( p < 0.05). head/neck disease or injury was associated with the absence of eds ( p = 0.014), with a trend linking opioid use to eds ( p = 0.082). conclusions eds in osa patients is not strongly tied to ahi but is associated with specific anthropometric features. the novel head/neck disease finding suggests neurological influences on eds. these results advocate for phenotype‐specific osa management in middle eastern populations brain and behavior
