health and environmental goals and behaviors: parallel and facilitating effects introduction: the concept of behavioral eco-wellness highlights behaviors that simultaneously influence personal health and environmental sustainability, including those relevant to the climate crisis. this study examined health- and environment-related goals and behaviors jointly, addressing the following questions: how important are health and environmental goals? how are these goals associated? how do they associate with behaviors that serve either one or both goals? and how do perceived inter-goal facilitation relations relate to these behaviors? methods: a sample of 228 participants completed an online questionnaire assessing the importance of health and environmental goals, perceived inter-goal relations, engagement in and expected benefits of four behaviors: reducing red meat consumption and preferring walking or biking over driving, both benefiting health and the environment, and attending recommended health checkups and recycling plastic bottles, which primarily benefit health or the environment, respectively. results: health goals were rated as significantly more important than environmental goals, and the two were positively correlated. the behavior most highly engaged in was attending recommended health checkups, perceived as highly beneficial for health, whereas reducing red meat consumption, perceived as low in benefits for both domains, was least engaged in. goal importance correlated with single-goal behaviors, whereas behaviors serving both goals showed only weak associations with either goal. perceived inter-goal facilitation explained additional variance in most behaviors beyond the contributions of each goal's importance. discussion: health and environmental goals, independently and jointly, help explain relevant behaviors. goal-behavior relationships differed across behaviors and their perceived benefits. health psychology and behavioral medicine

longitudinal associations between resilience and depressive symptoms during high school transition abstract in this study, the trajectories of depressive symptoms and the role of resilience were examined during the transition to high school. a five‐wave longitudinal survey, with 1‐month intervals, was conducted during the first semester of grade 10 among 639 chinese students (m age = 15.88; sd = 0.63; 52.2% females) from four high schools. latent growth modelling was employed to analyse the data. results indicated that a quadratic growth model adequately fit the data, showing a quadratic trajectory characterised by an initial rapid increase in depressive symptoms followed by gradual deceleration. sex significantly predicted initial symptom levels, with females reporting higher symptoms than males, but did not predict rates of change. higher resilience was associated with lower initial depressive symptoms and a decelerated trajectory over time. these findings suggest that resilience could be a valuable target for depressive symptom prevention and intervention programmes during the transition to high school. international journal of psychology

preference assessment and reinforcer effectiveness in domestic cats abstract understanding domestic cat ( felis catus ) preferences is important for identifying effective reinforcers that can support training, enrichment, and welfare. we assessed preference across three stimulus categories (food, toys, and social interaction) using free‐operant assessments with four adult cats in familiar home environments. the primary dependent measure was duration of quadrant engagement with concurrently available stimuli. within‐category assessments evaluated preference among multiple stimuli within each category to identify the most preferred item, and between‐category assessments presented the highest ranked stimuli from each category concurrently to evaluate cross‐category preference. a single‐operant reinforcer assessment evaluated whether the most and least preferred stimuli identified in the between‐category assessment differentially maintained operant responding, measured as a nose‐poke response to access the target stimulus. results showed that three of four cats responded at higher levels when the most preferred stimulus was available relative to the least preferred stimulus. this study is the first to combine within‐ and between‐category free‐operant preference assessments with a direct evaluation of reinforcer effectiveness in domestic cats using procedures that are feasible for home and applied settings, including shelters. these findings support the utility of systematic preference assessments for identifying candidate reinforcers in domestic cats. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

examining associations between low mmpi-3 disconstraint scale scores and facets of obsessive-compulsive personality. 考察低mmpi-3去抑制量表得分与强迫型人格各 facet 的关联 the personality psychopathology five (psy-5) traitis a personality dimension associated with behavioral control. conceptualizations of this construct posit under-controlled, antisocial personality and over-controlled, obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (ocpd) features to manifest at its high and low poles, respectively. robust empirical support has been reported for the posited high-end manifestations of this trait, as measured across versions of the minnesota multiphasic personality inventory (mmpi) by the disconstraint (disc) scale. empirical findings related to low-end manifestations of disc scores have been inconsistent across studies that have relied on broadband ocpd-related measures. the current study examined associations between mmpi-3 disc scores and narrowband ocpd-related constructs measured by the five-factor obsessive-compulsive inventory (ffoci) in a sample of 300 university students (125 men, 167 women, 8 another gender; aged 18-53 years [ = 19.94, = 4.40]). results of zero-order correlation and locally weighted regression smoothing (lwrs) analyses indicated that several ocpd features are associated with low mmpi-3 disc scores (but not all). risk aversion, ruminative deliberation, and punctiliousness emerged as the primary relevant (negative) correlates, with perfectionism, workaholism, and doggedness yielding somewhat weaker associations with low disc scores. theoretical and practical implications pertaining to the disconstraint construct and mmpi-3 disc scale are discussed. journal of personality assessment

motivational underpinnings of honor ideology: prevention focus, honor endorsement, and honor-based system justification / fundamentos motivacionales de la ideología del honor: enfoque en la prevención, defensa de los códigos de honor y justificación del sistema basado en el honor honor ideologies are sustained by gendered cultural systems, yet their motivational underpinnings remain understudied. drawing on regulatory focus theory (crowe & higgins, 1997) and system justification theory (jost & banaji, 1994), this study examined (1) whether prevention-focused self-regulation is associated with honor endorsement and honor-based system justification in türkiye, an honor culture context, and (2) whether these associations vary by gender. participants were 461 undergraduate students (256 women, 205 men; m age = 20.45, sd = 1.73). results indicated that prevention focus was positively associated with both honor endorsement and honor-based system justification. although men justified the honor system and endorsed honor beliefs more, gender did not moderate the association between prevention focus and honor-related beliefs. mediation analyses showed that honor endorsement statistically accounted for the association between prevention focus and honor-based system justification, although alternative ordering models also yielded significant indirect effects. findings highlighted prevention-focused self-regulation as a motivational correlate of both internalization and legitimization of honor norms, along with the conceptual proximity of honor-related constructs. international journal of social psychology
eyewitness misinformation susceptibility across data collection contexts: comparing laboratory, online, and prolific participant responses journal of cognitive psychology
non-consensual distribution of intimate images: the influence of perpetrator motivation on judgments journal of forensic psychology research and practice
severe chronic pain is associated with higher anxiety and depressive symptom burden and sleep disturbance in pakistani patients discover psychology

“one can have all sorts of good intentions but sometimes in everyday life, it turns out differently”: change agreements in couples' everyday lives abstract online couple interventions are increasingly used to support couples experiencing relationship distress. however, little is known about how couples integrate intervention elements into their everyday lives. this longitudinal qualitative study examined how distressed parenting couples integrate change agreements developed in the online ourrelationship program. six couples (12 participants) were included in the study. data consisted of one coach session, as well as two rounds of individual interviews conducted 3–6 weeks and 6–7 months after program completion. using longitudinal interpretative phenomenological analysis, we identified three main ways couples experienced, interpreted, and used the change agreements: (1) as instrumental contracts, (2) as expressions of mutual understanding, and (3) as making relational responsibility visible, including potential gendered asymmetries. findings suggest that change agreements do not transfer directly into couples' everyday lives and that consequences evolve over time. implications for practitioners, intervention design, and theories of relational change are discussed. journal of marital and family therapy

from shouting to calm conversations: a qualitative study of family communication transformation through a culturally adapted multiple family group therapy in hiv-affected families in ghana. family communication dysfunction significantly impacts hiv medication adherence and mental health outcomes among adolescents in sub-saharan africa, yet evidence-based family interventions remain scarce in resource-limited settings. this qualitative descriptive study examined family communication transformation following culturally adapted multiple family group therapy (mfgt) for adolescents living with hiv and their families in rural ghana. focus group discussions were conducted with 20 caregivers and 19 adolescents who completed the 11-session intervention. all core therapeutic content was delivered across sessions 1 through 10; the 11th session comprised a graduation ceremony and sustainability planning. reflexive thematic analysis revealed four major themes: preintervention dysfunction (public shaming, adolescent defiance, spousal teknonymy, extended family triangulation); mfgt-facilitated skills (tone modulation, privacy-preserving correction, active listening); postintervention transformation (caregiver behavioral consolidation, adolescent reciprocal adaptation, spousal reconnection); and sustaining mechanisms (observational learning, metacognitive awareness, positive reinforcement, peer accountability). communication improvements occurred bidirectionally, with caregiver changes catalyzing adolescent adaptations. findings are theoretically interpreted through family systems theory, communication accommodation theory, social cognitive theory, and self-determination theory. culturally adapted mfgt successfully transformed communication patterns while preserving traditional authority structures, suggesting potential for integration within hiv care systems in resource-limited settings. journal of marital and family therapy

self-assessed memory problems in everyday life in relation to assessed cognitive domains in neuropsychological tests: a longitudinal study of adult patients with acquired brain injury few long-term studies exist regarding memory problems following acquired brain injury and a minimal amount is known regarding the relationship between self-reported memory difficulties and objective neuropsychological measures. this knowledge gap may affect planning of effective rehabilitation interventions. self-reported memory problems in everyday life and performance on neuropsychological tests were examined in a longitudinal study. thirty-nine patients with acquired brain injury were recruited from a rehabilitation unit and assessed at one, two, and ten years post-injury using everyday memory questionnaire (emq-20). associations between subjective and objective measures were examined. at the one-year follow-up, self-reported distress related to memory problems were found to be significantly correlated with visual learning and memory. at the two-year follow-up, self-reported memory problems were significantly correlated with auditory-verbal learning and memory. at the ten-year follow-up, self-reported distress related to memory problems were found to be significantly correlated with auditory-verbal learning and memory. findings suggest that subjective experiences of memory problems and related distress may be associated with specific cognitive abilities. auditory-verbal abilities are essential for understanding and processing communication in social contexts and may be associated with distress. findings highlight the potential of combining subjective and objective assessments of cognitive functioning and planning rehabilitation interventions. applied neuropsychology-adult

test-retest reliability and practice effects across measures of attention in college-aged adults. attention is central to neuropsychological assessment, yet the psychometric properties, particularly practice effects and test-retest reliability are less well characterized for common attention measures compared to other domains. seventy-three undergraduate psychology students (86.5% female;age = 19.6) completed a two-session battery approximately two weeks apart, including the paced auditory serial addition test (pasat), auditory consonant trigrams (act), digit span (forward, backward, sequencing, and total score), and conners' continuous performance test-3 (cpt-3). reliability was excellent for pasat ( = .86), act ( = .78), digit span total ( = .82), and cpt-commissions ( = .77). reliability was good for digit span forward ( = .72), digit span backward ( = .71), cpt d' ( = .67), cpt-omissions ( = .60), cpt hrt ( = .72), and cpt isi ( = .68). fair reliability was observed for digit span sequencing ( = .53), cpt-perseverations ( = .46), and cpt hrt sd ( = .59). practice effects were largest for pasat ( = .95), medium for digit span total ( = .55), and small-to-medium for most remaining indices ( = .15-.47), with minimal change for digit span sequencing ( = .08). findings support cautious interpretation of short-interval improvement and suggest that act and select cpt-3 indices may be more suitable for brief retest intervals. applied neuropsychology-adult

effects of language of test administration as a predictor of progression to alzheimer's disease in bilingual hispanic americans: a pilot study. this pilot study investigated whether language of test administration (english versus spanish) influences story recall sensitivity for early detection of alzheimer's disease (ad) in hispanic americans. participants included 18 progressors who were initially cognitively normal or had mild cognitive impairment but later diagnosed with ad, and 27 healthy controls who were cognitively stable for at least two years. during annual neuropsychological evaluations, participants completed the logical memory test in english or spanish. immediate and delayed recall for story a were assessed via whole story, primacy, and recency scores. whole story immediate recall provided the highest diagnostic sensitivity. planned language-specific ancova and roc curves revealed descriptive patterns of higher diagnostic sensitivity for participants tested in english than for those tested in spanish, although the language × group interaction was not statistically significant, likely due to limited sample size. while all participants exhibited primacy and recency effects during immediate recall, the primacy effect was absent in delayed recall. these findings provide preliminary evidence that while story recall predicts ad risk in spanish-english bilingual hispanic older adults, its diagnostic sensitivity is moderated by administration language. this highlights the need for large-scale validation to ensure equitable and accurate cognitive assessment in diverse populations. applied neuropsychology-adult

it knows my emotions better than i do: digital phenotyping and the contest over symptom interpretation. digital phenotyping is increasingly presented as a means of detecting mental distress through smartphones, wearables, and other sensor-rich personal devices. in this article, we argue that the central philosophical and clinical issue raised by digital phenotyping extends beyond predictive accuracy to interpretive authority, which concerns who gets to name what a feeling, behavioral pattern, or physiological fluctuation means. psychiatry has always involved uncertainty, proxy reasoning, and the negotiation of testimony, but digital phenotyping intensifies these dynamics by translating lived states into behavioral and physiological signals that are then modeled as indicators of psychopathology. this translation promises earlier detection and more continuous monitoring, yet it also risks displacing first-person understanding, narrowing the available interpretive vocabulary, and recoding distress through pattern recognition in ways that can obscure meaning. drawing on work in digital phenotyping, philosophy of technology, phenomenological psychopathology, and epistemic injustice, we develop a theoretical account of how digital systems may compete with patients and clinicians for the right to interpret symptoms. we show that the most consequential conflicts concern credibility, categories, temporality, and subject formation. the result is a new diagnostic tool embedded in a new social arrangement of knowledge in which persons may come to mistrust their own experience unless it is confirmed by data. we conclude by proposing a dialogical and clinically modest model for digital mental health, one that treats algorithmic outputs as revisable prompts within a larger interpretive practice while preserving space for human interpretation. integrative psychological and behavioral science
do you ever get tired of being wrong? the unique impact of feedback on subjective experiences of effort affective science

block by block to success: teaching subtraction with regrouping to high school students with intellectual disabilities through a manipulative‐supported direct instruction package abstract this study examined the effectiveness of the manipulative‐supported direct instruction package for teaching three‐digit subtraction with regrouping to high school students with intellectual disabilities. in addition to examining acquisition, the study evaluated whether accurate responding occurred after the removal of the manipulatives, whether performance was maintained over extended follow‐up intervals, whether responding was generalized to computer‐presented subtraction problems, and teachers' evaluations of the intervention's goals, procedures, and outcomes. this study employed a multiple‐probe design across participants. the current study included four high school students, aged 15–17 years, diagnosed with mild intellectual disabilities and enrolled in a special education vocational school. findings indicated that three participants acquired the target behavior, achieving 80% or higher accuracy, maintained it for 4–12 weeks after instruction, and generalized it to computer‐based tasks without manipulatives. teachers provided positive feedback on the study's purpose, the acceptability of the intervention, and the significance of the results. the study contributes to the limited research on high school students and supports the integration of effective instructional practices into real‐world classrooms. implications for future research include exploring the combined use of physical and virtual manipulatives, broader measures of generalization, and contextual influences on learning outcomes. behavioral interventions

no evidence for rational adaptation during verb-argument processing in aphasia rational adaptation (ra) theories argue that people differ in how heavily they rely on knowledge about language versus event likelihood when they understand sentences depending on which type of knowledge is more reliable for them. findings from multiple paradigms hint that, in language tasks, people with aphasia (pwa) rely more on world knowledge than neurologically healthy controls do. we tested rational adaptation theories in pwa using a visual world eye-tracking study of sentence comprehension. both pwa and healthy controls showed similarly strong influences of world knowledge and verb constraints, with a slight delay in pwa, contrary to predictions of ra theories. additionally, pwa showed more interference from a semantically-related distractor. these findings together do not provide clear evidence in favour of ra theories' predictions, but are consistent with models suggesting that impaired control mechanisms may play a role in language processing deficits in aphasia. cognitive neuropsychology

religiosity, spirituality, and cardiovascular responses to acute psychological stress objective: religiosity and spirituality have both been associated with cardiovascular reactivity to acute psychological stress; however, findings across studies have been inconsistent, and it remains unclear whether these associations are distinct from one another. this study examined the independent relationships of religiosity and spirituality with cardiovascular responses to stress.
methods and measures: a sample of 221 healthy young adults who completed psychometric measures of religious identification and daily spiritual experiences, before undergoing a standardised stress-testing protocol. systolic, diastolic blood pressure (sbp, dbp) and heart rate (hr) were monitored throughout. hierarchical regressions analyses were conducted to examine association between religiosity, spirituality, and cardiovascular reactivity.
results: daily spiritual experiences were positively associated with hr reactivity at the uncorrected level, but not with sbp or dbp reactivity. after controlling for religious identification, daily spiritual experiences were also positively associated with sbp, dbp, and hr reactivity in uncorrected analyses. however, none of these associations remained statistically significant following false discovery rate correction.
conclusion: these findings provide limited evidence for associations between daily spiritual experiences and cardiovascular reactivity, with observed effects not remaining significant following adjustment for multiple comparisons. overall, the results do not support robust associations between spirituality and cardiovascular reactivity in this sample. psychology & health

investigating the influence of external and individual factors on perceived route difficulty montello’s research on navigation sheds light on the spatial cognition it involves. earlier research examines how different factors influence route difficulty, analyzing how efficiently navigators navigate a route and how they experience it. however, navigation also encompasses wayfinding activities before locomotion, e.g., when looking at a route suggestion displayed on a map. we explore route difficulty from this perspective by showing route suggestions to participants and asking them to rate how difficult they appear to be, examining the impact of factors associated with the difficulty of navigating a route. results indicate that the number of turns influences the perceived difficulty of a route, while other factors seem not to. spatial cognition and computation

loneliness in hoarding disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis abstract introduction: according to attachment theory, loneliness may be a cause of hoarding symptoms. however, due to mixed findings, it is unclear whether people with hoarding disorder (hd) are lonelier than healthy and clinical controls, whether there is a significant positive association between loneliness and hoarding, and whether loneliness causes more severe hoarding. method: we conducted a systematic review and included peer-reviewed quantitative cross-sectional, longitudinal, experimental and intervention research that measured hoarding and loneliness. we excluded hoarding due to other conditions and qualitative, review, and case study research. the final search was conducted on 16 may 2025 on psycinfo, medline, and web of science. we used the quality assessment with diverse studies to evaluate study quality and conducted a random effects meta-analysis to examine loneliness-hoarding correlations. results: eleven papers with 13 studies ( n = 2715) were included. four studies compared loneliness in hd relative to controls. ten studies examined the association between hoarding and loneliness. only one experimental study examined the causal link. results showed significantly higher loneliness in hd relative to healthy controls, but findings were mixed when compared with clinical controls. the meta-analysis showed a significant association between loneliness and hoarding, r = .38 [95% ci .33, .44]. discussion: our findings confirm that loneliness is a significant issue in hd. due to its wide-ranging effects, we recommend that clinicians should assess and address loneliness in hd. although we are confident that loneliness is positively associated with hoarding, further research is required to establish a causal link. behavioural and cognitive psychotherapy
mortality, social selection, and cognitive potential after the black death evolutionary psychological science

hope as a mediator in the relationship between social support and death anxiety in older adults abstract death anxiety is a prevalent concern in older adulthood that can significantly impair quality of life. perceived social support has been recognized as a protective factor; however, the mediating mechanisms underlying its relationship with death anxiety remain underexplored. this study aimed to investigate the mediating role of hope in the association between perceived social support and death anxiety among older adults. in this cross-sectional study, 200 participants aged 60 years and older (mean age = 69.79 ± 7.19 years) were selected using stratified proportional random sampling and were recruited between may and july 2025. death anxiety, hope, and perceived social support were measured using standardized questionnaires. analyses involved descriptive statistics, multiple linear regression, and structural equation modeling (sem) using spss 24 and amos 24 ( p < 0.05). structural equation modeling indicated that perceived social support significantly and positively predicted hope (standardized coefficient β = 0.72, p = 0.001), and hope in turn significantly and negatively predicted death anxiety (standardized coefficient β = − 0.62, p = 0.001). the direct path from perceived social support to death anxiety was not statistically significant (β = 0.021, p = 0.886). the bootstrapped indirect effect of perceived social support on death anxiety through hope was significant (standardized coefficient β = − 0.45, 95% ci [− 0.70, − 0.21], p = 0.001), consistent with full mediation. the findings suggest that hope may serve as a psychological mechanism underlying the association between perceived social support and death anxiety in older adults. hope-enhancing interventions, alongside strengthening social support networks, may represent a promising approach to addressing death anxiety, warranting evaluation in future longitudinal or intervention studies. discover mental health

convergent validity of measures of daily functioning in older adults. introduction: although information on daily functioning is needed for accurate diagnoses of neurocognitive disorders, little has been published on the psychometric properties of measures of daily functioning. convergent validity is one such psychometric property that examines the relationship between scales that purport to assess the same construct. whereas the convergent validity of measures of daily functioning has typically been examined relative to cognitive tests, the current objective was to analyze the relationships between different measures of daily functioning in older adults.
methods: two hundred thirty-seven older adults (age: = 74.8, sd = 5.6; education: = 16.9, sd = 2.4) completed a battery of functional assessments, including two subjective scales (alzheimer's disease cooperative studies - activities of daily living for mild cognitive impairment 23-item version and quick dementia rating system) and three performance-based measures (independent living scales, night-out task, and virtual kitchen challenge). scales were initially compared with spearman's correlations and then factor analysis.
results: small to medium but statistically significant correlations () were found among the scores of all functional measures, with better functioning on one scale being seen on other scales (r = 0.21 to 0.61). three factors were identified, and scores loaded together based on type of scoring (i.e. correct/incorrect vs. timed) and by assessment method (i.e. subjective vs. performance-based).
conclusions: despite differences between these measures that assess daily functioning, their associations suggest that they tap a similar construct. factor loadings were based on type of scoring within the performance-based measures (i.e. correct/incorrect vs. timed) and type of assessment method (i.e. subjective or performance-based). while further exploration is needed in larger, more diverse samples and using additional functional scales, these findings have implications for both clinical practice and research. journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
a graphing tutorial for the changing-criterion design: instructions for macos behavior analysis in practice

effects of reward magnitude on rats’ long-term spatial memory retention in the radial-arm maze abstract our study examined whether reward magnitude affects long-term spatial memory retention in rats performing a radial-arm maze task. previous studies, using a forced-choice learning phase followed by a free-choice test, have reported retention of up to 72 hours, but they typically used a large reward (10 pellets per arm; 45 mg each) rather than the standard reward (one pellet per arm), leaving open a reward-based explanation. in experiment 1, we conducted a between-subjects comparison of two reward conditions: a standard-reward group (one pellet per arm) and a large-reward group (10 pellets per arm). the delay interval was progressively extended from 1 min to 1 hr, 24 hr, 48 hr, and 72 hr. both groups performed significantly above chance at all delays, including 72 hr, and performance did not differ significantly between reward conditions. in experiment 2, we tested whether relative changes in reward magnitude modulate retention. within each reward group, reward magnitude was increased or decreased for only one arm during the learning phase, followed by a 24-hr retention test. accuracy for the arm with the changed reward did not differ significantly from that of the unchanged arms. together, these findings show that 72-hr retention can be obtained, even with the standard small reward (one pellet), and that radial-arm maze performance is robust to both absolute reward magnitude and relative changes in reward. learning & behavior
taking the helm, and a year of growth sa journal of industrial psychology

mild cognitive impairment and dance movement therapy: a scoping review abstract this scoping review examines dance movement therapy (dmt) interventions for individuals with mild cognitive impairment (mci), including their caregivers/family members. the review was registered on the open science framework (osf) on 26 july 2025. a search across medline, cinahl, and scopus from july 2025 to march 2026 identified 113 relevant records. only studies with participants living with mci and their family members, aged 85 or younger, published after 2010 and included dmt as interventions were selected. the results were reported and presented in prisma flow diagrams. no studies met the inclusion criteria for this scoping review, despite an extensive search of various databases and other sources. future research should prioritise the development and evaluation of dmt interventions specifically designed for people with mci and their caregivers, as this population may have unique therapeutic needs and relational dynamics. american journal of dance therapy
bernstein, b. and krantz, a.m.: the dance/movement therapy of blanche evan: life is movement american journal of dance therapy

viewpoint on computational modeling of multisensory integration abstract this article presents a compiled interview with three prominent figures in multisensory research: ulrik ravnsborg beierholm, hans colonius, and ladan shams. through structured dialogue, the authors reflect on the evolution of computational modeling, from early mathematical psychology to the current dominance of bayesian causal inference (bci). the discussion highlights key paradigm shifts, specifically the transition from descriptive studies of illusions to normative, mechanistic explanations of perception. the authors identify the 2002 demonstration by ernst and banks of statistically optimal integration as a pivotal milestone in establishing how the brain weighs sensory reliability. crucially, the authors discuss the subsequent development of bci as the first framework to formally address the ‘binding problem’ — the computational challenge of determining whether sensory signals originate from a common source (integration) or distinct sources (segregation). current trends and controversies are explored, including the application of computational phenotypes to clinical populations, the debate over the neural implementation of bayesian computations, and the rising influence of deep neural networks. while artificial intelligence (ai) offers new avenues for analyzing high-dimensional data, the authors emphasize the need for biological realism and explainability. the dialogue also addresses the importance of open science, the challenge of accounting for individual differences, and the necessity of moving toward naturalistic environments. the article concludes with professional advice for early-career scientists, emphasizing interdisciplinary training in mathematics and statistics. collectively, the authors argue that multisensory processing is not a ‘special case’ of perception but the default mode of brain operation, providing essential principles for understanding learning, plasticity, and memory. multisensory research

integrated life/career coaching for prelicensure baccalaureate nursing students: an exploratory mixed-methods study of performance, well-being, and coaching relationship outcomes the transition from student to practice-ready professional nurse is challenging, particularly for students from disadvantaged backgrounds. this exploratory mixed-methods study reports outcomes of a novel 6-month integrated life/career coaching program for prelicensure baccalaureate nursing students, designed to strengthen essential skills, support well-being, and ease professional transition. completers reported improvements in academic performance, work performance, and well-being over time. group differences across coaching effectiveness dimensions did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons, so these results are hypothesis-generating. integrated coaching models show promise for supporting students with diverse learning and personal needs and enhancing readiness for practice. international journal of evidence based coaching & mentoring

creative coaching methods in career transition: exploring reflection and meaning-making through lego ® serious play ® and collage this study explores how creative coaching methods may help support reflection and insight in the context of career transition. eight participants engaged in a facilitated workshop using lego ® serious play ® and collage to explore experiences of career change and uncertainty. these methods enabled engagement with physical and visual materials to support reflection and meaning-making. data was collected through pre- and post-workshop questionnaires, photographs of creative artefacts, reflective memos and researcher field notes. findings suggest that creative methods may enable a nuanced exploration of identity, priorities and future directions and support meaning-making and re-interpretation of perspectives pertaining to career options. international journal of evidence based coaching & mentoring

relational leadership: an experience of relational methods this article provides an account of using relational methods to make sense of the lived experiences of healthcare leaders through narrative interviews, visual artefacts and reflexive approaches. by foregrounding relational identity and reflexivity, this article contributes to leadership and coaching development by offering insight into how leaders, coaches and mentors can cultivate relational awareness within an ethical frame, moving ‘collaborative engagement’ from being a ‘role’ to part of our ‘identity’, values and behaviours. international journal of evidence based coaching & mentoring
adapting movement amplitude for temporal constraints: further tests of the reciprocity of space-time error journal of motor behavior
practice under physical fatigue: motor learning, fatigue resilience, and individual differences in healthy young adults journal of motor behavior

the longitudinal association between death attitudes and grief symptoms: a three-wave cross-lagged study prolonged grief disorder (pgd) is characterized by persistent and impairing grief symptoms following bereavement. although certain death attitudes have been associated with grief symptoms, their bidirectional relationships over time remain unclear. this three-wave (6-month intervals) study examined reciprocal associations between five dimensions of death attitudes (fear of death, death avoidance, neutral acceptance, approach acceptance, escape acceptance) and grief symptoms in 159 bereaved chinese college students using cross-lagged panel models. results showed that fear of death at time 1 predicted higher grief symptoms at time 2. conversely, higher grief symptoms at time 1 predicted lower neutral acceptance at time 2, while higher grief symptoms at time 2 predicted greater escape acceptance at time 3. no other significant cross-lagged effects emerged. these findings reveal a dimension-specific, bidirectional pattern of longitudinal associations between death attitudes and grief symptoms, and highlight the potential relevance of death-related cognition in grief interventions. omega-journal of death and dying

a study of naxi funerary beliefs, rituals, attire and bereavement experiences in china this article examines naxi funerary culture through the interrelated dimensions of belief, ritual, and materiality, drawing on historical sources, publicly available visual materials, and online semi-structured interviews. it first reviews core beliefs, including the conception that humans possess three souls and the return of the soul to the ancestors, and traces the development of naxi funerary practices from natural disposal and cremation to contemporary combinations of cremation and burial. building on existing case records from the sanba area, it discusses receiving the last breath, the wake, the funeral procession, and cremation, and analyzes dongba ritual vestments, the deceased’s funerary garment, and relatives’ mourning dress in marking identity, guiding the soul, and structuring mourning. it argues that naxi funerary practice understands death as spiritual transformation, ancestral reintegration, and social reorganization, offering a localized perspective on death, rites of passage, and dress symbolism. omega-journal of death and dying

innovation propensity as a cognitive structure that differentiates innovative farmers understanding why farmers exposed to similar innovation opportunities behave differently remains an important challenge in agricultural psychology. this study introduces innovation propensity as a complementary cognitive construct describing a relatively stable yet developable orientation that predisposes individuals to engage with innovation opportunities before specific behavioural intentions emerge. a six-item innovation propensity measurement scale (ipms) was examined using data from 545 smallholder farmers in benin across two contrasting contexts: adoption of sustainable land management practices and participation in cashew training programmes. exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, path analysis, bootstrap mediation analysis, moderation analysis, and group comparisons were used to assess the scale and examine the relationship between innovation propensity and innovative behaviour. the findings provide preliminary support for a predominantly unidimensional structure and acceptable internal consistency, although some item-level results indicate the need for further psychometric refinement. innovation propensity was positively associated with innovative behaviour in both studies and mediated some relationships between farmers' socio-economic characteristics and innovative behaviour, particularly those involving gender, education, and farming experience. its explanatory contribution nevertheless remained moderate, indicating that propensity operates alongside other individual and contextual influences on innovation. the study provides an initial conceptualisation and empirical assessment of innovation propensity and proposes the ipms as a context-specific instrument requiring further validation. more broadly, the findings highlight the value of considering psychological orientations alongside structural and socio-economic factors when examining farmers' engagement with innovation. acta psychologica

the beck hopelessness scale: psychometric properties in a sample of iranian medical students with suicidal ideation introduction: hopelessness has consistently emerged as the strongest predictor of suicide, underscoring the critical need for a reliable measure to assess this construct effectively. the present study aimed to investigate the psychometric properties of the beck hopelessness scale (bhs) among iranian medical students with suicidal ideation.
methods: this study employed a descriptive-correlational design. the statistical population consisted of medical students in tehran in 2024 who reported suicidal ideation. through convenience sampling, a sample of 355 medical students was recruited. data were collected using the beck hopelessness scale (bhs), beck scale for suicidal ideation (bssi), beck depression inventory-ii (bdi-ii), and tehran multidimensional perfectionism scale (tmps).
results: confirmatory factor analysis revealed that the single-factor structure of the beck hopelessness scale demonstrated good model fit among medical students with suicidal ideation in tehran. furthermore, the mcdonald's omega indicated a value of 0.92. the bhs exhibited significant correlations with depression (r = 0.61), suicidal ideation (r = 0.53), self-oriented perfectionism (r = 0.29), other-oriented perfectionism (r = 0.21), and socially prescribed perfectionism (r = 0.34; p < .01), thereby supporting its convergent validity.
conclusion: these results indicate that the beck hopelessness scale possesses robust psychometric characteristics among medical students experiencing suicidal ideation in tehran. acta psychologica

metabolic reality of cognitive load. haueis and colaço argue that metabolic constraints should prune and generate cognitive models. cognitive load theory offers an applied framework for testing these constraints. working memory load can be viewed as the behavioral expression of local atp limits. primary-secondary knowledge, embodied offloading, and instructional efficiency map onto bioenergetic trade-offs. extending clt to human-ai symbiosis further shows how shared systems can support dynamic load balancing and testable metabolic predictions. behavioral and brain sciences

delayed cardiac conduction disease in a young adult following childhood chagas infection. presentation: a bolivian man in his 30s presented to the ed with non-exertional chest pain and intermittent second-degree atrioventricular (2:1) block.
diagnosis: given a history of untreated childhood trypanosoma cruzi infection and family history of chagas heart disease, late cardiac manifestation was suspected. structural and ischaemic causes were excluded.
treatment: antiparasitic therapy was initiated. pacemaker implantation was considered but deferred following shared decision-making due to absence of symptoms.
discussion: chagas heart disease (chd) may present decades after infection with conduction abnormalities. recognition in the ed is essential to enable appropriate management and reduce the risk of progression to complete heart block and sudden cardiac death. irish medical journal

quality and reliability of clear aligner information on brazilian orthodontists' websites: a discern-based evaluation. objective: this study aimed to evaluate, using the discern questionnaire, the quality, reliability, and decision-support capacity of aligner-related information published on orthodontists' websites.
methods: a cross-sectional study was conducted in july 2024. google (www.google.com.br) was searched using portuguese-language keywords ("tratamento ortodôntico", "alinhadores", and "ortodontia") in incognito mode from a brazilian ip address. the first 130 non-sponsored websites were screened; 113 met the inclusion criteria. two calibrated orthodontists independently evaluated each website using the validated brazilian portuguese version of the discern instrument. inter-rater reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (icc). descriptive statistics and spearman rank-order correlations were calculated using spss v.25.
results: the mean overall discern score was 26.3 (sd = 5.8; range 15-52) out of a maximum of 75. the icc was 0.87 (95% ci = 0.82-0.91), indicating good-to-excellent inter-rater reliability. among the 113 websites, 54.3% were rated as very poor, 30.7% as poor, 11.5% as fair, 3.5% as good, and none as excellent. the lowest-scoring items were q4 (sources of information, 99.1% very poor or poor), q5 (publication date, 87.6%), q8 (areas of uncertainty, 95.6%), q11 (treatment risks, 98.2%), and q12 (consequences of no treatment, 100%).
conclusions: the quality of clear aligner information on brazilian orthodontists' websites is critically poor. orthodontists should provide evidence-based, transparent, and balanced content - including treatment risks, alternatives, and references - to support informed patient decision-making. dental press journal of orthodontics

mediating roles of family functioning and adverse childhood experiences between traumatized mothers and their adolescent children objective: trauma experiences of north korean defector (nkd) mothers during escape and resettlement may extend beyond the individual and shape the mental health of the next generation. this study examined the association between post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) symptoms in nkd mothers and the mental health of their adolescent children, focusing on the mediating roles of family functioning and adverse childhood experiences (ace).
methods: survey data from 113 nkd mother-adolescent child dyads (children aged 12-24) were collected from 2023 to 2024. mothers reported on their traumatic experiences, ptsd symptoms, and family functioning, whereas adolescent children reported on family functioning, ace, depression, and anxiety. serial mediation was tested using process macro model 6 with 5000 bootstrap resamples.
results: nkd mothers reported an average of 9.9 traumatic events, and 34.5% met criteria for probable ptsd. mothers with probable ptsd reported lower family functioning. similarly, their adolescent children reported lower family functioning and greater exposure to ace. analysis identified no significant direct association between maternal ptsd symptoms and children's mental health. however, significant indirect associations were identified, with family functioning and ace serving as sequential mediators linking maternal ptsd to adolescent depression and anxiety. family functioning preceded ace in this pathway.
conclusion: within this nkd sample, maternal trauma was associated with adolescent mental health not directly but through disrupted family functioning and adversity rooted in histories of separation and instability. these findings suggest that breaking the intergenerational cycle requires a multidimensional approach-one that pairs maternal ptsd treatment with parenting-focused support and addresses the structural sources of childhood adversity unique to the nkd resettlement experience. acta psychologica

filicide and other child homicides in spain: comparing victim, offender, and crime characteristics. background: filicide is a rare but severe form of lethal violence against children. although international research has identified several victim, offender, and contextual correlates, empirical evidence from spain remains scarce and fragmented.
objective: this study aimed to describe filicide cases adjudicated in spain and to examine how they differ from other child homicide cases.
participants and setting: the sample comprised 197 victim-based cases of completed or attempted homicide or murder involving victims under 18 years of age, adjudicated by spanish provincial courts between 2016 and 2025. of these, 116 were filicide cases and 81 were non-filicide child homicide cases.
methods: judicial decisions were retrieved from the spanish judicial documentation centre. information was extracted from the statement of proven facts and coded for victim, offender, and offense characteristics. descriptive and bivariate analyses were conducted to compare filicide with other child homicide cases.
results: filicide victims were substantially younger than victims of other child homicides (m = 4.69 vs. 12.66 years; welch's t(119.41) = 9.90, p < .001, cohen's d = 1.614). filicide cases were also more likely to involve female offenders (χ(2) = 57.43, p < .001, cramer's v = 0.540), older first offenders (welch's t(112.41) = 3.47, p < .001, cohen's d = 0.588), completed offenses, murder classifications, and methods involving close interpersonal proximity or caregiving access.
conclusions: filicide in spain presents a distinctive victim-offender profile within lethal violence against children. prevention efforts should address child maltreatment, mental health crises, domestic violence, and caregiving breakdown, with particular attention to infants and young children. child abuse & neglect

antepartum stress, trait anxiety, and medical risks as predictors of fathers' postpartum worry after threatened preterm birth. background: preterm birth (pb) or its threat (tpb) can negatively affect paternal mental health, leading to increased worry. as specific paternal risk factors are understudied, this study aimed to identify psychological, maternal, and infant-related medical factors associated with paternal postpartum worry in the context of tpb and pb.
methods: in this longitudinal study, 112 men were assessed during their partner's pregnancy (t1) and six weeks postpartum (t2). trait anxiety, worry, and chronic stress were measured using the state-trait anxiety-depression inventory (stadi) and the trier inventory for chronic stress (tics). maternal and infant medical data were collected from clinical records and standardised self-reports. participants were assigned to either a risk group (rg) with term birth (tb) or pb, or a control group (cg: no tpb, term birth). multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to identify predictors of paternal worry.
results: antepartum chronic stress predicted worry. trait anxiety and obstetric factors, cervical insufficiency and preterm premature rupture of membranes, were significant predictors in rg-tb only. in the rg-pb, low infant birth weight showed a small but non-significant association with paternal worry.
conclusion: fathers exposed to tpb are at increased risk of postpartum worry, particularly with higher antepartum chronic stress, trait anxiety, and maternal complications, even when the infant is born at term. chronic stress and trait anxiety, along with maternal complications and infant birth outcomes, contribute differentially to paternal worry. these findings highlight the importance of early support and stress prevention for fathers facing prenatal risk, regardless of birth outcome. journal of reproductive and infant psychology

care at the heart, leadership in practice: nasn's new brand for school nursing today. school nursing has evolved as student health needs, mental health concerns, public health pressures, and schools' focus on attendance and student well-being have grown more complex. nasn's brand needed to evolve with the profession. this article describes the thinking behind nasn's comprehensive rebrand, including input from school nurses, the meaning of the new visual identity, and the language that now anchors how nasn communicates the profession's authority, leadership, connection, rigor, support, and care. the new logo brings the s and n of school nursing together in a heart representing students and the broad, whole-child care school nurses provide. the new brand represents the collective strength of school nurses across the country and the role nasn plays in connecting, supporting, and advancing them. more than a visual update, the brand is intended to help school nurses, education leaders, policymakers, partners, families, and communities better understand the essential role school nurses play in keeping students healthy, safe, present, and ready to learn. nasn school nurse (print)

a goldilocks approach to youth psychotropic prescribing. psychotropic prescribing in youth is increasingly debated through concerns regarding both overmedicalisation and unmet mental health need. rising rates are often interpreted as evidence of overprescribing, yet clinicians often operate in under-resourced services, with long waiting lists and limited access to psychological therapies. this paper argues that the key issue is not whether prescribing rates are too high, but whether prescribing is proportionate to clinical need. drawing on international and recent irish camhs prescribing data, we propose a "goldilocks model" of psychotropic prescribing in youth, in which optimal prescribing lies on a continuum between the extremes of under- and over-prescribing. this position is shaped by evidence, patient factors, and service context. while psychotropics have an important evidence-based role within child psychiatry, safe and effective use depends on accurate assessment, appropriate monitoring, and access to multidisciplinary and psychosocial supports. achieving proportionate prescribing therefore requires systems capable of supporting evidence-informed, ethically grounded, and developmentally informed care, ensuring treatment is neither too much nor too little, but ultimately "just right." irish medical journal

avances en psicología latinoamericana (apl): un análisis bibliométrico (2006-2025) el presente estudio analiza la trayectoria y el impacto de la revista avances en psicología latinoamericana (apl) mediante una revisión histórico-bibliométrica del período 2006-2025. se examina la productividad, autoría, colaboración, citación, impacto y evolución temática. se analizaron 565 documentos (546 artículos y 19 revisiones) indexados en scopus, firmados por autores de 30 países. la productividad se ajustó a la ley de lotka y mostró un aumento sostenido en la colaboración científica, reflejado en los índices de lawani y subramanyam. la revista alcanzó un índice h de 19 y 2 300 citas, con brasil, colombia y argentina como principales países de afiliación. los artículos más citados abordaron temas como burnout, funciones ejecutivas, uso problemático de internet y empatía. el análisis de copalabras evidenció una alta estabilidad editorial y una transición temática hacia áreas como salud mental, educación y familia. los resultados dan cuenta de la importancia de apl en la difusión del conocimiento psicológico, con creciente internacionalización, equidad de género y compromiso ético en la comunicación científica. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

a cognitive behavioural therapy case study for emotional difficulties with sickle cell disease this case study describes a cognitive behavioural therapy (cbt) approach to working with an adolescent experiencing emotional difficulties including anxiety and stress, related to sickle cell disease (scd). the intervention incorporates cbt principles to develop a formulation, provide psychoeducation on anxiety and further skills to manage stress. it was hypothesised that by doing so, cbt would prove to be an effective intervention to manage the emotional difficulties linked with scd. throughout, identity and stigmatising attitudes are discussed, incorporating wider systemic factors into the intervention. outcomes support the hypothesis, indicating that cbt is effective in reducing anxiety and the client was able to manage further stress and worry. these findings are discussed in relation to the evidence base. clinical case studies

implicit causality in context: how topic status shapes remention preferences extensive research has shown that implicit causality verbs trigger rementions to either the subject (np1 verbs) or the object (np2 verbs) of a sentence. recent work demonstrates that these preferences interact with syntactic and discourse-related factors. this study investigates whether information structure—specifically topic status—interacts with verb biases and influences remention patterns in contexts with and without implicit causality verbs. in two dialog completion experiments, we manipulated whether an antecedent was maintained as a continuous topic or introduced as a shifted topic. experiment 1, using non-biased verbs, revealed a dispreference for rementioning continuous topics. experiment 2 tested np1 and np2 implicit causality verbs and showed that topic status affected rementions asymmetrically. with np1 verbs, there were fewer cause rementions in the topic-continuity condition compared to the topic-shift condition. in contrast, with np2 verbs, there were more cause rementions in the topic-continuity condition compared to the topic-shift condition. these findings demonstrate that topic status interacts with semantic biases and affects remention preferences as a function of how the two cues align, highlighting the role of information structure in coreference in broader contexts. discourse processes

comprehensive psychometric evaluation of the child/adult and family quality of life scale : third edition. purpose: quality of life (qol) has become a key concept for understanding the impact of neurodevelopmental conditions and for monitoring intervention progress. existing qol measures often focus on health-related qol in neurotypical populations or were developed specifically for autism. the cfql was designed to bridge this gap. the present study describes evaluation of the second revision of the cfql - the cfql-3/afql-3.
methods: psychometric evaluation was conducted in two samples: a large validation sample and a clinical intervention sample.
results: results indicated a clear factor structure, measurement invariance across demographic and clinical factors, good scale and conditional reliability, adequate or better test-retest stability, good construct validity, and good sensitivity to change during behavioral intervention.
conclusion: the cfql-3/afql-3 may be a useful clinical and research measure for qol in clinical and research settings. journal of autism and developmental disorders

evaluating the effects of skill-based treatment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of single-case studies abstract purpose the skill-based treatment for challenging behaviour (sbt) is an intervention package that combines functional communication training with contingency-based delay and denial tolerance training. this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to (a) investigate the application of sbt across diverse populations, setting, and target behaviours; and (b) to evaluate the effectiveness and social validity of sbt in reducing challenging behaviours. methods this review was pre-registered on prospero (id: crd42024561455). seven databases were searched. data were extracted on characteristics of studies, participants, and applications of sbt. literature was assessed for quality using the evaluative method and single case design risk of bias tool. sbt outcomes were quantified with baseline-corrected tau (tau-bc). results a total of 28 studies were reviewed, representing 99 individual sbt applications. sbt has been applied across participants with varying diagnoses, challenging behaviours, and levels of ability, though mostly in controlled settings by skilled implementers. studies provided evidence for the social validity of sbt. baseline-corrected tau indicated sbt shows good reduction in challenging behaviour ( m = 0.47, range: − 0.35–1.00). the evaluative method indicated the literature to be of varying quality (borderline-strong = 7%; adequate = 13%; borderline-adequate = 43%; weak = 37%), and the evidence-based practice score suggests sbt to be a potentially evidence-based practice. conclusion the evaluative method indicates sbt to be an emerging evidence-based practice for addressing challenging behaviour, although the majority of the literature scored lower than adequate. we make recommendations for strengthening the literature base and outline key implications for practitioners. journal of autism and developmental disorders

humble leadership and employee self-development in smes: a four-wave multilevel study of job autonomy and intrinsic motivation abstract background employee self-development is important for workers to update their skills and respond to changing work environments. however, less is known about how humble leadership is positively associated with self-development through employees’ psychological experiences. drawing on social information processing theory and the job demands-resources perspective, this study examines whether team-level humble leadership is positively associated with individual self-development through job autonomy and intrinsic motivation. methods a four-wave survey was conducted among employees from small and medium-sized enterprises in shandong province, china. the final sample included 368 employees nested in 83 teams. humble leadership was measured at time 1, job autonomy at time 2, intrinsic motivation at time 3, and self-development at time 4. multilevel structural equation modeling in mplus was used to test the hypotheses. confidence intervals estimated in mplus were used to examine the indirect effects. results at the between level, humble leadership was positively related to employee self-development, job autonomy, and intrinsic motivation. at the within level, job autonomy and intrinsic motivation were positively related to self-development. job autonomy was also positively related to intrinsic motivation at both the within and between levels. the sequential indirect effect of humble leadership on self-development through job autonomy and intrinsic motivation was significant. the indirect effect through job autonomy alone was not significant. conclusions the findings suggest that humble leadership is positively associated with employee self-development through employees’ perceived job autonomy and intrinsic motivation. job autonomy may provide room for self-development, but it may not be enough by itself in a cross-level process. employees are more likely to use autonomy for sustained self-development when autonomy is linked to intrinsic motivation. this study highlights a multilevel psychological mechanism linking humble leadership to employee self-development in smes. bmc psychology

sharing weal and woe: the perceived coworker support scale for healthcare staff abstract introduction perceived organizational support is a vital resource for workplace well-being among healthcare staff. however, most existing literature has focused on general social support provided when things go awry. less is known about coworker support for healthcare staff especially in positive workplace scenarios. objective this study aimed to: (a) develop and validate a perceived coworker support scale to comprehensively assess perceived support among healthcare staff in both positive and negative workplace scenarios and (b) associate this perceived support with both personal- and organizational - outcomes. methods a preliminary scale with three dimensions (i.e., general support, support in bad times, support in good times) was developed after a literature review and case interviews with representative healthcare staff ( n = 16). items of the draft scale were reviewed and revised by the research group to improve wording, semantic clarity and dimensionality. finally, an anonymous online survey investigation was conducted to test the psychometric properties of an 18-item version of the scale. this survey comprised the new scale as well as established scales evaluating workplace well-being for criterion validity (e.g., maslach burnout inventory, psychological safety scale). demographic and professional information was also collected. data was collected from three chinese hospitals in 2023. results responses were received from 878 hospital employees. after data cleaning, 626 participants were retained for data analysis (attrition rate = 28.7%). data analyses revealed that the proposed 18-item perceived coworker support scale exhibited a bifactor structure comprising one dominant general factor and three specific factors. moreover, the results provided evidence for criterion-related validity, incremental validity, and reliability. conclusion this study contributes to the field by providing a novel psychological assessment tool, the pcs-hs scale, for perceived coworker support, and byrevealing its relationship(s) with workplace well-being. implications were discussed regarding maximizing healthcare staff’s well-being in both positive and negative eventsvia workplace social capitalization processes. bmc psychology

digital agency tools: a way to buffer the negative effects of excessive phone use? in times of ubiquitous smartphone use, most users adopt one or more self-imposed rules regarding their device usage, also known as voluntary digital disconnection. drawing on the integrative model of mobile media use and need experiences (im³une), this study provides empirical evidence on the adoption of digital agency tools and their potential in mitigating ill-being (depression, anxiety, and stress) associated with excessive smartphone use. we conducted a quota-based online survey involving n = 384 ( m age = 49.6) smartphone users in flanders (belgium). the results provide a systematization of different digital agency tools, showing they are widely used among adults. importantly, we provide preliminary evidence on their potential in buffering ill-being due to excessive smartphone use. for users of detox apps and in-app well-being features, the associations between excessive use and ill-being were nonsignificant, unlike for nonusers of these tools. for users of default device settings, such as ios screentime, there were no differences. our findings contribute to theory by applying and empirically testing critical elements of the im³une model. empirically, our findings indicate the importance of studying different types of tools, as they do not appear to be equally beneficial. cyberpsychology behavior and social networking

what it takes to make sense of the world: the relationships between culture and sensemaking societies are naturally engaged in a perpetual endeavor to construct a shared reality by making sense of socially significant information. the role of culture in this process of sensemaking, however, remains surprisingly understudied. to fill this gap, we investigated how cross-cultural differences predict overt sensemaking in the activity of the world largest encyclopedia—wikipedia, which explicitly aims to create a shared system of meaning. adopting a longitudinal approach, we have conducted a series of hierarchical linear models and found that across 67 countries and different conceptualizations of culture, the cultural emphasis on independence, autonomy, and self-expression (individualism), as opposed to interdependence, conformity, and self-restriction (collectivism), was positively associated with engagement in sensemaking and its increase over a 19-year period between 2007 and 2025. in addition, distinguishing between the “sense” and “making” components of sensemaking revealed that cultural emphasis on control was associated with the increase in making but the decrease in sense created over time. these findings have significant implications for cross-cultural communication and collaboration in an increasingly globalized world. journal of cross-cultural psychology

the cultural content of genetic essentialism: how “black genes” and “white genes” shape multiracial perception in the united states polygenist ideas historically represented racial groups as having separate biological origins. the present research examines beliefs in specific race-linked genes (i.e., genes associated with racial groups), such as “black genes” and “white genes,” as a content-bearing form of genetic racial essentialism (i.e., the belief that race reflects inherited genetic differences). across two online surveys of u.s. adults (studies 1a–1b; n = 440; predominantly white samples), approximately 41% of participants endorsed the existence of both “black genes” and “white genes.” participants also consistently characterized “black genes” as more dominant than “white genes” and “white genes” as weaker than “black genes.” in study 2, an experiment with u.s. adults ( n = 320), black–white multiracial targets described as having greater black ancestry were perceived as possessing a higher proportion of “black genes.” these estimates were associated with a greater likelihood of categorizing targets as black. dehumanization judgments showed a different pattern: the association between inferred genetic composition and dehumanization varied according to participants’ endorsement of “dominant black genes,” becoming less differentiated as endorsement increased. together, the findings identify race-linked gene beliefs as culturally recognizable but contested representations through which some individuals interpret racial ancestry and multiracial targets in the united states. journal of cross-cultural psychology

cross-temporal meta-analysis of changes in individualism and collectivism among chinese previous research has shown a global trend of rising individualism and declining collectivism in recent decades. however, studies on the trends specifically among the chinese population have yielded inconsistent results. this study employed a cross-temporal meta-analysis to examine changes in individualism and collectivism among chinese individuals. the findings indicated that between 2001 and 2023, there was also a trend of increasing individualism and decreasing collectivism in china, though the magnitude of these changes was relatively small. these findings provide empirical evidence for modest cultural-value change in china and extend modernization accounts by showing that marketization, urbanization, and economic development are associated with individualism and collectivism. journal of cross-cultural psychology

nyc congestion charge in the public eye: how opponents and supporters consistently (mis) perceive public support across six survey waves, we examined perceived public support for the new york city congestion charge among new yorkers ( n wave1 = 1,460, n longitudinal = 361). consistent with the false-consensus effect, opponents underestimated public support across all six waves, whereas supporters appeared relatively well calibrated. opponents with more like-minded others in their social networks underestimated public support to a greater extent, while associations with media exposure were weak and inconsistent. to test a possible corrective intervention, 938 participants assessed supporters’ or opponents’ beliefs about public support (i.e., third-order beliefs). this perspective-taking task did not correct misperceptions; among opponents, it worsened them. our findings highlight the persistence of misperceptions about climate-policy support, the role of social networks in shaping them, and the limits of perspective-taking as a corrective tool. understanding these dynamics may help practitioners seeking to foster support for sustainability transitions. environment and behavior

from norms to behavior: examining the mechanisms of change in a social norms anti-bullying intervention among early adolescents social norm interventions offer a promising approach to bullying prevention, yet the mechanisms through which they operate remain unclear. using a parallel mediation structural equation model, this study examined potential mediators of a classroom-based social norms intervention previously shown to reduce direct and indirect bullying. participants were 809 students (52.78% female; m age = 10.15, sd age = 0.98) from grades 4 to 6 in six schools (36 classes) randomly assigned to an intervention or control condition. results showed that changes in direct bullying were mediated by changes in injunctive anti-bullying norms among most liked classmates, whereas the mechanisms underlying changes in indirect bullying remained unexplained. individuals’ perceptions of classroom, friend and teacher norms were unaffected by the intervention, challenging the widely held assumption that norm interventions operate through (conscious) norm perceptions. these findings highlight the importance of explicitly testing mediating pathways and identifying the reference groups through which norm-based interventions exert their effects. international journal of behavioral development

incremental advantage of extraversion and neuroticism facets in predicting state work engagement abstract we extend the literature on personality dynamics and state work engagement by examining whether facets of state extraversion and neuroticism incrementally predict state work engagement beyond state domain personality (and other conceptually related covariates). this research contributes to the literature on state engagement and state personality by highlighting the dynamic and unique predictive potential of particular state facets for day-to-day engagement and its respective dimensions. using a daily diary design, we collected data from 95 full-time employees over the course of 10 workdays (804 daily observations). results indicated that state extraversion and neuroticism facets were related to overall state work engagement and that the facets predicted both broad and narrow (i.e., dimensions of) state work engagement beyond state domain personality. specifically, state assertiveness predicted state work engagement beyond lagged engagement, state extraversion, and state positive affect. similarly, state anxiety predicted state work engagement beyond lagged engagement, state neuroticism, and state negative affect. these findings further support the idea that state personality has predictive value for important dynamic workplace outcomes and extends this conclusion to state personality facets. journal of business and psychology

a meta-analytic examination of the criterion-related validity and cognitive loading associated with traditional and new situational judgment test paradigms. traditionally, situational judgment tests (sjts) include text-based situations and ask candidates to pick the best and worst response option.over the years, various new sjt paradigms have been developed to increase validity, reduce incidental cognitive load, and/or lower costs.examples are multimedia sjts, constructed response sjts, and single-response sjts.first, this study investigates how the traditional sjt paradigm performs in terms of criterion-related validity by updating prior meta-analyses.second, this study provides initial, meta-analytic evidence on the criterion-related validity and cognitive load of several new sjt paradigms.on the basis of 457 independent samples from 302 studies (total n = 244,257), results showed that sjts were not only predictive of job performance but also of academic performance, organizational citizenship behavior, and counterproductive work behavior.sjt validity was higher in operational (i.e., applicant) settings than in nonoperational settings and could also be expanded to new content (e.g., emotion and cross-cultural management).in terms of comparing traditional and new sjt paradigms, multimedia sjts had validity equal to text-based ones but lower cognitive load.importantly, the multiple-choice modality did not significantly outperform written constructed response modalities in terms of validity, and the cognitive loading of webcamconstructed responses was even lower than that of other response modalities.the implications of these findings are among others discussed in the context of the cost effectiveness of sjts vis-à-vis other selection procedures. journal of applied psychology
