associations between generative ai usage orientations and critical thinking disposition among college students in china introduction research on generative artificial intelligence (genai) in higher education commonly describes use in terms of adoption or frequency. students, however, may engage with the same systems in different ways. methods this study conceptualises three genai usage orientations (tool, guidance, and collaboration) and surveys 430 college students in china to examine their bivariate and adjusted associations with critical thinking disposition (ctd). tool represented comparatively delegative use, including task completion centred on genai and direct adoption of its output with limited independent revision. guidance reflected instrumental requests for explanations, examples, clues, or diagnostic assistance. collaboration reflected iterative coordination directed by students. based on the measurement evaluation, ctd was used as the primary outcome. results tool showed no statistically significant bivariate association with ctd ( r = −0.044, p = 0.363) but had a negative adjusted association ( β = −0.189, p < 0.001). this pattern is consistent with statistical suppression; the adjusted tool coefficient represents a conditional association. guidance ( β = 0.126, p = 0.017) and collaboration ( β = 0.321, p < 0.001) showed positive adjusted associations. the orientation block explained an additional 10.37% of the variance in ctd, and the final model explained 38.95% of ctd variance. discussion the findings show that behavioural orientations provide information beyond general measures of genai experience. frontiers in psychology

doing respectful closeness: the role of minimal listening responses in supporting disclosure of sexual offenses objective across institutional settings, there are conversations in which the client’s disclosure of moral transgressions is a goal in itself or a necessary step toward change. such disclosure both depends on and may threaten the client–professional relationship. therefore, these conversations constitute a fruitful setting for examining how people build purposive relationships within institutional constraints. we aim to examine how participants interactionally co-achieve a relationship that is purposive toward disclosure of moral transgressions. methods drawing on conversation analysis (ca) of 19 research interviews with young people who have committed sexual violation(s), we apply longitudinal ca on one single successful case, substantiated by three contrastive examples. results our analysis demonstrates how a purposive relationship quality of respectful closeness is co-achieved through the interviewer’s responsive and skillful use of minimal listening tokens to support the interviewee’s progression toward disclosure. we specify one overarching dynamic (mutual trust) and three practices (staying with difficulty, relationally scaffolded storytelling, and managing absence with presence) characterizing this relational work. conclusion relationship quality is achieved on a turn-by-turn basis and may over time result in the relational robustness necessary to disclose sexual offenses. conversation analysis detailing this relational work can develop both theory and clinical practice, and unpacks expertise as practical, observable knowledge. frontiers in psychology
editorial: new horizons in human bonds: insights into interpersonal synchrony across the lifespan frontiers in psychology

academic burnout under geopolitical and economic uncertainty: longitudinal associations with future development anxiety, employment competition pressure, and perceived structural university support introduction students may interpret geopolitical and economic change as a threat to future development, but its cross-wave associations with academic burnout remain unclear. methods this study analyzed a two-wave convenience sample from four universities in zhengzhou, china. the baseline sample comprised 1,823 students, of whom 1,215 completed matched follow-up after approximately 5 months. wave-specific factor analyses, covariance-based confirmatory factor analysis, partial least squares structural equation modeling, and covariance-based sensitivity models were used. results after baseline adjustment, t1 perceived geopolitical and economic uncertainty was positively associated with t2 future development anxiety (beta = 0.175, p < 0.001) and t2 academic burnout (beta = 0.148, p < 0.001). t1 future development anxiety was positively associated with t2 academic burnout (beta = 0.176, p < 0.001), and the reverse cross-wave association was weaker (beta = 0.087, p < 0.001). the prospective-concurrent indirect association through t2 future development anxiety was significant (beta = 0.037, p < 0.001), but the mediator and outcome were measured concurrently. employment competition pressure strengthened the focal association (beta = 0.105, p < 0.001), whereas perceived structural university support attenuated this moderation (three-way interaction beta = −0.114, p < 0.001). discussion the results indicate small to moderate cross-wave between-person associations. they do not establish within-person causation or temporal mediation. universities may use these patterns to inform targeted support, but intervention effectiveness requires direct evaluation. frontiers in psychology

curriculum satisfaction and pre-service teachers’ social–emotional competencies: the serial mediation role of artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement this study examined the serial mediation role of artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement in the relationship between pre-service teachers’ curriculum satisfaction and social–emotional competencies. this study included 550 pre-service teachers from a public university in türkiye. this correlational study used the ibm spss process macro (model 6-two-mediator serial mediation analysis/model). in this study, the scales of student satisfaction, artificial intelligence anxiety, student engagement, and social–emotional expertise were used as data collection tools. to provide a coherent and integrated understanding of the structural relationships, this study was grounded in the input-process-output framework. in this model, curriculum satisfaction was regarded as an input. artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement were regarded as processes. social–emotional competencies were regarded as an output within the framework. as a result, curriculum satisfaction was negatively associated with artificial intelligence anxiety. artificial intelligence anxiety was negatively associated with learning engagement. learning engagement was positively associated with social–emotional competencies. curriculum satisfaction was also positively associated with social–emotional competencies. when the model included artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement simultaneously, the relationship between curriculum satisfaction and social–emotional competencies was reduced but remained statistically significant. in line with these results, artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement played a partial serial mediation role in the relationship between curriculum satisfaction and social–emotional competencies (β = 0.051, se = 0.010, 95% ci = [0.028, 0.074], p < 0.01). the findings may help clarify the importance of curriculum satisfaction, artificial intelligence anxiety, learning engagement, and social–emotional competencies together when designing teacher training curriculum. frontiers in psychology

latent profile analysis of sleep quality and its association with psychological resilience among emergency department nurses objective emergency department nurses are consistently exposed to high-intensity and high-pressure working conditions, leading to poor sleep quality. psychological resilience can help alleviate the negative impacts of work stress. however, few studies have explored how resilience varies across distinct subgroups defined by different sleep profiles. this study employed latent profile analysis to identify distinct sleep-quality profiles among emergency department nurses and explored their association with psychological resilience to provide a basis for targeted interventions. methods from october to december 2025, 611 emergency nurses were recruited from 12 tertiary hospitals in shandong through convenience sampling. data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the connor–davidson resilience scale, and the pittsburgh sleep quality index. sleep quality profiles were determined through latent profile analysis, and associated factors were analyzed using multiple logistic regression. results emergency department nurses exhibited generally poor sleep quality, which was classified into four distinct profiles: “severely disturbed sleep” (8.0%), “sleep onset difficulty-sleep medication use” (15.1%), “mildly disturbed sleep” (26.7%), and “good sleep quality” (50.2%). psychological resilience, age, work experience, monthly income, and monthly night shift number were significantly associated with these sleep quality profiles ( p < 0.05). conclusion emergency department nurses exhibit distinct sleep quality profiles. targeted interventions addressing the specific factors associated with each subgroup could improve their sleep outcomes. frontiers in psychology

evidence of validity, reliability, and measurement invariance of the psychological characteristics related to sport performance questionnaire in colombian athletes background the assessment of psychological characteristics is crucial for the intervention and monitoring of sports performance. however, there is a lack of instruments for measuring psychological characteristics in colombian athletes. methods this research aimed to examine the validity and reliability of the scores obtained from the psychological characteristics related to sport performance questionnaire (cprd in spanish). two complementary studies were conducted: study 1 included 1.305 athletes, comprising 412 women and 893 men, with an age range between 13 and 59 years, divided into age groups; study 2 included 478 athletes, comprising 150 women and 328 men, with an age range between 13 and 37 years. results the four-factor, 37-item cprd demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for stress control (sc), influence of performance evaluation (ipe), and motivation (m), but inconsistent reliability for team cohesion (tc) (ω = 0.64; α = 0.65), although overall reliability was satisfactory. the four-factor cprd showed adequate model fit indices. although the questionnaire demonstrated adequate concurrent validity, convergent validity was not satisfactory. inverse correlations were observed between the four-factor cprd and burnout dimensions, and acceptable ratios supporting discriminant validity were identified, along with measurement invariance across sport modality, sex, and age groups (δcfi and/or δrmsea ≤ 0.01). conclusion the four-factor cprd provides partial evidence of validity and reliability for assessing relevant psychological variables in the colombian sports context; however, interpretations based on factor-level scores should be made with caution. frontiers in psychology

virtual reality as a metacognitive training tool for lucid dreaming introduction lucid dreaming (ld) involves awareness of being in a dream during rem sleep and depends on the reactivation of metacognitive and reality-monitoring processes. this study tested whether a virtual reality (vr) intervention designed to rehearse lucid-dream-relevant metacognitive routines increases ld rates beyond baseline training, and whether generic vr exposure produces similar effects. materials and methods thirty-eight participants with low previous ld experience completed a 5-week program of daily dream diaries and reality checks, assigned to: vr-experimental ( n = 13), standard training plus eight luciddreamingvr sessions preceded by brief open monitoring (om) meditation; vr-control ( n = 12), standard training plus eight ld-unrelated vr sessions; or control ( n = 13), standard training only. dreams were classified as ordinary, semi-lucid, or lucid; semi-lucid and lucid dreams were treated as lucid-like. results vr-experimental participants reported the highest number of lucid like dreams (26), followed by control (11) and vr-control (4). a poisson model with total recalled dreams as offset showed that lucid-like dream rates were significantly higher in vr-experimental than in vr-control, rr = 8.60, 95% ci [3.00, 24.64], p_holm <0.001, and control, rr = 4.00, 95% ci [1.97, 8.09], p_holm <0.001. responder rates showed a convergent pattern, with at least one lucid-like dream reported by 84.6% of vr-experimental participants, 61.5% of control participants, and 33.3% of vr-control participants, showing that vr exposure alone was insufficient. discussion/conclusion dream-oriented vr training preceded by om meditation may facilitate ld by scaffolding metacognitive monitoring from wakefulness to rem sleep. frontiers in psychology

perceived generative ai teaching intelligence and pre-service teachers' professional identity: double-edged pathways through professional agency and ai replacement threat generative artificial intelligence (genai) is increasingly used in teacher education for lesson planning, feedback, and assessment support. however, how perceived genai teaching intelligence relates to pre-service teachers' professional identity remains unclear. this study examined a double-edged model linking perceived intelligence to professional identity through professional agency and ai replacement threat, with teacher–ai complementarity beliefs moderating these pathways. in a task-based between-subjects experiment, 598 pre-service teachers were randomly assigned to high- or low-intelligence genai teaching-support conditions. complementarity beliefs and baseline professional identity were measured before exposure; perceived intelligence, professional agency, replacement threat, and post-task identity were assessed afterward. confirmatory factor analysis and conditional process analyses with 5,000 bootstrap resamples tested the model. participants in the high-intelligence condition reported greater agency and replacement threat, but no statistically significant between-condition difference in post-task identity was detected. perceived intelligence was positively associated with both agency and replacement threat, which were, respectively, positively and negatively associated with professional identity. stronger complementarity beliefs were associated with a stronger agency pathway and a weaker replacement-threat pathway. these findings are consistent with two opposing identity-relevant processes following exposure to capable genai. teacher education should support professional judgment and clarify human–ai role boundaries when integrating genai into teaching practice. frontiers in psychology

moderating effects of media literacy and flow on the association between web-based learning environment and knowledge sharing among medical students: a cross-sectional study background online learning has become an integral part of medical education, and understanding the factors associated with medical students’ knowledge sharing is important for designing effective learning environments. objective this study examined the associations among web-based learning environment, media literacy, flow, and knowledge sharing, and tested whether media literacy and flow moderate the association between web-based learning environment and knowledge sharing. methods a cross-sectional online survey was conducted from july to september 2021 in china. of 1,200 undergraduate medical students invited, 987 valid responses were retained (response rate 82.25%; 70.7% women). hierarchical linear regression with mean-centered variables was used to examine factors associated with knowledge sharing and to test the moderating effects of flow and media literacy. results the mean knowledge sharing score was 3.91 ± 0.58. knowledge sharing was positively correlated with web-based learning environment ( r = 0.360, p < 0.01), flow ( r = 0.565, p < 0.01), and media literacy ( r = 0.460, p < 0.01). flow ( β = 0.732, p = 0.001; δ r 2 = 0.008) and media literacy ( β = 0.900, p = 0.001; δ r 2 = 0.009) significantly moderated the association between web-based learning environment and knowledge sharing, although the incremental explained variance was small. conclusion the association between web-based learning environment and knowledge sharing was stronger among medical students with high flow or high media literacy. these findings suggest that improving the web-based learning environment and integrating media literacy education may support knowledge sharing; causal conclusions require longitudinal or interventional evidence. frontiers in psychology

the impact of daily activities on the mental health of older adults in mexico objective this study analyzed the role that daily activities (goals and plans, healthy routines, social connections, healthy thinking, and meaningful activities) play in relation to two indicators of mental health (depressive symptoms and subjective well-being) among older adults. methods a non-probability sample of 1,018 residents of mexico city (23.3% men and 76.7% women) aged 60 to 97 years ( m = 74.97, sd = 7.60) was selected. the things you do questionnaire (tydq-21) was used to assess daily activities, along with the adapted version of the yesavage geriatric depression scale (gds) and the subjective well-being scale (ebs-8). results the results showed that 19% of the participants exhibited symptoms of depression. significant correlations were found among all variables, and multiple regression analyses indicated that most dimensions of daily activities were predictors of depressive symptoms (explaining 13% of the variance) and subjective well-being (explaining 20% of the variance). conclusion the findings of this study suggest that the daily activities assessed in this research could be taken into account when developing interventions that promote mental health in older adults. the results of this study provide empirical evidence that may be useful for developing mental health promotion programs for older adults based on everyday activities that do not necessarily require the involvement of specialists. frontiers in psychology

independent judgment before viewing generative ai recommendations reduces susceptibility to misleading advice: a randomized scenario-based experiment with preservice teachers introduction generative ai can support preservice teachers’ pedagogical decisions, but fluent recommendations may also redirect attention away from diagnostic classroom evidence. we compared an independent-judgment-before-recommendation sequence with a recommendation-before-judgment sequence under expert-keyed and misleading generative ai recommendations. methods a three-arm randomized scenario-based experiment enrolled 240 preservice teachers from one chinese university. group a recorded an independent judgment before viewing an ai recommendation, group b viewed the recommendation before its first recorded judgment, and group c completed the tasks without ai as a contextual benchmark and did not enter the primary sequence × recommendation-quality hypothesis test. groups a and b completed 12 fixed-order items, including six expert-keyed and six misleading recommendations. expert-keyed joint accuracy—agreement with the expert-designated plan and rationale—was the primary outcome. after data-quality exclusions, 218 participants remained in the main analysis. participant-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations tested sequence, recommendation quality, and their interaction. results under misleading recommendations, group a had higher expert-keyed joint accuracy than group b, or = 1.912, 95% ci [1.413, 2.589], p < 0.001. the estimate remained significant among all 160 randomized a/b participants with available outcomes, or = 1.814, 95% ci [1.345, 2.448], p < 0.001, and was similar after version adjustment. the difference appeared in both final plan accuracy and final rationale accuracy. group a was also less likely to reproduce the misleading recommendation completely, or = 0.403, 95% ci [0.296, 0.549], p < 0.001. under expert-keyed recommendations, the between-group contrast was not statistically significant, or = 0.821, 95% ci [0.598, 1.128], p = 0.225. discussion recording an independent judgment before viewing ai was associated with lower susceptibility to misleading recommendations in the selected controlled scenarios. the result supports further evaluation of independent-first workflows in teacher education, but it does not isolate a single cognitive mechanism or establish transfer to authentic classroom decision-making. these findings extend research on cognitive-forcing designs to contextualized pedagogical judgments that require both instructional action selection and evidence-based justification. frontiers in psychology

community-based sport-leisure participation and perceived community psychological resilience: a three-wave ri-clpm study of community identification and collective efficacy objective in modern risk societies, community psychological resilience has become an important concern for community psychology and behavioral science. yet less is known about how everyday community-based sport-leisure participation contributes to residents’ perceived community psychological resilience over time. this study examined whether residents’ community-based sport-leisure participation predicts subsequent perceived community psychological resilience and whether this association is explained by community identification and collective efficacy. methods a three-wave longitudinal survey with a 4-month time lag was conducted among 386 residents in hangzhou, china. data were analyzed using a random intercept cross-lagged panel model (ri-clpm) to separate within-person state dynamics from stable between-person differences. results within-person increases in community-based sport-leisure participation positively predicted subsequent perceived community psychological resilience (t1 → t2: β = 0.18, p < 0.01; t2 → t3: β = 0.21, p < 0.01). the theory-guided standardized sequential indirect effect through community identification and collective efficacy was also significant [standardized indirect effect = 0.065, 95% ci (0.032, 0.105)]. conclusion the findings provide longitudinal predictive evidence consistent with a behavior–identity–efficacy pathway linking residents’ sport-leisure participation with perceived community psychological resilience. given the observational design and modest effect sizes, the pathway should be interpreted as one prospective social-psychological association rather than as evidence of a causal intervention effect. the study positions community-based sport-leisure participation as an everyday behavioral context embedded in social relationships, with implications for community-based health promotion, social connection, and resilience-related perceptions. frontiers in psychology

goodness behind a wheel: moral judgment in realistic traffic simulations featuring agents, deeds, and consequences investigating how different stakeholders evaluate traffic situations is essential for aligning autonomous vehicle (av) decision-making with common-sense moral expectations. yet, empirical studies on traffic moral judgment remain limited and almost exclusively focused on dramatic high-stakes situations. to address this gap, this paper presents two studies testing moral judgment in low-stakes ordinary traffic simulations. drawing on the adc model of moral judgment, both studies systematically manipulated key moral features: the character of the driver (agent), adherence to traffic rules (deed), and the presence or absence of a collision (consequences). these components were embedded in a variety of stimuli, including textual vignettes, computer-generated video clips, and immersive audio-visual simulations. data were collected from both expert ethicists (study 1) and lay participants (study 2). the results show that participants' moral judgments were consistently and strongly influenced by the character of the agent, whereas the effects of rule compliance and consequences were less robust. the mode of presentation (textual vs. audio-visual) significantly moderated these effects in mixed ways, suggesting that different formats may be better suited to conveying specific types of moral information. notably, study 1 revealed that expert ethicists tended to converge in their evaluations of low-stakes traffic scenarios, despite endorsing different moral theories. this convergence supports the feasibility of designing av decision-making algorithms based on shared ethical judgments. furthermore, the findings highlight that character-based considerations play a significant role in moral judgment of traffic scenarios—alongside deontological and consequentialist reasoning. frontiers in psychology

from “viewing” to “participation”: a study on the mechanisms underlying consumption behavior among sports streaming audiences background driven by both the strategy to build a sports powerhouse and the development of digital technology, china's sports broadcasting market has shown rapid growth. however, academic research has yet to systematically explore the underlying psychological mechanisms associated with the transition from “viewing” behavior to “participatory” consumption. objective drawing on a management psychology perspective, this study aims to construct and test a sequential mediation model to examine the associations among motivation for watching sports events, emotional responses, psychological belonging, and consumption behavior. methods a questionnaire survey was conducted among a sample of 563 chinese viewers with experience watching live sports broadcasting. established scales were used to measure motivation for watching sports events, positive emotional responses, psychological belonging, and consumption behavior. data analysis was performed using spss 26.0 (ibm corp., armonk, ny, usa) and amos 24.0 (ibm corp., armonk, ny, usa) software, and sequential mediation effects were examined using process macro model 6 and the bootstrap method. results the study found that: (1) motivation for watching sports events was positively associated with consumption behavior (β = 0.575, p < 0.001) and showed indirect associations with consumption behavior through the mediating roles of emotional responses and psychological belonging, with mediation effect sizes of 0.114 and 0.088, respectively; (2) emotional responses and psychological belonging showed a significant sequential mediating effect in the association between viewing motivation and consumption behavior (effect size = 0.032). specifically, viewing motivation was associated with positive emotional responses, which were further associated with psychological belonging and consumption behavior. conclusion this study supported the proposed “cognitive-emotional-identity-behavior” sequential mediation model and examined the psychological mechanisms underlying the association between “viewing” and “consumption.” the findings enrich the theoretical understanding of sports consumption behavior and provide practical insights for stakeholders in the sports industry regarding strategies to enhance viewers' emotional experiences and strengthen community belonging. frontiers in psychology

organizational cynicism and job burnout: a moderated mediation model of work alienation and leader-member exchange background in organizational management practice, understanding the intrinsic link between employees’ negative perceptions of the organization and their state of emotional exhaustion, as well as identifying the transmission mechanisms and boundary conditions, has become a key issue in mitigating the risk of job burnout. however, the mechanisms through which organizational cynicism relates to work alienation and job burnout, in addition to the moderating role played by the leader-member exchange in this relationship, still lacks clear theoretical explanations and empirical tests. method based on conservation of resources theory, this study developed a moderated mediation model to systematically examine the relationships among the variables. using convenience sampling in cross-sectional survey, this study collected valid questionnaire data from 658 employees across 27 enterprises (varying in ownership type and scale) and conducted regression analysis and moderating effect analysis using spss. results according to the results, organizational cynicism and job burnout were significantly positively correlated, and the indirect effect of organizational cynicism on job burnout via work alienation was statistically significant. the results of the moderation analysis indicated that leader-member exchange moderated the relationship between organizational cynicism and work alienation, as well as the relationship between organizational cynicism and job burnout, in a negative manner. in addition, employees’ job burnout differed across groups defined by gender, age, educational background, years of working, and weekly working hours. conclusion the research results provide theoretical basis and practical inspiration for organizations to identify high-risk groups and design stratified intervention strategies to alleviate the risk of job burnout. frontiers in psychology

exploring associations between positive psychological and school adjustment of efl learners using the perma framework: roles of coping style and negative emotions background positive psychology has been associated with students’ school adjustment, but the indirect associations underlying this relationship remain underexplored, particularly in efl learners. methods an online survey was conducted with 462 university students to examine the associations among positive psychology, coping style, negative emotion, and school adjustment. indirect and sequential indirect associations were examined using process model 6 in spss. results positive psychology was positively associated with school adjustment. significant indirect associations were observed through coping style (effect = 0.025, 95% ci [0.002, 0.052]) and negative emotion (effect = 0.152, 95% ci [0.095, 0.216]), accounting for 3.61 and 21.93% of the total association, respectively. the sequential indirect association involving coping style and negative emotion was also significant (effect = 0.025, 95% ci [0.011, 0.042]), accounting for 3.61%. conclusion these findings highlight the relevance of positive psychological resources, coping style, and emotional experiences to school adjustment among efl learners. they also provide potential directions for future research examining student support and intervention approaches, while causal or intervention effects cannot be inferred from the present cross-sectional data. frontiers in psychology

perceived correctional climate and suicidal ideation among inmates in nigerian correctional centres this study examined the relationship between perceived correctional climate factors (activity, emotional feedback, freedom, privacy, safety, social structure, and support) and suicidal ideation among inmates in nigerian correctional centres. using a descriptive, cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from a purposive sample of 210 inmates across two major correctional facilities in southern nigeria. the prison environment inventory (pei) was used to assess seven dimensions of correctional climate, while the beck scale for suicide ideation (bss) measured suicidal ideation. data were analyzed using pearson product–moment correlation and multiple linear regression. the results showed that correctional climate factors were jointly significantly associated with suicidal ideation, accounting for 48.3% of its variance, r 2 = 0.483, f (7, 202) = 26.94, p < 0.001. individually, more favourable perceptions of privacy ( β = −0.34, p < 0.001), safety ( β = −0.29, p < 0.001), and emotional feedback ( β = −0.22, p = 0.004) were significantly associated with lower suicidal ideation. institutional support ( β = −0.19, p = 0.015) and structured activities ( β = −0.14, p = 0.049) were also significantly inversely related to suicidal ideation, whereas perceived freedom and social structure were not statistically significant. the findings suggest that perceived correctional climate is significantly related to suicidal ideation among inmates, with privacy and safety emerging as particularly important environmental correlates. the study recommends integrating mental health screening with environmental and institutional measures that strengthen privacy, safety, support, and meaningful activities within correctional settings. frontiers in psychology

reallocating childhood physical activity and sedentary time and adolescent mental health: a compositional data analysis of the uk millennium cohort study background physical activity during childhood may promote mental health, but the effects of reallocating time between intensity zones on specific mental health dimensions remain poorly understood. to address this research gap, this study examined prospective associations between the composition of device-based physical activity at age 7 and multiple mental health outcomes at age 14 using a compositional data analysis (coda) framework that accounts for the constrained nature of daily time use. methods data were drawn from 5,145 children (48.1% boys) in the uk millennium cohort study. physical activity was measured using waist-worn actigraph gt1m accelerometers at age 7 and classified into sedentary behavior (sb), light-intensity physical activity (lpa), and moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (mvpa). mental health was assessed at age 14 using the parent-reported strengths and difficulties questionnaire (sdq). isometric log-ratio (ilr) transformed activity compositions were entered into linear regression models adjusting for baseline sdq at age 7 and sociodemographic covariates. compositional isotemporal substitution models estimated the predicted change in each sdq outcome associated with reallocating 15 min per day between activity types. all analyses were stratified by sex. conventional linear regression was conducted as a sensitivity analysis. results reallocating 15 min per day from lpa to mvpa was associated with fewer peer problems (delta = −0.050, p = 0.008). however, reallocating time from sb to mvpa was concurrently associated with higher hyperactivity (delta = 0.050, p = 0.002) and externalizing scores. sex-stratified analyses revealed that the associations with peer problems were more pronounced among boys (e.g., lpa to mvpa on peer problems: delta = −0.097, p < 0.001) and were absent in girls, a pattern supported by formal interaction testing ( p = 0.004). conventional regression yielded directionally consistent results. conclusion childhood physical activity composition is prospectively associated with adolescent mental health in a dimension-specific manner, with suggestive evidence of sex differences. modeled reallocation of time to mvpa was associated with more favorable peer-relationship and internalizing outcomes, particularly in boys, while associations with externalizing outcomes likely reflect reverse causality. these findings highlight the potential relevance of physical activity intensity for future longitudinal and intervention research on youth mental health. frontiers in psychology

the effect of project-based learning on students’ motivation in school-based physical education and behavioral intention toward sport participation: a theoretical and empirical perspective in educational sport contexts this study examined the association of project-based learning (pbl) with students’ motivation in physical education (pe) and behavioral intention toward sport participation within an integrated theoretical framework combining self-determination theory (sdt), constructivist learning theory, and social cognitive theory. a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design involved 120 secondary school students from eight intact classes, with four classes assigned to pbl ( n = 60) and four to traditional instruction ( n = 60). the 12-week intervention comprised structured sport-based pbl activities, whereas the control condition used predominantly teacher-centered instruction. intervention effects were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models (lmm) accounting for repeated measurements and class-level clustering, followed by a baseline-adjusted two-level parallel mediation analysis accounting for students nested within classes. significant group × time interactions favored pbl for overall motivation ( p < 0.001, d = 1.60), intrinsic motivation ( d = 1.67), identified regulation ( d = 1.35), and behavioral intention ( d = 1.48; all p < 0.001). significant group × time interactions were also observed for psychological needs satisfaction, including autonomy ( d = 1.72), competence ( d = 1.80), and relatedness ( d = 1.62), as well as self-efficacy ( d = 1.70; all p < 0.001). psychological needs satisfaction [ b = 0.21, 95% ci (0.04, 0.38)] and self-efficacy [ b = 0.16, 95% ci (0.02, 0.30)] showed significant indirect effects on post-intervention motivation, while the direct effect remained significant [ b = 0.29, 95% ci (0.04, 0.54)], with a total effect of b = 0.66, 95% ci (0.37, 0.95), a pattern consistent with significant indirect associations. because the mediators and outcome were assessed concurrently at posttest, these indirect effects should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of causal mediation. these findings indicate that pbl was associated with greater improvements in motivational and psychological outcomes and that psychological needs satisfaction and self-efficacy may represent complementary pathways linking pbl with students’ motivation toward pe and behavioral intentions toward continued sport participation. frontiers in psychology

stress recovery and restorative effects of viewing different types of peony garden landscapes: a preliminary experiment background substantial evidence supports the health benefits of urban green spaces, yet most studies focus on general landscapes, leaving a gap regarding specialized gardens with topographic variations (flatland, tableland, mountain land). this study explored the restorative effects of peony garden scenes with different topographic characteristics on students’ physical and mental health using virtual reality (vr) and the trier social stress test (tsst). methods participants ( n = 56 per group, 23 ± 1.5 years old) were exposed to flatland peony garden (fpg), terraced peony garden (tpg), mountainous peony garden (mpg), or indoor environment (ie). physiological factors were examined using heart rate (hr), heart rate variability (hrv), and electroencephalogram (eeg). psychological evaluation was carried out using the profile of mood states (poms) and state–trait anxiety inventory (stai). perceived restorativeness scale (prs) was used to assess subjective perceived recovery. results results showed that: (1) after tsst, hr, lf/hf, and beta significantly increased ( p < 0.01), while r-r, hf, and alpha decreased ( p < 0.01); (2) compared to the stress stage, viewing fpg, tpg, and mpg led to significant physiological changes ( p < 0.05), increased positive emotion (v-a, p < 0.01), and decreased negative emotions (a-h, f-i, t-a, c-b, d-d, anxiety, p < 0.01); (3) perceived recovery was associated with emotional states, reflected in greater feelings of “being away” and “fascination.” the most pronounced changes occurred in the mpg. conclusion in the current vr experiment, peony garden landscapes, especially those with abundant landscape elements and visual experience, exhibited therapeutic potential for short-term stress recovery compared with the windowless indoor office scene. the findings offer preliminary guidance for creating health-promoting peony garden landscapes. frontiers in psychology

how negative parenting relates to adolescents’ perceptions of older adults: the roles of empathy and intergenerational contact introduction grounded in social learning theory, this study examines how negative parenting practices are associated with adolescents’ perceptions of older adults and investigates the roles of empathy and intergenerational contact in this process. methods data were collected from 2,011 chinese adolescents using a three-wave longitudinal design. structural equation modeling was used to test the hypothesized relationships. results negative parenting was significantly associated with less favorable evaluations of older adults on both the warmth and competence dimensions. empathy mediated these relationships. intergenerational contact further moderated the association between empathy and adolescents’ perceptions of older adults. specifically, the indirect effects of negative parenting through empathy varied according to adolescents’ levels of intergenerational contact. discussion these findings highlight family socialization as an important developmental context for adolescents’ perceptions of older adults and identify empathy as a key socio-emotional mechanism linking parenting experiences to intergenerational cognition. frontiers in psychology

specific learning disorders and underlying processes: can wisc-iv subtests predict sld neurocognitive profiles in italian children aged 7–14 years? introduction specific learning disorder (sld) is studied via wisc iv, as well as via neurocognitive impairment profiles arising from clinical tests. however, state-of-the-art appears to be deficitary about the possibility of shared neurocognitive profiles within a given phenotype. objectives we aim to fulfil this gap by investigating, in sld, formal correlations between wisc iv subtests and nine impairment domains, with their own degrees of severity. participants and methodology 160 italian children, aged 7 to 14 years, have been divided in four groups (males vs. females; primary vs. lower secondary school); scores obtained in nine specific domains of abilities have been confronted versus wisc iv scales, using pearson r correlations, and obtaining 15 × 9 matrices for each group. results the most relevant correlations have been found in the primary-school group only, and in the female group only. the primary-school children presented a strong correlation of wmi with handwriting and reading. on the other hand, in the female group, mental calculation abilities correlated to several subtest indexes, such as: iq; vci; wmi. reading comprehension abilities also correlated to wmi. interpretations a possible explanation to neurocognitive profiles in females is represented by fronto-parietal networks: anomalies in gray-to-white matter ratio, in gray-matter depth, and in white-matter tracts appear to be typical of young females. results found in the primary-school group underline the developmental role of working memory in learning how to properly read and write. thus, specific phenotypic areas are implicated in deficitary neurocognitive networks affected in children with sld. frontiers in psychology

peripheral vision as a key factor for decision-making in soccer peripheral vision is critical for processing dynamic visual information in team sports such as soccer; however, yet little is known about how individual differences in peripheral visual field extent relate to decision-making efficiency under time pressure. this study investigated whether peripheral visual field size is associated with decision-making performance in soccer players while controlling for competitive level. forty male soccer players (age: 21.65 ± 3.92 years) completed a peripheral vision assessment using a blazepod system positioned at eccentricities ranging from 60° to 100°, while maintaining central fixation under eye-tracking control. decision-making performance was assessed using 22 video-based soccer scenarios (presented twice) that required rapid pass/no-pass decisions. a composite performance ratio integrating decision accuracy and decision time served as the primary outcome. partial correlation analyses, controlling for playing level, revealed a significant positive association between peripheral visual field extent and the performance ratio. this relationship was more strongly reflected in faster decision times, whereas the association with decision accuracy was weaker. these findings suggest that a larger peripheral visual field is associated with more efficient decision-making in soccer, largely due to reduced response times rather than improved accuracy. peripheral visual capacity may therefore contribute uniquely to perceptual-cognitive performance beyond competitive level and could represent a potential target for future training interventions in time-constrained sport settings. frontiers in psychology

what size and shape am i? background body image disturbance is conceptualised as arising from the interaction between perceptual and attitudinal components, yet the psychological complexity embedded within the attitudinal domain remains underexplored. this study tested an integrated model of perceptual, attitudinal, and interoceptive influences on women’s judgments of their own body size. methods in a sample of 269 adult women, behavioural measures of body size estimation were combined with network analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and regression modelling to distinguish psychological processes exerting direct versus indirect effects on self-estimated body size. results three central findings emerged. first, contraction bias in perceptual body size estimation was robustly replicated, with lower-bmi individuals overestimating and higher-bmi individuals underestimating their body size. second, attitudinal body image concerns independently shifted self-estimated body size upward across the bmi range, acting additively rather than interactively with contraction bias. third, the network and factor analyses demonstrated that attitudinal body image comprised four interconnected domains: body image, mood, interoceptive sensibility, and sociocultural pressure. we found important connections between body image and interoceptive sensibility facilitated by mood acting as a bridging intermediary. however, the regression analysis showed that only body image, not interoceptive sensibility, sociocultural pressure, or mood, exerted direct effects on self-estimates of body size. conclusion attitudinal body image is multidimensional in structure, but only the body image domain directly influences behavioural judgments of body size; interoceptive sensibility and other attitudinal factors operate indirectly within the broader body image system. the two-component perceptual–attitudinal model remains a powerful framework for explaining body size judgments, while network methods clarify how the contributing psychological processes are organised. frontiers in psychology

always connected, not always balanced: the double-edged effects of after-hours work connectivity behavior on work–family conflict among civil servants introduction drawing on the work–home resources model, this study examines the double-edged effects of work connectivity behavior after-hours (wcba) on work–family conflict (wfc) among chinese civil servants. methods we conducted a three-wave survey of 240 civil servants. the proposed parallel mediation and moderated mediation relationships were tested using regression-based analyses with bootstrapping. results wcba indirectly reduced wfc by facilitating work goal progress, while simultaneously increasing wfc by heightening workplace anxiety. public service motivation moderated both pathways. higher public service motivation weakened the positive relationship between wcba and work goal progress but strengthened the positive relationship between wcba and workplace anxiety. discussion the findings reveal that wcba can function as both a resource enabler and a stressor in public organizations. they extend the work–home resources model by identifying distinct resource-gain and resource-loss pathways and demonstrate that public service motivation may generate both beneficial and adverse consequences in an always-connected work environment. frontiers in psychology

rates and correlates of nightmares and insomnia in active duty military service members pre- and postdeployment. objective: this study aimed to determine the rates, chronicity, and correlates of nightmares and insomnia, alone and in combination, in u.s. army personnel at predeployment and postdeployment.
method: service members were assessed prior to (= 3,952) and following (= 1,762) a combat deployment between 2010 and 2016. participants were categorized predeployment into nightmare and insomnia groups using the ptsd checklist-military version distressing dreams item (item 2 score ≥ 3) and the insomnia severity index (total score ≥ 15). postdeployment, participants were further classified into 16 groups reflecting the combination of nightmare and insomnia trajectories.
results: predeployment, 12% of participants were in the nightmares only group, 9% were in the insomnia only group, and 11% were in the both nightmares and insomnia group. predeployment, the nightmares only group was older, had more deployments, and had greater mental health symptoms than the neither group. the insomnia only group had more deployments and greater mental health symptoms than the neither group. the both nightmares and insomnia group was more likely to identify as native american, be older, have more prior deployments, and have greater anxiety symptoms than all other groups. postdeployment, the new-onset trajectory, chronic nightmare trajectory, and chronic insomnia trajectory were generally related to higher posttraumatic stress disorder, anger, and anxiety symptoms compared with the remitted, no nightmares, and no insomnia trajectories.
conclusions: nightmares and insomnia, singularly and comorbid, are associated with mental health problems. transdiagnostic treatments that target both conditions may be an efficient means to ameliorate sleep problems and minimize effects on mental health. training through trauma: a multivariate analysis of burnout and associated factors among physician trainees in guatemala. objective: burnout is a pervasive occupational hazard in medicine, beginning early in training and linked to depression, suicide, medical errors, and attrition. while extensively studied in high-income countries, little is known from latin america. guatemala faces scarce mental health resources, social inequities, and limited residency regulation. this study aimed to characterize burnout, psychological distress, and moral injury among guatemalan physicians in postgraduate medical training ("residents").
method: we conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents in guatemala (september-october 2024). surveys included demographics and validated spanish-language instruments assessing burnout, depression, anxiety, stress, self-compassion, impostor syndrome, and moral injury. logistic regression identified demographic and occupational risk factors.
results: of 1,729 eligible residents, 589 (34.1%) responded; 504 (29.1%) completed surveys. respondents averaged 30.6 years; 54.5% were female, and 95.6% guatemalan. most trained at the university of san carlos (89.6%), with a minority at universidad mariano galvez and "other." distress prevalence was high: 83% reported high emotional exhaustion, 90% high depersonalization, and 95% low personal accomplishment. moderate-to-severe depression affected 32.7%, anxiety 40.7%, stress 49.2%, and impostor syndrome 41.2%. moral injury was nearly universal (89.3%). harassment and frequent 24-hr shifts were strongly associated with greater burnout, depression, anxiety, and stress. female and lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer+ residents reported higher exhaustion, stress, impostor syndrome, and lower self-compassion. mid-level trainees had an elevated risk of exhaustion.
conclusion: guatemalan residents face unprecedented levels of burnout and moral injury, exceeding global rates. modifiable factors, including harassment and workload, compound structural inequities. findings underscore the urgent need for residency reform, standardized protections, and culturally responsive mental health infrastructure. why humans use generative ai at work (whai-w): scale development and validation of a needs-based measure. although generative ai (genai) is now widely used at work, research has mostly focused on how often people use it or how they prompt it, rather than why they use it.we address this gap by introducing why humans use genai at work (whai-w), a new construct capturing three motives for genai use: utilitarian, hedonic-social, and hedonic-play.we developed and tested 15 whai-w items in two german samples of genai users in 2024 (sample 1: n = 355; sample 2: n = 162 employees using genai at work at least weekly).exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a three-factor structure.the final nine-item scale showed acceptable to good reliability and evidence of convergent, discriminant, criterion, and incremental validity.all three whai-w subscales predicted work engagement beyond need strength, and hedonic-social whai-w predicted momentary genai use beyond ai literacy and later genai use.whai-w offers a concise new way to explain differences in employees' motives for genai use and, potentially, its consequences. technology, mind, and behavior

symptom networks, developmental pathways, and intervention evidence for co-occurring anxiety and depression in children and adolescents: a scoping review anxiety and depression frequently co-occur in children and adolescents, but studies of their joint presentation use different units of analysis. this scoping review examined how those approaches connect and where evidence remains limited. we searched pubmed, web of science core collection, scopus, and apa psycinfo for english-language studies available from 2010 to 11 may 2026. we mapped 205 eligible studies across eight non-exclusive empirical themes and interpreted their distribution from a developmental perspective. study designs varied with the constructs examined. among 52 symptom-network studies, 37 analysed cross-sectional data and 15 used longitudinal or trajectory cohort designs. only 16 of 170 risk-factor studies also evaluated treatment outcomes. one symptom-network study linked network-derived findings to a neurobiological measure. developmental and geographical coverage was uneven. three studies were child-focused, and the united states and china accounted for 69.27% of the evidence. the descriptive global south aggregate accounted for 5.85%. these patterns identify priorities for longitudinal within-person research, developmental stratification, and studies linking symptom models to biological measures and intervention mechanisms. locally validated measures and research in underrepresented settings are needed to assess whether findings transfer across populations. research on child and adolescent psychopathology
