adaptation and validity of the chinese version of the bicycle rider behaviour questionnaire (brbq) and its associations with personality traits, cycling behaviours, and traffic crashes. this study conducted an initial psychometric evaluation of a translated and contextually refined chinese-language version of the bicycle rider behaviour questionnaire (brbq) and examined its associations with personality traits, cycling behaviours measured by the cycling behaviour questionnaire (cbq), and self-reported traffic crashes. a total of 482 regular cyclists aged 18-60 years from four geographical regions of china were randomly divided into two subsamples (= 241 each) for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. the analyses supported a 25-item, four-factor structure comprising traffic violations, notice failures, distracted behaviours, and control errors. cronbach's α coefficients ranged from 0.70 to 0.84. average variance extracted values exceeded 0.50, and htmt ratios were below the prespecified threshold, supporting convergent and discriminant validity. the brbq factors showed theoretically consistent associations with personality traits and cbq dimensions. all four brbq factors were associated with retrospective crash outcomes in bivariate analyses, whereas only traffic violations remained independently associated with crash involvement after adjustment for demographic and cycling-exposure covariates. overall, the findings provide preliminary psychometric evidence for the adapted chinese-language brbq and support further independent validation. behavioral sciences

beyond associations between color and emotion: a scoping review of task-based evidence on color properties, emotional attention, and cognitive control. color may influence emotional cognition through perceptual salience, learned affective meaning, and response compatibility, yet task-based evidence has not been synthesized. reported under the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (prisma) extension for scoping reviews (prisma-scr) and the prisma extension for reporting literature searches (prisma-s), we conducted a scoping review of experiments that varied color during emotional attention, cognitive control, or emotional information processing. five database groups were searched on 26 july 2026 and rerun as a pre-submission update on 17 august 2026; three completed citation-searching rounds were also used. independent screening yielded 299 included reports. full-text charting organized these reports into 294 study families and 4923 descriptive result rows. reported result directions varied across color properties, task roles, emotional materials, comparators, and response levels. most families contained detected and null results, while 44 internally conflicting rows were retained for descriptive analysis. although 569 rows from 43 families provided directly weightable effect estimates, no cluster met prespecified homogeneity criteria, so effects were not pooled. in applied settings, color sometimes changed gaze, local task performance, or affect, but transfer to beliefs, sustained attention, or general performance was inconsistent. this descriptive mapping does not establish a general performance benefit or impairment for any named color. conflict and inhibition paradigms rarely manipulated saturation or lightness independently, leaving a specific design gap in research on color and cognitive control. behavioral sciences

beyond self-blame: a qualitative study of the changing experience of parental guilt following the death of a child parental guilt is one of the most pervasive emotional responses following the death of a child and has been consistently associated with adverse bereavement outcomes. however, little is known about how bereaved parents experience and integrate guilt over time. this qualitative study explored the lived experience of parental guilt, its relationship with the cause of death, and the processes that facilitate its integration. semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 27 bereaved mothers and fathers and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. four themes were identified. first, the intensity and meaning of guilt differed according to the cause of death: sudden or potentially preventable deaths were associated with overwhelming self-blame, whereas anticipated deaths following illness elicited guilt related to caregiving and perceived inadequacy. second, guilt was experienced as a multidimensional process, including protective, caregiving, counterfactual, survivor, and parental identity guilt. third, participants retrospectively described changes in their relationship with guilt, from pervasive self-blame towards greater integration rather than complete resolution. finally, meaning reconstruction, peer support, professional psychological support, and self-compassion facilitated this process. these findings highlight parental guilt as a dynamic process shaped by the circumstances of the loss, with implications for tailored bereavement assessment and intervention. behavioral sciences

ai-assisted speaking practice and human-directed communicative readiness: survey and scenario evidence on anxiety, self-efficacy, and evaluation pressure generative artificial intelligence (genai) voice tools create low-risk opportunities for second-language (l2) speaking practice, but it remains unclear whether ai-assisted speaking practice is associated with human-directed communicative readiness and how this relationship varies across learners and evaluation contexts. study 1 analysed cross-sectional survey data from 708 english learners. greater ai-assisted spoken english behaviour (aisb) was associated with higher human-directed willingness to communicate (hwtc; β = 0.384) and lower foreign-language speaking anxiety (flsa; β = −0.416); flsa was negatively associated with hwtc when aisb was controlled (β = −0.325), yielding a positive statistical indirect association (0.127, 95% ci [0.079, 0.184]). speaking self-efficacy (sse) moderated the flsa–hwtc association, including an unexpected upper-tail crossover. demographic adjustment left the substantive pattern essentially unchanged, and an unmeasured latent method factor (ulmc) sensitivity analysis showed materially stable focal factor-score associations after accounting for a general method factor. study 2 used a 2 × 2 nonrandom scenario comparison (n = 726), in which participants imagined preparation with an ai voice assistant versus smartphone recording under formal evaluation versus no evaluation. ai-voice-assistant scenarios showed lower anticipated flsa and higher anticipated hwtc, whereas formal evaluation showed the opposite pattern; tool × evaluation interactions were significant for flsa (ηp2 = 0.032) and hwtc (ηp2 = 0.047). speaking-initiation tendency showed a different interaction pattern, indicating that hwtc and speaking-initiation tendency are not identical. the findings support a competence–affect–context account of ai-assisted speaking practice and human-directed communicative readiness, but they do not establish ai-specific causal effects or transfer to actual human speaking. behavioral sciences

well-being measurement in africa: a systematic review. the general narrative in well-being measurement is a lack of representation of instruments developed and validated in the african context. however, there is no existing review solely focused on africa that clearly demonstrates the extent of progress in the field and the current methodological challenges. the present study aims to systematically review and collate evidence on the validation of well-being measures in africa. following the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (prisma) method, a total of 64 research articles were reviewed. the study's findings showed steady growth in well-being measurement in the african context. however, this growth has not been without challenges that are stifling our general understanding and consensus on how well-being should be measured in africa. a persistent research gap is the development of new, contextually relevant measures of well-being. among the recurring methodological challenges were translation issues, poor model fit indices and the use of small samples. we recommend further testing of locally developed well-being measures and their incorporation into international surveys, as cross-country assessments can only yield meaningful insights when the items used adequately capture local experiences. translation of existing measures is key in accessing hard-to-reach populations, with such data informing clinical and community-based interventions. behavioral sciences

a network analysis of childhood psychological abuse and overgeneralized autobiographical memory in vocational high school students. overgeneralized autobiographical memory (ogm) has been linked to adolescent psychological difficulties. the car-fa-x model proposes that capture and rumination, functional avoidance, and impaired executive control contribute to ogm, and childhood psychological abuse may be embedded in these same processes.a total of 1364 vocational high school students completed measures of childhood psychological abuse, ogm, ruminative responses, experiential avoidance, cognitive avoidance, and executive-function difficulties. a 20-node gaussian graphical model was estimated using a nonparanormal transformation and ebicglasso. strength, expected influence (ei), bridge expected influence (bei), node predictability, bootstrap stability, node redundancy, sensitivity analyses, ogm-specific connectivity, and exploratory gender differences were examined.the primary network retained 98 of 190 possible edges. symptom rumination showed the highest ei (1.33), followed by intimidation (1.15), avoidance of threatening stimuli (1.12), and contextual elaboration (1.10). experiential avoidance had the highest bei (0.69), followed by symptom rumination (0.43) and working memory difficulties (0.40); however, experiential avoidance constituted a singleton community, making its ei and bei identical by construction. a complementary ogm-specific analysis showed greater direct connectivity with the ogm community for working memory difficulties (0.065) and symptom rumination (0.058) than for experiential avoidance (0.009). mean node predictability was r= 0.68 (range = 0.22-0.84), and strength, ei, and bei each showed a cs coefficient of 0.75. five potentially redundant pairs formed three components, and the resulting 15-node sensitivity network closely reproduced the primary findings. gender network structure and global strength did not differ significantly in the primary npn analysis (= 0.166 and= 0.314, respectively), and no edge survived fdr correction. a modest global-strength difference emerged only in the spearman sensitivity analysis (= 0.044).rumination, experiential avoidance, and working memory difficulties occupied prominent but distinguishable positions in the broader network. the findings are broadly compatible with car-fa-x but do not establish causal pathways, and the ogm-specific analysis cautions against interpreting general bridge centrality as direct connectivity with autobiographical memory. behavioral sciences

stars, stripes, and perceptions: examining the impact of the american flag on anticipated interactions. the american flag is often associated with patriotism, solidarity, and national allegiance; however, it may not uniformly signal inclusion for all americans. across three studies (= 1658), we examined whether the presence of the american flag in professional settings influences perceptions and anticipated interactions. black, latine, and white students viewed a zoom background depicting a professor's office containing an american flag (versus no flag or a sports team flag in study 1; versus no flag or an inclusive flag in study 2). across both studies, participants perceived the professor displaying the american flag as more racist, more sexist, and higher in social dominance orientation (sdo), and black/latine (vs. white) participants reported less comfort and interest in interacting with the professor. in study 3, we examined perceptions of the american flag in a workplace context. replicating the previous studies, both black and white participants viewed a coworker displaying the american flag (vs. no flag) as more racist, more sexist, and higher in sdo. across all studies, these effects were generally stronger among participants lower in sdo. together, these findings demonstrate how national symbols can shape anticipated interpersonal dynamics depending on perceiver identity and ideological orientation. behavioral sciences

dose–response associations between screen-based digital media use and anxiety in children and adolescents: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis screen-based digital media use is widespread in childhood and adolescence, but its association with anxiety and dose–response relationship remain uncertain. we systematically reviewed observational studies of participants aged 6–19 years reporting time- or frequency-based screen exposure and anxiety-specific outcomes. pubmed/medline, web of science core collection, scopus, and cnki were searched through september 2026. study quality was assessed using the ahrq checklist or newcastle–ottawa scale. eligible estimates were synthesized using three-level random-effects meta-analysis and restricted cubic splines. fifty-seven reports were retained. the primary adjusted dataset included 79 odds-ratio effects from 17 independent studies (pooled or 1.40, 95% ci 1.26–1.54; i2 = 51.7%). screen type significantly moderated the association after holm correction. the dose–response analysis included seven independent studies; the linear component was significant (p = 0.039), whereas nonlinearity was not supported (p = 0.132; wild-cluster p = 0.163). evidence was predominantly observational and cross-sectional, and dose–response data were limited. greater screen exposure was associated with higher odds of anxiety, supporting a graded pattern without a discrete threshold. because the evidence was predominantly observational and cross-sectional, this exposure–response gradient should be interpreted as an association rather than evidence that greater screen use causes anxiety; reverse and reciprocal pathways remain possible. this review was not registered and was funded by two jiangsu provincial education science planning projects. behavioral sciences

fun and balanced learning experience: students’ perceptions of serious games in higher education serious games offer a pedagogical alternative to mitigate the generational disconnect and demotivation in higher education. however, empirical research often evaluates single game interventions, leaving a gap in understanding general student perceptions rather than learning effectiveness. this study addresses this gap by evaluating the general perceptions of 1302 undergraduate students from 12 spanish and dutch universities regarding the pedagogical dimension of serious games based on their prior experiences using the validated fun and balanced learning experience scale (fable-s). findings show a positive perception of serious games, with students highly valuing interactivity of the contents, progressive difficulty and goal clarity, while remaining more critical of curriculum alignment and topic organization. furthermore, statistically significant composite-level differences emerged based on country, gender, area of knowledge, and frequency of play, although these group differences exhibited small effect sizes. a strong positive relationship was also found between perceived learning and motivation. in conclusion, this study positions serious games as positively perceived pedagogical tools based on student perceptions. behavioral sciences

family coresidence, parent–child interaction, and deviant behavior among rural chinese adolescents family coresidence can structure adolescents’ access to parental guidance, but evidence often separates living arrangements from parenting processes. we analyzed 3612 rural-hukou adolescents from 110 schools in the china education panel survey. deviant behavior was measured as a five-item summed score (5–25). primary ordinary least squares models used the untransformed score, school-clustered inference, and a core set of stable or plausibly pre-exposure covariates; expanded-control, log-outcome, multiple-imputation, item-level, and instrumental-variable models served as sensitivity analyses. exploratory coefficient-product models assessed parental supervision and parent–child communication as parallel indirect associations. in the primary binary model, not living with both parents was associated with a 0.312-point higher score (95% ci [0.114, 0.510]). in the four-category model, the clearest multiplicity-adjusted association concerned adolescents living with neither parent (b = 0.388, 95% ci [0.148, 0.628]); estimates for the two one-parent groups were less precise. multiple imputation supported the binary and neither-parent patterns. school-level instrumental-variable estimates were positive but imprecise and were interpreted as triangulation rather than causal identification. lower supervision and less frequent communication formed statistically detectable indirect associations, although the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal mediation. item-level analyses indicated that the composite association was not uniform across behaviors. the findings support a structural–process account while defining clear limits on causal and measurement interpretation. behavioral sciences

from pester power to purposeful co-shopping, a dual-pathway pls-sem model: the influence of children’s food purchases in urban india children increasingly shape family purchasing decisions, not merely respond to them. drawing on consumer socialization theory, this study examines how in-store promotions affect children’s “pester power”, their persistence in asking parents to buy products directly and through peer influence. it also asks whether proactive parental engagement can redirect this pattern toward positive, collaborative shopping instead of conflict. using pls-sem with survey data from 169 urban indian parents of children aged 5–12, the study produces three findings. in-store promotions are the strongest market driver of both peer influence and pester power. peer influence fully mediates advertising’s weaker, indirect effect on pester power, suggesting that market stimuli gain force mainly through social amplification among children’s peers rather than direct exposure alone. pester power, in turn, strongly predicts parent–child conflict over food purchases. third, and central to this study’s contribution, proactive parental engagement independently predicts positive co-shopping experiences, regardless of how much pester power a child exhibits. this suggests that parental engagement acts as a structural “circuit breaker,” not simply as a response to conflict. the findings also point to the need for marketers and regulators to look more closely at in-store promotional environments rather than advertising alone. supporting parental engagement may do more to encourage healthy family shopping experiences than trying to manage children’s demands after they arise. the implications for fmcg marketers, public health regulators, and family consumer educators in emerging-market contexts are discussed. behavioral sciences

social media use and psychological symptoms among older adults: sequential indirect associations through attitudes toward aging and basic psychological need satisfaction with rapid population aging, older adults’ psychological symptoms are a growing public concern. this cross-sectional study examined associations among social media use, attitudes toward aging, basic psychological need satisfaction, and psychological symptoms in 325 older adults recruited by convenience sampling in tianjin, china. eligibility was restricted to older adults who used at least one social media platform. participants completed self-report measures of the study variables. social media use was positively associated with attitudes toward aging and basic psychological need satisfaction and negatively associated with psychological symptoms. in a cross-sectional indirect-effects model, the direct association between social media use and psychological symptoms was not significant after attitudes toward aging and basic psychological need satisfaction were included. the indirect association through basic psychological need satisfaction was statistically significant, whereas the indirect association through attitudes toward aging alone was not. the sequential indirect association involving attitudes toward aging and basic psychological need satisfaction was consistent with the hypothesized model, but the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causality. these findings suggest potential psychosocial correlates linking social media use with psychological symptoms among older social media users and highlight directions for future longitudinal research on healthy aging in digital contexts. behavioral sciences

trauma, hyperarousal, and sleep: neurobehavioral pathways in affective disorders sleep disturbances are common across affective disorders and may coexist with traumatic stress and persistent hyperarousal. this narrative review examines how trauma-related hyperarousal and sleep dysfunction are associated with major depressive disorder (mdd) and bipolar disorder (bd), while distinguishing observed associations from proposed mechanisms. a targeted search of pubmed, scopus, and google scholar identified clinical, neurobiological, and translational literature on trauma, hyperarousal, insomnia, nightmares, circadian disruption, mdd, and bd. the evidence supports a multidimensional view of hyperarousal involving partly overlapping autonomic, cognitive–attentional, affective, and behavioral domains; however, it does not establish hyperarousal as a unitary mechanism or justify equating trauma-related vigilance with manic activation. sleep disturbance may function as a symptom, vulnerability factor, or prodromal change, but no single sleep measure is currently a validated individual-level prognostic marker. clinically, trauma history, sleep phenotype, affective state, comorbidity, medication effects, and current safety should be assessed jointly. cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia and established trauma-focused treatments have the strongest clinical basis within their indicated populations, whereas imagery rehearsal therapy, prazosin, chronobiological strategies, and candidate biomarkers require diagnosis-specific and evidence-graded interpretation. longitudinal studies integrating objective sleep measures and explicit temporal modeling are needed before proposed pathways or precision approaches can be considered clinically validated. behavioral sciences

initial psychometric evaluation of the problematic use of generative artificial intelligence scale among chinese school students. generative artificial intelligence (gai) is increasingly used by school students, yet validated instruments for assessing problematic gai use (pugai) in this population remain scarce. this study evaluated the psychometric properties of the problematic use of generative artificial intelligence scale (pugais) in a large school-based sample of chinese students. a cross-sectional survey included 19,484 students in grades 4-9 who had used gai. the sample was randomly split for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. internal consistency, measurement invariance across sex, school type, and developmentally defined age groups, concurrent validity, latent classes, and a preliminary threshold were also examined. following item refinement, the 8-item pugais (pugais-8) showed a dominant one-factor structure, although confirmatory model-fit evidence was mixed. the scale showed high internal consistency (cronbach's α = 0.940) and measurement invariance of item thresholds and factor loadings across sex, school type, and age groups. ordinal sensitivity analyses indicated that the item-reduction results were partly sensitive to analytic treatment, although the pugais-8 showed a more favorable overall structural fit than the original 10-item specification. a substantial floor effect indicated limited differentiation at the lower end of the construct. pugais-8 scores were positively associated with depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, insomnia symptoms, and short-video addiction (r = 0.365-0.413, all< 0.01). latent class analysis identified a high-score subgroup (7.2%), and an exploratory roc analysis yielded an internally derived descriptive threshold of 20.5. overall, the findings provide initial psychometric support for the pugais-8 as a brief measure of pugai among chinese school students, while indicating the need for independent replication of the item-reduction findings and further evaluation of its measurement properties and proposed threshold. behavioral sciences

teachers’ ai belief profiles and their associations with ai use, pedagogical applications, and barriers: a person-centered analysis of talis 2024 teachers’ beliefs about the utility and risks of artificial intelligence (ai) may shape ai-related practice, yet these beliefs are often treated as a single attitude and practice as simple use. this study used a person-centered approach to identify configurations of ai utility and risk beliefs and examine their associations with ai use, pedagogical applications among users, and barriers among non-users. data were drawn from 40,680 lower-secondary teachers across 49 education systems in talis 2024. following fixed-alignment assessment of approximate measurement invariance, latent profile analysis, r3step, and posterior-probability-weighted comparisons were conducted. four profiles emerged: indifferent (6.13%), skeptical (21.41%), measured endorsement (56.29%), and risk-aware strong endorsement (16.18%). ai-related professional learning was most consistently associated with profile membership. reported ai use ranged from 12.8% in the indifferent profile to 76.3% in the risk-aware strong endorsement profile, which also showed the highest rates across all eight pedagogical applications. among non-users, pedagogical reservations were most prevalent in the indifferent and skeptical profiles, knowledge-and-skills constraints in the measured endorsement profile, and both knowledge-and-skills and resource constraints in the risk-aware strong endorsement profile. these findings show that distinct belief configurations correspond to meaningful heterogeneity in ai-related practice and support profile-sensitive professional learning and institutional support. behavioral sciences

longitudinal associations and gender-stratified patterns in adolescents’ emotional and behavioral problems—based on a cross-lagged panel network model adolescence is a critical period characterized by heightened emotional and behavioral challenges, profoundly impacting young people’s social adaptation and future development. previous research has predominantly employed traditional latent variable analysis to examine factors associated with emotional and behavioral problems, with less attention to the underlying symptom-level structure and prospective associations of these problems. this study utilized longitudinal data from the china family panel studies (cfps) collected in 2018 (t1) and 2022 (t2). it combined contemporaneous network analysis with cross-lagged panel network analysis (clpn), employing the 14-item adolescent problem behavior measure included in the cfps to examine contemporaneous and prospective symptom-level associations among emotional and behavioral problems in adolescents and to compare gender-stratified networks. the study included 1082 adolescents (mean age at t1 = 12.09 ± 1.54), with boys accounting for 54.5%. in the contemporaneous networks, worry about finishing homework (i10) had the highest expected influence at both waves, although other highly connected nodes differed across networks. in the clpn, worry about having someone to play with at school (i11) and sadness (i7) had the highest out-expected influence (o-ei) values, whereas difficulty paying attention (e4) and being easily distracted (e6) had the highest in-expected influence (i-ei) values. permutation tests did not provide evidence of significant between-gender differences. the findings provide a symptom-level perspective on contemporaneous and prospective associations among adolescent emotional and behavioral problems and identify symptom areas for further longitudinal and intervention research. behavioral sciences

social support and prosocial tendencies among chinese university students: parallel indirect associations through future self-continuity and positive empathy in the context of cultural change in china, an important developmental question is how attention to one’s own future relates to a willingness to benefit others. this cross-sectional study examined parallel indirect associations through future self-continuity and positive empathy in 4087 students from three universities in jiangxi province, china. analyses adjusted for four demographic covariates and used percentile-bootstrap confidence intervals. social support showed a positive total association with self-reported prosocial tendencies (β = 0.313). specific indirect associations were positive through future self-continuity (b = 0.0057, 95% ci [0.0047, 0.0067]) and positive empathy (b = 0.0077, 95% ci [0.0066, 0.0089]), and a positive direct association remained. an exploratory comparison retaining future self-continuity found a larger indirect association through positive than negative empathy. these findings suggest that connections with the future self and responses to others’ positive experiences provide complementary perspectives on the association between social support and prosocial tendencies. behavioral sciences

the relationship of cyberchondria, negative affect, and anthropometric indices with heart-rate variability among health sciences students: a psychophysiological study of digital health-information behavior background: we examined whether cyberchondria was associated with resting heart-rate variability (hrv) in health sciences students. methods: in this cross-sectional study of 600 students in türkiye, we assessed cyberchondria using the 12-item cyberchondria severity scale (css-12), negative affect using the 21-item depression anxiety stress scales (dass-21), self-reported screen exposure, anthropometry, and five-minute resting hrv. the root mean square of successive differences (rmssd) was the primary physiological outcome. a hierarchical model entered demographics, waist-to-height ratio, and physical activity, then screen exposure and anxiety, followed by css-12. results: css-12 correlated inversely with rmssd (r = −0.412). after covariate adjustment, css-12 was associated with lower rmssd (β = −0.256; p < 0.001), adding 4.9% to explained variance (final adjusted r2 = 0.272). waist-to-height ratio showed a smaller inverse association (β = −0.087). overall, the four-factor css-12 model fit was good; comparisons between academic programs were unadjusted and exploratory. conclusions: higher css-12 scores were associated with lower resting rmssd after adjustment for measured general anxiety and total screen exposure. health anxiety was not measured; therefore, the model cannot determine whether this association reflects cyberchondria-related behavior, overlapping health anxiety, or other unmeasured psychological and physiological factors. prospective studies incorporating validated health-anxiety assessment and detailed digital-behavior and hrv measures are needed. behavioral sciences

examining the benefits of spaced retrieval practice on transfer and the student experience in the classroom spaced retrieval practice is a learning strategy whereby information is retrieved multiple times with each retrieval attempt separated by a time gap. we conducted a semester-long classroom intervention to investigate the benefits of spaced retrieval practice on memory and transfer. each week, students engaged in three, spaced learning practice sessions (lpss) during which they either answered multiple-choice (mc) questions about that week's course content (retrieval practice) or were shown the mc questions with the correct answer selected (restudy). three weeks after the last lps, participants completed a final mc test comprising (1) repeated questions from the lpss, (2) transfer questions that had the same answer options as corresponding lps questions and queried related topics, but had different correct answers, or (3) new questions about lecture content. a typical retrieval practice effect was observed for repeated questions (retrieval > restudy). although we did not observe a transfer effect on overall final test accuracy (related = new), further exploratory analyses that used purer measures of transfer revealed evidence of both positive and negative transfer. furthermore, retrieval practice (vs. restudying) contributed to an enhanced student experience (greater sense of mastery, motivation, and attentional control, and reduced anxiety). memory
mitigating short-form video addiction through table tennis: testing the role of attentional processes in a randomized controlled trial international journal of sport and exercise psychology

the role of parental expressed emotion and loss-specific parental responses in children’s loss-related outcomes following traumatic loss: a mixed-methods observational study abstract there is a growing body of literature on the impact of parenting on bereaved children’s psychological outcomes. most studies focus on broad, positive parenting (e.g., warmth). research on parental expressed emotion (ee) (i.e., lack of emotional support, increased intrusiveness, irritation, and criticism) and loss-specific parental responses (e.g., parental positive or negative appraisals associated with the loss or lost person) remains limited. this study explored how parental ee and loss-specific parental responses relate to children’s loss-related outcomes (i.e., prolonged grief, depression, and posttraumatic stress (pts), and health-related quality of life (hrqol)) in the context of traumatic loss. twenty parent-child dyads that lost a close person in a traffic accident participated (youths were 8–18 years ( mdn = 13.50), 55% lost a parent). parents completed the level of expressed emotion questionnaire. loss-specific parental responses – appraisals and coping strategies – during a 20-minute parent-child interaction about the loss were coded. children’s loss-related outcomes were assessed using interview-based self-report ratings. we hypothesized that increased parental ee and negative loss-specific parental responses would be associated with worse outcomes in children, while positive loss-specific parental responses would show the opposite pattern. bayesian kendall’s τ correlations showed that parental criticism was positively associated with children’s depression and pts, and that positive loss-specific appraisals were negatively associated with children’s depression and hrqol. although the small scale of the study warrants caution in interpretation, the findings suggest that parental criticism may be harmful, while loss-related positive appraisals seem beneficial for certain loss-related outcomes. journal of child and family studies

building stability: a home-visiting financial education supplement to enhance family well-being abstract the earned income tax credit (eitc) access project delivered intensive, one-on-one home visiting in combination with financial empowerment and education surrounding the eitc in the state of michigan. given prior research demonstrating an inverse association between eitc receipt and adverse childhood experiences, the present qualitative study examined parents’ perceptions of the program and its potential impact on promoting family well-being through financial empowerment. semi-structured interviews were conducted with 32 parents of children aged between one and 16 years old. participants were asked a series of questions regarding their uptake of the eitc and changes in their financial circumstances, focusing on what ways it may have impacted their family and their parenting. thematic analysis revealed multiple areas of family well-being were enhanced through the eitc access project, including social connection, family-focused purchases, stress management, family cohesion, shared financial knowledge and values, and multigenerational financial empowerment. these findings suggest that increasing access to the eitc and providing financial education, in combination with evidence-based home visiting, may address immediate financial needs as well as longer-term family well-being through the development of financial knowledge and parental empowerment. journal of child and family studies

understanding the profound influences of nonviolent adverse childhood experiences, loneliness, and emotion regulation strategies on psychological distress in established adulthood journal of adult development

fitness-related instagram use and physical activity participation: a cross-sectional examination of the roles of physical activity information seeking and exercise self-schema among emerging adults social media is a source of health information for young people, including topics related to physical activity (pa). in the present study, we investigated whether fitness-related instagram (ig) use was associated with pa participation. we also explored whether exercise self-schema (i.e. viewing oneself as an exerciser and considering it important to one’s self-image) and pa information seeking moderated this relationship. higher fitness-related ig use was associated with more pa (moderate-to-vigorous pa: β = 0.31; total pa: β = 0.20). pa information seeking was associated with moderate-to-vigorous pa (β = 0.15), but did not moderate the relationship between fitness-related ig use and pa. for people with an exercise self-schema, fitness-related ig use was not associated with pa. for people without an exercise self-schema, pa participation was positively associated with fitness-related ig use ( β = 0.20). we discuss findings including how social media may be used to encourage pa participation among people without an exercise self-schema. journal of health psychology

the yoga mat divide: how racial identity and media prototypes shape black women’s willingness to practice yoga offers psychological benefits including improved well-being and relaxation. while participation is rising—with one in three u.s. adults having tried yoga—black individuals remain underrepresented in yoga media and have lower participation rates than other racial/ethnic groups. utilizing social identity theory and the prototype willingness model, this experimental study examined how racial centrality and prototype similarity affect black women’s willingness to engage in yoga. a sample of 105 u.s.-based black cisgender women (ages 18–40) completed surveys before and after viewing images of black or white yoga practitioners. similarity significantly predicted willingness ( β = 0.42, p < 0.001) and positive attitudes ( β = 0.34, p < 0.001). when viewing only white practitioners, willingness was highest when perceived similarity was high and racial centrality was low. findings highlight the importance of diverse representation to promote yoga engagement among black women. journal of health psychology

exploring the lived experience of food insecurity through the camera lens: a photo elicitation study healthy eating remains unattainable for many due to limited access to affordable, nutritious foods. in the united kingdom, over 11% of the population is estimated to be food insecure. this study explored the lived experiences of adults living with food insecurity and examined how these experiences shape their dietary health behaviours. using a photo-elicitation approach, food insecure adults ( n = 9) photographed their food environments. the photos were used to guide semi-structured interviews which were transcribed and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. participants viewed healthy foods as inaccessible, causing reliance on cheaper, more calorie-dense options. participants observed increasing food insecurity among people in full-time employment and described food bank support as inconsistent and often complicated by stigma. findings illustrate the multidimensional nature of food insecurity, influenced by economic hardship, limited food environments, and social change. policy responses must address structural barriers and enhance the accessibility and dignity of food support. journal of health psychology

developing and prioritising a recovery capital framework for emerging adults with drug addiction in malaysia this two-round modified exploratory delphi study identified and prioritized recovery-capital dimensions perceived as salient for emerging adults with drug addiction in malaysia. in round 1, 18 professionals and people with lived recovery experience provided open-ended responses that were thematically synthesized into six dimensions: identity reconstruction in emerging adulthood, recovery-oriented healthcare capital, cultural and religious resources for recovery, family-centered recovery capital, supportive social environments and stigma resilience, and structural reintegration and social stability. ten participants (55.6% retention) independently ranked the dimensions in round 2. identity reconstruction in emerging adulthood and family-centered recovery capital ranked highest. rankings showed statistically significant but limited concordance, kendall’s w = .259, χ 2 (5) = 12.971, p = .024. the framework is a preliminary, contextually grounded synthesis of expert and experiential judgments; it does not establish a validated hierarchy, causal effects, or population-level priorities. emerging adulthood

the role of resilience and ruminative tendencies on emerging adults’ mental health outcomes resilience is consistently linked to better mental health among emerging adults. however, less is known about the psychological processes that may explain this association, particularly in lower-middle-income contexts. this study examined whether ruminative brooding and reflection help explain associations between resilience and symptoms of depression and anxiety among 1,709 filipino emerging adults (mean age = 21.86, sd = 2.83) during the covid-19 pandemic. confirmatory factor analyses supported the measurement models, and structural equation modeling tested direct and indirect associations while controlling for gender, age, and educational attainment. resilience was negatively associated with both brooding and reflection. however, only brooding was positively associated with depression and anxiety. resilience was also indirectly associated with lower depression and anxiety through reduced brooding, but not reflection. these findings suggest that resilience may support mental health partly by limiting maladaptive brooding, highlighting resilience-building and brooding-focused strategies as potentially useful during periods of heightened stress and uncertainty. emerging adulthood

fitting in: exploring the relationship between recovery status, loneliness, and sense of belonging on mental health functioning among college students college students in recovery from alcohol and other drugs find themselves within a developmental and institutional context that often normalizes substance use, creating distinct challenges to recovery maintenance and social integration. this article examines differences in mental health symptoms by levels of belonging and loneliness among college students in recovery. latent class analysis yielded three classes within the sample: disconnected ( n = 581); mixed connection ( n = 1,073); and connected ( n = 850). significant differences were observed between classes on measures of anxiety and depression, with the disconnected class reporting the highest levels and the connected class reporting the lowest levels. given that sense of belonging was observed as moderate to high in this sample, results suggest loneliness may play an important role in understanding mental health among college students in recovery. recommendations related to findings and study limitations are discussed. emerging adulthood

the first year at work: a three-wave longitudinal study of short-term changes in the big five traits among emerging adults personality—particularly the big five traits—shapes how emerging adults adapt to work, yet while longer-term personality development across emerging adulthood is well documented, far less is known about short-term changes during the transition into the first year of employment. using a three-wave longitudinal design, we examined changes in the big five traits in 397 japanese university graduates ( m age = 22.19) across their first year at work. latent growth modeling showed significant decreases in self-reported extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness. higher pre-employment organizational desirability was associated with a more favorable initial profile—lower neuroticism and higher extraversion and conscientiousness—but did not predict the rate of change in any trait. these findings identify the first year of employment as a period of meaningful change and highlight the value of a short-term perspective complementing long-term approaches. whether these changes reflect genuine trait development or shifts in self-perception remains an open question. emerging adulthood

hypnosis using cognitive rehabilitation versus mindfulness suggestions on working memory and therapeutic alliance in patients in alcohol treatment. excessive alcohol use can impair working memory, potentially hindering treatment outcomes. suggestion-based cognitive rehabilitation (sbcr), a hypnotic technique of potential benefit for restoring working memory in brain injury patients, may hold promise for alcohol use disorder (aud). this randomized controlled trial compared sbcr-hypnosis to mindfulness-based hypnosis among individuals in aud treatment. forty-one participants who were at an inpatient facility were randomized to four weekly sessions of either intervention. pre- and post-intervention assessments included working memory, well-being, alexithymia, abstinence confidence, and therapeutic alliance. three-month follow-ups assessed relapse, abstinence confidence, and mental health. analyses included repeated measures anova, recurrent event regression, and structural equation modeling informed by factor analysis. no significant between-group differences emerged. however, both groups showed improved well-being. exploratory analysis identified a latent therapeutic improvement factor influenced by trait absorption. structural equation modeling revealed that sbcr-hypnosis predicted greater therapeutic alliance improvement, which further predicted reduced relapse, enhanced abstinence confidence, and improved mental health. although sbcr-hypnosis was not superior on clinical aud outcomes, it may uniquely enhance therapeutic alliance, a potential mechanism worth exploring in future studies. international journal of clinical and experimental hypnosis

mindful hypnotherapy intervention for well-being in older adults: a mixed-methods randomized clinical trial this randomized controlled trial examined the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of a mindful hypnotherapy intervention (mhi) integrating positive psychology suggestions to enhance well-being in older adults. sixty-two community-dwelling adults aged 60–95 years were randomized to mhi, non-hypnotic relaxation, or wait-list control. the four-session intervention combined hypnotic induction, guided imagery, and suggestions targeting gratitude, savoring, self-compassion, acceptance, positive relationships, hope, and optimism, followed by post-hypnotic cues to support self-practice. outcomes included happiness, life satisfaction, affect balance, and psychological distress; semi-structured interviews explored participants’ subjective experiences. a multivariate analysis controlling for baseline scores revealed a significant overall treatment effect, f(8, 104) = 2.88, p = .006, partial η2 = .18. compared with controls, mhi participants reported higher happiness, life satisfaction, and affect balance, and lower distress. qualitative findings indicated increased calmness, gratitude, emotional regulation, and perceived interpersonal benefits. the findings provide preliminary support for hypnosis as a potential medium for delivering strengths-based psychological content associated with resilience and well-being. the mhi demonstrated feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary benefits, supporting further investigation in larger, more rigorously controlled trials. international journal of clinical and experimental hypnosis

the dark side of honorio delgado. honorio delgado is an esteemed figure associated with psychiatry and psychology in peru and latin america, for his contributions to psychoanalysis, the pharmacological treatment of some mental illness, the publication of journals, the organization and participation in academic events, the publication of research and books of great impact, and so forth. however, many of the historiographical works on his life and work have had an apologetic nature, neglecting aspects of his life that present us a dark side of this character. the objective of this article is to analyze briefly the various aspects that have been negatively observed in honorio delgado by people who have known him directly, as well as various documents that support such claims. (psycinfo database record (c) 2026 apa, all rights reserved). history of psychology

psychometric properties of the turkish version of the musical activity and well-being scale: a methodological study from türkiye this study aimed to examine the validity and reliability of the turkish version of the musical activity and well-being scale. this methodological study was conducted with 424 adults engaged in musical activities at either amateur or professional levels. following the world health organization’s translation and back-translation protocol, the scale was adapted into turkish and evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency analyses, and correlations with related measures. the findings supported the original five-factor structure of the scale and provided evidence for construct validity. internal consistency analysis indicated excellent overall reliability (α = .93). in addition, meaningful relationships with measures of musical impact and psychological well-being offered further support for validity. overall, the results suggest that the turkish version of the musical activity and well-being scale is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing music-related well-being. the scale provides a valuable tool for research and practice in music psychology, education, and health contexts. psychology of music

rtms mitigates simulated spaceflight‐induced emotional dysfunction through vegfr‐2‐mediated neuroprotection abstract purpose repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rtms) has shown potential in mitigating emotional deficits induced by extreme environments, such as those encountered during spaceflight. however, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. this study investigates the role of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (vegfr‐2) in mediating the therapeutic effects of rtms in a mouse model of simulated space composite environment (ssce). method 10 hz rtms treatment was initiated after the last two weeks of ssce exposure and continued for the remaining 2 weeks. throughout the rtms treatment period, the vegf receptor antagonist su5416 was co‐administered via intraperitoneal injection. finding behavioral tests revealed that vegfr‐2 inhibition abolished the beneficial effects of rtms on depressive‐ and anxiety‐like behaviors, as measured by the tail suspension, forced swim, sucrose preference, and elevated plus maze tests. furthermore, su5416 blocked rtms‐induced improvement in social skills. at the cellular level, vegfr‐2 antagonism impaired axonal integrity in the prefrontal cortex. conclusion these findings suggest that vegfr‐2 signaling is critical for the neuroprotective and behavioral benefits of rtms under simulated spaceflight conditions, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for emotional regulation in extreme environments. brain and behavior

analysis of the mediating role of cytokines in the relationship between nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and cognitive impairment after ischemic stroke abstract objective to explore whether nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (nafld) is associated with poststroke cognitive impairment (psci) and to investigate the mediating role of cytokine levels. research methods this study included 247 patients with ischemic stroke. the subjects were divided into no‐to‐mild and moderate‐to‐severe groups according to the severity of nafld. the levels of peripheral blood cytokines and the scores of the montreal cognitive assessment scale (moca) were measured for all subjects. the scale scores and cytokine levels were compared between the two groups, and the correlations among nafld, cytokines, and cognitive function were analyzed. results compared with those in the no‐to‐mild group, the levels of il‐1β, il‐6, il‐10, and tnf‐α in the moderate‐to‐severe group were significantly higher, while the moca score was significantly lower. multivariate linear regression analysis indicated that the nafld grade could significantly affect the moca score and the levels of il‐1β and tnf‐α. mediation analysis revealed that the level of tnf‐α significantly mediated the relationship between nafld and cognitive function, with a mediation effect size of 0.36. conclusion elevated tnf‐α levels may be a key intermediate factor in the development of psci in patients with nafld. the prevention and treatment of nafld and the inhibition of the peripheral inflammatory response may lead to new targets for early screening and intervention in psci. brain and behavior

natural history and factors influencing 90-day clinical outcomes and 1-year recurrence of thalamic stroke. objective: to investigate the natural course of cerebral small vessel disease (csvd) manifested as pure thalamic infarction (pti) and identify predictors of 90-day clinical prognosis and 1-year recurrent major adverse cardiovascular/cerebrovascular events (mace).
methods: this retrospective cohort study analyzed 251 consecutive thalamic infarction patients admitted between january 2016 and may 2024. participants were classified into pti (n = 187) or combined-type thalamic infarction (cti, n = 64). primary endpoints included poor 90-day clinical prognosis (modified rankin scale [mrs] ≥ 2) and 1-year mace (composite of stroke, acute myocardial infarction, and cardiovascular death). intergroup comparisons utilized pearson chi-square or mann-whitney u tests, with variables showing p ≤ 0.10 in univariate analysis entered into multivariate logistic regression models.
results: compared with cti, pti patients demonstrated lower baseline national institutes of health stroke scale (nihss) scores (median 1 vs. 3, p < 0.001) and reduced prevalence of atrial fibrillation (2.7% vs. 12.5%), intracranial artery stenosis (icas; 48.1% vs. 76.6%), and early neurological deterioration (24.6% vs. 56.3%; all p < 0.05). the 90-day poor prognosis rate was significantly lower in pti (4.8% vs. 20.3%, p < 0.001), whereas 1-year mace rates did not differ between groups (12.3% vs. 15.6%, p = 0.497). among pti cases, territorial distributions comprised inferolateral (80.2%), tuberothalamic (13.4%), paramedian (including percheron artery, 5.9%), and posterior choroidal arteries (0.5%). tuberothalamic artery infarctions exhibited higher cognitive impairment rates (36.0%) than other subgroups. multivariate analysis identified baseline nihss as an independent predictor of 90-day poor prognosis (or = 1.634, 95% ci 1.152-2.320, p = 0.006), while icas was associated with 1-year mace (or = 3.908; 95% ci, 1.188-12.849; p = 0.025) in pti patients.
conclusion: pti presented favorable short-term outcomes, consistent with initial stroke severity, yet carried a 12.3% annual mace risk, particularly in patients with coexisting icas. these findings underscore the importance of addressing intracranial stenosis in secondary prevention strategies for csvd. brain and behavior

altered inter‐network functional integration underlies speech impairment in parkinson's disease: a resting‐state fmri analysis abstract background speech impairment is common in parkinson's disease (pd) and lacks effective clinical interventions due to poorly understood underlying mechanisms. therefore, this study aimed to explore the relationship between altered brain functional networks and speech impairments in pd, identifying neural correlates of abnormal brain activity linked to pd‐related speech disorders (sd). methods baseline clinical characteristics, neurobehavioral assessments, and resting‐state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs‐fmri) data were collected from three groups: pd individuals with sd (pd‐sd group), pd individuals without sd (pd‐non‐sd group), and healthy controls (hc group). independent component analysis (ica) was performed to identify resting‐state networks (rsns) using the group ica of fmri toolbox (gift) implemented in matlab. functional network connectivity (fnc) was subsequently quantified by calculating pearson correlation coefficients between the extracted rsns. one‐way analysis of variance (anova) was used to assess group differences in fnc, followed by post hoc pairwise comparisons for networks showing significant effects. given the reported association between speech impairment and cognitive impairment in pd, correlation analyses were further performed to investigate the relationships between fnc alterations and clinical measures, including speech performance and cognitive function assessed by the montreal cognitive assessment (moca). results significant differences in fnc were observed between the left frontoparietal network (lfpn) and auditory network (aun) across the three groups ( p = 0.0280). in particular, the fnc between lfpn and aun was significantly stronger in the pd‐sd group compared to the pd‐non‐sd group ( p = 0.0221) and the hc group ( p = 0.0047). spearman correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlation between lfpn‐aun functional connectivity and unified parkinson's disease rating scale part iii (updrs‐iii) speech subscores ( r s = 0.2624, p = 0.0466), as well as a significant negative correlation with moca scores ( r s = −0.2847, p = 0.0249). conclusion this study identifies disrupted functional connectivity between the lfpn and aun in individuals with pd‐sd. these findings suggest that altered integration of rsns involved in motor, cognitive, and auditory processing may contribute to speech impairment in pd. hyperconnectivity between lfpn and aun may thus serve as a neural substrate for speech impairment in pd. specifically, increased connectivity between the lfpn and aun may represent a neural signature associated with speech dysfunction in pd. these results provide potential mechanistic insights and highlight candidate neural targets for future neuromodulation strategies aimed at improving speech function. brain and behavior

improving video‐based prediction of cerebellar ataxia severity using a pretrained deep learning model abstract background ataxia severity in degenerative cerebellar diseases (dcds) is usually assessed with semi‐quantitative clinical rating scales such as the scale for the assessment and rating of ataxia (sara), which are subject to variability. deep learning‐based gait analysis offers an objective alternative, but labeled data in dcds are limited. we investigated whether pretraining on gait videos from patients with parkinson's disease (pd) could improve sara score prediction in dcd. methods gait videos from patients with dcd were processed using pose estimation, and the extracted time‐series keypoint coordinates were input to a transformer‐based model. separate models were developed for the sara total score and the posture and gait subscore (sum of items 1–3). models were pretrained on pd gait videos by supervised learning with the movement disorder society–sponsored unified parkinson's disease rating scale (mds–updrs) part iii axial subscore or by self‐supervised masked keypoint reconstruction. performance was evaluated by leave‐one‐participant‐out cross‐validation (mean absolute error [mae], coefficient of determination [ r 2 ]), and between‐model differences by participant‐level wilcoxon signed‐rank tests and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (cis). results we analyzed 75 patients with dcd and 141 with pd. for the sara total score, mae and r 2 were 1.91 ± 0.06 and 0.78 ± 0.01 with supervised pretraining, 1.95 ± 0.04 and 0.77 ± 0.01 with self‐supervised pretraining, and 2.04 ± 0.07 and 0.74 ± 0.02 with training from scratch; neither strategy significantly reduced participant‐level prediction error ( p = 0.25 and 0.24). for the posture and gait subscore, only supervised pretraining significantly reduced prediction error (mean difference: −0.078; 95% ci: −0.127 to −0.031; p = 0.003). conclusions pretraining on pd gait data modestly reduced sara prediction error, reaching statistical significance for the posture and gait subscore with supervised pretraining. pretraining across neurological disorders may help models acquire transferable representations of pathological gait, but its clinical significance requires validation in larger, multicenter datasets. brain and behavior

repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with median nerve electrical stimulation for severe traumatic brain injury abstract background severe traumatic brain injury (stbi) often leads to prolonged coma and poor neurological outcomes. noninvasive neuromodulation techniques such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rtms) and median nerve electrical stimulation (mns) have shown potential in promoting arousal. however, the efficacy of combining these two approaches remains unclear. methods in this randomized controlled trial, 86 patients with stbi‐induced coma were assigned to rtms ( n = 29), mns ( n = 29), or combination therapy ( n = 28) for 4 weeks. outcomes included awakening efficacy, eeg grading, cerebral blood‐flow parameters (vm, vd, vs, pulsatility index [pi]), gcs, and moca. safety events were recorded. results at week 4, the combination group demonstrated significantly higher overall awakening efficacy (92.86%, 26/28) compared with the rtms (65.52%, 19/29) and mns (62.07%, 18/29) groups ( p < 0.05; number needed to treat [nnt] ≈ 4 for combination vs. mns). gcs scores improved significantly within all groups (all p < 0.05), with the greatest mean change observed in the combination group (baseline 5.19 ± 0.62 → week 4: 11.23 ± 1.12; δ+6.04), followed by mns (δ+4.50) and rtms (δ+4.19); between‐group differences favored combination therapy ( p < 0.05). eeg grading shifted toward lower‐severity categories in all groups, with the combination group achieving the highest proportion of grade i–ii normalization at week 4 (71.4%, 20/28) compared with rtms (62.1%, 18/29) and mns (37.9%, 11/29). transcranial doppler–derived cerebral blood‐flow velocities (vm, vs, vd) increased and the pulsatility index decreased across all groups, with the combination group demonstrating the most pronounced hemodynamic improvement relative to either monotherapy (all p < 0.05). in an exploratory analysis restricted to patients who regained sufficient responsiveness to undergo cognitive testing (combination: 26/28 [92.9%]; rtms: 19/29 [65.5%]; mns: 18/29 [62.1%]), moca scores at week 4 indicated mild‐to‐moderate cognitive impairment across all groups (combination: 21.35 ± 2.87; rtms: 18.74 ± 3.26; mns: 18.22 ± 3.41), with numerically highest scores in the combination group; however, given the differential testability rates—which corresponded directly to awakening status—these findings are subject to inherent selection bias and should be interpreted as hypothesis‐generating only. no seizures were observed throughout the study period. adverse events were infrequent and did not differ significantly among groups (combination: 10.7%; rtms: 20.7%; mns: 27.6%; all pairwise p > 0.05), with rates numerically lowest in the combination group. conclusions in patients with severe traumatic brain injury and persistent coma, rtms combined with right mns significantly improves awakening efficacy, neurophysiological indicators (eeg grading), and cerebral hemodynamics compared with either modality alone. gcs improvement was greatest with combination therapy. exploratory cognitive findings (moca in testable subsets) suggest potential additional benefits, though these require confirmation in future trials employing outcome instruments applicable to all randomized patients. adverse event rates were low across all groups, with no seizures observed; the study was not powered for formal safety comparisons. these findings support the dual‐pathway neuromodulation paradigm as a promising strategy for consciousness recovery in stbi and warrant confirmation in multicenter, sham‐controlled trials with extended follow‐up. brain and behavior

modelscompete4 : an r package for comparing nested and non-nested structural equation models modelscompete4：用于比较嵌套与非嵌套结构方程模型的r包 modelscompete4 is an r package for comparing nested and non-nested structural equation models (sem). it streamlines the entire workflow by fitting a named list of model syntax strings, automatically detecting nesting relationships using parameter names and free-parameter counts, and applying the appropriate statistical test—likelihood ratio test for nested pairs and vuong test for non-nested pairs. unlike existing tools, it natively supports latent variables, handles any number of models simultaneously, and returns a comprehensive structured output including fit indices and a pairwise comparison matrix. bootstrapped standard errors and parallel processing are also supported. the package is freely available on github and cran. structural equation modeling-a multidisciplinary journal

effects of positive or negative reinforcement history and extinction arrangement on resurgence abstract the recurrence of previously reduced behavior following successful differential reinforcement has been termed resurgence . across studies, resurgence has occurred following either positive or negative reinforcement, but no direct within‐experiment comparisons have been conducted. the primary purpose of the current experiments was to address this gap by comparing resurgence following a history of positive or negative reinforcement with human participants responding to earn or avoid losing money. across experiments, we manipulated the arrangement of the resurgence test following negative reinforcement; money losses were discontinued in experiment 1 and made inescapable during experiment 2. avoidance responding persisted after the discontinuation of monetary loss during experiment 1, precluding comparisons of resurgence. conversely, unavoidable monetary losses resulted in greater resurgence relative to discontinuation of monetary earnings during experiment 2. the present experiments provide the first controlled within‐subject comparisons of resurgence following positive and negative reinforcement and show that the form of extinction affects avoidance responding. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

the early childhood curiosity questionnaire: development and psychometric properties in the united kingdom, the netherlands, and germany 幼儿好奇心问卷：在英国、荷兰和德国的开发与心理测量学特性 curiosity in early childhood is associated with exploration, learning, and cognitive growth, yet little is known about how trait curiosity can be reliably assessed in preschoolers. this paper reports the development and validation of a caregiver-report measure designed to assess curiosity in children aged 2-5 years across three cultural contexts: the united kingdom, the netherlands, and germany. pursuing three objectives, we (1) generated 41 age-appropriate items by adapting and extending the infant and toddler curiosity questionnaire (itcq; altmann et al., 2025a), first in english, followed by dutch and german translations; (2) examined the factor structure in each country independently (sample sizes: uk = 398; nl = 330; de = 540), discarded poorly fitting items, and integrated the results to produce a single, 25-item questionnaire comprising three subscales (novelty, investigative, and interactive curiosity); and (3) evaluated the reliability and validity of the final instrument within each national sample to assess its performance across cultural contexts. psychometric analyses indicated strong internal consistency, coherent relations with other validated measures, and evidence of cross-cultural applicability. the resulting questionnaire, a direct continuation of the previously developed infant version, enables systematic assessment of young children's curiosity as a multidimensional construct observable in everyday life. journal of personality assessment

common inclusive identity as a prevention against anti-muslim responses to threat: the roles of personal control and political orientation / la identidad común inclusiva para prevenir una respuesta anti islámica a la amenaza: el papel del control personal y la orientación política personal threat perceptions increase outgroup prejudice, potentially as an effort to restore a threatened sense of control through one’s ingroup. according to group-based control theory, personal threat effects on non-muslims’ prejudice toward muslims should disappear when muslims are perceived as part of the ingroup. we tested this in two experiments among non-muslim germans (total n = 1,141). we manipulated the salience of high (vs. low) threat to personal control and whether muslims were framed as outgroup or part of the (diverse superordinate) ingroup in the context of an imagined conflict with radical islamists. contrary to our preregistered hypothesis, the predicted two-way interaction of threat × categorization was not supported in either study. exploratory analyses indicated that framing muslims as part of the ingroup (vs. outgroup) increased left-wing, but not right-wing, participants’ anti-muslim prejudice under high (vs. low) threat (study 1). exploratory analyses also revealed that muslims as part of the ingroup (vs. outgroup) framing reduced conservatives’ anti-muslim prejudice under high threat (study 2)—however, only among those reporting that the russian–ukrainian war did not change their image of germany. conservatives’ anti-muslim responses to threat may not be unconditional but could be eliminated by mentally including muslims in diverse ingroups. international journal of social psychology

the influence of resilience and perceived social support on life satisfaction among teacher trainees with visual impairment in selected teacher education colleges of the amhara region, ethiopia abstract this study investigated the influence of resilience and perceived social support on the life satisfaction of trainees with visual impairment. a cross-sectional survey design within a quantitative research approach was employed. a total of 105 trainees with visual impairment were selected through comprehensive sampling from six purposively selected teacher education colleges. data were collected using structured questionnaires. descriptive statistics, pearson’s correlation, and multiple regression analysis were used to analyze the data. results revealed that both resilience ( r = .574, p < .001) and perceived social support ( r = .349, p < .001) had significant positive relationships with life satisfaction. furthermore, the multiple regression analysis indicated that resilience (b = 0.899, p < .001) and perceived social support (b = 0.142, p < .001) were significant predictors, jointly explaining 37.3% of the variance, with resilience accounting for a larger proportion (33%) than perceived social support (4.3%). the study concludes that resilience and perceived social support are important psychosocial resources associated with higher life satisfaction among trainees with visual impairment, with resilience demonstrating a comparatively stronger predictive contribution. it recommends that teacher education colleges implement programs to foster resilience and strengthen social support networks to enhance students’ life satisfaction. discover psychology

social–emotional ability and relationship satisfaction in marriage: the roles of partner consensus and commitment abstract although social–emotional abilities may support couple functioning, less is known about how they covary with relational appraisals relevant to couple therapy. using cross‐sectional self‐report data from 2139 married adults in the united states, this study estimated a structural equation model linking social–emotional ability, perceived partner consensus, dedication commitment, and relationship satisfaction. the gender‐adjusted model included 2137 participants. social–emotional ability was positively associated with perceived consensus. consensus was positively associated with commitment and satisfaction, and commitment was positively associated with satisfaction. the direct association between social–emotional ability and satisfaction was not significant after accounting for consensus and commitment. specific indirect associations through consensus alone and sequentially through consensus and commitment were statistically significant. because all constructs were assessed concurrently by one spouse, the findings do not establish temporal mediation or couple‐level processes. the results identify perceived consensus and commitment as potentially relevant domains for assessment and future longitudinal, dyadic research. journal of marital and family therapy

the couple relationship skills inventory: is there added benefit of partner's report? although many established measures assess individuals' relationship skills, relatively few incorporate reports from both partners to predict relationship functioning at the individual and couple levels. the couple relationship skills inventory (crsi) is a multidimensional measure of seven relationship skill domains developed using a racially and economically diverse sample. the current study extended the crsi by incorporating partner-reports of the focal individual's relationship skills and evaluated whether the self- and partner-report version (crsi-sp) improved prediction of relationship quality. using a large community sample (n = 2785), bayesian confirmatory factor analysis supported the 45-item, 13-factor measure. the crsi-sp demonstrated good psychometric properties, including reliability, discriminant validity, and measurement invariance across gender and relationship status. the crsi-sp explained more variance in individual- and couple-level relationship quality than the original crsi, supporting improved predictive utility. the crsi-sp can provide researchers and practitioners with a practical measure for assessing relationship skills and evaluating couple-focused interventions. journal of marital and family therapy

cdcatr: an r package for developing and evaluating cognitive diagnosis computerized adaptive tests cdcatr：用于开发与评估认知诊断计算机化自适应测验的r包 the cdcatr package, initially released on cran in 2020 and periodically updated to incorporate recent developments, provides functions for implementing and evaluating cognitive diagnostic computerized adaptive testing (cd-cat) procedures. the package incorporates a variety of item selection strategies and stopping criteria. it also provides functions for generating item banks and response data under different cognitive diagnosis models. in addition, the package includes tools to support item bank calibration and model comparison at the item level. overall, cdcatr provides a flexible framework for conducting cd-cat research and evaluating its performance using either empirical or simulated data. applied psychological measurement

towards a sequencing framework for teaching and using self-enactable behaviour change techniques: a conceptual review and proposed approach objective: self-enactable behaviour change techniques (bcts) may help individuals initiate and sustain health behaviour change. however, existing taxonomies provide limited guidance on how such techniques should be selected, taught, combined, and sequenced over time. this perspective aimed to review previous approaches and to develop a conceptual framework for organising and sequencing self-enactable bcts for intervention design and participant learning. methods: a critical conceptual review was conducted to identify published approaches to bct grouping, temporal organisation, prerequisites, and stage-specific sequencing. literature identified through four databases was synthesised alongside the compendium of self-enactable bcts to inform a five-step framework-development process. results: the review showed that existing taxonomies and sequencing approaches provide useful classifications but limited guidance for progressive teaching and self-enactment. to address this gap, we proposed a framework comprising 108 self-enactable bcts organised into nine clusters and 27 groups. we mapped prerequisite relations, classified techniques by their predominant prospective or reactive function, and sequenced their groups across the model of action phases. conclusion: our framework provides a theory-informed structure for teaching and applying self-enactable bcts. it is intended to guide intervention design and generate testable hypotheses about technique sequencing that need to be empirically explored in future studies. psychology & health
