the mediating role of post-traumatic growth in the relationship between post-traumatic stress disorder and psychological well-being this study aimed to analyze the mediating role of post-traumatic growth in the relationship between post-traumatic stress disorder and psychological well-being among nursing students after the kahramanmaraş earthquake. this study, which was a descriptive cross-sectional design, included 345 participants (201 female and 144 male). it used the descriptive characteristics questionnaire form, the post-traumatic stress disorder checklist for dsm-5, the post-traumatic growth inventory, and the psychological well-being scale to collect the research data one year after the kahramanmaraş earthquake. the mediating role of post-traumatic growth in the relationship between post-traumatic stress disorder and psychological well-being was tested using hayes' process macro model 4. the findings showed that post-traumatic growth significantly mediated the relationship between post-traumatic stress disorder and psychological well-being (indirect effect = .158, 95% ci [.114, .207], k² = .30). furthermore, post-traumatic stress disorder was negatively associated with psychological well-being, whereas post-traumatic growth was positively associated with psychological well-being. the mediation effect was of medium magnitude, indicating that post-traumatic growth partially buffered the negative impact of post-traumatic stress disorder on psychological well-being. in general, the study findings significantly contributed to the body of literature since they revealed that, even a year later, post-traumatic stress disorder negatively affected psychological well-being; however, post-traumatic growth positively predicted psychological well-being. moreover, this study is among the first to demonstrate the buffering role of post-traumatic growth in mitigating the negative impact of post-traumatic stress disorder on psychological well-being one year after a major earthquake. these findings underscore the importance of implementing both coping-focused and growth-oriented interventions to promote long-term psychological well-being among earthquake survivors. psychological reports

beyond conventional coaching: the role of transitional information in guiding athlete attentional search for adaptive performance in contemporary coaching, verbal augmented information (feedback and instruction) remains a widely used, but inconsistently applied tool for directing athletes’ attentional search to improve their performance. coaches often overlook how augmented information may be used to guide athletes’ search for functional solutions within dynamic performance environments. feedback is typically delivered either concurrently (during an action) or terminally (after an action), often in the form of error correction aimed at reproducing idealized movement solutions. this position paper draws on an ecological dynamics rationale to help coaches become more effective in their use of verbal augmented information. this paper presents the transitional learning model (tlm) as an applied framework that integrates and extends existing approaches to instruction, feedback, and practice design. within this model, coaches may use clues, challenges and questions, priming athletes to attune to affordances available in their performance environment. this approach aims to promote athletes to search, discover and exploit functional movement solutions within the performance environment. tlm may be applied concurrently or terminally, with transitional information functioning to guide the athletes’ ongoing search activities for their next action in a performance environment. the tlm is proposed as a conceptual framework and requires further empirical investigation through applied and in-situ research designs to examine its effectiveness in supporting athlete learning. perceptual and motor skills

effects of gamified physical activity on sensory integration dysfunction in primary school children this study investigated the effects of a gamified physical activity intervention on sensory integration ability and physical fitness in children aged 6–7 years with sensory integration dysfunction. forty first-grade students from a primary school in china, were randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. the intervention group participated in a 12-week gamified exercise program conducted twice per week for 60 min per session, while the control group attended regular physical education classes. pre- and post-intervention assessments were conducted for both sensory integration and physical fitness. repeated measures anova revealed significant interaction effects for vestibular function, tactile defensiveness, and proprioception (all p < .001), but not for learning ability ( p = .794). chi-square analyses indicated a significant improvement in the recovery rate of vestibular function ( p < .001), whereas tactile defensiveness, proprioception, and learning ability showed no significant changes ( p = .281, p = .178, p = .985, respectively). additionally, repeated measures anova demonstrated significant interaction effects for the 50-m sprint, one-minute rope skipping, and one-leg stance with eyes closed (all p < .001), but not for standing long jump or sit-and-reach ( p = .070, p = .868). these findings suggest that gamified physical activity interventions can produce significant improvements in both sensory integration ability and physical fitness among first-grade children with sensory integration dysfunction. perceptual and motor skills

glycemic regulation and teacher-reported behaviors in students with type 1 diabetes mellitus youth with type 1 diabetes mellitus (t1dm) are at elevated risk for emotional and behavioral challenges. although psychosocial screening is recommended as part of diabetes care, teacher perspectives have been largely overlooked. this study examined the associations between glycemic metrics, using continuous glucose monitoring (cgm), and teacher-reported behavior. participants included 92 students with t1dm (mean age = 13.46 years; 46.70% female, 48.90% minority). teachers completed the behavior assessment system for children, second edition, teacher rating scales (basc-2 trs). glycemic data included mean glucose, time in range, time above/below range, glycemic variability, and hemoglobin a1c (hba1c). higher mean glucose, reduced time in range, and greater glycemic variability were significantly associated with more teacher-reported internalizing symptoms and school problems. glycemic variability was also associated with more externalizing behaviors and lower adaptive functioning. subscale and content scale analyses revealed associations between glycemic variability and behavioral challenges, such as difficulties with attention, learning, emotional regulation, and executive functioning. hba1c was not significantly related to any behavioral outcomes. cgm metrics were more strongly associated with teacher-reported school behaviors than hba1c. findings highlight the value of teacher input in t1dm research to better understand how glycemic patterns relate to classroom functioning. journal of applied school psychology

patients with amnestic mild cognitive impairment are compromised in temporal order memory. introduction: temporal disorientation is frequently reported in amnestic mild cognitive impairment (amci), yet empirical evidence on temporal order memory in ecologically valid contexts remains scarce. the present study examined temporal order memory in patients with amci using a paradigm that captures the temporal organization of everyday activities.
method: twenty-six patients with amci and 36 healthy older controls underwent a comprehensive neuropsychological assessment and completed the temporal order memory for everyday events (tomee) task. differences in temporal order memory performance between the two groups were analyzed using a general linear model. immediate and delayed recall were assessed, and temporal order memory was analyzed using the total number of items evoked, items evoked in the correct position and in the correct sequence. indexes of ordinal positioning and of sequential clustering were calculated. associations between temporal order indexes and episodic memory and executive functioning were explored using correlational analyses.
results: patients with amci recalled fewer items overall than controls. participants evoked more items in the immediate recall condition than in the delayed free recall condition. significant differences were also found in the total number of items evoked, items evoked in the correct position and in the correct sequence. an interaction between group and temporal order measures showed that amci patients were disproportionately affected in recalling items in the correct temporal order. the index of sequential clustering was lower in patients with amci. temporal order indexes correlated positively with an episodic memory measure (logical memory delayed recall) and negatively with the time of an executive function test (trail making test b).
conclusions: patients with amci show deficits in temporal order memory for everyday events that extend beyond general episodic memory impairment. alterations in the ability to organize and retrieve temporal sequences may indicate cognitive vulnerability at early stages of neurodegenerative disease. journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology

mapping global research trends in art therapy for psychological distress: a bibliometric analysis abstract background art therapy is a psychological intervention that boosts emotional expression, enhances self‐awareness and has increasingly been employed within mental health settings to alleviate psychological distress. although extensive research has examined the art therapy interventions for reducing psychological distress, little is known about its bibliometric mapping. method accordingly, this study aims to identify emerging research trends in the use of art therapy for psychological distress components through a bibliometric analysis. we retrieved 935 articles that met the inclusion criteria published between 1980 and 2025 in wos core collection. results results show that annual scientific production has increased, especially in recent years. the results also show that the cooperation between the united states and israel is the most intensive, that the united states is the most productive country in terms of research trends, that haifa university is the most productive institution and that arts in psychotherapy is the most preferred journal. the co‐occurrence analysis findings revealed six primary thematic clusters: art therapy, cancer, stress, trauma, mindfulness and anxiety (items = 30, links = 189, total link strength = 1000). thematic map results indicated that anxiety, depression, stress and trauma topics were basic, structuring themes. thematic evolution results indicated that earlier studies mainly focused on health issues associated with cancer and medical problems; emerging topics expanded to incorporate general mental health problems including depression, anxiety, emotional regulation, psychological well‐being and refugee's problems. conclusions results indicate a sustained and expanding scholarly interest in the role of art therapy in psychological distress components. counselling & psychotherapy research

balance - imbalance: toward a systemic understanding of life distress despite extensive research efforts, biomedical psychiatry has struggled to provide sufficiently valid, reliable and comprehensive explanations for life distress. this has contributed to increasing international calls for broader and more contextual approaches to mental health. in this article, i propose as systemic and practice-informed framework for understanding life distress in terms of relationships, pattern, meaning and context. drawing on systems theory, feedback-informed clinical practice and contemporary critiques of diagnostic psychiatry, the article introduces the balance-imbalance model as a heuristic framework for understanding distress as emerging within complex and interacting systems rather than isolated pathological entities. the article situates itself within ongoing debates concerning biomedical, ecological, phenomenological and relational approaches to mental health. rather than presenting distress as evidence of underlying disease categories, the proposed framework conceptualizes imbalance as a dynamic process arising through interactions between biological, psychological, relational, social and cultural factors. healing is correspondingly understood as processes through which individuals and their environments may move toward more sustainable forms of balance. a clinical case example is used to illustrate how a systemic and contextual understanding may open alternative pathways for understanding and responding to severe distress beyond diagnostic categorization. the balance–imbalance model is presented not as a universal explanatory theory, but as a conceptual and clinical orientation intended to support more holistic, collaborative and context-sensitive approaches to mental health practice. the article discusses implications for clinical work, research, education and policy development, and argues for greater integration of lived experience, relational knowledge and practice-based evidence within mental health services. nordic psychology

how self-efficacy beliefs shape learning preferences: pre-service preschool teachers’ learning with online teaching video cases / cómo las creencias de autoeficacia influyen en las preferencias de aprendizaje: aprendizaje de futuros docentes de educación infantil mediante el uso de casos de vídeo para la enseñanza en línea self-efficacy beliefs are essential for pre-service preschool teachers (ppts) to navigate their future teaching challenges. while teacher educators often use online teaching video cases (otvcs) to provide authentic classroom scenarios, there is limited research on how ppts’ self-efficacy levels shape their specific learning preferences. this study investigated the learning preferences of 744 ppts regarding their demands for otvc content, use scenarios, facilitators, and targeted developmental dimensions, comparing differences across low, medium, and high self-efficacy groups. the results revealed significant disparities. teachers with high self-efficacy prioritized autonomous, peer-collaborated learning using modeled videos to refine holistic teaching competencies and classroom management. in contrast, teachers with medium and low self-efficacy preferred structured, expert-guided video case studies focused on mastering foundational knowledge and skills, reflecting a greater need for external scaffolding. these findings echo bandura’s self-efficacy theory and demonstrate that belief systems influence learning preferences. teacher preparation programs should move beyond a one-size-fits-all model and tailor otvc design to ppts’ self-efficacy levels, adopting psychologically informed strategies to ensure equitable and impactful learning for future educators. studies in psychology

regional disparities and impact of mental health literacy on help-seeking intention among chinese rural and urban adolescents: an empirical study. background: mental health literacy plays a crucial role in shaping adolescents' help-seeking intentions. however, regional disparities, specifically between rural and urban areas, in mental health literacy and help-seeking intentions, and their interrelationships, remain underexplored among chinese adolescents.
objective: this study aims to investigate the potential rural-urban differences in mental health literacy and help-seeking intentions and further examine the potential impact of mental health literacy on help-seeking intentions among chinese adolescents.
methods: junior high school students (urban: 70; rural: 70) aged 13 to 16 years were randomly selected as participants. the adolescent mental health literacy assessment and modified general help-seeking questionnaire were employed to measure mental health literacy and help-seeking intentions, respectively. covariance and-tests were utilised to analyse regional differences. pearson's correlation and multiple linear regression were conducted to explore mental health literacy's impact on help-seeking intentions.: adolescents from the urban site exhibited significantly higher mental health literacy than those from the rural site, whereas differences in formal and informal help-seeking intentions were not significant after covariates were considered. preferences for help-seeking resources varied descriptively, with urban adolescents favouring mental health counsellors and the rural group favouring teachers. specific dimensions of mental health literacy predicted both professional and non-professional help-seeking intentions.
conclusion: findings highlight a significant rural-urban difference in adolescents' mental health literacy, while formal and informal help-seeking intentions were not significantly different after controlling for covariates. specific aspects of mental health literacy partially predicted help-seeking intentions, emphasising the importance of targeted mental health education and developmental factors, such as age, in promoting effective help-seeking. journal of child and adolescent mental health

inclusion that excludes: rethinking the ecological model for mental disability through defensive dynamics, institutional power, and capital asymmetries. this article offers a critical reworking of ecological and social-ecological models as applied to intellectual and developmental disabilities, autism, and severe mental illness. drawing on a qualitative synthesis of 18 studies, we show that ecological frameworks are predominantly used as descriptive mapping devices, that power and inequalities enter analyses in partial and fragmented ways, and that intersystemic connections often generate formally inclusive yet experientially exclusionary arrangements. to address these limitations, we propose an integrated ecological model for mental disability, which retains bronfenbrenner's multilevel architecture but introduces four structural extensions: asymmetry of reciprocity in the microsystem, the defensive mesosystem, capital-modulated exosystemic permeability, and the performative and normalizing exosystem. these concepts integrate bourdieu's theory of capital and field, foucault's genealogy of,and group psychoanalysis, and they are grounded in recurrent patterns observed across school transitions, family-service relations, residential services, and autism employment programs. the framework has implications for research designs that move beyond barriers and facilitators for multilevel clinical and educational interventions, and for normative debates on relational justice and psychopolitical validity in mental-disability policy. perspectives on psychological science

integrating multicriteria analysis and economic valuation to assess nature-based water reuse systems (life renaturwat). the new urban wastewater treatment directive (eu) 2024/3019 introduces a substantially more stringent regulatory framework by extending its scope to all urban agglomerations of at least 1000 population equivalents, in response to evidence showing that small agglomerations contribute significantly to pressure on approximately 11% of the european union's surface water bodies-a source of pollution not fully addressed by previous regulations. against this background, this study assesses a nature-based treatment upgrade implemented at two wastewater treatment plants (wwtps) in the province of valencia (spain): carrícola and los monasterios. in both plants, the secondary effluent is further treated in constructed wetlands filled with aluminium-rich drinking water treatment sludge, enhancing phosphorus removal while integrating circular economy principles into the urban water cycle. to capture and monetise the resulting environmental and social benefits, the amuvam-anp framework was applied. the framework combines a panel of 12 multidisciplinary experts, who assess the interdependencies among ecosystem services, with an economic valuation that monetises non-market benefits using a pivot value of €1.09/m, corresponding to the market price of drinking water supply in spain. water availability emerged as the dominant service, accounting for 33.27% of total relevance. by category, overall relevance was distributed across provisioning (42.23%), fauna and flora (25.84%), cultural (22.54%), and regulating services (9.40%). over a 25-year horizon, the systems generate substantial economic benefits, estimated at approximately €242,200 for carrícola and €880,726 for los monasterios, with benefit-cost ratios of 6.6-7.5 that remain above unity even under conservative scenarios. by making benefits such as biodiversity enhancement and climate mitigation explicit, the approach provides a transparent and replicable economic basis for decision-making and supports the scalability of sustainable and resilient wastewater treatment models for small populations facing water stress. environmental science and pollution research international

social media use modalities and self-esteem among saudi youth and middle-aged adults: a community-based cross-sectional study. introduction: this study aimed to assess the levels and patterns of social media use among saudi adolescents and middle-aged adults, evaluate associations with self-esteem and identify which usage modalities (image-based, comparison-based, belief-based, consumption-based) are differentially linked to low self-esteem.
methods: a cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 600 saudi participants aged 14-50 years. the questionnaire included demographic and lifestyle items, medical history, the rosenberg self-esteem scale (rses) and the social media use scale (smus). logistic regression models assessed predictors of low self-esteem and comparison-based use.
results: participants reported high social media engagement, with 68.5% using it over 4 hours per day. comparison-based and consumption-based modalities were most frequent. low self-esteem was observed in 16.2% of participants and independently predicted by younger age (or=0.96, 95% ci 0.92 to 0.99), low socioeconomic status (or=3.00, 1.45 to 6.19), mental health history (or=2.02, 1.15 to 3.53), unhealthy diet (or=2.10, 1.01 to 4.34) and high comparison-based use (or=4.93, 2.58 to 9.43). moderate and high snapchat use were associated with lower odds of low self-esteem. comparison-based use was further associated with unhealthy diet, low spirituality, thyroid disorders and >8 hours of daily use.
conclusion: comparison-based social media use is a strong and independent predictor of low self-esteem, underscoring the importance of analysing usage patterns over mere frequency or platform type. these findings support the need for targeted interventions focusing on at-risk modalities of social media engagement. the results hold implications for youth-focused digital literacy, mental health prevention strategies and culturally informed psychosocial support in the saudi context. bmj public health

performance optimization-focused family behavior therapy to address verbal and physical aggression in an adolescent diagnosed with bipolar i disorder: a case report bipolar disorder is chronic and debilitating; characterized by fluctuations in mood that significantly interfere with day-to-day functioning. while symptom onset typically occurs in early adulthood, manifestations can occur at earlier developmental stages. existing research has shown that coordinated specialty care early treatment programs (csc etps) are effective in reducing both short- and long-term negative outcomes in individuals with serious mental illness, including schizophrenia. however, detailed descriptions of how these programs are implemented and evaluated in practice remain limited. this is a case report of an adolescent client, blake, diagnosed with dsm-5-tr bipolar i disorder, who presented with marked irritability, aggression, mild delusions, depression, suicidal ideation, and diminished interpersonal and academic functioning. he participated in performance optimization-focused family behavior therapy (poffbt) within the context of an evidence based interdisciplinary csc etp designed to treat early bipolar disorder. blake completed a comprehensive standardized test battery to establish diagnosis, evaluate symptoms, and assess cognition at baseline, and regularly scheduled post-intervention assessments to determine changes in symptoms and functioning over 13.5 months. results indicated significant improvement in functioning across all domains; supporting the utilization of poffbt within csc etp to optimize functioning in early bipolar disorder. clinical case studies

divergent patterns of speaker-intention discrimination and emotional valence ratings in self-reported autistic and non-autistic adults autistic adults often interpret verbal and non-verbal cues underlying non-literal language differently compared to non-autistic people, reflecting differences in communicative style and shared context. research on non-literal language in autism in controlled settings has typically depended on static stimuli that lack ecological validity and primarily focused on children, leaving non-literal language processing in autistic adults relatively understudied. the present study examined how self-reported autistic and non-autistic adults infer speaker intentions and emotional valence in dynamic, naturalistic videos. participants ( n = 66) viewed 50 brief videos from the relational inference in social communication database, depicting literal, sarcastic, teasing, or prosocial lie scenarios. after each video, they identified the speaker’s communicative intent and rated the emotional response of the addressee. participants also completed two measures of autistic characteristics (autism spectrum quotient; comprehensive autistic trait inventory). self-reported autistic participants showed lower speaker-intention discrimination than non-autistic participants, whereas valence ratings were similar across intentions. autistic traits predicted lower speaker-intention discrimination in non-autistic adults but were unrelated (comprehensive autistic trait inventory) or positively associated (autism spectrum quotient) in self-reported autistic adults. these findings highlight shared and differing aspects of social communication and support combining categorical and trait-based approaches to understand individual differences. lay abstract autistic adults often interpret non-literal language such as sarcasm differently, which can affect everyday communication. however, prior research studies have often used written or static materials that do not reflect real-life conversations. in this study, we examined how self-reported autistic and non-autistic adults understand sarcasm, teasing, and prosocial lies using short, realistic video clips. we used videos showing actors having a short conversation. after each video, we asked participants to identify the intention that was used (literal, sarcastic, teasing, or prosocial lie) and to evaluate how happy the person receiving the statement felt. participants also reported whether they had an autism diagnosis or self-identified as autistic and completed two questionnaires measuring autistic traits (autism spectrum quotient; comprehensive autistic trait inventory). we found that autistic adults were less accurate than non-autistic adults in identifying speaker intentions, but both groups judged the emotional impact of the statements in similar ways. among non-autistic adults, higher levels of autistic traits were linked to more difficulty identifying speaker intentions. in contrast, autistic traits were not linked, or were even linked to better performance, in autistic adults. these findings suggest that autistic and non-autistic people may use both shared and different strategies when interpreting social communication and highlight the importance of considering both diagnosis and individual traits. autism

development and validation of the human resilience scale: evaluating moderation effect between life-event stress and mental health. 人类韧性量表的开发与验证：评估生活事件压力与心理健康之间的调节效应 resilience refers to maintaining or quickly restoring health after experiencing stress. a recent model proposes that resilience develops with age and results from three factors: flexibility, sociality and meaning. the soundness of this model compared to the theoretical bases of existing scales motivated us to develop a new human resilience scale. a total of 409 participants were included. confirmatory factor analysis was applied to develop a 3-factor scale. hierarchical linear regression was used to prospectively examine how resilience interacts with stress experienced between two time points 1 year apart to moderate variation in psychopathology. incremental validity compared results from a similar regression using an existing scale. results support that an 18-item, 3-factor model of resilience yields high statistical reliability (mcdonald's ω = .91), moderates the relationship between stress and mental health more significantly than a current scale, and discriminates individuals according to their age and clinical status. assessment

electrocortical and physiological correlates of memory and attention during the anticipation of avoidable and inevitable threats abstract when confronted with danger, humans display a range of defensive behaviors, such as freezing and active avoidance. prior research has identified a distinct physiological response pattern to avoidable threats, characterized by heart rate bradycardia, reduced visual exploration, and suppressed visual alpha activity (8–13 hz), all of which are associated with faster flight responses. while this pattern indicates an adaptive state of attentive immobility, it is largely unclear how this state influences the encoding of explicit threat‐related memories. clarifying these mechanisms seems important to understand the processes contributing to the formation of pathological fear memories. to address this question, we recorded parieto‐occipital alpha activity, eye movements, and autonomic responses in 60 participants during anticipation of either an avoidable threat, an inevitable threat, or no threat, while viewing images of various facial identities. in a subsequent memory task, participants were asked to recognize previously seen faces among novel ones. results showed enhanced suppression of alpha activity during avoidable threats, accompanied by heart rate bradycardia, centralized gaze, and increased sympathetic arousal. however, these responses were not linked to memory encoding. instead, memory effects were associated with reduced pupillary responses, heightened visual exploration, and decreased alpha activity, particularly in occipitotemporal regions. together, these findings suggest that when individuals face avoidable threats, they enter a state of attentive immobility that enhances perceptual processing and prepares them for action but does not extend to improved memory encoding. psychophysiology

clinical ai liability literacy, disclosure confidence, and adoption readiness among romanian healthcare professionals: an exploratory single-center cross-sectional study background and objectives: errors generated by clinical artificial intelligence (ai) can obscure responsibility and complicate disclosure and incident reporting. this exploratory study examined ai-error liability literacy and its behavioral correlates among romanian healthcare professionals. materials and methods: an exploratory, single-center cross-sectional survey was conducted from february to may 2026 among 109 clinical, managerial, legal/compliance, and it/data professionals. no a priori sample-size calculation was performed; only moderate or larger effects were detectable. participants completed a 20-item ai error liability literacy index and five-point behavioral measures. analyses included spearman correlations, k-means clustering, logistic regression, and covariate-adjusted mediation, with firth penalization, role-adjusted, use-stratified, and competing-model sensitivity analyses, and bootstrap validation. results: mean liability literacy was 11.6 ± 4.2/20. familiarity was higher for the general data protection regulation (gdpr) (67.9%) than for the eu ai act (24.8%). literacy correlated with disclosure confidence (ρ = 0.49; 95% ci [0.33, 0.62]), an association that was attenuated but persisted after adjustment for professional role (partial ρ = 0.41), which correlated with adoption intention (ρ = 0.38), as did trust (ρ = 0.43); defensive stance correlated negatively (ρ = −0.31). three exploratory profiles were identified (bootstrap jaccard 0.71–0.82) that also differed on variables not used in clustering, and an indirect statistical association between literacy and adoption intention through disclosure confidence was observed (indirect effect 0.12; 95% ci [0.04, 0.22]), although concurrent measurement precludes causal or temporal interpretation. under penalization, associations for literacy, trust, and disclosure confidence persisted; defensive stance and prior training did not. conclusions: in this exploratory sample, adoption readiness was associated with regulatory knowledge, disclosure confidence, and calibrated trust. these hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger, longitudinal studies before informing practice, and the appropriate goal is calibrated rather than maximal adoption. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

psychological inflexibility and suicidal ideation in pregnant women: a cross-sectional multiple mediation analysis of depressive symptoms, insomnia, and generalized anxiety introduction: suicidal ideation during pregnancy is an important public health concern. psychological inflexibility may be associated with emotional and sleep-related symptoms linked to suicidal ideation; however, these patterns of association remain insufficiently understood in pregnant women. objective: the objective was to examine the relationship between psychological inflexibility and suicidal ideation in pregnant women by evaluating the multiple mediating roles of depressive symptoms, insomnia, and generalized anxiety. method: a quantitative, cross-sectional associative study using latent variables was conducted with 962 pregnant women receiving care at the national maternal and perinatal institute (inmp), located in cercado de lima, lima, peru, between october and december 2025. participants completed the acceptance and action questionnaire-ii (aaq-ii), frequency of suicidal ideation inventory (fsii), athens insomnia scale (ais), patient health questionnaire-2 (phq-2), and generalized anxiety disorder-2 (gad-2). structural equation modeling (sem) was performed using r version 4.5.1 within the rstudio version 4.5.1 environment. results: the proposed model showed a good fit, scaled χ2(179) = 506.334, p < 0.001, robust cfi = 0.968, robust tli = 0.963, robust rmsea = 0.052, 90% ci [0.046, 0.057], and srmr = 0.030. psychological inflexibility showed a significant direct association with suicidal ideation (β = 0.246, p < 0.001) and significant indirect associations through depressive symptoms (β = 0.245, p < 0.001) and insomnia (β = 0.030, p = 0.007), whereas the indirect association through generalized anxiety was not significant (β = 0.007, p = 0.749). the total indirect association was significant (β = 0.282, p < 0.001), while the direct association remained statistically significant after inclusion of the mediators. conclusions: psychological inflexibility was associated with suicidal ideation among pregnant women, with depressive symptoms and insomnia showing significant indirect associations. these cross-sectional findings identify relevant correlates of suicidal ideation that warrant further longitudinal investigation. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

reduced anticipatory pleasure in early-onset severe cannabis use disorder: a retrospective, cross-sectional study background: cannabis is the most widely used illicit substance, particularly among youth. earlier onset is associated with poorer clinical trajectories in cannabis use disorder (cud), but its relationship with hedonic–motivational components remains unclear. methods: outpatients with severe cud (n = 121) were stratified by age at onset (<18 vs. ≥18 years) and compared on hedonic–motivational functioning using the snaith–hamilton pleasure scale (shaps) and the temporal experience of pleasure scale (teps). healthy subjects (n = 112) served as a reference group. results: cud groups were comparable in clinical characteristics and cannabis use patterns. teps-anticipatory scores were lower in patients with onset before age 18 (p < 0.001) and remained associated with onset group after adjustment for gender, education, and cud duration (p < 0.001). when healthy subjects were included, significant group effects were observed (p < 0.001). post hoc comparisons confirmed reduced teps-anticipatory scores in early-onset vs. both later-onset and control groups, and higher shaps scores in both cud groups vs. controls. conclusions: cud onset before age 18 is associated with reduced anticipatory pleasure, suggesting a greater involvement of anticipatory than other dimensions of hedonic functioning. age at onset may therefore help identify patients with greater motivational vulnerability and inform early, targeted prevention and intervention strategies. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

chatgpt-assisted learning effectiveness and students’ academic outcomes: a mediation analysis of cognitive engagement and self-efficacy grounded in social cognitive theory, this study examines the association between chatgpt-assisted learning effectiveness and students’ academic performance, emphasizing the mediating roles of cognitive engagement and academic self-efficacy. data were collected from tourism and hospitality students at egyptian universities. findings indicate that perceived chatgpt-assisted learning effectiveness is positively associated with students’ academic performance, cognitive engagement, and academic self-efficacy. cognitive engagement and academic self-efficacy also show significant positive associations with academic performance, and both constructs significantly mediate the relationship between chatgpt-assisted learning effectiveness and academic performance. these findings suggest that the educational value students attribute to chatgpt may operate through complementary cognitive and motivational pathways, while the cross-sectional design prevents causal conclusions. european journal of investigation in health psychology and education

toward a black feminist framework of perinatal mental health perinatal mental health is a vital yet understudied dimension of maternal health disparities, particularly for black women who experience disproportionate rates of depression, anxiety, and distress during pregnancy and following pregnancy loss. traditional biomedical frameworks, constructed largely from the experiences of white, middle-class women, obscure the ways systemic racism, class inequities, and cultural expectations shape black women’s perinatal mental health. these frameworks often fail to address the structural drivers of inequity. this article proposes a black feminist theoretical framework that integrates intersectionality, critical race feminism, reproductive justice, and sojourner syndrome. together, these frameworks reframe perinatal mental health as both an individual and structural phenomenon. implications include the need for interdisciplinary collaboration, culturally responsive clinical assessments, and policies that affirm reproductive justice. centering black feminist thought offers a pathway toward more equitable and holistic approaches to maternal health. journal of black psychology

“most times i stay awake having a lot of things on my mind”: migration, masculinity, and self-care among african men in the united states this study examines how african men living in the united states understand and practice self-care, and how migration recasts their orientations to health and wellness. drawing on in-depth interviews with 16 african immigrant men aged 23–41, the study employs thematic analysis to map both the strategies through which participants “take care of themselves” and the migration-driven conditions that reconfigure their attitudes and approaches to wellness. the findings of the study reveal that self-care strategies of african men cluster around three core themes: physical and bodily care; leisure, social connection, and spirituality; and financial security and independence. migration further reconfigures their health orientations through preventive vigilance, changes in social and structural infrastructure, emotional recalibration, and shifting spatial and urban rhythms. the study advances an african-centered account of men’s health in the united states and substantiates the need for interventions grounded in african men’s own repertoires of care, with implications for research, community-based support, and the field of black psychology. journal of black psychology

from interest to intention: factors shaping black boys’ stem career expectation in early adolescence abstract this study examines the predictors of stem career expectation among black boys in ninth grade using nationally representative data from the high school longitudinal study of 2009. guided by social cognitive career theory, we analyze associations between math and science self‐efficacy, career exploration activities, and stem career expectation in early adolescence. binary logistic regression results indicate that math and science self‐efficacy is a significant correlate of stem career expectation for all but asian boys, whereas commonly emphasized career exploration activities show a positive relationship with stem career expectation for all but black boys. these findings suggest that mechanisms frequently targeted in stem career development initiatives may not operate uniformly across racial/ethnic groups. by centering black boys and focusing on early adolescence, this study underscores the importance of contextual and structural influences in supporting more equitable stem career pathways. career development quarterly

the= .17 verdict-comparative hypotheses, comparative trials and the real world. as in many areas of modern healthcare, major treatment breakthroughs are no longer easily achievable, even though optimism continues to fuel research. the real challenge is distinguishing random or trivial effects from small but meaningful ones. this is the central question of our umbrella review: what are the typical effect sizes generally expected when comparing two psychological therapies, and where might the boundary between random and meaningful effects lie in large studies? our umbrella review focuses on the margins relevant to newer large-scale trials of over 1000 participants. psychotherapy research
does smartphone application use impact adolescents’ affect? or vice versa? an experience sampling study media psychology

norm circles and the limitations of european union normative projection in afghanistan abstract norm diffusion research explains the international travel of norms in semantic terms, through resonance, framing, grafting and localisation. such accounts presuppose norms to be portable objects whose identity persists through transit. yet, ontologically, norms exert causal force only where a real social group endorses and enforces them. this article develops dave elder‐vass's critical realist norm‐circle theory into an account of normative projection, recasting ideational travel as a problem of carrier ecology. explanation turns on which circles operate in the receiving setting, which of them a sponsor can recruit and whether their endorsement and sanction outlast the sponsor's withdrawal. european liberal state‐building in afghanistan supplies the proof of concept. retrodicting european engagement from the 1980s to 2021 shows the european union constituting a distal and imagined circle among governing elites and international audiences while recruiting no proximal circles through which sanction is delivered. centralising reform had outrun its carriers long before bonn, from amanullah in the 1920s to the soviet‐sponsored reforms of the 1970s. bonn then conferred status functions without securing enforcers. gender provisions display the asymmetry most sharply, and the collapse of 2021 exposed rather than produced it. two amendments to the theory follow. circles can be spatially disarticulated and differentiated by content, with authority held in international institutions and sanction delivered in the district. carrier withdrawal operates as a mechanism of normative collapse distinct from contestation or rejection. normative foreign policy succeeds or fails on the social organisation of enforcement. journal for the theory of social behaviour

changes in reading attitudes and attitudes toward book-reading habits following literature circles among preservice turkish language teachers: an embedded mixed-methods study reading attitudes and attitudes toward book-reading habits are related but distinct constructs. this study examined within-group pretest–posttest differences in these constructs and participants’ experiences of a seven-week literature-circle program. a quantitatively driven embedded mixed-methods design combined a single-group pretest–posttest phase (n = 36) with post-program interviews (n = 35) at a public university in türkiye. analyses included paired-samples t tests, effect sizes, 95% confidence intervals, holm adjustment, and wilcoxon signed-rank sensitivity analyses. interviews underwent hybrid deductive–inductive content analysis, and findings were integrated through joint displays. after holm adjustment, the reading-attitude outcome meeting the significance threshold depended on the method: perceived importance and value met the threshold in the t test (dz = 0.54), whereas overall reading attitude did so in the wilcoxon analysis. no outcome met the threshold in both analyses. estimates for contribution to personal and social development and all outcomes concerning attitudes toward book-reading habits were small and imprecise, with confidence intervals including zero. participants reported interest, value awareness, purposeful reading, regular reading during the program, and peer sharing. these retrospective accounts contextualized rather than independently confirmed the quantitative findings. the results do not indicate uniform improvement across outcomes, and the single-group design precludes causal attribution. behavioral sciences

are pisa 2022 creativity-related self-reports comparable across education systems? measurement invariance, alignment, and associations with creative-thinking performance pisa 2022 creativity-related self-reports are used to study differences among education systems, but their interpretation depends on measurement structure, scoring and estimator choice. we audit six scales using item-level responses from up to 73 systems, the oecd item-response scaling record and associations with creative-thinking performance. because the rotated questionnaire leaves almost no complete records, the primary models read weighted pairwise-present moments; the parameter estimates are inferential, but the fit indices and dispersion-reduction r2 computed from them are descriptive summaries of that approximation rather than survey-robust tests, and we mark which conclusions are which. the continuous models show substantial unidimensional misfit for four published indices. loading constraints produce small fit decrements under the retained structures, scalar constraints larger ones. alignment for four constructs concerns a selected item subset and cannot establish comparability of the published scale. re-estimating all six by full-information marginal maximum likelihood on the ordinal responses, which handles the planned missingness and the response format exactly, lowers every loading r2 and rearranges their ordering (ρ = 0.14), leaves the intercept ordering essentially intact (ρ = 0.94), and reproduces the system means at r = 0.77 to 0.97 while moving 18% to 53% of systems by more than five rank positions. within systems, observed-score associations are small and heterogeneous. construct-level summaries are reasonably robust to these choices; individual system positions are not. behavioral sciences

patterns of pronoun affirmation across social contexts and opportunities for resilience among trans and nonbinary youth. this study examined chosen pronoun affirmation across multiple social contexts (i.e., home, online school, in-person school, work, friends, and extended family) as a predictor of mental health among 319 trans and nonbinary (tnb) youth (ages: 13-22;= 18.6, sd = 2.18). pronoun affirmation is increasingly restricted, particularly in schools, as part of widespread anti-trans legislation in the u.s. guided by an integration of resilience, minority stress, and intersectionality frameworks, this study used a person-centered approach (i.e., latent class analysis), identifying three distinct affirmation classes: predominantly friends affirmation (27.3%), non-familial affirmation (55.8%), and comprehensive affirmation (16.9%). transmasculine youth were more likely to be represented in comprehensive affirmation, while nonbinary youth were less likely to be represented in the comprehensive affirmation class. compared to youth in the predominantly friends affirmation class, youth in non-familial affirmation and comprehensive affirmation classes reported significantly lower depressive and anxiety symptoms, better future outlook, and lower odds of suicide thoughts. in variable-centered analyses, home affirmation was associated with fewer depressive and anxiety symptoms, online and in-person school affirmation was associated with all outcomes except suicide attempts, friend affirmation was similarly associated with all outcomes except suicide thoughts and attempts, and extended family affirmation was associated with lower depressive and anxiety symptoms and lower odds of suicide thoughts. findings underscore the importance of pronoun affirmation across institutional, peer, and family contexts and carry direct implications for school policy, family-based interventions, and advocacy amid increasing legislative restrictions on gender-affirming practices. behavioral sciences

‘we have to think out of the box they put us in’: a collective narrative study of refugee and asylum seeker subjectivities in south africa abstract forced displacement is often framed through dehumanising and pathologising narratives that portray refugees as passive victims or perceived threats, obscuring their agency and lived complexity. this qualitative research–intervention explores the everyday experiences of refugees and asylum seekers living in south africa through a collective narrative approach grounded in the tree of life methodology. conducted in collaboration with a community‐based psychosocial ngo in cape town, the study involved 20 adult participants with refugee status or active asylum claims. data were generated through collective narrative workshops and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. findings identify six interrelated themes spanning traumatic and life storylines, including identity, family legacies, gender, structural and legal constraints, faith, and the reclamation of knowledge and professional identities. together, these themes show how violence and legal precarity coexist with practices of meaning‐making, dignity, resistance and collective care. in particular, findings highlight how participants actively challenge imposed categories of identity and marginalisation, reclaiming the value of their knowledge, skills, and lived experience and challenging the deficit‐oriented representations of people with a history of forced migration. journal of community & applied social psychology

responding together: volunteering and community resilience in the reception of ukrainian refugees abstract in contexts of forced migration, volunteering and grassroots civic engagement can play a crucial role in building community resilience. this study explored how stakeholders involved in the reception of ukrainian refugees in italy perceived community resilience and its promoting factors. adopting a community‐based participatory research approach, the study engaged 19 stakeholders through four focus groups and participatory ecological mapping activities. the analysis developed an overarching theme of community resilience as an ecology of support, articulated across six subthemes as follows: trusted leadership, community engagement, resources, social support, religion and spirituality and communication and information. volunteering emerged as a key mechanism for mobilising resources, connecting actors, facilitating collaboration and promoting trust and social cohesion. ecological maps further revealed both collaborative strengths and significant gaps, particularly in relations with institutional actors and access to formal support structures. the findings suggest that coordinated, culturally sensitive and community‐based support systems are essential for strengthening resilience and fostering more sustainable and inclusive refugee reception practices. journal of community & applied social psychology

adolescents and the development of social touch preferences: the handson mobile app reveals gender differences in peer interactions abstract interpersonal social touch is a powerful form of communication whose meaning depends on the relationship between partners. this becomes especially salient in adolescence, where gender plays a central role in shaping the physical, neuropsychological and social factors underlying touch preferences. here we explore how gendered preferences for imagined touch within friendships evolve from adolescence to adulthood. using the handson mobile app, 59 adolescents (from 10 to 18 years of age, m age = 14.1) and 54 adults ( m age = 29.5) created heatmaps on full‐body avatars to indicate body zones they found soothing or unpleasant to be touched by a female or male friend. touch to intimate versus social body zones was more unpleasant for female versus male participants, and for adolescents versus adults. gendered interpersonal differences emerged during adolescence, with girls reporting reduced perceived pleasantness of touch from male friends. our app provides a safe environment for adolescents to reflect on physical aspects of their socio‐affective identity that are often treated as taboo. we highlight the need to further examine the intra‐personal, inter‐personal and inter‐group factors shaping adolescents' touch norms and behaviours. such insights can guide educational practices and interventions aimed at fostering socio‐emotional learning and the well‐being of individuals and inclusive communities. journal of community & applied social psychology

time perspective, intolerance of uncertainty and fear of recurrence: psychosocial predictors of quality of life after cancer the post-cancer period is often characterized by uncertainty, particularly regarding the risk of recurrence, which can shape individuals’ perceptions of time and influence their quality of life (qol). this study explored how different time perspectives relate to qol in cancer survivors, and whether intolerance of uncertainty and fear of recurrence mediate these relationships. a cross-sectional survey was conducted with 1082 participants recruited through the seintinelles platform, using standardized measures of time perspective, intolerance of uncertainty, fear of recurrence, qol, and socio-demographic/medical variables. analyses revealed that positive orientations toward the past and present, as well as a future-oriented perspective, were associated with higher qol, while negative past and fatalistic present orientations predicted lower qol. mediation analyses showed that intolerance of uncertainty and fear of recurrence partially explained these links. findings suggest that interventions fostering adaptive temporal orientations and managing uncertainty may enhance psychological adjustment and well-being in the post-cancer period. journal of health psychology
enabling postgraduate psychology students to see, hear and feel therapeutic engagement and interaction: use of practitioner demonstrations, simulation and authentic assessment australian psychologist

inclusive instruction for students receiving special education services for emotional disturbance: a conceptual replication of classroom practice schools may rely on placement in general education, or inclusion, to improve the school outcomes of students receiving services for emotional disturbance. however, inclusion does not guarantee student access to effective instruction and specialized supports. in this conceptual replication study, we sought to identify predictors of educator self-reported knowledge, use, and perceived effectiveness of classroom-based inclusive practices for students receiving services for emotional disturbance. in the fall of 2023, an electronic survey and a multistep recruitment procedure were used to collect data from 173 educators in the united states who provided inclusive instruction and/or support to at least one student receiving special education services for emotional disturbance in the past year. similar to trends in replication research, fewer statistically significant differences were found between general and special educators, with weaker effects found. special educators in the current study also had statistically significant lower perceptions of differentiation and classroom management practice effectiveness. study findings suggest the importance of educator experience and contingencies for educator and student support (e.g., contextual factors) to the provision of inclusive instruction for this student population. study limitations, areas for future research, and implications for practice are discussed. journal of emotional and behavioral disorders

glycyrrhizic acid relieves fatigue induced by acute and chronic exercise in mice via inhibition of the nf‐κb/nlrp3 signaling pathway abstract background glycyrrhizic acid (gly‐a) exhibits anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant effects in various central nervous system disorders. acute fatigue and chronic fatigue (cf) are associated with serious physical and psychological effects. however, the underlying pathophysiology and effective therapeutic strategies for these conditions remain poorly understood. purpose this study aims to evaluate the therapeutic potential of gly‐a against fatigue, and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of its action. methods we established a mouse model of acute exercise‐induced fatigue and evaluated fatigue‐related indices. to identify specific pathways involved in gly‐a's therapeutic effects, we employed rna sequencing, network pharmacology, and in vitro oxygen‐deficit models, aiming to clarify the mechanisms. additionally, we established a mouse model of cf to compare the therapeutic efficacy of gly‐a with positive control drugs by assessing identical parameters. results gly‐a significantly improved fatigue‐related indices without affecting body weight. rna sequencing and network pharmacology analyses showed that gly‐a modulates oxidative stress responses and targets the nf‐κb (nuclear factor‐kappa b)/nlrp3 (nod‐like receptor thermal protein domain associated protein 3) signaling and apoptotic pathways. in the cf mouse model, oral administration of gly‐a significantly increased motor activity, alleviated anxiety and depression, and improved neurocognitive function compared to model mice, exhibiting superior efficacy to positive control drugs. these findings suggest that gly‐a exerts anti‐inflammatory effects by targeting the nf‐κb/nlrp3 signaling pathway, thereby reducing neuronal apoptosis in cf. conclusions gly‐a exhibits therapeutic potential against acute exercise‐fatigue and cf, primarily by attenuating apoptosis through the inhibition of the nf‐κb/nlrp3 signaling pathway. brain and behavior

whether and how parental‐adolescent attachment and peer attachment relate to the development of self‐control in adolescents: a random intercept cross‐lagged panel analysis abstract self‐control denotes the capacity to intentionally pursue actions that align with long‐term, meaningful goals. although cumulative evidence has shown that parental‐adolescent attachment and peer attachment are closely associated with self‐control, the longitudinal links between mother attachment, father attachment, peer attachment, and self‐control are unclear. this study utilized random‐intercept cross‐lagged panel models (ri‐clpms) to analyse longitudinal data from 1312 chinese adolescents (age range 12–18, m age = 14.29, sd = 1.38; 50.2% boys) over 1 year with three measurements (i.e., 6 months apart across three cohorts). after separating within‐person and between‐person associations, the results from the ri‐clpms revealed that, at the between‐person level, both parental‐adolescent attachment (including attachment to both mother and father) and peer attachment were positively associated with self‐control. at the within‐person level, cross‐lagged effects were found between mother attachment and self‐control. additionally, self‐control was found to positively predict subsequent father attachment and peer attachment. furthermore, father attachment at t2 positively predicted self‐control at t3, while peer attachment at t1 positively predicted self‐control at t2. the differing findings regarding mother attachment, father attachment, and peer attachment highlight the importance of considering various significant figures in the study of attachment and self‐control. international journal of psychology
issue information journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

author diversity in the journal of the experimental analysis of behavior 1958–2025 abstract we used application programming interfaces (apis) to estimate gender and race/ethnicity based on names of first and last authors in 4,833 articles published in the journal of the experimental analysis of behavior (jeab) from 1958 to 2025. from the first to the most recent 5‐year interval, gender api estimated that the percentage of articles with women first authors increased from 6% to 33% and the percentage of first authors ethnicolr api classified as more likely than not to be authors of color (aoc) increased from 5% to 25%, with similar gains in percentages of last authors estimated to be women or aoc. the proportion of names classified as feminine and as less likely to be white has grown steadily, but even after two‐thirds of a century of growth, these groups are underrepresented relative to the u.s. adult population, college graduates working in science‐related fields, and higher education faculty. these findings underscore the need for ongoing efforts to address systemic barriers and promote equitable representation in scholarly publishing. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

epigenetic programming of stress-response systems: a systematic review of how early life stress shapes developmental trajectories of mental health. early life stress (els) is a critical environmental factor influencing developmental trajectories of behavioral and emotional regulation. increasing evidence suggests that such experiences can alter biological systems during sensitive developmental periods through epigenetic processes. this systematic review aims to synthesize empirical human studies examining how els contributes to the developmental programming of mental health via epigenetic regulation of stress-response systems. this systematic review was conducted in accordance with prisma 2020 guidelines. a comprehensive search of pubmed/medline, web of science, scopus, and psycinfo databases was performed for studies published up to march 2026. eligible studies included empirical human research investigating associations between els, epigenetic mechanisms (primarily dna methylation), and mental health-related outcomes across developmental stages. a total of 14 studies met inclusion criteria and were synthesized using a qualitative approach. findings indicate that els is associated with persistent epigenetic modifications in key genes regulating stress-response systems, particularly within the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (hpa) axis. altered dna methylation patterns in genes such as nr3c1, fkbp5, slc6a4, maoa, and ank3 were consistently linked to developmental alterations in emotional regulation and increased vulnerability to psychiatric conditions, including depression, anxiety disorders, and post-traumatic stress disorder. importantly, evidence highlights early childhood as a sensitive developmental window during which environmental inputs exert stronger and more enduring biological effects. some studies further suggest that epigenetic profiles may show partial plasticity in response to environmental or therapeutic changes across development. this review supports the concept that els contributes to the developmental programming of mental health through epigenetic mechanisms affecting stress-response systems. these findings underscore the importance of timing and environmental context in shaping long-term behavioral outcomes. however, the existing literature remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, including variability in developmental stages, tissue types, and measurement approaches. future research should prioritize longitudinal and developmentally informed designs to better capture the dynamic interplay between environment, biology, and behavior across the lifespan. developmental psychobiology

psychological determinants of low carbon digital behavior among university students in bangladesh abstract the rapid digitalization of higher education has significantly increased students’ reliance on energy-intensive platforms, yet sustainable digital practices remain limited despite rising awareness of digital carbon emissions. this study examines the awareness-action paradox among bangladeshi university students by developing and validating a digital carbon awareness action paradox model that integrates environmental concern, perceived behavioral control, habit strength, digital addiction, and eco-anxiety. using a cross-sectional survey of 400 students from public, private, and national university, structural equation modeling revealed that awareness does not directly predict intention but strongly influences both environmental concern and perceived behavioral control. both environmental concern and perceived behavioral control fully mediated the awareness-intention relationship, confirming that awareness alone is insufficient for motivating sustainable digital behavior. intention emerged as the strongest predictor of low-carbon digital action, whereas habit strength and digital addiction exerted strong direct negative effects on actual behavior rather than acting as moderators, highlighting the independent constraining role of entrenched digital routines and compulsive usage. eco-anxiety did not moderate the awareness-intention pathway, suggesting that emotional distress does not translate awareness into motivation without supportive psychological mechanisms. the model explained 43.4% of the variance in intention and 50.8% in behavior, offering one of the first empirically grounded frameworks for understanding digital sustainability behavior in a developing-country context. findings emphasize the need for interventions that enhance emotional engagement and perceived capability while addressing habitual and addictive digital consumption patterns to effectively bridge the awareness-action gap. discover psychology
economic evaluation of psychological outcomes across postoperative breast cancer treatment pathways in a conflict-affected setting: a cross-sectional study from iraq discover psychology
understanding purchase intention in livestream commerce through the cognition-affect-behavior framework discover psychology
spirituality, self-transcendence, and the creative power: perspectives on subbulakshmi phenomenon psychological studies

psychological transformation and integration: the convergence of the i ching and jungian psychology in supporting cancer patients a cancer diagnosis brings not only physiological suffering but also plunges the individual into a profound existential crisis, often leading to the erosion of social connections and a loss of life’s meaning. while existing psychological models may lack cultural congruence for individuals from eastern backgrounds, they also frequently prove insufficient for addressing the profound existential and spiritual threats faced by any patient globally when confronting a fatal illness. this theoretical analysis places the cosmological life-view of “producing and reproducing” from the chinese classic, the i ching , and carl jung’s theory of psychic integration, “individuation,” within a single framework. the philosophical wisdom of the i ching can be regarded as a unique manifestation of the individuation archetype in eastern culture, providing indigenous cultural and spiritual guidance for cancer patients worldwide on their path toward psychological transformation and integration. this integrated framework offers robust theoretical support for understanding how cancer patients can convert a life crisis into post-traumatic growth and provides crucial insights for developing culturally adaptive psychological intervention models addressing patients’ deeper needs for meaning and spiritual transcendence. the ultimate goal is to advance psychological assistance from mere symptom alleviation to a profound reconstruction of life’s meaning and personality integration. journal of humanistic psychology

sites of insight: blackness, psychology, and methods of liberation this essay explores what black aesthetics might engender for black people, centering the mutuality between black living and aesthetic production as a liberatory praxis. drawing from liberation psychology, i engage blackness not as an object of analysis but as a force that unsettles dominant epistemological and psychological frameworks, opening pathways for theorizing differently in the discipline of psychology. rather than limiting black aesthetics to modes of representation or reaction, i examine their affective and resonant dimensions, attuned to the texture, shape, and emotional force of black creative expression. through a black aesthetic analysis of elizabeth catlett’s public sculpture students aspire , i illuminate how its visual and affective elements enact a breach of the order of western psychology as rooted in anti-blackness. the sculpture becomes a site of assembly and relationality, animating possibilities for black worldmaking. i conclude with a discussion on how black aesthetics are generative sites of psychological insight and liberative potential. journal of humanistic psychology

working with post-psychedelic difficulties: a meta-aggregation of users’ experiences and implications for counselling practice with the increasing use of psychedelics in both clinical and non-clinical contexts, there is growing potential for harm arising from challenging experiences and post-psychedelic difficulties. this qualitative review aimed to explore psychedelic users’ experiences of acute and post-psychedelic challenges in non-clinical contexts, to identify practice considerations for safer and more effective client work supporting the evolving role of counselling psychologists and practitioners in related fields. a comprehensive search across ebsco databases and google scholar identified seven studies (n = 721) published between 2021 and 2025. data extraction, quality appraisal, and meta-aggregative synthesis were conducted in accordance with jbi methodology. four synthesised findings were identified: (1) complex experiences of distress; (2) diverse and individualised coping strategies; (3) external support and challenges; and (4) internal adjustment and ambiguous outcomes. findings indicate that experiences are varied, complex, and paradoxical; this highlights the value of pluralistic harm-reduction approaches that acknowledge diversity of experience to ensure safer and more effective outcomes for those navigating post-psychedelic difficulties. counselling psychology quarterly
from boredom to problematic ai chatbot use: a three-wave half-longitudinal mediation study of loneliness and dual-system self-control australian journal of psychology

cognitive analytic therapists' experiences of working with ethnic minority clients: an interpretative phenomenological analysis abstract objectives cognitive analytic therapy (cat) is a relational therapy offered within the national health service (nhs). this study aimed to explore the experiences of therapists using cat with ethnic minority clients, including how they engage with issues of power and identity which are often neglected in psychotherapy. method individual, semi‐structured interviews were conducted remotely with seven cognitive analytic therapists who had experience of working therapeutically with ethnic minority clients. data were analysed using interpretative phenomenological analysis (ipa). results four group experiential themes (gets) were generated: (1) broaching identity in cat: balancing relational risks and responsibility; (2) navigating positionality and power within cat; (3) seeing the bigger picture: the power of integrating identity in cat (4) cat within the limits of unequal systems. conclusion acknowledging and exploring aspects of power and identity felt important and meaningful, with the model providing a strong framework for this work. future research and clinical implications are discussed. counselling & psychotherapy research

public mass shooters and the prevalence of suicidality it is well documented that over a third of public mass shooters die by suicide. however, the rate of suicidality among public mass shooters during their attacks may be greater. using the notion of a final act mentality, we operationalize suicidality as not only intentionally ending one’s life but also as accepting that committing the act will end one’s life as they know it. to assess the rate of suicidality in public mass shooters, we analyze publicly available data on plans to avoid capture, initial outcomes post-attack, and suicidal capability for 54 offenders who killed six or more people between january 1, 2000, and may 6, 2023. our findings indicate that nearly all public mass shooters were suicidal at the time of the attack. although based on a small sample, we found no statistically significant difference in suicidal capability between those who lived versus those who died by suicide. omega-journal of death and dying

you are needed again, my fellow: intergroup allocation of illegitimate tasks to native and migrant professionals while extensive research demonstrates that individuals prefer their own groups when distributing positive stimuli such as resources or rewards, less is known about intergroup behaviors related to negative stimuli. this paper examines the allocation of legitimate and illegitimate tasks (i.e., unreasonable or unnecessary tasks that can cause psychological or physiological harm to those carrying them out) to german and turkish doctors, and the individual differences influencing these decisions. across two vignette-based experiments under free-choice (study 1; n = 98) and forced-choice (study 2; n = 239) conditions, participants consistently assigned more illegitimate tasks to native professionals than to migrant professionals. by contrast, legitimate task allocation did not differ significantly between groups. under forced-choice conditions, allocation decisions were further associated with prejudice toward migrant professionals and felt similarity to them. complemented by a third vignette-based experiment exploring potential explanations for the allocation of illegitimate tasks (n = 190), these findings highlight the asymmetric effects of stimulus valence on intergroup allocation and suggest that differences in task assignment may be related to warmth-based attributions. acta psychologica

different hippocampal subfield volumes predict source memory performance and general cognitive ability in an adult lifespan sample. modest positive associations between episodic memory performance and whole hippocampal and hippocampal subfield volumes have been reported in numerous prior studies. a smaller number of studies have reported associations between hippocampal volume and performance on tests of non-mnemonic cognition. the present study examined whether these associations were evident in a lifespan sample of cognitively healthy adults. of particular interest was whether any identified associations were sensitive to age, and whether associations between subfield volumes and mnemonic and non-mnemonic performance were subfield dependent. we acquired high-resolution t1- and t2-weighted structural images from 163 adults (18-87 years of age). participants also undertook a comprehensive neuropsychological test battery and an in-scanner test of source memory. principal components analysis was employed to reduce the neuropsychological test scores to 5 cognitive components. two components reflected memory performance while the other three reflected different aspects of non-mnemonic cognition. hippocampal subfields (cornu ammonis (ca)1, ca2-3, dentate gyrus (dg) and subiculum) were segmented and measured with the automated segmentation of hippocampus subfields (ashs) package. source memory performance was selectively associated across participants with ca2-3 volume. by contrast, both mnemonic and non-mnemonic component scores derived from the test battery were associated exclusively with the volume of the dg. all associations were age-invariant. the findings indicate that different cognitive domains can be dissociated by virtue of their associations with different hippocampal subfields. of importance, these associations appear to be life-long and hence are unlikely to reflect individual differences in age-related decline in structural integrity. biorxiv : the preprint server for biology
