assessment of psychosocial services for flood survivors in tanzania. a case study of kilosa district, morogoro region flooding can disrupt psychological well-being, social support networks, and everyday functioning, particularly in rural communities with limited access to psychosocial services. this study assessed the availability, utilization, and perceived effectiveness of psychosocial services among flood-affected communities in kilosa district, tanzania. a convergent mixed-methods design was employed, combined a household survey of 214 respondents with key informant interviews and structured observations. quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests, while qualitative data were thematically analyzed and integrated during interpretation. findings showed that 62.95% of respondents received at least one psychosocial service following flooding. counselling was the most frequently reported service (47.66%), followed by therapy (30.84%) and public awareness or mental health education (21.03%). village of residence was significantly associated with participation in public awareness and mental health education (χ = 13.0572, p = 0.0015), therapy utilization (χ = 16.6930, p = 0.0002), and perceived effectiveness (χ = 24.5579, p < 0.0001). duration of residence was also associated with perceived effectiveness (p = 0.0400). education level was associated with counselling (p = 0.0205) and therapy utilization (p = 0.0425). qualitative findings highlighted geographical disparities, shortages of trained personnel, limited continuity, and reliance on community-based support. effectiveness reflects perceived usefulness, not measured psychological outcomes, and does not demonstrate improved coping, recovery, or resilience. acta psychologica

patriarchal beliefs and men's mental health in india: associations with emotional expressivity, help-seeking behaviour, and family relationships in this study, the association between conformity to masculine norms and emotional expressivity, help-seeking behaviour and psychological distress among men in india were explored as well as the potential mediating role of family relationships. a total of 200 men aged 21-50 were sampled using purposive sampling for the study, which was conducted using an online survey. the participants filled out the conformity to masculine norms inventory-22 (cmni-22), emotional expressivity scale (ees), general help-seeking questionnaire (ghsq), and brief family relationship scale (bfrs). the pearson correlations and mediation analyses were run in spss using hayes' process macro (model 4). emotional expressivity (r = -0.311, p < .01) and help-seeking behaviour (r = -0.218, p < .01) were significantly negatively associated with conformity to masculine norms, while psychological distress was not significantly associated with conformity to masculine norms (r = 0.084). family relationships were also negatively and significantly correlated with conformity to masculine norms (r = -0.161, p < .05). the associations between masculine norm conformity and emotional expressivity and help-seeking behaviour were not significantly mediated by family relationships. by contrast, a large indirect association between masculine norm conformity and psychological distress was mediated by family relationships (b = 0.0366, 95% ci [0.0015, 0.0718]). the results of this study suggest an outcome-specific pattern of involvement of family relationships. family relationships were not significantly associated with the behavioural associations between masculine norm conformity and emotional expressivity or help-seeking but they were significantly indirectly associated with psychological distress. the results underscore the significance of taking into account the family relationship in conjunction with the constraining masculine norms when studying men's psychological wellbeing in the indian context. the conclusions drawn should be viewed as associations and not as causal pathways as per the cross-sectional design. future studies with different samples and different methods of measurement are required for longitudinal research on the temporal relationships between masculine norms, family relationships and psychological outcomes. acta psychologica

beyond the binary: a critical synthesis of colorism, racism, and health disparities in puerto rico although puerto rican society has long been shaped by the heritage of spanish and united states (u.s.) colonization, current research has started to examine how racism and colorism interact to create and maintain health inequalities throughout the archipelago. however, this body of work remains theoretically fragmented and methodologically inconsistent, limiting its ability to inform public health practices. to address this gap, this article presents a systematic review of peer-reviewed studies examining colorism, racism, and health outcomes among puerto ricans residing in the archipelago. the publications were identified through searches in three different databases (i.e., cinahl, medline, and pubmed) following the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (prisma) guidelines. the findings highlight the underutilization of decolonial and community-based frameworks and the need for more nuanced, culturally grounded measures of racial classification and skin tone. in this article we present arguments for a shift toward intersectional, participatory, and longitudinal research designs that center the experiences of the population of african descent and challenge u.s.-centric racial paradigms. by mapping the current landscape and its limitations, this work contributes to a more equitable and contextually relevant research agenda on racialization, color, and health in puerto rico. the conclusion calls for a paradigm shift in public health research and practice—one that centers the experiences of the population of african descent, community-based knowledge, and structural transformation. hispanic journal of behavioral sciences

modular cognitive-behavioral treatment of comorbid insomnia and posttraumatic stress disorder: a clinical transfer case study cognitive-behavioral (cbt) interventions have empirical support for insomnia and posttraumatic stress disorder (ptsd), yet clinicians often underprioritize insomnia when psychiatric comorbidity complicates treatment. this clinical case study describes a flexible cbt approach for “ava,” a bisexual woman in her twenties who transferred to a new therapist in a university-affiliated community training clinic. although prior treatment had targeted trauma symptoms, ava identified insomnia as her primary concern at transfer. treatment began with modules from the transdiagnostic sleep and circadian intervention (trans-c) and was followed by improvements in sleep quality and daytime functioning. midway through treatment, menstruation-linked ptsd symptoms were disclosed, and the therapist implemented written exposure therapy to target avoidance and maladaptive trauma-related beliefs. the trans-c nightmare module, which incorporates imagery rehearsal therapy principles, was later implemented to address nightmares. self-report measures showed reductions in sleep disturbance and ptsd symptoms. this case illustrates how modular, evidence-based cbt can flexibly address shifting treatment targets in a complex transfer case. clinical case studies

the great wave of awareness: ocean-featured art enhances anthropomorphisation of the ocean, indirectly causes pro-environmental moral obligation to rise / la gran ola de concienciación: el arte dedicado al océano fomenta su antropomorfización y facilita indirectamente el aumento de la obligación moral proambiental due to the impact of moral variables on behaviour, fostering moral commitment towards natural resources is a promising strategy for promoting pro-environmental action. this study tests whether art-based interventions can enhance anthropomorphisation of the ocean and, subsequently, pro-environmental moral obligation. in an experiment with 304 us participants, individuals were randomly assigned to view either ocean-themed artwork or a non-artistic ocean photograph, paired with either a moral or technical description. results showed that observing artwork significantly increased anthropomorphisation of the ocean, regardless of the description of the piece or participants’ ideology. in turn, this fostered a greater sense of moral obligation to protect the ocean, showing that anthropomorphisation mediates the relationship between art observation and moral obligation. these findings suggest that contemplating ocean-themed art can enhance moralisation and pro-environmental attitudes. more broadly, art-based interventions may serve as effective tools for promoting the moralisation of natural resources and even marginalised human groups by increasing their perceived humanness, highlighting their potential for mobilising social movements. psyecology-bilingual journal of environmental psychology-revista bilingue de psicologia ambiental

school exclusion as a partial mediator between autism and adolescent mental health. purpose: this study investigated whether school exclusion during secondary school mediates the association between autism spectrum conditions (asc) and adolescent internalising and externalising mental health difficulties.
methods: we analysed data from the uk millennium cohort study (n = 10,228, waves 1-7). parents reported asc diagnosis at ages 5-11 and whether their child had been excluded at ages 11-14. internalising and externalising symptoms were self-reported by adolescents at age 17 on the strengths and difficulties questionnaire. confounders were mapped onto a directed acyclic graph. causal mediation analyses, using the g-formula for randomised interventional analogues, estimated direct and indirect effects while accounting for these confounders without biasing the causal pathway.
results: autism was associated with higher internalising and externalising scores, with autistic adolescents more likely to experience school exclusion than peers. school exclusion partially mediated the association between asc and externalising symptoms (indirect effect = 0.03 (95% ci: 0.004, 0.06, p = 0.024) . no evidence of mediation was found for internalising symptoms.
conclusion: school exclusion acts as one modifiable environmental mechanism contributing to externalising difficulties in autistic adolescents, likely through the loss of protective school supports. preventative, autism-informed strategies that reduce reliance on exclusion and provide appropriate support could form part of wider efforts to improve mental health outcomes in autistic adolescents. journal of autism and developmental disorders
multimodal human–computer interaction interventions for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a scoping review journal of autism and developmental disorders

factor structure and validity of the burnout assessment for developmental disability settings (badds). purpose: this study examined the factor structure, reliability, and validity of the burnout assessment for developmental disability settings (badds), a self-report scale for measuring workplace stressors that contribute to burnout specifically among behavioral health providers for autism and related developmental disabilities.
method: we conducted an online survey of 566 autism service providers that comprised the badds, the maslach burnout inventory - human services survey (mbi), areas of worklife survey (aws), and the patient health questionnaire - 9 (phq-9). conducted confirmatory factor analysis based on (bottini et al., 2026) showed poor fit. an expert panel cut 17 redundant items. exploratory factor analysis on the remaining 56 items resulted in further reduction to 39 items. to evaluate the validity of the 39-item version, the badds was compared to the mbi, aws, and phq-9.
results: the 39-item badds had six factors: physical safety, training & supervision, stakeholder interactions, professional development, stress management, and ethics & values. across subscales, internal reliability ranged 0.75-0.92. correlations with mbi and aws subscales ranged from 0.04 to 0.60. elevations across badds subscales were associated with incremental increases in mbi scores.
conclusion: the badds subscales showed solid internal consistency. consistent increases in burnout symptoms (mbi scores) with elevations on badds subscales, supporting convergent validity. additional research to confirm the psychometrics and utility of the badds is warranted. journal of autism and developmental disorders
cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the french-moroccan version of the engaging leadership scale among knowledge workers in morocco bmc psychology

the dutch three-domain disgust scale (tdds): structural validity, measurement invariance, and nomological associations across two large samples this research provides a comprehensive validation of the dutch three-domain disgust scale (tdds) across two large samples (study 1: n = 991; study 2: n = 1806). confirmatory factor analyses supported the theorized three-factor structure, pathogen, sexual, and moral disgust, with domain-specific loadings and acceptable global fit. measurement invariance across sex was fully supported in study 2 and approximately supported in study 1, indicating largely comparable measurement across men and women. women showed higher latent levels of sexual disgust, whereas sex differences in pathogen and moral disgust were smaller and sample-dependent. construct validity was supported through theoretically coherent associations: sexual disgust was robustly linked to pair bonding; moral disgust was substantially negatively associated with low morality; and pathogen disgust showed selective associations, including consistent positive links with low morality and weaker, sample-dependent relations with outgroup avoidance. criterion validity was partly supported: predictors of low morality were stable across studies, whereas predictions of outgroup avoidance were less consistent. overall, the dutch tdds emerges as a reliable and valid instrument capturing domain-specific disgust sensitivity relevant to moral, social, and intergroup processes in dutch-speaking populations. bmc psychology

how locus of control shapes digital nomads’ subjective well-being: the mediating roles of telepressure, technostress, and boundary control abstract background as digital nomadism becomes an increasingly prevalent form of digital labor, understanding how psychological mechanisms shape well-being under highly autonomous yet weakly institutionalized work conditions is critical. drawing on the job demands–resources (jd-r) model and conservation of resources (cor) theory, this study examines how locus of control influences digital nomads’ subjective well-being through technostress, telepressure, and boundary control, while also testing the moderating role of offline social interaction. methods survey data from 540 digital nomads recruited through online remote work and digital nomad communities were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (pls-sem) with a bootstrapping procedure based on 5,000 resamples. results the results show that locus of control does not directly affect subjective well-being but operates through multiple mediating pathways. a stronger internal locus of control reduces technostress and telepressure and enhances boundary control, which in turn improves subjective well-being. boundary control emerges as the strongest positive predictor of well-being. in addition, offline social interaction significantly buffers the negative effect of telepressure on subjective well-being. conclusions these findings suggest that digital nomads’ well-being depends less on work flexibility itself and more on individuals’ capacity to manage digital demands and psychological boundaries. bmc psychology

generalization of motor learning in psychological space abstract the capacity to generate adaptive movements largely depends on how we generalize what we have previously learned to novel situations. the generalization of adapted movements has typically been framed as a consequence of neural tuning functions that overlap for similar movement kinematics—what might be considered bottom‐up generalization. however, as is true in many domains of human behavior, generalization can also be framed as the result of goal‐directed, deliberate decisions about how to act (top‐down generalization). here, we attempt to broaden the scope of theories about motor generalization, hypothesizing that part of the typical motor generalization function is associated with goal‐directed decisions concerning the subjective similarity of different movement contexts. we tested this proposal by having participants make explicit similarity ratings over both traditional kinematic contextual dimensions (movement direction) and more abstract contextual dimensions (target shape) and perform a visuomotor adaptation generalization task where trials varied over those dimensions. across five experiments, we measured the relationship between subjective similarity ratings and motor generalization. in some cases, this link was rather strong, though it was determined by the inferred goals of participants (e.g., task relevance, explicit instruction, etc.). these results support a broadening of current frameworks to explain the generalization of motor behaviors and support a more careful deployment of goal‐ and task‐relevant instructions in generalization studies. topics in cognitive science

higher craving and pleasure in response to exercise‐related cues in patients with anorexia nervosa and exercise dependence abstract background physical activity is common in patients with anorexia nervosa (an), who often reported symptoms consistent with exercise dependence. craving, the subjective urge to engage in a specific behaviour, is an important mechanism in the development of addiction and could be triggered by cues from the environment. aim of the present study was to investigate craving in people with an with respect to the presence of exercise dependence in response to video cues of physical activity and sedentary behaviours, comparing them to a sample of healthy women. methods a total of 57 women with an and 20 healthy women completed the exercise dependence scale—revised (eds‐r). according to eds‐r, 21 women with an were classified as non‐dependent asymptomatic (nda), 21 as non‐dependent symptomatic (nds) and 15 as dependent (d). all healthy women were nda. all participants were exposed to video cues depicting subjects engaging in exercise and sedentary activities, and filled in the crave experience questionnaire at three timepoints: at baseline, after exposure to sedentary activity videos, and after exposure to exercise activity videos. results patients with an displayed higher craving after exposure to physical exercise videos. d participants reported higher intensity and intrusiveness of craving for exercise, compared to all other groups. finally, we found an association between pleasure evoked by physical activity cues and the craving triggered by these videotapes. conclusions our study suggests that craving is an existing dimension of exercise dependence in an, supporting the positive reinforcement provided by exercise, and to take into account as a relapse factor. european eating disorders review

semantic schema and group differences in everyday conceptions of happiness and unhappiness: an investigation with a word-association network what does happiness mean to ordinary people? answering this requires examining not only the components people associate with happiness, but also how these components are organized and structurally connected into a semantic schema. the same questions apply to its conceptual counterpart—unhappiness—and to how both vary across social groups. to address these questions, this study employs a word-association network approach to investigate the semantic schemas and group differences in people’s perceptions of happiness and unhappiness. specifically, we create semantic representations of happiness and unhappiness using a word-association task in which participants freely listed words they associate with happiness and unhappiness, and then listed further words associated with each response; these word pairs are used to construct association networks from which underlying schemas are identified and demographic differences examined. based on a survey conducted in japan, our findings reveal major components, such as “ wealth ” and “ relationships ,” widely identified in existing theories, as well as underrepresented components, such as “ food .” moreover, our analysis provides insights into the structural relationships among these components, allowing us to understand how different components are connected to one another and what roles they play within the schema. furthermore, we demonstrate that the word-association network approach provides a useful framework for investigating how everyday conceptions of happiness and unhappiness differ across demographic groups, revealing variation across groups in both schema structure and specific semantic features. overall, this study demonstrates the value of word-association networks for capturing everyday conceptions of happiness and unhappiness, offering both theoretical insights and practical implications for developing more accurate and culturally grounded measures. journal of happiness studies
wives’ managerial employment and husbands’ well-being: evidence of intra-household asymmetry in japan journal of happiness studies

survivance and resurgence in a maya diaspora abstract this paper explores how displaced maya peoples are working toward justice and resurgence amid increasing government persecution in the united states. the authors facilitated multi‐year critical participatory action research with communities living in northeast ohio, united states, where a large diaspora of maya people has been growing since the 1980s. participants reported increased suffering resulting from oppressive border enforcement policies. at the same time, they shared their work to cultivate what gerald vizenor (2009), white earth anishinaabe writer and literary theorist, called “survivance”: resistance and survival in vibrant communities despite structural violence. their strategies included cultural continuity, community orientation, and land‐based healing. these themes intersected in an array of practices such as reviving ancestral relational traditions, building shared power and alliances (even with state institutions), restoring ecological care, and telling the truth about their indigenous histories. the praxis highlights maya knowledges that can inform how community‐based psychologists and scholars work alongside indigenous peoples severely impacted by border violence, supporting their resurgence strategies through research and action. american journal of community psychology
issue information british journal of health psychology

gender minority stress experiences after gender-affirming medical care. understanding experiences of gender minority stress after gender-affirming medical care can improve post-treatment outcomes and provide transdiagnostic interventions targets for trans and gender diverse (tgd) individuals. this study aimed to describe proximal gender minority stress after gender-affirming care, and correlate high versus low stress to patient characteristics. in a cross-sectional study, participants were recruited through healthcare providers and community outlets to complete an online questionnaire. the quartiles with highest and lowest minority stress on the transgender identity survey were included for analyses and compared on demographic and validated outcome questionnaires. participants ( = 86) frequently reported limited openness (42.4%) or support (19.7%) related to their tgd identity after medical treatments. low proximal minority stress was associated with younger age, non-binary gender, moderate to full openness on tgd, and higher treatment satisfaction. low minority stress was also associated with less anxiety/depression, higher self-esteem, social connectedness and life satisfaction (moderate to large effect sizes). open-text answers suggested that minority stress experiences were heterogeneous and related to persistent gender-based distress, stressful social interactions, and/or negative treatment outcomes. minority stress theory can provide a transdiagnostic concept to improve the wellbeing of tgd individuals after medical transition, while substantial conceptual overlap with mental health outcomes exists. journal of sex & marital therapy

building career pathways within men of color programs: a qualitative analysis of black faculty, staff, and administrator men abstract nationally, men of color struggle with college persistence and graduation; therefore, four ethnic‐ and gender‐specific retention programs have been launched to counter these trends and promote degree attainment and career readiness. however, little is known about the programming and strategies used to foster career development practices and attitudes from the perspective of black faculty, staff, and administrator men who lead these programs. guided by social cognitive career theory, this qualitative study examined the experiences of eight black men who lead campus‐based efforts. key findings emphasize the following: (1) trust‐building by institutional agents, (2) staff as role models and connectors, and (3) asset‐based strategies in coaching. the paper concludes with recommendations for research, practice, policymakers, and counselor education training programs. career development quarterly

spaced repetition and list-strength in recognition memory abstract intuition and classic mathematical models suggest that “strong” list items should see a competitive recognition-memory advantage when mixed with “weak” list items within a single list. this holds for manipulations of reading aloud but not other manipulations. study time per item (e.g., 500 vs. 2000 ms), can even invert the effect, with a larger strength effect between pure-strength lists than within mixed lists. this inversion remained when the longer study time comprised three massed repetitions. an attentional subsetting theory account explained the inverted list-strength effect by assuming weak items had primarily shallow features encoded, and participants disregarded those on pure-strong lists, when the better, deeper features were available. here we asked whether spaced repetition is an exception, rendering disregarding ineffective, or like massed repetition, produces an inverted list-strength effect if presentation time is short. in three experiments, spaced repetition produced a null or upright list-strength effect. under equated conditions, massed repetition and long duration produced inverted or null effects. thus, despite being within an experimental regime that has robustly produced inverted list-strength effects, spaced repetition appears resilient. these boundary conditions constrain models, including attentional subsetting theory and retrieving effectively from memory, and we discuss how various theories may need to adjust to explain the full range of list-strength data. memory & cognition

using womanism counseling to support black girls abstract black girls have had to navigate adultification, criminalization, and marginalization at significantly higher rates. the application of frameworks rooted in womanist tenets has the ability to create safe and affirming spaces that can empower black girls and foster resilience while promoting their socioemotional development. consequently, the authors explore how womanism can be integrated into mental health practices to support the academic, social, and personal development of black girls. five womanist‐based strategies are presented: building communal connections, developing critical consciousness, engaging in creative expression, embracing holistic well‐being, and pursuing empowerment and leadership. implications and research recommendations are discussed. journal of counseling and development

empathy and violence tendency: the mediating roles of emotional intelligence and masculine behaviour violence represents a significant psychosocial problem affecting both individuals and societies. this cross-sectional study examined the relationship between empathy and violence tendency and investigated the mediating roles of emotional intelligence, emotional regulation, and masculine behaviour dimensions in this relationship within the sociocultural context of türkiye. data were collected from 703 individuals aged 18 and over through an online questionnaire between october and december 2024 and analysed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling. the findings indicated that empathy was negatively associated with violence tendency and positively related to emotional intelligence and emotional regulation. emotional regulation demonstrated a significant negative relationship with violence tendency, whereas selected masculine behaviour dimensions, particularly independent lifestyle/exaggerated self-confidence and control, were positively associated with violence tendency. the proposed model explained 29% of the variance in violence tendency, highlighting the role of emotional and sociocultural behavioural factors. by examining empathy, emotional competencies, and selected masculine-coded behavioural dimensions together in the turkish context, this study contributes to the literature by showing that individual emotional capacities and control-oriented behavioural tendencies may have distinct associations with violence tendency. journal of interpersonal violence

influence of positive childhood experiences profiles on bullying victimization and perpetration in youth: a latent class analysis bullying has enduring negative effects on development in adolescents. while research has focused on reducing risk factors such as adverse childhood experiences for bullying, growing evidence highlights the protective role of positive childhood experiences (pces) in fostering resilience and preventing bullying. however, little is known about how combinations of pces within the social-ecological context influence bullying. the researchers aimed to (a) identify patterns of pces, (b) examine demographic factors associated with these patterns, and (c) investigate how different pces patterns relate to bullying victimization and perpetration. data were drawn from the 2022 national survey of children’s health (nsch), a nationally representative survey of u.s. children’s well-being. the final sample included 17,157 adolescents aged 12 to 17 years. this cross-sectional study used a three-step approach for latent class analysis to identify latent pces profiles and to examine their demographic predictors and associations with bullying behaviors. the study results identified three pces profiles: resilient and supported (rs; high across all indicators), supported and low engagement (sle; high in most indicators but low in social engagement), and vulnerable and unsupported (vu; low across all indicators). family- and individual-level factors served as significant predictors of membership in the three pces profiles. both sle and vu groups reported higher bullying victimization and perpetration than rs, with vu showing the highest levels. the current findings suggest that bullying prevention strategies should extend beyond individual and school-based efforts to include community-level approaches and to coordinate school–family–community partnerships that strengthen protective experiences and address persistent inequities in access to pces among adolescents. journal of interpersonal violence

predicting adaptive and maladaptive narcissistic traits from theory of mind and empathy in early adolescence this study examined associations between adaptive and maladaptive narcissistic traits, theory of mind (tom), and empathy in a sample of 10- to 12-year-old adolescents. participants ( n = 130, m age = 10.84 years, 69 girls) completed self-report measures assessing dimensions of narcissism (adaptive and maladaptive) and empathy (cognitive empathy, affective empathy, and intention to comfort) as well as two advanced tom tasks, the strange stories test and the reading the mind in the eyes test. performance on the strange stories test was positively associated with adaptive narcissistic traits (authority and self-sufficiency), whereas a stronger self-reported intention to comfort others was associated with lower levels of these traits. in addition, both higher affective empathy and a greater intention to comfort were associated with lower levels of maladaptive narcissistic traits (entitlement, exploitativeness, and exhibitionism). age and gender did not have a moderating impact on these relationships. journal of early adolescence

costly prosociality, familiarity among peers, and school climate: a predictive model the objective of this study is to examine the associations between costly prosociality toward known and unknown school peers and well-being, school aggression, and school climate among chilean secondary school students by estimating structural paths from costly prosociality to these variables. a correlational and explanatory quantitative study was conducted using a sample of 529 chilean secondary school students recruited through convenience sampling. likert-type self-report scales were administered to measure costly prosociality, school aggression, well-being, and school climate. hcpb toward both known and unknown peers was positively associated with well-being and school climate. in the structural models, the model involving known peers showed a significant negative path to school aggression, whereas the model involving unknown peers did not show a significant path to school aggression. the two structural models showed different descriptive patterns of associations, with the model involving unknown peers accounting for 34% of the variance in school climate, while the model involving known peers accounted for 27%. these findings provide descriptive evidence of distinct patterns of associations between costly prosociality and school-related variables according to beneficiary familiarity. in the discussion section, results are analyzed in light of the literature. behavioral sciences

the interface between parental and occupational burnout in critical care unit staff: a multicentre cross-sectional study occupational burnout among critical care unit (ccu) staff is a pressing issue, yet the relationship between parental burnout and this high-demand professional domain remains underexplored. thus, this study aimed to analyze the association between parental and occupational burnout in critical care healthcare professionals. a multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted across three ccus in hospitals within the vigo health area (northern spain). the sample included 106 ccu staff members with dependent children. data were collected using the burnout screening inventory, parental burnout assessment, and oslo social support scale. although the overall prevalence of occupational burnout was low in this sample, total parental burnout emerged as a statistically significant positive predictor of occupational burnout (β = 0.303, p = 0.003). among its dimensions, parental emotional distancing acted as the most salient predictor (β = 0.409, p = 0.006). parental burnout is significantly associated with higher levels of occupational burnout among ccu professionals, with parental emotional distancing being the most relevant dimension in this relationship, with perceived social support as an inverted association. these findings highlight the co-occurrence of both phenomena and the need to acknowledge the intersection of family demands and high-intensity work environments when addressing occupational wellbeing in critical care settings. behavioral sciences
posterior cortical atrophy: a seven-year single case study of neurocognition and adaptation clinical neuropsychologist

counseling trainees’ burnout, professional identity, and multicultural and social justice counseling competencies: a two‐wave prospective study abstract the authors of this study examined how counseling trainees’ ( n = 89) burnout and professional identity influenced their multicultural and social justice counseling competencies (msjcc) based on the conservation of resources theory. prospective multiple regression analyses using a two‐wave survey design showed that professional efficacy and professional identity positively and significantly predicted their msjcc, whereas exhaustion and cynicism were not statistically significant predictors of msjcc. no differences in counseling trainees’ msjcc scores were found across their sociodemographic characteristics. implications for counseling trainees’ msjcc development are provided. counselor education and supervision

with others, more myself: personal expressiveness as identity enactment in adult daily life abstract personal expressiveness (pe), the feeling that an activity reflects one’s true self, is a core experiential marker of eudaimonia and identity functioning, signaling that identity commitments are reflective of one’s “daimon.” in adulthood, identity commitments are often organized around relatively stable roles and relationships, suggesting that experiences of personal expressiveness may reflect not only the types of activities individuals pursue but also the relational contexts in which those activities are enacted. the present research examined how social context relates to pe across adulthood. study 1 analyzed cross-sectional data from 294 adults (m age = 40.19) who reported on a personally expressive activity and its typical social context. pe did not differ reliably across social formats and showed continuity across adult developmental age groups, though descriptively higher levels emerged in socially embedded pursuits. study 2 used experience sampling with 52 adults (m age = 40.46) to examine momentary associations between pe and social context in daily life. multilevel mediation analyses showed that above-average momentary pe was associated with a greater likelihood of concurrent social presence and was indirectly associated with continued social presence across adjacent sampling occasions through concurrent social presence. together, these findings suggest that in adulthood, personal expressiveness may function less as a property of specific activities and more as a momentary process through which established identities are socially enacted in daily life. journal of adult development

predicting adolescent conduct problems: a machine learning approach using early family and child predictors abstract early recognition of predictors of adolescents' conduct problems is crucial for timely intervention. the use of traditional regression models, however, is limited in the ability to identify non‐linear relationships between predictor variables. this study employed multiple machine learning algorithms to predict adolescent conduct problems from earlier family and child functioning variables, comparing algorithm performance to identify which methods and early indicators most accurately forecast later problems. data from 242 families were analysed using eight machine learning algorithms. the algorithms were used to predict conduct problems in adolescence, as assessed by the sdq conduct problems scale, from 15 predictor variables assessed 1 year earlier, including but not limited to interparent conflict, emotional security, depression, anxiety and somatic concerns. support vector regression emerged as the best‐performing model ( r 2 = .343, rmse = 1.381), outperforming baseline prediction. feature importance analyses indicated that disengagement in response to interparental conflict was the strongest predictor of later conduct problems. insecurity in the interparental relationship, depressive symptoms and aggressive behaviour also contributed substantially to prediction. this pattern suggests that children's dysregulated coping and perceived lack of safety within the family system are more proximal predictors of later conduct problems than exposure to conflict alone. british journal of developmental psychology

preschoolers' peer preferences for observable empathy‐related responses to others' emotions abstract empathy supports early peer relationships, yet whether preschoolers use unfamiliar peers' observable empathy‐related responses when making initial peer choices remains unclear. guided by a functionalist perspective, the present research examined whether preschoolers' peer preferences are shaped by outward behavioural cues associated with empathy‐related responding to others' emotional states. across three primary ( n = 64 each) and two follow‐up experiments ( n = 60 each), children watched puppet vignettes where peer characters displayed different empathy‐related responses to another's emotional event. in study 1, children chose a character who expressed concern and offered comfort after injury over a nonresponsive one. in studies 2a and 2b, children preferred a distress‐responsive character over joy‐sharing and nonresponsive characters; this pattern held after removing the touch‐based comforting cue. in studies 3a and 3b, children chose an inquiry‐based responder over either a distress‐matching responder or a nonresponsive character; this pattern remained when the distress‐matching display was less emotionally intense. exploratory covariate checks revealed no statistically detectable associations with age, gender or individual empathy measures, though statistical precision was limited. together, findings suggest that preschoolers use observable empathy‐related response profiles when making initial peer choices, distinguishing both emotional context and response form within constrained forced‐choice tasks. british journal of developmental psychology
conceptualization and validation of the adolescent barriers to accessing psychotherapy questionnaire child & youth care forum
emotion regulation in early adolescence: using dyadic experience sampling to examine the regulatory strategies used by youths and their trauma-exposed mothers child & youth care forum

what is it like to recover from psychosis? an interpretative phenomenological analysis abstract this study aims to explore the lived experience of recovery from psychosis, with a focus on pre-reflective, embodied, and intersubjective aspects. semi-structured interviews were conducted with six individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia. the data collected were analyzed using interpretative phenomenological analysis (ipa). in total, six persons (age 35-78y, m = 4 w = 2, diagnosis f20.0; f25.-) who claim themselves to be recovered took part in this study. the analysis revealed six key experiential themes. recovery was characterized as a dynamic, non-linear process involving feelings of being pulled downward, self-doubt, emergence, resonance with oneself, resonance with others, and self-acceptance. the findings indicate that recovery is not solely cognitive or narrative-based but is also deeply embodied and relational, with significant roles played by experiential dimensions of verticality (e.g. a sense of being pulled downward or lightness) and horizontality (losing or re-gaining intercorporeal connection). the study challenges existing models by emphasizing existential transformation over mere symptom remission. it advocates for more holistic and experience-based approaches in clinical practice to better support individuals recovering from psychosis. human arenas

dravet syndrome: a primer for behavior analysts abstract dravet syndrome (ds) is a rare and severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy that is characterized by prolonged seizures beginning in the first year of life, followed by debilitating and complex features, including sleep disturbances, feeding problems, social‐emotional difficulties, speech deficits, and cognitive and motor impairments. while research with the ds population has been primarily focused on reducing seizures and other medical symptoms of ds, caregivers report many additional symptoms, such as behavior and cognitive impairment, that significantly impact their loved one with ds and the caregiver and family quality of life. as is common in rare disease research, medical and pharmacological research often takes precedent due to the significant burden of disease. however, therapies based on the science of applied behavior analysis could potentially address the behaviors, skill deficits, and cognitive challenges associated with ds. this article aims to provide an introduction to the complex and unique characteristics of ds for those working in the field of behavior analysis, with the hope of facilitating innovative research to discover effective applied behavior analytic interventions and treatments to help individuals with ds receive the needed supports and live a higher quality of life. behavioral interventions

“it’s between life and death”: nigerian women’s experience of pregnancy and childbirth these findings imply that greater attention to women's psychological needs could retain their autonomy, competence and relatedness during pregnancy and childbirth. women should be encouraged to become informed about pregnancy and birth but may need guidance to reliable sources. practitioners should be aware that women need the support of significant others during labour. psychology & health
association between depression, anxiety, and problematic opioid use among adults with cancer at a tertiary referral hospital in northern iran discover mental health

metabolic, endocrine and reproductive comorbidities in functional neurological disorder: a retrospective study of a tertiary neuropsychiatry cohort abstract background functional neurological disorder (fnd) is a common and disabling condition increasingly recognised to coexist with multiple comorbidities, though metabolic, reproductive and endocrine profiles remain underexplored. methods a retrospective case record review was conducted of 282 adults with neurologist-confirmed fnd attending a tertiary neuropsychiatry service. data on metabolic, reproductive and endocrine comorbidities were extracted from clinical records. associations between metabolic/endocrine comorbidities and fnd subtypes were examined using fisher’s exact tests with false discovery rate correction. selected associations with functional cognitive disorder (fcd) were further examined using multivariable logistic regression. results metabolic and endocrine disorders were recorded in 25.5% and 24.8% of the cohort, respectively. diabetes mellitus (12.4%), thyroid dysfunction (11.7%) and hypertension (10.6%) were the most prevalent individual conditions. several nominal associations were observed between fnd subtypes and metabolic/endocrine comorbidities, but none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. fcd showed the strongest association with dyslipidaemia (29.2% vs. 7.4%; or 5.18, 95% ci 1.91–14.03; unadjusted p = 0.003), which persisted after adjustment for age and sex (aor 3.75, 95% ci 1.29–10.90; p = 0.015), although this finding remained exploratory and the corresponding unadjusted association did not survive fdr correction. conclusions metabolic, reproductive and endocrine comorbidities were commonly recorded in adults with fnd. exploratory analyses suggest that metabolic comorbidity may vary across fnd subtypes, particularly in relation to fcd and dyslipidaemia, but these findings require replication in larger prospective controlled studies. discover mental health
all bi myself: addressing biphobia and bi-erasure in couples therapy with mixed-orientation couples journal of couple & relationship therapy-innovations in clinical and educational interventions

a methodology for assessing the content-related aspect of intrinsic motivation in learning activity the productivity of learning activity in recent research is often linked to the presence of intrinsic motivation, which determines the relevance of this study. the research problem lies in the heterogeneity of intrinsic motivation as the relationship between formal-dynamic and substantive components within self-determination theory and activity theory. according to e. deci and r. ryan, intrinsic motivation is largely determined by formal-dynamic factors - interest and enjoyment of the activity. a. n. leontiev not only emphasizes the content of the meaning-making motive but also underscores the change in content (subject matter) as a mechanism for the development of intrinsic motivation. this logic is detailed specifically in the motivation for learning activity. the aim of this study is a pilot approbation of a methodology that distinguishes the content-related side from the formal-dynamic side of intrinsic motivation in student learning activity. methods. the study involved 93 students from psychology departments in moscow (ages m = 21.50; sd = 6.99; 80 females). the following instruments were used: the academic motivation questionnaire (gordeeva, sychev, osin, 2014) to assess formal-dynamic intrinsic motivation, and a modified methodology for the involuntary memorization of professional-thematic texts (dusavitsky, 2012) to assess content-related intrinsic motivation. the texts were structured into four parts: "fact", "theory", "experiment", "application". results. a significant positive correlation was found between the completeness of recall of the theoretical part of the text and the assessment of interest (r = 0.23, p < 0.05), which confirms the hypothesis about the relationship between content-related intrinsic motivation and interest in theoretical content. when comparing groups of students oriented toward theoretical versus practical content, it was revealed that "theorists" show a tendency toward greater interest in the texts (u = 54, p = 0.073), while "practitioners" show significantly higher positivity of emotions (u = 46, p = 0.036). a positive correlation was found between the completeness of recall of the "experiment" part and the self-development scale of the academic motivation questionnaire (r = 0.22, p < 0.05). conclusions. the modified involuntary memorization methodology, on the one hand, allows for the empirical separation of the content-related and formal-dynamic sides of intrinsic motivation in student learning activity. on the other hand, a deeper analysis of the formal-dynamic features of intrinsic motivation developed within self-determination theory appears necessary. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

effectiveness of remote training of long-term consequences of post-covid cognitive dysfunction depending on patient age the study evaluated the effectiveness of a 7-day remote cognitive training program delivered via the "aita" mobile application in 110 patients with long-term consequences of post-covid cognitive dysfunction. to assess the modifying role of age, the sample was stratified into two groups: group 1 (n = 28, median age 39 years, mean time since covid-19 3.9 ± 0.9 years) and group 2 (n = 82, median age 22 years, time since covid-19 4.4 ± 0.8 years). at baseline assessment, significant intergroup differences were identified: participants in the older age group demonstrated more pronounced deficits in the domains of neurodynamics, spatial memory, visual recognition, and information selection (p < 0.05). following the one-week training program, significant positive changes were observed in both groups. in group 1, improvements were focused in nature (neurodynamics, working memory, speed of schulte table completion, and duplicate word search), whereas in group 2, the restorative effect was more differentiated and encompassed all modules, including visuospatial memory and attention switching. subjectively, participants reported moderate improvements in attention and memory and a reduction of "brain fog" (overall effectiveness: 0.48 ± 0.3 points; satisfaction: 3.63/5). correlation analysis revealed associations between objective performance metrics and retrospective self-ratings, indicating a "regression to the mean" phenomenon and underscoring the importance of balancing cognitive load with user comfort. the findings suggest that the effectiveness of digital rehabilitation for post-covid cognitive dysfunction is determined not by the linear time elapsed since infection, but by age-related characteristics and baseline cognitive reserve. the "aita" application demonstrated sustained therapeutic potential; however, target domains of correction vary substantially depending on age profile, supporting the need to implement personalized, age-adapted protocols in remote neurorehabilitation practice. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

the relationship between screen time duration and non-verbal imagination in preschoolers from different regions of russia the involvement of modern preschoolers in the digital environment raises the question of how different forms of screen activity affect the development of higher mental functions, including imagination. the inconsistency of existing findings indicates the need to move from analyzing total screen time to studying the differentiated contribution of its types while considering individual characteristics. the aim of this study was to analyze the relationship between active and passive screen time and parameters of imagination (flexibility, originality, elaboration) in preschoolers, taking into account gender and regional context. the study involved 1,670 children from preparatory groups of kindergartens (mean age 6.6 years, 51.5% girls) from three regions of russia - moscow, perm krai, and the republic of sakha (yakutia) - which significantly differ in the typical daily screen time. imagination was assessed using o. m. dyachenko's "figure completion" technique. data on active and passive screen time were obtained through a parent survey. the results showed that active screen time was negatively associated with certain imagination parameters (flexibility and originality coefficient), and these effects were significant only for boys and emerged exclusively in regions with low and medium screen time load. passive screen time showed no consistent associations with imagination. the findings highlight the need for a differentiated approach to analyzing a child's digital experience, taking into account the type of activity, gender, and regional context. the results contribute to understanding the non-linear and mediated nature of the influence of the digital environment on imagination development in preschool age. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

psychological resources of professional development and psychological well-being of college and university students under uncertainty stress latest social challenges have increased the interest in uncertainty stress research. these studies are particularly relevant in the context of young people's professional development and psychological well-being, given the increasing uncertainty of both the professional world and life in general. therefore, it is important to study the psychological resources that contribute to the professional development and psychological well-being of students under uncertainty stress. this study aimed to analyze the psychological resources of professional development and psychological well-being under uncertainty stress in students of secondary vocational and higher educational institutions. methods. survey methods were used to diagnose psychological resources, uncertainty stress, professional development, and psychological well-being. statistical analysis included correlation analysis and structural equation modeling (sem). sample: 1,822 students (935 college students and 887 university students). results. conscious self-regulation is a universal resource for professional development and psychological well-being under uncertainty stress. for the first time, the specificity of psychological resources under the various types of uncertainty stress was described. the results showed that under conditions of objective uncertainty stress, psychological well-being makes the most significant positive contribution to professional development, whereas under conditions of subjective uncertainty stress, the contributions of well-being and the level of conscious self-regulation are almost equal. hardiness is a significant resource, mitigating the impact of subjective and objective uncertainty stress on psychological well-being, whereas dispositional optimism becomes a resource only under conditions of objective uncertainty stress. the specific nature of college or university education does not directly influence students' professional development and psychological well-being. however, the level of uncertainty stress and the expression of psychological resources are higher among university students than among college students. conclusion: thus, psychological resources for professional development and psychological well-being vary depending on the type of stress and enable russian students to successfully overcome subjective and objective uncertainty stress. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

imagination as a moderator of the relationship between screen time and resistance to using digital devices in children 6–7 years old today's preschoolers are experiencing increased screen time and new behavioral phenomena, including resistance to stopping digital device use (negative emotions, protest, and affective outbursts). despite evidence linking screen time to emotional and behavioral difficulties in children, the psychological factors that may weaken or strengthen this association remain insufficiently studied. imagination, as a key mental function of preschool age, may serve as an internal resource facilitating the child's transition to alternative activities. the aim of this study was to assess the role of imagination as a moderator of the relationship between screen time and a child's resistance to discontinuing the use of digital devices. methods. the study involved 350 preschool children (ages 6-7 years) attending kindergartens in moscow, kazan, perm, and yakutsk. data on the duration of screen time and the occurrence of resistance upon discontinuing the use of digital devices were obtained through a survey of mothers. imagination was assessed using o. m. dyachenko's "figure completion" method, which evaluates the originality, flexibility, elaboration, and coefficient of originality of imagination. descriptive statistics, the mann-whitney u test, and moderation analysis were employed for data analysis. results. resistance to discontinuing the use of digital devices was observed in the majority of children. boys exhibited longer screen time duration, whereas girls demonstrated higher levels of imagination development. moderation analysis revealed that the elaboration of imagination is a significant moderator of the relationship between active screen time on weekdays and the occurrence of resistance in girls. at low levels of imagination elaboration, an increase in active screen time was associated with a higher probability of resistance upon discontinuing device use. no statistically significant effects were found for other indicators of imagination or for the subsample of boys. conclusions. a developed imagination can be an important internal resource, facilitating a child's successful transition from digital activities to alternative pursuits. the development of imagination can be considered one of the factors in the psychological adaptation of preschoolers to the digital environment. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

typological features of the value-based determination of cognitive choice at the initial stage of professional training the purpose of this study is to identify the value foundations of cognitive choice and their relationships with strategies and decision-making tendencies prevalent among students at the initial stage of vocational training. this paper examines current research by russian and international scholars dedicated to identifying the relationships between personal values and behavior, as well as their views on the selectivity that determines the direction of life choices. the paper presents the results of a study examining the typological characteristics of the value-based determination of student's cognitive choices. sample. the study was conducted on a sample of freshmen in various fields of study at the siberian university of consumer cooperatives in novosibirsk. the total number of respondents was 191, including 73 males (38.22%) and 118 females (61.78%). the average age was 19 years. the selection of respondents was based on the fact that freshmen had recently made an important life decision related to choosing a field of vocational training. methods. the diagnostic methods used were several questionnaires, which included 5 techniques aimed at diagnosing decision-making tendencies and strategies and 1 questionnaire examining the motivational continuum of personality (s. schwartz), consisting of 19 individual values. data analysis was conducted using the varimax method in the jamovi 2.2.5 statistical program. research results. five factors demonstrating the specificity of the relationship between various decision-making strategies and personal values were empirically identified: a) "personal stability in cognitive choice"; "openness to cognitive choice"; "maladaptation and lack of initiative"; "orientation to personal success and achievements in conditions of cognitive choice"; "rationalism and orientation towards ensuring one's own safety in a situation of cognitive choice". conclusions and findings. as a result of the study, four types of value conditioning of cognitive choice were identified and described, demonstrating selectivity that determines the direction of cognitive choice. the obtained results allow us to consider cognitive choice as a process of cognitive-motivational orientation of a person under conditions of cognitive uncertainty and multitasking. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

a review of contemporary databases with emotional ratings for words information on the emotional characteristics of words is widely used in contemporary research on emotional stimulus processing, as well as in linguistic and psycholinguistic studies. since the parameters of the emotional valence of words constitute subjective linguistic characteristics and therefore require dedicated empirical studies, some researchers have focused on developing databases containing information on the emotional properties of large numbers of words. to date, numerous such databases have been created for different languages, and the data they provide are often used uncritically, without sufficient consideration of the methods employed for data collection, the substantive meaning of the ratings, and related issues. in this context, a critical synthesis of the key aspects involved in the development of such databases appears highly relevant. the aim of the present study is to provide an overview of psycholinguistic tools containing information on the emotional parameters of words and to conduct a critical analysis of the information they contain from both theoretical and methodological perspectives. the article reviews the major contemporary databases containing ratings of the emotional parameters of words, describes which emotional parameters they include and why, examines how methodological issues are addressed during data collection, and outlines the challenges that users of such databases may encounter. in addition, the paper provides, for the first time, the most comprehensive overview to date of russian-language databases and word lists containing emotional parameters. particular attention is devoted to the analysis of the conceptual content of emotional parameters. it is noted that most databases use the dimensional rather than categorical approach. with regard to whether the databases assess affective reactions to words or representations of their connotative meaning, it is suggested that the published ratings cannot be unambiguously classified according to this distinction. it was also demonstrated that, despite the large overall samples involved in database development, the actual number of individuals who rated a particular word may be relatively small. finally, attention is drawn to the fact that relying solely on averaged ratings to characterize the emotional properties of words may be insufficient; standard deviations of ratings should also be taken into account in analyses of word emotional characteristics. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

electrophysiological correlates of the influence of transformational psychological methods on coping behavior this work aims to investigate the impact of a transformational psychological game on changes in psychological parameters of coping behavior and to identify electrophysiological correlates, taking into account the age characteristics of the subjects. the intervention was carried out using the transformational psychological game "shambhala-5" (by t. e. sizikova). the article analyzes psychologists' views on transformation, a concept with a history of over a century but rarely applied in scientific and practical psychology. from c. g. jung to m. sh. magomed-eminov, the concept of transformation has acquired its deepened and expanded meaning. the conducted experimental study on the influence of the transformational psychological gaming method on an individual's state and their reflection is novel and necessary in the contemporary direction of psychology's development. a sequence of tests was used: the proactive coping inventory (pci), adapted by e. p. belinskaya and a. v. vecherin (2018); the ways of coping questionnaire (wcq), adapted by the national institute of psychiatry and neurology (2009); the coping strategy indicator (csi), adapted by n. a. sirota and v. m. yaltonsky (1994). for the objective diagnosis of a person's psychophysiological state, an electroencephalogram (eeg) was recorded before and after the transformational game. the study involved 156 people (mean age 27 ± 9 years). the sample was divided by age criterion: under 22 years old (mean age 20 ± 2 years) and over 22 years old (mean age 33 ± 8 years). the results showed that the transformational psychological game, as a method working with coping strategies, had the greatest impact on the age group over 22 years old and consistently influenced the search for and acceptance of the need for constructive methods and strategies of self-regulation and self-organization under stressful conditions. the results revealed interhemispheric differences in the theta- and beta-rhythm ranges of the eeg in the older group of participants (over 22 years old), indicating a significant impact of the game on the psychophysiological state. the conducted study emphasizes the importance of using transformational gaming methods in psychology to improve overall emotional state, including stress management, based on reflection, and opens new directions for further research. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

the relationship between cognitive and personal characteristics among students of high-tech and humanitarian education the relationship between cognitive and personal aspects of student development as a complex and multifaceted problem is becoming an object of research in the context of studying the psychological factors of university success. cognitive and personality traits can interact both directly and through mediating factors, influencing learning success, psychological wellbeing, and other aspects of educational and professional activities. along with this, personal and cognitive characteristics underlie educational and professional choices, thus acting as an important factor in the success of education and professional development at a university. at the same time, it is noted that, both in the cognitive and personal spheres, the question of determining the factors determining the success of learning remains open. the purpose of the study: to identify typo-logical differences in the relationship of non-verbal intelligence with the personal qualities of students, depending on the profile of training (high-tech or humanities). materials and methods. the sample consisted of 116 high-tech students and 130 university humanities students. research methods: the raven progressive matrices test, the big five questionnaire (version bfi-2-s), the intellectual risk assessment scale, the aspiration index questionnaire, and the method of diagnostics of subjective well-being. the results of the study. according to the university's study profiles, the factors and types of students are described according to the criteria of severity of non-verbal intelligence and personal qualities (conscientiousness, tolerance to uncertainty, life aspirations and subjective well-being). both general trends and differences in the characteristics of connections between nonverbal intelligence and significant age-related personal qualities among students of high-tech and humanitarian education are highlighted. based on the psychological content of the identified factors and types of students, possible psychological predictors of educational and professional success have been identified, which, as a working hypothesis, will be tested taking into account the real results of students’ academic performance at subsequent stages of the longitudinal study. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

educational activity strategy as a subject of psychological research: a theoretical model the relevance of the present study is determined by transformations of the educational environment, expansion of informal and digital learning formats, and the increasing role of learner agency, which necessitates moving beyond traditional approaches to the analysis of educational strategies. the absence of a comprehensive conceptualization of educational activity strategy as an integrative construct uniting goal-related, motivational, instrumental, and resource-based aspects of cognitive organization constitutes the core research problem. the aim of the article is to develop a theoretical model of educational activity strategy and to substantiate the possibilities of its operationalization in psychological research. the main methods employed include a theoretical review of contemporary studies on cognitive and metacognitive strategies, as well as theoretical modeling, which enabled the synthesis of empirical data into a unified conceptual framework. the resulting model of educational activity (ea) strategy delineates goal-oriented, motivational, instrumental, and resource components, manifested at both the cognitive and metacognitive level. the goal-oriented component involves setting goals and tasks at the cognitive level and reflection on goal setting at the metacognitive level. the motivational component reflects perceived value and interest in learning at the cognitive level, and reflexive evaluation of educational activity motives at the metacognitive level. the instrumental component comprises techniques for information processing at the cognitive level and a system supporting their implementation at the metacognitive level. the resource component pertains to assessing task accessibility relative to anticipated costs at the cognitive level and managing these resources by aligning personal readiness with the sufficiency of external resources at the metacognitive level. within this model, educational activity strategy is defined as a set of methods by which an individual organizes their own cognition and development within the educational process, grounded in their agentive position and entailing conscious management of goals, resources, motives, and means during learning. sibirskiy psikhologicheskiy zhurnal-siberian journal of psychology

effects of land acknowledgements on non-indigenous audiences in australia and the usa nature human behaviour, published online: 25 september 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02520-6 mcnamee and peyton find that land acknowledgements raise awareness of, but not curiosity about, indigenous nations. these practices improve organizational reputations, but their effects on political attitudes and support for reparations are insignificant. nature human behaviour

shared friend criteria modulate aesthetic judgment of faces and paintings but not moral beauty aesthetic preferences are shaped by social context, yet the influence of close peers’ standards across different aesthetic domains remains unclear. this study investigated whether friends’ aesthetic criteria modulate individuals’ judgments of faces, paintings, and moral beauty using a modified social conformity paradigm across three experiments. results showed that individuals’ aesthetic judgments of faces and paintings were significantly influenced by their friends’ ratings, shifting systematically toward peer evaluations. in contrast, judgments of moral beauty were largely unaffected by peer influence. these findings suggest that social cognitive factors shape aesthetic judgment in a domain-specific manner: stimuli with relatively objective perceptual features (e.g., facial averageness and painting composition) are more susceptible to social influence, whereas moral beauty—grounded in internalized values—remains more resistant. evolutionary psychology

pluralism within limits: how to make the idea of multiple ncc kinds useful abstract recently, several authors have argued that the current impasse in consciousness science supports a pluralistic interpretation: the view that seemingly contradictory findings may both be valid because consciousness can be brought about in different ways, each sufficient to generate conscious experience. we analyze different versions of pluralism to determine under what conditions it offers a viable interpretation of consciousness science. we argue that viable pluralism requires a two-factor framework distinguishing general consciousness factors (mechanisms rendering contents conscious) from content encoding itself. moreover, neural correlates of consciousness (ncc) kinds must be finite in number and systematically ordered to enable a unified scientific model. while pluralism enables testable hypotheses, significant ontological tensions arise: how can consciousness constitute a unified natural kind if realized by fundamentally distinct ncc kinds? drawing on philosophy of science, we propose an alternative interpretation in terms of scientific rather than natural kinds. our goal is not to advocate for pluralism, but rather, to critically examine its viability and implications. based on this, we urge the field to engage more explicitly with the foundational assumptions that shape consciousness research. neuroscience of consciousness

why girls have worse mental health than boys. nature human behaviour, published online: 22 september 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02577-3 analyses of data from more than 3,000 adolescents found that loneliness and desire for thinness contribute to the higher prevalence of depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation among girls than in boys. young people’s perspectives informed the pathways that were investigated. nature human behaviour

motor and operative intentionality in computational phenomenology: from shallow to deep active inference models abstract computational phenomenology has been recently presented as a novel and promising approach to modelling human experience with the use of computational techniques. more specifically, as it has been discussed in recent work, it links phenomenological descriptions and analyses of lived experience and generative modelling techniques, most prominently, through active inference. it is argued that the experiential disclosure of the world and time-consciousness can be cast in terms of free energy minimization and inferential dynamics. it has not been addressed yet, however, whether and to what extent active inference may be able to model fundamental structures that constitute what phenomenologists call ‘motor intentionality’, i.e. our general embodied and practical openness to our experiential world. this openness is taken to underlie all experience. to address this gap in the literature, we propose to distinguish two different kinds of practical aspects within active inference. first, we discuss the approximation to a true posterior as a form of active process that can be linked with some of the core characteristics of what phenomenologists call ‘passive syntheses’. secondly, we discuss the process of action selection under likelihood mappings and preferences and link it with the constitution of a field of affordances of an embodied subject, as well as with the idea that the body is ‘the first prior’ within an active inference model. this embodied constitution is the core of what phenomenologists call ‘motor intentionality’. insofar as these two practical aspects of active inference are processes undertaken within the model, we emphasize the temporality that underlies them in terms of subjective temporality and objective time. neuroscience of consciousness

tinkering with social tinkering abstract our commentators have broadly welcomed the notion of social tinkering, while also offering a range of suggestions, refinements, and potential challenges. in our response, we clarify the concept of social tinkering, sharpen our account of the six stages of cultural evolution, consider whether additional mechanisms are needed to explain the emergence of cultural complexity, and explore a range of possible extensions to the social tinkering framework. we conclude by discussing broader implications and future directions for this research program, including a reconsideration of rogers’ paradox. behavioral and brain sciences
