development and temporal validation of a screening-based prediction model for suicidal ideation at first contact with university counseling services. background: suicidal ideation among university students is a major public health concern. yet counseling services still lack practical tools that can identify students at elevated risk during their first clinical contact. this study aimed to develop and temporally validate a screening‑based prediction model for suicidal ideation at the time of initial presentation to university counseling services.
methods: this retrospective observational study analyzed routinely collected data from a japanese university counseling services. predictor variables were exclusively derived from annual mental health screening data collected before participants used counseling services. the variables included psychological distress, self‑esteem, lifestyle‑related factors, and demographic characteristics. the outcome was suicidal ideation assessed during the first counseling intake interview. we developed a multivariable logistic regression model using a development cohort of students who accessed counseling services between 2017 and 2019 and temporally validated the model in an independent cohort from 2021 to 2023. we evaluated the model performance using discrimination, measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (auc), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (dca). a reference value threshold was identified using a youden index-based cutoff.
results: the development and validation cohorts included 1,136 and 1,286 students, respectively. the prevalence of suicidal ideation at intake was comparable across cohorts (14.0% and 14.7%). the model achieved moderate discrimination in the development cohort (auc = 0.71) and good discrimination in the validation cohort (auc = 0.74), with acceptable calibration in both cohorts. higher levels of screening‑based psychological distress, particularly feelings of worthlessness, female sex, and lower self-esteem increased the odds of suicidal ideation at intake. conversely, call-based or early outreach referral routes were associated with lower odds. dca showed that the model provided greater net benefit than strategies that intervened in all or no students across clinically plausible threshold probabilities, including the youden index‑based cutoff (approximately 0.13).
conclusions: routinely collected mental health screening data can predict suicidal ideation at the time of initial counseling contact with reasonable accuracy and potential clinical utility. screening‑based prediction models may strengthen existing student support systems by enabling earlier identification of elevated risk and guiding proportionate intervention strategies. bmc psychology

change to the recognition and revision of target problems and target problem procedures during eight‐session cognitive analytic therapy for self‐harm abstract objectives defining target problems (tps) and associated target problem procedures (tpps) is a key competency of cognitive analytic therapy (cat). this study sought to categorize types of tpps identified, assess the acceptability of tp/tpp sessional tracking, assess whether changes in tp/tpp recognition and revision occurred and also whether change in tp/tpps predicted severity of self‐injury urges and psychological distress. methods as part of the relate clinical trial, n = 31 participants were allocated to eight‐session cat. tps/tpps were rated for recognition and revision at every session in a nested abc plus follow‐up single case design. the competency of therapists was assessed. tpps were coded as to whether they were a snag, trap of a dilemma. linear mixed‐effects models tested whether tp/tpps changed over time and according to phase of cat. change in tps/tpps were used to predict self‐injury urges and psychological distress (i.e., research follow‐up measures taken by blinded researchers). results there was strong interrater agreement on whether the tpp was a snag, trap or dilemma. the sessional rating of tps/tpps appeared acceptable, as during 97.68% of treatment sessions and 82.60% of follow‐up sessions, tracking occurred. compared to the reformulation phase, awareness and then therapeutic change of tps/tpps significantly increased during the recognition and revision phases. recognition and revision of tps/tpps during cat in the revision phase did not predict self‐injury urges and psychological distress at research follow‐up. conclusion early definition and sessional tracking of tps/tpps appear acceptable and changes to awareness and ability to change tps/tpps appears linear. cat therapists should routinely integrate sessional tracking of tp/tpps into their work. british journal of clinical psychology

meta-analysis of executive function in children with cerebral palsy: an investigation of challenges to measurement validity abstract executive function (ef) has been increasingly identified as an area of difficulty in children with cerebral palsy (cp), but the exact nature of deficit remains elusive as accurate assessment of abilities is limited due to the physical and speeded task requirements of many standardised assessment tools. with the aim of estimating the magnitude of ef impairment and evaluating the validity of ef assessments, the current meta-analysis examined the impacts from cp characteristics, assessment task features, and study design factors through adopting a comprehensive cattell-horn-carroll cognitive ability taxonomy to ensure coverage of available assessments of ef and related subdomains. psycinfo, medline, web of science, and cinahl were searched to identify peer-reviewed studies that compared children with cp with neurotypical controls up to april 2025. a total of 43 studies with 448 effect sizes based on the ef and related cognitive task performance of 1240 participants with cp and 1554 neurotypical children were included. a large effect size for reduced performance across ef and related cognitive measures was identified in children with cp (hedges’ g = -.85) and effect sizes differed across ef and related ability subdomains, with greater effect sizes observed for processing speed, long-term memory, and visual-spatial skills. measurement validity was impacted differentially by ef and related subdomain, type of outcome measure, and level of motor impairment. timed measures were associated with larger effect sizes, and measures that accommodated motor difficulties showed smaller effects, highlighting the potential for non-ef factors to confound the validity of ef and related ability assessments. aligning participant capability with assessment demand will benefit accurate evaluation of cognitive function and guide targeted interventions for people with cp. neuropsychology review

transdiagnostic mri-derived features of psychopathology following traumatic brain injury: a systematic review. the biological basis of psychopathology outcomes in moderate-severe traumatic brain injury (tbi) remains poorly understood. previous reviews have found limited convergence in associations between brain regions or functions and specific psychopathology categories (e.g., anxiety, depression). the current systematic review aimed to evaluate mri-derived features of psychopathology transdiagnostically across available diagnostic categories in moderate-severe tbi. eligible studies investigated associations between mri-derived features (macro-, micro-structure, function) and psychopathology in adults with closed-moderate-severe tbi. we searched english literature from embase, psycinfo, and medline via ovid sp, and the review was last assessed as up to date on 2nd november 2023. risk of bias was assessed using a customised tool based on the joanna brigg's institute critical appraisal tools. the total number of records screened was 7,777 articles, with 18 meeting eligibility criteria. studies predominantly investigated hippocampal morphology (n = 7) and depression (n = 9). the average risk of bias fell within the "intermediate" range, associated with sampling, measurement, and statistical bias. findings were heterogeneous and inconsistent within specific psychopathology categories, yet some morphological features converged transdiagnostically (e.g., hippocampus, thalamus, fronto-temporal regions). notably, lower hippocampal volume was associated with higher depression (n = 2), anxiety (n = 1), apathy (n = 1), and psychosis (n = 1). no consistent microstructural and functional features converged across studies. this review provides a comprehensive evaluation of the current evidence regarding transdiagnostic mri-derived features of psychopathology and critiques common limitations across the literature, including the focus on structural mri, lack of appropriate comparators, and the narrow focus on specific psychopathology categories. we propose that transdiagnostic-dimensional frameworks may help address these gaps and advance the understanding of shared and distinct biological features of psychopathology in moderate-severe tbi.review registration: prospectively registered on 6/9/2022 in prospero (crd42022358358). neuropsychology review

description and effectiveness of environmental approaches to cognitive rehabilitation for traumatic brain injury: a systematic review of randomised controlled trials abstract interventions addressing cognitive impairments after traumatic brain injury (tbi) often rely on survivors’ relatively preserved capacity to learn, initiate, and consistently use rehabilitation strategies, along with the ability to apply strategies in various contexts. the cognitive functions required for such active engagement in rehabilitation are commonly impaired after tbi, consequently limiting the benefits of many existing cognitive rehabilitation approaches. environmental approaches, which involve manipulating the environment to support cognition and function, may benefit tbi survivors, as they do not require active involvement of the user to initiate and maintain their use. although these approaches are recommended by experts and frequently used, their effectiveness and components are largely unknown. we conducted a systematic review, searching for randomised controlled trials of adults with tbi who received environmental interventions for cognitive or related functional outcomes, compared to any control. two reviewers independently undertook screening and data extraction following a standardised protocol. risk of bias was assessed using joanna briggs institute critical appraisal instruments. five studies were included in the review. environmental intervention approaches included prompting (three studies) and trained communication partners (two studies), both of which demonstrated relatively strong evidence for their effectiveness. key methodological limitations included insufficient blinding to group allocation, randomisation concealment, reliability of outcome measurement, and lack of baseline similarity between groups. whilst environmental approaches involving prompting and trained communication partners demonstrate potential for improving the daily functioning of individuals with tbi, further research is needed. systematic review registration number: prospero crd42024592708, registered september 2024. neuropsychology review

momentary energy management profiles: associations with energy, heart rate variability, and motivational states abstract during work, employees use a variety of energy management strategies to conserve or recover their subjective energy, including microbreaks (e.g., socializing, walking) or work-related strategies (e.g., organizing, reflecting on meaning). research is yet to examine how these strategies co-occur and the implications of different configurations. moreover, little is known about other associated benefits of energy management, beyond energy. thus, we paired experience sampling with ambulatory heart rate monitoring to collect hourly data on energy management strategies and outcomes (i.e., energy, stress regulation as indexed by heart rate variability, and motivational states including intrinsic motivation and work mastery). ninety-one employees provided hourly data throughout a workday ( m = 6.62 occasions). multilevel latent profile analysis revealed a five-profile solution of momentary energy management strategies within hours of the workday: active strategizing (6%), moving (5%), socializing (15%), meaningful organizing (9%), and passive strategizing (65%). outcome analyses revealed the active, moving, and socializing profiles were better for vitality than the meaningful organizing and passive profiles. the moving profile was best for heart rate variability, compared to meaningful organizing, active, and passive profiles. finally, the active profile was better than all other profiles for motivational states. overall, results suggest the combination of microbreaks and work-related strategies is associated with more energy and motivational states, whereas distinctive use of physical microbreaks is linked to energy and physiological stress regulation, and socializing is related to energy. use of some work-related strategies (i.e., organizing, meaning) seems unrelated to outcomes when not paired with microbreaks. journal of business and psychology

clinician perspectives on barriers and enablers to autism‐affirming eating disorder care abstract objective autistic people with an eating disorder (ed) report more negative experiences of ed treatment and are at greater risk of requiring higher intensity services. current ed treatment options do not fully meet underpinning drivers of autistic people's experiences of eds. there remains little guidance or understanding on how autism‐informed adaptations are implemented. this paper aims to explore clinician‐perceived barriers and enablers to implementing autism‐affirming adaptations in uk ed services. method semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 12 clinicians in multidisciplinary roles across uk ed services who were beginning to implement autism‐affirming care. data were analysed using critical realist thematic analysis. results clinicians described many barriers associated with implementing autism‐affirming care underpinned by longstanding beliefs about the risks of accommodating ed behaviours. this contributed to anxiety about making adaptations to care and the potential to over‐ or under‐accommodate autistic needs. an underlying assumption that evidence‐based practice solely equates to manualised treatment for eds constrained adaptation. a commitment to individualised formulation and care, regardless of diagnosis, and valuing a diverse multidisciplinary team were key enablers. system‐level barriers included siloed autism and ed resources and training. conclusions autism‐affirming adaptations challenge some core underpinning messages historically embedded in siloed ed services. european eating disorders review

leisure guilt across four studies, we investigate a novel psychological construct: leisure guilt—the feeling of guilt or unease about spending time leisurely rather than productively—and examine its links to daily leisure and well-being. in studies 1a to 1c, we developed and validated the leisure guilt proneness (lgp) scale, which is internally consistent, stable over time, and predictive of poorer leisure experiences and lower well-being. in study 2, we employed the experience sampling method to capture leisure guilt dynamics in everyday life. on average, people experienced leisure guilt during 14% of leisure occasions, with higher rates among women, individuals with lower socioeconomic status, and younger adults. leisure type also mattered: leisure guilt was more common during solitary than social leisure. lastly, individuals high in lgp reported experiencing reduced psychological benefits from leisure. our findings identify leisure guilt as a potential barrier to the psychological benefits of leisure and daily well-being. personality and social psychology bulletin

generating collective social safety in times of political change: the motivating effects of inexplicable behavior a model of the generation of collective safety in social connection is proposed. this model posits that not being able to make sense of the behavior of others functions as an alert that motivates people who feel more vulnerable to the actions of societal collectives to find compensatory reason to trust in others. in two separate studies, participants in the united kingdom and participants in the united states completed surveys the day before, and after, the 2024 general/federal elections. preregistered moderated mediation analyses revealed that when family/friends behaved more (vs. less) inexplicably, participants who felt more (vs. less) vulnerable to the political party in power trusted sociopolitical relationships more rather than less. such compensatory affirmations predicted renewed trust in personal relationships and strengthened feelings of connection post-election, suggesting that inexplicable behavior can motivate vulnerable people to generate the safety they need to see during societal transitions. personality and social psychology bulletin

examining black emerging adults’ decision points for engaging parents versus peers as racial socialization sources while emerging adulthood is a period of significant transitions and adjustments, for black emerging adults, racial injustices are particular challenges that necessitate racial socialization from parents and peers to navigate these experiences. however, it is unclear what factors may influence their engagement with these different sources, which may subsequently impact their ability to cope with the racial injustices they experience. the current study addressed this gap in the existing literature by examining reasons why black emerging adults go to parents and peers as different sources of racial socialization. participants included 35 college-attending emerging adults (ages 18–26 years) attending a predominately white institution (pwi) in the southeastern region of the u.s. approximately 60% of participants were female, and the remainder were male. reflexive thematic analysis was used to analyze participants’ responses. three themes were developed from the data, including: (1) uncensored venting with peers, (2) parental wisdom and guidance from experience, and (3) managing parents’ fears and emotions (through strategic omission). findings highlight the ways that black emerging adults actively and strategically engage in the racial socialization process. journal of adolescent research

stress factors in parents of autistic children: an umbrella review abstract parents of autistic children are more prone to high levels of stress in their daily lives. this umbrella review synthesises evidence from 41 reviews on stressors parents face at micro-, meso-, and macrolevels. at microlevel, common stressors included children’s distress behaviours, autism characteristics, child-parent dependency, and parent’s worries and characteristics. at mesolevel, financial, marital, sibling, and community issues (e.g., stigmatisation, social isolation, and lack of social support) were frequent, while macrolevel stressors involved healthcare, education, and other support services. these findings highlight the need for an integrated approach to support parents, more attention to under-researched groups (e.g., fathers and parents of autistic daughters), and longitudinal research on parental stress over time. review journal of autism and developmental disorders

social and healthcare professionals working with family caregivers: fostering sustainable and socially transformative careers abstract in recent years, the concept of a sustainable career has evolved from an individual‐centered perspective to a relational, prosocial and community‐oriented model. care work, traditionally marginalised and characterised by a high risk of burnout, represents a privileged context for observing this transformation. this study explores the experiences of professionals involved in the caregiver bergamo project, developed by ats bergamo in collaboration with the asst, the social territorial districts, and the university of bergamo. the project establishes interprofessional teams composed of social workers, family and community nurses (ifec) and educators supporting family caregivers. the qualitative analysis of 14 interviews conducted with members of these teams identified four key dimensions of transformative sustainability: (1) relationship and proximity as drivers of change; (2) ethics of care and commitment to social justice; (3) social impact and community regeneration; and (4) identity reflection and professional development. these dimensions illustrate how caregiver teams foster practices that integrate individual well‐being, ethical responsibility, and social value, turning work experience into a collective, community‐oriented process. the caregiver team thus emerges not only as an essential support structure for those caring for dependent family members but also as a laboratory for rethinking the sustainability of careers in the social and healthcare professions. journal of community & applied social psychology

illness appraisals and self-actualisation in parents of children with rubinstein–taybi syndrome: a comparative analysis with educational and therapeutic professionals

parents of children with rubinstein–taybi syndrome (rts) face distinctive and often persistent caregiving stressors. the ways in which they appraise the illness—and how these appraisals differ from those of teachers and therapists—may shape parental self‑actualisation and inform the design of family‑centred support.

four groups were compared: mothers (n = 9), fathers (n = 8), teachers (n = 9), and therapists (n = 6). illness meaning was assessed with the disease related appraisals scale (dras; polish sowch), and parental self‑actualisation with the as‑5‑r (actualization of self scale). because score distributions deviated from normality, mann–whitney u tests (caregivers vs professionals) and kruskal–wallis tests (four‑group comparisons) were applied, followed by dunn–bonferroni contrasts. within‑parent associations were examined using spearman correlations.

parents reported higher threat, obstacle/loss, and harm appraisals than professionals, whereas teachers and therapists endorsed higher profit (benefit finding) and value. challenge and importance did not differ across groups. post hoc tests indicated that mothers scored higher than therapists and fathers higher than teachers on threat and harm (p < .05). among parents, challenge was positively associated with social relatedness, creative self‑expression, and global self‑actualisation. profit correlated positively with social relatedness, self‑regard, and global self‑actualisation. in contrast, value showed a negative association with self‑regard. creative self‑expression was additionally related to threat and importance.

parents often construe their child’s rts in terms of threat and loss, yet appraising the condition as a challenge or source of potential benefit aligns with richer relationships, greater creativity, and higher self‑actualisation. professionals already tend to endorse these more adaptive appraisals. structured parent–professional dialogue and benefit‑finding practices may support families in shifting toward growth‑promoting meanings without minimising the genuine burdens of caregiving.

initial validation of the computerized hebrew version of the morel emotional numbing test (ment) for detecting feigned ptsd in israel

post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) is among the most prevalent mental health disorders in israel. due to significant secondary gains (e.g., financial compensation), there is a substantial risk of malingering. performance validity tests (pvts) are essential for diagnostic integrity. this study aimed to perform an initial validation of the computerized hebrew version of the morel emotional numbing test (ment) and examine its psychometric properties within a simulated malingering design.

ninety participants were randomly assigned to either a control group (n = 45), instructed to respond honestly, or a simulation group (n = 45), instructed to feign ptsd symptoms based on a clinical vignette. all participants completed the ment, the structured inventory of malingered symptomatology (sims), and the ptsd checklist for dsm‑5 (pcl‑5). three individuals were excluded due to incomplete data, resulting in a final sample of 87 (control: n = 43; simulation: n = 44). roc curve analysis was used to determine optimal cut‑off scores.

the hebrew ment demonstrated excellent internal consistency (cronbach’s α = 0.966) and significantly differentiated between honest and simulated responders (p < 0.001; cohen’s d = 1.285). roc analysis yielded an area under the curve (auc) of 0.826, indicating acceptable discriminative accuracy. a cut‑off of five errors provided a sensitivity of 0.818 and a specificity of 0.767. significant positive correlations were observed between ment scores and both the sims total (r = 0.643) and sims affective (r = 0.633) scales.

preliminary evidence suggests that the hebrew version of the ment is a promising and efficient screening tool for detecting symptom exaggeration in israel. when combined with the sims affective scale within a tiered diagnostic framework, it may help reduce false‑positive classifications. further validation in clinical ptsd populations is required to confirm these findings.

percepções de preconceito e conflito trabalho-família: estudo com mulheres negras e homens brancos na década de 2020, as mulheres negras representam o maior grupo demográfico do brasil. apesar disso, apresentam as piores condições de trabalho. ademais, continuam sendo as principais responsáveis pelas tarefas domésticas, mesmo diante de uma elevada jornada de trabalho. com base nessas afirmações, este estudo teve como objetivo comparar os níveis de percepção de discriminação cotidiana, negação do preconceito, afirmação de diferenças e conflito entre trabalho e família em quatro grupos definidos pela interseção entre raça e gênero: homens negros, mulheres negras, homens brancos e mulheres brancas. participaram 628 trabalhadores/as brasileiros/as, sendo 17.5 % homens negros, 38.7 % mulheres negras, 14.2 % homens brancos e 29.6 % mulheres brancas, com idade entre 18 e 73 anos. devido à não normalidade dos dados, as análises foram conduzidas por meio do teste de kruskal-wallis, com comparações post hoc de dunn e correção de holm; foram reportados tamanhos de efeito e intervalos de confiança. os resultados evidenciaram que as mulheres negras apresentaram maiores níveis de discriminação cotidiana, enquanto pessoas brancas tiveram os menores níveis dessa experiência. em relação à negação do preconceito, os homens registraram maiores níveis em comparação às mulheres. não foram observadas diferenças significativas para a afirmação de diferenças e conflito trabalhofamília. em conjunto, os resultados sugerem a persistência de desigualdades consistentes com a literatura sobre racismo e sexismo, oferecendo reflexões relevantes sobre a temática. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

entre el contexto y la experiencia: inclusión laboral de personas con discapacidad en uruguay el presente estudio analiza los perfiles de inclusión laboral de personas con discapacidad a partir de la articulación entre los factores contextuales de la clasificación internacional del funcionamiento, la discapacidad y la salud (cif) y el modelo de calidad de vida (cdv). con un enfoque mixto, descriptivo y exploratorio, se estudian cuatro casos de personas participantes del programa suma, una iniciativa de la intendencia de montevideo orientada al diseño de soluciones técnicas personalizadas para la adaptación al puesto de trabajo. se aplicaron instrumentos estandarizados (whodas 2.0 para la evaluación del funcionamiento y la severidad de la discapacidad, y mos para el apoyo social percibido) y entrevistas semiestructuradas. los resultados fueron analizados mediante una operacionalización conjunta de ambos modelos, que permitió construir perfiles individuales y visualizarlos a través de gráficos radiales (spider charts). a partir del modelo cif se identifican configuraciones heterogéneas de barreras y facilitadores, destacándose el rol central de los apoyos sociales y las persistentes tensiones vinculadas a la accesibilidad. y con el modelo de cdv se evidencian desbalances entre dimensiones del bienestar, aún en contextos de inclusión laboral activa, lo que subraya la distancia entre inclusión formal y experiencia subjetiva de calidad de vida. la articulación de ambos enfoques aporta una comprensión integral de los procesos de inclusión laboral, poniendo en valor el análisis casuístico y la complementariedad entre indicadores contextuales y percepciones subjetivas. los hallazgos refuerzan la necesidad de políticas y programas que integren apoyos técnicos, sociales y psicosociales para promover trayectorias laborales significativas. avances en psicologia latinoamericana

financial coping following job loss: initial validation of a multidimensional measure and test of an expanded career self-management model research on coping with job loss has emphasized job search behavior aimed at re-employment, with comparatively less attention to how individuals manage the psychological and financial challenges associated with unemployment. to address this gap, we developed a multidimensional measure of financial coping and used it in an initial test of an expanded social cognitive model of career self-management (csm) in the context of job loss. participants were 554 u.s. adults without full-time employment after leaving a full-time job. exploratory factor analysis in one randomly selected sub-sample ( n = 250) yielded a 5-factor financial coping structure, which was supported in a confirmatory factor analysis in the second sub-sample ( n = 304). an expanded csm model, including the financial coping scales, generally fit the data well in predicting emotional functioning and job search progress. however, collectively, the financial coping dimensions explained only modest additional variance beyond established predictors, suggesting that they may reflect context-specific reactions to financial strain rather than broadly adaptive, protective resources. we discuss implications for theory, research, and career practice related to coping with unemployment. journal of career assessment
social anxiety, social avoidance, self-esteem, and loneliness: the role of class type for autistic adolescents journal of autism and developmental disorders

systematic review of the efficacy of parent-mediated interventions in reducing problem behaviours shown by autistic adolescents abstract purpose problem behaviours exacerbate the challenges associated with the core characteristics of autism during adolescence. parenting interventions have demonstrated efficacy in addressing such behavioural challenges in younger autistic individuals, however, their evidence for autistic adolescents is sparse, particularly in low-income settings. methods this systematic review narratively synthesised studies outlining parenting interventions targeting problem behaviours in autistic adolescents. results seven studies were included with three providing comparable quantitatively data for their efficacy in improving problem behaviours. five out of seven studies reported positive evidence on reducing problem behaviours. characteristics including fewer sessions, instructional mode of intervention delivery and use of behavioural management skills were most commonly shared among statistically significant studies. parenting interventions had a positive effect on adaptive behaviours for children, and improved parent wellbeing and knowledge. the overall satisfaction with interventions was high, however, only one study was conducted in a lower- and middle-income country. conclusion the findings underscore the encouraging evidence in an understudied area. the results emphasise the need to conduct further research for autistic adolescents and highlight potential parent-mediated interventions carry, given their acceptability and logistically scalable nature. journal of autism and developmental disorders

ptr-yc in action: child, parent, and family outcomes of a challenging behavior management program in real-world public early intervention settings abstract purpose the aim of this study was to determine the efficacy of the prevent-teach-reinforce for young children (ptr-yc) as implemented within public early behavioral intervention (ebi) for children with autism or intellectual disability. several adjustments to the research design and to training and intervention protocols were made in response to organizational constraints, the covid-19 several waves and families’ needs within this real-world intervention context. methods ebi educators were trained in the ptr-yc program, which they then applied with the parents of a child in their caseload who presented challenging behavior. parent-practitioner intervention teams were divided in two cohorts according to their readiness to apply the program. parents evaluated their chid’s challenging behavior, their parenting stress levels, caregiving strain, and sense of competence, as well as their family’s quality of life before and after program application, as well as the acceptability of the program after its application. results frequency of children’s aggressive behavior, decreased significantly after program application, but not self-injurious, stereotyped or overall challenging behavior. parents’ feelings of strain and parental stress also decreased after the program, while family quality of life had improved. the program did not change parents’ sense of competence. parents rated the ptr-yc as generally acceptable. conclusion as implemented within this real-world context of public ebi services, the ptr-yc program has shown promising results on child, parent, and family outcomes. journal of autism and developmental disorders

norms of conversation: autistic and neurotypical judgments of conversational coherence abstract purpose challenges in conversational topic management have been widely reported in autistic individuals, sometimes leading to negative social judgments. such challenges could stem from differences in conversational norms implicitly endorsed across neurotypes. this study investigated whether autistic and neurotypical adults differ in their judgments of conversational coherence, specifically regarding different types of topic shifts. methods we collected data from 49 spanish-speaking autistic adults aged 18–53 years ( m = 31.2, sd = 8.7) without intellectual disability, and compared their judgments with those of 96 neurotypical adults from a previous study (age: m = 35.5, sd = 9.9). participants read anonymized transcripts of child-adult conversations and were asked to rate the naturalness of the child’s utterance (containing either a topic shift or a contingent response) using a seven-point likert scale. the materials were identical to those used in a previous study with neurotypical adults. results autistic and neurotypical adults shared a similar implicit understanding of conversational coherence. both groups evaluated different types of topic shifts in broadly comparable ways, with those judged as less natural by neurotypical adults also receiving lower naturalness ratings from autistic adults. in addition, contingent responses which maintained the previous topic were consistently rated as more natural than topic shifts. conclusion these findings suggest that autistic and neurotypical individuals do not differ in their implicit understanding of conversational coherence. differences in conversational behavior are therefore unlikely to arise from different norms of conversation, at least insofar as topic management is concerned. journal of autism and developmental disorders

the combined effects of teachers’ caring behavior and academic self-efficacy on the academic achievement of chinese undergraduates: a fsqca approach abstract existing literature focuses on the influence of single or multiple factors on college students’ academic achievement, and few studies analyze the synergistic effect of multiple factors on college students’ academic achievement. taking 276 college students as samples, this study used the fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis method to explore the linkage effect of 5 antecedents on college students’ academic achievement from the two aspects of teachers’ caring behavior and academic efficacy. the results show that conscientiousness, supportiveness, inclusiveness, academic ability efficacy and academic behavior efficacy are not necessary conditions for the high or nonhigh academic achievement, and single anthems have weak explanatory power for the academic achievement. there are three ways to drive college students’ academic achievement, namely, the supportiveness-ability efficacy driving model, the conscientiousness-supportiveness-behavior efficacy driving model, and the conscientiousness-efficacy driving model. there are two paths leading to nonhigh academic achievement, and they are asymmetrical with the path of academic achievement improvement. by unpacking the configurational causal relationships among teachers’ caring behavior, academic self-efficacy, and academic achievement, this study enriches extant literature through the fsqca approach. it further delivers theoretical underpinnings and actionable suggestions for improving college students’ academic performance. bmc psychology

body image, associated stigma as a determinant of depression, anxiety, and stress among adolescents in salem, tamil nadu: a cross-sectional study. background: body image shaming is a growing public health concern affecting adolescent mental health. adolescents face increasing pressure from peers, families, and the media regarding their appearance. negative comments about appearance have been associated with depression, anxiety, and stress during this critical developmental stage.
aim: to explore the association between body image shaming and depression, anxiety, and stress among adolescents in salem, tamil nadu.
methods: a cross-sectional study was conducted among 310 adolescents aged 10-19 years, selected through multistage random sampling in salem. data were collected using a structured questionnaire including socio-demographics, the body image shaming scale (biss-20), and the depression, anxiety, and stress scale (dass-21). inferential statistics included chi-square tests to examine associations between categorical variables and binary logistic regression analyses adjusted for gender, bmi category, residence, and education level to assess the independent association between body image shaming and depression, anxiety, and stress.
results: high levels of body image shaming were reported by 46.8% of the participants. mild depression (19.7%), extremely severe anxiety (22.6%), and moderate stress (19.7%) were observed. there was a significant association between body image shaming and depression (χ²=13.5; p = 0.009), anxiety (χ²=41.2; p < 0.001), and stress (χ²=36.78; p < 0.001). bmi was significantly associated with stress (p < 0.02).
conclusion: body image shaming is prevalent among adolescents and is strongly associated with adverse mental health outcomes. awareness campaigns should target both adolescents who experience shaming and those who engage in it, promoting empathy, body positivity, and supportive peer interactions. targeted interventions, such as awareness campaigns, peer support groups, counselling services, and school-based programs, are essential to address this issue and promote adolescent well-being. bmc psychology

unlocking the power of the family: emotional resilience as the critical threshold for the protective role of family functioning against adolescent internet addiction abstract objective although both family functioning and emotional resilience are recognized as protective factors for adolescent internet addiction, the precise synergistic mechanism linking them remains unclear. in particular, it is unknown whether an individual’s level of emotional resilience serves as a prerequisite for the family environment to exert its protective effect. methods this study employed a two-year longitudinal design, following 7,853 junior high school students across two assessment waves. multilevel linear models with cluster-robust standard errors were used to test main effects and the interaction between family functioning and emotional resilience, while lagged models examined causal directionality. the johnson‑neyman technique was applied to probe the moderation pattern of emotional resilience. results longitudinal analyses confirmed that both family functioning (β = -0.168, 95% ci: -0.212~-0.124, p < 0.001) and emotional resilience (β = -0.137, 95% ci: -0.165~-0.109, p < 0.001) are significant independent protective factors against internet addiction. interaction analysis, however, revealed a finding: emotional resilience and family functioning interact negatively (β = -0.0065, 95% ci: -0.0091~-0.0039, p < 0.001). johnson‑neyman interval analysis identified a clear emotional-resilience threshold (score = 21; observed range = 11–66). only when an individual’s emotional-resilience level exceeds this critical point does high family functioning significantly reduce the risk of internet addiction; for adolescents whose emotional-resilience scores fall below the threshold, the protective effect of the family environment disappears. conclusion this study moves beyond the simple confirmation of independent protective factors and proposes a ‘protective-factor activation threshold model’ — an emotional resilience ‘switch’ that must be tripped before family support can protect against addiction. the findings indicate that emotional resilience is not merely a co-protective factor with family functioning but functions as a psychological “switch” that activates the family’s protective influence. this has clinical implications: for youths with low emotional resilience (≤ 21), interventions targeting the family environment alone are likely to fail. effective prevention strategies therefore must be dual-focused, simultaneously and preferentially enhancing individual emotional resilience levels to “unlock” the potential of the family support system. bmc psychology

balancing work and life: how employee welfare programs influence mental health with a gendered lens abstract background balancing work and private life is challenging, particularly for women, who continue to shoulder more domestic responsibilities than men. this disproportionate burden, exacerbated during and after the pandemic, negatively impacts women’s mental health. while company welfare programs could help alleviate this imbalance, there has been limited research on their effectiveness. methods in our cross-sectional study ( n = 7180 employees from four italian companies, data were collected between september 2020 and july 2024), we investigated the role of employee welfare in reducing work-life conflict and enhancing mental health for both men and women. we tested a moderated mediation model in which satisfaction with employee welfare was linked to workers’ mental health through a reduction in perceived work-life conflict. results descriptive analyses revealed that women more frequently reported lower levels of mental health compared to men. the mediational hypothesis was confirmed: satisfaction with welfare was associated with lower work-to-life conflict and with lower life-to-work conflict, leading to improved mental health for both genders. gender moderated the relationship between employee welfare and mental health through work-to-life conflict, with the employee welfare being less supportive in reducing work-to-life conflict and in turn enhancing mental health for women. conclusions overall, the results suggest that although welfare programs help reduce work-to-life conflict, they appear to be less effective in addressing life-to-work conflict and this is particularly detrimental for women. bmc psychology

behaviour–affect pathways and sociodemographic moderation in the well-being mechanism of urban parks: evidence from yangzhou, a ‘park city’ as urban park systems have developed worldwide, urban planning across different regions has exhibited a converging trend, characterised by ecological networks comprising multi-level green spaces and greenways. this study explores the mechanism linking park environments to users’ perceived well-being, taking yangzhou as a case study. based on questionnaire surveys and interviews, this study employs structural equation modelling and identifies four main findings: (1) the well-being mechanism of urban parks operates through behaviour–affect pathways; (2) accessibility and affordance predict perceived well-being indirectly through behavioural patterns and place attachment, respectively; (3) place attachment serves as a key mediator linking temporal regularity and perceived well-being; (4) pathways to temporal regularity are moderated by age, whereas the subsequent pathway to place attachment is moderated by socioeconomic status and age. furthermore, evidence-based recommendations for the development of urban park systems are proposed, highlighting subjective accessibility, functional integration, and social inclusion. environment and behavior

rtm protocol’s developments in war-affected ukraine abstract: the full-scale russian invasion of ukraine has created unprecedented mental health challenges, with post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) prevalence reaching critical levels among civilians, refugees, and military personnel. traditional trauma-focused therapies, while effective, are often difficult to implement in war conditions due to their duration, resource intensity, and emotional burden. the reconsolidation of traumatic memories (rtm) protocol, a brief, imagery-based intervention grounded in memory reconsolidation theory and research, offers a scalable alternative. this article examines the rtm protocol’s implementation in ukraine, including professional training, adaptations for frontline and hospital settings, and its integration into the armed forces’ psychological support framework. we discuss procedural modifications for high-risk environments, hybrid delivery models for continuity of care, and strategies to overcome stigma and logistical barriers. additionally, the paper explores the rtm protocol’s application for ukrainian refugees across europe and outlines the rationale for developing a child version of the rtm protocol to address trauma in children. emerging evidence suggests that rtm reduces intrusive symptoms, improves sleep, and restores functionality within three to five sessions, even under disrupted conditions. its brevity, minimal verbal disclosure, and compatibility with remote delivery make rtm uniquely suited for humanitarian and military contexts. these findings underscore the rtm protocol’s potential as an evidence-based, adaptable intervention for mitigating trauma in ukraine and similar conflict-affected regions. european psychologist

future directions for the advancement of person-centered culturally responsive treatment to support youth mental healthcare equity. youth from minoritized backgrounds face significant inequities in accessing and benefiting from evidence-based mental healthcare. although decades of research highlight the central role of sociocultural context in shaping mental health needs and treatment outcomes, current evidence-based interventions (ebis) rarely provide explicit guidance for addressing the intersecting sociocultural experiences of minoritized youth. in this article, we synthesize approaches to culturally responsive care and argue for a shift toward person-centered culturally responsive (pccr) treatment. pccr treatment is an individualized, practice-oriented approach that flexibly integrates youth and family cultural identities, contextual stressors, and strengths. using the development of the revamping evidence-based supports to promote effective culturally responsive treatment (respect) toolkit as an illustrative example, we outline a systematic, community-engaged, practice-based process for supporting pccr treatment within exposure-based cbt. we then identify key gaps in the current evidence base, including limited operationalization of pccr strategies, insufficient research on their effectiveness and mechanisms, and the lack of implementation strategies to support clinician training, decision-making, and sustainment. finally, we propose future directions to support a path toward advancing pccr treatment that prioritizes practice-based community-engaged methods. journal of clinical child and adolescent psychology

facilitators and barriers to latino/a adolescents' help-seeking behaviors: discussing mental health needs with parents and engaging in mental health services. latino/a adolescents report worse mental health than other ethnic-racial groups in the united states, including elevated depressive symptoms and anxiety, yet they remain less likely to access mental health services. negative perception about mental health within latino/a communities, shaped by negative beliefs about mental illness and limited knowledge of treatment, poses significant obstacles to care. low mental health literacy, including poor understanding of depression, anxiety, and the role of therapy and medication, further contributes to negative attitudes about mental health. prior work shows that latino/a adolescents often avoid disclosing mental health concerns to parents to prevent burdening them, and this lack of communication impacts their help-seeking behaviors. to examine these challenges, we conducted six focus groups (n = 56) with latino/a parents and adolescents aged 14-17 from michigan and texas. analysis identified negative perceptions about mental health as a central obstacle for both parents and adolescents, limiting open dialogue about mental health. adolescents reported fears of judgment or symptom minimization, contributing to delayed help-seeking behaviors. parents expressed a need for greater mental health knowledge, including symptom recognition, treatments, and strategies for discussing mental health with their adolescent children. adolescents emphasized the importance of trust, confidentiality, and family acceptance in facilitating disclosure and support. findings underscore the need for interventions that reduce negative perception about mental health, improve mental health literacy, and strengthen parent-adolescent communication to enhance latino/a adolescents' access to mental health care. practitioners can support families by providing tools that support dialogue and reduce negative-perceptions about mental health. journal of research on adolescence
‘we are first responders’: coaches’ management of suicide-related thoughts and behaviors among young people in sport journal of applied sport psychology
eating disorder recovery among athletes: a grounded theory of key people and actions involved in athletes’ recovery and reintegration into sports journal of applied sport psychology

longitudinal relationships between basic psychological need satisfaction and self-esteem among chinese children: between-person and within-person effects basic psychological need satisfaction (bpns), encompassing autonomy, competence, and relatedness needs, is theorized to support positive self-development, including self-esteem. at the same time, self-esteem, as a psychological resource, may shape individuals’ perceptions and behaviors, potentially influencing need satisfaction. this study examined the temporal ordering between bpns and self-esteem among children, with a particular focus on specific needs and the distinction between between-person and within-person effects. a sample of 739 chinese primary school students (48.4% girls, m age = 10.32 years) completed questionnaires across three waves over one year. random intercept cross-lagged panel models demonstrated that, when bpns was treated as a unified construct, bpns consistently predicted later self-esteem, whereas self-esteem did not predict later bpns. when autonomy, competence, and relatedness were incorporated simultaneously into an integrated model, competence need satisfaction emerged as the most consistent need-specific predictor of later self-esteem across both time intervals. conversely, self-esteem predicted later competence only in the first interval, and its associations with autonomy and relatedness were weaker and less stable. these findings suggest that within-person increases in bpns, particularly competence need satisfaction, predicted subsequent increases in self-esteem over time. the findings also underscore the potential relevance of need-supportive environments for children’s positive self-evaluative development. european journal of personality

what memory teaches: experiential knowledge, imagination, and accuracy in remembering abstract this paper clarifies and then indicates a conflict between, on the one hand, influential and longstanding ideas in the epistemology of imagination and, on the other, an emerging view of the accuracy conditions of remembering and the content of episodic memory—namely, alethism . although we explore several ways to resolve the conflict, we take the most plausible to be to reject alethism. drawing on assumptions made on both sides of debates about the epistemic limits of imagination, the paper constitutes an extended argument in favour of (‘strong’) authenticism about the accuracy conditions of remembering. authenticists can maintain that experience is necessary for certain forms of imagining and also that episodic memory is what supports and explains this fact by virtue of providing a privileged store of experiential knowledge. review of philosophy and psychology

school fairness as a bullying victimization protective factor: structure or personality? recent research finds students' perceived school fairness to be a protective factor against bullying. these findings are consistent with organizational research suggesting organizations and states characterized by more procedural justice have less rule-breaking in their membership. the rationale in extant research is based on structural arguments about the nature of the organization or state, but the research overwhelmingly measures perceived fairness as an individual characteristic. this approach creates omitted variable bias via the personality trait of agreeableness, which has a robust negative relationship with bullying victimization and is likely to be correlated with an individual's perception of school fairness. further, extant research tends to define fairness narrowly as fairness around punishments, neglecting fairness in grading. using a nationally representative sample of 3,098 tunisian middle and high school students in 40 schools, this study addresses these gaps using multilevel models to test relationships between structural (school-level) academic fairness averages while controlling for individual-level perceived academic fairness. item non-response is handled via multiple imputation using chained equations, and survey weights are used to produce national prevalence estimates. about 21.1% of tunisian students were victims of physical bullying, and 52.7% of tunisian students were victims of verbal bullying by other children. controlling for academic performance and other risk factors for bullying victimization, individual-level perceived academic fairness was associated with significantly less physical and verbal bullying victimization. controlling for individual-level perceived academic fairness, average school academic fairness (using school-level means for the same variable) was associated with significantly less verbal bullying victimization. neglect was also significantly associated with both types of bullying victimization, and intimate partner violence exposure was significantly associated with physical bullying victimization. findings suggest the need to target or include structural fairness as part of the protective measures for bullying in schools. journal of interpersonal violence

the effect of influencer image types on purchase intention: the mediating role of persuasion knowledge and the moderating role of parasocial relationships understanding how visual content shapes consumers’ persuasion processes in social media environments has become an important research issue. drawing primarily on the persuasion knowledge model (pkm) and parasocial relationship (psr) theory, while incorporating insights from self-reference theory and the elaboration likelihood model (elm), this study investigates how three instagram image types—brand selfies, consumer selfies, and packshots—influence purchase intention through persuasion knowledge and examines the moderating role of psr. a between-subjects experiment was conducted with 460 participants recruited through amazon mechanical turk. the results revealed significant differences in persuasion knowledge and purchase intention across image types. brand selfies were associated with lower levels of persuasion knowledge and higher purchase intention, whereas consumer selfies were associated with higher persuasion knowledge and lower purchase intention, with packshots showing intermediate effects. persuasion knowledge mediated the relationship between image type and purchase intention, and psr attenuated the negative effect of persuasion knowledge on purchase intention. these findings suggest that visual image composition itself can function as a persuasive cue and highlight the important role of relational context in shaping consumers’ responses to persuasive intent in influencer marketing. behavioral sciences

revising career goals on linkedin: the role of career-related social comparison and goal discrepancy professional networking platforms provide opportunities for career development but may also encourage career-related social comparison. this study examined whether the relationship between linkedin use and career goal revision is explained by career-related social comparison and perceived career goal discrepancy. data from 188 linkedin users were analyzed using correlation and serial mediation analysis. more intensive linkedin use was associated with more frequent career-related social comparison, which was related to greater perceived career goal discrepancy and, in turn, stronger career goal revision. the proposed serial mediation model was supported. post hoc analyses revealed differences between upward and downward career goal revision. whereas the serial mediation pathway explained downward goal revision, upward goal revision was directly associated with linkedin use and was not explained by the proposed mediators. career centrality was positively associated with career-related social comparison but did not influence the proposed relationships. the findings highlight linkedin as a context for career-related self-evaluation and goal regulation. behavioral sciences

passive aggression and life satisfaction in middle adulthood: sequential mediating roles of emotion-regulation difficulties and interpersonal relationship quality this study examined the relationship between passive aggression and life satisfaction among middle-aged korean adults, focusing on the sequential mediating roles of emotion-regulation difficulties and interpersonal relationship quality. participants were 299 adults aged 40–64 years who completed an online survey. the proposed sequential mediation model was tested using process macro 4.2 model 6 with 5000 bootstrap samples. passive aggression was positively associated with emotion-regulation difficulties and negatively associated with interpersonal relationship quality and life satisfaction. emotion-regulation difficulties were negatively associated with both the quality of interpersonal relationship and life satisfaction, whereas interpersonal relationship quality was positively associated with life satisfaction. sequential mediation analysis indicated that passive aggression did not directly predict life satisfaction when the mediators were included in the model. instead, the indirect effects through emotion-regulation difficulties and interpersonal relationship quality were statistically significant, whereas the remaining direct effect of passive aggression on life satisfaction was not significant. these findings were consistent with a pathway in which passive aggression was associated with greater emotion-regulation difficulties, poorer interpersonal relationship quality, and lower life satisfaction. behavioral sciences

integrating established apa resources with ai proficiency will empower the psychology major the introduction of artificial intelligence (ai) continues to impact higher education, providing an unprecedented opportunity to further increase the value of the psychology major. we emphasize ai proficiency as an essential and valuable skill for the psychology major and focus on purposeful and ethical integration into the established curriculum. we expand on the valuable american psychological association resources, including the guidelines for the undergraduate psychology major 3.0 , the principles for quality undergraduate education in psychology , and the skillful psychology student . each resource addresses the value of information and skills learned with a psychology bachelor's degree, enabling students to excel in a wide variety of career choices beyond traditional psychology applications. to continue effectively preparing students for their chosen careers, we propose that ai proficiency is a critical component for students moving forward as the workforce demands ai mastery. psychology learning and teaching-plat

problems of professional competence, remediation interventions, and outcomes in counselor education: a case‐level study abstract this study examined ppcs, remediation interventions, and outcomes in completed remediation cases within cacrep‐accredited counselor education programs. full‐time counselor educators who served as primary faculty on at least one completed remediation in the past 3 years completed a brief survey for each case, yielding 80 unique remediation cases ( n = 80). descriptive analyses indicated that remediation typically involved multiple co‐occurring ppcs and multiple interventions; 61.3% of cases resulted in successful outcomes. we conducted hierarchical binary logistic regression to examine whether the number of ppcs, the number of interventions, and faculty tenure status predicted remediation outcome. the number of ppcs was a modest negative predictor of success, whereas the number of interventions and faculty tenure status were not statistically significant predictors. findings indicate that remediation is typically multidimensional and highlight the importance of earlier identification of ppc patterns. counselor education and supervision

person-centered support from chatbots versus humans abstract: this study aims to examine whether and how perceived identity of a support provider and message quality would affect perceived agency of the provider and support outcomes. a total of 196 college students in china participated in a laboratory experiment. each participant was instructed to discuss a personal problem with either a chatbot or a human who would provide higher or lower person-centered support as preprogrammed. the results showed that perceived identity of a support provider and person-centeredness of support messages jointly affected participants’ perceptions of the provider agency, which in turn positively influenced participants’ emotional distress reduction, reappraisal, and perceived validation. the findings provide theoretical and pragmatic implications for the application of human–computer interaction in supportive communication. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

trust formation in ai expert systems abstract: as artificial intelligence expert systems (aies) are increasingly used in domains such as medicine, psychotherapy, law, finance, and education, it remains important to understand what shapes their perceived trustworthiness relative to human experts. a central limitation of prior research is that findings are often difficult to generalize across domains because domain and stakes are rarely varied together within the same design. we address this issue in a preregistered online vignette experiment in which uk participants ( n = 898) evaluated advice from an aies and a human expert under low- and high-stakes conditions in one of five domains. across all domains and both stake levels, human experts were perceived as more trustworthy than aies, whereas aies were perceived as riskier. for trustworthiness, between-domain effects were significant but small on average, mainly affecting the size of the human–aies difference, which was largest in medicine and psychotherapy and smallest in education. for perceived risk, stakes played a larger role than domain, with high-stakes situations increasing perceived risk across domains. importantly, trustworthiness and perceived risk did not change in parallel across conditions: domain differences were comparatively small for trustworthiness, whereas stakes played a larger role in perceived risk. overall, the findings suggest that cross-domain differences are smaller than often assumed once stakes are controlled, and that stakes matter more than domain for understanding perceived risk when people evaluate aies advice. journal of media psychology-theories methods and applications

adverse childhood experiences and subjective well-being in emerging adulthood: the mediating roles of loneliness and depression adverse childhood experiences have been linked to lower levels of subjective well-being in adulthood. however, the psychological mechanisms underlying this association in emerging adulthood remain underexplored. this study examined the association between adverse childhood experiences and subjective well-being among individuals aged 18 to 34 years and tested the mediating roles of loneliness and depressive symptoms. data from 2,041 participants were analyzed using multiple linear regression and serial mediation models, with indirect effects tested via bootstrapping. greater exposure to adverse childhood experiences was significantly associated with lower subjective well-being. both loneliness and depression emerged as significant mediators of this relationship, and a sequential indirect pathway involving both factors was also significant. these findings suggest that early adversity may be associated with lower well-being in emerging adulthood partly through loneliness and depression, highlighting that interventions targeting these factors may improve subjective well-being among individuals with a history of adverse childhood experiences. emerging adulthood

self-esteem as a psychosocial pathway between reading ability and psychological distress in chinese early adolescents background: reading ability is associated with adolescents’ self-esteem, and self-esteem is, in turn, closely related to mental health outcomes. however, the psychological mechanisms linking these three constructs remain unclear. objective: this cross-sectional study aimed to explore the relationship between reading ability and general psychological distress among chinese early adolescents and examine the mediating role of self-esteem, while controlling for literacy achievement. methods: a total of 373 seventh-grade students were recruited. reading ability was assessed via a battery of tests. general psychological distress and self-esteem were measured using the chinese version of the general health questionnaire (ghq-12) and the rosenberg self-esteem scale, respectively. data were analyzed with correlation analysis, mediation analysis, and latent profile analysis (lpa). results: reading ability was positively correlated with self-esteem (r = 0.18), while self-esteem was significantly correlated with psychological distress (r = −0.60). the indirect association between reading ability and psychological distress through self-esteem was significant (indirect effect = −0.09, 95% confidence interval [−0.16, −0.02]), whereas the direct association was not significant. lpa identified poor readers (14.7%) and typical readers (85.3%); typical readers reported higher self-esteem (cohen’s d = 0.29) and marginally better mental health (cohen’s d = 0.26). conclusion: these findings suggest that self-esteem may represent an important psychosocial factor linking reading ability with general psychological distress among early adolescents. the results highlight the potential value of school-based support that attends to both reading-related difficulties and students’ self-evaluations. given the cross-sectional design, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causal relationships. health psychology research

evaluating the longitudinal measurement properties of the social media disorder scale in early adolescents: associations with depressive symptoms and health-related behaviors abstract problematic social media use (smu) is an increasing concern for adolescents’ wellbeing worldwide. the nine-item social media disorder scale (smd) is widely used to assess problematic social media engagement in youth, yet its longitudinal psychometric properties remain insufficiently examined. establishing the scale’s robustness across time is crucial for valid developmental inferences and for informing prevention and intervention efforts. this study evaluated the longitudinal measurement invariance, item-level informativeness and test-level precision of the smd, as well as its criterion and predictive validity. self-report data were collected from 306 greek early adolescents ( m age = 13.30, sd = 0.58 at wave 1; 42.8% boys) across three waves spanning 12 months. the one-factor structure of the smd was confirmed and remained invariant across the three waves. item response theory analyses, estimated separately at each wave, indicated that the scale achieved peak measurement precision at moderate levels of problematic smu, while several items showed modest fluctuations in informativeness. higher levels of problematic smu were consistently associated with elevated depressive symptoms, and, longitudinally, predicted lower daytime alertness, reduced physical activity, and greater energy drink consumption one year later. these findings provide novel evidence for the longitudinal robustness of the smd, underscoring its utility for developmental research on adolescents’ digital behavior and supporting its application as a screening tool within the greek context. journal of psychopathology and behavioral assessment

development and psychometric evaluation of the adolescent and young adults trait-state irritability reactivity and regulation inventory (irrit-ij) abstract irritability is central to developmental psychopathology, especially in adolescence and young adulthood. however, existing measures do not consistently integrate tonic/phasic manifestations with trait-like and recent state-like assessment frames. this study presents the development and initial psychometric evidence of the adolescent trait-state irritability reactivity and regulation inventory (irrit-ij). methods: the study included 286 brazilian participants aged 11 to 24 years. items were developed through a narrative literature review, expert evaluation, and semantic assessment with the target population. internal structure was examined using polychoric exploratory procedures, the correlation gaussian mixture model, and confirmatory model evaluation. validity evidence was examined using spearman correlations with external measures and known-groups comparisons based on self-reported gender. results: expert evaluation showed high agreement (gwet’s ac1 = 0.87), and semantic evaluation supported item comprehension. the final reduced version included 26 items: 13 state items and 13 trait items. analyses supported a tonic/phasic two-dimensional structure for both subscales, with adequate fit and high internal consistency for state (α = 0.892; ω = 0.891) and trait (α = 0.891; ω = 0.890). irrit-ij scores were positively associated with measures of irritability, psychological distress, minor mental disorder symptoms, and emotional regulation, with stronger associations for irritability and psychopathological symptoms. female participants showed higher observed state and trait scores than male participants. conclusions: findings provide initial support for the irrit-ij as a complementary self-report measure for assessing recent state-like and trait-like irritability through tonic and phasic manifestations in adolescents and young adults. further studies should examine temporal stability, measurement invariance, discriminant validity, and independent cross-validation. journal of psychopathology and behavioral assessment

the effect of culture mix or not conflict against the decision making-a fnirs study. with increasing globalisation and deepening integration of local cultures, a growing number of product advertisements incorporate diverse, mixed cultural elements, designed to attract consumer attention and enhance purchase interest. however, the underlying mechanisms by which visual stimuli successfully influence consumer purchase behaviour remain poorly understood. in the present study, 300 college students aged 18-22 were recruited and randomly assigned to one of three between-subjects experiments (a, b and c), each comparing a control group (n = 50) with an experimental group (n = 50). the experiment employed a single-exposure paradigm, using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fnirs) to monitor changes in participant haemoglobin in brain cortical areas. facial expressions and vital signs were simultaneously recorded in parallel. based on these measurements, visual stimuli with mixed cultural elements collectively influence consumer decision-making through their intensity characteristics, potentially involving cognitive conflict processing and may be associated with enhanced emotional arousal and modulated autonomic nervous activity. these results provide exploratory evidence for the neural correlates underlying visual strategies in cross-cultural marketing and offer new methodological support for brand design and consumer cognition studies. international journal of psychology

hypothetical food purchase tasks and eating behavior: a systematized review and future directions abstract findings from hypothetical purchase tasks have significant implications for clinical and public health applications. despite this potential, research using food purchase tasks to assess the reinforcing value of food commodities and relations to eating behavior remains limited. in this systematized review, we sought to synthesize the literature on hypothetical food purchase tasks to enhance standardization, methodological rigor, and suggest future directions for expanding application to promising yet untested areas of eating behavior. a literature search was conducted using pubmed and psycinfo. the 14 qualifying studies identified highlight the variability in hypothetical food purchase tasks applications and provide preliminary evidence of their effectiveness in measuring food demand across diverse populations. results underscore implications for complementing clinical assessments and informing intervention efforts. results also highlight the capacity of food purchase tasks to differentiate demand across specific food stimuli, experimental manipulability, and sensitivity to variations in food demand. further, results demonstrate convergent validity between demand indices and other validated measures of reinforcing value and eating‐related measures (e.g., progressive ratio schedule tasks, binge eating). heterogeneity in application and reporting across studies could influence results and interpretation, but also demonstrate robust generality in applications. standardization in administration, analysis, and reporting may enhance rigor and reproducibility. journal of the experimental analysis of behavior

fear of childbirth and social support in women with and without previous traumatic pregnancy or birth experiences background fear of childbirth (foc) is a prevalent psychological concern with implications for maternal well-being and obstetric out-comes. although previous traumatic pregnancy or birth experiences and perceived social support are recognized correlates of foc, their combined effects remain underexplored. this study investigated whether previous traumatic pregnancy or birth experiences moderate the association between perceived social support and foc among pregnant women. participants and procedure the sample comprised 152 pregnant women (aged 22-42 years, m = 32.32, sd = 4.39) recruited online and through gynaeco-logical clinics across croatia. participants completed the wijma delivery expectancy/experience questionnaire-version a (w-deq-a), the social support appraisals scale, and the partner support scale. previous traumatic pregnancy or birth experience was assessed via a single self-report item. multiple linear regression models tested the main and interaction ef-fects of social support and prior trauma on foc, controlling for age and gestational week. results greater perceived family support was associated with lower foc scores (p < .001). women reporting a previous traumatic experience showed significantly higher foc than those without such experiences (p < .001). the interaction between trau-ma history and family support was significant (p < .05), such that family support exerted a protective effect among women with prior trauma, but not among women without prior trauma. the effect of partner support was not significant. conclusions the findings suggest that social support, particularly from family, may be relevant to childbirth-related fear in women with prior traumatic pregnancy or birth experiences. assessing such previous experiences and considering the role of supportive family communication may represent potential components of preventive approaches aimed at addressing foc and promoting perinatal wellbeing. health psychology report
